verdict.rationale: A 'Registeered applicant' is a Person (a conference applicant who has registered, with child Paid applicant), while B 'Registration' is a Conference activity (an event with children like Delegate and siblings like Lecture, Coffee break). One denotes a person/role, the other an activity/process, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote sponsorship in the conference domain: edas Sponsorship has a Travel Grant child and provider/cost properties, while iasted Sponzorship is a Money subtype alongside Fee/Tax/Tip. The spelling difference (Sponzorship) is a typo, and the intended instances (sponsorship funding) coincide.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to its author (Person), while B's 'is paid by' relates Money to the Person who pays it. Different domains (Document vs Money) and different intended relations (authorship vs payment), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of regular contribution (a document type submitted to a conference, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract), whereas B's 'Final manuscript' is a stage in the submission workflow (sibling of Initial manuscript, child of Submission). They denote different concepts: a document type vs. a submission stage, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee (organisational structure), while B's 'write' links a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's 'has First Name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'is connected with' is a broad object property linking Activity or Person to Item or Place. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's Social Event is a non-academic conference event (with children Excursion and Reception, siblings Break Event and Meal Event), while B's Speaker is a person role (a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited Speaker). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. person) and share no intended instances.

A 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about the conference, with a URL), while B 'Hotel registration form' is a form document for hotel registration. They share no intended instances: one is a web document, the other a registration form. Different parents (Conference document vs Form) and different properties confirm they are unrelated.

A's markConflictOfInterest relates a person (Author/Chairman/Reviewer) to a Paper to record a conflict of interest; B's is_paid_by relates Money to a Person (a financial payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is the event itself (has dates, accepts submissions, has members, administered by an Administrator). B's Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a person contributing to a conference, with subclasses Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author). One denotes an event, the other a person role; they are not equivalent.

A's 'early Registration' is a boolean flag on a Participant indicating whether they registered early, while B's 'Price' is an integer fee amount on a Registration fee. Different domains (Participant vs Registration fee), different ranges (boolean vs int), and different intended meaning (early-registration status vs monetary price), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to a Program committee (a structural/organisational relation), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person performing/giving something). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A is a Conference Chair, a leadership role in the organising committee (child of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Program Committee Chair). B is a specific kind of Author (an author whose CD proceedings are included), a participant role under Speaker/Delegate. The two denote different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Powerline Transmission Topic' is a research subject area under Topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the set of conference deadlines/important dates: A's 'Important dates' has properties for submission, abstract, camera-ready, acceptance, start/end dates and is linked to a conference volume; B's 'Deadline' has subclasses for abstract submission, author notification, and paper submission, and a Date property. The intended instances (specific dates/deadlines in the conference process) coincide, so they are equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact. B 'Coctail reception' is a Conference activity (sibling of Coffee break, Lecture, Registration), i.e. a social event. Different kinds of things with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference Member' is a Person subtype (a person involved in the conference: chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), while B's 'Conference days' is a Time subtype (a period of days during the conference, with children Delegate and One conference day). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. time period) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's NGO is a subclass of Organization (a non-governmental organisation type, sibling of Academia/Government/Industry Organization), i.e. an organisational affiliation of a person. B's Organizing Committee member is a subclass of Organizator under Person, i.e. a person role in the conference committee. Different kinds of entities (organisation vs. person role) with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is the whole conference event (has a name, has parts, proceedings, publisher, topics). B's Conference days is a time sub-concept under Time, with children Delegate and One conference day and siblings Deadline and Trip day — it denotes the set of days over which a conference runs, not the conference itself. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a document/paper submitted to a conference (a subclass of Conference document, with children like Poster, Presentation, Written contribution, and properties has contributions/is submitted at). B's 'Conference' is the event itself (with dates, country, members, topics, deadlines). A contribution is not a conference event; the entities denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its members (people on the organising committee), while B's hasLocation links a Conference Event to a Place (venue). Different domain, range and meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'max Papers' is a numeric constraint on how many papers a Program Committee Member may handle, while B's 'abstract' is the textual abstract of a Contribution. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

Both classes denote papers that have been reviewed/evaluated: EDAS 'Rated Papers' are papers that received ratings (reviews), and EKAW 'Evaluated Paper' are assigned papers that have been evaluated, with accepted/rejected children. They occupy the same stage of the paper lifecycle (after submission/assignment, before decision), so their intended instances coincide.

A is a class of document (a paper in its camera-ready form), while B is a deadline (a time point by which the camera-ready manuscript must be submitted). They belong to different branches (Document vs Time/Deadline) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic's preference for a reviewer), while B's 'review Written By' links a Review to a Possible Reviewer (the reviewer who wrote the review). Different domains (Topic vs Review), different ranges (Review preference vs Possible Reviewer), and different directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (a reviewer adjusting their bid/review score), while B's writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B 'Conference Trip' is a social event (subclass of Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet). They denote entirely different kinds of things — a document vs. an event — so they are unrelated.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (a conference/tutorial/workshop activity), while B 'Cryptography Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'Conference www' is a document/web-page artefact (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with property 'has a URL'), i.e. the conference website. B's 'Conference' is the actual conference event (with dates, country, members, topics, deadlines). Different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference volume' is a publication/proceedings entity (it has committees, contributions, tracks, important dates), whereas B 'Conference days' is a temporal entity under Time (with children Delegate and One conference day, siblings Deadline and Trip day). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted; B's 'has Name' is a string property giving the conference's full name. They share only the domain (Conference) but denote entirely different attributes with different ranges (boolean vs string), so they are unrelated.

A is a physical place (a type of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) in the conference venue domain. B is a document/form (a type of Form, sibling of Registration form and Hotel registration form) used to collect author information. They denote different concepts: a location versus a document artefact, so they are unrelated.

A's Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes or submits papers), while B's 'Author attendee book registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a monetary fee category for an author who attends and books registration. The two denote different kinds of things (person vs. fee) and are not equivalent.

A's `need` relates a Person to an Item (a person needs an item), while B's `presentation` relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presents a document). Different domains (Person vs Speaker) and ranges (Item vs Document) and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Member PC' is a program-committee member/reviewer (comment 'Reviewer', properties expert On Topic and reviewes Contribution), i.e. a role in the reviewing process. B's 'IASTED member' is a subclass of Delegate (a conference attendee) distinguished from 'IASTED non member', i.e. a membership/registration status of an attendee. The intended instances do not coincide: a PC member need not be an IASTED member and vice versa, and the contexts (reviewing role vs. attendee membership) differ.

A's updatedVersionOf relates a Document to another Document (a later version of the same document), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (the document a speaker presents). Different domains (Document vs Speaker) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a document/paper in the submission workflow (a subclass of Paper, with child Assigned Paper), whereas B 'Committee' is an organisational group with children such as Program Committee and Organizing Committee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Conference part to its Track/Workshop/Tutorial chair (an organizational role assignment), while B's property links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to the Events it lists (a publication/content relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration), while B's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment). Different range types and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (the venue/proceedings where it is submitted), while B's 'written By' relates a Contribution to an Author. Different domain/range and different meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a submitted/regular paper, sibling of Extended abstract), while B's Published Paper is a subclass of edas Paper restricted to papers that have been published (siblings Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn etc.). A Paper in the Conference ontology is not necessarily published, so it is broader than Published Paper; Published Paper is a specialization of Paper, hence A is subsumed by B.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a specific kind of conference contributor (a person invited to speak), while B's 'Science Worker' is a broad top-level person category (sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.) covering anyone working in science. The intended instances do not coincide: an invited speaker is not necessarily a science worker, and a science worker need not be an invited speaker. Different granularity and different domain roles, so unrelated.

A's has_a_committee_co-chair relates a Committee to a Co-chair (a person role on the committee), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper). Different domain and range concepts, so the properties are not equivalent.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a person (a conference applicant who has registered, with a child 'Paid applicant') in the Person hierarchy. B 'Travel Grant' is a sponsorship/funding entity under Sponsorship, not a person. Different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Invited Talk' is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation, sibling of Contributed Talk and Tutorial), whereas B's 'Speaker' is a kind of person (a role of an attendee, sibling of Listener and Organizator, with children Author and Invited Speaker). They denote different categories (event vs. person) and are not equivalent; at most an invited talk is presented by an invited speaker, but the entities themselves are unrelated.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration), while B's hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a review score). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote a review of a conference submission: A's Review is a Conference document with properties 'reviews' (Review -> Reviewed contribution) and 'has a review' (Reviewed contribution -> Review), and B's Review is a Document in the iasted ontology, whose sibling Submission and other conference documents place it in the same domain. The labels and intended instances (reviews of papers) coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'Conference document' is a broad class covering calls, announcements, www pages, reviews and contributions, while B's 'Contribution' is specifically a submitted work (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with authors, title, abstract and reviews. The Contribution is one kind of conference document, so Conference document is more general and Contribution is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit for a committee member), while B's hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership of a conference). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

Both denote the person who chairs the conference: cmt's Conference Chair is a Chairman/Conference Member (the general chair role), and Conference's Chair is a Committee member who chairs a committee (has a committee chair / was a committee chair of). The intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

A is a registration deadline (a date by which attendees must register), while B is the author-notification deadline (when authors learn of acceptance). They are distinct deadlines in the conference timeline, with different siblings (A: camera-ready, hotel reservation, submissions; B: abstract/paper submission) and B is tied to the 'notification until' property relating authors to the notification deadline. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

Conference contributor is a person role in the conference domain; Hotel room is a physical place (a room in a hotel). Different kinds (person vs. place), different paths (Person vs. Place), and no shared properties or comments indicating equivalence.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a paper that has undergone review (a document in the submission workflow, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution). B 'Review Rating' is the rating value assigned during review (with children Accept/Reject/Weak Reject ratings). One is a document, the other a rating value; they are different concepts, not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (an organized gathering such as a workshop or tutorial), while B's Conference Paper is a type of document/paper. They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.
A's 'expert On' links a PC member to a Topic (expertise area), while B's 'notification until' links an Author to a notification deadline. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'Call for paper' is a Conference document (a call for papers document), while B's 'Call For Manuscripts' is a Call subtype in edas, sibling to 'Call For Papers'. Both concern soliciting submissions, but A denotes the document/announcement and B denotes the call activity/type; they overlap in the conference domain without denoting the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (a call soliciting submissions), while B's 'Company' is an organization type (sibling of University). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A Workshop is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, with conferences having workshops), while B Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment (sibling of LCD projector and Overhead projector). They denote entirely different concepts in different branches of the domain.
Organizational Meeting (edas) is a conference event type, while Organizing Committee (sigkdd) is a committee/group of people; different kinds of entities.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs a conference (a role in the organising committee, sibling of Program Committee Chair and Associated Chair). B 'Student lecturer' is a kind of Lecturer/Speaker, i.e. a student who gives a lecture/talk. The two denote different roles with no overlap; the shared word 'Chair' is absent and the paths (Chairman vs Lecturer) confirm they are unrelated.

A Programme Brochure is a conference document listing events (it has properties event On List / lists Event and is published by an organisation), whereas a Hotel registration form is a form used for hotel registration. They share only the broad Document ancestor; their intended instances and roles in the conference domain differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's Organizer is a person/agent role (someone who organises the conference), while B's Organization is an institutional entity with subclasses Academia/Government/Industry/NGO and is the provider of sponsorships. Different kinds of instances, so not equivalent.

confOf's Participant is the general class of all conference participants (children Member, Regular, Student; siblings Author, Chair PC, etc.), while ekaw's Late Registered Participant is a specific subclass of Conference Participant distinguished by registration timing. Participant is strictly more general, so it subsumes Late Registered Participant, not equivalent.

Conference document is a document/artefact class in the conference domain (parent of Call for paper, Review, Conference contribution, etc., with properties contributes, has a date of issue, has authors). State in iasted is a geographical/administrative region (parent of Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state; involved in is situated in, is occupied by, occupy). They share no intended instances and no domain role; the only overlap is the word 'state' appearing in a child label, which is coincidental.

A's acceptPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (accepting a paper), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (authoring a paper). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; not equivalent.

A's hasAttendee relates a Conference Event to a Person (its range is Person), while B's hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (its range is Event). They connect different kinds of entities and are not the same relation.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing domain), while B's `hasMenu` relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (catering domain). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property of the class Review expertise, linking a review-expertise record to a literal expertise value. B's 'reviewes' is an object property linking a PC member to a Contribution (the paper they review). They differ in domain (Review expertise vs Member PC), range (literal vs Contribution), and meaning (expertise topic vs reviewing a paper), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference participant' is the general class of all people participating in a conference (its children are Active/Passive conference participant), while B's 'Early Registered Participant' is a specific subclass of ekaw's 'Conference Participant' distinguished by registration timing. Thus A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document announcing/inviting participation (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, Conference www), whereas B 'Conference Paper' is a scholarly paper submitted to a conference (subclass of Paper, sibling of Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, etc.). They denote different concepts: an announcement/invitation vs. a research paper.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a Conference-level datatype property giving the number of reviews per paper (domain Conference, range int). B's 'min Choice' is a Social/Working event property giving a minimum number of choices (domain Social event, Working event, range positiveInteger). Different domains, different ranges, different intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'registration Due On' is the deadline for conference registration (comment: 'Conference Registration Date and Time Deadline'), while B's 'Start of conference' is the date the conference begins. Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, but they denote different deadlines/events in the conference timeline, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Written contribution' is a broad category of written conference contributions (parent of Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, sibling of Poster, Presentation, Invited talk), whereas B's 'Submitted Paper' is a specific stage of a paper (a Paper that has been submitted, parent of Assigned Paper, sibling of Camera Ready Paper). They overlap in that submitted papers are written contributions, but neither subsumes the other cleanly: A includes non-submitted written contributions and B includes submitted items that may not be 'written contributions' in A's sense. Hence related, not equivalent.

Both are classes named Review under Document, representing a review of a paper in the conference domain. ekaw's Review has subclasses (Negative/Neutral/Positive Review) and properties linking it to Paper and Possible Reviewer, while sigkdd's Review is a sibling of Paper and Abstract under Document. The intended instances coincide: a review document/artefact. The extra structure in ekaw does not change the concept's identity, so they are equivalent.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is a document stage under Paper, specifically the abstract version of a paper, while Initial manuscript (iasted) is the first submission stage under Submission, typically the full initial version. They are related submission-stage concepts but not equivalent: an abstract is not the same as an initial manuscript.

A's reviewerOfPaper relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the paper they review), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (the paper they submit). Different domains (reviewer vs author) and different intended relations (reviewing vs submitting), so they are not equivalent.

A's studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (where they study); B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (what they receive). Different domains and ranges, different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Company (a commercial organization, sibling of University under Organization) and Academic Institution (an educational/research organization, parent of University and Research Institute) denote different kinds of organizations; Company is not an Academic Institution and vice versa.

A's has City relates an Organization/Person to a City (person's city of affiliation). B's is occupied by relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a place occupied by a person). They are inverses in direction and concern different subject/object kinds, so they are not equivalent.

Activity in iasted is a broad event/action class (children include 'Activity before conference', 'Activity after conference', 'Conference activity'; it is given by persons, dated, held in places, paid for, etc.). Conference in sigkdd is a specific kind of event with a name, city, start and end, held by ACM SIGKDD. A conference is a kind of activity, so Activity is more general and subsumes Conference; they are not equivalent.

A's Credit card is a payment card (Item > Card > Credit card), while B's Author of paper is a person role (Person > Speaker > Author > Author of paper). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

Accommodation Place is a physical location (a place where attendees stay, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place under Place), whereas Conference Trip is a social event (a planned excursion, sibling of Conference Banquet under Social Event). They denote different kinds of entities (place vs. event) and are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a university: confOf places University under Organization alongside Company, and ekaw places University under Academic Institution alongside Research Institute. Same label and same intended instances (universities are organizations/academic institutions), so they are equivalent.

A 'Dinner banquet' is a social-program activity (a conference event), while B 'Program Committee member' is a person role in the organization. They belong to disjoint branches (Activity vs Person) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Non Academic Event' is a conference event type (sibling of Academic Event, parent of Break/Meal/Social Event) in the EDAS event taxonomy. B's 'Non speaker' is a subtype of Delegate (a person role, sibling of Speaker, Session chair, etc.) in the iasted building/attendee taxonomy. One denotes an event, the other a person role; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a submitted contribution' links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (the paper a reviewer is qualified to review), while B's 'reviewes' links a Member PC (a person) to a Contribution (the paper they review). The ranges are comparable (submitted contribution ~ contribution), but the domains differ: expertise vs. person. They both concern reviewing a contribution, so they overlap, but they are not the same relation.

edas:Paper is a specific conference submission artefact (with children Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper, reviewed by reviewers, written by authors), whereas iasted:Document is a broad administrative item (children include Form, Invitation letter, Mailing list, Payment document, Transport vehicle). Paper is at most a kind of document, but the iasted Document class is not the same concept as a paper; the two classes do not have coinciding instances.

A is a kind of document (an abstract for an invited talk), while B is a registration fee category for non-authors. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. money/fees) and share no intended instances.

Departure is an activity that occurs after the conference (a temporal event, sibling of Full day tour), whereas Conference hall is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

Both are object properties with domain Person and range a document/item produced by that person (Conference document vs Item). In the conference domain, 'contributes' (a person contributes a conference document) and 'prepare' (a person prepares an item such as a paper) denote the same authoring relation, so a reference alignment would likely record them as equivalent.

A 'Call For Reviews' is a call document/event soliciting reviewers, a subclass of Call alongside Call For Papers/Manuscripts. B 'Reviewer' is a person role (a Delegate/Speaker who reviews). A call is not a person and a reviewer is not a call; they denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee, a specific committee membership. B's isMemberOf relates any Person to a Conference, a broader membership relation. A is a specialization of B (committee membership is a kind of conference membership), so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

Both properties link a person (Person/Speaker) to something produced or presented (Activity/Item vs Document), so they overlap in the conference domain, but the ranges differ: iasted's give can target an Activity or Item, while sigkdd's presentation targets a Document. They are not the same relation, so not equivalent; they are related.
A's hasAuthor relates Paper to Author; B's hasTopic relates Conference/Paper to Topic. Different domain/range kinds and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A is a kind of conference contribution (a document type, sibling of Paper, child of Regular contribution), while B is an award category in the sigkdd ontology (child of Award, sibling of Best Research Paper Award). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

heldIn relates an Event to a Location (object property), while City_of_conference relates a Conference to a string city name (datatype property). They are not the same relation: one is a general event-to-location link, the other a specific conference-to-city-name attribute. They overlap in intent (where an event/conference takes place) but differ in domain, range and kind, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Chair PC' is a person role (a PC chair, a subclass of Person in confOf), while B's 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (subclass of Conference in edas). They denote different kinds of entities (person role vs. conference structure) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.
A's hasCity relates Organization/Person to City; B's hasReview relates Paper to Review. Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop Chair is a specific conference role (a PC Member who chairs a workshop), while B Organizing Committee member is a broader organizer role (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). They overlap in that both are conference organizers, but neither subsumes the other: a Workshop Chair need not be on the organizing committee, and an OC member need not chair a workshop. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document submitted to a conference (with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Important dates is a set of deadline dates for a conference volume. They denote entirely different concepts and share no instances.

Both are datatype properties of the Deadline class pointing to a date/time value; 'done till' is the deadline's due date and 'Date' is the deadline's date, so they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

A 'Non Academic Event' is a conference event type (breaks, meals, social events) under Conference Event, while B 'Registration Non Member' is a fee category under Registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. fee) and denote different concepts.

A's reject Paper relates an Administrator to a Paper (a rejection action), while B's related To Event relates an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (a presentation/event link). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Sponzorship is a general money/financial category (sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip under Money), while B's Platinum Supporter is a specific sponsorship tier/role under Sponzor. They denote different concepts: a broad financial category vs. a particular sponsor level, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasName is a datatype property giving a Conference's full name (domain Conference, range string), while B's has_amount_of gives a Money value's amount (domain Money, range int). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

In confOf, Conference is a specific working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) under Working event. In edas, ConferenceEvent is the broad superclass of Academic Event and Non Academic Event, covering all conference-related events. A confOf Conference is a kind of edas ConferenceEvent, but edas ConferenceEvent is more general (it also covers tutorials, workshops, etc.), so Conference is subsumed by ConferenceEvent rather than equivalent.

A's Social Event is a specific kind of non-academic conference event (siblings Break Event, Meal Event; children Excursion, Reception), whereas B's Event is the most general event class, with children Scientific Event and Social Event. A's Social Event is therefore strictly narrower than B's Event, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'issues' relates a Publisher to a Conference proceedings (a publisher issues proceedings), while B's 'updated Version Of' relates a Document to another Document (versioning). Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is the overall conference event/entity (has members, submissions, administrators, dates, logo). B's Conference days is a temporal sub-concept under Time, denoting the days on which a conference takes place (children: Delegate, One conference day; siblings: Deadline, Trip day). The concepts differ: one is the conference as an organisational entity, the other a time interval. They are not equivalent.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property linking a Conference document to a date, while B's 'listsEvent' is an object property linking a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. They differ in domain, range, and kind (datatype vs object), so they cannot denote the same relation.

A's has Country relates an Organization or Person to a Country (a geopolitical entity), while B's can stay in relates a Person to a Place (a location where one can stay). The domains differ (Organization/Person vs Person only) and the ranges differ (Country vs Place), and the intended meanings are distinct: nationality/affiliation country versus accommodation location. They are not the same relation.

confOf's Social event is a specific kind of event (with children Banquet, Reception, Trip) under Event, while edas's Non Academic Event is a broader category under Conference Event that includes Break Event, Meal Event and Social Event. The edas Social Event (a child of Non Academic Event) is the closer match to confOf's Social event, so confOf's Social event is strictly narrower than edas's Non Academic Event.

A's has title is a datatype property of Social event / Working event giving the title of an event, while B's has Name is a datatype property of Conference giving the full name of a conference. Different domains (events vs. conference) and different intended meanings (event title vs. conference name), so they are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Tutorial Chair is a Person/Conference Participant role (an organiser who chairs a tutorial, sibling of Workshop Chair, Demo Chair, etc.). In iasted, Tutorial speaker is a Speaker/Author role (a person who presents a tutorial), placed under Author with siblings Lecturer and Plenary lecture speaker. The two denote different roles (organiser/chair vs. presenter/speaker) in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's email is a Person's email address; B's has Street is a street address line of a Contact Information record. Different attributes (email vs. street address) and different domains (Person vs. Contact Information), so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a conference participant who has paid/registered early. A's 'Early paid applicant' is a subclass of 'Paid applicant' under 'Registeered applicant', while B's 'Early Registered Participant' is a subclass of 'Conference Participant' with sibling 'Late Registered Participant'. The intended instances coincide: a person who registered/paid early for the conference. The differing parent chains reflect different modelling of the registration/payment hierarchy, not different concepts.

confOf Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas iasted Simulating is a research activity performed before the conference (sibling of Modelling). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a research activity, so they are unrelated.

Audiovisual equipment is a physical item/device category (siblings: Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle; children: Computer, LCD projector, etc.), while Organizator is a person role in the conference organization (siblings: Listener, Speaker; children: General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote entirely different kinds of entities and share no domain overlap.

A 'Steering committee' is a committee (a group) that governs a conference series, while B 'Sponsor' is a person (subclass of Person, sibling of Delegate) who funds an event. Different kinds (group vs. person) and different roles, so they are unrelated.

A's Student is a Person (conference participant role), while B's Van is a Transport vehicle (a type of vehicle). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

A's 'is situated in' is a spatial/geographic containment relation between places (domain/range Building, City, Place, State), while B's 'submit' is an author-to-paper action relation (domain Author, range Paper). They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are unrelated.

A's property is the inverse of a part-of relation whose range is Event (i.e., it relates something to an Event that it is part of), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about the conference, with a URL), while B's 'Tutorial' is a lecture-type conference activity. Different kinds of entities (document vs. event/activity), no overlap.

A's markConflictOfInterest relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to record a conflict of interest, whereas B's has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution relates a Review preference to a Topic or Submitted contribution to express a reviewer's preference. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, mapping a person to their family name; 'last name' and 'Surname' are synonyms in the conference domain.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'is connected with' is a broad object property linking Activity/Person to Item/Place. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (a person role within the committee), while B's 'organised By' links an Event to an Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domains (Committee vs Event), different ranges (Chair vs Organisation/Person), and different intended relations; they are not the same property.

A 'Communications Topic' is a subject area of the conference (a research topic under Topic), while B 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a document type (an abstract of an invited talk under Abstract). They denote different kinds of things — a topic vs. a document — and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Meal Menu is a specific kind of Document (a menu for a meal event), while B's Document is the general superclass of many conference artefacts (forms, invitations, reviews, submissions). Meal Menu is therefore strictly narrower than Document, not equivalent.

A's 'speak in' relates a Person to a Place or Time (giving a talk at a venue/time), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (accommodation). Different intended relations despite both having domain Person and range Place.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B 'Reception' is a subclass of Social event (a social gathering at the conference). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (person/registration vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document/paper artefact (a kind of Paper, sibling of Paper Full Version) in cmt, whereas B 'Workshop Session' is a scientific event/session (a kind of Session, sibling of Conference Session, Poster Session, etc.) in ekaw. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Review Question' is a question posed to reviewers (with numerical/textual subtypes), while B 'Submission' is a document submitted to the conference (with initial/final manuscript subtypes). They denote different concepts and are not related by subsumption.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the act/phase of submitting contributions), while B 'Record of attendance' is a document recording who attended. Different kinds (event vs document) and different meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper), while B's `pay` relates a Person to Money (a fee payment). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A Conference Session is a session within a scientific event (a slot containing several talks, with subtypes like Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session), whereas B Plenary lecture is a single lecture/activity (a talk), sibling of Session and Tutorial. They are related (a plenary lecture can occur within a conference session) but denote different concepts: a session is a container of talks, a plenary lecture is one talk.

Both are classes named Review under Document in the conference domain; ekaw's Review has subtypes (Negative/Neutral/Positive Review) and properties linking it to Paper and Possible Reviewer, which is consistent with edas's Review as a document type. Same intended instances (reviews of papers), so equivalent.

A is a subject/topic area for papers (a Topic subclass about satellite and space communications), while B is a type of conference lecture event (a Lecture subclass). They belong to different branches (Topic vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Pending Paper' is a paper in a submission state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper) in the document hierarchy. B 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a deadline event (sibling of Deadline Paper Submission and Author notification) in the deadline hierarchy. One is a document state, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

Conference document is a class of documents (call for papers, contributions, reviews) with properties like has authors and date of issue, while Participant is a subclass of Person (attendees such as Member, Student, Regular) with property early Registration. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection, child of Decision) about whether a paper is accepted; B's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip, child of Social event). They share only a superficial word stem and denote entirely different concepts.

A's 'Numerical Review Question' is a specific type of review question (a question on a review form, sibling of Textual Review Question), whereas B's 'Review' is the review document itself (sibling of Abstract and Paper under Document). They denote different concepts: a question vs. a review artefact, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee (a committee of people), while B's 'occupy' links a Person to a Building/City/State (a physical location). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to the people who review it (domain Paper, range Conference Chair/Reviewer/Session Chair/TPC Member). B's 'reviewer Of Paper' relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (domain Possible Reviewer, range Paper), i.e. it is the inverse direction and a different subject kind. A property and its inverse are not equivalent, so the two are unrelated.

A is a person who participates in a conference (a subclass of Person, with children Active/Passive conference participant), while B is a physical location (a subclass of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Accommodation Place). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. place), so they are unrelated.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property of Contact Information with range string (a postal code), while B's has_amount_of is a datatype property of Money with range int (a monetary amount). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they denote different relations.

Both denote a hotel used in the context of a conference: iasted's 'Conference hotel' is a Building subclass for conference lodging, and sigkdd's 'Hotel' is a Place subclass serving the same role (conference venue/lodging). The domain context (conference organisation) and intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent despite differing parent classes.

A's 'Student lecturer' is a person role (a Lecturer who is a student) in the delegate/author hierarchy, while B's 'Registration Student' is a fee category (a registration fee for students) under Registration fee. They denote different concepts (person vs. fee), so they are unrelated.

Country in edas is a geographical entity used as the range of Conference's has Country property, while Money in iasted is a monetary/payment concept with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment, amounts and payers. They share no meaning, no properties, and no position in the conference domain; a reference alignment would not relate them.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses like Invited speaker, Regular author), while B's 'Session' is a subclass of Lecture under Conference activity (a scheduled event slot with a Speaker lecture child). One is a person role, the other a conference event; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper a reviewer has been assigned to review). B's is_given_by relates an Activity/Item to a Person (the person who gives/presents the activity or item). The domains and ranges are disjoint in kind (Reviewer->Paper vs Activity/Item->Person), and the directions differ, so they are not the same relation.
A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/meeting), while B's Conference Participant is a person role. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and cannot be equivalent.

A's 'written By' links a Review to its Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), while B's 'designed by' links a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (domain Deadline, range ACM SIGKDD). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

In cmt, Review is a subclass of Document (a specific document type produced in the review process, with children like Meta Review and properties linking it to Reviewer/PC Chair). In iasted, Document is a broad class under Item whose children include Review, Submission, Form, Invitation letter, etc. Thus iasted's Document is a general superclass of the review artefact, and cmt's Review is one specific kind of iasted Document. They are not equivalent: Review is strictly narrower than Document, so Review is subsumed_by Document.

Conference applicant is a general person who applies to/registers for a conference (parent of Registered applicant), while Tutorial Chair is a specific organizing role (a Conference Participant and PC Member who chairs tutorials). They denote different concepts with no subsumption: an applicant is not a tutorial chair and vice versa.

A 'Regular contribution' is a kind of conference document/contribution (a paper-like submission, with children Extended abstract and Paper), whereas B 'Regular Session' is a kind of scientific event session (a scheduled event, sibling of Conference Session, Demo Session, etc.). They belong to different branches (document vs event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Reviewer is a person role (a Conference Member/User who reviews papers), while B's Reviewed contribution is a document class (a submitted contribution that has reviews). They belong to different branches (Person vs Conference document) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

Bid in cmt is a reviewer's bid on a paper (Reviewer -> Bid, Paper -> Bid), while ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd is the conference organisation itself (holds conferences, designs deadlines, searches sponsors). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Conference activity' is a subclass of Activity covering events/programme items (coffee break, lecture, presentation, registration, social program), while B's 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person covering people roles (general chair, program chair, webmaster). They denote different kinds of things (events vs. persons) and are not equivalent.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates Administrative events that run concurrently (symmetric, co-occurring sessions), while ekaw's 'part Of Event' is a mereological relation expressing that one Event is a component of another. Both are Event-to-Event relations, so they overlap in domain/range, but concurrency is not parthood (and parthood is not symmetric), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a physical location (a subtype of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place) where meetings take place. B 'Conference Trip' is a social event (subtype of Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet) that attendees go on. One is a place, the other an event; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string biography; B's writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person author. Different domain, range, and direction of relation, so they are not equivalent.

A is a full version of a paper (a document type under Paper), while B is a student registration fee category under Registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. fees) and share no intended instances.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a kind of conference event with two levels), while B 'IASTED non member' is a subclass of Delegate (a person/attendee role). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it (domain Presentation, range Active conference participant). B's 'is given to' links an Item to a Person it is given to (domain Item, range Person). Both concern the giving of a presentation/item to a person, but the direction and the entity types differ: A is presentation -> giver, B is item -> recipient. They are not the same relation, though they overlap in the conference-giving scenario, so 'related' is the safest non-equivalent verdict.

Regular Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a paper submitted to the regular track), while sigkdd's Paper is the general class of conference papers. Regular Paper is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

A's Review is a subclass of Document (a written evaluation of a paper, with children Positive/Negative/Neutral Review and properties review Of Paper, review Written By). B's Money is a financial entity with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment amounts and payers. They share no meaning in the conference domain; the only overlap is the word 'review'/'money' being unrelated concepts.

A's 'Co chair' is a committee member role (sibling of Chair, parent Committee member, linked to Committee via committee co-chair properties), i.e. a co-chair of a conference/committee. B's 'Session Chair' is a Person role that initiates calls and reviews papers, i.e. the chair of a session. Different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'paper ID' is an identifier of a Paper (domain Paper, range unsignedLong), while B's 'remark' is a free-text comment on a Contribution (domain Contribution, range string). Different domain, range and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Reviewer is a specific committee role (a Conference Member/User who reviews papers, with children Meta Reviewer and siblings Author, PC Member, Chair, etc.). B's Conference contributor is a broad superclass of all people contributing to a conference (children: Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author), and B has a separate sibling class Reviewer. The two are not the same concept; A's Reviewer is at most a subclass of B's Conference contributor, but the pair as given is not equivalent.

A's Poster is a kind of conference contribution (a document/paper type, sibling of Presentation, Invited talk, Written contribution), whereas B's Individual Presentation is a scientific event (sibling of Conference, Session, Track, Workshop) with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial. The two denote different categories (document vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

A's `name` is a datatype property of Conference and Person, giving the name of a conference or a person. B's `has title` is a datatype property of Social event and Working event, giving the title of an event. The domains are disjoint (Conference/Person vs. Social event/Working event), so the properties relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip under Social event), while B's Review is a document (sibling of Paper and Programme under Document). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (a reviewer adjusting their bid/review score), while B's pay relates a Person to a Registration fee (paying to register). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (a person/role), while B's has_a_publisher relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher (an organisation). Different domains and ranges, no overlap in meaning.

cmt:name is a datatype property with domain Conference and Person, while sigkdd:Name has domain Person only. The cmt property is broader (applies to both Conference and Person), so it is more general than sigkdd:Name, which is restricted to Person. They are not equivalent because their domains differ; sigkdd:Name is subsumed by cmt:name.

Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision) in cmt, while Banquet is a social event (sibling of Reception and Trip under Social event) in confOf. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'has Review' relates a Paper to its Review (domain Paper, range Review). Different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Shuttle bus' is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Taxi, Van) used for conference transportation, while B's 'Registration Student' is a registration fee category for students. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (transport vs. fees) and share no intended instances.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a person is a member of the conference/committee), while B's is given by relates an Activity or Item to a Person (the person who gives/presents the activity or item). The domains differ (Conference vs Activity/Item) and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it (domain Sponsorship, range Organization), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they give (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Call is a specific conference-organisation artefact (a call for papers/reviews/manuscripts, with submission deadlines and instructions, initiated by chairs), while B's Event is the general superclass of scientific and social events (with location, organisers, part-of relations). Their children, properties and intended instances do not coincide; a Call is not an Event.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is an administrative event (Camera Ready event) in the event hierarchy; they denote different kinds of entities and share no meaning.

OC Member (Organizing Committee Member) in ekaw is a Conference Participant who is part of the organizing committee, with children like OC Chair; sigkdd's Organizing Committee member is an Organizator with siblings General Chair, Program Chair, etc. Both denote members of the conference organizing committee, so the intended instances coincide.

Both are classes named Reception, placed under a Social Event parent within the conference event hierarchy (confOf: Event > Social event > Reception; edas: Conference Event > Non Academic Event > Social Event > Reception). Same label, same intended instances (a social reception at the conference), and matching parent concept Social Event, so they denote the same concept.

Conference www is a conference document (a web page about a conference, with a URL), while Research Institute is an academic organisation. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs organisation) and share no intended instances.

Topic in edas is a subject area of papers/conferences (has Topic from Conference/Paper, is Topic Of to Conference/Paper), while ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd is an organisation/agent that designs deadlines, holds conferences and searches sponsors. Their intended instances and roles in the domain do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Presentation' is an Academic Event (a session/event at which a paper is presented), with siblings Workshop, Talk Event, Organizational Meeting, and it is linked to Accepted Paper via relatedToEvent/relatedToPaper. B's 'Paper' is a Document (the written artefact) with children such as Conference Paper, Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, and properties like hasReview, coversTopic, paperPresentedAs. The two denote different kinds of things (an event vs. a document), so they are not equivalent; at most they are loosely related through the presentation relation, but the intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it; B's 'is paid in' links Money to the Building where it is paid. Different domains (Sponsorship vs Money), different ranges (Organization vs Building), and different intended meanings, so the properties are unrelated.

ekaw's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference) sitting under Scientific Event alongside Session, Track, Workshop. iasted's Conference activity is an Activity whose children are the individual happenings of a conference (Lecture, Presentation, Registration, Coffee break, Welcome address, etc.). The two overlap in that both concern a conference, but they denote different things: a whole scientific event vs. the collection/type of activities that take place at a conference. Neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both properties relate an entity to a city, but they differ in domain (Organization/Person vs Conference) and range (City class vs string literal). They are not the same relation, though they are conceptually related (both express a city association).

A's 'Final manuscript' is a stage of a submission (a document that has been finalized), while B's 'Best Research Paper Award' is a type of award given to a paper. They belong to entirely different branches (Submission/Document vs Award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to an anyURI (a logo image address), while B's 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item (acquiring something). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Person), and range (anyURI vs Item), so they denote different relations.

A is a subclass of Paper representing a paper in the pending state (siblings: Accepted, Rejected, Published, Withdrawn Paper). B is a subclass of Deadline representing the time point for notification of acceptance. One is a document/paper state, the other a temporal deadline; their intended instances cannot coincide.

A's 'assign External Reviewer' is a specific relation from a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (a person assigned to review), while B's 'give' is a very general relation from a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or a paper). The domains and ranges differ (Reviewer vs Person, External Reviewer vs Activity/Item), and the intended meanings do not coincide; 'give' is far broader and not the same relation as assigning an external reviewer.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who started the bidding process), while B's 'reviewer Of Paper' relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the paper they review). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee (a conference has a committee), while B's 'hold' links an ACM SIGKDD (the organisation/series) to a Conference (the organisation holds a conference). Different domains and ranges, different intended relations; not equivalent.

Conference Member (cmt) is a Person subtype representing people involved in a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs), while Social event (confOf) is an Event subtype (banquet, reception, trip). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person who presents a paper), while B's Hotel presenter is a subclass of Delegate (a conference participant who presents at a hotel venue). Both denote a person who presents, but they sit in different taxonomies (Author vs Delegate) and B is restricted to a hotel setting, so they overlap without being equivalent.

cmt's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (author submits paper), while ekaw's written By relates a Document to a Person (document written by person). These are inverse in direction and differ in domain/range: submit Paper goes Author->Paper, written By goes Document->Person. A property and its inverse are not equivalent, and here even the argument types differ (Author vs Document, Paper vs Person), so they are unrelated.

A is a piece of audiovisual equipment (LCD projector) under Item > Audiovisual equipment, while B is a person role (Organizator) under Person. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Conference Hiker is a subclass of Delegate (a person role/attendee type in the iasted ontology), while B's Conference is an event class with properties such as start/end date, city, and name, held by an ACM SIGKDD. A person role and an event are different concepts, so the two classes are unrelated.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title; B's ends on is a datatype property of Event giving the event's end date/time. Different domains (Paper vs Event) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Possible Reviewer is a Person (a person who may review papers, parent of PC Member, involved in reviewing via has Reviewer / reviewer Of Paper), while B's Review is a Document (a written review artefact, sibling of Abstract and Paper). One is an agent role, the other a document type, so they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's isWrittenBy links a Paper to its Author (authorship relation), while B's hasUpdatedVersion links a Document to another Document (versioning relation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Reviewer is a person role (a Conference Member/User who reviews papers, with properties like adjust Bid, assign External Reviewer, has Been Assigned Paper). B's Review is a conference document (a child of Conference document, sibling of Conference contribution and Call for paper, with properties has a review / reviews linking Reviewed contribution to Review). One denotes a person, the other a document artefact, so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event sibling to Conference and Tutorial, i.e. a small working meeting held alongside a conference. B's Organizational Meeting is an academic event sibling to Paper Presentation, Talk Event and Workshop, i.e. a generic organisational/academic meeting that also has Workshop as a sibling. The two overlap in the conference domain (both are meeting-like events) but neither subsumes the other: A's Workshop is a specific working event, while B's Organizational Meeting is a broader academic-event category that even lists Workshop separately. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an Administrator action that assigns papers to reviewers/committees and has range Conference, while B's 'paper Presented As' links a Paper to its Individual Presentation (a presentation event). Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

Evaluated Paper is a specific stage in the ekaw paper lifecycle (a Submitted Paper that has been assigned and evaluated, with Accepted/Rejected children), whereas sigkdd's Paper is the general document class for any paper (parent of Abstract and Review, submitted by an Author). Every Evaluated Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is an evaluated one, so Evaluated Paper is strictly narrower.
A's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (submission act), while B's is paid in relates Money to a Building (payment location). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

Reviewing event is a specific administrative event (the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions) in confOf, whereas ekaw's Event is the most general event class with children Scientific Event and Social Event. A reviewing event is a kind of event, so confOf's Reviewing event is strictly more specific than ekaw's Event; they are not equivalent.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered and paid late), while B 'Cheque' is a subclass of Payment document (a payment instrument). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Item/Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Associated Chair is a chair/committee role (a kind of Chairman and Conference Member, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), while B's Technical commitee is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. a category of conference attendee/participant, not an organising role. Different intended instances and different positions in the hierarchy, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a Person (a conference attendee who does not present), while B 'Conference Trip' is a Social Event (an excursion). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A 'Signal Processing Topic' is a research topic area (a subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.) used to classify papers. B 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a document type (a subclass of Abstract, sibling of Tutorial Abstract) representing the abstract text of an invited talk. They belong to entirely different branches (Topic vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while B's isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event (spatial location relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'scientifically Organises' has domain Academic Institution and concerns organising scientific events (conferences/workshops), while B's 'give' has domain Person and range Activity/Item, meaning a person gives a talk/presentation or item. Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Chair is a role within a committee (a person who chairs a committee, sibling of Co chair, domain/range of committee-chair properties), while B's Country is a geographic entity used as the range of a conference's country property. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'is situated in' relates a Building/City/Place to a Building/City/Place/State (a spatial containment relation between places), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (a person's ability to lodge somewhere). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Accepted contribution' is a reviewed contribution that was accepted (sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution) — a stage in the submission/review workflow. B's 'Review' is a document that evaluates a paper (sibling of Abstract and Paper under Document). One is an accepted paper, the other is the review/evaluation of a paper; they denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Textual Review Question' is a question on a review form (sibling of Numerical Review Question, child of Review Question), i.e. a component of the reviewing instrument. B 'Abstract' is a document type (child of Document, sibling of Paper and Review), i.e. a summary text of a paper. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A 'Written contribution' is a document/paper artefact (a subclass of Conference contribution, with children Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, sibling of Poster and Presentation). B 'Talk Event' is an event (subclass of Academic Event, with children Closing Talk and Welcome Talk, sibling of Paper Presentation and Workshop). One denotes a written document, the other a scheduled event; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Sponsorship is a funding arrangement/event with cost amounts, currencies, and provider relations to Organizations; B's Sponsor is a subclass of Person (a person who sponsors, sibling of Delegate). One denotes a sponsorship act/entity, the other a sponsoring person, so their instances cannot coincide.

A's title is the title of a Paper; B's has an ISBN is the ISBN of Conference proceedings. Different domains (Paper vs Conference proceedings) and different attributes (title vs ISBN), so they are not the same relation.

ekaw's Student is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference domain), while iasted's Student lecturer is a subclass of Lecturer under Speaker/Author/Delegate, i.e. a conference participant who is both a student and a lecturer/speaker. The two overlap (a student who lectures) but neither subsumes the other: ekaw Student includes students who are not lecturers, and iasted Student lecturer includes lecturers who are not students. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'reviewes' relates a PC member to a contribution (a reviewing relation), while B's 'is paid with' relates money to an item (a payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving a string name for a Conference or Person, while B's `has End Date Time` gives a dateTime end time for a Conference Event. Different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings (a name vs. an end timestamp), so they are unrelated.

City in iasted is a location class (a place where buildings, persons, and conferences are situated), while Conference in sigkdd is the event itself, with properties for its city, name, start/end dates, and being held by ACM SIGKDD. The sigkdd Conference merely has a 'City of conference' string attribute, so City and Conference denote different concepts (location vs. event), not the same class.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman who chairs the conference), while B 'Conference Session' is an event (a session within a conference). They belong to different top-level categories (Person vs Event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Security Topic' is a research topic in the conference subject taxonomy (sibling of Cryptography Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Card' is a physical item (parent of Credit card, sibling of Document, Transport vehicle). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a paper document), while B is a subclass of Deadline (the registration deadline time point). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. time) and share no intended instances.

Both classes are named Listener and denote a conference participant who listens rather than presents. In iasted, Listener is a subclass of Delegate (a conference attendee), and in sigkdd it is a subclass of Person alongside Speaker and Organizator. The intended instances coincide: a person attending a conference to listen. The differing parent (Delegate vs Person) reflects the different upper structure of the two ontologies, not a different concept.

A's 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a structural part-of relation within a conference). B's 'scientificallyOrganises' has domain Academic Institution and relates an institution to what it organises (e.g. a conference/event), i.e. an institution-to-event relation. Different domain, range and direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Conference volume' is the root conference entity that has committees, tracks, contributions, important dates and a location — i.e. one edition of a conference, matching ekaw's 'Conference' (comment: 'One edition of a conference'). The label 'volume' is a synonym for a conference edition/proceedings entity, and the property context (committees, tracks, contributions, dates) agrees with ekaw Conference's role as the central event entity.

A's isMenuOf relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (a menu belongs to an event), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (a person requires an item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both classes denote a tutorial in the conference domain: ekaw places Tutorial under Individual Presentation (a scientific event presented at a conference), iasted places Tutorial under Lecture (a conference activity). Despite different parent hierarchies, the intended instances coincide — a tutorial is a tutorial — and both are siblings of other presentation/lecture types (Contributed/Invited Talk vs Plenary lecture/Session). No contextual evidence suggests a different meaning, so they are equivalent.

Academia Organization is a type of organization (a kind of institution, sibling to Government/Industry Organization/NGO) in edas, whereas Organizing Committee is a committee (a group of people, sibling to Program Committee) in sigkdd. They denote different concepts: an institution vs. a committee, so they are not equivalent.

A's Review is a conference document (a review of a contribution, with properties linking it to a Reviewed contribution), while B's Slide Set is a presentation document (slides) under Document. Their intended instances differ: a review is an evaluation text, a slide set is presentation material. Although both are documents, they are not the same concept.

An Accommodation Place in edas is any place where attendees can stay (a general lodging concept, sibling to Dining Place and Meeting Room Place under Place), whereas iasted's Conference hotel is a specific kind of Building used for conference lodging. Every conference hotel is an accommodation place, but accommodation places also include non-hotel lodging, so Accommodation Place is broader and Conference hotel is subsumed by it.

A's 'is situated in' is a general object property relating places (Building/City/Place) to places/states, while B's 'City of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string city name. Different domain, range, and kind, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a name' is a datatype property assigning a string name to conferences, proceedings, publishers, topics, etc. B's 'End of conference' is a datatype property assigning a dateTime end time to a conference. They relate different kinds of things (name vs. end time) and have different ranges (string vs. dateTime), so they are not the same relation.

confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while ekaw's 'referenced In' links a paper to a publication/venue where it is cited (citation relation). Different kinds of things are related in different directions, so the properties are not equivalent.
