Both classes denote a generic location/venue in the conference domain. iasted Place is a broad location class with children Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office, Session room and is used as the range of location-related properties (is held in, is present in, is situated in). sigkdd Place is likewise a generic location class with children Conference hall, Hotel, Main office and is the range of can stay in. The shared children (Conference hall, Main office) and the same intended instances (physical locations where conference activities occur) indicate the two classes are equivalent, with sigkdd's narrower child set reflecting a smaller ontology rather than a different concept.

A's has Location relates a Conference Event to a Place (event -> venue), while B's is equipped by relates a Place to an Item (place -> equipment). Different domains, ranges and directions; they denote different relations.

A is a subclass of Paper denoting a paper that was rejected; B is a subclass of Deadline denoting the notification-of-acceptance date. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation from abstract to the work it belongs to), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker giving/presenting a document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's User is a general person role in the conference system (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while B's Non speaker is a specific subtype of Delegate (a conference attendee who does not present). The intended instances do not coincide: a User can be an author or reviewer, not necessarily a delegate, and a Non speaker is a delegate, not a system user. Different paths and sibling sets confirm they denote different concepts.

confOf's Member is a subclass of Participant (a person participating in a conference, with siblings Regular and Student), while ekaw's Conference Participant is a broad class directly under Person covering all conference roles (chairs, presenters, authors, etc.). Member is a narrower notion (a registered participant category) and is thus subsumed by the more general Conference Participant; they are not equivalent.

A's 'gives presentations' links an Active conference participant to a Presentation (the act of presenting), while B's 'presentation Of Paper' links an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper being presented. They concern the same conference activity but relate different kinds of entities (participant->presentation vs presentation->paper), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a research topic in wireless communications (a subject area under Topic in the edas ontology), while B is a physical item (a card, with child Credit card) under Item in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A is an academic organisation (a university), while B is a research activity (simulating) under Activity before conference > Research. They belong to different top-level branches (Organisation vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned By Administrator' links a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned them (domain Reviewer, range Administrator). B's 'has Reviewer' links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (domain Paper, range Possible Reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and direction of the relation; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of conference session/event such as Tutorial or Workshop) within the Event hierarchy. B's Activity after conference is a post-conference activity (with children Departure and Full day tour) under Activity, i.e. a social/logistical activity occurring after the conference, not a conference event itself. Different intended instances and different positions in the hierarchies, so they are unrelated.

A's isReviewedBy relates a Paper to the people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. the review assignment relation. B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item, i.e. a person giving/presenting something. The domains (Paper vs Person) and ranges (reviewer roles vs Activity/Item) differ, and the directions of the relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Contribution is a general submission entity (children Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by an Author, has title/abstract/keywords, reviewed by PC members). ekaw's Document is a broader bibliographic artefact class (children include Abstract, Flyer, Paper, Programme Brochure, Review, Web Site) with properties authorOf, hasUpdatedVersion, writtenBy. A Contribution is a kind of Document (a submitted paper is a document), but Document also covers non-contribution artefacts such as Flyers, Web Sites and Programme Brochures, so Contribution is strictly narrower: Contribution is subsumed by Document, not equivalent.

A's defaultChoice is a confTool-specific datatype property on Social/Working events holding a positiveInteger (a default choice count), while B's hasEndDateTime is a datatype property on Conference Event holding a dateTime (an end timestamp). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

Both properties link a presentation to the paper it presents: edas 'related To Paper' has domain Paper Presentation and range Accepted Paper, while ekaw 'presentation Of Paper' has domain Individual Presentation and range Abstract/Paper. The domains (Paper Presentation vs Individual Presentation) and ranges (Accepted Paper vs Abstract/Paper) denote the same concepts in the conference domain, and the direction is the same (presentation -> paper), so the two relations are equivalent.

A's 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person representing an individual who belongs to a conference (author, reviewer, chair, etc.), with properties linking it to a Conference. B's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and oddly also of Person/TPC Member) representing a type of conference with two levels, not a person. The entities denote different kinds of things (person vs. conference type), so they are unrelated.

Both properties link an event/activity to a location/place, but they are inverses in direction: ekaw's 'location Of' has domain Location and range Event (location -> event), while iasted's 'is held in' has domain Activity and range Place (activity -> place). Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, and 'is held in' is the more general relation (its range also includes Time), 'location Of' is subsumed by the inverse of 'is held in' rather than equivalent to it.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving the name of a Conference or Person (domain Conference, Person). B's `has Keyword` is a datatype property giving keywords of a Contribution (domain Contribution). They relate different kinds of things (names of conferences/people vs. keywords of papers) and have disjoint domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'written By' links a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'is paid for' links Money to an Activity or Item (payment). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

confOf's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while ekaw's Conference Session is a session within a scientific event (a part of a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session). They denote different concepts: a conference vs. a session track inside a conference.
Both are datatype properties with string range that give the title of a paper/contribution; cmt's Paper corresponds to confOf's Contribution, so title and has Title denote the same relation.

A Reception is a social event (a gathering with food/drink, sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B Departure is an activity after the conference (sibling of Full day tour), i.e. the act of leaving. Different event types with different temporal placement and purpose; not equivalent.

A's Lecture is a conference activity (an event type with children Plenary lecture, Session, Tutorial), while B's Organizator is a role/person type (a Person with children General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties giving an end date, but A's 'is an ending date' is a sub-property of the 'Important dates' class (a deadline/event end date within a dates structure), while B's 'end Date' is the end date/time of a Conference itself. They relate different kinds of things (important-date event vs. conference), so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship relation), while B's 'obtain' links an Author to an Award (receiving an award). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'go through' is an object property mapping an Item to an Activity (an item undergoing/participating in an activity). Different domain, range, and meaning; no equivalence.

A (Member PC) is a person role in the conference domain (a program-committee member/reviewer, subclass of Person, with properties expert On Topic and reviewes Contribution). B (Week Reject Rating) is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a rating value category used in the EDAS review process. They denote entirely different concepts (a person vs. a rating), so they are unrelated.

A 'Contribution co author' is a role of an author who co-authored a contribution (a person/author concept under Conference contribution > Regular author), while B 'Double hotel room' is a type of hotel room (an accommodation place under Place > Hotel room). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (authorship vs. accommodation) and share no intended instances.

A's 'occupy' relates a Person to a Building/City/State (where a person is located), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (who pays the fee). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not the same relation.

A is a submission event (an administrative event in the conference process, sibling of reviewing and camera-ready events), while B is a deadline for hotel reservation (a time/deadline entity, sibling of submission and registration deadlines). They belong to different branches (Event vs Time/Deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Attendee in edas is a general person role (sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.) covering anyone attending the conference, while Speaker in iasted is a specific sub-role of Delegate with children Author and Reviewer, denoting someone who presents. The intended instances do not coincide: an attendee need not be a speaker, and the iasted Speaker is a narrower presenting role, not the general attendee concept.

A 'Session Chair' is a Person role (a person who chairs a session), while B 'Session room' is a Place (a physical room where a session is held). Different kinds and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.
A's hasFax relates a Person to a fax number, while B's E-mail relates a Person to an email address. These are distinct contact channels, not the same relation, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is Initiated By' relates a Call to people (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. who initiated a call for papers. B's 'is equipped by' relates a Place to an Item, i.e. physical equipment of a room. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

Both are datatype properties with domain a deadline/important-dates class and range date, denoting the end/expiry date of a deadline; 'is an ending date' and 'done till' express the same relation (the date by which something must be done).

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' relates an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who was assigned to them (reviewer-assignment relation). B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, and no subsumption.

A's 'has gender' is a datatype property from Person to a literal (gender value), while B's 'is needed for' is an object property from Item to Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (literal vs Person), and meaning; no equivalence or subsumption holds.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete version of a conference paper (a Document/Paper in the cmt ontology), while B 'Cheque' is a payment document (a financial instrument) under Item > Document > Payment document. Despite both being Documents, their intended instances are entirely different: a paper is an academic contribution, a cheque is a means of payment. No synonymy or subsumption holds.

confOf's 'follows' relates two Administrative events (event-to-event ordering), while iasted's 'is held after' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal position). Different domain and range, so the relations do not coincide.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is a publication artefact (has publisher, volume, ISBN, name) produced from a conference. B's 'Conference activity' is an event/activity within a conference (parent Activity, children such as Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break, Registration). The two denote different kinds of things — a published document versus a scheduled event — so they are not equivalent.

A's Chairman is a Person role in the conference organisation (a person who chairs, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while B's Credit card is a payment Item/Card in the iasted ontology. They share no meaning, no properties, and no common context; the only superficial link is the word 'card' in 'Chairman' vs 'Credit card', which is coincidental.

A is a Person subclass (a conference participant with roles like Member, Student, Author), while B is a Money/Fee subclass (a specific registration fee amount for students). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies to attend the conference (parent of 'Registeered applicant'), i.e. a prospective attendee. B's 'Organizator' is a person who organises the conference (parent of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, committee members). The two denote different roles with disjoint instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's Review is a review of a contribution (has a review: Reviewed contribution -> Review; reviews: Review -> Reviewed contribution), i.e. an evaluation document. B's Programme is a conference programme document belonging to a conference event (belongs To Event: Programme -> Conference Event; has Programme: Conference Event -> Programme). Although B lists Review as a sibling under Document, B's Review is a distinct class from Programme; A's Review corresponds to B's Review, not to B's Programme. The two entities denote different concepts.

A's 'was a program committee of' relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (a specific committee-to-conference relation), while B's 'part Of Event' is a mereological relation between an Event and a broader Event. Different domain/range kinds and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference Chair is a specific chair role (sibling of Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair) under Chairman/Conference Member, while B's Co chair is a committee member role that is a sibling of Chair, i.e. a co-chair of a committee. Both are conference/committee chair roles, so they overlap, but the intended instances do not clearly coincide: a Conference Chair is not necessarily a Co chair, and a Co chair is a committee-level co-chair rather than the conference chair. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (the abstract is part of the paper), while B's 'presentation Of Paper' relates an Individual Presentation to an Abstract/Paper (the presentation is of the paper). Both connect a presentation/abstract to a paper, but the direction and the subject differ: A is abstract->paper, B is presentation->paper. They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Contributed Talk is a submitted, peer-reviewed individual presentation (sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial under Individual Presentation), whereas a Plenary lecture is a keynote-style lecture given to the whole conference (sibling of Session and Tutorial under Lecture). They denote different kinds of conference presentations, so they are not equivalent.

An IASTED non member is a specific kind of Delegate (a conference participant who is not an IASTED member), while Attendee is the general class of all persons attending the conference. The IASTED non member is therefore a narrower concept subsumed by the broader Attendee class, not an equivalent one.

A's 'has a publisher' links a Conference proceedings to a Publisher, while B's 'relates To' links a Document to events, sessions or persons. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Reviewer is a person who reviews papers and has review expertise/preferences; B's Conference Chair is a distinct role that initiates calls and reviews papers as part of a chairing role. They are different roles in the conference domain (a reviewer is not a conference chair), and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers submitted to the volume), while B's 'paper Presented As' links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the presentation form of a paper). The domains and ranges are entirely different concepts (volume->contribution vs paper->presentation), so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Tip is a monetary payment (child of Money, sibling of Fee/Tax/Sponzorship). They share no meaning despite the surface similarity of the labels.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'has Programme' links a Conference Event to its Programme. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Event is a broad umbrella for all conference events (its children are Administrative, Social and Working events), while edas's Break Event is a specific non-academic event (children Coffee Break, Free Time Break, Meal Break) sitting under Non Academic Event. Break Event is therefore a narrower concept than Event, so Event subsumes Break Event rather than being equivalent to it.

A's `reviews` links a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's `write` links a Person to an Item they authored (domain Person, range Item). Different domains, ranges and directions of relation; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving an integer volume number, while B's 'has Name' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's full name as a string. Different domains (proceedings vs conference), different ranges (int vs string), and different intended meanings (volume number vs name), so they are not equivalent.

A is a placeholder/test topic under the Topic taxonomy in edas, while B is a specific kind of document (an abstract for a tutorial) under Document > Abstract in ekaw. They denote different concepts (a subject area vs. a document type) and share no intended instances.

ekaw:Organisation is a general body (academic institutions, organising agencies, publishers) that organises events and publishes proceedings; sigkdd:Committee is a group of people (organizing/program/awards committees) within a conference. Their instances and roles differ, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of contribution (a document type submitted to a conference), while B 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a deadline/date for submitting abstracts. They belong to different branches (Contribution vs Deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a mereological/containment relation within a conference's proceedings). B's 'has Location' relates a Conference Event to a Place (a spatial location relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote the sponsorship concept in the conference domain: edas Sponsorship has a provider organization and cost, and sigkdd Sponzor has a sponsor name and is linked to the conference organization; the child types (Travel Grant vs. Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor) are specific sponsorship kinds, so the intended instances coincide.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered early and paid), while B is a subclass of Fee (a monetary charge for a hotel). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Track is a thematic subdivision of a conference (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, part of a Conference volume, with has tracks from Conference volume to Track). B Paper Presentation is an academic event (a session type) at which accepted papers are presented, sibling of Talk Event and Workshop, linked to Accepted Paper. A track is a topic/stream, not an event, so the two denote different concepts.

A 'Conference Session' is a scheduled event/meeting within a conference (an Academic Event subtype, related to Documents and Persons), whereas B 'Conference Proceedings' is a published multi-author volume (a Document/Proceedings subtype). They denote different concepts: an event versus a publication, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship relation), while B's 'has City' links an Organization or Person to a City (location relation). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and denote entirely different relations, so they are unrelated.

A's Demo_Chair is a conference committee role (a kind of Person/Conference Participant who chairs demo sessions), while B's Tutorial_speaker is a subclass of Author/Speaker who gives a tutorial. The intended instances differ (committee organiser vs. tutorial presenter), and neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a scholarly conference part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, with has workshops linking a Conference volume to workshops), whereas B's Coffee Break is a non-academic break event (sibling of Free Time Break and Meal Break). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Computer Networks Topic' is a research topic (a subclass of Topic, with subtopics like Security, Sensor, Optical), whereas B 'Paper' is a document (subclass of Document, with children like Camera Ready Paper, Submitted Paper). They denote different kinds of things: a topic is a subject area, a paper is a publication artefact. Although ekaw's Paper has a 'covers Topic' property linking papers to research topics, that is a relation between the two concepts, not equivalence. Hence unrelated.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference, Tutorial and Workshop (organisational events with topics, titles, choices and fees). B 'Hotel room' is a subclass of Place covering Double/Single hotel rooms (physical accommodation locations). They share no instances and belong to different branches (Event vs Place), so they are unrelated.

Workshop is a kind of working event (an activity/session type) in confOf, while Session room is a physical place (a room) in iasted. They belong to different branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person who writes papers: edas Author is a Person with 'is Written By' (Paper -> Author) and 'has Related Paper', while sigkdd Author is a Speaker who 'submit's a Paper and is the author of papers. The differing parents (Person vs Speaker) and extra subclasses in sigkdd reflect local taxonomy choices, not a different intended concept; the domain role of paper author coincides.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property giving a person's given name, while B's 'Nation' gives a person's nationality/country. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a conference-organisation entity to a conference/event entity, but the domains differ: A's domain is 'Important dates' (deadlines) and its range is 'Conference volume', while B's domain is 'Programme' and its range is 'Conference Event'. They are not the same relation (different source and target concepts), though they both connect organisational items to a conference/event, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Numerical Review Question' is a type of review question (a question on a review form, sibling of Textual Review Question) in edas, whereas B 'Negative Review' is a type of review (a review document with a negative evaluation, sibling of Neutral/Positive Review) in ekaw. They denote different concepts: a question vs. a review, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Chair is a Person who initiates calls and reviews papers (a conference-level organizer role), while B's Session chair is a Delegate (a conference participant/attendee) placed under Delegate in the building/place hierarchy. The roles differ: conference chair vs. session chair, and the contexts (Person organizer vs. Delegate participant) do not coincide.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track (a part/containment relation within a conference), while B's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (where an event takes place). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent.

A's memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation). B's give links a Person to an Activity or Item (contribution/participation relation). Different domains (Conference Member vs Person) and ranges (Conference vs Activity/Item), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Science Worker is a generic person role (sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.), while ekaw's Agency Staff Member is a person affiliated with an agency (sibling of Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student). The intended instances do not coincide: a science worker need not be agency staff and vice versa, so the classes are unrelated.

A's location is a datatype property giving the venue/place string of a Social or Working event, while B's registration Due On is a datatype property giving the registration deadline dateTime of a Conference. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Full Version' is the complete version of a paper (sibling of Paper Abstract, both subclasses of Paper in cmt), whereas B 'Demo Paper' is a paper type/submission category (sibling of Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc. in ekaw). They denote different concepts: one is a version/form of a paper, the other a kind of paper submission. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

In confOf, Assistant is a direct subclass of Person, a generic support/assistant role (comment 'confTool'), sibling to Administrator, Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, Scholar, Science Worker, Volunteer. In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a subclass of Organizator, i.e. a specific organizing role, sibling to General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Webmaster. The two denote different roles: a general assistant vs. a PC member, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property of Conference www whose range is a string URL, while B's 'Name of conference' is a datatype property giving the conference's name. They relate different kinds of information (URL vs. name) and are not the same relation, so they are unrelated.

Banquet is a social event (a meal/celebration) in confOf, while Publication is a document item (with children Book proceeding, Cd proceeding) in iasted. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a whole-part relation within a conference), while B's 'speak in' links a Person to a Place/Time (a person speaking at a venue/time). Different domains, ranges and meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (where a paper is submitted), while B's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who provides the sponsorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A Presenter in ekaw is a Conference Participant who presents a paper (parent Conference Participant, child Invited Speaker), i.e. a role of a person at the conference. B Plenary lecture speaker in iasted is a subclass of Author (path ... Delegate > Speaker > Author > Plenary lecture speaker), i.e. an author who gives a plenary lecture. Both denote people who present, but the ekaw class is broader (any presenter, including invited speakers) and is rooted in the participant hierarchy, while the iasted class is a specific kind of author/speaker. They overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a committee (a group of people) that organizes a conference, whereas B's 'Administrative event' is a subclass of Event denoting a process/activity (e.g. submission, reviewing, registration). They belong to different branches (Committee vs Event) and have incompatible properties (committee membership vs temporal ordering/parallelism), so they do not denote the same concept.

A's 'is an ending date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a literal date (the deadline by which something ends). B's 'is sent after' is an object property linking an Item to a Time resource, expressing a temporal ordering of submission/sending. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Important dates vs Item), range (literal date vs Time), and meaning (end deadline vs sent-after ordering), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'is a starting date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a literal date, i.e. it marks the beginning of a deadline/event. B's 'is held before' is an object property relating one Activity to another Time/Activity, expressing temporal ordering between events. Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

An Accommodation Place in edas is a general lodging location (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), while Hotel room in iasted is a specific room type with children Double/Single hotel room. A hotel room is a kind of accommodation place, so Accommodation Place is broader and Hotel room is subsumed by it.

A's hasDecision is an object property linking a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome), while B's has_a_degree is a datatype property linking a Review preference to an int (a reviewer's degree of preference). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the person reviewing the paper), while B's 'scientifically Organised By' links an event/conference to an Academic Institution (the organising body). Different domain, different range, different meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'author Of' relates a Person (domain) to a Document (range), i.e. person -> document. B's 'is used by' relates an Item (domain) to a Person (range), i.e. item -> person. The directions and the kinds of entities differ (Person/Document vs Item/Person), so they are not the same relation; at best they are inverses in a different domain, which does not count as equivalence.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome), while B's dealsWith relates a Contribution to a Topic (subject area). Different domain, range and meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration), while B's hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country. Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

Conference part is a structural component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) that is part of a Conference volume, whereas Individual Presentation is a scientific event (a presentation of a paper) with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial. Although both can have Tutorial as a child, the intended instances differ: Conference part covers organisational units of a conference, Individual Presentation covers presentation events. They are not the same concept.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person (domain) to an Organization (range), i.e. a person is employed by an organization. iasted's is_paid_by relates Money (domain) to a Person (range), i.e. money is paid to a person. The kinds of things related and the direction differ entirely, so the two properties are not equivalent (nor inverses, since the arguments are different types).

A's Abstract is a document type (a paper abstract, with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and it is presented as a paper), while B's Payment document is a financial document (children Bank transfer and Cheque). They share only the parent Document and denote different concepts.

Conference volume is a specific conference event (a conference with its proceedings/contributions, committees, tracks, dates), while Working event in confOf is the general superclass of Conference, Tutorial and Workshop. A Conference volume is a kind of working event (specifically a conference), so it is strictly more specific: subsumed_by.

A's Multi author Volume is a published document (a volume with multiple authors, parent of Proceedings, published by an Organisation), while B's Form is an administrative document (parent of registration/author-information/hotel forms). They share only the generic Document parent; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's User is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Talk Event is a kind of academic event (parent Academic Event, children Closing/Welcome Talk). They belong to different branches (person vs event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has short title' is a datatype property of Social event / Working event (a short/abbreviated title for events, per the confTool comment), while B's 'has Name' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's full name. Different domains (events vs. conference) and different intended values (short title vs. full name), so they are not the same relation.
A's Conference Member is a Person subtype (author, reviewer, chair), while B's Conference part is a structural component of a conference (track, tutorial, workshop). Different domains entirely.

A Conference Banquet is a formal social event (sibling of Conference Trip under Social Event), while B Coctail reception is a conference activity (sibling of Coffee break, Welcome address, etc.) that is a social gathering but not a banquet. Both are social events in the conference domain, but they denote different kinds of events, so they are related rather than equivalent.

hasDecision relates a Paper to its Decision (domain Paper, range Decision), while reviewOfPaper relates a Review to the Paper it reviews (domain Review, range Paper). They have different domains, different ranges, and opposite directions of association; they are not the same relation nor inverses.

A is the deadline for submitting papers (submission deadline), while B is the deadline for author notification of acceptance. They are distinct deadlines in the conference timeline, with different siblings (A has camera-ready, notification, registration deadlines; B has abstract and paper submission deadlines) and B is the range of 'notification until'.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (domain Program Committee, range Program Committee Member). B's was_a_committe_co-chair_of relates a Co chair to a Committee (domain Co chair, range Committee), i.e. it is the inverse direction and concerns co-chairs of a committee, not committee membership. Different kinds of things and opposite direction, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (a committee-to-conference relation), while B's 'parallel with' links two Administrative events (a scheduling relation between concurrent events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'abstract' is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its textual abstract (string), while B's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location. Different domain, range, and meaning; no overlap.

A 'Poster Paper' is a kind of academic paper (a document submitted/presented at a conference), while B 'Bank transfer' is a payment document (a financial instrument). They belong to entirely different subdomains of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's email is a datatype property of Person holding an email address; B's has Phone is a datatype property of Contact Information holding a phone number. Different domains (Person vs Contact Information) and different kinds of contact data (email vs phone), so they are not equivalent.

A's title is the title of a Paper; B's has Keyword is the keyword string of a Contribution. Different attributes (title vs keyword) of different (though related) classes, so they are not the same relation.

A's User is a person role in the conference domain (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Computer Networks Management Topic is a subject area for papers. They share no meaning; the pair is a cross-domain mismatch.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete version of a conference paper (a document type under Paper, sibling of Paper Abstract). B 'Bank transfer' is a payment document type (sibling of Cheque) under Payment document. They belong to entirely different subdomains (academic submission vs. payment/finance) and share no intended instances.

A's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its committee members (people), while B's hasCountry links a Conference to a Country (a location). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Chair PC' is a person who chairs the program committee (a role/position), while B's 'PC Member' is a program committee member, a broader category that in ekaw has 'PC Chair' as a child. The two denote different roles: chair vs. member. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other (a chair is not a member in ekaw's hierarchy, and a member is not a chair).

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a conference has members), while B's sign relates a Person to an Item (a person signs an item). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they denote different relations.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs paper assignment tools), while B's property relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (the issues it publishes). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Conference is the event itself (has a name, has parts, proceedings, topics). B's Conference building is a physical building (Place > Building) that hosts delegates, sibling of Conference hotel/airport. Different concepts despite the shared word.

A is a research topic in mobile computing (a subcategory of Topic in the edas ontology), while B is a physical transport vehicle category (with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) under Item in the iasted ontology. They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different domains.

A's has Decision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome of a submission), while B's study At relates a Scholar to a University (where a person studies). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'has gender' is a datatype property linking a Person to a gender value, while B's 'written By' is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They differ in domain, range, and kind, so they denote different relations.

Active Paper is a subclass of Paper in edas, representing a paper that is under review and has a rating; Abstract in sigkdd is a sibling of Paper under Document, representing the abstract text of a document, not a paper in the review process. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference), while B's is_present_in relates a Person to a Place/Time (physical presence at a location/time). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property giving the title (string) of a social/working event, while B's 'Start of conference' gives the dateTime at which a conference starts. Different domain (event vs conference), different range (string vs dateTime), and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a Committee (a group) that organizes a conference, with properties linking it to a Conference volume. B's 'Conference Chair' is a Person role (a single individual) who initiates calls and reviews papers. A group and an individual person role denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A relates a Co chair to a Committee (a committee-role membership relation), while B relates a Document to a Speaker (a presentation relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision) about a submitted paper. B's Renting is an activity before the conference (sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript), i.e. renting a venue or equipment. Different domains and no shared meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the chair ends a review), while B's expertOn relates a PC Member to a Topic (expertise area). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'has a name' is a datatype property mapping a broad set of entities (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic) to a string literal. B's 'covers Topic' is an object property mapping Event/Paper to a Research Topic class. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, and range, so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'has authors' relates a Conference document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'occupy' relates a Person to a Building/City/State (location/occupancy). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'review Criteria Entered By' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered review criteria), while B's 'invited by' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has gender' is a datatype property of Person capturing gender, while B's 'has First Name' captures a person's first name (with a comment about middle name). They relate different attributes of a Person, so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime that give the end time of the conference event/conference. 'Conference Event' in edas corresponds to 'Conference' in sigkdd, and the property names ('has End Date Time' vs 'End of conference') denote the same relation: the end date/time of the conference. Same direction, same kinds of things related.

A's Place is a general location class whose children include Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office and Session room, and it is used as the range of location properties such as is held in and is situated in. B's Main office is a specific kind of place, a direct subclass of Place in sigkdd alongside Conference hall and Hotel. Thus Place is strictly more general than Main office: every Main office is a Place, but not every Place is a Main office. The relation is subsumes (A subsumes B), not equivalence.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/Chair, with properties linking to Conference), whereas B 'Conference city' is a subclass of City denoting a location associated with a conference. They belong to different branches (Person vs City) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

edas:isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author (authorship relation). ekaw:referencedIn is a citation/reference relation between documents (a paper being cited/referenced in another), not authorship. Different kinds of things are related in different directions, so the properties are not equivalent.

A relates a Conference to an Administrator (who prints hardcopy mailing manifests), while B relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the presentation of a paper). Different domains and ranges, different intended relations; they are not equivalent.

A 'Pending Paper' is a paper in a submission state (a document whose review outcome is not yet decided), while B 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline/event for submitting papers. They belong to different branches (Document vs Deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'written By' relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship of papers). B's 'searched by' relates a Sponzor (sponsor) to ACM SIGKDD, i.e. a sponsor being searched by a specific organisation. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.
A's remark is a free-text note on a Contribution (paper), while B's has Cost Currency is a currency string for a Sponsorship. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Conference Member is a Person subtype (a person involved in a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Presentation is a Conference activity (an event with children Power Point presentation, Video presentation). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. activity) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Dinner is a Meal Event (a meal/banquet), while B's Conference Trip is a Social Event sibling of Conference Banquet (an excursion). They denote different social activities, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while B's 'Reviewer' is a subclass of Speaker/Delegate in a building hierarchy, denoting a person who reviews. The two concepts denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A is a research topic in microelectronics (a subject area under Topic), while B is a physical transport vehicle class (with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) under Item. They share no meaning in the conference domain.

confOf's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper), while ekaw's references relates a paper to another paper it cites. Different domain/range and different direction of meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A Tutorial Chair is a specialized conference participant role (a chair of the tutorial track), while B Program Committee member is a general organizer role for reviewing papers. Although ekaw's Tutorial Chair is also a PC Member, the sigkdd Program Committee member is a broader organizer class that does not specifically denote tutorial chairs; the intended instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the conference event itself (has dates, country, topics, papers due). B's Conference Hiker is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. a person who attends a conference, not the conference event. Different kinds of entities, so unrelated.

Conference in confOf is a working event (a whole conference event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas Industrial Session in ekaw is a specific kind of conference session (a sub-event within a conference). They denote different concepts: a conference is not a session, and neither subsumes the other.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Powerline Transmission Topic is a research subject area under Topic. They denote different concepts: an event type versus a topic category, with no overlap in instances.

A is a conference document (informational document for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a scheduled conference activity (coffee break, sibling of Lecture, Registration, Welcome address). Different kinds and domains; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page/URL about a conference, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B's 'Conference restaurant' is a building/place (a restaurant at a conference venue, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (document vs. place) and share only the word 'Conference'.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution), while B's 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment). Different ranges and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasTitle is a datatype property of Contribution (the title of a paper/contribution), while B's hasName is a datatype property of Conference (the full name of a conference). They relate different kinds of things (contribution vs. conference) and are not the same relation.

A is an organizational meeting, a kind of academic event (a session/event in the conference programme). B is a subclass of Author describing an author whose CD proceedings are included, i.e. a person role. The two denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's has Street is a datatype property of Contact Information with range string (a street address line), while B's has amount of is a datatype property of Money with range int (a monetary quantity). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they share no concept.

In cmt, Conference is the top-level event entity (has members, accepts submissions, has dates, administered by an Administrator). In edas, Conference Session is a sub-event/session within a conference, linked to documents and academic events. A conference is not a session; the entities denote different concepts.

A's 'has a publisher' links a Conference proceedings to a Publisher (publication venue), while B's 'covers Topic' links an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (subject matter). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Paper Author' is a role of a person (a subclass of Person in ekaw), whereas B 'Registration form' is a document/form artefact (subclass of Form under Document). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Conference part (Track/Tutorial/Workshop) is a component of a conference, while Person (Attendee/Author/Reviewer) is a human participant; their instances, parents, and properties (has a track workshop tutorial chair vs. has Email/First Name) do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an excursion) within the conference, while B Coctail reception is a conference activity (a reception). Both are conference social/activity events, so they overlap as kinds of conference social gatherings, but a trip and a cocktail reception are distinct event types, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Track workshop chair' is a Person who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial part of a conference, while B 'Session chair' is a Delegate (a person role) who chairs a session. Both are chairing roles for conference parts, so they overlap, but the scopes differ (track/workshop/tutorial vs session) and the ontologies place them in different hierarchies (Person vs Delegate under Conference building), so they are not the same concept.

A's Track is a conference part (a thematic session track, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, range of 'has tracks' from Conference volume), while B's Car is a transport vehicle (sibling of Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). The shared word 'track' is coincidental; the concepts belong to entirely different domains and do not denote the same class.

Both are the general superclass of the written artefacts submitted to a conference: cmt's Document has children Paper and Review, confOf's Contribution has children Paper, Poster and Short paper. Both are the thing that is written by an author and reviewed (cmt: has Conflict Of Interest Person->Document; confOf: written By Contribution->Author, reviewes Member PC->Contribution). The intended instances coincide, so the classes are equivalent.
A's 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher, while B's 'has Topic' links Conference/Paper to a Topic. Different domain, range, and intended relation; no overlap.

A's Paper is a document type (subclass of Document, with children Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper, written by authors, reviewed by committee members). B's Deadline is a temporal milestone (has a dateTime, children Abstract Submission / Author notification / Paper Submission, and is the range of 'submit until' from Document). They denote different concepts: a paper is not a deadline.

Written contribution is a broad category of conference contributions that includes regular contributions, submitted contributions, posters, presentations, and invited talks. Short paper is a specific type of contribution (a short paper), which is a kind of written contribution. Thus Written contribution is more general than Short paper, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.
A is a Person subclass (a role: someone who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial), while B is an Academic Event subclass (the workshop event itself). Different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Both properties relate a reviewer/PC member to the item they review: cmt's write Review has domain Reviewer and range Review, confOf's reviewes has domain Member PC and range Contribution. Reviewer and Member PC are the same role (a person who reviews), and Review and Contribution are the same artefact (a submitted paper/review object), so the two properties denote the same relation in the same direction.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (the author), while B's 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (the person prepares an item). The domains and ranges are reversed and the intended meanings differ: authorship vs. preparation. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A 'Steering committee' is a committee within a conference organisation (sibling of Organizing/Program committee, linked to a Conference volume), whereas B 'Academic Institution' is an organisation such as a university or research institute. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chair of the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while Accommodation Place is a physical location (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A is a conference topic (a subject area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a kind of scientific event (a presentation type under Individual Presentation). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic taxonomy vs. event taxonomy) and share no intended instances.

A's 'follows' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal ordering of events), while B's 'for Event' relates a Call to an Academic Event (a call being issued for an event). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Track is a conference part (a thematic session stream, sibling of Tutorial/Workshop, range of 'has tracks' from Conference volume), while B's Tax is a monetary charge (subclass of Money, with children Departure tax and Value added tax). The shared word 'Tax'/'Track' is coincidental; the concepts belong to entirely different domains.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people/committees), while B's has_important_dates relates a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

A's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location (where the event takes place). B's 'Name of sponsor' is a datatype property linking a Sponzor to a string (the sponsor's name). They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Event vs Sponzor), and range (Location vs string), so they denote entirely different relations.

Delegate is a person/role class (a conference participant, with subclasses like Speaker, Session chair, Listener) in iasted, whereas Conference hall is a physical place (a room/venue) in sigkdd, sibling of Hotel and Main office. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a committee (a group of people) that organizes a conference, with siblings Program committee and Steering committee. B's 'University' is a type of Organization (sibling Company) that scholars study at. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

A's hasCo-author relates a Paper to its Co-author (domain Paper, range Co author), while B's has_a_committee_co-chair relates a Committee to its Co-chair (domain Committee, range Co chair). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's heldIn relates an Event to its Location (where an event takes place). B's search relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (sponsor), which is a sponsorship relation, not a location relation. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both entities denote the same concept: a conference paper. In Ontology A, 'Paper' is a class in the conference domain; in Ontology B, 'Paper' is also a class representing submitted papers. The labels and domain context match, and no conflicting properties or comments suggest a different meaning.

cmt:User is a general person role (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while iasted:Author is a specific role under Speaker. Author is a kind of User, so User subsumes Author; they are not equivalent.

A's Pending Paper is a paper awaiting a decision (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn), while B's Rejected Paper is a paper that has been evaluated and rejected. They denote different states of the review process, so they are not equivalent.
Conference Member is a person role in the cmt ontology, while Hotel room is a physical place in the iasted ontology; they share no semantic overlap.

A 'Welcome address' is a conference activity (an event in the programme, sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break), whereas B 'Main office' is a Place (a physical location, sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. location) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Administrative event' is a conference-organisation event (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration) under Event, while B 'Active Paper' is a document state (a paper under review) under Paper. They belong to different branches (Event vs Document) and share no instances; the only superficial link is the word 'active/reviewing', which is not enough.

A's Sponsor is a Person who sponsors (sibling of Delegate under Person), i.e. a generic sponsoring person/entity. B's Platinum Supporter is a specific sponsorship tier under Sponzor, alongside Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter and Exhibitor. A generic Sponsor is broader than a specific Platinum Supporter tier, so Sponsor subsumes the tier concept rather than being equivalent; the specific tier is subsumed by the generic sponsor notion.

Talk Event is a specific kind of academic event (a talk), while ekaw's Event is the most general event concept covering scientific and social events. Talk Event is therefore strictly narrower than Event, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'review Criteria Entered By' has domain Conference and range Administrator, i.e. it records which administrator entered the review criteria for a conference. B's 'review Written By' has domain Review and range Possible Reviewer, i.e. it records the author of a review. Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's `name` is a general name property whose domain includes both Conference and Person, while B's `has the first name` is specifically the first name of a Person. A's `name` is broader (it can denote a full name or a conference name), so it subsumes B's more specific first-name property; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Regular author' is a person/role class (a kind of conference contributor, with children Contribution 1th author and Contribution co author), while B's 'Regular Paper' is a document type (a kind of Paper, sibling of Poster Paper, Workshop Paper, etc.). They denote different concepts (author vs. paper) and are not equivalent.

A's 'for Event' links a Call to the Academic Event it is issued for (domain Call, range Academic Event). B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (who prints hardcopy mailing manifests), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document/paper artefact (a subclass of Paper, sibling of Paper Full Version) in the conference-submission hierarchy, whereas B 'Computer Networks Optical Topic' is a subject-area topic under Computer Networks Topic. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts.

A's 'abstract' is the text of a Contribution (domain Contribution, range string), while B's 'done till' is a date by which a Deadline is completed (domain Deadline, range date). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence.

Both are conference-domain classes named Session, but they sit in different hierarchies: ekaw's Session is a Scientific Event (a scheduled event with children like Conference Session, Workshop Session, Poster Session), whereas iasted's Session is a Lecture (a talk-type activity with child Speaker lecture, siblings Plenary lecture and Tutorial). The intended instances overlap (a session is a scheduled slot containing talks) but neither is strictly more general than the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'belong to a conference volume' links an Important dates entity to a Conference volume, while B's 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Both are object properties linking a conference/event to the committee that organizes it. 'has an organizing committee' (Conference) and 'technicallyOrganisedBy' (ekaw) relate the same kinds of things in the same direction (event -> committee), so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'lists Event' links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to the Events it lists. Different domains (Conference vs. Programme Brochure/Web Site), different ranges (Administrator vs. Event), and different intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's Meta Review is a subclass of Review (a review of reviews), while B's Review is the general review class. Meta Review is strictly more specific than Review, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's min Choice is a datatype property giving the minimum number of choices (positiveInteger) for a social/working event, while B's lists Event is an object property linking a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, and range, so they are not the same relation.

A Workshop is a conference event/session type (sibling of Track and Tutorial, part of a Conference volume), while B Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Taxi, Van). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Attendee (edas) is a generic person who attends a conference, sibling to Author, Reviewer, Chair roles. Listener (sigkdd) is a person who listens, sibling to Speaker and Organizator, i.e. a passive participant in a talk/session. Both are person roles in the conference domain and overlap (a listener is typically an attendee), but they are not the same concept: Attendee is broader (any participant), Listener is narrower (one who listens, contrasted with Speaker). Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's 'Conference Trip' is a subclass of Social Event (an organised excursion during the conference). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Late Registered Participant' is a conference attendee classified by registration timing (sibling of Early Registered Participant), whereas B's 'Program Committee member' is an organizer role (child of Organizator, sibling of Program Chair, General Chair). Different concepts: attendee vs. committee/organizer role.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a specific role: the first author of a conference contribution, a subclass of 'Regular author'. B's 'Paper Author' is the general class of persons who author papers, a direct subclass of Person. Every first author of a contribution is a paper author, but not every paper author is a first author, so A is strictly more specific than B.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs the conference (a Chairman/Conference Member role in cmt), while B 'Worker non speaker' is a delegate who is a non-speaker worker (a kind of attendee) in iasted. They denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

Conference document is a specific kind of document/artefact (call for papers, contributions, reviews, announcements) that is a subclass of the broader iasted Item, which covers documents, publications, equipment, cards, vehicles, etc. The intended instances of Conference document form a proper subset of Item, so Conference document is subsumed by Item, not equivalent.

Student is a subclass of Person in the conference domain (a person role), while Single hotel room is a subclass of Hotel room (a type of accommodation place). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'scientifically Organised By' relates an event/paper to an Academic Institution (a sub-property of organised By), while B's 'occupy' relates a Person to a Building/City/State. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to a Conference proceedings (a publication relation), while B's `has Event` relates an Event to a sub-Event (a mereological/structural relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role/type of author of a conference contribution (a subclass of Regular author, sibling of Contribution co author), i.e. a person in the author role for a paper. B's 'Participant' is a general person attending the conference (parent of Member, Regular, Student, etc.), with property early Registration. The author-of-a-contribution concept and the general attendee concept do not coincide; an author may or may not be a participant and a participant need not be an author. Different paths (Conference document > ... vs Person > Participant) and different siblings/properties confirm they are distinct concepts.

A's 'assigned To' relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the person a paper is assigned to for review), while B's 'topic Covered By' relates a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (the event/paper that covers the topic). They differ in domain, range, and direction of meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A is a student registration fee (fee category for students), while B is a registration fee for SIGKDD members. They are distinct fee categories: student status vs. SIGKDD membership. B's sibling 'Registration Student' is the actual counterpart of A, so A and B are unrelated.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a kind of conference event/session), while B's Renting is an activity performed before the conference (logistics/venue rental). They share no meaning; the only overlap is the word 'renting' being absent entirely, so they are unrelated.

A's reviewWrittenBy links a Review to its Possible Reviewer (who wrote the review), while B's notification_until links an Author to a Deadline Author notification (a deadline for notifying the author). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Reception' is a social event (a gathering/activity) in the conference event hierarchy, while B 'Invited Speaker' is a person role under Speaker. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (author), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (presenter). Authorship and presentation are different relations with different ranges (Person vs Speaker), so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the top-level academic event (parent of Single Level Conference / Two Level Conference, with deadlines, topics, members, country), while B's Conference Banquet is a social event (sibling of Conference Trip under Social Event), i.e. a dinner, not the conference itself.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, a human who chairs the conference), while B's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a subclass of Conference document with a URL), i.e. a web page. They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A Program Committee Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs the program committee, a role in the reviewing process (it ends Reviews). B Session Chair (ekaw) is a conference participant who chairs a session at the event. Different roles with different responsibilities; the shared parent PC Member in ekaw does not make them the same concept.

A Conference Paper is a full paper submitted to/published at a conference (a kind of Paper, sibling of Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). B Abstract is a short summary document, a sibling of Paper and Review under Document in sigkdd. An abstract is not a conference paper; the two denote different artefacts, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person in the conference domain. ekaw Person is the general superclass of conference participants, authors, reviewers, students; sigkdd Person is the general superclass of listeners, organizers, speakers. The intended instances coincide (human individuals involved in the conference), and both are used as domain/range for person-related properties (authorOf/writtenBy vs Name/email/pay). No conflicting context indicates a narrower artefact meaning.

A's property links a Committee to its Co chair (a specific role within a committee), while B's organisedBy links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domains (Committee vs Event), different ranges (Co chair vs Organisation/Person), and different intended relations; they do not denote the same relation.

Subject Area in cmt is a classification category for papers (domain of hasSubjectArea with range Paper), while Topic in Conference is a thematic category used for conference parts, review preferences, and submissions. Although both are thematic/classification concepts, their intended instances and roles differ: Subject Area classifies papers, Topic classifies conference parts and review preferences. They are not the same concept in the reference alignment.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subclass covering all people contributing to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors), while sigkdd Author is a narrower Speaker subclass specifically for paper authors (with children Author of paper, Author of paper student, and properties submit->Paper, obtain->Award). Every Author is a contributor, but contributors include non-author roles, so Conference contributor subsumes Author rather than being equivalent.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to the Organization that employs them, while iasted's speak_in relates a Person to a Place/Time where they speak. Different intended relations (employment vs. speaking at an event), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'assign External Reviewer' relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (assignment of an external reviewer to a reviewer), while B's 'reviewes' relates a PC member to a Contribution (the act of reviewing a paper). Different domain, range, and intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'gives presentations' links an Active conference participant to a Presentation. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are unrelated.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, e.g. a co-chair of the conference), while Administrator in confOf is a generic administrative person (comment 'confTool'), sibling of Assistant, Volunteer, Participant. The roles differ: chairing vs. administration, so the classes are not equivalent.

confOf's Event is a broad class covering administrative, social and working events, while ekaw's Social Event is a narrower subclass of ekaw's Event (with children Conference Banquet and Conference Trip). Event is strictly more general than Social Event, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

cmt's Associated Chair is a specific chair role under Chairman (a Person who chairs), while ekaw's OC Member is a member of the Organising Committee, a Conference Participant role that is broader and includes non-chair members (its child is OC Chair). The two overlap in the conference-organisation domain but neither subsumes the other cleanly: Associated Chair is a chairing role, OC Member is committee membership. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a limit on papers), while B's expertOn relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise). Different domains, ranges and meanings.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that announces a conference. B 'Industrial Session' is a type of Conference Session, i.e. a scientific event within a conference programme. One is a document, the other an event; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event where attendees are received (siblings Banquet, Trip), while B's Conference Trip is an excursion/outing (sibling Conference Banquet). They are distinct social-event subtypes, not synonyms.

A's 'Written contribution' is a document/contribution artefact (a subclass of Conference contribution, with children Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, siblings Poster, Invited talk, Presentation). B's 'Presentation' is a conference activity (a subclass of Conference activity, with children Power Point presentation and Video presentation, siblings Coffee break, Welcome address, Lecture). One denotes a written document, the other a scheduled event/activity; their instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property of Person giving a person's first name (comment mentions middle name), while B's hasName is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's full name. Different domains (Person vs Conference) and different intended values (first name vs conference name), so they are not equivalent.

Accepted Paper in ekaw is a specific subclass of paper (a paper that has been accepted, part of the Evaluated Paper branch), whereas sigkdd's Paper is the general class of all papers (submitted, under review, accepted or not). Every accepted paper is a paper, but not every paper is accepted, so Accepted Paper is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Paper.

A's Conference is the central event class of the cmt ontology, with properties for submissions, dates, administrators, members and review criteria. B's Conference www is a document/web-page class (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) under Conference document, with only a URL property. They denote different concepts: the event vs. its web page.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract (a text artefact). B's 'related To Paper' links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a document/paper entity). The ranges differ in kind (Abstract vs Accepted Paper) and the relations are different: one attaches an abstract text, the other associates a presentation with a paper. They are not the same relation.

Conference document is a broad class covering calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc., with properties like contributes, has a date of issue, and has authors. Sponsorship is a funding arrangement with cost amount/currency and provider relations, and its only child is Travel Grant. The two classes have disjoint intended instances and no shared context, so they are unrelated.

A is a chair role (a kind of Person/Chairman who is also a Conference Member), while B is a subclass of Author describing an author whose book proceedings are included. They denote different concepts: one is an organisational role, the other an author subtype, with no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

Sponsor (a person/organisation funding the conference) and Organizing Committee member (a role within the organizing committee) are distinct concepts; Sponsor is a sibling of Delegate under Person, while Organizing Committee member is a subrole of Organizator alongside General Chair, Program Chair, etc. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's forEvent relates a Call to the Academic Event it is issued for; B's search relates the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper it presents (domain Individual Presentation, range Abstract/Paper). B's presentationed_by links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (domain Document, range Speaker).
