The domains and ranges are disjoint kinds (presentation vs document; paper vs speaker), and the directions differ, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'accept Paper' relates an Administrator to a Paper (accepting a submitted paper), while B's 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing proceedings). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent.

A's Conference Session is a scientific session (a subtype of Session under Scientific Event, with siblings Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session and child Industrial Session), i.e. a scholarly programme unit. B's Conference activity is a general activity (subtype of Activity, with children such as Coffee break, Registration, Social program, Welcome address), i.e. any scheduled conference event/activity. The two concepts denote different kinds of things and their contexts (parents, siblings, children) do not agree, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the organisation that issues conference proceedings: Conference's Publisher has properties 'has a publisher' (Conference proceedings -> Publisher) and 'issues' (Publisher -> Conference proceedings), and ekaw's Proceedings Publisher is an Organisation that publishes proceedings. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

An Attendee in edas is any person attending the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc. under Person), while iasted's Conference Hiker is a specific kind of Delegate (a paying participant who hikes), a narrower concept. The iasted class is thus a specialization of the general Attendee notion, so Attendee subsumes Conference Hiker rather than being equivalent.

A 'Performance Topic' is a subject area/topic category in the EDAS topic taxonomy (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Invited Talk' is a kind of scientific event/individual presentation (sibling of Contributed Talk, Tutorial). They denote entirely different concepts (a topic vs. an event type), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property on Conference volume with range string, while B's 'held In' is an object property on Event with range Location. They both express a location association but differ in domain (Conference volume vs Event), range (string vs Location), and property type, so they are not equivalent; they are related concepts.

A's read By Reviewer relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the person who reads/reviews it), while B's written By relates a Contribution to an Author (the person who wrote it). They are different relations in different directions with different ranges (Reviewer vs Author), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to the people who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. who issues/organises the call. B's 'is writen by' links an Item (a paper/contribution) to its author Person. Different domain (Call vs Item), different range (organisational roles vs Person) and different meaning (initiating a call vs authoring a paper), so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Active conference participant' is a person who gives presentations, a subclass of Conference contributor/participant. B's 'Speaker' is a subclass of Delegate with children Author and Reviewer, i.e. a person who speaks/presents at the conference. The two overlap in intended instances (active participants who present are speakers), but A is narrower: it excludes passive participants and is defined by giving presentations, while B's Speaker is a broader delegate role that also covers authors and reviewers. Thus A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'Committee member' is a Person (a role an individual plays, with children Chair/Co chair and properties linking to a Committee), whereas B's 'Committee' is the organizational body itself (with children Best Paper Awards Committee, Organizing Committee, Program Committee). The entities denote different kinds of things (person vs. group/committee), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (sessions running in parallel), while edas's 'related To Event' links an Accepted Paper to its Paper Presentation. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (the schedule of papers), while B's technicallyOrganises is a sub-property of organises linking an Organisation to what it organises (e.g. a conference/event). The domains (Conference Event vs Organisation) and ranges (Programme vs unspecified event) differ, and the directions of the relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (a dinner/banquet activity) in ekaw, while B 'Conference city' is a type of City (a location) in iasted. They denote different concepts: an event versus a location, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' relates a Contribution to an Author; B's 'review Written By' relates a Review (a subclass of Contribution) to a Possible Reviewer (a subclass of Author). B's property is a specialization of A's, as confirmed by B declaring 'written By' as its parent. They are not equivalent because B's domain and range are strictly narrower.

A's 'has a name' is a generic naming datatype property whose domain spans Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, whereas B's 'City of conference' is a specific datatype property with domain Conference and range string that records the city where a conference is held. They relate different kinds of information (a name vs. a location), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasStartDateTime is a datatype property of Conference Event giving the start time of an event; B's Date is a datatype property of Deadline giving the date of a deadline. Different domains (Conference Event vs Deadline) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Regular contribution' is a subclass of Conference contribution (a document/contribution type, with children Extended abstract and Paper), i.e. a kind of written submission. B's 'Paper Presentation' is an Academic Event (a conference event with relatedToEvent/relatedToPaper links to Accepted Paper), i.e. the event of presenting a paper. A contribution/document type and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are not equivalent and neither subsumes the other.

OC Chair (Organizing Committee Chair) in ekaw is the head of the organizing committee, matching sigkdd's General Chair, which is the top role in the Organizator hierarchy alongside Program Chair and Webmaster. Both denote the person chairing the conference's organizing body, so the intended instances coincide.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document giving practical information to attendees, while B's 'Review' is a document containing a referee's evaluation of a submission. They share no intended instances; the only overlap is the generic 'Document' parent, which is not enough for equivalence.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while Proceedings Publisher is an organisation (sibling of Academic Institution and Organising Agency). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

Administrator in cmt is a User who manages the conference (accepts papers, assigns reviewers, enters conference details), while Reviewer in edas is a Person who reviews papers. They are different roles in the conference domain, not synonyms.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving an integer volume number, while B's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution giving the abstract text (string). They relate different kinds of things (proceedings volume number vs. paper abstract text) and have different domains and ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasSubjectArea links a Paper to a Subject Area (a topic classification), while B's go_through links an Item to an Activity (an event/process the item passes through). The domains (Paper vs Item) and especially the ranges (Subject Area vs Activity) denote different concepts, so the two properties are not the same relation.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'is designed for' is an object property mapping Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person (a purpose/intended-use relation). They share neither domain, range, nor meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of conference contribution (sibling of Paper and Poster), while B 'Bank transfer' is a payment document (sibling of Cheque) in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (submission types vs. payment methods) and share no intended instances.

Talk Event (edas) is a specific academic event such as a welcome or closing talk, a single presentation event. Regular Session (ekaw) is a session within a scientific event that groups several presentations. They are related in that a session contains talks, but they are not the same concept: a talk is an individual event, a session is a container of events. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (a paper related to the author's work), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (an award the author received). Different ranges (Paper vs Award) and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event such as Tutorial or Workshop), while B's Worker non speaker is a kind of delegate/non-speaker person located in a conference building. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Talk Event is a subclass of Academic Event covering talks such as welcome/closing talks and paper presentations. B's Introduction of speaker is a conference activity under Introduction, i.e. the act of introducing a speaker, not a talk event. The concepts differ in kind (event vs. activity) and in intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

Conference participant is a Person (an attendee/actor in the conference), while Social Event is an Event (a social gathering such as a banquet or trip). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings). B's `is Topic Of` relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper that the topic belongs to (domain Topic, range Conference/Paper). The domains, ranges and intended meanings are entirely different, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Camera Ready Paper' is a paper in its final, accepted, camera-ready form. They denote different concepts: one is an announcement/document, the other a type of paper. Their paths and siblings (A under Conference document alongside announcements; B under Paper alongside Conference Paper, Submitted Paper, etc.) confirm they are unrelated.

A's 'has workshops' is a specific part-whole relation from a Conference volume to its Workshops, while B's 'part Of Event' is a general mereological relation between Events. The workshop relation is a specialization of the general event parthood relation, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

In cmt, Review is a document-like entity (a subclass of Document, sibling of Paper, with children Meta Review, and properties write Review / written By linking Reviewer to Review). In edas, Numerical Review Question is a kind of review form question (subclass of Review Question, sibling of Textual Review Question), i.e. a question item on a review form, not a review document. The intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are unrelated.

A's Conference is the top-level conference event/publication entity (it has a name and is linked to proceedings, parts, publishers, topics). B's Conference Banquet is a social event (a meal) that is a subclass of Social Event, sibling of Conference Trip. A banquet is not a conference; the entities denote different concepts.

A's Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster and Short paper under Contribution), while B's Final manuscript is a specific stage of a submission (sibling of Initial manuscript under Submission). They overlap in that a paper can become a final manuscript, but they are not the same concept: Paper is a document/contribution kind, Final manuscript is a version/state of a submission.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the participant who gives it (domain Presentation, range Active conference participant). B's 'awarded by' links an Award to the entity that grants it (domain Award). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings: presenting a talk is not the same relation as granting an award.

A is a conference topic (Medicine Topic, a subject area under Topic), while B is an award category (Best Applications Paper Award under Award). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

A's `end Review` relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the chair ends a review), while B's `is Reviewing` relates a reviewer-type agent (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper (the agent is reviewing a paper). The domains and ranges differ (Chair vs. reviewer roles; Review vs. Paper), and the intended relations are different: ending a review is not the same as reviewing a paper. They are not inverses either, so they are unrelated.

Working event (confOf) is a subclass of Event covering conferences, tutorials and workshops, while Web Site (ekaw) is a subclass of Document representing a published web resource. They belong to different branches (Event vs Document) and share no intended instances.

A's Topic is a subject area of papers/reviews/conference parts, while B's Person is a human participant (parent of Delegate and Sponsor) involved in giving, paying, and attending activities. Their instances, properties, and positions in the hierarchy do not overlap; the only shared word is absent, so they are unrelated.

A's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (author's related papers), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents the document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

In edas, Published Paper is a status-based subclass of Paper (siblings Accepted/Active/Pending/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), i.e. a paper that has been published. In ekaw, Regular Paper is a type-of-submission subclass of Paper (siblings Camera Ready, Conference, Demo, Industrial, Poster, Submitted, Workshop Paper), i.e. a full research paper as opposed to demo/poster/workshop papers. The two classifications are orthogonal: a regular paper may be submitted or camera-ready, and a published paper may be any submission type. Neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Co chair' is a committee member who co-chairs (sibling of Chair, with committee co-chair roles), while B's 'General Chair' is a specific organizing role (sibling of Program Chair, Webmaster) heading the conference. Both are senior chairing roles in the conference domain, so they overlap, but a co-chair is not the same concept as a general chair; hence related rather than equivalent.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a conference event (Closing Talk, a kind of Talk Event). Their paths, parents and siblings are entirely disjoint (Person vs Conference Event), so they denote different concepts.

A's 'Conference Session' is a subclass of Session (a scientific event such as a regular, poster, demo or industrial session) within the event hierarchy. B's 'Conference state' is a subclass of State, alongside Presenter state and Sponsor state, i.e. a status/state of a conference or its participants, not an event. The shared word 'Conference' does not make them the same concept; their paths, parents and siblings show different intended instances.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' relates an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the committee is a body that organized a particular conference/volume), while B's 'organises' relates an Organisation or Person to an Event (an agent organizes an event). The domains differ (committee body vs. organisation/person) and the ranges differ (conference volume vs. event), and the direction/meaning of the relation is not the same, so they are not equivalent.

A's `date` is a datatype property of a Conference giving a date value (range date), while B's `has a URL` is a datatype property of a Conference www giving a string URL. They relate different kinds of things (a date vs. a URL string) and are not the same relation.

Contribution in confOf is the general submission class (children Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by Author, reviewed by PC member, has abstract/title/keywords). Rated Papers in edas is a narrower class under Active Paper (Document > Paper > Active Paper > Rated Papers), i.e. papers that have received ratings. Contribution is strictly more general than Rated Papers, so Contribution subsumes Rated Papers rather than being equivalent.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property of Conference www with range string, giving a web address for a conference website. B's 'has Cost Amount' is a datatype property of Sponsorship with range int, giving a monetary amount for a sponsorship. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'employed By' links a Person to an Organization (employment). Different domain, range, and meaning; they are not the same relation.

Both denote a social gathering/reception event at a conference: confOf's Reception is a Social event (sibling of Banquet, Trip), and iasted's Coctail reception is a Conference activity alongside Social program and Coffee break. The intended instances (a reception held during the conference) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite the spelling difference.

Both denote a poster contribution: A's Poster is a Conference contribution with an abstract, sibling of Presentation/Invited talk; B's Poster Paper is a Paper subtype alongside Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc. Same intended instances (poster submissions/presentations) in the conference domain.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings whose range is a string holding an ISBN identifier, while B's 'has Title' is a datatype property of Contribution holding a title string. They relate different kinds of things (proceedings vs. contribution) and carry different information (ISBN vs. title), so they are not the same relation.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during a conference, while Audiovisual equipment is a physical item category (parent of Computer, LCD projector, etc.) in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Participant in confOf is a general attendee role (parent of Member, Regular, Student; sibling of Author, Chair PC, etc.), while Organizator in sigkdd is specifically an organizer role (parent of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc.). They denote different conference roles and are not equivalent; Participant is broader and does not subsume Organizator either, since organizers are not participants in the confOf sense.

A's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines), while B's 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person. Different domain, range and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Abstract is a general abstract of a conference contribution (paper, poster, presentation), while B's Tutorial Abstract is a specific kind of abstract for a tutorial, a subclass of ekaw's Abstract. A's Abstract is broader and does not correspond specifically to a tutorial abstract, so A is subsumed by B's more general Abstract concept, not equivalent to the narrower Tutorial Abstract.

A's co-writePaper relates a Co author (a co-authoring agent) to a Paper, while B's authorOf relates a Person to a Document. Both express authorship of a written work, but the domains differ (Co author vs Person) and the ranges differ (Paper vs Document), so they are not the same relation; they overlap in meaning but are not equivalent.

A is a class of accepted conference contributions (a document/contribution in the submission workflow, sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B is a class of review ratings (a value in the review-rating scale, sibling of Accept Rating and Week Reject Rating). One denotes a kind of contribution, the other a kind of rating value; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.
A Reception is a social gathering (standing reception) while a Conference Trip is an excursion/outing; both are Social Events but denote different activities, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Workshop Paper' is a kind of Paper (a scientific contribution submitted to a workshop), while B 'Mailing list' is a Document used for communication/administration in the conference organisation. They share no intended instances: a paper is not a mailing list, and their paths (Paper vs Document) and sibling sets (Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper... vs Form, Invitation letter, Review...) confirm different concepts.

confOf's 'Member PC' is commented 'Reviewer' and has the property 'reviewes' (Member PC -> Contribution), i.e. a person who reviews contributions. iasted's 'Reviewer' is a person (under Delegate > Speaker) who reviews papers. Both denote the same conference-domain role of a program-committee member/reviewer, so the classes are equivalent despite the different labels and paths.

Paper Full Version is a subclass of Paper (a document type: the full version of a submitted paper), while Call for paper is a conference document announcing a call for submissions. They denote different concepts: one is a kind of paper, the other a kind of announcement/document, so they are not equivalent.
Associated Chair (a committee role/person) and Trip city (a location) are different kinds of entities; no subclass, instance, or property relation holds between them.

A 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (a dinner/banquet activity) in the event hierarchy, while B 'Fee for extra trip' is a monetary fee for an optional excursion. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Money) and denote different concepts; the only superficial link is the trip/banquet social aspect, which does not make them equivalent.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation between a document and its published forms), while B's 'written By' relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Reject Rating' is a rating value on a review indicating rejection (siblings: Accept Rating, Accept If Room Rating, Week Reject Rating), i.e. a negative recommendation score. B's 'Positive Review' is a review document whose content is positive (siblings: Negative Review, Neutral Review), i.e. a review with positive sentiment. The two denote different concepts: a rating category vs. a review type, and their polarity is even opposite (reject vs. positive).

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property on Review expertise (a review's expertise topic, a literal), while B's 'has Reviewer' is an object property from Paper to Possible Reviewer (the person who reviews a paper). Different domain, range, and meaning; they are not the same relation.

Published Paper in edas is a paper that has been published (a status/state of a paper, sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), whereas Workshop Paper in ekaw is a paper type distinguished by the venue/kind of paper (sibling to Conference Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Regular Paper). They classify papers along different dimensions (publication status vs. paper category), so their instances do not coincide.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship of a paper), while B's 'send' links a Person to an Item (a person sending something). The domains and ranges are reversed and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

Author in cmt is a specific role (a Conference Member/User who writes papers), while Person in iasted is the general top-level class for all people (parents of Delegate and Sponsor). Every Author is a Person, but not every Person is an Author, so Author is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Person.

A's hasPhone is a datatype property linking a Person to a string phone number, while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in both kind (datatype vs object) and range (string vs Item), so they do not denote the same relation.

A is a research topic in computer networks (a subject area under Topic), while B is an organizational body (a committee that organizes the conference). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

Both properties link a paper/contribution to a topic, but confOf's 'deals With' has domain Contribution only, while edas's 'has Topic' has domain Conference and Paper. The intended relation (paper-to-topic) overlaps, but the domains differ (Conference is not a Contribution), so they are not strictly equivalent; they are related.

A's 'has a review expertise' links a submitted contribution to a review expertise (a topic/skill area), while B's 'give' links a person to an activity or item (e.g. giving a talk or presentation). Different domains (contribution vs person) and different ranges (review expertise vs activity/item), so they denote different relations.

A 'Conference Session' is a sub-event (a session within a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session), whereas B 'Conference' is the whole conference event with properties like start/end date, city, and held-by relationship. A session is a part of a conference, not the conference itself, so the two classes are not equivalent.

cmt:assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review a paper), while iasted:send relates a Person to an Item (a person sending an item). The domains (Paper vs Person) and ranges (Reviewer vs Item) differ, and the intended meanings (review assignment vs sending) do not coincide, so the properties are not equivalent.

Author is a person role in the conference domain (a Person who writes papers, with properties has Related Paper and is Written By), while Fee is a monetary charge (a subclass of Money with children Registration fee, Hotel fee, etc.). They share no meaning, no properties, and no common instances; the pair is unrelated.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a person/contact to a string email address, while B's locationOf is an object property linking a location to an event. They share neither domain/range kinds nor meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation between a document and its abstract), whereas ekaw's 'volume Contains Paper' relates a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. The domains and ranges differ (Abstract vs. Volume; Paper/Poster/Presentation vs. Paper), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's Workshop is a kind of working event (a session/event type, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas B's Plenary lecture speaker is a person role (a speaker/author subtype, sibling of Lecturer and Tutorial speaker). One denotes an event, the other a person, so they cannot be equivalent.

A's max Choice is a datatype property giving a numeric maximum number of choices for a social/working event (range positiveInteger), while B's lists Event is an object property linking a Programme Brochure or Web Site to the Events it lists (range Event). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have different domains/ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's Speaker is a subclass of Delegate (a conference participant who speaks, with children Author and Reviewer), while B's Organizator is a subclass of Person covering organisers (General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, committee members). They denote different roles: a speaker presents, an organiser runs the conference. B even lists Speaker as a sibling of Organizator, confirming they are distinct concepts.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while B's 'awarded by' links an Award to some unspecified entity (award attribution). Different domains (Paper vs Award), different ranges (Reviewer vs unspecified), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's hasPhone is a datatype property linking a Person to a string phone number, while B's is_used_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person (essentially the inverse of a 'uses' relation). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a subclass of Topic (a security research topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's Conference is a working event (an organised academic meeting, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas B's Conference building is a physical building/venue (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel/airport, parent of Delegate). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. place), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Review preference' is a class describing a reviewer's preference/degree for a topic or submission (domain/range of properties like 'has a degree', 'has a topic or a submission contribution', 'belongs to reviewers'), whereas B's 'Person' is a general agent class (parent of Delegate and Sponsor) involved in giving, being paid, being present, etc. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving the name of a Conference or Person, while B's `starts on` is a datatype property giving the start time/date of an Event. Different domains (Conference/Person vs Event) and different intended meanings (name vs start date), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), whereas B's 'Academia Organization' is a type of organization (sibling of Government/Industry Organization, NGO). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. organization) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'study At' relates a Scholar to a University (person -> institution), while B's 'is visited by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (place -> person). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the directions differ; they are not the same relation.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of Contribution (a submission to a conference, sibling of Paper and Poster), whereas B 'Flyer' is a kind of Document (a printed/published artefact, sibling of Programme Brochure and Web Site, with publisher Of). They denote different concepts: a short paper is an academic submission, a flyer is a promotional document. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's Workshop Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a scientific contribution submitted to a workshop), while B's Document is a broad administrative item covering forms, invitation letters, payment documents, reviews, submissions, etc. The two concepts do not coincide: a workshop paper is not a document in B's sense, and B's Document is far more general and administrative. No subsumption or overlap in the intended domain, so unrelated.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title; B's Nation is a datatype property of Person giving a person's nationality. Different domains (Paper vs Person) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a specific role (a co-author of a contribution, sibling of 'Contribution 1th author' under 'Regular author'), whereas B's 'Author' is the general person class (parent of Presenter, with properties has Related Paper / is Written By). The co-author role is a narrower concept than the general Author, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.
Trip (a social event / excursion) and Taxi (a transport vehicle) denote different kinds of things; they are not the same concept despite both being travel-related.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer). B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presented it (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A relates an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (committee-to-event link), while B relates a Person to an Organization (employment). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'review Criteria Entered By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who entered review criteria), while B's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to the people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). Different domain (Conference vs Paper), different range (Administrator vs reviewers), and different meaning (entering criteria vs performing a review), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while edas's 'initiates' links a chair/committee member to a Call (the act of starting a call for papers). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Review Rating is a class of ratings (accept/reject/weak-reject) attached to an active paper via has Rating; B's Place is a physical location (conference hall, hotel, main office) where a person can stay. Different domains and no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Review is a subclass of Document (a specific kind of document). In iasted, Document is a general class with Review as one of its children. Thus edas Review is strictly more specific than iasted Document, so Review is subsumed by Document, not equivalent.

A's Committee member is a general role for anyone on a committee (children Chair, Co chair; siblings Reviewer, Track workshop chair), whereas B's SC Member is a specific sub-role of PC Member (Steering Committee member) under PC Member. The SC Member is a narrower concept than the general Committee member, so A is subsumed by B's broader committee-membership notion; they are not equivalent.

A's reviewes relates a PC member to a contribution (the reviewer writes a review of a paper), while B's hasReview relates a paper to its review (the paper has a review). The domains and ranges differ (Member PC vs Paper; Contribution vs Review), and the direction of the relation is different, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an Administrator action whose range is a Conference (finalizing the assignment of papers to a conference), while B's 'prepare' is a Person action whose range is an Item (a person preparing an item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about a conference, with a URL), while B's 'Computer Networks Security Topic' is a research topic in the EDAS topic hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author; B's 'review Of Paper' links a Review to the Paper it reviews. Different domain (Contribution vs Review), different range (Author vs Paper), and different meaning (authorship vs reviewing), so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference Member is a Person (a role played by an individual, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Conference www is a Conference document (a web page/document with a URL). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and are not equivalent.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper (the title of a paper), while B's has title is a datatype property of Social event and Working event (the title of an event). Although both are string-valued title properties, their domains are disjoint kinds of things (Paper vs. Event), so they do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

A's hasReviewer relates a Paper to its Possible Reviewer (a person who reviews the paper), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/contributing something). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Paper vs Person; Possible Reviewer vs Activity/Item), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Call for participation' is a general conference document announcing the event and inviting participation, sibling to 'Call for paper' and 'Conference announcement'. B's 'Call For Reviews' is a specific call soliciting reviewers, sibling to 'Call For Papers' and 'Call For Manuscripts' under a generic 'Call' class. They are both calls/documents in the conference domain but denote different artefacts (participation announcement vs. reviewer recruitment), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's read Paper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (a reviewer reads a paper for review). B's related To Paper relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a presentation is related to the accepted paper it presents). Different domains (Reviewer vs Paper Presentation) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.
Trip is a social event (an activity), while Fee for extra trip is a monetary fee. They belong to different branches of the conference domain (Event vs Money) and denote different kinds of things.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), a subclass of Scientific Event, while B's Conference hall is a physical Place (a venue room), a subclass of Place. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a session within a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session), whereas B 'One conference day' is a temporal unit (a day of the conference, sibling of Delegate under Conference days). They belong to different branches (Event vs Time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the person assigned to review the paper). B's 'has been assigned a review reference' links a Submitted contribution/Topic to a Review preference (a preference/rating entity, not a person). The ranges denote different kinds of things (Reviewer vs Review preference), so the two properties do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class for people involved in the conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers) with properties linking to Conference. Registeered applicant in Conference is a specific subclass of Conference applicant (a person who has registered/paid), a different concept. The two classes do not denote the same set of instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

A's hasCostCurrency is a datatype property linking a Sponsorship to a currency string, while B's heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap.

Both denote a member of the organising committee: A's Committee member is a Person who was a member of a Committee and is parent of Chair/Co-chair; B's OC Member is a Conference Participant who is parent of OC Chair. Same intended instances (organising committee members), with chair subclasses in both.

A is a paper abstract (a document type in the conference domain), while B is a double hotel room (accommodation type). They share no meaning, no properties, and belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Place).

Both are object properties with domain Conference, but the ranges differ: cmt's 'details Entered By' points to an Administrator (a person who entered the conference details), while sigkdd's 'holded by' points to ACM SIGKDD (the organising body/society). They relate a conference to different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent; they are only loosely related as conference-level metadata properties.

A 'Conference Event' is an event (with attendees, programme, start/end dates, location) in edas, while B 'Organisation' is an organising body (academic institution, organising agency, publisher) in ekaw. They denote different concepts: an event vs. an organisation. Although ekaw links Organisation to Event via organises/organised By, that is a relation between distinct entities, not equivalence. No subsumption or overlap of instances exists.

A's Member is a subclass of Participant (a person who is a member of the conference, with siblings Regular and Student), i.e. a person role. B's Registration Student is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a fee category for students, not a person. Different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's Presenter is a role of a person (a Conference Participant who presents), with child Invited Speaker and siblings that are all person roles (chairs, participants). B's Registration is a conference activity/event, with child Delegate and siblings that are all activities (Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break). The two denote different kinds of things (person role vs. activity), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a steering committee' links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a committee-membership relation), while B's 'sign' links a Person to an Item (a signing/authoring relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (path Person > Conference Member > Author > Co author), i.e. a co-author is a specific kind of author, whereas B's 'Author' is the general author class (Person > Author). The intended instances of Co author are a subset of those of Author, so Co author is subsumed by Author, not equivalent.

A 'Paid applicant' is a person (a subclass of Conference applicant/Registeered applicant, with children Early/Late paid applicant), whereas B 'Fee' is a monetary charge (with children Registration fee, Sponzor fee). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. payment) and are not equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to a Conference Member (a person role in the conference organisation), while B's has_a_steering_committee relates a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a committee body). The ranges differ (person vs committee) and the domains differ (Conference vs Conference volume), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's reviewCriteriaEnteredBy links a Conference to the Administrator who entered review criteria, while B's write links a Person to an Item they authored. Different domains (Conference vs Person), different ranges (Administrator vs Item), and different intended relations (administrative metadata vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A is an administrative event (camera-ready event) in confOf, while B is a deadline for hotel reservation in iasted. Although both ontologies have a 'camera ready' concept, A is an event and B is a deadline; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.
Both are classes named Abstract under Document, with Paper and Review as siblings in both ontologies; they denote the same concept of an abstract document.

A's 'Chair PC' is a Person who chairs the program committee (a PC chair role), while B's 'General Chair' is an Organizator role that is the overall conference chair, distinct from the Program Chair role which is a sibling of General Chair in sigkdd. The two denote different conference roles, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'read By Meta Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (a specific reviewer role), while B's 'reviewes' relates a Member PC (a program committee member) to a Contribution. The domain and range classes differ (Paper vs Member PC, Meta Reviewer vs Contribution), and the direction/roles are distinct: one is a meta-reviewer reading a paper, the other a PC member reviewing a contribution. They are not the same relation.

confOf's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while ekaw's Regular Paper is a specific subtype of ekaw Paper (siblings Camera Ready Paper, Submitted Paper, etc.). The confOf Paper is broader and corresponds to ekaw's Paper, not to the narrower Regular Paper, so confOf Paper is subsumed by ekaw Regular Paper only in the sense of being more general; the correct relation is that confOf Paper is more general, i.e. ekaw Regular Paper is subsumed by it.

A's Conference is the central event/organisation entity of the cmt ontology (has members, accepts submissions, has dates, administrators). B's Conference building is a physical building (a Place/Building subclass) that hosts delegates, sibling to Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc. The shared word 'Conference' is a modifier of a venue, not the event itself; instances do not coincide.

Both properties link an author/person to the written contribution/document. confOf's writes has domain Author and range Contribution; ekaw's authorOf has domain Person and range Document. In the conference domain, Author and Person denote the same role, and Contribution and Document denote the same written artefact, so the two properties relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are equivalent.

A's has Phone relates a Person to a phone number string, while B's has Street relates Contact Information to a street address string. They denote different attributes (phone vs. street address) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a review of a paper/contribution: A's Review is a Conference document with properties 'has a review' (Reviewed contribution -> Review) and 'reviews' (Review -> Reviewed contribution); B's Review is a Document with 'has Review' (Paper -> Review) and 'review Of Paper' (Review -> Paper). Same intended instances (reviews of submissions), same domain role, so equivalent despite differing parents.

A's 'ends on' is a datatype property mapping an Event to a string (a date/time when the event ends), while B's 'go through' is an object property mapping an Item to an Activity (an item being used in/associated with an activity). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Event vs Item), and range (string vs Activity), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's hasTitle is a datatype property of Contribution giving the title of a paper; B's hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property of Call giving instructions for submitting. Different domains (Contribution vs Call) and different intended meaning (title text vs submission instructions), so they are not equivalent.

cmt's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (a specific submission act), while iasted's obtain relates a Person to an Item in a generic acquisition sense. The domains/ranges differ (Author/Paper vs Person/Item) and the intended relations are not the same, so they are not equivalent.

Both are object properties from Person to a document/item, expressing that a person contributes to / writes a conference document. 'contributes' (Person -> Conference document) and 'write' (Person -> Item) relate the same kinds of things in the same direction, so they are equivalent in the conference domain.

Meta Reviewer (cmt) is a specialized Reviewer who aggregates reviews for a paper, while Author (confOf) is a Person who writes Contributions. They are distinct roles with different parents (Reviewer vs Person) and different properties (read By Meta Reviewer vs writes/written By), so they are not equivalent.

Conference Chair in cmt is a specific role (a person chairing the conference, sibling of Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair, Author, Reviewer) under Chairman/Conference Member. Delegate in iasted is a broad category of conference participant (parent of Speaker, Listener, Session chair, IASTED member, etc.) under Conference building. A conference chair is a specific organiser role, not a generic delegate/attendee; the two concepts do not coincide.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a document submitted to a conference (child of Conference document, with children Poster/Presentation/Written contribution and properties has contributions/is submitted at). B's 'Building' is a physical place (child of Place, with children Conference hotel/Conference airport and properties is occupied by/is situated in). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Organization in confOf is an institution (parent of Company and University) that employs Persons and has an address; Conference in sigkdd is an event with start/end dates, a name, and a city, held by ACM SIGKDD. Different intended instances and different properties, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Person is a broad class covering all people in the conference domain (administrators, participants, authors, chairs, etc.), while sigkdd's Author is a narrower class (a subclass of Speaker) denoting only people who submit papers. Person is strictly more general than Author, so Person subsumes Author rather than being equivalent.

A's `date` is a generic datatype property on Conference (the conference's date), while B's `is an ending date` is a specific deadline property on Important dates (the end date of an important-dates interval). Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Social Event in ekaw is a general class for social events at a conference (with children Conference Banquet and Conference Trip), while Dinner banquet in iasted is a specific social program activity (a dinner banquet). The ekaw class is broader and would include the iasted Dinner banquet as one of its instances, so Social Event subsumes Dinner banquet, not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship of a paper), while B's 'is occupied by' links a Building/City/State to a Person (occupancy of a place). Different domains and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Program Committee Member' is a Person (an individual member of the committee), while B's 'Program Committee' is a Committee (the collective body). They denote different concepts: a person vs. an organizational group. Although related in the domain, they are not equivalent; the correct counterpart of B's Program Committee in cmt would be the class 'Program Committee' (the committee), not its member.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a session within a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session), whereas B 'Organizator' is a person role (a Person who organizes, parent of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Person) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the conference administrator role: cmt's Administrator is a User (Person) with administrative powers over papers, reviewers, PC members and conference details, and confOf's Administrator is a Person (comment 'confTool') sitting alongside Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, etc. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

Both denote the money a participant pays for a conference: A's 'Conference fees' is the class of fees charged for the conference, and B's 'Fee' (under Money, with children Registration fee, Hotel fee, Fee for extra trip) is the general fee class in the conference domain. The intended instances coincide (registration/hotel/extra-trip fees are conference fees), so they are equivalent.

Both properties link a Reviewer to review-related information, but A's range is review expertise/preference (topics the reviewer can or wants to review), while B's range is the reviewer's personal review history (past reviews performed). They are different aspects of a reviewer's profile, so they overlap in domain but are not equivalent.

A's Poster is a conference contribution presented as a poster (sibling of Presentation, Invited talk, Regular contribution), while B's Short paper is a written contribution type (sibling of Paper and Poster in confOf). In confOf, Poster and Short paper are distinct siblings, so A's Poster does not correspond to B's Short paper; they denote different contribution types.

A's 'technically Organises' is a subproperty of 'organises' with domain Organisation, describing an organisation that organises an event/conference. B's 'presentation' has domain Speaker and range Document, describing a speaker presenting a document. Different domains, ranges and intended relations; they are not equivalent.

A's 'adjusted By' links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it (domain Bid, range Reviewer), while B's 'invited by' links a Reviewer to the Reviewer who invited them (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's `send` relates a Person to an Item (Person -> Item), while B's `payed by` relates a Registration fee to a Person (Registration fee -> Person). They have different domains, different ranges, and opposite directions; they are not the same relation.

Both denote a paper/contribution that has been submitted but not yet reviewed/accepted. A's 'Submitted contribution' sits under 'Written contribution' with sibling 'Regular contribution' and child 'Reviewed contribution' (a submitted item that then gets reviewed), and is linked to review expertise/preferences. B's 'Submitted Paper' sits under 'Paper' with child 'Assigned Paper' (submitted paper assigned to a reviewer) and siblings for camera-ready/conference/workshop etc. The intended instances coincide: a submitted manuscript in the conference workflow. The differing parents (Written contribution vs Paper) reflect the different upper taxonomies, not different concepts.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a paper submitted to a conference (a Document/Paper in the conference domain), while B 'Card' is an Item with child 'Credit card' (a payment/identity card). Different domains and no shared meaning; unrelated.

A 'Written contribution' is a conference paper/document submitted to a conference, while B 'Bank transfer' is a payment document (a financial instrument). They belong to entirely different domains and share no instances; the only superficial link is the word 'document' in their paths, which is not enough for equivalence.

A's hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (the schedule of sessions/papers), while B's hold links an ACM SIGKDD (the organising body/society) to a Conference it runs. Different domains, ranges and meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who started the bidding process), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's hasReview relates a Paper to its Review (domain Paper, range Review), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not the same relation.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). B's 'Author cd proceedings included' is a subclass of Author describing an author whose CD proceedings are included — a person role, not an event. Different kinds and domains, so they are unrelated.

Computer Networks Security Topic is a research topic class under Computer Networks Topic in edas, while Organizing Committee is a committee class under Committee in sigkdd. They denote entirely different concepts (a subject area vs. an organizational body), so they are unrelated.

A's Time is a temporal class (parent of Conference days, Deadline, Trip day; domain/range of temporal relations like is held before/after, is present, is sent before/after). B's ACM SIGKDD is an organisation/society class (holds conferences, designs deadlines, searches sponsors). They denote different concepts and are unrelated.
A is an activity/process (accepting a manuscript) in the pre-conference phase, while B is a person role (Author) who submits papers. Different kinds of entities with no overlap.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is an event type (Workshop, a kind of Working event). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'was a program committee of' relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (a committee-to-event relation). B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person-to-thing relation). Different domains and ranges, different directions of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

Organization in edas denotes an institution (with subclasses Academia/Government/Industry/NGO) that provides sponsorships, whereas Person in iasted denotes an individual human (with subclasses Delegate and Sponsor) who gives items, is paid, is present at times, etc. The two classes have disjoint intended instances and no subsumption relation.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for students). They belong to different branches (Person vs Fee) and denote different concepts: a person vs a fee type. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's Conference Chair sits under Chairman/Conference Member and is a general conference-level chair role, while B's PC Chair is a specific Program Committee chair under Conference Participant/PC Member. They are distinct roles (conference chair vs. program committee chair), though both are chairing roles in the conference domain, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a paper in the submission stage of the conference process (a subclass of Paper, with sibling Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, etc., and child Assigned Paper). B 'Form' is a document artefact such as a registration or author-information form, a subclass of Document with children like Registration form and Hotel registration form. Although both are documents, their intended instances do not coincide: a submitted paper is not a form, and a form is not a paper. They are unrelated.

A's Web Site is a Document that lists events and is published by an organisation (a conference web page), while B's Hotel registration form is a Form document used for hotel registration. Different intended instances and roles; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (a dependency/requirement relation), while B's 'design' relates the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline (a conference-organisation relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like abstract, has Title, written By, and is reviewed by PC members. Sponzor in sigkdd is a conference sponsor (parent of Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor) with a sponsor name and a search relation to ACM SIGKDD. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event whose instances are the outcome/notification of reviewing, accessible to authors; B 'Workshop' is an academic event (a type of conference session/meeting). They denote different concepts with different parents (Administrative event vs Academic Event) and different siblings, so they are unrelated.

Committee member in Conference is a Person who is part of a committee (children Chair, Co chair; properties has members / was a member of). Organizator in sigkdd is a broader Person role whose children include General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster. Every committee member is an organizer in the sigkdd sense, but organizers also include roles (e.g. Webmaster) that are not committee members, so Committee member is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Organizator.

A's hasName is a datatype property giving a Conference's full name (domain Conference, range string), while B's listsEvent is an object property linking a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event. They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's property relates an Administrator to a Conference (enabling a virtual meeting), while B's property relates a Conference to a Person (having a member). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's property relates a Conference part to a Topic (domain Conference part, range Topic), while B's isTopicOf relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper (domain Topic, range Conference/Paper). They are inverse-like in direction and have different domains/ranges, so they are not equivalent relations.

confOf's Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster and Short paper under Contribution), whereas ekaw's Assigned Paper is a specific stage in the submission workflow (a Submitted Paper that has been assigned to a reviewer, with child Evaluated Paper). The intended instances do not coincide: a Paper need not be assigned, and an Assigned Paper is a workflow state rather than a document type.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome of a submission), while B's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment affiliation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'follows' orders Administrative events (domain and range both Administrative event), while B's 'is Menu Of' links a Meal Menu to a Meal Event. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Item is a general physical/abstract object class (children: Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle; properties about being given, paid for, made from, needed for), whereas B's Person is a human agent class (children: Listener, Organizator, Speaker; properties E mail, Name, Nation, can stay in, pay). The two denote entirely different concepts and do not overlap.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a Person who attends a conference without an active role (sibling of Active conference participant), while B 'Conference Banquet' is a Social Event (sibling of Conference Trip). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an Administrator action whose range is a Conference (it assigns papers to reviewers for a conference), while B's 'is Written By' relates a Paper to its Author. Different domain, range, direction and meaning; they are unrelated.

A's 'name' is a datatype property with domain Conference and Person, ranging over string, i.e. a general naming attribute for conferences and people. B's 'start Date' is a datatype property with domain Conference only, ranging over dateTime, and its comment explicitly says it is the conference start date and time. They denote different attributes (a name vs. a temporal start point) with different ranges and different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasRelatedDocument links an event/session/person to a Document (a general related-document association), while B's presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (the presenter of a document). They differ in domain, range, and direction of the relation, so they are not equivalent.
Conference Trip is a social event (an activity) in ekaw, while Main office is a physical place in sigkdd; they denote different kinds of entities and share no meaning.

A's email is a datatype property of Person holding an email address; B's hasCity is a datatype property of Contact Information holding a city name. Different domains, different ranges semantically (email address vs city), and different intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's co-writePaper relates a Co author (co-author entity) to a Paper, i.e. co-authorship between a co-author and a paper. B's submit relates an Author to a Paper, i.e. the act of submitting a paper. Different domains (Co author vs Author) and different intended relations (co-authorship vs submission), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor, i.e. a role played by a person who is an author of a regular (non-invited) contribution. B's 'Author' is a subclass of Speaker (a Person) who submits papers, obtains awards, etc. The B class is the general person/author concept, while A's class is a specific contribution-role (regular vs. invited). A's instances are contributions authored by a regular author, not the author persons themselves, so A is narrower and subsumed by the broader Author concept; they are not equivalent.

A 'Written contribution' is a kind of conference contribution (a paper/document submitted to a conference), while B 'Registration fee' is a monetary fee paid by attendees. They belong to entirely different branches (document/contribution vs money/fee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is an event/meeting entity (has a name, has a Conference volume, related to Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic), whereas B's Organization is an agent/organisational entity (parent of Company and University, with employed By, has City/Country/Postal Code/Street). The two denote different concepts in the conference domain (event vs. organisation), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property of Person with range string, denoting an email address. B's 'has Postal Code' is a datatype property of Contact Information with range string, denoting a postal code. Different attributes (email vs postal code) on different domains (Person vs Contact Information); they are not the same relation.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (a conference/tutorial/workshop activity), while B 'Multimedia Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

cmt's hasCo-author relates a Paper to its Co-author(s), while confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author. Paper and Contribution are equivalent classes, and Co-author is a kind of Author, so the two properties overlap in meaning but are not identical: hasCo-author points specifically to co-authors (a subset of authors), whereas writtenBy points to any author. They are related rather than equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the outcome of reviewing a paper), while B's obtain relates a Person to an Item (a person acquiring something). Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to the Event held there (domain Location, range Event), while B's 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time (domain Activity, range Time). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and express different relations (spatial hosting vs. temporal ordering), so they are not equivalent.

Ontology A's 'Active conference participant' is a class representing a person who actively participates in a conference, while Ontology B's 'has Member' is an object property linking a conference to a person. A class and a property are different kinds of entities, so they cannot be equivalent or in a subsumption relation; they are unrelated.

Both denote a person who authors papers: ekaw's Paper Author is a Person who writes papers, and iasted's Author is a Delegate/Speaker who authors papers. The differing parents (Person vs Speaker) reflect different modelling choices, but the intended instances coincide in the conference domain.

A is a subclass of Abstract (a document type for invited talks), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary fee category for authors who book registration). Their paths, parents, and siblings are entirely different, so they denote unrelated concepts.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role for anyone involved in a conference (including chairs, authors, reviewers, etc.), while Speaker in iasted is a specific role for someone who presents, under Delegate. Their scopes and hierarchies differ; no equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's 'attendee At' relates a Person to a Conference Event (person attends event), while B's 'is prepared by' relates an Item to a Person (item prepared by person). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they denote different relations.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a Chairman/Conference Member role (a general chair-like role in cmt), while B's 'Chair PC' is the program-committee chair, a distinct role. The labels and contexts differ: A sits under Chairman alongside Conference Chair and PC Chair, whereas B is a Person sibling of Member PC and Author. They denote different conference roles, so they are not equivalent.

Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a subclass of Person (a person who may review papers, with children PC Member), while iasted's Person is the general superclass of all people (children Delegate, Sponsor). Possible Reviewer is strictly more specific than Person, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

confOf's Paper is a generic contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper) covering any paper, while ekaw's Accepted Paper is a specific stage in the review workflow (a paper that has been accepted, sibling Rejected Paper). The concepts overlap but neither subsumes the other: a Paper need not be accepted, and an Accepted Paper is a particular kind of paper. Hence related, not equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like has Title, abstract, written By, and is reviewed by PC members. Topic in edas is a subject area (parent of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.) that conferences and papers are about. They denote different concepts: a contribution is a document/artefact, a topic is a subject category. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman who organizes the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B 'Speaker lecture' is a session-related activity/role within a lecture session. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'Proceedings Publisher' is an Organisation (an agent that publishes proceedings), while B's 'Book proceeding' is a Publication (a document/item). They denote different kinds of entities (agent vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties linking a conference/activity to a date/time value. cmt's Conference:date and iasted's Activity:is dated on express the same relation (the date on which the event occurs), with Conference and Activity being the corresponding event classes in the two ontologies.

A 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while B 'Topic' is a subject area of conference parts and submissions. They denote different concepts (person vs. subject), so they are unrelated.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (where it takes place), while B's 'is held after' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domain, different range, and different meaning (spatial location vs. temporal precedence), so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad class whose children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, and Conference Chair, and whose properties link it to a Conference. In edas, TPC Member is a narrower role (Technical Program Committee member) that participates in reviewing and initiating calls, with siblings Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair, etc. TPC Member is a specific kind of Conference Member, so the edas class is subsumed by the cmt class, not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) used to announce a conference, whereas B 'Cd proceening' is a publication type (a CD proceedings item, sibling of Book proceeding) under Publication. They denote different concepts: an announcement document vs. a proceedings publication medium, so they are unrelated.

A's publisherOf relates an Organisation to documents it publishes (Flyer, Programme Brochure, Web Site, etc.), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper they submit. Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to people who initiate it (chairs/TPC members), while B's 'is visited by' links a location (Building/City/State) to a Person who visits it. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a numeric count (int) of reviews per paper, while B's 'manuscript Due On' is a dateTime deadline for manuscript submission. They share only the Conference domain; their ranges and intended meanings differ, so they are not the same relation.

In the Conference ontology, Extended abstract is a subclass of Regular contribution (a full-length contribution type), with sibling Paper and child Abstract. In ekaw, Poster Paper is a subclass of Paper, a distinct presentation/publication format alongside Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc. An extended abstract is a short version of a regular contribution, not a poster paper; the two denote different contribution types and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an administrative action relating an Administrator to a Conference (bidding phase initiation), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship of a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that informs participants, whereas B's 'Form' is a document with children like Registration form, Hotel registration form, Author information form — a fillable form artefact. Different intended instances; no subsumption or overlap.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference domain (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Building (iasted) is a physical Place (venue building such as conference hotel, airport, university) occupied by persons. Their paths, parents, siblings and properties (write Paper/submit Paper vs. is situated in/occupy) do not overlap; they denote different concepts.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (membership), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent.

A's Submitted Paper is a specific stage of a paper (a Paper that has been submitted, with child Assigned Paper and siblings like Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper), whereas B's Publication is a broad top-level category of published items (children Book proceeding, Cd proceeding; siblings Document, Card, Transport vehicle). Submitted Paper is a submission-stage document, not a published item, and Publication is far more general and covers proceedings/books. Their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference volume' is a publication/proceedings entity (it has contributions, tracks, committees, important dates, and belongs to a conference), whereas B 'Conference Session' is a scheduled event within a scientific event (a Session subtype with children like Industrial Session and siblings like Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session). The two denote different kinds of things (publication volume vs. event session) and do not coincide in the conference domain.

A 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the reviewing procedure/phase for submitted contributions), while B 'Review Form' is a document/artefact used to record a review. One is an event, the other a form; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's hasFax relates a Person to a fax number string; B's hasEmail relates a Person/Contact Information to an email address string. Different contact channels, so the properties are not equivalent (nor does one subsume the other).

A's User is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Break Event is a non-academic conference event (parent Non Academic Event, children Coffee Break/Meal Break). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Conference hotel' is a subclass of Building (a physical lodging place used by a conference), while B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with properties for city, start/end dates, name, and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. A hotel is a venue/building, not the conference event, so the two classes denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's Paper is a conference submission document with authors, reviews, decisions and subject areas. B's Mailing list is a document used to distribute information to participants, sibling to Invitation letter, Payment document and Record of attendance. They share only the generic Document parent and denote different artefacts, so they are unrelated.

A's Chairman is a Person who chairs (a role, parent Person, children Conference Chair/PC Chair, involved in Conflict Of Interest), while B's Author is a Speaker who writes papers (parent Speaker, children about proceedings/lectures). Different roles in the conference domain; not equivalent.

Both denote the outcome/activity of a submitted manuscript being rejected: A is the class of rejected contributions (sibling of Accepted contribution under Reviewed contribution), B is the activity of refusing a manuscript (sibling of Accepting manuscript under Activity before conference). The intended instances coincide in the conference domain, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Preference (cmt) is a class of preference values/statements used in the review bidding process, not a person. B's Possible Reviewer (ekaw) is a subclass of Person (a person who may review a paper, parent of PC Member). The two denote different kinds of things (a preference vs. a person role), so they are not equivalent.

Delegate in iasted is a broad participant role (attendee) with children like Speaker, Listener, Session chair, and is a subclass of Conference building/Person/Registration; Organizator in sigkdd is a narrower role for people who organize the conference (General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, committee members). The intended instances do not coincide: a delegate need not be an organizer, and an organizer is a specific kind of participant, not a generic delegate. Different paths and sibling sets confirm distinct concepts.

A is a subject/topic area within the EDAS topic taxonomy (a research area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a kind of scientific event (a presentation type under Individual Presentation, sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic vs. event) and cannot denote the same concept.
