edas:Document is a general document class whose children include Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, etc. ekaw:Review is a specific subclass of ekaw:Document (path Document > Review). Thus edas:Document is strictly more general than ekaw:Review; they are not equivalent.

A's 'referenced In' relates a paper/contribution to the document or event in which it is referenced (a citation-like relation), while B's 'awarded by' relates an Award to the agent/organisation that granted it. They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and share no meaning in the conference domain.

Attendee (Person > Attendee) and Delegate (a Person subtype in the conference building context) both denote a person participating in a conference; Delegate's children (Listener, Speaker, Session chair, etc.) are all kinds of attendees, and the sibling/parent context (Person, Registration) agrees with the conference-participant meaning, so the two classes are synonyms in the conference domain.

The edas property 'is Initiated By' has domain Call and range Conference Chair/Session Chair/TPC Member, i.e. it links a call to the people who initiated it. The iasted property 'is sent by' has domain Item and range Person, i.e. it links a submitted item (paper) to the person who sent it. Different domains (Call vs Item) and different intended relations (initiating a call vs sending an item), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person role, sibling of 'Author Not Reviewer', linked to Paper via co-write/has-Co-author), while B's 'Poster' is a subclass of Conference contribution (a document/contribution type, sibling of Invited talk, Presentation, Written contribution). One denotes a person, the other a kind of contribution; they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee (payment). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A Track is a thematic stream of the conference that groups papers/sessions (a conference part, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, linked from Conference volume via has tracks). A Plenary lecture is a specific kind of Lecture (a conference activity, sibling of Session and Tutorial) — a single talk given to all attendees. The two denote different concepts: one is an organisational grouping, the other a type of event/talk, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (organisational/event structure), while B's submit links an Author to a Paper (submission act). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A's Paper is a conference document (subclass of Document, with reviews, topics, presentations), while B's Transport vehicle is a means of transport (parent of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs the conference (a chairman role, sibling of Program Committee Chair and Associated Chair, under Chairman/Conference Member). B 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies/registers for the conference (parent of Registeered applicant, sibling of Conference participant and Conference contributor). The roles are distinct: chairing vs. applying/attending, so the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman who chairs the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair). B 'Sponsor city' is a kind of City (a location, sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Trip city). A person role and a city location cannot denote the same concept; they are unrelated.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (where an event takes place), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (an author writing a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote a conference event: A's Conference has a name and a conference volume/proceedings, B's Conference has name, city, start/end dates and is held by an ACM SIGKDD. Same intended instances in the conference domain.

In edas, Attendee is a generic person who attends the conference, sibling to Author, Reviewer, etc. In ekaw, OC Member is a member of the organising committee, a specific role under Conference Participant with children like OC Chair. An attendee is not necessarily an organising committee member and vice versa, so the classes denote different concepts.

Reception is a social event (a gathering held during the conference, sibling of Banquet and Trip), while Travel Grant is a form of sponsorship (financial support). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's has Cost Amount is a datatype property mapping a Sponsorship to an int (a monetary amount), while B's is paid in is an object property mapping Money to a Building (a location/venue). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Sponsorship vs Money), and range (int vs Building), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's Person is a general human participant class (children Delegate, Sponsor; involved in giving, paying, being present), while B's Sponzor is specifically a sponsor organization/entity with subtypes like Gold Supporter and Exhibitor and properties linking it to ACM SIGKDD. Although A has a Sponsor child, the classes themselves denote different concepts (person vs. sponsoring entity), so they are not equivalent.

A is a research topic (a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic) in the EDAS topic taxonomy, while B is a Program Committee, an organisational body of people. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject area vs. committee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Introduction is a conference activity (an event/session type, sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Welcome address), while B's Organizator is a person role (parent of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

An IASTED member is a specific kind of Delegate (a person attending an IASTED conference), while Attendee is the general class of persons attending a conference. The IASTED member is thus narrower than Attendee, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's Review Rating is a class of rating values (Accept/Reject/Week Reject) attached to an Active Paper via has Rating. B's Document is a general document class whose children are Abstract, Paper and Review, and which is presented by a Speaker and has a submission deadline. A rating value is not a document, and the two classes share neither instances nor context, so they are unrelated.

A's 'ends on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string (its end date/time), while B's 'part Of Event' is an object property linking an Event to another Event (mereological containment). They differ in kind, range, and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person/registrant who paid early), while B is a subclass of Paper (a document in pending review status). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person vs. document) and share no intended instances.

A 'Security Topic' is a subject area (a kind of Topic) in the edas ontology, while B 'Tutorial' is a type of lecture/activity (a kind of Lecture under Conference activity) in the iasted ontology. They denote different concepts: a topic of interest versus a teaching event, so they are unrelated.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location). B's 'searched by' relates a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD, i.e. a sponsor being searched by a specific organisation. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Paper is a contribution/document (sibling of Poster and Short paper under Contribution), while B's Paper Presentation is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented, with properties linking it to Accepted Paper). The two denote different kinds of things — a written contribution versus a conference event — so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference topic area (Computer Networks Topic) under Topic, while B is a document type (Invited Talk Abstract) under Abstract. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject area vs. document type) and share no instances.

A's 'review Criteria Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered review criteria; B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the presentation material). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the act/phase of submitting contributions), while B 'Final manuscript' is a document type (the final version of a submitted paper). One is an event, the other a document; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated despite both relating to submission.

Organization in edas denotes an institution (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provides sponsorship, while Committee in sigkdd denotes a group of people organizing the conference (organizing, program, awards committees). Different intended instances and roles; no subsumption or overlap.

A's `name` is a datatype property applying to Conference and Person (a general naming property for people/conferences), while B's `Name of sponsor` applies only to Sponzor (sponsor name). Different domains and intended concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Accepted contribution' is a specific stage of a conference contribution (a reviewed, accepted written contribution, with 'Camera ready contribution' as a child and 'Rejected contribution' as a sibling). B's 'Paper' is the general document submitted by an author (submit: Author -> Paper), covering all stages including rejected ones. Thus Accepted contribution is a narrower concept than Paper, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A is a generic accommodation place (hotel-like venue) under Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place. B is a university building that hosts presenters, under Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference building, etc. Although both are places, they denote different kinds of location: lodging vs. a presenter's university building. No shared label, no shared properties, and the intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (a conference/tutorial/workshop activity), while B 'Mobile Computing Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'Conference fees' is a fee/payment concept (a monetary amount associated with attending), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself, a subclass of Working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to an email address string, while B's Name links a Person to a name string. Although both are Person->string datatype properties, they denote different attributes (email address vs. name), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a part-whole relation, sibling of 'has parts'), while B's 'has Programme' links a Conference Event to its Programme (the schedule of sessions). The ranges (Workshop vs Programme) and domains (Conference volume vs Conference Event) denote different concepts, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'written By' goes from Contribution to Author (a paper is written by an author), while B's 'submit' goes from Author to Paper (an author submits a paper). They are inverse in direction and denote different relations (authorship vs. submission), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Review Rating' is a class of rating values (children: Accept Rating, Reject Rating, etc.) used as the range of 'has Rating' (Active Paper -> Review Rating). B's 'Review' is a document type (sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter) under Document. A rating value and a review document are different concepts, so the classes are unrelated.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a conference participant role), while B's Lecturer is a subclass of Author under Delegate/Speaker, i.e. a speaker/author role. Although B has a child 'Student lecturer', the classes themselves denote different concepts: a student attendee vs. a lecturer/author. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a kind of conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational document. B's 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a deadline (sibling of Deadline Paper Submission and Author notification), i.e. a point in time. Different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Sponsorship (edas) is a funding arrangement provided by an Organization, with cost amount/currency and a Travel Grant child. Registration fee (sigkdd) is a Fee subtype paid by a Person, with member/non-member/student variants and a sibling Sponzor fee. They denote different concepts: sponsorship funding vs. registration payment, so they are not equivalent.

A is the class of persons who write papers (Person > Author, with properties has Related Paper and is Written By). B is a subclass of Registration fee (Money > Fee > Registration fee > Memeber registration fee), i.e. a monetary fee category. They denote entirely different concepts and cannot be equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs the conference (a Chairman/Conference Member role), while B 'Tutorial speaker' is a speaker who gives a tutorial, placed under Author/Speaker in iasted. The roles are different: chairing the conference vs. presenting a tutorial. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A Meta Review is a review of reviews (a distinct document type under Review in cmt), while B Negative Review is a review whose recommendation/score is negative, sibling to Neutral and Positive Review. They denote different concepts: one is a meta-level review artefact, the other a polarity-based review classification. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper representing the complete paper document, while B's 'Abstract' is a top-level class under Document representing the abstract text, a sibling of Paper. They denote different concepts (full paper vs. abstract), so they are not equivalent.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference organisation hierarchy (Person > Conference Member > Author) who writes/submits papers, while Topic (edas) is a subject area of papers/conferences with subtopics like Antennas Topic and Cryptography Topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances or properties.

A's 'name' is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's 'has Email' is specifically an email address property for Person. They denote different attributes (a name vs. an email address), so they are not equivalent.

Assigned Paper is a specific stage of a paper (a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer), while sigkdd's Paper is the general paper class. Every Assigned Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is assigned, so Assigned Paper is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Paper.

Both properties link a document-like entity to a person, but the domains differ: A's 'is given by' relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (a speaker giving a talk), while B's 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person (an author signing a paper). They overlap in the general sense of attributing a document to a person, but they are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Author is a person role in the conference domain (a Person who writes papers, with properties linking to Paper), while Tax is a monetary charge under Money with children Departure tax and Value added tax. They share no meaning, instances, or context; the pair is unrelated.

A 'Poster Session' is a type of scientific event/session in the conference programme, while B 'Sponzor fee' is a type of fee (a monetary charge). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (event vs. fee) and share no intended instances.

confOf's Paper is a generic contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while ekaw's Camera Ready Paper is a specific stage of a paper (sibling of Submitted Paper, Conference Paper, etc.) under a broader Paper class. A camera-ready paper is a paper, but not every paper is camera-ready, so confOf Paper is more general and is subsumed by ekaw's Paper, not equivalent to Camera Ready Paper.

A 'Committee member' is a Person role in the conference organisation (parent Person, children Chair/Co chair, related to Committee via has members/was a member of). B 'Registration SIGKDD Member' is a fee category (parent Registration fee, siblings Registration Non Member/Student), i.e. a type of registration fee, not a person role. Different intended instances and different paths, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a whole-part relation, subproperty of has parts), while B's 'expert On' links a PC member to a Topic they are expert in. Different domains (Conference volume vs Member PC), different ranges (Tutorial vs Topic), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Paper Abstract is a document part (an abstract of a paper), while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award given to a paper. They belong to different branches (Document vs Award) and denote different concepts.

A's hasFax is a datatype property linking a Person to their fax number, while B's Nation links a Person to their nationality/country. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote different attributes (fax number vs. nation), so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime and both concern conference paper deadlines, but they are not equivalent: A's 'paper Due On' is a property of Conference directly giving the paper submission deadline, while B's 'Date' is a property of Deadline (a separate class representing a deadline entity) giving the date of that deadline. They relate different kinds of subjects (Conference vs Deadline) and thus are only related, not equivalent.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (where the event takes place). B's 'holded by' relates a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD (the organising body), i.e. the inverse direction of 'holds'. Different domain/range and opposite direction, so they are not equivalent.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), i.e. the rejection of a paper. B's Reception is a social event (sibling of Excursion under Social Event) held at the conference. The labels are only superficially similar; the concepts belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (member -> committee). B's has_members relates a Committee to a Committee member (committee -> member), the inverse direction. Since the direction differs, they are not equivalent; A's property is the inverse of B's, so A is subsumed_by B (B is the more general committee-membership relation).
Associated Chair in cmt is a conference organizational role (chair), while Author in iasted is a delegate/speaker role. They are different kinds of roles and not equivalent.

Acceptance in cmt is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection, child of Decision), i.e. the state of a paper being accepted. Deadline for notification of acceptance in iasted is a time point (child of Deadline, sibling of submission and camera-ready deadlines). One is a decision result, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts.

In cmt, Review is a subclass of Document representing an individual review document written by a reviewer for a paper. In edas, Personal Review History is a subclass of Personal History representing an aggregate/history of reviews associated with a reviewer, not an individual review. The entities have different intended instances and different roles in the domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's PC Member is a reviewer role (a person who reviews papers, parent Possible Reviewer, children include PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair), while B's Program Chair is an organizer role (parent Organizator, sibling of General Chair and Program Committee member). A PC member is not a program chair; the program chair leads the committee, so the two denote different roles and are unrelated.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference, sibling of Workshop/Session/Track), while B's Conference hall is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel/Main office). They denote different kinds of things: an event vs. a location, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is an abstract submission date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date literal (a deadline for abstract submission). B's 'location Of' is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the event held at that location). They relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions and domains, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event such as Tutorial/Workshop), while B's Conference city is a kind of City (sibling of Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a city associated with a conference, so they are unrelated.

A's 'publisher Of' relates an Organisation to documents it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site), while B's 'is paid in' relates Money to a Building where it is paid. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract; B's 'design' links the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's hasStartDateTime gives the start time of a Conference Event, while B's End_of_conference gives the end time of a Conference. They denote different temporal aspects (start vs end) and different scopes (event vs conference), so they are not equivalent; at best they are related but not the same relation.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer assigned to review a paper). B's is_sent_by relates an Item to a Person (e.g. a submission sent by an author). The domains and ranges differ (Reviewer->Paper vs Item->Person), and the directions/meanings are distinct: assignment for reviewing is not the same relation as being sent by a person. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

Submission (iasted) is a subclass of Document representing a submitted paper with children Initial/Final manuscript, whereas Committee (sigkdd) is an organizational body with children Best Paper Awards, Organizing and Program committees. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain and share no instances.

A's Associated Chair is a chair/committee role (a Person who chairs, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), while B's Plenary lecture speaker is a speaker role under Author (sibling of Lecturer and Tutorial speaker). The two denote different roles in the conference domain: chairing versus giving a plenary talk. No subsumption or overlap holds.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'is paid with' is an object property mapping Money to an Item (the means of payment). They have different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members (a part-whole/group membership relation within the organisation structure). B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (an authorship/presentation relation). Different domains (Committee vs Document), different ranges (Committee member vs Speaker), and different intended meanings; they are not the same property nor inverses.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (a static informational artefact, sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.), whereas B's 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event in the event hierarchy (sibling of Submission event, Reviewing event, Camera Ready event). One is a document, the other an event; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is an academic event (has dates, country, members, topics, deadlines), while B's Proceedings is a published multi-author volume (a Document) that merely results from a conference. They denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (where they study), while ekaw's authorOf relates a Person to a Document (what they authored). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman who chairs the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B 'Conference Venue Place' is a physical location (a kind of Place, sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. location) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members (people belonging to the committee), while B's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domains (Committee vs Event), different ranges (Committee member vs Organisation/Person), and different intended relations (membership vs organisation). They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Person (a registered applicant who paid late), while B 'Fee for extra trip' is a subclass of Money/Fee (a charge for an extra trip). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `abstract` is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its textual abstract (range string), while B's `obtain` is an object property linking a Person to an Item (e.g. obtaining a document). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Contribution vs Person), range (string vs Item), and meaning, so they are not the same relation.

cmt:assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review a paper), while iasted:need relates a Person to an Item (a person needs an item). Different domain, range and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Textual Review Question' is a kind of question (a prompt/item on a review form, sibling of Numerical Review Question) used to elicit a textual answer. B 'Review' is a document (a subclass of Document, with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review) that is written about a paper by a reviewer. A question is not a review document; they denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property linking a Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while B's 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop is a type of academic event (a gathering/session at a conference), while a Video presentation is a type of presentation activity (a recorded talk format). They belong to different branches (Event vs Activity/Presentation) and denote different concepts; a workshop is not a video presentation.

A's hasStartDateTime is a datatype property of Conference Event giving the start date/time of an event; B's done_till is a datatype property of Deadline giving the date by which a deadline is done. Different domains (Conference Event vs Deadline) and different intended meaning (event start vs deadline completion), so they are not equivalent.

A's relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to the Paper Presentation it is related to (domain Accepted Paper, range Paper Presentation), i.e. a paper-to-presentation association. B's partOfEvent is a mereological relation between Events (domain Event, range Event), expressing that one event is part of another. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship relation), while B's 'is paid by' links Money to a Person (payment relation). Different domains (Conference document vs Money) and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, choices), while B's 'Performance Topic' is a subclass of Topic, a subject area for papers. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class covering all people involved in a conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), while Passive conference participant in Conference is a narrower class for attendees who do not actively contribute (siblings with Active conference participant). The two overlap in that both include non-active participants, but Conference Member also includes active roles, so they are not equivalent; the broader/narrower relation is only partial, making 'related' the safest verdict.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property of Review preference (an integer degree of preference for a review), while B's 'max Choice' is a datatype property of Social event / Working event (a positiveInteger maximum number of choices for an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

An Invited speaker is a distinguished person invited to give a talk, a subtype of Conference contributor in the Conference ontology. A Volunteer is a person who helps run the conference (confTool), a direct subtype of Person in confOf. The two concepts denote different roles with no overlap in intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to the Person who authored it; B's 'is visited by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person who visits it. Different domains (Document vs. Building/City/State) and different intended meanings (authorship vs. visitation), so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Student non speaker is a kind of delegate/person (a non-speaker attendee who is a student). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Registration form' is a Document/Form artefact used to register for the conference, while B 'Hotel' is a Place (a physical venue). They share no intended instances and belong to different branches (Document vs Place), so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to the Reviewer it is assigned to (review assignment). B's 'has a topic or a submission contribution' links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic (the subject matter a reviewer prefers). Different domains (Paper vs Review preference), different ranges (Reviewer vs Submitted contribution/Topic), and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Paper is a document/contribution class (subclass of Document, with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To). B's 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Author (a person role), i.e. an author who has written a paper, not the paper itself. The two denote different concepts (a document vs. a person role), so they are unrelated.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event (a time-bounded activity in the conference process, sibling of Reviewing event, Camera Ready event) in confOf. B 'Viza' is a Document (a physical/paper artefact, sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Review, Submission) in iasted. One is an event, the other a document; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people), while B's partOfEvent relates an Event to its sub-events (events). Different domain/range kinds and different meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's write Paper goes Author -> Paper (author writes paper), while B's written By goes Document -> Person (document written by person). These are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

Both classes denote a program committee member: confOf's 'Member PC' is a Person whose comment is 'Reviewer' and who reviews Contributions and has expertise in Topics; sigkdd's 'Program Committee member' is a Person/Organizator role alongside Program Chair and General Chair. The intended instances (people serving on the program committee) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A's Conference is the overall conference event (accepts submissions, has members, dates, administrators), while B's Deadline is a submission/notification deadline with children for abstract submission, author notification and paper submission. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A is a research topic in computer architecture (a subject area under Topic in the edas conference ontology), while B is a physical audiovisual device (a video cassette player) under Audiovisual equipment in the iasted equipment taxonomy. They denote entirely different kinds of entities with no overlap.

A Call for paper is a public announcement soliciting submissions, while an Invitation letter is a private document inviting a specific person (e.g. a speaker or VIP). They are different document types in the conference domain, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a person attending without an active role), while B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Working event (an event type). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote a person versus an event, so they are unrelated.

A 'Workshop Paper' is a kind of academic paper (a document submitted to a workshop), while B 'Van' is a transport vehicle. The two entities belong to entirely different domains and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Social Event is a specific non-academic conference event (with children Excursion and Reception), while B's Conference activity is a broad umbrella covering all conference activities including lectures, presentations, registration, coffee breaks and social program. Social Event is thus a narrower concept subsumed by the broader Conference activity; they are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is a document/paper type — the abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper. Author of paper student (sigkdd) is a person role — a student author of a paper, under Author. They denote different kinds of things (a document vs. a person role), so they are unrelated.

A's `abstract` is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its textual abstract (string), while B's `written By` is an object property linking a Document to a Person author. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and cannot be equivalent.

Both properties link a conference to a group of people involved in its organization, but the domains and ranges differ: A's domain is Conference and range is Conference Member, while B's domain is Conference volume and range is Organizing committee. They are not equivalent because they relate different kinds of entities (Conference Member vs. Organizing committee) and have different domain/range restrictions. However, they are related in that both capture organizational roles within a conference context.

A 'Track workshop chair' is a Person who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial (a specific role tied to a Conference part, with properties linking to Conference part). B 'Program Committee member' is an Organizator role within the Program Committee hierarchy (siblings: General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). The two roles are distinct: a track/workshop chair is not a PC member, and the ontologies place them in different role hierarchies (Person vs Organizator). No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's 'study At' relates a Scholar to a University (a person's affiliation/study location). B's 'scientifically Organises' relates an Academic Institution to an unspecified range, i.e. an institution organising something scientific (e.g. an event). Different domains (Scholar vs Academic Institution) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Session Chair (edas) is a Person role that initiates calls and reviews papers, sitting alongside Conference Chair, TPC Member, Reviewer. Program Chair (sigkdd) is an Organizator role alongside General Chair and committee members. Both are senior organising roles, but they are not the same concept: a session chair runs a session, a program chair heads the program committee. They overlap in the conference-organisation domain but are distinct roles, so 'related' rather than 'equivalent'.

A's 'Short paper' is a type of contribution (a paper of short length), while B's 'Pending Paper' is a paper in a submission/review state (not yet accepted/rejected). They classify papers along different dimensions (length vs. status) and are not the same concept.

A's 'Rejected Paper' is a subclass of Paper representing a paper that was rejected in the review process, while B's 'Abstract' is a sibling of Paper under Document, denoting the abstract text of a document rather than a rejected paper. They differ in both kind and role, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a conference to a group of people involved in it, but the ranges differ: cmt's Conference Member is a person (member of the conference/committee), while Conference's Committee is a collective body. A committee is not a conference member, so the properties are not equivalent; they are related in that both connect a conference to its organisational people/body.

A's 'has Surname' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'is used by' is an object property mapping an Item to a Person (an inverse of a usage relation). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop is a small interactive academic event where participants discuss work in progress, a subtype of Academic Event alongside talks and paper presentations. A Plenary lecture is a large formal lecture given to the whole conference, a subtype of Lecture alongside Session and Tutorial. They denote different kinds of conference activities with different formats and roles, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a registered conference applicant who paid late), while B is a subclass of Paper (a document awaiting a decision). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person/registration vs. document/paper status) and share no intended instances.

A's `name` is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's `has Street` is a specific address component for Organization and Person. Although both are datatype properties with string ranges and share Person as a domain, they denote different relations (a name vs. a street address), so they are not equivalent.

Assistant in confOf is a Person subtype (a helper role, comment 'confTool'), while Two Level Conference in edas is a Conference subtype (a conference structure with TPC members), so the two classes denote entirely different concepts.

A 'Free Time Break' is a non-academic break event in the conference schedule (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break), while B 'Main office' is a physical place (sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They denote different concepts: a scheduled break versus a location, so they are unrelated.

A is a document type (the abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B is a subject/topic category (a child of Topic in a topic taxonomy). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Performance Topic' is a subject area of papers (a subclass of Topic), while B 'Program Committee' is an organisational committee (a subclass of Committee). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of 'Conference participant' and denotes a person attending without an active role (e.g. listener). B's 'Participant' is the general class of persons taking part in the conference, with subclasses Member, Regular, Student, etc. The passive participant is a specific kind of participant, so A is strictly narrower than B: subsumed_by, not equivalent.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's is_designed_for is an object property relating Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person. They have different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both entities concern conference registration: A's class is a registration event/activity, B's class is a registration activity. They are closely related but not clearly equivalent because A models the event and B models the activity/process.

Invited Talk Abstract is a specific kind of Abstract (a subclass of Abstract in ekaw), while sigkdd's Abstract is the general class covering all abstracts. The ekaw class is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by the sigkdd Abstract rather than equivalent.

A's 'Written contribution' is a broad class of written conference contributions (parents: Conference contribution; children: Regular contribution, Submitted contribution), while B's 'Submission' is a document submitted to a conference (parents: Document; children: Initial manuscript, Final manuscript). They overlap in that submissions are written contributions, but A also covers non-submitted written contributions and B is specifically the submitted document artefact, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both denote a person who actively presents at the conference: A's 'Active conference participant' gives presentations and is a Conference contributor/participant, with siblings Invited speaker, Passive conference participant, Regular author; B's 'Presenter' is a Conference Participant whose child is Invited Speaker and who presents. The intended instances coincide (active presenters), so they are equivalent.

A's 'Written contribution' is a kind of conference contribution (a paper/submission), sitting under Conference contribution with siblings like Poster, Presentation, Invited talk. B's 'Form' is a document artefact (a form to be filled in), under Document with children like Registration form, Hotel registration form, Author information form. They denote different concepts: a scholarly contribution vs. an administrative form, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Session Chair) in the conference organization, while B is a document type (Brief introduction for Session chair) under Document. They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a session within a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session, child of Session under Scientific Event). B 'Activity before conference' is a temporal activity phase (parent of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript, Renting, Research), sibling of 'Activity after conference' and 'Conference activity'. They denote different concepts: a session type vs. a pre-conference activity phase, with no overlap in instances.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Person) while B is an administrative event (the reviewing procedure, a subclass of Event). They denote different kinds of entities (a person vs. a process/event) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Social event' is a general category of social events (its children include Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B's 'Reception' is a specific kind of social event (sibling of Excursion under Social Event). Thus A is broader and subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Industry Organization' is a subtype of Organization (a type of institution/affiliation, sibling to Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO), whereas B's 'Organizing Committee' is a subtype of Committee (a group of people organizing the conference, sibling to Program Committee). They denote different concepts: an organization type vs. a committee role, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' links a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it (domain Review, range Reviewer). B's 'has a review expertise' links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise topic (domain Submitted contribution, range Review expertise). Different domains, ranges and meanings: authorship of a review vs. topical expertise of a submission. Not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like abstract, title, keywords, written by Author, reviewed by PC member. Review Form in edas is the form used to record a review, not a submitted contribution. Different concepts.

hasProgramme relates a Conference Event to its Programme (a whole-to-part/component relation with a specific range), while partOfEvent relates an Event to a broader Event (a part-to-whole relation between events). They differ in direction and in the kinds of entities related, so they are not equivalent.

The two properties are inverses of each other: 'write Paper' goes from Author to Paper, while 'is Written By' goes from Paper to Author. They describe the same relationship in opposite directions, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword; B's locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. Different domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Possible Reviewer is a person role (a Person who may review papers, superclass of PC Member, involved in review relations), while B's Registration fee is a fee category (a Fee subclass with price/currency and payment relations). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a class of conference contributions (a paper that was rejected after review), whereas B 'Accpet If Room Rating' is a review rating value in EDAS (a rating category meaning accept if space is available). They belong to different branches (contribution vs. review rating) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties linking a document/activity to a date, but the domains differ (Conference document vs Activity) and the ranges differ (date vs dateTime). They express a similar 'dated on' notion but are not the same relation across the two ontologies.

A 'Conference volume' is a whole conference event/proceedings container (it has committees, tracks, contributions, important dates, locations), whereas B 'Organizing Committee member' is a person role within a conference. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and are not equivalent.

A's Conference Chair is a specific chair role under Chairman (a Person subtype), while B's OC Member is a generic member of the Organising Committee, the parent of OC Chair. They overlap in the conference-organisation domain (both concern organising-committee leadership) but neither subsumes the other: OC Member is broader than a chair role, and Conference Chair is a chair role not necessarily tied to the OC hierarchy. Hence related, not equivalent.

Reviewer in cmt is a conference committee role (a Person who reviews papers, with bid/assignment/conflict-of-interest properties, sibling of Author, PC Member, Chair). Paid applicant in Conference is a registration-payment status of a conference applicant (subclasses Early/Late paid applicant), with no reviewing role. The two denote different concepts despite both being persons, so they are unrelated.

A's hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a keyword string, while B's hasCostAmount links a Sponsorship to an integer cost. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they denote different relations.

A's Participant is a subclass of Person (a conference attendee with subclasses Member, Regular, Student), while B's Research is a subclass of 'Activity before conference' (a pre-conference activity with subclasses Modelling, Simulating). They denote entirely different concepts in different branches of the domain, so they are unrelated.

Accepted Paper is a paper that has been accepted (a subclass of Paper, sibling of Rejected Paper, Pending Paper, etc.), whereas Invitation letter is a document type (a subclass of Document, sibling of Form, Review, Submission, etc.) used to invite someone. They denote different concepts and do not overlap.

A's title is a datatype property linking a Paper to its string title; B's submit is an object property linking an Author to a Paper. They differ in kind, domain, range and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Poster is a kind of conference contribution (a document/paper type, sibling of Presentation and Written contribution, with an abstract). B's Paper Presentation is a kind of academic event (sibling of Workshop and Talk Event, linked to an Accepted Paper). One is a document, the other an event, so they denote different concepts despite the shared word 'presentation'.

A's 'contributes' goes Person -> Conference document (a person contributes a document), while B's 'is signed by' goes Item -> Person (an item is signed by a person). They are inverse in direction and relate different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Co chair' is a specific committee role (a Person who is a Committee member, sibling of Chair, with committee co-chair properties). B's 'Scholar' is a price/registration category for a Person (comment 'price category - scholar', sibling of Administrator, Author, Participant, etc., with a studyAt property). They denote different concepts: a committee role vs. a fee category, so they are not equivalent.
A is a research topic (a subject area under Topic), while B is an award category (under Award). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A is a person role (chair of a conference, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while B is a physical building (a type of Building, sibling of Conference building/hotel/restaurant). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

Conference document is a broad class covering all conference-related documents (calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc.), while Form in iasted is a specific subclass of Document for fillable forms (registration, author information, hotel registration). The intended instances do not coincide: a Form is a specific kind of document, not a general conference document, and Conference document is not a kind of Form. They are unrelated concepts.

Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes papers), while Conference document is a document artefact (parent of Call for paper, Review, etc.). They are different kinds of entities: Author's properties (write Paper, submit Paper) relate a person to papers, whereas Conference document's properties (has authors, has a date of issue) relate a document to persons and dates. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A 'Technic activity' is a kind of conference activity/event (sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Registration) in iasted, whereas B 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person (a role played by a person, with children General Chair, Program Chair, etc.) in sigkdd. One denotes an event, the other a person role; they are not the same concept.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact. B 'Conference building' is a physical place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport), i.e. a location. They denote different kinds of entities and share only the word 'Conference', so they are unrelated.

A's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while B's 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B's 'Viza' is a Document subtype (sibling of Review, Submission, Invitation letter) in the iasted ontology, i.e. a paper/administrative artefact, not a person. Different kinds and domains, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Registration form' is a form used to register for the conference. They belong to different sub-hierarchies (Conference document vs Form) and denote different artefacts; no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's Non Academic Event is a subclass of Conference Event covering breaks, meals and social events, while B's Conference activity is a broader class covering all conference activities including lectures, presentations and registration. They overlap (both include social/break activities) but neither subsumes the other: B includes academic activities that A excludes, and A is a sibling of Academic Event rather than a superclass of all activities.

A is a research topic in radio communications (a subclass of Topic in the edas ontology), while B is a physical transport vehicle (a subclass of Item with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van in the iasted ontology). They share no meaning in the conference domain and belong to entirely different hierarchies.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is an event type (Tutorial, a kind of Working event). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

In cmt, Reviewer is a specific role under Conference Member with children Meta Reviewer and properties for bidding, assignment, and reviewing. In ekaw, Possible Reviewer is a broad class directly under Person, with PC Member as a child, and properties indicating anyone who may review a paper. A cmt Reviewer is a kind of Possible Reviewer, but Possible Reviewer is more general (includes PC Members and others who may review), so Reviewer is subsumed by Possible Reviewer, not equivalent.

Camera Ready Paper is a specific final version of a paper (a subclass of Paper), while Abstract is a distinct document type (a short summary document) that is a sibling of Paper, not a kind of paper. They denote different concepts.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to an anyURI (a logo image location), while B's 'Name of conference' links a Conference to a string (its name). Although both are datatype properties with domain Conference, they capture different attributes (logo vs. name) and different value types, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item to a Person (e.g. a presentation given by a person), while B's 'awarded by' relates an Award to an unspecified entity. Different domains (Activity/Item vs Award) and different intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Session Chair' is a conference participant role (a person who chairs a session), while B's 'IASTED member' is a membership status of a delegate in the IASTED organisation. B's sibling 'Session chair' is the actual role counterpart, so the two entities denote different concepts.

confOf's 'Chair PC' is a Person who chairs the programme committee (a PC chair role), while ekaw's 'Session Chair' is a Conference Participant who chairs an individual session; both are chairing roles but over different objects (PC vs session), so they overlap as chair roles without denoting the same concept.
hasMenu relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (catering), while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (a talk). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's property links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (a preference for reviewing), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/presenting something). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Conference proceedings' is a published volume (has publisher, volume, ISBN, name) — a document/artifact. B 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a Session within an Event hierarchy, with children like Industrial Session). They denote different kinds of things: a publication vs. a scheduled event, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote members of the program committee. cmt's ProgramCommitteeMember is a subclass of Conference Member and Person, with children Program Committee Chair; ekaw's PC_Member is a subclass of Possible Reviewer with children PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair. The intended instances coincide: individuals serving on the program committee. The slight difference in children (ekaw includes additional chair roles) does not change the core concept, and the labels and paths agree.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Conference Chair is a person role (a subclass of Person, sibling of Attendee, Author, Reviewer). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and cannot be equivalent.

A's hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its title string, while B's hasSubmissionDeadline links a Call to a dateTime deadline. They relate different kinds of things (title text vs. a deadline date) in different domains, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (an author contributing a paper). B's 'is paid for' relates Money to an Activity or Item (a payment covering a fee). Different domains (Person vs Money), different ranges (Conference document vs Activity/Item), and different directions of meaning; they denote distinct relations.

A Presenter in ekaw is a Conference Participant who presents at the conference (parent Conference Participant, child Invited Speaker), i.e. a role of a person at the event. B Tutorial speaker in iasted is a subclass of Author (path Delegate > Speaker > Author > Tutorial speaker), i.e. an author who gives a tutorial. Both denote people who present, but the ekaw class is a general presenting role under Conference Participant while the iasted class is a specific authoring/presenting role for tutorials; they overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who funds it), while B's 'written By' links a Document to a Person (who authored it). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (the document they have a conflict of interest about), while B's is_given_to relates an Item to a Person (the recipient of the item). The domains and ranges are swapped and the intended meanings differ: conflict-of-interest declaration vs. item handover. They are not the same relation, nor inverses in a meaningful sense (Person->Document vs Item->Person).

A's 'Active conference participant' is a broad class of contributors who actively take part (giving presentations, e.g. authors/speakers), while B's 'OC Member' is a specific organising-committee role under Conference Participant. The two concepts do not coincide: an OC member need not give a presentation, and an active participant (e.g. a regular author) need not be on the organising committee. Different paths, parents, siblings and properties confirm they denote different roles.

A's 'has important dates' is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity (a set of deadlines), while B's 'has Start Date Time' is a datatype property linking a Conference Event to a single xsd:dateTime value. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Conference volume vs Conference Event), and range (Important dates vs dateTime), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to its Reviewer (domain Paper, range Reviewer), while B's 'has Related Paper' links an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (a reviewer adjusting their own bid/review score), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (an author writing a paper). Different domains (Reviewer vs Author) and ranges (Bid vs Contribution), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an Administrator action whose range is a Conference (the event), while B's 'issues' is a Publisher action whose range is Conference proceedings (the published volume). Different domains (Administrator vs Publisher), different ranges (Conference vs Conference proceedings), and different intended relations (assigning papers to reviewers vs publishing proceedings), so they are not equivalent.

Author in cmt is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Registration fee in iasted is a monetary Fee subclass with children such as Student registration fee and Nonmember registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic in computer networks (a subject area), while B is a program committee (an organizational body). Their paths, parents, and siblings are entirely different, and no domain relation connects a topic to a committee.

A is a datatype property giving the start date/time of a Conference Event (domain Conference Event, range dateTime). B is an object property linking a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (domain Programme Brochure/Web Site, range Event). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have different domains/ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the conference event itself (it has a name, proceedings, publisher, topics, and a 'Conference volume' child). B's Conference hall is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel and Main office), i.e. a venue room, not the conference event. Different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

A's property relates an Administrator to a Conference (printing/mailing hardcopy manifests), while B's property relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (issuing proceedings). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'member Of Conference' relates a Conference Member to a Conference (domain Conference Member, range Conference), while B's 'has members' relates a Committee to a Committee member (domain Committee, range Committee member). These are inverse-like relations: A goes member->conference, B goes committee->member. They are not equivalent because the direction and the domain/range roles are swapped. However, a Conference Member is a kind of Committee member and a Conference is a kind of Committee, so A's relation is more specific than B's; A is subsumed by B.

A is a research topic in computer networks (a subject area under Topic), while B is a kind of conference presentation event (a Contributed Talk under Individual Presentation). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (a conference/tutorial/workshop activity), while B 'Building' is a subclass of Place (a physical location such as a conference building or hotel). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. place) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'accepted By' relates a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it; B's 'awarded by' relates an Award to whatever grants the award. Different domains (Paper vs Award) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class (parent of Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.) denoting anyone affiliated with the conference, while Student in confOf is a specific participant subtype (sibling of Member and Regular) denoting a participant's academic status. Their intended instances do not coincide: a Student participant need not be a conference member in the cmt sense, and a Conference Member (e.g. an author or chair) need not be a student. Different paths, parents and siblings confirm they are unrelated concepts.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a conference submission that has undergone review (parent Submitted contribution, children Accepted/Rejected contribution, linked to Review). B 'Money' is a financial resource with children Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment amounts and payers. The two concepts share no meaning in the conference domain.

Attendee in edas is a generic person attending the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles), while SC Member in ekaw is a Steering Committee member, a specific sub-role of PC Member. They denote different concepts: an attendee need not be a steering committee member and vice versa.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Poster Paper' is a type of paper (a document submitted/presented as a poster). They belong to different branches (document/announcement vs. paper) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property linking a conference web resource to a string URL, while B's 'locationOf' is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the inverse of an event's location). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have different ranges (string vs Event), so they are not equivalent.

A's title is the title of a Paper (domain Paper), while B's has short title is a short title of Social event / Working event (domain events). Different domains and different intended concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Conference announcement is a document type (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) under Conference document, while Banquet is a social event (sibling of Reception, Trip) under Event. They denote different concepts in different branches of the conference domain.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Conference contribution, etc.) that provides informational material to attendees. B's 'Trip' is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception) that is a type of event. They belong to different branches (document vs. event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it; B's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to the chair/TPC members who initiate it. Different domains (Presentation vs Call) and different ranges (participant vs chair roles), so the relations do not coincide.

A's property is a specific administrative action (Administrator -> Conference) for printing hardcopy mailing manifests, while B's 'send' is a general Person -> Item action. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not the same relation.
A is a submission-deadline date property on Important dates; B is a person's first-name string property on Person. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's reviewWrittenBy relates a Review to a Possible Reviewer (a person who wrote the review), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Trip is a social event (a kind of excursion/outing, sibling of Banquet and Reception under Social event), whereas B's IASTED member is a role of a Delegate (a person category under Conference building). They denote entirely different concepts—an event versus a person role—so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Platinum Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. sponsor) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Company in confOf is an organizational entity (sibling of University under Organization), whereas Renting in iasted is a pre-conference activity (sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript). They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A's Bank transfer is a subclass of Payment document (a financial instrument used to pay conference fees), while B's Paper is a document submitted by an author and reviewed. They share only the generic Document ancestor and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution to a paper), while B's 'is occupied by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (occupancy of a place). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation nor inverses.

confOf's Contribution is a submitted academic work (children Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by an Author, reviewed by PC members, has title/abstract/keywords), whereas iasted's Activity is a general event/action (children Activity before/after conference, Conference activity; given by a Person, held in a Place, dated, paid for). The intended instances do not coincide: a paper is not an activity, and the property contexts (authorship/review vs. person/place/time/money) are disjoint.

A is a conference-organisation role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, a person who chairs a conference), while B is a research activity (Modelling, a subactivity of Research before the conference). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Activity) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a student registration fee (a fee category for students), while B is a registration fee for non-members. They are distinct fee categories: A's siblings include member/nonmember/author/nonauthor fees, and B's siblings include SIGKDD member, SIGMOD member, and student fees. A student may be a member or non-member, so the two classes do not coincide.

A's 'Co chair' is a committee member who co-chairs a committee (sibling of Chair, domain/range Committee -> Co chair). B's 'PC Chair' is a conference participant who chairs the program committee (sibling of Demo Chair, Session Chair, etc., under PC Member). Both denote a chairing role, but they are distinct roles: a co-chair of a committee vs. the program-committee chair. They overlap in the conference domain without coinciding, so 'related' rather than equivalent.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete version of a submitted paper (sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper). B 'Conference announcement' is a document announcing the conference, sibling of Call for paper, Conference contribution, etc. under Conference document. They denote different document types with no overlap.

A's read By Meta Reviewer relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (the person who reads it at the meta level), while B's has Reviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (any potential reviewer). The ranges are disjoint roles (meta-reviewer vs. reviewer) and the relations differ in kind, so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a conference part (sibling of Track and Tutorial) that can be contained in a conference volume; B's Track is a scientific event (sibling of Conference, Session, Workshop) representing a thematic track of the conference. Although both are conference components, they denote different concepts: a workshop is a distinct event, while a track is a thematic subdivision. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A's Person is the broad superclass of all conference participants (Attendee, Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Speaker is a narrower subclass of Person (siblings Listener, Organizator) denoting someone who presents a document. Person is strictly more general than Speaker, so A subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

Personal Publication History is a class representing a history/record of a person's publications, whereas Paper Author is a role of a person who authors a paper. They are not equivalent: one is a history entity, the other is a person role.

Both classes denote a review of a conference contribution/paper: A's Review is a Conference document with properties 'has a review' (Reviewed contribution -> Review) and 'reviews' (Review -> Reviewed contribution); B's Review is a Document sibling of Paper, Programme and Slide Set, i.e. the same review artefact in the EDAS conference system. Same label, same intended instances, matching domain context.

confOf University is an Organization (a type of institution, sibling of Company, domain of studyAt), whereas iasted Presenter university is a Building/Place (sibling of Conference hotel, Presenter house, Sponsor company house). One denotes an academic institution, the other a physical venue building, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type, the abstract version of a paper) in cmt, while B is a research topic (Radio Communications) under Topic in edas. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

A's Author is a person role (subclass of Person, with children like Presenter and properties linking to papers). B's 'Author attendee cd registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, i.e. a monetary fee category for author attendees. They denote different concepts (person vs. fee), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person denoting someone who authors papers; B's 'Lecturer' is a subclass of Author (under Speaker/Delegate) denoting a person who gives lectures. Although both are persons involved in academic work, the intended instances differ: a paper author need not be a lecturer and a lecturer need not author papers. The paths and sibling sets (A: Person roles like Possible Reviewer, Student; B: Author roles like Plenary lecture speaker, Tutorial speaker) show different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Review preference' is a reviewer's declared preference/expertise over topics and submissions (domain of 'has a degree', linked to Reviewer and Review expertise). B's 'Contribution' is a submitted paper/poster/short paper with title, abstract, keywords, authors and PC reviews. They denote different concepts: a preference record vs. a submission artefact, so they are unrelated.

A Travel Grant is sponsorship money given to help an attendee cover costs, while a Fee for extra trip is a charge paid for an additional trip; one is financial support received, the other a cost owed, so their instances do not coincide.

Scholar in confOf is a price category (a person attending at a reduced/scholar rate, with property study At -> University), while Session Chair in edas is a role that initiates calls and reviews papers. They denote different concepts despite both being subclasses of Person.

Both properties link a Paper to the reviewers of that paper. cmt's 'read By Reviewer' has domain Paper and range Reviewer; ekaw's 'has Reviewer' has domain Paper and range Possible Reviewer, where Possible Reviewer is the class of people who can review (i.e. reviewers). The direction is the same (paper -> reviewer), and the intended relation (the reviewers assigned to a paper) coincides, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'Name of sponsor' is a datatype property of Sponzor giving a sponsor's name. Different domains (Person vs Sponzor) and different intended meanings (surname vs sponsor name), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'was a committe co chair of' relates a Co chair to a Committee (a role/committee-membership relation, subproperty of 'was a member of'), whereas B's 'writtenBy' relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship of a paper). Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (a text/web page giving practical info to attendees), while B's 'Workshop' is an academic event type in the event hierarchy. They denote different kinds of things (document vs. event) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a type of event/conference), while B's 'Conference Participant' is a subclass of Person (a role played by people). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Rejected Paper' is a class of documents (a paper that was evaluated and rejected), while B's 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity/process (accepting a manuscript) under 'Activity before conference', sibling to 'Receiving manuscript' and 'Refusing manuscript'. Different kinds (document vs. activity) and different meaning (rejected paper vs. accepting action), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant under Conference applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B 'Published Paper' is a subclass of Paper under Document (a published document). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person/registration vs. document/publication) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property of a Conference giving the number of reviews per paper (an integer count of reviews), while B's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving the volume number of the proceedings. They have different domains (Conference vs Conference proceedings) and different intended meanings (review count vs volume number), so they are not equivalent.

Both denote the physical venue where a conference takes place: iasted's 'Conference building' is a Building subtype that hosts Delegates, and sigkdd's 'Conference hall' is a Place subtype alongside Hotel and Main office, i.e. the conference venue location. The labels differ (building vs hall) but the intended instances (the conference venue) coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'written By' links a Document to the Person who authored it; B's 'payed by' links a Registration fee to the Person who pays it. Different domains (Document vs Registration fee) and different intended relations (authorship vs payment), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call For Papers' is a call/announcement event (sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews, under Call), whereas B's 'Review' is a document type (sibling of Abstract and Paper, under Document). They denote different concepts: an announcement soliciting submissions vs. a review document, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about a conference, with a URL), while B's 'Conference airport' is a building/place (an airport used by a conference). They denote different kinds of entities and share no intended instances.
