A is a person role (Associated Chair) in the conference committee hierarchy, while B is a social event (Dinner banquet) in the social program; they denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Published Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been published), while B's 'Research' is an activity performed before a conference (with children Modelling and Simulating). They denote different kinds of things (document vs. activity) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Active conference participant' is a subclass of 'Conference contributor'/'Conference participant' and is characterized by giving presentations, making it a narrower concept than ekaw's 'Conference Participant', which is a direct subclass of Person and has broad children such as Presenter, Paper Author, and various chairs. Every active conference participant is a conference participant, but not vice versa (e.g., a passive participant or author who does not present), so A is subsumed by B.

Published Paper (edas) is a paper that has been published, sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Pending/Withdrawn Paper under Paper. Poster Paper (ekaw) is a paper presented as a poster, sibling of Camera Ready/Conference/Demo/Industrial/Regular/Submitted/Workshop Paper under Paper. They denote different subclasses of Paper with different intended instances; a poster paper need not be published and a published paper need not be a poster.

A's Reviewer is a Person (a person who reviews papers), while B's Review is a Document (the review text/artefact produced). They are different kinds of entities: a person vs. a document, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Co chair' is a Committee member (a committee role, sibling of Chair, with committee co-chair properties), while B's 'Conference Chair' is a Person-level role that initiates calls and reviews papers. They both denote a chairing role in the conference domain and overlap, but A is a committee-specific co-chair role and B is the general conference chair; neither clearly subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'has contributions' relates a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (a whole-part containment between a volume and its papers). B's 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (an agent creating/preparing an item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (person-to-committee membership). B's has_a_program_committee relates a Conference volume to a Program committee (conference-to-committee containment). Different domains, ranges and directions of relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an Administrator action that assigns papers to reviewers/committee members and has range Conference, while B's 'write' is a Person->Item relation expressing authorship of a paper. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's 'Introduction of speaker' is a conference activity (a subclass of Introduction, an event/talk type), whereas B's 'Speaker' is a person role (subclass of Person). One denotes an activity, the other a person, so they cannot be equivalent.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, a committee person who chairs the conference). B's 'Presenter state' is a state of a presenter (a subclass of State, sibling of Conference state and Sponsor state), i.e. a situation/status, not a person. Different kinds of entities (person vs. state), so they are unrelated.

A's hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper's rating), while B's is_used_for relates an Item to an Activity or Money (a resource used for something). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Associated Chair is a chair/committee role (a kind of Chairman and Conference Member, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), while B's IASTED non member is a delegate/attendee category (a kind of Delegate, sibling of Speaker, Listener, Session chair). The two denote different concepts: an organisational chair role versus a non-member attendee, so they are not equivalent.

A's Abstract is a specific kind of conference contribution (an extended abstract's abstract, part of a Paper/Poster/Presentation), while B's Document is a broad class whose children include Abstract, Paper, Review, etc. Abstract is therefore strictly narrower than Document, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A 'Conference Session' is a temporal event/activity within a conference (it relates to Documents and Academic Events), whereas B 'Place' is a spatial location (with children Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room) that activities and persons are held in or present in. The two denote different concepts (event vs. location) and do not coincide.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (the venue/proceedings where it is submitted), while B's 'paper Presented As' relates a Paper to an Individual Presentation (the presentation event/format). The ranges are different kinds of entities (volume vs presentation) and the relations capture different aspects of the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's Program Committee is a group of people who review papers (has Program Committee Member / member Of Program Committee). B's State is a geographical/administrative region occupied by persons and situated in places (is occupied by, is situated in, is visited by, occupy). The two concepts share no intended instances and no domain relation; they are unrelated.

Paper in cmt is a document (submitted contribution) with children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version and properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To. Call For Reviews in edas is a call/announcement (sibling of Call For Papers, Call For Manuscripts) under Call, not a document. Different concepts despite both being conference-domain entities.

In edas, Document is a broad class whose children include Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, and Meal Menu, and which is related to academic events, conferences, sessions, and persons. In iasted, Form is a specific subclass of Document (path Item > Document > Form) whose children are Author information form, Hotel registration form, and Registration form. The iasted Form denotes a specific kind of document (a form), not the general Document class of edas. The two classes do not have coinciding intended instances: edas Document includes papers and reviews, which are not forms, and iasted Form is a narrow subclass of its own Document class. Therefore they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a name' is a general naming datatype property whose domain spans Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, whereas B's 'Name' is restricted to Person. They share the string range and the naming sense, but the domains are disjoint (Person is not among A's domain classes), so they do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an organised excursion during the conference), while a Double hotel room is a type of hotel room (accommodation place). They belong to different branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are classes named Review, both sit directly under Document in their respective hierarchies, and both denote the conference-domain concept of a review of a paper (ekaw's Review has review Of Paper / review Written By properties; iasted's Review is a Document subtype in the conference document taxonomy). Same intended instances, so equivalent.

A's property links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (the contribution being reviewed), while B's hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a person). Different domain and range kinds, and the direction/meaning differ: one relates expertise to a contribution, the other a paper to a reviewer. They are not the same relation.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members (a committee-to-person membership relation), while B's is_given_by links an Activity/Item to the Person who gives it (e.g. a presentation given by a speaker). Different domain (committee vs activity/item) and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.
A's 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while B's 'is paid with' relates Money to an Item (payment). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

Both classes denote a person who reviews papers: Conference's Reviewer is a Person with review expertise/preferences and review assignments, and confOf's Member PC is a Person whose rdfs:comment is literally 'Reviewer' and who has 'expert On' topics and 'reviewes' contributions. Same intended instances, same parent Person, so they are equivalent.

A's rejectedBy links a Paper to the Administrator who rejected it (domain Paper, range Administrator). B's relatedToPaper links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (domain Paper Presentation, range Accepted Paper). Different domains, ranges and meanings: one expresses a rejection decision, the other a presentation-to-paper association. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

University in confOf is a subclass of Organization (path Organization > University, sibling Company), while edas Organization is the general superclass with subclasses Academia Organization, Government Organization, Industry Organization, NGO. A university is a kind of organization, so University is strictly more specific than Organization; they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference (domain Reviewer, range Review expertise/Review preference), while B's hasReview links a Paper to its Review (domain Paper, range Review). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B 'Program Committee' is a subclass of Committee (an organisational body). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person/registration vs. committee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a conference has members), while B's send relates a Person to an Item (a person sends something). Different domain, range, and direction; they denote different relations.

Both properties link a document-like entity to a person, but the domains differ: ekaw's writtenBy has domain Document (a paper/document), while iasted's is_given_by has domain Activity, Item (an event/activity or item). They overlap in the sense of attributing something to a person, but they are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'written By' relates a Contribution to an Author, i.e. authorship of a paper. Different kinds of things in different directions, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's property links a Conference to an Administrator (who prints hardcopy mailing manifests), while B's property links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Full day tour' is a post-conference social activity (sibling of Departure under Activity after conference), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical venue/place (sibling of Hotel and Main office under Place). Different domains (activity vs. location) and no shared meaning, so they are unrelated.
A's has Last Name is a datatype property holding a person's surname, while B's E mail holds an email address; they relate persons to different kinds of string values and are not the same relation.

Organizer is a person/role class (someone who organizes a conference), while Workshop is an academic event type (a kind of Academic Event). They denote different concepts: a person versus an event, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution (a document type, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract) in the Conference ontology. B's 'Rated Papers' is a state/status of an active paper in the EDAS review workflow (a paper that has received ratings), not a document type. The two denote different concepts: one is a submission category, the other a review-process state, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Hiker is a subclass of Delegate (an attendee role in the iasted ontology, sibling of Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc.), whereas Organizator is a Person subclass whose children are organizational roles (General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, committee members). A hiker/attendee is not an organizer; the two denote different roles in the conference domain.

A's has Decision links a Paper to its Decision (accept/reject outcome), while B's has Topic links a Working event to a Topic (subject area). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it (domain Presentation, range Active conference participant). B's 'is used by' links an Item to the Person who uses it (domain Item, range Person). The domains (Presentation vs Item) and ranges (Active conference participant vs Person) differ, and the intended relations (giving a presentation vs using an item) are distinct, so the properties are not equivalent.

Track in ekaw is a scientific event (a thematic stream of the conference, sibling of Conference, Session, Workshop), whereas 'One conference day' in iasted is a time unit under Conference days. They denote different concepts (event vs. temporal unit), so they are unrelated.

A's Registration is a conference activity (an event/process in the Activity hierarchy, with Delegate as a child), while B's Speaker is a Person subtype (with Author and Invited Speaker as children). They denote different kinds of things — an activity vs. a person role — so they are unrelated.

Contact Information in edas is a class holding address/contact details (city, email, phone, postal code, street), while Person in sigkdd is a person with name, nation, role subclasses, and registration-fee relations. They denote different concepts: one is contact data, the other is an agent. Although edas's has Email has Person in its domain, that does not make Contact Information equivalent to Person.

A's Paper is a general contribution type (siblings Poster, Short paper), while B's Pending Paper is a specific submission state under Paper (siblings Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper). Pending Paper is a narrower concept, so A is subsumed by B's broader Paper, not equivalent.

In cmt, Associated Chair is a kind of Chairman (a person chairing/associated with the conference), sibling to Conference Chair and PC Chair. In ekaw, SC Member is a kind of PC Member (a member of the Steering Committee, a reviewer role), sibling to PC Chair and Session Chair. The roles differ: one is a chairing role, the other a committee-member/reviewer role, so the classes are not equivalent.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference organisation hierarchy (Person > Conference Member > Author) who writes/submits papers. Registration fee (sigkdd) is a fee class under Fee with price/currency and payment relations. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation within the document structure), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity/Item (an agent-to-activity relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

confOf Scholar is a price/registration category of Person (a person attending under a scholar fee), while sigkdd Speaker is a person who gives a presentation (parent of Author and Invited Speaker, with presentation properties). The intended instances do not coincide: a scholar need not present, and a speaker need not be a scholar. Different concepts despite both being subclasses of Person.

A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (location of the conference), while B's is_held_after relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'read By Meta Reviewer' relates a Paper to its Meta Reviewer (domain Paper, range Meta Reviewer), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item). They differ in domain, range, and direction of the relation; 'write' is closer to an authorship relation, not a paper-to-meta-reviewer reading relation.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper they author), while B's `has Review History` relates a Reviewer to their Personal Review History. Different domains (Author vs Reviewer), different ranges (Contribution vs Personal Review History), and different intended relations (authorship vs review record), so they are not equivalent.

A's Topic is the general class of conference topics (it has names, is linked to conference parts, reviews, and submissions). B's Medicine Topic is a specific topic category under the general Topic class in edas. Thus Medicine Topic is a narrower concept, strictly subsumed by A's Topic.

A is a conference topic (a subject area for papers, sibling of Cryptography, Mobile Computing, etc.), while B is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation, sibling of Invited Talk). They denote different concepts: a topic vs. a presentation event, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Conference to the Administrator who finalizes paper assignments; B's property links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domain, range, and intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Mailing list' is a document used to distribute announcements to a group of people, while B 'Abstract' is a summary of a paper. They share only the generic parent Document and have no overlapping instances; the labels and intended meanings differ, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person and is the general actor class (parents: Person; children: Administrator, Author, Reviewer). In iasted, Person is the top-level actor class with children Delegate and Sponsor. The iasted Person is broader (any person, including delegates and sponsors), while cmt User is a more specific actor role within the conference system. Thus cmt User is subsumed by iasted Person, not equivalent.

A 'Withdrawn Paper' is a paper in a withdrawn submission state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper under Paper). B 'Mailing list' is a document artefact (sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Review, Submission) under Document. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A's Review is the general review document class (sibling of Paper, Programme, etc. under Document), while B's Neutral Review is a specific review outcome, a subclass of Review alongside Positive and Negative Review. A's Review is therefore more general and subsumes B's Neutral Review; they are not equivalent.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), expressing that events run in parallel. B's 'covers Topic' relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic, expressing subject coverage. Different domain, different range, different meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's property relates a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference (domain Reviewer, range Review expertise/Review preference), while B's property relates a Paper to a possible reviewer (domain Paper, range Possible Reviewer). They differ in domain, range, and direction of the relationship, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Student is a Participant (a person attending the conference) who is a student. iasted's 'Student non speaker' is a Delegate who is a Non speaker and a student, i.e. a student attendee who does not present. Every iasted Student non speaker is a student participant, so it is a narrower concept; confOf's Student is more general (it does not require non-speaker status). Hence Student subsumes Student non speaker, i.e. A is subsumed_by B's narrower class.

A's Accommodation Place is a generic lodging place (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) under Place. B's Presenter house is a specific building type (a house for presenters) under Building, alongside Conference hotel, Conference restaurant, etc. Although both concern lodging, A is a broad category of accommodation place while B is a specific presenter residence; they do not denote the same concept, and neither subsumes the other in the conference domain.

Both cmt:Paper and confOf:Paper denote the conference submission/contribution artefact; cmt places it under Document with children for abstract/full versions and review siblings, confOf uses it as the paper entity in the same domain, so the intended instances coincide.

cmt's writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (the author writes a paper), while iasted's prepare relates a Person to an Item (a person prepares an item). Both are authoring/creation relations between a person and a document-like entity, so they overlap conceptually, but the ranges differ (Paper vs Item) and 'prepare' is broader than 'write', so they are not equivalent.

Company (a for-profit organization, sibling of University under Organization) and University (an academic institution under Academic Institution) are distinct, non-overlapping organization types; they are not synonyms and neither subsumes the other.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who has paid early), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount for student registration). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `writes` goes Author -> Contribution (author writes a paper), while B's `is Written By` goes Paper -> Author (paper is written by an author). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

A's Review is the evaluation/referee report of a contribution (it is the range of 'has a review' and the domain of 'reviews', pointing to a Reviewed contribution). B's Contribution is the submitted paper itself (superclass of Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by an Author, reviewed by a PC member). A review is not a contribution: they are distinct concepts in the conference domain, so the pair is unrelated.

University is an Organization (a type of institution where scholars study), while Organizing Committee is a Committee (a group of people organizing the conference). They share no intended instances and belong to different branches of the domain.

Both properties link a paper (Accepted Paper / Abstract, Paper) to the way it is presented at the conference (Paper Presentation / Individual Presentation). The domain and range concepts coincide in the conference domain, and the direction is the same (paper -> presentation), so the two properties denote the same relation.

A's 'Submitted contribution' is a document/contribution class (a paper submitted to the conference, with reviews and topics), while B's 'Deadline Author notification' is a deadline/event class (the date by which authors are notified). They denote different concepts: one is a submission artefact, the other a temporal milestone. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's `reviewer Of Paper` relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the reviewing relation), while B's `write` relates a Person to an Item (the authorship relation). They are different relations with different domains and ranges, not inverses or subsumption-related.

A's Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes papers, submits papers, marks conflicts of interest), while B's Workshop is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, part of a Conference volume). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), i.e. the final verdict on a paper. B's Reject Rating is a review rating value (sibling of Accept Rating, Week Reject Rating under Review Rating), i.e. a score given in a review. They belong to different hierarchies and denote different concepts: a decision vs. a rating.

A's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper that is related to (but not authored by) them, while B's write relates a Person to an Item they authored. Different direction of meaning and different relation type; not equivalent.

A's `Member PC` is a Person subclass (a reviewer/PC member, an agent), while B's `Review` is a Document subclass (the review artefact). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Document) and denote different concepts: a person who reviews versus the review document itself. Although A's comment says 'Reviewer' and B's Review is written by a Possible Reviewer, the entities are not the same concept.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship of a paper), while B's 'speak in' links a Person to a Place/Time (giving a talk at a venue/time). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to a Subject Area (topic classification), while B's is_situated_in relates a Building/City/Place to a Building/City/Place/State (spatial containment). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap.

A's 'is sent after' relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering relation), while B's 'submit until' relates a Document to a Deadline (a submission deadline constraint). Although both involve time, they express different relations: one is a temporal ordering, the other a submission deadline. They are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference submission document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Credit card is a payment card (child of Card under Item). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person (a person affiliated with a conference, with subclasses Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), whereas Organizing committee in Conference is a subclass of Committee (a collective body, sibling of Program committee and Steering committee). One denotes an individual person, the other a group/organisational unit, so their instances cannot coincide.

A's hasFirstName relates a Person to their first name (comment mentions middle name), while B's hasLastName relates a Person to their last name. These are distinct name components, not the same relation, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference document type (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a sponsorship level (Bronze Supporter, sibling of Gold/Silver/Platinum Supporter). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A is a research topic class (a subarea of Computer Networks topics) in the edas ontology, while B is an organizational committee class (Program Committee) in the sigkdd ontology. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a general document that can be submitted, reviewed, accepted, etc. (it has children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version and properties for acceptance, assignment, decisions). B's Camera ready contribution is a much more specific stage: an accepted contribution that has been finalized for publication. Thus Paper is broader and subsumes Camera ready contribution, not equivalent.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's 'is visited by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a person visiting a place). Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation nor inverses.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Person) while B is an administrative event (Reviewing results event, a subclass of Administrative event). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's title is the title of a Paper (domain Paper, range string); B's hasCostCurrency is the currency of a Sponsorship cost (domain Sponsorship, range string). Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review a paper), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving something). Different domains (Paper vs Person), different ranges (Reviewer vs Activity/Item), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference contributor' is a Person role (a person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses like author, speaker, participant), while B 'Dinner banquet' is a social-program activity/event, not a person. Different kinds and domains, so they are unrelated.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person who finalizes paper assignments), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship of a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Location in ekaw denotes a place/venue where events are held (domain/range of held In and location Of link Event and Location). Money in iasted denotes a monetary amount with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment. The two concepts share no meaning, instances, or properties; they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference www' is a document/web page about a conference (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with property 'has a URL'), whereas B's 'Conference activity' is a subclass of Activity denoting the event itself (parent of Lecture, Presentation, Registration, etc.). One is an informational artefact, the other a temporal event; they do not denote the same concept.

Both classes denote a human being in the conference domain. ekaw's Person is the general agent class (authors, participants, students, staff) with properties like authorOf, writtenBy, organises; iasted's Person is likewise the general human class (delegates, sponsors) with properties like give, is given by, is paid by. Same label, same intended extension, and both serve as the top-level human/agent class in their respective ontologies.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class of expertise/topic areas used to describe a reviewer's competence (it is the range of 'has an expertise' and is linked to reviewers and submitted contributions). B's 'Member PC' is a person class (a PC member/reviewer, subclass of Person) that has 'expert On' some Topic and 'reviewes' Contributions. One is an expertise/topic concept, the other is a person role; they denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of Contribution (a submission type, sibling of Paper and Poster) in the conference domain. B 'Invitation letter' is a Document (an administrative artefact, sibling of Form, Payment document, Review, Submission, etc.). They denote different concepts: a submission type versus an administrative document. No subsumption or overlap.

iasted's `give` relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives/presents something), while sigkdd's `award` relates something to an Award (awarding a prize). They overlap in the general sense of a person conferring something, but the ranges differ (Activity/Item vs Award) and the intended relations are not the same, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'done till' is a datatype property of Deadline giving the date by which something must be done (a deadline date), while B's 'Start of conference' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's start dateTime. They have different domains (Deadline vs Conference) and different intended meanings (deadline completion date vs event start time), so they are not equivalent.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses like Invited speaker, Regular author), whereas edas Conference is an event class with children Single Level Conference / Two Level Conference and properties such as end Date, has Country, has Member, paper Due On. One denotes a person role, the other a conference event; they are not the same concept.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (a call soliciting submissions), while B's 'Main office' is a physical place (an office location) under Place. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

confOf's Trip is a specific social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception under Social event), while ekaw's Social Event is the general category whose children include Conference Trip and Conference Banquet. Trip is therefore strictly more specific than Social Event, so Trip is subsumed by Social Event, not equivalent.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while B's Bronze Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsorship level). They denote entirely different concepts: a person role versus a funding/sponsorship category, with no overlap in instances.

A's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A 'CAD Topic' is a subject area (a topic in computer-aided design) under the Topic hierarchy of the edas ontology, whereas B 'Card' is a physical item (with child Credit card) under Item in the iasted ontology. They share no meaning, instances, or context; the superficial word overlap is absent and the domains differ entirely.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (author -> paper), while B's `is given by` relates an Activity/Item to a Person (item -> person), i.e. the inverse direction and different kinds of things; they are not the same relation.

A's prepare relates a Person to an Item (a person prepares an item, e.g. a paper), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference (the organisation holds a conference). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, a human who chairs the conference), while B 'Conference activity' is an event/activity in the conference schedule (parent of Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break, etc.). They denote fundamentally different kinds of things (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to a Review (the review artefact), while B's 'has Reviewer' links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a person). Different range kinds (Review vs. person) and different direction of meaning, so they are not equivalent; the closest relation would be inverse-like (a review has a reviewer), which is not equivalence.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but 'has Last Name' relates a person to their surname while 'Nation' relates a person to their country/nationality. Different intended relations, so not equivalent.

A's name is a datatype property giving the name of a Conference or Person, while B's location gives the venue of a Social/Working event. Different domains, different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a kind of Chairman/Person) while B is a social event (Conference Banquet, a kind of Social Event/Event). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain and denote entirely different concepts.

A relates a Conference to an Administrator (who prints hardcopy mailing manifests), while B relates an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract (the paper being presented). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's has Keyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a keyword string, while B's Nation links a Person to a country string. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property linking a Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while B's 'volume Contains Paper' is an object property relating a volume to the papers it contains. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), in domain/range, and in meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, a committee person), while B's 'Conference contribution' is a document type (a subclass of Conference document, with children like Poster, Presentation, Written contribution). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. document), so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' relates an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer), i.e. a reviewer-assignment relation. B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item they authored (domain Person, range Item), i.e. an authorship relation. Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent, not subsuming.

A 'Short paper' is a type of contribution (a submission category, sibling of Paper and Poster) in confOf, whereas B 'Final manuscript' is a stage/version of a submission (sibling of Initial manuscript) in iasted. They denote different concepts: one is a document category, the other a submission lifecycle stage, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'relates To' is a very general Document-to-anything (event/session/person) relation, while B's 'scientifically Organised By' is a specific sub-property of 'organised By' linking an event to an Academic Institution. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'is designed for' is an object property linking Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person (a design/purpose relation), while B's 'Name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Participant is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference, with subclasses Member/Regular/Student and property early Registration), while B's Nonmember registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, i.e. a monetary amount, not a person. Different kinds of entities (person vs. fee), so they are unrelated.

Assistant in confOf is a Person subtype (a helper/assistant role, sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.), while Author in iasted is a Speaker subtype (a delegate who presents/author of proceedings). They denote different roles in the conference domain; an assistant is not an author and vice versa.

Both classes are named Person and represent the same general concept of a human in the conference domain. In confOf, Person is the superclass of roles like Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, etc., with properties for name, email, phone, address. In edas, Person is likewise the superclass of Attendee, Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member, with properties for name, email, biography, and conference membership. The intended instances coincide: any person involved in a conference. The differing property sets reflect different modelling detail, not different concepts.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (author -> paper), while B's 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (item -> person), the reverse direction and different kinds of entities; they are not the same relation.

A's paperPresentedAs links a Paper to its Individual Presentation (domain Paper, range Individual Presentation), while B's write links a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

Travel Grant is a sponsorship/funding category (a form of financial support under Sponsorship), while Invited Speaker is a role of a person (a Presenter who is invited). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, with no overlap in instances or meaning.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving a string name for a Conference or Person, while B's `registration Due On` is a datatype property giving a dateTime registration deadline for a Conference. They relate different kinds of values (string vs dateTime) and capture different concepts (naming vs deadline), so they are not equivalent.

assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to a paper), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (a document being presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's hasPhone is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string phone number, while B's heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

has Author goes from Paper to Author, while writes goes from Author to Contribution. They are inverse relations (Paper has Author / Author writes Contribution), not equivalent since direction differs.

A's 'scientificallyOrganisedBy' relates an event/paper to an Academic Institution (a subproperty of organisedBy, range Academic Institution), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domain, range and direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's User is a Person role (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer) in the conference domain, while B's Proceedings is a Document/Multi author Volume (a published collection of papers). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

Accepted contribution is a subclass of Reviewed contribution, representing a paper that has been accepted after review. Paper in edas is a broader class encompassing all papers regardless of status (Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, Pending Paper, etc. are its subclasses). Thus Accepted contribution is a specific type of Paper, making it subsumed by Paper.

A's Country is a geographic class used as the range of Conference -> Country (the country where a conference is held). B's Conference is the conference event itself, with properties for city, name, start/end dates and being held by ACM SIGKDD. Country and Conference denote different concepts; the only connection is that a conference has a country, which is a domain/range relation, not equivalence.

A 'CAD Topic' is a subject area (a child of Topic, sibling of Computer Architecture Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.) used to classify papers, whereas B 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a specific award type (child of Award, sibling of Best Research Paper Award). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic taxonomy vs. award taxonomy) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has Surname' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a name component), while B's 'author Of' is an object property mapping a Person to a Document (authorship relation). They relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name, while B's 'has Street' is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a street address. They have different domains (Person vs Contact Information) and different intended meanings (first name vs street), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Security Topic' is a research subject area under Topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

ekaw:Person is a human agent (author, participant, reviewer) with properties like authorOf and writtenBy. iasted:State is a geographical/administrative region (parent of Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state) that is situated in places and occupied by persons. The two denote entirely different concepts; the only overlap is that State is occupied by a Person, which is a relation, not equivalence.

A's hasPhone relates a Person to a phone number string, while B's hasEmail relates a Person/Contact Information to an email address string. They are different contact attributes (phone vs email), so they are not equivalent.

accept Paper has domain Administrator and range Paper (an administrator accepting a paper), while submit has domain Author and range Paper (an author submitting a paper). They relate different kinds of agents to papers and are not the same relation; they are not inverses either.

In ekaw, 'Assigned Paper' is a Submitted Paper that has been assigned to a reviewer (a stage in the paper's lifecycle, with child Evaluated Paper). In sigkdd, 'Abstract' is a Document subtype that is a short summary document, sibling to Paper and Review. They denote different concepts: a lifecycle stage of a paper vs. a document type. No subsumption or overlap of intended instances.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property linking a Conference document to a date, while B's 'has title' links a Social/Working event to a string. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Administrative event is a subclass of Event in confOf, covering submission, reviewing, registration, camera-ready, etc. Organizing Committee is a subclass of Committee in sigkdd, denoting a group of people. They belong to different branches (Event vs Committee) and have no shared instances or properties, so they are unrelated.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property of a Conference giving a URI for the conference logo; B's 'has a location' is a datatype property of a Conference volume giving a string location. Different domains (Conference vs Conference volume) and different intended values (anyURI logo vs string location), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property of Review expertise (the expertise a reviewer has), while B's 'Name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's name. Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's email is a datatype property holding a person's email address, while B's has Home Page holds a URL of a person's homepage. Different kinds of values and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a kind of conference contributor (a person invited to speak), a sibling of Regular author and Active conference participant. B's 'Author cd proceedings included' is a subclass of Author, i.e. an author whose paper is included in the CD proceedings — a publication-status role, not an invited-speaker role. The paths, parents and siblings differ (B sits under Author alongside book-proceedings authors, lecturers, tutorial/plenary speakers), so the intended instances do not coincide.

A 'Session chair' is a Delegate who chairs a session, while B 'General Chair' is an Organizator who chairs the whole conference. Both are chairing roles in the conference domain, so they overlap, but they are not the same concept: a session chair is a participant/delegate role, a general chair is an organizing role, and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Paper Full Version' is the complete version of a paper (sibling of Paper Abstract), whereas a 'Workshop Paper' is a paper submitted to or published at a workshop (sibling of Conference Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). They classify papers along different dimensions (completeness vs. venue/type), so their instances do not coincide.

Both properties connect a person/speaker to what they present, but the domains and ranges differ: 'speak in' links a Person to a Place/Time (speaking at an event), while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the presented paper). They overlap in the act of presenting but are not the same relation.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a document type (Conference Proceedings, a kind of Proceedings). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. documents) and share no intended instances.

A is a research topic in computer networks (a subject area under Topic), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical computer under Audiovisual equipment). They share only the word 'computer' and denote entirely different concepts.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event whose instances are the outcomes/results of reviewing made accessible to authors, while B 'Workshop' is a scientific event (a meeting held alongside a conference). They belong to different branches (Administrative event vs Scientific Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's External Reviewer is a Person (a reviewer role) with properties linking it to Reviewer, while B's Review is a Document (the review text/artefact) under Document alongside Abstract and Paper. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs document) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Person/Chairman, sibling of Author and Reviewer), while B's 'Program Committee' is a committee entity (a subclass of Committee, sibling of Organizing Committee). One denotes an individual person, the other a group/organisational body, so they cannot be equivalent.

A's property links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (expertise -> contribution), while B's property links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (history -> reviewer). The domains and ranges denote different concepts and the direction of the relation differs, so they are not the same relation.

In iasted, Lecturer is a leaf-ish subclass of Author (a kind of speaker who gives lectures), while in sigkdd Speaker is the broader class whose children include Author and Invited Speaker. A Lecturer is a specific kind of Speaker, so Lecturer is subsumed by Speaker, not equivalent.

ekaw's Social Event is a subclass of Event covering banquets and trips, while iasted's Conference activity is a broader class under Activity that includes social program items but also lectures, presentations, registration, coffee breaks, etc. Social Event is thus narrower than Conference activity, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's Author is a conference-domain person role (a Person who writes papers, with properties has Related Paper / is Written By), while B's Value added tax is a financial tax concept under Money > Tax. The entities share no meaning, no properties, and no context; they are unrelated.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subclass covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors; Speaker in iasted is a Delegate subclass whose children are Author and Reviewer. Both cover people who contribute to a conference (authors/speakers), so they overlap, but neither is strictly more general: contributor includes non-speaking roles and Speaker includes listeners/other delegates. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's Paper is the general document class (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, sibling of Review), while B's Rejected Paper is a specific subclass of Paper in edas (sibling of Accepted Paper, Active Paper, etc.). The general Paper subsumes the more specific Rejected Paper, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Submission event' is an administrative event (a happening in the conference process, sibling of Reviewing event, Camera Ready event), whereas B's 'Submission' is a Document (an item, parent of Initial/Final manuscript). One denotes an event, the other a document artefact, so their instances cannot coincide.

In cmt, Rejection is a subclass of Decision, i.e. the decision outcome/act of rejecting a paper. In edas, Rejected Paper is a subclass of Paper, i.e. a document/paper in the rejected state. They are closely related (a rejection decision results in a rejected paper) but denote different kinds of entities: a decision vs. a paper. Thus they are not equivalent; the best relation is 'related'.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track (a structural part-of relation, subproperty of has parts), while B's 'speak in' relates a Person to a Place/Time (a person speaking at an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, with has workshops from Conference volume), whereas B's Session room is a physical place (sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room). They denote different concepts: an event versus a location, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'for Event' links a Call to the Academic Event it is issued for (domain Call, range Academic Event). B's 'searched by' links a Sponzor (sponsor) to the ACM SIGKDD organisation that searches it (domain Sponzor, range ACM SIGKDD). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property giving a person's first name (comment mentions middle name), while B's E-mail gives a person's email address. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document submitted to a conference (parent Document, sibling Review, properties for authorship, review assignment, bidding, decisions). B's Award is a prize given to authors (children are Best Paper awards, properties award/awarded by/obtain). A paper is not an award; the concepts are disjoint in the conference domain.

A's isMenuOf relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (a menu is associated with a meal event), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives/provides something). Different domain (Meal Menu vs Person), different range (Meal Event vs Activity/Item), and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

cmt:Conference is the main conference event entity (has members, submissions, deadlines, logo), while ekaw:Conference_Trip is a social event (a trip) under Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet. Different concepts.

A's 'Mailing list' is a Document subtype for distributing messages to a group, while B's 'Paper' is the submitted scholarly contribution (domain of submit from Author). They share only the Document parent; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's start Date is a temporal property (range dateTime, comment 'Conference Start Date and Time'), while B's Name of conference is a string-valued naming property. They relate different kinds of values and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a paper submitted to a conference (a Document/Paper in the scientific sense), while B 'Cheque' is a payment document (a financial instrument). They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different subdomains, so they are unrelated.

A's 'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract (its summary text). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference-document class about information for participants (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic in a topic taxonomy (Computer Networks Enterprise Topic under Computer Networks Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's Tutorial is a small conference part (sibling of Track and Workshop, part of a Conference volume), while B's Conference is a large working event that has Tutorial and Workshop as siblings/children. They denote different concepts: a tutorial session versus the whole conference event.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference event, sibling of Paper Presentation and Talk Event), whereas B's Tutorial Abstract is a document/abstract (a subclass of Abstract, sibling of Invited Talk Abstract). One denotes an event, the other a written abstract, so their instances cannot coincide.

A's Meal Break is a subclass of Break Event (a non-academic conference event such as a coffee or free-time break), while B's Conference hall is a subclass of Place (a physical venue location alongside Hotel and Main office). A break event and a venue location are different kinds of things, so the classes are unrelated.

has Member relates a Conference to a Person (its members/committee members), while organised By relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organiser). Both link an event-like entity to people, but the domain concepts (Conference vs Event) and the intended relation (membership vs organising) differ, so they are not equivalent; they only overlap in linking events to persons.

A is a class of published volumes of conference papers (a Document/Multi author Volume), while B is a person role (an Author who is a Speaker/Delegate). They denote entirely different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic in computer architecture (a subject area under Topic), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (an overhead projector) under Item > Audiovisual equipment. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Rejection is a subclass of Decision, i.e. the outcome/decision that a paper is rejected. B's Receiving manuscript is an activity in the 'Activity before conference' branch, i.e. the act of a conference receiving a submitted manuscript. One is a decision outcome, the other a submission/receiving activity; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent (nor in a subsumption relation).

A's 'Reject Rating' is a specific review-rating value (a subclass of Review Rating, sibling of Accept Rating), i.e. a verdict/score category. B's 'Review' is a document type (subclass of Document, sibling of Paper and Abstract), i.e. the review document itself. A rating value and a review document are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the person who delivers it), while B's 'is prepared by' links an Item to a Person (the person who authored/prepared it). Both relate a document-like entity to a person, but the intended relations differ: giving a presentation (delivering it) versus preparing an item (authoring it). They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same relation, so 'related' rather than 'equivalent'.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper), while B's `presentationed by` relates a Document to a Speaker (the document is presented by a speaker). The domains and ranges differ (Author->Contribution vs Document->Speaker), and the directions/roles are different: writing a paper is not the same relation as a paper being presented by a speaker. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'follows' links one Administrative event to another (temporal ordering). Different domain, range and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a single person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt person hierarchy, while B's 'Organizing Committee' is a collective committee entity under Committee, sibling to Program Committee. A person role and a committee group are different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'contributes' goes Person -> Conference document (author contributes a paper), while B's 'is writen by' goes Item -> Person (paper written by author). They describe the same authorship relation but in opposite directions, so they are inverses, not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document/contribution in the conference domain (parent Document, children Accepted/Rejected/Pending Paper, properties is Written By Author, is Reviewed By Reviewer, has Topic). B's Fee is a monetary charge (parent Money, children Registration fee, Hotel fee, Fee for extra trip). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Published Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been published), while B's 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a subclass of Deadline (a submission deadline event). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Program committee' is a committee of people that reviews papers for a conference (a subclass of Committee, with properties linking it to a Conference volume). B's 'University' is an organization where scholars study (a subclass of Organization, sibling of Company, domain of 'study At'). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, sharing no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string email address, while B's hasEvent is an object property linking an Event to another Event (e.g. sub-events). They differ in domain (Person vs Event), range (string vs Event), and kind (datatype vs object), so they denote different relations.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (sibling of Extended abstract) in the Conference ontology, i.e. a full paper submission. B's Poster Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a poster-format paper) under Document > Paper, sibling to Regular Paper, Conference Paper, etc. A's Paper corresponds to B's Regular Paper, not to Poster Paper; the two denote different artefact types, so they are unrelated.

A's 'accepted By' links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it (domain Paper, range Administrator), while B's 'parallel with' links two Administrative events that run in parallel (domain and range Administrative event). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is an event type (Contributed Talk, a kind of Individual Presentation). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

A is a research topic (Powerline Transmission Topic) under Topic in edas, while B is a conference activity type (Power Point presentation) under Presentation in iasted. They denote entirely different concepts: a subject area versus a presentation format, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Important dates' is a class of deadline/date entities (submission, acceptance, camera-ready, start/end dates) belonging to a conference volume. B's 'Contribution' is a submitted work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) with title, abstract, authors, keywords, topics. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's has Street is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a street address string, while B's has City links Contact Information to a city string. They denote different address components (street vs city) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a review expertise' links a submitted contribution to a review expertise (a topic/skill area the reviewer must have), while B's 'has Reviewer' links a paper to a possible reviewer (a person). The ranges differ (Review expertise vs Possible Reviewer) and the intended meaning differs: one assigns a required expertise to a submission, the other assigns candidate reviewers to a paper. They are related in the review-assignment context but not the same relation.
Author (cmt) is a conference member who writes/submits papers; Place (sigkdd) is a location where a person can stay (conference hall, hotel, office). Different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a class of conference contributions (papers) that were rejected after review, a subclass of Reviewed contribution. B 'Accept Rating' is a class of review ratings (a value/score category used in reviewing, sibling of Reject Rating, Accept If Room Rating, etc.). One denotes a kind of paper, the other a kind of rating value; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

Person in cmt is a general class whose children include Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member and User, so it covers all conference participants. Member PC in confOf is a specific subclass of Person (a reviewer who has expert On topics and reviewes contributions). Member PC is therefore strictly narrower than Person; Person subsumes Member PC, they are not equivalent.

Committee member (Conference) is a Person who belongs to a Committee, with subclasses Chair and Co chair, and is linked to Committee via has members / was a member of. Author (confOf) is a Person who writes Contributions, linked to Contribution via writes / written By. The two concepts overlap (a committee member may also be an author) but neither subsumes the other: committee membership is about organisational role, authorship about producing papers. They are related but not equivalent.

A's 'is held after' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events), while B's 'notification until' relates an Author to a notification deadline (a deadline by which an author is notified). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A is a kind of document (an abstract for an invited talk), while B is a registration fee category for an author attendee paying by CD. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Money/Fee) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a kind of conference contributor (a person role for giving an invited talk), while B's 'Technical commitee' is a subclass of Delegate under Conference building, denoting a committee/group role rather than an individual invited speaker. Different intended instances and different domain roles, so they are unrelated.

Chairman is a role/person (a Person subclass, with children like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), whereas Committee is a group/organisational body with children like Organizing Committee and Program Committee. A person who chairs is not the same concept as a committee, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Call for participation' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.) that announces/solicits participation. B's 'Submission event' is an administrative event (subclass of Administrative event, sibling of Camera Ready event, Reviewing event, etc.) representing the act/process of submitting contributions. One is a document, the other an event; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Attendee is a generic Person role (sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.) covering anyone attending the conference. In sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is a specific Organizator role (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster) denoting someone on the organizing committee. The intended instances do not coincide: an attendee need not be an organizer, and an organizing committee member is a narrower, distinct role. Hence unrelated.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (path Person > Conference Member > Author > Co author) and is specifically an author who co-writes a paper, whereas B's 'Author' is the general class of authors (Person > Speaker > Author) with children Author of paper and Author of paper student. The co-author concept is narrower than the general author concept, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

In iasted, Lecturer is a subclass of Author (path Author > Lecturer), i.e. a lecturer is a kind of author. In sigkdd, Author is the broader class (Person > Speaker > Author) with children Author of paper etc. Thus Lecturer is strictly more specific than Author, so Lecturer is subsumed by Author rather than equivalent.

A's Committee is a group of people (chairs, members) that organises a conference; B's Organisation is an institutional body (academic institution, agency, publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings. The intended instances do not coincide: a committee is not an organisation, and the property contexts (committee chair/member vs. publisher of/technically organises) differ.

A's Reception is a social event (a gathering held during the conference, sibling of Banquet and Trip), while B's Cheque is a payment document (a financial instrument, sibling of Bank transfer). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor, i.e. a contribution role played by a person who is a regular (non-invited) author. B's 'Author' is a subclass of Person, i.e. the person who writes contributions. The two denote different kinds of things (a contribution vs. a person), so they are not equivalent; the author-person concept is more general than the specific regular-author contribution role, hence A is subsumed by B.

A 'Numerical Review Question' is a specific type of review question (a question on a review form whose answer is numeric), sibling to 'Textual Review Question' under 'Review Question'. B 'Review' is a document artefact (a review document, sibling to Submission, Form, Invitation letter, etc.) under Document. The two denote different concepts: a question item versus a review document. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'is Review History Of' relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer, i.e. the reviewer that a review-history record belongs to. Different domains and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author (authorship relation), while B's hasUpdatedVersion relates a Document to another Document (versioning relation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, and both denote a person's email address; the differing labels (email vs has Email) are just naming conventions.

A's 'has a review' relates a Reviewed contribution to a Review (the review artefact), while B's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to the person/role who performs the review (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). They concern the same reviewing activity but link different kinds of entities (review document vs. reviewer role) and are not inverses of each other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a submission type, sibling of Paper, child of Regular contribution). B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline event (a date by which papers must be submitted), sibling of other deadlines. One is a document type, the other a temporal milestone; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's Conference Venue Place is a generic place where a conference is held (sibling of Accommodation/Dining/Meeting Room places), while B's Main office is the organisation's office location (sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They denote different kinds of places and neither subsumes the other.

A is a research topic (a subject area of papers, under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a conference event type (a session in the conference schedule, under Session). They belong to entirely different branches (Topic vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of individual presentation (an event/session type) in ekaw, whereas B 'Speaker' is a person role in sigkdd. They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Associated Chair is a kind of Chairman/Conference Member (a chairing role in the conference organisation), while in ekaw Session Chair is a Conference Participant who chairs a session (and is also an PC Member). Both are chairing roles for persons, but they denote different specific roles: an associated chair is a general conference chair role, whereas a session chair moderates a session. They overlap in that both are persons chairing something, but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'has Call' links an Academic Event to its Call for Papers. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

A (confOf 'Member PC') is a person role — a program-committee member/reviewer, a subclass of Person with properties expert On and reviewes. B (edas 'Accpet If Room Rating') is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a rating value/decision category, not a person. Different kinds of entities with no overlap.

Both are object properties linking a paper/contribution to its subject/topic: cmt's hasSubjectArea has domain Paper and range Subject Area, confOf's dealsWith has domain Contribution and range Topic. Paper and Contribution are equivalent classes in the conference domain, and Subject Area and Topic are equivalent, so the properties relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are equivalent.

A's hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (whole-to-part containment), while B's organises links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise (agent-to-event). Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (its location), while B's is_present_in relates a Person to a Place/Time (attendance). Different domains (Conference vs Person) and ranges (Country vs Place/Time), so they are not the same relation.

A's Presentation is a conference contribution that is given by an active participant and has an abstract; B's Short paper is a written contribution (sibling of Paper and Poster) in confOf. A Presentation is an event/talk, whereas a Short paper is a written document, so they are not equivalent. They overlap only in that both are kinds of conference contributions, hence related.

A's 'is used for' relates an Item to an Activity or Money (a general usage relation), while B's 'obtain' relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a role/class for a co-author of a contribution (a regular author who is not the first author), sitting under Regular author in the document/contribution branch. B's 'Invited Speaker' is a person who gives an invited talk, under Speaker in the person branch, sibling of Author. They denote different concepts (co-author role vs. invited speaker role) with no subsumption or overlap.

Regular Paper (ekaw) is a specific kind of Paper (a full research paper submitted to a conference), while Abstract (sigkdd) is a short summary document, a sibling of Paper and Review under Document. They denote different document types with different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a kind of document/contribution with an abstract), while B's Assigned Paper is a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer (it has Evaluated Paper as a child, i.e. it is in the review workflow). The intended instances do not coincide: A covers all regular papers regardless of review assignment, B only papers assigned for evaluation. Different concepts, so unrelated.

A Committee member is a person who belongs to a committee (has members / was a member of Committee), with subclasses Chair and Co chair. B Speaker is a person who gives a presentation (presentation -> Document), with subclasses Author and Invited Speaker. The intended instances do not coincide: committee membership and speaking/presenting are different roles, and the property contexts (Committee vs Document) confirm this. They share only the parent Person, so they are unrelated.

confOf Person is a human agent (author, participant, chair) with personal attributes like email, phone, first name. iasted State is a geographic/administrative region (a place) that is occupied by or visited by persons, with children Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state. The two denote entirely different concepts: a person vs. a location/state. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

A Travel Grant is a form of sponsorship/funding (a financial support category under Sponsorship), whereas a Conference Trip is a social event (a kind of trip/activity under Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet). They denote different concepts: funding vs. social activity, so they are not equivalent.

Conference volume is a class representing the whole conference event/publication (it has committees, tracks, contributions, important dates), whereas Conference Chair is a person role (a subclass of Person) who initiates calls and reviews papers. They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A's hasCall relates an Academic Event to its Call (call for papers), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD (the organisation/series) to a Conference it holds. Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; not the same relation.

A's 'was a committe co chair of' relates a Co chair to a Committee (a role-holding relation within the conference organisation), while B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Conference (an organisation holding an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is an ending date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates entity to a date (end of a deadline/event period), while B's 'has First Name' links a Person to a string (given name). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Conference is the main event entity (has members, accepts submissions, has dates, administrators). B's Call is a call-for-papers/reviews/manuscripts entity, a child-bearing class with submission deadlines and instructions, initiated by chairs. A Call is not a Conference; it is a document/announcement associated with an event, so the two classes denote different concepts.

Conference applicant is a subclass of Person (a person applying to attend a conference), while Accommodation Place is a subclass of Place (a physical location for lodging). They belong to disjoint top-level categories (Person vs Place) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Topic is the general class of research topics (it is the range of has a track workshop tutorial topic, has a topic or a submission contribution, etc., and has instances like any subject area). B's Security Topic is a specific topic, a child of edas Topic. Thus Security Topic is strictly narrower than Conference Topic, so Conference Topic subsumes Security Topic (A is subsumed_by B's parent, not equivalent to the specific child).

A is a research topic (Computer Architecture Topic) under Topic, while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee) under Committee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History (a collection/aggregate of a reviewer's reviews) to a Reviewer, i.e. it is the inverse of a reviewer-to-history relation. B's 'review Written By' links an individual Review to a Possible Reviewer, i.e. the authorship relation of a single review.
