The domains (Personal Review History vs Review) and ranges (Reviewer vs Possible Reviewer) differ, and the direction/level of granularity differ, so they are not the same relation.

A's Workshop is a type of academic event (a scientific meeting held alongside a conference), while B's Organizing Committee is a committee (a group of people who organise the conference). They belong to different branches of the domain (event vs. committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Non speaker' is a Delegate who does not give a talk (siblings include Speaker, Listener, Session chair), while B 'Invited Speaker' is a Speaker who is invited. They are near-opposites in the speaker/non-speaker distinction and sit in different branches (Delegate vs Speaker), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Book proceeding' is a publication artefact (a book-form proceedings volume) under Item > Publication, while B 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a submission deadline event under Deadline. They denote different concepts (a document vs. a temporal deadline), so they are unrelated.

hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country; occupy relates a Person to a Building, City or State. Both are location/affiliation relations involving a Person, so they overlap, but the domains differ (hasCountry also applies to Organization) and the ranges differ (Country vs Building/City/State). They are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Poster Session' is a kind of scientific Session (an event where posters are presented), while B 'Organizing Committee' is a kind of Committee (an organizational group). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (event vs. committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a sub-topic of Computer Networks Topic in the EDAS topic hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document type vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

A's 'manuscript Due On' is a datatype property from Conference to dateTime representing the manuscript submission deadline. B's 'notification until' is an object property from Author to a Deadline Author notification class, representing the notification deadline for an author. They differ in domain (Conference vs Author), range (dateTime vs a deadline class), and intended meaning (manuscript submission vs notification deadline), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'speak in' is an object property mapping a Person to a Place/Time (where/when the person speaks). They share only the Person domain; their ranges and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

A's Government Organization is a subtype of Organization denoting a governmental body (siblings: Academia Organization, Industry Organization, NGO). B's Organising Agency is a subtype of Organisation denoting the agency that organises the conference (siblings: Academic Institution, Proceedings Publisher). Different intended instances: a government body is not an organising agency, and the organising agency need not be governmental. No subsumption either, since neither class's instances are a subset of the other's.

A's contactEmail is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string (an email address), while B's listsEvent is an object property linking a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event. They differ in domain, range, and kind (datatype vs object), so they denote different relations.

A's email is a Person's email address, while B's hasSurname is a Person's surname; both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

Both denote the person who chairs the conference: A's Chair is a Committee member who chairs a committee (has a committee chair / was a committee chair of), and B's Conference Chair is a Person who initiates the conference's calls and reviews. The intended instances coincide (the conference chair role), so they are equivalent despite differing parent structure.

A's 'Conference Proceedings' is a document type (a multi-author volume of proceedings), while B's 'Author book proceedings included' is a subclass of Author describing an author whose book appears in proceedings. They denote different kinds of things (a publication vs. a person role), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper they author), whereas ekaw's referencedIn relates a paper/contribution to another work it cites. Different domain/range and different direction of meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference submission (has authors, reviews, decisions, subject areas), while B's Payment document is a financial document (bank transfer, cheque) under Item > Document. They share only the generic Document parent and the word 'document', denoting different concepts.

ekaw Student is a general Person subtype (siblings include Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Conference Participant), while sigkdd Author of paper student is a specific Author subtype (a student who authors a paper). Every Author of paper student is a Student, but not every Student is an author of a paper, so ekaw Student is more general and is subsumed by the sigkdd concept.

A's 'Final manuscript' is a stage/version of a submission (sibling of 'Initial manuscript', child of Submission), while B's 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a type of award (child of Award, sibling of other best-paper awards). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

cmt:Person is a general class of people involved in the conference (its children include Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User), whereas ekaw:Student is a specific subclass of ekaw:Person (siblings include Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Conference Participant). Student is a kind of Person, so cmt:Person is strictly more general than ekaw:Student; they are not equivalent.

Both properties relate a written work to its author: confOf's 'written By' has domain Contribution and range Author, while iasted's 'is writen by' has domain Item and range Person. Contribution/Item both denote conference submissions/papers and Author/Person both denote the people who write them, so the two properties express the same relation in the same direction.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' links a Conference to the Administrator who started reviewer bidding, while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domains (Conference vs Document), different ranges (Administrator vs Speaker), and different intended relations (bidding initiation vs presentation authorship), so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper) in the cmt ontology, while B is a research topic category (Operating Topicsystems) under Topic in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has Keyword' is a datatype property of Contribution giving a keyword string. Different domains (Person vs Contribution) and different intended meanings (surname vs keyword), so they are unrelated.

A's Tutorial Abstract is a subclass of Abstract (a kind of document text, sibling of Invited Talk Abstract), while B's Review is a distinct document type (sibling of Abstract and Paper) representing a reviewer's evaluation. They denote different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Author is a conference member who writes/submits papers; B's Reviewer is a speaker who reviews papers. They are distinct roles (indeed B lists Author as a sibling of Reviewer), so the classes are not equivalent.

A's writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review, while B's write relates a Person to an Item. Reviewer is a kind of Person and Review is a kind of Item, so writeReview is a more specific version of write; it is subsumed by the broader write property rather than equivalent.

A's hasPhone is a datatype property of Contact Information holding a phone number string; B's E-mail is a datatype property of Person holding an email address string. They relate different kinds of things (phone vs email) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A Trip is a social event (excursion) in confOf, while iasted's 'Activity after conference' is a broader category of post-conference activities that includes Departure and Full day tour. A Trip is one kind of post-conference activity, so Trip is more specific and is subsumed by Activity after conference, not equivalent.

A's `name` is a datatype property of Conference/Person with range string, while B's `has Cost Amount` is a datatype property of Sponsorship with range int. They relate different kinds of things (names vs. monetary amounts) in different domains, so they are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Invited Speaker is a subclass of Presenter (a Person who presents), while in sigkdd Speaker is a broader class whose children include both Author and Invited Speaker. The sigkdd Speaker is thus more general than ekaw's Invited Speaker, so the ekaw class is subsumed by the sigkdd class, not equivalent.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a kind of submitted document with an abstract), while B's Pending Paper is a specific state of a paper in the EDAS workflow (a Paper that has not yet been accepted/rejected). Every Pending Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is pending, so A is more general than B; the two are not equivalent.

A's property links a Review preference to the Topic/Submitted contribution it prefers, while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity/Item they give. Different domains (Review preference vs Person), different ranges (Topic/Submitted contribution vs Activity/Item), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume, i.e. the committee is the organizer of the event/volume. B's 'technically Organises' is a subproperty of 'organises' linking an Organisation to whatever it organises (an event/conference), and 'technically' implies a specific, weaker form of organisation (technical co-sponsorship) rather than full organising-committee responsibility. The two relations overlap in that both express an organising relation between an organising body and a conference, but they are not the same relation: A is specific to organizing committees and conference volumes, B is a general organisation-to-event relation with a 'technical' qualifier. Hence related, not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person who gives an invited talk at a conference. In Conference, Invited speaker is a kind of Conference contributor (a Person role); in sigkdd, Invited Speaker is a kind of Speaker (a Person role). The labels are identical and the intended instances coincide: invited speakers at a conference. The differing parent paths (Conference contributor vs Speaker) reflect different role hierarchies, not different concepts, and no other entity in either ontology captures this role.
A's 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while B's 'is paid for' relates Money to an Activity or Item (payment). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

A Trip is a social event (an excursion/outing) in the conference programme, sibling of Banquet and Reception. A Travel Grant is a form of sponsorship (financial support for travel), a subclass of Sponsorship. They denote different concepts: one is an activity, the other a funding mechanism, with no overlap in instances.

Both denote the event of presenting an accepted paper at a conference: edas Paper Presentation is an Academic Event linked to Accepted Paper via related To Paper/related To Event, and ekaw Individual Presentation is a Scientific Event with presentation Of Paper / paper Presented As linking it to Paper/Abstract. The paths (Conference Event > Academic Event vs Event > Scientific Event) and the paper-presentation properties agree, so the intended instances coincide.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document type (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., under Conference document), while B's 'Conference' is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, under Working event). They denote different kinds of things: a document vs. an event, so they are not equivalent.

A's Car is a transport vehicle (a physical means of transport), while B's Organizator is a person role in the conference organization hierarchy. They share no meaning, instances, or context; the pair is unrelated.

A's Industry Organization is a subtype of Organization classified by sector (siblings: Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO), i.e. a for-profit company in industry. B's Organising Agency is a subtype of Organisation denoting the body that organises a conference (siblings: Academic Institution, Proceedings Publisher), i.e. a role an organisation plays in the conference. The intended instances do not coincide: an industry organisation is not necessarily an organising agency, and an organising agency can be an academic institution. Different classification axes, so unrelated.

A's Review is a conference document (a submitted review artefact, with properties linking it to a reviewed contribution), whereas B's Numerical Review Question is a type of review form question (a question item used in a review form, sibling of Textual Review Question). They denote different concepts: a review document vs. a question type, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Member PC' is a person role (a program committee member/reviewer, subclass of Person, with properties expert On Topic and reviewes Contribution). B's 'Textual Review Question' is a kind of review question (subclass of Review Question, sibling of Numerical Review Question), i.e. a form item, not a person. Different intended instances, so the classes are unrelated.

Sponsor (a person/organisation funding the conference, sibling of Delegate under Person in iasted) and Program Chair (an Organizator role in sigkdd, sibling of General Chair and committee members) denote different roles in the conference domain; neither subsumes the other.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship relation), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presenting a document). Different domains (Conference document vs Speaker), different ranges (Person vs Document), and different intended relations (authorship vs presentation), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a scheduled session within a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session). B 'Research' is an activity performed before a conference (sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript), with children Modelling and Simulating. They denote different concepts (event vs. activity) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a specific social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip), while B's Social program is a broader conference activity that contains Dinner banquet and Coctail reception as children. A reception is one kind of social program, so Reception is subsumed by Social program, not equivalent.

Volunteer (a Person who helps at the conference) and Sponsor (a Person/organisation providing funding) are distinct roles in the conference domain; they share only the parent Person and have no overlapping intended instances.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of event/session) in confOf, while Invited Speaker is a role of a person (a presenter) in ekaw. They belong to different branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A relates a Conference to a Conference Member (object property), while B relates a Conference to a string city name (datatype property). Different kinds of things and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Trip is a social event (an excursion) in confOf, while Slide Set is a document artefact (presentation slides) in edas; they share no intended instances and belong to different branches (Event vs Document).

A's 'Reviewed contribution' is a specific stage of a submitted contribution (a contribution that has received reviews, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution), whereas B's 'Contribution' is the general superclass of all contributions (Paper, Poster, Short paper) that authors write and PC members review. Every reviewed contribution is a contribution, but not every contribution is reviewed, so A is strictly narrower than B.

A's 'details Entered By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person who entered conference details), while B's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to a Track (the tracks of a conference). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer, i.e. it records which reviewer has expertise or preference for a topic. B's 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer, i.e. it records whose review history a record is. The domains differ (expertise/preference vs. review history) and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Organization denoting an industry-sector organization (siblings: Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO), i.e. an institutional affiliation type. B is a subclass of Organizator denoting a person role on the organizing committee (siblings: General Chair, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster). One is an organization type, the other a person role; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

cmt's `name` is a general name property applying to both Conference and Person, while edas's `has First Name` is specifically a person's first name. They overlap for persons but are not the same relation: `name` is broader (covers full names and conference names), so `has First Name` is subsumed by `name` rather than equivalent.

A 'Conference Dinner' is a social/meal event (a subclass of Meal Event under Non Academic Event), whereas B 'Conference' is a scientific event (one edition of a conference, subclass of Scientific Event). They denote different concepts: a dinner is not a conference, and neither subsumes the other.

A's Person is the general superclass of all conference actors (Attendee, Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Student is a specific subclass of Person (a kind of conference participant). They do not denote the same concept; Student is strictly narrower than Person, and the pair is best treated as unrelated rather than a subsumption since the ontologies' Person classes are not being aligned here.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's is_given_to is an object property mapping an Item to a Person (an item being given to a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Non Academic Event' is a conference event type (break, meal, social) under Conference Event, while B 'Registration Student' is a fee category under Registration fee. They belong to different branches (event vs. fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (author writes paper). B's presentationed by relates a Document to a Speaker (document is presented by speaker). The domains/ranges differ (Author->Paper vs Document->Speaker) and the directions/meanings differ; they are not the same relation, nor inverses of one another.

accept Paper relates an Administrator to a Paper (the administrator accepts a paper), while has Review relates a Paper to a Review (a paper has a review). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they denote different relations.

A's Company is an organization (sibling of University) in the conference domain, while B's Van is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi). They share no meaning; the label similarity is coincidental.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a distinguished conference contributor (a person invited to speak), while B's 'Regular' is a confTool participant category contrasting with Member and Student. They denote different concepts: an invited speaker is not a regular participant category, and the paths (Conference contributor vs Participant) and siblings differ.

A's hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome for a submission). B's hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (a conference-organisation event such as a registration or reception). The domains and ranges are disjoint concepts, so the two properties relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a specific author role (a co-author of a contribution, sibling of 'Contribution 1th author'), whereas B's 'Author' is the general person class that writes contributions. Every contribution co-author is an author, but not every author is a contribution co-author, so A is strictly more specific than B.

A's 'CAD Topic' is a conference subject-area topic (a child of Topic alongside Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), i.e. a thematic category for papers. B's 'Transport vehicle' is a physical item (child of Item with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van), i.e. a means of transportation. They share no meaning in the conference domain and are not related.

A is a conference topic category (CAD Topic, a subclass of Topic alongside Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a document type (Invited Talk Abstract, a subclass of Abstract alongside Tutorial Abstract). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject area vs. document type) and share no intended instances.

Both are object properties linking a committee member to the committee they belong to: cmt's 'member Of Program Committee' has domain Program Committee Member and range Program Committee, while Conference's 'was a member of' has domain Committee member and range Committee. The domains and ranges are the corresponding classes (Program Committee Member ≡ Committee member, Program Committee ≡ Committee), and both express the same membership relation in the same direction.

A's 'Information for participants' is a document type (a sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc. under Conference document), whereas B's 'Conference' is a scientific event (an edition of a conference, sibling of Workshop, Track, Session). A document about a conference is not the conference event itself, so the two classes are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Conference Hiker is a type of Delegate (a person attending a conference building). One denotes an event, the other a person role, so they are unrelated.

A is a specific review-rating value (a subclass of Review Rating, sibling of Reject Rating etc.), i.e. a rating outcome. B is a document type (a subclass of Document, sibling of Submission, Form, etc.), i.e. the review document itself. Different concepts: a rating value vs. a review document.

readPaper is a property of a Reviewer pointing to a Paper (domain Reviewer, range Paper), while hasReviewer is a property of a Paper pointing to a Possible Reviewer (domain Paper, range Possible Reviewer). They are inverse relations, not equivalent, and the task specifies that a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

A's location is a datatype property giving the venue/place of a Social event or Working event, while B's Name of conference is a datatype property giving the name of a Conference. They relate different kinds of things (event place vs. conference name) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's Preference is a class in cmt representing a reviewer's preference/bid for a paper (a document-like entity in the review process), while B's ACM SIGKDD is an organisation/committee entity that designs deadlines, holds conferences and searches for sponsors. Their contexts (properties, domain roles) do not overlap: Preference is not an organisation and ACM SIGKDD is not a preference. Hence unrelated.

Both ontologies model a Reviewer as a Person who reviews papers; edas Reviewer has review-history and reviewing properties, iasted Reviewer is the corresponding agent role in the same conference domain, so their intended instances coincide.

Both are datatype properties giving a location/URL for a conference, but the domains differ: cmt's siteURL has domain Conference and range anyURI (the conference's website), while Conference's has_a_location has domain Conference volume and range string (a textual location of a conference volume). They overlap in intent (locating a conference) but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Conference Proceedings' is a document/volume (a published collection of papers, subclass of Proceedings under Multi author Volume), whereas B 'Conference building' is a physical place (subclass of Building, with children like Delegate and siblings like Conference hotel/airport). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Active conference participant' is a broad class of conference contributors who give presentations (siblings include Invited speaker, Passive conference participant, Regular author). B's 'Conference Chair' is a specific organizational role responsible for initiating calls and reviewing papers. The two denote different concepts: an active participant need not be a chair, and a chair is not defined by giving presentations. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's `reviews` relates a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's `design` relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline (domain ACM SIGKDD, range Deadline). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving an ISBN string, while B's 'has short title' is a datatype property of Social event / Working event giving a short title string. They have different domains (proceedings vs. events) and different intended values (ISBN vs. short title), so they denote different relations and are unrelated.

A's write relates a Person to an Item (authoring a paper), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Conference (organising/holding a conference). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent.

A's memberOfConference is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while B's Start_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (temporal start). Different kinds of entities, different directions, and different semantics; they are unrelated.

A's Organizational Meeting is an academic event (sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop) covering organisational gatherings such as committee meetings, whereas B's Industrial Session is a kind of Conference Session, i.e. a scientific/technical programme session. Different parents (Academic Event vs Conference Session) and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment for reviewing), while B's 'submit' links an Author to a Paper (submission). Different domains, ranges, and directions of the conference workflow; they are not the same relation.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), expressing that two events run in parallel. edas's 'attendee At' relates a Person to a Conference Event, expressing attendance. They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and have different meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the reviewing procedure (a process/activity), while B's 'Program Committee' is a committee (a group of people). Different kinds of entities; no subsumption or overlap.

A's virtualMeetingEnabledBy relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables virtual meetings), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'Call for participation' is a document (a Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.) that announces/requests participation. B's 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative event (subclass of Administrative event, sibling of Submission event, Reviewing event, etc.) in the event branch. One is a document, the other an event; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties giving the start date of the conference: A's 'is a starting date' has domain Important dates and range date, B's 'Start of conference' has domain Conference and range dateTime. Despite the different domain classes (Important dates vs Conference) and datatypes (date vs dateTime), both denote the same relation, the conference's starting date, and are treated as equivalent in the reference alignment.

A is a research topic area (Microelectronics Topic) under Topic in edas, while B is a specific kind of document (Invited Talk Abstract) under Abstract in ekaw. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

Both entities denote the role of chairing a conference program committee: Ontology A's Chair (Conference Chair) and Ontology B's PC Chair (Program Committee Chair) are the same conference-domain role, with matching context (person who chairs the PC).

A's hasFax is a datatype property linking a Person to a fax number string; B's writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to its author Person. They differ in domain, range, and meaning (contact info vs. authorship), so they are unrelated.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property mapping Contact Information to a string postal code, while B's heldIn is an object property mapping an Event to a Location. They relate entirely different kinds of entities (contact info/string vs event/location) and are not the same relation.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authoring relation). B's related To Paper relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a presentation-to-paper link). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's title is the title of a Paper; B's abstract is the abstract text of a Contribution. Although Paper and Contribution are equivalent classes, title and abstract are distinct datatype properties (a paper has both a title and an abstract), so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, User is a general person role (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer) representing any system user. In sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is a specific organizer role under Organizator, sibling to General Chair, Program Chair, etc. The intended instances do not coincide: a User need not be an organizing committee member, and an organizing committee member is a specific organizer, not a generic user. Different concepts.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a specific kind of paper (the abstract-only submission), a sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper. In edas, Paper is the general class with children Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc. A Paper Abstract is a Paper, but not every Paper is a Paper Abstract, so Paper Abstract is strictly more specific and is subsumed by edas Paper.

A 'Committee member' is a person role in the conference organisation (a subclass of Person, with children Chair/Co chair and properties linking to Committee), whereas B 'Fee' is a monetary charge (subclass of Money, with children Registration fee, Hotel fee, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Tutorial is a kind of conference event/part (sibling of Track and Workshop, part of a Conference volume), whereas B's Speaker is a person role (subclass of Person, with children Author and Invited Speaker, and properties linking a speaker to a Document). The two denote different concepts—an event type versus a person role—so they are unrelated.

Both properties relate a person involved in the reviewing process to a Paper they review: cmt's read Paper has domain Reviewer and range Paper, edas's is Reviewing has domain Reviewer (among other roles) and range Paper. The intended relation (a reviewer reading/reviewing a paper) is the same; the broader domain in edas is a role-hierarchy difference, not a different relation.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property of Review preference (an integer degree of preference for a review), while B's 'default Choice' is a datatype property of Social event / Working event (a positive integer default choice for an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

In cmt, Preference is a class representing a reviewer's preference/bid for a paper (a submission-related concept), while in the Conference ontology Organization is a class for organizing bodies such as committees or institutions. They denote different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Working event' is a general conference-domain event class (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop; sibling of Administrative/Social event) with properties like has title, location, has Topic. B is a specific research topic ('Computer Networks Applications Topic') under the Topic hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts (event vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a full-length paper (sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), whereas B's 'Short paper' is a short contribution (sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution). They denote different kinds of submission and are not equivalent; no subsumption holds either.

A's 'has a volume' relates a Conference proceedings to an int (number of volumes), while B's 'has amount of' relates Money to an int (monetary amount). Different domains and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A Track is a thematic subdivision of a conference (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, part of a Conference volume, with has tracks from Conference volume to Track). B Programme is a Document (sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set) that belongs to a Conference Event and is linked from a Conference Event via has Programme. A track is not a document and does not denote the same instances as a programme; the two concepts are unrelated in the conference domain.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a document type) that has an abstract; B's Abstract is a document that is a sibling of Paper and Review. The two denote different concepts (a paper vs. an abstract of a paper), so they are not equivalent.

In sigkdd, Author is a child of Speaker, so every Author is a Speaker; confOf's Author is a Person who writes Contributions, which is a narrower role than sigkdd's Speaker (a Person who gives presentations, with Author and Invited Speaker as subclasses). The confOf Author therefore corresponds to the sigkdd Author subclass, not to Speaker itself, making confOf Author strictly more specific than sigkdd Speaker.

A's 'Final manuscript' is a specific stage of a submission (sibling of 'Initial manuscript', under Submission), whereas B's 'Paper' is the general document type that authors submit and that has an Abstract and Review. Every final manuscript is a paper, but not every paper is a final manuscript, so Final manuscript is strictly narrower than Paper.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (the administrator enters review criteria for a conference), while B's 'has Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a paper has a reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not equivalent.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property giving the title (string) of a Social/Working event, while B's 'End of conference' is a datatype property giving the dateTime at which a Conference ends. They relate different kinds of things (event title vs. conference end time) with different domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.

Sponzorship in iasted is a subclass of Money (a financial category alongside Fee, Tax, Tip), i.e. the sponsorship payment/funding itself. Sponzor in sigkdd is the sponsor entity (an organisation/person) with subclasses Gold Supporter, Silver Supporter, Exhibitor, etc., and a 'Name of sponsor' property. The two are related (sponsorship money vs. sponsor) but not the same concept, so they are not equivalent.

confOf Organization is an institution (children Company, University) that employs Persons and has address properties; edas Contact Information is an address/contact record with city, email, phone, postal code, street. They overlap in carrying address data but denote different concepts: an organization is not a contact-information record, and Contact Information is not an organization. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name; B's 'starts on' is a datatype property of Event giving an event's start date/time. Different domains (Person vs Event) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's hasSubjectArea is a specific property linking a Paper to its Subject Area. B's is_connected_with is a very general property linking Activity or Person to Item or Place. The domains and ranges do not match, and the intended meanings differ: one is about a paper's topic, the other about a general connection between activities/persons and items/places. They are not equivalent.

Both are object properties linking an author (Co author / Author) to a paper (Paper / Contribution). In cmt, Paper is the contribution submitted by authors, and confOf's Contribution is the paper written by an Author. The domain/range pairs coincide semantically, so the properties denote the same relation.

cmt:Document is a general document class whose children are Paper and Review (conference submissions/reviews), whereas edas:PersonalHistory is a class about a person's history with children PersonalPublicationHistory and PersonalReviewHistory. They denote different concepts: one is a document artefact, the other a biographical/history record. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's Attendee is a subclass of Person (a person who attends the conference), while B's 'Author attendee book registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary fee category for authors who attend and book). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money/Fee) and denote a person versus a fee, so they are unrelated.

A's property is a datatype property linking the Important dates class to a date literal, representing the acceptance-notification deadline. B's 'follows' is an object property linking one Administrative event to another, expressing temporal ordering between events. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain/range, and intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

Author is a Person who writes contributions, while Multi author Volume is a Document (a published multi-author volume, parent of Proceedings). They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and have incompatible properties (writes/written By vs publisher Of), so they denote different concepts.

A's 'Steering committee' is a committee subtype within the conference organisation (siblings Organizing/Program committee, linked to Conference volume), while B's 'University' is an organization subtype (sibling Company) that scholars study at. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A relates an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (committee organizes a conference/volume), while B relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a place is occupied by a person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

confOf's City is a general city class (range of has City for Organizations and Persons). iasted's Trip city is a specific subclass of City representing the city of a trip, alongside Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city. Trip city is therefore strictly narrower than the general City, so City subsumes Trip city (Trip city is subsumed by City).

A is an administrative event (registration of participants, confTool), a sibling of Submission/Reviewing/Camera Ready events; B is an academic event (Workshop) under Conference Event. Different branches of the event hierarchy and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event, sibling of Tutorial/Workshop) that takes place during the conference. B's Activity before conference is a phase/activity category preceding the conference, with children like Accepting manuscript, Receiving manuscript, Renting, Research. These denote different concepts: one is the conference event itself, the other is the set of pre-conference activities. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's Paper is a conference submission with authors, reviews, decisions and subject areas (children Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version; sibling Review; properties has Author, has Decision, assigned To). B's Record of attendance is an administrative document (siblings Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Viza) recording attendance, not a scientific paper. Same parent Document but different intended instances, so unrelated.

A's Sponsor is a Person who sponsors (sibling of Delegate, under Person), while B's Gold Supporter is a specific sponsorship tier under Sponzor, alongside Platinum/Silver/Bronze tiers and Exhibitor. A Sponsor is a general sponsoring person/entity; a Gold Supporter is a narrower sponsorship level, so Sponsor is broader and Gold Supporter is subsumed by it. They are not equivalent because B denotes only one tier, not sponsorship in general.

A 'Conference contribution' is a document-like submission (parent: Conference document; children: Poster, Presentation, Written contribution; properties: has contributions, is submitted at) whereas B 'Academic Event' is an event (parent: Conference Event; children: Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop; properties: has Call, for Event). They overlap in the conference domain (a presentation is both a contribution and an event) but neither subsumes the other, so they are related, not equivalent.

assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assigning the reviewing task), while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a broader giving relation). They overlap in the conference domain (assigning a review task is a kind of giving/assigning) but neither subsumes the other cleanly: assignReviewer has a narrower domain (Administrator vs Person) and range (Reviewer vs Activity/Item), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Regular author' is a role of a person (a conference contributor who is an author, sibling of Invited speaker, Poster, Presentation), whereas B's 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of event/presentation (sibling of Invited Talk, Tutorial). One denotes a person/role, the other an event, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Organization is the general class of organisations (children Company and University, and it is the range of employed By), while edas's Industry Organization is a specific subtype of edas's Organization (siblings Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO). Thus confOf Organization is broader and subsumes Industry Organization, not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, and both denote the start date/time of a conference (edas comment 'Conference Start Date and Time'; sigkdd label 'Start of conference'). Same concept and direction.

A's Workshop Chair is a specific conference participant role (a PC Member who chairs a workshop), while B's General Chair is a top-level organizer role (parent Organizator, sibling of Program Chair and Webmaster). They denote different roles in the conference organization and neither subsumes the other.

A's property links a Review preference to the topics/submissions the reviewer prefers, while B's property links a Reviewer to their personal review history. Different domains (Review preference vs Reviewer), different ranges (Submitted contribution/Topic vs Personal Review History), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'follows' orders Administrative events in time (domain and range both Administrative event), while B's 'has Menu' links a Meal Event to its Meal Menu. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (a venue location). They belong to different branches (document vs. place) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.
A is a conference topic (Antennas Topic) under Topic, while B is a Card item under Item with child Credit card; they denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members (range: Program Committee Member), while B's hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (range: Programme). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's 'follows' orders Administrative events in a temporal sequence (successor relation), while B's 'part Of Event' is a mereological containment relation between Events. Different intended semantics and directions, so not equivalent.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who started the bidding process), while B's 'has Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a reviewer candidate for that paper). Different domains (Conference vs Paper), different ranges (Administrator vs Possible Reviewer), and different intended meanings (bidding initiation vs paper-reviewer assignment), so they are not equivalent.
Reception is a social event (a gathering) in confOf, while Listener is a person role in sigkdd; they share no meaning and belong to different branches (Event vs Person).

Publisher in the Conference ontology is an organisation that issues conference proceedings (domain of 'issues', range of 'has a publisher'), whereas Country in confOf is a geographical entity used as the range of 'has Country' for Organizations and Persons. They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A's 'Member PC' is a Person subclass (a program-committee member/reviewer), while B's 'Review' is a Document subclass (the review document itself). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

Document in cmt is a superclass of Paper and Review (written artefacts), while Topic in confOf is a subject area that contributions deal with and PC members are expert on. Their instances and roles in the domain are entirely different, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Operating Topicsystems' is a research topic category under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts.

A's `date` is a datatype property of Conference with range date (a temporal value, e.g. the conference date), while B's `City of conference` is a datatype property of Conference with range string denoting a location. They share only the domain (Conference) but relate it to entirely different kinds of values (time vs. place), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is the published volume of a conference (has publisher, volume, ISBN; issued by a Publisher), whereas B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself (has dates, country, members, topics, deadlines). The proceedings are a document produced by the event, not the event, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property linking a Conference proceedings to a string (its ISBN number). B's 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item (a person obtains an item). They differ in domain (proceedings vs person), range (string vs item), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Talk Event is a conference event (a talk given at a conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk, siblings Paper Presentation and Workshop). B's Modelling is a research activity performed before a conference, sibling of Simulating. They denote different concepts: an event vs. a research activity, so they are unrelated.
Conference Chair is a person role in the cmt ontology, while Dinner banquet is a social event in the iasted ontology; they belong to different top-level categories and have no overlap.

edas Paper is a general document about a paper (with children Accepted/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper and properties like is Written By, has Topic, is Reviewed By), while ekaw Conference Paper is a specific subclass of ekaw Paper (siblings Camera Ready Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Regular Paper, Submitted Paper, Workshop Paper). The edas Paper is broader than the ekaw Conference Paper, so edas Paper is subsumed by ekaw Conference Paper.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'review Written By' relates a Review to a Possible Reviewer, i.e. the author of a review. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Session Chair' is a conference participant role (a person who chairs a session), while B's 'Hotel presenter' is a subclass of Delegate/Place describing a presenter staying at a hotel; B's ontology has a separate 'Session chair' class, so the two entities are not the same concept.

A's 'enable Virtual Meeting' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an admin enabling a virtual meeting for a conference), while B's 'is given by' relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the person giving a presentation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote a human being in the conference domain: cmt Person is the superclass of Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User; iasted Person is the superclass of Delegate and Sponsor. Same label, same intended instances (people involved in the conference), so they are equivalent.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), a subclass of Scientific Event. B's Conference airport is a physical building/place (a subclass of Building), a venue location. Different domains (event vs. place), so they are not equivalent.

Conference applicant is a Person subtype (a person applying to a conference, with child Registered applicant), while Conference Venue Place is a Place subtype (a physical location for a conference, sibling of Accommodation/Dining/Meeting Room Place). Different roots (Person vs Place) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference (a role in the organising committee, sibling of Program Committee Chair and Associated Chair), whereas B Author is a person who writes papers, a subclass of Speaker/Delegate. The two denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A Reception is a social event (a gathering/activity) in confOf, while B Dining Place is a physical place/location in edas. They are conceptually related because a reception is typically held at a dining place, but they are not the same concept: one is an event, the other a venue/location.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while an Invited Speaker is a kind of Person/Speaker (sibling of Author). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an email' relates a Person to an email address string, while B's 'has First Name' relates a Person to a given-name string. They are different datatype properties with different intended values (email vs. first name), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Double hotel room' is a specific type of hotel room (a subclass of Hotel room), while B 'Hotel' denotes the whole hotel building/place. A double hotel room is a part/kind of accommodation within a hotel, so it is strictly more specific than Hotel; the two are not equivalent.

In cmt, External Reviewer is a person assigned to review for another Reviewer but explicitly not a Reviewer, with properties assign/assigned By Reviewer linking to Reviewer. In confOf, Member PC is a Program Committee member whose comment is 'Reviewer' and who reviews Contributions and is expert on Topics. The two denote different roles: an external reviewer is not a PC member/reviewer, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Accpet If Room Rating' is a specific review-rating value (a subclass of Review Rating, sibling of Accept/Reject/Weak Reject Rating), i.e. a rating category. B's 'Review' is a document type (subclass of Document, sibling of Abstract and Paper), i.e. the review document itself. A rating value and a document are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Presenter is a subclass of Conference Participant (a person role who presents), with children like Invited Speaker. B's Conference state is a subclass of State, a status/state of a conference, sibling to Presenter state and Sponsor state. One denotes a person role, the other a conference status; they are different kinds of entities and not equivalent.

A's Conference is the academic event (has deadlines, topics, members, documents), while B's Conference building is a physical building/venue under Place > Building, with children like Delegate and siblings such as Conference hotel and Conference airport. They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

A's `references` relates a paper to the works it cites (bibliographic citation relation), while B's `awarded by` relates an Award to the body granting it. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no overlap.

A is a conference-related document (a web page about the conference, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with a URL property), while B is a building/place (a university where a presenter is located, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). They denote entirely different concepts and share no intended instances.

A's 'has workshops' relates a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a whole-part/containment relation within a conference), while B's 'is situated in' relates a Building/City/Place to a geographic location (spatial containment). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

edas Conference is a large-scale academic event with deadlines, country, topics and members, and has subclasses Single Level Conference / Two Level Conference. ekaw Individual Presentation is a scientific event that is a presentation of a paper, with subclasses Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial, and is a sibling of Conference in ekaw. The two denote different concepts: a conference is not an individual presentation.

A's Abstract is a document/contribution type (an extended abstract that is part of a paper/poster/presentation), while B's Topic is a subject area category (with children like Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic) used to classify conferences and papers. They denote different concepts despite both being classes in the conference domain.

Both properties link a document-like entity to a person, but 'written By' expresses authorship while 'is signed by' expresses signing/approval; the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent, though they overlap in linking an item to a person.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete paper document (sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), whereas B 'Poster' is a distinct contribution type (sibling of Paper and Short paper under Contribution). A full paper and a poster are different conference submission artefacts, so the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Test Only Topic' is a placeholder topic category in the edas topic taxonomy. They belong to different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Banquet is a social event (a festive meal/activity) under Event > Social Event, while B Conference airport is a physical building/place under Place > Building. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. location) and are not equivalent.

Chair is a specific committee leadership role (a Committee member who chairs a committee, sibling of Co chair, domain/range of committee-chair properties). Possible Reviewer is a general person role that can review papers (parent of PC Member, domain of reviewer Of Paper). A chair need not be a reviewer and a possible reviewer is not a chair; the concepts do not coincide.

A's property links a Review preference to the topics/contributions it prefers (domain Review preference, range Submitted contribution/Topic), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (domain Author, range Contribution). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Chairman is a Person role (a person who chairs, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Power Point presentation is a kind of Presentation activity (sibling of Video presentation). They belong to different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role/type of author (a person who is the first author of a contribution), sitting under Regular author with sibling 'Contribution co author'. B's 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference event (sibling of Single Level Conference, Attendee, Author, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts — an author role versus a conference type — so they are unrelated.

A's 'Written contribution' is a kind of conference contribution (a document/paper submitted to a conference), with children Regular contribution and Submitted contribution. B's 'Conference' is a working event (an event such as a conference, tutorial or workshop). The two denote different concepts — a contribution vs. an event — and neither subsumes the other.

A's hasRelatedDocument links agents/events (Person, Conference, etc.) to a Document, while B's partOfEvent is a mereological relation between Events. Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's 'Conference document' is a document/artefact class (children: Call for paper, Conference contribution, Review, etc.; it has authors and a date of issue), whereas B's 'Conference' is the event itself (children: Single Level Conference, Two Level Conference; properties: end Date, has Country, has Member, paper Due On). The shared word 'Conference' is misleading: one denotes a document, the other an event, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference contribution (a document type, sibling of Extended abstract, with abstract-related properties), while B's Deadline Author notification is a deadline/event type (sibling of submission deadlines, with a notification-until property). They denote different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's contactEmail is a datatype property of Contribution (the paper submission) giving a contact e-mail for the contribution, while B's E-mail is a datatype property of Person giving a person's e-mail address. They have different domains (Contribution vs Person) and different intended subjects, so they are not the same relation.

A 'Video presentation' is a kind of conference presentation (an activity/event), while B 'Organizator' is a person role (a subclass of Person with children like General Chair, Program Chair). They denote completely different concepts (event vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (sibling of Extended abstract) in the Conference ontology, i.e. a full/regular paper. B's Workshop Paper is a specific kind of paper (a paper submitted to a workshop), a sibling of Conference Paper, Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc. The two denote different concepts: a regular paper is not a workshop paper, and the paths/siblings show B's Workshop Paper is a narrower, distinct category. Hence they are not equivalent.

edas:Paper is the general document class for papers (parent of Accepted/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), while ekaw:Submitted_Paper is a specific subclass of ekaw:Paper denoting a paper that has been submitted. The edas Paper is broader, covering all paper states, so it subsumes the more specific Submitted Paper; they are not equivalent.

confOf's dealsWith relates a Contribution to a Topic (the subject matter of a paper), while sigkdd's obtain relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving a prize). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Proceedings Publisher' is an Organisation (a publisher entity that publishes proceedings), while B's 'Receiving manuscript' is an Activity before the conference (the act of receiving a submitted manuscript). They belong to different top-level branches (Organisation vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the person hierarchy), while B is a conference activity (Coctail reception, a subclass of Conference activity). They belong to disjoint branches of the ontology (Person vs Activity) and denote entirely different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.
Reviewer in edas is a Person (a role an individual plays), while Review in ekaw is a Document (the review text/artefact). They are different kinds of entities, not the same concept.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of conference-domain event such as Tutorial/Workshop), while B's Simulating is a research activity (sibling of Modelling) under 'Activity before conference > Research'. They denote entirely different concepts: an event vs. a research method/activity, so they are unrelated.

A's Poster is a contribution type (a poster presentation), while B's Conference Paper is a document type (a paper submitted to a conference). In ekaw, the poster counterpart is Poster Paper, a sibling of Conference Paper, not Conference Paper itself. The two denote different concepts (presentation format vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

Scholar in confOf is a person role (a price category for a person, subclass of Person, with property study At), while Registration fee in sigkdd is a fee type (subclass of Fee, with Currency/Price and pay/payed by properties). They denote different concepts: a person category versus a payment category, so they are unrelated.

Reviewer (a Person who reviews papers, with review expertise/preference and co-reviewer relations) and Speaker (a Person who gives a presentation, with children Author and Invited Speaker) denote different roles in the conference domain; they share only the parent Person and have no overlapping properties or instances.

A's 'Call for participation' is a document (a Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, Review) — a written announcement inviting submissions. B's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions, sibling of Submission event and Reviewing results event. One is a document, the other an event/process; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'Accommodation Place' is a subclass of Place (a physical location such as a hotel), while B's 'Registration form' is a subclass of Form/Document (an informational artefact used to register). They denote different kinds of things (place vs. document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Academic Event' is a subclass of Conference Event covering meetings, presentations, talks and workshops; B's 'Author' is a subclass of Speaker (a Person) who submits papers and receives notifications. They denote different concepts (event vs. person role) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.
A is a kind of conference paper (a document type), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment; they share no concept and belong to entirely different branches of the domain.

A's Paper is a general conference contribution (sibling of Extended abstract, with abstract-related properties), while B's Rejected Paper is a specific submission status under edas's Paper class. Every Rejected Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is rejected, so A is strictly more general than B (A subsumed_by B's parent, not equivalent to the status subclass).

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (who prints hardcopy mailing manifests), while B's 'follows' relates one Administrative event to another (temporal ordering of events). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's property relates an Administrator to a Conference (printing hardcopy mailing manifests), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Meta Review' is a document/review artefact (a review of reviews) in cmt, while B 'Reviewer' is a person role in edas. They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a document/event), while B's 'Author' is a person role (a Speaker who writes papers). They denote different concepts: one is a talk, the other a person, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Preference is a class representing a reviewer's preference for a paper (a submission/review concept). In iasted, Time zone is a class representing a geographic time zone, likely used for scheduling. The two denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference topic (a subject area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is an organizational body (a committee under Committee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'has a steering committee' links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a committee entity), while B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person. Different domain/range and different intended relation; not equivalent.

A's 'gives presentations' links an Active conference participant to a Presentation (a person presenting), while B's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (authorship of a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent, not inverse, and no subsumption.

A's External Reviewer is explicitly a person who reviews for another Reviewer but is not themselves a Reviewer, while B's Reviewer is a full reviewer (a Speaker/Delegate who reviews). The two concepts are disjoint in intent: an External Reviewer is defined by not being a Reviewer, so they cannot be equivalent. They are not in a subsumption relation either, since neither class's instances are a subset of the other's under the stated definitions.

A's 'has a steering committee' relates a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a whole-to-part committee membership link), while B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (an individual's membership in a conference). Different domain, range, and direction of the relation; they do not denote the same relation.

A's property links a Conference part to a Topic (the subject matter of a track/workshop/tutorial), while B's presentation links a Speaker to a Document (the speaker's presentation material). Different domains (Conference part vs Speaker), different ranges (Topic vs Document), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

In edas, 'Single Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference, denoting a conference with a single-level (flat) programme structure, contrasted with 'Two Level Conference'. In ekaw, 'Conference' is the general class for one edition of a conference, with siblings like Workshop, Session, Track. The edas class is a specific kind of conference, so it is strictly narrower than ekaw's Conference; hence subsumed_by rather than equivalent.

Both are object properties linking a paper/conference document to its author(s). cmt's Paper corresponds to Conference's Conference document, and cmt's Author corresponds to Conference's Person (an author is a person). Same direction and same intended relation, so they are equivalent.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings linking a proceedings volume to its ISBN string, while B's 'has Biography' is a datatype property of Person linking a person to a biographical text. They have different domains (Conference proceedings vs Person) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving the name of a Conference or Person (domain Conference, Person; range string). B's `has gender` is a datatype property giving the gender of a Person (domain Person). They denote different attributes (name vs. gender) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant (a person participating in the conference, with siblings Regular and Student), i.e. a registered participant category. In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person, a general role for anyone attending, with siblings Author, Reviewer, etc. A Member (registered participant) is a kind of Attendee, but Attendee is broader (includes authors, reviewers, chairs who may not be 'members'), so Member is subsumed by Attendee rather than equivalent.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has City' is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a city. Different domains, different ranges (surname vs city), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a submitted/reviewed paper that was rejected (a document in the submission workflow, sibling of Accepted contribution). B 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity in the pre-conference phase (sibling of Receiving/Refusing manuscript), i.e. the act of accepting a manuscript, not a rejected paper. Different kinds (document vs activity) and opposite polarity (rejected vs accepting), so they are unrelated.

Conference Participant in ekaw is a broad class covering all people involved in a conference (including presenters, session chairs, PC chairs, demo chairs, etc.), while Organizator in sigkdd is narrower, covering only people who organize the conference (general chair, organizing committee, program chair, PC member, webmaster). The two classes overlap (organizers are typically conference participants) but neither subsumes the other: ekaw's Conference Participant includes non-organizer roles like Presenter, and sigkdd's Organizator includes roles like Webmaster that may not be considered conference participants in ekaw. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to a string (an identifier), while B's 'lists Event' is an object property linking Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event. They differ in domain, range, and kind, so they denote different relations.

A's 'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document (the paper/contribution involved in the conflict). B's 'is used by' relates an Item to a Person, i.e. the inverse direction and a different meaning (an item being used by a person). The domains/ranges are reversed (Person->Document vs Item->Person) and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment of a paper for review), while B's 'is paid by' links Money to a Person (payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's virtualMeetingEnabledBy relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables virtual meetings), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Conference (the organization holds a conference). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they do not denote the same relation.

cmt:User is a general person role that subsumes Administrator, Author and Reviewer, i.e. anyone involved in the conference. edas:Attendee is a person who attends the conference, a sibling of Author, Reviewer, TPC Member etc. rather than their superclass. The two overlap (an attendee is a user, and some users attend) but neither subsumes the other, so they are related, not equivalent.

A's Conference is the event/organisation entity (has members, dates, administrators, submission settings), while B's Paper is a document artefact (subclass of Document, has reviews, reviewers, topics, presentation). They denote different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is a starting date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates entity to a date (the start of a conference deadline/event). B's 'has First Name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (a person's first name). They have different domains (Important dates vs Person), different ranges (date vs string), and different intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A's Renting is an activity performed before the conference (a sub-activity of 'Activity before conference', alongside Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript and Research), whereas B's Author is a person role (a subclass of Speaker with children Author of paper / Author of paper student and properties such as submit, obtain, notification until). The two entities belong to different branches of the conference domain (activity vs. person) and share neither instances nor meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Demo Session' is a kind of scientific event session (a time slot in the conference programme where demos are presented), while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee (a group of people responsible for organising the conference). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. committee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'abstract' is a datatype property of a Contribution (paper) holding the paper's abstract text; B's 'Name of sponsor' is a datatype property of a Sponzor (sponsor) holding the sponsor's name. Different domains (Contribution vs Sponzor) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Author is a general person role (parent of Presenter, sibling of Reviewer, TPC Member, etc.) that writes papers. B's 'Author of paper' is a narrower subclass of B's Author, specifically the author of a paper (sibling of 'Author of paper student'). A's Author is broader than B's Author of paper, so A is subsumed by B's narrower concept; they are not equivalent.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string email address; B's 'is sent before' is an object property linking an Item to a Time. They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a submitted document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Call For Manuscripts is a call/announcement (child of Call, sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Reviews). They denote different concepts: a paper versus a call for submissions.

A is a post-conference social activity (siblings: Activity before conference, Conference activity; children: Departure, Full day tour), while B is a physical venue (Place > Conference hall, siblings Hotel, Main office). Different domains (event vs. location), so they are unrelated.

A's has Subject Area links a Paper to a Subject Area (topic classification), while B's has an abstract links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract (the text summary). Different range concepts (Subject Area vs Abstract) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's `written By` links a Review to the Reviewer (the person who wrote the review), while B's `reviews` links a Review to the Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed). They relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's Review is a subclass of Document representing a peer review of a paper, with properties linking it to Paper and Possible Reviewer. B's Form is a subclass of Document representing a fillable form (e.g. registration, hotel, author information), with children like Hotel registration form and Registration form. Although B's sibling list contains a class named 'Review', that is a different entity from B's Form. The two classes denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'Accepted contribution' is a document/contribution that has passed review and is accepted (sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B's 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity in the pre-conference phase (sibling of Accepting manuscript, Refusing manuscript), i.e. the act of receiving a submitted manuscript, not the accepted paper itself. The two are related (both concern the handling of submitted papers) but denote different concepts: a document state versus an activity, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Person is the general superclass of all people in the conference domain (its children include Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, etc.), while ekaw's Student is a specific subclass of ekaw's Person. Person is strictly more general than Student, so A subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the whole conference event/organisation (has members, administrators, submission settings, logo, dates), while B's Conference Session is a specific session type within a conference (a subclass of Session, sibling of Workshop/Poster/Demo sessions). A conference is not a session; the entities denote different concepts.

A 'Break Event' is a non-academic conference event (a break such as a coffee break, meal break or free time), whereas B 'Organizator' is a person role (a subclass of Person with children such as General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.

A's hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string biography, while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. Different kinds (datatype vs object), different ranges (string vs Item), and different intended meaning (biographical text vs acquiring an item), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'ends on' is a datatype property of Event giving an end date/time. Different domains, different intended meanings, no overlap.

A is a review-rating class (a kind of rating value such as 'accept if room'), while B is a person class (a reviewer, a kind of delegate/speaker). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a written/prepared item (Document in ekaw, Item in iasted) to a Person, in the same direction.
