'written By' and 'is prepared by' both express authorship of a document/item by a person, and the domain/range contexts (Document/Item -> Person) agree, so they denote the same relation.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that announces a conference. B 'Welcome Talk' is a talk event (subclass of Talk Event, sibling of Closing Talk) that occurs during a conference. One is a document, the other an event; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

An External Reviewer is explicitly a person who reviews papers but is not themselves a Reviewer, so it is a narrower concept than EDAS's Reviewer. Every External Reviewer is a reviewer of papers (subsumed by Reviewer), but not every Reviewer is an External Reviewer, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'Active conference participant' is a conference contributor who gives presentations (siblings: invited speaker, passive participant, regular author), while B's 'Author' is a speaker who submits papers and obtains awards, with children 'Author of paper'. Both are persons involved in the conference who produce/present work, so they overlap, but A is defined by giving presentations and B by submitting papers; neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Chair PC' is a Person who chairs the Programme Committee (sibling of Member PC, Author, Participant; comment 'confTool'), while B's 'OC Chair' is a Person who chairs the Organising Committee (subclass of OC Member). Programme Committee chair and Organising Committee chair are distinct roles in the conference domain, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a subclass of Abstract (a document type, sibling of Tutorial Abstract), i.e. a kind of abstract document. B's 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a subclass of Deadline (a time point, sibling of Deadline Paper Submission and Deadline Author notification), i.e. a submission deadline. One is a document type, the other a temporal event; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's 'Invited talk' is a subclass of Conference contribution/Presentation, i.e. a kind of document/contribution (the talk as an artefact). B's 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Presenter, i.e. a kind of person (the person who gives an invited talk). They denote different kinds of entities (contribution vs. person), so they are not equivalent; at most they are related through the invited-talk event, but the classes themselves are unrelated.

NGO is a subclass of Organization (a type of organization such as academia, government, industry), while Organizing Committee is a subclass of Committee (a group within the conference organization). They denote different concepts: an NGO is an organization type, not a committee, and the paths, parents, and siblings are entirely different.

A's 'lists Event' relates a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event (a document listing events), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker's presentation slides). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's `reviews` links a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution). B's `reviewer Of Paper` links a Possible Reviewer (a person) to a Paper they may review (domain Possible Reviewer, range Paper). Different domain and range, and different direction of the relation (review artefact -> reviewed paper vs. person -> paper), so they are not equivalent.

Administrator (confOf) is a Person who administers the conference (comment 'confTool'), while Attendee (edas) is a Person who attends the conference. They are distinct roles: an administrator need not attend, and an attendee need not administer. Different siblings (Assistant, Author, Chair PC... vs Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer...) and no shared properties indicate no equivalence.

Both classes represent the set of conference deadlines/dates: 'Important dates' has properties for submission, acceptance notification, camera-ready, and start/end dates, while 'Deadline' has children for camera-ready, notification of acceptance, registration, and submission deadlines. The intended instances (specific dates/deadlines in a conference) coincide, so they are equivalent.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or producing an item). Different domain/range semantics and direction of meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (Paper -> Reviewer), while B's reviewOfPaper relates a Review to a Paper (Review -> Paper). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions; reviewOfPaper is closer to the inverse of a paper-to-review relation, not to assignedTo.

A Program Committee Member is a specific kind of conference member (a reviewer on the PC), while B's Member is a generic participant category (siblings Regular, Student) under Participant. Every PC member is a member/participant, but not every Member is a PC member, so A is strictly narrower than B.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes papers), while B's 'Conference' is an event with city, start/end dates and a name, held by ACM SIGKDD. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference document type (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic in computer networks (a subtopic of Computer Networks Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving its textual title (range string); B's has Cost Amount is a datatype property of Sponsorship giving a monetary integer amount. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a mereological/containment relation within the conference structure). B's 'is Topic Of' relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper (a topical-subject relation). The domains and ranges differ (Conference part vs Topic; Conference volume vs Conference/Paper), and the intended meanings are different relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper they author), while B's 'award' relates something to an Award (a prize). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

University is an academic organisation (a subclass of Academic Institution under Organisation), while Review is a document type (a subclass of Document, sibling of Paper and Abstract). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's hasHomePage relates a Person to a homepage URL string, while B's hasLastName relates a Person to a surname string. They are different datatype properties with different intended values, so they are not equivalent.

A's isTopicOf relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper (a topic is the subject of a paper/conference), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presents a document). Different domains (Topic vs Speaker), different ranges (Conference/Paper vs Document), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in cmt), while B 'Closing Talk' is a talk event (a subclass of Talk Event in edas). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person vs. event) and share no intended instances.

A's 'author Of' relates a Person (domain) to a Document (range): a person authors a document. B's 'is given to' relates an Item (domain) to a Person (range): an item is given to a person. The directions and the kinds of things related are reversed and different, so they are not equivalent (they are not even inverses, since Item and Document are not the same concept).

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (author writes paper), while B's `has Reviewer` relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (paper has reviewer). Different domain, range, and direction of the underlying relation; they are not the same property.

A is a Program Committee Chair, a committee role (subclass of Chairman and Program Committee Member) that reviews papers. B is an Author, a person role under Speaker in the delegate hierarchy who writes papers. The two denote different roles in the conference domain with no subsumption or overlap, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document type (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) used to announce a conference, whereas B 'Book proceeding' is a published book-form proceedings volume (sibling of Cd proceeding). They denote different concepts: an announcement is not a proceedings publication, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'was a steering committee of' relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume, while B's 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' is an Administrator action whose range is a Conference (setting review criteria for a conference), while B's 'give' is a Person action whose range is an Activity or Item (giving something). Different domains (Administrator vs Person) and different ranges (Conference vs Activity/Item) mean the relations do not coincide.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on a Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted; B's 'has a volume' is an integer property of Conference proceedings giving the volume number. Different domains (Conference vs Conference proceedings), different ranges (boolean vs int), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'paper Due On' is the submission deadline for conference papers, while B's 'End of conference' is the date the conference ends. Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, but they denote different deadlines/events in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's OC Member is a person role (an Organising Committee member, a subclass of Conference Participant with child OC Chair), while B's Session is a conference activity (a subclass of Lecture with child Speaker lecture). One denotes a person, the other an event; they cannot have the same instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Non Academic Event is a conference event that is not academic (breaks, meals, social events), while B's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference). They denote different concepts: one is a non-scholarly event category, the other is the conference itself, so they are unrelated.

OC Chair is a person role (an Organizing Committee member who chairs the committee) under Person > Conference Participant > OC Member, whereas Introduction of speaker is a conference activity (the act of introducing a speaker) under Activity > Conference activity > Introduction. They denote different kinds of entities (a person vs. an activity) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a review of a conference contribution (domain/range: reviews -> Reviewed contribution, has a review from Reviewed contribution), i.e. an evaluation document. B's Programme Brochure is a document that lists events and is published by an organisation (event On List, lists Event, publisher Of), i.e. a conference programme booklet. Different intended instances and roles, so they are unrelated despite both being documents.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person/role who has paid early), while B is a subclass of Payment document (a cheque, a payment instrument). They belong to different branches (Person vs Item/Document) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) in the Conference ontology, while B 'Computer Networks Management Topic' is a research topic in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'initiates' relates a chair/TPC member to a Call (a person initiates a call for papers), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (a paper related to the author, e.g. another paper by the same author), while B's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship). They differ in domain (Author vs Document) and in meaning (related paper vs authorship), and are not inverses either.

A's 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'hasMenu' links a Meal Event to its Meal Menu. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Chairman is a Person role (a person who chairs, with subclasses Conference Chair, PC Chair, Associated Chair), while B's Video presentation is a kind of Presentation activity (sibling of Power Point presentation). They belong to different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event in the reviewing workflow (results of reviewing procedures made accessible to authors), a sibling of Submission/Reviewing/Camera Ready events. B 'Conference' is a scientific event, one edition of a conference, with siblings Session, Track, Workshop, Individual Presentation. They denote different concepts: one is a workflow milestone, the other a scientific event type. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference domain (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while City (iasted) is a geographical location class with children like Conference city and Presenter city and properties about being occupied by or visited by persons. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Accommodation Place is a lodging/housing place (sibling of Dining Place and Meeting Room Place under Place), whereas B's Conference hall is a large meeting venue (sibling of Session room and Building). They denote different kinds of places in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Member PC' is a Person who reviews contributions (comment 'Reviewer', property reviewes -> Contribution), i.e. a program-committee member. B's 'Webmaster' is an Organizator responsible for the website, a sibling of General Chair and Program Chair. Different roles in the conference organisation; no subsumption or overlap.

A's Paper is a conference submission/document with authors, topics, reviews and acceptance states (Accepted/Rejected/Pending Paper). B's Viza is a sibling of Submission, Review, Form, Invitation letter, Payment document etc. under Document, i.e. a visa/travel document, not a scientific paper. Same parent Document but different intended instances, so unrelated.

A's Review is a conference document (a review of a contribution, with properties linking it to a reviewed contribution). B's Call is a call for manuscripts/papers/reviews issued by chairs, with properties for event, deadlines and instructions. They denote different concepts: a review artefact versus a call announcement, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the conference event itself: cmt's Conference is the central event entity with conference-level properties (dates, members, submissions), and confOf's Conference is a working event subclass alongside Tutorial and Workshop, i.e. the same conference event concept. The labels and intended instances coincide.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (a paper is submitted to a venue/proceedings), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives a talk/presentation). Different domains (contribution vs person) and different ranges (volume vs activity/item), so the relations are not equivalent.

A Bid in cmt is a reviewer's expressed willingness/score to review a paper (domain Reviewer, range Bid, linked from Paper via has Bid). A Conference Session in edas is a temporal event/venue grouping within a conference that relates to documents and people. Their intended instances and roles in the conference domain do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (author -> paper), while B's has authors relates a Conference document to a Person (document -> person). They are inverse in direction and have different domains/ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Non speaker' is a subclass of Delegate (a conference attendee who does not present), while B's 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person covering chairs, committee members and webmaster. They denote different concepts: an attendee role vs. an organiser role, with no overlap in intended instances.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to a Conference Member (a person/role on the organising committee), while B's holded_by relates a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD (the organising body/society). The ranges denote different kinds of entities (person vs. organisation), so the two properties are not equivalent.

Sponsor (a person/org funding the conference) and Organizator (a person organizing the conference, with children General Chair, Program Chair, etc.) denote different roles in the conference domain; they share only the parent Person and are not synonyms.

A 'Coffee break' is a scheduled conference activity (a social/refreshment event under Conference activity), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (under Place, alongside Hotel and Main office). They denote different kinds of things—an event versus a location—so they are not equivalent.

Both denote the money a participant pays to register for the conference: A's 'Conference fees' is a Fee subclass, and B's 'Registration fee' is a Fee subclass whose children are the various attendee registration fees (author, member, nonmember, student). The intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

A's Reception is a social/non-academic event (sibling of Excursion under Social Event), while B's Technic activity is a conference activity (sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Registration, Coffee break). They belong to different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts; the only overlap is that B's sibling 'Coctail reception' is a social event, not a technic activity.

A's `writes` goes Author -> Contribution (author writes a paper), while B's `is writen by` goes Item -> Person (an item is written by a person). The directions are opposite: `writes` is the inverse of `is writen by`, and a property is not equivalent to its inverse. Even ignoring direction, the domain/range classes (Author/Contribution vs Item/Person) do not coincide, so the two relations are not the same.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Person in cmt), while B 'Information for participants' is a conference document (subclass of Conference document). They denote entirely different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee (domain Committee member, range Committee), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (domain Conference, range Person). They differ in both domain and range and are not inverses of each other, so they denote different relations.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a registered conference attendee (a Person who has registered, with child Paid applicant), whereas B 'Author' is a Speaker who writes papers (submits papers, obtains awards, receives notifications). Registration status and authorship are different roles in the conference domain; neither subsumes the other.

cmt:Paper is the general document class for conference submissions (parent Document, children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version, with properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To). ekaw:Evaluated Paper is a much narrower class deep in the hierarchy (Document > Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper > Evaluated Paper) whose children are Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper, i.e. only papers that have been evaluated. Every Evaluated Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is an Evaluated Paper, so cmt:Paper is more general and is subsumed by the ekaw class.

Both properties relate an event to the place/location where it occurs: edas hasLocation has domain Conference Event and range Place, ekaw heldIn has domain Event and range Location. Conference Event is a kind of Event and Place is a kind of Location, so the intended relation (event held at a location) coincides; the labels differ but the domain/range contexts agree.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (person-to-event membership). B's has_an_organizing_committee relates a Conference volume to an Organizing committee (event-to-committee composition). Different domain, range, and direction of relation; not equivalent.

A's 'max Papers' is a datatype property giving an integer limit on the number of papers a Program Committee Member can handle. B's 'topic Covered By' is an object property linking a Research Topic to the Event or Paper that covers it. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Program Committee Member vs Research Topic), range (int vs Event/Paper), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an Administrator action that opens the bidding phase for a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference). B's 'invites co reviewers' is a Reviewer action inviting another Reviewer to co-review a paper (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer). Different agents, different targets, and different intended effects; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering all people contributing to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors, committee members, reviewers, etc.). B's 'Author cd proceedings included' is a narrow subclass of Author, specifically an author whose paper is included in the conference proceedings CD. Every instance of B is a conference contributor (an author contributing to the conference), but not vice versa, so A is more general and B is subsumed by A.

A 'Committee member' is a Person role in the conference organisation (parent Person, children Chair/Co chair, related to Committee via has members/was a member of). B 'Accommodation Place' is a subtype of Place (siblings Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), i.e. a physical location. Different kinds and domains; no overlap.

A's Conference is the event itself (has dates, administrators, conference members, virtual meeting settings), while B's Contribution is a submitted work (Paper/Poster/Short paper) with abstract, title, keywords, authors and reviews. The concepts denote different things in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Conference document is a broad category covering calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc., while ekaw's Document is also broad but its children (Abstract, Flyer, Multi author Volume, Paper, Programme Brochure, Review, Web Site) are specific document types. Conference document includes non-document items like Call for paper and Conference www, and its properties (contributes, has a date of issue, has authors) differ from Document's (author Of, has Updated Version, updated Version Of, written By). The two overlap but neither is strictly equivalent; Conference document appears more general in the conference-organisation sense, so it subsumes Document.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an Administrator action that assigns papers to the conference (domain Administrator, range Conference). B's 'related To Paper' links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (domain Paper Presentation, range Accepted Paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's reviewOfPaper relates a Review to the Paper it reviews (domain Review, range Paper). B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document that is presented (domain Speaker, range Document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

confOf Topic is a subject area of contributions/events (dealsWith, expertOn, hasTopic), while sigkdd Document is a written artefact (Abstract, Paper, Review) presented by a Speaker and submitted by a Deadline. Their instances and roles in the conference domain do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A is a full version of a conference paper (a document type under Paper), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a video cassette player) under Audiovisual equipment. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's property records the issue/publication date of a Conference document (domain: Conference document, range: date), while B's property records the start date-time of a Conference Event (domain: Conference Event, range: dateTime). Different domains (document vs. event) and different intended meanings (issue date vs. event start), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Poster Paper' is a kind of conference paper (a document/contribution), while B 'LCD projector' is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. equipment) and share no intended instances.

A's 'belong to a conference volume' links an Important dates entity to a Conference volume (a deadline/event belongs to a proceedings volume), whereas B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (a paper is presented by a person). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who provides sponsorship), while B's 'payed by' links a Registration fee to a Person (who pays the fee). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same property.

University is an Organization (a type of institution) in confOf, while Meal Menu is a Document (a menu artefact) in edas. They share no meaning, no properties, and no common parent; the only overlap is the generic word 'menu'/'university' being absent entirely. Clearly unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in cmt), while B 'Mailing list' is a document artefact (subclass of Document in iasted). They denote entirely different kinds of entities and share no intended instances.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (event-to-event, symmetric co-occurrence), while ekaw's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (location-to-event). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered early and paid), while B is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been published). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person/registration vs. document/publication) and share no intended instances.

A Program Committee Member is a specific kind of committee member (a member of the program committee), while B Committee member is the general class of members of any committee. The A class has additional constraints and properties (max Papers, member Of Program Committee) and is a subclass of Conference Member/Person, whereas B is a direct subclass of Person with broader children (Chair, Co chair). Thus A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

Sponsor (a person or organization providing financial support) and Webmaster (a technical role within the organizing committee) are distinct roles in the conference domain. Sponsor is a direct subclass of Person, while Webmaster is a subclass of Organizator, indicating different conceptual categories. No subsumption or overlap exists between them.

Both properties relate a person who reviews to the Paper being reviewed, in the same direction (person -> Paper). 'is Reviewing' has domain Conference Chair/Reviewer/Session Chair/TPC Member and range Paper; 'reviewer Of Paper' has domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper. The domains are both reviewer-capable persons (the EDAS domain is broader, including chairs who may also review), and the range is identical (Paper). In the conference domain these denote the same reviewing relation, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A 'Possible Reviewer' is a person role in the conference domain (a Person who may review papers, parent of PC Member, involved in review relations), while B 'Value added tax' is a kind of Tax under Money. The entities belong to entirely different domains and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

Attendee in edas is a generic participant in a conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles under Person), while Webmaster in sigkdd is a specific organizing role responsible for the website, a subclass of Organizator alongside General Chair and Program Chair. A webmaster is an organizer, not a generic attendee, and the two classes have different intended instances and different positions in their hierarchies.

Company in confOf is an organization (sibling of University, subclass of Organization) that participates in the conference, whereas Bank transfer in iasted is a payment document (subclass of Payment document, sibling of Cheque) used to pay fees. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

confOf's Person is a broad class covering all people (Administrator, Author, Chair, Participant, etc.), while ekaw's Conference Participant is a subclass of ekaw's Person restricted to those attending the conference. Thus confOf Person is more general and Conference Participant is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' relates an Administrator to a Conference (a mailing/manifest action), while B's 'presentation Of Paper' relates an Individual Presentation to an Abstract/Paper (the paper being presented). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Document is a broad class whose children are conference artefacts (Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, Meal Menu) and which is linked to events/persons via has Related Document / relates To. In iasted, Item is a general physical/abstract object class (children: Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle) with properties about being given, paid for, equipped, made from, etc. The iasted Document is a child of Item, so Item is a much broader category (equipment, vehicles, money-related things) and does not denote the same concept as edas Document. They are not equivalent, nor does one clearly subsume the other in the intended domain.

A's Programme is a conference programme document (sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set; linked to a Conference Event via belongs To Event / has Programme). B's Flyer is a promotional leaflet published by an Organisation (sibling of Programme Brochure, Web Site, Multi author Volume). Although both are Documents, a programme and a flyer are different artefacts; ekaw even has a separate Programme Brochure class, so Flyer is not the equivalent of Programme.

A's max Choice is a capacity/limit property of a Social/Working event (range positiveInteger, comment confTool), while B's done till is a deadline date property (range date). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'One conference day' is a temporal unit (a single day of the conference, under Conference days in the Time branch), while B 'Organizing Committee member' is a person role (under Organizator in the Person branch). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a conference submission/review artefact (children Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper, properties is Reviewed By, is Written By, has Topic), while B's Flyer is a promotional document (sibling of Programme Brochure, Web Site; only property publisher Of). They share the Document parent but denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

OC Member in ekaw is a Conference Participant who is a member of the organising committee (parent Conference Participant, child OC Chair, siblings PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.), i.e. an organising-committee role. IASTED member in iasted is a Delegate who is a member of the IASTED organisation (parent Delegate, siblings IASTED non member, Speaker, Listener, etc.), i.e. a membership status of an attendee. The intended instances do not coincide: one is an organiser role, the other an attendee membership type, so the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person (a human attending the conference), while B 'Break Event' is a Non Academic Event (a scheduled break such as a coffee break). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person vs. event) and cannot denote the same concept.
Both denote the same conference-domain concept: a submitted paper/contribution. Labels and context (author, review, conference) agree.

confOf Participant is a general person role (parent of Member, Regular, Student; has early Registration property) covering anyone taking part in the conference, while iasted Sponsor is a specific funding role under Person, sibling of Delegate. A sponsor is not a participant role in the same sense, and the two classes have different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to an email address string, while B's 'Name' links a Person to a name string. Although both are Person->string datatype properties, they denote different attributes (email vs. name), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'was a steering committee of' links a Steering committee to a Conference volume (a committee-to-event relation), while B's 'organisedBy' links an Event to an Organisation or Person (an event-to-organiser relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class whose children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, Conference Chair, etc., and it is linked to Conference via member Of Conference. Reviewer in edas is a specific role (a person who reviews papers, with review-history and reviewing properties). The cmt class is strictly more general than the edas Reviewer, so Conference Member subsumes Reviewer, not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Antennas Topic' is a research subject area under Topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details; B's 'has Administrative Event' links a Working event to an Administrative event (a sub-event). Different domain, range and meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person (a person who authors papers), while B 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a subclass of Award (a type of prize). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (people vs. awards) and share no intended instances.

A's Author is a general person role who writes papers (has Related Paper, is Written By). B's 'Author of paper student' is a narrower subclass of Author (path Person > Speaker > Author > Author of paper student), specifically a student author. Thus A's Author is more general and B's class is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to the Location where it is held; B's 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place/Time where they are present. Different domains (Event vs Person) and different ranges (Location vs Place/Time), so the relations are not the same.

A's 'end Review' relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the chair ends a review), while B's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to a person/role who reviews it. They have different domains (Program Committee Chair vs Paper), different ranges (Review vs Conference Chair/Reviewer/Session Chair/TPC Member), and opposite directions of the reviewing relation; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference contributor' is a Person who contributes to a conference (author, speaker, participant), while B 'Transport vehicle' is an Item such as a car or bus used for transportation. They share no meaning, no properties, and belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Item).

cmt's Paper is the general document class for submissions (with children Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version, and properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To), while edas's Active Paper is a specific lifecycle state of a Paper (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn/Pending/Published Paper, with only has Rating). Active Paper is strictly narrower than cmt Paper, so cmt Paper subsumes edas Active Paper.

A's `reviews` links a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's `writes` links an Author to the Contribution they authored (domain Author, range Contribution). Different subject and different meaning (reviewing vs authoring), so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Co chair to a Committee (a role-holding relation within the conference organization), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or presentation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to the Contribution they review (domain Member PC, range Contribution), i.e. the reviewing act by a person. B's `has Rating` relates an Active Paper to its Review Rating (domain Active Paper, range Review Rating), i.e. a paper's rating value. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; not equivalent.

Associated Chair is a specific conference-organisation role (a chair who is associated with the conference, sibling of Conference Chair, PC Chair, Author, Reviewer) under Chairman/Conference Member. Scholar in confOf is a generic person category (price category - scholar) with sibling roles like Administrator, Assistant, Author, Participant, Volunteer, and a property study At (Scholar -> University). The two denote different concepts: one is a committee/chair role, the other a generic academic person category, so they are not equivalent.

Program Committee in cmt is a specific committee with members, while Committee in Conference is the general committee class with subclasses Organizing committee, Program committee, Steering committee. The cmt Program Committee corresponds to the Conference Program committee subclass, so it is strictly narrower than the general Committee class.

A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee (a group), while B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (an individual member). Different ranges (Committee vs Person) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a Conference-level datatype property giving the number of reviews per paper (domain Conference, range int). B's 'max Choice' is a Social/Working event property giving a maximum number of choices (domain Social event, Working event, range positiveInteger). Different domains, different ranges, different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person (a human role in the conference, with subclasses Active/Passive participant), while B 'Conference Dinner' is a Meal Event within the conference event hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

Rejected Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that was rejected), while sigkdd's Paper is the general class of all papers. Rejected Paper is strictly more specific, so it is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

A's Associated Chair is a conference-organisation role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member who helps chair the event), while B's Conference Hiker is a subtype of Delegate (an attendee/participant category in the iasted ontology). The two denote different concepts: one is an organiser role, the other an attendee role, so they are not equivalent.

A's Organization is an institution (sponsor/provider of sponsorships, with subclasses Academia/Government/Industry/NGO), while B's Speaker is a person role (subclass of Person, with Author/Invited Speaker children, related to Document via presentation). Different kinds of entities with no overlap.

In iasted, Reviewer is a subclass of Speaker (a role a delegate can take), while in sigkdd Author is a subclass of Speaker with properties submit/obtain/notification and children Author of paper. A reviewer and an author are distinct roles in the conference domain; the shared parent Speaker does not make them equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A's relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to its Paper Presentation (domain Accepted Paper, range Paper Presentation), while B's hasEvent links an Event to a sub-Event (domain Event, range Event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference Trip' is a social event (an excursion, sibling of Conference Banquet) within the conference, while B's 'Conference' is the whole conference event with city, start/end dates, name, and held-by relation. A trip is a part/activity of a conference, not the conference itself, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (a conference with a two-level programme committee structure), a subclass of Conference. B's 'Conference Hiker' is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. a person attending a conference. A conference and a person/attendee are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated despite both containing the word 'conference'.

cmt's Conference Member is a subclass of Person (path Person > Conference Member) restricted to people involved in a conference (authors, chairs, PC members, reviewers), while ekaw's Person is the general superclass of all people (including students, agency staff, participants). Conference Member is therefore strictly narrower than Person, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (domain Conference, range Country), while locationOf relates a Location to an Event (domain Location, range Event). They differ in both domain and range and are inverse in direction (Conference->Country vs Location->Event), so they are not the same relation.
A's title is the title of a Paper; B's hasStreet is the street address of Contact Information. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'follows' relates Administrative events to Administrative events (a temporal/ordering relation between events), while ekaw's 'organised By' relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the agent organising the event). Different domain, different range, different meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (a person leading the committee), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (the person presenting the document). Different domains (Committee vs Document), different ranges (Chair vs Speaker), and different intended relations; they are not the same property.

Both are subclasses of Paper, but 'Paper Full Version' in cmt contrasts with 'Paper Abstract' (a full-length vs. abstract version of a submission), while 'Regular Paper' in ekaw is a paper category contrasting with demo, poster, workshop, industrial, camera-ready, submitted papers. They overlap in that a full version is typically a regular (non-demo/poster) paper, but the intended distinctions differ, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a subclass of Conference applicant (a Person role), while B 'Conference' is the event itself with children Single/Two Level Conference and properties like paper Due On, has Member, etc. They denote entirely different concepts (person role vs. event), so they are unrelated.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper), while B's `provided By` relates a Sponsorship to an Organization. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A Welcome Talk is a talk event (a speech given at the start of a conference), while B Introduction is a conference activity that has a child 'Introduction of speaker' and sits alongside Welcome address, Lecture, Presentation, etc. Both are opening/plenary-type events, but A is specifically a talk and B is a broader activity category that may include the speaker introduction; they overlap without coinciding, so related rather than equivalent.

A's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to the Conference Event it belongs to (domain Programme, range Conference Event). B's 'technically Organised By' is a sub-property of 'organised By' relating an event/conference to the agent that technically organises it. The two relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to a paper), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (authoring a paper). Different domain, range, and intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B 'Presenter university' is a Building/Place (a university where a presenter is located) in iasted. They denote entirely different concepts (person role vs. physical location), so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (sibling of Extended abstract) in the Conference ontology, i.e. a full research paper. B's Demo Paper is a specific subtype of Paper in ekaw, alongside Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc. A's Paper corresponds to ekaw's Regular Paper, not to Demo Paper; the two denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Tutorial is a kind of scientific event/individual presentation in the conference programme, while B Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Item/Audiovisual equipment) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A Reviewer is a Person who evaluates submissions (has review expertise/preferences, belongs to reviewers, invites co-reviewers), while B's Invited Speaker is a Speaker who gives a talk at the conference. They are distinct roles in the conference domain with no subsumption or overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a call/announcement text, sibling of Call for paper and Conference announcement), while B's 'Workshop' is an academic event type (sibling of Talk Event, Paper Presentation). A document and an event type denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a paper-like entity to a topic, but confOf's dealsWith has domain Contribution (papers) and range Topic, while ekaw's coversTopic has domain Event, Paper and range Research Topic. The domains differ (Contribution vs Event/Paper) and the ranges are different topic classes, so they are not the same relation; they overlap in the paper-to-topic sense, hence related rather than equivalent.

A is a document type (an abstract for an invited talk, a subclass of Abstract under Document), while B is a conference activity (a tutorial lecture, a subclass of Lecture under Activity). They belong to different top-level branches (Document vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things: a written abstract versus an event/lecture. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (sessions scheduled in parallel), while B's 'volume Contains Paper' relates a proceedings volume to a paper. Different domain, range, and meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A Session Chair is a person who chairs a conference session and is involved in initiating calls and reviewing papers (siblings: Conference Chair, Reviewer, TPC Member). B Speaker is a person who gives a presentation (children: Author, Invited Speaker; properties: presentation/presentationed by). The roles are distinct: chairing a session is not the same as speaking/presenting, and neither class subsumes the other.
hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country, while obtain relates a Person to an Item; different domain, range and meaning, so they are not the same relation.

An Organizational Meeting (a conference event such as a committee/business meeting) and a Plenary lecture (a type of lecture activity) denote different concepts; they share no parent, sibling, or property context indicating equivalence.

Accommodation Place is a specific kind of Place (a place where one stays, sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), whereas ekaw's Location is the general notion of a location at which events are held (held In / location Of). Every accommodation place is a location, but not every location is an accommodation place, so Accommodation Place is strictly narrower than Location.

Subject Area (cmt) is a topic classification of papers, the range of 'has Subject Area' (Paper -> Subject Area). Speaker (sigkdd) is a Person subtype who gives presentations. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances or properties.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome of a submission), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving a prize). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Workshop Paper is a kind of Paper (a document, sibling of Conference Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Document) and denote different concepts: an event versus a document artefact.

A's 'lists Event' is an object property linking a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event (it lists events), while B's 'Start of conference' is a datatype property giving a Conference's start date/time. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

An Accepted contribution is a reviewed contribution that has been accepted, whereas Submission in iasted is the general document submitted (with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript). Every accepted contribution is a submission, but submissions also include rejected/initial versions, so Accepted contribution is strictly narrower: subsumed_by.

A's Personal History is a container of a person's publication and review records (children: Personal Publication History, Personal Review History), whereas B's Submission is a document type in the conference submission workflow (path Item > Document > Submission, children Initial/Final manuscript). They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference event/activity), while B Author information form is a document/form used for author details. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Document/Form) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference Venue Place in edas is a generic place for a conference venue, while Presenter house in iasted is a specific building type for presenters' accommodation. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A Call is a request for submissions (with children Call For Papers/Reviews/Manuscripts, and properties linking it to an Academic Event, submission deadlines and instructions, and chairs who initiate it). B Deadline is a point in time (parent Time, children like Submissions deadline, Camera ready deadline) with property done till -> date. A Call is not a time point; it is an event/activity that has deadlines. They overlap only in that a Call is associated with submission deadlines, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document addressed to attendees (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.), while B's 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a document aimed at session chairs. Different audiences and purposes; no subsumption or overlap.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Conference airport is a physical building/place (sibling of Conference building, Conference hotel, etc.). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. location) and are not equivalent.

cmt:name is a datatype property with domain Conference and Person, while edas:hasName is restricted to Conference (comment 'Conference Full Name'). The cmt property is broader, covering both conferences and persons, so it subsumes the edas property rather than being equivalent to it.

Acceptance is a decision outcome on a paper (sibling of Rejection under Decision), while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B 'Full day tour' is a post-conference social activity (sibling of Departure). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a human role: active/passive participants, reviewers, committee members), whereas B's 'Scientific Event' is a subclass of Event (an occurrence: Conference, Workshop, Session, Track). One denotes people, the other denotes events, so their instances cannot coincide; they are unrelated.

A's 'has gender' is a datatype property of Person capturing a person's gender, while B's 'has Last Name' captures a person's surname. They relate different attributes of Person and are not the same relation.

Listener in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (an attendee who listens, sibling of Speaker, Session chair, etc.), whereas Organizator in sigkdd is a subclass of Person whose children are General Chair, Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, etc. (an organiser role). They denote different concepts: an attendee/listener vs an organiser, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' is an Administrator->Conference property (an administrative action of printing mailing manifests for a conference), while B's 'write' is a Person->Item property (a person writing an item such as a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Rejected Paper' is a specific status of a paper (a Paper that was rejected), while B's 'Paper' is the general class of all papers (with children like Submitted Paper, Conference Paper, etc.). Every rejected paper is a paper, but not every paper is rejected, so Rejected Paper is strictly narrower and subsumed by Paper.

A's Associated Chair is a Person/Chairman role (a conference committee member who chairs), while B's Regular author is a Conference contribution/contributor role (an author of a regular contribution). Different domains (person role vs. contribution role) and different meanings; not equivalent.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's Price is a datatype property linking a Registration fee to an int (a monetary amount). They have different domains (Person vs Registration fee), different ranges (string vs int), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B Mailing list is a kind of Document (sibling of Form, Review, Submission, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Item/Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic's preference in a review), while B's 'reviewes' links a PC member to a Contribution (a reviewer reviewing a paper). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

A's property links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (a role/committee relation within the conference organisation), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or presentation). Different domains (Track workshop chair vs Person) and different ranges (Conference part vs Activity/Item), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity) in confOf, while Presenter is a subtype of Author (a person role) in edas. They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (event vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.

Company (a for-profit organization) and Government Organization are distinct organization types; both are siblings under Organization in their respective ontologies, but they denote different concepts, not synonyms.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings). B's `event On List` relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site on which it is listed (domain Event, range Programme Brochure/Web Site). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's assignedByAdministrator relates a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned the review (domain Reviewer, range Administrator). B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (the talk/slides presented). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.
A is a specific type of tax (Value added tax) under Tax, while B is a sponsor fee under Fee; they denote different financial concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

Both classes represent the general notion of a document in the conference domain. In cmt, Document is the parent of Paper and Review; in ekaw, Document is the parent of Abstract, Flyer, Multi author Volume, Paper, Programme Brochure, Review, and Web Site. The ekaw class is more granular but the intended meaning is the same general document concept, and both are used as the range of person-document relations (has Conflict Of Interest in cmt; author Of / written By in ekaw). Thus they are equivalent.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract, while B's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author. They relate different kinds of entities (abstract vs. author) and are not inverses or synonyms, so they are unrelated.

A's 'registration Due On' is a datatype property of Conference giving the registration deadline date/time; B's 'Date' is a datatype property of Deadline giving the date of a deadline. Both are dateTime-valued deadline-related properties, but they are not the same relation: A attaches the registration deadline directly to a Conference, while B attaches a date to a generic Deadline entity. They overlap in meaning (both express a deadline date) but differ in domain and specificity, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is a conference submission (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by Author, reviewed by PC members, has title/abstract/keywords). ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd is the organisation/society that designs deadlines, holds conferences and searches sponsors. Different intended instances, so the classes are unrelated.

A is a role/class of people (a chair who is associated with the conference, under Person > Chairman), while B is a kind of conference contribution/document (an invited talk, under Conference document > Conference contribution). They denote different kinds of entities (person role vs. document type) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper (the title of a paper), while B's Name of conference is a datatype property of Conference (the name of a conference). They apply to different classes and denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (the inviter), while B's 'send' relates a Person to an Item (e.g. a submission or message). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'accepted By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person who authors a conference contribution/paper: A's 'Contribution co author' is a subclass of 'Regular author' (an author of a conference contribution), and B's 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person representing an author of a paper. The intended instances coincide (authors of papers/contributions), and the differing parent paths (Regular author vs Person) reflect only the different upper-level structure of the two ontologies, not a difference in meaning.

A's 'written By' links a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'is paid with' links Money to an Item (payment instrument). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to the people who review it (Reviewer, TPC Member, etc.), while B's 'is used by' links an Item to a Person in a generic usage sense. Both relate a document-like entity to a person, but the review relation is a specific kind of use, so they overlap without being equivalent.

A's hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property of Call giving textual submission instructions (range string), while B's done_till is a datatype property of Deadline giving a date by which something must be done. Different domains (Call vs Deadline), different ranges (string vs date), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a person role (a kind of Conference contributor, sibling of Regular author), while B's 'Presenter city' is a kind of City (sibling of Conference city, Sponsor city, Trip city). They denote different concepts: a person role versus a location, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a conference-domain relation about reviewing), while B's property links a Scholar to a University (an academic affiliation relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but 'has the first name' relates a person to their given name, while 'has Biography' relates a person to a biographical text. They denote different attributes of a person, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Industrial Session' is a kind of Conference Session (a track/session type within a conference programme), while B 'Speaker lecture' is a kind of Session under Lecture in the iasted activity hierarchy, denoting a lecture given by a speaker. Although both sit under a Session node, their intended instances differ: an industrial session is a thematic conference session, not a speaker's lecture. No synonymy or subsumption holds.

ekaw's partOf is a general mereological/structural property with unspecified domain and range, while iasted's sign is a specific relation from a Person to an Item (e.g. signing a document). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's Review is a conference document that reviews a contribution (domain/range: Review -> Reviewed contribution, and Reviewed contribution -> Review). B's Meal Menu is a document attached to a Meal Event (has Menu: Meal Event -> Meal Menu; is Menu Of: Meal Menu -> Meal Event). They share only the generic Document parent; their intended instances and relations are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

A's assignReviewer relates an Administrator (domain) to a Reviewer (range), i.e. the act of assigning a reviewer to a paper. B's has_a_review_reference_or_expertise relates a Reviewer (domain) to review expertise/preference topics (range), i.e. a reviewer's stated expertise or preference. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection under Decision) in the conference domain, while B's Van is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi under Transport vehicle). Different domains and meanings; no overlap.

A Workshop is a type of conference part/event (a small specialised meeting held alongside a main conference), while an Industrial Session is a session within a conference programme (a slot in the schedule, typically industry-oriented). They differ in kind: Workshop is an event type, Industrial Session is a session type; neither subsumes the other and their instances do not coincide.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a specific chair role under Chairman/Conference Member, while Conference contributor (Conference) is a broad superclass of all people contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants, etc.). The chair role is not the same concept as the general contributor class; they are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a way a reference alignment would record.

University in confOf is a specific kind of Organization (sibling of Company), while ekaw's Organisation is the general superclass with children Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher. A University is an Organisation, but not every Organisation is a University, so University is strictly more specific: subsumed_by.

A's hasCostAmount is a datatype property of Sponsorship (the cost amount of a sponsorship), while B's Price is a datatype property of Registration fee (the price of a registration fee). They relate different kinds of things (sponsorship cost vs. registration fee price) in different domains, so they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Poster Session is a kind of Session within a scientific event. A poster session is a component/activity of a conference, not the conference itself, so the classes denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter of a paper), while B's 'is given to' links an Item to a Person (recipient of an award/item). Different domain, range and meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Demo Session is a session within a scientific event, sibling of Conference Session, Poster Session, Regular Session and Workshop Session. A conference is not a session and a demo session is not a conference; the shared word 'conference' in 'Conference Session' does not make them the same concept.

A's Accommodation Place is a generic lodging place (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place under Place). B's Conference airport is a Building subtype, specifically an airport used for a conference, not a lodging/accommodation place. Different intended instances; no subsumption or overlap.

Both are direct subclasses of Person representing people involved in a conference. cmt's Conference Member has children Author, Reviewer, PC Member, chairs; ekaw's Conference Participant has children Presenter, PC Chair, Session Chair, Paper Author, etc. The intended instances coincide: persons participating in a conference. The differing children (e.g. Early/Late Registered Participant) are specialisations, not evidence of a different concept.

A's Conference is the event itself (has a name, has a Conference volume, has Conference proceedings, has a Publisher, has a Topic). B's Conference state is a state of a conference participant (sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state under State), i.e. a status/role in the conference process, not the conference event. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

A 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (a social gathering such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B 'Deadline' is a subclass of Time (a point in time such as submission or camera-ready deadline). They denote different concepts with different parents, children and properties, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a whole document (parent Document, siblings Review, has authors, decisions, subject areas, bids), while B's Abstract is a part of a contribution (parent Extended abstract, part-of Paper/Poster/Presentation). The Abstract is a component of a paper, not the paper itself, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'paper ID' is a datatype property linking a Paper to an unsignedLong identifier, while B's 'write' is an object property linking a Person to an Item (authorship relation). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Paper vs Person), range (unsignedLong vs Item), and meaning (identifier vs authorship), so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) in confOf, while B's Technic activity is a technical conference activity (sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Registration) in iasted. They denote different kinds of conference events and do not coincide.

A's property links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (organisational role assignment), while B's expertOn links a PC member to a Topic (expertise). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.
Both denote the conference paper/contribution artefact; labels Paper and Contribution are synonyms in this domain and their contexts (authored document submitted to a conference) agree.

A's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (a specific role), while B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (any member). Different domains (Committee vs Conference), different ranges (Chair vs Person), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference hotel' is a Building (a lodging venue where attendees stay), while B 'Conference hall' is a Place (the room/venue where the conference takes place). Both are conference-related places, but they denote different kinds of venue: a hotel is not a hall. They overlap only in being conference locations, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper), while B's 'is Initiated By' relates a Call to people who initiate it (chairs/TPC members). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; not the same relation.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document (path Document > Paper) and is the specific artefact that is reviewed, accepted, assigned to reviewers, and has authors. In edas, Document is a broad class whose children include Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set and Meal Menu, and which is related to events, conferences, sessions and persons. Thus edas Document is strictly more general than cmt Paper; Paper is subsumed by Document, not equivalent to it.

A's Form is a Document subtype (a form document such as registration/author information form), while B's Author is a Person/Speaker subtype (a person who submits papers). Different kinds of entities entirely; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people/committee members), while B's has_workshops relates a Conference volume to its Workshops (events). Different domain/range kinds and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string email address, while B's send is an object property linking a Person to an Item (e.g. sending a paper). They relate different kinds of things (string vs Item) and denote different relations, so they are not equivalent.

Research Topic in ekaw is a subject area that events and papers cover (covers Topic: Event, Paper -> Research Topic), whereas Conference in sigkdd is a concrete event with city, start/end dates, name, and held-by relation to ACM SIGKDD. A topic is not a conference; the entities denote different concepts and share no properties or context.

Conference Chair is a person role in the conference organisation (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member who chairs the conference), while Sponsor in iasted is a Person subtype denoting an entity that funds the conference. They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap, so they are unrelated.

Conference participant is a general class for anyone participating in a conference (with subclasses Active/Passive conference participant), while Session Chair is a specific role held by a conference participant. Session Chair is therefore strictly more specific, so Conference participant subsumes Session Chair.

A's title is the title of a Paper (a document's name), while B's has Street is the street address of an Organization or Person. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they share only the datatype string.

Chairman is a role/person class (a Person who chairs, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair) in cmt, while Session is an event class (a Scientific Event with subclasses Conference Session, Demo Session, etc.) in ekaw. They denote different kinds of things (a person role vs. an event) and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.), while B's 'Presenter city' is a subclass of City denoting a city where a presenter is located. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs City) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'related To Event' links an Accepted Paper to its Paper Presentation (a paper-to-presentation relation), while B's 'awarded by' links an Award to the body that granted it. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Industrial Session is a kind of conference session (an event in the programme), while Hotel is a kind of place/venue. They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (event vs. location) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's hasCostCurrency is a datatype property of Sponsorship giving the currency of a sponsorship cost, while B's Name_of_sponsor is a datatype property of Sponzor giving the sponsor's name. They relate different attributes (currency vs. name) of different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Presentation is a conference activity (an event such as a talk or video presentation), while B's Speaker is a person role (a person who gives a presentation). They belong to different top-level branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'paper In Volume' relates a paper to the volume/proceedings it appears in, while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (the talk given by the speaker). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Contribution is a general submission entity (children Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by Author, reviewed by PC member, has title/abstract/keywords). ekaw's Abstract is a specific document type under Document, sibling of Paper, with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and is linked to presentations. Contribution is broader and subsumes Abstract, not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'payed by' links a Registration fee to a Person (payer). Different domains and different intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's readByReviewer relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the act of reviewing a paper), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the act of presenting a document). The domains (Paper vs Document) and especially the ranges (Reviewer vs Speaker) denote different roles and different relations, so they are not equivalent.

edas:relatesTo is a broad Document-to-entity relation whose range includes Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session and Person, while sigkdd:presentationed_by is a narrower Document-to-Speaker relation. A presentation is one specific way a document relates to a person, so relatesTo is strictly more general and subsumes presentationed_by; they are not equivalent.

The two properties are inverses of each other: 'is paid by' goes from Money to Person (a payment is made by a person), while 'pay' goes from Person to Registration fee (a person pays a fee). They relate the same kinds of things but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise), while B's 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place/Time (attendance). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person attending it; B's is_prepared_by links an Item (e.g. a paper/contribution) to the Person who prepared it. Different domains (event vs item) and different intended relations (attendance vs authorship/preparation), so they are not equivalent.

A is a registration fee category for authors who are also attendees and book registration (Author attendee book registration fee), while B is a registration fee category for non-members (Registration Non Member). They denote different fee categories with different intended instances; neither subsumes the other.

In ekaw, Web Site is a specific kind of Document (a conference web site that lists events and is published by an organisation), while in iasted Document is a broad class of conference items (forms, invitations, submissions, reviews, etc.). Web Site is therefore a narrower concept subsumed by the general iasted Document, not equivalent to it.

A 'Poster Paper' is a kind of document/paper (a submission type), while B 'Registation deadline' is a time/deadline concept. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Time) and denote different things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (a reviewing/assignment relation), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (a talk/presentation relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's hasProgramme links a Conference Event to a Programme (the scientific programme of the conference), while B's eventOnList links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (publicity/listing artefacts). The ranges denote different concepts (scientific programme vs. brochure/web site), so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a part-whole relation within a conference's proceedings), while B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Conference part vs Person; Conference volume vs Conference), so the properties denote different relations.
A's University is an Organization (a conference venue/affiliation), while B's Value added tax is a kind of Tax under Money; they share no concept, instances, or properties, so they are unrelated.
