A 'Conference part' is a component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) that has a name, chair, and topic, and is part of a conference volume. B 'Conference Event' is a broader event concept with attendees, location, programme, and start/end times, whose children are Academic and Non Academic Event. A conference part is a kind of conference event, but the edas class is more general (it also covers non-academic events and has scheduling/location properties absent from A), so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, choices), while B's 'Wireless Communications Topic' is a subject-area topic under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper, specifically the full version of a paper (sibling of Paper Abstract). In ekaw, 'Paper' is the general class covering all paper types (camera ready, conference, demo, poster, submitted, etc.). A full version paper is a kind of paper, so Paper Full Version is strictly more specific than ekaw's Paper; the two are not equivalent.

A's 'has VAT' is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving the value-added tax amount (a tax on an event), while B's 'Currency' is a datatype property of a Registration fee giving the currency unit of the fee. They relate different subjects (event vs. fee) to different kinds of values (tax amount vs. currency code), so they are not the same relation.

A 'Short paper' is a short contribution (sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution), while B 'Abstract' is a document type (sibling of Paper and Review under Document). A short paper is a full submission, not an abstract; the concepts denote different artefacts in the conference domain.

confOf's writes relates Author to Contribution (a paper), and iasted's sign relates Person to Item (a paper/contribution). Both express the authorship relation between a person/author and a written contribution, so they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

A's Meta Reviewer is a subclass of Reviewer (a person role), while B's Review is a conference document (the review text itself). They denote different kinds of entities: a person role vs. a document, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the outcome of reviewing a paper), while B's is_present_in relates a Person to a Place/Time (attendance at an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a person attending a conference without an active role (sibling of 'Active conference participant', under 'Conference participant'). B 'Full day tour' is a post-conference social activity (under 'Activity after conference', sibling of 'Departure'). They belong to different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them; B's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation/Person that organised it. Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has parts' relates a Conference volume to its Conference part (a structural decomposition of a volume into parts), while B's 'has Programme' relates a Conference Event to its Programme (an event's schedule). The domains (Conference volume vs Conference Event) and ranges (Conference part vs Programme) differ, so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's 'assigned To' relates a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while B's 'searched by' relates a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (sponsor search). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A is a deadline for hotel reservation (an accommodation/logistics deadline), while B is the deadline for submitting papers (an academic submission deadline). They are different deadlines in the conference domain, sharing only the parent class Deadline.

A's 'was a steering committee of' relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume (organisational governance), while B's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both are classes named 'Conference hall' located directly under the same parent 'Place' in their respective ontologies, with similar sibling sets (other venue/room types). The label, path and context agree, so they denote the same concept.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. a textual artefact. B's 'Coctail reception' is a conference activity (sibling of Coffee break, Lecture, Registration), i.e. an event. Different kinds and domains, so they are unrelated.

In iasted, Document is a broad class of conference items (subclasses include Review, Submission, Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc.), whereas in sigkdd Abstract is a specific document type alongside Paper and Review. Abstract is a kind of Document, so iasted Document is more general and subsumes sigkdd Abstract; they are not equivalent.

A's Industry Organization is a subclass of Organization (a type of organisation, sibling of Academia/Government/NGO), i.e. an organisational actor. B's Sponsor state is a subclass of State (sibling of Conference state and Presenter state), i.e. a status/role a participant can be in. Different parents, siblings and intended instances: an organisation is not a state/role, so the classes are unrelated.

In ekaw, Session Chair is a Conference Participant who chairs a session (a role within the conference programme), with parents Conference Participant and PC Member. In sigkdd, Program Chair is an Organizator (organising role) alongside General Chair and Webmaster. The two roles differ: a session chair moderates a session, while a program chair heads the programme committee and is part of the organising structure. Different parents (Conference Participant vs Organizator) and different sibling sets confirm they are distinct concepts, not synonyms.

A's 'has contributions' relates a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (whole-part containment), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains and ranges and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Both denote the chair of the conference organising committee: cmt's Conference Chair is a Chairman/Conference Member (the person chairing the conference), and ekaw's OC Chair is the chair of the OC Member (Organising Committee) hierarchy. In the conference domain the conference chair heads the organising committee, so the intended instances coincide.

Both classes denote a person who authors papers: cmt's Author is a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers (write Paper, submit Paper, has Author range), while ekaw's Paper Author is a Person who authors papers. The intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent despite differing parents and siblings.

PC Member is a person role (a reviewer on the program committee) in ekaw, while Fee is a monetary charge with subclasses Registration fee and Sponzor fee in sigkdd. They share no meaning, instances, or properties; the only overlap is none at all.

A's 'gives presentations' relates an Active conference participant to a Presentation (participant -> presentation). B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (document -> speaker), i.e. the inverse direction and different domain/range kinds. They describe the same underlying presentation act but with reversed direction and different entity types, so they are not equivalent; they are merely related.

A's hasMenu relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (a specific catering/meal sub-event), while B's hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event in a general mereological/partitive sense. Different domains and ranges (Meal Event/Meal Menu vs Event/Event) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties giving the end time of an event/conference, but A's domain is the broader Event (any event in the conference organisation, e.g. a session or deadline) while B's domain is specifically Conference. B is thus a specialisation of A, so A is subsumed by B's narrower concept; they are not equivalent because the domains differ in generality.

Both classes are named Paper, sit directly under Document in the same path, and represent the same conference-domain concept of a submitted/published paper. Although ekaw's Paper has more subclasses and properties, the intended instances coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Meal Event is a non-academic social/meal gathering (sibling of Break Event and Social Event, parent of Conference Dinner, with menu properties), while B's Scientific Event is the academic event branch (parent of Conference, Session, Track, Workshop) and is a sibling of Social Event. They denote disjoint kinds of event, so they are unrelated.

A's Committee is a broad organisational body with subclasses Organizing committee, Program committee and Steering committee, and it has chairs, co-chairs and members. B's OC Member is a person role (a member of the organising committee), sitting under Conference Participant with child OC Chair. The two denote different things: a committee (group) versus a member of one (person). They are related because OC Member is a member of an Organizing committee, which is a subclass of A's Committee, but they are not equivalent.

A's Session Chair is a Person who initiates calls and reviews papers, a distinct role from B's Reviewer, which is a Speaker/Delegate who reviews papers. Although both can review papers, Session Chair is a separate organizational role (initiates calls, chairs sessions) and is not equivalent to Reviewer; the ontologies place them in different hierarchies (Person vs Delegate/Speaker) and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a specific subclass of Paper (sibling of Paper Abstract), while B's 'Paper' is the general class of regular contributions (sibling of Extended abstract). The full version is a kind of paper, so A is strictly more specific than B: subsumed_by.

A's Presenter is a role of a person (a Conference Participant who presents), while B's Presenter university is a type of Building/Place (a venue associated with presenters). Different kinds of entity (person role vs. building), so they are unrelated despite the shared word 'Presenter'.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' is a Conference->Administrator property recording which administrator opened reviewer bidding; B's 'need' is a Person->Item property expressing a person's requirement for an item. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is the general conference contribution (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with review/decision/author properties), while B's Short paper is a specific kind of contribution, sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution. A Paper is not a Short paper, but a Short paper is a kind of paper/contribution, so A is more general: Paper subsumes Short paper, i.e. A is subsumed_by B's broader Contribution, not equivalent to Short paper.

A's 'Worker non speaker' is a delegate who is not a speaker (a conference attendee/worker), while B's 'Organizator' is a person who organizes the conference (parent of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc.). The two denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's hasFax is a datatype property from Person to string (a fax number), while B's is_used_by is an object property from Item to Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and direction/meaning, so they cannot denote the same relation.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title string; B's 'is an ending date' is a datatype property of Important dates giving a date. Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

Payment document is a specific kind of Document (a subclass of Document in iasted, with children Bank transfer and Cheque), whereas sigkdd's Document is the general superclass of Abstract, Paper and Review. The two do not denote the same concept: every Payment document is a Document, but not vice versa, so Payment document is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Document.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a role of a person (a Conference contributor, sibling of Regular author), while B's 'Conference' is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). They denote different kinds of things (person role vs. event) and are not equivalent.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers (children Author Not Reviewer, Co author; properties write Paper, submit Paper, has Author). Committee member in Conference is a person belonging to a committee (children Chair, Co chair; properties has members, was a member of). The intended instances differ: an author need not be a committee member and vice versa, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Workshop, linked from Conference volume via has tutorials), whereas B's Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment (sibling of Computer and LCD projector). They denote entirely different concepts despite no shared meaning.

A's `follows` relates Administrative events to Administrative events (a temporal/ordering relation between events), while B's `has Call` relates an Academic Event to its Call for papers. Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

Both are the general class of scholarly/academic events: edas Academic Event (parent Conference Event, children Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop) and ekaw Scientific Event (parent Event, children Conference, Individual Presentation, Session, Track, Workshop). They occupy the same position in their taxonomies, share the Workshop child, and both contrast with a non-scholarly sibling (Non Academic Event / Social Event). The labels differ but denote the same conference-domain concept.

A's 'has a review' relates a Reviewed contribution to its Review (domain Reviewed contribution, range Review), i.e. the paper-to-review link. B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item), i.e. authorship. Different domains, ranges and directions; they are not the same relation.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' is an administrative action performed by an Administrator to add a person to a Program Committee (domain Administrator, range Program Committee Member). B's 'organised By' relates an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it (domain Event, range Organisation, Person). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; neither is a subsumption of the other.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Multimedia Topic is a subject area/topic of papers in EDAS. They denote different concepts: an event type versus a research topic category, so they are unrelated.

A 'Regular Session' is a kind of scientific event session (a scheduled slot in a conference programme), while a 'Program Committee' is a committee of people (a group of reviewers). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (Event vs Committee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a subclass of Document representing a review of a paper, while B's Abstract is a subclass of Document representing an abstract of a paper. They are distinct document types (siblings in B: Paper, Review), so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties named 'has Email' mapping a person (or contact information) to a string email address. The edas domain is broader (Contact Information, Person) but the intended relation — a person's email — is the same, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them, while B's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair. Different domains (Program Committee Member vs Committee), different ranges (Administrator vs Chair), and different intended meanings (record-keeping provenance vs committee leadership), so they are not equivalent.

A's email is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (the person's email address). B's is used by is an object property linking an Item to a Person (the person who uses the item). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a whole-part relation, subproperty of has parts), while B's 'expert On' links a PC member to a Topic they are expert in. Different domains (Conference volume vs Member PC), different ranges (Workshop vs Topic), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

IASTED non member is a subclass of Delegate (a conference attendee who is not an IASTED member), while Organizator is a subclass of Person covering organisers (General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc.). They denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (sibling of Computer, Overhead projector, Video cassette player), while B's Listener is a person role (sibling of Organizator, Speaker). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Author in cmt is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Administrative event in confOf is an event in the conference schedule (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of regular conference contribution (sibling of Paper, child of Regular contribution), i.e. a submitted paper type. B's 'Tutorial Abstract' is a document abstract specifically for a tutorial event (sibling of Invited Talk Abstract, child of Abstract). They share the word 'abstract' but denote different concepts: a contribution type vs. an abstract document for a tutorial. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's Review is a subclass of Document (a review document/artefact), while B's Paper is a subclass of Document denoting a paper; in ekaw, Review is a separate sibling class of Paper (a review of a paper), so the two entities denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Building is a general physical place that subsumes specific building types (conference building, hotel, restaurant, etc.), while Main office is a specific kind of building/place. Building is strictly more general than Main office, so Building subsumes Main office rather than being equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is a general category of submitted work with children Paper, Poster, Short paper, and properties like has Title, abstract, written By, reviewes. Paper in ekaw is a specific subclass of Document with children such as Conference Paper, Poster Paper, Submitted Paper, and properties like has Review, has Reviewer, paper Presented As. Contribution is broader than Paper, so confOf Contribution subsumes ekaw Paper.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an announcement text about a conference. B's 'Conference' is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), a subclass of Scientific Event. A document and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated despite the shared word 'conference'.

A's Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment (sibling of projectors and video players) used in the conference domain, while B's Listener is a person role (sibling of Speaker and Organizator). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Published Paper' is a document state (a paper that has been published), a subclass of Paper in the document hierarchy. B 'Refusing manuscript' is an activity (a subclass of 'Activity before conference') describing the act of rejecting a manuscript, not a document. Different kinds (class of documents vs. class of activities) and different meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people), while B's hasEvent relates an Event to sub-events; different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a publication/volume structure), while B's 'is Menu Of' relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (catering at an event). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

confOf's Working event is a broad category of events (conference, tutorial, workshop) that are work-related, while ekaw's Individual Presentation is a specific scientific event (a talk presenting a paper). They overlap in that tutorials/workshops can be presentations, but Working event also covers whole conferences and administrative aspects, and Individual Presentation covers contributed/invited talks that are not working events in confOf's sense. Neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Lecture is a conference activity (an event type, sibling of Presentation, Session, Tutorial), while B's Speaker is a person role (subclass of Person, with Author and Invited Speaker as children). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and cannot be equivalent.

A's Individual Presentation is a scientific event (a talk given at a conference, with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial) that a paper is presented as. B's Power Point presentation is a conference activity, a presentation format/session type (sibling of Video presentation), i.e. the medium/format rather than the event of presenting. They overlap in the conference domain but denote different concepts (event vs. presentation format), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's property is specifically the camera-ready submission deadline, while B's 'done till' is a generic deadline date for any task in the Deadline class. The camera-ready deadline is a kind of deadline, so A is more specific and is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's 'has First Name' is a datatype property holding a person's given name, while B's 'E mail' holds an email address; both are Person->string datatype properties but they denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

A's Review is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a paper (written by Reviewer, has Meta Review child, sibling of Paper). B's Abstract is a document that is a summary/abstract of a paper, sibling of Paper and Review. They denote different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'rejected By' links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who rejected it), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents it). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so the properties are not equivalent.

Both are the general superclass of Paper and Review in the conference domain; cmt's Document has children Paper and Review, edas's Document has children Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, Meal Menu, all of which are documents. The intended instances (papers, reviews, and other written artefacts) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite edas having more specific subclasses.

A's Conference Participant is a broad role class covering all people taking part in a conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.), while B's Sponsor is a person or organisation providing financial support, a distinct role. They share only the parent Person and do not denote the same concept.

A's `location` is a datatype property mapping an event (Social/Working event) to a string literal (its venue name). B's `is Location Of` is an object property mapping a Place to a Conference Event, i.e. the inverse direction of a place-event relation. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), direction, and argument types, so they are not equivalent; at best B is the inverse of a place-event relation, not of A's string-valued location.

A's 'written By' links a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it (domain Review, range Reviewer). B's 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (domain Reviewer, range Personal Review History). The domains, ranges, and directions differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'belong to a conference volume' is an object property linking Important dates to a Conference volume, while B's 'Start of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Proceedings Publisher' is an Organisation (a publisher of conference proceedings), while B 'Renting' is an Activity before the conference (renting a venue/equipment). Different kinds and different meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (an event/document), while B's 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a kind of person (a delegate/author who gives a plenary lecture). They denote different categories (contribution vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Welcome Talk' is a type of Talk Event (an academic event in the conference programme), while B 'Conference hall' is a type of Place (a physical venue location). They belong to disjoint branches (event vs. place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Written contribution' is a broad class of written conference contributions (parent of Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, sibling of Poster, Presentation, Invited talk). B 'Final manuscript' is a specific stage of a submission (sibling of Initial manuscript, child of Submission). The intended instances do not coincide: a written contribution is not necessarily a final manuscript, and a final manuscript is a submission-stage document rather than the general category of written contributions. Thus they are unrelated concepts.

cmt:User is a general person role in the conference system (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while confOf:Scholar is a specific person category with a price category comment and a 'study At' property linking to a University. They overlap in denoting persons involved in the conference, but Scholar is a narrower, fee-category concept rather than the same general user role, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Meeting Room Place is a specific kind of place (a room where meetings occur), while sigkdd's Place is the general superclass of locations such as Conference hall, Hotel and Main office. The edas class is therefore narrower than the sigkdd class, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (setting review criteria for a conference), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authoring a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both are subclasses of Registration fee, but A (Nonauthor registration fee) covers any non-author registrant (member, nonmember, student), while B (Registration Student) is specifically the student registration fee. They overlap (a student who is not an author) but neither subsumes the other; A's siblings include Student registration fee, showing student is a distinct category from nonauthor in iasted.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation from abstract to its containing document), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domain, range, and direction of relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's Regular is a participant category sibling to Student and Member (a regular, non-student attendee), while B's Student is a person who is a student. They denote different, in fact contrasting, concepts; Regular is not equivalent to Student.

A's `date` is a datatype property whose domain is Conference and range is a date value, i.e. the date of a conference. B's `has a name` is a datatype property with domain Conference/Conference part/Conference proceedings/Publisher/Topic and range string, i.e. a naming property. They relate different kinds of things (a temporal value vs. a name string) and are not the same relation.

A's Workshop is an Academic Event (a type of event/meeting), while B's Poster Session is a Session (a slot within a conference). Although B has a sibling Workshop Session, the entities themselves denote different concepts: a workshop event vs. a poster session. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

ekaw's hasPart is a generic mereological/part-whole property with unspecified domain and range, whereas iasted's give is a specific relation from a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or presenting a paper). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

Both classes denote a workshop as a kind of academic/scientific event; edas places it under Academic Event and ekaw under Scientific Event, which are the corresponding event subhierarchies, and both have the same label and intended instances.

A 'Submitted contribution' is a written contribution that has been submitted and is under review (its child is 'Reviewed contribution', and it is the object of review-expertise/review-preference properties). B 'Paper' is the general document class for any paper in EDAS, with children Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn/Published/Pending/Active Paper, i.e. it covers papers in all states, not only submitted ones. A submitted contribution is thus a narrower concept than Paper, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'obtain' is an object property mapping a Person to an Item (acquiring something). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A is a specific kind of registration fee (Student registration fee), a subclass of Registration fee, which in turn is a subclass of Fee in ontology B. Thus A is strictly more specific than B's Fee, so A is subsumed by B's Fee, not equivalent.

A's 'Steering committee' is a committee (a group/body) that oversees a conference series, with properties linking a Conference volume to a Steering committee. B's 'Organizing Committee member' is a Person (an individual role-holder) under Organizator, sibling to General Chair, Program Chair, etc. One denotes a collective body, the other an individual person role; they are not the same concept.

Both are object properties linking a Paper (and a broader container: Conference in edas, Event in ekaw) to a topic (Topic / Research Topic). Same direction, same intended meaning: the subject is about the topic. The domain/range differences are only in the naming of the container and topic classes, which are themselves equivalent in the conference domain.

OC Member is a person role (an Organising Committee member, a subclass of Conference Participant with child OC Chair), whereas Registration fee is a monetary amount (a subclass of Fee with children such as Member registration fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (people vs. money) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.
A is a research topic in cryptography (a subject area under Topic), while B is a physical item (a card, with child Credit card) under Item. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

A's markConflictOfInterest records a conflict-of-interest association between a reviewer/author/chair and a paper, preventing bidding/assignment/review. B's isReviewing relates a person (chair, reviewer, session chair, TPC member) to a paper they are reviewing. The intended meanings differ: one is a conflict flag, the other a reviewing assignment relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's Administrator is a Person/User role (a human who administers the conference, with properties like assign Reviewer, enter Conference Details), while B's Review is a Document/Item (a written review artefact). Different kinds and meanings; no equivalence.

A's 'Review Form' is the document/form on which a review is recorded, while B's 'Review' is the review content itself (a Document subtype with review Of Paper and review Written By). They are closely connected in the conference domain but denote different concepts: the form vs. the review it carries. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'Author book proceedings included' is a subclass of Author in the iasted hierarchy, denoting an author role tied to book proceedings; B's 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Speaker denoting a person invited to speak. Different parents (Author vs Speaker) and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a general conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, Review) providing information to attendees. B's 'Registration form' is a specific Form document (sibling of Author information form, Hotel registration form) used to register. A registration form is one possible piece of participant information, but the classes are not the same concept; the intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address), while B's 'is sent after' is an object property linking an Item to a Time. They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a person who may review the paper), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (the author submits the paper). They have different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while B's 'Publisher' is an organisation that issues Conference proceedings. Different kinds of entities with no overlap; the shared word 'author/publisher' does not make them equivalent.

A's `give` relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives/presents something), while B's `awarded by` relates an Award to its awarding body/person — different domain, range and direction of relation, so they are not the same property.

A is a class recording a reviewer's personal history of reviews in the EDAS conference system; B is a departure tax, a monetary tax concept in the iasted ontology. They share no meaning, no properties, and no domain overlap.

Both classes denote a person in the conference domain: edas Person is the superclass of Attendee, Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc., and sigkdd Person is the superclass of Listener, Organizator, Speaker. Both have name/email properties and are the central human actor class, so they coincide.

Accommodation Place is a lodging venue for conference attendees (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), whereas Main office is an administrative office location (sibling of Conference hall, Hotel). They denote different kinds of places and do not coincide.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) relation between a Conference volume and its Conference parts, while B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference it holds/organises. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.
hasLocation goes from Conference Event to Place, while locationOf goes from Location to Event; they are inverse relations, not equivalent.

Associated Chair in cmt is a kind of Chairman/Conference Member (an organising role in the conference committee), whereas Assistant in confOf is a generic Person role (confTool helper) with no committee-chair meaning. Different intended instances and different positions in the hierarchy, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Scholar is a price/registration category of Person (a person attending under a scholarship fee category, with property study At -> University), whereas sigkdd's Author of paper is a subclass of Author denoting a person who authored a paper. The intended instances do not coincide: a Scholar need not be an author and an author need not be a scholar, and the contexts (siblings, properties) differ.

A is a conference event (a working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while B is a person role (OC Chair, a subclass of OC Member under Conference Participant). An event and a person role cannot denote the same concept, so the pair is unrelated.

A Coffee Break is a short informal refreshment pause within the conference schedule (a Break Event alongside Free Time Break and Meal Break), whereas a Conference Banquet is a formal social event (a Social Event alongside Conference Trip). They differ in kind, formality, and position in the event hierarchy, so they are not the same concept.

write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authoring), while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (presenting). Both connect a person to a written work, but the relations differ in kind (authorship vs. presentation) and the classes are not equivalent (Author vs. Speaker, Paper vs. Document), so they are only related, not equivalent.

A's hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string biography, while B's speak_in is an object property linking a Person to a Place/Time (speaking at an event). Different range types and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Co author is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper, with co write Paper / has Co author properties). B's Possible Reviewer is a Person who may review papers (parent of PC Member, with has Reviewer / reviewer Of Paper properties). The intended instances differ: co-authors write papers, possible reviewers review them; neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the conference program committee: cmt's ProgramCommittee has members (Program Committee Member) and a member-of relation, while sigkdd's Program_Committee is a subclass of Committee alongside Organizing Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee, matching the same intended concept of the group of reviewers/PC members.

A 'Review Question' is a question (numerical or textual) used to structure a review form, whereas B 'Review' is a document (a subclass of Document, sibling of Submission, Form, etc.) representing the completed review itself. The two denote different concepts: a question vs. a review document. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Both properties link an event/activity to the person or organisation responsible for it, but they differ in domain and range: ekaw's organisedBy has domain Event and range Organisation or Person, while iasted's is_given_by has domain Activity or Item and range Person only. They overlap in meaning (responsibility for an event/activity) but are not the same relation, since organisedBy can point to an organisation and is_given_by cannot, and the domains differ.

Reviewer in cmt is a conference member role responsible for reviewing papers (assigned papers, bids, conflicts), while Scholar in confOf is a generic person category defined by a price category and studying at a university. Their contexts, siblings, and properties do not coincide; a scholar is not necessarily a reviewer and a reviewer is not necessarily a scholar.

A's 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to its Review (domain Reviewed contribution, range Review), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (domain Author, range Contribution). They relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent; 'writes' is closer to an inverse of a paper-authorship relation than to 'has a review'.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving its textual title (range string); B's Price is a datatype property of Registration fee giving a monetary amount (range int). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Week Reject Rating is a review rating value (a score category used in the review process, sibling of Accept Rating and Reject Rating), whereas Rejected Paper is a document/paper class in the submission workflow (a paper that was rejected). One is a rating datum, the other a paper, so they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

edas Attendee is a Person who attends a conference, a broad role covering all participants; iasted Listener is a Delegate (a building/place role) specifically a non-speaking participant. They overlap in that both can denote a conference participant who is not presenting, but Attendee is broader and includes speakers, chairs, etc., while Listener is a narrower non-speaker role. Hence related, not equivalent.

Organization in edas is an entity that provides sponsorship (with subclasses Academia/Government/Industry/NGO), while Money in iasted is a monetary amount with subclasses Fee/Sponzorship/Tax/Tip. They denote different concepts: one is an agent/organisation, the other a financial quantity. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's Topic is a subject area of papers/reviews/conference parts (it has a name, is a topic of conference parts, is linked to review preferences and submitted contributions). B's Time is a temporal entity (parent of Conference days, Deadline, Trip day; used as range of is held before/after, is present, is sent before/after). The two denote completely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's title is a datatype property giving a Paper's string title; B's paperPresentedAs is an object property linking a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation. Different kinds of values (string vs. presentation) and different meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Technical commitee' is a subclass of Delegate (a person role/attendee type) in the iasted ontology, while B's 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person with children General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster. Both concern people involved in organising a conference, but 'Technical commitee' denotes a committee/role of delegates whereas 'Organizator' denotes an organiser person; they overlap in the conference-organisation domain but are not the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

An Active conference participant is a conference contributor who gives presentations, while an Author in edas is a broader role (parent of Presenter) that writes papers. Every active participant who presents is an author-like person, but authors need not be active participants (they may be passive authors or non-presenters). Thus Active conference participant is strictly narrower than Author, so it is subsumed by Author.

A's has Street is a datatype property giving the street address of an Organization or Person, while B's Name is a datatype property giving a Person's name. They relate different kinds of information (address vs. name) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Review expertise' models a reviewer's area/level of expertise (linked to Reviewer and Submitted contribution), while B's 'Review Rating' models the recommendation/rating given to a paper (linked to Active Paper, with children Accept/Reject ratings). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document (a written contribution that is authored, reviewed, and published), while B's 'Author of paper' is a role/type of person (a subclass of Author, sibling of 'Author of paper student'). They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person role), so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Document is a general document class whose children include Paper and Review, so it subsumes ekaw:Review. ekaw:Review is a specific document type (a review of a paper), not equivalent to the general Document class.
A's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's Currency relates a Registration fee to a string (monetary unit). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while B's 'Deadline Author notification' is a subclass of Deadline (a date by which authors are notified). They belong to different branches (Person vs Deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person (a human role in the conference), while B 'Dinner banquet' is a Social program activity/event. They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Company is an organizational entity (sibling of University under Organization) in the conference domain, while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Taxi, Van under Transport vehicle). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper in a specific publication state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper under Paper), i.e. a scientific contribution. B 'Record of attendance' is a document recording that someone attended, sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc. Different intended instances; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer), i.e. an assignment relation. B's 'has a review reference or expertise' links a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference topics (domain Reviewer, range Review expertise/Review preference). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

cmt Reviewer is a person who reviews papers (has Been Assigned, read By Reviewer, adjust Bid), while ekaw PC Member is a program-committee member, a broader role that includes chairs and is a subclass of Possible Reviewer. A PC member is typically a reviewer, but the classes are not coextensive: cmt Reviewer includes non-PC reviewers (e.g. external reviewers) and ekaw PC Member includes non-reviewing roles (chairs). They overlap without being equivalent.

A's 'end Date' is the end date/time of a Conference (domain Conference, range dateTime). B's 'done till' is the date by which a Deadline is done (domain Deadline, range date). Different domains (Conference vs Deadline) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Track is a conference part (a thematic session/stream of the conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, linked from Conference volume via has tracks). B's Tip is a monetary category under Money, sibling of Fee, Sponzorship and Tax. The two denote entirely different concepts (conference track vs. gratuity/payment), so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Country is a geopolitical entity used as the range of has Country (Organization, Person -> Country). In iasted, State is a geographic/administrative region (a place) that contains Cities and Buildings, is situated in other places, and is occupied/visited by Persons. The two denote different concepts: a nation-state vs. a sub-national geographic region/place. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A is a conference topic about computer networks sensors (a research subject area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a Computer under Audiovisual equipment, sibling of LCD projector and video cassette player). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a person who participates in a conference, with subclasses Active/Passive participant), while B's 'Conference days' is a subclass of Time (a temporal span of conference days, with children Delegate and One conference day). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Time) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person role in the conference), while B's Registration SIGKDD Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for SIGKDD members). They denote different concepts: a person type vs. a fee type. Note B's sibling Registration Student is the fee counterpart, not A's Student.

confOf's Volunteer is a Person subtype (a helper at the conference, comment 'confTool'), while iasted's Reviewer is a Speaker subtype (a delegate who reviews papers). They denote different roles with no subsumption or overlap; the shared 'person involved in the conference' context is too generic to make them equivalent.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member who helps organise the conference), whereas Volunteer in confOf is a generic helper person directly under Person with no chairing role. Their parents, siblings and intended instances differ, so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties linking a conference call/important-dates entity to a submission deadline date. 'is a full paper submission date' in the Conference ontology and 'has Submission Deadline' in edas both denote the deadline for submitting a full paper, with matching domain (Important dates / Call) and range (date / dateTime). The intended relation is the same, so they are equivalent.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant under Person/Conference applicant, i.e. a kind of person who registered late and paid. B 'Nonauthor registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee under Money/Fee, i.e. a monetary amount charged to non-authors. One is a person role, the other a fee; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

Dining Place is a specific kind of Place (a place where one dines), while sigkdd's Place is the general superclass covering conference halls, hotels and offices. Dining Place is therefore strictly narrower than Place, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A 'Conference proceedings' is the published collection of papers (has publisher, volume, ISBN, name), while B 'Conference Session' is a temporal event/session within a conference that relates to documents and academic events. They denote different concepts and share no properties or context.

A's hasEmail relates a Person to an email address string, while B's hasFirstName relates a Person to a first name string. They are different datatype properties with different intended values, so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Paper is a Document that is authored, reviewed, assigned to reviewers, and decided upon — the conference submission/contribution concept. In iasted, Publication is an Item whose only children are Book proceeding and Cd proceeding, i.e. a published proceedings artefact, not a submitted paper. A Paper is not a Publication in this sense (a paper may become part of a publication), so Paper is strictly narrower than Publication; the two are not equivalent.
A's Committee is a body of people (chairs, members) organising a conference; B's Conference is the event itself with dates, country, topics and papers. Different concepts, no subsumption.

A's 'has Been Assigned' relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper the reviewer was assigned to review), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper the author wrote). Different subject kinds (Reviewer vs Author) and different relation semantics (review assignment vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a place where conference sessions/meetings are held, while B 'Main office' is the administrative office of the organisation. They are different kinds of places with no overlap in intended instances; siblings also differ (A has Conference Venue Place, B has Conference hall/Session room).

A 'Session Chair' is a Person role (a person who chairs a session), while B 'Workshop Session' is an Event/Session type (a kind of scientific event). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track(s) (a structural/part-like relation, sibling of 'has parts'), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (membership of people). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Social event is a general category of social events with children Banquet, Reception and Trip, while ekaw's Conference Banquet is a specific social event (a banquet) under Social Event. The confOf class is strictly more general than the ekaw class, so it subsumes it rather than being equivalent.

Conference Banquet is a social event (a dinner/banquet activity) in the event hierarchy, while Hotel fee is a monetary fee in the money hierarchy. They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

City in confOf is a location class used as the range of the has City property (Organization/Person -> City), whereas Conference in sigkdd is the central event class with properties such as City of conference, Start/End of conference, and hold/holded by. A city is a place, not a conference event; the two classes denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's Scholar is a price/fee category of Person (a person attending under a scholar fee category, with property study At), while B's Author of paper student is a subclass of Author denoting a student who authored a paper. The intended instances differ: a Scholar need not be an author, and a student author need not be in the scholar price category. Different parents (Person vs Author) and different sibling sets confirm they are distinct concepts.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial/workshop), while B's One day presenter is a subtype of Delegate (a person role). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A's 'organised By' relates an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it (domain Event, range Organisation/Person). B's 'is occupied by' relates a Building/City/State to the Person occupying it (domain Building/City/State, range Person). Different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings (organising an event vs. occupying a place); they are not the same relation.
Author (cmt) is a person role who writes/submits papers; Call (edas) is a call-for-papers document/event with submission deadlines and instructions. Different kinds of entities with no overlap.
A's 'adjusted By' links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it; B's 'pay' links a Person to a Registration fee. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Programme is a Document (a conference programme/schedule artefact) with siblings Paper, Review, Slide Set, and is linked to a Conference Event. B's Program Committee is a Committee (an organisational body) with siblings Organizing Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee. They denote different concepts: a document vs. a committee, so they are unrelated.

Conference Member is a person role in the conference organisation (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/Chair), while City is a geographic location (children Conference city, Presenter city; properties about being situated in/visited by persons). They share no intended instances and no domain relation.

Both are subclasses of Author and denote people who speak/present at a conference, but Presenter (edas) is a person who presents a paper, while Lecturer (iasted) is a speaker/lecturer role with children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer, a broader teaching-oriented role. They overlap in the speaking role but are not the same concept, so related rather than equivalent.

Both denote the abstract of a paper: cmt's Paper Abstract is a subclass of Paper (a document type), while sigkdd's Abstract is a Document sibling of Paper and Review, i.e. the abstract text as a document. In the conference domain both refer to the same concept, the paper abstract, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.
A's 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while B's 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

A's 'Conference fees' is a general class of fees paid for the conference (registration, etc.), while B's 'Sponzor fee' is a specific fee paid by sponsors, a sibling of Registration fee under Fee. They denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to people (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) who initiate it, while B's 'held In' links an Event to a Location where it takes place. Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A is a chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member who organises the conference), while B is a subtype of Author denoting an author whose CD proceedings are included. They belong to different branches (chair vs author) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Session' is an event/activity (a time slot in the conference programme) that documents relate to, whereas B 'Session Chair' is a person role (a Conference Participant who chairs a session). One denotes an event, the other a person/role, so they cannot be equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a public announcement inviting submissions to a conference (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, Conference www), whereas B 'Invitation letter' is a personal document sent to an individual (sibling of Viza, Payment document, Record of attendance). They share only the loose idea of inviting, but denote different document types in the conference domain.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference organisation hierarchy (Person > Conference Member > Author) who writes/submits papers and can be a reviewer or chair. Topic (Conference) is a subject area of papers/reviews/conference parts, with properties linking it to Review preference, Submitted contribution and Conference part. The two denote different concepts (person vs. subject area) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

A's Proceedings is a class of published multi-author volumes (a document type, parent Multi author Volume, child Conference Proceedings). B's Author cd proceedings included is a subclass of Author describing an author role (an author whose paper is included in the proceedings CD), sibling of Author book proceedings included and Lecturer. One denotes a publication artefact, the other a person/role; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a name' is a generic naming property whose domain is a broad set of conference-domain entities (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic), while B's 'has First Name' is specific to Person and denotes a person's given name. Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Speaker is a person role (a Delegate who speaks, with children Author/Reviewer), while B's Conference hall is a physical place (a sibling of Hotel and Main office under Place). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A's read By Meta Reviewer relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (a reviewing/assignment relation within the conference review process), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (a recognition relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Coffee Break is a specific break event (sibling of Free Time Break and Meal Break), while B's Conference activity is a broad category whose children include Coffee break, Lecture, Presentation, Registration, etc. Thus Coffee Break is strictly more specific than Conference activity, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a meeting/session held at a conference), while B's Workshop Paper is a document/paper type. They belong to different branches (Event vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic's preference in a review), while B's property links an Item to a Person (an item given to a person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Break Event is a non-academic conference event (a break in the schedule, with children Coffee Break, Free Time Break, Meal Break), whereas B's Lecture is an academic conference activity (with children Plenary lecture, Session, Tutorial). They denote different concepts: a break is not a lecture, and neither subsumes the other.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's go_through is an object property mapping an Item to an Activity (an item undergoing/participating in an activity). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), and range (string vs Activity), so they denote entirely different relations.

A's 'was a program committee of' relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (a committee's service relation to a conference), while B's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (scheduling concurrency). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent.

A's Conference is the academic event (has papers, members, topics, deadlines), while B's Conference hotel is a building/venue type under Place > Building, a physical location rather than the event; the shared word 'conference' does not make them the same concept.

A is an event type (a sub-event of Event covering submission, reviewing, registration, camera-ready), while B is a person role (a staff member of an agency, sibling of Conference Participant and Paper Author). They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Person) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.
A's writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while B's pay relates a Person to Money (payment). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B is a physical location (Meeting Room Place, a kind of Place) in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (people vs. places) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an Administrator action on a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), while B's 'technically Organises' is a subproperty of 'organises' relating an Organisation to what it organises. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's min Choice is a datatype property giving a minimum number of choices (positiveInteger) for social/working events, while B's has Start Date Time gives a dateTime start for a conference event. Different domain, range and meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A Conference is a working event (a whole event with tutorials, workshops, etc.), while a Power Point presentation is a specific kind of presentation activity within a conference. They denote different concepts: an event vs. a presentation artefact/activity, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving the ISBN string, while B's 'City of conference' is a datatype property of Conference giving the host city. They relate different kinds of things (proceedings identifier vs. conference location) and have different domains, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a human being in the conference domain: confOf's Person is the superclass of all human roles (Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.) with personal attributes, and ekaw's Person is likewise the superclass of Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student, with author/writing relations. Same intended extension, so equivalent.

confOf's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), i.e. a person writes a paper. iasted's `is prepared by` relates an Item to a Person, i.e. a paper is prepared by a person. These are inverse relations (writes vs. is prepared by), so they are not equivalent. However, `writes` is more specific: it only covers authorship of contributions, whereas `is prepared by` covers any item prepared by any person, so `writes` is subsumed by the broader `is prepared by` relation.

A's Conference Member is a subclass of Person (a person involved in a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Conference state is a subclass of State (a status/state of a conference participant, sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. state) and share no intended instances.

A's has Topic relates a Conference/Paper to a Topic (Paper -> Topic). B's topic Covered By relates a Research Topic to an Event/Paper (Research Topic -> Event/Paper), i.e. it is the inverse direction and a different subject/object pairing. They are not the same relation; at best they are inverses, which the instructions say do not count as equivalent.

A 'Positive Review' is a subclass of Review (a document/evaluation artefact with a positive outcome), while B 'Reviewer' is a person role (a Delegate/Speaker who reviews). They denote different kinds of entities (review document vs. person) and are not equivalent.

cmt:User is a general person role with subclasses Administrator, Author, Reviewer; confOf:Administrator is a specific role (confTool administrator) that is one of the roles a User can take. User is strictly more general than Administrator, so User subsumes Administrator, not equivalent.

A 'Conference contribution' is a submitted scholarly work (paper, poster, talk) that is part of a conference volume and is submitted at a volume. B 'Form' is a document used for administrative data collection (author information, hotel registration, registration). Their children, siblings and properties do not overlap: contributions are reviewed and published, forms are filled in. They denote different concepts.

A's 'Conference www' is a web page/document about a conference (a Conference document with a URL), while B's 'Conference Paper' is a scholarly paper submitted to a conference. Different intended instances: one is a website, the other a publication. No subsumption or overlap.

A Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference (a Chairman subtype in cmt), while B Volunteer is a generic helper person in confOf with comment 'confTool'. They denote different roles: chairing/organising leadership vs. voluntary assistance. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances, so unrelated.

A's hasLocation relates a Conference Event to a Place (its location), while B's hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event (part/whole or containment of events). Different domain/range kinds and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its committee members (range Conference Member), while B's hasTopic relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (range Topic). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Bid in cmt is a reviewer's expressed interest in reviewing a paper (domain/range Reviewer->Bid, Paper->Bid), while Country in edas is a geographic country associated with a conference (Conference->Country). They share no meaning, instances, or context; the only overlap is the word 'Bid' vs 'Country' being unrelated concepts.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (membership in the conference), while B's reviewes relates a PC Member to a Contribution (the reviewing relation). Different domains (Conference Member vs Member PC) and different ranges (Conference vs Contribution), so they denote different relations.

Author Not Reviewer is a conference member who is an author but not a reviewer (a role restriction on Author), while Invited Speaker is a speaker who has been invited to speak. They belong to different branches (Author vs Speaker) and denote different roles; neither subsumes the other.

A's hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (domain and range both Event), while B's is_sent_after relates an Item to a Time. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

In edas, Call is a specific document/announcement class (Call For Papers, Call For Manuscripts, Call For Reviews) that initiates submissions and has deadlines/instructions. In iasted, Activity is a broad event/action class (conference activities, activities before/after conference) with properties like give, go through, is held in, is paid for. The intended instances do not coincide: a Call is not an Activity, and Activity is not a Call. They are unrelated concepts despite both being involved in conference organisation.

A's property is a specific deadline (full paper submission date) within the Important dates class, while B's property is a general dating relation for any Activity. They differ in domain (Important dates vs Activity) and in specificity; the full paper submission date is one particular kind of date, not the general 'is dated on' relation.

Both properties link a Person to a document/paper they authored: Conference's 'contributes' has domain Person and range Conference document, while ekaw's 'author Of' has domain Person and range Document. In the conference domain, a person contributing a conference document is exactly the authorship relation, so the two properties denote the same relation in the same direction.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a submission of a paper to a conference), while B's is_paid_with relates Money to an Item (a payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B is a temporal concept (One conference day, a kind of Conference days) in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Time) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic in the antennas/communications domain (sibling of CAD Topic, Communication Theory Topic, etc.), while B is a physical item category for audiovisual equipment (sibling of Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle) with children like LCD projector and Video cassette player. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Both classes denote a person who authors papers: confOf's Author is a Person that writes Contributions (and is written by them), while ekaw's Paper Author is a Person subclass representing someone who authors papers. The intended instances coincide (people who write papers), so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent despite the different labels.

A Programme Brochure is a document listing events (it has properties event On List / lists Event and is published by an organisation), whereas a Registration form is a form used to register (sibling of Author information form and Hotel registration form). They denote different artefacts in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a person's conflict of interest in a paper/document), while B's is_designed_for relates an Activity/Money/Time to an Activity/Person (something being designed/intended for an activity or person). The domains and ranges do not coincide and the intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Reviewer is a subclass of Conference Member/User that reviews papers and can be assigned papers, with Meta Reviewer as a child. In edas, TPC Member is a Person who reviews papers (is Reviewing / is Reviewed By) and initiates calls, and Reviewer is a separate sibling class. The two overlap in that both review papers, but TPC Member is a broader program-committee role while cmt's Reviewer is a specific reviewing role; they are not the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Banquet is a social event involving a meal, while a Conference Trip is an excursion/outing. They are distinct sibling social events (confOf Banquet vs ekaw Conference Trip, whose sibling is Conference Banquet), so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but A's 'has End Date Time' is a specific end-date property of a Conference Event, while B's 'is dated on' is a general dating property of an Activity. They overlap in that both relate an event/activity to a date, but the end-date semantics is narrower than the general 'dated on' relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's Time is a temporal entity (children: Conference days, Deadline, Trip day; used as range of is held after/before, is present, is sent after/before), whereas B's Document is an information artefact (children: Abstract, Paper, Review; domain of submit until, range of presentation). They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, a human who chairs the conference), while B 'Introduction of speaker' is a conference activity (a subclass of Introduction, an event in which a speaker is introduced). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A 'Meal Event' is a non-academic conference event (a meal, with a menu, parent of Conference Dinner), while B 'Speaker' is a person role (parent of Author and Invited Speaker, who presents documents). They belong to entirely different branches (event vs person) and share no intended instances.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action of finalizing paper assignments), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents a document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's hasUpdatedVersion relates a Document to a later version of that same Document (domain Document, range Document), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item they provide (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Building in iasted is a general place that subsumes specific venue types (conference building, hotel, restaurant, university, etc.), while Hotel in sigkdd is one specific kind of building/venue. Thus Building is broader and subsumes Hotel, not equivalent.

Both properties link a person/participant-like entity to a conference/event, but the domains differ: cmt's memberOfConference has domain Conference Member (a person role) and range Conference, while edas's belongsToEvent has domain Programme (a programme/committee entity) and range Conference Event. They relate different kinds of things (a member to a conference vs. a programme to an event), so they are not equivalent; they are only loosely related by both involving conference/event membership.

A's Conference Member is a Person role (author, chair, reviewer, PC member) participating in a conference, while B's Conference hall is a Place (a physical venue building alongside Hotel and Main office). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. location) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop is a small interactive event and a sibling of Track and Tutorial under Conference part; B Plenary lecture is a kind of Lecture (a talk given to all attendees) under Conference activity, sibling of Session and Tutorial. They denote different kinds of conference events, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Rejected Paper' is an evaluated paper that was not accepted, while B 'Final manuscript' is the final version of a submission (sibling of 'Initial manuscript'), i.e. a stage/version of a document, not an outcome of review. Their paths, parents and siblings differ (Evaluated Paper vs Submission), so they denote different concepts.

A's Talk Event is an Academic Event (a scientific talk session with children Closing Talk and Welcome Talk, siblings Paper Presentation and Workshop), whereas B's Social Event is a non-scientific social gathering (children Conference Banquet and Conference Trip, sibling Scientific Event). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship relation), while B's 'need' links a Person to an Item (a person's requirement). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

confOf's Scholar is a registration price category (comment: 'price category - scholar') for a person attending the conference, with a property study At (Scholar -> University). ekaw's Paper Author is a person who authors a paper, a role tied to the paper submission process. Although both are subclasses of Person, their intended instances differ: a scholar is a fee category, a paper author is an authorship role. They are not synonyms and do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'author Of' goes Person -> Document (a person authors a document), while B's 'is signed by' goes Item -> Person (an item is signed by a person). They are inverse in direction and relate different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an Administrator action relating an Administrator to a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (domain Author, range Contribution). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee), while B's occupy relates a Person to a Building, City or State (physical location/occupancy). The ranges are disjoint and the intended meanings differ, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property holding a person's first name (comment mentions middle name), while B's hasBiography holds a person's biography text. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote different attributes; a first name is not a biography, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chairing role within the conference committee hierarchy (sibling of Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair), whereas Late Registered Participant (ekaw) is a conference attendee distinguished by registration timing (sibling of Early Registered Participant). Different concepts: one is an organiser role, the other an attendee category.

A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country; B's publisherOf relates an Organisation to published artefacts (Flyer, Volume, Brochure, Web Site). Different domain, range and meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's Non Academic Event is a conference event type (breaks, meals, social events) under Conference Event, while B's Student non speaker is a kind of delegate (person) under Non speaker. They belong to different branches (event vs. person) and denote different concepts.

A's Presentation is a kind of conference contribution (a talk given by an active participant, with an abstract, possibly an invited talk), while B's Audiovisual equipment is a physical item (parent of Computer, LCD projector, etc.). They share no instances and no meaning; the word overlap is absent and the contexts (contribution vs. equipment) are disjoint.
