A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property linking a Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while B's 'paper Presented As' is an object property linking a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation. They relate different kinds of entities (proceedings->int vs paper->presentation) and have different domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Workshop is a Working event (a small interactive event alongside the main conference), sibling of Conference and Tutorial. In edas, Single Level Conference is a type of Conference (a conference without sub-conferences), sibling of Two Level Conference. The concepts differ: a workshop is not a conference, and a single-level conference is not a workshop. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a call/announcement artifact, sibling of Call for paper and Conference announcement), whereas B's 'Conference' is a working event (a type of event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). They denote different kinds of things (document vs. event), so they are unrelated.

confOf Member is a Participant subtype (a person attending the conference, sibling of Regular and Student, i.e. a registration category), whereas edas TPC Member is a program-committee role (sibling of Reviewer, Author, Session Chair) that reviews papers and initiates calls. The shared word 'member' does not make them the same concept; their parents, siblings and properties differ.

TPC Member in edas is a program-committee person who reviews papers and initiates calls; Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives a presentation of a Document. Their roles, siblings (Reviewer/Author vs Listener/Organizator) and properties (reviewing/initiating vs presenting) do not coincide, so they are not the same concept.

A's 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (a conference social gathering such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B's 'Fee' is a subclass of Money (a payment such as Registration fee, Hotel fee). They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to the Paper Presentation it is associated with (domain Accepted Paper, range Paper Presentation), whereas B's give links a Person to an Activity or Item they present/produce (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; not the same relation.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a role of a person (a Conference contributor, sibling of Regular author), while B's 'Conference city' is a kind of City (sibling of Presenter city, Sponsor city). They denote different concepts in different branches of the domain (person role vs. location), so they are unrelated.

Tip (a gratuity/payment under Money) and Registration fee (a specific conference fee under Fee) denote different concepts; a tip is not a registration fee, and their contexts (siblings Fee, Sponzorship, Tax vs. Sponzor fee and registration subclasses) do not align.

A's 'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation). B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (authorship/presentation relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Conference is a specific conference entity (has dates, administrators, submissions, members, logo), while edas:ConferenceEvent is a broader event concept with subclasses Academic Event and Non Academic Event, attendees, locations, programmes and start/end times. A conference is a kind of conference event (an academic event), so cmt:Conference is strictly more specific and is subsumed by edas:ConferenceEvent; they are not equivalent.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative sub-event of a conference (the act/phase of submitting contributions), while B 'Conference' is a scientific event denoting one edition of a conference. They are different kinds of events: one is a temporal administrative activity, the other is the overarching scientific event. Neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a paper document), while B is a subclass of Topic (a subject area in mobile computing). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference ontology (document vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

A 'Plenary lecture' is a kind of conference activity/lecture (an event), while a 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is a committee (an organizational group). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a part-whole relation within a conference's proceedings). B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference (an organization hosting/conducting a conference). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Conference applicant is a Person subclass (a person who applies to attend a conference, with child Registeered applicant), whereas Registration Non Member is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a fee amount category, not a person. Different kinds of entities (person vs. fee), so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that run in parallel (domain and range both Administrative event), while ekaw's 'scientifically Organises' relates an Academic Institution to the event it organises. Different domain, different range, different meaning; not equivalent.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration), while B's is_used_for relates an Item to an Activity or Money (resource usage). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name; B's 'has City' is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a city. Different domains, different intended values (a name vs. a city), no overlap in meaning.

A's 'has a publisher' links a Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organisation/person publishing the proceedings), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (the person who presented it). Different domains (Conference proceedings vs Document) and different ranges (Publisher vs Speaker), and the intended relations are distinct: publishing vs presenting. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Chairman in cmt is a person role (a subclass of Person, with subclasses Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair, and a conflict-of-interest property involving Author/Reviewer/Paper). Card in iasted is an Item (a physical/administrative artefact with subclass Credit card, siblings Document, Publication, Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A Track is a thematic stream of the conference to which papers are submitted (a Conference part, sibling of Tutorial/Workshop, linked from Conference volume via has tracks). B Meal Event is a non-academic social event (a meal, parent of Conference Dinner, with has Menu/is Menu Of). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a contribution (a document submitted to a conference, sibling of Poster and Short paper), while B's Author of paper is a role/person type (a subclass of Author, sibling of Author of paper student). They denote different concepts: a document versus a person role, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while edas's Accepted Paper is a specific state of a Paper (siblings Pending/Rejected/Withdrawn/Published). Accepted Paper is a narrower concept, so confOf Paper subsumes edas Accepted Paper; they are not equivalent.

A Programme Brochure is a document listing events (it has properties event On List / lists Event and publisher Of), whereas a sigkdd Abstract is a short summary document of a paper. They are different document types with different roles and properties, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (an event delivered at the conference), while B's 'Invitation letter' is a Document (a written artefact sent to invite someone). Different kinds of things: one is a presentation event, the other a document, so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Bid is a reviewer's expressed interest in reviewing a paper (domain/range Reviewer->Bid, Bid->Reviewer, Paper->Bid). In ekaw, Research Topic is a subject area covered by events/papers (Event, Paper -> Research Topic). They denote different concepts: a bid is a reviewing commitment, a research topic is a subject classification. No subsumption or overlap.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people/roles), while B's has_tutorials relates a Conference volume to its Tutorials (event parts). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Chair is a committee role (a person who chairs a committee, sibling of Co-chair, domain/range of committee-chair properties), while B's Building is a physical place (parent Place, with children like Conference hotel, Session room, and properties about being occupied/visited/paid in). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision) in the conference domain, while B's Car is a transport vehicle (sibling of Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) in a travel/accommodation domain. They share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a location' is a general datatype property of a Conference volume whose range is a string, covering any location (city, country, venue, etc.). B's 'City of conference' is a more specific property of a Conference whose range is a string restricted to the city. The city is one kind of location, so B's property is strictly narrower than A's; they are not equivalent.

A's 'early Registration' is a boolean flag on a Participant indicating whether they registered early; B's 'Currency' is a string-valued property of a Registration fee giving the currency of the fee. They have different domains (Participant vs Registration fee), different ranges (boolean vs string), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a mereological/containment relation), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (a reviewing-related assignment), while B's property links a document to a speaker (a presentation relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's has Conference Member relates a Conference to its members (people on the conference committee), while B's has_tracks relates a Conference volume to its Track (thematic subdivisions of the conference). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference document' is a class of documents (call for papers, contributions, reviews, announcements) with properties like has authors and date of issue. B's 'Conference' is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) in the event hierarchy. The two denote different concepts: a document vs. an event, so they are unrelated.

A 'Signal Processing Topic' is a research topic under Topic in edas, while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee under Committee in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject area vs. organizational body) and share no intended instances.

Paper Abstract (a document type in cmt, sibling of Paper Full Version) and Government Organization (an organization type in edas, sibling of Academia/Industry Organization) belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings), while B's `locationOf` relates a Location to the Event held there (domain Location, range Event). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Poster is a kind of conference contribution (a document/presentation form), while B's Abstract is a document type that is the abstract of a paper. Although A's Poster has an abstract, the classes denote different concepts: Poster is a contribution/presentation category, Abstract is the abstract document itself. They are not equivalent.

A's Neutral Review is a specific kind of review (sibling of Positive/Negative Review), while B's Review is the general review class. Neutral Review is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by Review, not equivalent.

Conference document is a class of documents (calls, announcements, contributions, reviews) authored by persons and issued on dates, whereas Sponzor is a sponsor organisation with supporter subclasses and a name; their instances, children and properties do not overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Rejection' is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision) in the conference domain, while B's 'Van' is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi) under Item. The labels, paths, parents and siblings show entirely different concepts with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship relation). B's design relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline (a deadline/design relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no overlap.

Both properties link an author/person to the contribution/item they produce: confOf's writes has domain Author and range Contribution, iasted's send has domain Person and range Item. In the conference domain, Author/Person and Contribution/Item are the corresponding classes, and both relations express authorship submission in the same direction, so they denote the same relation.

A 'Conference announcement' is a kind of conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational text. B 'Activity after conference' is a social/programme activity (parent of Departure, Full day tour) occurring after the event. Different domains (document vs. activity), no overlap.

A's co-writePaper relates a Co author (an author entity) to a Paper, i.e. authorship from author to paper. B's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person, i.e. authorship from document to person. They are inverses in direction and use different entity types (Co author vs Document, Paper vs Person), so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial or workshop), while B's Technic activity is a conference activity (a scheduled item such as lecture, presentation, or coffee break). The two concepts belong to different branches of the conference domain and do not denote the same class of instances.

Both classes denote a person who authors conference contributions/papers. In confOf, Author is a Person who writes Contributions; in sigkdd, Author is a Speaker who submits Papers and can obtain awards. Despite different parent paths (Person vs Speaker), the intended instances coincide: people who author papers. The differing properties (writes/written By vs submit/obtain) are ontology-specific relations on the same concept, not evidence of a different concept.

A's 'organised By' is an object property linking an Event to an Organisation or Person (who organises it), while B's 'Name of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (its name). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have different domains/ranges, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is an event type (Workshop, a kind of Scientific Event). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Proceedings Publisher' is an Organisation (an agent that publishes proceedings), while B's 'Cd proceening' is a Publication/Item (a physical or digital artefact, a CD of proceedings). They denote different kinds of entities (agent vs. artefact), so they are not equivalent.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving a string name for a Conference or Person; B's `is used by` is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Submitted Paper is a scholarly paper submitted to a conference (a subclass of Paper, with siblings like Camera Ready Paper and Regular Paper). B's Payment document is a financial document (parent Document, children Bank transfer and Cheque) used for paying conference fees. They share no intended instances: one is a research contribution, the other a payment instrument. The shared word 'document' in the paths reflects different domains, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'is used for' relates an Item to an Activity or Money (domain Item, range Activity/Money), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (domain Person, range Place). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Both classes denote the same social conference event: a formal meal/banquet held during the conference. confOf's Banquet is a Social event alongside Reception and Trip, while edas's Conference Dinner is a Meal Event under Non Academic Event. The labels and contexts (social/meal event at a conference) coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (sibling of Tutorial/Workshop) that hosts papers and talks; B's Coffee Break is a non-academic break event (sibling of Meal Break/Free Time Break). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Trip is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception), i.e. an excursion/outing. B's Break Event is a non-academic event with children Coffee Break, Free Time Break and Meal Break, i.e. a scheduled pause in the programme. The intended instances do not coincide: a trip is not a break, and neither class subsumes the other.

A's hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property of Call giving submission instructions text, while B's Name is a datatype property of Person giving a person's name. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A is a physical place for lodging (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place under Place), while B is a person role (a student who is also a lecturer) under Lecturer in a person hierarchy. Different kinds of entities, no overlap.

A's Flyer is a promotional document (sibling of Programme Brochure, Web Site, Multi author Volume, and publisher Of range), while B's Abstract is the summary of a paper (sibling of Paper and Review). They are different document types despite both being Documents.

A's 'has an email' relates a Person to an email address string, while B's 'has Home Page' relates a Person to a homepage URL string. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote different attributes (email vs. homepage), so a reference alignment would not equate them.

A's hasStreet is a datatype property linking an Organization or Person to a string (a street address), while B's organisedBy is an object property linking an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organiser). They differ in domain (Organization/Person vs Event), range (string vs Organisation/Person), and meaning (address vs organiser relation), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property giving a person's given name (range string), while B's 'has Home Page' gives a person's web page URL (range string). They relate different kinds of information about a Person, so they are not equivalent.

A's Speaker is a general delegate role (parent of Author and Reviewer, sibling of Listener, Session chair, etc.), while B's Invited Speaker is a specific kind of speaker (a Person who is a Speaker, sibling of Author). Every Invited Speaker is a Speaker, but not every Speaker is an Invited Speaker, so A is more general and is subsumed by B.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on a Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are allowed, while B's 'is a date of acceptance announcement' is a date property on Important dates giving when acceptance is announced. They have different domains, different ranges (boolean vs date), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property giving the postal code of an Organization or Person, while B's E-mail gives the email address of a Person. They relate different kinds of data (postal code vs. email address) and have different domains (Organization/Person vs. Person only), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'has an organizing committee' relates a Conference volume to an Organizing committee, while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to its website URI (range anyURI), while B's 'start Date' links a Conference to its starting date/time (range dateTime). They relate conferences to entirely different kinds of values (a URL vs. a date), so they are not the same relation.

A 'Hotel room' is a specific room inside a hotel, while B 'Hotel' is the whole building/place. A hotel room is part of a hotel, so the room concept is narrower than the hotel concept; they are not equivalent. The room is subsumed by the broader hotel/place notion.

Both classes are named Review and sit under Document in their respective hierarchies. In cmt, Review is a Document subclass with children Meta Review and siblings Paper, and is linked to Reviewer via write Review / written By, matching the conference-domain notion of a review of a paper. In iasted, Review is likewise a Document subclass alongside Submission and other conference documents. The intended instances (reviews of submissions) coincide, so the two are equivalent.
Both ontologies model the same conference organization domain, with classes such as Conference, Paper, Author, Committee, Event, and Chair/Reviewer roles aligning closely in meaning and structure.

hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country (a geographic affiliation), while obtain relates a Person to an Item (an acquisition relation). Different domains (Organization/Person vs Person) and completely different ranges (Country vs Item) mean the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's registrationDueOn is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (the registration deadline), while B's eventOnList is an object property linking an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (where the event is listed). They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to a Subject Area (topic classification), while B's obtain relates a Person to an Item (acquisition). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but A's 'registration Due On' is specifically the conference registration deadline (domain Conference), while B's 'is dated on' is a general dating property for any Activity. They overlap in that a registration deadline is a date associated with an activity, but they are not the same relation: B is broader and not restricted to registration deadlines.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer, while B's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event. Different domains and ranges, different intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's 'Program Committee' is the committee as a whole (a group/collection), with properties has Program Committee Member and member Of Program Committee linking it to individual members. B's 'Program Committee member' is an individual person role (a subclass of Organizator, sibling of Program Chair, General Chair, etc.). The two denote different concepts: a committee vs. a person who is a member of it. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other (a committee is not a kind of person, and a member is not a kind of committee).

ekaw:Paper is a scientific contribution (subclasses: Conference Paper, Workshop Paper, Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, etc.) with properties like has Review, covers Topic, paper Presented As. iasted:Document is a generic administrative artefact (subclasses: Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Mailing list, Record of attendance, Viza, Transparency) under Item, with no scholarly-paper semantics. The shared word 'Document'/'Paper' does not make them the same concept; Paper is a specific kind of document, not the generic Document class, and the sibling/child contexts are entirely different.

An Invited speaker is a distinguished person who gives a talk by invitation, a subtype of Conference contributor alongside Regular author and Active conference participant. A Listener is a subtype of Delegate who attends without presenting. The two denote different roles in the conference domain: an invited speaker is a speaker, whereas a listener is explicitly a non-speaker. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), while B's 'has Topic' relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (domain Conference/Paper, range Topic). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), expressing that events run in parallel. edas's 'for Event' relates a Call to an Academic Event, expressing which event a call is issued for. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A is a hotel reservation deadline (a logistical/registration-related deadline), while B is the author notification deadline (when authors learn of acceptance). They are distinct deadlines in the conference timeline with different meanings, despite sharing the parent Deadline.

A's 'referenced In' relates a paper/contribution to the document/event in which it is referenced (bibliographic citation relation), while B's 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (a person signs an item, e.g. a registration or document). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a person/contact to a string email address; B's writtenBy is an object property linking a document to a person author. They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.
A's Paper is a conference submission/document with authors, topics and reviews; B's Credit card is a payment card item. Different domains and no shared context, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Author is a general person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers, with children Author Not Reviewer and Co author), whereas Conference:Regular author is a specific kind of conference contribution/contributor (a regular, non-invited author of a contribution, sibling of Invited speaker and Poster). Every regular author is an author, but authors also include invited speakers and other contributor types, so cmt:Author is broader and Regular author is subsumed by it.

A's 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment relation), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (who pays the fee). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings differ, and the directions are not even inverses of each other, so the two properties are unrelated.

A's hasEmail relates a Person to an email string, while B's hasLastName relates a Person to a last name string. They are different datatype properties with different intended values, so they are not equivalent.

cmt:name is a general name property with domain Conference and Person, while confOf:hasFirstName is specifically a person's first name (comment notes it involves middle name). They overlap for persons but are not the same concept: name is broader and also applies to Conference, and hasFirstName is narrower (first name only). Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property of Conference volume giving the location/venue of a volume, while B's 'has Name' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's full name. Different domains (Conference volume vs Conference) and different intended values (location vs name), so they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is the event itself (has a name, has Conference volume/parts, proceedings, publisher, topic), while B's Conference hotel is a physical building (Place > Building) that is merely a venue/hotel used by a conference. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a conference-domain relation about reviewing), while B's property links a Building/City/State to a Person (a location-visitation relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented), while B 'Best Student Paper Award' is a type of award. They belong to different branches of the conference domain (event vs. award) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person who presents at the conference: ekaw's Presenter is a Conference Participant who gives a presentation (with Invited Speaker as a child), and iasted's Speaker is a Delegate who speaks (with Author and Reviewer as children). The intended instances coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent despite the different parent paths.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for SIGMOD members). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. fee) and share no intended instances.

Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection under Decision) about whether a submitted paper is accepted, while Invited Talk is a kind of individual presentation (sibling of Contributed Talk and Tutorial) at a scientific event. They belong to different branches of the conference domain (decision vs. presentation type) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A Program Committee Chair is a person who chairs the PC and reviews papers (it has a Review range property), while a Reviewer is any person who reviews. A PC Chair is a specialized reviewer/chair role, not the same concept as a generic Reviewer; they overlap in that both review, but the PC Chair has additional chairing duties and a distinct position in the hierarchy (under Chairman/PC Member, sibling of Conference Chair), whereas Reviewer is a generic delegate/speaker role. Hence related, not equivalent.

In cmt, Document is a general class whose only named children are Paper and Review, and it is the range of 'has Conflict Of Interest'. In Conference, Conference document is a broader class covering calls, announcements, contributions, www pages, participant information and reviews, with properties 'contributes', 'has a date of issue' and 'has authors'. Every cmt Document (paper or review) is a kind of conference document, but Conference document also includes non-paper artefacts such as calls and announcements, so cmt Document is strictly narrower and is subsumed by Conference document.

confOf's 'parallel with' is a symmetric relation between two Administrative events (domain and range both Administrative event), indicating events that run in parallel. edas's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event (domain Programme, range Conference Event), i.e. a containment/association relation in the opposite direction and between different kinds of entities. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has an email' relates a Person to an email address string, while B's 'has Last Name' relates a Person to a surname string. They are different datatype properties with different intended values (email vs. last name), so they are not equivalent.

University is an organizational class (a type of Organization, sibling of Company) representing an academic institution, while Personal Review History is a personal-history class representing a reviewer's record of reviews. Their paths, parents, siblings and properties (study At vs. has/is Review History Of) show entirely different intended instances; they share no concept in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class (parent of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles) tied to conferences via member Of Conference, while Session Chair in edas is a specific chair role for a session, tied to Call/Paper review relations. The intended instances do not coincide: a Conference Member need not chair a session, and a Session Chair is a specific chair role, not the general membership class.

A's Conference is the whole conference event (has members, dates, administrators, submissions), while B's Abstract is a document subtype under Document, sibling of Paper and Review, presented at a presentation. They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A's max Papers is a datatype property of Program Committee Member giving an integer limit on papers; B's Name of conference is a datatype property of Conference giving a string name. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's 'Author cd proceedings included' is a subclass of Author (a person role whose proceedings are included on a CD). They denote entirely different concepts — an event versus a person/author category — so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Demo Paper' is a specific kind of paper (a demo submission). They belong to different branches (document/announcement vs. paper type) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a specific datatype property capturing only the surname of a Person, while B's 'Name' is the general full-name property of a Person. Every last name is a name, but not every name is a last name, so A is strictly narrower than B (subsumed_by). They are not equivalent because the intended values differ in scope.

A is a research topic class (a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic, sibling of Network Security/Sensor/etc.), while B is an organizational committee class (a subcategory of Committee, sibling of Program Committee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject areas vs. organizational roles) and share no instances.

A 'Social event' is a conference social gathering (banquet, reception, trip) under Event, while B 'Evaluated Paper' is a document that has received reviews under Submitted/Assigned Paper. They belong to different branches (Event vs Document) and denote entirely different concepts.

A's 'has a review expertise' links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (a reviewer's topic expertise), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the talk/slides given by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same property.

OC Member (Organizing Committee Member) in ekaw and Program Committee member in sigkdd both denote members of the conference's organizing/program committee. In ekaw, OC Member sits under Conference Participant alongside PC Chair, Session Chair, etc., and has child OC Chair; in sigkdd, Program Committee member sits under Organizator alongside General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair. Both refer to the committee that reviews papers and organizes the conference, so the intended instances coincide.

A's Reviewer is a Person role (a person who reviews, with review expertise/preferences and co-reviewer relations), while B's Personal Publication History is a record/history of a person's publications, sibling of Personal Review History. They denote different concepts (person vs. publication record), so they are unrelated.

A's Social Event is a general category of non-academic social events (children Excursion, Reception; siblings Break Event, Meal Event), while B's Conference Banquet is a specific social event (sibling Conference Trip) under a Social Event parent. Thus A is broader and subsumes B, not equivalent.

A's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while B's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (location). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's Reviewer is a Person who reviews papers (a human role, with properties like 'invited by', 'invites co reviewers', 'belongs to reviewers'). B's Numerical Review Question is a subclass of Review Question, i.e. a question type on a review form, not a person. They share no meaning despite the word 'review'.
A is a research topic (a subject area under Topic), while B is an award category (under Award). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'Agency Staff Member' is a generic Person subtype for staff working for the organising agency (siblings: Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student), with no connection to authorship. B's 'Author of paper student' is a subtype of Author restricted to students who authored a paper. The two denote different concepts: agency staff vs. student paper author. Neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

A's Registration is a conference activity (an event/process with Delegate participants, sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break), whereas B's Registration Non Member is a specific registration fee category (sibling of Registration SIGKDD Member, Registration Student). They denote different concepts: an activity vs. a fee type, so they are not equivalent.

Meta Reviewer in cmt is a subclass of Reviewer (a person role), while Review in sigkdd is a subclass of Document (a written artefact). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and are not equivalent.

A's property links a Review preference to the topic/contribution it prefers, while B's 'reviewes' links a PC member to the contribution they review. Different domains (Review preference vs Member PC) and different intended relations (preference vs reviewing), so they are not equivalent.

Associated Chair (cmt) is a chair role associated with the conference/chairman hierarchy, while Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is a specific chair for tutorials under Conference Participant. Different roles with no subsumption or overlap.

Topic in edas is a subject area of papers/conferences (has Topic links Conference/Paper to Topic), while Person in sigkdd is a human participant (Listener/Organizator/Speaker) with name, email, nation, fees. Different intended instances and roles; no overlap.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses like Invited speaker and Regular author), while Social Event is a subclass of Non Academic Event (a conference event such as Excursion or Reception). They belong to different branches of the domain (people vs. events) and cannot denote the same concept.

Scholar in confOf is a price category (a person who studies at a university, with property study At), while Reviewer in edas is a person who reviews papers (with review-history and reviewing properties). They denote different roles in the conference domain and share no defining properties, so they are not equivalent.
A's has Author relates a Paper to an Author; B's has a publisher relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher. Different domain, range and intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'relates To' is a general Document-to-entity relation (domain Document, range Academic Event/Conference/Conference Session/Person), while B's 'scientifically Organises' is an Academic Institution-to-? relation. They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Final manuscript' is a Submission/Document (the camera-ready version of a paper), while B's 'Best Student Paper Award' is an Award, a recognition given to a paper/author. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property linking a Person to their family name (string). B's 'Nation' links a Person to their nationality/country (string). Although both are Person->string datatype properties, they denote different attributes (surname vs. nation), so they are not equivalent.

A Tutorial is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation session at a conference), while a Power Point presentation in iasted is a presentation activity/artefact (a slide-based presentation), sibling of Video presentation. They denote different concepts: an event type vs. a presentation medium/activity, so they are not equivalent.

A is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date value (the acceptance-notification deadline), while B is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the venue of an event). They share neither domain, range, nor intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a document produced by a reviewer (a subclass of Document, sibling of Paper, with properties write Review / written By linking Reviewer to Review). B's Call For Papers is a call/announcement (subclass of Call, sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews) that solicits submissions. A review document and a call for papers are different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is sent by' is an object property linking an Item to a Person (the sender of a submission), while B's 'E mail' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their email address). They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Item vs Person), and range (Person vs string), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's hasCo-author relates a Paper to a Co-author (a person who co-authored the paper), while B's contributes relates a Person to a Conference document (the person contributes to the document). The domains and ranges are swapped in direction and kind: A goes Paper -> Co-author, B goes Person -> Conference document. They are not the same relation, nor inverses in a meaningful sense (a co-author relation is not the same as a contribution relation).

Conference part is a structural component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) with properties like has a name, has a track workshop tutorial chair, and is part of conference volumes. Building is a physical place (Place > Building) with children such as Conference airport, Conference hotel, and properties about occupancy, payment, and location. The two denote different concepts: one is an event component, the other a physical venue, so they are unrelated.

A's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (a reviewer inviting a co-reviewer), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (a person writing a paper/item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

OC Member (Organising Committee member) is a Conference Participant role in ekaw, with child OC Chair; Speaker in iasted is a Delegate subtype whose children are Author and Reviewer. The two denote different conference roles (organising committee membership vs. speaking/presenting), with no subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's 'Short paper' is a subclass of Contribution (a document/paper type, sibling of Paper and Poster), whereas B's 'Paper Presentation' is an Academic Event (a conference activity, sibling of Talk Event and Workshop) that relates Accepted Paper to the event. One denotes a kind of submission, the other a kind of event, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document type (a short summary of a paper, sibling of 'Paper Full Version' under 'Paper'), whereas B 'Mailing list' is a document used for conference communication (sibling of 'Invitation letter', 'Form', 'Review', etc. under 'Document'). They denote different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'Program committee' is a collective committee (a group) that is part of the conference organisation, with siblings Organizing committee and Steering committee. B's 'Possible Reviewer' is a role of an individual Person, the superclass of PC Member, and is the range of review-related properties. A committee (group) and an individual reviewer role are different kinds of entities, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper they review), while B's has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic (the subject matter a reviewer prefers). Different domains (Reviewer vs Review preference), different ranges (Paper vs Submitted contribution/Topic), and different intended meaning (assignment of a paper to review vs. expressed preference for a topic/submission). They are not the same relation.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship). B's paper Presented As relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (presentation format). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's User is a general person role in the conference system (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while B's Student is a specific person type (sibling of Paper Author, Possible Reviewer). A User is not a Student and a Student is not necessarily a User; the concepts denote different things and neither subsumes the other.

A's Document is a written artefact (children Abstract, Paper, Review, etc., with author/writtenBy properties), while B's Money is a monetary amount (children Fee, Tax, Tip, with amount/payment properties). Different domains entirely; no overlap.

A's Conference is an event/venue class (it has a name and is a whole with parts such as Conference volume, proceedings, publisher, topic), whereas B's Conference Paper is a subclass of Paper, i.e. a document artefact. The two denote different kinds of things (event vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property of a Conference document (a paper/contribution) giving its issue/publication date, while B's 'end Date' is the end date/time of the Conference event itself. Different domains (document vs. conference) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Review preference' is a class describing a reviewer's preference/degree for a topic or submission (domain of 'has a degree', 'has a topic or a submission contribution', linked to Reviewer and Topic). B's 'Time' is a temporal class (parent of Conference days, Deadline, Trip day; range of 'is held after/before', 'is sent after/before'). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Invited speaker (a distinguished speaker invited to a conference) and Assistant (a helper role, per the confTool comment) denote different roles in the conference domain; they share no intended instances and neither subsumes the other.

cmt:Review is the general review document class (parent of Meta Review, sibling of Paper, written by a Reviewer), while ekaw:Negative Review is a specific review outcome, a subclass of ekaw:Review alongside Neutral and Positive Review. The cmt class is strictly more general than the ekaw subclass, so cmt:Review subsumes ekaw:Negative Review rather than being equivalent to it.

A's hasSurname is a datatype property linking a Person to their surname string, while B's hasBiography links a Person to a biographical text string. They capture different attributes of a person (family name vs. biography), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, choices), while B's 'Computer Networks Topic' is a subclass of Topic, a subject area with subtopics like security and switching. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (events vs. topics) and share no instances.

A's property links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (a role/committee position), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or item). Different domains (Conference part vs Person) and ranges (Track workshop chair vs Activity/Item), so they denote different relations.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people/roles), while B's has_contributions relates a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers). Different domain and range concepts, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's property links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (the preference of a reviewer for reviewing that contribution), while B's 'reviewes' links a PC member to a contribution they review. The domains and ranges are disjoint (Submitted contribution/Topic vs Member PC; Review preference vs Contribution), and the directions/roles differ, so they are not the same relation.

Pending Paper is a specific submission state of a paper (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published/Withdrawn Paper), whereas sigkdd's Paper is the general paper class (parent of Abstract and Review, domain of submit). Every Pending Paper is a Paper, but not vice versa, so Pending Paper is strictly more specific.
A is an accepted paper/contribution in the submission workflow; B is a hotel-reservation deadline. Different domains (document vs. time/deadline), no shared instances.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' is an administrative action relating an Administrator to a Program Committee Member, while B's 'occupy' relates a Person to a Building/City/State (a location). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's hasPhone is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a phone number; B's Name is a datatype property of Person giving a person's name. Different domains and different intended values, so they are not the same relation.

Trip (confOf) is a social event, a subcategory of Event, typically an excursion during the conference. Full day tour (iasted) is an activity after the conference, a subcategory of Activity. Both denote an organized excursion/tour, but they belong to different top-level categories (social event vs. post-conference activity) and different temporal contexts, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'has Topic' links a Conference or Paper to a Topic. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance, under Decision), while B's Accepting manuscript is an activity in the conference process (sibling of Refusing manuscript, Receiving manuscript). They denote different concepts: a decision result versus a process activity, and B is not even the negative counterpart of A.

Conference document is a broad class covering calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc., while Conference Proceedings is a specific multi-author volume of conference papers. The Conference document class is more general and would include Conference Proceedings as one kind of document, so it subsumes rather than being equivalent.
A's topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to the Events/Papers that cover it, while B's need relates a Person to an Item they need. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' links a Conference to an Administrator (the person who finalizes paper assignments), while B's 'paper Presented As' links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the presentation form of a paper). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' links a Conference to an Administrator (the person who finalizes paper assignments), while B's 'parallel with' links two Administrative events (scheduling relation between concurrent events). Different domain, range, and meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'technically Organised By' is a sub-property of 'organised By' linking an event/conference to the agent that organises it technically. B's 'occupy' links a Person to a Building/City/State (a location-occupancy relation). Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent.

A's 'Negative Review' is a specific subtype of Review (sibling of Neutral/Positive Review), while B's 'Review' is the general review document class. Every Negative Review is a Review, but not vice versa, so A is strictly more specific and is subsumed by B.

A's 'Personal Publication History' is a subclass of Personal History describing an author's record of publications; B's 'Sponzor fee' is a subclass of Fee describing a sponsor's payment. Different domains (history vs. fee), different parents and siblings, no shared properties or comments; they denote unrelated concepts.

Attendee in edas is a general Person who attends the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles), while Invited Speaker in ekaw is a specific Presenter role. An invited speaker is a kind of attendee/presenter, but the two classes do not have coinciding extensions: not every attendee is an invited speaker, and the ekaw class is a narrow presenter subtype. They are not equivalent; at most a loose relatedness, but the intended concepts differ.

A 'Committee member' is a person role in the conference organisation (a Person subclass, parent of Chair/Co chair, involved in committees via has members/was a member of). B 'Meeting Room Place' is a physical location (a Place subclass, sibling of Conference Venue Place, Accommodation Place, Dining Place). They denote entirely different concepts — a person role versus a venue location — so they are unrelated.

Both are deadline classes under a Deadline parent; A is the deadline for notification of acceptance and B is the deadline for author notification, which denote the same conference milestone (notification of acceptance to authors).

A's property links a Conference part to a Topic (the subject matter of a track/workshop/tutorial), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/presenting something). Different domains (Conference part vs Person), different ranges (Topic vs Activity/Item), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'virtual Meeting Enabled By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables virtual meetings), while B's 'gives presentations' relates an Active conference participant to a Presentation. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Author is a subclass of Person in confOf, denoting a person who writes contributions. Web Site is a subclass of Document in ekaw, denoting a document/artefact that lists events. They belong to disjoint branches (person vs document) and share no properties or intended instances, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person and is a broad role covering anyone attending the conference (siblings include Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, etc.). In ekaw, Early Registered Participant is a subclass of Conference Participant, which is itself a subclass of Person; it denotes a participant who registered early, a narrower notion than a general attendee. Thus Attendee is more general than Early Registered Participant, so the edas class is subsumed by the ekaw class (equivalently, the ekaw class is a specialization). They are not equivalent because the ekaw class adds the early-registration condition and sits under Conference Participant.

A Free Time Break is a non-academic break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break) within the conference schedule, whereas a Conference Banquet is a social event (sibling of Conference Trip). Although both are non-academic conference events, a free-time break is unstructured downtime while a banquet is an organised social gathering; they are distinct concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome of a submission), while B's is_held_after relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the person who gives it (an Active conference participant), while B's 'has Attendee' links a Conference Event to any Person attending. The domains differ (Presentation vs Conference Event) and the ranges differ in specificity (Active conference participant vs Person); a presenter is a kind of attendee, so the relations overlap but are not the same relation in the same direction.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event in confOf, covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, choices). B 'Powerline Transmission Topic' is a subclass of Topic in edas, a subject area for papers. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Tutorial is a scientific event (an individual presentation session, sibling of Contributed Talk and Invited Talk), whereas B's Tutorial speaker is a person role (a subclass of Author/Speaker, sibling of Lecturer and Plenary lecture speaker). One denotes an event, the other a person, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'accept Paper' relates an Administrator (a person/role) to a Paper they accept, i.e. the acceptance decision. B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker, i.e. who presents the document. Different domains (Administrator vs Document), different ranges (Paper vs Speaker), and different meanings (accepting vs presenting); they are not the same relation.

A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (a location attribute of an event), while B's is_visited_by relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a visitor relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a Person who may review papers (parent of PC Member, domain/range of review-related properties). Author in sigkdd is a Speaker who submits papers and receives notifications/awards. The intended instances differ: reviewers vs authors, and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Meal Break' is a break event (a scheduled pause for eating) within the conference event hierarchy, while B 'Trip day' is a time unit (a day of a trip) under Time. They denote different concepts: one is an event type, the other a temporal interval, with no shared instances.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip), while B Dinner banquet is a specific social-program activity. Both are social events, but a reception is not a dinner banquet; they overlap as social events without being equivalent.

Location in ekaw is a venue/place where events are held (domain/range of held In and location Of with Event), while Currency in iasted is a monetary unit. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'max Papers' is a datatype property giving the maximum number of papers a Program Committee Member may review/handle (domain Program Committee Member, range int). B's 'paper Presented As' is an object property linking a Paper/Abstract to its Individual Presentation (domain Abstract/Paper, range Individual Presentation). They relate entirely different kinds of entities (a numeric limit vs. a presentation relation) and have different domains/ranges, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'location Of' is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's 'is dated on' is a datatype property linking an Activity to a dateTime (its date). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have different ranges (Event vs dateTime), so they are not equivalent.

Conference contributor is a broad role class covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors (people who contribute to a conference), whereas confOf's Assistant is a helper role (comment 'confTool') alongside Administrator, Volunteer, etc. The intended instances do not coincide: an assistant is not a contributor in the paper/authoring sense, and the sibling sets (Committee member, Reviewer, Track workshop chair vs Administrator, Chair PC, Member PC, Volunteer) show different role taxonomies. No subsumption either, since neither class's instances are a subset of the other's.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author (a person who writes papers but is not a reviewer), while B's 'Worker non speaker' is a subclass of Non speaker under Delegate (a conference attendee who works but does not give a talk). The two concepts come from different branches (Author vs Delegate/Non speaker) and denote different roles in the conference domain; they are not equivalent.

A Conference Chair is a specific chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while B Organizing Committee member is a broader category covering all organizers (General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). A Conference Chair is one type of organizing committee member, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a part-whole/structural relation), while B's 'parallel with' links an Administrative event to another Administrative event (a scheduling relation between events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Event is the general event class (children include Administrative, Social and Working events), while ekaw's Scientific Event is a subclass of ekaw's Event restricted to scientific happenings (Conference, Session, Workshop, etc.) and is a sibling of Social Event. Thus confOf Event is broader and subsumes ekaw Scientific Event; they are not equivalent.

A's 'is an ending date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date literal (a temporal deadline), while B's 'location Of' is an object property linking a Location to an Event (spatial containment). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper Abstract is a subclass of Paper (a document type for submitted papers), while B's Tutorial Abstract is a subclass of Abstract under Document, specifically the abstract of a tutorial event. They share the word 'Abstract' but denote different document types in different branches (Paper vs. Abstract/event), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI (its website address), while B's 'is present in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place/Time (attendance). They have different domains (Conference vs Person), different ranges (anyURI vs Place/Time), and different kinds (datatype vs object), so they denote different relations.

A's defaultChoice is a datatype property of Social/Working event with range positiveInteger (a confTool default choice count), while B's End_of_conference is a datatype property of Conference with range dateTime (the conference end time). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'set Max Papers' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a per-member paper limit), while B's 'has a program committee' relates a Conference volume to a Program committee (linking a conference to its committee). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a property of a Conference document giving the date the document was issued/published (domain: Conference document, range: date). B's 'registration Due On' is a property of a Conference giving the registration deadline date/time (domain: Conference, range: dateTime, comment: 'Conference Registration Date and Time Deadline'). Different domains (document vs conference) and different intended meanings (issue/publication date vs registration deadline), so they are not equivalent.

A's studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (where a scholar studies/works), while B's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (its author). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Rated Papers' is a subclass of Active Paper (a paper that has received at least one review/rating) in edas, whereas sigkdd's 'Abstract' is a distinct document type (a short summary document) sibling to Paper and Review. They denote different concepts: one is a status of a full paper, the other a separate document artefact, so they are not equivalent.

A's Non Academic Event is a broad category covering breaks, meals and social events, while B's Social Event is a narrower category (with children Conference Banquet and Conference Trip) that corresponds to A's Social Event child. Thus Non Academic Event is more general than Social Event, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A is a conference document type (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic in a topic taxonomy (Computer Networks Topic with subtopics). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's property relates an Administrator to a Conference (printing/mailing hardcopy manifests), while B's property relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Chairman is a role/person class (a person chairing a conference, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Sponzor fee is a subclass of Fee (a monetary charge). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's `is Location Of` goes Place -> Conference Event (a place hosts an event), while B's `is held in` goes Activity -> Place, Time (an activity takes place at a location/time). They are inverses in direction and differ in domain/range (B also includes Time), so they are not equivalent; they are related as inverse/overlapping notions of event-location association.

In confOf, Conference is a working event (a whole event with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while in edas TalkEvent is a specific academic talk session (with Closing Talk and Welcome Talk as children, siblings Paper Presentation and Workshop). A conference is not a talk event; the entities denote different concepts.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while B's Best Student Paper Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsorship category). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. sponsor role), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity in the conference process (sibling of Receiving/Refusing manuscript), i.e. the act of accepting a manuscript. B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline (a point in time) for submitting papers, sibling of abstract submission and author notification deadlines. They are not the same concept: one is an activity, the other a temporal deadline. They are only loosely related as parts of the submission/acceptance workflow, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

Conference Member (cmt) is a Person subtype representing people involved in a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs), while Academic Event (edas) is a Conference Event subtype representing scheduled academic activities (talks, workshops, presentations). They belong to different branches (Person vs Conference Event) and have incompatible properties (member Of Conference vs has Call/for Event), so they denote different concepts.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class under Person whose children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, Conference Chair, etc., and it is linked to Conference via member Of Conference. Reviewer in Conference is a specific role (a person who reviews) with review-expertise properties. Reviewer is one of the many sub-roles of Conference Member, so Conference Member is strictly more general than Reviewer; they are not equivalent.

Both denote a workshop event in the conference domain. confOf's Workshop is a Working event alongside Conference and Tutorial; ekaw's Workshop Session is a Session (a scientific event) alongside Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session. The intended instances coincide: a workshop held at a conference. The differing parent (Working event vs Session) reflects different upper-level structuring, not different concepts, and the sibling sets are parallel (Conference/Tutorial vs Conference Session/Regular Session).

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (a whole-part containment relation between a volume and its papers). B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person produces/gives an activity or item). The domains (Conference volume vs Person) and ranges (Conference contribution vs Activity/Item) differ, and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. a written announcement. B 'Talk Event' is an academic event (a subclass of Academic Event, with children Closing Talk and Welcome Talk), i.e. a scheduled talk. A document and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated despite both relating to conferences.

A's Conference is the conference event itself (has members, country, topics, deadlines). B's Conference state is a state of a conference participant/entity (sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state under State), not the conference event. Different concepts.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property giving a person's surname, while B's 'has Fax' gives a person's fax number. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote entirely different attributes (surname vs. fax number), so they are not equivalent.

edas:Paper is a scholarly contribution (has authors, topics, reviews, and subclasses Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper), whereas iasted:Form is a document form (Author information form, Hotel registration form, Registration form). They share only the generic Document parent and denote different concepts.

Both classes denote the published collection of conference papers: A's 'Conference proceedings' has publisher, volume, ISBN and name properties, and B's 'Conference Proceedings' is a subclass of Proceedings (a Multi author Volume) under Document, matching the same intended instances.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a human role: active/passive participants, reviewers, committee members), while B's 'Conference building' is a subclass of Building (a physical place, sibling of conference airport/hotel/restaurant). Different kinds of entity (person vs. place), so the classes are unrelated despite both containing the word 'Conference'.

A is a research topic (a subject area under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is an award category (under Award, sibling of Best Research Paper Award). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Closing Talk' is a specific talk event that closes a conference, sibling of 'Welcome Talk' under 'Talk Event'. B 'Plenary lecture' is a type of lecture (a session format) under 'Lecture', sibling of 'Session' and 'Tutorial'. A closing talk could be a plenary lecture, but the concepts are not the same: one denotes a role/position in the programme, the other a lecture format. They are not equivalent and neither subsumes the other in the intended ontology.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'is used for' is an object property mapping an Item to an Activity or Money. They have different domains, different ranges, and different kinds (datatype vs object), so they cannot denote the same relation.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chairing/organisational role under Chairman/Conference Member, while Invited Speaker (ekaw) is a presenting role under Presenter/Conference Participant. They denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Accepted contribution' is a specific stage of a contribution (a reviewed contribution that was accepted, with 'Camera ready contribution' as a child and 'Rejected contribution' as a sibling). B's 'Contribution' is the general superclass of all submissions (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like has Title, written By, reviewes. Every accepted contribution is a contribution, but not every contribution is accepted, so A is strictly narrower than B: subsumed_by.

A 'Regular Session' is a kind of scientific event/session (a scheduled meeting where papers are presented), while B 'Session room' is a kind of Place (a physical room where a session is held). They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a general conference contribution (sibling of Extended abstract, with abstract-related properties), while B's Withdrawn Paper is a specific submission status under edas's Paper class. A Paper in the general sense is broader than a withdrawn paper, so A is subsumed by B's broader Paper concept; the two named classes are not equivalent.

A's property links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic (object property, domain Review preference, range Submitted contribution/Topic), while B's property links a Call to a string of submission instructions (datatype property, domain Call, range string). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A's readByMeta-Reviewer relates a Paper to its Meta Reviewer (domain Paper, range Meta Reviewer), while B's reviewWrittenBy relates a Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it (domain Review, range Possible Reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and direction of the underlying relation (paper-to-reviewer vs review-to-reviewer), so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Conference hall is a physical place (a kind of Place, sibling of Building, Hotel room, Session room). An event and a location are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'event On List' links an Event to the Programme Brochure/Web Site where it is listed. Different domains (Conference vs Event), different ranges (Administrator vs publication media), and different intended relations; they are not equivalent.

A's 'is sent before' relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering of submission), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

cmt's Associated Chair is a kind of Chairman/Conference Member (a chair role associated with the conference), while ekaw's PC Chair is a specific Program Committee chair role under Conference Participant/PC Member. Both are chair roles in the conference domain, but they are not the same concept: Associated Chair is broader/generic chair role, PC Chair is specifically the program committee chair. They overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so related.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's is_dated_on links an Activity to a dateTime (a temporal dating of an event). Different domains (Person vs Activity), different ranges (string vs dateTime), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote a conference contribution/paper that was reviewed and rejected. The paths are parallel (Reviewed contribution > Rejected contribution vs Evaluated Paper > Rejected Paper), both have an Accepted sibling, and the labels are synonymous in the conference domain.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) with title, abstract, keywords, authors and reviews. Review Rating in edas is the rating a reviewer gives to a paper (parent of Accept/Reject ratings) and is the range of has Rating from Active Paper. They denote different concepts: a submission versus an evaluation score, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document type in the conference-document hierarchy (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B 'Computer Networks Switching Topic' is a research topic in the edas topic taxonomy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's `obtain` is an object property linking a Person to an Item (a person obtains an item), while B's `Name of conference` is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string. They differ in domain (Person vs Conference), range (Item vs string), and kind (object vs datatype), so they denote different relations.

SC Member is a person role (a member of the steering committee, under PC Member in the Person hierarchy), while Sponzorship is a financial concept (money/sponsorship, under Money alongside Fee, Tax, Tip). Different domains and no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's Session Chair is a conference participant who chairs a session (a role with PC Member as parent, sibling of PC Chair, Workshop Chair, etc.). B's Listener is a kind of Delegate/attendee who merely listens, sibling of Speaker, Session chair, Non speaker. The two denote different roles: a session chair is an organiser/moderator, a listener is a passive attendee. Note B has its own 'Session chair' class, which is the proper counterpart of A's Session Chair, not Listener.

A's Paper is a contribution type (a submitted/ published document, sibling of Poster and Short paper under Contribution), whereas B's Call For Papers is a call/announcement event (sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews under Call). A paper is the object solicited by a call, not the call itself, so the classes denote different concepts.

Personal History in edas is a container of a person's publication and review history (children: Personal Publication History, Personal Review History), i.e. a record about a person's activities. Document in sigkdd is a conference submission artefact (children: Abstract, Paper, Review) with properties presentation, presentationed by, submit until. The two denote different concepts with no overlap in instances, so they are unrelated.

Location in ekaw is a general place where events are held (held In: Event -> Location; location Of: Location -> Event), covering any venue. Hotel in sigkdd is a specific kind of Place (sibling of Conference hall and Main office), i.e. a particular type of location.
