A Hotel is a Location, but not every Location is a Hotel, so Location is more general and subsumes Hotel.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a submission type, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract). B's 'Active Paper' is a paper in a particular submission/review state (under review, has a rating), sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper. The two denote different concepts: a document type versus a workflow status of a paper, so they are not equivalent.

A's Organizational Meeting is a conference event (sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop) such as a business or committee meeting, while B's Tutorial is a lecture-type conference activity (sibling of Plenary lecture, Session). They denote different concepts: a meeting vs. an instructional lecture, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (adding a member to a committee), while B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference (holding a conference). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to a Review (the review of a submission), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent.

Both properties link a written work to its author: confOf's 'written By' has domain Contribution and range Author, while iasted's 'is signed by' has domain Item and range Person. Contribution/Item both denote written contributions (papers) and Author/Person both denote the people who write them, so the two relations relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are equivalent.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of regular contribution (a submission type, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract), while B's 'Workshop Paper' is a paper type under Paper in ekaw, sibling of Conference Paper, Regular Paper, etc. They denote different concepts: an extended abstract is not a workshop paper, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf's 'writes' relates an Author (domain) to a Contribution (range), i.e. the author is the subject and the written work the object. iasted's 'is signed by' relates an Item (domain) to a Person (range), i.e. the written item is the subject and the person the object. The two properties are inverses of each other (author writes paper vs. paper is signed by author), so they are not equivalent; they are related as inverse relations.

A's Publication is a subclass of Item (a physical/artefact item such as book proceeding or CD proceeding), while B's Author is a subclass of Speaker/Person representing a person who writes papers. They denote different kinds of things (artefact vs. person) and are not equivalent.

A is a document type (a paper abstract, sibling of full paper) in the conference ontology; B is a research subject area (medicine) under Topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'is designed for' relates Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person (a broad 'intended for' relation), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (accommodation/location). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not the same relation.

Both are datatype properties with range int that give the monetary amount of a funding-related entity: edas hasCostAmount has domain Sponsorship, iasted has_amount_of has domain Money. Sponsorship and Money are the funding/monetary concepts in the two ontologies, and both properties express the amount of money involved, so they denote the same relation.

Both classes denote a person who reviews papers: cmt's Reviewer is a Conference Member/User who is assigned papers to review, adjusts bids, and can be assigned external reviewers; edas's Reviewer is a Person with a review history who is reviewing papers. The intended instances coincide (people who perform reviews), and the surrounding properties (assigned To / has Been Assigned vs is Reviewing / is Reviewed By) express the same review relation, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a subclass of Person (a human who applies/registers for a conference, with child 'Registeered applicant'), whereas B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Scientific Event (an edition of a conference). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property of Conference document giving the publication/issue date of a document. B's 'done till' is a datatype property of Deadline giving the date by which a deadline is completed. Different domains (document vs. deadline) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A is an Organizational Meeting, an academic event (sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop) such as a conference committee or organising meeting. B is Conference Proceedings, a document (a multi-author volume of published papers). An event and a publication are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

A's Paper is a full document (parent Document, with children like Conference Paper, Submitted Paper, Review, etc.), while B's Abstract is a distinct sibling of Paper under Document in sigkdd. An abstract is a summary, not a paper, so the two classes do not denote the same concept.

A 'Registration form' is a Document/Form artefact used for registration, while B 'Author' is a Person/Speaker role who submits papers. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Welcome Talk is a ceremonial opening talk at a conference, while a Contributed Talk is a regular submitted presentation. They are different kinds of talks with different roles, so they are not equivalent.

A's has End Date Time is a datatype property of Conference Event giving the event's end date/time, while B's done till is a datatype property of Deadline giving the date by which a deadline is finished. They have different domains (Conference Event vs Deadline) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Member' is a Person subtype (a person involved in the conference: chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), while B's 'Non Academic Event' is a Conference Event subtype (breaks, meals, social events). They belong to disjoint top-level branches (Person vs Conference Event) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Both denote a conference as an organised event: A's Conference has a name and a conference volume/proceedings, while B's Conference Event has a programme, location, start/end date times and attendees. The intended instances (a specific conference such as EDAS-hosted events) coincide, and B's subclasses Academic/Non Academic Event are just specialisations of the same concept. The differing property sets reflect modelling choices, not different concepts.

A's remark is a free-text note attached to a Contribution (confTool comment), while B's has Submission Instructions is a text field on a Call describing how to submit. Different domains (Contribution vs Call) and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Program Committee is a collective body of reviewers (with members, member-of relations), while B's Conference Chair is an individual person role (a Person subclass that initiates calls and reviews papers). They denote different concepts: a committee vs. a person role, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Closing Talk' is a talk that closes a conference (sibling of Welcome Talk, a ceremonial boundary event), whereas B 'Contributed Talk' is a regular submitted presentation (sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial). They denote different kinds of talks with no subsumption or overlap.

Both are leaf registration-fee classes under Registration fee, but A is specifically the fee for an author who is also an attendee (with CD), while B is the fee for a non-member registrant. They are distinct fee categories that overlap only in being registration fees, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (the document with which the person has a conflict), while B's writtenBy relates a Document to its author Person. They are inverse in direction and denote different relations (conflict-of-interest vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A's Author is a person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers), while B's Memeber registration fee is a monetary fee category under Registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document type (a short version of a paper, sibling of 'Paper Full Version' under 'Paper'), whereas B 'CAD Topic' is a subject-area topic (a kind of 'Topic', sibling of other research topics). They denote entirely different concepts: a document vs. a research subject category.

Company is an organizational entity (a type of Organization, sibling of University) in confOf, whereas Conference hall is a physical venue/place (a type of Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office) in sigkdd. They denote different kinds of things and do not coincide.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is a publication artefact (has publisher, volume, ISBN, name) that a Publisher issues. B's 'Conference Event' is a temporal event with start/end date-times, location, programme, and attendees, and is the parent of Academic/Non Academic Event. The two denote different concepts (publication vs. event), so they are unrelated.

Author in cmt is a specific role (a Person who writes/submits papers, sibling of Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while Person in ekaw is the general superclass of all people including Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student, etc. Author is strictly narrower than Person, so Author is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.
Both entities denote the same concept in the conference domain based on matching labels, paths, and context.

A 'Single hotel room' is a specific room type (a subclass of Hotel room, sibling of Double hotel room), while B 'Hotel' is the whole building/place. A room is not a hotel; the entities denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's Review is a document produced by a reviewer about a paper (child of Document, sibling of Paper, written by a Reviewer, parent of Meta Review). B's Personal Publication History is a personal history record listing a person's publications, sibling of Personal Review History under Personal History. They denote different concepts: a review document vs. a personal publication history listing, so they are unrelated.

A's 'write Paper' relates an Author to a Paper they authored (domain Author, range Paper, path Author > write Paper > Paper). B's 'has Related Paper' relates an Author to a Paper that is merely related (e.g. a paper they reviewed or are otherwise associated with), not necessarily authored. The intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.
A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while B's 'award' links something to an Award (a prize). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; no overlap.

cmt:Conference Member is a broad person role in the conference (parent of Author, Reviewer, PC Member, Chair roles) tied to a Conference via member Of Conference. confOf:Participant is a person attending/registering for the conference (has early Registration, children Member/Regular/Student). They overlap in that conference members are typically participants, but the intents differ: Conference Member covers organisational roles (chairs, PC members, reviewers) while Participant covers attendees/registrants. Neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (a gathering such as a banquet, reception or trip), while B 'Programme' is a subclass of Document (a printed/electronic schedule artefact). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Document) and have incompatible properties (location, VAT, choice counts vs belongs To Event), so they do not denote the same concept.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a Person who chairs the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, TPC Member), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical Place (sibling of Building, Hotel room, Session room). They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. venue location), so they are unrelated.

confOf's Administrator is a Person role (comment 'confTool') sitting as a sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc., i.e. a generic administrative person. sigkdd's Organizator is a Person whose children are the concrete organising roles (General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster), i.e. the organiser side of the conference. Both denote persons involved in running the conference, so they overlap, but Administrator is a narrower administrative role while Organizator is the broader organiser category; they are not the same concept, so related rather than equivalent.

A 'Camera Ready event' is an administrative event in the conference workflow (the deadline/activity for submitting camera-ready versions), while B 'Program Committee' is a committee of people. They belong to different branches (Event vs Committee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `obtain` is an object property linking a Person to an Item (a person obtains an item), while B's `Name of sponsor` is a datatype property linking a Sponzor to a string (the sponsor's name). They differ in domain, range, and kind (object vs datatype), so they denote different relations.

A's Conference is the event itself (has a name, has parts, proceedings, publisher, topic), while B's Conference hall is a physical Place (sibling of Building, Hotel room, Session room) where such events are held. Different intended instances, so not equivalent.

A 'One conference day' is a temporal unit within the Conference days hierarchy, while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee grouping people. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that run in parallel (a symmetric, specific co-occurrence relation), while ekaw's 'has Event' is a general partitive/containment relation between an Event and its sub-events. They both link events to events but are not the same relation: 'parallel with' is symmetric and denotes co-occurrence, 'has Event' is directed and denotes composition, so they are related but not equivalent.

Attendee in edas is a generic person who attends the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles), while Program Committee member in sigkdd is a specific organizer role under Organizator (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). A PC member is an organizer, not a generic attendee; the intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution (a document submitted to a conference, sibling of Paper), while B's 'Transport vehicle' is a physical means of transport (parent of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) under Item. The domains are entirely different, so the classes are unrelated.

EDAS 'Accept Rating' is a specific rating value indicating acceptance, a sibling of Reject Rating and other rating values under Review Rating. EKAW 'Negative Review' is a review whose overall assessment is negative, a sibling of Neutral and Positive Review under Review. They both concern the outcome/assessment of a review, but one is a rating value (accept) and the other is a review classification (negative); an accepted review is not the same as a negative review, so they overlap in the review-assessment area without denoting the same concept.

A Trip is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception) in confOf, i.e. an excursion/activity. B's Hotel presenter is a kind of Delegate (a person role) under Conference building. Different kinds of entities (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A Workshop is an Academic Event (a type of conference event/session), while B Tutorial is an Individual Presentation (a type of talk). Although both are conference activities, they denote different concepts: a workshop is a distinct event with its own call and papers, whereas a tutorial is a presentation/instructional talk. Their paths and siblings (Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event vs Contributed Talk, Invited Talk) confirm they are not the same concept.

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property of the class Review expertise, linking a review-expertise record to a literal expertise value. B's 'has Review History' is an object property of Reviewer linking a reviewer to a Personal Review History individual. They differ in domain (Review expertise vs Reviewer), range (literal vs Personal Review History) and intended meaning (expertise topic vs past reviews), so they are not the same relation.

A 'Co chair' is a committee member who co-chairs a committee (sibling of Chair, domain/range Committee -> Co chair). B 'Session chair' is a Delegate who chairs a session, a role within the conference programme rather than a committee office. Both are chairing roles in the conference domain, so they overlap, but they are not the same concept: committee co-chair vs session chair. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a conference contributor who gives an invited talk, a role distinct from authorship. B's 'Author of paper student' is a subtype of Author (a student who authored a paper). The two denote different concepts: an invited speaker need not be a student author, and a student author need not be an invited speaker. Their paths and siblings (Active conference participant/Regular author vs Author of paper) confirm no equivalence.

A's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. a peer invitation relation. B's 'has Review History' relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History, a distinct record entity. Different kinds of things are related in the two properties, so they are not equivalent.

A's reviewWrittenBy relates a Review to its Possible Reviewer (domain Review, range Possible Reviewer), i.e. the authorship of a review. B's write relates a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item), i.e. a person writing a paper/item. They are inverse-like and cover different kinds of things (review vs. item, reviewer vs. author), so they are not equivalent; they overlap only in the general notion of authorship.

A's Accommodation Place is a generic place where conference attendees stay (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place under Place). B's Sponsor company house is a specific Building used by a sponsor company, sibling of Conference hotel, Presenter house, etc. The intended instances differ: one is lodging for attendees, the other a sponsor's building; they are not the same concept.

A's 'Submission event' is an administrative event (the act/process of submitting contributions) in the event hierarchy, while B's 'Program Committee' is a committee (a group of people) in the committee hierarchy. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Call For Reviews' is a subclass of Call (an announcement/invitation document, sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Manuscripts), whereas B's 'Review' is a subclass of Document denoting the actual review artefact produced by a reviewer (with children Positive/Negative/Neutral Review and properties review Of Paper, review Written By). A call for reviews is not a review; the entities denote different concepts despite the shared word 'review'.

A 'Hotel registration form' is a Document/Form used to register for a hotel, while B 'Conference hall' is a Place (a physical venue). They belong to different branches of the domain (document vs. location) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

edas 'Academia Organization' is a broad category of academic organizations (siblings: Government, Industry, NGO), while ekaw 'University' is a specific academic institution under 'Academic Institution' (sibling: Research Institute). A university is a kind of academia organization, but academia organization also covers research institutes and other academic bodies, so A is more general than B.

Author is a subclass of Person representing someone who writes papers (has Related Paper, is Written By), while Registration fee is a subclass of Fee representing a payment category with Price/Currency and pay/payed by relations. They share no meaning, no parent, and no properties; the only link is that a Person may pay a fee, which is not equivalence.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname, while B's 'has Name' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's full name. Different domains (Person vs Conference) and different intended meanings (surname vs conference name), so they are not equivalent.

A's Reception is a social event (a gathering) in the conference domain, sibling of Banquet and Trip. B's Accept Rating is a review rating category, sibling of Reject Rating and Accept If Room Rating. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Conference Chair is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Person) in cmt, while Scientific Event is an event category (subclass of Event) in ekaw. They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B's 'Trip day' is a time entity (sibling of Conference days, Deadline). They denote different concepts in different branches of the domain, so they are unrelated.

A's `writes` links an Author to a Contribution (the paper they authored), while B's `presentation` links a Speaker to a Document (the material they present). Different domains (Author vs Speaker) and different ranges (Contribution vs Document), and the relations denote different activities (authoring vs presenting), so they are not equivalent.

A's Reviewer is a Person role (a person who reviews), while B's Neutral Review is a subclass of Review, i.e. a document/review artefact with a neutral outcome. They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer). B's 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (domain Reviewer, range Personal Review History). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

Person in the Conference ontology is a general class covering all people (committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers, chairs), while Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a specific subclass of Person restricted to those who may review papers (parent Person, child PC Member, and properties linking it to Paper and Review). Person is strictly more general than Possible Reviewer, so the relation is subsumes, not equivalence.

A's hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string title, while B's hasEvent is an object property linking an Event to another Event (e.g. sub-events). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have different domains/ranges, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Submission event' is an administrative event in the conference timeline (the act/phase of submitting contributions), while B's 'Committee' is an organisational group of people with subclasses like Program Committee. They denote different concepts and are not related by subsumption.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a subclass of Computer Networks Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference ontology (document vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

Both properties link a written work (Paper/Item) to its author (Author/Person) in the same direction. 'has Author' and 'is writen by' are inverse-labelled but semantically the same relation: a paper has an author iff it is written by a person. Domain/range align (Paper~Item, Author~Person), so they denote the same relation.

A is a conference topic category (Operating Topicsystems, a child of Topic in the edas topic taxonomy), while B is a document type (Invited Talk Abstract, a child of Abstract in the ekaw document hierarchy). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject area vs. document genre) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's assignExternalReviewer relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (assigning a reviewer role), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (giving a talk). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's Participant is a subclass of Person (a conference attendee with subclasses Member, Regular, Student), while B's Renting is an activity performed before the conference (sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript). They denote entirely different concepts: a person role versus a pre-conference activity, so they are unrelated.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action of entering review criteria for a conference), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presenting a document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A is a research topic (Antennas Topic) under the Topic hierarchy, while B is an award category (Best Research Paper Award) under Award. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, and their labels ('email' / 'has an email') denote the same relation: a person's email address. Same kind, same domain, same range, same direction.

A's Author is a person (a Conference Member/User who writes papers), while B's Submitted contribution is a document (a Conference document / Written contribution that is reviewed). They belong to different top-level branches (person vs document) and have incompatible properties (Author writes Paper; Submitted contribution has reviews/topics), so they are not equivalent.

Card in iasted is a physical item (a card, with child Credit card) under Item, while Speaker in sigkdd is a Person who gives presentations. Different domains (artefact vs. person), no shared instances or properties; unrelated.

A's Meta Review is a subclass of Review (a document that reviews other reviews), while B's Member PC is a subclass of Person (a reviewer, per its comment and its properties expertOn/reviewes). One is a document type, the other a person role, so their instances cannot coincide.

In cmt, Preference is a class representing a reviewer's preference/interest in a paper (used for bidding), whereas in ekaw, Review is a document class (subclass of Document) representing the actual review written about a paper, with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review and properties like review Of Paper and review Written By. They denote different concepts: a preference is not a review, and a review is not a preference. Thus they are unrelated.

A 'Textual Review Question' is a type of review question (a question whose answer is free text), sibling of Numerical Review Question, under Review Question. B 'Neutral Review' is a type of Review (a document) classified by sentiment, sibling of Positive/Negative Review, under Review. They denote different concepts: a question vs. a review document with neutral sentiment. No subsumption or overlap.

A 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person (a role a person plays in writing a paper), while B 'Best Student Paper Award' is a subclass of Award (a prize given for a paper). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (people vs. awards) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Company in confOf is a subclass of Organization, a specific kind of organization (a commercial one), while ekaw's Organisation is the general superclass covering academic institutions, organising agencies, publishers, etc. Company is therefore strictly more specific than Organisation, so Company is subsumed by Organisation rather than equivalent to it.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) announcing a conference, while B 'Power Point presentation' is a kind of Presentation activity (sibling of Video presentation). They denote different concepts: a document vs. a presentation activity, so they are unrelated.

A's 'organises' relates an Organisation or Person (domain) to an Event (range), i.e. who organises an event. B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document (domain) to a Speaker (range), i.e. who presents a document. Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (author has a related paper), while B's designed_by relates a Deadline to an ACM SIGKDD entity (deadline designed by the conference). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

confOf's 'Administrative event' is a specific kind of event (sibling of Social event and Working event, with children like Submission event, Reviewing event, Registration event), whereas ekaw's 'Event' is the general superclass of all events (parent of Scientific Event and Social Event). The administrative event is thus strictly more specific than the general Event, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'is a starting date' is a datatype property of the class Important dates, pointing to a date value that marks the start of a conference-related period (e.g. a deadline or event). B's 'starts on' is a datatype property of Event, pointing to a string that gives the start time of an event. They belong to different subject classes (Important dates vs Event) and different value types (date vs string), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'has a steering committee' links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a governance body), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (a person presenting). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote the organizing committee of a conference: same label (modulo capitalization), same parent Committee, and analogous sibling committees (Program committee / Program Committee). The Conference ontology's properties (has an organizing committee / was an organizing committee of) confirm it is the committee that organizes a conference volume, matching sigkdd's Organizing Committee under Committee.

A's 'Conference Event' is a broad event class (parent of Academic/Non Academic Event) with attendees, programme, location and start/end times. B's 'Conference days' is a temporal subdivision under Time, with children Delegate and One conference day, i.e. it denotes the days of a conference, not an event. Different intended instances and different position in the hierarchy, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string email address, while B's send is an object property linking a Person to an Item (e.g. sending a submission). They relate different kinds of things (string vs. Item) and denote different relations, so they are not equivalent.

Both are Person subclasses denoting the role of chairing a session: confOf's 'Chair PC' (comment 'confTool', sibling of Member PC/Author/Participant) and edas's 'Session Chair' (sibling of Reviewer/TPC Member/Conference Chair, and a reviewer/initiator of calls and reviews). The intended instances coincide: a person chairing a session/PC role.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (administrative data entry), while B's 'is Menu Of' relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (catering). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Talk Event is a kind of Academic Event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), while B's Workshop Session is a kind of Session (a time slot within a workshop). They sit in different branches (Academic Event vs Session) and denote different concepts: a talk is not a session, and a workshop session is not a talk event.

confOf's Contribution is a conference submission (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like abstract, hasTitle, writtenBy, reviewedBy. edas's Personal History is a container for a person's publication and review records (children Personal Publication History, Personal Review History). They denote different concepts and share no instances.

Both Document classes are the general superclass of the same conference artefacts (Paper, Review, Programme, etc.) and are related to Person via author/written-by and to other documents via version/related-document properties. The intended instances coincide: any paper, review, programme or abstract is a Document in both ontologies, so the classes are equivalent.

Break Event (edas) is a non-academic conference event covering coffee breaks, free time and meals; Social program (iasted) is a conference activity covering dinner banquet, cocktail reception, coffee break, welcome address, etc. They overlap in that both include social/catering activities (coffee break, dinner), but neither subsumes the other: Break Event is restricted to breaks/meals while Social program also includes welcome addresses and other social activities, and Break Event includes free time not necessarily part of a social program. Hence related, not equivalent.

A Workshop Chair is a specific conference role (chair of workshop activities), while B Program Committee member is a general reviewer role. In ekaw, Workshop Chair is a subclass of PC Member, so a Workshop Chair is a kind of PC member, but the two classes are not coextensive: many PC members are not workshop chairs, and the sigkdd class covers all committee members. They overlap (a workshop chair may be a PC member) but neither subsumes the other in the reference alignment, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a kind of person (a conference contributor who is invited), while B's 'Speaker lecture' is a kind of session/lecture activity, not a person. They belong to different top-level categories (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Active conference participant' is a subclass of Conference contributor/participant that gives presentations; B's 'Speaker' is a broader Person subclass whose children include Author and Invited Speaker and which presents Documents. A is narrower (only active participants who present), while Speaker covers all presenters including authors and invited speakers, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

Research Institute is an academic organisation (sibling of University under Academic Institution), while Review is a document type (sibling of Abstract and Paper under Document). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

Chairman in cmt is a Person who chairs a committee (has children Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair and is involved in conflict-of-interest marking), whereas Registeered applicant in Conference is a conference attendee who has registered (child Paid applicant), a different role in the conference domain.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role/type of author (a person who is the first author of a contribution), sitting under 'Regular author' alongside 'Contribution co author'. B's 'Multi author Volume' is a document (a volume with multiple authors) under 'Document', with children like 'Proceedings' and a 'publisher Of' property. One denotes an author role, the other a publication artefact; their intended instances cannot coincide.

Workshop is a type of scientific event (a meeting held alongside a conference), while Program Committee is a committee (a group of people). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (Event vs Committee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Conference applicant is a Person who applies to register for a conference (parent Person, child Registered applicant), whereas PC Chair is a Conference Participant who chairs the program committee (parent PC Member). They denote different roles: an applicant is not yet a participant, and a PC Chair is a specific committee role, not an applicant.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name). B's 'go through' is an object property mapping an Item to an Activity (an item undergoing/participating in an activity). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Activity), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

SC Member is a steering-committee member, a subtype of PC Member (a reviewer/organiser role), while Author is a speaker who writes papers. The two denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Call For Manuscripts' is a call/announcement document (sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Reviews under Call), whereas B's 'Review' is a document type (sibling of Abstract and Paper under Document). One is a solicitation event/document, the other is a review document; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's isWrittenBy goes Paper -> Author (paper to its author), while B's write goes Person -> Item (person to what they wrote). They describe the same underlying authorship relation but in opposite directions and with different domain/range, so they are inverses rather than equivalent properties.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (a person qualified to review), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives/presents a paper or activity). The domains and ranges differ (Review expertise/Review preference -> Reviewer vs Person -> Activity/Item), so they relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A is a research topic (Microelectronics Topic) under Topic, while B is an organizational body (Organizing Committee) under Committee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

Both are social events at a conference, but a Reception (a standing social gathering) is not the same as a Conference Banquet (a formal meal). They are siblings under Social Event in both ontologies, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, whereas B's Record of attendance is a document (sibling of Form, Review, Submission) recording who attended. They belong to different branches (Event vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference (a qualification/interest relation), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (authorship of a paper). Different domains (Reviewer vs Author), different ranges (Review expertise/preference vs Contribution), and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Regular is a subclass of Participant (a person who is a regular participant, sibling of Member and Student), i.e. a kind of attendee. B's Registration Student is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a fee category for students, not a person. The two denote different kinds of things (person vs. fee), so they are unrelated despite the shared notion of 'regular/student'.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (a conference with two levels, sibling of Single Level Conference under Conference), while B's 'Listener' is a kind of Delegate/attendee who listens without presenting. They denote different concepts: one is a conference structure, the other a person role.

has Country relates an Organization or Person to a Country (a location of affiliation), while speak in relates a Person to a Place or Time (where/when they present). Different domains (Organization included vs Person only) and different ranges (Country vs Place/Time), and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area for conference papers (a subclass of Topic), whereas 'Audiovisual equipment' is a physical item (subclass of Item) with children such as Computer, LCD projector, and Video cassette player. They denote different kinds of entities (topic vs. equipment) and do not coincide.

A's Administrative event covers submission, reviewing, camera-ready and registration events (organisational/administrative activities), while B's Social Event covers banquet and trip (social activities). They are sibling branches under Event in both ontologies and denote disjoint kinds of events, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Trip day' is a day of the conference trip/event (a time period within the conference schedule, sibling of Conference days and Deadline), whereas B 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a specific submission deadline (a due date for abstract submission, sibling of author-notification and paper-submission deadlines). They denote different concepts: a general event day versus a particular submission deadline, so they are not equivalent.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to the Conference they belong to (membership relation). B's initiates relates a chair/TPC member to a Call they initiate (a call-for-papers creation relation). Different domains (Conference Member vs Chair/TPC) and different ranges (Conference vs Call), so the relations are not equivalent.

A's SessionChair is a Person role (a chair who initiates calls and reviews papers), while B's Demo Session is a type of event session. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'follows' relates two Administrative events (temporal ordering of events), while B's 'has Attendee' relates a Conference Event to a Person (participation). Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent.

A's Organizational Meeting is an academic event (like a workshop or talk) that organises the conference, while B's Poster Session is a specific kind of scientific session (sibling of Regular/Demo/Workshop Session). They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B Payment document is a financial document (parent of Bank transfer and Cheque) used for paying fees. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Item/Document) and share no intended instances.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to its author (Person), while B's 'speak in' relates a Person to a Place/Time where they speak. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a role/type of author (a person who co-authors a contribution), sitting under Regular author with sibling 'Contribution 1th author'. B's 'Multi author Volume' is a document/publication artefact (a volume with multiple authors), a subclass of Document with child Proceedings and publisher property. One denotes an author role, the other a publication volume; their intended instances do not coincide.

Both denote the person who chairs the program committee: cmt's Program Committee Chair is a Chairman and Program Committee Member who reviews (end Review), while sigkdd's Program Chair is an Organizator sibling of Program Committee member and General Chair, i.e. the head of the program committee. Same intended role in the conference domain.

A is a research topic area (Cryptography Topic) under Topic in edas, while B is a document type (Invited Talk Abstract) under Abstract in ekaw. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Both classes denote a person taking part in a conference: A's 'Conference participant' is a Person with active/passive participant subclasses, and B's 'Delegate' is a Person (among its parents) with subclasses such as Speaker, Listener, Session chair, IASTED member — i.e. conference attendees. The intended instances coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent despite the different labels and paths.

Both are object properties from Author to a written work (Contribution in confOf, Paper in edas). In the conference domain, an author writing a contribution is the same relation as an author having a related paper; the domain and range match and the labels denote the same authorship relation.

confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author (paper -> author), while iasted's write relates a Person to an Item (author -> paper). They describe the same authorship relation but in opposite directions, so they are inverses rather than equivalent properties.

Reception is a social event (a gathering) in confOf, while Positive Review is a type of Review document in ekaw. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Document) and denote different concepts.

Social event is a subclass of Event in confOf (a conference social activity such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while Fee in sigkdd is a payment concept with subclasses Registration fee and Sponzor fee. They denote different concepts and are not related by subsumption or overlap.

Both properties link a paper to the topic/subject area it deals with. cmt's hasSubjectArea has domain Paper and range Subject Area; ekaw's coversTopic has domain Event, Paper and range Research Topic. The intended meaning (a paper covering a research topic) coincides, and the ekaw domain is only broader because it also applies to events, which does not change the relation's core semantics for papers. Subject Area and Research Topic are the same concept in the conference domain, so the two properties are equivalent.

Both properties link a conference/event to the organisation that runs it, but they are not equivalent: 'scientifically Organised By' is a sub-property of 'organised By' with range Academic Institution (the scientific organiser of an event), whereas 'holded by' has domain Conference and range ACM SIGKDD (the hosting/sponsoring body). They overlap in the general idea of an event being run by an organisation, but differ in domain, range and specificity, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Review is the general class of reviews of a contribution (domain/range: reviews Reviewed contribution -> Review), while B's Neutral Review is a specific subclass of Review (sibling of Positive/Negative Review). A's Review is therefore more general and subsumes B's Neutral Review; they are not equivalent.

A is a placeholder/test topic under the Topic taxonomy in edas, while B is a specific kind of conference document (an abstract for an invited talk) under Document > Abstract in ekaw. They share no meaning: one is a subject category, the other a document type, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Information for participants' is a general conference document category (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, Review) covering material sent to attendees; B's 'Invitation letter' is a specific document type (sibling of Form, Payment document, Viza) sent to invitees. Both are conference documents aimed at participants, so they overlap, but an invitation letter is only one possible piece of participant information, not the same concept.

Both properties link a Paper to people who review it, but A's range is restricted to Meta Reviewer while B's range covers Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair and TPC Member. The intended relations overlap (both express 'reviewed by') but neither subsumes the other cleanly: A is narrower in range, B is broader and includes non-reviewer roles, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Rejected Paper' is a class of document (a paper that was rejected), while B 'Submissions deadline' is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to different branches (Document vs Time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Workshop Paper' is a kind of academic Paper (a Document) in the conference domain, while B 'Car' is a transport vehicle. They share no meaning, instances, or context; the only superficial link is the word 'car' inside 'Workshop Paper' (camera-ready), which is coincidental.

A's 'Registation deadline' is the deadline for conference registration (sibling of hotel reservation and camera-ready deadlines), while B's 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is the deadline for submitting abstracts (sibling of paper submission and author notification). They are distinct deadlines in the conference timeline, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'is held after' is an object property relating an Activity to a Time. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Activity), range (string vs Time), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' and denotes the written/submitted contribution (its children are Written contribution, Poster, Presentation, Regular contribution, etc., and it is linked to a Conference volume via has contributions / is submitted at). B's 'Paper Presentation' is a subclass of 'Academic Event' and denotes the event of presenting an accepted paper (linked to Accepted Paper via related To Event / related To Paper). One is a document/contribution, the other an event; their paths, parents, siblings and properties do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

Rejection is a subclass of Decision (the outcome of a review decision, sibling of Acceptance), while Listener is a subclass of Person (a conference participant who listens, sibling of Organizator and Speaker). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (decision outcome vs. person role) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class representing a reviewer's expertise/preference information (linked to Reviewer, Review preference, Submitted contribution), whereas B's 'Reviewer' is a person role class (subclass of Person, sibling of Author, TPC Member, etc.) that performs reviews. The two denote different concepts: one is expertise metadata, the other is the person/role. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A 'Textual Review Question' is a specific kind of review question (a question whose answer is free text) under Review Question, while B 'Review' is a document (a review of a paper) under Document. They denote different concepts: a question vs. a review document.

A's 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer), i.e. it records whose review history a history is. B's 'review Of Paper' links a Review to a Paper (domain Review, range Paper), i.e. it records which paper a review is about. Different domains, different ranges, different intended relations; they are not equivalent.

A relates a Conference to an Administrator (who prints hardcopy mailing manifests), while B relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not the same relation.

A's Paper is a document/contribution class (subclass of Document, with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To). B's Paper Author is a subclass of Person representing a person role (an author of a paper), not a document. The two denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Free Time Break' is a non-academic break event in the conference schedule (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break), while B 'Registration SIGMOD Member' is a registration fee category for SIGMOD members (sibling of Registration Non Member, Registration Student). They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. fee) and denote different concepts.

A's 'has workshops' relates a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a whole-part containment relation), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it (an authorship/presentation relation). Different domains (Conference volume vs Document), different ranges (Workshop vs Speaker), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Steering committee' is a subclass of Committee (a group of people governing the conference), while B's 'Author' is a subclass of Person (an individual who writes contributions). Their parents, siblings, and properties (steering-committee-of a conference volume vs. writes a contribution) do not overlap, so they denote different concepts.

A's virtualMeetingEnabledBy relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables virtual meetings), while B's is_given_by relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (who gives the presentation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Late Registered Participant' is a conference participant classified by registration timing (sibling of Early Registered Participant), whereas B 'Tutorial speaker' is a speaker/author role in a tutorial. Different classification axes and no shared instances; not equivalent.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (the paper they contribute), while B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership in the event/organisation). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them; B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person member. Different domains (Program Committee Member vs Conference), different ranges (Administrator vs Person), and different intended relations (provenance/adding vs membership), so they are not equivalent.

A's Participant is a subclass of Person (a conference attendee role, with subclasses Member/Regular/Student and property early Registration), while B's 'Memeber registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, i.e. a monetary amount paid by members. One is a person role, the other a fee, so they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to the people who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. the organisers issuing a call. B's 'is given by' links an Activity or Item to a Person who gives/presents it (e.g. a talk given by a speaker). The domains (Call vs Activity/Item) and ranges (specific chair roles vs any Person) differ, and the intended relations are different: initiating a call is not the same as giving an activity/item. Hence they are not equivalent.
A's Trip is a social event (sibling of Banquet/Reception) in the conference domain, while B's Van is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car/Taxi). Different kinds of things; not equivalent.

A's Talk Event is a general academic talk event (parent of Welcome/Closing Talk, sibling of Paper Presentation and Workshop), while B's Plenary lecture is a specific kind of Lecture (sibling of Session and Tutorial). A plenary lecture is a talk event, but Talk Event is broader and includes non-plenary talks, so they overlap without being equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Invited Talk Abstract is a document (a kind of Abstract, sibling of Tutorial Abstract). They belong to different branches of the domain (event vs. document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'belong to a conference volume' links an Important dates entity to a Conference volume (a publication/volume), while B's 'held In' links an Event to a Location. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A Tutorial is a kind of Individual Presentation (a scientific event such as a talk given at the conference), while a Video presentation is a kind of Presentation in the iasted ontology, i.e. a presentation medium/format (sibling of Power Point presentation). The two denote different concepts: one is an event type, the other a presentation format, so they are not equivalent.

A's `need` relates a Person to an Item (a person needs an item), while B's `design` relates the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline (designing a deadline). Different domains (Person vs ACM SIGKDD) and different ranges (Item vs Deadline), and the intended relations are distinct, so they are not equivalent.

A's Session is a scientific event (a scheduled meeting such as a conference session, workshop session, poster session) under Event > Scientific Event. B's Hotel room is a physical place (a room in a hotel, with single/double subtypes) under Place, sibling of Session room and Conference hall. The shared word 'session' does not make them the same concept: one is an event, the other a location. Unrelated.

edas:Place is a spatial location (venue, room, accommodation, dining) that conference events are held at, with children Accommodation/Conference Venue/Dining/Meeting Room Place and properties has Location / is Location Of linking Conference Event to Place. iasted:State is a geopolitical/administrative region (with children Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state) that persons occupy or visit and that is situated in other places. Although both are geographic-ish, State is a specific kind of region (a state/province) whereas Place is a generic location for events; their instances and roles in the domain do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (scheduling parallelism), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (a talk given by a speaker). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent.

In ekaw, Conference Participant is a broad class covering all people involved in the conference (chairs, presenters, committee members, etc.), with children such as Demo Chair, PC Chair, Presenter, Session Chair. In sigkdd, Author is a narrower class under Speaker, specifically someone who submits papers and receives notifications/awards. The two classes do not have the same intended instances: a Conference Participant need not be an Author, and an Author is not necessarily a Conference Participant in the ekaw sense. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in a way that would be recorded as a direct taxonomic relation.

A's Document is a superclass of Paper and Review (written artefacts in the conference), while B's Review expertise is a topic/expertise area linked to reviewers and submissions. They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A's 'Invited Talk' is a kind of scientific event / individual presentation (an event entity), while B's 'Listener' is a kind of person (an attendee role). They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's assignExternalReviewer relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (a person assigned to review), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the presenter of a document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

confOf's 'parallel with' is a symmetric relation between Administrative events (events scheduled in parallel), while ekaw's 'part Of' is a mereological/containment relation (an entity being part of another). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not inverses or synonyms, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a subclass of Person (a person who applies to a conference, with child 'Registeered applicant'), while B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with properties such as city, start/end date, name, and being held by ACM SIGKDD. A person role and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

hasAuthor goes from Paper to Author, while contributes goes from Person to Conference document. They are inverse-like in direction and have different domains/ranges, so they are not equivalent properties.

A's has Country relates an Organization or Person to a Country (a location of affiliation), while B's is present in relates a Person to a Place or Time (attendance at an event). Different domains (Organization included in A) and different ranges (Country vs Place/Time), and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

cmt's Chairman is a generic person role (parent Person, children include Conference Chair, PC Chair, Associated Chair) that chairs committees; ekaw's OC Member is a member of the organising committee (parent Conference Participant, child OC Chair). A chairman is typically a member of the committee they chair, so the concepts overlap, but they are not the same: an OC Member need not chair anything, and a Chairman (e.g. Conference Chair) is a distinct role from OC Member. Hence related rather than equivalent.

confOf's Social event (banquets, receptions, trips) and ekaw's Scientific Event (conferences, sessions, workshops) are sibling subclasses of Event denoting disjoint kinds of event; they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a paper/item to its author/person. 'has Author' (Paper -> Author) and 'is signed by' (Item -> Person) express the same authorship relation in the same direction; Paper/Item and Author/Person are the corresponding classes in the two ontologies.

Scholar in confOf is a price category (a person with a scholarship, studying at a university), while Author in sigkdd is a speaker who submits papers and receives notifications/awards. Their intended instances and roles in the conference domain differ, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Chair in edas is a senior organising role (initiates calls, reviews papers, chairs sessions) and is a sibling of Author/Reviewer/TPC Member. Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a general person who may review, with PC Member as a child, and is a sibling of Paper Author/Student. The two denote different roles: a conference chair is not a possible reviewer, and the ekaw class is broader/different in intent. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document type (the abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version), whereas Rejected Paper in edas is a paper status (a paper that was rejected, sibling of Accepted/Pending/Published/Withdrawn Paper). They denote different concepts: one is a kind of document, the other a review outcome, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a Conference contributor (a person who gives an invited talk), while B's 'Conference Hiker' is a subclass of Delegate in the Place/Building branch, a role for an attendee at the conference building. The paths, parents and siblings (Speaker, Session chair, Listener vs. Regular author, Active conference participant) show different intended concepts; an invited speaker is not a conference hiker.

Both properties relate a review/item to the person who wrote it. ekaw's reviewWrittenBy has domain Review and range Possible Reviewer (a person who may review), while iasted's is_writen_by has domain Item and range Person. In the conference domain, a Review is a kind of Item and a Possible Reviewer is a Person, so the two properties denote the same authorship relation in the same direction. The slight difference in generality (Review vs Item, Possible Reviewer vs Person) is a modelling granularity difference rather than a different relation, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Conference Member is a subclass of Person (a person affiliated with a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Conference contribution is a subclass of Conference document (a written artefact such as a paper, poster or talk). They denote different kinds of entities (people vs. documents) and are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a whole conference event (has country, members, paper/manuscript deadlines, topics), while B's Conference Session is a session within a scientific event, a child of Session alongside Workshop/Poster/Demo sessions. They denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (author submits a paper), while B's deals With relates a Contribution to a Topic (a contribution deals with a subject). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent.

Both are short, non-full contributions: Conference's Extended abstract is a kind of Regular contribution (sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract), while confOf's Short paper is a kind of Contribution (sibling of Paper and Poster). They overlap in the sense of a brief contribution, but an extended abstract is not the same as a short paper, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Review (cmt) is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a paper, a subclass of Document with children like Meta Review and properties linking Reviewer to Review. B Call For Manuscripts (edas) is a call/announcement soliciting submissions, a subclass of Call alongside Call For Papers and Call For Reviews. They denote different concepts: an evaluation artefact versus a solicitation announcement, so they are unrelated.

A's hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (a specific conference-organisation relation between event types). B's go_through links an Item to an Activity, a generic participation/association relation. The domains (Working event vs Item) and ranges (Administrative event vs Activity) do not coincide, and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

A is a document type (a brief introduction used by a session chair) under Document, while B is a submission deadline under Deadline. They denote different concepts (document vs. temporal deadline) and share no intended instances.

A's hasKeyword links a Contribution to its keywords, while B's hasSubmissionInstructions links a Call to submission instructions text. Different domains (Contribution vs Call) and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper, sibling of Paper Abstract) in the document hierarchy, while B is a subclass of Topic (a subject area such as Antennas or Cryptography) in the topic hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's hasFax relates a Person to a fax number string, while B's hasFirstName relates a Person to a first name string. They are different datatype properties with different intended values, despite sharing the Person domain.

A's hasPhone is a datatype property linking a Person to a string phone number, while B's locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Location), range (string vs Event), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Trip is a specific social event (an excursion), while B Social program is a broader category of social activities that includes dinners, receptions, etc. The Conference Trip is one kind of social program, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

cmt:name is a general name property with domain Conference and Person, while confOf:hasSurname is specifically a person's surname (family name). A surname is a kind of name, but the cmt property is broader (covers full names and conference names), so they are not equivalent; they overlap as related concepts.

In cmt, Review is a subclass of Document: it is the actual review document/contribution produced by a reviewer (it has a written By property to Reviewer and is written by a Reviewer). In edas, Textual Review Question is a subclass of Review Question, i.e. a question on the review form (a field/attribute of the reviewing process), sibling of Numerical Review Question. One denotes a document artefact, the other a form question; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Slide Set is a document artefact (sibling of Paper, Review, Programme). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a presentation document, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference event/session), while B's Lecturer is a person role under Author/Speaker. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/committee member who chairs the conference), while B 'Conference hotel' is a building/place where the conference is held. They belong to different branches (Person vs Place/Building) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration about a paper), while B's is_present relates a Person to a Time (attendance at an event). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a registered applicant who has paid, specifically late), while B's 'Early Registered Participant' is a subclass of Conference Participant denoting early registration. They differ in both payment status and timing (late vs early), so they are not equivalent; in fact they are opposites in timing and one involves payment while the other does not.

Both denote the social/recreational part of a conference: confOf's Social event (parent Event, children Banquet/Reception/Trip) and iasted's Social program (parent Conference activity, child Dinner banquet, sibling Coctail reception) cover the same instances (banquets, receptions, trips). The differing granularity (iasted also lists coffee break as sibling) is minor; the intended concept coincides.

Paper Abstract is a document component (an abstract of a paper), while Poster Session is a type of scientific event session. They belong to different top-level branches (Document vs Event) and share no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Track workshop chair' is a Person who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial part of a conference, while B 'Program Chair' is an Organizator who chairs the program committee. Both are conference-organising chair roles, so they overlap, but they are distinct roles: a track/workshop chair is not the same as the program chair, and neither subsumes the other (different parents: Person vs Organizator, different siblings and properties).

Organizer is a person/role who organizes a conference, while Conference is the event itself (a Working event with siblings Tutorial and Workshop). They denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A (confOf 'Member PC') is a person role — a program-committee member/reviewer, a subclass of Person with properties expert On (Topic) and reviewes (Contribution). B (edas 'Accept Rating') is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a value/verdict category used in reviewing, not a person. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Review Rating) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Country in confOf is a geographical/political entity used as the range of has Country for Organizations and Persons. Time zone in iasted is a temporal offset region, a different concept with no shared instances or properties; the labels and contexts do not coincide.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (range Reviewer), while B's 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (domain Reviewer, range Personal Review History). The directions and the kinds of things related are different: one points to a reviewer, the other points from a reviewer to a history. They are not the same relation.

Both denote the act/event of presenting a paper at a conference. A's Presentation is a Conference contribution given by an active participant and having an abstract; B's Individual Presentation is a Scientific Event that a paper is presented as and that presents a paper. The intended instances (a talk presenting a paper) coincide, and both have Invited talk as a child, confirming the match.

A 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the conference process (a phase/activity of reviewing), while B 'Conference Participant' is a role of a person attending the conference. They belong to different top-level categories (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A: class `User` (id User, ontology cmt) is a person who uses the system (author, reviewer, chair). B: class `Proceedings_Publisher` (id Proceedings_Publisher, ontology ekaw) is an organisation that publishes proceedings. Different kinds of entities (person vs organisation), so unrelated.

A Presenter is a conference participant who gives a presentation; B Conference Hiker is a subtype of Delegate in the iasted ontology, sitting alongside Speaker, One day presenter, Hotel presenter, etc. Both denote people attending/presenting at a conference, so they overlap, but the iasted hierarchy distinguishes Delegate subtypes by registration/attendance mode rather than by presenting role, and Conference Hiker is not clearly the same as a Presenter. They are related but not equivalent.

A's rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (rejecting a paper), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (submitting a paper). Different domain (Administrator vs Author) and opposite/opposing actions, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call for participation' is a general conference document announcing the event and inviting participation, while B's 'Call For Papers' is specifically a call soliciting paper submissions (sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews). They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same concept; the more specific Call for Papers would be subsumed by the broader Call for participation, so 'related' is the safest non-equivalent verdict.

In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (a person who gives a talk/paper), with children covering proceedings inclusion and lecture/tutorial speaking roles. In sigkdd, Invited Speaker is a subclass of Speaker denoting a specifically invited presenter, and its sibling is Author, showing the two are distinct concepts in that ontology. An author is not necessarily an invited speaker, and an invited speaker is not necessarily an author, so the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (a gathering such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B 'Submission' is a subclass of Document (a paper manuscript with Initial/Final manuscript children). They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Item/Document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip under Social event), while B's Document is a physical/informational item (sibling of Audiovisual equipment, Card, Publication). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Submitted contribution' is a document/contribution that has been submitted (a subclass of Written contribution, with children Reviewed contribution and siblings Regular contribution, and it is the range of review-expertise and review-preference properties). B 'Review Question' is a class of questions (with children Numerical Review Question and Textual Review Question) used in the EDAS review form. A submission is not a review question; the entities denote different concepts and are unrelated.

Both are object properties with domain Person relating a person to what they produce/present: A's range is Conference document (a paper/contribution), B's range is Activity, Item (the item being the paper/contribution). In the conference domain 'contributes' and 'give' both express a person's authorship/submission relation to a paper, so a reference alignment would likely record them as equivalent.

confOf's 'study At' relates a Scholar to a University (where a person studies), while iasted's 'is given to' relates an Item to a Person (e.g. an award given to a person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote a person in the conference domain: A's Person is the general superclass of committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers and chairs, with properties for name, email, gender and authorship; B's Person is the general superclass of listeners, organisers and speakers, with properties for name, email, nation, place, and registration-fee payment. The intended instances coincide (humans involved in the conference), so the classes are equivalent.

In edas, Workshop is a subclass of Academic Event, a kind of event held at a conference. In ekaw, Conference is a subclass of Scientific Event and is the umbrella event that contains Workshop as a sibling (along with Session, Track, etc.). A workshop is not a conference; the two classes denote different event types, and the ekaw Conference is the broader event that would contain an edas Workshop. Thus they are not equivalent.

A 'Closing Talk' is a talk event (a kind of academic event) in the conference schedule, while B 'Listener' is a person role (a kind of Person) who attends talks. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Paper is the general document submitted to a conference (has authors, reviews, decisions, subject areas), while edas:PublishedPaper is a specific subclass of edas:Paper representing only papers that have been published. PublishedPaper is strictly narrower than the general Paper concept, so cmt:Paper is subsumed by edas:PublishedPaper's parent rather than equivalent to it.

A's 'Final manuscript' is a document/submission artefact (a version of a submitted paper, sibling of 'Initial manuscript'), whereas B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline/date entity (sibling of 'Deadline Abstract Submission' and 'Deadline Author notification'). They belong to different branches (Document vs Deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Rated Papers' is a subclass of Active Paper in the conference domain (a paper that has received ratings), while B 'Credit card' is a subclass of Card, a payment artefact. They share no meaning, no properties, and no common instances; the only superficial link is the word 'card'/'paper' being unrelated concepts.

Both entities denote the conference event itself: 'Conference' in ontology A and 'Conference' in ontology B have identical labels, are both classes at the root of the conference-organisation domain, and their intended instances (a specific conference event) coincide. No conflicting context (different parents, properties, or comments) distinguishes them.

A's Chair is a committee role (a kind of Committee member, sibling of Co chair, domain/range of committee-chair properties), whereas B's Author is a Person who writes Contributions. A chair need not author papers and an author need not chair a committee; the concepts denote different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Published Paper' is a Paper in a publication state (siblings: Accepted, Active, Pending, Rejected, Withdrawn Paper) — a paper that has been published.
