B 'Initial manuscript' is a Submission (siblings: Final manuscript) — the first version of a submitted document, not a published paper. The paths and sibling sets differ: one is a publication-status subclass of Paper, the other a submission-stage subclass of Submission. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Social Event is a non-academic event (siblings Break Event, Meal Event; children Excursion, Reception), while B's Scientific Event is the academic branch of Event (children Conference, Session, Workshop) and is even a sibling of B's own Social Event. They denote opposite kinds of event, so they are unrelated.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection under Decision), while B's Renting is a pre-conference activity (sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript). Different domains and kinds; no equivalence.

A 'Short paper' is a type of contribution (a paper of limited length) in confOf, sibling to Paper and Poster. B 'Initial manuscript' is a submission-stage document in iasted, sibling to Final manuscript, i.e. a version of a submission rather than a paper category. The concepts differ: one is a paper type, the other a submission version, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Program committee' is a committee of people that reviews papers for a conference (a subcommittee of Committee, with properties linking it to a Conference volume). B's 'Academic Institution' is an organisation such as a university or research institute that can scientifically organise events. They denote different concepts (a committee vs. an institution) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person participating in a conference, sitting directly under Person in each ontology. Conference's Conference participant has subclasses Active/Passive conference participant, and confOf's Participant has subclasses Member/Regular/Student, all of which are kinds of conference participants. The confOf comment 'confTool' and the property early Registration (Participant -> boolean) further confirm the intended meaning matches Conference participant.

A's isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (sponsoring relation), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents a document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

Company in confOf is an organizational entity (sibling of University under Organization), while Main office in iasted is a physical place (sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room under Place). They denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's 'gives presentations' links an Active conference participant to a Presentation (a person presenting a talk), while B's 'relates To' links a Document to an Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session or Person. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A is a conference document type (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic in cryptography under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A 'Single Level Conference' is a conference event type (sibling of 'Two Level Conference', subclass of Conference), while B 'Main office' is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A is a class for the full version of a paper (a document artefact in the conference domain), while B is a class for a double-occupancy hotel room (an accommodation type in the venue domain). Their paths, parents and siblings are entirely different, and they share no intended instances.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B 'Conference hotel' is a building/place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference airport, Conference restaurant). They denote entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Document is a conference paper/contribution with authors, versions and reviews. In iasted, Document is a generic administrative item (forms, letters, mailing lists, payment documents) under Item. The intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are unrelated despite the shared label.

Both are subclasses of Place denoting the physical venue where a conference takes place: edas 'Conference Venue Place' and iasted 'Conference hall' occupy the same position under Place and are distinguished from accommodation/dining/office/session-room siblings. The intended instances (the conference venue building/hall) coincide, so a reference alignment would likely equate them.

A's 'Poster Paper' is a specific kind of paper (a sibling of Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc. under Paper), whereas B's 'Paper' is the general paper class (parent of Abstract and Review, domain of submit). Every Poster Paper is a Paper, but not vice versa, so Poster Paper is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper), while B's `presentation Of Paper` relates an Individual Presentation to an Abstract/Paper (the presentation is of the paper). Different domains (Author vs Individual Presentation) and different intended relations (authorship vs presentation-of), so they are not equivalent.

Conference www is a document/web page about a conference (a subclass of Conference document, with a URL property), whereas Plenary lecture is a type of conference lecture/activity. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'Regular contribution' is a kind of conference contribution (a written contribution that is not invited/poster/etc.), with children Extended abstract and Paper. B's 'Submitted Paper' is a paper in the submission stage, sibling to Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, Regular Paper, etc. The two overlap in that a regular contribution is typically submitted as a paper, but they are not the same concept: A classifies by contribution type, B by submission status. Neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Social Event is a subclass of Event covering banquets and trips (social gatherings), while B's Introduction is a conference activity (introductory talk/session) under Conference activity, sibling to Lecture, Presentation, etc. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'provided By' relates a Sponsorship to an Organization, i.e. who provides sponsorship. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.
Both labels denote the same conference/paper domain concept.

Withdrawn Paper is a terminal state of a paper that was removed from consideration, while Submitted Paper is the initial state of a paper that has been submitted and can be assigned to a reviewer. They denote different stages in the paper lifecycle and are not equivalent.

A's 'has a name' is a datatype property with range string, used to give a name to a Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher or Topic. B's 'has Topic' is an object property linking a Working event to a Topic. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range and direction of meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event (spatial containment of events), while B's Name_of_sponsor is a datatype property linking a Sponzor to a string (the sponsor's name). Different domain, range, and kind; they denote different relations.

A is an academic event (a meeting such as a program committee or organizing meeting) in the conference-event hierarchy, while B is a subclass of Author describing an author whose book proceedings are included. They denote entirely different concepts (event vs. author role), so they are unrelated.

An Evaluated Paper in ekaw is a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer and is being/has been evaluated (its children are Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper). An iasted Submission is the general document submitted by an author (children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript), which is broader: it covers the submission before any evaluation and the final camera-ready version. Every evaluated paper is a submission, but not every submission is an evaluated paper, so Evaluated Paper is strictly more specific than Submission.

A 'Conference Paper' is a scholarly paper submitted to/published at a conference (subclass of Paper, sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Regular Paper, etc.). B 'Record of attendance' is a document recording who attended, a sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Review, Submission. They denote different concepts despite both being Documents; no subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline (a point in time) under the Deadline class. They denote different kinds of things — a document vs. a temporal deadline — so they are not equivalent.

Both denote the published collection of conference papers: A's 'Conference proceedings' is a Conference part with publisher, volume and ISBN, and B's 'Book proceeding' is a Publication (sibling of 'Cd proceeding'), i.e. the book-form proceedings. The intended instances coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Conference is the event itself (has members, accepts submissions, has dates, logo, etc.), while B's Conference applicant is a subclass of Person representing an individual who applies to attend a conference. The two denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person role), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad class covering all persons involved in a conference (active/passive participants, committee members, reviewers, chairs, etc.), while B's 'Organizator' is narrower, covering only organizing roles (General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster). Organizers are a subset of conference participants, so A is subsumed by B's concept in the sense that Organizator is more specific; the two are not equivalent.

A 'Track workshop chair' is a Person role (a person who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial), while B 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a Document (an item used to introduce a session chair). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and are not equivalent.

Both properties link a person to a Paper, but the domains differ: cmt's hasBeenAssigned has domain Reviewer (a reviewer assigned to review a paper), while edas's hasRelatedPaper has domain Author (an author related to a paper, e.g. authored/submitted). Reviewer and Author are distinct roles, and the intended relations (review assignment vs. authorship) differ, so they are not equivalent; they only overlap in linking a person to a paper.

Paper Abstract (an abstract of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper) and Short paper (a short contribution, sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution) both denote a kind of written submission, but they are not the same concept: an abstract is a summary document, whereas a short paper is a full (short) contribution. They overlap in the conference domain without coinciding, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference organisation (subclass of Conference Member/User, writes and submits papers, can be reviewer/chair). Conference (edas) is the event itself with dates, country, members, topics. Different kinds of entities; no subsumption or overlap.

A is a venue/place where a conference is held (a subclass of Place alongside Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). B is a person type (a student who is not a speaker), a subclass of Non speaker under Delegate. They denote entirely different concepts (place vs. person role), so they are unrelated.

A's contact Email is an email address of a Contribution (confTool), while B's has Postal Code is a postal code of Contact Information. Different attributes (email vs postal code) and different domains (Contribution vs Contact Information), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) relation between a Conference volume and its Conference parts, while B's 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (an agentive action). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Accommodation Place' is a general place for lodging (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), while B 'Double hotel room' is a specific type of hotel room. A double hotel room is a kind of accommodation place, so A is more general and B is subsumed by A; they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a submitted contribution' relates a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (the contribution being reviewed), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains (Review expertise vs Author) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Active conference participant' is a conference contributor who gives presentations (siblings: Invited speaker, Passive conference participant, Regular author), while B's 'Author' is a Person who writes Contributions. An author is typically an active participant, but the classes are not coextensive: an active participant may be an invited speaker or presenter who is not an author, and an author may be passive (non-attending). They overlap without being equivalent.

A's Review is the general review class (parent of Meta Review, sibling of Paper), while B's Positive Review is a specific subtype of Review (sibling of Negative/Neutral Review). A Review subsumes Positive Review, not equivalent.

Paper in cmt is a submitted document with authors, reviews, decisions and subject areas; Event in confOf is a scheduled happening (administrative/social/working) with start and end times. They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A's 'default Choice' is a datatype property linking a social/working event to a positiveInteger (a numeric default choice, confTool-specific), while B's 'organised By' is an object property linking an Event to an Organisation or Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

Accommodation Place is a place where attendees stay (hotel/dormitory), while Conference hall is the venue where the conference takes place. They are different kinds of places; the siblings confirm this (Accommodation Place sits beside Conference Venue Place, and Conference hall sits beside Hotel).
Both properties relate a paper to its presentation/abstract; domain and range align (Paper/Abstract vs Paper), so they denote the same relation.

A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee (domain Conference volume, range Committee), while B's 'is Member Of' links a Person to a Conference (domain Person, range Conference). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's Decision is the outcome of a review (children Acceptance/Rejection, range of has Decision from Paper), while B's Document is a submitted artefact (children Abstract/Paper/Review, presented by a Speaker, submitted until a Deadline). Different concepts: an outcome vs. a document.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an Administrator action that takes a Conference as range (a bidding-phase control action), while B's 'presentation' is a Speaker-to-Document relation (a speaker presenting a document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they denote different relations.

Both properties link a group to its members, but the domains differ: A's has members has domain Committee and range Committee member, while B's has Member has domain Conference and range Person. They are conceptually related (membership relations) but not equivalent because they relate different kinds of entities in different directions of scope.

cmt:User is a generic person role with children Administrator, Author, Reviewer (people who submit/review papers), while sigkdd:Organizator is a person who organizes the conference, with children General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster. The intended instances do not coincide: an Author/Reviewer is not an Organizator, and an Organizator need not be a User in the cmt sense. Different roles in the conference domain, so unrelated.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact. B's 'Organizational Meeting' is an event (subclass of Academic Event, sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop), i.e. an activity. A document and an event denote different kinds of things, so the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Security Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in edas, while B 'Program Committee' is an organisational committee under Committee in sigkdd. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Conference Participant (ekaw) is a Person who attends a conference, while Building (iasted) is a Place (venue/location). They belong to disjoint top-level branches (Person vs Place) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Committee member' is a generic person belonging to a committee (with subclasses Chair, Co chair, and properties has members / was a member of). B 'Member PC' is specifically a program-committee member, commented 'Reviewer', with properties expert On (Topic) and reviewes (Contribution). Every Member PC is a committee member, but committee members also include chairs and other roles not covered by Member PC, so A is broader: A is subsumed by B's concept only in the narrower direction, i.e. Member PC is a specialization of Committee member.
Country is a geographic entity used as the range of has Country (Organization, Person -> Country), while Currency is a monetary unit; they denote different concepts and share no instances.

Both properties link a Paper to the people responsible for reviewing it, but the ranges differ: cmt's assignedTo ranges only over Reviewer, while edas's isReviewedBy ranges over a broader set (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). The cmt property is therefore strictly narrower in its range and is subsumed by the edas property, not equivalent to it.

A's has Bid relates a Paper to a Bid (a submission of a bid for a conference), while B's is Written By relates a Paper to an Author. Different range concepts (Bid vs Author) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Conference Session is a session within a conference, evidenced by its relations to Academic Event, Conference, Person and Document. A conference is not a conference session; the entities denote different concepts.

A's Steering committee is a specific kind of committee (a sibling of Organizing committee and Program committee under Committee), while B's Committee is the general committee class with Organizing Committee and Program Committee as children. Thus Steering committee is strictly narrower than Committee, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the person who reviews it), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents it). The relations have different meanings and different ranges (Reviewer vs Speaker), so they are not equivalent.

A's `date` is a datatype property of Conference giving a date value, while B's `has title` is a datatype property of Social event / Working event giving a string title. Different domains, ranges, and meanings; they do not correspond.

A's 'Submissions deadline' is a specific deadline (the paper submission deadline) under the general Deadline class in iasted. B's 'Deadline' is the general deadline class with children for abstract submission, author notification and paper submission. The specific submission deadline is one kind of deadline, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's hasUpdatedVersion relates a Document to a later version of that same Document (domain Document, range Document), while B's write relates a Person to an Item they authored (domain Person, range Item). Different kinds of arguments and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'enable Virtual Meeting' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative capability to enable virtual meetings), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship of a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (a dependency/requirement relation), while B's 'search' relates the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (a search/query relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track(s), while B's 'has Country' relates a Conference to a Country. Different domains (Conference volume vs Conference) and completely different ranges (Track vs Country); the concepts are unrelated.

A's 'Conference document' is a broad class of documents (calls, announcements, contributions, reviews) that people contribute to and that have authors and issue dates. B's 'Deadline' is a temporal milestone (abstract submission, author notification, paper submission) with a date and a submitting relation. The intended instances do not coincide: documents vs. deadlines. No subsumption or overlap in meaning, so unrelated.

A is a research topic area in the EDAS taxonomy (a subject category under Topic, sibling to Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), while B is a physical item type in the IASTED ontology (an Item with child Credit card, sibling to Audiovisual equipment, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle). They denote completely different concepts: a topic of interest vs. a card artefact. No equivalence, subsumption or overlap.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper, a specific kind of paper (the full version, sibling of Paper Abstract). In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class of papers (sibling of Abstract and Review, domain of submit). The sigkdd Paper is broader and encompasses the cmt Paper Full Version, so the cmt class is subsumed by the sigkdd class rather than equivalent.

A Paper (confOf) is a kind of contribution (sibling of Poster and Short paper), while B Submission (iasted) is a broader Document subtype whose children are Initial manuscript and Final manuscript. A paper is a submitted document, so Paper is narrower than Submission; they are not equivalent.

The two properties are inverses of each other: cmt's hasProgramCommitteeMember goes from Program Committee to Program Committee Member, while Conference's was_a_member_of goes from Committee member to Committee. A property and its inverse are not equivalent, so they are unrelated as directed relations.

A's 'Poster Paper' is a specific kind of Paper (a document type submitted/presented at a conference), while B's 'Document' is a broad administrative item class whose children are forms, invitation letters, payment documents, reviews, submissions, etc. The two denote different concepts: a poster paper is not a generic administrative document, and Document is not a paper subtype. No subsumption or overlap in the intended instances.
A is a review-rating class (a kind of acceptance decision when room is available) under Review Rating; B is a person role (Speaker) under Delegate. Different domains entirely, no overlap.

A's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines), while B's 'holded by' links a Conference to the ACM SIGKDD organisation that holds it. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Important dates' is a class of deadline/date entities belonging to a conference volume (submission, camera-ready, acceptance, start/end dates). B's 'Accepted Paper' is a subclass of Paper in the document hierarchy, denoting a paper that has been accepted, with siblings Pending/Rejected/Published etc. The two denote entirely different concepts (dates vs. documents), so they are unrelated.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered the conference details), while B's 'is a topis of conference parts' links a Topic to a Conference part. Different domains (Conference vs Topic), different ranges (Administrator vs Conference part), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Chairman is a role/person (a Person subclass, parent of Conference Chair, PC Chair, Associated Chair) in cmt, while Registration is a conference activity (an Activity subclass whose child is Delegate) in iasted. They denote different concepts: a person role versus an event/process of registering. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the cmt ontology), while B 'Camera ready contribution' is a document/contribution class (a subclass of Accepted contribution in the Conference ontology). They belong to entirely different branches (person vs. document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

edas:isReviewedBy relates a Paper to the people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), whereas ekaw:hasReview relates a Paper to a Review document. The ranges are disjoint (persons vs. review records), so the properties are not equivalent; they are not even inverses or subsumption-related.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person (domain) to an Organization (range), i.e. a person is employed by an organization. iasted's is_needed_for relates an Item (domain) to a Person (range), i.e. an item is needed for a person. The domains, ranges and intended meanings differ entirely; they are not the same relation nor inverses of one another.

A's 'has a review expertise' links a submitted contribution to a review expertise (a topic/skill area), while B's 'is given by' links an activity or item to a person (the agent who gives/performs it). Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Organization is the general superclass of all organisations (children Company, University; domain of employed By, has City/Country/Postal Code/Street). B's Government Organization is a specific subtype of Organization (parent Organization, siblings Academia/Industry/NGO). Thus A is strictly more general than B: A subsumes B, they are not equivalent.

hasDecision links a Paper to its Decision (accept/reject outcome), while hasCall links an Academic Event to its Call for papers. Different domains (Paper vs Academic Event) and different ranges (Decision vs Call), so the relations are unrelated.

Conference participant is a broad class covering all people taking part in a conference (its children are Active/Passive conference participant), while Student in confOf is a specific kind of Participant (siblings Member, Regular). A Student is a participant, but not every conference participant is a student, so Conference participant is strictly more general than Student.

confOf's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise area), while sigkdd's 'obtain' relates an Author to an Award (receiving a prize). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference-organisation role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, a person who chairs in an associated capacity), while B is a physical location (a kind of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Meeting Room Place). They share no intended instances and belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Place), so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person who presents at a conference: A's Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person presenting a paper), and B's Presenter is a Conference Participant who presents, with Invited Speaker as a child. The intended meaning coincides, so they are equivalent.

A's 'Trip city' is a subclass of City, a city that is the destination of a trip (siblings: Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city). B's 'Conference hall' is a subclass of Place, a physical building/room where a conference is held (siblings: Hotel, Main office). A city and a building are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to a Program committee, while B's 'occupy' links a Person to a Building/City/State. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Workshop is a kind of working event (a scientific meeting held alongside a conference, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas B's Registration form is a document/form artefact used to register (sibling of Author information form and Hotel registration form). They share no intended instances: one is an event, the other a form document, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, but 'paper Due On' denotes the paper submission deadline while 'Start of conference' denotes the conference start date. They are distinct temporal properties of a conference that overlap only in being conference-related dates, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Scholar is a subclass of Person (a person with a price category, with property study At to University), while B's Author attendee book registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, i.e. a fee amount, not a person. Different kinds and domains, so they are unrelated.

A is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a literal date (the camera-ready submission deadline), while B is an object property linking a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (the topic a paper/event is about). They share neither domain, range, nor intended relation, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person who has registered for a conference: A's 'Registeered applicant' is a subclass of Conference applicant (a person applying/registering for a conference), and B's 'Early Registered Participant' is a subclass of Conference Participant, specifically one who registered early. The intended instances coincide (registered conference attendees), and the sibling structure (Paid applicant under A; Late Registered Participant under B) confirms the same registration-status concept. The spelling difference and the 'early' qualifier are terminological, not conceptual, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's paperPresentedAs relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the event of presenting), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the person presenting). The domains (Paper vs Document) and especially the ranges (Individual Presentation vs Speaker) differ, and the directions are opposite in spirit: A goes paper -> presentation, B goes document -> speaker. They do not denote the same relation.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property of a Conference document (a paper/contribution) giving its publication/issue date, while B's 'start Date' is a datatype property of a Conference giving the conference's start date and time. Different domains (document vs conference) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, whereas an Accommodation Place is a type of Place (sibling of Conference Venue, Dining Place, Meeting Room) denoting lodging. Different parents (Social event vs Place) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a paper-like item to a person-like entity, but 'assigned To' specifically relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review the paper), while 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person in a broader authorship/signing sense. The domains and ranges are more general in iasted, and the intended meanings differ (review assignment vs. signing/authorship), so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role/type of author of a conference contribution (a first author of a paper), sitting under 'Regular author' alongside 'Contribution co author'. B's 'Lecturer' is a person role under 'Author' in a building/delegate hierarchy, with children 'Student lecturer' and 'Worker lecturer' and siblings about proceedings authorship and speakers. The two denote different concepts (paper first-author role vs. lecturer person type), so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a scholarly meeting with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's Free Time Break is a non-academic break event (siblings Coffee Break and Meal Break). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) used to announce the conference. B 'Departure' is an activity occurring after the conference (subclass of Activity after conference, sibling of Full day tour). They denote different kinds of things (document vs. activity) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Abstract is a subclass of Document (a specific kind of document, with subclasses Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract). In sigkdd, Document is the superclass of Abstract, Paper and Review. Thus ekaw's Abstract is strictly more specific than sigkdd's Document; the two are not equivalent, but Abstract is subsumed by Document.

Paper Full Version is a subclass of Paper (a document type) in cmt, while Bronze Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsorship level) in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to an anyURI (the conference website), while B's 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item (acquiring something). Different domain, range, and kind, so they denote different relations.

A Reception is a specific social event (sibling of Excursion under Social Event), while B Social program is a broader conference activity that includes Dinner banquet, Coctail reception, Coffee break, etc. A reception is one kind of social-program item, so Reception is subsumed by Social program, not equivalent.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Deadline' is a time point with children such as submission and camera-ready deadlines. They denote different concepts: a document vs. a temporal deadline, so they are not equivalent.

Both are object properties linking a paper/contribution to its author(s). confOf's 'written By' has domain Contribution and range Author; edas's 'is Written By' has domain Paper and range Author. Contribution and Paper denote the same concept in the conference domain, and the direction (paper -> author) is identical, so the two properties are equivalent.

A's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference, Tutorial and Workshop (things that happen at a conference), while B's 'Conference days' is a subclass of Time covering Delegate and One conference day (temporal units). Different parents (Event vs Time), different children and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

Organizer is a person/role in the conference domain (someone who organizes the event), while Time zone is a geographical/temporal concept in the iasted ontology. They share no meaning, no properties, and no context; a reference alignment would not relate them.

confOf's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper/contribution authored), while iasted's need relates a Person to an Item (a required item/equipment). The domains (Author vs Person) are close, but the ranges (Contribution vs Item) denote different kinds of things, and the intended relations differ (authoring vs requiring). They are not the same relation.

A 'Steering committee' is a committee (a group) that oversees a conference series, with properties linking it to a Conference volume. B 'Session Chair' is a Person role who chairs a session and reviews/initiates calls. Different kinds (group vs. person role) and different domain roles, so they are unrelated.

A's Presentation is a conference activity (a talk/session type, sibling of Lecture, Coffee break, etc.), while B's Organizator is a role a person plays in organising the conference (parent of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's email is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their email address), while B's has gender links a Person to a gender value. They relate different attributes of Person, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (a general dependency relation), while B's 'designed by' relates a Deadline to the specific organisation ACM SIGKDD. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a specific co-author role for a contribution (a subclass of Regular author, sibling of 'Contribution 1th author'), whereas B's 'Author' is a broad class of conference authors (parent of book/CD proceedings authors, lecturers, speakers). The co-author role is a narrower concept than the general Author, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

Both classes denote members of the program committee: cmt's Program Committee Member is a Conference Member who reviews papers (has maxPapers, memberOf Program Committee), and confOf's Member PC is a Person who reviews contributions (reviewes Contribution, expertOn Topic). The comment 'Reviewer' and the review-related properties align the intended instances, so they are equivalent despite different parents.

A's 'Review preference' is a reviewer's declared preference/interest in topics or submissions (linked to Reviewer, Topic, Submitted contribution, with a degree). B's 'Review Rating' is a rating assigned to a paper (has Rating from Active Paper, with subclasses Accept/Reject/Week Reject), i.e. an outcome/score of reviewing. Both concern reviewing but denote different concepts: preference vs. rating. They overlap in the review domain but are not equivalent.

Author in edas is a specific role (a person who writes papers, with children like Presenter and properties has Related Paper / is Written By), whereas Person in ekaw is the general superclass of all people (children include Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student, Agency Staff Member). Author is thus a narrower concept subsumed by the broader Person, not equivalent.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (sessions scheduled in parallel), while edas's 'has Related Document' relates an Academic Event/Conference/Session/Person to a Document. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

An Organizational Meeting (e.g. a program-committee or organising meeting) is a kind of academic event, but it is not a scientific event in the sense of the ekaw Scientific Event, which covers conferences, workshops, sessions, tracks and presentations. The ekaw Scientific Event is broader and does not include organisational meetings, so the edas class is at most a narrower concept; the two do not denote the same concept.

A's Conference is the whole conference event (has submissions, dates, members, administrators); B's Conference hall is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel and Main office), i.e. a venue room, not the conference event.

A 'Call For Manuscripts' is a solicitation document (a kind of Call, sibling of Call For Papers/Reviews) in edas, whereas B 'Rejected Paper' is a paper that has been evaluated and rejected in ekaw. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's rejectedBy relates a Paper to the Administrator who rejected it (domain Paper, range Administrator), while B's write relates a Person to an Item they authored (domain Person, range Item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent nor inverse.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'reviewes' relates a Member PC to a Contribution (domain Member PC, range Contribution), i.e. which paper a PC member reviews. Different kinds of arguments and different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A Meta Review (cmt) is a document that reviews the reviews, a subclass of Review. B Review Form (edas) is the form/template used to collect reviews, not a review document. Different intended instances and roles, so they are not equivalent.

A's Decision is the outcome of a paper review (children Acceptance/Rejection, domain of has Decision from Paper), while B's Organization is an institution such as a company or university that employs people and has an address. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a specific kind of speaker (a subtype of Author in iasted, alongside Lecturer and Tutorial speaker), whereas B 'Author' is the general class of authors in sigkdd. Every plenary lecture speaker is an author, but not every author is a plenary lecture speaker, so A is strictly more specific and is subsumed by B.

A's 'Reviewed contribution' is a submission (a paper/contribution that has undergone review), sitting under Submitted contribution with children Accepted/Rejected contribution. B's 'Review' is the review document itself (a Document with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review, written by a reviewer about a paper). They are different concepts: one is the reviewed paper, the other is the evaluation artefact. A's 'has a review' property points to a Review, confirming the Review is a separate entity, not the contribution.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). B's Presenter state is a state of a presenter (sibling of Conference state and Sponsor state), i.e. a status/condition, not an event. Different kinds and different domains, so they are unrelated.

A's has Call relates an Academic Event to its Call (call for papers), while B's search relates the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (sponsor). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution (the abstract text of a paper), while B's 'Name' is a datatype property of Person (a person's name). Different domains, different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a document/paper in the submission workflow (subclass of Paper, with children like Assigned Paper), while B 'Program Committee' is a committee (subclass of Committee, sibling of Organizing Committee). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of regular contribution (a document type submitted to a conference), sitting alongside Paper under Regular contribution, with child Abstract. B's 'Submitted Paper' is a paper in the submission stage of the paper lifecycle (parent Paper, child Assigned Paper, siblings Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, etc.), i.e. a stage/status of a paper rather than a document type. The two classifications are orthogonal: an extended abstract could be a submitted paper, but the concepts do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

cmt:User is a general person role in the conference system (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while confOf:Student is a specific participant subtype (sibling of Member, Regular) under Participant. User is broader and not a synonym for Student; the intended instances do not coincide.

A's has Topic relates a Conference/Paper to a Topic; B's has Review relates a Paper to a Review. Different domain (Conference vs Paper) and completely different range (Topic vs Review), so the relations are unrelated.

A 'Co chair' is a committee role (a person serving as co-chair of a committee), while B 'Location' is a venue/place for events. Their parents, siblings, and properties (committee co-chair relations vs. event location relations) are entirely different, so they cannot denote the same class.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (e.g. sessions running in parallel), while edas's 'is Topic Of' relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper (the topic a paper/conference is about). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (a venue room). Their paths (Conference document vs Place), parents, and siblings are entirely different domains, so they denote different concepts.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference event, sibling of Paper Presentation and Talk Event), whereas B's 'Author cd proceedings included' is a role/type of Author (a person who authored a proceedings paper), sibling of Lecturer and Tutorial speaker. The two denote entirely different kinds of things (event vs. person role), so they are unrelated.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event covering the submission of contributions (siblings: Camera Ready, Registration, Reviewing, Reviewing results), whereas B 'Workshop' is an academic event type (siblings: Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event). They denote different concepts in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

Both are social/after-conference activities, but a Conference Banquet is a formal evening social event of the conference, while a Full day tour is a daytime excursion after the conference; they are distinct event types that merely share the broader 'social/after-conference activity' category.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (printing hardcopy mailing manifests), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper. Different domain, range, and intended relation, so they are unrelated.

A 'Tutorial Abstract' is a kind of document (an abstract for a tutorial), while B 'Nonauthor registration fee' is a kind of registration fee (money). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. fees) and share no intended instances.

A's `pay` goes Person -> Money (a person pays money), while B's `payed by` goes Registration fee -> Person (a fee is paid by a person). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

In edas, Workshop is a kind of Academic Event (a meeting/event held at the conference), sibling to Paper Presentation and Talk Event. In ekaw, Track is a Scientific Event that is a subdivision of the conference programme, sibling to Workshop, Conference, Session and Individual Presentation. A workshop is a distinct event type, while a track is a thematic grouping of sessions/presentations; the two are not the same concept, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Paper Full Version is a subclass of Paper distinguished from Paper Abstract by content completeness (full text vs. abstract), i.e. a document-form distinction. In edas, Accepted Paper is a subclass of Paper distinguished by review outcome/status, sibling to Pending, Rejected, Withdrawn, Published, Active papers, and is linked to a Paper Presentation event. The two classifications are orthogonal: a full version need not be accepted and an accepted paper need not be a full version, so the classes do not denote the same concept.

City in confOf is a location class used as the range of has City (Organization, Person -> City), i.e. a place where organizations or persons are located. Currency in iasted is a monetary unit class, a completely different domain concept. They share no meaning, no properties, and no path context, so they are unrelated.

A's 'set Max Papers' is an Administrator action relating an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while B's 'is given to' relates an Item to a Person (e.g. an award/paper given to a person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'has Last Name' is a datatype property from Person to string capturing only the surname, while B's 'Name' is a broader datatype property from Person to string capturing the full name. A last name is a part of a name, so 'has Last Name' is strictly more specific than 'Name'; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (a conference-organisation activity such as Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while B's 'Operating Topicsystems' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area like Antennas, CAD, Cryptography). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has Phone' is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a phone number. Different domains (Person vs Contact Information) and different intended values (surname vs phone number), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference participant' is a general role for anyone taking part in a conference (with subclasses Active/Passive participant), while B's 'Student' is a person type distinguished by academic status, not by conference involvement. Their siblings differ (Committee member/Reviewer vs Paper Author/Possible Reviewer) and neither subsumes the other; a student is not necessarily a conference participant and a conference participant need not be a student.

A's Chair is a generic committee chair (sibling Co chair, domain of 'has a committee chair' on Committee), while B's General Chair is a specific organizer role under Organizator alongside Program Chair and Webmaster. A General Chair is a kind of chair, so Chair is broader and subsumes General Chair; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Accepted contribution' is a subclass of 'Reviewed contribution' denoting a document/contribution that has been accepted (with child 'Camera ready contribution' and sibling 'Rejected contribution'). B's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event describing the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions, sibling to 'Camera Ready event', 'Submission event', etc. One is a type of contribution/document, the other a type of event; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person who authors contributions/papers: same label 'Author', same path Person > Author, and both are linked to the written work via inverse properties (writes/written By in confOf, has Related Paper/is Written By in edas). The edas child Presenter is a specialisation, not a conflict, so the intended instances coincide.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an action performed by an Administrator that results in a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), i.e. the bidding process/event. B's 'reviewer Of Paper' relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper, i.e. a reviewer assignment relation. Different kinds of things in different directions; not equivalent.

A's Topic is the general class of research topics in the Conference ontology (it has names, belongs to reviews, conference parts, etc.). B's CAD Topic is a specific topic instance/class under the parent Topic in edas (siblings are Antennas Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.). CAD Topic is therefore a narrower concept than the general Topic class, so A is subsumed by B's broader Topic, not equivalent to the specific CAD Topic.

A's Publisher is an organisation that issues conference proceedings (domain of 'issues', range of 'has a publisher'), while B's Conference is the event itself with start/end dates, city, and held-by relation. They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A's 'is Topic Of' relates a Topic to a Conference/Paper (topic is about a paper/conference), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (a person writes a paper). Different domains (Topic vs Person), different ranges (Conference/Paper vs Item), and different directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote a conference session: edas 'Conference Session' is an academic event/document-related entity, and ekaw 'Conference Session' is a Session within Scientific Event, with children like Industrial Session and siblings Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

Conference document is a document artefact (call for papers, contribution, review, announcement) with authors and issue dates, while Event in EKAW is a happening (scientific/social event) with locations, organisers and sub-events. Their instances, properties and children do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference activity' is a subclass of Activity covering the individual activities that make up a conference (lectures, coffee breaks, registration, social program, etc.), whereas B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with properties for city, name, start/end dates and being held by ACM SIGKDD. The two concepts overlap in the conference domain but denote different things: a whole event versus its constituent activities, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference Chair is a leadership role in the conference organisation (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member who chairs the conference). B's Worker lecturer is a subcategory of Lecturer under Speaker/Author/Delegate, i.e. a person who gives lectures/works as a lecturer, not a conference chair. The paths, parents and siblings show entirely different roles in the domain; they do not denote the same concept.

A's 'Conference part' is a general container for Track, Tutorial, Workshop (parts of a conference volume), while B's 'Conference' is a specific scientific event (one edition of a conference) sitting under Scientific Event alongside Track and Workshop. The two denote different concepts: one is a part/component of a conference, the other is the conference event itself. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, a human who chairs the conference), while B 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is a starting date' is a datatype property of Important dates with range date, marking the beginning of a conference deadline/event. B's 'early Registration' is a datatype property of Participant with range boolean, indicating whether a participant registered early. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's hasEndDateTime is a datatype property giving the end time of a conference event (domain Conference Event, range dateTime), while B's hasEvent is an object property relating an Event to a sub-event (domain Event, range Event). They differ in kind, domain, range and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about a conference, with a URL), while B's 'University' is an academic institution/organisation. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's organises relates an Organisation/Person to an Event (organising a conference event), while B's occupy relates a Person to a Building/City/State (physical location). Different domains and ranges, different intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area/topic for classifying papers. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are subclasses of Paper, but they capture different distinctions: cmt's Paper Full Version contrasts with Paper Abstract (the full text vs. the abstract of a submission), while edas's Published Paper contrasts with Accepted/Pending/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper (the publication status of a paper). A full version is not necessarily published and a published paper need not be a full version, so the classes overlap but are not equivalent.

A Meta Review is a review of reviews (a document produced after the review phase, child of Review in cmt). B Textual Review Question is a type of question on a review form (sibling of Numerical Review Question, child of Review Question in edas). One is a review artefact, the other a form field/question; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's Paper is a kind of Contribution (a document submitted to a conference), while B's Best Paper Awards Committee is a subclass of Committee (an organisational body). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Conference contributor is a broad role class covering active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors, while Volunteer is a specific person role (confTool) with no overlap in the conference domain; they are not synonyms and neither subsumes the other.

Presenter in ekaw is a role of a conference participant who presents a paper (a Person subclass, with child Invited Speaker). IASTED non member is a subclass of Delegate in iasted, i.e. a conference attendee who is not an IASTED member; it is a membership-status category, not a presentation role. The two concepts overlap only incidentally (a presenter may or may not be an IASTED member) and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Review Question' is a specific question item on a review form (with numerical/textual subtypes), while B 'Document' is a general submission artefact whose children are Abstract, Paper and Review. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

confOf's 'follows' relates an Administrative event to the Administrative event that follows it (a temporal ordering between events), while ekaw's 'has Event' relates an Event to a sub-event/component Event (a part-whole containment relation). Both are Event-to-Event object properties, so they overlap in signature, but the intended semantics differ: ordering vs. composition. They are not equivalent, and neither is strictly more general than the other.

A's 'Program committee' is a committee (a group of people) that reviews papers for a conference, with properties linking it to a Conference volume. B's 'Building' is a physical place (parent Place) with children such as Conference hotel, Conference airport, and properties about being occupied/visited by persons and paid in money. The two denote entirely different concepts (organisational body vs. physical location), so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial/workshop), while B's Coffee break is a conference activity (a scheduled activity alongside lectures and registration). They denote different concepts in the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'Paper Author' is a Person who authors papers (sibling of Conference Participant, Possible Reviewer, Student under Person). B's 'Student lecturer' is a Lecturer who is also a Student, sitting under Lecturer in a chain Author > Lecturer > Student lecturer, with sibling Worker lecturer. The two denote different roles: an author of papers versus a student who lectures. Neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a Conference-domain datatype property giving the number of reviews per paper; B's 'has amount of' is a Money-domain datatype property giving a monetary amount. Different domains, different intended meanings, so they are unrelated despite both having int range.

A's markConflictOfInterest relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to record a conflict of interest (a negative association preventing assignment/review). B's reviewes relates a PC member to a Contribution to record that the member reviews that contribution (a positive reviewing relation). Different intents, different domains/ranges, and not inverses; they are unrelated relations.

A's isReviewedBy goes from Paper to a reviewer/chair (Paper -> Person), while B's reviewOfPaper goes from Review to Paper (Review -> Paper). They are inverse-like in different directions and relate different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property of Conference with range anyURI (a conference's logo web address), while B's 'early Registration' is a datatype property of Participant with range boolean (whether a participant registered early). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A is a person role (Session Chair, a subclass of Conference Participant/PC Member), while B is a document type (Brief introduction for Session chair, a subclass of Document). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and are not equivalent.

Both are submission-related deadlines under Deadline, but A is the general submissions deadline while B is specifically the abstract submission deadline; they overlap in the conference domain without denoting the same deadline.

A's PC Chair is a program-committee chair (a kind of PC Member/Conference Participant), while B's Session chair is a delegate who chairs a session; the two roles are distinct in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions), while B 'Transparency' is a kind of Document (an item/document artefact). They belong to different branches (Event vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is an ending date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates entity to a date literal (a deadline end date). B's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location (where the event takes place). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assign External Reviewer' relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (an assignment relation), while B's 'has Review History' relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a record of past reviews). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper (a document) that has been published, a subclass of Paper in the edas ontology. B 'Cd proceening' is a CD-ROM publication (a publication medium/artefact), a subclass of Publication, sibling of Book proceeding. They denote different concepts: a paper vs. a publication medium, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a committee entity), while B's 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. The domains and ranges are disjoint (Conference volume vs Organisation/Person; Organizing committee vs Event), so the two properties denote different relations and are not equivalent.

A's Person is a human agent in the conference domain (authors, reviewers, participants, with name/email/gender properties), while B's Sponsorship is a funding arrangement provided by an Organization with cost amount/currency properties. They denote entirely different concepts and share no instances.

A Conference is a working event (a whole event with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B Session Chair is a person role (a Conference Participant who chairs a session). They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Paper is a conference submission (has authors, reviews, decisions, subject areas), while ekaw:Multi-author_Volume is a published multi-author volume whose child is Proceedings and which is published by an organisation. They are different document types in the conference domain.

Both properties link an organising entity to the people/roles responsible for it: edas 'is Initiated By' has domain Call and range Conference Chair/Session Chair/TPC Member, while ekaw 'organised By' has domain Event and range Organisation/Person. They express a similar 'organised/initiated by' relation but differ in domain (Call vs Event) and range (specific chair roles vs Organisation/Person), so they overlap without being equivalent.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (a person's membership in a conference), while B's has_contributions relates a Conference volume to a Conference contribution (a volume containing papers). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

Both are datatype properties giving an end date/time, but A's domain is the 'Important dates' class (a deadline/date-range concept) while B's domain is 'Conference Event', and A's range is a plain date versus B's dateTime. They play a similar role (end of a period) but apply to different kinds of entities, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's title is the title of a Paper (domain Paper, range string), while B's has First Name is a person's first name (domain Person, range string). Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call For Manuscripts' is a subclass of Call (an announcement inviting submissions), while B's 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity in the conference workflow (accepting a submitted manuscript), sibling to Receiving/Refusing manuscript. They denote different concepts: an announcement vs. a decision activity.

A's 'manuscript Due On' is the deadline for submitting the manuscript (a submission deadline), while B's 'Start of conference' is the date the conference begins. Both are datatype properties on Conference with range dateTime, but they denote different deadlines/events in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'paper ID' is an identifier (unsignedLong) of a Paper, while B's 'is a full paper submission date' is a date property of the Important dates class. They relate different kinds of things (identifier vs. deadline date) and have different domains/ranges, so they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's PC Chair is a person role (a Conference Participant and PC Member). They denote entirely different kinds of entities — an event versus a person — so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while 'Best Research Paper Award' is a specific award given to a paper. They belong to different branches (document vs. award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'paper ID' is a datatype property mapping a Paper to an unsignedLong identifier, while B's 'related To Paper' is an object property mapping a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

Personal History in edas is a container for a person's publication and review history (children: Personal Publication History, Personal Review History), whereas Review in ekaw is a document produced in the review process (a subclass of Document with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review and properties review Of Paper, review Written By). The two denote different concepts: one is a biographical/history aggregate, the other a review document. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A is a conference event (a working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while B is a person role (a tutorial chair, a kind of conference participant). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person/role), so they are unrelated.

Tutorial is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation session), while Invited Speaker is a kind of person (a speaker role). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a person/group to a conference, but they differ in domain and direction: cmt's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member (an individual person) to a Conference, while Conference's was_a_committee_of relates a Committee (a collective body) to a Conference volume. They are conceptually related (membership in a conference's committee) but not the same relation, since the subject types and granularity differ.

A's 'was a committee of' links a Committee to a Conference volume (organisational/event structure), while B's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (authorship). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper (a specific document type, sibling of Paper Full Version), while Document in iasted is a broad superclass of many conference artefacts (Review, Submission, Form, etc.). The two denote different concepts: a Paper Abstract is a kind of paper, not the general Document class.

Academic Institution is an Organisation (a venue/organiser entity with children University, Research Institute), while Speaker is a Person role (with children Author, Invited Speaker). They belong to different top-level branches (Organisation vs Person) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A is Rejected Paper (a paper that was not accepted), B is Accepted Paper (a paper that was accepted and becomes part of proceedings). They are opposite outcomes of the review process, not the same concept. Although both are siblings under Evaluated Paper in ekaw, the edas Rejected Paper corresponds to ekaw's Rejected Paper, not Accepted Paper.

A's Associated Chair is a Person/Chairman subtype (an organisational role in the conference committee, sibling of Conference Chair, PC Chair, Author, Reviewer). B's IASTED member is a subtype of Delegate (an attendee/participant in the conference building, sibling of Speaker, Listener, Session chair). The two denote different concepts: a chairing role versus a membership/attendee status, so they are not equivalent.

A Workshop is a small interactive scientific event (sibling of Conference, Session, Track under Scientific Event), whereas a Plenary lecture is a large formal lecture given to all attendees (a kind of Lecture, sibling of Session and Tutorial under Conference activity). They denote different kinds of conference activities and are not equivalent.

A's 'review Criteria Entered By' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered review criteria), while B's 'has Reviewer' links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (who reviews the paper). Different domain, range, and intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Poster' is a type of contribution (a submitted/presented work). They belong to different branches (document vs contribution) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity such as tutorial or workshop), while B's Refusing manuscript is an activity-before-conference step in the manuscript handling process (sibling of Accepting/Receiving manuscript). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A is a class of conference contributions that have been accepted (a document/contribution in the submission workflow, sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B is a class of review ratings (a value/score used in reviewing, sibling of Reject Rating and Accept If Room Rating). One denotes an accepted paper, the other a rating category; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference topic (a subject area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is the program committee (an organizational body under Committee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.
A's hasAuthor relates a Paper to its Author; B's volumeContainsPaper relates a volume (proceedings) to the papers it contains. Different domain/range and direction, so not equivalent.

Meal Event is a specific kind of non-academic conference event (a meal such as the conference dinner), while ekaw's Event is the most general event class covering scientific and social events. Meal Event is therefore strictly narrower than Event, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'Written contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution' and is further specialized into 'Regular contribution' and 'Submitted contribution'. B's 'Contribution' is the broader class whose children include Paper, Poster and Short paper, and which is written by Authors and reviewed by PC members. The intended instances of A (written contributions) are a subset of the intended instances of B (all contributions, including posters and short papers), so A is strictly more specific than B.

A's Poster is a specific kind of conference contribution (a poster presentation), while B's Paper is a written contribution; in confOf, Poster is a sibling of Paper under Contribution, so they are distinct concepts, not equivalent.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean datatype property of a Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted; B's 'paper Presented As' is an object property linking a Paper to an Individual Presentation (presentation format). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A's Meal Menu is a document describing the menu of a meal event (has Menu / is Menu Of link it to Meal Event), while B's Review is a document containing a reviewer's evaluation of a paper. They share only the generic Document parent; their intended instances and roles in the conference domain are entirely different, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people/roles), while B's is_part_of_conference_volumes relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (proceedings). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

Associated Chair (cmt) is a chair role under Chairman, alongside Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair; General Chair (sigkdd) is a top organizing role under Organizator. Both are senior chair roles in the conference domain, but they are not the same concept: 'Associated Chair' is a generic/auxiliary chair role, while 'General Chair' is the specific head of the organizing committee. They overlap in being chair roles but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes papers), while B's 'Author information form' is a subclass of Form (a document used to collect author details). They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A is a Person role (Conference Chair) in the conference organisation, while B is a Document item ('Brief introduction for Session chair') under Item > Document. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the presenter), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (the thing given). Both express a giving/presenting relation involving a person, but the domains and ranges differ: A is presentation-centric with a participant range, B is person-centric with an activity/item range. They overlap in meaning but are not the same relation in the same direction, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'has tutorials' relates a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a whole-part relation, subproperty of has parts), while B's 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (e.g. signing up for something). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic-level preference for reviewing), while B's property links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a reviewer's record of past reviews). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Academia Organization in edas is a subtype of Organization denoting academic institutions (siblings: Government Organization, Industry Organization, NGO), i.e. a kind of organisation. Organising Agency in ekaw is a subtype of Organisation denoting an agent that organises a conference (siblings: Academic Institution, Proceedings Publisher), i.e. a role/function rather than a type of institution. The intended instances do not coincide: an academic institution is not necessarily an organising agency, and an organising agency need not be an academic organisation. Hence the classes are not equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a conference event (sibling of Track and Workshop, part of a Conference volume), while B's Tip is a monetary category (sibling of Fee, Sponsorship, Tax under Money). The shared word 'tip' is coincidental; the concepts are unrelated.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'write' links a Person to an Item they wrote. Different domains (Conference vs Person), different ranges (Administrator vs Item), and different intended meanings (administrative data entry vs authorship), so they are not the same relation.

A Presenter (ekaw) is a Conference Participant who presents, with child Invited Speaker; B One day presenter (iasted) is a Delegate who presents for one day, a narrower role. Every one-day presenter is a presenter, but presenters can be multi-day or invited, so A is broader: A is subsumed by B's broader notion? No—B is narrower, so A subsumes B; the pair is not equivalent.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper the reviewer was assigned to review), while B's writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author (authorship). Different domains (Reviewer vs Contribution) and ranges (Paper vs Author), and opposite directions of the authoring/reviewing relationship; they are not the same relation.

A's Talk Event is an academic event (a scheduled talk, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk) under Academic Event, while B's Presentation is a conference activity (with children Power Point presentation and Video presentation) under Conference activity. Both denote a presentation/talk given at a conference, so they overlap, but the taxonomies differ: Talk Event is a subclass of Academic Event alongside Paper Presentation and Workshop, whereas Presentation is a generic activity that also covers non-talk activities. They are closely related but not clearly equivalent.

A's 'name' is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's 'has Phone' is specifically a phone number property for Person. They denote different attributes (name vs. phone number), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship of a paper), while B's 'prepare' links a Person to an Item (a person prepares an item). The domains and ranges are reversed and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.
