A's email is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address), while B's send is an object property linking a Person to an Item (sending something). They relate different kinds of things and have different ranges, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a name' is a general naming property whose domain spans Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, while B's 'location' is a datatype property restricted to Social event and Working event giving where an event is held. They relate different kinds of things (names vs. event venues) and have disjoint domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's `need` relates a Person to an Item (a person needs an item), while B's `presentationed by` relates a Document to a Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes represent the general concept of a person in the conference domain. In Conference, Person is the superclass of all human roles (Committee member, Reviewer, etc.) and has properties like first name, last name, email, and authorship. In edas, Person is likewise the superclass of Attendee, Author, Reviewer, etc., with analogous properties (first name, last name, email, biography, membership). The intended instances coincide: any individual who is a person in one ontology would be a person in the other. The slight differences in property sets reflect modeling choices, not a difference in the class's meaning.

A's `date` is a generic datatype property on Conference (the conference's date), while B's `is an abstract submission date` is a specific deadline property on Important dates. They both have range date but denote different relations (general conference date vs. abstract submission deadline), so they are not equivalent; they are only loosely related.

Reviewer (cmt) is a conference member who evaluates papers, with properties about bids, assignments, conflicts of interest and reading papers. Speaker (sigkdd) is a person who gives a presentation of a document, with children Author and Invited Speaker. The two roles are distinct in the conference domain: a reviewer reviews submissions, a speaker presents work. Their paths, siblings and properties do not overlap, so they are not equivalent.

A's Slide Set is a specific kind of Document (a presentation slide set), while B's Document is a broad class covering forms, invitations, reviews, submissions, etc. Slide Set is therefore strictly narrower than Document, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

Both properties link Author to Paper, but they denote different relations: 'has Related Paper' expresses an association between an author and a paper that is related to them (e.g. a paper they are connected to but did not necessarily author), whereas 'submit' expresses the act of an author submitting a paper. Same domain/range does not make them the same relation, and neither subsumes the other.

A's Paper is a conference document (subclass of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Departure tax is a subclass of Tax under Money; the two concepts share no meaning in the conference domain.

edas Conference Event is a broad umbrella covering both Academic and Non Academic Events (its children), while ekaw Conference is a specific Scientific Event (one edition of a conference) sitting alongside Workshop, Session, Track. A Conference is a kind of Conference Event, but Conference Event also includes non-academic events, so Conference Event is strictly more general: Conference is subsumed by Conference Event.

A's readByReviewer relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the person who reads it), while B's hasReview relates a Paper to a Review (the review document/process). Different ranges (Reviewer vs Review) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Social event' is a conference event (banquet, reception, trip) under Event, while B 'Building' is a physical place (conference building, hotel, restaurant) under Place. Different domains and no shared instances.

Author is a person role (a conference member who writes papers), while Multi author Volume is a document type (a collection of documents, parent of Proceedings). They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and have incompatible properties (Author writes/submits papers; Multi author Volume is published by an organisation). No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee (organisational structure), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (a presentation relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper, sibling of Paper Abstract), while B is a subclass of Topic (a subject area such as Multimedia). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track parts (a whole-part relation within a conference), while B's 'holded by' relates a Conference to the organisation that holds it (ACM SIGKDD). Different domain/range and different meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (a person on the committee), while B's isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both are narrow subclasses of Author/Lecturer denoting a student who is also an author/speaker, but they sit in different taxonomies (iasted: Student lecturer under Lecturer; sigkdd: Author of paper student under Author) and neither is strictly more general than the other, so they overlap without being equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event (like Conference, Tutorial) held as a distinct event type, while B's Poster Session is a session type within a scientific event (siblings: Conference Session, Demo Session, Regular Session, Workshop Session). The corresponding concept to A's Workshop in ekaw is Workshop Session, not Poster Session; the two denote different kinds of event/session and are not equivalent.

A's name is a general naming property for Conference and Person, while B's remark is a free-text comment on a Contribution (confTool note). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but A's 'manuscript Due On' is a specific submission deadline for a Conference manuscript, while B's 'is dated on' is a general date association for any Activity. They overlap in that a manuscript deadline is a date of an activity, but neither subsumes the other cleanly and they are not the same relation.

A's 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (a conference social gathering such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B's 'Tax' is a subclass of Money (a monetary charge such as Departure tax, Value added tax). They share no meaning, no parent, and no properties; the only superficial link is that confOf's Social event has a 'has VAT' property, but that does not make the event class equivalent to a tax class.

A's acceptedBy relates a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it (domain Paper, range Administrator). B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domains, ranges, and direction of meaning; not the same relation.

A's Conference Member is a broad person role encompassing chairs, authors, PC members and reviewers, with properties linking it to a Conference. B's Conference applicant is a person who applies/registers for a conference, with a child Registeered applicant and siblings like Conference participant and Conference contributor. The intended instances do not coincide: a conference member (organiser/participant role) is not the same as an applicant (pre-registration role), and the contexts (children, siblings, properties) differ.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a conference attendee who does not actively contribute (sibling of 'Active conference participant' under 'Conference participant'), whereas a 'Program Committee member' is an organizer role (under 'Organizator', sibling of chairs and webmaster). The two denote different roles in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A's Review is a conference document (a review of a contribution), while B's Departure tax is a kind of Tax under Money. The domains are entirely different (conference documents vs. financial taxes), so the two classes are unrelated.

A 'Call For Manuscripts' is a call/announcement event (sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Reviews under Call), whereas B 'Abstract' is a document part (sibling of Paper and Review under Document). They denote different concepts: an announcement versus a text artefact, so they are unrelated.

A is a review rating value ('Accept If Room', a rating category used in the EDAS review scale), while B is a paper that has been rejected in the EKAW submission workflow. One is a rating/decision category, the other a document state; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person who authors a paper: ekaw's Paper Author is a Person subclass directly representing authors of papers, and sigkdd's Author of paper is a subclass of Author (itself under Speaker/Person) representing the same role. The labels and paths agree on the intended instances (persons who write papers), so they are equivalent.

A's email is a Person's email address (string), while B's Name is a Person's name (string). Both are datatype properties on Person with string range, but they denote different attributes (email address vs. name), so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (a role for workshop/tutorial tracks), while B's isInitiatedBy links a Call to a Conference Chair, Session Chair, or TPC Member. The domains (Conference part vs Call) and ranges (Track workshop chair vs chair roles) differ, and the intended relations are different: one assigns a workshop/tutorial chair to a conference part, the other records who initiated a call. They are not the same relation.

A's `follows` relates Administrative event to Administrative event (temporal ordering of administrative events), while B's `lists Event` relates a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event (a publication listing events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

isWrittenBy goes from Paper to Author (paper has an author), while submit goes from Author to Paper (author submits a paper). They are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

A's Paper is a conference document (written by authors, reviewed, has topics), while B's Transport vehicle is a physical means of transport (Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different domains.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote different attributes: hasBiography relates a person to their biography text, while Nation relates a person to their nationality/country. Different intended meaning, so not equivalent.

A's 'is an abstract submission date' is a datatype property of the Important dates class whose value is a date (a deadline for abstract submission). B's 'contact Email' is a datatype property of Contribution whose value is a string (an email address, per the confTool comment). They relate different kinds of things (dates vs. email strings) in different domains (Important dates vs. Contribution), so they are unrelated.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event such as Conference or Tutorial) in confOf, whereas 'Introduction of speaker' is a conference activity subsumed by Introduction in iasted, i.e. a session/activity of introducing a speaker. They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings). B's `for Event` relates a Call to the Academic Event it is a call for (domain Call, range Academic Event). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

cmt:Paper is the general document class for submitted papers (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with authors, reviews, decisions). edas:Rated Papers is a narrower subclass of Active Paper, i.e. only papers that have received ratings/reviews. Every rated paper is a paper, but not every paper is rated, so cmt:Paper is more general and is subsumed by the narrower edas class.

A's has Phone relates a Person to a phone number string, while B's Nation relates a Person to a country/nationality string. They share only the domain (Person) and range (string) but denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'was a program committee of' relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (the committee is a committee of a specific conference volume/edition). B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD (the organising body/society) to a Conference (the society holds a conference). The subject kinds differ (committee vs. society) and the object kinds differ (conference volume vs. conference), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

cmt's `date` is a generic conference date (likely the main/start date), while edas's `end Date` is specifically the conference end date and time. They both relate a Conference to a date, so they overlap, but they are not the same relation: one is a general date, the other a specific end date. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's Regular is a participant who is not a Member or Student (a regular, non-student attendee), while B's Student non speaker is a delegate who is a student and not a speaker. The two concepts are disjoint: one excludes students, the other requires being a student. Different paths (Participant vs Delegate/Non speaker) and different siblings confirm they denote different concepts.

A's 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events), while B's 'submit until' relates a Document to a Deadline (submission deadline for a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a program committee' relates a Conference volume to its Program committee (a part/committee relation), while B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference it organises. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both are datatype properties giving the start time of an event/conference; confOf's 'starts on' has domain Event (the conference is an Event) and sigkdd's 'Start of conference' has domain Conference, so they relate the same kind of thing in the same direction, differing only in the literal datatype (string vs dateTime).

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a Document item (sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Review, Submission). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. document) and share no intended instances.

cmt:Conference Member is a broad role class under Person, covering chairs, authors, PC members and reviewers, and is linked to Conference via member Of Conference. ekaw:Presenter is a specific Conference Participant role (someone who presents, with Invited Speaker as a child), not a general membership role. The intended instances do not coincide: a conference member need not present, and a presenter need not be a member of the conference organisation. Different paths, parents, siblings and properties, so the classes are unrelated.

A's `date` is a datatype property of Conference whose range is a date (the conference's date), while B's `has Name` is a datatype property of Conference whose range is a string and whose comment says it is the conference's full name. They relate a conference to entirely different kinds of values (a date vs. a name string), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a specific kind of paper (sibling of 'Paper Abstract' under 'Paper'), while B's 'Paper' is the general contribution type (siblings 'Poster', 'Short paper'). A full paper is a Paper, but Paper is broader, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's Accommodation Place is a kind of Place (lodging venue) alongside Conference Venue Place, Dining Place and Meeting Room Place, i.e. a physical location for lodging. B's Trip city is a kind of City, a city that is the destination of a trip, alongside Conference city, Presenter city and Sponsor city. One is a lodging place, the other a city role in travel; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a kind of working event (a session/activity at the conference, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Presenter is a kind of person (an Author who presents). They belong to different branches of the domain (event vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.

Conference Banquet is a social event (a dinner/banquet activity) in ekaw, while Hotel is a physical place in sigkdd. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. location) and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's write Review relates a Reviewer to a Review (domain Reviewer, range Review), while B's is Review History Of relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer). They differ in both domain and range and are not inverses either, so they denote different relations.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to the contributions they review (domain Member PC, range Contribution), i.e. reviewer -> paper. B's `review Written By` relates a Review to the person who wrote it (domain Review, range Possible Reviewer), i.e. review -> reviewer. The arguments and direction differ: one links a person to a paper, the other links a review to a person. They are not the same relation, nor inverses of the same relation (the review entity is absent from A's property).

A 'Paper Full Version' is a document type (a full paper submission, sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), while B 'Departure' is a post-conference activity (sibling of Full day tour under Activity after conference). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. activities) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Member PC' is a program-committee member (comment: Reviewer; reviews Contributions, has expertise in Topics), while B's 'Organizing Committee member' is a member of the organizing committee, a sibling of Program Chair and Program Committee member under Organizator. The two denote different roles, so they are not equivalent.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (membership relation). B's parallel_with links an Administrative event to another Administrative event (scheduling concurrency). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

Presenter (a Conference Participant who presents) and Lecturer (a Speaker/Author who gives lectures) both denote people who deliver content at the conference, but they sit in different hierarchies: Presenter is a role of a Conference Participant with children like Invited Speaker, while Lecturer is a subtype of Author/Speaker with children Student/Worker lecturer. They overlap in the domain (a presenter may be a lecturer) but are not the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome), while B's is_given_to relates an Item to a Person (e.g. a review or award given to a person). Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the person who delivers the talk), while B's 'is sent by' links an Item (e.g. a submission/paper) to a Person (the sender/submitter). Both relate a conference artefact to a person, but the artefact types (Presentation vs Item) and the intended relation (presenting vs sending/submitting) differ, so they are not equivalent; they merely overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a person role (a Conference contributor, sibling of Regular author), while B's 'Tutorial' is a kind of presentation event (an Individual Presentation, sibling of Invited Talk). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and are not equivalent.

In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (path: Delegate > Speaker > Author), so every Author is a Speaker. In sigkdd, Speaker is a superclass of Author (Speaker has child Author). Thus Author is strictly more specific than Speaker; the two are not equivalent. The relation is subsumed_by (Author subsumed by Speaker).

University (confOf) is an Organization subtype whose instances are academic institutions that scholars study at; Sponzorship (iasted) is a Money subtype denoting financial sponsorship. Different domains (organization vs. monetary concept), no shared instances or properties, so they are unrelated.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a reviewed submission that was not accepted (a document/contribution in the submission workflow, sibling of Accepted contribution). B 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity that occurs before the conference (sibling of Accepting manuscript, Refusing manuscript), i.e. the act of receiving a manuscript, not a rejected paper. Different kinds (contribution vs. activity) and different meanings, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Trip is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception) organised during the conference, whereas iasted's Transport vehicle is a physical means of transport (parent of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) used as equipment/item. They denote different concepts despite both relating to travel.

Conference Member in cmt is a person role (a member of the conference organisation, parent of Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while Travel Grant in edas is a sponsorship/funding category, not a person. Different domains and no overlap.

A's Abstract is a document/contribution type (an extended abstract that is part of a paper/poster/presentation), while B's Conference is an event with dates, country, members and topics. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Committee member' is a person role in the conference organisation (parent Person, children Chair/Co chair, related to Committee via has members/was a member of). B 'Meal Event' is a non-academic conference event (parent Non Academic Event, child Conference Dinner, related to Meal Menu). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

cmt:Review is a document produced by a reviewer (a subclass of Document, sibling of Paper, written by a Reviewer, with a Meta Review child). edas:ReviewRating is a rating value assigned to an active paper (has Rating from Active Paper, with children Accept/Reject/Weak Reject ratings). A review document and a review rating are different concepts, though both concern the reviewing process, so they are related but not equivalent.

Both classes denote a conference edition in the conference-organisation domain. cmt's Conference is the central event entity with properties for submissions, dates, administrators and committee members; ekaw's Conference is explicitly 'One edition of a conference' under Scientific Event. The intended instances coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

Author is a person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers), while Activity before conference is a temporal phase of conference activities (accepting/receiving/refusing manuscripts). Different kinds and domains; no overlap.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while B's 'payed by' links a Registration fee to a Person (payment). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; they are not the same property.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad class covering all persons involved in a conference (its children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, Conference Chair, Associated Chair), whereas edas Conference Chair is a specific role class for the chair of the conference. Conference Member is strictly more general than Conference Chair, so A subsumes B, not equivalence.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's 'is occupied by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a person occupying a place). Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Conference Member/User and is defined by writing/submitting papers and being a reviewer/committee member. In sigkdd, Speaker is a Person who presents a Document, with Author as a child (subclass) of Speaker. Thus every sigkdd Author is a Speaker, but not every cmt Author is a Speaker (authors need not present). The cmt Author is more specific than the sigkdd Speaker, so Author is subsumed by Speaker.

A's 'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to the people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. the review relation. B's 'is writen by' links an Item to its author (Person), i.e. the authorship relation. Different kinds of things in the same direction (reviewer vs. author), so they are not equivalent.

Publisher in the Conference ontology is an organisation that issues conference proceedings (domain of 'issues', range of 'has a publisher'), whereas Conference Session in edas is a temporal event/activity within a conference that relates to documents and persons. Their intended instances do not coincide; they share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

A's acceptedBy relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper written). Different domains (Paper vs Author), different ranges (Administrator vs Contribution), and different directions/meanings; they are not the same relation.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class covering all persons involved in a conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), whereas Co chair in Conference is a specific committee role (co-chair of a committee), sibling of Chair under Committee member. The two denote different concepts: one is a general membership class, the other a specific committee position, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a document/announcement soliciting submissions (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Conference announcement and Review). B 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a temporal deadline (subclass of Deadline, sibling of Deadline Paper Submission and Deadline Author notification). A call for papers is not a deadline; they denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

An Invited Talk in ekaw is a kind of Individual Presentation (a talk given by an invited speaker), while a Plenary lecture in iasted is a kind of Lecture (a large-audience lecture). Both are presentation/lecture events, but they are not the same concept: an invited talk need not be plenary, and a plenary lecture need not be by invitation. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

A's 'Review preference' is a class representing a reviewer's preference/degree for a topic or submission (it has a degree, belongs to reviewers, and links to topics/submissions). B's 'Reviewer' is a person class (subclass of Person) representing an individual who reviews papers. The two denote different concepts: one is a preference record, the other is a person role. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A Conference Chair is a specific role (a person chairing the conference, sibling of Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair, etc.), whereas B Conference participant is a broad class covering all persons participating in a conference, with children Active/Passive participant and siblings Committee member, Reviewer, etc. Every Conference Chair is a conference participant, but not every participant is a conference chair, so A is strictly more specific than B.

A's Conference Member is a broad person role (parent of Author, Reviewer, PC Member, Chair) tied to a Conference; B's Steering committee is a committee body (sibling of Organizing/Program committee) tied to a Conference volume. Different kinds of entities (person role vs. committee), so not equivalent.

A's Meta Reviewer is a special subtype of Reviewer (its parent is Reviewer, and the comment explicitly says 'A special type of Reviewer'), while B's Reviewer is the general reviewer class. Thus Meta Reviewer is strictly more specific than Reviewer, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a human role: active participant, invited speaker, regular author), while B 'Social program' is a subclass of Conference activity (an event such as a dinner banquet). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.
Both denote the same conference-domain concept; labels and context agree.

A's Workshop is a conference event (sibling of Track and Tutorial, part of a Conference, hosting workshops in a proceedings volume), while B's Van is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi). The shared word 'van'/'workshop' does not indicate the same concept; the domains are entirely different.

A's memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (a person-to-event membership relation), while B's has_a_commtitee links a Conference volume to a Committee (a whole-to-part relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's adjustedBy relates a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it, while B's hasReview relates a Paper to its Review. Different domain (Bid vs Paper), different range (Reviewer vs Review), and different direction of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Written contribution' is a kind of conference contribution (a document/paper submitted to a conference, sibling of Poster, Presentation, Invited talk), while B's 'Author' is a person (a Speaker who writes papers, with properties submit, obtain, notification until). The two denote different concepts — a document versus a person — so they are unrelated.

A's 'is occupied by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (occupancy of a location), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (who pays the fee). Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event at which an accepted paper is presented. They belong to different branches (document vs. event) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Programme is a specific document type (a conference programme/schedule) that belongs to a Conference Event, sibling to Paper, Review, Slide Set. B's Document is a broad superclass of many artefacts (forms, invitations, submissions, reviews, etc.). Programme is at most a kind of Document, but the pair as given is not equivalent; the intended concepts differ (programme schedule vs. generic document).

A's coversTopic relates an Event/Paper to a Research Topic (the subject matter a paper or event is about), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domain (Event/Paper vs Person), different range (Research Topic vs Item), and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a person/committee entity to a conference, but the domains differ: cmt's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member (an individual person role) to a Conference, while Conference's was_an_organizing_committee_of relates an Organizing committee (a collective body) to a Conference volume. They overlap in the conference-organisation domain but are not the same relation, since one is about individual membership and the other about a committee's association with a conference volume.

A is a research topic area (Operating Topicsystems, a child of Topic in the edas ontology), while B is a committee role/group (Organizing Committee, a child of Committee in sigkdd). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject areas vs. organizational bodies) and share no intended instances.

A's Paper is a contribution type (sibling of Poster and Short paper) in the conference-organisation domain, while B's Antennas Topic is a subject/topic category under Topic. They denote different concepts: a paper artefact versus a research topic area, so they are unrelated.

A 'Tutorial Abstract' is a document (an abstract text for a tutorial), while B 'Plenary lecture' is a conference activity/lecture type. They belong to different branches (Document vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a scientific paper with an abstract), while B's Form is a document type with children like Author information form, Hotel registration form, and Registration form. These denote different concepts: a paper is a contribution, not a form. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

Both denote the opening welcome event of a conference: A's 'Welcome Talk' is a Talk Event (sibling of Closing Talk) within Academic Event, while B's 'Welcome address' is a Conference activity (sibling of Introduction, Lecture, Presentation). The intended instances coincide — the welcoming speech/address that opens the conference — so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent despite the different parent categories.

A's Abstract is a document type (an abstract of a paper/talk, with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and it is presented as a presentation), while B's Paper is the full paper document that authors submit. They are distinct document types in the conference domain, not synonyms.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to the Reviewer who invited them (domain and range both Reviewer), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item they authored. Different kinds of things are related in different directions, so the two properties are not equivalent.

Conference in confOf is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas Invited Speaker in ekaw is a role of a person (a presenter). They belong to disjoint branches (event vs. person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are the central class representing a written scientific work submitted to a conference; identical labels, matching context (authored by persons, reviewed, published in proceedings), and no conflicting properties distinguish them.

A's Cheque is a payment document (a financial instrument, sibling of Bank transfer) under Item > Document > Payment document, while B's Paper is a submitted research paper (sibling of Abstract and Review, domain of submit(Author -> Paper)). They share only the generic Document ancestor and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's max Papers is a datatype property of Program Committee Member with range int, expressing the maximum number of papers a PC member may review/be assigned. B's paper Due On is a datatype property of Conference with range dateTime, expressing a submission deadline. They have different domains, different ranges (int vs dateTime), and different intended meanings (a numeric limit vs a temporal deadline), so they are unrelated.

A's Author is a conference member who writes/submits papers; B's Reviewer is a person who reviews papers. They are distinct roles (an author is not a reviewer), and the properties confirm this: Author has write Paper/submit Paper, Reviewer has is Reviewing/has Review History. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a person is a member of the conference), while B's is needed for relates an Item to a Person (a person needs the item). The domains differ (Conference vs Item) and the intended meanings are different relations, so they are not equivalent.

Conference document is a class of documents (calls, contributions, reviews) authored by persons and issued on dates, while Organisation is an entity that organises events and publishes proceedings. Their children, properties and domain roles do not overlap; they denote different concepts in the conference domain.

A's `remark` is a datatype property attaching a free-text string to a Contribution (a comment/note field, confTool-specific). B's `review Written By` is an object property linking a Review to a Possible Reviewer (the author of the review). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Contribution vs Review), and range (string vs Possible Reviewer), so they denote different relations.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document type (a short summary version of a paper, sibling of 'Paper Full Version' under 'Paper'), whereas B 'Computer Architecture Topic' is a subject area/topic of the conference domain (sibling of other research topics under 'Topic'). They denote entirely different kinds of things and share no meaning.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'adjusted By' links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it (domain Bid, range Reviewer), while B's 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (domain Reviewer, range Personal Review History). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

confOf's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while edas's Published Paper is a specific subcategory of Paper (siblings Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper). Published Paper is strictly narrower, so confOf Paper is subsumed by edas Published Paper.

confOf Member is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference, with siblings Regular and Student), i.e. a conference attendee/registrant. ekaw SC Member is a subclass of PC Member (a reviewer role), specifically a member of the steering committee. The two denote different roles in different hierarchies (attendee vs. committee/reviewer), so they are not equivalent.

Both are classes named Paper under Document in the conference domain; cmt's Paper (with abstract/full version subclasses, authors, reviews, decisions) and ekaw's Paper (with conference/workshop/poster/etc. subclasses, reviews, topics) denote the same concept of a submitted/published conference paper. The differing subclasses reflect different granularity, not different intended instances.

confOf's 'Working event' is a broad category of events (children: Conference, Tutorial, Workshop; siblings: Administrative event, Social event), whereas edas's 'Conference' is a specific kind of event with children Single Level Conference and Two Level Conference. A Working event is more general than a Conference, so Working event subsumes Conference; they are not equivalent.

A's 'is connected with' is a broad relation between Activity/Person and Item/Place, while B's 'can stay in' is a narrower relation specifically between a Person and a Place (accommodation). A subsumes B: every 'can stay in' link is a kind of connection, but not vice versa.

A's hasCostCurrency is a datatype property of Sponsorship (the currency of a sponsorship cost), while B's Currency is a datatype property of Registration fee (the currency of a registration fee). They belong to different domains and different concepts in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

ekaw's authorOf relates a Person to a Document (the paper they authored), while iasted's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or presentation). Both express a person's involvement in producing/contributing to something, but the ranges differ (Document vs Activity/Item) and the intended relations are not the same, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Member PC' is a program-committee member/reviewer (comment 'Reviewer', properties expert On Topic and reviewes Contribution), while B's 'Attendee' is any person attending the conference. A PC member may attend, but the intended instances do not coincide; the sibling sets also differ (B has Reviewer and TPC Member as separate classes, A's Member PC is the reviewer role).

A's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution holding the paper's abstract text; B's 'has Cost Currency' is a datatype property of Sponsorship holding a currency string. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (the venue/proceedings where it is submitted), while B's 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (its subject matter). Different domain/range semantics and direction of meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's start Date is the start date/time of a Conference (domain Conference, range dateTime). B's done till is a date property of a Deadline (domain Deadline, range date). Different domains (Conference vs Deadline) and different intended meaning (conference start vs deadline completion date), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role a person plays on a contribution (the first author of a paper), a subclass of Regular author within the document/contribution branch. B's 'Presenter' is a Conference Participant who presents at the conference, with children like Invited Speaker and siblings like Session Chair. The first author of a paper need not present it, and a presenter need not be an author, so the intended instances do not coincide.

A's property links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (a person/role), while B's eventOnList links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (a publication/medium). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

Van is a transport vehicle (a means of transportation) in the iasted ontology, while Listener is a person role (attendee who listens) in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Item > Transport vehicle vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name; B's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution giving the text of a paper's abstract. Different domains, different ranges semantically (name string vs. abstract text), and different intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's Programme is a conference programme document (sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set; linked to a Conference Event via belongs To Event / has Programme), whereas B's Paper is a submitted contribution (sibling of Abstract and Review, with submit from Author). They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's defaultChoice is a datatype property linking a social/working event to a positiveInteger (a default number of participants/choices), while B's listsEvent is an object property linking a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. They have different domains, different ranges (datatype vs. object), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Person (a registered applicant who paid late), while B 'Hotel fee' is a subclass of Fee/Money (a monetary charge for a hotel). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Banquet is a specific social event (a formal meal), while B's Meal Event is a broader category of non-academic conference events that includes meals and has Conference Dinner as a child. A banquet is a kind of meal event, so Banquet is subsumed by Meal Event, not equivalent.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while B's pay relates a Person to a Registration fee (payment). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (a task/action of entering review criteria for a conference), while B's 'need' relates a Person to an Item (a generic need relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'enter Conference Details' is an Administrator action whose range is a Conference; B's 'prepare' is a Person action whose range is an Item. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

Academia Organization is a subtype of Organization denoting academic institutions, while Proceedings Publisher is a subtype of Organisation denoting entities that publish proceedings. They are different specializations with no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'Paper Author' is a Person who authors papers (sibling of Conference Participant, Possible Reviewer, Student under Person). B's 'Worker lecturer' is a very specific role deep under Lecturer > Author > Speaker > Delegate > Conference building, denoting a lecturer who is also a worker. The two denote different concepts: one is an author of papers, the other a lecturing worker; neither subsumes the other in the conference domain.

A is a document type (an abstract of an invited talk), a subclass of Abstract under Document. B is a conference activity (a plenary lecture), a subclass of Lecture under Activity. One denotes a written document, the other a scheduled event, so their instances cannot coincide.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman of the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B 'Session room' is a physical place (sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

hasTopic relates a conference paper to its topic; write relates a person to an item they authored. Different domains (Conference/Paper vs Person), different ranges (Topic vs Item), and different intended relations (subject classification vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A's `written By` goes from Document to Person (a document is written by a person), while B's `write` goes from Person to Item (a person writes an item). They describe the same underlying authorship relation but in opposite directions, so they are inverses rather than equivalent properties.

Conference Banquet is a social event (a subclass of Event), while Sponzorship is a financial/money concept (a subclass of Money). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of Conference participant (a person role, sibling of Active conference participant), whereas B 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a conference type, sibling of Single Level Conference). They denote different kinds of entities (person role vs. conference type) and are unrelated.

A is a research topic (Wireless Communications Topic) under Topic, while B is an organizational body (Organizing Committee) under Committee. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) in the Conference ontology, whereas B 'Computer Networks Sensor Topic' is a research topic in the edas topic hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Co chair' is a committee member who co-chairs a committee (sibling of Chair, linked to Committee via committee co-chair properties). B's 'OC Chair' is a chair within the Organising Committee, a subclass of OC Member. Both denote a chairing role in conference organisation, so they overlap, but A is a generic committee co-chair while B is specifically the head of the organising committee; neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference event with two levels), while B's 'PC Chair' is a role/person (Conference Participant > PC Chair). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person role), so they are unrelated.

A Workshop Chair is a conference participant who chairs a workshop (a PC Member/Conference Participant role), while B Tutorial speaker is an author who speaks in a tutorial. Different roles in different sub-hierarchies (organisational role vs. speaker/author role); no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about the conference, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with a URL property), whereas B's 'Conference hall' is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel, Main office). They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who started the bidding process), while B's 'reviewes' relates a PC Member to a Contribution (the reviewing relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

Both properties link a document-like entity to a subject/topic classification: cmt's hasSubjectArea goes from Paper to Subject Area, confOf's hasTopic goes from Working event to Topic. The ranges (Subject Area vs Topic) are plausibly the same kind of classification concept, but the domains differ: Paper is a submitted document, whereas Working event is the conference event/session at which a paper is presented. Since the property relates different kinds of source entities, they are not equivalent; they overlap in the sense of assigning a topic to a paper-related item, so 'related' is the safest verdict.

A is a class of documents (a paper that has been published, sibling of Accepted/Rejected Paper under Paper), while B is a deadline (a time point, sibling of submission and registration deadlines under Deadline). They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. time point) and are not equivalent.
A is a person role (Invited speaker), B is an event type (Invited Talk); different kinds of entities, so not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document/announcement soliciting submissions, while B 'Rated Papers' is a subclass of Active Paper denoting papers that have received ratings/reviews. They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing practical info to attendees. B's 'Communications Topic' is a research subject area under Topic (sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.). Different domains: document vs. topic taxonomy; no overlap.

A 'Conference contribution' is a broad category of submitted/accepted contributions (children include Invited talk, Poster, Presentation, Regular contribution, Written contribution) that are submitted at a conference volume. B 'Abstract' is a specific document type (a short summary document) with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and is presented as a paper. The intended instances do not coincide: an Abstract is one kind of contribution, but many contributions (e.g. posters, presentations) are not abstracts. Thus Conference contribution is more general than Abstract, so A subsumes B.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document type (the abstract-only submission, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper). Rated Papers in edas is a state of an Active Paper (a paper that has received ratings), not a document type. Their intended instances differ: an abstract submission is not a rated paper, and a rated paper need not be an abstract. Different paths, parents and siblings confirm distinct concepts.

edas:hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (a conference has a member person), while ekaw:partOf is a general mereological/participation relation with unspecified domain and range. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Co chair' is a specific committee role (sibling of Chair, a Person/Committee member who co-chairs a committee), while B 'Organizing Committee member' is a broader class covering all organizing committee roles (General Chair, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster). A co-chair is a kind of organizing committee member, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's has Location relates a Conference Event to a Place (venue/location), while B's holded by relates a Conference to the ACM SIGKDD organization (the organizing body). Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's given name), while B's 'has amount of' is a datatype property from Money to int (a monetary quantity). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they denote no common relation.

In ekaw, Possible Reviewer is a broad class of persons who could review (parent of PC Member, with properties reviewer Of Paper and review Written By), i.e. anyone capable of reviewing. In iasted, Reviewer is a narrow subclass of Speaker (a delegate who gives a talk and also reviews), so it is a specific kind of reviewer. The iasted Reviewer is thus a specialization of the ekaw Possible Reviewer, not an equivalent concept.

In ekaw, Presenter is a Conference Participant who presents at the conference, with Invited Speaker as a child; in iasted, Author is a Speaker who is a Delegate, with children like Lecturer, Plenary lecture speaker, Tutorial speaker. Both denote people who present/author conference content, but the intended instances do not coincide: an author of a paper need not present it, and a presenter need not be an author. They overlap (a presenting author is both) but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a research topic area (a subject category under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), while B is a kind of document (an abstract for an invited talk, under Abstract). They denote entirely different concepts: a topic vs. a document type, with no overlap in instances.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper/document authored). B's 'technically Organised By' is a subproperty of 'organised By' and relates an event/conference to the person or body that technically organises it. Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a kind of paper submitted to a conference), while B's Evaluated Paper is a paper that has been assigned and evaluated, with subclasses Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper. Every Evaluated Paper is a paper, but not every Paper is evaluated, so Paper is more general and is subsumed by Evaluated Paper.

A is a conference-document class (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic class (Mobile Computing Topic, sibling of Antennas, Cryptography, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's Conference is the whole conference event (has a name, has parts, proceedings, publisher, topics), while B's Conference Session is a session within a conference (a part of an academic event, linked to documents and persons). A session is a component of a conference, not the conference itself, so the two classes overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent; the relation is 'related'.

A's hasPhone is a datatype property linking a Person to a string phone number, while B's hasCall is an object property linking an Academic Event to a Call (call for papers). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; they share no concept.

Volunteer (confOf) is a Person subtype for helpers at a conference, while Attendee (edas) is a Person subtype for anyone attending. They overlap (a volunteer typically attends) but neither subsumes the other: volunteers are defined by a role of helping, attendees by presence, and edas has no volunteer-specific class. Thus related rather than equivalent.

A is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, a chair of the conference), while B is an administrative event (the registration-of-participants event, per its comment 'confTool'). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote a person versus an event, so they are not equivalent.

ekaw:Person is a general human agent (author, participant, reviewer, student) with properties linking to documents and events. sigkdd:Sponzor is a sponsoring organisation (gold/silver/bronze supporters, exhibitors) with a name and a search relation to ACM SIGKDD. A person is not a sponsor; the classes denote different concepts and have no overlap in instances.

attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event (a person attends an event), while partOfEvent relates an Event to an Event (mereological part-of between events). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

A's 'has a publisher' links a Conference proceedings to a Publisher (publication venue), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the talk given). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Poster Session' is a kind of scientific session/event where posters are presented, while a 'Program Committee' is a committee of people who review papers. They belong to different branches of the conference domain (event vs. committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's volumeContainsPaper relates a volume (proceedings) to the papers it contains, while B's give relates a Person to an Activity/Item they give (e.g. a presentation or talk). Different domain and range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties relate a person involved in the reviewing process to a Paper they are assigned to review. cmt's hasBeenAssigned has domain Reviewer and range Paper; edas's isReviewing has range Paper and a domain that includes Reviewer (plus other committee roles that also review). The intended relation — a reviewer being assigned/reviewing a paper — is the same, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent despite the broader domain in edas.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has Submission Instructions' is a datatype property of Call giving submission instructions text. Different domains (Person vs Call), different intended meanings, no overlap.

confOf's Conference is a working event (a type of event, sibling of Tutorial/Workshop), i.e. the conference as a whole. iasted's Conference activity is an Activity whose children are the individual sub-activities of a conference (lectures, coffee breaks, registration, welcome address), i.e. the conference programme/activity rather than the event itself. The two overlap in the conference domain but denote different concepts (event vs. activity/programme), so they are related, not equivalent.

edas:Organization is an agent-like entity (sponsor/provider of sponsorships, with subclasses Academia/Government/Industry/NGO), whereas iasted:Place is a physical location (building, room, city) that activities and persons are held in or present in. Their children, properties and domains/ranges do not overlap, so they denote different concepts.

A's 'adjusted By' links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it (domain Bid, range Reviewer), while B's 'has Updated Version' links a Document to a later version of that same Document (domain Document, range Document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of contribution (a submission type, sibling of Paper and Poster), while B 'Best Student Paper Award' is a kind of Award (a prize category). They denote different concepts: a submission type versus an award, so they are unrelated.

A's Deadline is a general time-point class with children for camera-ready, notification, hotel, registration and submission deadlines. B's Deadline Abstract Submission is a specific deadline (abstract submission) and is a child of B's own Deadline class. A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

In ekaw, PC Chair is a subclass of both Conference Participant and PC Member, i.e. the person who chairs the program committee. In sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is a subclass of Organizator, a broad category covering General Chair, Program Chair, Program Committee member and Webmaster. The two concepts overlap (a PC Chair is typically part of the organizing committee) but neither subsumes the other: sigkdd's Organizing Committee member includes roles such as Webmaster and General Chair that are not PC Chairs, and ekaw's PC Chair is a specific chairing role rather than a general committee membership. Hence they are related, not equivalent.

A's 'written By' links a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it (domain Review, range Reviewer). B's 'belongs to reviewers' links a Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer, i.e. it expresses which reviewer a review expertise/preference belongs to, not authorship of a review. The domains differ (Review vs Review expertise/Review preference) and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

Conference document is a class of documents (calls, contributions, reviews) with authors and issue dates, while City is a geographic location class with buildings and persons occupying/visiting it. Their children, properties and domains/ranges are entirely disjoint, so they denote different concepts.

A is a conference document type (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic in computer networks management under the Topic hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the act/phase of submitting contributions), while B 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a document item used at a session. They belong to different branches (Event vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact. B's 'Presentation' is a conference activity (subclass of Conference activity, sibling of Lecture, Welcome address, Coffee break), i.e. an event that takes place at the conference. A document and an activity denote different kinds of things, so the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Textual Review Question' is a kind of review question (a free-text question on a review form, sibling of Numerical Review Question), whereas B 'Final manuscript' is a submission document (the camera-ready version, sibling of Initial manuscript). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (review process vs. submission documents) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a whole-part/containment relation), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presenting a document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Committee is the general committee class with children Organizing committee, Program committee and Steering committee; B's Program Committee is one specific kind of committee (a child of B's Committee). A's Committee is therefore strictly more general than B's Program Committee, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

Both denote a conference document that has undergone review: cmt's Review is a Document with reviewers (written By) and a Program Committee Chair, and Conference's Reviewed contribution is a Submitted contribution that has a review and is reviewed. The paths (Document > Review vs Conference document > ... > Reviewed contribution) and properties (write/written By vs has a review/reviews) align in the same domain role, so they are equivalent.

A's Paper is a general contribution type (siblings Poster, Short paper) covering any paper submitted to a conference, while B's Rejected Paper is a specific subclass of Evaluated Paper denoting only papers that were rejected. A general paper is not the same concept as a rejected paper; the intended instance sets differ (a Paper may be accepted, rejected, or under review). Thus they are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a way a reference alignment would record (Paper is not a superclass of Rejected Paper in A's hierarchy, and Rejected Paper is not a subclass of A's Paper).

A Conference Trip is a social event (an organized excursion/activity within a conference), while B Taxi is a type of transport vehicle. They belong to different top-level categories (Event vs Item) and denote different concepts; a taxi may be used for transport during a trip, but the classes themselves are not equivalent.

A 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation given at a conference), while B 'Presenter university' is a building/place (the university building where a presenter is located). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (Event vs Place/Building) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Review preference to either a Submitted contribution or a Topic, while B's dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic. They overlap in that both can relate a contribution/submission to a topic, but A's domain (Review preference) and broader range (including Submitted contribution) differ from B's domain (Contribution) and single range (Topic), so they are not the same relation.

A is the class Paper (a document submitted to a conference, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B is a registration deadline (a time point in the Deadline hierarchy). They denote entirely different concepts: a document vs. a temporal deadline. No subsumption or overlap exists.

A is a person/role class (an active conference participant, a kind of Conference contributor who gives presentations), while B is a document class (an Active Paper, a kind of Paper that has a rating). They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated despite the shared word 'Active'.

Important dates is a class collecting all conference deadlines (abstract, full paper, camera-ready, acceptance, start/end), while confOf's Submission event is a specific administrative event for submitting contributions. They overlap in that submission deadlines are important dates, but Important dates is broader and includes non-submission dates, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a kind of conference paper (a document type), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (Document vs Item/Audiovisual equipment) and share no intended instances.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts. Different domain (Conference vs Conference volume), different range (Administrator vs Workshop), and different meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is prepared by' relates an Item (e.g. a paper/contribution) to a Person who prepared it, whereas B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document that is presented. The domains (Item vs Speaker) and ranges (Person vs Document) differ, and the directions/meanings are distinct: preparing an item is not the same relation as a speaker presenting a document. Hence they are not equivalent.
No candidate pair content was provided in the prompt; the single pair is empty, so no alignment relation can be asserted.

markConflictOfInterest relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to record a conflict of interest, whereas is_signed_by relates an Item to a Person as a generic authorship/signature relation. The domains, ranges and intended meanings differ; they are not the same relation.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (setting review criteria for a conference), while B's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (inviting co-reviewers). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

An Invited speaker is a conference contributor (a person who gives an invited talk), while a Webmaster is an organizing role responsible for the conference website. They belong to different branches (contributor vs. organizer) and denote different roles, so they are not equivalent.
A is a narrow research topic (optical networking) under Computer Networks Topic; B is an organizational committee (Program Committee) under Committee. Different domains entirely, no overlap.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname, while B's 'has Street' is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a street address. Different domains (Person vs Contact Information) and different intended values (surname vs street), so they are unrelated.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person (a human role in the conference), while Working event is a subclass of Event (a scheduled activity such as Conference, Tutorial, Workshop). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.
A relates a Review preference to a Topic/Submitted contribution (object property), while B relates a Call to a dateTime (datatype property). Different domain, range, and meaning; no alignment.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to its authors (Person), while B's 'is sent by' links an Item (e.g. a submission) to the Person who sent it. Both relate a document-like entity to a Person, but authorship and sending are different relations (a paper can be sent by someone who is not an author, and authors need not be the sender), so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'Accepted contribution' is a document/contribution that has passed review (a subclass of Reviewed contribution, sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B's 'Submission event' is an administrative event (the act/process of submitting contributions), sibling of Reviewing event and Camera Ready event. One is a document state, the other a process/event; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Both are the general class of conference documents: ekaw's Document has children Abstract, Paper, Review (plus Flyer, Programme Brochure, Web Site, Multi author Volume) and is written by a Person; sigkdd's Document has children Abstract, Paper, Review and is presented by a Speaker. The shared children and the same intended instances (papers, abstracts, reviews) make them the same concept, with sigkdd's being a slightly narrower but still equivalent-in-domain version.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a Conference contributor (a person invited to speak, sibling of Regular author), while B's 'Student non speaker' is a Delegate who is a Non speaker (a student attendee who does not present). They denote different concepts: an invited speaker is a speaker, whereas a student non speaker is explicitly a non-speaker; no subsumption or overlap holds.

cmt:Document is a general document/paper artefact whose children are Paper and Review, and it is the range of hasConflictOfInterest. ekaw:Organisation is an organising body (academic institution, organising agency, proceedings publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings. The two concepts share no instances and no meaning; they are unrelated.

A relates a Paper to a person who reviews it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), while B relates a Place to an Item it is equipped with. Different domain, range, and meaning; no overlap in the conference domain.

confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution (paper) to its Author, and iasted's 'is sent by' links an Item (submission) to a Person. Both express the authorship relation between a submitted work and its author, with matching direction (work -> person), so they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Banquet is a social event (a meal/celebration) in confOf, while Listener is a person role (attendee who listens) in sigkdd. They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Person) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Excursion is a social event (sibling of Reception) held during the conference, while B's Activity after conference is a post-conference activity with children Departure and Full day tour. They overlap in that a full-day tour/excursion can be a post-conference activity, but the concepts are not coextensive: B is broader (includes Departure) and temporally restricted to after the conference, whereas A is a social event type not tied to that time. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property with domain Conference and range int, counting the number of reviews per paper. B's 'has a name' is a datatype property with domain Conference/Conference part/Conference proceedings/Publisher/Topic and range string, giving a name. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they are unrelated.

A's `need` relates a Person to an Item (a person needs an item), while B's `search` relates the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (searching for sponsors). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'is equipped by' relates a Place to an Item (Place -> Item), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (Person -> Place). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the directions differ, so they denote different relations.

A 'Single Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference describing a conference with a single track/level, while B 'Presenter state' is a subclass of State describing a state of a presenter in a workflow. They share no meaning, no properties, and belong to different branches (Conference vs State).

A's 'Initial manuscipt' is a subclass of Submission (a document/artefact submitted to a conference), while B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a subclass of Deadline (a point in time by which papers must be submitted). One denotes a document, the other a temporal deadline; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Member PC' is a generic PC member (comment: Reviewer; reviews Contributions), while B's 'PC Chair' is a specific chair role that is a subclass of PC Member. A PC member is not the same concept as the PC chair; the chair is a distinct, more specific role. Thus the two classes are not equivalent.

A's `Credit card` is a payment card (Item > Card > Credit card), while B's `Speaker` is a person role (Person > Speaker) with presentation properties. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'end Review' relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the chair ends a review), while B's 'go through' relates an Item to an Activity (an item goes through an activity). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not the same relation.

A 'Committee member' is a person role in the conference organisation (a Person subclass with children Chair/Co chair and properties linking to Committee), while B 'Dining Place' is a physical location (a Place subclass alongside Accommodation/Conference Venue/Meeting Room). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A Conference volume is the whole conference event/volume with committees, tracks, parts and contributions; B Proceedings is a multi-author document (a publication) that is a part of a conference. They overlap in that a conference volume is published as proceedings, but the intended instances differ (event/organisational entity vs. document), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a record of reviews the reviewer wrote), while B's presentation links a Speaker to a Document (the talk material presented). Different domains (Reviewer vs Speaker), different ranges (Personal Review History vs Document), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

confOf's Social event is a subclass of Event (path Event > Social event, siblings Administrative event and Working event), while ekaw's Event is the general superclass with children Scientific Event and Social Event. The confOf class is strictly narrower than ekaw's Event, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

In cmt, 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while in iasted 'Author' is a subclass of Speaker, a role for delegates who present authored works. The iasted Author is a broader role that includes co-authors, so cmt's Co author is subsumed by iasted's Author, not equivalent.

A 'Poster Paper' is a kind of Paper (a scientific contribution presented as a poster), while B 'Mailing list' is a Document used for communication/administration. They share no intended instances and have different parents (Paper vs Document) and different sibling sets, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property for a person's family name, while B's 'has First Name' is for a person's given name (comment notes it involved the middle name). They denote different name parts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial) in confOf. B's 'Author book proceedings included' is a subclass of Author in iasted, i.e. an author role/type related to book proceedings, not an event at all. Different domains (event vs. author role), no shared meaning.

A's Abstract is a document type (a subclass of Document, with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and it is presented as a paper), whereas B's Deadline Abstract Submission is a submission deadline (a subclass of Deadline, sibling of Deadline Paper Submission and Deadline Author notification). One is a document, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (an authorship/contribution relation), while B's 'notification until' relates an Author to a notification deadline. Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

An Invited Speaker (a presenter who gives an invited talk) and a Reviewer (a delegate who reviews submissions) are distinct roles in the conference domain; they share no intended instances and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'author Of' is an object property linking a Person to a Document (the papers they wrote), while B's 'Name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their name). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and cannot be the same relation.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' is an Administrator action whose range is a Conference (the administrator enters review criteria for a conference), while B's 'reviewes' is a Member PC relation whose range is a Contribution (a PC member reviews a paper). Different domain (Administrator vs Member PC), different range (Conference vs Contribution), and different meaning (setting review criteria vs reviewing a paper), so they are not equivalent.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection, child of Decision) — the state/result of a paper being accepted.
