B's Receiving manuscript is an activity in the pre-conference phase (sibling of Accepting manuscript, Refusing manuscript), i.e. the act of a conference receiving a submitted manuscript. Different kinds (decision outcome vs. activity) and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

In edas, Workshop is a kind of Academic Event (a whole event), while in ekaw Session is a Scientific Event that has Workshop Session as a child, i.e. a session is a time slot within an event and a workshop session is a session type. The two concepts overlap in the conference domain (a workshop can be organised as sessions) but they are not the same: Workshop is an event type, Session is a scheduling unit. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'adjusted By' relates a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it (domain Bid, range Reviewer), while B's 'has Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (domain Paper, range Possible Reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

Both classes denote the conference paper artefact: confOf's Paper is a kind of Contribution (alongside Poster and Short paper), and sigkdd's Paper is a kind of Document (alongside Abstract and Review) that authors submit. Same intended instances, so they are equivalent.

A's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (submission act), while B's paper Presented As relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (presentation act). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A is a Person role (Program Committee Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Program Committee Member), while B is a Committee (an organizational body). A chair is a person who leads a committee, not the committee itself; the entities denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

Both denote the outcome/state of a paper/manuscript that has been rejected: edas models it as the class Rejected Paper (a subclass of Paper, sibling to Accepted Paper, Pending Paper, etc.), while iasted models the corresponding activity 'Refusing manuscript' (sibling to Accepting manuscript, Receiving manuscript) in the pre-conference phase. Despite the class-vs-activity modelling difference, the intended concept (a rejected submission) coincides, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property linking a conference web resource to a string URL, while B's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference www vs Event) and range (string vs Location), so they denote different relations.

A's `remark` is a datatype property attaching a string note to a Contribution (comment 'confTool'), while B's `obtain` is an object property relating a Person to an Item. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Contribution vs Person), and range (string vs Item), so they denote different relations.

A 'Coffee Break' is a scheduled break event in the conference programme (sibling of Meal Break and Free Time Break), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical place/venue (sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. location) and are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to the Reviewer assigned to review it (domain Paper, range Reviewer). B's 'reviews' links a Review to the Reviewed contribution it evaluates (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution). They relate different kinds of things in different directions (paper->reviewer vs review->paper), so they are not equivalent; at best they are inverses across different entity types, which the alignment does not record as equivalent.

A's title is the title of a Paper (a string naming the paper), while B's starts on is the start date/time of an Event. Different domains (Paper vs Event) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property mapping a Review preference to an int (a numeric degree of preference), while B's 'obtain' is an object property mapping a Person to an Item (acquiring something). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

In cmt, Document is a broad class whose children are Paper and Review, so a Document is any written contribution (paper or review). In edas, Paper is a specific subclass of Document (path Document > Paper) with subclasses Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc. Thus every edas Paper is a cmt Document, but not every cmt Document is an edas Paper (reviews are Documents too). Therefore cmt Document is broader and edas Paper is subsumed by it, not equivalent.
Organization (a group/institution in the conference domain) and Currency (a monetary unit) denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in meaning or context.

A's Submission is a document class (a paper/manuscript submitted to the conference, with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript), whereas B's Deadline Paper Submission is a deadline (a point in time) for submitting papers, sibling of Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Author notification. Different kinds of entities (document vs. temporal deadline), so they are not equivalent.
A relates a Program Committee to its members; B relates a Speaker to a Document (presentation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings.

A is a conference topic area (Operating Systems) under Topic, while B is a research activity (Modelling) under Activity before conference > Research. Different domains (topic vs. activity) and no shared meaning.

PC Chair (ekaw) is a Conference Participant who chairs the program committee, a subrole of PC Member; Webmaster (sigkdd) is an Organizator responsible for the website, sibling of General Chair and Program Chair. Different roles in the conference organisation with no overlap in intended instances.

A 'Coffee break' is a social/refreshment activity in the conference programme (sibling of Coctail reception, Welcome address, etc.), whereas B 'Main office' is a physical place (sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They denote different kinds of entities (activity vs. location) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is paid for' has domain Money and range Activity/Item, meaning money is paid for an activity or item. B's 'pay' has domain Person and range Registration fee, meaning a person pays a registration fee. The domains and ranges are disjoint (Money vs Person, Activity/Item vs Registration fee), so the properties relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not equivalent.

A's 'Short paper' is a specific contribution type (sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution), while B's 'Submitted Paper' is a stage-of-lifecycle class (a Paper that has been submitted, parent of Assigned Paper, sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, etc.). They overlap in that a short paper is typically submitted, but neither subsumes the other: a submitted paper need not be short, and a short paper need not be in the submitted state. Hence related, not equivalent.

In confOf, Poster is a subclass of Contribution (a kind of submitted document, sibling of Paper and Short paper). In edas, Paper Presentation is a subclass of Academic Event (a scheduled event at the conference, sibling of Talk Event and Workshop), and it is linked to Accepted Paper via related To Paper. One denotes a document type, the other a presentation event, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Camera ready contribution' is a contribution that has been accepted and finalized for publication, i.e. the version of a paper that is actually published. B 'Published Paper' is a paper that has been published. Both denote the final, published version of an accepted paper, so their intended instances coincide. The path in A (Accepted contribution > Camera ready contribution) and B (Paper > Published Paper) both capture the post-acceptance, published state, making them equivalent in the conference domain.

confOf's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (author writes paper), while ekaw's reviewOfPaper relates a Review to a Paper (review is of a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while B's payed_by relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's Paper is a conference document (subclass of Document, with children like Conference Paper, Review, topics), while B's Credit card is a payment card (subclass of Card under Item). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

Both properties express the end of a temporal entity: confOf's 'ends on' gives the end date of an Event, while iasted's 'done till' gives the end date of a Deadline. They relate different kinds of things (Event vs Deadline) and have different ranges (string vs date), so they are not equivalent, but they are conceptually related as end-time properties.

A's `name` is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's `has Fax` is specifically a fax number for a Person. Different intended relations (name vs. fax number), so they are not equivalent.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings), while B's `presentation` relates a Speaker to a Document they present (domain Speaker, range Document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Associated Chair is a conference-organisation role (a chair/member of the organising committee, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), whereas One day presenter is a type of Delegate/attendee who presents for one day. They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (a sibling of Call for paper, Conference contribution, Review) — a textual artefact addressed to attendees. B's 'Camera Ready event' is an administrative event in the event hierarchy (sibling of Submission event, Reviewing event, Registration of participants event) — a process/activity, not a document. Different kinds (document vs. event) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a type of conference session (an event where industrial talks/presentations occur), while B is a physical place (a hall/venue where a conference is held). They belong to different branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country (the country an organization/person is located in). B's is_held_in relates an Activity (event) to a Place or Time (where/when the event is held). Different domains (Organization/Person vs Activity) and different ranges (Country vs Place/Time), and different intended meaning (affiliation/location vs event venue/time). They are not the same relation.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property of Person giving a person's first name (string), while B's done_till is a datatype property of Deadline giving a date by which something must be done. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person (domain) to an Organization (range), i.e. a person's employer. iasted's is_occupied_by relates a Building/City/State (domain) to a Person (range), i.e. the occupant of a place. The kinds of things related and the direction differ, so they are not equivalent (they are not even inverses, since the domain/range classes differ).

A's contact Email is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string (an email address), while B's has Submission Deadline links a Call to a dateTime (a deadline). They relate different kinds of things in different domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Banquet is a formal social event (sibling of Conference Trip under Social Event), while B Coffee break is a small refreshment activity under Conference activity, alongside Coctail reception, Lecture, etc. They denote different kinds of conference activities/events and are not equivalent.

A's 'Worker non speaker' is a delegate who is explicitly a non-speaker (sibling of Student non speaker, under Non speaker), while B's 'Speaker' is a person who gives a presentation. They are complementary/opposite roles, not the same concept.

A's Subject Area is a topic classification of papers (domain of 'has Subject Area' is Paper), while B's Building is a physical place (subclass of Place, occupied by persons, situated in cities). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's User is a Person subtype (a human role: Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Working event is an Event subtype (Conference/Tutorial/Workshop). Different roots (Person vs Event) and incompatible instances, so they are unrelated.

A's hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword; B's has_amount_of links Money to an int amount. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

Withdrawn Paper and Rejected Paper are both non-accepted papers but denote different concepts: a withdrawn paper is removed by the author before/without a rejection decision, while a rejected paper has been evaluated and rejected. They overlap in being unsuccessful papers but are not equivalent; the sibling sets (Accepted/Active/Pending/Published/Rejected vs Accepted) and the ekaw path through Evaluated Paper confirm distinct intended meanings.

A is a subject-area topic class (a research topic in computer networks/applications) under the Topic hierarchy, while B is a kind of scientific event (a contributed talk, i.e. an individual presentation) under Event > Scientific Event > Individual Presentation. They denote entirely different concepts (topic vs. event type) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Reviewed contribution' is a Submitted contribution that has undergone review, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution. B's 'Paper' is a broader Document subtype covering all papers regardless of review state (children include Accepted, Active, Pending, Published, Rejected, Withdrawn Paper). A reviewed contribution is a kind of paper, but Paper is not restricted to reviewed ones, so A is strictly narrower than B.

A's hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to a string URL (homepage), while B's authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document. They relate different kinds of things (string vs Document) and denote different relations, so they are unrelated.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection) in the decision process, while B's Accept Rating is a review rating value (sibling of Reject Rating, Accept If Room Rating, etc.) used to score a paper. They are related in that a positive rating often leads to acceptance, but they denote different concepts: a decision vs. a rating category.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (author), while B's 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item (acquisition). The domains and ranges are reversed and the intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (a person giving a talk), while B's 'is equipped by' links a Place to an Item (equipment). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person who finalizes paper assignments), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'is present in' is an object property mapping a Person to a Place/Time (attendance at an event). They share only the Person domain; their ranges and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an Administrator action on a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's `date` is a generic datatype property on Conference (any conference date), while B's `is a full paper submission date` is a specific deadline property on Important dates. They overlap in that both relate a conference/event to a date, but B is a narrower, specific deadline whereas A is a general date property, so they are related rather than equivalent.

hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country, while is_present relates a Person to a Time. They have different domains (Organization/Person vs Person) and different ranges (Country vs Time), and denote different relations in the conference domain.

In iasted, Document is a broad Item covering forms, invitations, reviews, submissions, etc. In sigkdd, Paper is a specific Document (a submission/contribution) with siblings Abstract and Review and is the range of submit. Paper is thus a narrower concept than iasted's Document, so iasted Document subsumes sigkdd Paper rather than being equivalent.

A 'Conference contribution' is a document submitted to a conference (parent Conference document, children Poster/Presentation/Written contribution, related to Conference volume via submission), whereas B 'Award' is a prize given to authors (children Best Paper Awards, obtained by Author). They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A's Research is a conference activity (a kind of 'Activity before conference', sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript), whereas B's Author is a person role (Person > Speaker > Author) who submits papers and obtains awards. The two denote different kinds of things (activity vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while iasted's is_paid_with relates Money to an Item (payment). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (a person's reviewing competence), while B's 'references' is a general bibliographic relation between documents/papers. Different domain and range, different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Week Reject Rating' is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a rating value used in the review process (siblings: Accept Rating, Reject Rating). B's 'Abstract' is a subclass of Document, i.e. a textual part of a paper (siblings: Paper, Review). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property linking a Conference document to a date (publication/issue date). B's 'topic Covered By' is an object property linking a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (the event/paper covers the topic). They differ in domain, range, kind (datatype vs object) and meaning, so they are unrelated.

Money in iasted is a monetary amount class (children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip; properties like has amount of, is paid by, is paid for), whereas ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd is an organisation/society that designs deadlines, holds conferences and searches for sponsors. They share no intended instances and no meaningful relation.

Conference contributor is a Person who contributes to a conference (authors, speakers, participants), while Delegate in iasted is a Person involved in a conference building/registration context with children like Speaker, Session chair, Listener. Both denote people involved in a conference, but the iasted Delegate is a more specific role tied to registration/attendance, and Conference contributor is broader (includes authors, invited speakers). They overlap but are not equivalent.

Presenter (ekaw) is a Conference Participant who presents a paper, with child Invited Speaker; Session chair (iasted) is a Delegate role that chairs a session. Different roles in the conference domain, not synonyms.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in cmt), while B is an event type (Workshop Session, a subclass of Session in ekaw). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `references` is a generic bibliographic citation relation between documents/papers (unspecified domain/range), while B's `presentation` relates a Speaker to a Document (the talk a speaker gives). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property holding a person's surname, while B's 'has Phone' holds a telephone number. Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they relate persons to entirely different kinds of data (name vs. phone number), so they are not the same relation.

Rejection is a subclass of Decision (the outcome of a review decision, sibling of Acceptance) in cmt, while Company is a subclass of Organization (an organisational affiliation, sibling of University) in confOf. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

A's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to the Conference Event it belongs to (domain Programme, range Conference Event), i.e. a programme is part of an event. B's 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise (domain Organisation/Person, range Event). The subjects differ (Programme vs Organisation/Person) and the meanings differ (membership/part-of vs organising), so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person denoting people who contribute to a conference (authors, speakers, participants). B's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and oddly also Person/TPC Member) denoting a conference with a two-level structure, contrasted with 'Single Level Conference'. The entities denote different kinds of things (a person role vs. a conference type), so they are unrelated.

confOf Participant is a general person role (parent of Member, Regular, Student; sibling of Author, Chair PC, etc.) covering anyone taking part in the conference, whereas ekaw OC Member is a specific organising-committee member (parent of OC Chair, sibling of PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.). OC Member is a narrower role not equivalent to the broad Participant class; the two are not the same concept.

In the Conference ontology, Extended abstract is a specific kind of Regular contribution (a short/early version of a paper), while ekaw's Paper is the general document class covering all paper types (regular, demo, poster, workshop, etc.). Extended abstract is therefore narrower than Paper, not equivalent; the correct relation is subsumed_by.

A's 'organised By' relates an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it (domain Event, range Organisation/Person). B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity/Item they give (domain Person, range Activity/Item). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the directions differ, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Call For Reviews' is a call/announcement (a subclass of Call, sibling of Call For Papers/Manuscripts) soliciting reviewers, whereas B's 'Review' is a document artefact (subclass of Document, sibling of Submission, Form, etc.). One is an event/announcement, the other a document; they do not denote the same concept.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of conference Contribution (a submission/paper type, sibling of Paper and Poster), while B 'Mailing list' is a Document item (an administrative artefact, sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'writtenBy' is an object property mapping a Document to a Person (authorship). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Document), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a written conference contribution (a document, sibling of Extended abstract, with an abstract). B's Paper Presentation is an academic event (a session in which an accepted paper is presented), sibling of Talk Event and Workshop. The two denote different kinds of things (document vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the outcome/acceptance decision for a paper), while B's is_held_before relates an Activity to a Time (a temporal ordering between events). They share neither domain/range nor meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a scientific event (a kind of conference event), while B's Modelling is a research activity performed before a conference. They denote different concepts in different branches of the domain (event vs. activity), so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, and their labels ('has the first name' / 'has First Name') denote the same attribute of a person's given name in the conference domain.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) in confOf, while B's Excursion is a distinct social event in edas whose sibling is Reception. The two ontologies both distinguish Reception and Excursion as separate social events, so the classes denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A 'Paid applicant' is a subclass of person (a registrant who has paid), while B 'Registration fee' is a subclass of Fee (a monetary charge). They belong to different branches (Person vs Fee) and cannot denote the same concept; the only connection is that a paid applicant pays a registration fee, which is an association, not equivalence.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (a conference with two levels/tiers, sibling of Single Level Conference under Conference), while B 'One day presenter' is a kind of Delegate (a person who presents for one day). They denote different concepts (event type vs. person role) and share no meaningful context.

A's hasTopic relates a Working event to a Topic (the subject matter of a conference event), while B's go_through relates an Item to an Activity (an item participating in / undergoing an activity). Different domain, range and intended meaning; the shared notion of 'topic' vs 'activity' does not align.

A 'Break Event' is a non-academic conference event (a break such as a coffee break, meal break or free time), while B 'Speaker' is a person role in the conference (a person who gives a presentation). They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a Person subtype (a conference attendee who does not present), while B 'Workshop' is an Event subtype (a working event). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper in a specific publication state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Pending Paper under Paper), whereas B 'Book proceeding' is a publication artefact (a proceedings volume) under Publication, sibling of 'Cd proceeding'. They denote different kinds of entities (a paper vs. a proceedings book), so they are not equivalent.

Chairman in cmt is a generic person role that subsumes specific chair roles (Conference Chair, PC Chair, Associated Chair) and is a sibling of Program Committee Member; PC Member in ekaw is a member of the program committee, a role distinct from chairing, though both are conference-committee roles. They overlap in the committee domain but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.
A's paper ID is an identifier (unsignedLong) of a Paper, while B's abstract is a textual summary (string) of a Contribution. Different kinds of information, different ranges, no overlap in meaning.

A's Conference Member is a Person subtype (a person involved in a conference: chairs, authors, reviewers, PC members), while B's Workshop is a Conference part (an event/activity within a conference, sibling of Track and Tutorial). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

A's coversTopic relates an Event/Paper to a Research Topic (subject matter), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Session Chair' is a Person role (a person who chairs a session), while B's 'Session' is an Event (a scientific event with children like Conference Session, Poster Session). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a speaker who gives a plenary (full-session) lecture, while B 'Invited Speaker' is a speaker invited by the organisers; both are speaker roles under Speaker/Author, but plenary and invited are distinct kinds of talks, so they overlap without being equivalent.

A's 'Conference www' is a document (a web page about the conference, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with a URL property), while B's 'Main office' is a physical place (sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B 'Presenter state' is a state of a presenter in the iasted ontology. They belong to different branches (Person vs State) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' is an object property linking a Review to its Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), while B's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property on Review expertise with an unspecified range. They relate different kinds of things (reviewer individual vs. expertise value) and are not the same relation.

A's Poster is a kind of Contribution (a paper/poster submission in the conference), while B's Exhibitor is a kind of Sponzor (a sponsoring organisation that exhibits). They belong to entirely different branches (Contribution vs Sponzor) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to a Conference proceedings (publishing relation), while B's `coversTopic` relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (subject/topic relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has short title' is a datatype property mapping events to a string abbreviation, while B's 'go through' is an object property mapping items to activities. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (the schedule of the event), while B's presentationed_by links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domains (Conference Event vs Document), different ranges (Programme vs Speaker), and different intended relations; they are not the same property.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference domain (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Academic Institution (ekaw) is an Organisation subtype (parent of University/Research Institute) that organises events. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs organisation) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Regular Session' is a specific kind of session (sibling of Conference/Demo/Poster/Workshop Session) under ekaw's Session. B's 'Session' is a broader lecture-type activity in iasted, with children like Speaker lecture and siblings Plenary lecture and Tutorial. A Regular Session is a narrower concept than the general iasted Session, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's Meal Menu is a document describing the menu of a meal event (has Menu / is Menu Of link it to Meal Event), while B's Review is a document containing a reviewer's evaluation of a paper (has Review / review Of Paper / review Written By). They share only the parent Document and are semantically distinct concepts.

A Program Committee Chair is a specific role (a chair of the PC, also a PC member) in cmt, while confOf's Member PC is the general class of PC members (comment 'Reviewer', parent Person, with reviewes property). Every PC chair is a PC member, but not every PC member is a chair, so A is strictly narrower than B.

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (a whole-part containment relation). B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (an agent relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Steering committee is a distinct committee type (sibling of Organizing committee and Program committee in Conference), while B's Organizing Committee is the organizing committee itself. They are different committee roles, not synonyms.

Program Committee is a group/organisational body whose members are Program Committee Members, whereas Person is a general human agent class (with subclasses Delegate and Sponsor). A committee is not a person; the two classes have disjoint intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type: conference paper), while B is a subclass of Time representing the days of a conference. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Personal Publication History' is a class under Personal History representing a person's record/history of publications (sibling of Personal Review History), whereas B 'Cd proceening' is a subclass of Publication representing a CD proceedings publication artefact (sibling of Book proceeding). They denote different concepts: a personal history record vs. a type of published proceedings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a specific role (the first author of a contribution), a subclass of 'Regular author' in the Conference ontology. B's 'Author' is the general class of persons who write papers, with subclasses like Presenter and properties linking to Paper. The first-author role is strictly narrower than the general Author class, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's co-writePaper relates a Co author (a person acting as co-author) to a Paper, while B's write relates a Person to an Item. Both express authorship/writing of a document by a person, so they overlap, but the domain and range differ (Co author vs Person, Paper vs Item) and co-writePaper is specifically the co-authorship relation, not the general writing relation. They are related rather than equivalent.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with children like Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author), whereas Social Event is a subclass of Event (a social gathering such as Conference Banquet or Conference Trip). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's Fee is a general money category (parent Money, children include Registration fee, Hotel fee, Fee for extra trip), while B's Sponzor fee is a specific kind of fee (parent Fee, sibling Registration fee). Thus A is broader and subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Event' is an event/activity class (children Academic Event, Non Academic Event; has start/end date, location, programme, attendees), whereas B's 'Conference Participant' is a subclass of Person denoting a person role (children Demo Chair, PC Chair, Presenter, etc.). An event and a person are disjoint concepts, so the two are unrelated.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a type of conference lecture/activity; they belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Activity) and share no intended instances.

A's hasUpdatedVersion relates a Document to another Document (a revised version of the same document), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the person who presented it). Different domain/range semantics and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Video cassette player' is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a device) under Item > Audiovisual equipment, while B 'Listener' is a person role under Person. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (device vs. person) and share no meaning in the conference domain.

Both are social events that are outings/trips during a conference: edas Excursion and ekaw Conference Trip are siblings of Reception/Conference Banquet under Social Event, denoting the same kind of non-academic social activity.

In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person who presents a paper). In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker, a role of a Delegate, and is broader than Presenter: it covers all authors, not only those who present. Presenter is thus strictly more specific than Author, so Presenter is subsumed by Author, not equivalent.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a physical venue/location (a subtype of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place), whereas B 'Registration form' is a document/form (subtype of Form, sibling of Author information form and Hotel registration form). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (location vs. document) and share no intended instances.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a conference submission that has undergone review (a document/contribution in the submission workflow, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution and a has-a-review relation to Review). B 'Review Question' is a question on a review form (with children Numerical/Textual Review Question), a component of the reviewing instrument, not a contribution. Different intended instances and different roles in the domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Invited Talk' is a kind of Individual Presentation (a talk given at a scientific event), while B's 'Tutorial' is a kind of Lecture (a conference activity). Although ekaw also has a Tutorial class, the candidate pairs ekaw's Invited Talk with iasted's Tutorial; these denote different concepts (an invited presentation vs. a tutorial lecture), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Review preference' is a class in the Conference ontology representing a reviewer's preference/degree of interest in reviewing a topic or submission (it has a degree, belongs to reviewers, and links to topics/submissions). B 'ACM SIGKDD' is the ACM Special Interest Group on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, an organisation that designs deadlines, holds conferences and searches for sponsors. The two denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A is a person role (a presenter who is invited), while B is a conference activity (the act of introducing a speaker). They belong to different top-level categories (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A is a research topic class (a subject area under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a document type (an abstract of an invited talk under Document > Abstract). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action of entering conference details), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (an author writing a paper/item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about a conference, with a URL), while B 'Computer Networks Measurements Topic' is a research topic in a topic hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a short introductory document used by a session chair, a sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc. B's 'Paper' is the scientific contribution submitted by an author (submit: Author -> Paper), sibling of Abstract and Review. They denote different artefacts in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

Both denote the final version of an accepted paper prepared for publication: A is the terminal stage of an accepted contribution (Accepted contribution > Camera ready contribution), B is a Paper subtype (Paper > Camera Ready Paper). Same intended instances in the conference domain.

A's Research Topic is a subject area that events and papers cover (domain of 'covers Topic' with range Event/Paper). B's Time is a temporal entity with children Deadline, Conference days, Trip day and is used as range of temporal relations (is held before/after, is present in). The two denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property of Social event / Working event giving the title of an event, while B's 'Name of conference' is a datatype property of Conference giving the name of the conference. Different domains (events vs. conference) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Banquet is a specific social event (a meal), while iasted's Social program is the broader category of social activities and has Dinner banquet as a child. Thus Banquet is subsumed by Social program, not equivalent.

Both properties link a programme (or programme brochure/web site) to the event it describes: edas 'belongs To Event' has domain Programme and range Conference Event, while ekaw 'lists Event' has domain Programme Brochure/Web Site and range Event. The intended relation is the same (a programme belongs to / lists the event), with the domain difference reflecting only the broader notion of programme in ekaw.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property of a Conference document (a paper/contribution) giving its issue/publication date, while B's 'has End Date Time' is a datatype property of a Conference Event giving when the event ends. Different domains (document vs event) and different intended meanings (issue date vs end time), so they are not the same relation.

Both properties express where an event/activity takes place, but they are not equivalent: confOf's `location` is a datatype property with range string (a textual location), while iasted's `is held in` is an object property with range Place, Time (a structured place/time entity). They overlap in meaning but differ in kind and range, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper's rating), while B's is_held_after relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

Both denote a presentation given at a conference that is not an invited talk: A's Presentation is a Conference contribution with child Invited talk and is given by an active conference participant; B's Contributed Talk is an Individual Presentation sibling of Invited Talk. The intended instances (contributed/oral presentations) coincide, so they are equivalent.

confOf's Science Worker is a generic Person subtype (sibling of Author, Participant, Chair PC, etc.), while sigkdd's Program Chair is a specific organizer role under Organizator. A Science Worker is not a Program Chair; the concepts denote different things and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'is visited by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a place is visited by a person), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (a person can stay in a place). They are inverses in direction and describe different relations (visiting vs. staying), so they are not equivalent.

A's Track is a conference part (a thematic session track, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, with has tracks from Conference volume), while B's Van is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi). The shared word 'van'/'track' is coincidental; the concepts are in completely different domains and denote different things.

A's `related To Event` links an Accepted Paper to the Paper Presentation it is associated with (domain Accepted Paper, range Paper Presentation). B's `presentation` links a Speaker to a Document (domain Speaker, range Document). The domains, ranges and intended meanings differ: one relates a paper to its presentation event, the other relates a person to a document. They are not the same relation.

Preference in cmt denotes a reviewer's preference/interest in a paper (a value/attribute concept), while Person in sigkdd denotes a human participant with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker and properties E mail, Name, Nation, can stay in, pay. The two classes have different intended instances and no subsumption relation; they are unrelated.

Accommodation Place is a specific kind of Place (a place where one can stay), while sigkdd's Place is the general superclass with children Conference hall, Hotel, Main office and property 'can stay in'. Accommodation Place is therefore strictly more specific, i.e. subsumed by Place, not equivalent.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference www to a string URL, while B's 'hasEvent' is an object property linking an Event to another Event (e.g. sub-events). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference www vs Event), and range (string vs Event), so they denote different relations.

Author (cmt) is a person role who writes/submits papers, a subclass of Conference Member/User. Academic Event (edas) is an event such as a workshop or talk, a subclass of Conference Event. They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to the Organization that employs them, while sigkdd's can_stay_in relates a Person to a Place where they can stay (e.g. a hotel). The ranges (Organization vs Place) and intended meanings differ, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's hasReview relates a Paper to a Review (the evaluation of the paper), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

cmt:Preference is a class whose instances are the preference values a reviewer/committee member expresses (e.g. accept/reject/neutral preferences), while edas:ReviewRating is a class whose instances are the ratings attached to a review (with subclasses Accept Rating, Reject Rating, etc.). Both concern the accept/reject judgement dimension of reviewing, so they overlap conceptually, but they are not the same class: Preference is the expressed preference of a person, ReviewRating is the rating value of a review, and the EDAS class is the range of has Rating (Active Paper -> Review Rating), not a preference entity. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's start Date is a datatype property giving the start date/time of a Conference (domain Conference, range dateTime). B's is dated on is a datatype property giving the date of an Activity (domain Activity, range dateTime). Both relate an event-like entity to a dateTime, so they overlap, but A is specifically the start of a conference while B is a general dating relation for any activity; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial/workshop), while B's 'Author book proceedings included' is a subclass of Author describing an author whose book is included in the proceedings. They denote entirely different concepts (event vs. author role), so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a document type) with an abstract; B's Rated Papers is a subclass of Active Paper, i.e. papers that have received ratings. Every Rated Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is rated, so Paper is more general and subsumes Rated Papers (A is subsumed_by B's class in the sense that B is narrower). The two are not equivalent.

A's publisherOf relates an Organisation to documents it publishes (Flyer, Volume, Brochure, Web Site); B's obtain relates an Author to an Award they receive. Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'presentation Of Paper' links an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper it presents (domain Individual Presentation, range Abstract/Paper). B's 'write' links a Person to an Item they authored (domain Person, range Item). Different domains, ranges and intended relations (presenting vs. authoring), so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference topic (a subject area under Computer Networks Topic in edas), while B is a document type (an abstract for an invited talk under Abstract in ekaw). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic taxonomy vs. document type) and share no intended instances.

A is a conference document about information for participants (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a sponsorship level (Gold Supporter) under Sponzor. Different domains within the conference ontology; no overlap.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference domain), while B's Best Research Paper Award is a subclass of Award (an award category). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.
A's email is a datatype property linking a Person to a string address; B's has amount of links Money to an int quantity. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class covering all people affiliated with the conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), while Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a narrower role for people who may review papers, with PC Member as its only child. Every Possible Reviewer is a conference member, but not vice versa, so Conference Member is more general.

A's Demo Session is a specific kind of Session (a session type within a scientific event), while B's Session is the general session concept under Lecture. Demo Session is strictly narrower than Session, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's `remark` is a datatype property of Contribution (a free-text note about a paper), while B's `Nation` is a datatype property of Person (a person's country). Different domains, different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings with range int, recording a volume number. B's 'has Title' is a datatype property of Contribution with range string, recording a title. Different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings (volume number vs. title), so they are not equivalent.

A's Chair is a committee member who chairs a committee (domain Committee, range Chair, with inverse was a committee chair of). B's Session chair is a Delegate who chairs a session, a role under Delegate alongside Speaker, Listener, etc. Both denote a chairing role, but A is specifically a committee chair while B is a session chair; the intended instances overlap but do not coincide, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome for a paper). B's expertOn relates a PC member to a Topic (the subject area they are competent in). Different domains (Paper vs Member PC), different ranges (Decision vs Topic), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A Track is a thematic stream of the conference (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, part of a Conference volume), while B Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Taxi, Van). Different domains and no shared context, so they are unrelated.

Item in iasted is a very general class covering equipment, cards, documents, publications, vehicles, etc., with properties about being given, paid for, made from, etc. Award in sigkdd is a specific recognition given to papers/authors, with children like Best Research Paper Award and properties award/awarded by/obtain. The two concepts do not coincide: an Award is not a general Item, and Item is far broader than Award. No subsumption or overlap in the intended domain.

A's title is the title of a Paper (domain Paper, range string), while B's has Phone is a phone number of Contact Information (domain Contact Information, range string). Different domains and different intended relations; sharing the datatype string does not make them equivalent.

A's Person is a human agent in the conference domain (authors, reviewers, participants), while B's State is a geographical/administrative region (a place occupied by or visited by persons, situated in other places). Their instances and roles are disjoint, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B 'Technic activity' is a kind of conference activity/event (sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break) in the iasted ontology. A person role and an event/activity are fundamentally different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference Member in cmt is a person role (a member of a conference, with subclasses Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while Sponzor in sigkdd is a sponsoring organisation (with subclasses Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor) that sponsors ACM SIGKDD. Different kinds of entities, no overlap.

A's read Paper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewing/reading a submission), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (authoring a contribution). They are different relations with different domains and ranges, and are not inverses either.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass whose children include Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author, and whose siblings include Committee member and Reviewer; it covers anyone contributing to a conference. B's 'Program Committee member' is a specific Organizator role (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster) denoting only PC members. The two overlap (PC members are conference contributors) but neither subsumes the other: A is broader than B, yet B sits under Organizator, not under A's hierarchy, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in cmt), while B 'Conference' is the event itself (with children Single Level Conference, Two Level Conference and properties like paper Due On, has Country). A person role and an event are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's email is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (the person's email address). B's is sent by is an object property linking an Item to a Person (the sender of the item). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property of Review preference with range int (a reviewer's degree/qualification level), while B's 'Nation' is a datatype property of Person with range string (a person's nationality). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Conference Chair is a person role in the conference organisation (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while Research Institute is an academic organisation (a subclass of Academic Institution). They belong to different branches of the domain (person vs organisation) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Talk Event is a kind of academic event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), whereas B's Activity before conference is a pre-conference activity such as accepting/receiving/refusing manuscripts or renting. They share no instances: one is a scheduled talk event, the other is preparatory activity, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has gender' is a datatype property from Person to a literal gender value, while B's 'is used by' is an object property from Item to Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (literal vs Person), and direction/meaning, so they cannot denote the same relation.

A's topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to the Event/Paper that covers it, while B's design relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline; different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Program Committee' is a group of people (committee members) that reviews papers, with properties linking it to Program Committee Members. B's 'Programme' is a Document (sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set) that belongs to a Conference Event, i.e. the conference schedule/program booklet. They denote different concepts despite the similar word 'program'.

In edas, Author is a subclass of Person whose instances write papers (has Related Paper / is Written By). In sigkdd, Speaker is a subclass of Person whose instances give presentations (presentation / presentationed by), and Author is a child of Speaker, i.e. an author is a kind of speaker. The two classes do not denote the same concept: an author need not be a speaker, and a speaker need not be an author. Since edas Author is more specific than sigkdd Speaker (sigkdd explicitly places Author under Speaker), the correct relation is subsumed_by.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property of Conference www pointing to a string URL, while B's 'has Email' is a datatype property of Contact Information/Person pointing to an email string. They relate different kinds of things (a conference website URL vs. a person's email address) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's Member is a subclass of Participant (a person role: regular/student member attending the conference), while B's Registration SIGMOD Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for SIGMOD members). One denotes a person role, the other a fee type; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a specific organizational role under Chairman/Conference Member, while Attendee (edas) is a general participant role under Person. They denote different concepts: a conference chair is not necessarily an attendee in the same sense, and the ontologies place them in different role hierarchies.

A's 'Science Worker' is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference, sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.), while B's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a kind of conference event, sibling of Single Level Conference). They denote different concepts (a person vs. a conference type) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), while B's Sponzorship is a money/funding concept (sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip under Money). Different domains and no shared meaning.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a specific kind of regular contribution (a short/abstract-length submission), while B's 'Conference Paper' is the general class of papers presented at a conference, with siblings like Regular Paper, Poster Paper, Demo Paper. The two overlap in that an extended abstract is a conference contribution, but they are not the same concept: 'Conference Paper' is broader and includes full papers, whereas 'Extended abstract' denotes a shorter abstract-type contribution. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of 'Conference participant' (a person who attends without an active role such as presenting or chairing). B's 'Conference Participant' is the broader parent class covering all participants, including active roles (Presenter, Session Chair, etc.). Thus A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A Reception is a social event (evening gathering) in confOf, sibling of Banquet and Trip. B Full day tour is an activity after the conference in iasted, sibling of Departure. Different kinds of event/activity with no overlap in intended instances.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving a string name for a Conference or Person; B's `writtenBy` is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

Sponsorship in edas is a specific funding arrangement (has cost amount/currency, provided by an Organization, provides travel grants), while Money in iasted is a broad monetary-resource class with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip and general payment properties. Sponsorship is a kind of Money (its iasted child Sponzorship is the direct counterpart), so the edas class is strictly narrower than the iasted class: subsumed_by, not equivalent.

A's 'Proceedings Publisher' is an Organisation (a company/institution that publishes proceedings), while B's 'Organizing Committee member' is a Person role within the Organizator branch. They denote different kinds of entities (organisation vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a conference activity (Coctail reception, a social event). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Activity) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on a Conference indicating whether paper copies are accepted; B's 'has Submission Instructions' is a string on a Call giving textual submission instructions. Different domains (Conference vs Call), different ranges (boolean vs string), and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Submission event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the act/occasion of submitting contributions), while B's 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a specific deadline date for abstract submission. They are related (both concern the submission phase) but not the same concept: one is an event, the other a deadline.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial/workshop), while B's Student lecturer is a person role (a kind of lecturer/speaker/author/delegate). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A is an object property linking a conference part to a conference volume (part-whole relation between documents/volumes), while B is a datatype property giving the end date/time of a conference. They relate entirely different kinds of entities (Conference part -> Conference volume vs Conference -> dateTime) and have no shared meaning, so they are unrelated.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a role played by people who contribute to a conference), while Scientific Event is a subclass of Event (an occurrence such as a conference, session, or workshop). Their instances are disjoint kinds of things (people vs. events), so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Person is the general person class (parent of Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User), while confOf:Participant is a subclass of confOf:Person restricted to people attending/participating in the conference (children Member, Regular, Student; siblings Author, Chair PC, etc.). Participant is a narrower concept than Person, so cmt:Person subsumes confOf:Participant; they are not equivalent.

confOf's Administrative event is a broad category of organisational events (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration, reviewing results) that are part of the conference process. iasted's Registration is a specific conference activity (with Delegate as a child), i.e. the act of registering delegates. Registration is one kind of administrative event, so Administrative event is more general: Registration is subsumed by Administrative event. They are not equivalent because Administrative event also covers submission, reviewing, camera-ready etc., which are not Registration.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document (a short summary of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B 'Best Student Paper Supporter' is a sponsorship role/level (sibling of Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter under Sponzor). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's 'Conference Trip' is a social event (a planned excursion/activity) under Event > Social Event, while B's 'Fee for extra trip' is a monetary charge under Money > Fee. One denotes an activity, the other a payment; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (co-author, a kind of Author who co-writes papers), while B is a monetary registration-fee category for members. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money) and share no intended instances.

Both properties link a Paper to its authors, but they are not equivalent: cmt's 'has Co author' has range 'Co author' (a co-author role, distinct from the main author), while edas's 'is Written By' has range 'Author' and covers all authors of the paper. The cmt property is narrower (co-authors only) and its range class differs, so the two overlap in meaning without coinciding; a reference alignment would not record them as equivalent.

A's Chair is a Committee member (a role within a committee, with a co-chair sibling and committee-chair relations), while B's Chair PC is a direct subclass of Person denoting the person chairing the programme committee. The B concept is broader (any PC chair person) and does not require committee membership modelling, so A's Chair is more specific and is subsumed by B's Chair PC rather than equivalent.

Both denote the person who chairs the conference organization: edas 'Conference Chair' is a Person who initiates calls and reviews, and ekaw 'OC Chair' is the chair of the Organizing Committee (OC Member > OC Chair), i.e. the conference chair role. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

Both are subclasses of Place denoting the physical location where a conference takes place: edas 'Conference Venue Place' and sigkdd 'Conference hall' occupy the same position under Place and are used for the same purpose (the venue/hall of the conference). The sibling sets (Accommodation/Dining/Meeting Room vs Hotel/Main office) are compatible with a venue-location reading, so the intended instances coincide.

cmt:User is a generic person role in the conference system, with subclasses Administrator, Author, Reviewer, and siblings Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member. ekaw:Agency Staff Member is a specific person role (staff of an agency) with siblings Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student. The intended instances do not coincide: a User need not be agency staff, and an Agency Staff Member is not necessarily a system User. Different concepts despite both being subclasses of Person.

A's 'Demo Paper' is a specific kind of Paper (a document type), while B's 'Document' is a broad top-level artefact class whose children are administrative items (Form, Invitation letter, Review, Submission, etc.). A Demo Paper is a document, but the two classes do not denote the same concept; the intended instances do not coincide.

An Extended abstract is a specific kind of conference contribution (a short/early version of a paper), whereas Submission in iasted is a broad document category whose children are Initial manuscript and Final manuscript. Every extended abstract is a submission, but submissions also include full papers, reviews, forms, etc., so Extended abstract is strictly narrower than Submission.

A's 'rejected By' links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who rejected it), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (the paper they wrote). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they are not the same relation.
A's Reception is a social event (a gathering) in the conference domain, while B's Negative Review is a type of document/review. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (event-to-event co-occurrence), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (the preference for reviewing), while B's property links a reviewer to their personal review history. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a document), while B's is_occupied_by relates a Building/City/State to a Person (physical occupancy of a place). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Academic Institution is an Organisation (a venue/organiser entity with children University, Research Institute), while Author is a Person (a Speaker who submits papers and obtains awards). They denote different kinds of entities in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a member of the organising committee who chairs the conference), while B 'Tutorial' is a type of conference activity/lecture event. They belong to disjoint branches of the domain (Person vs Activity) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Company is a for-profit commercial organization, sibling of University under Organization. B's Academia Organization is a non-profit academic/research organization, sibling of Government, Industry and NGO. They denote different kinds of organizations (industry vs academia), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a whole-part relation within the conference structure), while B's 'obtain' links a Person to an Item (an acquisition/possession relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's email is a Person's email address; B's has Postal Code is a postal code of a Contact Information record. Different domain concepts (email address vs postal code) and different domains (Person vs Contact Information), so they are not the same property.

Sponsorship (edas) is a funding arrangement with cost amount/currency and provider relations to Organization; Person (ekaw) is a human agent with authoring and organising relations. They share no instances and no meaning in the conference domain.

A is a subclass of Abstract (a document type for invited talk abstracts), while B is a subclass of Document (an invitation letter). They denote different document types with no overlap in intended instances.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Session room is a physical place (a kind of Place, sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room). An event and a location are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a paper/document to its authors, but they are not equivalent: A's range is the class 'Co author' (a person acting as co-author of a paper), while B's range is the broader class 'Person'. A's domain 'Paper' is narrower than B's 'Conference document'. The intended relations overlap (authorship of a document) but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's submit Paper is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (a submission act). B's is a full paper submission date is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date (a calendar deadline). Different domain, range, and kind of relation; they do not denote the same concept.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (domain PC Member, range Administrator). B's 'was a member of' links a Committee member to the Committee they belong to (domain Committee member, range Committee). Different domains, ranges, and meanings: one is an administrative provenance relation, the other a membership relation. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

ekaw:Document is a specific conference artefact (parent of Abstract, Paper, Review, etc., with properties authorOf/writtenBy to Person), whereas iasted:Item is a very broad class covering equipment, vehicles, money-related things, etc., with Document as one of its children. Document is strictly more specific than Item, so Document is subsumed by Item, not equivalent.

A's 'has a review expertise' links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (the topic/skill area a paper is about), while B's 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (a PC member reviews a paper). Different domain, different range, and different meaning (expertise topic vs. reviewing action), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Late Registered Participant' is a conference participant distinguished by late registration; B 'Session chair' is a delegate who chairs a session. They denote different roles with no subsumption or overlap, despite both being under a participant/delegate hierarchy.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings linking to a string identifier, while B's 'done till' is a datatype property of Deadline linking to a date. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Chair is a committee chair (leads a committee, sibling of Co chair, domain of 'has a committee chair' on Committee), whereas B's Program Committee member is a member of the program committee, sibling of Program Chair and General Chair. A chair leads a committee; a PC member is a member of it, so the concepts do not coincide.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Conference contribution, Review) addressed to attendees. B's 'Transparency' is a document type in iasted (sibling of Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance, Viza) denoting a transparency/overhead document. Different intended instances and different document subdomains; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) property linking a Conference volume to its Conference parts, while B's 'has Location' links a Conference Event to a Place. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' is a specific relation from an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who was assigned to them (a reviewing-assignment relation). B's 'give' is a broad relation from any Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or a paper). The domains (External Reviewer vs Person) and ranges (Reviewer vs Activity/Item) differ, and the intended meanings do not coincide, so the properties are not equivalent.

A is an inverse part-of property whose range is Event (it relates something to an Event it is part of), while B is the award property whose range is Award (it relates something to an Award). Different ranges and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

ekaw:Location is a venue/place where events are held (held In: Event -> Location; location Of: Location -> Event). sigkdd:ACM_SIGKDD is an organisation/agent that designs deadlines, holds conferences and searches sponsors. A place and an organising body are different concepts, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an Administrator action that opens the bidding phase for a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference). B's 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (domain Reviewer, range Personal Review History). Different subjects, objects, and intended meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions, while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee (a group of people) that organizes the conference. They belong to different branches (Event vs Committee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (who is qualified to review), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the talk material). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence.

OC Member (Organizing Committee Member) in ekaw is a Conference Participant who is part of the organizing committee, with children like OC Chair. In sigkdd, Organizator is a broader Person role whose children include General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, and Webmaster. The ekaw OC Member corresponds to the sigkdd 'Organizing Committee member' child, not to the broader Organizator class, which also covers program committee members and webmasters. Thus OC Member is strictly more specific than Organizator, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer assigned to review a paper), while B's design relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A is a document type (the abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B is a subject-area topic in a topic taxonomy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class under Person with subclasses Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, etc. Committee member in Conference is also under Person but is a narrower concept referring specifically to committee membership. They overlap (a committee member is a conference member) but are not equivalent; Conference Member is more general.

CAD Topic is a research topic area (a subject category under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), whereas Tutorial Abstract is a document type (an abstract of a tutorial, under Abstract/Document). They denote different kinds of things—a topic vs. a document—so they are unrelated.

A (ekaw Paper Author) is a subclass of Person denoting a person who authors papers. B (iasted Author attendee book registration fee) is a subclass of Registration fee denoting a monetary fee category for an author attendee who books registration. They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Money/Fee) and denote different kinds of things (a person vs a fee), so they are unrelated.

cmt:Reviewer is a Person/Conference Member who reviews papers (has Been Assigned Paper, assigned To Paper, adjust Bid), and confOf:Member_PC has the explicit comment 'Reviewer' and reviews Contributions (reviewes). Both denote the program-committee reviewer role, so they are equivalent despite differing sibling structures.

TPC Member (edas) is a Person who reviews papers and initiates calls, a program-committee role. IASTED member (iasted) is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. a conference attendee who is a member of the IASTED organisation, with siblings like Speaker, Listener, Session chair. The two overlap in that both are conference participants, but TPC Member is a reviewing/organising role while IASTED member is an attendee membership status; neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a class of paper (a document that has been accepted), while B is a deadline (the date by which authors are notified of acceptance). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (document vs. deadline) and have incompatible properties: Accepted Paper is related to events and paper presentations, whereas Deadline Author notification is the range of 'notification until' from Author. No equivalence or subsumption holds.
