Both classes denote a workshop as a kind of conference event: confOf places Workshop under Working event (siblings Conference, Tutorial), ekaw places Workshop under Scientific Event (siblings Conference, Session, Track). Same label and same intended instances (workshop events in the conference domain), so they are equivalent.

A's `date` is a datatype property of a Conference giving a literal date value, while B's `has important dates` is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Conference volume) and range (literal date vs Important dates class), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a part-whole relation within a conference's proceedings). B's 'is Location Of' relates a Place to a Conference Event (a spatial location relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Person) while B is a document type (Conference Proceedings, a subclass of Proceedings/Document). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. publications) and cannot denote the same concept.

A Review (cmt) is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a paper, with children Meta Review and properties linking Reviewer to Review. B Evaluated Paper (ekaw) is a paper that has been assigned and evaluated, with children Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper. The two denote different concepts: a review document versus a paper in an evaluated state. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Chairman is a role/person class (a Person who chairs, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Administrative event is an event class (an Event with subclasses like Submission event, Reviewing event). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'assign External Reviewer' relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (a reviewer-assignment relation), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship of a paper). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Paper is the general document class (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, sibling of Review), while B's Workshop Paper is a specific kind of Paper (sibling of Conference Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). Workshop Paper is strictly narrower than Paper, so A is subsumed by B's broader Paper concept; they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person (a human attending the conference), while B 'Conference Session' is a Scientific Event (a scheduled session such as a regular or poster session). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (a person entering details of a conference), while B's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (scheduling overlap). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no equivalence.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action of entering conference details), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a paper being presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Subject Area in cmt classifies papers (has Subject Area: Paper -> Subject Area), while Country in edas is a geographic attribute of a conference (has Country: Conference -> Country). They denote different concepts with different domains/ranges, so they are unrelated.

Meal Menu is a document describing the menu of a meal event (has Menu / is Menu Of link it to Meal Event), whereas Web Site is a generic published document (event On List, lists, publisher Of) with no connection to meals. They share only the Document parent, so they are unrelated.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' is an object property linking a Conference to an Administrator (the person who finalized paper assignments), while B's 'paper Due On' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime deadline. They differ in both kind (object vs datatype), range (Administrator vs dateTime), and intended meaning (assignment finalization vs submission deadline), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to an email address string, while B's 'has Surname' links a Person to a surname string. They relate different kinds of information (email vs. surname) and are not synonyms or inverses, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a committee role within a conference (siblings Program committee, Steering committee; domain/range tied to Conference volume), whereas B's 'Government Organization' is a type of organization (siblings Academia Organization, Industry Organization, NGO). Different domains and no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

A's property is the camera-ready submission date (a deadline for submitting the final, camera-ready version of an accepted paper), while B's hasSubmissionDeadline is the call's paper submission deadline (the initial deadline for submitting papers to the conference). These are distinct deadlines in the conference lifecycle, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Abstract is a document type (a subclass of Document, with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and it is presented as a Paper). B's Deadline Author notification is a deadline/date entity (subclass of Deadline, sibling of Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Paper Submission, and it is the range of 'notification until' from Author). They denote different concepts: a document vs. a notification deadline, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the assignment tools), while B's property links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role in the conference (a subclass of Person, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc., and properties linking it to a Conference). B 'Conference hotel' is a subclass of Building/Place, a physical venue location. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. building), so they are unrelated.

A's hasCall relates an Academic Event to a Call (a call for papers), while B's inverse_of_partOf_7 relates something to an Event as the inverse of a part-of relation (i.e., an Event is part of something). The two properties have different domains/ranges and different intended meanings: one links events to calls, the other expresses mereological containment of events. They are not equivalent.

A's `date` is the date of a Conference; B's `done till` is the deadline date of a Deadline. Different domains (Conference vs Deadline) and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

Both are object properties linking a conference-organisation entity (Programme / ACM SIGKDD) to the event it is associated with (Conference Event / Conference). 'belongs To Event' and 'hold' express the same relation between a programme/organisation and its conference, so they are equivalent despite the different labels.

Presenter in edas is a subclass of Author (path Person > Author > Presenter), so every Presenter is an Author but not every Author is a Presenter. The confOf Author is the more general concept, hence Author is subsumed by Presenter's superclass relationship; the two classes are not equivalent.

A 'Session chair' is a Delegate who chairs a session, while B 'Program Chair' is an Organizator who heads the program committee. Both are chairing roles in the conference domain, but they are distinct roles with different scopes (session vs. program) and different parent classes (Delegate vs. Organizator), so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both classes denote a human being in the conference domain. cmt:Person has children Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User; edas:Person has children Attendee, Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member. The role subclasses differ in granularity but the parent concept (a person involved in the conference) is the same, and both are used as domain/range for person-related properties (email, name, membership).

A 'Medicine Topic' is a subject area (a subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.) used to classify papers. B 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of scientific event/presentation (subclass of Individual Presentation, sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial). One denotes a research topic, the other a type of presentation event; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

Hotel is a specific kind of Place (a venue/accommodation location), while edas Place is the general location class covering venues, dining, meeting rooms, etc. Hotel is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by Place.

A's 'Sponsor state' is a state/role that a conference participant can be in (sibling of Conference state and Presenter state under State), whereas B's 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person denoting an organizing person (parent of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). One is a state, the other a person class; their intended instances do not coincide.

Both properties are named 'written By' and relate a written artefact to its author, but the domains and ranges differ in generality: cmt's property is restricted to Review -> Reviewer, while ekaw's is Document -> Person. A Review is a kind of Document and a Reviewer is a kind of Person, so cmt's writtenBy is strictly more specific than ekaw's; the two are not equivalent as a reference alignment would record them.

A is a document type (the full version of a paper, sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), while B is a subject/topic category in a topic taxonomy (a kind of Computer Networks Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot share instances.

A's Social event is a broad category of social events (children Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B's Excursion is a specific kind of social event (sibling Reception). Excursion is thus a narrower concept subsumed by the broader Social event, not equivalent.

A 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering all people contributing to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors, committee members, reviewers, etc.). B 'Author book proceedings included' is a narrow subclass of Author, specifically an author whose book/proceedings is included, sitting under Speaker > Author in the iasted hierarchy. Every instance of B is a person contributing to a conference, hence an instance of A, but not vice versa; therefore B is strictly more specific and A subsumes B.

A 'Working event' is a conference-domain event class (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop; has title, location, topics, VAT, choices), while B 'Computer Networks Security Topic' is a specific research topic under Computer Networks Topic. They denote entirely different concepts (event vs. topic), so they are unrelated.

A's Decision is the outcome of a paper review (children Acceptance/Rejection, range of has Decision from Paper), while B's Country is a geographic entity associated with a conference (range of has Country from Conference). Different domains and no shared context, so they are unrelated.

A's 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment relation), while B's 'is held in' relates an Activity to a Place/Time (location/scheduling relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Country (a geographic/political entity used as the location of a conference) and Currency (a monetary unit) denote different concepts; they share no instances and are not related in the conference domain.

A's 'Accpet If Room Rating' is a specific review-rating value (a rating category alongside Accept/Reject/Week Reject) used in EDAS's rating scale, whereas EKAW's 'Negative Review' is a review whose overall assessment is negative. Both concern the outcome/assessment of a review, so they overlap conceptually, but a rating value is not the same concept as a review with a negative verdict; they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Co author' is a person role (an author who co-writes a paper, sibling of 'Author Not Reviewer', domain of 'co write Paper'), while B 'Student registration fee' is a monetary fee (subclass of 'Registration fee' under Money). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A 'Full day tour' is a post-conference social activity (sibling of Departure under Activity after conference), while B 'Main office' is a physical place (sibling of Conference hall and Hotel under Place). Different domains (activity vs. location) and no shared meaning.

A's reviewOfPaper relates a Review to the Paper it reviews (domain Review, range Paper). B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domain, range, and direction of relation; not equivalent.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' is a mereological/structural property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume (domain Conference part, range Conference volume). B's 'need' links a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item), expressing a requirement relation. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A Program Committee Chair (cmt) is a Person/Chairman who chairs the program committee and reviews papers (end Review). A Session chair (iasted) is a Delegate who chairs a conference session, a different role in a different hierarchy (Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate). The roles are distinct: program committee chairing vs. session chairing, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that informs participants about the conference; B's 'Mailing list' is a Document used to manage email distribution. They share no intended instances and differ in purpose, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference topic (a subject area under Computer Networks Topic in the EDAS topic taxonomy), while B is a kind of scientific event (a contributed talk, sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial under Individual Presentation). A topic and an event type denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Document is a written artefact (parent of Paper and Review, involved in conflict-of-interest) while B's Organization is an institution (parent of Company and University, with address and employment properties). Different intended instances; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property giving a string title to Social/Working events, while B's 'lists Event' is an object property relating a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. They differ in domain, range, and kind (datatype vs object), so they are not the same relation.

A is a submission deadline (a time point in the Deadline hierarchy), while B is an award category (a type of award). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (Time vs Award) and share no intended instances.

Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity), while Organizing Committee is a committee (a group of people). They belong to different branches of the conference domain and their instances cannot coincide.

A's Conference is the event/organisation itself (has members, administrators, dates, accepts submissions), while B's Conference document is a document artefact (call for papers, review, announcement) with authors and a date of issue. Different intended instances, so not equivalent.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a subtype of 'Regular contribution' (a full/regular submission category), while B's 'Industrial Paper' is a subtype of 'Paper' denoting an industry-authored paper. They are different submission/paper categories with no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime that assign a date/time to an event/activity. 'has Start Date Time' on Conference Event and 'is dated on' on Activity denote the same relation (an event's date/time), differing only in label and domain class naming (Conference Event vs Activity, which are the same concept in the conference domain).

A's 'Invited speaker' is a role of a person (a conference contributor who gives an invited talk), while B's 'University' is an academic organisation. They belong to different branches (Person vs Organisation) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (a gathering at the conference, sibling of Banquet and Trip), while B's Neutral Review is a type of review document (sibling of Positive/Negative Review). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. document/review) and share no intended instances.

A's 'initiates' relates a chair/TPC member to a Call (issuing a call for papers), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (giving a talk/item). Different domains and ranges, different intended relations.

A's Person is a human agent in the conference domain (parent of Chairman, PC Member, Reviewer, User; has email, name, conflict of interest). B's State is a geographical/administrative region (parent of Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state; occupied by/visited by Person, situated in Place). The two denote different concepts; the only link is that a State can be occupied by a Person, which is a relation, not equivalence.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a kind of conference contributor/person (a role of a person), while B's 'Sponsor state' is a state of a sponsor in the iasted ontology, sibling of Conference state and Presenter state. They denote different concepts (person role vs. sponsor state) with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B's Transport vehicle is a physical item category (parent of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) used for transportation. They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Item).

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on a Conference indicating whether paper submissions are accepted in hardcopy; B's 'has an ISBN' is a string property of Conference proceedings giving its ISBN. They concern different subjects (conference submission policy vs. proceedings identifier) and different value types, so they are unrelated.

A's 'related To Paper' links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a presentation-to-paper relation), while B's 'volume Contains Paper' links a volume to the papers it contains (a containment relation between a proceedings volume and papers). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A is a research topic area (Computer Networks Topic) under Topic, while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee) under Committee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

In edas, 'Review Form' is the document/artifact used to submit a review (a form), whereas sigkdd's 'Review' is the review itself (a Document subtype alongside Abstract and Paper). They are related (the form is used to produce the review) but not the same concept, so not equivalent.

Research Topic in ekaw is a subject area of papers/events (covered by events, papers cover topics), while Money in iasted is a monetary amount with children Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment. They share no instances or meaning; the only overlap is the word 'topic'/'money' being unrelated concepts.

Both properties link a committee-like entity to a conference-like entity, but they are not the same relation: cmt's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member (an individual person who is a member of a conference) to a Conference, whereas Conference's was_a_steering_committee_of relates a Steering committee (a committee body) to a Conference volume. The domains differ (person vs. committee) and the ranges differ (Conference vs. Conference volume), so the properties are related but not equivalent.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of regular contribution (a document type submitted to a conference), while B's 'Initial manuscript' is a submission stage (the first version of a manuscript, sibling of 'Final manuscript'). They overlap in that an extended abstract can be an initial manuscript, but the concepts differ: one is a contribution type, the other a submission version. Hence related, not equivalent.

Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes papers), while Conference contribution is a document type (a Conference document such as a paper, poster or talk). They belong to different branches (Person vs Conference document) and have incompatible properties (Author writes/submits papers; Conference contribution is submitted at a volume).

A's hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper they were assigned to review), while B's hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (the rating given to a paper). Different domain (Reviewer vs Active Paper), different range (Paper vs Review Rating), and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'read Paper' relates a Reviewer to a Paper (domain Reviewer, range Paper), while B's 'belongs to reviewers' relates a Review expertise/Review preference to a Reviewer (domain Review expertise/Review preference, range Reviewer). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a subclass of Committee (a group of people organizing a conference), while B's 'Building' is a subclass of Place (a physical location with children like Conference hotel, Session room). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'Payment document' is a financial document (children Bank transfer, Cheque) used for conference fees, while B's 'Paper' is a scientific submission (submitted by an Author, siblings Abstract and Review). They share only the generic parent Document and denote different concepts.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'issues' links a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it issues. Different domains (Conference vs Publisher), different ranges (Administrator vs Conference proceedings), and different intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's 'related To Paper' links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (the paper being presented), while B's 'paper Presented As' links an Abstract/Paper to an Individual Presentation (the presentation format/event). The domains and ranges are swapped and denote different concepts (paper vs. presentation), so the properties are not equivalent; they are essentially inverses of each other in intent, which the guidelines say does not count as equivalence.

A's Review is a document type (a review of a contribution), while B's Paper is a document type (a submitted/published paper). In ekaw, Review is a separate sibling class of Paper, and Paper has a 'has Review' property pointing to Review, confirming they are distinct concepts. A's Review corresponds to B's Review, not B's Paper.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete paper document (sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), while B 'Tutorial Abstract' is an abstract of a tutorial (sibling of Invited Talk Abstract under Abstract). They denote different document types in different branches of the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's Review is a document evaluating a paper (child of Document, with review Of Paper and review Written By properties), while B's Value added tax is a kind of Tax under Money. The two concepts belong to entirely different domains and share no meaning.

A's 'is present' relates a Person to a Time (attendance at an event/time), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (submission of a paper). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper's rating), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission act). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent nor inverse.

A's 'Published Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been published), while B's 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Author (a person who authored a paper). They belong to different branches (Document vs Person) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Participant in confOf is a subclass of Person (path Person > Participant) restricted to conference participants with subclasses Member, Regular, Student and property early Registration. Person in edas is the broader superclass of all people (Attendee, Author, Reviewer, etc.) with general properties like name, email, biography. Participant is strictly more specific than Person, so Participant is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a part-whole relation within a conference's proceedings), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (membership). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's property is a specific deadline (abstract submission date) whose domain is the Important dates class and range is a date; B's property is a generic 'is dated on' relating any Activity to a dateTime. They differ in domain (Important dates vs Activity) and in specificity, so they are not the same relation.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of Contribution (a document type, sibling of Paper and Poster), while B 'Sponzor fee' is a kind of Fee (a payment, sibling of Registration fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (contribution vs. fee) and share no intended instances.

A Tutorial is a conference event/session type (sibling of Track and Workshop, part of a Conference), while B Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (sibling of Computer, LCD projector, Video cassette player). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

cmt's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member (a person on the programme/organising committee), while edas's hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person attending. Both relate a conference-related entity to a person, but the ranges differ (Conference Member vs. Person) and the domains differ (Conference vs. Conference Event); committee membership and attendance are distinct roles, so they are related but not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B 'Presenter university' is a building/place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Both 'Delegate' (confOf) and 'Delegate' (ekaw) represent the same conference role: a person attending an event with a specific participation status. Their labels match exactly, and their contexts (Event/Person) align across the two ontologies, so instances coincide.

A is a research topic (Cryptography Topic) under Topic, while B is an award category (Best Research Paper Award) under Award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference), while B's is_present relates a Person to a Time (attendance/presence at a time). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call for participation' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B's 'NGO' is a type of organization (sibling of Academia/Government/Industry Organization). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

A's 'is given by' relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the presenter), while B's 'attendee At' relates a Person to a Conference Event (attendance). The domains and ranges differ (Presentation vs Person, participant vs Conference Event), and the directions/meanings are distinct: presenting a paper is not the same relation as attending an event. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's 'Call For Papers' is a call/announcement event (sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews, child of Call), whereas B's 'Paper' is a document submitted by an author (child of Document, sibling of Abstract and Review, range of submit). A call for papers is not a paper; the entities denote different concepts and are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties linking an event/activity to a temporal value: confOf's 'starts on' (domain Event, range string) and iasted's 'is dated on' (domain Activity, range dateTime). Event and Activity are the corresponding event classes in the two ontologies, and both properties record the date/time at which the event takes place, so they denote the same relation despite the string vs dateTime range difference.

A is a research topic (Mobile Computing Topic) under Topic, while B is an award category (Best Research Paper Award) under Award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

Both classes denote a person who gives a presentation at a conference. In iasted, Speaker is a subclass of Delegate with children Author and Reviewer; in sigkdd, Speaker is a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited Speaker and is linked to Document via presentation/presentationed by. The intended instances coincide (a person presenting a paper/talk), so the classes are equivalent despite differing parent hierarchies.

Conference in confOf is a working event (an organised meeting such as a tutorial or workshop), whereas Proceedings in ekaw is a multi-author volume document containing conference proceedings. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

A's Reviewer is a Person (a person who reviews, with review expertise/preferences and co-reviewer relations), while B's Review is a Document (a written review artefact, sibling of Abstract and Paper). The entities denote different kinds of things (agent vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

A's User is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Hotel room is a physical place (parent Place, siblings Building/Conference hall). Different domains entirely; no overlap.

A's property links a Committee to its Co chair (a specific committee role), while B's hasMember links a Conference to a Person (general membership). Different domains (Committee vs Conference), different ranges (Co chair vs Person), and different intended relations; they are not equivalent.

A's contactEmail is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string email address (comment 'confTool'), while B's writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person author. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Contribution vs Document) and range (string vs Person), so they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event (the act/process of submitting contributions), while B 'Accepted Paper' is a document (a paper that has been accepted). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Document) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing/issuing a proceedings volume), while B's `prepare` relates a Person to an Item (an author preparing a paper). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Departure tax' is a tax paid when leaving a country, a subclass of Tax. B 'Sponzor fee' is a sponsorship fee, a subclass of Fee. They denote different concepts (tax vs. fee) with different parents and no shared instances.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while B's 'paper Presented As' links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (presentation-format relation). Different domain, range and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a device used in presentations), while B's Organizator is a person role in the conference organization hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches (equipment vs. person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties linking a committee to its members: cmt's hasProgramCommitteeMember has domain Program Committee and range Program Committee Member, while Conference's has_members has domain Committee and range Committee member. Program Committee is a subclass of Committee and Program Committee Member is a subclass of Committee member, so the properties relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are the standard alignment for committee membership.

A is the class Paper (a document submitted to a conference, with children Paper Abstract / Paper Full Version and properties such as has Author, assigned To Reviewer, has Decision). B is a deadline class 'Submissions deadline' (a time point in the Time > Deadline branch, sibling of Camera ready manuscript deadline and Registration deadline). A paper is a document, not a deadline, so the two entities are unrelated despite both being classes in the conference domain.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a scientific paper with an abstract, part of a conference contribution hierarchy). B's Programme Brochure is a document that lists events and is published by an organisation, sibling to Paper/Abstract/Review. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while B's Conference restaurant is a building/place (a restaurant at a conference venue). Different kinds of entities with no overlap.

A's title is a datatype property giving the literal title string of a Paper; B's presentationOfPaper is an object property linking an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper it presents. Different kinds (data vs object), different domains (Paper vs Individual Presentation), and different meanings (title text vs presented paper), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a short summary document of a paper (sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B 'Registration form' is a form used to register for the conference (sibling of Author information form and Hotel registration form under Form). They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A's Conference Participant is a broad Person subclass covering all attendees (chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.). B's Non speaker is a Delegate subclass specifically for delegates who do not present, with children Student non speaker and Worker non speaker. The two overlap (a non-speaking delegate is a conference participant) but neither subsumes the other: Conference Participant includes speakers and non-delegates, while Non speaker is restricted to non-presenting delegates. Hence related, not equivalent.

Paper Presentation is an academic event (a talk/session where accepted papers are presented), while Web Site is a document (a web page that lists events and is published by an organisation). They belong to different branches (event vs document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference part' is a structural component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) that has a name, chairs and topics and is part of a conference volume. B's 'Conference Paper' is a kind of Document/Paper (a written submission such as a regular, poster or workshop paper). The two denote different concepts: an event/structural part versus a document artefact, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document that is written by authors, reviewed by reviewers, and has accepted/rejected/published subclasses. B's Review is a document in the iasted ontology whose siblings are administrative artefacts (Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance, Submission, Transparency, Viza) — it denotes the review form/record, not the paper being reviewed. The two classes have different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's Topic is the general class of conference topics (domain of dealsWith, expertOn, hasTopic), while B's Security Topic is a specific topic under the parent Topic. Security Topic is strictly narrower than Topic, so A is subsumed by B's broader concept.

edas:Place is a physical location/venue (children Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place; it is the range of has Location and domain of is Location Of, i.e. a place where conference events occur). ekaw:Event is a happening/activity (children Scientific Event, Social Event; it has topics, is organised by persons/organisations, is held in a Location, and has part-of relations). The two are different concepts: an Event is held in a Place, so Place is the location of an Event, not the Event itself. Although ekaw:Event has a property location Of (Location -> Event), that is a relation, not a class equivalence, and edas:Place is not the same as ekaw:Location either. Hence the classes denote different things and are unrelated.

A 'Program Committee Chair' is a specific leadership role within the program committee (a chair), while B 'Program Committee member' is the broader class of all program committee members. A chair is a member, but not every member is a chair, so A is strictly more specific than B (A subsumed_by B).

A's 'initiates' relates a chair/TPC member to a Call (issuing a call for papers), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (giving a presentation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference Session is the general session class (it is the domain/range of document-relation properties and has no parent session class), while B's Industrial Session is a specific subtype of Conference Session (path: Event > Scientific Event > Session > Conference Session > Industrial Session). Thus A is more general than B; they are not equivalent.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's email address), while B's 'is used by' is an object property from Item to Person (an item being used by a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and direction/meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword, while B's hasReview is an object property linking a Paper to a Review. They relate different kinds of things (string vs. Review) and represent different relations (keyword assignment vs. review association), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Contribution is a general submitted work (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with title, abstract, keywords, authors, reviews. ekaw's Assigned Paper is a narrower stage in the paper lifecycle (Document > Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper, with child Evaluated Paper), i.e. a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer. Every Assigned Paper is a contribution, but not every contribution is an assigned paper, so Contribution is more general and is subsumed by Assigned Paper.

Paper in ekaw is a subclass of Document (path Document > Paper), while sigkdd's Document is the broader class with Paper as a child. Thus ekaw Paper is strictly more specific than sigkdd Document, so Paper is subsumed by Document, not equivalent.
hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject outcome), while hasCity relates an Organization or Person to a City (location). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Conference is an event/venue class (has a name, has a Conference volume, related to proceedings, publisher, topic), while B's Speaker is a subclass of Person (a role played by an attendee, with children Author and Invited Speaker and properties presentation/presentationed by). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chairing role under Chairman/Conference Member, while Speaker (iasted) is a delegate role under Delegate with children Author and Reviewer. They denote different concepts: chairing/organising vs. presenting/speaking, with no shared parent or property alignment.

Both are object properties linking a reviewer to the paper they review; cmt's 'assignedByAdministrator' and confOf's 'reviewes' have matching domain (Reviewer/Member PC) and range (Administrator/Contribution) roles in the conference domain.

A's 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to its Program committee (a part-whole/structural relation), while B's 'parallel with' links two Administrative events that run concurrently. Different domain, range and meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A is a research topic area (a subject category under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), while B is a document type (a kind of Abstract under Document, sibling of Invited Talk Abstract). They denote entirely different concepts: a topic of interest vs. a type of conference submission document. No subsumption or overlap.

A's Conference is the event itself (has members, accepts submissions, has dates, administrators). B's Conference announcement is a document type (sibling of Call for paper, Conference contribution, Review) under Conference document. The event and a document announcing it are different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Fee (iasted) is a monetary charge paid by participants (subclasses: Registration fee, Hotel fee, Fee for extra trip), while Silver Supporter (sigkdd) is a sponsorship level under Sponzor (siblings: Gold Supporter, Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor). Different concepts: one is a cost, the other a sponsor category.
A's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (requirement). Different domain, range, and direction of relation; no conceptual overlap.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (author writes paper), while B's 'is paid by' relates Money to a Person (payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while B's volume Contains Paper relates a volume/proceedings to a paper (containment). Different domain/range and direction of meaning, so not equivalent.

A is a person role (a chair of the conference, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while B is a physical building (a restaurant venue for the conference, a subclass of Building). They denote entirely different kinds of entities and share no meaning.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a role/leadership relation within an organization), while B's 'writtenBy' relates a Document to a Person (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both denote the final, complete version of a paper submitted for publication: cmt's Paper Full Version is the full paper (as opposed to the Paper Abstract) under Paper, while iasted's Final manuscript is the final submission (as opposed to the Initial manuscript) under Submission. The intended instances coincide (the finished paper document), so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of event alongside Conference and Tutorial), while B's Demo Session is a kind of Session (alongside Conference Session, Poster Session, Regular Session, Workshop Session). In ekaw, the corresponding concept to confOf's Workshop is Workshop Session, not Demo Session; a demo session is a session where demos are presented, a distinct concept. Thus the two classes are unrelated.

Conference proceedings is a published volume of collected papers with a publisher, volume number and ISBN, whereas Web Site is a kind of Document (a web page) that lists events and is published by an organisation. They share no intended instances and have different properties and contexts, so they are unrelated.

Both are specific registration-fee classes under Registration fee, but A is a nonmember fee while B is a SIGMOD-member fee; they are different fee categories (member vs nonmember), so they overlap only as sibling registration-fee subtypes, not equivalent.

A is a research topic in computer networking (a subfield of the conference's Topic taxonomy), while B is a physical means of transport (with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) under Item. They share no instances and belong to entirely different domains, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the person who gives it (range: Active conference participant), while B's 'event On List' links an Event to a publication medium such as a Programme Brochure or Web Site. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Committee member' is a Person role within the conference organisation (parent Person, children Chair/Co chair, related to Committee via has members/was a member of). B 'Place' is a physical location (children Accommodation/Conference Venue/Dining/Meeting Room Place, related to Conference Event via has Location/is Location Of). They denote different concepts with no overlap.
Travel Grant is a sponsorship/funding category (child of Sponsorship), while Invited Speaker is a person role (child of Speaker). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Committee member is a Person who belongs to a committee (domain/range: Committee member -> Committee, inverse of Committee -> Committee member), with subclasses Chair and Co chair. B's Speaker is a Delegate (a person role) who speaks, with subclasses Author and Reviewer, and is not tied to committee membership. The intended instances do not coincide: a committee member need not be a speaker and a speaker need not be on a committee. Different concepts.

A's Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster and Short paper under Contribution), while B's Best Applications Paper Award is a specific award category under Award. They denote different concepts: a document vs. an award, so they are unrelated.

A's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Members (people belonging to the conference), while B's was_an_organizing_committee_of links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume. The domains and ranges differ (Conference->Conference Member vs Organizing committee->Conference volume), and the directions/meanings are distinct: one relates a conference to its members, the other relates a committee to the conference it organized. They are not the same relation.

A 'Review Question' is a question (numerical or textual) used to structure a review form; B 'Review' is the review document itself, a subclass of Document with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review and properties linking it to Paper and Possible Reviewer. The two denote different concepts (question vs. review artefact), so they are unrelated.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it (domain Sponsorship, range Organization), while B's 'pay' links a Person to the Registration fee they pay (domain Person, range Registration fee). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Conference Member in cmt is a person role (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/Chair, linked to Conference via member Of Conference), while Organization in edas is an institutional entity (children Academia/Government/Industry/NGO, linked to Sponsorship via is Provider Of). They denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation that is invited, while B's 'Contributed Talk' is an individual presentation that is contributed (submitted), the opposite category. In ekaw the counterpart of A is 'Invited Talk' (a sibling of Contributed Talk), so the two entities denote different, mutually exclusive presentation types.

Withdrawn Paper is a specific status of Paper (a subclass of Paper in edas), while sigkdd's Paper is the general paper class. Every withdrawn paper is a paper, but not every paper is withdrawn, so Withdrawn Paper is strictly narrower and is subsumed by Paper.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that announces a conference. B 'Tutorial' is a kind of lecture/session activity (subclass of Lecture, sibling of Plenary lecture and Session) that takes place at a conference. One is a document artefact, the other an event/activity; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' relates a Contribution to its Author (authorship of a paper), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to the Person who pays it. Different domains, ranges and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole event such as a conference with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's Presentation is a conference activity (a talk/presentation session with children like Power Point presentation and siblings like Lecture, Coffee break). They denote different concepts: an event vs. an activity within an event, so they are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a specific kind of paper (the abstract-only submission), a sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper. Paper in confOf is the general contribution type (siblings Poster, Short paper). The abstract is a narrower concept than the general Paper, so Paper Abstract is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a call inviting participation, sibling of Call for paper and Conference announcement). B 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a specific deadline (the abstract submission deadline, sibling of paper submission and author notification deadlines). One is a document, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Committee member is a specific role within the conference domain (a Person who is part of a Committee, with children Chair and Co chair), whereas ekaw's Person is the general superclass of all people (including authors, participants, students). Every committee member is a person, but not every person is a committee member, so Committee member is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Person.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Registation deadline' is a time/deadline entity. They belong to different branches (document vs. time) and denote different concepts; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'is made from' is an object property relating an Item to another Item (a composition/derivation relation). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Item), and meaning, so they cannot denote the same relation.

A is a subject/topic area within the conference taxonomy (a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic), while B is a kind of presentation event (a Contributed Talk, sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (topic vs. event) and share no intended instances.

A's 'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (domain PC Member, range Administrator). B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to the Conference they belong to (domain Person, range Conference). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Important dates' is a class of deadline/date entities (submission, camera-ready, acceptance, start/end dates) belonging to a conference volume. B's 'Abstract' is a subclass of Document (a text artefact, sibling of Paper and Review, with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract). The two denote entirely different concepts — a set of dates versus a document type — so they are unrelated.

A is a time/phase class (an activity occurring before the conference, with children like Receiving manuscript, Accepting manuscript), while B is a person role (Organizator, a subclass of Person with children like General Chair, Program Chair). They denote different kinds of entities (event phase vs. person role) and are not equivalent.

confOf's Person is the general superclass of all people in the conference (Administrator, Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.), while edas's Author is a specific subclass of Person (sibling of Attendee, Reviewer, etc.). Person is strictly more general than Author, so Person subsumes Author; they are not equivalent.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B is a geographic city associated with a conference (a subclass of City) in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's University is an Organization (a venue/institution where scholars study), while B's Student lecturer is a person role (a lecturer who is also a student) under Lecturer in the delegate/author hierarchy. They denote different kinds of entities (institution vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'manuscript Due On' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime deadline (the manuscript submission deadline). B's 'topic Covered By' is an object property linking a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (the event/paper that covers the topic). They differ in domain (Conference vs Research Topic), range (dateTime vs Event/Paper), and meaning (deadline vs coverage relation), so they are unrelated.

A's employedBy relates a Person to the Organization that employs them; B's providedBy relates a Sponsorship to the Organization providing it. Different domains (Person vs Sponsorship) and different intended relations (employment vs sponsorship provision), so they are not equivalent.

A Paper Full Version is a full-content paper document (sibling of Paper Abstract), while an Accepted Paper is a paper that has passed review and will appear in proceedings. They overlap (an accepted paper is often a full paper) but neither subsumes the other: a full paper can be rejected, and an accepted paper can be a short/abstract paper. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's property is the camera-ready submission deadline (a specific important date within the Important dates class), while B's paperDueOn is the conference paper submission deadline (domain Conference). These are different deadlines in the conference lifecycle, so the properties are not equivalent.

A 'Numerical Review Question' is a type of review question (a question on a review form whose answer is numeric), while B 'Abstract' is a document part of a paper (the abstract text). They belong to different branches (Review Question vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Research Topic is a subject area that events and papers cover (domain/range: Event, Paper -> Research Topic). In iasted, Research is a specific activity performed before the conference (a sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript), i.e. an action, not a topic. The intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are unrelated.

A 'Conference contributor' is a Person (a role an individual plays: author, speaker, reviewer), while B 'Lecture' is a Conference activity (an event such as plenary lecture, session, tutorial). They belong to disjoint top-level branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Paid applicant' is a specific kind of registered conference applicant who has paid, while B 'Conference Participant' is the broader class of all participants (including chairs, presenters, students, etc.). The A class is strictly narrower than B, so it is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (Paper/Poster/Short paper) with authors, title, abstract, keywords, and reviews. Call in edas is a call for submissions/reviews issued by chairs, with submission deadlines and instructions. They denote different concepts: a contribution is the submitted artefact, a call is the solicitation event. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'Working event' is a broad category covering Conference, Tutorial and Workshop (siblings are Administrative event and Social event), whereas ekaw's 'Social Event' covers Conference Banquet and Conference Trip and is a sibling of Scientific Event. They denote disjoint kinds of event, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Member PC' is a generic PC member (comment: Reviewer) directly under Person, while B's 'SC Member' is a specific kind of PC Member (Steering Committee member) under PC Member, sibling to PC Chair, Session Chair, etc. Every SC Member is a PC member, but not every PC member is an SC member, so A is more general and B is subsumed by A.

A 'PC Chair' is a conference participant who chairs the program committee (a role in the reviewing/organising structure, sibling of PC Member and other chairs). B 'Tutorial speaker' is a kind of Author/Speaker who gives a tutorial. The two denote different roles with no subsumption or overlap: a PC chair need not be a tutorial speaker and vice versa.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies to register for a conference, while B 'Conference Participant' is a broader class covering anyone taking part in the conference (chairs, presenters, authors, registered participants, etc.). The applicant is a narrower, pre-registration role, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's Paper is a kind of Contribution (a scientific submission, sibling of Poster and Short paper) in the conference domain. B's Mailing list is a Document used for communication, sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc. They denote different concepts; no subsumption or overlap.

Assigned Paper is a subclass of Submitted Paper (a document that has been assigned to a reviewer), while Committee is an organizational group with subclasses such as Program Committee and Organizing Committee. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances or meaning.

cmt:name is a datatype property with domain Conference and Person, giving the name of a conference or a person. confOf:hasTitle has domain Contribution and gives the title of a contribution/paper. Different domains (Person/Conference vs Contribution) and different intended values (person/conference name vs paper title), so they are not the same relation.

Person in cmt is the general superclass of all people in the conference domain (Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User), whereas Committee member in Conference is a subclass of Person restricted to committee members (with children Chair, Co chair). Committee member is strictly narrower than Person, so Person subsumes Committee member; they are not equivalent.

A is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date (camera-ready paper submission deadline), while B links Participant to a boolean (early registration flag). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A's Review Rating is a class of rating values (Accept, Reject, etc.) assigned to a paper, whereas B's Negative Review is a subclass of Review denoting a review with negative content. They both concern reviews/ratings but denote different concepts: one is a rating value, the other a review type. They overlap in the review domain but are not equivalent.

A 'Conference contribution' is a specific kind of conference document (a submitted/accepted contribution such as a paper, poster, or talk), while B 'Document' is a broad class covering any document in the EDAS system (papers, reviews, programmes, slides, menus). Every conference contribution is a document, but not every document is a conference contribution, so Conference contribution is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Document.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper-writing relation), while B's `search` relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (a sponsorship/search relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string biography, while B's is_designed_for is an object property linking Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to the Conference they belong to (domain Conference Member, range Conference). B's organisedBy relates an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it (domain Event, range Organisation, Person). The domains and ranges are disjoint kinds of entities (member vs. organiser; conference vs. event), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (membership in a conference), while B's occupy relates a Person to a Building/City/State (physical location). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; not equivalent.

A's Reviewer is a Person/Conference Member role (a human who reviews papers, with properties like adjust Bid, has Been Assigned, assign External Reviewer). B's Reviewing event is an Event/Administrative event (the reviewing procedure/process for submitted contributions, sibling of Submission event and Camera Ready event). One denotes a person role, the other an event/process; they are different kinds of entities and not equivalent.

Review Rating is a class of ratings assigned to papers (children Accept/Reject ratings, domain of has Rating from Active Paper), while Activity in iasted is a general event/activity class (children Activity before/after conference, Conference activity) with properties about persons, places, times and money. The two denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Early paid applicant' is a narrow subclass of paid conference applicants (sibling of 'Late paid applicant'), while B's 'Participant' is a broad person role covering members, regulars, students, etc. Every early paid applicant is a participant, but not vice versa, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A Workshop Session is a kind of Session (a parallel track of contributed presentations within a conference), while a Plenary lecture is a kind of Lecture (a single talk given to the whole conference). They differ in both parent class (Session vs Lecture) and intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (a person who wrote reviews), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/performing something). The domains, ranges and intended meanings differ: one is about review-history ownership by a reviewer, the other about a person giving an activity/item. They are not the same relation.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property of Review preference with range int (a reviewer's degree of expertise), while B's 'has Surname' is a datatype property of Person with range string (a person's family name). They relate different kinds of things in different domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.

A is a datatype property linking an 'Important dates' node to a date value (the camera-ready submission deadline), while B is an object property linking a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the event at which the paper is presented). They relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions and domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while B's Demo Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a sibling of Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). Thus A's Paper is more general and B's Demo Paper is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

Both properties describe a person initiating/signing a call or item, but the domains and ranges differ: edas initiates is restricted to conference organisers (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) and its range is Call, while iasted sign has the broader domain Person and range Item. They overlap in meaning but are not equivalent.

A's Decision is the outcome of reviewing a paper (children Acceptance/Rejection, domain of has Decision with range Paper), whereas B's Submitted contribution is a document/contribution that has been submitted and is reviewed (parent Written contribution, child Reviewed contribution, involved in review expertise/preference relations). A decision is not a contribution; the concepts are unrelated.

A 'Pending Paper' is a paper in the submission/review state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper under Paper). B 'Bank transfer' is a payment document (sibling of Cheque under Payment document). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (submission status vs. payment method) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Registration form' is a Document/Form artefact used to register (siblings: Author information form, Hotel registration form), while B's 'Registration fee' is a Fee with price/currency and payer properties. A form and a fee are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Chairman in cmt is a general role (parent of Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair), while sigkdd's Program Committee member is a specific organizer role. A Chairman is not necessarily a PC member, but a PC member is a kind of chair/organizer role; the cmt Chairman is broader and subsumes the more specific PC member role, so Chairman is subsumed_by Program Committee member in the sense of the specific role being a subtype of the general chair role.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a specific role/class for the first author of a contribution, sitting under 'Regular author' with sibling 'Contribution co author'. B's 'Author' is a broader class of conference delegates who author works, with children covering proceedings, lectures, tutorials, etc. Every instance of a first author of a contribution is an author, but not every author is a first author of a contribution, so A is strictly more specific than B (subsumed_by).

A 'Paid applicant' is a subclass of registered conference applicant (a person who has paid the registration fee), while B 'Activity before conference' is a subclass of Activity covering pre-conference tasks such as accepting/receiving/refusing manuscripts, renting and research. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'follows' relates two Administrative events (an event ordering relation between events), while B's 'is sent after' relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering of an item relative to a time point). Different domains and ranges, and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name (string), while B's 'Price' is a datatype property of Registration fee giving a monetary amount (int). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they denote no common relation.

A's Talk Event is a specific kind of academic event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), while B's Lecture is a broader conference activity that subsumes Session and Tutorial as well as plenary lectures. They overlap in that a talk/lecture is a spoken presentation, but neither subsumes the other cleanly: Talk Event is narrower (a single talk event) and Lecture is broader (a category of activity including sessions and tutorials). Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's `name` is a datatype property of Conference/Person giving a string name, while B's `has a location` is a datatype property of Conference volume giving a string location. They relate different kinds of things (a name vs. a location) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's Dining Place is a place for eating (sibling of Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Meeting Room Place), while B's Conference hall is a large room for conference sessions (sibling of Session room, Hotel room, Building, Main office). They denote different kinds of places in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person who finalizes paper assignments), while B's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution). Different domain, range, and direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

In the Conference ontology, Person is a broad class whose children include Committee member, Conference applicant, Conference contributor, Conference participant, Reviewer, and Track workshop chair, and it is the domain of properties like has an email, has gender, has first/last name, and contributes. In sigkdd, Author is a narrower class under Speaker (Person > Speaker > Author) with children Author of paper and Author of paper student, and properties specific to submitting papers and receiving notifications/awards. Every Author is a Person, but not every Person is an Author (e.g., committee members, applicants, participants). Thus Person is more general than Author, so the relation is subsumes (Person subsumes Author), not equivalence.

Ontology A's 'has a commtitee' is a property linking a Conference volume to a Committee, while Ontology B's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to a Conference Chair, Session Chair, or TPC Member. The domains (Conference volume vs Call) and ranges (Committee vs person roles) differ, so the two properties denote different relations in the conference domain.

Non Academic Event is a broad category covering breaks, meals, and social events, while Social program is a narrower activity focused on social events (e.g., dinner banquet, cocktail reception). Thus Non Academic Event is more general and subsumes Social program.

A's Author is the general class of people who write papers (parent of Author Not Reviewer and Co author, domain of write Paper/submit Paper). B's Contribution 1th author is a specific role: the first author of a conference contribution, a sibling of Contribution co author under Regular author. Every first author is an author, but not every author is a first author, so A is more general and B is subsumed by A.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial/workshop), while B's Hotel presenter is a kind of Delegate (a person role). They denote different concepts (event vs. person role) and are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person role in the conference organization (chair of the conference, sibling of Program Committee Chair, Author, Reviewer), while Early paid applicant (Conference) is a registered conference attendee who paid early, sibling of Late paid applicant. The two denote different concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (an academic meeting with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's Conference hotel is a building/place used as lodging. Different kinds (event vs. place) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Free Time Break is a generic break event (siblings Coffee Break and Meal Break), while B's Coffee break is a specific kind of break. They overlap in that a coffee break is a free-time break, but neither subsumes the other cleanly: A is broader than B, yet B is a specific sibling concept under A's Break Event. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a paper has a bid/review bid), while B's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (an author has a related paper). Different domains (Paper vs Author), different ranges (Bid vs Paper), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Published Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been published), while B's Best Research Paper Award is a subclass of Award (a prize given to a paper). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (document vs. award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has Surname' is a datatype property holding a person's family name, while B's 'E mail' holds an email address. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote different attributes of a person (surname vs. email address), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (the person who has the expertise), while B's 'has Reviewer' links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a candidate reviewer for that paper). Different domains (Review expertise/Review preference vs Paper) and different intended meanings (expertise ownership vs paper-reviewer assignment), so they are not equivalent.

Chairman (cmt) is a Person role who chairs committees/conferences, with children Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair. Social Event (ekaw) is an Event (banquet, trip). Different kinds and domains; no overlap.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document/paper component in the cmt ontology (sibling of Paper Full Version), while B 'Computer' is a piece of audiovisual equipment in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Both classes denote a co-author of a paper/contribution: A's 'Co author' is an Author who co-writes a Paper (with has Co author inverse on Paper), and B's 'Contribution co author' is a Regular author of a Conference contribution, sibling to 'Contribution 1th author'. The intended instances (persons who are not the first/sole author but an additional author) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A's 'Academic Institution' is an Organisation subtype (a university/research institute that hosts or organises conferences), while B's 'Research' is an Activity-before-conference subtype (a scholarly activity such as modelling or simulating). They belong to different top-level branches (Organisation vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, choices), while B 'Microelectronics Topic' is a specific research subject under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. subject area) and share no instances.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a kind of Chairman/Person) while B is a type of event session (Demo Session, a kind of Session/Event). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' relates an External Reviewer to the Reviewer they are assigned to (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer), while B's 'has Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (domain Paper, range Possible Reviewer). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (topic has a review preference), while B's property links a Programme to a Conference Event (programme contains an event). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (ending a review phase), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (giving a presentation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

confOf's hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (organisational sub-event), while sigkdd's obtain links an Author to an Award (an author receiving a prize). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the two properties are unrelated.

Both classes denote an organisation in the conference domain: edas Organization is the sponsor/provider side (is Provider Of Sponsorship, provided By), while ekaw Organisation organises events and publishes proceedings. The children (Academia/Government/Industry/NGO vs Academic Institution/Organising Agency/Proceedings Publisher) are different specialisations of the same general concept, and the properties are complementary roles of an organisation rather than conflicting definitions, so the intended instances coincide.

A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (object property, domain Conference, range Country), while B's Nation relates a Person to a string (datatype property, domain Person, range string). Different domain, different range, different kind of property, and different direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Non Academic Event' is a conference event type (breaks, meals, social events) under Conference Event, while B 'Organizator' is a person role (chairs, committee members, webmaster) under Person. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (event vs. person) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses like Invited speaker, Regular author, Reviewer). B's 'Presenter state' is a subclass of State (a status/phase in the conference process, sibling of Conference state and Sponsor state). One is a person role, the other a process state, so they denote different concepts.

A's Tutorial is a working event (a kind of conference session), while B's Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment; the shared word 'tutorial' vs 'computer' aside, the concepts belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Item/Audiovisual equipment) and denote different things.

A's property links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (an assignment of a reviewer preference), while B's 'submit' links an author to a paper (the act of submitting). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' links a Conference to an Administrator (who finalized paper assignments), while B's 'related To Paper' links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's hasCostCurrency is a datatype property linking a Sponsorship to a currency string; B's locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. Different domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/meeting, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Individual Presentation is a scientific event that is a presentation of a paper (sibling of Conference, Session, Track, Workshop). They denote different concepts: a conference is an event, an individual presentation is a talk given at such an event. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.
