Rated Papers is a subclass of Active Paper (a paper that has received at least one review/rating), whereas ekaw's Paper is the general document class covering all papers (submitted, camera-ready, demo, poster, etc.). Every Rated Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is rated, so Rated Papers is strictly narrower and is subsumed by Paper.

Company in confOf is an organization type (sibling of University under Organization), denoting an industrial institution. Security Topic in edas is a research topic (child of Topic, sibling of Cryptography Topic etc.), denoting a subject area. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot share instances.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while B's location Of relates a Location to an Event (an event's venue). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

hasBeenAssigned goes Reviewer -> Paper, while isReviewedBy goes Paper -> Reviewer (and other roles). They are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation. They are related because they describe the same review assignment link in opposite directions.

Track in ekaw is a scientific event (a thematic stream of the conference containing sessions/presentations), while Organizing Committee in sigkdd is a committee (a group of people organizing the conference). They denote different concepts: one is an event, the other an organizational body, so they are unrelated.

A is a class of accepted papers/contributions in the Conference ontology (a reviewed, accepted written contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution, sibling of Rejected contribution). B is a class of deadlines in the iasted ontology (a time point with children such as submission and camera-ready deadlines). They denote entirely different concepts: one is a document/contribution, the other a temporal deadline. No equivalence, subsumption or meaningful overlap.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Person (via Conference Member/User) and denotes a conference participant who writes/submits papers. In sigkdd, Person is the general superclass of all conference participants (Listener, Organizator, Speaker) and is not restricted to authors. Thus Author is strictly more specific than Person, so Author is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's obtain is an object property mapping a Person to an Item (acquiring an item). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

edas:Place is a general spatial location (accommodation, venue, dining, meeting room) that conference events are located at, while iasted:City is a specific kind of place (a city) that buildings and persons are situated in/occupy. City is narrower than Place, so Place is subsumed by City's broader notion of location; they are not equivalent.

A's 'IASTED non member' is a subclass of Delegate (a person/attendee role), while B's 'Registration Non Member' is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. fee), so they are not equivalent.

A's Submission is a document class (a submitted paper, with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript) in the iasted ontology. B's Deadline Abstract Submission is a deadline/time-point class (a date by which abstracts must be submitted), sibling of Deadline Paper Submission and Deadline Author notification under Deadline. A document and a deadline are different concepts, so the classes are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Wireless Communications Topic' is a subject area/topic in the EDAS taxonomy. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a Document subtype in the iasted ontology, sibling to Submission, Form, Payment document, etc., i.e. the review document/artefact. B's Abstract is a Document subtype in sigkdd, sibling to Paper and Review, i.e. the abstract text of a paper. They denote different document types (a review vs. an abstract), so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the subject area of a paper/contribution: confOf's Topic is dealt with by Contributions and is the expertise of PC members and the topic of working events; ekaw's Research Topic is covered by Events and Papers and covers them in return. Same intended instances (research topics), so equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman who chairs the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B 'Talk Event' is an academic event (a talk session, sibling of Paper Presentation and Workshop). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. event) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a human role: active participant, invited speaker, regular author), while B's 'Break Event' is a subclass of Non Academic Event (a scheduled break such as coffee break, meal break, free time). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Conference Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has Last Name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'can stay in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place (accommodation). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

Both are datatype properties giving a start date/time, but A's domain is the 'Important dates' class (a deadline/date record) while B's domain is 'Conference Event', and A's range is a date whereas B's is a dateTime. They denote related but not identical relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Social Event is a non-academic conference event (with children Excursion, Reception, siblings Break Event, Meal Event) that occurs during the conference. B's Activity after conference is a post-conference activity (children Departure, Full day tour, siblings Activity before conference, Conference activity). Both cover social/tour activities, but B is specifically temporally after the conference while A is a general social event category, so they overlap without being equivalent.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (a conference/tutorial/workshop activity with titles, locations, choices), while B 'Communications Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area such as Antennas or Cryptography). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (events vs. topics) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Written contribution' is a conference paper/document submitted to a conference, a subclass of Conference contribution. B 'Card' is a physical item (parent Item, child Credit card, siblings Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle) — a payment/identity card, not a conference document. Different domains and no shared instances.

A's property is a specific important-date relation (acceptance announcement date) whose domain is the Important dates class, while B's Date is a generic deadline date property with domain Deadline. They relate different kinds of things (announcement date vs. deadline date) and are not the same relation.

A is an administrative event (the reviewing procedure/activity) in confOf, while B is a deadline (a point in time) for submissions in iasted. They belong to different branches (Event vs Time/Deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's partOfEvent is a mereological relation between Events (an event being part of another event), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (a person needing an item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Invited Talk' is a kind of presentation/event (an Individual Presentation under Scientific Event), while B's 'Invited Speaker' is a kind of person (a Speaker under Person). They denote different categories (event vs. person) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Personal Review History' is a collection/history of reviews performed by a reviewer (a Personal History subclass, with properties linking Reviewer to the history). B's 'Review' is a single review document (a Document subclass, with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review and properties linking Paper to Review). One is an aggregate history of reviewing activity, the other an individual review artefact; their instances do not coincide.

A's Conference is the top-level conference entity (has submissions, dates, administrators, members), while B's Conference Dinner is a specific meal event under Conference Event > Non Academic Event > Meal Event. They denote different concepts; the shared word 'Conference' is incidental.

Author in edas is a person role (a subclass of Person, with children like Presenter and properties linking to papers), whereas Form in iasted is a document type (subclass of Document, with children like Registration form and Author information form). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad class of persons taking part in a conference, with subclasses Active/Passive conference participant and siblings like Committee member, Reviewer, Track workshop chair. B's 'Agency Staff Member' is a person employed by an agency (e.g. staff at the organising agency), a sibling of Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer and Student in ekaw. The two denote different roles: agency staff are not necessarily conference participants, and conference participants need not be agency staff. Despite both being subclasses of Person, their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Tutorial Chair is a Conference Participant and PC Member role responsible for tutorials, a specialized role alongside Demo Chair, Workshop Chair, etc. In sigkdd, Program Chair is an Organizator (organizing role) alongside General Chair and Webmaster, responsible for the overall program. The two denote different roles in different role hierarchies (participant/PC member vs organizer), so they are not equivalent; a Tutorial Chair is not a Program Chair.

Both denote the monetary charge for conference participation: A's 'Conference fees' is the general class of fees, and B's 'Fee' has children Registration fee and Sponzor fee, i.e. the same concept of a conference fee. The plural/singular difference and the shared domain (conference organisation) indicate synonymy.

A's Workshop is a type of working event (a conference activity), while B's Session chair is a role/person (a Delegate subtype). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role), so they are unrelated.

Both denote a speaker who gives an invited/plenary lecture at a conference. In ekaw, Invited Speaker is a subclass of Presenter (a person who presents at a conference); in iasted, Plenary lecture speaker is a subclass of Author/Speaker, i.e. a person who gives a plenary (invited) lecture. The intended instances coincide: distinguished speakers invited to give a keynote/plenary talk. The differing parent chains reflect different modelling choices (Presenter vs Author/Speaker), not different concepts.

A 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area (a kind of Topic) in the edas ontology, while a 'Tutorial Abstract' is a document type (a kind of Abstract) in the ekaw ontology. They belong to different branches (Topic vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'write Review' relates a Reviewer to a Review (domain Reviewer, range Review), while B's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer). Different ranges and different intended meanings (writing a review vs. being invited by a reviewer), so they are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract is a document type (an abstract of a paper) in cmt, while Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship level in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. sponsors) and share no intended instances.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a conference/event type (a subclass of Conference in edas, alongside Single Level Conference), whereas B 'Registration SIGKDD Member' is a fee category (a subclass of Registration fee in sigkdd, alongside Non Member/Student fees). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a scientific conference with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's 'Conference airport' is a Building/Place (a physical venue such as an airport used for a conference). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a specific kind of conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B's 'Document' is a broad class covering many document types (forms, invitations, submissions, reviews). The A class is therefore narrower than B's Document, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A 'Session Chair' is a Person role (a person who chairs a session), while B 'Regular Session' is an Event/Session type (a kind of scientific event). They belong to different top-level categories (Person vs Event) and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of scientific event / individual presentation (a talk given at the conference), while B's 'Invited Speaker' is a kind of person (a speaker role). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'technically Organises' is a subproperty of 'organises' with domain Organisation (an organisation technically organises a conference/event), while B's 'is occupied by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'has tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a whole-part containment relation, sibling of 'has parts'). B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (an authorship/presentation relation). Different domains (Conference volume vs Document), different ranges (Tutorial vs Speaker), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference participant' is the general class of all people participating in a conference (its children include Active/Passive conference participant, Reviewer, Committee member, etc.), whereas B's 'Presenter' is a specific kind of conference participant (a person who presents, with child Invited Speaker). Thus Conference participant is broader and subsumes Presenter; they are not equivalent.

A's contributes goes Person -> Conference document (a person contributes a document), while B's presentationed by goes Document -> Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). The directions are opposite and the roles differ: contributing is not the same relation as being presented by, and neither is the inverse of the other (inverse of contributes would be Document -> Person, not Document -> Speaker).

A's 'is Reviewing' relates a committee member (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper they review. B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. Different domain (reviewer vs document), different range (paper vs speaker), and different meaning (reviewing vs presenting). No equivalence or subsumption.

A's markConflictOfInterest relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to record a conflict of interest, while B's notification_until relates an Author to a notification deadline. Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's contributes links a Person to a Conference document (a person contributes a paper/document to a conference), while B's presentation links a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presents a document). The domains differ (Person vs Speaker, where Speaker is a narrower role) and the intended relations differ (contributing vs presenting), so they are not equivalent; they overlap in that both connect an agent to a document in the conference domain.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it; B's 'is paid by' links Money to the Person who pays it. Different domains (Presentation vs Money), different ranges (participant vs Person), and different meanings (delivery vs payment), so the properties are unrelated.

A's External Reviewer is a Person who reviews papers for another Reviewer but is not a Reviewer; B's Author is a Speaker (a Delegate) who writes papers. Different roles with different parents (Person vs Speaker) and different properties (review assignment vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A's Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while B's Poster is a kind of conference contribution/document (a presentation format with an abstract). They denote different concepts: a person versus a document/contribution type, so they are unrelated.

A's property links an Administrator to a Conference (mailing hardcopy manifests), while B's property links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's writeReview goes from Reviewer to Review (a reviewer writes a review), while B's reviews goes from Review to Reviewed contribution (a review reviews a contribution). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the directions differ, so they are not the same relation; they are not even inverses since the endpoints differ.

A's 'Conference www' is a document (a web page/URL about the conference, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with property has a URL), whereas B's 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session at which accepted papers are presented, related to Accepted Paper). They denote different kinds of things (document vs. event) and share no intended instances.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Satellite And Space Communications Topic' is a research topic category in EDAS. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference contributor is a broad role class under Person whose children include Active conference participant, Invited speaker and Regular author, i.e. anyone contributing to a conference. Presenter in ekaw is a narrower role under Conference Participant, with only Invited Speaker as a child, denoting someone who presents at the conference. The two overlap (a presenter is a kind of conference contributor) but are not coextensive: contributors need not present, and the ekaw Presenter is restricted to conference participants. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (a dinner/banquet activity) in the ekaw ontology, sibling of Conference Trip under Social Event. B 'Sponsor city' is a subclass of City, i.e. a city that sponsors, a location concept, sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Trip city. One is an event, the other a city/location; they share no intended instances and are semantically unrelated.

A's Form is a Document subtype for administrative forms (author information, hotel registration, registration), while B's Paper is the scientific contribution submitted by an author. Different intended instances and different subtrees; the shared parent Document is too generic to make them equivalent.

A's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship of a paper). B's is_designed_for relates an Activity/Money/Time to an Activity/Person (purpose/design of an event or resource). The domains and ranges differ substantially and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasCall relates an Academic Event to a Call (conference call for papers), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (a person requires an item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's has Decision links a Paper to its Decision (the accept/reject outcome for a submission). B's follows links one Administrative event to another (temporal ordering of events). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence.

A's Conference is a working event (a scientific event with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's Presenter university is a building/place (sibling of Conference airport, Conference hotel, etc.). They denote entirely different kinds of things — an event versus a venue building — so they are unrelated.
Both ontologies model conference organization concepts, but confOf and iasted are distinct ontologies with different scopes and vocabularies; the candidate pair is related rather than equivalent.

A's volumeContainsPaper relates a volume (proceedings) to the papers it contains, while B's write relates a Person (author) to an Item (paper). Different domain and range and different direction of relation, so they are not equivalent.

A is a confOf administrative event class (Submission event, the act/process of submitting contributions, sibling of Reviewing event and Camera Ready event), while B is an iasted deadline class (Camera ready manuscript deadline, a point in time under Deadline). Different kinds (event vs. deadline) and different intended instances; the shared word 'submission/camera ready' does not make them equivalent.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper (a specific part/version of a paper), while Paper in sigkdd is the general paper class. The abstract is a narrower concept, so Paper Abstract is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

Both are direct subclasses of Person representing people involved in a conference. cmt's Conference Member has children Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, Conference Chair, Associated Chair; Conference's Conference contributor has children Regular author, Reviewer, Invited speaker, Active conference participant. The intended instances coincide: any person contributing to a conference (authors, reviewers, committee members, chairs). The sibling sets differ slightly (cmt also lists Chairman/External Reviewer/User as siblings, Conference lists Committee member/Conference applicant/Conference participant/Track workshop chair), but the core meaning of a person contributing to a conference is the same, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A Tutorial is a kind of scientific event / individual presentation (a session given at a conference), whereas B 'Cd proceening' is a publication item (a CD of proceedings), a physical/digital artefact. Different kinds of things despite both being conference-domain entities.

A's Passive conference participant is a conference participant who does not actively contribute (sibling of Active conference participant), while B's Worker non speaker is a delegate at a conference building who is a non-speaker, sibling of Student non speaker. Both denote non-speaking attendees, but B is restricted to workers (a subtype of non-speaker delegate) and A is a broader passive participant category; they overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so related.

Both are datatype properties mapping an entity to a string name/title, but their domains differ: A's 'has a name' applies to a broad set of conference entities (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic), while B's 'has Title' applies specifically to Contribution. They overlap in intent (naming/titling) but are not the same relation, so 'related' rather than 'equivalent'.

A's 'is equipped by' relates a Place to an Item (equipment/facility of a venue), while B's 'obtain' relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving a prize). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

Author is a person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers), while Tutorial is a kind of conference part/event (sibling of Track and Workshop). Their contexts, parents, siblings and properties do not overlap; they denote different concepts.

Both denote the role of a person who chairs a conference committee: cmt's Associated Chair is a Chairman and Conference Member, and Conference's Chair is a Committee member with properties linking it to a Committee as its chair. The labels differ but the intended instances (committee chairs) coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is a committee that selects award winners. They belong to different branches (document vs. committee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a subclass of 'Regular author' (a role/author type), while B's 'Contribution' is the general conference contribution (paper/poster/short paper) with properties like hasTitle, writes, writtenBy. The A entity is a kind of author role, not a contribution, so it is strictly narrower and unrelated in kind; it is subsumed by the broader contribution concept only in the loose sense of being part of the contribution-authoring structure, hence subsumed_by rather than equivalent.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted; B's 'default Choice' is a positiveInteger on Social/Working event (confTool) indicating a default choice count. Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Two Level Conference' (edas) is a conference/event type that is also a Person/TPC Member in the edas hierarchy, denoting a conference with a two-tier programme committee structure. B 'Agency Staff Member' (ekaw) is a Person who works for an agency, a human role unrelated to conference organisation structure. Different kinds of entities (event vs. person role), no shared instances.

Subject Area in cmt is a topic classification of papers (Paper -> Subject Area), while Location in ekaw is a physical/geographic venue where events are held (Event -> Location, Location -> Event). They denote different concepts with no overlap in instances or properties.

Both classes denote a generic location/place in the conference domain. EDAS Place is the parent of Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place and is linked to Conference Event via has Location / is Location Of. SIGKDD Place is the parent of Conference hall, Hotel, Main office and is the range of can stay in (Person -> Place). The children (accommodation, venue, meeting room vs. hall, hotel, office) and the event-location / person-stay properties all describe the same broad notion of a physical place associated with conference activities, so the two classes are intended to coincide.

A's 'Review preference' is a reviewer's declared preference/degree over topics or submissions (properties: has a degree, belongs to reviewers, has a topic or submission contribution), whereas B's 'Review' is a Document subclass representing an actual review of a paper. The two denote different concepts (preference vs. review document), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference state' is a state/status of a conference (sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state under State), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (sibling of Hotel and Main office under Place). They denote different concepts (status vs. location) and are unrelated.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address), while B's 'writtenBy' is an object property linking a Document to a Person (authorship). They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

cmt:User is a subclass of cmt:Person, restricted to conference actors (Author, Reviewer, Administrator, Chairman, etc.). confOf:Person is the general superclass of all persons including Administrator, Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, Scholar, Science Worker, Volunteer, with personal data properties. User is narrower than Person, so User is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.

A's max Papers is a datatype property of Program Committee Member giving the maximum number of papers a reviewer may be assigned (range int). B's done till is a datatype property of Deadline giving a date by which something is done (range date). Different domains, different ranges, different intended meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Camera Ready event' is an administrative event in confOf (a deadline/phase in the submission workflow, sibling of Submission and Reviewing events), whereas B 'Conference' is a scientific event denoting one edition of a conference. They denote different concepts: a workflow milestone versus the conference itself, so they are not equivalent.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a person belongs to a conference, e.g. as committee member/participant). B's is signed by relates an Item to a Person (a person signs an item, e.g. a paper/review). The domains differ (Conference vs Item) and the intended relations differ (membership vs signing), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'scientifically Organises' has domain Academic Institution and concerns organising scientific events (conferences/workshops), while B's 'occupy' has domain Person and range Building/City/State, denoting a person occupying a place. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Both are classes named Review, both are direct subclasses of Document, and in the conference domain a review is the document/assessment produced by a reviewer. The shared parent Document and identical intended meaning (a review document) make them equivalent despite differing sibling sets.

In cmt, Associated Chair is a subclass of Chairman (a person who chairs/assists in chairing, alongside Conference Chair, PC Chair, PC Member, Reviewer). In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a subclass of Organizator, sibling to General Chair, Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, Webmaster. The cmt counterpart of a PC member is Program Committee Member (a sibling of Associated Chair), not Associated Chair. Associated Chair denotes a chairing role, whereas Program Committee member denotes a committee membership role; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'has short title' is a datatype property linking a Social/Working event to a string (a short name/title), while B's 'has Start Date Time' links a Conference Event to a dateTime (a temporal value). They relate different kinds of things (string vs dateTime) and have different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Week Reject Rating' is a review-rating category (a rating value assigned to a paper, sibling of Accept/Reject Rating) within the review process, whereas B's 'Refusing manuscript' is an activity in the conference timeline (sibling of Accepting/Receiving manuscript). Both concern rejection, but one is a rating class and the other an activity, so they are not equivalent; they are only loosely related by the rejection concept.

A's property links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (a role-to-event relation within the conference structure), while B's eventOnList links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (a publication/listing relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Presenter is a subclass of Conference Participant (a person role who presents a paper), while B's Sponsor state is a subclass of State (a status/phase of a sponsor, not a person). Different kinds of entities and different domains, so they are unrelated.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class (parent of Author, Reviewer, Chair, PC Member) covering anyone affiliated with a conference, while Active conference participant in Conference is a narrower subclass of Conference contributor/participant restricted to those who give presentations. The two overlap (an active participant is a conference member) but neither subsumes the other cleanly: cmt's Conference Member includes passive attendees and organisers, and Conference's Active conference participant is defined by presentation activity. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference document (submitted/ reviewed/ published paper) under Document, while B's Departure tax is a kind of Tax under Money; the two concepts share no meaning in the conference domain.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a document/paper in the submission stage (a subclass of Paper, with children like Assigned Paper), while B 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is a type of Committee (sibling of Organizing and Program Committees). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (paper vs. committee) and share no intended instances.

A's 'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to the people who review it (Reviewer, TPC Member, chairs), while B's 'is signed by' links an Item to a Person who signs it. Both relate a document-like item to a person, but the intended relations differ: reviewing is not signing, and the ranges differ (reviewer roles vs. any Person). They overlap in the general sense of a person being associated with an item, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B 'Sponzorship' is a subclass of Money (a funding category). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track (a part-whole relation between a conference volume and its tracks), while B's 'has Event' relates an Event to a sub-Event (a mereological/structural relation within the event hierarchy). The domains and ranges differ (Conference volume -> Track vs Event -> Event), so the two properties do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are not equivalent.

A's relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to the Paper Presentation it is presented in (domain Accepted Paper, range Paper Presentation), while B's listsEvent links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (domain Programme Brochure/Web Site, range Event). Different domains, different ranges, and different intended relations (paper-to-presentation vs. document-to-event listing), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's first name), while B's is_used_by is an object property from Item to Person (an item being used by a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and direction/meaning, so they are unrelated.

Chairman in cmt is a general person role (parent of Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair), while Co chair in Conference is a specific committee-member role sibling to Chair. They are related committee roles but not the same concept; a co-chair is not a chairman in general.

A is a person role (Possible Reviewer, a subclass of Person with children PC Member and properties linking to Paper/Review), while B is a financial concept (Departure tax, a subclass of Tax under Money). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A is a conference document about information for participants (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a sponsorship level (Silver Supporter) under Sponzor. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it (domain Presentation, range Active conference participant). B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person who is a member of that conference (domain Conference, range Person). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Bronze Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. sponsor) and denote different concepts.

A's property links a Conference to the Administrator who runs paper assignment tools; B's property links an Individual Presentation to the Paper/Abstract being presented. Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Working event' is a general conference-domain event class (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop; sibling of Administrative/Social event) with properties like has title, location, has Topic. B 'Computer Networks Sensor Topic' is a specific research-topic leaf under Topic > Computer Networks Topic. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference Member' is a Person subclass (a person involved in a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's 'Conference' is a Working event subclass (the event itself). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

confOf Member is a subclass of Participant alongside Regular and Student, i.e. a category of conference participant (likely a member of the organisation/association, comment 'confTool'), whereas ekaw Early Registered Participant is a subclass of Conference Participant distinguished by registration timing, with sibling Late Registered Participant. The two classifications are orthogonal: a Member need not be early registered and an early registered participant need not be a Member, so the classes do not denote the same concept.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a Committee (a group that organizes a conference), while B's 'Session Chair' is a Person role who chairs a session. Different kinds of entities (group vs. person) with no overlap in instances or properties.

A's Workshop is a working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Conference is a scientific event with Workshop as a sibling. In ekaw, Workshop and Conference are distinct sibling classes, so confOf's Workshop does not correspond to ekaw's Conference; they are unrelated.

Meta Reviewer in cmt is a specialized Reviewer role responsible for overseeing reviews and producing a meta-review; Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a broad class of people who could review, with PC Member as a subclass. The two denote different concepts: one is a specific reviewer role, the other a general potential reviewer category. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in the intended sense.

A's 'paper Due On' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime deadline (submission deadline), while B's 'paper Presented As' is an object property linking a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (presentation format). They relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions and domains, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a committee co chair' links a Committee to its Co chair (a committee role), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domains (Committee vs Document), different ranges (Co chair vs Speaker), and different intended relations; they are not the same property.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) written by an Author and reviewed by PC members, whereas Sponsorship in edas is a funding arrangement provided by an Organization with cost amounts. Their instances, properties and contexts do not coincide.

A's hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property from Call to string (textual instructions for submitting to a call), while B's send is an object property from Person to Item (a person sending an item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's runPaperAssignmentTools relates an Administrator to a Conference (running the assignment process), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (submitting a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's `name` is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's `Nation` is a nationality/country property only for Person. They denote different attributes (name vs. nation), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasFax is a datatype property linking a Person to a fax number string, while B's authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document. They share neither domain/range types nor meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Demo Session' is a type of scientific event/session (a scheduled gathering where demos are presented), while B 'Session room' is a type of place (a physical room where sessions are held). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are social events of a conference, but Banquet (a meal) and Excursion (a trip) are distinct kinds of social event; they are siblings under Social event in both ontologies, so they are related rather than equivalent.

In cmt, Paper is a specific document type (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version) that is reviewed, assigned to reviewers, and has decisions. In confOf, Contribution is the broader category of submitted work, with Paper, Poster, and Short paper as subclasses. Thus cmt:Paper is a narrower concept than confOf:Contribution, so Paper is subsumed by Contribution rather than equivalent.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role/position class for the first author of a contribution (sibling: 'Contribution co author'), while B's 'Author of paper student' is a subclass of Author denoting a student author of a paper (sibling: 'Author of paper'). The first-author role and the student-author role are different concepts; neither subsumes the other.

Both denote the classification subject of a paper/contribution: cmt's Subject Area is the range of 'has Subject Area' (Paper -> Subject Area), and confOf's Topic is the range of 'deals With' (Contribution -> Topic), with additional uses for PC expertise and working-event topics. The intended instances (research topics/subject areas) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a paper), while B's is_equipped_by relates a Place to an Item (equipment of a venue). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'Passive conference participant' is a conference participant who does not actively contribute (sibling of 'Active conference participant'), i.e. an attendee who is not a speaker. B's 'Student non speaker' is a delegate who is a non-speaker and specifically a student, sibling of 'Worker non speaker'. Both denote non-speaking attendees, so they overlap, but B is restricted to students whereas A covers any passive participant (including workers, guests, etc.). Neither subsumes the other cleanly across the two taxonomies, so 'related' is the safest relation.

A 'Signal Processing Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in the edas ontology, whereas B 'Simulating' is a research activity (a kind of work done before a conference) under Activity > Research in iasted. A topic and an activity are different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference document' is a broad class of documents (calls, announcements, contributions, reviews) with authors and issue dates. B's 'Conference Session' is a scheduled event/session, not a document, and is related to documents only via 'has Related Document'/'relates To'. The two denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a written paper). B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domain/range concepts (Author vs Speaker) and different intended relations (authorship vs presentation), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to its Review (domain Reviewed contribution, range Review). B's 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and direction of meaning; they do not relate the same kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's Chairman is a person role (a subclass of Person, with children like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), while B's Computer Networks Security Topic is a subject area under Topic. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. topic) and share no meaning in the conference domain.

Excursion is a specific kind of social event (a trip/outing), while ekaw's Social Event is the general category that also covers banquets and conference trips. Excursion is therefore strictly narrower than Social Event, not equivalent to it.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a paper receiving a bid/review offer), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person mapping to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'has amount of' is a datatype property of Money mapping to an int (a monetary quantity). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they denote no common relation.

A's 'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation). B's 'reviewes' relates a PC member to a Contribution (reviewing relation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'is paid with' is an object property linking Money to an Item (the means of payment). They share neither domain, range, nor intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

Subject Area in cmt is a topic classification of papers (range of has Subject Area, Paper -> Subject Area). Review preference in Conference is a reviewer's preference/degree of interest in a topic or submission contribution, linked to reviewers and review expertise. One is a topic category, the other a preference relation between a reviewer and a topic; their instances do not coincide.

A's 'has a submitted contribution' links a reviewer's expertise to a submitted contribution (domain Review expertise, range Submitted contribution). B's 'awarded by' links an Award to the entity that granted it (domain Award). They relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Speaker lecture' is a subclass of Session (a kind of conference activity/session in the iasted ontology), whereas B's 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person (an organizing role in sigkdd). They denote different kinds of things (an event/session vs. a person role), so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'has First Name' is a specific datatype property for a person's first name (comment mentions middle name), while sigkdd's 'Name' is the general name of a person. A first name is a kind of name, so hasFirstName is strictly narrower than Name; they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role in the conference organisation (a Chairman/Conference Member who chairs the conference), while B 'Hotel presenter' is a Delegate subtype in the Place/Building branch, i.e. a presenter staying at the conference hotel. Their paths, parents and siblings differ entirely (Chairman vs Delegate), so they denote different concepts.

A is a research topic in wireless communications (a subject area under Topic in the EDAS ontology), while B is a physical transport vehicle (a class of items with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session/activity at the conference) whose related papers are Accepted Papers; B 'Author of paper' is a role of a person (a subclass of Author/Speaker). One denotes an event, the other a person role, so their instances cannot coincide.

A 'Written contribution' is a conference contribution (a paper-like submission, with children Regular/Submitted contribution), while B 'Document' is a broad administrative item covering forms, invitation letters, payment documents, reviews, submissions, etc. They overlap in that a written contribution can be a document, but neither subsumes the other cleanly: Document is far broader and includes non-contribution artefacts, and Written contribution is a specific contribution type. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Value added tax is a monetary tax concept under Money > Tax. They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'Program committee' is a committee (a group of people) that reviews papers, sibling of Organizing/Steering committee. B's 'Administrative event' is a subclass of Event covering submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration, etc. A committee is not an event; the concepts are disjoint in the conference domain.

Sponzorship (sponsorship money) and Registration fee are different financial concepts: sponsorship is money given by sponsors, while registration fee is paid by attendees. They are siblings under Money/Fee but denote distinct concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A Bid in cmt is a reviewer's expressed willingness/offer to review a Paper (adjust Bid, adjusted By, has Bid from Paper), whereas Conference's Review preference is a reviewer's stated preference over topics/submissions used for matching (has a degree, has a topic or a submission contribution, belongs to reviewers). Both concern reviewer-to-paper/topic matching, so they overlap, but a Bid is a concrete offer on a paper while a Review preference is a topic-level preference, so they are not the same concept.

A's Topic is a general conference topic class (used by Contribution, Member PC, Working event), while B's Cryptography Topic is a specific subclass of Topic. Thus A is broader and B is strictly more specific, so A is subsumed by B's parent Topic, not equivalent to the narrower Cryptography Topic.

An Invited speaker is a distinguished person invited to give a talk, while a Presenter is any author who presents a paper. The concepts overlap (both can present at a conference) but neither subsumes the other: an invited speaker is not necessarily an author/presenter in the edas sense, and a presenter is not necessarily invited. Thus they are related, not equivalent.

Trip is a specific kind of social event (a trip/excursion), while Social Event is the broader category that includes excursions, receptions, meals, etc. Thus Trip is strictly more specific than Social Event, so Trip is subsumed by Social Event rather than equivalent.

A's 'set Max Papers' is an administrative action assigning a paper limit to a Program Committee Member (domain Administrator, range Program Committee Member). B's 'follows' is a temporal ordering relation between Administrative events (domain and range Administrative event). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Chair PC' is a Person who chairs the program committee (a role held by a person, sibling of Author/Participant under Person). B's 'Program Committee member' is an Organizator role, sibling of Program Chair and General Chair, i.e. a member of the PC rather than its chair. The two denote different roles (chair vs. member) in the PC, so they are not equivalent; they overlap only in both being PC-related person roles, hence 'related'.

cmt:Document is a general document class whose children are Paper and Review, and which is the range of a conflict-of-interest property. edas:Review Question is a question asked during reviewing, with children Numerical Review Question and Textual Review Question. A document and a review question denote different concepts; they do not coincide in the conference domain.

attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event (the person attends the event), while prepare relates a Person to an Item (the person prepares an item). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who funds it); B's 'is given by' links an Activity/Item to a Person (who presents/delivers it). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's Paper is a specific document type (a submitted contribution with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Document is a broad category covering forms, invitations, mailing lists, payments, etc. Paper is one kind of Document, so Paper is subsumed by Document, not equivalent.

A's Registration is a conference activity (an event/process during the conference, with child Delegate), while B's Organizator is a person role (a subclass of Person, with children like General Chair, Program Chair). They denote different kinds of things (activity vs. person role), so they are unrelated.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (adding a member), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (authorship/presentation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title; B's location is a datatype property of Social event/Working event giving where an event is held. Different domains, different intended meaning, no overlap.

A's Meal Menu is a Document (a menu artefact for a meal event, with has Menu / is Menu Of properties), while B's Tip is a Money subclass (a gratuity payment, sibling of Fee, Sponsorship, Tax). Different domains and no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

Both denote a tutorial as a conference activity/part. In Conference, Tutorial is a sibling of Workshop and Track under 'Conference part', i.e. a type of conference event. In iasted, Tutorial is a subclass of Lecture under Conference activity, also a type of conference event. The intended instances (tutorial sessions at a conference) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite differing parent hierarchies.

confOf's Scholar is a Person subclass used as a price/fee category (comment 'price category - scholar') with a studyAt property to University, i.e. a student-type participant. sigkdd's Invited Speaker is a Speaker subclass (a person invited to give a talk), sibling of Author. The two denote different roles in the conference domain and share no properties or context, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has short title' is a datatype property mapping an event to a string (an abbreviation of the event's title), while B's 'has Event' is an object property relating an Event to another Event (e.g. a sub-event or part-of relation). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain/range (string vs Event), and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A is the inverse of a partOf property whose range is Event (i.e. it relates an Event to its parts, likely sub-events or components), while B 'is given by' relates an Activity or Item to a Person (the agent who gives/presents it). The kinds of things related (Event-to-part vs Activity/Item-to-Person) and the direction of the relation differ, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to its website URI, while B's 'early Registration' links a Participant to a boolean indicating early registration. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to the people who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), while B's 'is prepared by' links an Item to a Person who prepares it. The domains (Call vs Item) and ranges (specific chair/committee roles vs generic Person) differ, and the intended relations (initiating a call vs preparing an item) are distinct, so they are not equivalent.

A's Review is a subclass of Document in cmt, a scholarly review of a paper (written by a Reviewer, ended by the PC Chair, with Meta Review as a child). B's Payment document is a subclass of Document in iasted, an administrative payment artefact with children Bank transfer and Cheque. Although iasted also has a separate Review class (a sibling of Payment document), the candidate pairs cmt:Review with iasted:Payment document, which denote different concepts.

Both classes denote the general concept of a person in the conference domain. In edas, Person is the superclass of Attendee, Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member, etc., and is linked to conferences, documents and contact information. In ekaw, Person is likewise the superclass of Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student, etc., and is linked to documents and events. The intended instances coincide: any human involved in the conference organisation. The differing children reflect different sub-taxonomies, not a different concept.

A's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution holding the abstract text (range string), while B's 'manuscript Due On' is a Conference deadline property with range dateTime. They relate different kinds of things (text vs. date) in different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's Call For Papers is a call/announcement event (sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews, under Call), while B's Abstract is a document part (sibling of Paper and Review, under Document). They denote different concepts: an announcement versus a document component, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Chair is a specific role (chair of the conference, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while B Conference Participant is a broad class covering all people participating in a conference (including chairs, presenters, authors, etc.). Every Conference Chair is a Conference Participant, but not vice versa, so Conference Chair is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Conference Participant.

Author (cmt) is a conference member who writes/submits papers, while Sponzor (sigkdd) is a sponsor organisation that supports the conference financially; their children, properties and domain roles do not overlap, so they denote different concepts.

A's Workshop is an Academic Event (a type of event/meeting), while B's Demo Session is a Session (a slot within a conference). Although B has a sibling Workshop Session, the candidate pairs Workshop with Demo Session, which are different concepts: a workshop is a meeting, a demo session is a session type. They are not equivalent.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to the contribution they review (domain Member PC, range Contribution). B's `is given to` relates an Item to the Person it is given to (domain Item, range Person), i.e. the direction and the kinds of things related are different (and it is closer to an inverse of a review relation). They are not equivalent.

A is a document type (an abstract of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B is a research topic category (Mobile Computing Topic, sibling of other topics under Topic). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A is a post-conference social activity (siblings: Activity before conference, Conference activity; children: Departure, Full day tour), while B is a physical location (Place > Main office, siblings Conference hall, Hotel). Different kinds and domains, so they are unrelated.

A's 'read By Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer who reads the paper), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (the person who writes the item). They differ in domain (Paper vs Person), range (Reviewer vs Item), and direction of the authoring/reading relation; they are not the same relation nor inverses.

A is a person role (Chairman, a subclass of Person with subroles like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), while B is a monetary fee (Hotel fee, a subclass of Fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the presenter), while B's 'is Written By' links a Paper to an Author. Different domains (Presentation vs Paper) and different ranges (participant/presenter vs author), so the relations do not coincide.

Committee member is a subclass of Person in Conference (path Person > Committee member), while confOf's Person is the general superclass of all people (Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, etc.). A committee member is a kind of person, so Committee member is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference domain), while B's Best Student Paper Award is a subclass of Award (a prize for a paper). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. award) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair in cmt is a chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), whereas Presenter in ekaw is a conference participant who presents (parent Conference Participant, child Invited Speaker). One is an organising/chairing role, the other a presenting participant role; their intended instances do not coincide.

ekaw:Person is a general person class (children include Conference Participant, Paper Author, Student, etc.), while sigkdd:Speaker is a narrower subclass of Person (siblings Listener, Organizator; children Author, Invited Speaker) representing someone who gives a presentation. Every Speaker is a Person, but not every Person is a Speaker, so Person is more general and Speaker is subsumed by it.

A's 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor (a role a person plays in producing a contribution), while B's 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Speaker under Person (a person who gives an invited talk). They denote different concepts: an author of a regular contribution vs. an invited speaker, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (where the event takes place), while B's 'is sent before' relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering of items). Different domain, range, and meaning; no subsumption or overlap.
Both properties link a paper to the volume/proceedings it appears in; identical domain (Paper) and range (Volume/Proceedings), so they denote the same relation.

edas:TwoLevelConference is a conference type (a conference with two levels, e.g. main conference plus workshops), a subclass of Conference. iasted:One_conference_day is a temporal entity, a single day within the conference days, a subclass of Conference days under Time. They denote different concepts (conference vs. time interval) and share no intended instances.

A's hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event (domain Event, range Event), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract, while B's 'is Written By' links a Paper to an Author. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (the proceedings/venue where the paper is submitted), while B's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (where the event takes place). Different domains and ranges and different intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'writtenBy' is an object property mapping a Document to a Person (authorship). They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'early Registration' is a boolean datatype property on Participant indicating whether a participant registered early; B's 'has First Name' is a string datatype property on Person giving a person's first name. They relate different kinds of things (registration status vs. name) and have different ranges (boolean vs. string), so they are unrelated.

Trip is a social event (an excursion/activity) in confOf, while Double hotel room is a type of accommodation place in iasted. They belong to different branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Trip is a social event involving an excursion/outing, while a Dinner banquet is a meal event. Both are social events but denote different kinds of activities; they are siblings under the social-event branch rather than the same concept.

Contribution in confOf is a general class whose children include Paper, Poster, and Short paper, so it is broader than edas Paper. Paper in edas is a specific kind of contribution (a document), so Contribution subsumes Paper rather than being equivalent.

Attendee (edas) is a general person who attends the conference, while Presenter (ekaw) is a Conference Participant who presents, a more specific role with child Invited Speaker. The two overlap (a presenter is typically an attendee) but neither subsumes the other cleanly: Attendee is broader than Presenter, yet Presenter is a distinct role not equivalent to the general attendee concept.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to the Reviewer it is assigned to (reviewing workflow). B's 'is the 1th part of' links an Abstract to the Paper/Poster/Presentation it is part of (part-whole composition). Different domains (Paper vs Abstract), different ranges (Reviewer vs Paper/Poster/Presentation), and different meanings (assignment vs partonomy), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Hiker' is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference), while B 'Conference hall' is a subclass of Place (a physical location). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. location) and are not equivalent.

Conference contributor is a broad class covering all people who contribute to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors), while Listener in sigkdd denotes a passive attendee who only listens, sibling to Speaker and Organizator. The two overlap in that both are persons involved in a conference, but Listener is much narrower and excludes authors/speakers, so they are not equivalent; the broader contributor class subsumes a listener-like role only loosely, making 'related' the safest relation.

Conference Chair is a person role in the conference organization (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while Coffee break is a conference activity/event. They belong to disjoint branches of the ontology (Person vs Activity) and share no meaning.

A 'Poster Session' is a specific kind of Session (a scientific event session), while B 'Session' is a broader conference activity/lecture type. A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, i.e. the person chairing the whole conference. In edas, Session Chair is a distinct role (chairing a single session) and is a sibling of Conference Chair, not the same concept. The two denote different roles in the conference domain.

Both denote the published collection of conference papers: A's 'Conference proceedings' is a Conference part with a publisher, volume and ISBN, and B's 'Proceedings' is a Multi author Volume whose child is Conference Proceedings, i.e. the same bibliographic artefact.

NGO is a specific subtype of Organization (a non-governmental organization), while Organization in the Conference ontology is the general superclass. NGO is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by Organization rather than equivalent.

Chair PC in confOf is a person who chairs the program committee (a specific role), while Organizator in sigkdd is a broader class of people involved in organizing the conference, with children including General Chair, Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, etc. Chair PC is thus a more specific role subsumed by the broader Organizator class, not equivalent.

A's hasEmail relates a Person to an email string, while B's hasPostalCode relates Contact Information to a postal code string. Different domains (Person vs Contact Information) and different ranges (email vs postal code) mean they denote different relations, not the same concept.

A relates a Topic to a Review preference (a topic's review preference), while B relates an Author to a Deadline Author notification (an author's notification deadline). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Conference is the whole conference event (has members, dates, submissions, administrators), while B's Conference fees is a fee/payment concept, not the conference event itself. Different intended instances, so not equivalent.

Banquet is a social event (a meal/ceremony) in confOf, while Speaker is a person role in sigkdd who gives a presentation. They belong to different branches (Event vs Person) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's has Author is an object property linking a Paper to an Author; B's has an ISBN is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to a string. Different domain, range, and kind, so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties named 'written By' linking a written work (Contribution/Document) to its author (Author/Person). Contribution and Document denote the same concept (a paper/contribution), and Author and Person coincide in the conference domain, so the relations are the same in the same direction.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Speaker lecture is a session within a lecture, a part of a conference activity. They denote different concepts at different granularities and are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Tutorial speaker is a person role (an Author who speaks at a tutorial). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Working event (confOf) is a general event category (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) in the event hierarchy, while Multi author Volume (ekaw) is a document/publication type (parent of Proceedings) in the document hierarchy. They belong to different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

edas:relatesTo is a broad Document-to-entity relation whose range includes Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session and Person, whereas ekaw:paperPresentedAs is a narrow relation from Abstract/Paper to Individual Presentation only. The ekaw property is essentially a special case of the edas relation (a paper being presented as a presentation is one way a document relates to an event), so they overlap but are not equivalent; the edas property is strictly more general.

A's endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (ending the review process), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (submitting a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Publisher in the Conference ontology is an agent/organisation that issues conference proceedings (it has a name and issues Conference proceedings), whereas Location in ekaw is a place where an Event is held (held In / location Of). They denote different concepts with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Review is a subclass of Document (path Document > Review), and in ekaw, Review is also a child of Document. However, the candidate pair compares cmt:Review with ekaw:Document, not with ekaw:Review. ekaw:Document is a broader class whose children include Abstract, Flyer, Paper, Review, etc., so cmt:Review is strictly more specific than ekaw:Document. Thus cmt:Review is subsumed by ekaw:Document, not equivalent.

A's Author is a person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers), while B's 'Author attendee cd registration fee' is a monetary fee category (a registration fee amount for an author attendee paying by CD). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money/Fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a name' is a datatype property giving a string name to entities such as Conference, Publisher, Topic, etc. B's 'min Choice' is a datatype property giving a positiveInteger minimum choice for Social event / Working event (confTool). They have different domains, different ranges (string vs positiveInteger), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper they have been assigned to review), while write relates a Person to an Item (authored work). Different domain (Reviewer vs Person) and range (Paper vs Item), and different intended meaning (review assignment vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is visited by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a place is visited by a person), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (an author submits a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same property.

Participant in confOf is a subclass of Person (a person attending the conference, with subclasses Member, Regular, Student and a property early Registration), whereas Fee in sigkdd is a payment/fee concept with subclasses Registration fee and Sponzor fee. They denote different kinds of things (person vs. payment) and are not equivalent.

confOf Scholar is a price category (a person attending under a scholar fee, with a study At property to a University), while ekaw SC Member is a member of the Steering Committee, a subrole of PC Member. Different intended instances and different positions in the hierarchy, so they are not equivalent.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while Attendee in edas is a general person who attends the conference. They denote different concepts: one is an organizational role, the other a participation status. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

Academic Institution is an Organisation (a social/institutional entity that organises conferences scientifically), while Building is a physical Place with children like conference airport, hotel, restaurant and properties about being occupied/visited by persons. They denote different kinds of things and share no instances.

A's hasUpdatedVersion relates a Document to a later version of that same Document (domain Document, range Document), i.e. a versioning relation between documents. B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (domain Speaker, range Document), i.e. a speaker presenting a document. Different domains, different intended meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

Attendee in edas is a general Person role covering anyone attending the conference (siblings include Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, etc.), while iasted's Non speaker is a specific subclass of Delegate denoting a delegate who does not give a talk, with its own children (Student non speaker, Worker non speaker). The two overlap (a non-speaker delegate is an attendee) but neither subsumes the other: Attendee includes speakers, and Non speaker is restricted to delegates. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's has Country relates an Organization/Person to a Country (a location attribute of an agent), while B's is equipped by relates a Place to an Item (equipment of a venue). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Presenter university' is a Building subtype denoting a university where presenters stay/are affiliated, while B's 'Hotel' is a Place subtype denoting lodging. Different intended instances and different paths (Building vs Place), so not equivalent.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (the conflict-of-interest declaration), while B's has_authors relates a Conference document to a Person (authorship). They differ in both direction and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

markConflictOfInterest relates a reviewer/author/chairman to a paper to record a conflict of interest, while isReviewedBy relates a paper to a reviewer/chair to record the review assignment. They have opposite directions and different meanings (conflict vs. review relationship), so they are not equivalent.

A's assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (the act of assigning a reviewer to a paper, from the administrator's side), while B's hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a paper having a candidate reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'event On List' is an object property linking an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (where the event is listed), while B's 'End of conference' is a datatype property giving a Conference's end date/time. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

Both classes are named Poster and sit under a Contribution parent in the conference domain; A's Poster is a kind of conference contribution (with abstract, part of a paper/presentation), and B's Poster is a kind of Contribution alongside Paper and Short paper. The intended instances (poster contributions at a conference) coincide, so they are equivalent.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (a role-to-committee relation), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person-to-artefact/event relation). Different domains and ranges, different intended meaning; not equivalent.

A is an Early Registered Participant (a conference participant distinguished by early registration), while B is a Session chair (a delegate who chairs a session). They are different roles in the conference domain: registration status vs. session-chairing role. Neither subsumes the other, and they do not overlap in intended instances.

A is a person role (a conference contributor who gives presentations), while B is an event/activity category (parent of Presentation, Lecture, Coffee break, etc.). Their intended instances are disjoint: people vs. events. No subsumption or overlap holds.

Conference contributor is a broad role class covering anyone who contributes to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors), while ekaw's Paper Author is specifically a person who authors a paper. Paper Author is one kind of conference contributor, so Conference contributor is more general and subsumes Paper Author; they are not equivalent.

A 'Contribution co author' is a role/type of author (a person who co-authors a contribution), sitting under Regular author in the Conference ontology. B 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference event (a conference with two levels, sibling of Single Level Conference, Attendee, Author, etc.) in edas. They denote entirely different concepts — an author role versus a conference type — so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a paper/contribution to its abstract, but A's range is the class Abstract (object property) while B's range is a plain string (datatype property). They capture the same relation at different modelling granularities, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'end Date' is a datatype property giving the Conference's end date/time (domain Conference, range dateTime). B's 'event On List' is an object property linking an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site where it is listed (domain Event, range Programme Brochure/Web Site). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have incompatible ranges, so they are unrelated.

A 'Review Form' is the artefact/blank form used to record a review, whereas B 'Paper' is the submitted document itself.
