They are different concepts in the conference domain: a review form is not a paper, and a paper is not a review form. The contexts also differ (ReviewForm is a review-related entity, Paper is a Document subclass with a submit property from Author).

A's 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the committee is the subject, the event/volume is the object). B's 'organisedBy' links an Event to an Organisation or Person (the event is the subject, the organiser is the object). The directions and the kinds of entities related are different: A relates a committee to what it organises, B relates an event to who organises it. They are not the same relation, nor inverses of one another (A's range is a Conference volume, not an Organisation/Person).

A's has End Date Time gives the end time of a Conference Event, while B's Start of conference gives the start time of a Conference. They differ in both the temporal aspect (end vs start) and the entity (event vs conference), so they are not equivalent.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing a person's email address; the labels 'email' and 'E mail' are spelling variants of the same concept.

Both are subclasses of Document in the conference domain. Submission in iasted has children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript, i.e. the submitted paper versions, and sigkdd's Paper is the document an Author submits (submit: Author -> Paper). The intended instances coincide: a paper submitted to a conference. Sibling differences (Review, Abstract) reflect modelling granularity, not a different concept.

A's property links a Review preference to the Topic/Submitted contribution it prefers, while B's submit links an Author to the Paper they submit. Different domains (Review preference vs Author), different ranges (Topic/Submitted contribution vs Paper), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.
Both denote the conference paper entity; Paper and Contribution are synonyms in the conference domain with matching context.

A's User is a subclass of Person (a human role in the conference: Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while B's Organization is a collective entity (e.g. a company or institution), not a person. Different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'default Choice' is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a positive integer (a default choice count, confTool-specific), while B's 'done till' is a Deadline property giving a date (the deadline's end date). Different domains (event vs deadline), different ranges (positiveInteger vs date), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Active Paper (edas) is a paper that has been submitted and is under review, with a rating; its children are Rated Papers. Evaluated Paper (ekaw) is a paper that has been assigned to a reviewer and evaluated, with children Accepted/Rejected Paper. Both denote papers in the review process, but Active Paper is broader (any paper currently active, including pending/rated) while Evaluated Paper specifically requires assignment and evaluation. They overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so related.

A's Trip is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception) under Event, i.e. an excursion/outing. B's Trip day is a temporal concept under Time, sibling of Conference days and Deadline, i.e. a day of the trip. Different kinds (event vs. time) and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

EDAS 'Reject Rating' is a specific rating value (a score category used when a review recommends rejection), sibling to Accept Rating, Accept If Room Rating and Week Reject Rating, all subclasses of Review Rating. EKAW 'Negative Review' is a type of Review document (sibling to Neutral Review and Positive Review), i.e. a review whose content/verdict is negative. The two overlap in that a negative review typically carries a reject rating, but one is a rating value and the other is a review document, so they are not equivalent; they are merely related.

confOf's Participant is a subclass of Person (path Person > Participant) restricted to conference attendees with subclasses Member, Regular, Student and an early Registration property. sigkdd's Person is the general superclass of all people (Listener, Organizator, Speaker) with contact and payment properties. Participant is thus strictly more specific than Person, so Participant is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.

A's Associated Chair is a specific chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), whereas B's Conference contributor is a broad class covering all people contributing to a conference (parents Person, children Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author). The Associated Chair is a narrow role, not the general contributor concept, and the two do not coincide in intended instances.

Chairman is a person role in the conference organisation (a subclass of Person, with subclasses Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, etc.), while Fee for extra trip is a monetary charge (subclass of Fee, sibling of Registration fee and Hotel fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (person is a member of a conference), while B's 'is sent by' relates an Item to a Person (an item is sent by a person). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Person->Conference vs Item->Person), and the intended relations differ; they are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

A's writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship of a paper), while B's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

In iasted, Reviewer is a subclass of Speaker (a conference delegate who reviews), whereas in sigkdd Organizing Committee member is a subclass of Organizator (an organizer role such as General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). A reviewer is a participant role, not an organizing committee role, so the two classes denote different concepts.

A's `location Of` relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's `submit until` relates a Document to a Deadline (the submission deadline for that document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Review is a document produced in the conference review process (child of Document, sibling of Paper, written by a Reviewer, subject of Meta Review), while B's Tax is a monetary charge (child of Money, sibling of Fee, Sponsorship, Tip). The shared word 'review' is coincidental; the concepts are in entirely different branches of the domain and cannot denote the same class.

A's property is a datatype property linking an Important dates entity to a submission deadline date for camera-ready papers; B's property is a datatype property linking Social/Working event entities to a location string. They relate different kinds of things (dates vs. locations) in different domains, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a kind of conference event with a two-tier programme committee structure), while B's 'Conference state' is a subclass of State (a status/state of a conference, sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state). They denote different concepts: a conference type versus a state, so they are unrelated.

A's Proceedings is a multi-author volume document (a publication artefact, parent Multi author Volume, child Conference Proceedings). B's Lecturer is a person role under Author (a delegate/speaker who lectures, with children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer). A publication volume and a person role denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic (a subject area under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation such as a contributed talk or tutorial). A topic and an event type denote entirely different things, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that run concurrently, while ekaw's 'event On List' relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site where it is listed. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

External Reviewer (cmt) is a person who reviews papers on behalf of a Reviewer, subordinate to Reviewer/PC Member. Conference Chair (edas) is a senior organising role that initiates calls and reviews papers. Different roles with different properties (assign/assigned By Reviewer vs initiates/is Initiated By/is Reviewed By/is Reviewing); no subsumption either way.

A's hasCountry relates an Organization/Person to a Country (a location), while B's organises relates an Organisation/Person to an Event (an activity they arrange). Different ranges (Country vs Event) and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Program Committee Chair is a chair of the program committee (a subrole of Chairman and PC Member, ending reviews); B's Workshop Chair is a conference participant who chairs a workshop, a sibling of PC Chair, Tutorial Chair, etc. They denote different chairing roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

Security Topic is a specific topic (a child of Topic in edas), while Research Topic is the general topic class in ekaw that events and papers cover. Security Topic is a narrower concept, so it is subsumed by Research Topic, not equivalent.

Both classes are named 'Main office' and sit directly under the same parent 'Place' in their respective ontologies, with sibling classes that are all conference-venue place types (Conference hall, Hotel, Building, Session room). The identical label, identical path, and matching domain context indicate they denote the same concept.

A's Presentation is a conference contribution (a document/event type with an abstract, given by a participant), while B's Speaker is a person role (a subclass of Person who presents a Document). They belong to different branches (contribution vs. person) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a paper that has been rejected. In edas, Rejected Paper is a direct subclass of Paper alongside Accepted/Pending/Published/Withdrawn Paper, i.e. a paper in the rejected state. In ekaw, Rejected Paper is a subclass of Evaluated Paper (a paper that has been evaluated) with sibling Accepted Paper, i.e. a submitted paper whose evaluation outcome is rejection. The intended instances coincide: papers that were rejected. The differing intermediate parents (Paper vs Evaluated Paper) reflect different modelling of the submission/evaluation workflow, not a different concept, so the classes are equivalent.
A's hasMenu relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (catering), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation authorship). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

A is a conference-document class about information for participants (siblings: Call for paper, Review, Conference contribution), while B is a research topic class under Topic (siblings: Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

In edas, Organizational Meeting is a kind of Academic Event (a meeting held during a conference, sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop), whereas in ekaw Conference is a Scientific Event representing one edition of a conference, the parent-level event that contains sessions, tracks and workshops. The two denote different concepts: an organizational meeting is a sub-event within a conference, not the conference itself, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference announcement soliciting submissions, while B 'Record of attendance' is a document recording who attended. They are different document types with no overlap in intended instances.

Both 'Session Chair' classes denote the person role responsible for chairing a conference session; the EDAS class sits under Person alongside Conference Chair/Reviewer/TPC Member, and the EKAW class is the corresponding role concept in the conference domain, so their intended instances coincide.

Member in confOf is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference, with siblings Regular and Student), while Sponsor in iasted is a subclass of Person representing a sponsoring entity, not a participant. The concepts denote different roles in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

Both properties link a paper/conference document to its authors: Conference's 'has authors' has domain Conference document and range Person, while edas's 'is Written By' has domain Paper and range Author. Paper/Conference document and Person/Author denote the same concepts in the conference domain, and both properties relate the same kinds of things in the same direction (document -> author).

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with two levels, sibling of Single Level Conference, under Conference), whereas B 'Delegate' is a person role (a participant/attendee, with children like Speaker, Listener, Session chair). They denote different concepts: an event type vs. a person role, so they are not equivalent.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author (domain Paper, range Author), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (domain Author, range Award). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's User is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Social Event is a non-academic conference event (parent Non Academic Event, children Excursion/Reception). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'assign External Reviewer' relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (domain Reviewer, range External Reviewer), i.e. an assignment relation. B's 'is Review History Of' relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer), i.e. a provenance relation. Different domains, ranges and directions; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers), while B's 'has Call' links an Academic Event to its Call for papers. The domains (volume vs event) and ranges (contribution vs call) differ, so the relations are not the same.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a conference attendee who has registered (a subtype of Conference applicant, with child Paid applicant), i.e. a participant/attendee role. B 'Organizator' is a person who organises the conference (parent of General Chair, Program Chair, PC member, Webmaster), i.e. an organiser role. The two denote disjoint roles in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A is an administrative event (the act/process of registering participants) in confOf, while B is a time point (a deadline for notification of acceptance) in iasted. They belong to different branches (Event vs Time) and denote different concepts: an activity versus a temporal deadline. Although iasted has a 'Registation deadline' sibling, that is a deadline, not the registration event itself, so the two entities are unrelated.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property linking a Review preference to an int (a numeric degree of preference), while B's 'studyAt' is an object property linking a Scholar to a University. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Review preference vs Scholar), and range (int vs University), so they denote different relations.

A's markConflictOfInterest relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to record a conflict of interest, while B's submit relates only an Author to a Paper to record submission. The domains differ (A includes Chairman and Reviewer) and the intended meaning differs (conflict marking vs. paper submission), so they are not equivalent.

A's `name` is a datatype property with range string, applying to Conference and Person, giving a textual name. B's `has Country` is an object property from Conference to Country, linking a conference to a country entity. Different kinds (datatype vs object), different ranges (string vs Country), and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

Track in ekaw is a scientific event (a thematic stream of the conference containing sessions/presentations), while Program Committee in sigkdd is a committee (a group of people reviewing papers). Different kinds of entities with no overlap.

In ekaw, Tutorial is a kind of Individual Presentation (a scientific event where a person presents), sibling to Contributed Talk and Invited Talk. In iasted, Plenary lecture is a kind of Lecture, sibling to Session and Tutorial. The two concepts denote different things: a tutorial is an instructional presentation, while a plenary lecture is a general-session talk. Moreover, in iasted Tutorial is a sibling of Plenary lecture, so they cannot be equivalent. They are unrelated.

A's Conference Session is a session within a conference (a part of an event, related to documents/persons), while B's Conference is the whole conference event with city, start/end dates, name, and held-by relation. A session is not the same concept as a conference; the session is a component of the conference, so the classes are unrelated (not even a clean subsumption since B's Conference is the whole event, not a session).

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Presenter house is a building/place (sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a Paper to the reviewer(s) assigned to it. cmt's 'assigned To' has domain Paper and range Reviewer; ekaw's 'has Reviewer' has domain Paper and range Possible Reviewer, where Possible Reviewer is the class of people who can review (i.e. reviewers). The direction is the same (paper -> reviewer), and the intended relation (a paper has an assigned reviewer) coincides, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a kind of conference lecture/activity (an event type), while B's Organizator is a role of a person (a subclass of Person with children like General Chair, Program Chair). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a person role, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Chair is a high-level organising role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Program Committee Chair and Author), whereas B's Session chair is a Delegate who chairs a single session (sibling of Speaker, Listener, Presenter). The roles differ in scope and in the surrounding hierarchy, so they do not denote the same concept.

A's 'has a name' is a generic naming property whose domain spans Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, whereas B's 'has title' is restricted to Social event and Working event. The domains are disjoint and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing practical information to attendees. B's 'Modelling' is a research activity performed before the conference (sibling of Simulating). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.
A's 'start Date' is the conference start date/time, while B's 'End of conference' is the conference end date/time. They are opposite temporal boundaries of a Conference, not the same relation.

A is a physical place (a type of Place for lodging, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place), while B is a person role (a kind of Lecturer, under Speaker/Author/Delegate in the iasted hierarchy). They denote entirely different concepts: a venue vs. a worker/lecturer, so they are unrelated.

A 'One day presenter' is a Delegate who presents for a single day (a specific attendee role), while B 'Organizator' is a Person who organises the conference, with children General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc. The two denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (a record of reviews a person wrote), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (who presented it). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's relatedToPaper links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a paper-to-paper relation within the submission/presentation structure). B's presentation links a Speaker to a Document (a person-to-artefact relation). Different domains (Paper Presentation vs Speaker) and ranges (Accepted Paper vs Document), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while ekaw's Submitted Paper is a specific stage of a paper (a Paper that has been submitted, with child Assigned Paper and siblings Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, etc.). The ekaw entity is narrower, so confOf Paper is subsumed by ekaw Submitted Paper rather than equivalent.

A's locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the event held at that location). B's Currency is a datatype property linking a Registration fee to a string (the currency code). They relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions and domains, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' links a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it (domain Review, range Reviewer), while B's 'invites co reviewers' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer they invite (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of academic event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Sponsor company house is a building/place (sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts — an event versus a physical venue — so they are unrelated.

A's 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (a conference social gathering such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B's 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person (a person who organises the conference, with children General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Person) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Track workshop chair' is a Person role for chairing a track/workshop/tutorial, with properties linking it to a Conference part. B's 'Demo Chair' is a Conference Participant role specifically for demo sessions, sibling to Workshop Chair and Tutorial Chair. The two denote different chairing roles (track/workshop vs demo), so they are not equivalent; at most they share the general 'chair' notion, but neither subsumes the other in the given hierarchies.

A is an organisation (an organising agency, a kind of Organisation with siblings Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher), while B is a publication artefact (a book proceeding, a kind of Publication with sibling Cd proceeding). They belong to different branches of the domain (agent vs. document) and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) relation from a Conference volume to its Conference parts, whereas B's 'belongs To Event' is a membership/association relation from a Programme to a Conference Event. The domains (Conference volume vs Programme) and ranges (Conference part vs Conference Event) differ, and the intended meanings (composition vs participation in an event) do not coincide, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer), i.e. an assignment relation. B's 'invites co reviewers' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer they invite as a co-reviewer (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer), i.e. an invitation relation. Different domains, different intended meaning; not equivalent.

A 'Member PC' (confOf) is a Person who is a PC member/reviewer, with properties expert On (Topic) and reviewes (Contribution). B 'Two Level Conference' (edas) is a Conference subtype (a conference with two levels), not a person role. Different kinds and meanings, so unrelated.

A's writtenBy relates a Review to its Reviewer (the person who wrote the review). B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents the document). The domains (Review vs Document) and ranges (Reviewer vs Speaker) differ, and the intended relations are different: reviewing vs presenting. They are not the same relation.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment relation), while iasted's is_designed_for relates an Activity/Money/Time to an Activity/Person (a purpose/design relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad class covering all persons taking part in a conference (its children include Active/Passive conference participant, and its siblings include Committee member, Reviewer, etc.). B's 'Organizing Committee member' is a specific role under Organizator, alongside General Chair, Program Chair, etc. An organizing committee member is a kind of conference participant, but not every conference participant is an organizing committee member, so A is strictly more general than B (A subsumes B).

A's hasPart is a general mereological object property with unspecified domain/range, while B's has_amount_of is a datatype property linking Money to an int value. They relate different kinds of entities (parts vs. numeric amounts) and have different types (object vs. datatype), so they are not equivalent.
A's 'has Bid' links a Paper to a Bid (a review/offer), while B's 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher. Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's property links a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference (a topic or skill area), while B's 'reviewes' links a PC member to a Contribution (the paper they review). Different domain (Reviewer vs Member PC) and different range (Review expertise/preference vs Contribution), and different meaning (expertise/preference vs actual reviewing act), so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a specific kind of organized meeting with a name, parts, proceedings, publisher and topics, while B's Event is a broader class covering administrative, social and working events with start/end times. A Conference is a type of Event, so Conference is subsumed by Event, not equivalent.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review-expertise/preference record to a Reviewer (domain: Review expertise, Review preference; range: Reviewer), whereas B's 'has Review' links a Paper to its Review (domain: Paper; range: Review). They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a submitted paper that was not accepted, a subclass of Reviewed contribution. B 'Review' is a document (an evaluation of a submission), a sibling of Submission and Form under Document. The two denote different concepts: one is a rejected paper, the other is the review document itself. No subsumption or overlap in the intended instances.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person (Person > User), so every User is a Person, but not every Person is a User. In the Conference ontology, Person is the broader class with children such as Committee member, Conference participant, Reviewer, etc. Thus User is strictly more specific than Person, making User subsumed_by Person rather than equivalent.

A's 'Conference document' is a class of documents (calls, announcements, contributions, reviews) that have authors and dates of issue and are contributed by persons. B's 'Conference' is the event itself, with a city, start/end dates, a name, and held-by relations to ACM SIGKDD. The two denote different concepts (document vs. event), so they are unrelated despite the shared word 'conference'.

Paper Full Version is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Abstract), whereas Information for participants is a conference document category (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.). They denote different concepts: one is a full paper document, the other is informational material for attendees.

edas:hasAttendee relates a Conference Event to a Person who attends it, while ekaw:organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person that organises it. The ranges differ (Person vs Organisation/Person) and the intended relations are different (attendance vs organisation), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a human attending a conference), while B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Scientific Event (one edition of a conference). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event), so they are unrelated despite the shared word 'conference'.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract text. B's 'related To Event' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (an event/session at which it is presented). Different domain, different range, different meaning: one is a document-part relation, the other an event-participation relation. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Accepted Paper is a specific status of a paper (a Paper that has been accepted), while ekaw's Paper is the general class covering all papers regardless of status (with children like Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, etc.). Accepted Paper is therefore strictly more specific than Paper, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A is a conference-organisation event class (parent of submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration events), while B is a subject-area topic in a topic taxonomy (Computer Networks Management). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's property links a Steering committee (a group) to a Conference volume, expressing that the committee steers that conference series/volume. B's property links a Person to a Conference, expressing individual membership. Different domain (group vs person) and different intended relation (steering a conference series vs being a member of a conference), so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a conference paper/contribution: confOf's Paper is a subclass of Contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), and edas's Paper is a subclass of Document with subclasses Accepted/Pending/Rejected Paper and properties is Written By Author, is Reviewed By Reviewer, has Topic Topic — the same intended instances in the conference domain.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper with range string, while B's has amount of is a datatype property of Money with range int; they relate different kinds of things (paper titles vs monetary amounts) and are not the same relation.

A's 'Time zone' is a geographic/temporal region concept (a zone for expressing times), while B's 'Deadline' is a submission/notification due date with children Abstract Submission, Author notification, Paper Submission and properties Date, submit until. A time zone is not a deadline; the concepts denote different things, so they are unrelated.

A 'Talk Event' is an academic event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), while B 'Gold Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (academic events vs. sponsors) and share no instances.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while B's 'Active Paper' is a paper in the review process (a subclass of Paper with a rating). They denote different concepts: one is a call/announcement, the other is a submitted paper under review.

Administrator is a person role (a User who manages the conference: accepts papers, assigns reviewers, enters conference details), while Review is a conference document (a review of a contribution). They belong to different branches (Person vs Conference document) and share no properties or meaning, so they are unrelated.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to the Organization that employs them (employment relation). ekaw's publisherOf relates an Organisation to the things it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). Different domain (Person vs Organisation), different range (Organization vs publications), and different meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to the people who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. the initiators of a call. B's 'is used by' links an Item to a Person who uses it, a general usage relation. The domains (Call vs Item) and ranges (specific chair roles vs Person) differ, and the intended meanings (initiation vs usage) are distinct, so the properties are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs/organises the conference (a Chairman/Conference Member role), while B 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a speaker who gives a plenary lecture, a kind of Author/Speaker. The roles are distinct: chairing a conference is not the same as giving a plenary talk, and neither subsumes the other.

Scholar in confOf is a price category for a person (comment: 'price category - scholar') and has a property study At (Scholar -> University), indicating a student-like participant. Attendee in edas is the general class of persons attending the conference, with siblings Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, etc. The two overlap (a scholar is typically an attendee) but are not the same concept: Scholar is a specific fee/role category, Attendee is the broad participation class. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to its Program committee (a committee entity), while B's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event (the event the programme belongs to). The domains (Conference volume vs Programme) and ranges (Program committee vs Conference Event) differ, and the directions/intended meanings do not coincide; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote a person who authors contributions/papers. confOf's Author is a subclass of Person with properties writes (Author -> Contribution) and written By (Contribution -> Author). iasted's Author is a subclass of Speaker (itself under Delegate) and has children for proceedings authorship and lecture/tutorial speaking roles, but its core intended meaning is still the author of a paper/contribution. The differing parent hierarchies (Person vs Speaker/Delegate) reflect different modelling choices, not different concepts; the domain role 'author of a contribution' coincides, so a reference alignment would record equivalence.

A's 'Accept Rating' is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a rating value/decision used in the review process (siblings: Reject Rating, Weak Reject Rating, Accept If Room Rating). B's 'Abstract' is a subclass of Document, i.e. the abstract text of a paper (siblings: Paper, Review). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain — a review rating versus a document part — so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given to' relates an Item to a Person (e.g. a paper given to an attendee), while B's 'obtain' relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings differ, and the properties are not inverses or subsumption-related.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to an email address string, while B's 'has First Name' links a Person to a first-name string (comment notes it also covers middle name). They relate different kinds of data (email vs. given name), so they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members (a membership/containment relation), while B's reviewes links a PC member to the Contribution they review (a reviewing relation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Camera Ready event' is an administrative event in confOf (sibling of Submission, Reviewing, Registration events) marking the camera-ready submission milestone. B 'Organizational Meeting' is an academic event in edas (sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop) denoting an organisational meeting held at the conference. Different parents (Administrative vs Academic event), different siblings, and different intended instances: one is a deadline/administrative milestone, the other a meeting. They are not the same concept.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) relation between a Conference volume and its Conference parts, whereas B's 'has Event' is a temporal/structural relation between Events (e.g. an event having sub-events). They relate different kinds of entities in different domains and are not the same relation.

In ekaw, Submitted Paper is a Paper (a document submitted to a conference, with children like Assigned Paper and siblings like Camera Ready Paper), whereas in sigkdd Abstract is a Document that is a distinct sibling of Paper and Review, i.e. the abstract text of a paper rather than a submitted paper. Different intended instances and different positions in the hierarchy, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Working event is the general category of academic/professional events (Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) with topics, titles, VAT and choices; edas's Break Event is a non-academic event (Coffee Break, Free Time Break, Meal Break) under Non Academic Event. They denote disjoint kinds of event, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic' is a subject area/topic in the EDAS taxonomy. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' and denotes submitted written artefacts (papers, posters, talks) that are part of a conference volume and can be reviewed. B's 'Conference activity' is a subclass of 'Activity' and denotes scheduled events at a conference (coffee breaks, receptions, lectures, registration). Although both contain 'Conference', their intended instances differ: documents vs. activities. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's Lecturer is a general author role (parent Author) with children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer, i.e. a person who lectures/authors. B's Author of paper student is a specific subclass of Author restricted to students who author papers. They overlap (a student lecturer could be an author of a paper student) but neither subsumes the other: Lecturer is broader in role (includes non-student lecturers) while Author of paper student is narrower in both role and person type. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's Talk Event is a kind of academic event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk, siblings Paper Presentation and Workshop). B's Research is an activity performed before the conference (with children Modelling and Simulating, siblings Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript). The two denote different concepts in different parts of the domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing practical information to attendees. B's 'Communication Theory Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in the EDAS taxonomy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Conference is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) denoting the whole conference; B's Conference Dinner is a meal event, a social/non-academic event during a conference. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Conference part (topic is a topic of conference parts), while B's property links a Document to a Speaker (document is presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both properties link a submission-like entity to people involved in handling it, but they are not the same relation: edas 'is Reviewed By' has domain Paper and range specifically reviewers/committee members (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. the reviewing relation, whereas iasted 'is sent by' has the broader domain Item and range Person, denoting the sender/submitter of an item. The ranges and intended meanings differ (reviewer vs. sender), so they overlap only loosely and are not equivalent.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property from Conference to int, counting the number of reviews per paper. B's 'reviewes' is an object property from Member PC to Contribution, linking a PC member to the contribution they review. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Member PC), and range (int vs Contribution), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a person role: active/passive participant, reviewer, committee member), while B's 'Dining Place' is a subclass of Place (a physical location alongside accommodation, venue, meeting room). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. location) and share no domain overlap, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the conference event itself: A's Conference is the central event class with a name and proceedings, and B's Conference is a Working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop, i.e. the same conference event concept.

Chairman is a person role (a subclass of Person, with subclasses like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), while Fee is a monetary charge (with subclasses Registration fee and Sponzor fee). They denote entirely different concepts and cannot be equivalent.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a submission of a bid for a paper), while B's is_paid_in relates Money to a Building (where a payment is made). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A is a person role (Tutorial Chair, a kind of Conference Participant/PC Member) in the conference organisation; B is a monetary fee category (Memeber registration fee, a kind of Registration fee) in the fee hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise area), while B's 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item (acquiring something). Different domains (Member PC vs Person) and ranges (Topic vs Item), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

The property 'email' in cmt is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address), while 'authorOf' in ekaw is an object property linking a Person to a Document. They have different ranges and semantics, so they are unrelated.

Company (a commercial organization, sibling of University under Organization) and Student non speaker (a delegate who is a student and not a speaker, under Non speaker) denote entirely different concepts: one is an organization type, the other a person role. No overlap in intended instances.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to the Person who authored it (authorship relation). B's 'is used by' relates an Item to a Person who uses it (usage relation). Although both have domain Item/Document and range Person, the intended relations differ: authorship vs. usage. They are not the same relation, nor is one a generalization of the other.
Organizer and Organizator are spelling variants of the same concept; both are subclasses of Person and cover the same roles (chairs, committee members, webmaster), so their instances coincide.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of conference session/event) in confOf, while B Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment in iasted. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

Organization in the Conference ontology is a general entity (an organisation such as a university, company or society that authors/attendees belong to), whereas Organizing Committee in sigkdd is a specific committee (a subclass of Committee, sibling of Program Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee) that organises the conference. They are conceptually related (a committee is a kind of organisation) but do not denote the same concept, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Dining Place' is a kind of Place (a venue where meals are served, sibling of Accommodation Place and Meeting Room Place), while B 'Car' is a kind of Transport vehicle (sibling of Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's isReviewing goes from a person (Conference Chair/Reviewer/Session Chair/TPC Member) to a Paper, meaning the person reviews the paper. B's hasReviewer goes from a Paper to a Possible Reviewer, the inverse direction and a different relation. A property and its inverse are not equivalent, and here the domains/ranges are swapped, so they are unrelated (or at best inverses, which the schema does not allow as equivalent).

A's Tutorial is a kind of working event (a session type held at a conference, sibling of Conference and Workshop), while B's One conference day is a temporal unit within the Conference days hierarchy (sibling of Delegate). They belong to different branches of the domain (event type vs. time period) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assignment of a reviewer to a paper by an administrator), while B's belongs_to_reviewers relates a Review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (a reviewer's declared expertise/preference). Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has gender' is a datatype property linking a Person to a gender value, while B's 'author Of' is an object property linking a Person to a Document. They relate different kinds of things (literal vs. document) and have different meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a document type (a scientific paper with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Conference www is a web page/document about the conference (has a URL), a sibling of Call for paper and Review. They denote different concepts despite both being documents.

hasTrack relates a conference volume to its tracks, while hasCountry relates an organization or person to a country; the domains and ranges are entirely different, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Administrator is a User/Person role (a person who administers the conference, with properties like assign Reviewer, accept Paper), while B's Paper is a Document (a written submission with children Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts and share no instances.

A Banquet is a formal social event (sibling of Reception and Trip under Social event), while a Meal Break is a scheduled break for eating during the conference (sibling of Coffee Break and Free Time Break under Break Event). Both involve food, but they denote different concepts: a banquet is a social event, a meal break is a break. They are related but not equivalent.

A's has Last Name is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's written By is an object property mapping a Document to a Person (the author of a document). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Document), range (string vs Person), and direction of the relation, so they cannot denote the same relation.

cmt:assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (a person reviewing a paper), while iasted:occupy relates a Person to a Building/City/State (a physical location). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (a person role), while B's was_a_track-workshop_chair_of relates a Track workshop chair to a Conference part. Different domains, ranges, and directions; the entities denote different relations.

Author (cmt) is a conference member who writes/submits papers, while Meal Event (edas) is a non-academic conference event such as a dinner with a menu. They share no meaning, instances, or properties; the only overlap is the generic word 'event'/'member' context, which is not enough.

In cmt, Review is a subclass of Document, sibling of Paper, and is the object of review-related properties (write Review, written By Reviewer, end Review by PC Chair); it denotes the review document/record produced by a reviewer. In confOf, Contribution is a general submission category (comment 'confTool') with subclasses Paper, Poster, Short paper, and is written by an Author and reviewed by a PC member. Contribution corresponds to cmt's Paper (submitted work), not to Review, which is the evaluation artefact. The two classes have different intended instances and different roles in the domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference (enabling a virtual meeting), while B's hasAttendee relates a Conference Event to a Person (attendance). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Tutorial is a conference event/activity (sibling of Track and Workshop, with property 'has tutorials' from Conference volume), whereas B's Tutorial speaker is a person role (a subclass of Author/Speaker). The two denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

A is a person role (a chair involved in a conference, subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while B is a physical location type (a venue place, subclass of Place). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range string, capturing the conference's name (A's comment 'Conference Full Name' matches B's 'Name of conference'). Same kind, same domain/range, same intended relation.

A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to its Committee; B's 'organisedBy' links an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it. Both express an organisational association between a conference/event and the agents responsible for it, but the ranges differ (Committee vs Organisation/Person) and the domains differ (Conference volume vs Event), so they are not the same relation; they merely overlap in the conference-organisation domain.

Paper Abstract (a part/version of a Paper, sibling of Paper Full Version) is a document artefact, whereas Review is a distinct document type used to evaluate papers; they denote different concepts despite both being Documents.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a role of a person (a conference contributor who gives an invited talk), while B's 'Reception' is a social event in the conference programme. They belong to different branches (Person vs Conference Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property linking a Review preference to an int (a preference degree), while B's 'has Review' is an object property linking a Paper to a Review. They differ in domain, range, and kind, so they denote different relations.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented), while B 'Exhibitor' is a sponsoring entity (a subtype of Sponzor, alongside Gold/Bronze/Platinum supporters). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. sponsor) and share no intended instances.

Both classes denote a program-committee member/reviewer: confOf's Member PC has comment 'Reviewer' and reviews Contributions; edas's TPC Member reviews Papers and is a Person. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

A's `adjust Bid` is a specific action performed by a Reviewer on a Bid (domain Reviewer, range Bid). B's `give` is a much broader property relating a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk, giving a review). The Reviewer/Bid relation is a special case of the general Person-to-Activity/Item giving relation, so `adjust Bid` is subsumed by `give`, not equivalent.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (a conference/tutorial/workshop activity), while B 'Computer Architecture Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's max Choice is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a positive integer (a maximum number of choices, e.g. for event options), while B's has End Date Time is a datatype property of Conference Event giving a dateTime (the end time of an event). They relate different kinds of things (integer count vs. date/time) and have different domains, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'is paid in' relates Money to Building (where a payment is made), while B's 'payed by' relates Registration fee to Person (who pays). Different domain, range, and direction of the payment relation; they are not the same property.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to the Location where it takes place, while B's 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time point, expressing a temporal ordering relation. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

Author in edas denotes a person who writes papers (domain of has Related Paper, range of is Written By), while Possible Reviewer in ekaw denotes a person who may review papers (range of has Reviewer, domain of reviewer Of Paper). The intended instances and roles differ: an author is not necessarily a possible reviewer, and the properties linking them to papers/reviews are different. They share only the parent Person, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume, while B's 'inverse of part Of 7' is a generic inverse part-of relation whose range is Event. Both express a part-of/containment relation, but the domains/ranges differ (Conference part/Conference volume vs unspecified/Event), so they are not the same relation; they overlap only as part-of relations.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class describing a reviewer's expertise/competence area, tied to Reviewer and Submitted contribution. B's 'Money' is a financial amount class with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment. They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A Tutorial is a working event (interactive, hands-on session) alongside Conference and Workshop, whereas B Plenary lecture is a type of Lecture (a formal talk) alongside Session and Tutorial. Although Tutorial appears as a sibling of Plenary lecture in iasted, the two entities denote different concepts: a tutorial is not a plenary lecture, and the paths/parents differ (Working event vs Lecture).

Individual Presentation in ekaw is a specific kind of scientific event (a talk/presentation session with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial), whereas Item in iasted is a broad physical/abstract object category (children Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle) used as a resource in activities. Their intended instances do not coincide; the ekaw class is an event, the iasted class is a thing, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has amount of' is a datatype property of Money giving an integer amount, while B's 'Name of sponsor' is a datatype property of Sponzor giving a string name. Different domains (Money vs Sponzor), different ranges (int vs string), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's `location Of` relates a Location to an Event (the event takes place at the location), while B's `is situated in` relates a Building/City/Place to another Building/City/Place/State (spatial containment of places). The domains and ranges are disjoint in kind (Event vs. Place), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person/attendee who has paid early), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount for non-authors). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Money) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Welcome address' is a conference activity (an event occurring in the programme), while B 'Conference hall' is a place/venue where activities happen. They belong to different branches (Activity vs Place) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a steering committee' relates a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a committee-assignment relation), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'adjust Bid' relates a Reviewer to a Bid (domain Reviewer, range Bid), while B's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer). Different ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering all people contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants, committee members). B's 'Student lecturer' is a narrow role under Lecturer (a Speaker/Author/Delegate) in the iasted hierarchy, denoting a student who lectures. The two concepts do not coincide: a student lecturer is a specific kind of contributor, but the classes are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other given the different role taxonomies.

A's email is a datatype property holding an email address of a Person; B's has Postal Code holds a postal/zip code and applies to Organization and Person. Different attributes with different intended values, so they are not equivalent.

Conference applicant is a Person subclass (a person applying to a conference), while Registration SIGKDD Member is a Registration fee subclass (a fee category for SIGKDD members). They belong to different taxonomies (Person vs Fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a keyword string, while B's Name links a Person to a name string. Different domains (Contribution vs Person) and different intended meanings (keyword vs name), so they are not the same relation.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event whose instances are the outcomes/results of reviewing made accessible to authors (a notification/results event). B 'Call For Manuscripts' is a call document/announcement soliciting manuscript submissions, sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Reviews. One is an event in the conference timeline, the other is a call for submissions; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a Conference-domain datatype property giving the number of reviews per paper (range int). B's 'default Choice' is a Social/Working event-domain datatype property (range positiveInteger, comment 'confTool') giving a default choice for an event. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event (person attends event), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (document is presented by speaker). Different domains, ranges, and directions; not equivalent nor inverse.

A is a document type (a paper in its camera-ready form, a subclass of Paper), while B is a time point (a submission deadline, a subclass of Deadline). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (document vs. time) and cannot denote the same concept.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Plenary lecture is a specific kind of lecture/session within a conference. A plenary lecture is a part of a conference, not the conference itself, so the classes denote different concepts.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the presenter/speaker), while B's 'written By' links a Contribution (paper) to an Author. Both relate a conference artefact to a person, but the artefact types (Presentation vs Contribution) and the person roles (presenter vs author) differ, so they are not the same relation; they merely overlap in the general sense of attributing a work to a person.

A 'Pending Paper' is a paper in a submission state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper under Paper), whereas B 'Mailing list' is a document artefact (sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Review, Submission) under Document. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

TPC Member in edas is a committee role (a Person who reviews papers and initiates calls), while Author in sigkdd is a speaker who submits papers and receives notifications. They are distinct roles in the conference domain: a TPC member reviews, an author submits. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's forEvent links a Call to the Academic Event it is a call for (domain Call, range Academic Event). B's eventOnList links an Event to the Programme Brochure/Web Site where it is listed (domain Event, range Programme Brochure, Web Site). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings: one is a call-to-event relation, the other an event-to-publication listing relation.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to the Reviewer it is assigned to (reviewing assignment), while B's 'updated Version Of' links a Document to another Document that it is a later version of (versioning). Different domain/range kinds and different intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is writen by' relates an Item (paper/contribution) to a Person (its author), i.e. authorship. B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document, i.e. a speaker presenting a document. Different domains (Item vs Speaker), different ranges (Person vs Document), and different intended meanings (authorship vs presentation), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'name' is a datatype property giving the name of a Conference or Person, while B's 'ends on' is a datatype property giving the end date of an Event. They have different domains (Conference/Person vs Event) and different intended meanings (name vs end date), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Workshop is a specific kind of working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while ekaw's Conference Session is a generic session type whose siblings include Workshop Session, Demo Session, Poster Session and Regular Session. A Workshop is not a Conference Session; rather a Workshop Session is a kind of Conference Session, and a Workshop is a kind of event that may be held as a session. The two concepts overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

confOf's Assistant is a generic Person role (sibling of Author, Participant, Volunteer, etc.), while sigkdd's Organizing Committee member is a specific organizer role under Organizator (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). The intended instances do not coincide: an assistant is not necessarily an organizing committee member, and committee members are not assistants. Different paths, parents and sibling sets indicate distinct concepts.

Both classes denote a student person in the conference domain. In confOf, Student is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), and in ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person alongside Conference Participant, Paper Author, etc. The intended instances coincide: a student involved in the conference. The differing parent (Participant vs Person) reflects modelling granularity, not a different concept, so the classes are equivalent.

Both properties relate a PC member/reviewer to the paper/contribution they review; 'reviewes' (Member PC -> Contribution) and 'is Reviewing' (Reviewer/TPC Member -> Paper) denote the same reviewing relation, with Contribution and Paper being equivalent classes in the conference domain.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad class covering all people taking part in a conference (its children are Active/Passive conference participant, and its siblings include Committee member, Reviewer, etc.). B's 'General Chair' is a specific organizational role under Organizator, a sibling of Program Chair, PC member, Webmaster. A General Chair is a kind of conference participant, but the two classes are not equivalent: the participant class is far more general and the General Chair is a specific role. Thus they are unrelated as classes (at most General Chair would be subsumed by participant, but the pair is not an equivalence).

A 'Invited speaker' is a person role (a kind of Conference contributor/Person), while B 'Trip city' is a kind of City (a location). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A 'Conference days' is a time span/period class (parent Time, children Delegate and One conference day, sibling Trip day) denoting the days on which a conference takes place. B 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a specific deadline event (parent Deadline, siblings Deadline Abstract Submission, Deadline Author notification) denoting the due date for submitting papers. They denote different concepts: a duration/period versus a submission deadline, so they are unrelated.

A's 'ends on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string (its end date/time), while B's 'has Event' is an object property linking an Event to another Event (sub-events). They differ in kind, domain/range and meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Both denote an organisation that organises a conference. In the Conference ontology, Organization is the general class for organising bodies; in ekaw, Organising Agency is the class of organisations that organise events, sitting under Organisation alongside Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher. The intended instances coincide (a body that organises a conference), so they are equivalent.

A's 'Review preference' is a reviewer's expressed preference/degree of interest in topics or submissions (it belongs to reviewers, has a degree, and links to topics/submissions). B's 'Review' is a document produced for a paper (a subclass of Document, with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review, written by a reviewer about a paper). The two denote different concepts: a preference is not a review document, and their properties and contexts do not coincide.

A's 'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepts it), while B's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (the person who writes it). Different domain/range and different intended relation (acceptance vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property of Review preference with range int (a numeric degree of preference), while B's 'Name' is a datatype property of Person with range string. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Conference volume' is a publication/proceedings entity (it has contributions, tracks, committees, important dates), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (sibling of Building, Hotel room, Session room). They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (paper authorship), while B's `hold` relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference (organising/holding an event). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision) in cmt, while Invited Talk is a kind of individual presentation (an event) in ekaw. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Conference participant is a broad class covering anyone taking part in a conference (active/passive participants, committee members, applicants, contributors, reviewers, workshop chairs), whereas edas Attendee is a narrower role (a person attending, sibling to Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). Every Attendee is a conference participant, but not every conference participant is an attendee, so Conference participant subsumes Attendee.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it (domain Sponsorship, range Organization), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B 'Introduction' is a conference activity (a subclass of Conference activity, sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Welcome address) in the iasted ontology. One denotes a person, the other an event/activity; they share no meaning and cannot be equivalent.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a Person subclass (a person who applies to a conference, with child 'Registeered applicant'), while B's 'Registration SIGMOD Member' is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a fee category for SIGMOD members, not a person. Different kinds of entities despite the shared registration theme.

confOf Organization is an employer entity (Company/University) that employs Persons and has address properties; sigkdd Place is a physical location (Conference hall/Hotel/Main office) where a Person can stay. Different intended instances and roles, so not equivalent.

A is a research topic (a subject area under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is an award category under Award (sibling of Best Research Paper Award). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both denote a paper/contribution submitted to a conference: cmt's Paper is a Document with authors, reviews, decisions and subject areas, and Conference's Submitted contribution is a written conference contribution that is reviewed and assigned to reviewers. The intended instances coincide (a submitted paper), so they are equivalent despite the different labels and paths.

Acceptance is a decision outcome on a paper (sibling of Rejection under Decision), while Trip is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception under Social event). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's has Decision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject outcome), while B's has a publisher links Conference proceedings to a Publisher. Different domains, ranges and intended relations; no overlap.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author (authorship of a paper). B's publisherOf relates an Organisation to things it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). Different domain, range and intended meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

Company in confOf is a subtype of Organization (an organizational entity such as a business, sibling of University). Conference state in iasted is a subtype of State (a status/role state, sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state). One denotes an organization type, the other a state/status; they share no intended instances and are unrelated.

Organization in edas is a broad class covering academia, government, industry, and NGOs, while Academic Institution in ekaw is a narrower subclass of Organisation restricted to academic bodies (universities, research institutes). Thus Organization is more general and subsumes Academic Institution, not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Tutorial Abstract is a document (an abstract of a tutorial talk), a subclass of Abstract. They belong to different branches (event vs. document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (Person -> Conference document), while B's 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (Item -> Person). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the directions differ, so they are not the same relation; at best they are inverses of different concepts, not equivalent.

Conference Chair is a person role in the conference committee (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while Trip day is a temporal concept (a subclass of Time, sibling of Conference days and Deadline). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (person vs. time) and share no intended instances.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference domain, a subclass of Conference Member/User, with properties linking authors to papers (write Paper, submit Paper, has Author). Organization (edas) is an institutional entity that provides sponsorships, with children Academia/Government/Industry/NGO and properties is Provider Of / provided By Sponsorship. They denote different concepts (person vs institution) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Paper is the general document class for submissions (it has children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and is the domain of submission/review properties like assigned To, has Author, has Decision), whereas ekaw:Accepted Paper is a specific subclass of Evaluated Paper denoting only papers that were accepted into the proceedings. The cmt class is strictly more general, so it subsumes the ekaw class rather than being equivalent to it.

Both properties link a person to a Paper in the reviewing context, but they are not the same relation: edas 'is Reviewing' has domain of persons (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) and range Paper, i.e. a person reviews a paper; ekaw 'review Of Paper' has domain Review and range Paper, i.e. it links a Review document to the paper it reviews. The subject kinds differ (person vs. review record), so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'early Registration' is a boolean flag on a Participant indicating whether that participant registered early; B's 'registration Due On' is a dateTime deadline on a Conference. Different domain (Participant vs Conference), different range (boolean vs dateTime), and different meaning (early-registration flag vs registration deadline), so they are not the same relation.

A's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a record of reviews performed), while B's write links a Person to an Item (an authored work). Different domain (Reviewer vs Person) and range (Personal Review History vs Item), and different meaning (reviewing history vs authoring), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a name' is a generic naming datatype property whose domain spans Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, with range string. B's 'start Date' is a specific temporal property with domain Conference and range dateTime, described as the conference start date and time. They relate different kinds of values (names vs. dates) and are not the same relation.

cmt:User is a broad person role class whose children are Administrator, Author, Reviewer (roles in the conference system), while confOf:Participant is a person who takes part in the conference, with children Member, Regular, Student and a property early Registration. The two overlap (an author/reviewer is typically a participant) but neither subsumes the other: User includes roles like Administrator that are not participants, and Participant includes Regular/Student attendees that need not be system users. Hence related, not equivalent.

A is a Person subclass (Conference Participant) representing an attendee role, while B is a Money/Fee subclass (Registration fee) representing a payment amount. They belong to disjoint top-level categories (Person vs Money) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Sponzorship (sponsorship money) and Fee are both subclasses of Money in their respective ontologies, but they denote different financial concepts: sponsorship is money given by sponsors, while Fee is money paid (with children Registration fee and Sponzor fee). They overlap only in being monetary categories, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Presenter (edas) is an Author who presents a paper at the conference; B Plenary lecture speaker (iasted) is a Speaker/Author who gives a plenary lecture, a much narrower role. Every plenary lecture speaker is a presenter of sorts, but not every presenter is a plenary speaker, so Presenter is more general and subsumes the plenary-speaker concept; from A's perspective it is subsumed_by the broader notion only in the sense that the iasted class is a specialization. The two are not equivalent.

A's end Review is a property of Program Committee Chair (domain: Program Committee Chair, range: Review), i.e. the chair ends a review. B's has Review is a property of Paper (domain: Paper, range: Review), i.e. a paper has a review. Different domains and directions of relation; they are not equivalent.

A is a class of rejected paper submissions (a document/contribution in a review outcome hierarchy), while B is a time/deadline concept (the notification-of-acceptance deadline) under Deadline. They denote different kinds of things (contribution vs. temporal deadline) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a person who takes part in a conference, with subclasses Active/Passive participant), while B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Working event (an event such as a conference, tutorial or workshop). One denotes a person role, the other an event; they cannot have the same instances and are unrelated.

Both are the top-level conference-domain event class: confOf's Event has children Administrative/Social/Working event and start/end date properties, while edas's Conference Event has children Academic/Non Academic Event and start/end date, location, programme and attendee properties. The intended instances (conference events with a start and end time) coincide, so they are equivalent despite differing labels.

A's Review Rating is a class of ratings assigned to papers (children Accept/Reject ratings, domain of has Rating from Active Paper), i.e. an evaluation outcome. B's Time is a temporal class (children Conference days, Deadline, Trip day; range of is held after/before, is present, is sent after/before). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'is dated on' is a general datatype property on Activity (any activity, e.g. a conference or a session, can be dated on a dateTime), while B's 'End of conference' is a specific datatype property on Conference denoting the conference's end date. The B property is a specialisation of the general dating relation, so A subsumes B (B is subsumed by A); they are not equivalent because A applies to all activities and any date, not just the end of a conference.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (administrative data entry), while B's 'has Menu' relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (catering). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A is a class of documents (a camera-ready contribution, i.e. the final version of an accepted paper), while B is a deadline (a point in time) for submitting the camera-ready manuscript.
