They belong to different branches (document vs. time) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a general contribution type (sibling of Poster and Short paper) covering any submitted paper, while B's Rejected Paper is a specific status subclass of Paper in edas, denoting only papers that were rejected. The two do not have coinciding instances: a Paper in confOf can be accepted, rejected, etc., and Rejected Paper is strictly narrower than Paper, not equivalent to it.

A's 'related To Event' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (the paper is presented at an event), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (the document is presented by a person). Both concern the presentation of a paper/document, but the ranges differ (event vs. person) and the directions/roles are not the same, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'is used by' relates an Item to a Person (domain Item, range Person), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (domain Person, range Place). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings differ entirely, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference www' is a document/webpage about the conference (a subclass of Conference document, with a URL property), while B's 'Author' is a person role (subclass of Speaker, who submits papers and receives notifications). They denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is Reviewing' relates a reviewer-type person (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper they review. B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give/produce, a broader relation covering giving a talk, item, etc. The domains overlap (Person vs reviewer roles) and the ranges overlap (Paper is a kind of Item/Activity output), but 'is Reviewing' is a specific reviewing relation while 'give' is a general production/giving relation; they are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A relates a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (organisational role over an event part), while B relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Single Level Conference' is a conference event type (a conference without sub-events, sibling of 'Two Level Conference' under Conference), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical venue/place (sibling of Hotel and Main office under Place). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a location.

A's 'has Conference Member' relates a Conference to a Conference Member (a person participating in the conference), while B's 'has a track workshop tutorial chair' relates a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (a specific role for a workshop/tutorial track). The ranges denote different concepts (general conference member vs. track workshop chair) and the domains differ (Conference vs. Conference part), so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with children such as Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author). B's 'Presenter city' is a subclass of City (a city where a presenter is located, sibling of Conference city, Sponsor city, Trip city). One denotes a person role, the other a geographic location; they cannot denote the same concept.

Both classes denote a person participating in a conference, sit directly under Person, and have subclasses for the various participant roles (active/passive in Conference; chairs, presenters, registered participants in ekaw). The intended instances coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

Organization in confOf is an institution (parent of Company and University, employer of Persons, with address properties), while Sponsorship in edas is a funding arrangement (parent of Travel Grant, with cost amount/currency, provided by an Organization). They denote different concepts; the only link is that a Sponsorship is provided by an Organization, not that they are the same.

A 'Social program' is a conference activity (a social event such as a dinner banquet) in the iasted ontology, while B 'Program Chair' is a person role (an organizer) in the sigkdd ontology. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'end Review' is an object property linking a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the review phase ending), while B's 'ends on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string date/time. Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

A's 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an Administrator action that produces/relates to a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), i.e. the act of running the paper-assignment process. B's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), expressing that two events occur in parallel. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), i.e. authorship. Different kinds of things in different directions; not equivalent.

IASTED member is a subclass of Delegate (an attendee/participant role in the iasted ontology), while Organizing Committee member is a subclass of Organizator (an organizer role in sigkdd). They denote different roles in the conference domain: an attendee versus an organizer, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment affiliation), while B's 'is present' relates a Person to a Time (attendance/presence at a time). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's hasReview relates a Paper to a Review (the review of a paper), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (the document a speaker presents). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (sessions scheduled in parallel), while B's 'paper In Volume' relates a paper to a proceedings volume. Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

Conference participant is a broad class covering all participants (active/passive, committee members, reviewers, etc.), while OC Member is a specific organizational-committee role nested under Conference Participant in ekaw. The A class is strictly more general than the B class, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (a call/announcement artefact, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B 'Computer Networks Aapplications Topic' is a research topic in the EDAS topic taxonomy. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class describing a reviewer's expertise/preference for reviewing a submitted contribution (it is linked to Reviewer and Submitted contribution). B's 'Review Question' is a class of questions asked during reviewing, with subclasses Numerical and Textual Review Question. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' is a specific meronymic relation restricted to Conference part -> Conference volume, whereas ekaw's 'part Of' is a general, domain/range-unspecified part-whole property. The specific property is a subproperty of the general one, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

Both are post-conference social/leisure activities, but an Excursion is a general social event (sibling of Reception) while a Full day tour is a specific all-day activity after the conference; they overlap but neither subsumes the other.

A's reject Paper relates an Administrator to a Paper (rejection action), while B's has Reviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (reviewer assignment). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent nor inverse.

Both denote a program-committee member/reviewer: confOf's 'Member PC' (comment 'Reviewer', reviews Contributions, expert on Topics) matches ekaw's 'PC Member' under 'Possible Reviewer', which also reviews papers and is a Person. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document (path Document > Paper), while in sigkdd Document is the broader class with Paper as a child. Thus cmt:Paper is strictly more specific than sigkdd:Document, so Paper is subsumed by Document rather than equivalent.

A's Event is a general conference-domain event (scientific/social events, held in a location, organised by people, part of other events), while B's City is a geographic location with buildings, states and persons occupying/visiting it. They denote different concepts and share no intended instances.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a first name literal), while B's authorOf is an object property mapping a Person to a Document. They relate different kinds of things (string vs Document) and have different meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'accept Paper' relates an Administrator to a Paper (the act of accepting a paper for the conference), while B's 'paper Presented As' relates a Paper to an Individual Presentation (the presentation form of a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a committee role within a conference (siblings: Program committee, Steering committee; it organizes a conference volume), whereas B's 'Academia Organization' is a type of organization (siblings: Government, Industry, NGO) classifying the affiliation sector of an author/participant. They denote different concepts despite both involving 'organization'.

Both are mereological part-of properties: Conference's 'has parts' relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts, and ekaw's 'has Part' is the standard OWL part relation. They denote the same relation (whole -> part) in the conference domain, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

edas:hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (an author's related paper), while ekaw:references is a general bibliographic citation relation between documents/papers. They both concern papers but differ in domain/range and direction of the relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Author in edas is a subclass of Person (path Person > Author) and denotes a person who writes papers, with properties linking to Paper. Person in sigkdd is the general superclass of all conference participants (Listener, Organizator, Speaker) and has only contact/registration properties, no paper-writing relation. Thus Author is strictly more specific than Person: every Author is a Person, but not every Person is an Author. The relation is subsumed_by, not equivalence.

A 'Conference Event' is an event (with attendees, programme, start/end date times, location) that takes place at a venue; B 'Building' is a physical place (a subtype of Place) that hosts events and is occupied/visited by persons. They belong to different branches (event vs. place) and their properties (has Programme, has Start Date Time vs. is situated in, is occupied by) do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's is_used_by is an object property mapping an Item to a Person (inverse of uses). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), and range (string vs Person), so they cannot denote the same relation.

Both classes denote a submitted paper/contribution that was reviewed and rejected. A's 'Rejected contribution' is a subclass of 'Reviewed contribution' with sibling 'Accepted contribution'; B's 'Rejected Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper' with sibling 'Accepted Paper'. The intended instances coincide: a rejected submission in the conference domain. The differing parent (Reviewed contribution vs Paper) reflects ontology structure, not a difference in meaning.

A is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a literal date (the acceptance-announcement date), while B is an object property linking a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event. They have different domains, different ranges (literal vs. Event), and different intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to its Decision (accept/reject outcome), while B's hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a person). Different domain/range semantics: outcome vs. person, so the properties are not equivalent.

Both classes denote members of the program/technical program committee. cmt's Program Committee Member is a Person who reviews papers and belongs to the Program Committee; edas's TPC Member is a Person who reviews papers and initiates calls, matching the same role. The differing labels (Program Committee vs. TPC) are synonymous in the conference domain, and the surrounding context (Person, reviewer role, paper review relations) agrees.
hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author, while heldIn relates an Event to a Location. Different domain, range, and intended relation; no equivalence.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with a two-level programme committee structure), sitting under Conference alongside Single Level Conference. B 'Author' is a person role (a delegate/speaker who authors papers). A conference event and an author role denote different concepts; the shared parent Person in A's hierarchy is incidental and does not make them equivalent.
Paper Abstract is a document type (a paper's abstract) in cmt, while Silver Supporter is a sponsorship level in sigkdd; they share no meaning in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a person who reviews papers. In Conference, Reviewer is a subclass of Person with review-related properties (belongs to reviewers, has a review reference or expertise, invited by, invites co reviewers). In iasted, Reviewer is a subclass of Speaker (itself under Delegate) with sibling Author, i.e. a conference participant who reviews. Despite different parent hierarchies, the intended instances coincide: a reviewer in the conference domain. The label match plus the review-specific properties in Conference and the participant role in iasted support equivalence.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the outcome of the review process), while B's is_situated_in relates a Building/City/Place to a Building/City/Place/State (a spatial containment relation). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the intended meanings are entirely different, so the two properties are unrelated.

A's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (accommodation/location). Different ranges (Conference vs Place) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Talk Event is a subclass of Academic Event covering talks (Welcome Talk, Closing Talk) within the conference programme; B's Introduction is a conference activity (with child Introduction of speaker) sitting alongside Lecture, Presentation, Welcome address. Both are conference-session-like entities, but Talk Event is a broader academic-event category while Introduction is a specific introductory activity, so they overlap without coinciding.

A's hasPostalCode is a postal-code datatype property on Organization/Person, while B's Name is a person's name property; different attributes with different domains, so they are not the same relation.

Pending Paper is a specific state of a paper (a paper that has been submitted but not yet accepted/rejected), whereas ekaw's Paper is the general class covering all papers including camera-ready, conference, demo, poster, submitted, etc. Pending Paper is thus strictly narrower than Paper, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's Chair is a generic committee chair (parent Committee member, sibling Co chair, domain/range Committee->Chair). B's Demo Chair is a specific conference participant role (parent Conference Participant, sibling of PC Chair, Workshop Chair, etc.), i.e. the chair of the demo session, not a committee chair. Different intended instances and different positions in the hierarchy, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Programme Brochure is a Document (sibling of Paper, Review, Abstract) that lists events and is published by an organisation. They denote different concepts: an event versus a publication artefact, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a conference document (submitted paper with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Computer Networks Switching Topic is a subject-area/topic category in a topic hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts and cannot be equivalent.

Conference contributor is a broad Person role covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors; Hotel presenter is a specific Delegate subtype (a presenter staying at the conference hotel). They overlap in that both can denote people contributing to the conference, but neither subsumes the other: a contributor need not be a hotel presenter, and a hotel presenter is a delegate/presenter rather than the general contributor role. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an Administrator action whose range is Conference (an administrative process of assigning papers to reviewers), while B's 'writes' is an Author-to-Contribution relation (authorship). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that announces a conference, whereas B's 'Conference Proceedings' is a published multi-author volume collecting conference papers. They denote different artefacts and are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Person/Chairman in cmt), while B 'Submission event' is an administrative event (subclass of Event in confOf). They belong to disjoint top-level categories (person vs. event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is the full conference submission (parent Document, children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To). B's Abstract is a distinct sibling of Paper under Document, i.e. the abstract artefact, not the paper itself. Different concepts despite both being documents.

A is a committee (a group/organisational body) that a conference volume has; B is a person role (a member of such a committee) under Person > Organizator. The two denote different kinds of entities (group vs. individual person), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) announcing the conference; B 'Mailing list' is a Document used to distribute information to a list of recipients. Although both are documents, their intended instances differ: an announcement is a notice, a mailing list is a distribution mechanism. No synonymy or subsumption holds.

A's 'early Registration' is a datatype property of Participant with boolean range, indicating whether a participant registered early. B's 'is held before' is an object property relating an Activity to a Time, i.e. a temporal ordering between events. They share no domain, range, or meaning; the only superficial link is the word 'early/before', which does not make them the same relation.

A's 'review Criteria Entered By' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered the review criteria), while B's 'is Reviewing' links a person (Chair/Reviewer/TPC) to a Paper they review. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference city' is a city that hosts a conference (a geographic location, sibling of Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city under City), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a building/room where a conference takes place (a Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote different kinds of entities (city vs. building/venue) and are not equivalent.

A's 'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's 'paper Presented As' links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the presentation event/format). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

cmt's assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review a paper), while iasted's sign relates a Person to an Item (a person signing an item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not the same relation.

A's Committee is a group/organisational body (with chairs, members, subcommittees like Program committee), while B's Participant is a person role (a subclass of Person, with early registration and siblings like Author, Chair PC). A committee is not a person, so the classes are unrelated.

Sponsorship (edas) is a funding arrangement class with cost amount/currency and provider relations to Organization; Possible Reviewer (ekaw) is a Person subclass that reviews papers. Different domains (funding vs. reviewing), no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document they authored (range Document, a paper-like artefact). B's 'send' relates a Person to an Item they send (e.g. a submission or email), a different relation with a broader, non-authoring range. They do not denote the same relation.

cmt:Paper is the general document class for submissions (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with review/decision/author properties), while edas:PendingPaper is a specific submission state (sibling of Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.) under edas:Paper. Pending Paper is a narrower concept than the general Paper class, so A is subsumed by B's broader Paper, not equivalent to the state-specific Pending Paper.
Trip is a social event (an excursion) in confOf, while Listener is a person role (attendee who listens) in sigkdd; they belong to different branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts.

Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Conference part is a structural component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) with children Track/Tutorial/Workshop and properties like 'has parts' and 'is part of conference volumes'. Their paths, siblings, children and properties do not overlap; they denote different concepts.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to a Contribution (reviewing a paper), while B's `obtain` relates an Author to an Award (receiving an award). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Presenter state' is a state (a phase/status of a presenter within the conference process, sibling of Conference state and Sponsor state under State), whereas B's 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Person/Speaker, i.e. a kind of person. A state and a person role are different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Conference applicant is a general person who applies to/attends a conference, with a child 'Registered applicant'; ekaw's Late Registered Participant is a specific subclass of Conference Participant (a registered attendee who registered late). They overlap in that both concern people registering for a conference, but neither subsumes the other: an applicant need not be registered (and certainly not late-registered), and a late-registered participant is a registered participant, not merely an applicant. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class linking a Reviewer to a Submitted contribution and expressing the reviewer's expertise/preference for reviewing that contribution. B's 'Review Form' is the form used to record a review (scores, comments) for a paper. They concern different concepts (expertise/preference vs. review form) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

confOf's writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while ekaw's hasUpdatedVersion links a Document to another Document (a later version). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

Accommodation Place is a kind of Place (lodging location) in edas, while Shuttle bus is a kind of Transport vehicle (a vehicle) in iasted. They denote different concepts: a place vs. a vehicle, with no overlap in instances.

A 'Conference Event' is an event (with attendees, programme, start/end date, location) in the edas ontology, whereas B 'City' is a geographic place with buildings and people occupying/visiting it. Their children, properties and domains/ranges do not overlap; a city is not a conference event.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details (domain Conference, range Administrator), while B's 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to the Event they organise (domain Organisation/Person, range Event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'manuscript Due On' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime deadline (the manuscript submission deadline). B's 'paper Presented As' is an object property linking an Abstract/Paper to an Individual Presentation (the presentation format/event). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI (its logo image), while B's 'is present in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place/Time (attendance). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap.

A's `contributes` goes Person -> Conference document (a person contributes a document), while B's `is prepared by` goes Item -> Person (an item is prepared by a person). They are inverse in direction and relate different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

Both are classes named 'Program committee'/'Program Committee' sitting directly under a 'Committee' parent, with sibling committees (Organizing/Steering vs Organizing/Best Paper Awards). Same intended concept: the committee that reviews papers for a conference.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome for a submission). B's is_visited_by relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a place being visited by a person). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A 'Review Question' is a question (numerical or textual) used in reviewing a paper, whereas B 'Possible Reviewer' is a person who may review papers (parent of PC Member, with properties has Reviewer, review Written By, reviewer Of Paper). They denote entirely different concepts (a review form item vs. a person role), so they are unrelated.

Topic is a subject area of papers/reviews in the Conference ontology, while Reviewer is a person role in edas. They denote different kinds of entities (a topic vs. a person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper in a specific publication state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper under Paper). B 'Transparency' is a document type under Document in iasted, alongside forms, invitation letters, mailing lists, etc. — an administrative artefact, not a paper. Different concepts despite both being documents.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title. B's has_a_name is a general naming property for Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic — it does not apply to papers and is a broader naming relation. The domains are disjoint (Paper vs. conference/venue entities), so the two properties do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A 'Conference contribution' is a document/artefact (a paper, poster, talk) that is part of a conference volume and is submitted at a volume; its children are document types (Poster, Presentation, Written contribution). B 'Speaker' is a person role (a Person who presents a Document), with children Author and Invited Speaker. The two denote different kinds of things (artefact vs. person role), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Regular contribution' is a specific kind of conference contribution (a written, non-invited contribution, with children Extended abstract and Paper), whereas B's 'Contribution' is the general superclass of all contributions (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like hasTitle, hasKeyword, writtenBy. Every regular contribution is a contribution, but not vice versa, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who started the bidding process), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman who chairs the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (a venue building, sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a document (subclass of Document, with children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version, sibling Review, and properties like has Author, assigned To, has Decision). B's Topic is a subject area/category (children are research topics like Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic; used via has Topic from Conference/Paper). A Paper is not a Topic; they denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is designed for' relates an Activity/Money/Time to an Activity/Person (a general purpose/audience relation), while B's 'designed by' relates a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation. Different domains, ranges, and direction; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Single Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference describing a conference with a single level (as opposed to a two-level conference), while B 'Sponsor state' is a subclass of State describing a state/status of a sponsor. They share no meaning, no properties, and belong to entirely different branches (Conference vs State).

Organizer is a person/role in the conference domain (someone who organises a conference), while Currency in iasted is a monetary unit class. They share no meaning, no properties, and no instances; the pair is unrelated.

A is a research topic area (a subject category under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a document type (an abstract for an invited talk, under Abstract). They denote entirely different kinds of things: a topic of study versus a conference document, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a document/artefact (a paper, poster, talk, review) submitted to and contained in a conference volume, with children like Poster, Presentation, Regular contribution. B's 'Conference' is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), sibling of Workshop, Session, Track. The two denote different kinds of things (artefact vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference document type (information for participants) under Conference document, while B is a research topic (Antennas) under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration), while B's hasCity relates an Organization or Person to a City (location). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Talk Event is an academic event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), while B's Speaker lecture is a session within a lecture activity, i.e. a specific speaking session. Both concern talks/lectures in the conference domain, but they sit at different levels of the event taxonomy (event vs. session) and neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a subclass of Person (a person who can review), while Person in sigkdd is the general superclass of all people (Listener, Organizator, Speaker). Possible Reviewer is strictly more specific than Person, so it is subsumed by Person.

A's 'written By' links a Document to the Person who authored it (authorship relation). B's 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person for whom the item is required (requirement/need relation). The domains (Document vs Item) and the intended meanings differ: authorship is not the same as being needed for someone. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Paper in cmt is a document (submitted contribution with authors, reviews, decisions), while Deadline in iasted is a point in time (submission/notification/camera-ready deadlines). Different domains (Document vs Time), no shared instances or properties; clearly unrelated.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is a document type: the abstract-only version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper. Active Paper (edas) is a paper in an active review state, sibling of Accepted/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper and parent of Rated Papers, with property has Rating. The two denote different concepts (document form vs. review status), so they are not equivalent.

A is a datatype property giving a person's last name (domain Person, range string); B is an object property linking activities/money/time to activities/persons. Different kinds, domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'name' is a datatype property giving a string name for a Conference or Person; B's 'early Registration' is a boolean flag on a Participant indicating early registration. Different domain, different range, different meaning — no overlap.

Organization in confOf is an institution (Company, University) that employs people and has an address; Committee in sigkdd is a group of people (Organizing, Program, Best Paper Awards committees). Different concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

Both are object properties linking a place/location to an event in the inverse direction (place -> event). edas 'is Location Of' has domain Place and range Conference Event; ekaw 'location Of' has domain Location and range Event. Place/Location and Conference Event/Event are the corresponding classes in the two ontologies, and the property names and directions match, so they denote the same relation.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the person hierarchy), while B 'Conference city' is a subclass of City, i.e. a location. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. place) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

Author is a person role in the conference (a subclass of Person, with children like Presenter and properties linking to Paper), whereas 'Nonauthor registration fee' is a monetary fee category (subclass of Registration fee under Money). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (people vs. fees) and share no intended instances.

A's Conference is the central event/organisation class of the cmt ontology (with submissions, dates, administrators, members). B's Conference_restaurant is a physical building/venue subtype under Place > Building, sibling to Conference airport, Conference hotel, etc. The shared word 'Conference' denotes a location in B, not the conference event itself, so the two classes are unrelated.
A's 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while B's 'is paid in' relates Money to a Building (payment location). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) in the event hierarchy, while B's Fee for extra trip is a monetary fee (sibling of Hotel fee and Registration fee) in the money hierarchy. They denote different concepts in different branches of the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Review preference' is a class representing a reviewer's preference/degree for a topic or submission (with properties has a degree, has a topic or a submission contribution, belongs to reviewers). B's 'Member PC' is a Person subclass (comment: Reviewer) representing a program-committee member who reviews contributions and is expert on topics. One is a preference record, the other a person role; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (range: Program Committee Member), while B's was_a_program_committee_of relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (range: Conference volume). They connect different kinds of entities and are not inverses either, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property of Conference volume giving its location (string), while B's 'has Title' is a datatype property of Contribution giving its title (string). They relate different kinds of things (a volume to a location vs. a contribution to a title) and are not the same relation.

A 'Conference Paper' is a kind of document (a paper submitted to/published at a conference), while B 'Program Committee' is a committee of people who review papers. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (where it is submitted), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and directions; not equivalent nor inverse.

A is a class of accepted conference contributions (a document/contribution in the submission workflow, sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B is a review-rating category (Week Reject Rating, sibling of Accept Rating and Reject Rating) — a value/type of rating, not a contribution. Different domains and kinds; no equivalence or subsumption.

confOf's Member PC is a program-committee member/reviewer (comment 'Reviewer', reviews Contributions, expert on Topics), while ekaw's Agency Staff Member is a person belonging to the organising agency (sibling of Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student). The two denote different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines), while B's 'need' links a Person to an Item (things a person requires). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Meal Menu is a document describing the menu of a meal event (has Menu / is Menu Of link it to Meal Event), whereas Abstract is the abstract text of a paper. Although both are subclasses of Document, their intended instances and roles in the conference domain differ completely, so they are not equivalent.

A Conference Trip is an excursion/outing (sibling of Conference Banquet under Social Event), while B Dinner banquet is a banquet meal event under Social program. They are distinct social-program activities, not the same concept.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole event such as a conference with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's Contributed Talk is an individual presentation within a scientific event, a much narrower and different kind of entity. They share no intended instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'remark' is a datatype property of Contribution holding a free-text note (confTool comment). Different domains (Person vs Contribution) and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's printHardcopyMailingManifests relates an Administrator to a Conference (a mailing action), while B's follows relates one Administrative event to another (temporal ordering of events). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (a sub-event relation within the event hierarchy), while B's forEvent links a Call to an Academic Event (a call-for-papers targeting an event). Different domains (Working event vs Call), different ranges (Administrative event vs Academic Event), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Author (cmt) is a person role who writes/submits papers, a subclass of Conference Member/User. Conference Event (edas) is an event with attendees, location, programme and start/end times, a subclass of nothing person-related. Their instances (people vs. events) cannot coincide, so the classes are unrelated.

A 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area under Topic in edas, while B 'Program Committee' is a committee of people under Committee in sigkdd. They denote entirely different concepts (research topic vs. committee), so they are unrelated.

A's Contact Information is a class aggregating address/contact details (city, email, phone, postal code, street) of a person or organisation, whereas B's City is a geographical place class with children like Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city and properties about being occupied by or situated in places. A City is only one component of contact information, not the same concept; the two classes have different instances and different property sets, so they are unrelated.

A's forEvent relates a Call to the Academic Event it is a call for (domain Call, range Academic Event), while B's partOfEvent is a mereological relation between an Event and a larger Event (domain Event, range Event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Proceedings is a multi-author volume document (a publication artefact, parent of Conference Proceedings). They denote different concepts in the conference domain: an event versus a published document, so they are unrelated.

A's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (a reviewer inviting co-reviewers), while B's 'is Review History Of' relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A Tutorial is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Workshop, linked from a Conference volume), whereas B Meal Menu is a document describing food for a meal event (sibling of Paper, Review, Programme). Different domains and no shared instances.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Trip day' is a time entity (a day of a trip/excursion). They belong to different branches (document vs. time) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop Chair is a conference participant role (a PC Member who chairs a workshop), while B Program Chair is an organizer role (head of the program committee, sibling of General Chair). Different roles in the conference organization: workshop chairing vs. program chairing, so they are not equivalent.

A's `name` is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's `has short title` is a short/abbreviated title for Social event and Working event. Different domains (Conference/Person vs Social event/Working event) and different intended meaning (full name vs short title), so they are not equivalent.

A's has Street is a datatype property giving the street address of an Organization or Person, while B's Nation gives a person's country. They relate different kinds of information (street address vs. nationality) and have different domains (Organization/Person vs. Person only), so they are not equivalent.

Track is a thematic stream of the conference (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, part of the conference structure, with has tracks from Conference volume), whereas Program Committee is a committee of people (sibling of Organizing Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee). They denote different concepts and share no instances.

Program Committee Chair (a chairing role within the program committee, subclass of Chairman and Program Committee Member) and Session Chair (a person who chairs a session, sibling of Author/Reviewer/TPC Member) are distinct chairing roles in the conference domain. They overlap in that both are chairing roles performed by persons, but neither subsumes the other: a PC Chair is not necessarily a Session Chair and vice versa. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document (authorship of a paper), while B's 'need' relates a Person to an Item (a need for some item). Different domain/range semantics and different intended relations; not equivalent.

A Presenter is a conference participant (a person role) in ekaw, while Sponsor company house is a building/place in iasted. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. location) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper). B's `paperPresentedAs` relates an Abstract/Paper to an Individual Presentation (the paper is presented as a presentation). Different domain and range, different direction of meaning; they are not the same relation.

Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Event is a happening such as a scientific or social event with a location, organisers and programme listings. Their paths, siblings and properties are entirely disjoint, so they denote different concepts.

A is a class of accepted papers (a document/contribution in the review workflow, sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B is a deadline (a time point, sibling of submission and notification deadlines). A document and a deadline are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

confOf's Social event is a general category of social events (with children Banquet, Reception, Trip), while ekaw's Conference Trip is a specific kind of social event (a sibling of Conference Banquet under Social Event). The confOf class is broader and subsumes the ekaw class, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B's 'Reception' is a social event (subclass of Social event, sibling of Banquet and Trip). They denote entirely different kinds of things in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial) held during a conference. B's Modelling is a research activity performed before the conference (sibling of Simulating), i.e. a kind of scientific activity, not an event. Different domains (event vs. activity) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is an administrative event (the registration-of-participants event in the conference schedule), while B is a committee (the program committee). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (Event vs Committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Introduction is a conference activity (an event segment, with child 'Introduction of speaker'), while B's Speaker is a person role (a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited Speaker). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members (people), while B's 'hold' links an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference it holds. Different domains, ranges and intended relations; no overlap.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event whose instances are the outcomes/results of reviewing made accessible to authors (a notification/result event). B 'Call For Reviews' is a call (solicitation) for reviewers, sibling of Call For Papers/Manuscripts. One is a result event, the other a call for participation; their intended instances do not coincide.

Reception (confOf) is a social event, while Registration fee (iasted) is a monetary fee; they are not equivalent, but both are part of the conference organisation domain and may be loosely associated through registration activities.

A's 'was a committee of' relates a Committee to a Conference volume (organisational affiliation), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents a paper). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

cmt:Author is a person who writes/submits papers (siblings include Reviewer, Program Committee Member; properties write Paper, submit Paper). edas:TPC Member is a program-committee member who reviews papers and initiates calls (properties is Reviewing, is Reviewed By, initiates). The two roles are distinct in the conference domain: an author writes papers, a TPC member reviews them. Although edas also has a separate Author class (sibling of TPC Member), the given pair Author vs TPC Member denotes different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has Been Assigned' is a domain-specific relation from Reviewer to Paper (a reviewer has been assigned a paper to review). B's 'has Part' is a generic mereological/part-whole relation with unspecified domain and range, used for decomposing entities into components. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's 'has an organizing committee' relates a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a subproperty of 'has a committee'), while B's 'holded by' relates a Conference to the ACM SIGKDD organization that holds it. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a paper document submitted to a conference, while B 'Audiovisual equipment' is a physical item (with children Computer, LCD projector, etc.). They share no meaning, no properties, and belong to entirely different branches (Document/Paper vs Item/equipment).

A 'Co author' is a Person/Author role (a person who co-writes a Paper), while B 'Multi author Volume' is a Document (a published volume with multiple authors, parent of Proceedings). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Document) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Event' is an event (with attendees, location, start/end times, programme) in edas, while B 'Conference Proceedings' is a published document (a Proceedings volume) in ekaw. An event and a publication are different kinds of things, so the classes are unrelated.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subtype covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors, while iasted Author is a narrow Speaker subtype for authors of proceedings/lectures. They overlap (authors are contributors) but neither subsumes the other: contributor includes non-author roles, and Author sits under Speaker with children like Lecturer and Tutorial speaker that are not contributors in the Conference sense.

Social event (confOf) is a subclass of Event denoting social gatherings like Banquet/Reception/Trip, while Speaker (sigkdd) is a subclass of Person denoting a person who presents. Different kinds (event vs person), no shared instances; unrelated.

A's Paper is a general document that can be accepted or rejected (it has hasDecision, accept Paper, accepted By, assigned To, etc.), whereas B's Accepted contribution is specifically a contribution that has already passed review and been accepted. Every Accepted contribution is a paper-like document, but not every Paper is accepted, so Paper is strictly more general than Accepted contribution.

A 'Slide Set' is a presentation artefact (sibling of Paper, Review, Programme under Document), while B 'Abstract' is a short summary document (sibling of Paper and Review). They denote different document types in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about the conference, with a URL), while B's 'Main office' is a physical place (a kind of Place alongside Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room). A document and a physical location denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference document class (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic class under Computer Networks Topic. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a conference as a working event in the conference-organisation domain. In confOf, Conference is a subclass of Working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop, i.e. a specific kind of organised academic event. In edas, Conference is the central academic event class with children Single Level Conference and Two Level Conference, and properties such as has Name, has Country, paper Due On, manuscript Due On, has Topic, has Member — all characteristic of a conference. The intended instances coincide (conferences), so the two classes are equivalent despite the different surrounding structure.

A's TPC Member is a generic program-committee member (sibling of Reviewer, Author, Session Chair; reviews papers). B's SC Member is a specific sub-role under PC Member, sibling of PC Chair, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair — a steering-committee-like member, not the general PC member. They overlap in being committee persons but denote different roles, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Conference Chair is a person role (a committee member who chairs the conference), while Proceedings is a document/volume of published papers. They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (the schedule of sessions), while hasEvent links an Event to its sub-events (a part-whole decomposition of events). Both are structural relations within the conference/event hierarchy, but they relate different kinds of things: a conference to its programme versus an event to its constituent events. They overlap in that a programme is composed of events, but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'belong to a conference volume' links an Important dates entity to a Conference volume, while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'adjust Bid' relates a Reviewer to a Bid (the bid being adjusted), while B's 'has Review History' relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History. The ranges are different concepts (Bid vs Personal Review History) and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's Committee is a conference-organisation body (with chairs, co-chairs, members, and subclasses Organizing/Program/Steering committee), whereas B's Organization is an institution such as a Company or University that employs Persons and has an address (city, country, postal code, street). The intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are unrelated.

In ekaw, Conference Participant is a broad role class under Person covering all attendees (chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.). In iasted, Author is a narrow role under Speaker, with children like Lecturer and Tutorial speaker, and sibling Reviewer. The two classes denote different concepts: a conference participant need not be an author, and an author is a specific speaker role, not the general participant class. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in the intended domain.

A's Conference is the event itself (it has a name and is a whole conference), while B's Conference Proceedings is a document (a Proceedings volume containing papers). The event and its published proceedings are different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Poster Paper' is a specific kind of Paper (a document presented as a poster), while B 'Abstract' is a distinct document type (a summary of a paper) that is a sibling of Paper, not a kind of Paper. Their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Track workshop chair' is a specific conference-organisation role (a person who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial, with properties linking to Conference part), while B's 'Scholar' is a generic person category (comment: 'price category - scholar') with a 'study At' property. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Banquet is a social event (a meal/ceremony) in confOf, while Dining Place is a physical location (a place where one dines) in edas. They are conceptually linked (a banquet occurs at a dining place) but denote different kinds of entities: an event vs. a location. Hence not equivalent; they are related.

A's Workshop is a specific kind of academic event, while B's Scientific Event is a broad category whose children include Conference, Session, Track and Workshop. Workshop is therefore strictly more specific than Scientific Event, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A Bid in cmt is a reviewer's expressed willingness/preference to review a paper (domain Reviewer, range Bid, linked to Paper via has Bid). Location in ekaw is a venue/place where an Event is held (held In: Event -> Location). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Communications Topic' is a subject area of papers (a Topic in the edas ontology, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Transport vehicle' is a physical item (a subclass of Item with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'location Of' is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's 'Price' is a datatype property linking a Registration fee to an integer amount. They relate entirely different kinds of entities (Location/Event vs Registration fee/int) and have no overlap in meaning, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Administrator (comment 'confTool') is a person administering the conference tool/system, while ekaw's Agency Staff Member is a person belonging to an agency (e.g. a funding or organising agency) in the conference domain. They share only the parent Person and do not denote the same concept.

A's 'adjusted By' relates a Bid to a Reviewer (who adjusts the bid), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (who pays the fee). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's min Choice is a datatype property on Social/Working event with range positiveInteger (minimum number of choices for an event, per confTool comment), while B's Start of conference is a datatype property on Conference with range dateTime (the conference start date). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during a conference, whereas a Single hotel room is a type of accommodation place (sibling of Double hotel room). They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship of a paper), while B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (membership in the conference/committee). Different domains (document vs. conference) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

cmt's Review is a document-like entity (subclass of Document, sibling of Paper, has a Meta Review child, and is written by a Reviewer), whereas edas's Review Form is the form/artifact used to submit a review rather than the review itself. They are closely related in the conference domain but not the same concept, so a reference alignment would not record them as equivalent.

Both denote a physical venue for a conference, but 'Conference airport' is a Building (a specific building type alongside conference building/hotel/restaurant), while 'Conference hall' is a direct subclass of Place (a room/hall venue alongside Hotel and Main office). They overlap in the conference-venue sense but are not the same concept, so a reference alignment would not record them as equivalent.

cmt:date is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's date, while confOf:starts on is a datatype property of Event giving the start time of an event. Both concern temporal information, but they apply to different entities (Conference vs Event) and cmt:date is a general date rather than specifically a start time, so they are not equivalent; they are merely related temporal properties.

A's has Street is a datatype property of Organization/Person giving a street address, while B's City of conference is a datatype property of Conference giving a city. They have different domains (Organization/Person vs Conference) and different intended values (street vs city), so they do not denote the same relation.

An 'Initial manuscript' is a specific stage of a submission (sibling of 'Final manuscript' under 'Submission'), whereas 'Paper' in sigkdd is the general document type that authors submit and that has reviews. Every initial manuscript is a paper, but not every paper is an initial manuscript (it could be a final manuscript or a camera-ready version), so the iasted class is strictly narrower than the sigkdd class.

A's 'Conference part' is a general container for Track, Tutorial and Workshop (its children), i.e. any component of a conference. B's 'Conference' is a specific working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop under Working event), not a container of them. The two do not denote the same concept: A's class is broader and includes the very things B's Conference is distinct from, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property linking a Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while B's 'relates To' is an object property linking a Document to events, sessions or persons. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (proceedings vs document) and range (int vs entities), so they denote different relations.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a kind of Paper (a scientific contribution submitted to a conference), while B 'Mailing list' is a Document used for communication (a list of addresses). They share no intended instances: one is a research paper, the other a mailing list artefact. Different parents (Paper vs Document) and different sibling sets confirm they denote different concepts.
A's email is a Person's email address; B's has Fax is a Person's fax number. Different contact attributes, so the properties are not equivalent (nor does one subsume the other).

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the person assigned to review it), while B's 'covers Topic' links an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (the subject matter it deals with). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

hasCity relates an Organization/Person to a City (the city where a person or organization is located), while is_situated_in relates a Building/City/Place to a Building/City/Place/State (spatial containment of places). They overlap in the sense of locating something in a city, but the domains and ranges differ substantially (agents vs. places), so they are not equivalent; they are merely related.

Both are places for dining/restaurant at a conference, but A is a generic dining place under Place while B is a specific restaurant building under Building; they overlap in the conference domain but are not the same concept.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), i.e. a symmetric co-occurrence relation between events. B's 'is Initiated By' relates a Call to a person role (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. who issued/started a call. Different domain, different range, different meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's Poster is a kind of Contribution (a submission type, sibling of Paper and Short paper), while B's Best Student Paper Supporter is a kind of Sponzor (a sponsorship level, sibling of Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (submission vs. sponsorship) and share no intended instances.

A's reviewCriteriaEnteredBy links a Conference to the Administrator who entered review criteria, while B's give links a Person to an Activity or Item they give. Different domains (Conference vs Person), different ranges (Administrator vs Activity/Item), and different intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'has parts' is a whole-part (meronymic) relation from a Conference volume to its Conference parts, whereas B's 'part Of Event' is a mereological relation between Events (an event being part of a larger event). Both express composition/parthood, so they overlap conceptually, but their domains and ranges differ (Conference volume/Conference part vs Event/Event), so they are not the same property.

A's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Accepted contribution' is a class of documents (a reviewed contribution that was accepted, with child Camera ready contribution), while B's 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity/process (sibling of Receiving manuscript, Refusing manuscript) in the pre-conference phase. They are related in that the activity results in the accepted contribution, but they denote different kinds of entities (document vs. activity), so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Paper is a submitted scientific contribution (has authors, reviews, decisions, subject areas), while iasted:Form is an administrative document (registration, hotel, author-information forms). They share only the generic Document parent; their instances and roles in the conference domain do not coincide.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about a conference, with a URL), while B's 'Computer Networks Optical Topic' is a research topic in the EDAS topic hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. topic) and share no intended instances.
A is a kind of conference paper (a document type), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment; they share no intended instances and belong to entirely different branches of the domain.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a session type in a conference programme), while B's Worker lecturer is a person role (a lecturer who is also a worker) under Speaker/Author/Lecturer. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

In EDAS, Session Chair is a direct subclass of Person, a role distinct from Author/Reviewer/TPC Member. In EKAW, PC Member is a subclass of Possible Reviewer and is the parent of Session Chair (along with PC Chair, SC Member, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair). So EKAW's Session Chair is a kind of PC Member, meaning EDAS Session Chair is more specific than EKAW PC Member; the two are not equivalent.

IASTED member is a subclass of Delegate (a person role/attendee type), while Conference hall is a subclass of Place (a physical location). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. location) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Volunteer in confOf is a Person subtype (sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.) denoting someone who helps at the conference, while Author in iasted is a Speaker subtype denoting someone who writes papers. They are different roles with no subsumption or overlap; the shared word 'author' does not appear in the confOf entity.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean datatype property of Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted; B's 'lists Event' is an object property linking a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event. They have different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (paper-to-proceedings/venue), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (conference-to-participant). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.
A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a count of reviews per paper, a property of a Conference; B's 'Price' is the fee of a Registration fee. Different domains, different intended meanings, no overlap.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to the Organization they work for, while iasted's is_present_in relates a Person to a Place/Time where they are present. Different domain/range semantics (Organization vs Place/Time) and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class covering all people involved in a conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), while Chair in Conference is a specific committee role. Conference Member is strictly more general than Chair, so it subsumes it rather than being equivalent.

A's 'Conference restaurant' is a subclass of Building (a physical place, sibling of Conference hotel/airport), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself with properties like start/end date, city, and held-by relation. They denote different concepts (a venue building vs. the conference event), so they are unrelated.
Trip is a social event (an excursion) in confOf, while Tax is a monetary charge in iasted; they share no meaning, no properties, and belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Money).

A 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the actual reviewing procedure for submitted contributions), while B 'Call For Manuscripts' is a call document/announcement soliciting manuscript submissions. One is an event, the other a call; they denote different concepts despite both relating to reviewing/submission.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (author contributes a paper). B's 'is paid by' relates Money to a Person (a fee is paid by a person). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they denote different relations.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (a person), while B's 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (a paper). Different domain and range, and different direction of meaning (expertise association vs. reviewing action), so they are not the same relation.

A's Reception is a social event (a gathering/activity) in the conference domain, while B's Speaker is a person role (a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited Speaker). They denote entirely different kinds of entities — an event versus a person — so they are unrelated.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a specific leadership role within a committee), while B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (general membership in a conference). The domains (Chair vs Person), ranges (Committee vs Conference), and intended meanings differ; they are not the same relation.

A Conference Trip is a social event (a type of event/activity) in the ekaw ontology, while One conference day is a temporal unit (a day within the conference schedule) in the iasted ontology. They belong to different top-level categories (Event vs Time) and denote different concepts: a trip is an activity, a conference day is a time interval. Therefore they are unrelated.

A's 'is Topic Of' relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper (a topic is the subject of a paper/conference), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Radio Communications Topic' is a research subject area under Topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's property links a conference part to a topic (domain Conference part, range Topic), while B's property links administrative events to each other (domain/range Administrative event). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

Trip is a specific social event (an excursion) in confOf, while Social program in iasted is the broader category of social activities, with Dinner banquet as a child. A trip is a kind of social program, so Trip is subsumed by Social program, not equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a public announcement inviting the community to submit papers/register for a conference; B 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is an internal document introducing a session chair. They are different document types with different purposes and no subsumption relation.

A's 'Written contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution' (a document/contribution artefact, with children Regular contribution and Submitted contribution), whereas B's 'Contributed Talk' is a subclass of 'Individual Presentation' (an event/presentation activity, sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial). One denotes a written document, the other a spoken presentation event; they are different kinds of things despite the shared 'contributed' wording.

A is a research topic category (Operating Topicsystems) under Topic, while B is the Program Committee, an organizational committee under Committee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chairing/organisational role under Chairman/Conference Member, whereas Invited Speaker (sigkdd) is a speaking role under Speaker. They denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's Talk Event is a general academic event (parent of Welcome/Closing Talk, sibling of Paper Presentation and Workshop), while B's Tutorial is a specific kind of individual presentation (sibling of Contributed/Invited Talk). A tutorial is a presentation type, not a general talk event, and the two classes have different parents and siblings, so they do not denote the same concept.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a specific award given to a paper. They belong to different branches (Conference document vs Award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's prepare relates a Person to an Item (a person prepares an item), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). The domains, ranges and directions differ, so they are not the same relation.

A is a Person subclass (a role: track/workshop chair), while B is an Event subclass (a Workshop event). They belong to disjoint top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's Session is a kind of conference activity/lecture (an event slot in the programme), while B's Organizator is a role of a Person (someone who organises the conference). They belong to different top-level branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's `location Of` is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's `Name of conference` is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (its name). They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain/range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Member is a Person role (author, reviewer, chair) in the conference domain, while B's University is an Organization (a venue/affiliation), not a person. Their parents (Person vs Organization), siblings (Chairman/Reviewer vs Company) and properties (member Of Conference vs study At) are entirely different, so the classes denote different concepts.

A's 'paper Presented As' relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the paper is presented as a presentation), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity/Item (a person gives a presentation/talk). They both concern presenting at a conference but differ in domain (Paper vs Person) and direction of the relation, so they are not equivalent; they are merely related concepts in the presentation sub-domain.

A's 'Program committee' is a specific kind of committee (a sibling of Organizing and Steering committees under Committee), while B's 'Committee' is the general superclass with 'Program Committee' as one of its children. Thus A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's Dining Place is a place for eating, sibling to Accommodation Place and Conference Venue Place; B's Hotel is a lodging place, sibling to Conference hall and Main office. They denote different kinds of places (dining vs. lodging), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving an integer volume number, while B's 'min Choice' is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a positive integer minimum choice (confTool). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held at a conference, while B's Week Reject Rating is a review rating category (sibling of Accept Rating and Reject Rating) in the EDAS review process. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a conference attendee who does not present (a subtype of Conference participant, sibling of Active conference participant). B 'Sponsor' is a person or organisation providing financial support, a direct subtype of Person, sibling of Delegate. The two denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's Program Committee is a specific kind of committee (the one that reviews papers), while B's Committee is the general superclass with children Best Paper Awards Committee, Organizing Committee, and Program Committee. Thus Program Committee is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Committee, not equivalent.

A's authorOf relates a Person (author) to a Document they wrote; B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker who presented it. Different domains/ranges and different directions of meaning (authorship vs. presentation), so they are not equivalent.

A's Trip is a social event (a kind of excursion/activity, sibling of Banquet and Reception under Social event), whereas B's Sponsor city is a kind of City (a location, sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Trip city). One denotes an event, the other a place, so they are not equivalent.

A is an administrative event (the reviewing-results event, accessible to authors) in confOf's event hierarchy, while B is a committee (the organizing committee) in sigkdd's committee hierarchy. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper in a specific publication state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper under Paper), while B 'Bank transfer' is a payment document (sibling of Cheque under Payment document). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (scientific document vs. payment method) and share no intended instances.

In edas, Attendee is a Person who attends the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.), whereas in ekaw Paper Author is a Person who authors a paper (sibling of Conference Participant, Student, etc.).
