An attendee is not necessarily an author and an author is not necessarily an attendee, so the two classes denote different concepts.

Conference Chair in cmt is a chairing role (subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Program Committee Chair), whereas Assistant in confOf is a generic helper role (sibling of Administrator, Volunteer, Participant). They denote different conference roles and do not coincide.

A's hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper (a general related-paper relation), while B's hasUpdatedVersion links a Document to a Document (a versioning relation between successive versions of the same document). Different domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A is a phase/activity class ('Activity before conference') in the iasted event taxonomy, a subclass of Activity with children like Accepting manuscript, Receiving manuscript, Renting, Research. B is a person role class ('Author') under Person > Speaker, with properties submit, obtain, notification until. The two denote entirely different kinds of things (a temporal activity phase vs. a person role), so they are unrelated.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a conference applicant who has registered (a subclass of Conference applicant, with child Paid applicant), i.e. a person in the registration process. B 'Participant' is a broader Person subclass covering all attendees (Member, Regular, Student, etc.) with an early Registration property. A registered applicant is a kind of participant, but Participant is not restricted to applicants, so A is strictly narrower than B: subsumed_by.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it, while B's 'need' links a Person to an Item they need. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

confOf's Science Worker is a generic person role (sibling of Author, Participant, Chair PC, etc.) under Person, while sigkdd's Organizing Committee member is a specific organizer role under Organizator, sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, etc. The intended instances do not coincide: a Science Worker need not be an organizing committee member, and an organizing committee member is a specific conference organizer rather than a generic science worker.

A's 'reviews' relates a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's 'search' relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (domain ACM SIGKDD, range Sponzor). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Steering committee' is a distinct committee (sibling of Organizing and Program committees) that oversees the conference series, while B's 'Program Committee' is the committee that reviews papers. They are different committees, not synonyms.

A is a conference document type (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic category (Signal Processing Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author denoting a person who authors but does not review; B's 'Reviewer' is a subclass of Speaker denoting a person who reviews. They are complementary/opposed roles, not the same concept, and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Short paper' is a type of contribution (a document category), while B 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is a committee. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (Contribution vs Committee) and share no intended instances.

A's writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (domain Reviewer, range Review), while B's is_writen_by relates an Item to a Person (domain Item, range Person). The directions and the kinds of entities differ: writeReview is a reviewer-to-review relation, whereas is_writen_by is an item-to-author relation (the inverse of writes). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them, while B's 'occupy' links a Person to a Building/City/State they occupy. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are unrelated.

A's 'Committee member' is a subclass of Person restricted to people who are members of a committee (children Chair, Co chair; properties has members / was a member of). B's 'Person' is the general superclass of all people in the conference domain (Attendee, Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). Every committee member is a person, but not every person is a committee member, so Committee member is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Person.

A's 'lists Event' relates a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event (a publication lists events), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an excursion/outing) in ekaw, while B Welcome address is a conference activity (an opening speech) in iasted. They denote different concepts: one is a recreational social event, the other a formal talk/activity. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference organisation (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Place (edas) is a physical location such as a venue, meeting room or accommodation, related to Conference Events via has Location. The two concepts share no instances and no meaning; they are unrelated.

hasCity relates an Organization or Person to a City, while occupy relates only a Person to a Building, City, or State. They overlap in the Person-to-City case but differ in domain (Organization vs Person only) and range (City vs Building/City/State), so they are not equivalent; occupy is broader in range and narrower in domain.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper in a specific publication state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper under Paper), while B 'Mailing list' is a document artefact (sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Review, Submission) under Document. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A Free Time Break is a specific kind of break (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break under Break Event), whereas B Conference activity is a broad category covering coffee breaks, lectures, presentations, registration, social program, etc. Every free time break is a conference activity, but not vice versa, so A is strictly more specific than B.

In cmt, Preference is a class representing a reviewer's preference/interest in a paper (a submission-related concept), while in iasted Currency denotes a monetary unit (e.g. registration fee currency). They share no intended instances and belong to different subdomains, so they are unrelated.

A is a full version of a paper (a document type in the conference submission hierarchy), while B is a sponsorship level (Silver Supporter) under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a numeric/quality score assigned to a paper), while B's go_through links an Item to an Activity (an item participating in or undergoing an event). The domains and ranges denote different concepts and the relations are not the same, so they are not equivalent.

cmt:name is a general label property applying to Conference and Person, while edas:hasBiography is a specific property for a person's biography text. They share only the string range; the intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's Reviewer is a Person (a person who reviews), while B's Review is a Document (the review artefact itself, with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review). They denote different concepts (agent vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'starts on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string (a date/time), while B's 'has Event' is an object property linking an Event to another Event (e.g. a session to its sub-events). They relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a human person in the conference domain. cmt Person has children Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User; confOf Person has children Administrator, Assistant, Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, Scholar, Science Worker, Volunteer. Both are the general superclass of conference actors with contact properties (email/name vs has Email/has First Name), so they coincide.

A's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines), while B's 'parallel with' links an Administrative event to another Administrative event (sessions running concurrently). Different domain, range and meaning; no overlap.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a submitted paper that was not accepted, a subclass of Reviewed contribution. B 'Textual Review Question' is a kind of review question (free-text question on a review form), a subclass of Review Question. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (contribution outcome vs. review form element) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Review preference' is a class representing a reviewer's declared preference/degree of interest in reviewing a topic or submission (it has a degree, belongs to reviewers, and links to topics/submissions). B's 'Review Question' is a class representing a question on a review form, with subclasses Numerical Review Question and Textual Review Question. The two denote different concepts: a preference/interest record versus a form question. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Conference Chair (edas) is the general chair of the whole conference, a Person who initiates calls and reviews; Demo Chair (ekaw) is a Conference Participant responsible only for the demo track. Different roles with different scopes and different siblings (edas: Attendee/Author/Reviewer; ekaw: PC Chair/Tutorial Chair/Workshop Chair), so they are not equivalent.

A is an administrative sub-event of a conference (the registration process, sibling of Submission/Reviewing events), while B is the conference itself, a scientific event. They denote different concepts: one is a procedural event within a conference, the other is the conference edition.

A's `need` relates a Person to an Item (a person needs an item), while B's `designed by` relates a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (the deadline is designed by the conference). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), expressing a scheduling/co-location relation between events. B's 'has Attendee' relates a Conference Event to a Person, expressing participation. They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and have no overlap in meaning, so they are unrelated.

In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (a person who gives a talk and writes papers), while in sigkdd Organizator is a Person who organizes the conference (General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc.). The intended instances differ: authors are not organizers, and the paths/parents/children show no overlap in meaning.

A's Web Site is a kind of Document that is a programme brochure-like web artefact (siblings include Programme Brochure, Flyer, Paper) and is listed by events; B's Abstract is a document that is a summary of a paper. They denote different concepts despite both being Documents, so they are unrelated.

Excursion is a social/non-academic conference event (sibling of Reception), while Invited Speaker is a person role (sibling of Author). They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. person) and denote different concepts.

Conference announcement is a conference document (call for papers/participation, review, etc.) in the Conference ontology, while Operating Topicsystems is a research topic category under Topic in edas. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

Paper in cmt is a document (submitted contribution with authors, reviews, decisions), while 'Deadline hotel reservation' in iasted is a time/deadline concept under Deadline. They denote entirely different things and share no instances.

A's 'Rejected Paper' is a class of documents (a paper that was evaluated and rejected), while B's 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity/process (the act of receiving a manuscript), sibling of Accepting/Refusing manuscript. Different kinds (class of document vs. event/activity) and different meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Conference hall and Hotel are distinct sibling classes under Place in the respective ontologies; a conference hall is a venue room, while a hotel is a lodging establishment, so their instances do not coincide.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a type of conference session event (Industrial Session). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Program committee' is a committee (a group of people) that reviews papers for a conference, with properties linking it to a Conference volume. B's 'Social program' is a conference activity (a social event such as a dinner banquet) under Conference activity. They denote entirely different concepts—an organisational body versus a social event—so they are unrelated.

OC Member is a person role (a conference participant who is a member of the organising committee, parent of OC Chair), while Registration is a conference activity (an event with Delegate as a child). They belong to different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Short paper' is a contribution type (sibling of Paper and Poster) in confOf, while B's 'Poster Paper' is a specific paper format under Paper in ekaw. A short paper is not the same concept as a poster paper; they are distinct submission/paper categories, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'has tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a part-whole relation over event components), while B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (membership/participation). Different domain (Conference volume vs Conference) and different range (Tutorial vs Person), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

SC Member (ekaw) is a Steering Committee member, a role of a person within the conference organisation hierarchy (Person > Possible Reviewer > PC Member > SC Member). Registration Non Member (sigkdd) is a fee category for attendees who are not members of the sponsoring society (Fee > Registration fee > Registration Non Member). One is a committee role, the other a registration fee type; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's Modelling is a research activity (a kind of Activity before conference, sibling of Simulating), while B's Webmaster is an organizational person role (a kind of Organizator, sibling of General Chair and Program Chair). They belong to entirely different branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' relates a Contribution to its Author (domain Contribution, range Author), while B's 'reviewer Of Paper' relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (domain Possible Reviewer, range Paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning (authorship vs. reviewing), so they are not equivalent.

Both properties relate an author/person to a paper/item they write. cmt's writePaper has domain Author and range Paper; iasted's write has domain Person and range Item. Author is a kind of Person and Paper is a kind of Item in the conference domain, so the two properties denote the same relation (writing a paper), just with more general domain/range in iasted.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a Conference contributor (a person role in the conference organisation, sibling of Regular author and Active conference participant). B's 'IASTED member' is a Delegate subtype under Conference building, i.e. an attendee membership category (sibling of IASTED non member, Listener, Speaker). An invited speaker is a distinguished presenter, not a membership status of a delegate; the paths, parents and siblings differ, so the classes do not denote the same concept.

Both properties link a person who presents (Active conference participant / Speaker) to the thing presented (Presentation / Document). In the conference domain a presentation is the document/paper being presented, so the two relations denote the same concept in the same direction, despite the different range class names.

A's Invited speaker is a kind of conference contributor (a person invited to speak), while B's Lecturer is a subclass of Author in a person/building hierarchy with children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer, i.e. a teaching role rather than an invited conference speaker. The two roles overlap in that both can be speakers, but they are not the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a conference-domain role (first author of a contribution), while B is a hotel-room type in the iasted ontology. They share no concept, no properties, and belong to entirely different branches (document/author vs. place/hotel room).

A's User is a Person (an agent role: Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Lecture is a Conference activity (an event with children Plenary lecture, Session, Tutorial). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and share no context, so they are unrelated.

has City relates an Organization or Person to a City (domain Organization/Person, range City), while is visited by relates a Building, City or State to a Person (domain Building/City/State, range Person). They are inverse in direction and concern different subject/object kinds, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the program committee of a conference: cmt's Program Committee has members and is the domain of 'has Program Committee Member', while Conference's Program committee is a subclass of Committee with a program committee membership relation to Conference volume. Same intended concept, just different naming conventions.

A's scientificallyOrganisedBy relates an event/conference to an Academic Institution (a subproperty of organisedBy), while B's hold relates ACM SIGKDD (an organisation) to a Conference. The domains and ranges differ (Academic Institution vs ACM SIGKDD; unspecified event vs Conference), and the direction of the relation is not the same concept, so they are not equivalent.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (Reviewer -> Bid), while hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (Paper -> Possible Reviewer). They have different domains, different ranges, and opposite directions of the reviewer-paper relationship; they are not equivalent.

confOf's Science Worker is a broad Person subtype (siblings include Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, etc.) covering anyone involved in the conference, while edas's Attendee is a Person subtype specifically denoting someone who attends the conference (siblings Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). The two overlap (an attendee is a science worker in the broad sense) but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Academia Organization' is a subclass of Organization (an institutional type such as university, alongside Government/Industry Organization and NGO), whereas B's 'Organizing Committee member' is a subclass of Person/Organizator (a role a person plays in a conference committee). They denote different kinds of entities (institution vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Paper is the general document class for submitted papers (parent Document, children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version, with review/decision/author properties), while edas:Accepted Paper is a specific status subclass of edas:Paper (siblings Active/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper). Accepted Paper is strictly narrower than Paper, so Paper subsumes Accepted Paper (Accepted Paper is subsumed_by Paper).

A 'Registeered applicant' is a person who has registered for a conference (a subclass of Conference applicant, with Paid applicant as a child). B 'Delegate' is a broad conference participant class (parent of Speaker, Session chair, Listener, etc.) that also sits under Person and Registration. A registered applicant is a kind of delegate/participant, but Delegate is much broader (includes speakers, chairs, sponsors' people, etc.), so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person (a person who authors papers), while B 'Best Research Paper Award' is a subclass of Award (a prize). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a kind of person (a conference attendee who does not present), while B 'Conference Dinner' is a meal event within the conference schedule. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Conference Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Record of attendance' is a Document (an administrative artefact recording who attended, sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document), whereas B's 'Author' is a Person/Speaker who writes papers and has properties like submit(Paper) and obtain(Award). Different kinds (document vs. person) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Reviewed contribution' is a subclass of Submitted contribution (a paper that has undergone review, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution) and is the range of 'has a review' / domain of 'reviews'. B's 'Review' is a Document sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter, etc., i.e. the review document itself, not the reviewed paper. The two denote different concepts (reviewed paper vs. review document), so they are unrelated.

Conference participant is a broad Person subclass covering all participants (active/passive, committee members, reviewers, etc.), while Non speaker is a Delegate subclass specifically for attendees who do not present (students/workers). They overlap in that non-speaking delegates are conference participants, but neither subsumes the other: Conference participant includes speakers and organisers, and Non speaker is restricted to delegates. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'has a review' relates a Reviewed contribution to its Review (domain Reviewed contribution, range Review). B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (domain Person, range Activity/Item), i.e. a person giving/performing something. Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; not the same relation.

Conference Event is a class of conference-related events (with attendees, programme, location, start/end times), while Time zone is a temporal/geographic concept with no overlap in intended instances; they are unrelated.

Contribution in confOf is a general submission entity (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) that is written by authors, reviewed by PC members, and has title/abstract/keywords. Award in sigkdd is a prize given to authors (obtain: Author -> Award, awarded by, award), with children being specific best-paper awards. They denote different concepts: a submission vs. a prize, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic in computer networks (a subject area under Topic), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical computer under Audiovisual equipment). They share only the word 'computer' and denote entirely different concepts.

A's Paper is a scholarly contribution (written by authors, reviewed, has topics, subclasses Accepted/Rejected/Pending Paper). B's Payment document is a financial document (subclasses Bank transfer, Cheque) under Item > Document. They share only the generic Document parent and are semantically unrelated.

A's 'end Review' relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (chair ends a review), while B's 'review Written By' relates a Review to a Possible Reviewer (author of the review). They have different domains/ranges and opposite directions of the review relationship, so they are not equivalent.

A's `write` relates a Person to an Item (authorship), while B's `holded by` relates a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD organisation (event sponsorship/organisation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'accepted By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting). They have different domains, ranges, and directions, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract, while B's 'has Related Paper' links an Author to a related Paper. Different domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

Company in confOf is an organization (sibling of University) that participates in the conference, while Cheque in iasted is a payment document (sibling of Bank transfer) used to pay fees. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Presenter city' is a subclass of City denoting the city where a presenter is located, while B's 'Hotel' is a subclass of Place denoting a lodging venue. They share no intended instances and belong to different branches (City vs Place), so they are unrelated.

A's Topic is a subject area of contributions/PC expertise/working events (dealsWith, expertOn, hasTopic), while B's Time is a temporal entity with children Conference days, Deadline, Trip day and properties like is held before/after, is present in. They denote different concepts (subject matter vs. time point/interval) and share no instances.

A Travel Grant is a type of sponsorship/funding (a subclass of Sponsorship), while B Sponsor is a person role (a subclass of Person, sibling of Delegate). They denote different concepts: a funding mechanism versus a person who provides funding, so they are not equivalent.

A's Industrial Session is a specific kind of Conference Session (a session type within a conference), while B's Session is a broader Lecture subtype in iasted covering plenary, tutorial and speaker lectures. A is narrower than B, so Industrial Session is subsumed by Session, not equivalent.

A's `date` is a generic conference date property (domain Conference, range date), while B's `registrationDueOn` is specifically the conference registration deadline (comment: 'Conference Registration Date and Time Deadline'). Although both are datatype properties on Conference, they denote different relations: one is a general date, the other a specific deadline. A reference alignment would not equate them.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference organisation, a subclass of Conference Member/User, with properties linking authors to papers (write Paper, submit Paper, has Author). Sponsorship (edas) is a funding arrangement with cost amount/currency and a provider organization, with child Travel Grant. The two concepts share no instances and no meaning; they are unrelated.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a paper submitted to a conference (a document in the scientific paper hierarchy), while B 'Bank transfer' is a payment document (a financial instrument). They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different domains within the conference ontology.

A 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area for conference papers (a subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Overhead projector' is a piece of audiovisual equipment (subclass of Audiovisual equipment, sibling of LCD projector, Video cassette player). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Workshop in confOf is a working event (a kind of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas CAD Topic in edas is a research subject area (sibling of Antennas Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.). The two denote different concepts: an event vs. a topic, so they are unrelated.

The two properties are inverses, not equivalents: cmt's writeReview goes from Reviewer to Review (a reviewer writes a review), while ekaw's reviewOfPaper goes from Review to Paper (a review is of a paper). They relate different kinds of things in opposite directions, so a reference alignment would not record them as equivalent.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Person), while Organizing Committee in sigkdd is a committee (a subclass of Committee), i.e. a group/organizational entity. They denote different kinds of things (person vs. committee), so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a contribution/paper that has passed review and been accepted: A's 'Accepted contribution' sits under 'Reviewed contribution' with sibling 'Rejected contribution' and child 'Camera ready contribution'; B's 'Accepted Paper' sits under 'Paper' with siblings 'Rejected Paper', 'Published Paper', etc. The intended instances coincide (accepted submissions), so the classes are equivalent.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while B's searched_by relates a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (sponsor search relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Presenter is a role of a person (a Conference Participant who presents), while B's Introduction is a conference activity/event (the introductory session, with child 'Introduction of speaker'). One denotes a person role, the other an event; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A 'Contributed Talk' is a submitted/accepted presentation given by an author, a sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial under Individual Presentation. B 'Tutorial' is a distinct kind of lecture/instructional activity, sibling of Plenary lecture and Session. Although ekaw also has a Tutorial class, the candidate pairs Contributed Talk with Tutorial, which denote different concepts; they are not equivalent.

A's 'written By' is an object property linking a Document to a Person (its author), while B's 'Name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string literal. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and cannot denote the same relation.

A's 'Co author' is a person who co-writes a paper (a co-author role, sibling of 'Author Not Reviewer', with properties co write Paper / has Co author). B's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role of the first author of a conference contribution, sibling of 'Contribution co author' and parent/child of 'Regular author'. Both are author roles in the conference domain, but one denotes a co-author (non-first author) and the other the first author of a contribution; they overlap as author roles but do not denote the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Trip in confOf is a social event (an activity, sibling of Banquet and Reception), whereas Hotel fee in iasted is a monetary fee (sibling of Registration fee and Fee for extra trip). One is an event, the other a cost, so they denote different concepts.

confOf's Social event is a broad category of social/leisure events (children Banquet, Reception, Trip) under Event, while edas's Meal Event is a narrower non-academic event specifically involving meals (child Conference Dinner, property has Menu). They overlap (a banquet is both a social event and a meal event) but neither subsumes the other: Social event includes trips/receptions that are not meals, and Meal Event includes breaks/dinners that need not be social events in confOf's sense. Hence related, not equivalent.

confOf's Participant is a general role of a Person attending the conference (children include Member, Regular, Student, Author, Chair PC, etc.), while iasted's Speaker is a specific kind of Delegate (a presenter) with children Author and Reviewer. Every Speaker is a conference participant, but not every Participant is a Speaker, so Participant is broader and Speaker is subsumed by it.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B's 'Tutorial' is a working event (sibling of Conference and Workshop). They belong to different branches (document vs event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Tutorial Abstract' is a document (an abstract of a tutorial, sibling of Invited Talk Abstract under Abstract), while B 'Tip' is a monetary concept (a gratuity, sibling of Fee, Sponsorship, Tax under Money). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's Conference is the whole conference event (has a name, has parts, proceedings, publisher, topics), while B's Social event is a sub-event of a conference (banquet, reception, trip) with choices, VAT and location. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a biographical text, while B's Name links a Person to their name string. Although both are Person->string datatype properties, biography and name denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract is a document type (a kind of Paper, sibling of Paper Full Version) in the conference-submission hierarchy, whereas Microelectronics Topic is a subject-area topic (a kind of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts: one is a paper artefact, the other a research topic, so they are unrelated.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to the Organization that employs them, while ekaw's organises relates a Person or Organisation to an Event they organise. Different domain (Person vs Person/Organisation) and different range (Organization vs Event), and the intended relations (employment vs event organisation) are distinct, so they are not equivalent.
Both entities denote the same conference-domain concept/relation; labels and context agree.

A's 'email' is a datatype property for a person's email address, while B's 'has the first name' is a datatype property for a person's first name. They represent different attributes of a Person and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Author in cmt is a conference member who writes/submits papers, with children like Author Not Reviewer and Co author and properties linking to Paper. Agency Staff Member in ekaw is a Person subtype for staff of an agency, sibling to Paper Author and Conference Participant, with no paper-related properties. The intended instances do not coincide; Author is not equivalent to Agency Staff Member.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer). B's 'reviewer Of Paper' links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper they review (domain Possible Reviewer, range Paper). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings differ; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Published Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document state: a paper that has been published), while B's 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity in the pre-conference phase (the act of receiving a submission). One is a document, the other an event/activity, so they do not denote the same concept.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (a text/web page giving practical info to attendees), while B's 'Organizational Meeting' is an academic event (a scheduled meeting). They belong to different branches (document vs event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (a paper related to the author), while B's is_writen_by relates an Item to a Person (authorship, the inverse direction of writes). They differ in domain, range, and meaning: one is a loose 'related paper' association, the other is the authorship relation. Not equivalent, not inverse-equivalent either since the semantics differ.

A's Poster is a kind of conference contribution (a document/paper type with an abstract), while B's Poster Session is a session event in which posters are presented. They denote different concepts (document vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a conference/event type (a conference with two levels of reviewing/committees), while B's 'Reviewer' is a person role (a delegate/speaker who reviews). They denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to its Review, while B's 'has Updated Version' links a Document to another Document (a later version). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Best Student Paper Award' is a type of award given to a student paper. They belong to entirely different branches (Conference document vs Award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a steering committee' links a Conference volume to its Steering committee (a specific committee role), while B's 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper), while B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domains (Conference vs Event), different ranges (Administrator vs Organisation/Person), and different intended meanings (data entry vs organisation), so they are not equivalent.

A's PC Member is a reviewer-role person (a Possible Reviewer who serves on the programme committee, with children PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc.). B's Author is a speaker-role person (a Speaker who authors papers, with children Lecturer, Plenary lecture speaker, Tutorial speaker, and sibling Reviewer). The two denote different roles in the conference domain — committee membership versus authorship — and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Bank transfer' is a payment document (a financial instrument, sibling of Cheque) in the iasted ontology, while B 'Abstract' is a document type (sibling of Paper and Review) in sigkdd. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain; the shared word 'document' is only an ancestor, not a synonym.

A's 'Submitted contribution' is a specific stage in the contribution lifecycle (a written contribution that has been submitted, with children like 'Reviewed contribution' and siblings like 'Regular contribution'), whereas B's 'Contribution' is the general superclass of all contributions (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with authorship, title, abstract and review properties. Every submitted contribution is a contribution, but not every contribution is submitted, so A is strictly more specific than B.

A's Author is a person who writes/submits papers (path Person > Conference Member > Author, with properties write Paper, submit Paper, has Author). B's Session Chair is a person who chairs a session and participates in reviewing (initiates Call, is Reviewing Paper), a role distinct from authoring. The two classes denote different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'gives presentations' links an Active conference participant to a Presentation (the act of presenting), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (authorship of a paper). Different domains (participant vs author), different ranges (presentation vs contribution), and different intended relations (presenting vs authoring); they are not the same relation.

A's Proceedings is a document/volume class (a collection of papers, parent Multi author Volume, child Conference Proceedings). B's Author book proceedings included is a subclass of Author describing a person (an author whose book proceedings are included), sitting among Speaker/Lecturer roles. One denotes a publication artefact, the other a person role, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B 'Meal Break' is a scheduled non-academic event (subclass of Break Event, sibling of Coffee Break). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. event) and share no intended instances.

Both properties link a conference (Conference volume / Conference Event) to its programme committee (Program committee / Programme). The domain and range concepts coincide in the conference domain, and the labels 'has a program committee' and 'has Programme' denote the same relation, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a specific kind of committee (sibling of Program committee and Steering committee under Committee), while B's 'Committee' is the general parent class with 'Organizing Committee' as a child. Thus A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A 'Conference Member' is a Person (a person involved in a conference, with subclasses Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B 'Conference Proceedings' is a Document (a published multi-author volume of proceedings). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Document) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Camera Ready Paper is a specific stage/type of paper (the final version accepted for publication), a subclass of Paper in ekaw. The sigkdd Paper class is the general paper concept (submitted to a conference, with submit property from Author). Camera Ready Paper is strictly narrower than Paper, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Paper (a document/artefact: the abstract text of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version), whereas B's 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Author (a person role: someone who authors a paper, sibling of Author of paper student). One denotes a document part, the other a person/role; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

Both denote a regular (non-invited, non-poster) conference paper/contribution. In Conference, Regular contribution is a kind of Conference contribution with children Extended abstract and Paper; in ekaw, Regular Paper is a kind of Paper. The intended instances (regular papers) coincide, so they are equivalent despite the different parent structure.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person (a person who authors a paper). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (membership of people in a conference), while B's is held before relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

edas:isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference/committee), while ekaw:partOf is a generic mereological/participation relation with unspecified domain and range. They overlap in that both can express a person being involved in a conference, but isMemberOf is a specific membership relation and partOf is a broader part-whole relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with two levels, sibling of Single Level Conference), while B 'Early Registered Participant' is a kind of person (a conference participant who registered early). They denote different concepts (event vs. person) and are unrelated.

Scholar in confOf is a price/fee category of person (comment: 'price category - scholar') with property study At (Scholar -> University), while Conference Chair in edas is an organisational role that initiates calls and reviews papers. They share only the parent Person; their intended instances and properties do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

Presenter in ekaw is a Conference Participant who presents a paper (a speaker role, with child Invited Speaker), whereas iasted's Worker non speaker is a Delegate who is a non-speaker (explicitly not a speaker). The two denote disjoint roles: one is a speaking participant, the other a non-speaking participant, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Administrative event' is a subclass of Event covering organisational events like submission, reviewing, registration and camera-ready; B's 'Program Committee' is a subclass of Committee denoting a group of people. They belong to different branches (Event vs Committee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property of Conference with range int, counting the number of reviews per paper. B's 'has Review' is an object property from Paper to Review, linking a paper to its review entities. They differ in domain (Conference vs Paper), range (int vs Review), and kind (datatype vs object), so they are not the same relation.

Money is a general monetary amount class with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip, and properties for paying for activities/items and being paid by persons. Registration fee is a specific kind of Fee (path Fee > Registration fee) with concrete subclasses for member/student/non-member registrations and properties Currency, Price, pay, payed by. Registration fee is thus a narrower concept than Money, so Money subsumes Registration fee (Registration fee is subsumed by Money).

has City relates an Organization or Person to a City (the city where they are located), while can stay in relates a Person to a Place (a venue/hotel where they can stay). Both link a person to a location, so they overlap, but the domains differ (Organization is included in has City) and the ranges differ (City vs. the broader Place), and the intended meanings (residence/affiliation city vs. accommodation place) are not the same, so they are not equivalent.

A Volunteer is a generic Person subtype (sibling of Participant, Author, etc.) in confOf, while B Program Committee member is an Organizator subtype (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair) in sigkdd. A volunteer is not a program committee member; the concepts denote different roles with no subsumption or overlap.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the outcome of reviewing a paper), while B's is_equipped_by relates a Place to an Item (equipment of a location). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property linking a Social/Working event to a string title, while B's 'has Event' is an object property linking an Event to another Event (a part/containment relation). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, and range, so they denote different relations.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation from abstract to the contribution it belongs to), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains (Abstract vs Author), different ranges (Paper/Poster/Presentation vs Contribution), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property linking a Conference volume to a string (its location text), while B's 'is present in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place/Time. Different domains (Conference volume vs Person), different ranges (string vs Place/Time), and different kinds (datatype vs object), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'assigned To' goes from Paper to Reviewer (a paper is assigned to a reviewer), while B's 'is Reviewing' goes from a person role (Reviewer, Chair, etc.) to Paper (a person is reviewing a paper). They are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

A's `is Location Of` goes from Place to Conference Event (a place is the location of an event), while B's `held In` goes from Event to Location (an event is held in a location). They are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

A's Workshop is a Working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Tutorial is a Lecture under Conference activity. They denote different conference concepts (workshop vs. tutorial), and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (a paper/contribution), while B's 'need' relates a Person to an Item (a needed resource). Different ranges and different intended meanings; not the same relation.

A's 'Track workshop chair' is a Person (a role/committee member who chairs a track, workshop, or tutorial), while B's 'Track' is a Scientific Event (a thematic track of a conference). They belong to different top-level categories (Person vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Meeting Room Place is a specific kind of place (a room for meetings), while B Building is a broader physical structure that can contain rooms and is occupied/visited by persons. They overlap in that a meeting room is typically inside a building, but neither subsumes the other: a building is not a meeting room, and a meeting room is not necessarily a whole building. Hence related, not equivalent.

A 'Textual Review Question' is a specific kind of question (a free-text question on a review form), sibling of 'Numerical Review Question' under 'Review Question'. B 'Review' is a document artefact (a completed review), sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter, etc. under Document. A question is not a review document; the entities denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authoring a paper), while B's 'awarded by' relates an Award to some entity (the recipient/issuer of an award). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a document type (a full paper submission) in the cmt ontology, while B 'Computer' is a piece of audiovisual equipment in the iasted ontology. They share no meaning in the conference domain and have completely different paths, parents and siblings.

Both are subclasses of Author, but A (Co author) is a co-author of a paper, while B (Author book proceedings included) is an author whose book appears in the proceedings. They overlap in that both are authors, but neither subsumes the other; the intended instances do not coincide.

Chairman in cmt is a person who chairs (a role with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), whereas Participant in confOf is any person taking part in the conference (subclasses Member, Regular, Student). A chairman is a participant, but the classes are not coextensive: most participants are not chairmen, and the intended instances do not coincide. The shared parent Person and the differing subclasses/properties (Conflict Of Interest vs early Registration) confirm they denote different concepts.

A 'Short paper' is a specific kind of contribution (a short version of a paper), while B 'Paper' is the general document class covering all paper types (regular, demo, poster, workshop, etc.). A Short paper is thus a Paper, but not every Paper is a Short paper, so Short paper is subsumed by Paper.

Member PC is a person role (a PC member/reviewer) in confOf, with properties expert On and reviewes. Personal Review History in edas is a record/history entity (a collection of reviews) that is the range of has Review History and domain of is Review History Of, linked to a Reviewer. One is a person, the other a data record, so their instances cannot coincide.

SC Member (Steering Committee Member) is a subclass of PC Member in ekaw, i.e. a member of the steering committee of reviewers, whereas Program Chair in sigkdd is an organizer role (chair of the program committee), a sibling of General Chair and Program Committee member. The two denote different roles: one is a committee member, the other a chair/organizer, so they are not equivalent.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee), while B's sign relates a Person to an Item (signing up for an item such as a registration or event). The ranges differ (Conference vs Item) and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's Poster is a specific kind of conference contribution (a presentation format, sibling of Presentation and Invited talk, with an abstract). B's Document is a general administrative item (parent of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Review, Submission, etc.), not a contribution type. The two concepts do not coincide; Poster would at best be a Submission/Publication in B, not a Document.

A's 'detailsEnteredBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person who entered details). B's 'has_a_track-workshop-tutorial_chair' relates a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (a role for a workshop/tutorial track). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while B is a conference activity (Welcome address, a subclass of Conference activity). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `give` relates a Person to an Activity/Item (a person gives/presents something), while B's `presentationed by` relates a Document to a Speaker (the document is presented by a speaker). The domains and ranges are reversed and the kinds of entities differ (Person vs Document, Activity/Item vs Speaker), so they are not the same relation; at best they are inverses of a broader 'presentation' relation, which does not count as equivalence.

A's Conference Chair is the overall conference organizer (a Person who initiates calls and reviews, sibling of Author/Reviewer/TPC Member), while B's Session Chair is a conference participant who chairs a single session (subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member, sibling of Workshop Chair/Tutorial Chair). Different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

In confOf, Participant is a subclass of Person (path: Person > Participant), so every Participant is a Person, but not every Person is a Participant. The Conference ontology's Person is the broader class (with children like Committee member, Reviewer, etc.), while confOf's Participant is a narrower role. Thus Conference Person subsumes confOf Participant.

Both are subclasses of Place denoting physical locations used for conference activities, but 'Meeting Room Place' is a general meeting-room location while 'Conference hall' is a specific large hall; they overlap without coinciding, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both are object properties linking an organising body (Administrator / ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference, i.e. the same relation 'organises/holds a conference' in the conference domain; the differing labels are synonyms and the domain/range structure matches exactly.

A's property links a Review preference to the Topic/Submitted contribution it prefers, while B's property links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domains (Review preference vs Document), different ranges (Topic/Submitted contribution vs Speaker), and different intended relations (preference about topics vs presentation by a speaker). No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's Review is a document produced by a reviewer about a paper (sibling of Paper, parent of Meta Review, written by a Reviewer). B's Review expertise is a topic/expertise area linking reviewers to submitted contributions (domain/range involve Reviewer, Review preference, Submitted contribution). They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'Review'.

A's isWrittenBy goes from Paper to Author (paper -> author), while B's authorOf goes from Person to Document (person -> document). They are inverse relations, not equivalent: one relates a paper to its author, the other relates a person to the documents they authored. A property and its inverse are not equivalent.

Both denote a paper/contribution that has been submitted to a conference. A's 'Submitted contribution' is a written contribution submitted for review (parent Written contribution, child Reviewed contribution, involved in review expertise/preference and review assignment). B's 'Submission' is a Document that is submitted, with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript, i.e. the submitted paper. The intended instances coincide: the submitted paper/contribution. The differing siblings (Review, Form, etc.) reflect a broader document taxonomy in iasted, but the concept itself matches.

A's 'has tracks' is a specific part-whole relation from a Conference volume to its Tracks, while B's 'part Of Event' is a general mereological relation between Events. The general Event-to-Event part relation subsumes the more specific volume-to-track relation, so 'has tracks' is subsumed by 'part Of Event' rather than equivalent.

cmt:Conference is the central event entity (has members, accepts submissions, has dates, administered by an Administrator), while confOf:Organization is an institution (parent of Company and University) that employs Persons and has an address. They denote different concepts and share no instances.

In edas, Document is a broad class whose children include Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, etc. In sigkdd, Paper is a subclass of Document (path Document > Paper), so sigkdd's Document is the broader concept and Paper is one kind of document. The edas Document therefore corresponds to sigkdd's Document, not to sigkdd's Paper; edas Document is strictly more general than sigkdd Paper, so it subsumes it.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Person, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology, while B's 'Single Level Conference' is a kind of conference event (subclass of Conference, sibling of Two Level Conference) in edas. One denotes a person, the other an event type; they share no intended instances and are unrelated.

A's `follows` relates two Administrative events (an ordering/succession relation between events), while B's `attendee At` relates a Person to a Conference Event (attendance). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person (a person affiliated with a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself (with a name and a conference volume). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

Workshop is a working event (a meeting/activity) in confOf, while Book proceeding is a publication item (a book of proceedings) in iasted. They belong to different branches (Event vs Item/Publication) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference document is a class of documents (calls, contributions, reviews, announcements) with authors and issue dates, while Organization is an organizational entity (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provides sponsorships. Their instances, children, and properties do not overlap, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair in edas is a Person role that initiates calls and reviews papers, while Program Chair in sigkdd is an Organizator role. Both are senior organizational roles in the conference domain, but they are not the same concept: a Conference Chair typically oversees the whole conference, whereas a Program Chair specifically leads the program committee. They overlap in being high-level organizers but are distinct roles, so 'related' is the safest relation.

A is a placeholder/test topic within the conference Topic taxonomy (a subject area for papers), while B is a physical item type (Card, with child Credit card) in an Item hierarchy of equipment/documents. Different domains and no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a review rating category (accept-if-room rating) under Review Rating, while B is the abstract of a document under Document. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Person is a human agent (children: Committee member, Reviewer, Conference participant; properties: has an email, has gender, has first/last name, contributes to a Conference document). B's Place is a spatial location (children: Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room; properties: is equipped by, is situated in, is held in). The two classes denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a person who has registered for a conference (a subclass of Conference applicant, with child Paid applicant), whereas B 'Personal History' is a container of a person's publication and review records. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Assigned Paper is a conference paper that has been assigned to a reviewer (a subclass of Submitted Paper in the paper-review workflow), while Credit card is a payment card item in the iasted ontology. They share no meaning, instances, or context; the only superficial overlap is the word 'card' in unrelated senses.

A's hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a person who may review the paper), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents it). The domains (Paper vs Document) and especially the ranges (Possible Reviewer vs Speaker) denote different roles, and the relations point to different kinds of participants, so they are not the same property.

A's reviewCriteriaEnteredBy relates a Conference to the Administrator who entered review criteria; B's presentationed_by relates a Document to the Speaker who presented it. Different domain, range, and intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is the general document class for conference submissions (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Demo Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a sibling of Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). The general Paper in cmt corresponds to the general Paper in ekaw, which subsumes Demo Paper; thus cmt Paper is more general than ekaw Demo Paper.

A's 'Introduction of speaker' is a conference activity (a sub-event of Introduction, under Conference activity) — the act of introducing a speaker. B's 'Invited Speaker' is a person role (a subclass of Speaker, sibling of Author). One is an event/activity, the other a person, so they cannot denote the same concept.

City in confOf is a geographic location used as the range of 'has City' (Organization/Person -> City), i.e. the place where an organization or person is located. 'Time zone' in iasted denotes a time-offset region, not a city or location of an organization/person. They share no intended instances and no subsumption relation, so they are unrelated.

A is a class of documents (a Paper in the Accepted state, sibling of Rejected/Pending/Published Paper), while B is a class of people (an Author, a Speaker who submits papers). Their intended instances are disjoint: papers vs. persons. No subsumption or overlap exists, so they are unrelated.

A's hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author (authorship relation). B's paperInVolume relates a paper to a volume/proceedings (containment relation). Different kinds of things are related in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a reviewed contribution that was rejected, while B 'Pending Paper' is a paper still awaiting a decision. Their paths and siblings differ: A's sibling is 'Accepted contribution' under 'Reviewed contribution', whereas B's siblings include 'Accepted Paper', 'Rejected Paper', 'Withdrawn Paper', etc. under 'Paper'. They denote different stages of the submission process, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a call inviting submissions), while B's 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event reporting review outcomes to authors. Different kinds (document vs event) and different meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both classes are named Person and represent the same general concept of a human participant in the conference domain. In edas, Person is the superclass of Attendee, Author, Reviewer, etc.; in iasted, Person is the superclass of Delegate and Sponsor. The differing children reflect different modelling granularity, not a different intended meaning, so the two classes denote the same concept.

A's 'was a member of' links a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation). B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (giving/presenting relation). Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's isReviewHistoryOf links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (a person's review record), while B's presentation links a Speaker to a Document (a talk given by a speaker). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both classes denote a paper that has been submitted but not yet accepted/finalized: ekaw's Submitted Paper is a Paper that is not yet camera-ready (its child Assigned Paper is the reviewed version), and iasted's Initial manuscript is the submission-stage document, sibling of Final manuscript. Same intended instances in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a social event that is a trip/excursion during a conference. They share the same parent (Social event / Social Event) and the same sibling structure (Banquet, Reception vs Conference Banquet), and the labels Trip and Conference Trip are synonymous in this domain.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document representing the abstract of a paper, while Submitted Paper in ekaw is a paper that has been submitted for review. They are related in that a submitted paper typically includes an abstract, but they are not equivalent: a submitted paper is a full paper submission, not just its abstract, and an abstract need not be submitted as a paper.

A's hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (event -> programme), while B's give links a Person to an Activity or Item (person -> activity/item). Different domain, range and direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a topic in the Computer Networks topic hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document type vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

confOf Organization denotes an institution (Company, University) that employs people and has an address; edas Place denotes a physical location (accommodation, venue, dining, meeting room) that is the location of a conference event. Their instances, children, and properties do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Personal Review History' is a subclass of Personal History describing a reviewer's own review record, with properties linking it to a Reviewer. B's 'ACM SIGKDD' is the conference organisation itself, with properties to Deadline, Conference and Sponzor. They denote entirely different concepts (a personal history record vs. an organisation), so they are unrelated.

Poster is a type of contribution (a paper presented as a poster) in confOf, while Final manuscript is a stage of a submission document (the camera-ready version) in iasted. They denote different concepts: one is a submission category, the other a document version, so they are not equivalent.

Pending Paper is a paper in a submission/review state (siblings: Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, Published, Active), whereas Demo Paper is a paper category/type (siblings: Regular, Poster, Industrial, Workshop, Conference). They denote different dimensions of classification and do not coincide.

hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author (Paper -> Author), while write relates a Person to an Item (Person -> Item). They describe the same underlying authorship relation but with reversed direction and different (more general) domain/range, so they are not equivalent; they are related as inverse-like relations over the same domain concepts.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (membership in a committee), while B's organises relates an Organisation or Person to an Event (organising an event). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is a publication artefact (has publisher, volume, ISBN, issued by a Publisher), while B's 'Conference' is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop under Working event). They denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while B's Poster Paper is a specific kind of paper (sibling of Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc.) under Paper. A's Paper is broader and would include B's Poster Paper, so A is subsumed by B's more specific concept; they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property linking a Person to their surname string, while B's 'has Email' links a Person to an email address string. Although both are Person->string datatype properties, they denote different attributes (surname vs. email address), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Program committee' is the committee that reviews papers, while B's 'Organizing Committee' is the committee that organises the conference. In B, the corresponding entity is the sibling 'Program Committee', not 'Organizing Committee'. They are distinct committees, so the pair is unrelated.

A's 'parallel with' relates Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), expressing that two events run in parallel. B's 'topic Covered By' relates a Research Topic to the Event or Paper that covers it, a topic-to-artefact relation. Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/committee member who chairs the conference), while B 'Conference building' is a physical place (a building where the conference is held, with children like Delegate). They denote entirely different concepts: one is a person, the other a venue/building. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

A's 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session/talk in which an accepted paper is presented), sitting under Conference Event > Academic Event alongside Talk Event and Workshop, and is linked to Accepted Paper via relatedToPaper/relatedToEvent. B's 'Conference Paper' is a document (a paper submitted to/published at a conference), under Document > Paper alongside Camera Ready Paper, Submitted Paper, etc. One is an event, the other a document; they are different kinds of things, not equivalent.

Both denote a reviewer's preference for reviewing a topic/submission. cmt's Preference is the class of reviewer preferences over topics/papers, and Conference's Review preference is the class of a reviewer's preference for a topic or submitted contribution, with properties linking it to reviewers, topics and submissions. The intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

cmt's submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper), while iasted's write relates a Person to an Item (the act of authoring a document). Both connect an author/person to a paper/item, so they overlap in the conference domain, but submission and writing are distinct relations (one can write without submitting and vice versa), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B 'Sponsor company house' is a building/place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (document vs. physical location), so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chair of the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in cmt, while Industry Organization is a type of organization (sibling of Academia/Government/NGO Organization) in edas. They denote different kinds of entities (person role vs. organization type) and share no meaning.

Session Chair (ekaw) is a conference participant who chairs a session, a role distinct from PC Member (its parent is Conference Participant and PC Member). Program Committee member (sigkdd) is an Organizator, i.e. a member of the program committee, not a session chair. The two roles are different: a session chair need not be a PC member, and a PC member need not chair a session. Thus the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document type in the conference-organisation domain (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B 'Satellite And Space Communications Topic' is a research subject area under Topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Working event' is a conference-domain event class (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop; sibling of Social/Administrative event), while B is a specific research topic in a topic taxonomy under Computer Networks Topic. They denote entirely different kinds of things and share no instances.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole event type alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Lecture is a conference activity (a sub-event/session type with children Plenary lecture, Session, Tutorial). They denote different concepts: an event type vs. a talk/session activity, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole event such as a conference with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's Track is a scientific event sub-unit (siblings include Conference, Workshop, Session, Individual Presentation). A conference is not a track; they denote different concepts in the conference domain.

A's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines), while B's 'organisedBy' links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domain, range and meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

Both classes denote a person who is an author of a paper/contribution. In Conference, 'Contribution co author' is a subclass of 'Regular author' (a person who co-authors a contribution), with sibling 'Contribution 1th author' (first author). In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a subclass of 'Author' (a person who authors a paper), with sibling 'Author of paper student'. The intended instances coincide: individuals who are authors of papers/contributions. The slight difference in naming (co-author vs author) does not change the concept, as both refer to the author role in the context of a paper/contribution.

A's 'Reject Rating' is a specific rating value in EDAS's review-rating scale (siblings: Accept Rating, Accept If Room Rating, Week Reject Rating), i.e. a recommendation/score category. B's 'Neutral Review' is a review whose overall polarity is neutral (siblings: Negative Review, Positive Review), a kind of review document, not a rating value. Different intended instances and different parents (Review Rating vs Review), so they are not equivalent.
A is a Document/Form subclass (a hotel registration form document), while B is a Place subclass (a hotel venue). Different kinds: form vs. location, so they are unrelated.

A 'Single Level Conference' is a conference whose organisation has a single tier (as opposed to a 'Two Level Conference'), i.e. a kind of conference event. B 'Conference Trip' is a social event (an excursion) that is part of a conference, sibling of 'Conference Banquet'. They share only the word 'conference' and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Place is a general location concept whose children include Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place and Meeting Room Place, and it is the range of has Location / domain of is Location Of for Conference Events. In iasted, Building is a subclass of Place (path Place > Building) and denotes a physical building (conference airport, hotel, restaurant, university, company house, etc.) that is occupied/visited by persons and situated in a place. Thus Building is a narrower, physical kind of Place; every Building is a Place, but not every Place (e.g. a city or state) is a Building. Hence A is more general than B: subsumed_by.

A is a datatype property giving a person's first name (Person -> string), while B is an object property linking an Item to an Activity or Money (Item -> Activity, Money). They have different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.
A's email is a Person's email address; B's has the last name is a Person's family name. Different datatype properties with different intended values, so they are not equivalent.

A 'One conference day' is a single day within the conference-days subdivision of the time axis, whereas B 'Conference' is the whole conference event with a city, name, start/end dates and a holding organisation. A day is a temporal part of a conference, not the conference itself, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (who added the member), while B's 'was a committe co chair of' relates a Co chair to a Committee (the committee they co-chaired). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'is paid in' relates Money to Building (where money is paid), while B's 'pay' relates Person to Registration fee (a person paying a fee). Different domain, range, and direction of the relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B 'Bank transfer' is a subclass of Payment document (a document/artefact describing a payment method). They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote different attributes: an email address versus a biography text. They are not synonyms and do not relate the same kinds of things, so a reference alignment would not equate them.

Both classes denote the chair of the organising committee: cmt's Associated Chair is a Chairman who is also a Conference Member (i.e. an organiser), and ekaw's OC Chair is an OC Member who chairs the organising committee. The intended instances coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing domain), while B's 'is Menu Of' relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (catering domain). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI (its website address), while B's 'lists Event' is an object property linking a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event.
