They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Programme Brochure/Web Site) and range (anyURI vs Event), so they denote different relations.

A's authorOf relates a Person (author) to a Document (authored work). B's is_needed_for relates an Item to a Person, i.e. the Person needs the Item — a different direction and different kinds of things (Item vs Document, and the Person is the range rather than the domain). They are not the same relation.

A's 'issues' relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes; B's 'designed by' relates a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation that set it. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the two properties are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a conference part (a type of event/venue component alongside Track and Tutorial, with has workshops linking a Conference volume to a Workshop). B's Paper Presentation is an Academic Event in edas, a session in which accepted papers are presented, sibling to Workshop and Talk Event. Although edas also has a Workshop class, the candidate pairs A:Workshop with B:PaperPresentation, which denote different concepts: a workshop is not a paper presentation session. They are unrelated.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document type (a short version of a paper, sibling of 'Paper Full Version' under 'Paper'), whereas B 'Performance Topic' is a subject area/topic category (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc. under 'Topic'). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's hasRelatedDocument links a broad set of agents/events (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person) to a Document, i.e. an association between a person/event and a document. B's prepare links a Person to an Item, i.e. a person preparing some item. The domains differ (A includes events, B only Person) and the ranges differ (Document vs Item), and the intended meanings (having a related document vs preparing an item) do not coincide, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'accepted By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains (Paper vs Person), different ranges (Administrator vs Item), and different meanings (acceptance vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A's Poster is a kind of Contribution (a paper/presentation type, sibling of Paper and Short paper), while B's Gold Supporter is a sponsorship level under Sponzor (sibling of Platinum/Bronze/Silver Supporter and Exhibitor). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (scientific contribution vs. sponsorship), so they are unrelated.

A's Tutorial is a kind of working event (a session type at a conference, sibling of Conference and Workshop), whereas B's Conference city is a subclass of City describing the city in which a conference takes place (sibling of Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city). They share no meaning: one is an event type, the other a location role. Unrelated.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property of a Conference document (a paper/contribution) giving the date the document was issued/published, with domain Conference document and range date. B's 'manuscriptDueOn' is a datatype property of a Conference giving the deadline by which a manuscript must be submitted, with domain Conference and range dateTime. The domains differ (document vs conference) and the intended meanings differ (issue/publication date vs submission deadline), so they are not the same relation.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event) in confOf, while a Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment in iasted. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (a person role), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the talk/slides). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; no equivalence.

A is a research topic class (Radio Communications Topic) under Topic in edas, while B is a deadline class (Deadline Abstract Submission) under Deadline in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject area vs. event deadline) and share no intended instances.
A's authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while B's pay relates a Person to Money (payment). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Short paper' is a contribution type (a short version of a paper), while B 'Demo Paper' is a specific paper category for demonstrations. They denote different kinds of documents and are not synonyms; no subsumption holds either.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented), while B 'Best Research Paper Award' is a type of award given to a paper. They belong to different branches (event vs. award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's 'is sent after' relates an Item to a Time (temporal ordering of an item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount for student registration). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'follows' relates two Administrative events (temporal ordering of events), while ekaw's 'organises' relates an Organisation or Person to an Event (agent organising an event). Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'enable Virtual Meeting' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an agent enabling a virtual meeting), while B's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (a physical/spatial containment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote the general concept of a person in the conference domain. Conference:Person is the root person class with children covering committee members, participants, reviewers, etc., and properties for name, email, gender, and authorship. ekaw:Person is likewise the general person class with children covering participants, authors, reviewers, students, and properties for authorship and organising events. The intended instances coincide (all humans involved in conferences), so the classes are equivalent.

A's forEvent relates a Call to the Academic Event it is issued for (domain Call, range Academic Event). B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document they present (domain Speaker, range Document). Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'name' is a datatype property of Person (path Conference, Person > name > string), giving a person's name. B's 'endDate' is a datatype property of Conference (path Conference > endDate > dateTime), giving the conference end date/time. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

cmt:Paper is a document (a written contribution with abstract/full version, authors, reviews, decisions), while ekaw:Individual_Presentation is a scientific event (a talk given at a conference, with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial). A paper is presented as a presentation, but the paper itself is not the event; the two entities belong to different branches (Document vs Event) and denote different concepts.

A's hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string title; B's heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. Different domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper (a document type: the full version of a paper, sibling of Paper Abstract). B's 'Author of paper student' is a subclass of Author (a person role: a student author of a paper, sibling of Author of paper). One denotes a document, the other a person role; they are in different branches of the taxonomy and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (the person who is qualified to review), while B's 'reviewer Of Paper' links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the paper the reviewer is assigned to). Different domain and range, and different direction of meaning: one expresses reviewer qualification, the other a reviewer-paper assignment. They are not the same relation.

A's Presenter is a role of a person (subclass of Author, a Person), while B's Presenter house is a building/place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. location), so they are unrelated despite the shared word 'Presenter'.

City is a location class used as the range of 'has City' (Organization, Person -> City), whereas Person is an agent class with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker and properties such as Name, E mail, Nation, can stay in, pay. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

confOf's Organization is a general organisation class with subclasses Company and University and is the range of 'employed By'; edas's Academia Organization is a specific subclass of Organization (siblings Government/Industry/NGO). Academia Organization is strictly narrower than Organization, so A is subsumed by B.

A's User is a general person role (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer) in the cmt ontology, while B's Registration SIGKDD Member is a specific registration-fee category under Fee > Registration fee. They denote different concepts: a person role vs. a fee type, so they are not equivalent.
A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while B's 'held In' links an Event to a Location (venue of an event). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; no overlap.

A is a datatype property giving the end time of a conference event (domain Conference Event, range dateTime). B is an object property linking a programme brochure or web site to the events it lists (domain Programme Brochure/Web Site, range Event). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and cannot be equivalent.

A's property links a Committee to its Co chair (a role within a committee), while B's property links a Person to an Item they prepare. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a person role in the conference committee hierarchy (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while Free Time Break is a scheduled non-academic conference event (a kind of Break Event). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (person vs. event) and share no intended instances.
A's 'written By' links a Document to its author (Person), while B's 'is present' links a Person to a Time. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Contribution in confOf is a general submitted work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) written by authors and reviewed by PC members. Review in ekaw is a document that reviews a paper, written by a possible reviewer, with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review. They denote different concepts: a submission vs. an evaluation document, so they are not equivalent.

A is 'Rejected contribution' (a reviewed contribution that was rejected), while B is 'Accepted Paper' (an evaluated paper that was accepted). They are opposite outcomes of the review/evaluation process, so they are not equivalent; in fact they are disjoint concepts.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (the person who is qualified to review), while B's 'write' links a Person to an Item (authorship of a paper). Different domain, range and direction of meaning; not the same relation.

A's Conference Banquet is a social event (a dinner/banquet activity) under Event > Social Event, while B's Conference days is a temporal concept under Time, with children Delegate and One conference day. They denote different kinds of things (an event vs. a time period), so they are not equivalent.

A's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship of a paper), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity/Item (a person giving something). The domains and ranges are reversed and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

hasAuthor (Paper -> Author) and writtenBy (Contribution -> Author) relate the same kinds of things but in opposite directions: writtenBy is the inverse of hasAuthor, not equivalent to it. Since Paper and Contribution are equivalent classes, the two properties are inverses, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's Dining Place is a place for eating (sibling of Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Meeting Room Place), while B's Conference hall is the venue where the conference takes place (sibling of Hotel, Main office). They denote different kinds of places in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A Program Committee is a group/committee entity with members, whereas Possible Reviewer is a role class for persons who may review papers (parent of PC Member). They are related in the conference domain (PC members are reviewers) but not the same concept: one is a collective committee, the other a person role.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a written or presented contribution, sibling of Poster and Regular contribution, parent Conference contribution), whereas B's 'Talk Event' is a scheduled academic event (sibling of Paper Presentation and Workshop, with children Closing Talk and Welcome Talk). They overlap in that an invited talk is both a contribution and an event, but the intended instances do not coincide: B's Talk Event covers any talk event (welcome, closing, paper presentation), not specifically an invited contribution. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's Topic is a subject area of papers/conferences (children are research topics like Antennas, Cryptography), while B's Money is a monetary amount with children Fee, Tax, Tip and properties about payment. They share no meaning; the pair is unrelated.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with a two-tier programme committee structure), while B 'OC Chair' is a person role (chair of the organising committee). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Refusing manuscript' is an activity of rejecting a submitted manuscript, a sub-activity of the pre-conference phase. B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline (a date) for submitting papers, a sub-type of Deadline. One is an activity, the other a temporal deadline; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event covering the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions, while B's 'Call For Reviews' is a call (solicitation) for reviewers, sibling of Call For Papers/Manuscripts. They both concern reviewing but one is the process/event and the other is the solicitation document, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. a reviewer inviting a co-reviewer. B's 'reviewes' relates a Member PC to a Contribution (domain Member PC, range Contribution), i.e. a PC member reviewing a paper. Different domain, different range, and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's `name` is a general datatype property with domain Conference and Person, covering names of both conferences and people. B's `Name of conference` is restricted to Conference only. The conference-naming part of A's property is more general than B's, so A's property subsumes B's; they are not equivalent because A also names persons.

A's 'Conference Member' is a Person subclass (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/PC Member, properties member Of Conference), i.e. a person participating in a conference. B's 'Conference fees' is a fee/payment concept, not a person. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

Conference Member (cmt) is a subclass of Person representing people involved in a conference (chairs, authors, reviewers), while Time (iasted) is a temporal concept with children Conference days, Deadline, Trip day. They share no instances and no meaning; the only overlap is the word 'Conference' in a child label, which is incidental.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person (a person attending the conference, with subclasses Active/Passive participant), while B 'Social event' is an Event (a social gathering such as Banquet, Reception, Trip). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (its members/participants), while B's holded by relates a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD organisation (the organising body). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Rejected contribution' is a class of papers/contributions that were rejected (sibling of Accepted contribution, subclass of Reviewed contribution). B's 'Reject Rating' is a class of review ratings (sibling of Accept Rating, Week Reject Rating, subclass of Review Rating). One denotes a rejected paper, the other a rating value used in reviews; their instances are disjoint kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'virtual Meeting Enabled By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables virtual meetings), while B's 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (a person prepares an item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption holds.

A is a conference-document class (a document giving information to participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a subject-area topic (Medicine Topic, sibling of Cryptography Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's Workshop is a type of Academic Event (a whole event/meeting), while B's Regular Session is a type of Session within a Scientific Event; a workshop is not a session, and B even has a separate Workshop Session sibling, so the two concepts do not coincide.

A's 'submit Paper' relates an Author to a Paper (submission act), while B's 'is sent after' relates an Item to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

Administrator in cmt is a User/Person role that manages the conference (accepts papers, assigns reviewers, enters conference details), while Mailing list in iasted is a Document artefact (sibling of Review, Submission, Invitation letter). Different kinds and domains, so they are unrelated.

A's writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (domain Reviewer, range Review), while B's hasReview relates a Paper to a Review (domain Paper, range Review). They link different kinds of subjects to a Review and are not inverses either, so they are distinct relations.

Both classes denote the same concept: a committee in the conference organisation domain. Ontology A's Committee is the general class for committees (with subclasses Organizing committee, Program committee, Steering committee), and Ontology B's Organizing Committee is a subclass of Committee. The labels and hierarchical context (both under a Committee parent, with Program Committee as a sibling) indicate they refer to the same organisational body. The properties of A's Committee (chair, co-chair, members) apply equally to B's Organizing Committee, confirming equivalence.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (a subclass of Place, sibling of Building, Session room, Hotel room). They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. location) and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a subclass of 'Conference document' (a document type, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational document about a conference. B's 'Conference' is the event itself, with properties for city, start/end date, name, and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. A document and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's PC Member is a person who reviews papers as part of the programme committee (a Possible Reviewer, with children PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc.). B's Speaker is a Delegate who gives a talk (with children Author and Reviewer, siblings Listener, Non speaker, Session chair, etc.). The intended instances do not coincide: a PC member need not speak, and a speaker need not be on the programme committee. The shared word 'member'/'reviewer' in the surrounding hierarchy is not enough, and the paths (Possible Reviewer vs Delegate) and sibling sets differ, so the classes are unrelated.

A's `prepare` relates a Person to an Item (preparing something), while B's `presentation` relates a Speaker to a Document (giving a presentation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Regular author' is a conference-contribution role (a kind of author/contributor to a contribution), while B 'Author attendee cd registration fee' is a specific registration-fee category for an author attendee. They belong to different branches (contribution/author vs. money/fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Co chair is a committee member role (sibling of Chair, tied to Committee via committee co-chair properties), while B's Demo Chair is a conference participant role (sibling of PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.) specifically for demo sessions. Different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's title is the title of a Paper (domain Paper, range string), while B's has Postal Code is a contact-information attribute (domain Contact Information, range string). They relate different kinds of things and are not the same relation.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference/committee), while B's is_given_by relates an Activity/Item to a Person (the person who gives/presents the activity). The domains and ranges are reversed and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference document' is a broad class covering all documents produced in the conference process (calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc.), while B's 'Document' is a similarly broad class but its children (Meal Menu, Paper, Programme, Review, Slide Set) and its relations to Academic Event/Conference/Person indicate a more general document notion that includes non-conference-process items like menus. A's class is more specific to conference documents, so it is subsumed by B's more general Document class rather than equivalent.

Both properties link a reviewer to the item they review, but the domains differ: cmt's assignedByReviewer has domain External Reviewer (a reviewer outside the PC), while confOf's reviewes has domain Member PC (a program-committee member). They express the same reviewing relation for different reviewer roles, so they overlap but are not equivalent.
Conference is a type of event/activity, while Registration is a process/activity of registering; they are not the same concept.

Acceptance is a decision outcome on a paper (sibling of Rejection under Decision), while Excursion is a social event during the conference (sibling of Reception under Social Event). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author denoting people who author papers but do not review; B's 'Reviewer' denotes people who review papers. They are complementary/opposite roles, not the same concept, and neither subsumes the other.

A's `reviews` goes from a Review to the contribution it reviews (Review -> Reviewed contribution), while B's `is Reviewed By` goes from a Paper to the people who review it (Paper -> Reviewer/Chair). They relate different kinds of things in different directions; B is closer to an inverse of a 'reviewed by' relation, not equivalent to A's reviews.

A is an administrative event (a process/activity of registering participants) under Event, while B is a deadline (a point in time) under Time/Deadline. Although both concern registration, one is an event and the other a temporal deadline, so their instances cannot coincide; they are different kinds of entities and thus unrelated.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a subclass of Conference applicant (a person who has registered, with child Paid applicant), while B 'Credit card' is a subclass of Card (a payment item). They belong to different branches (Person vs Item) and denote different concepts; no equivalence, subsumption or meaningful overlap.

A's volumeContainsPaper relates a volume (proceedings) to the papers it contains, while B's presentationed_by relates a document to the speaker who presented it. Different domain/range and direction of relation; no overlap in meaning.

confOf's University is a specific kind of academic organization (sibling of Company under Organization, with property 'study At' linking Scholars to it), whereas edas's Industry Organization is a commercial/industrial organization, sibling of Academia Organization, Government Organization and NGO. They denote different, non-overlapping concepts, so they are unrelated.

Company in confOf is an organization type (sibling of University, subclass of Organization), while Tip in iasted is a monetary category (sibling of Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, subclass of Money). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's property links a Topic to a Conference part (a topical/structural relation within the conference organisation), while B's presentation links a Speaker to a Document (a person presenting a paper). Different domains (Topic vs Speaker), different ranges (Conference part vs Document), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's `abstract` is a datatype property of Contribution (the abstract text of a paper), while B's `Name of conference` is a datatype property of Conference (the name of the event). Different domains, different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'Currency' is a datatype property of Registration fee giving the currency of a fee. Different domains, different intended meanings, no overlap.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc. under Conference document), while B's 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (sibling of Conference Trip under Social Event). They denote different kinds of things in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Both denote the conference paper artefact: cmt's Paper is a Document with authors, reviews, decisions and subject areas, and Conference's Written contribution is a conference contribution (with Regular/Submitted subclasses) that is written by authors. The intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the person the paper is assigned to for review); B's 'is sent by' links an Item to a Person (the sender). Both relate a document-like entity to a person, but the direction and meaning differ: assignment for reviewing vs. sending. They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same relation, and neither subsumes the other.

Acceptance is a decision outcome class (sibling of Rejection under Decision) in the conference domain, while Taxi is a transport vehicle class in iasted. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A is a research topic in computer networks (a subject area under Topic), while B is a committee role in the conference organization (under Committee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete version of a conference paper (a Document/Paper in the cmt ontology, sibling of Paper Abstract). B 'Hotel registration form' is a Form document used for hotel booking in the iasted ontology, sibling of Author information form and Registration form. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain; no subsumption or overlap.

Both properties link an author/person to a paper/conference document they authored. 'submit Paper' (Author -> Paper) and 'contributes' (Person -> Conference document) denote the same authorship relation in the conference domain; Author and Person are the same class, Paper and Conference document are the same class, and the direction is identical.

Both classes denote the abstract of a conference contribution. In Conference, Abstract is a subclass of Extended abstract and is the part of a Paper/Poster/Presentation (has an abstract, is the 1th part of). In sigkdd, Abstract is a subclass of Document alongside Paper and Review, i.e. the abstract text as a document artefact. The intended instances (abstracts of papers) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite the different parent paths.

A is a conference-document class ('Information for participants', sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic in a topic taxonomy (Computer Networks Measurements Topic, child of Computer Networks Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's hasLastName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's surname), while B's is_used_by is an object property from Item to Person (an item is used by a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and direction/meaning, so they are unrelated.

Week Reject Rating is a subclass of Review Rating in edas, i.e. a rating value/score category used in the review process. Review in sigkdd is a subclass of Document, i.e. the review document/artefact itself. A rating category and a document are different kinds of things, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property holding the conference's web address (range anyURI), while B's 'Name of conference' holds the conference's name (range string). Although both are datatype properties of Conference, they capture different attributes (URL vs. name), so they are not equivalent.

Both properties have domain Reviewer, but their ranges differ: cmt's writeReview points to a single Review (the review a reviewer writes), while edas's hasReviewHistory points to a Personal Review History (a collection/record of reviews). They concern the same activity of reviewing but relate different kinds of objects, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both are datatype properties on Person with string range, but 'has an email' relates a person to an email address while 'has Fax' relates a person to a fax number. Different contact information attributes, not the same relation.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has Cost Currency' is a datatype property of Sponsorship giving a currency for a sponsorship cost. Different domains, different intended meanings, no overlap.

In Conference, Presentation is a specific kind of Conference contribution (a document presented at the conference, with children like Invited talk and siblings Poster, Regular contribution, Written contribution). In sigkdd, Document is a broader class whose children include Abstract, Paper and Review, and which is presented by a Speaker. A Presentation is a kind of Document (it is presented, has an abstract, is part of a paper), but Document also covers things like Review and Abstract that are not Presentations. Hence Presentation is strictly more specific than Document: subsumed_by.

A is a subclass of Presenter (a person role: a speaker who is invited), while B is a subclass of State (a state of a presenter, alongside Conference state and Sponsor state). They belong to different branches (Person vs State) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's University is a subtype of Organization alongside Company, denoting an academic institution; B's Government Organization is a subtype of Organization alongside Academia/Industry/NGO, denoting a public-sector body. They are different kinds of organization, not synonyms, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property on Conference giving an integer count of reviews per paper, while B's 'reviewer Of Paper' is an object property linking a Possible Reviewer to a Paper. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Possible Reviewer), and range (int vs Paper), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (the venue/proceedings where it is submitted), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (the act of an author submitting a paper). Different domain, range, and direction of relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'paper Assignment Tools Run By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the assignment tools), while B's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (like call for papers, announcements) aimed at attendees, while B's 'Abstract' is a document type alongside Paper and Review, i.e. a summary of a paper. Different concepts despite both being documents.

A's submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (author submits a paper). B's submit_until relates a Document to a Deadline (a document is submitted until a deadline). Different domain, range, and meaning; not the same relation.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about the conference, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with a URL property), whereas B's 'Conference hotel' is a building/place (a hotel used by the conference, sibling of Conference airport, Conference restaurant). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (document vs. building), so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a subclass of Topic (a subject area in computer architecture). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference ontology and denote different concepts.

A Reception is a social event (a gathering/party) in confOf, sibling of Banquet and Trip under Social event. B Conference Venue Place is a physical location (a place where the conference is held) in edas, sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place and Meeting Room Place under Place. A social gathering and a physical venue are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference-document class ('Information for participants', sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. informational material for attendees. B is a research topic category ('Multimedia Topic') under Topic in the EDAS ontology. They share no intended instances and belong to different branches of the domain.

A is an administrative event (registration of participants, confTool) under Administrative event, while B is a scientific event type (Workshop) under Scientific Event. They denote different concepts: one is a process/event of registering participants, the other is a kind of scientific gathering. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

confOf's Event is a conference event (administrative/social/working) with start/end dates, while edas's Personal History is a container for a person's publication and review records. They share no instances or properties and belong to different branches of the conference domain.

A 'Submitted contribution' is a document/contribution artefact (a paper submitted to a conference, with review expertise and review preferences attached), whereas B 'Author' is a person role (a Person who writes papers). Their paths, parents, children and properties are entirely different: A is under Conference document/Conference contribution and is linked to reviews and topics, while B is under Person and is linked to Paper via has Related Paper / is Written By. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee (a subproperty of has a committee), while B's 'is occupied by' links a Building/City/State to a Person. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Withdrawn Paper is a specific status of Paper in edas (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper), while ekaw's Paper is the general class covering all papers including withdrawn ones. Thus Withdrawn Paper is strictly narrower, i.e. subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

A 'Conference Paper' is a document/paper type (subclass of Paper under Document), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (subclass of Place). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a kind of Paper (a document containing the abstract of a paper), while Transparency in iasted is a generic document item (e.g. a transparency/slide document) under Document, with siblings like Form, Invitation letter, Review, Submission. The two classes denote different concepts and do not overlap in the conference domain.

A's hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area (a topic classification), while B's is_made_from links an Item to another Item (a composition/material relation). The domains and ranges differ (Paper->Subject Area vs Item->Item), and the intended meanings are distinct: topic assignment versus part/composition. They are not the same relation.

A 'Committee member' is a Person role in the conference organisation (parent Person, children Chair/Co chair, related to Committee via has members/was a member of). B 'Hotel room' is a Place (parent Place, children Double/Single hotel room, siblings Conference hall, Session room). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Tutorial is a kind of lecture/session in the conference programme (an activity), while Exhibitor is a sponsoring organisation (a subtype of Sponzor). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A 'One day presenter' is a specific kind of Delegate who presents for one day, while B 'Speaker' is a general Person role that presents documents. Every one-day presenter is a speaker, but not every speaker is a one-day presenter, so A is strictly more specific than B.

A's remark is a free-text string annotation on a Contribution (confTool comment), while B's manuscriptDueOn is a dateTime deadline on a Conference. Different domain, range, and meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A Welcome Talk is a talk event (a session with a speaker) that opens a conference, while B Introduction of speaker is a conference activity in which a speaker is introduced. Both occur at the start of a conference and involve a speaker, so they overlap, but a welcome talk is a talk/session whereas an introduction of a speaker is a distinct activity (often a short presentation of a person), so they are not the same concept.

The two properties relate different kinds of things: 'has Administrative Event' links a Working event to an Administrative event, while 'has Call' links an Academic Event to a Call. Although both are object properties in the conference domain, their domains and ranges do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Submitted contribution' is a document/contribution entity (a written contribution that has been submitted, with reviews and topics attached), while B 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the event hierarchy (the reviewing procedure). They belong to different branches (document vs event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

The two properties are inverses of each other: edas 'is Topic Of' goes from Topic to Conference/Paper, while ekaw 'covers Topic' goes from Event/Paper to Research Topic. They relate the same kinds of things (a paper/event and its topic) but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (expertise -> contribution), while B's hasReview links a Paper to a Review (paper -> review). The domains and ranges are different concepts and the direction of the relation differs, so they are not the same relation.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (membership in a committee). B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presented the document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference event with two levels), while B 'Non speaker' is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending without presenting). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and share no intended instances.

A's contributes goes Person -> Conference document (a person contributes a document). B's relatesTo goes Document -> Person/Event/etc. (a document relates to a person or event). The directions are opposite and the domains/ranges differ, so they are not equivalent; they are inverses/overlapping notions, hence related.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted; B's 'done till' is a date property on Deadline indicating when a deadline ends. Different domains (Conference vs Deadline), different ranges (boolean vs date), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author (a person who writes papers but is not a reviewer), while B's 'Student non speaker' is a subclass of Non speaker under Delegate (a student attendee who does not give a talk). They belong to different branches (Author vs Delegate) and denote different concepts; neither subsumes the other.

Acceptance in cmt is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection) under Decision, while Rejected contribution in Conference is a subclass of Reviewed contribution representing a rejected paper. The two denote different concepts: one is a decision/acceptance event, the other is a rejected contribution document. They are not equivalent.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'has Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer, i.e. the reviewers assigned to a paper. Different domain, different range, different direction of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Attendee is a general Person subtype (siblings Author, Reviewer, TPC Member, etc.), i.e. any participant. B's Session chair is a Delegate subtype (siblings Speaker, Listener, IASTED member, etc.), i.e. a specific role of chairing a session. A session chair is a kind of attendee, but the classes are not coextensive: most attendees are not session chairs, and the iasted hierarchy places Session chair under Delegate rather than as a general participant. Different intended instances, so unrelated (not equivalent, and neither strictly subsumes the other as named classes).

A's 'rejected By' links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who rejected it), while B's 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the publishing body). Different domain, range, and meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'Record of attendance' is a document recording who attended (siblings include Invitation letter, Payment document, Viza, Mailing list), whereas B's 'Paper' is a submitted scientific contribution (siblings Abstract, Review; domain of submit from Author). They denote different concepts despite both being Documents.

A's Review is the general review document class (sibling of Paper, Programme, etc. under Document), while B's Negative Review is a specific subtype of Review (sibling of Neutral/Positive Review). A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (domain Program Committee, range Program Committee Member). B's presentationed_by relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Main office' is a physical place (an office location) under Place. Their intended instances and domains differ completely, so they are unrelated.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a specific leadership role within a committee), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (membership of a conference). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Associated Chair is a Chairman/Conference Member role (a chair associated with the conference, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), while B's Program Chair is an Organizator role specifically heading the program committee. The paths and sibling sets differ: A sits under Chairman alongside Conference Chair, B sits under Organizator alongside General Chair. They are distinct committee roles, not the same concept.

A 'Submitted contribution' is a written contribution that has been submitted and is under review (it has review expertise, review preferences, and assigned review references). B 'Paper' is a broader document class whose children include Submitted Paper, Conference Paper, Camera Ready Paper, etc. A submitted contribution corresponds to a submitted paper, which is a kind of Paper, so A is strictly more specific than B.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is a publication artefact (has name, publisher, volume, ISBN; issued by a Publisher), whereas B's 'Activity' is a general event/activity class (held in a place, dated, given by a person, paid for). The proceedings are a document produced by a conference, not an activity, so the two classes do not denote the same concept.
A's 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Paper (a document part), while B's 'Best Student Paper Award' is a subclass of Award (a prize). Different domains and no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B's Hotel fee is a monetary fee (sibling of Registration fee and Fee for extra trip). They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's min Choice is a datatype property of Social/Working event giving a minimum number of choices (positiveInteger), while B's End of conference is a datatype property of Conference giving a dateTime. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence.

A's 'Positive Review' is a specific subclass of Review (sibling of Negative/Neutral Review), while B's 'Review' is the general review document class. A Positive Review is a kind of Review, so A is strictly more specific and is subsumed by B; they are not equivalent.

A 'Meta Reviewer' is a person role (a special type of Reviewer) in cmt, while B 'Review' is a document/artefact (a subclass of Document) in ekaw. They denote different kinds of things (agent vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

A's Associated Chair is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B's Speaker lecture is a session/lecture activity in the iasted ontology (child of Session under Lecture). One is a person/committee role, the other an event/session type; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's Social Event is a non-academic conference event (with children Excursion and Reception, siblings Break Event and Meal Event), while B's Organizator is a role of a person (parent Person, children General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts: an event versus a person role, so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties linking a person who produces a review to the review/contribution artefact. In cmt, Reviewer write Review -> Review; in confOf, Author writes Contribution -> Contribution. In the conference domain, a reviewer is an author-type role and a review is a contribution, so the relations coincide in direction and intended meaning.

A's `contributes` goes Person -> Conference document (a person contributes a document), while B's `written By` goes Document -> Person (a document is written by a person). They are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

A's Social event is a subclass of Event (a conference social activity with children Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B's Time is a temporal entity (parent of Conference days, Deadline, Trip day) used as the range of temporal properties like is held before/after. They denote different concepts (activity vs. time), so they are unrelated.

A's 'is used by' is an object property linking an Item to a Person (who uses the item), while B's 'Name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (the person's name). They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain/range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Regular is a subclass of Participant (a person role: regular participant, sibling of Member and Student). B's Two Level Conference is a subclass of Conference (a conference type, sibling of Single Level Conference). One denotes a person role, the other a conference type; they share no intended instances and are unrelated.

A's hasFax is a datatype property linking a Person to their fax number, while B's Name links a Person to their name. Although both are Person->string datatype properties, they denote different attributes (fax number vs. name), so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Preference is a class of preferred values/options (e.g. preferred paper or topic choices) in the CMT ontology, not a person. confOf:Participant is a subclass of Person (a conference attendee with subclasses Member, Regular, Student and property early Registration). The two denote different kinds of things (a preference vs. a person), so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference submission (has authors, reviewers, decisions, subject areas), while B's Web Site is a published document artefact (publisher, event listings). They share only the Document parent; B's Paper is the true counterpart of A's Paper, so these two are unrelated.

A 'Government Organization' is a type of organization (sibling of Academia/Industry Organization/NGO under Organization), whereas B 'Main office' is a physical place (sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room under Place). They denote different concepts: an organizational actor vs. a venue location, so they are unrelated.

A's hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to its Subject Area (a topic classification), while B's is_equipped_by relates a Place to an Item (equipment located at a venue). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Scholar is a price/fee category of Person (a person attending under a scholar rate), while B's Reviewer is a role of a Speaker who reviews papers. Different intended instances and different positions in the hierarchy; no subsumption or overlap.
A's 'reviews Per Paper' is an integer count of reviews per paper, while B's 'Name of conference' is a string name; different meaning, range, and purpose.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's OC Member is a person role (a Conference Participant who is on the organising committee, parent of OC Chair). They denote entirely different kinds of things — an event versus a person — so they are unrelated.

Active Paper is a subclass of Paper in edas (path Document > Paper > Active Paper), representing papers that are under review/active. The sigkdd Paper class is the general paper concept (path Document > Paper) with no active-status restriction. Thus Active Paper is strictly more specific than Paper, so it is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

A Reception is a social event (a gathering) in confOf, sibling of Banquet and Trip, whereas an Invitation letter in iasted is a Document (a written artefact), sibling of Form, Review, Submission. Different kinds of entities: event vs document, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that informs attendees, while B's 'Publication' is an item with children Book proceeding and Cd proceeding, i.e. a published artefact. Different intended instances and different contexts, so they are not equivalent.

Chair is a committee role (a person who chairs a committee), while City is a geographical location used as the range of has City for organizations/persons. They share no meaning, instances, or properties; the only overlap is the word 'Chair' vs 'City' being unrelated concepts.

A's Conference is an event/organisational entity with properties like accepts Hardcopy Submissions, date, and has Conference Member. B's Conference hall is a physical place (subclass of Place) alongside Building, Hotel room, and Session room. The entities denote different kinds of things (event vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'enter Conference Details' is an object property linking an Administrator to a Conference (a person enters details about a conference), while B's 'Start of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (the conference's start time). They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Administrator vs Conference), and range (Conference vs dateTime), so they denote different relations.
A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country; B's is_used_for relates an Item to an Activity or Money. Different domain, range and meaning, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'written By' links a Review to its Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), while B's 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (domain Topic, range Review preference). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference/committee). B's is_signed_by relates an Item to a Person (a person signs an item, e.g. a paper). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the directions differ, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (a person-to-committee membership relation). B's organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (an event-to-organiser relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author (authorship relation). B's is_needed_for relates an Item to a Person, expressing a dependency/requirement relation, not authorship. The domains (Paper vs Item) and ranges (Author vs Person) differ in intent, and the property names denote different relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome of a paper). B's belongs_to_a_review_reference relates a Topic to a Review preference (a reviewer's topic preference). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Workshop is a kind of working event (a conference session type, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Lecturer is a person role under Author/Speaker in the delegate hierarchy. They denote different concepts (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paid applicant' is a subclass of registered conference applicant (a person who has paid the registration fee), while B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with children Single Level Conference / Two Level Conference and properties such as paper Due On, has Topic, has Member. The two denote entirely different concepts (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

Multi author Volume in ekaw is a collection/volume of documents (parent of Proceedings, published by an Organisation), whereas sigkdd Paper is a single submitted document (submitted by an Author). They are both Documents but denote different artefacts: a volume is a collection, a paper is an individual contribution. They overlap in the domain but are not equivalent; the volume is a container of papers, so the relation is 'related' rather than equivalence.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'pay' links a Person to a Registration fee (payment). Different domain, range, and intended relation; they are unrelated.

Chair PC (a PC chair, i.e. a person chairing the program committee) and Attendee (a person attending the conference) are distinct roles. Chair PC is a specific committee role, while Attendee is a generic participant role; neither subsumes the other in the intended sense, and they are not synonyms.

A's remark is a free-text string annotation on a Contribution (comment 'confTool'), while B's has Cost Amount is an integer amount attached to a Sponsorship. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to the Organization that employs them, while ekaw's organisedBy relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domains (Person vs Event), different ranges (Organization vs Organisation/Person), and different meanings (employment vs event organisation); they are not the same relation.

A's Topic is the general conference subject area (used by Contribution, PC member, Working event), while B's Multimedia Topic is a specific topic under the Topic parent in edas. Multimedia Topic is a narrower concept, so A is more general: A is subsumed by B's broader Topic class, but the specific Multimedia Topic is not equivalent to the general Topic.

A's rejectedBy relates a Paper to the Administrator who rejected it; B's issues relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes. Different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (domain Location, range Event), i.e. the event held at a location. B's 'speak in' relates a Person to a Place/Time (domain Person, range Place, Time), i.e. a person speaking at a place/time. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

Both denote a person who authors papers: ekaw's Paper Author is a Person who writes papers, and sigkdd's Author is a Speaker who submits papers and obtains awards, with children Author of paper. The intended instances coincide (people who author conference papers), so the classes are equivalent despite differing parent paths.

A's 'Neutral Review' is a specific kind of review (sibling of Positive/Negative Review, child of Review), while B's 'Review' is the general review document class. A is strictly narrower than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a subclass of 'Conference document' (a document type, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B's 'Academic Event' is a subclass of 'Conference Event' (an event type with children like Workshop, Talk Event). A document announcing a conference is not the same concept as an academic event; they belong to different branches (document vs event) and have incompatible properties.

A's Proceedings is a document/volume class (a collection of papers from a conference), while B's Organizator is a person role class (someone who organises a conference). They denote entirely different kinds of entities and share no subsumption or overlap.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a conference event (Organizational Meeting, a kind of Academic Event). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

A's Review is a subclass of Document in the edas ontology, i.e. a review document/artefact. B's Viza is a subclass of Document in iasted, but its siblings (Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance, Mailing list, Brief introduction for Session chair, Transparency) show it is an administrative/paperwork document (a visa-related document), not a review. The shared parent Document and the word overlap are not enough; the intended instances differ, so the classes are unrelated.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a review offer/commitment), while B's dealsWith relates a Contribution to a Topic (subject area). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent relations.

A's 'Conference volume' is a container/volume entity that has committees, tracks, parts, contributions and important dates, i.e. the whole conference event with its structure. B's 'Conference' is a simpler event with only name, city, start/end dates and a held-by relation to ACM SIGKDD. They overlap in denoting the conference event, but A is a richer, more structured notion (volume with parts/tracks/committees) while B is a plain event; the intended instances do not clearly coincide, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (conference membership), while B's is present relates a Person to a Time (attendance/presence at a time). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's has Programme relates a Conference Event to a Programme (the schedule of events), while B's is given by relates an Activity/Item to a Person (the presenter/author). Different domain and range, different meaning; not equivalent.

A's 'has a publisher' links a Conference proceedings to a Publisher; B's 'topic Covered By' links a Research Topic to an Event or Paper. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter of a paper), while B's 'submit' links an Author to a Paper (submission act). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call For Reviews' is a call/announcement for reviewers (a subclass of Call, sibling of Call For Papers/Manuscripts), whereas B's 'Abstract' is a document part (subclass of Document, sibling of Paper and Review). They denote different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Abstract) in the cmt ontology, whereas B 'Test Only Topic' is a subclass of Topic in edas, a subject area used for classifying submissions. A document/paper type and a topic category denote different kinds of things and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome), while B's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a reviewer's topic preference), while B's property links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a numeric score). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Person) in cmt, while B 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative event in confOf. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has important dates' is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity (a set of deadlines), while B's 'has End Date Time' is a datatype property linking a Conference Event to a single xsd:dateTime value. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Conference volume vs Conference Event), and range (Important dates vs dateTime), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise), while B's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's property relates a Co chair to a Committee (a role-in-organisation relation), while B's property relates an Item to a Person (a signing/authorisation relation). Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a scheduled meeting of a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (a building/room, sibling of Building, Hotel room, Session room). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. location), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference state' is a state/role a person holds during a conference (sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state under State), whereas B's 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person denoting an organizing person (with children General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). One is a state/role concept, the other a person type; their intended instances do not coincide.

A is a document/form artefact ('Author information form') used to collect author details, a subclass of Form alongside registration forms. B is a person role ('Author'), a subclass of Speaker who submits papers and receives notifications. A form and a person are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated despite the shared word 'Author'.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Computer Networks Topic' is a subject-area topic in the EDAS taxonomy. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Administrator is a User with administrative powers (accepts papers, assigns reviewers, enters conference details), while B's Author is a Speaker who submits papers and obtains awards. They are different roles in the conference domain, not synonyms.

A's 'Review preference' is a class representing a reviewer's preference/degree of interest in a topic or submission, with properties linking it to Reviewer, Topic, Submitted contribution and an integer degree. B's 'Paper' is a document submitted by an author (submit: Author -> Paper), a sibling of Abstract and Review under Document. The two denote different concepts: a preference/interest record versus a submitted paper document. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference-member hierarchy who writes/submits papers; Conference Session (edas) is an event/session entity related to documents and academic events. They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

Country in edas is a geographic nation used as the location of a conference (has Country: Conference -> Country). Research Topic in ekaw is a subject area covered by events and papers (covers Topic: Event, Paper -> Research Topic). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances or properties.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology, whereas B 'Conference days' is a temporal concept (subclass of Time, with children Delegate and One conference day, sibling of Deadline and Trip day) in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (a person vs. a time period), so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the same concept: a working/academic event in the conference domain. confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop, and edas's 'Academic Event' is a subclass of Conference Event with children Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop. The shared child Workshop and the parallel role as the main event category (sibling to Administrative/Social event in confOf and Non Academic Event in edas) indicate they are intended to coincide.

Both properties link an Author to a Paper, but they denote different relations: 'submit Paper' is the act of submitting a paper (authorship/submission), whereas 'has Related Paper' expresses a topical/relatedness association between an author and a paper. Same domain and range do not make them equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A's property links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (the assignment of a reviewer preference), while B's 'writes' links an author to a contribution (authorship). Different domains (Submitted contribution/Topic vs Author) and ranges (Review preference vs Contribution), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the central event class of the cmt ontology (with submissions, dates, administrators, committee members), while B's Conference city is a subclass of City describing the city where a conference is held. They denote different concepts (event vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

Tutorial is a working event (a type of academic session/event) in confOf, while Conference hall is a physical place (venue location) in sigkdd. They denote different concepts: an event vs. a location, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (authorship relation), while B's 'holded by' links a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD organisation (organiser/host relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.
Conference Chair is a person role in the conference domain, while Book proceeding is a publication type in the iasted domain; they are semantically unrelated.

A's 'Conference days' is a temporal class (a subdivision of Time, with children like One conference day and Delegate) denoting the days on which a conference takes place. B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with properties for city, name, start/end dates and organisers. The two denote different concepts (a time span vs. the event), so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person who authors papers/contributions in the conference domain. In edas, Author is a subclass of Person with properties linking to Paper (has Related Paper, is Written By), and its children (Presenter) and siblings (Reviewer, TPC Member, etc.) fit the conference-role hierarchy. In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (itself under Delegate) with children like Lecturer, Tutorial speaker, and siblings like Reviewer, again representing a person who authors conference contributions. Despite different parent paths (Person vs Speaker), the intended instances coincide: individuals who write papers. The shared label and the consistent role in the conference domain support equivalence.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's surname), while B's 'is used by' is an object property from Item to Person (an item being used by a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Reviewer to a Review expertise/preference (a reviewer's declared expertise or preference), while B's 'write' links a Person to an Item (authorship of a paper). Different domain (Reviewer vs Person) and range (expertise/preference vs Item), and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering anyone contributing to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors), while B's 'Non speaker' is a Delegate subclass specifically for attendees who do not give a talk (students, workers). The two concepts overlap only incidentally: a non-speaker delegate could be a contributor, but contributors include speakers and authors, and non-speakers include delegates who contribute nothing. Different paths (Person vs Delegate under Conference building) and different sibling sets confirm they are not the same concept.

A's Topic is the general subject area of a contribution, PC member expertise, or working event. B's CAD Topic is a specific topic (Computer-Aided Design) under the parent Topic in edas. Thus CAD Topic is a narrower concept than the general Topic, so A subsumes B (B is subsumed_by A).

A's Rejection is a final decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), while B's Accpet If Room Rating is a review rating category (sibling of Accept/Reject/Week Reject Rating under Review Rating). They belong to different hierarchies and denote different concepts: a decision vs. a rating.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole event with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's One conference day is a temporal unit under Conference days. They denote different concepts: an event vs. a day within an event, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is the general class of all people participating in a conference (its children are Active/Passive conference participant), while B's 'Late Registered Participant' is a specific subclass of ekaw's 'Conference Participant' distinguished by registration timing. Thus A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subtype covering all people contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants, committee members), while ekaw's PC Member is a narrower role under Possible Reviewer denoting program-committee members. The two overlap (a PC member is a conference contributor) but neither subsumes the other cleanly: Conference contributor includes many non-PC roles, and PC Member is a specific reviewer/committee role. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action of entering conference details), while B's 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing/issuing proceedings). Different domains (Administrator vs Publisher), different ranges (Conference vs Conference proceedings), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to reviewers/committee members (reviewing activity), while B's 'is prepared by' relates an Item to a Person (authorship/preparation). Different domains (Paper vs Item) and different intended relations (review vs preparation), so they are not equivalent.

A is a research topic (Mobile Computing Topic) under Topic, while B is an award category (Best Applications Paper Award) under Award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

Both classes denote a conference event: confOf's Conference is a Working event (sibling of Tutorial/Workshop) in the conference domain, and sigkdd's Conference is the central event class with city, start/end dates, name, and held-by relation to ACM SIGKDD. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

A 'Medicine Topic' is a subject area of conference papers (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc. under Topic), whereas B 'Card' is a physical item (sibling of Audiovisual equipment, Document, Transport vehicle, with child Credit card). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a talk given by an invited speaker), while B's 'Workshop Session' is a session-type event within a workshop. They belong to different branches (contribution vs. event/session) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both Document classes are the general superclass of Paper and Review in the conference domain; sigkdd additionally has Abstract as a child, but the intended instances (papers, reviews, abstracts as documents) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment affiliation), while iasted's obtain relates a Person to an Item (acquiring something). Different range kinds and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Session Chair is a Person who chairs a session (sibling of Conference Chair, Reviewer, TPC Member; initiates calls, reviews papers). B's PC Chair is a Program Committee Chair, a Conference Participant and PC Member (sibling of Session Chair, Workshop Chair, etc.). In ekaw, Session Chair is a separate sibling class, so PC Chair denotes the program-committee chair, not the session chair. Different roles, so unrelated.

A's Paper is a document/contribution class (subclass of Document, with children Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc., and properties like is Written By, has Topic, is Reviewed By). B's Paper Author is a subclass of Person denoting a person who authors papers, not a document. The two entities denote different kinds of things (document vs. person), so they are unrelated despite the shared word 'Paper'.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an Administrator action relating an Administrator to a Conference (finalizing the assignment of papers to the conference), while B's 'submit' is an Author action relating an Author to a Paper (submitting a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's title is the title of a Paper (domain Paper), while B's has Submission Instructions is a property of a Call (domain Call) giving submission instructions text. Different domains and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area for papers in the edas ontology (a subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), whereas 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a document type in ekaw (a subclass of Abstract, sibling of Tutorial Abstract). They denote entirely different concepts—a research topic versus a kind of abstract document—so they are unrelated.

The two properties are inverses of each other: cmt's hasBeenAssigned goes from Reviewer to Paper, while ekaw's hasReviewer goes from Paper to Possible Reviewer. They relate the same kinds of entities (a reviewer and a paper) but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent; a reference alignment would record them as inverse/related rather than equivalent.

A is a document type (a multi-author volume, parent of Proceedings, published by an organisation), while B is a deadline (the date by which authors are notified), a subclass of Deadline. They belong to different branches of the conference domain (document vs. deadline) and share no intended instances.

A's remark is a free-text comment on a Contribution (range string, comment 'confTool'), while B's Date is a dateTime value attached to a Deadline. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'was a track workshop chair of' relates a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (a role-to-event relation), while B's 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item to a Person (an event-to-agent relation). The domains and ranges are disjoint in kind, so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's Paper is a Contribution (a submitted work, sibling of Poster and Short paper), while B's Abstract is a Document (sibling of Paper and Review). In sigkdd, Paper and Abstract are distinct document types, so confOf Paper does not coincide with sigkdd Abstract; they are different concepts.
