Conference's 'Committee member' is a Person who belongs to a Committee (has members / was a member of), with subclasses Chair and Co chair. confOf's 'Member' is a Participant subtype (siblings Regular, Student) with comment 'confTool', i.e. a registered conference participant category, not a committee role. They overlap in that both are persons involved in the conference, but they denote different concepts, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Short paper is a contribution type (a short version of a paper, sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution), while B's Published Paper is a publication-status stage of a Paper (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper under Paper). They denote different dimensions (contribution format vs. publication state) and do not coincide.

Both entities denote the same concept in the conference domain: cmt:Paper and confOf:Contribution are synonymous classes for a submitted paper/contribution, with matching context (authored, reviewed, has decision).

A's attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event (a person attends an event), while B's hold relates ACM SIGKDD (an organisation) to a Conference (the organisation holds a conference). Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title; B's has Name is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's full name. Different domains (Paper vs Conference) and different intended concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Sponzorship in iasted is a subclass of Money (a financial category, sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip), i.e. the sponsorship payment/funding concept. Exhibitor in sigkdd is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsor entity, sibling of Gold Supporter, Silver Supporter, etc.), i.e. an organisation that exhibits. One is a monetary amount, the other an agent/organisation; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

Both properties relate a person/author to a conference document/contribution, i.e. authorship of a paper. 'contributes' (Person -> Conference document) and 'writes' (Author -> Contribution) denote the same relation in the conference domain, with Person/Author and Conference document/Contribution being synonymous classes.

A's Chair is a generic committee chair role (sibling Co chair, domain of 'has a committee chair' over Committee), while B's Tutorial Chair is a specific conference-participant role (siblings Demo Chair, Workshop Chair, PC Chair, etc.). A Tutorial Chair is a kind of chair, so the generic Chair subsumes Tutorial Chair; they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties linking a deadline/important-dates class to a date, but 'is an abstract submission date' denotes the specific abstract-submission deadline, whereas 'done till' is a generic deadline-completion date. They overlap in the deadline/date relation but are not the same specific property.

accept Paper relates an Administrator to a Paper (the act of accepting a paper), while has an abstract relates a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.
A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country; B's is_made_from relates an Item to an Item. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper's rating value), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; not equivalent.

Abstract is a document type (a paper abstract, child of Document, with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and related to Paper via presentation properties). Tax is a monetary charge (child of Money, with children Departure tax and Value added tax). They share no meaning in the conference domain.
A 'Plenary lecture' is a kind of conference activity/lecture (an event), while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee (a group of people). Different domains and no overlap; unrelated.

confOf's Event is a general conference event (administrative, social, working events) with start/end dates, while sigkdd's Award is a specific prize given to authors (best paper awards, awarded by, obtained by authors). They denote different concepts and share no instances.

Workshop is a type of working event (an activity/event class) in confOf, while Presenter state is a state/status class in iasted describing the condition of a presenter. They belong to different branches (Event vs State) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Dinner' is a social meal event in the conference schedule, while B 'General Chair' is a person role in the organizing committee. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assignment of a reviewer to a paper), while B's hasReviewHistory relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a reviewer's record of past reviews). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's `location Of` relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's `go through` relates an Item to an Activity (an item used in/through an activity). The domains (Location vs Item) and ranges (Event vs Activity) differ, and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has Street' is a datatype property of Organization and Person giving a street address. Different attributes (surname vs. street address), so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract version of a paper (sibling of Paper Full Version), while B is a conference topic category (Powerline Transmission Topic) under Topic. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), expressing that events run concurrently. ekaw's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location, expressing where an event takes place. Different domain/range and different meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Contact Information in edas is a class holding address details (city, email, phone, postal code, street) of a person, while Conference in sigkdd is the conference event itself with name, start/end dates, city, and organisers. They denote different concepts and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A Multi author Volume is a Document (a multi-author volume such as proceedings) that can be published by an organisation; B Publication is a broader Item covering books, CDs and proceedings. A multi-author volume is a kind of publication, but Publication is not restricted to multi-author volumes, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'belong to a conference volume' links Important dates to a Conference volume (a publication/volume relation), while B's 'parallel with' links Administrative events to other Administrative events (a scheduling/co-location relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime value (the deadline date of a call). B's is_sent_after is an object property linking an Item to a Time, expressing a temporal ordering between two entities. They differ in domain (Call vs Item), range (dateTime literal vs Time object), and meaning (deadline date vs ordering relation), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property holding a person's surname (a name component), while B's 'has Biography' holds a biographical text about a person. Although both are datatype properties on Person with range string, they denote different attributes (surname vs. biography), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a conference contribution (a paper) that has undergone review, sitting in the contribution hierarchy with children Accepted/Rejected contribution and linked to reviews. B 'Review Form' is the form/artefact used to record a review, not a contribution. They denote different concepts (the reviewed paper vs. the review instrument), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference document' is a class of documents (calls, announcements, contributions, reviews) that people contribute to and author. B's 'Conference Event' is a scheduled event with attendees, location, programme and start/end date times. The two denote different kinds of things (document vs. event) and their properties do not overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Abstract), while B's 'Review' is a distinct document type (sibling of Paper and Abstract under Document). A full paper and a review are different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor, i.e. a role a contribution plays (a regular, non-invited author of a contribution), with children 'Contribution 1th author' and 'Contribution co author'. B's 'Author' is a subclass of Person, a person who writes papers (has Related Paper, is Written By), with child Presenter. The edas Author is the person, the Conference Regular author is the contribution-side role; the person concept is more general, so Regular author is subsumed by Author rather than equivalent.

A Flyer is a publicity document (sibling of Paper, Review, Programme Brochure) that an Organisation can be publisher of. B Author information form is a Form (sibling of Registration form, Hotel registration form) used to collect author data. Different intended instances and roles; no subsumption.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is the published volume/collection of papers (has publisher, volume, ISBN; issued by a Publisher), whereas B's 'Conference' is a single edition of a conference event (an Event > Scientific Event, with siblings Session, Track, Workshop). The proceedings are a publication artefact, not the event itself, so the two classes are unrelated.

A's 'Regular contribution' is a broad category of conference contributions (siblings include Invited talk, Poster, Presentation; children Extended abstract, Paper), i.e. any regular (non-invited) contribution. B's 'Assigned Paper' is a paper that has been assigned to a reviewer, a stage in the submission/review workflow (parent Submitted Paper, child Evaluated Paper). The two overlap in that a regular contribution is typically a submitted/assigned paper, but neither subsumes the other: not every regular contribution is an assigned paper (e.g. an invited talk is not, and a regular contribution need not be assigned), and an assigned paper need not be a 'regular' contribution in A's sense. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'relates To' is a general Document->(Event/Conference/Session/Person) relation, while B's 'presentation' is a Speaker->Document relation (a speaker presents a document). They differ in domain, range, and direction, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Organizing committee' is the general committee that organizes the conference (siblings: Program committee, Steering committee; it organizes a Conference volume). B's 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is a specific committee for selecting best paper awards, and B already has a separate sibling 'Organizing Committee' that would correspond to A's class. The two denote different committees, so they are unrelated.

A's Abstract is a document/contribution type (an extended abstract that is part of a paper/poster/presentation), while B's Author is a person role (a subclass of Person who writes contributions). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Reviewed contribution' is a class of documents/contributions (a subclass of Submitted contribution, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution, and it is the range of 'reviews' and domain of 'has a review'). B's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event (a subclass of Administrative event, sibling of Submission event, Camera Ready event, etc.) representing the reviewing procedure/process, not a contribution. The two denote different kinds of things (a document vs. an event/process), so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Decision is the outcome of reviewing a paper (children Acceptance/Rejection, range of hasDecision from Paper). ekaw:Evaluated Paper is a paper that has been evaluated (a subclass of Assigned Paper with children Accepted Paper/Rejected Paper). The two are closely related — the decision determines whether a paper becomes accepted or rejected — but they are not the same concept: one is the decision/outcome, the other is the paper in its evaluated state. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented), while B 'Gold Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (academic events vs. sponsors) and share no intended instances.

A assigns an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (domain Reviewer, range External Reviewer), while B relates a Person to an Item via writing. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Company in confOf is an organization (sibling of University) that participates in the conference domain, while Credit card in iasted is a payment card item under Card; they share no meaning, instances, or properties, so they are unrelated.

Both denote the social event of a conference banquet/dinner: ekaw's Conference Banquet is a Social Event, iasted's Dinner banquet is a Social program activity; same intended instances (the conference dinner event), so they are equivalent despite differing labels.

In confOf, Poster is a kind of Contribution (a submission type, sibling of Paper and Short paper). In edas, Published Paper is a state of a Paper document (sibling of Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.), i.e. a paper that has been published. A poster is not a published paper, and a published paper is not a poster; the concepts denote different things (submission type vs. publication status), so they are unrelated.

A's Poster is a kind of conference contribution (a document/paper type with an abstract), while B's Author is a person role (parent Person, with children Presenter and properties relating to papers). They denote different concepts entirely, so they are unrelated.

A's hasCity is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string city name, while B's heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They differ in domain (Contact Information vs Event), range (string vs Location), and kind (datatype vs object), so they do not denote the same relation.
read Paper (Reviewer -> Paper) and is Reviewed By (Paper -> Reviewer/Chair/TPC) are inverse relations, not equivalent; they relate the same kinds of things in opposite directions.

A's 'has tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a whole-part relation, subproperty of has parts), while B's 'has Related Document' links an Academic Event/Conference/Session/Person to a Document. The domains and ranges differ (Conference volume vs. Event/Person; Tutorial vs. Document), and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Talk Event' is a kind of academic event (a scheduled session such as a welcome or closing talk) in the edas ontology, whereas B 'Organizator' is a role of a person (a conference organiser, parent of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.) in the sigkdd ontology. One is an event, the other a person role; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A Conference is a large working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) that hosts papers and presentations, whereas an Invited Talk is a single individual presentation (sibling of Contributed Talk and Tutorial) given by an invited speaker. They are at different levels of granularity and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair in cmt is a chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), i.e. a person helping organise the conference. Invited speaker in Conference is a conference contributor who gives a talk, sibling of Regular author and Active conference participant. The roles are distinct: an organiser role versus a speaker/contributor role, with different parents and siblings, so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties with range string that record an email address, but their domains differ: confOf's contactEmail is a property of Contribution (the paper/submission), while edas's hasEmail is a property of Person/Contact Information. They relate different kinds of subjects to an email string, so they are not equivalent; they overlap in meaning (both express an email contact) and are best recorded as related.

A's partOfEvent is a mereological relation between Events (an event is part of another event), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents the document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's property relates a Topic to a Conference part (domain Topic, range Conference part), while B's hasTopic relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (domain Conference/Paper, range Topic). The direction and the kinds of things related are reversed and different, so they are not equivalent; they are not even inverses since the domain/range classes differ (Conference part vs Conference/Paper).

A's Presenter is a subclass of Conference Participant (a person role who presents), while B's Presenter state is a subclass of State (a situation/status of a presenter, sibling of Conference state and Sponsor state). They denote different kinds of entities (person role vs. state), so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a conference topic category (Satellite and Space Communications). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document types vs. subject topics) and share no intended instances.

EDAS 'Published Paper' is a specific status of a paper (a paper that has been published), a subclass of Paper. EKAW 'Paper' is the general class covering all papers (submitted, camera-ready, conference, workshop, etc.). Thus Published Paper is strictly narrower than Paper, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), i.e. a symmetric co-occurrence relation between events. B's 'has Programme' relates a Conference Event to a Programme, a part-whole/containment relation with different domain and range. They relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Personal Publication History' is a record/history of a person's publications (a subclass of Personal History, sibling of Personal Review History), whereas B 'Initial manuscript' is a submission document type (subclass of Submission, sibling of Final manuscript). They denote different concepts: one is a biographical/history entity, the other a document artefact in the submission process.

A Programme Brochure is a document that lists events (it has properties 'event On List'/'lists Event' and is published by an organisation), whereas sigkdd Paper is a submitted contribution with property 'submit' (Author -> Paper). They share only the parent Document; their intended instances and roles in the conference domain differ, so they are not equivalent.

EDAS Workshop is an academic event type (a whole workshop event), while EKAW Workshop Session is a session within a workshop (a part of a workshop event). They are related but not equivalent: a workshop session is a sub-part of a workshop, not the workshop itself.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving the ISBN string of the proceedings volume, while B's 'Name of conference' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's name. They have different domains (proceedings vs. conference) and different intended values (ISBN vs. name), so they are not the same relation.

Author is a person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers), while Deadline is a temporal event with a date and submission cut-off. Their paths, siblings, and properties (write Paper vs Date/submit until) are entirely different, so they denote different concepts.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Demo Chair is a person role (a Conference Participant, sibling of PC Chair, Workshop Chair, etc.). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Person) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A 'Negative Review' is a subclass of Review (a document containing an evaluation with negative outcome), while B 'Abstract' is a subclass of Document (a summary of a paper). They denote different concepts: one is a type of review, the other a type of document summary. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'Chair PC' is a person who chairs the programme committee (PC chair), while B's 'Demo Chair' is a person chairing the demo session/track. They are distinct conference roles with different responsibilities; the shared word 'Chair' does not make them equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.
A's hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area, while B's obtain links an Author to an Award. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's Rejected Paper is a specific outcome of review (a paper that was rejected), while B's Evaluated Paper is the broader class of papers that have been evaluated, with Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper as its children. Rejected Paper is therefore strictly more specific than Evaluated Paper, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a submission type, sibling of Paper, child of Regular contribution). B's 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a deadline (a point in time) for submitting abstracts, child of Deadline. One is a document type, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented) in the edas ontology, sitting under Academic Event alongside Talk Event and Workshop, and linked to Accepted Paper. B 'Video presentation' is a kind of Presentation activity in iasted, a sibling of Power Point presentation, i.e. a presentation format/medium rather than an event. The intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are unrelated.

A's Author is a person who writes/submits papers (a Conference Member/User with paper-related properties). B's Track workshop chair is a chair role for a track/workshop event, a sibling of Reviewer and Committee member, not a paper author. The concepts denote different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Security Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in edas, while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee type under Committee in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic taxonomy vs. committee structure) and share no intended instances.

A's PC Member is a reviewer role in the programme committee (a subclass of Possible Reviewer, with children PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc.). B's IASTED member is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. a conference attendee who is a member of the IASTED organisation, alongside IASTED non member, Listener, Speaker, etc. The two denote different concepts (programme-committee reviewer vs. paying/organisational attendee membership), so they are not equivalent.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection) under Decision, i.e. the state of a paper being accepted. B's Week Reject Rating is a review rating category (sibling of Accept Rating, Reject Rating) under Review Rating, i.e. a score value used in reviewing. Different domains (decision outcome vs. rating value), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Industrial Paper' is a kind of Paper (a submitted/published document). They belong to different branches (document/announcement vs. paper) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while ekaw's updatedVersionOf relates a Document to another Document (versioning relation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

confOf Organization is an institution (Company, University) that employs people and has an address; iasted Place is a physical location (Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room) where activities are held and people are present. Their instances and properties do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Academic Event is a broad umbrella for scholarly events (workshops, talks, paper presentations, organizational meetings) with calls and related documents; B's Session is a specific lecture-type activity within a conference (sibling of plenary lecture and tutorial, parent of speaker lecture). A session is a kind of academic event, but the two classes are not coextensive: Academic Event covers many event types beyond sessions, and Session is a narrower lecture slot. They overlap in the conference domain but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so 'related' is the safest non-equivalent verdict.

cmt:User is a general person role class whose subclasses include Administrator, Author and Reviewer, and whose siblings include Chairman and Program Committee Member. edas:TPC Member is a specific committee role (a program-committee member) that is a sibling of Author and Reviewer, not their parent. The two classes do not have the same intended instances: a User need not be a TPC Member, and a TPC Member is a specific role rather than the general user class. They are therefore not equivalent.

A's 'has parts' relates a Conference volume to its Conference part (whole-part decomposition of a volume), while B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Science Worker in confOf is a broad person role (sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.), while Student in ekaw is a specific person type (sibling of Paper Author, Conference Participant, Possible Reviewer). A student is not necessarily a science worker and a science worker is not necessarily a student; the concepts overlap only incidentally and are not equivalent.

A's 'event On List' is an object property linking an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (where the event is listed), while B's 'Start of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (its start time). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), a subclass of Scientific Event. B's Conference city is a subclass of City, denoting the city where a conference is held. They belong to different branches (event vs. location) and have different instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's Break Event is a non-academic conference event (parent Non Academic Event, children Coffee Break, Free Time Break, Meal Break), i.e. a scheduled pause in the programme. B's Introduction is a conference activity (parent Conference activity, child Introduction of speaker, siblings Lecture, Presentation, Welcome address), i.e. a talk/session introducing a speaker. Different concepts despite both being conference-schedule items; no subsumption or overlap.

Both properties link a paper/item to its author/person. In cmt, Paper has Author Author; in iasted, Item is prepared by Person. The domain/range pairs (Paper->Author vs Item->Person) are the same conceptual relation in the conference domain, with Paper/Item and Author/Person being synonymous classes. Direction is the same (work -> creator), so the properties are equivalent.

Workshop is a type of working event (a small meeting held alongside a conference), while Program Committee is a committee of people that reviews papers. They belong to different branches of the conference domain (event vs. committee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the cmt ontology), while B 'Video presentation' is a kind of Presentation activity in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Abstract' is a document/paper type (a subclass of Paper, sibling of Paper Full Version) representing the abstract text of a paper. B's 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a subclass of Deadline representing the due date for submitting abstracts. One is a document artefact, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's has Phone is a datatype property from Contact Information to string, while B's has amount of is a datatype property from Money to int. They relate entirely different kinds of things (phone numbers vs monetary amounts) in different domains, so they are unrelated.

Author in confOf is a subclass of Person (path Person > Author) and is specifically someone who writes contributions. Person in ekaw is the broader superclass with children including Paper Author. Thus confOf Author is strictly more specific than ekaw Person, so Author is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.

A's updatedVersionOf relates a Document to another Document (a versioning relation between documents), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents the document). Different domain/range semantics and directions of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Poster Paper' is a kind of Paper (a document presented as a poster), while B 'Gold Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. sponsors) and share no intended instances.

A's Chairman is a Person role (a person who chairs, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, and a conflict-of-interest property), while B's Presentation is a Conference activity (an event with subclasses Power Point presentation and Video presentation). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. activity) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'reviews' relates a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's 'is paid in' relates Money to a Building (domain Money, range Building). The domains, ranges and intended meanings are entirely different, so the two properties are unrelated.

A is a conference topic (a subject area for papers, under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical device alongside projectors and video players). They share only the word 'computer' and denote entirely different concepts.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (author writes paper). B's topic Covered By relates a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (a topic is covered by an event/paper). Different domains (Author vs Research Topic), different ranges (Paper vs Event/Paper), and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference Proceedings' is a published multi-author volume (a document/artifact) in ekaw, while B 'Conference state' is a state of a conference (alongside Presenter state, Sponsor state) in iasted. They denote different concepts: a publication versus a conference status, so they are unrelated.

A 'Industrial Session' is a type of conference session (an event in the conference programme), while B 'Session room' is a physical place (a room where sessions are held). They belong to different branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Negative Review' is a subclass of Review (a document/evaluation artefact), while B's 'Reviewer' is a subclass of Speaker/Delegate (a person role). They denote different kinds of entities (review document vs. person), so they are unrelated.

hasAuthor goes from Paper to Author (paper -> author), while authorOf goes from Person to Document (author -> paper). They are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers), while B's 'relates To' links a Document to events, sessions or persons. The ranges differ (contribution vs. event/session/person) and the domains differ (volume vs. document), so they are not the same relation; they only overlap in that both connect a publication-like entity to other conference-domain entities.

A's 'Student lecturer' is a role of a person (a lecturer who is a student), sitting under Lecturer/Author/Speaker/Delegate in the conference-people hierarchy. B's 'Best Student Paper Supporter' is a sponsorship category (a kind of Sponzor, alongside Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter and Exhibitor), i.e. an organisation funding a best-student-paper award. They share only the word 'Student' and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Chair is a Person who initiates calls and reviews papers (an organisational role in the conference committee), while B's Speaker is a Delegate (a conference building occupant) with children Author and Reviewer, i.e. a presenting participant. The roles differ in kind and in the surrounding hierarchy, so they do not denote the same concept.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation between a document and its presentation forms), while B's 'is Written By' relates a Paper to an Author (authorship). Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a specific kind of speaker (a speaker at a plenary lecture), sitting under Author in the iasted hierarchy. B's 'Speaker' is the general class of persons who give presentations, with children Author and Invited Speaker. A plenary lecture speaker is a speaker, but not every speaker is a plenary lecture speaker, so A is strictly more specific than B: subsumed_by.

A 'Single Level Conference' is a conference type (a conference without sub-events, sibling of 'Two Level Conference' under Conference), whereas B 'Conference days' is a temporal concept (a period of days during a conference, under Time, with children like Delegate and One conference day). They denote different concepts: a conference kind vs. a time span, so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Paper is the general paper class (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with review/decision/author properties), while ekaw:Submitted Paper is a specific subclass of ekaw:Paper (sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, etc.). cmt:Paper is broader than ekaw:Submitted Paper, so it is subsumed by the more general ekaw:Paper rather than equivalent to the submitted-paper subclass.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type: the final camera-ready version of a paper), while B is a subclass of Deadline (a time point for hotel reservation). They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is a full paper submission date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date literal (a deadline attribute), while B's 'submit' is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper). They differ in kind, domain, range and meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property of Conference www pointing to a string URL, while B's 'has Email' is a datatype property of Person pointing to an email string. They have different domains (Conference www vs Person) and different intended values (URL vs email address), so they are not the same relation.

Conference fees is a monetary/fee concept (a cost associated with attending a conference), while Workshop is a working event (a type of event alongside Conference and Tutorial). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Conference Chair is a chairing role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Program Committee Chair), while B's Program Committee member is a member of the program committee under Organizator, sibling of Program Chair. The roles differ: chairing the conference vs. serving on the PC; they are not the same concept.

A's readByReviewer links a Paper to the Reviewer who reads it; B's reviewWrittenBy links a Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it. The domain and range differ (Paper->Reviewer vs Review->Possible Reviewer), and the direction of the reading/writing relation is not the same, so they are not equivalent; they are only related in that both connect a document-like entity to a person involved in reviewing.

A's Sponsor is a Person who sponsors (sibling of Delegate under Person), while B's Bronze Supporter is a specific sponsorship tier under Sponzor, alongside Gold/Silver/Platinum/Exhibitor. Sponsor is the general sponsoring entity/role; Bronze Supporter is one particular level of supporter, so Sponsor is broader and subsumes the tier concept rather than being equivalent to it.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship relation), while B's 'is present' links a Person to a Time (attendance/presence at a time). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Co chair' is a specific committee role (sibling of Chair, parent Committee member, domain/range of committee co-chair properties), while B's 'Author' is a person who writes contributions (parent Person, sibling of Chair PC/Member PC/Participant, domain of writes). The intended instances and relations differ: a co-chair is a committee officer, an author is a contributor of papers; neither subsumes the other.

A is a subject/topic area within the EDAS topic taxonomy (a research area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a type of conference session event (a subclass of Session under Scientific Event). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic classification vs. event type) and share no intended instances.

confOf's Administrative event covers organisational/administrative conference events (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration) and is a sibling of Social and Working events under Event. edas's Academic Event covers academic programme events (organizational meeting, paper presentation, talk, workshop) and is a sibling of Non Academic Event under Conference Event. Both are broad categories of conference events, but their intended instances differ: administrative events are not academic events and vice versa. They overlap only in being subclasses of a general conference event, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to its Subject Area (domain Paper, range Subject Area), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document (the paper/contribution that creates the conflict), while B's 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item (something the person acquires, e.g. a document or award). The intended meanings differ: conflict-of-interest declaration vs. acquisition, so the properties are not equivalent.

The two entities are from different ontologies and represent different concepts: one is a property 'submitPaper' with domain Author and range Paper, while the other is a property 'obtain' with domain Author and range Award. They relate different types of objects and are not equivalent.

confOf's Person is the general superclass of all people in the conference (authors, chairs, participants, etc.), while sigkdd's Speaker is a subclass of Person restricted to those who give a presentation. Person is strictly more general than Speaker, so A subsumes B, not equivalent.

A Conference is a working event (an activity with a venue and deadlines, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B Book proceeding is a publication item (a document, sibling of Cd proceeding). An event and a publication are different kinds of things, so the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Administrative event' is a conference-organisation event (submission, reviewing, registration, camera-ready) under Event in confOf, while B 'Computer Networks Sensor Topic' is a subject/topic area under Computer Networks Topic in edas. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Paper is a Document (a written contribution with authors, reviews, decisions), while in Conference, Presentation is a Conference contribution that is given by an active participant and has an abstract; it is a presentation event, not the written paper. The two denote different concepts (written document vs. presentation act), so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper, sibling of Paper Abstract) in the cmt ontology, while B is a research topic category (CAD Topic) under Topic in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document type vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, a committee member who chairs the conference), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself (with a name, proceedings, volume, topics). A person role and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a document type (a full paper as opposed to an abstract) in the conference domain, while B 'LCD projector' is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They share no meaning, no instances, and belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Item/Audiovisual equipment).

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name; B's 'has VAT' is a datatype property of Social/Working event giving a value-added-tax string. Different domains, different intended meanings, no overlap.

A's Review is the review document/contribution produced in the reviewing process (it is a Conference document, with properties linking it to a Reviewed contribution). B's Review Form is the form used to submit a review, not the review itself. They are related (a review form is filled in to produce a review) but not the same concept, so not equivalent.

A's memberOfConference is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while B's End_of_conference is a datatype property giving a Conference's end date/time. Different kinds (object vs datatype), different arguments, and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (sessions running in parallel), while ekaw's 'scientifically Organised By' relates an event to an Academic Institution that organises it scientifically. Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is a document/paper component in the conference domain, while Audiovisual equipment (iasted) is a physical item used at events; their paths, parents, and siblings (Document/Publication vs. Computer/LCD projector) show no conceptual overlap.

A's 'has a location' relates a Conference volume to a string (a venue/location), while B's 'has amount of' relates Money to an int (a monetary amount). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

In cmt, Document is a general class whose children are Paper and Review, so it subsumes Review. In Conference, Review is a specific document type (a review of a contribution), not the general document class. Thus Document is strictly more general than Review, not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Delegate/Non speaker (a person role: a student attending without speaking), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for non-members). They belong to different branches (person vs. fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Track is a conference event/part (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, range of 'has tracks' from Conference volume), while B's Value added tax is a kind of Tax under Money. The shared word 'track' is coincidental; the concepts are in completely different domains.

A's relatedToPaper links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a presentation-to-paper relation), while B's paperInVolume links a paper to the volume/proceedings it appears in. Different domain and range concepts and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address), while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item (acquiring something). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote an invited speaker at a conference. In Conference, Invited speaker is a subclass of Conference contributor (a person contributing to the conference); in ekaw, Invited Speaker is a subclass of Presenter (a conference participant who presents). An invited speaker is a person who gives an invited talk/presentation at the conference, so the intended instances coincide. The differing parent paths reflect different modelling choices (contributor vs presenter), not different concepts.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, a sibling of 'Conference announcement' and 'Review'. B's 'Paper' is the submitted document itself, the range of the 'submit' property (Author -> Paper). A call for papers is not a paper: the entities denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Pending Paper (edas) is a paper awaiting a decision, sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper. Camera Ready Paper (ekaw) is a paper in its final, accepted-for-publication form, sibling to Submitted Paper and various accepted paper types. They denote different stages of the paper lifecycle and are not equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic belongs to a review preference), while B's property links a Person to a Place/Time (a person is present in a place/time). Different domains (Topic vs Person), different ranges (Review preference vs Place/Time), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Paid applicant' is a registered conference applicant who has paid (a registration/attendance concept under Registeered applicant), while B 'Author' is a speaker who writes papers (under Speaker, with properties submit/obtain/notification). Different intended instances and different branches of the taxonomy; they are not the same concept.

A 'Tutorial Abstract' is a subclass of Abstract (a document summarising a tutorial talk) in ekaw, whereas B 'Viza' is a sibling of Submission, Review, Invitation letter etc. under Document in iasted, denoting an administrative document (likely a visa/authorisation form), not a tutorial abstract. Different intended instances and different domain roles, so unrelated.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's given name), while B's 'is visited by' is an object property from Building/City/State to Person (a place being visited by a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.
A is a general conference document giving information to participants; B is a specific hotel registration form, a kind of Form. They share no intended instances and neither subsumes the other.

Trip is a social event (an excursion/outing) under Social event, while Coctail reception is a specific social gathering under Conference activity. Both are social activities of a conference, so they overlap in the broader social-event sense, but a trip is not a cocktail reception; they are distinct event types, hence related rather than equivalent.

A 'Conference Dinner' is a specific social/meal event within a conference (a subclass of Meal Event), whereas B 'Conference' is the whole conference event with properties like city, start/end date, and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. A dinner is a part of a conference, not the conference itself, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document they present. Different domains (Conference vs Speaker), different ranges (Administrator vs Document), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Review preference' is a class representing a reviewer's stated preference/degree of interest in topics or submissions, with properties linking it to topics, submissions, reviewers, and an integer degree. B's 'Possible Reviewer' is a subclass of Person (a role a person can play), with properties linking it to papers and reviews. The two denote different kinds of entities (a preference record vs. a person role), so they are not equivalent.

A's email is an electronic mail address of a Person, while B's has First Name is a person's given name (comment mentions middle name). They denote different attributes of a person, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing information to attendees, while B's 'Exhibitor' is a sponsoring entity under Sponzor (sibling of Gold/Platinum Supporter). Different domains (document vs. sponsor role) and different paths; no equivalence.

Both are object properties named 'pay' with domain Person; the ranges (Money vs Registration fee) are compatible since a registration fee is a kind of money, and the intended relation 'a person pays a fee' is the same in the conference domain.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant under Person/Conference applicant, i.e. a person who registered late and paid. B 'Author attendee cd registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee under Money/Fee, i.e. a monetary amount for a specific registration category. They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Money) and denote different kinds of entities (a person vs a fee), so they are not equivalent.

A is an administrative event (the act/process of registering participants, a subclass of Event), while B is a person role (a Conference Participant who registered late, a subclass of Person). They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Person) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

Both are chair roles for a conference session/track, but they sit in different hierarchies: cmt's Associated Chair is a kind of Chairman/Conference Member (an organising-committee role), while iasted's Session chair is a kind of Delegate (a participant role who chairs a session). They overlap in that both chair something, but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is a published volume artefact (has publisher, volume, ISBN, issued by a Publisher), whereas B's 'Contribution' is a submitted work (Paper/Poster/Short paper) with abstract, keywords, authors and reviews. They denote different concepts in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'starts on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string (a start date/time), while B's 'part Of Event' is an object property linking an Event to another Event (mereological/structural containment). They differ in kind, range, and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (person-to-committee membership). B's was_a_program_committee_of relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (committee-to-event/volume association). The domains and ranges differ, so they are not equivalent; they are related only in that both involve a program committee, but they relate different kinds of things in different directions.

A is a specific conference topic under Computer Networks Topic (a subject area for papers), while B is a research activity (Simulating) under Activity before conference > Research, a kind of process/activity. Different categories (topic vs activity) with no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

Money is a broad class covering Fee, Sponzorship, Tax and Tip (its children), while sigkdd's Fee is only one specific kind of money (with Registration fee and Sponzor fee as subclasses). Money is therefore strictly more general than Fee, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A's Conference Trip is a social event (sibling of Conference Banquet), while B's Technic activity is a technical conference activity (sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break). They denote different kinds of conference activities and do not coincide.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship). B's presentation Of Paper relates an Individual Presentation to the paper being presented. Different domains (Author vs Individual Presentation) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'was a member of' links a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation), while B's 'organisedBy' links an Event to an Organisation or Person (organising relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is dated on' is a general datatype property on Activity (any activity, e.g. conference, workshop, review deadline) pointing to a dateTime. B's 'Start of conference' is a specific datatype property on Conference pointing to a dateTime, denoting the start date of a conference. The general activity-date property subsumes the more specific conference-start property; they are not equivalent because A applies to all activities and does not specifically mean the start of a conference.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper authored by a person), while B's `has Updated Version` relates a Document to another Document (a revised version of the same document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review the paper). B's 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person (the person who needs the item). The domains (Paper vs Item) and ranges (Reviewer vs Person) differ, and the intended meanings are different relations in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has Been Assigned' relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the reviewer is assigned a paper to review). B's 'has been assigned a review reference' relates a Submitted contribution/Topic to a Review preference (a submission is assigned a review preference). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Reviewer vs Submitted contribution/Topic; Paper vs Review preference), so the properties denote different relations despite the similar wording.

A's Review is a document/contribution class (a review artefact, sibling of Conference contribution, with properties linking it to a Reviewed contribution). B's Possible Reviewer is a person class (a role a person can play, parent of PC Member, with properties linking a person to papers they review). The two denote different kinds of entities (artefact vs. person/role), so they are not equivalent.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision) in the conference domain, while B's Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Taxi, Van) in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Paper Author' is a Person who writes papers; B 'Best Student Paper Supporter' is a sponsorship role (a kind of Sponzor) that funds a best-student-paper award. Different domains (person vs. sponsor role) and different parents (Person vs. Sponzor), so they are unrelated.

A's `follows` relates Administrative events to Administrative events (temporal ordering of events), while B's `submit` relates an Author to a Paper (submission act). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent.

In cmt, Associated Chair is a subclass of Chairman (a person who chairs/associates with the conference organisation), while in edas Session Chair is a Person who chairs a session and is involved in reviewing/initiating calls. The two roles differ: an Associated Chair is a conference-organisation chair role, whereas a Session Chair is a session-level chair with review and call-initiation duties. They share no parent (Chairman vs Person) and their property contexts differ, so they are not the same concept.

Both are object properties from a Topic/Research Topic to the things the topic is used in: A's range is Conference part (papers, events, etc.) and B's range is Event, Paper. The direction is the same (topic -> covered artefact), and the domains coincide (Topic / Research Topic). The slight difference in range breadth (Conference part vs Event, Paper) reflects the different granularity of the two ontologies rather than a different relation, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.
Student (a Person subtype in ekaw) and Bronze Supporter (a Sponzor subtype in sigkdd) denote entirely different concepts: a person role vs. a sponsorship level. No overlap in intended instances.

cmt:rejectedBy relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person/role who rejected it), while iasted:give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving something). Different domain (Paper vs Person), different range (Administrator vs Activity/Item), and different meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a steering committee' links a Conference volume to its Steering committee (a specific committee body), while B's 'organisedBy' links an Event to an Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domain (Conference volume vs Event), different range (Steering committee vs Organisation/Person), and different meaning (committee membership vs organising agent), so they are not equivalent.

A's writtenBy links a Review to its Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), while B's hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (domain Active Paper, range Review Rating). Different domains, ranges, and directions of relation; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person (a human attending the conference), while B 'Activity after conference' is an Activity (a post-conference event such as a tour or departure). They belong to disjoint top-level categories (Person vs Activity) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Tutorial is a working event (a kind of event/session), while B's Tutorial speaker is a person role (a subclass of Author/Speaker). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper Abstract is the abstract of a submitted paper (sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B's Invited Talk Abstract is the abstract of an invited talk (sibling of Tutorial Abstract under Abstract). They share the word 'Abstract' but denote abstracts of different document types, so they are not equivalent.

cmt's writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (the author writes a paper), while iasted's need relates a Person to an Item (a person needs an item). The domains/ranges differ in meaning (Author vs Person, Paper vs Item) and the relations are semantically distinct, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasStreet is a datatype property mapping Contact Information to a string street address, while B's obtain is an object property mapping a Person to an Item. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (person is a member of a conference), while B's 'is prepared by' relates an Item to a Person (item is prepared by a person). They have different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation, nor is one a generalization of the other.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person (a human role in the conference, with subclasses Active/Passive participant), while B 'Social program' is a Conference activity (an event such as a dinner banquet). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to a paper), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (authoring a document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's read By Meta Reviewer relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (a specific reviewing relation in the cmt ontology), while B's obtain relates a Person to an Item (a generic acquisition relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (a reviewer reads a paper for review). B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a generic participation/contribution relation). The domains (Reviewer vs Person) and ranges (Paper vs Activity/Item) differ, and the intended meanings are distinct: reading a paper for review is not the same as giving/participating in an activity. No subsumption holds either, since neither property's instances are a subset of the other's.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Paper' is the scholarly document itself (with children like Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, Review relations). They denote different concepts: a call for papers is not a paper.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented), while B 'Silver Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. sponsor) and share no instances.

hasCity relates an Organization/Person to a City (a location), while organises relates an Organisation/Person to an Event (an activity they organise). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference document (subclass of Document, with reviews, topics, presentations, and many paper subtypes), while B's Card is a physical item (subclass of Item, sibling of Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle, with child Credit card). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Best Student Paper Supporter' is a sponsorship role/level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. sponsor) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasPhone relates a Person to a phone number string, while B's Name relates a Person to their name string. They are different datatype properties with different intended values, despite sharing domain Person and range string.

Both are subclasses of Paper representing a paper that has been submitted but not yet accepted/rejected. EDAS 'Pending Paper' is a paper awaiting decision; EKAW 'Submitted Paper' is a paper that has been submitted (with child Assigned Paper, i.e. assigned to a reviewer). Both denote the same stage of a paper in the submission/review process, and their sibling sets (Accepted/Rejected/Published vs Camera Ready/Regular/Poster) are consistent with the same intended class of submitted papers.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's 'is sent before' relates an Item to a Time (temporal ordering of an item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Abstract is a subclass of Document (a written artefact, with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and it is presented as a Paper). B's Deadline is a temporal milestone class (with children for abstract submission, author notification, paper submission, and a Date property). They denote different concepts: a document type versus a time point, so they are unrelated.

Both entities denote the same concept in the conference domain: a person who contributes to or is involved with a conference (e.g., author, reviewer, committee member). The labels 'Person' and 'Contribution' (or similar) align as the core human actor class, and their contextual roles (domain/range of submission, review, authorship properties) coincide.

A's 'has a committee co chair' relates a Committee to a Co chair (a role within a committee), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or paper). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Publisher in the Conference ontology is an organisation that issues conference proceedings (it has a name and issues Conference proceedings), whereas City in confOf is a geographical location used as the city of an Organization or Person (has City domain Organization/Person). The two concepts share no instances and no meaning in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Abstract is a kind of Document that is the written abstract of a paper (it is presented as a paper and has children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract). B's Form is a document used for administrative purposes (author information form, hotel registration form, registration form). They share only the parent Document; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic (Wireless Communications Topic) under Topic, while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee) under Committee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

A's 'Agency Staff Member' is a Person who works for the organising agency (sibling of Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student), while B's 'Student lecturer' is a Lecturer who is also a student (sibling of Worker lecturer) in the delegate/speaker/author hierarchy. They denote different roles with no overlap in intended instances.

A's isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event (a venue hosting an event), while B's holded_by relates a Conference to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (the body that holds the conference). Different domains (Place vs Conference) and ranges (Conference Event vs ACM SIGKDD), and the directions/meanings do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A's authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship of a paper), while B's prepare relates a Person to an Item (preparing something, e.g. a contribution or presentation). The ranges differ (Document vs Item) and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.
A Meta Review is a specific kind of Review (a review of reviews), while B Review is the general review class; Meta Review is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by Review rather than equivalent.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class representing a reviewer's expertise/preference about a submitted contribution (it is linked to Reviewer and Submitted contribution, and is a sibling of Review preference). B's 'Paper' is a document submitted by an author (path Document > Paper, sibling of Abstract and Review). The two denote different concepts: expertise metadata versus the paper document itself, so they are unrelated.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment of a reviewer to a paper), while B's partOf is a generic mereological/part-whole relation with unspecified domain and range. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no shared meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Conference is a working event (a type of event such as workshop/tutorial), while Introduction is a conference activity (a session/activity such as welcome address or lecture). They denote different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a tutorial in the conference domain. Although their paths differ (confOf places Tutorial under Working event alongside Conference and Workshop; ekaw places it under Individual Presentation alongside Contributed Talk and Invited Talk), the intended instances coincide: a tutorial is a tutorial event. The differing parent categories reflect different modelling choices, not different concepts.

Both properties relate an event/activity to the location where it takes place. ekaw's heldIn has domain Event and range Location; iasted's is_held_in has domain Activity and range Place, Time. Event/Activity and Location/Place are the corresponding classes in the two ontologies, so the properties denote the same relation. The extra Time range in iasted is a modelling difference (time of the event) rather than a different relation.

Contribution in confOf is a conference submission (Paper/Poster/Short paper) written by an Author and reviewed by PC members, whereas Person in iasted is a human agent (Delegate/Sponsor) who gives activities and is paid. The two classes denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Evaluated Paper is a specific stage in the paper lifecycle (a submitted paper that has been assigned and evaluated, with children Accepted/Rejected Paper), whereas B's Document is a broad artefact category (parent of Review, Submission, Form, Payment document, etc.). Evaluated Paper is a kind of paper, not a kind of document in B's sense; the two concepts do not coincide and neither subsumes the other in the conference domain.

A 'Working event' is a conference-domain event class (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while B 'Computer Networks Optical Topic' is a specific research topic in the edas topic hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property of Person giving a person's first name; B's Name_of_sponsor is a datatype property of Sponzor giving a sponsor's name. Different domains (Person vs Sponzor) and different intended concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'organised By' relates an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it (domain Event, range Organisation/Person). B's 'occupy' relates a Person to a Building/City/State they occupy (domain Person, range Building/City/State). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A 'Plenary lecture' is a kind of conference activity/lecture (an event), while B 'Organizator' is a kind of Person (an agent role). They belong to disjoint branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Academic Event' is a subclass of Conference Event (an event such as a workshop, talk or paper presentation), while B's 'Academic Institution' is a subclass of Organisation (a university or research institute). They denote different kinds of things (events vs. organisations) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

A's Topic is a subject area classification (children are research areas like Antennas, Cryptography) used to categorize conferences and papers. B's Event is a conference-domain happening (children Scientific Event, Social Event) with properties like held In, organised By, part Of Event. Topic and Event denote different concepts; the only link is that an Event covers a Research Topic, which is a relation, not equivalence.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a reviewed paper that was not accepted, a subclass of Reviewed contribution in the document/contribution hierarchy. B 'Reception' is a social event (a gathering) under Social event. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances or meaning.

A's Person is a general human agent in the conference domain (authors, reviewers, committee members, participants) with properties like contributes, has an email, has authors, has gender, first/last name. B's Sponzor is a funding/sponsoring organisation (Gold Supporter, Exhibitor, etc.) with a sponsor name and a search relation to ACM SIGKDD. A sponsor is not a person; the two classes have disjoint intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Call is a call-for-papers/reviews announcement issued by chairs and tied to an academic event, with children Call For Manuscripts/Papers/Reviews. B's Fee is a monetary charge with children Registration fee and Sponzor fee. Different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Conference restaurant' is a Building subtype (a dining facility within the conference venue), while B's 'Hotel' is a Place subtype for lodging. Different intended instances and different parent categories; the shared 'Place' root is too generic to make them equivalent.

Paper Full Version is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Abstract) in cmt, whereas Cd proceening is a subclass of Publication (a published CD proceedings artefact, sibling of Book proceeding) in iasted. They denote different concepts: a full paper document vs. a published proceedings medium, so they are not equivalent.

A's email is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address), while B's writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person (its author). They differ in domain, range, and meaning; email is not the inverse or a subproperty of writtenBy.

A 'Early paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant under Person/Conference applicant, i.e. a type of person/registrant. B 'Memeber registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee under Money/Fee, i.e. a type of monetary fee. One denotes a person category, the other a fee category; they are in different branches of the domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A 'Co chair' is a committee member who co-chairs a committee (sibling of Chair, with committee co-chair roles). B 'Session Chair' is a conference participant who chairs a session, a distinct role from committee co-chairing. The paths, parents and siblings differ (Committee member vs Conference Participant/PC Member), so the intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'Conference city' is a subclass of City denoting the city where a conference is held (siblings: Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city), whereas B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with properties for its city, name, start/end dates and SIGKDD holding. The two denote different concepts (a location vs. an event), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasStreet is a datatype property linking an Organization or Person to a string street address, while B's heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They differ in domain (Organization/Person vs Event), range (string vs Location), and intended meaning (address component vs event venue), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property giving the title (string) of a Social/Working event, while B's 'start Date' is a datatype property giving the dateTime at which a Conference starts. They have different domains (event vs. conference), different ranges (string vs. dateTime), and different intended meanings (title vs. start time), so they are not the same relation.

A's `obtain` relates a Person to an Item (a person acquires/obtains an item), while B's `submit` relates an Author to a Paper (an author submits a paper). Although both involve a person and a document-like object, the intended relations differ: obtaining is acquiring an item, submitting is handing in a paper for review. They are not the same relation and neither subsumes the other.
Both are datatype properties linking a Person to a string email address, with identical domain (Person) and range (string); the labels 'has an email' and 'has Email' denote the same relation.

A's virtualMeetingEnabledBy relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables virtual meetings), while B's parallel_with relates two Administrative events that run in parallel. Different domain, range and meaning; no equivalence.

A's Published Paper is a specific status of Paper (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), while B's Paper is the general class of all papers (parent of Abstract and Review, domain of submit). Published Paper is strictly narrower than Paper, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's hasCo-author relates a Paper to a Co-author (a person who co-authored the paper), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (the person writes the item). The directions and the kinds of things related are different: A goes paper->person, B goes person->item. B's write is closer to an inverse of an authorship relation, not to hasCo-author, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) in the Conference ontology, whereas B 'Technic activity' is a scheduled event/activity (sibling of Lecture, Coffee break, Registration) in iasted. A document and an activity are different kinds of things, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a talk/session in which an accepted paper is presented), sitting under Academic Event alongside Talk Event and Workshop, and is linked to Accepted Paper. B's 'Power Point presentation' is a specific presentation format/medium (a slide-based presentation) under Presentation, sibling of Video presentation. They overlap in that a paper presentation may be given as a PowerPoint presentation, but they are not the same concept: one is an event type, the other a presentation medium/format. Hence related, not equivalent.
A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country; B's is_equipped_by relates a Place to an Item. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Submission event' is an administrative event covering the submission of contributions (siblings: camera ready, registration, reviewing, reviewing results). B's 'Organizational Meeting' is an academic event (siblings: paper presentation, talk, workshop) denoting a meeting, not a submission deadline/process. Different parents (Administrative vs Academic event) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a specific kind of conference contribution (a regular contribution, sibling of Extended abstract) that has an abstract and is part of a presentation. B's Document is a broad administrative item (parent of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Review, Submission, etc.), not a scientific contribution. The intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are unrelated.

confOf's `follows` is a temporal/ordering relation between Administrative events (one event follows another). ekaw's `inverse of part Of 7` is the inverse of a mereological part-of relation, relating an Event to its whole (range Event, domain unspecified). Ordering and parthood are different relations, and the inverse direction further distinguishes them; they are not equivalent.

A 'Microelectronics Topic' is a subject area of papers (a subclass of Topic in edas), while B 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of scientific event/presentation (subclass of Individual Presentation in ekaw). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic vs. event) and cannot denote the same concept.
