A 'Regular author' is a kind of conference contribution/contributor role (a paper authored by a regular, non-invited author), sitting alongside Invited speaker, Poster, Presentation. B 'Presenter' is a person role under Author, i.e. someone who presents at the conference. The two denote different concepts (a contribution type vs. a person role), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (a conference/tutorial/workshop activity), while B 'Communication Theory Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author restricted to people who are authors but not reviewers. B's 'Author' is a broader class (a Speaker who authors things, with subclasses for various author types and a sibling Reviewer). Every Author-Not-Reviewer is an Author, but not every Author is an Author-Not-Reviewer (an Author could also be a Reviewer). Thus A is strictly more specific than B: subsumed_by.

A's Decision is the outcome of a review (children Acceptance/Rejection, range of has Decision from Paper), while B's Money is a monetary amount with children Fee/Sponzorship/Tax/Tip and payment properties. Different domains entirely; no overlap.

In cmt, Preference is a class representing a reviewer's preference/interest in a paper (a bidding or preference statement), whereas edas ReviewForm is the form/artifact used to submit a review. They denote different concepts: one is a preference expression, the other a review submission form. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain, so unrelated.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a kind of document/paper in the conference domain (a paper that has been submitted), while B 'Deadline' is a time point (with children such as submission deadline, notification deadline). They denote different concepts: one is a document, the other a temporal entity. No equivalence, subsumption or meaningful overlap.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' is an administrative action relating an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (domain Administrator, range Program Committee Member). B's 'parallel with' is a symmetric relation between Administrative events (domain and range both Administrative event). They relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's Document is a broad superclass of Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, Meal Menu (conference artefacts), while B's Payment document is a specific administrative item under Item > Document, with children Bank transfer and Cheque. The shared word 'Document' does not make them the same concept; A's Document is a general document class, B's is a payment-specific document. They denote different concepts.

A's 'end Date' is a datatype property giving the Conference's end date/time (domain Conference, range dateTime), while B's 'lists Event' is an object property linking a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (domain Reviewer, range Personal Review History), while B's hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (domain Paper, range Possible Reviewer). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not inverses either, so they are unrelated.

A's readByReviewer goes Paper -> Reviewer (a paper is read by a reviewer), while B's reviewerOfPaper goes Possible Reviewer -> Paper (a reviewer is reviewer of a paper). They are inverse relations, not equivalent, and their domains/ranges differ (Paper vs Possible Reviewer).

A's 'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership in an organisational body). B's 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person (authorship/signing of a document). Different domains (Committee member vs Item), different ranges (Committee vs Person), and different intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's end Review relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the chair ends a review), while B's belongs to a review reference relates a Topic to a Review preference (a topic's review preference). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's date is a datatype property of a Conference giving its date (range date), while B's has_a_volume is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving a volume number (range int). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

An Attendee in edas is any person attending the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), a general participant role. 'One day presenter' in iasted is a specific kind of Delegate who presents for one day, a much narrower role. Every one-day presenter is an attendee, but not every attendee is a one-day presenter, so the edas Attendee is more general and the iasted class is subsumed by it.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address), while B's 'send' is an object property linking a Person to an Item (a thing sent). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.
A's hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to its Subject Area (topic), while B's is_present_in relates a Person to a Place/Time (attendance). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Reviewer is a person who reviews (belongs to reviewers, has review expertise, invites co-reviewers). B's Possible Reviewer is a broader role: it is the range of 'has Reviewer' and 'review Written By', and it has PC Member as a child, so it covers anyone who could review, including PC members. Every Reviewer in A is a Possible Reviewer in B, but B's Possible Reviewer also includes people who merely could review, so A's Reviewer is strictly narrower: subsumed_by.

A's 'has a publisher' links a Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organisation that publishes the proceedings), whereas B's 'write' links a Person to an Item (an author writing a paper). Different domain, different range, different direction of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A Presenter is a conference participant who gives a presentation (parent Conference Participant, child Invited Speaker). B Author cd proceedings included is a Speaker/Author whose paper is included in the conference proceedings (parent Author, siblings Lecturer, Plenary lecture speaker, Tutorial speaker). Both denote people who present work at the conference, so they overlap, but neither is strictly more general: a presenter need not be an author of an included paper, and an author of an included paper need not present. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a conference participant role), while B's Silver Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsorship level). They share no meaning, no properties, and no common parent; the only overlap is the word 'student' appearing in a sibling label, which is irrelevant.

A's 'paper Assignment Tools Run By' is a Conference-domain property linking a Conference to an Administrator (the person who runs the paper-assignment tool for the conference). B's 'give' is a Person-domain property linking a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives/presents something). The domains (Conference vs Person), ranges (Administrator vs Activity/Item) and intended meanings differ, so they are not the same relation.

A's Conference Venue Place is a physical location (a subtype of Place, sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), whereas B's Conference Trip is a social event (a subtype of Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet). A location and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type, with children like Assigned Paper), while B is a subclass of Deadline (a time point for camera-ready manuscript submission). They belong to disjoint branches (Document vs Time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both properties record the end time of an event/conference, but A's 'ends on' has domain Event and range string (a generic end date for any event), while B's 'End of conference' has domain Conference and range dateTime (specifically the end of a conference). They overlap in meaning but are not the same property: different domains (Event vs Conference) and different ranges (string vs dateTime).

Conference contributor is a broad role class covering anyone who contributes to a conference (authors, speakers, participants, etc.), while SC Member is a specific committee role (Steering Committee member) under PC Member. The two concepts do not coincide: a contributor need not be an SC member, and an SC member is a committee member rather than a generic contributor. Their paths and sibling sets differ substantially, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Chair is the general chair of the whole conference (a Person who initiates calls and reviews, sibling of Author/Reviewer/TPC Member). B's Workshop Chair is a Conference Participant and PC Member who chairs a workshop, a much narrower role under a different hierarchy. They denote different roles, so they are not equivalent.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a document), while B's is_visited_by relates a Building/City/State to a Person (physical visitation of a place). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Contributed Talk is a kind of scientific event/individual presentation (a talk given at a conference), while Conference state is a state of a conference (a phase/status in the conference process). They belong to different branches (Event vs State) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Scholar in confOf is a subclass of Person (a person with a price category), while Meal Menu in edas is a subclass of Document (a menu document for a meal event). They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and have unrelated properties (study At vs has Menu/is Menu Of), so they denote different concepts.

A's 'was a committee of' relates a Committee to a Conference volume (a committee is part of a conference's organisation), while B's 'organised By' relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the agent that organises the event). The domains (Committee vs Event) and ranges (Conference volume vs Organisation/Person) differ, so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (submitting a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole event such as a conference with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's Video presentation is a specific kind of presentation activity (sibling of Power Point presentation). They denote different concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a complete paper document (sibling of Paper Abstract, under Paper), while B's 'Initial manuscipt' is a submission-stage document (sibling of Final manuscript, under Submission). Both denote a full-text paper artefact, but one is classified by document type and the other by submission stage, so they overlap rather than coincide.

A's writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (a reviewer writes a review). B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; not the same relation.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, choices), while B 'Medicine Topic' is a subclass of Topic, a subject area. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. topic) and share no instances.

A Meta Review (cmt) is a document/review artefact that aggregates reviews of a submission, a subclass of Review. B Call For Reviews (edas) is a call/announcement soliciting reviewers, a subclass of Call alongside Call For Papers and Call For Manuscripts. They denote different concepts (an artefact vs. a solicitation event) and are not equivalent.

Late paid applicant is a narrow subclass of Paid applicant (a registered conference applicant who paid late), whereas Participant is a broad Person subclass covering all conference participants (members, students, authors, chairs, etc.). Every late paid applicant is a participant, but not vice versa, so the A class is strictly subsumed by the B class.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'parallel with' links an Administrative event to another Administrative event that runs in parallel. Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.
A's title is the title of a Paper; B's Name of sponsor is the name of a Sponzor (sponsor). Different domains (Paper vs Sponzor) and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

University is an academic organisation (a type of Organisation/Academic Institution), while Best Research Paper Award is a type of Award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

Conference document in ontology A is a broad class covering calls, announcements, contributions, and reviews, with properties for authors and issue date. Call in edas is specifically a call for papers/manuscripts/reviews, initiated by committee members and linked to an academic event and submission deadline. While both can include calls for papers, Conference document is broader and includes non-call documents, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Poster Paper, etc.), while B's 'Conference' is an event class with properties such as start/end date, city, and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. A paper and a conference event are different concepts, so the entities are unrelated.

A 'Coctail reception' is a social conference activity (sibling of Coffee break, Welcome address, etc.), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (sibling of Hotel, Main office). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a location, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a contribution/document class (sibling of Poster and Short paper, under Contribution), whereas B's Paper Author is a person role (subclass of Person, sibling of Conference Participant and Student). They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing information to attendees, while B's 'Departure' is an activity after the conference (sibling of Full day tour). They denote different concepts in different branches of the domain, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but A's domain is Call (a call for papers with a submission deadline) while B's domain is Activity (an event dated on some date). A submission deadline is a specific kind of date associated with a call, not the general dating of an activity, so the properties are not equivalent; they overlap only in that both relate something to a dateTime.

A Workshop (edas) is a type of Academic Event, a small-scale meeting held alongside a conference. B Session (iasted) is a subdivision of a Lecture (a talk slot within a conference activity), with children like Speaker lecture. A workshop is not a lecture session; the two denote different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Speaker lecture' is a session/event type (a lecture session given by a speaker) under Activity > Conference activity > Lecture > Session, whereas B's 'Invited Speaker' is a person role under Person > Speaker. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and are not equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an organized excursion during the conference), while a Single hotel room is a type of hotel room (accommodation place). They belong to different branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the outcome/acceptance decision for a paper), while B's is_sent_before relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering relation). They differ in both domain/range and intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it (domain Sponsorship, range Organization), while B's 'pay' links a Person to Money paid (domain Person, range Money). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

In cmt, Document is the general class whose children are Paper and Review, so Document subsumes Paper. In sigkdd, Paper is a subclass of Document, confirming that Paper is a narrower concept. Therefore Document (A) is more general than Paper (B), not equivalent.

A's Conference Participant is a subclass of Person (a person attending a conference, with subclasses like Presenter, Session Chair, PC Chair), while B's Conference is the event itself (with properties such as start/end date, city, name, held by ACM SIGKDD). A person and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated despite the shared word 'Conference'.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (a person's membership in a conference), while B's is_part_of_conference_volumes relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a part-whole relation between conference components and proceedings volumes). The domains (Conference Member vs Conference part) and ranges (Conference vs Conference volume) differ, so the relations are not the same.

Company in confOf is a general commercial organization, sibling of University under Organization. Proceedings Publisher in ekaw is a specific role/organization that publishes proceedings, sibling of Academic Institution and Organising Agency under Organisation. The intended instances do not coincide: a company is not necessarily a proceedings publisher, and a proceedings publisher need not be a company (e.g., academic institution).

A 'Written contribution' is a subclass of Conference contribution (a document/paper kind, with children Regular contribution and Submitted contribution), whereas B 'Speaker' is a subclass of Person (a role played by an agent, with children Author and Invited Speaker). They belong to different top-level branches (document vs. person) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment relation), while iasted's is_used_for relates an Item to an Activity or Money (usage relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A is a research topic in the conference subject taxonomy (a kind of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a physical item type (a kind of Item with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Tutorial Abstract is a specific kind of abstract (an abstract for a tutorial), while sigkdd's Abstract is the general class of abstracts (siblings Paper, Review under Document). The ekaw class is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by the general Abstract class rather than equivalent to it.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that run in parallel (a symmetric co-scheduling relation between events), while ekaw's 'technicallyOrganisedBy' is a sub-property of 'organisedBy' linking an event to the agent that technically organises it. Different kinds of arguments (event-event vs event-agent) and different meanings, so they are not equivalent.
employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; not equivalent nor inverse.

A is the class of people who write papers (Person > Author, with properties has Related Paper and is Written By). B is a subclass of Registration fee (Money > Fee > Registration fee > Nonmember registration fee), i.e. a monetary amount, not a person. They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain.

Both are subclasses of Place denoting physical locations used for conference activities, but 'Meeting Room Place' is a generic room location while 'Conference hall' is a specific large hall; they overlap in use but are not the same concept.

A 'Co chair' is a committee role (a person who co-chairs a committee), while B 'Building' is a physical place that hosts conference venues. Their paths, parents, siblings and properties (committee co-chair relations vs. occupancy/location relations) are entirely disjoint, so they denote different concepts.

Both are object properties linking an author/person to the written contribution/item; confOf's Author/Contribution correspond to iasted's Person/Item, and the direction (writer -> written work) is the same, so writes and write denote the same relation.

A's Company is an Organization (a business entity, sibling of University) that participates in the conference domain. B's Conference restaurant is a Building/Place (a physical venue location, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). A company is an organization, not a building or place, so the two concepts do not coincide.

Both are documents in the conference domain that are submitted and reviewed. cmt's Paper is a Document with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and is reviewed (assigned To Reviewer, has Decision). iasted's Submission is a Document with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript, and is reviewed (sibling Review). The intended instances coincide: a submitted paper/submission. The differing siblings in iasted (forms, letters, payments) are administrative documents, not counterexamples to the core concept match.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B's 'Conference state' is a state/status category (sibling of Presenter state, Sponsor state) under State in iasted. One denotes a committee person, the other a status of a conference participant; they share no intended instances and are not related.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Lecturer is a person role (a kind of Author, with children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair is a person role (a chair who is associated with the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Member), while Meal Break is a non-academic conference event (a break for eating, sibling of Coffee Break and Free Time Break). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person vs. event) and share no intended instances.

A's `location Of` is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the inverse of an event's location), while B's `has amount of` is a datatype property linking Money to an integer amount. They relate entirely different kinds of entities (Location/Event vs Money/int) and have no overlap in meaning.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/member of the conference committee) in the cmt ontology, while B 'Conference airport' is a physical building/place in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class representing a reviewer's area/level of expertise, linked to Reviewer and Submitted contribution. B's 'Review' is a Document subclass representing the review document itself, sibling to Submission and other conference documents. They denote different concepts (expertise vs. review document), so they are unrelated.

A's 'contributes' goes Person -> Conference document (a person contributes a document), while B's 'written By' goes Contribution -> Author (a contribution is written by an author). These are inverse-like relations between the same kinds of entities (person/author and document/contribution), not the same directed relation, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'has a committee chair' relates a Committee to its Chair (a role/person leading the committee), while B's 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (a person signing something). Different domains (Committee vs Person), different ranges (Chair vs Item), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a person's role in organizing the conference), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a paper being presented by a person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person who takes part in a conference (with subclasses Active/Passive participant), while B 'Research' is an Activity before the conference (with subclasses Modelling/Simulating). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location (where the event takes place), while B's 'Date' is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a dateTime value. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A's Tutorial is a Working event sibling of Conference and Workshop; B's Workshop is an Academic Event sibling of Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation and Talk Event. Tutorial and Workshop are distinct kinds of conference events (a tutorial is instructional, a workshop is a collaborative meeting), and neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Camera ready contribution' is a subclass of Accepted contribution (a document/contribution that has been accepted and prepared for publication), while B's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the reviewing procedure. They belong to different branches (document vs. event) and denote different concepts; the only overlap is the word 'reviewing/camera ready' appearing in B's sibling 'Camera Ready event', which is a different entity.

A's property links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (a topic/skill area), while B's hasReview links a Paper to a Review (the review document/process). The ranges are different kinds of entities (expertise vs. review), so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a conference part sibling to Track and Workshop, while B's Workshop is a working event sibling to Conference and Tutorial. Although both ontologies have a Tutorial and a Workshop, the candidate pairs A:Tutorial with B:Workshop, which denote different concepts (a tutorial vs. a workshop); they are not equivalent.

Trip is a social event (an excursion/outing) in confOf, while Speaker is a person role in sigkdd who gives a presentation. They belong to different branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person who presents a paper), while B's Presenter state is a subclass of State (a status/phase of a conference, sibling of Conference state and Sponsor state). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. state), so they are not equivalent.

In confOf, Company is a subclass of Organization, denoting an organisation type (a company as an entity, sibling of University). In iasted, Sponsor company house is a subclass of Building, denoting a physical building/venue where sponsors are housed, sibling of Conference hotel, Presenter house, etc. The intended instances differ (organisations vs. buildings), so the classes are not equivalent.

confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (domain Contribution, range Author), while ekaw's 'references' is a citation relation between papers/documents. They relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference days' is a time span/period class (parent Time, children Delegate and One conference day, sibling Trip day) denoting the days on which a conference takes place. B 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a specific submission deadline (parent Deadline, siblings Author notification and Paper Submission). They denote different concepts: a duration/period versus a submission deadline, so they are unrelated.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a postal/zip code string, while B's E-mail is a datatype property of Person giving an email address string. They relate different kinds of things (postal address vs. email address) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while B's Silver Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsor organisation). They denote entirely different concepts: a person role vs. a sponsorship level, so they are unrelated.

In iasted, Lecturer is a subclass of Author (path ... > Author > Lecturer), i.e. a lecturer is a specific kind of author (with children Student lecturer, Worker lecturer). In edas, Author is the general class of people who write papers, with Presenter as a child. The two are not equivalent: Lecturer is strictly narrower than Author, so edas Author subsumes iasted Lecturer (Lecturer is subsumed_by Author).
A Meta Review is a specific kind of review (a review of reviews), while B Review is the general review class. Meta Review is therefore narrower and subsumed by Review, not equivalent.

A's Session Chair is a person role (a Conference Participant who chairs a session, also a PC Member). B's Technical commitee is a subclass of Delegate in a building/place hierarchy, and B already has a separate sibling 'Session chair' class, so Technical commitee denotes a committee/group of delegates, not the session-chair role. Different intended instances; not equivalent.

A's 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members (people belonging to a committee), while B's 'sign' links a Person to an Item (a person signing an item, e.g. a document). Different domains (Committee vs Person) and ranges (Committee member vs Item), so the relations are not the same.

A's presentationOfPaper relates an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper it presents (domain Individual Presentation, range Abstract/Paper). B's give relates a Person to an Activity/Item they give (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domains and ranges: one is a presentation-to-paper link, the other a person-to-activity link, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a kind of conference contributor (a person role in the programme), while B's 'IASTED non member' is a delegate classification based on membership status, not on being invited. Their paths, parents and siblings differ entirely, so the classes do not denote the same concept.

SC Member in ekaw is a Steering Committee member, a subclass of PC Member (a reviewer/organiser role within the program committee hierarchy). IASTED member in iasted is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. a conference attendee who is a member of the IASTED organisation. The two denote different concepts: one is a committee role, the other an attendee membership status. Their paths, parents and siblings do not align, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the overall conference event (has dates, administrators, members, submissions), while B's One conference day is a single day within a multi-day conference (a part/component of a conference, sibling of Delegate under Conference days). They denote different entities: a whole event vs. one day of it, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people on the organising committee), while B's is_given_by relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it. Different domains (Conference vs Presentation), different ranges (Conference Member vs Active conference participant), and different intended meaning (committee membership vs presentation authorship/speaking). They are not the same relation.

A's 'Proceedings Publisher' is an Organisation (a publisher entity that publishes proceedings), while B's 'Author book proceedings included' is a subclass of Author describing an author whose book/proceedings contribution is included. One denotes an organisation, the other a kind of author; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Reviewer is a sibling of TPC Member under Person, and both are distinct roles that can review papers (is Reviewing has domain Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). In ekaw, PC Member is a subclass of Possible Reviewer and is the parent of PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair, i.e. it denotes the programme-committee membership role, not the generic reviewer role. The two overlap (PC members are typically reviewers) but neither subsumes the other cleanly: edas Reviewer is broader than ekaw PC Member in that it is not restricted to committee membership, while ekaw PC Member carries committee-specific subroles absent from edas Reviewer. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A is a submission deadline (a time point in the Deadline branch), while B is a best student paper award (an award type in the Award branch). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a leadership role within the conference organization, while One day presenter (iasted) is a type of delegate who presents for one day. They belong to different subhierarchies (Chairman vs Delegate) and have no overlap in meaning.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference domain, a subclass of Person/Conference Member who writes and submits papers. Organisation (ekaw) is an institution or agency that organises events and publishes proceedings, with children Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. institution) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee), while B's send relates a Person to an Item (submitting/sending a paper or item). Different range types (Conference vs Item) and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's email is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address), while B's is dated on links an Activity to a dateTime (a date). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions/attendance), while B 'Proceedings Publisher' is an organisation that publishes proceedings. They belong to different branches (document vs organisation) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference-organisation event type (a subclass of Event, with children such as Submission event, Reviewing event, Camera Ready event), while B is a research subject area (a subclass of Topic, sibling of Computer Networks Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'has VAT' is a datatype property linking Social/Working events to a string tax value, while B's 'is dated on' links an Activity to a dateTime. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings (tax amount vs. date), so they are unrelated.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a specific stage of a conference contribution (a submitted contribution that has received reviews, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution). B 'Document' is a broader class whose children include Abstract, Paper and Review, and which is the range of presentation/submit-until properties. A reviewed contribution is a kind of document/paper, but Document also covers abstracts and reviews, so A is strictly narrower than B: subsumed_by.

A's Conference Member is a Person subtype (a person involved in a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's State is a geographical/administrative region (children Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state; properties like is situated in, occupy, is visited by relate it to Building/City/Person as a location). The two denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a physical location (a subtype of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place) where meetings take place, whereas B 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (subtype of Social Event, sibling of Conference Trip). One is a place, the other an event, so their instances cannot coincide.

A's forEvent relates a Call to an Academic Event (the call is for an event), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (a person needs an item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B 'Conference restaurant' is a building/place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a written paper). B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). The ranges differ (Author vs Speaker) and the relations differ (authorship vs presentation), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'referenced In' relates a paper/contribution to the document that cites it (inverse of cites), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they present/produce. Different domain, range and direction of relation; no overlap in meaning.
Transparency and Abstract are both subclasses of Document but represent different document types in different conference ontologies; they are not equivalent.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a type of physical location (a room where meetings take place), a sibling of Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place and Dining Place under Place. B 'Worker non speaker' is a subclass of Non speaker under Delegate, i.e. a kind of conference participant (a non-speaking delegate who is a worker), not a place at all. The two entities belong to different branches of the domain (location vs. person/role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Main office' is a place where the conference organisation is run (an administrative office), while B's 'Hotel' is accommodation for attendees. They are distinct sibling concepts under Place in both ontologies (in sigkdd, Hotel and Main office are siblings), so they are not equivalent.

A's `obtain` is an object property relating a Person to an Item (a thing obtained), while B's `Nation` is a datatype property relating a Person to a string (their nationality). They share only the Person domain; the ranges (Item vs string) and intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Abstract), while B's 'Best Research Paper Award' is a subclass of Award (a prize category, sibling of other best-paper awards). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (document vs. award) and denote different concepts.

A's Event is a broad class covering scientific and social events (conferences, workshops, etc.), with properties like held In, organised By, has Event. B's Speaker is a subclass of Person (a role played by an author/invited speaker) with properties presentation/presentationed by. They denote different concepts (an event vs. a person role) and are not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

A's Track is a subdivision of a conference (a conference has tracks, siblings Tutorial and Workshop under Conference part), whereas B's Conference is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop under Working event). Track is a part/stream of a conference, not a conference event itself; the shared sibling names reflect different roles, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a kind of conference event/session), while B's Workshop Chair is a person role (a conference participant who chairs a workshop). They belong to different branches of the domain (event vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.

Both classes denote the subject area of a paper/event: Conference's Topic is linked to submitted contributions, reviews and conference parts, while ekaw's Research Topic is covered by Events and Papers. The intended instances (research subject areas) coincide, so the two classes are equivalent.

Both entities denote the same concept in the conference domain: the class from ontology A and the class from ontology B have matching intended instances, as confirmed by their shared context (labels, paths, and properties).

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes papers), while B's 'Reviewer' is a person who reviews papers and has review expertise/preferences. The two denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is a publication artefact (has publisher, volume, ISBN, name) that a Publisher issues; B's 'Topic' is a subject area dealt with by contributions, on which PC members are expert, and which working events have. Their instances and roles in the domain are entirely different, so they are not equivalent.

An Invited Speaker is a specific kind of Presenter (a person invited to present), while the iasted Speaker is a broader Delegate role that has Author and Reviewer as children. Every invited speaker is a speaker/presenter, but not every speaker is an invited speaker, so Invited Speaker is strictly narrower and is subsumed by Speaker.

A's 'Personal History' is a container class whose children are Personal Publication History and Personal Review History, i.e. a record of a person's activities. B's 'Review' is a subclass of Document, a specific document artefact produced in the reviewing process. The two denote different concepts (a history/record vs. a review document), so they are unrelated.

A's Tutorial is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation given at a conference), while B's Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. They belong to different branches (Event vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Abstract' is a document type (a short version of a paper, sibling of 'Paper Full Version' under 'Paper'), while B's 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject-area category under 'Topic'. They denote different kinds of things (a document vs. a topic), so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of conference event such as tutorial/workshop), while B's Introduction of speaker is a conference activity (a sub-activity of Introduction). They denote different concepts: an event type vs. a speaker-introduction activity, with no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a generic place type for meeting rooms, while B 'Conference building' is a specific building type (a subclass of Building) that hosts conference activities and has Delegate as a child. They overlap in that conference buildings contain meeting rooms, but neither subsumes the other: a meeting room is not a building, and a conference building is not a meeting room. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

Both denote the decision/activity of rejecting a submitted manuscript: cmt's Rejection is a subclass of Decision (sibling of Acceptance), and iasted's Refusing manuscript is an activity before the conference (sibling of Accepting manuscript). Same intended concept, differing only in classification as decision vs. activity.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/submission), while B's 'providedBy' relates a Sponsorship to an Organization (sponsor funding). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'was a committee of' relates a Committee to a Conference volume (a committee is part of a conference), while B's 'part Of Event' relates an Event to a broader Event (mereological parthood between events). Different domains/ranges and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Workshop is a scientific event (sibling of Conference). They denote different event types: a conference is not a workshop. Although both are events, neither subsumes the other in the intended domain, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Company is a subclass of Organization (path Organization > Company), with sibling University. In the Conference ontology, Organization is the general class covering companies, universities, etc. Thus Company is strictly more specific than Organization: Company is subsumed by Organization, not equivalent.
Author in cmt is a conference member who writes/submits papers, while Student in ekaw is a person role unrelated to authorship; the ekaw counterpart of Author is Paper Author, not Student.

A's 'has Conference Member' links a Conference to its members (domain Conference, range Conference Member). B's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to the people who initiated it (domain Call, range Conference Chair/Session Chair/TPC Member). Different domains (Conference vs Call), different ranges (Conference Member vs specific chair/member roles), and different intended meaning (membership vs initiation). They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Accepted Paper is a paper in an accepted state (sibling of Rejected/Pending/Published Paper, related to a Paper Presentation), whereas Award is a prize given to authors (with children Best Research Paper Award etc. and properties award/awarded by/obtain). They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Program Committee Chair' is a specific chair role (a kind of Program Committee Member who chairs the PC), while B's 'Chair' is the general committee-chair role (parent of 'Co chair', with properties linking Chair to Committee). The PC Chair is a specialization of the generic Chair, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a conference part alongside Track and Workshop, i.e. a type of event/session in the conference programme. B's Plenary lecture is a subclass of Lecture, a kind of talk given at the conference, and its sibling is Tutorial (a different concept in iasted). The two entities denote different things: a tutorial event vs. a plenary lecture talk. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference/Conference Event and range dateTime, denoting the start date-time of a conference event; the labels 'has Start Date Time' and 'Start of conference' refer to the same relation.

A's Paper is a conference submission (has authors, reviews, decisions, subject areas), while B's Transparency is a document artefact (a transparency/slide document) under Item > Document, sibling to Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc. They share no intended instances.

A is a University (an academic organization, sibling of Company, domain of 'study At'), while B is a Departure tax (a kind of Tax under Money). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain and share no meaning.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document type (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an announcement about a conference. B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with dates, country, members, topics and deadlines. The two denote different kinds of things (document vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Active Paper' is a specific state of a Paper (a document under review, with a rating), while B's 'Document' is a broad top-level artefact class whose children include forms, invitations, mailing lists, payments and reviews. 'Active Paper' is a kind of Paper/Document, but 'Document' is far more general and covers many non-paper artefacts, so the two do not denote the same concept.

cmt:User is a general person role in the conference organisation (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer, and sibling of Chairman, PC Member, etc.), i.e. a participant in the conference process. sigkdd:Listener is a specific attendee role (sibling of Organizator and Speaker) in a different role taxonomy. The intended instances do not coincide: a User need not be a Listener, and a Listener is a specific audience role, not the general User concept. Hence unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip), while B's Presentation is a conference activity (a talk, with children Power Point presentation and Video presentation). They denote different concepts: a social gathering versus a presentation/lecture.

Both classes denote a workshop as a conference-domain event/part. In Conference, Workshop is a kind of Conference part alongside Track and Tutorial, and is the range of 'has workshops' (Conference volume -> Workshop). In ekaw, Workshop is a Scientific Event alongside Conference, Session, Track, etc. The intended instances coincide: a workshop is a scientific event held as part of a conference. Same label and compatible context support equivalence.

A 'Personal Publication History' is a record of an author's own publications (a subclass of Personal History, sibling of Personal Review History), while B 'Sponzorship' is a financial category under Money (sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip). They share no concept, properties, or domain role; the only overlap is the word 'history'/'sponsorship' being unrelated, so they are unrelated.

Both denote the full-length version of a paper submitted to a conference: cmt's 'Paper Full Version' is the complete paper (sibling of 'Paper Abstract'), and Conference's 'Extended abstract' is a regular contribution that is the full paper (its child 'Abstract' is the short version, sibling 'Paper'). The intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

A's hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event (part/whole or containment within the event hierarchy), while B's is_made_from relates an Item to an Item (composition/material relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence.

A's Paper is a conference submission (has authors, reviewers, decisions, subject areas), while B's Programme Brochure is a published document listing events, sibling to Paper in ekaw. Different concepts despite both being Documents.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Early Registered Participant is a person role (a subclass of Conference Participant, sibling of Late Registered Participant and various chairs). They belong to disjoint branches (event vs. person) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties giving the start time of an event/conference event; 'starts on' with range string and 'has Start Date Time' with range dateTime denote the same relation (start time of an event), differing only in the literal datatype used, which is a representation detail rather than a conceptual difference.

A's Workshop is a small event type that is a part of a conference (sibling of Track and Tutorial, linked via 'has workshops' from Conference volume), whereas B's Conference is the top-level working event that contains Workshop and Tutorial as siblings. They denote different concepts: one is a component event, the other is the whole event, so they are not equivalent.
A's title is the title of a Paper; B's hasCity is the city of a Contact Information. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'end Date' is a datatype property giving the end date/time of a Conference (domain Conference, range dateTime). B's 'is dated on' is a datatype property giving the date of an Activity (domain Activity, range dateTime). Both relate an event-like entity to a dateTime, but A specifically denotes the end of a conference while B denotes a general dating relation for any activity; they overlap in the conference domain but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

In ekaw, Presenter is a broad role for any conference participant who presents, with Invited Speaker as a narrower child. In sigkdd, Invited Speaker is a specific kind of Speaker (sibling of Author). The ekaw Presenter is more general than the sigkdd Invited Speaker, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A's property links a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference (a qualification of the reviewer), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they produce/present. Different domain (Reviewer vs Person) and different range (Review expertise/preference vs Activity/Item), and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is occupied by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a location is occupied by a person), while B's 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee (a person pays a fee). The domains, ranges, and directions differ completely, so the two properties are unrelated.

A's Conference Event is a broad event entity (parent of Academic/Non Academic Event, with attendees, programme, location, start/end times), while B's Conference Session is a specific kind of Session within Scientific Event (sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session). A conference session is a part/kind of conference event, but the two classes are not coextensive: A covers whole conferences and academic/non-academic events, B covers only sessions. Hence they overlap but are not equivalent.

A Conference Chair is a specific organizational role (chair of the conference, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in cmt, while B Passive conference participant is a generic attendee who does not actively contribute (sibling of Active conference participant) in the Conference ontology. The role of chairing a conference is an active organizational function, not a passive participation role, so the two classes do not denote the same concept and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Signal Processing Topic' is a research topic (a subclass of Topic in edas), while B 'Program Committee' is a committee (a subclass of Committee in sigkdd). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while B's 'has Reviewer' links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (reviewing relation). They relate different kinds of entities in different roles and directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. a written artefact. B's 'Welcome address' is a conference activity (sibling of Lecture, Registration, Coffee break), i.e. an event. Different kinds and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Early Registered Participant' is a Conference Participant distinguished by registration timing (sibling of Late Registered Participant), while B's 'Program Committee member' is an Organizator role (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). Different parents (Conference Participant vs Organizator) and different distinguishing criteria; the concepts do not coincide.

Both are classes named Paper under Document in the conference domain, with matching roles: cmt Paper has authors, reviewers, decisions, subject areas; edas Paper has authors, reviewers, topics, and paper statuses. The intended instances (submitted contributions) coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's hasCo-author relates a Paper to its Co-author (domain Paper, range Co author), while B's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'is a full paper submission date' is a specific deadline (the full-paper submission date) within the 'Important dates' class, while B's 'Date' is the generic date property of any 'Deadline'. The generic Deadline/Date relation subsumes the specific full-paper submission date, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings with range string, identifying a publication by ISBN. B's 'has title' is a datatype property of Social event and Working event with range string, giving the title of an event. Different domains (proceedings vs events) and different intended relations (ISBN identifier vs title), so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the event itself (has a name, has a Conference volume, has Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic), while B's Building is a physical Place (subclass of Place, with children like Conference airport, Conference hotel, Conference restaurant, and properties is occupied by / is situated in / is visited by). A conference is not a building; the shared word 'Conference' in B's children refers to buildings used by a conference, not the event. The two classes denote different concepts.

In cmt, Administrator is a User (a system role) with administrative powers over the conference (accepting papers, assigning reviewers, entering conference details). In confOf, Member PC is a Person whose comment is 'Reviewer' and whose properties are expert On Topic and reviewes Contribution, i.e. a program-committee reviewer. The two denote different roles: an administrative user vs. a PC reviewer. They are siblings under Person in confOf but that does not make them equivalent, and the cmt Administrator's properties (accept Paper, assign Reviewer, enter Conference Details) do not match the reviewer role of Member PC.

A is a research topic (Cryptography Topic) under Topic, while B is an award category (Best Applications Paper Award) under Award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

Paper in cmt is a conference submission/document with authors, reviews, decisions; Money in iasted is a monetary amount with fees, taxes, payments. Completely different concepts despite no shared context.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad class covering all people taking part in a conference (its children are Active/Passive conference participant, and its siblings include Committee member, Reviewer, etc.). B's 'Program Chair' is a specific organizational role under Organizator, sibling to General Chair and Program Committee member. A participant is not the same concept as a program chair; the program chair is a specific organizer role, not a general participant category. They are unrelated (or at most the chair is a kind of participant, but the ontologies place them in different hierarchies and the intended instances do not coincide).

A is a research topic area in the EDAS subject taxonomy (sibling of CAD Topic, Communication Theory Topic, etc.), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (sibling of LCD projector, Overhead projector) in the iasted ontology. They share only the word 'computer' and denote entirely different concepts.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Conference Paper' is a scholarly paper submitted/published at a conference. They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'paper'.

Associated Chair (cmt) is a chair role in the conference organisation, a sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair under Chairman. Late Registered Participant (ekaw) is a conference participant distinguished by registration timing, a sibling of Early Registered Participant under Conference Participant. The two denote different concepts (organisational role vs. registration status) with no overlap in intended instances.

A's 'Published Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been published), while B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a subclass of Deadline (a submission deadline event). They denote different kinds of things (document vs. deadline) and are not equivalent.

A Program Committee in cmt is a group of reviewers with members (Program Committee Member), whereas ekaw's Organisation is an organising body (academic institution, agency, publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings. The intended instances do not coincide: a program committee is not an organisation in the ekaw sense, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a document submitted to a conference (a subclass of Conference document, with children like Poster, Presentation, Regular contribution), whereas B's 'Conference' is a working event (a subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). The two denote different kinds of things (a paper/contribution vs. an event), so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the conference event itself (has members, topics, deadlines, related documents). B's Conference city is a subclass of City describing the city in which a conference takes place, a location concept, not the event. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

Both denote the person who chairs a conference session: confOf's Chair PC is a Person role (comment 'confTool'), and iasted's Session chair is a Delegate role whose label explicitly names the session-chairing function. The differing parent (Person vs Delegate) reflects the ontologies' different role hierarchies, not a different concept; both are the session-chair role.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (membership of people in a conference), while B's has Part is a generic mereological/part-whole property with unspecified domain and range. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Programme Brochure is a Document (a physical/informational artefact, sibling of Paper, Review, Flyer). They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Document) and share no properties or intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (submission act), while B's is held before relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Signal Processing Topic' is a subject area of papers in the EDAS topic taxonomy, while a 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of individual presentation event in EKAW. They belong to entirely different branches (topic vs. event) and denote different concepts.

A's Participant is a Person subclass (a conference attendee role, with children Member/Regular/Student and property early Registration), while B's entity is a specific Registration fee (a Money subclass, sibling of Member/Nonmember/Student registration fees). They denote different concepts (person role vs. monetary fee), so they are unrelated.

A's 'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' is an Administrator->Conference action for producing hardcopy mailing manifests, while B's 'relates To' is a generic Document->(Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person) association. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Social Event' is a subclass of Event (a social gathering such as a banquet or trip), while B's 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person (a person who organises the conference, with children like General Chair and Webmaster). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Person) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with range date, but A's `date` is a general date of a Conference, while B's `is a starting date` is specifically the start date of an Important dates entity. They overlap in that both express a date, but they are not the same relation: A is more general and B is a specific starting date, so they are related rather than equivalent.

confOf's City is a specific kind of place (a city where an organization or person is located), while ekaw's Location is a general place where an event is held. City is narrower than Location, so City is subsumed by Location rather than equivalent.

Both are object properties linking a committee member to the committee they belong to: cmt's 'member Of Conference' has domain Conference Member and range Conference, while Conference's 'was a member of' has domain Committee member and range Committee. Conference Member/Committee member and Conference/Committee are the corresponding classes in the two ontologies, so the properties denote the same relation in the same direction.

Both Document classes are the general superclass of the same conference artefacts: edas Document has children Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, Meal Menu; sigkdd Document has children Abstract, Paper, Review. Both are the broad 'document' concept in the conference domain, with properties linking documents to people/events (edas: relates To / has Related Document; sigkdd: presentation / presentationed by / submit until). The intended instances coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

TPC Member is a person role (a kind of Person who reviews papers and initiates calls), while Registration fee is a fee category with price/currency and payment relations. They belong to different branches (Person vs Fee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A Program Committee Member is a conference member who reviews papers and belongs to a Program Committee (with properties like member Of Program Committee, max Papers). B Speaker is a Delegate who presents at the conference, with children Author and Reviewer. The two concepts denote different roles in the conference domain; a PC member is not necessarily a speaker and a speaker is not necessarily a PC member. Their paths, siblings and properties do not align, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link an abstract/paper to a presentation, but they are not the same relation: 'is the 1th part of' is a general part-of relation from an Abstract to Paper, Poster, or Presentation, while 'paper Presented As' specifically relates an Abstract/Paper to an Individual Presentation. The ranges differ (Paper/Poster/Presentation vs Individual Presentation) and the direction/intent differ, so they overlap but are not equivalent.

Administrator in cmt is a system/organisational role (a User who manages the conference: accepts papers, assigns reviewers, enters conference details, enables virtual meetings). Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a person who may review a paper (has Reviewer, review Written By, reviewer Of Paper), and is a superclass of PC Member. The two denote different concepts: one is an administrative user role, the other a reviewing-capable person. They share no intended instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

A's 'Personal Publication History' is a class under Personal History describing a person's record of publications; B's 'Review' is a document type (a review of a paper) under Document. They denote different concepts: one is a history/record of publications, the other is a review document. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

A is a registration-status subclass of Conference Participant (early vs late registration), while B is a speaker role subclass of Author in iasted. Different concepts: registration timing vs tutorial-speaking role; no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Conference contribution' is a document submitted to a conference (a subclass of Conference document, with children like Poster, Presentation, Written contribution, and properties linking it to a Conference volume). B 'Tax' is a monetary charge (subclass of Money, with children Departure tax and Value added tax). The two concepts belong to entirely different domains and share no intended instances.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a member of the organising committee who chairs the conference), while B 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of scientific event/presentation. They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Proceedings' is a document (a published multi-author volume of papers), while B 'Conference activity' is an event/activity (with children like Coffee break, Lecture, Registration). They denote different kinds of things (publication vs. event), so they are unrelated.

Both properties link an author/person to the paper/document they produce: cmt's write Paper has domain Author and range Paper, while Conference's contributes has domain Person and range Conference document. Author and Person denote the same role, and Paper and Conference document denote the same artefact, so the two object properties relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are equivalent.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track parts (a whole-part relation within a conference), while B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference it holds (an organisational hosting relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasCostCurrency is a datatype property linking a Sponsorship to a string currency code, while B's is_paid_for is an object property linking Money to an Activity or Item. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Sponsorship vs Money), and range (string vs Activity/Item), so they denote different relations.

Country in confOf is a geographical entity used as the range of has Country (Organization, Person -> Country), i.e. the nation an organization or person belongs to. Research Topic in ekaw is a subject area covered by events and papers (covers Topic / topic Covered By). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances or properties, so they are unrelated.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members (people), while B's listsEvent links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to the events it lists. Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same property.

Chairman in cmt is a specific role (a person who chairs, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), whereas Committee member in Conference is the broader class of anyone belonging to a committee, with Chair and Co chair as its subclasses. A chairman is a committee member, but not every committee member is a chairman, so Chairman is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Committee member.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's writtenBy is an object property mapping a Document to a Person (the author of a document). They differ in domain (Person vs Document), range (string vs Person), and direction of relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title (range string), while B's is a starting date is a datatype property of Important dates giving a date. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they are unrelated.

A's 'is a starting date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date literal (a temporal attribute of a deadline/event). B's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location (a spatial relation). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), in domain (Important dates vs Event) and in range (date literal vs Location), so they denote different relations.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a submission type, sibling of Paper under Regular contribution), while B's 'Best Research Paper Award' is a type of Award (an honour given to a paper). They denote different concepts in the conference domain: one is a document/submission category, the other an award category. No subsumption or overlap holds.

A 'Written contribution' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a paper-like artefact, with children Regular contribution and Submitted contribution), whereas B 'Author' is a person role (a subclass of Person, with child Presenter and siblings Attendee, Reviewer, TPC Member). They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author; B's is_used_by relates an Item to a Person. Both connect a document-like artefact to a person, but the intended relations differ: authorship vs. usage, and the domains/ranges (Paper/Author vs Item/Person) are not the same concepts. They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both classes denote a conference as a kind of event: confOf places Conference under Working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop, while ekaw places Conference under Scientific Event with the comment 'One edition of a conference'. The intended instances (conference events) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite differing parent paths.

A is a research topic (a subject area under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is an award category (a kind of Award, sibling of Best Student Paper Award). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain and share no instances.

Acceptance is a subclass of Decision (the outcome of a review decision, sibling of Rejection), while Speaker is a subclass of Person (a person who gives a presentation, with children Author and Invited Speaker). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a specific role class (the first author of a contribution), a subclass of 'Regular author' within the Conference contribution branch. B's 'Author' is the general class of persons who write papers, with subclasses 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student'. A first author is a kind of author, so the specific role is subsumed by the general Author class; they are not equivalent because Author covers all authors, not just first authors of contributions.

Both classes denote a paper that has been accepted (edas: Accepted Paper under Paper, sibling of Rejected/Published Paper; ekaw: Accepted Paper under Evaluated Paper, sibling of Rejected Paper, comment 'Accepted paper to become part of proceedings'). Same intended instances in the conference domain, so equivalent.

Both properties link a paper-like entity (Paper / Item) to a person (Author / Person) in the same direction, expressing authorship. The iasted property is broader in domain (Activity, Item) but the shared intended meaning for the paper-author relation is the same, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Workshop is a kind of working event (a conference-organisation event such as Conference or Tutorial), while B's Radio Communications Topic is a subject area/topic in the EDAS taxonomy. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Topic in edas is a subject area of papers/conferences (children like Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic), while Award in sigkdd is a prize given to authors/papers (children Best Research Paper Award etc.). They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a numeric (int) property of a Conference giving the number of reviews per paper, while B's 'has Name' is a string property giving the conference's full name. They share only the domain (Conference) but have different ranges and completely different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Extended abstract (Conference) is a kind of regular contribution/document, a short paper variant. Assigned Paper (ekaw) is a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer, a workflow state of a submission. Their intended instances do not coincide: one is a document type, the other a review-process state, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Memeber registration fee' is a specific kind of registration fee (a member's fee), a sibling of nonmember, student, author, nonauthor fees under 'Registration fee'. B's 'Registration fee' is the general class with children for member/non-member/student registrations. Thus A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's Slide Set is a presentation artefact (sibling of Paper, Review, Programme under Document), while B's Review is the evaluation document of a paper. They denote different concepts despite both being Documents.

A's Conference is an event class (has dates, country, members, topics, deadlines), while B's Conference Proceedings is a document class (a Proceedings volume containing papers). They denote different kinds of things: an event vs. a publication, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Medicine Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in edas, while B 'Best Research Paper Award' is a type of award under Award in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different branches (topic vs. award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties named 'has Phone' with range string, but their domains differ: confOf attaches the phone to a Person, while edas attaches it to a Contact Information entity. They denote the same kind of relation (an entity's phone number) but are not equivalent because the domain classes are not the same concept; they overlap in intent without coinciding, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with a two-level programme committee structure), while B 'Late Registered Participant' is a kind of person (a conference participant who registered late). Their intended instances are disjoint (events vs. people), so they are unrelated despite both appearing in the conference domain.
submit Paper goes Author -> Paper, while is Written By goes Paper -> Author. They are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

confOf's Working event is a broad category of events that includes Conference, Tutorial and Workshop (its children), i.e. any event with a working/professional purpose. edas's Talk Event is a narrower academic event (parent Academic Event) whose children are Closing Talk and Welcome Talk, i.e. a specific kind of talk/presentation session. A Working event is not a Talk Event; rather, a Talk Event (as an academic event) would fall under the broader Working event category. Hence Working event subsumes Talk Event, not equivalence.

A's `writes` goes Author -> Contribution (an author writes a paper/contribution). B's `is sent by` goes Item -> Person (an item is sent by a person), which is the inverse direction and relates a submitted item to its sender, not an author to a paper. Different domain/range and opposite direction, so they are not equivalent.

ekaw's hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event (domain and range both Event), while sigkdd's award relates something to an Award. Different domains/ranges and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a short summary document that is part of a paper (sibling of 'Paper Full Version' under 'Paper'), whereas B 'Cd proceening' is a CD-ROM publication medium (sibling of 'Book proceeding' under 'Publication').
