They denote different concepts: a document type versus a publication format, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's 'related To Event' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (the event at which it is presented). The domains differ (Paper vs Accepted Paper) and, more decisively, the ranges denote different kinds of entities (a person/administrator vs an event/presentation), so the two properties do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property from Conference volume to a string literal, while B's 'location Of' is an object property from Location to Event. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and direction, so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'abstract' is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its textual abstract (string), while B's 'Date' links a Deadline to a dateTime. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

Paper Full Version (cmt) is the complete version of a paper, sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper. Industrial Paper (ekaw) is a paper type for industry contributions, sibling of Regular Paper, Conference Paper, etc. They denote different concepts: one is a completeness/version distinction, the other a submission category. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

iasted:Activity is a broad event/action class (children: Activity before/after conference, Conference activity; it is given by persons, held in places, dated, paid for), whereas sigkdd:Deadline is a specific submission/notification deadline with a Date and a submit-until relation to a Document. A deadline is a kind of time point, not an activity, and the two classes have disjoint instances; they are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A 'Cryptography Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in edas, while B 'Tutorial Abstract' is a document type (an abstract of a tutorial) under Abstract in ekaw. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

In confOf, University is a subclass of Organization (path Organization > University), so University is a narrower concept than the general Organization class in the Conference ontology. They are not equivalent; University is subsumed by Organization.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution to a paper), while B's 'occupy' relates a Person to a Building, City or State (physical location/occupancy). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

confOf's 'follows' relates two Administrative events (an event ordering relation between events), while iasted's 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of an activity relative to a time point). Different domain and range kinds, so the relations are not equivalent.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it, while B's 'is paid by' links Money to the Person who pays it. Different domains (Sponsorship vs Money), different ranges (Organization vs Person), and different intended meanings (sponsorship provision vs payment), so they are not equivalent.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the cmt ontology), while B is a research activity (Simulating, a subclass of Research under 'Activity before conference' in iasted). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (people vs. activities) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Flyer is a promotional document (sibling of Programme Brochure, Web Site, Multi author Volume) that an Organisation publishes; Paper is a scholarly contribution submitted by an Author. Different intended instances and different properties, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Rejected contribution' is a final, terminal state of a reviewed contribution (sibling of Accepted contribution, under Reviewed contribution). B's 'Active Paper' is a paper still in the review process (parent of Rated Papers, sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Pending/Published/Withdrawn Paper) — it is the in-progress category, not the rejected outcome. B's actual counterpart to A is 'Rejected Paper', so the two entities denote different concepts.

A's Industry Organization is a subtype of Organization denoting a for-profit company (siblings: Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO). B's Proceedings Publisher is a subtype of Organisation denoting the entity that publishes conference proceedings (siblings: Academic Institution, Organising Agency). A commercial company and a proceedings publisher are different concepts; a publisher may be an organisation but not specifically an industry organisation, and an industry organisation need not publish proceedings. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A Volunteer is a generic Person subtype (sibling of Participant, Author, etc.) in confOf, while B Organizing Committee member is a specific Organizator role (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster) in sigkdd. A volunteer is not necessarily an organizing committee member and vice versa; the concepts denote different roles in the conference domain.

University is an academic organization (a subclass of Organization, sibling of Company, and the range of 'study At' from Scholar), whereas Tip is a monetary payment (a subclass of Money, sibling of Fee, Sponsorship and Tax). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, choices), while B 'Radio Communications Topic' is a subclass of Topic, a subject area. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Topic) and denote different concepts.

A's 'belong to a conference volume' links an Important dates entity to a Conference volume (a publication/volume), while B's 'hold' links an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Conference (an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's Dining Place is a subclass of Place (a physical location where dining occurs), while B's Conference Banquet is a subclass of Social Event (an event/activity). They belong to different top-level categories (place vs. event) and are not the same concept; at most they are loosely related by the banquet taking place at a dining location, but not equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a conference part sibling to Track and Workshop, while B's Workshop is a scientific event sibling to Conference, Session and Track. Although both are event-like, Tutorial and Workshop are distinct kinds of conference events; a reference alignment would not equate them.

Both classes are named Paper, sit directly under Document, and represent the same conference-domain concept: a written contribution that is authored, reviewed, and presented. Their children (Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper vs. Submitted/Camera Ready/Regular Paper) are just different lifecycle/type subdivisions of the same class, and their properties (is Written By / has Reviewer / covers Topic) describe the same role in the domain. The shared path Document > Paper and matching sibling context (Review, Programme) confirm equivalence.

A is a subclass of Paper (an abstract document), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (overhead projector). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a topic they are expert in (domain Member PC, range Topic). B's 'topic Covered By' relates a research topic to the events/papers that cover it (domain Research Topic, range Event/Paper). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings differ; they are not the same relation nor inverses.

A 'Workshop Paper' is a specific kind of Paper (a document submitted to a workshop), while B 'Abstract' is a distinct document type (a summary of a paper), sibling of Paper and Review in sigkdd. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.) aimed at informing attendees, whereas B's 'Conference Paper' is a scholarly paper submitted/published at a conference (sibling of Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, etc.). They denote different concepts despite both being documents.

Organizer in the Conference ontology denotes a person/role that organises the conference, whereas Organization in confOf denotes an institution (with children Company and University, and address properties such as has City, has Country, employed By). The two classes have different intended instances (a person vs. an institution), so they are not equivalent.

confOf Participant is a general person role (parent of Member, Regular, Student, Author, Chair PC, etc.) with property early Registration; ekaw PC Member is a specific reviewer role under Possible Reviewer with children PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc. PC Member is a specialization of a conference participant, not the same concept, and neither subsumes the other in the intended alignment (Participant is broader but not a direct superclass of PC Member in ekaw's hierarchy).

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (sessions scheduled in parallel), while edas's 'relates To' relates a Document to events/persons it concerns. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a kind of Contribution (a submitted document, sibling of Poster and Short paper), while B's Best Student Paper Supporter is a sponsorship category under Sponzor (sibling of Gold/Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor). They share only the word 'Paper' and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Individual Presentation' is a scientific event (a talk/presentation event with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial, and properties linking it to papers). B's 'Time' is a temporal entity (parent of Conference days, Deadline, Trip day; used as range of temporal relations like is held before/after). They denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Tutorial is a type of conference event/session (sibling of Track and Workshop, part of a Conference), while an LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (sibling of Computer and Overhead projector). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'was a steering committee of' relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume (organisational body -> event), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (person -> paper). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both classes denote the conference event itself: cmt's Conference has conference-level attributes (dates, administrators, members, submissions) and edas's Conference is the central event class with dates, members, topics and papers. Same intended instances, so equivalent.
A's Poster is a kind of Contribution (a paper/poster submission), while B's Mailing list is a Document used for communication; different concepts with no overlap.

confOf's Participant is a general person role (parent of Member, Regular, Student; has early Registration property), while edas's TPC Member is a program-committee member role (parent of Two Level Conference; involved in paper review and call initiation). They denote different conference roles and are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a human role: authors, speakers, participants), while B's 'Conference state' is a subclass of State (a status/condition of a conference, sibling to Presenter state and Sponsor state). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. state) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that announces a conference. B 'Organising Agency' is an organisation (subclass of Organisation, sibling of Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher) that organises a conference. A document and an organisation are different kinds of entities with no overlap, so the classes are unrelated.

Registration in iasted is a conference activity (an event during the conference, with Delegate as a child), whereas Committee in sigkdd is an organizational body with subcommittees (Best Paper Awards, Organizing, Program). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them; B's 'parallel with' links two Administrative events that run in parallel. Different domain, range and meaning, so the properties are unrelated.

Conference Chair is a person role in the conference committee hierarchy (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while Government Organization is a type of organization (a subclass of Organization). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person role vs. organization type) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class representing a reviewer's expertise/preference record, linked to Reviewer, Review preference, and Submitted contribution. B's 'Possible Reviewer' is a subclass of Person (a role a person can play, with PC Member as a child) linked to Paper and Review. The two denote different concepts: an expertise record vs. a person role, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a kind of conference event with a two-tier structure), while B's 'Sponsor state' is a subclass of State (a status/state in the conference process, sibling of Conference state and Presenter state). They belong to different branches of the domain (event type vs. state) and share no intended instances.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), i.e. the result of a paper being rejected. B's Accept Rating is a review rating value (sibling of Reject Rating, Week Reject Rating under Review Rating), i.e. a score given by a reviewer. They denote different concepts in different branches of the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to a Contribution (a review action), while B's `is used for` relates an Item to an Activity or Money (a resource-usage relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

In cmt, Document is a general class whose children are Paper and Review (scientific contributions). In iasted, Form is a subclass of Document and denotes administrative forms (registration, hotel, author information). Although both sit under a 'Document' node, the intended instances differ: cmt's Document covers papers/reviews, iasted's Form covers administrative paperwork. They are not the same concept.

A's 'Co chair' is a committee member role (sibling of Chair) tied to committees via 'has a committee co chair' / 'was a committe co chair of'. B's 'Program Chair' is an organizer role (sibling of General Chair, Program Committee member, etc.) in the sigkdd ontology. Both denote a chairing role in conference organization, but they are not the same concept: 'Co chair' is a generic committee co-chair, while 'Program Chair' is a specific organizer role for the program. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. a written announcement about the conference. B 'Plenary lecture' is a kind of conference activity/lecture (subclass of Lecture, sibling of Session and Tutorial), i.e. an event held at the conference. A document and an event are different kinds of things, so the classes are unrelated.

In confOf, Company is a subclass of Organization (a legal/organisational entity, sibling of University). In iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person (an individual, sibling of Delegate). A company is an organisation, not a person, and a sponsor is a person role; the two classes have different intended instances and different superclasses, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes are named Person and represent the same general concept of a human in the conference domain. In cmt, Person is the superclass of roles like Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, and User, with properties email, name, and has Conflict Of Interest. In Conference, Person is the superclass of roles like Committee member, Conference applicant, Conference contributor, Conference participant, Reviewer, and Track workshop chair, with properties contributes, has an email, has authors, has gender, has the first name, and has the last name. The differing role subclasses and property names reflect ontology-specific modeling choices, but the intended instances (people involved in conferences) coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

In cmt, Document is a general class whose children are Paper and Review, i.e. written conference artefacts. In iasted, Item is a very broad class covering physical/abstract things (Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle) with properties like 'is made from', 'is paid with', 'is equipped by'. Document in iasted is only one child of Item, so cmt:Document is narrower than iasted:Item; the two do not denote the same concept.

A's 'was a committe co chair of' is a specific sub-property of 'was a member of' (its parent), linking a Co chair to a Committee. B's 'is Member Of' is a general membership property linking a Person to a Conference. A's property is strictly more specific than B's general membership relation, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment relation), while B's 'is made from' relates an Item to another Item (composition/material relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's reject Paper relates an Administrator to a Paper (a decision action), while B's written By relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; not equivalent nor inverse.

A's 'Technical commitee' is a subclass of Delegate (a conference participant role), while B's 'Organizing Committee member' is a subclass of Organizator (an organizer role). Both denote committee membership in the conference domain, but they sit in different branches (participant vs organizer) and are not the same concept; they overlap only loosely, so 'related' is the safest non-equivalent verdict.

A's 'Author book proceedings included' is a very specific subclass of Author (an author whose book is included in the proceedings), sitting under Author in the iasted hierarchy. B's 'Author' is the general class of authors. The specific A concept is strictly narrower than B's general Author, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

Conference volume is a conference event/proceedings entity with committees, tracks, contributions and dates, while Conference city is a subclass of City describing a location (the city where a conference takes place). They denote different concepts and are not related by subsumption or overlap.

has Country relates an Organization or Person to a Country (nationality/affiliation), while is situated in relates a Building, City or Place to a Building, City, Place or State (spatial containment). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the intended meanings differ, so the properties are not equivalent.

cmt:Conference Member is a general person role in a conference (parent of Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while iasted:Delegate is a participant/attendee role under Conference building with children like Speaker, Listener, Session chair. They overlap in that both denote conference participants, but Conference Member is broader (includes organisers/chairs) and Delegate is more attendee-focused, so they are related rather than equivalent.

In edas, 'Industry Organization' is a subclass of 'Organization' (path: Organization > Industry Organization), so it is strictly more specific than the Conference ontology's general 'Organization' class. The two do not denote the same concept; the edas class is subsumed by the broader Conference class.

A's Review is a subclass of Document (a review document written by a reviewer about a paper), while B's Paper is a subclass of Document denoting the submitted/published paper itself. In ekaw, Review is a separate sibling class of Paper, and Paper has properties like has Review, review Of Paper, paper Presented As, which confirm Paper is the reviewed artefact, not the review. The two classes denote different concepts (review vs. paper), so they are unrelated.

A's 'virtual Meeting Enabled By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables virtual meetings), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives something). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Paper is the general document class for all conference papers (parents Document, children Accepted/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), while B's Industrial Paper is a specific kind of Paper (parent Paper, siblings Regular Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). The general Paper subsumes the specific Industrial Paper, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Invited speaker' is a person role (a kind of Conference contributor/Person), while B 'Sponsor city' is a kind of City (a location). They denote different concepts with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

Committee member is a subclass of Person in Conference (path Person > Committee member), while sigkdd's Person is the general superclass of all conference attendees (Listener, Organizator, Speaker). A committee member is a person, but not every person is a committee member, so Committee member is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Person.

Both properties are datatype properties with domain 'Important dates'/'Deadline' and range 'date', but their labels and intended meanings differ: 'is a starting date' marks the beginning of an event, while 'done till' likely marks a deadline or end date. They are related (both temporal properties) but not equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad class covering all people taking part in a conference (its children include Active/Passive conference participant, and siblings include Committee member, Reviewer, etc.). B's 'OC Chair' is a specific role: the chair of the Organising Committee, a subclass of OC Member, itself a subclass of Conference Participant. Thus every OC Chair is a conference participant, but not vice versa; A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B (B is subsumed_by A). They are not equivalent.

A's 'has important dates' is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity (a container of multiple deadlines), while B's 'End of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a single dateTime value. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain, and range, and denote different concepts (a set of important dates vs the conference end date), so they are not equivalent.

Attendee in edas is a general Person role (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles) covering anyone attending the conference, while Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a specific kind of Speaker (a distinguished presenter). An invited speaker may attend, but the classes are not coextensive; Attendee is far broader and the two are not in a subsumption relation in the intended domain.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection, child of Decision) denoting the state/result of a paper being accepted. B's Accepting manuscript is an activity in the conference workflow (sibling of Receiving/Refusing manuscript), denoting the process of accepting a manuscript. They are conceptually linked (the activity produces the decision) but not the same entity: one is a decision state, the other an activity.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chairing role within the conference/committee structure (sibling of Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair), whereas Webmaster (sigkdd) is a technical organizing role under Organizator, sibling of General Chair and Program Chair. They denote different roles in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

EDAS 'Published Paper' is a paper that has appeared in proceedings, while EKAW 'Accepted Paper' is a paper accepted after evaluation but explicitly not the camera-ready/published form. They overlap (an accepted paper typically becomes published) but are not the same concept: acceptance precedes publication, and the EKAW comment distinguishes accepted from camera-ready. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to a Program committee (a committee entity), while B's 'lists Event' links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. The domains and ranges are disjoint kinds of things (committee vs. event, conference volume vs. brochure/website), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page/URL-bearing document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B's 'Conference Session' is a scientific event session (a temporal event with children like Industrial Session). They denote different kinds of things (document vs. event) and share no intended instances.

A 'Co author' is a person role (an author who co-writes a paper, sibling of 'Author Not Reviewer', domain/range of co-write/has-Co-author properties), while B 'Nonmember registration fee' is a monetary fee category under Registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts.

A's 'was a committee of' relates a Committee to a Conference volume (organisational structure), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (the authoring of a paper), while B's `is Reviewing` relates a committee role (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper (the act of reviewing). Different domains, different ranges, and different intended relations (authorship vs. reviewing), so they are not equivalent.

Program Committee (cmt) is the body of reviewers that evaluates submissions, with members and member-of relations. Steering committee (Conference) is a distinct committee that oversees the conference series, sibling to Organizing committee and Program committee. They are different committees in the conference domain, so not equivalent.

A's hasCity is a datatype property of Contact Information (the city in a contact address), while B's City_of_conference is a datatype property of Conference (the city where the conference is held). Although both yield a city string, their domains differ: one describes a contact's address, the other the conference venue location. They are not the same relation.

A's 'has been assigned a review reference' links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (a preference/assignment of a reviewer), while B's 'has Reviewer' links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (the actual reviewer). Both concern assigning reviewers to papers, but the ranges differ (Review preference vs Possible Reviewer) and the direction/intent is not identical, so they are related rather than equivalent.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair). In edas, Two Level Conference is a conference structure type (subclass of Conference, sibling of Single Level Conference, Attendee, Author). They denote different concepts: a person role vs. a conference organisation type, so they are unrelated.

A 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a kind of Author/Speaker who gives a plenary talk, while B 'Program Committee member' is an Organizator who reviews papers. They belong to different branches (Author vs Organizator) and denote different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.
A is a datatype property linking a Sponsorship to an integer cost amount; B is an object property linking a Location to an Event. Different domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Sponsor city is a kind of City (a location, sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Trip city). One denotes an event, the other a location, so they cannot be equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is a general Person role with children Active/Passive conference participant and siblings Committee member, Reviewer, etc., covering all people involved in a conference. B's 'Conference Chair' is a specific role (a chair who initiates calls and reviews papers), one of several sibling roles (Attendee, Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). A Conference Chair is a kind of conference participant, but not every conference participant is a Conference Chair, so A subsumes B.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' is an action property with domain Administrator and range Program Committee Member, i.e. it records an administrator adding someone to the PC. B's 'has Member' is a structural property with domain Conference and range Person, linking a conference to its members. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference applicant' is a Person who applies to a conference (a subclass of Person, with child Registeered applicant, siblings Committee member/Reviewer/etc.). B 'Research' is an Activity before the conference (subclass of Activity before conference, with children Modelling/Simulating). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. activity) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both are subclasses of Registration fee, but A is specifically the fee for an author who is also an attendee booking registration, while B is the registration fee for a student. They are different fee categories (author-attendee vs student) that share the same parent concept, so they overlap in the registration-fee domain but are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties mapping a person (or contact information) to an email string. The domain of B is broader (Contact Information, Person) but the intended relation — a person's email address — is the same, so they are equivalent.

A's 'Non speaker' is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference who does not present), while B's 'Registration Non Member' is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for non-members). They denote different concepts: a person role vs. a fee type, so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Conference is the top-level organisational entity (the whole conference, with administrators, submissions, review criteria, members). In iasted, Conference activity is a subclass of Activity and denotes a scheduled event within a conference (siblings include Activity before/after conference, children include Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break). The two denote different concepts: the conference as an organisation vs. an activity occurring at a conference.

A is an Accepted contribution (a reviewed, accepted paper in the submission workflow), while B is a Reception (a social event). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. event) and share no intended instances.

A's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (domain Member PC, range Topic), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (domain Conference, range Person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'has Related Document' links an event/session/person to a Document. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

confOf Contribution is a broad submission concept (children Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by Author, reviewed by PC member). ekaw Evaluated Paper is a narrower class under Assigned Paper, denoting a paper that has been evaluated. Every Evaluated Paper is a Contribution, but not every Contribution is an Evaluated Paper, so Contribution is subsumed by Evaluated Paper.

A's 'has Been Assigned' relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper the reviewer was assigned to review), while B's 'referenced In' relates a paper to the paper/venue that references it (citation relation). Different domain/range and direction of meaning; not the same relation.

A's 'Presenter state' is a state of a presenter within a State hierarchy (siblings Conference state, Sponsor state), i.e. a situational/status class, whereas B's 'Speaker' is a subclass of Person (a role-bearing agent) with children Author and Invited Speaker and properties linking to Document. The two denote different kinds of entities (state vs. person/role), so they are not equivalent.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title; B's Currency is a datatype property of Registration fee giving the fee's currency. Different domains, ranges' meaning, and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop in confOf is a working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), i.e. a type of event/meeting. In ekaw, Regular Session is a kind of Session within a Scientific Event, and Workshop Session is a separate sibling. A workshop is not a regular session; the two denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both denote a workshop event, but the paths and siblings differ: confOf's Workshop is a Working event alongside Conference and Tutorial, while edas's Workshop is a sub-event of Academic Event alongside Organizational Meeting and Paper Presentation. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent concepts in their respective hierarchies.

A's Workshop is a type of academic event (a conference session/meeting), while B's Modelling is a research activity performed before the conference, sibling of Simulating. They denote different concepts (event vs. activity) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a kind of conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational document. B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a kind of Deadline (sibling of Deadline Abstract Submission, Deadline Author notification), i.e. a temporal milestone. The two denote different concepts (document vs. deadline) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Reviewed contribution' is a Submitted contribution that has undergone review (it has children Accepted/Rejected contribution and is linked to Review via has a review/reviews). B's 'Paper' is the general document submitted by an Author (submit: Author -> Paper), sitting directly under Document alongside Abstract and Review. A reviewed contribution is a specific stage of a paper, so it is strictly narrower than the general Paper concept; hence subsumed_by rather than equivalent.

read Paper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reading/reviewing), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission). Different domains (Reviewer vs Author) and different intended relations; they are not equivalent nor inverse-equivalent in the same direction.

In iasted, Form is a general document class whose children include Author information form, Hotel registration form, and Registration form. The edas Review Form is a specific kind of form used for reviewing, so it is a narrower concept than the generic Form. Thus Review Form is subsumed by Form, not equivalent.

A's 'has an abstract' relates a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract (domain Paper, Poster, Presentation; range Abstract). B's 'presentation Of Paper' relates an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper it presents (domain Individual Presentation; range Abstract, Paper). The directions and the kinds of things related differ: A goes from the written work to its abstract, B goes from a presentation event to the paper/abstract being presented. They are not the same relation, nor inverses of one another in a way that would make them equivalent.

A is the deadline for notifying authors of acceptance decisions; B is the deadline for submitting abstracts. They are different deadlines in the conference timeline (notification vs. abstract submission), so they are not equivalent.

Both denote the fee a participant pays to register for the conference: A's 'Conference fees' and B's 'Registration fee' (a subclass of Fee with children for member/non-member/student registration and properties Price, Currency, pay/payed by). The intended instances coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.
A's has Author links a Paper to an Author, while B's has Review links a Paper to a Review. Different range (Author vs Review) and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

Committee member (Conference) denotes a person serving on a committee, with subclasses Chair/Co-chair and properties linking to Committee. Author (edas) denotes a person who writes papers, with child Presenter and properties linking to Paper. The two concepts overlap (a committee member may also be an author) but neither subsumes the other: committee membership is not authorship, and authorship is not committee membership. Hence they are related, not equivalent.

In confOf, Conference is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) under Event > Working event. In ekaw, Session is a scientific event that has Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session, Workshop Session as children, and Conference is a sibling of Session under Scientific Event. Thus ekaw's Session is a broader scientific-event category that contains conference sessions, while confOf's Conference is a specific working event; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Reviewer is a person role (a conference member who reviews papers), while Review preference is a data entity describing a reviewer's topic preferences and degree. They are different kinds of things and not equivalent.

A's memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while B's has_parts links a Conference volume to a Conference part (mereological composition). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A is 'Accepted contribution' (a contribution that passed review, sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution), while B is 'Rejected Paper' (a paper that failed evaluation, sibling of Accepted Paper). They are opposite outcomes of the review process, not the same concept; in fact A corresponds to ekaw's Accepted Paper, not Rejected Paper.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (scheduling concurrency), while B's 'has Menu' relates a Meal Event to its Meal Menu (catering). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

A's 'done till' is a datatype property of Deadline giving the date by which a deadline is finished, while B's 'End of conference' is a datatype property of Conference giving the dateTime when the conference ends. They have different domains (Deadline vs Conference) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property of Review preference with range int (a reviewer's degree of expertise/preference), while B's 'has First Name' is a datatype property of Person with range string. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a specific kind of reviewed/submitted contribution (a paper that was rejected), while B 'Paper' is the general document class (sibling of Abstract and Review, submitted by an Author). Every rejected contribution is a paper, but not every paper is a rejected contribution, so A is strictly narrower than B.

A's 'Registration fee' is the general category of registration fees (its children include member, nonmember, student, author attendee variants), while B's 'Registration SIGMOD Member' is a specific member-type registration fee sitting under B's own 'Registration fee'. A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.
Both entities represent the same conference-domain concept (cmt vs confOf), so they are aligned as equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its committee members (Conference Member), while B's hasRelatedDocument links events/sessions/persons to Documents. Different domain and range, different intended relation; not equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is the general class of all people participating in a conference (its children include Active/Passive conference participant, Reviewer, Committee member, etc.), while B's 'Tutorial Chair' is a specific role held by a conference participant (a subclass of Conference Participant in ekaw). Thus A is strictly more general than B: A subsumes B, they are not equivalent.

A's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise area), while B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference, sibling of Program Committee Chair, Author, Reviewer), while Invited Talk is a kind of scientific event/presentation (sibling of Contributed Talk and Tutorial). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a conference participant who registered/paid late. A's 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of 'Paid applicant' under 'Registeered applicant' (registered applicant), while B's 'Late Registered Participant' is a subclass of 'Conference Participant' distinguished by late registration. The intended instances coincide: a person who registered late and paid. The differing parent chains reflect different ontology structure (A splits paid applicants into early/late; B splits participants into early/late registered), but the concept is the same.

A's 'is held in' relates an Activity to a Place/Time (where an event takes place), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a document presented at a conference), while B's 'Conference' is a working event (the event itself, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). They denote different concepts: a contribution vs. an event, so they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Full Version' is the complete version of a paper (sibling of Paper Abstract, i.e. the full-text counterpart of an abstract), whereas ekaw's 'Poster Paper' is a paper accepted for poster presentation, a distinct submission category alongside Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc. They share the parent Paper but denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to a Review (the review of that paper), while B's 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (the collection of reviews that reviewer wrote). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (a whole-part containment relation between a proceedings volume and its papers). B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the act/object a speaker presents). The domains (Conference volume vs Speaker) and ranges (Conference contribution vs Document) differ, and the intended relations are different: containment of papers in a volume versus a speaker presenting a document. They are not the same relation, nor is one a generalisation of the other.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property mapping a Conference volume to a string, while B's 'has Location' is an object property mapping a Conference Event to a Place. They differ in domain, range, and kind (datatype vs object), so they do not denote the same relation.

Both are object properties from Person to a document/item, but 'contributes' specifically targets a Conference document (a paper/contribution), while 'send' targets a generic Item. They overlap in that a person sends/contributes something, but the ranges differ in specificity and the intended relations are not identical, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Workshop is a working event (a small conference-like gathering with papers and attendees), while an Invited Talk is a single individual presentation given by an invited speaker. They are different kinds of events: Workshop is a sibling of Conference and Tutorial under Working event, whereas Invited Talk is a sibling of Contributed Talk and Tutorial under Individual Presentation. No subsumption or overlap in the intended instances.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a conference submission that has undergone review (a subclass of Submitted contribution, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution, and linked to Review via has a review/reviews). B 'Personal History' is a container class for a person's publication and review history (children Personal Publication History, Personal Review History). They denote different concepts: one is a document/submission in a review state, the other is an aggregation of a person's past activities. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an Administrator action that produces/assigns papers to a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference). B's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that occur concurrently (domain and range both Administrative event). They share no meaning, direction, or argument types, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is the whole academic event (has country, members, topics, deadlines, sessions), while B's One conference day is a single day within the conference-days schedule, a part of the event rather than the event itself. Different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given by' relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (a person giving a talk), while B's 'is occupied by' relates a Building, City, or State to a Person (occupancy of a location). The domains and ranges differ fundamentally, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an Administrator->Conference action property (an administrator opens the bidding phase for a conference), while B's 'invited by' is a Reviewer->Reviewer relation (one reviewer was invited by another). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Session Chair is a Person role that initiates calls and reviews papers (sibling of Conference Chair, Reviewer, TPC Member). B's SC Member is a Steering Committee member, a subclass of PC Member, sibling of PC Chair and Session Chair — in ekaw the Session Chair is a distinct sibling class, so SC Member denotes steering-committee membership, not session chairing. Different concepts.

cmt:User is a person role in the conference domain (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while ekaw:Research Institute is an academic organisation (parent Academic Institution, sibling University). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. organisation) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines), while B's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event. The domains (Conference volume vs Programme) and ranges (Important dates vs Conference Event) are different concepts, so the two properties relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

confOf's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (an author writes a paper), while ekaw's updatedVersionOf relates a Document to another Document (a versioning relation between documents). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited talk' is a conference contribution/presentation (an event or talk given at the conference), while B's 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a document (an abstract of such a talk). They are related in that the abstract is the written form of the invited talk, but they are not the same concept: one is a contribution/presentation, the other a document/abstract.

Acceptance is a decision outcome on a paper (sibling of Rejection under Decision), while Tip is a monetary payment under Money (sibling of Fee, Sponsorship, Tax). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

A's property records the specific date on which acceptance announcements are made (a milestone in the conference timeline), while B's 'done till' records the end date of a deadline period. Although both are datatype properties with domain a dates/deadline class and range date, they denote different temporal concepts: an announcement date versus a deadline expiration date. They are not the same relation.

A is a conference topic (a subject area for papers, under Computer Networks Topic), while B is an organizational committee (a group of people organizing the conference, under Committee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

Both classes denote the same social event: a banquet held at a conference. confOf's Banquet sits under Event > Social event alongside Reception and Trip, while ekaw's Conference Banquet sits under Event > Social Event alongside Conference Trip. Same parent concept (Social event), same sibling structure, and the labels are synonymous in the conference domain.

A's 'issues' relates a Publisher to a Conference proceedings (publisher issues proceedings), while B's 'has Updated Version' relates a Document to another Document (versioning). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property linking a Review preference to an integer (degree of preference), while B's 'review Written By' is an object property linking a Review to a Possible Reviewer (the reviewer who wrote it). Different domain, range, and meaning; they are unrelated.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (the author of a paper). B's reviewWrittenBy relates a Review to a Possible Reviewer (the reviewer who wrote the review). Different domains (Paper vs Review) and different ranges (Author vs Possible Reviewer), and the relations denote different things (authorship of a paper vs authorship of a review). Although both are 'written by' relations, they are not the same relation in the conference domain.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to the Conference they belong to (membership), while B's organises relates an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise (organisation/chairing). Different domain and range concepts and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference, sibling of Program Committee Chair, Author, Reviewer), while Industrial Session is a type of conference session event. They belong to different branches (Person vs Event) and denote entirely different concepts.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a submission/review artefact), while B's hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event (e.g. a conference to its sessions). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Talk Event (edas) is an academic event such as a welcome/closing talk or paper presentation, a subclass of Academic Event. Proceedings (ekaw) is a multi-author volume document, a subclass of Multi author Volume. They denote different concepts (event vs. document) with no subsumption or overlap, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Event is a general event class with children Administrative/Social/Working event, while iasted's Conference activity is a subclass of Activity covering specific conference activities (lecture, presentation, registration, etc.). The iasted class is narrower and more specific, so confOf Event is subsumed by Conference activity rather than equivalent.

Both classes denote the same concept: a conference paper. In Conference, Paper is a Regular contribution (a kind of Conference contribution/document) with an abstract; in sigkdd, Paper is a Document that authors submit. The labels match and the surrounding context (Document/contribution, abstract, submission by authors) agrees, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Review is a document produced by a reviewer about a paper (written by Reviewer, ended by PC Chair, has Meta Review child), whereas B's Submission is a document submitted by an author (has Initial/Final manuscript children). They are different document types in the conference process, not synonyms.

A's 'remark' is a datatype property attaching a free-text string to a Contribution (a paper submission), while B's 'written By' is an object property linking a Document to a Person author. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and intended meaning, so no reference alignment would equate them.

A's Conference Event is a broad event class with children Academic Event and Non Academic Event, covering the whole conference programme (has Programme, has Attendee, start/end date, location). B's Conference Trip is a narrow social event (sibling of Conference Banquet) under Social Event. A Conference Trip is a social activity, not a general conference event, so the two classes do not denote the same concept.

Both entities denote the conference event itself: Conference in Ontology A and confOf in Ontology B are the central event concept of the conference domain, with matching intended instances (the organised conference/event), so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A is the camera-ready manuscript deadline (final version due after acceptance), while B is the abstract submission deadline (initial abstract due before review). They are distinct deadlines in the conference timeline with no subsumption or overlap.

Person in confOf is a human agent (author, chair, participant) with contact properties (email, phone, first name), while Document in edas is an information artefact (paper, review, programme) that relates to persons and events. Their instances cannot coincide; the only link is that a Person can be related to a Document, which is a relation, not equivalence.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (a person's membership in a conference), while B's belong_to_a_conference_volume relates an Important dates entity to a Conference volume (a deadline belonging to a proceedings volume). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's Workshop is a kind of working event (a conference activity with Conference and Tutorial as siblings), whereas B's Student lecturer is a role of a person (a Lecturer who is a student), sitting under Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer. The two denote entirely different concepts (an event vs. a person role) and share no intended instances.

A's Conference Member is a Person (a person affiliated with a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Conference hall is a Place (a physical venue location, sibling of Building and Session room). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. place) and share no intended instances.

Talk Event is a subclass of Academic Event (an event such as a welcome or closing talk), while Presenter is a subclass of Conference Participant (a person who presents). They belong to different branches of the taxonomy (event vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.

A's Conference is a working event (a meeting such as a tutorial or workshop), while B's Workshop Paper is a type of document/paper. They denote different concepts (event vs. document) and are not related by subsumption.

Topic in confOf is a subject area of contributions/events (dealt with by Contribution, expertise of PC members, topic of working events), whereas Conference in sigkdd is a concrete event with city, start/end dates, name, and held-by relation to ACM SIGKDD. Their intended instances do not coincide: a topic is not a conference. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A 'Communications Topic' is a subject area (a research topic under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of scientific event/presentation (an Individual Presentation, sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial). One denotes a topic of papers, the other a type of talk event; their instances cannot coincide.

A's 'Important dates' is a class collecting the various deadline dates of a conference (abstract, full paper, camera-ready, acceptance, start/end), linked to a Conference volume. B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with children Single/Two Level Conference and properties such as has Name, has Country, has Member, paper Due On. The two denote different concepts (a deadline-dates container vs. the conference event), so they are not equivalent.

A's has VAT is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a tax value; B's has Postal Code is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a postal code. Different domains, different intended values, no conceptual overlap.

A's has Last Name is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's is made from is an object property relating an Item to another Item (material composition). They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's has Cost Amount is a numeric (int) cost of a Sponsorship, while B's Currency is a string-valued currency unit of a Registration fee. They differ in domain (Sponsorship vs Registration fee), range (int vs string), and meaning (amount vs currency unit), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Committee member' is a person role in the conference organisation (a Person who serves on a committee, with subclasses Chair/Co-chair and a 'was a member of' relation to Committee). B 'Registration SIGMOD Member' is a fee category (a subclass of Registration fee, sibling of Registration Non Member/Student) denoting a price for SIGMOD members, not a person. Different intended instances and different paths, so they are unrelated.

A's Program Committee Member is a member of the program committee (a Person/Conference Member who reviews papers), while B's Conference Chair is the person chairing the conference, a distinct role. In cmt, Conference Chair is a separate sibling class, and in edas Conference Chair is a sibling of TPC Member, confirming they are different concepts.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a role/class of authors (a person who co-authored a contribution), sitting under 'Regular author' in the document/contribution branch. B's 'Conference' is a working event (a kind of event/venue), sibling of Tutorial and Workshop. They denote entirely different concepts (an author role vs. an event), so they are unrelated.

A's 'follows' relates Administrative event to Administrative event (temporal ordering of events), while B's 'obtain' relates Person to Item (a person acquiring an item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's property links a Review preference to the Topic/Submitted contribution it prefers, while B's property links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Both are datatype properties of a Conference whose value is a URL/URI string; 'logo URL' and 'has a URL' both attach a web address to a conference, so they denote the same relation despite the range datatype difference (anyURI vs string).

Both classes denote a conference event. Ontology A's Conference is a top-level class with a 'has a name' property and a 'Conference volume' child, while ekaw's Conference is a subclass of Scientific Event described as 'One edition of a conference'. Despite the different placement (A treats it as a broad event concept, ekaw as a specific edition), the intended instances coincide in the conference domain, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.
A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while B's Program Committee is a committee of people. They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

A is a research topic (Radio Communications Topic) under Topic, while B is an organizational body (Program Committee) under Committee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

A's property links a Topic to a Conference part (a topic is a topic of a conference part), while B's property links an Item to a Person (an item is needed for a person). Different domains (Topic vs Item) and different ranges (Conference part vs Person), and the intended meanings do not coincide, so the two properties are unrelated.

A 'Call For Reviews' is a call/announcement soliciting reviewers (a subclass of Call, sibling of Call For Papers/Manuscripts), whereas a 'Negative Review' is a specific review document with a negative outcome (subclass of Review, sibling of Positive/Neutral Review). They denote different concepts in different branches of the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume (organisational/venue-level relation), while B relates a Document to a Speaker (a paper being presented by a person). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a conference activity type (Tutorial, a kind of Lecture). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

A's property links a Conference part to its Track workshop chair (a role assignment), while B's 'parallel with' links two Administrative events that run concurrently. Different domain, range, and meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's `has a name` is a generic naming datatype property whose domain is the union of several classes (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic), whereas B's `has Name` is specific to Conference (comment: 'Conference Full Name'). B's property is strictly narrower in domain, so A is more general: A is subsumed by B's narrower concept, i.e. B subsumes A. They are not equivalent because A applies to many entity types while B only names conferences.

A's 'Conference Session' is a temporal event/program unit (related to Academic Event, Conference, Person, Document), while B's 'Session room' is a physical Place (sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room). They denote different concepts: an event versus a location.

A 'Conference applicant' is a Person who applies to register for a conference (parent Person, child Registeered applicant, siblings Committee member/Reviewer/etc.), whereas B 'Speaker' is a Delegate (a role at a conference building) whose children are Author and Reviewer. The two denote different concepts: an applicant is a prospective attendee, a speaker is a presenting delegate. They do not coincide, nor is one strictly more general than the other, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Working event is a subclass of Event restricted to working (non-social) events, with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop. ekaw's Event is the top-level class covering both Scientific Event and Social Event. Working event is therefore strictly narrower than Event, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's assignedByAdministrator relates a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned them (domain Reviewer, range Administrator). B's presentationed_by relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A Publisher is an organisation that issues conference proceedings (it has a name and issues Conference proceedings). B Contact Information is a value/record class holding city, email, phone, postal code and street for a person or organisation. Their instances and properties do not coincide; a publisher may have contact information, but the concepts are distinct.

A's property links a Conference part to its Track workshop chair (a role assignment within the conference organisation), while B's 'need' links a Person to an Item (a requirement relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Review is a subclass of Document (a written artefact produced in the review process, with children like Meta Review and siblings like Paper). B's Member PC is a subclass of Person (a person who is a reviewer, with comment 'Reviewer' and properties expert On and reviewes). One denotes a document/artefact, the other a person/role; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Working event' is a conference-domain event class (parent Event, children Conference/Tutorial/Workshop, with properties like has title, location, has Topic), while B is a specific research topic (Satellite And Space Communications Topic) under Topic. They denote entirely different kinds of things and cannot be equivalent.

A's Review is a document produced in the conference peer-review process (child of Document, sibling of Paper, written by a Reviewer, subject of a Program Committee Chair's end-review action). B's Departure tax is a monetary tax (child of Tax, sibling of Value added tax) in the iasted ontology. The two concepts share no meaning in the conference domain and are clearly unrelated.

A's rejectedBy links a Paper to the Administrator who rejected it, while B's hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer. Different range types (Administrator vs Possible Reviewer) and different intended meaning (rejection decision vs review assignment), so the properties are not equivalent.

A 'Review Form' is a document/artefact used to submit reviews of papers in the EDAS conference ontology, whereas B 'Time zone' is a temporal/geographic concept in the iasted ontology. They share no meaning, no properties, and no instances; the pair is unrelated.

A's Conference Participant is a broad role class under Person covering all attendees/roles (chairs, presenters, authors, etc.), while B's Lecturer is a narrow subclass of Author (a speaker who gives lectures), with children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer. The two denote different concepts: a conference participant need not be a lecturer, and a lecturer is a specific kind of author/speaker, not the general participant role. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

confOf's 'Working event' is a broad category of events (its children include Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while edas's 'Workshop' is a specific academic event type. Working event is strictly more general than Workshop, so it subsumes it rather than being equivalent.

A's hasCo-author relates a Paper to a Co-author (a co-author role/agent), while B's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (the author). Both express authorship of a paper/document, but the ranges differ: Co-author is a role concept, Person is the agent, and the direction is the same (paper -> author). They overlap in meaning but are not identical, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering all contributors (authors, speakers, participants, etc.), while B's 'OC Member' is a specific Conference Participant role (organising committee member) with child OC Chair. The two concepts do not coincide: OC Member is a narrow role, not a general contributor category, and neither subsumes the other in the intended domain.

A is a conference topic area (a subject category under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a document type (an abstract for an invited talk, under Document > Abstract). They denote entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Rejected Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that was evaluated and rejected), while sigkdd's Paper is the general class of all papers. Rejected Paper is strictly more specific, so it is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

A's `write Paper` goes Author -> Paper (author writes a paper). B's `is writen by` goes Item -> Person (an item is written by a person), which is the inverse direction and a different domain/range pairing. A property and its inverse are not equivalent, so these are unrelated.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while B's 'Author attendee book registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary fee category). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference contributor is a broad Person role covering all people contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants, etc.), while Workshop Chair is a specific conference participant role (chair of a workshop). The Workshop Chair is a kind of conference contributor, so Conference contributor subsumes Workshop Chair, not equivalence.

A's Individual Presentation is a scientific event (a talk given at a conference, with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial) that a paper is presented as. B's Video presentation is a kind of Presentation activity (sibling of Power Point presentation), i.e. a presentation medium/format rather than a scientific event. They overlap in that both concern presenting work, but the intended instances differ (event vs. presentation format), so they are not equivalent; they are merely related.

A's 'has tutorials' is a specific part-whole property from a Conference volume to its Tutorials (a subproperty of 'has parts'), while B's 'part Of Event' is a generic mereological relation between Events. They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning; neither is a subsumption of the other.

The two properties are inverses of each other: cmt's hasSubjectArea goes from Paper to Subject Area, while ekaw's topicCoveredBy goes from Research Topic to Event/Paper. They relate the same kinds of things (papers and topics) but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent; a reference alignment would record them as related (inverse) rather than equivalent.

A's 'is sent after' relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering of an item relative to a time), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (an authorship submission action). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A Workshop is a scholarly conference part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, with a conference volume having workshops), while B Meal Break is a non-academic break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Free Time Break). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's 'Member PC' is a program-committee member/reviewer (comment: Reviewer; reviews Contributions, expert on Topics), while B's 'Conference Chair' is the conference chair who initiates calls and reviews papers. They are distinct roles in the conference domain, so the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of Contribution (a submission/paper type), while B 'Exhibitor' is a kind of Sponzor (a sponsor/exhibitor at the conference). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (submissions vs. sponsors) and share no intended instances.

A's Document is a broad Item covering many artefacts (forms, invitations, reviews, submissions, etc.), while B's Review is a specific document type (a review of a paper). Document in iasted is strictly more general than Review in sigkdd, so Document subsumes Review; they are not equivalent.

Author in cmt is a person (a conference member/user who writes papers and submits them), while Review expertise in Conference is a topic/skill area associated with reviewers and submissions, not a person. Their properties and contexts do not overlap: Author has properties like write Paper and submit Paper, whereas Review expertise is linked to Reviewer and Submitted contribution as an expertise value. They denote different concepts.

A's location is a datatype property linking a Social/Working event to a string (where the event is held), while B's is present in is an object property linking a Person to a Place or Time. Different domain, range, and kind, so they are not the same relation.

A's setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while B's organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (event organisation). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Both denote a member of the technical/program committee: edas TPC Member is a Person who reviews papers and initiates calls, and ekaw PC Member is a Possible Reviewer (a Person) that reviews papers and is parent of PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc. The intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

A's 'Call for participation' is a conference document announcing the call (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, Review), whereas B's 'Viza' is a visa-related document (sibling of Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance). Different intended instances; no subsumption or overlap.

Both entities denote the same conference venue concept: 'Conference Venue Place' in the edas ontology and 'Conference Place' in the iasted ontology are classes representing the location where a conference takes place, with matching paths (Place > Conference Venue Place vs. Place > Conference Place) and sibling context (both under Place, alongside other venue-related classes).

A's adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (a reviewer adjusting their bid/review score), while B's payed_by relates a Registration fee to a Person (who paid the fee). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's Event is a conference-domain class (scientific/social events, with properties like held In, organised By, part Of Event), while B's Time zone is a temporal/geographic concept with no overlap in intended instances; they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a submitted contribution with authors, reviews, decisions and subject areas; B's Invitation letter is a document sent to invite someone (sibling of Form, Payment document, Viza). They share only the Document parent and denote different artefacts, so they are unrelated.

A's Program Committee Chair is a chair of the program committee (a subrole of Chairman and Program Committee Member, ending reviews). B's OC Chair is the chair of the Organising Committee, a subrole of OC Member. Both are conference chair roles but of different committees (program vs organising), so they are related but not equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is the general class of things submitted to a conference (children Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by Author, reviewed by PC member, has title/abstract/keywords). Submission in iasted is likewise the general submitted document (children Initial manuscript, Final manuscript) under Document. Both denote the same concept of a submitted contribution, so they are equivalent.

ekaw's partOf is a generic mereological/structural property (unspecified domain/range, used to decompose events, documents, etc.), whereas iasted's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or an award). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's 'issues' relates a Publisher to a Conference proceedings (publisher issues proceedings), while B's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (event held in a place). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's `author Of` goes Person -> Document (a person authors a document). B's `is given by` goes Activity/Item -> Person (an activity/item is given by a person), i.e. the inverse direction and different domain/range kinds. A property and its inverse are not equivalent, and the entity types (Document vs Activity/Item) differ, so the two are unrelated.

A's property links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (the contribution a reviewer is qualified to review), while B's write links a Person to an Item (an author writing a paper). Different domains (Review expertise vs Person), different ranges (Submitted contribution vs Item), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's min Choice is a minimum-participant-count datatype property on Social/Working events (range positiveInteger), while B's done till is a deadline date property (range date). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a leadership role in the conference organisation, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member. Conference Hiker (iasted) is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. an attendee type, not an organiser role. The two denote different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

edas:Paper is a general document about a paper (with children Accepted/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper and properties like is Written By, has Topic, is Reviewed By), while ekaw:Abstract is a specific document type (abstract) with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract and is linked to presentations. They are both subclasses of Document and overlap in the conference domain, but an abstract is not the same concept as a paper; ekaw also has a separate Paper class, so the intended instances do not coincide. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'Track workshop chair' is a specific chair role for a track/workshop/tutorial, while B's 'Conference Chair' is the general conference chair role. Both are Person subclasses with chairing responsibilities, so they overlap, but neither subsumes the other: a track workshop chair is not necessarily the conference chair, and the conference chair is not necessarily a track workshop chair.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented), while B 'Platinum Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. sponsor) and share no intended instances.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman who chairs the conference), while Main office is a physical place (a location/room). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Place) and have no overlapping instances, so they are unrelated.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (membership in a conference committee), while B's sign relates a Person to an Item (signing something). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A 'Member PC' is a person role (a program-committee member/reviewer, subclass of Person, with properties expert On and reviewes), while B 'Reject Rating' is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a value/verdict of a review. They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. rating value) and are unrelated.

A's Conference Chair is a leadership role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) who chairs the conference, while B's Reviewer is a participant role under Speaker who reviews submissions. They denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'adjusted By' relates a Bid to a Reviewer (the reviewer who adjusted the bid), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship of a paper).
