Different domains (Bid vs Author), different ranges (Reviewer vs Contribution), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

In iasted, Submission is a subclass of Document (path Item > Document > Submission), with children Final manuscript and Initial manuscript. In sigkdd, Document is the broader class whose children include Abstract, Paper and Review, and which is the range of presentation/submit until. A Submission is a kind of Document, but a Document in sigkdd also covers abstracts and reviews, so Submission is strictly narrower than sigkdd's Document: subsumed_by rather than equivalent.

A's 'was a steering committee of' relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume (organisational role to event), while B's 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (e.g. signing a document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's has Location relates a Conference Event to a Place (event venue/location). B's is present in relates a Person to a Place and Time (attendance/presence). Different domains (Conference Event vs Person) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Event is a conference-domain event (scientific/social events, organised by people, held in locations, part of other events). B's Time is a temporal entity (conference days, deadlines, trip days) used as the time argument of properties like is held before/after/in. An event is not a time; the intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) denoting the whole conference; B's Closing Talk is a specific talk event (sibling of Welcome Talk) within the conference programme. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (a committee-to-event relation), while B's 'occupy' links a Person to a Building/City/State (a person-to-location relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a registered conference applicant who has paid early), while B is an activity performed before the conference (renting). They belong to different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string email address; B's hasReview is an object property linking a Paper to a Review. Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Country is a geographical entity that a Conference has (Conference -> Country). In iasted, State is a sub-national administrative/geographical region (a child of Place, with children Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state) that can be situated in, occupied by, and visited by persons. A Country is a sovereign nation, whereas a State is a smaller region within a country; the intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's writtenBy relates a Review to its Reviewer (the author of the review). B's isReviewHistoryOf relates a Personal Review History (a collection/record of reviews) to a Reviewer, i.e. the reviewer who owns that history. The domains differ (Review vs Personal Review History) and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has parts' relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts (a whole-part relation within a document/volume structure), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (membership of people in a conference). Different domains (Conference volume vs Conference) and ranges (Conference part vs Person), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the event/meeting class (has a name, has Conference volume, related to proceedings/publisher/topic). B's Conference restaurant is a physical building/place (path Place > Building > Conference restaurant, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport, Presenter house), i.e. a restaurant located at a conference venue. Different intended instances: events vs. buildings. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

Both are datatype properties linking an event-like entity to a date/time, but the domains differ: A's 'is a starting date' is a property of the 'Important dates' class (a deadline/date node) and specifically denotes a start date, while B's 'is dated on' is a property of 'Activity' and denotes the date an activity occurs. They overlap in the general sense of associating a date with an event, but neither subsumes the other and they are not the same relation.

A Meta Review is a review of reviews (a document type in the review hierarchy), while B Personal History is a container for a person's publication and review records. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A's Review Rating is a class of rating values (Accept Rating, Reject Rating, etc.) attached to an active paper via has Rating. B's Review is a document (subclass of Document) with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review, written by a reviewer about a paper. A rating is a value/assessment, not a document, and the two have different parents, children and properties, so they denote different concepts.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving a string name for a Conference or Person, while B's `End of conference` is a datatype property giving a dateTime for a Conference. They have different domains (Person included in A) and different ranges (string vs dateTime), so they denote different relations.

Company in confOf is an organizational entity (sibling of University under Organization), while Computer Architecture Topic in edas is a research subject area under Topic. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A's hasTopic relates a Working event to a Topic (event has a subject area), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (author submits a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's rejectedBy links a Paper to the Administrator who rejected it (a rejection decision relation), while B's relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to the Paper Presentation event it is associated with (an acceptance/presentation relation). Different domains (Paper vs Accepted Paper), different ranges (Administrator vs Paper Presentation), and opposite polarity (rejected vs accepted), so they are not the same relation.

In edas, Attendee is a generic person who attends the conference, sibling to Author, Reviewer, Chair roles. In ekaw, Agency Staff Member is a person working for the organising agency (a staff role), sibling to Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student. The intended instances do not coincide: an attendee is a participant, not agency staff. Different concepts despite both being subclasses of Person.

In confOf, Author is a subclass of Person whose instances write Contributions. In iasted, Reviewer is a subclass of Speaker (under Delegate) and is a sibling of Author, so the two ontologies treat Author and Reviewer as distinct roles. An author writes papers while a reviewer evaluates them; the intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a subclass of 'Regular author' in the conference-contribution hierarchy, denoting a first author of a contribution. B's 'Author attendee book registration fee' is a subclass of 'Registration fee' under 'Money > Fee', denoting a fee category for author attendees who book. They belong to entirely different branches (author role vs. fee type) and share no intended instances.

Both are object properties linking a Paper to a topical classification entity (Subject Area in cmt, Topic in edas). The edas property additionally allows Conference as domain, but for the Paper case they relate the same kinds of things in the same direction, so they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Both denote a person serving on the program committee: edas 'TPC Member' (Technical Program Committee Member) is a Person who reviews papers and initiates calls, and sigkdd 'Program Committee member' is a Person under Organizator alongside Program Chair. The intended instances coincide (PC/TPC members), so they are equivalent despite differing parent paths.

A's `reviews` links a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's `presentationed by` links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference event/session), while B's Tutorial speaker is a person role (a kind of Author/Speaker). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and are not equivalent.

Both properties link a document/item to a person involved in its presentation, but the directions and intended meanings differ: 'is needed for' (Item -> Person) expresses a requirement/dependency, while 'presentationed by' (Document -> Speaker) expresses authorship/presentation of a document by a speaker. They overlap in the conference domain (a paper needs an author/presenter) but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference submission (children Accepted/Rejected/Pending Paper, reviewed by reviewers, written by authors, has topics). B's Multi author Volume is a published document (child Proceedings, publisherOf by an Organisation) — a collection of papers, not a submission. Different concepts.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property of Conference giving the number of reviews per paper (domain Conference, range int). B's 'has a degree' is a datatype property of Review preference giving the degree/level of a reviewer's preference (domain Review preference, range int). Different domains (Conference vs Review preference) and different intended meanings (count of reviews vs preference degree), so they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a person/author to a paper/conference document they are involved with. 'contributes' has domain Person and range Conference document; 'has Related Paper' has domain Author and range Paper. Author is a subclass of Person and Paper is a subclass of Conference document in the conference domain, so the two relations denote the same authorship/contribution link in the same direction.

A's 'early Registration' is a boolean flag on a Participant indicating whether they registered early; B's 'done till' is a date property on a Deadline indicating when the deadline is completed. They have different domains (Participant vs Deadline), different ranges (boolean vs date), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'related To Event' links an Accepted Paper to its Paper Presentation (a paper-to-presentation relation), whereas B's 'technically Organised By' is a subproperty of 'organised By' relating an event/conference to the body that technically organises it. The domains and ranges differ (paper vs. event/organiser), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's Conference Venue Place is a generic place type (sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) under Place, denoting the venue location of a conference. B's Trip city is a city used for trip/travel arrangements (sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city) under City. Both concern the location of a conference, but A is a broad venue-place concept while B is specifically a city used for travel; they overlap in the conference-location sense but are not the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Scientific Event is a subclass of Event covering conferences, workshops, sessions, presentations, tracks — scholarly gatherings. B's Conference activity is a subclass of Activity covering receptions, coffee breaks, lectures, registration, social program — the activities/events occurring at a conference. They overlap (both include presentations/lectures and social events) but neither subsumes the other: Scientific Event includes Conference/Workshop/Track which are not 'activities', while Conference activity includes Coffee break/Registration which are not 'scientific events'. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a conference event/activity (sibling of Track and Workshop, range of 'has tutorials' from Conference volume), whereas B's Tutorial Chair is a person role (a Conference Participant and PC Member). The entities denote different kinds of things (event vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker, i.e. who presented a document. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's 'Worker lecturer' is a Lecturer who is also a Worker (a person who lectures and works), sitting under Lecturer in the Delegate/Speaker/Author chain. B's 'Author of paper' is an Author who has written a paper, sitting under Author. Both are specialisations of Author in the conference domain, but they capture different aspects (employment/lecturing vs. paper authorship) and neither subsumes the other; they overlap only in that both are Author subclasses, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a Paper Abstract (a document type under Paper in cmt), while B is an Exhibitor (a sponsor subtype under Sponzor in sigkdd). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (submission vs. sponsorship) and share no intended instances.

A's `name` is a general naming property for Conferences and Persons, while B's `has VAT` is a specific financial property (value added tax) for Social/Working events. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

Both denote the outcome/state of a submission that was not accepted: cmt's Rejection is a subclass of Decision (sibling of Acceptance), and Conference's Rejected contribution is a subclass of Reviewed contribution (sibling of Accepted contribution). They describe the same concept in the conference domain, differing only in whether the ontology models it as a decision outcome or as a document state.

A's Poster is a subclass of Contribution (a kind of paper/submission), while B's Poster Session is a subclass of Session (a kind of event). They denote different concepts: a contribution type versus an event type, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's City is a general city class used as the range of has City (Organization, Person -> City), i.e. any city associated with a person or organization. iasted's Presenter city is a specific subclass of City (its parent is City) denoting the city of a presenter, alongside sibling subclasses Conference city, Sponsor city, Trip city. Presenter city is therefore strictly narrower than the general City class, so A is more general than B: subsumed_by.

A 'Conference Paper' is a scientific paper submitted to/published at a conference (a subclass of Paper within Document). B 'Transparency' is a physical/administrative item (a slide/overhead transparency) under Document in the iasted ontology, alongside forms, invitation letters and payment documents. They denote different concepts despite both being Documents.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution (a document submitted to a conference, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract). B's 'Test Only Topic' is a topic category in the EDAS topic taxonomy (sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), used to classify submissions, not a document type. Different domains of discourse (document vs. topic), so they are unrelated.

Meal Event is a specific kind of non-academic conference event (a meal, e.g. conference dinner), while ekaw's Social Event is the broader category of social events that includes the conference banquet and trip. A meal event is a social event, but not every social event is a meal event, so Meal Event is subsumed by Social Event rather than equivalent.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (setting review criteria for a conference), while B's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to a Reviewer (who invited a reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's `written By` goes from Contribution to Author (a paper is written by an author), while B's `author Of` goes from Person to Document (a person is the author of a document). They are inverse relations, not equivalent: a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

A TPC Member is a person who reviews papers and is on the program committee; in ekaw, Possible Reviewer is the broader class of anyone who may review, with PC Member as a child. A TPC Member is thus a specific kind of Possible Reviewer (indeed a PC Member), so TPC Member is subsumed by Possible Reviewer rather than equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference document (submitted/ reviewed/ written by authors, has topics), while B's Tax is a monetary charge (sibling of Fee, Tip, Sponsorship) under Money. Different domains and no shared instances.

confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author (paper authorship), while iasted's prepare relates a Person to an Item (a person preparing an item). The domains (Contribution vs Person) and ranges (Author vs Item) differ, and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's Reject Rating is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a rating value indicating rejection of a paper. B's Abstract is a subclass of Document, i.e. the abstract text of a paper. They belong to entirely different branches (review ratings vs. document parts) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Location is a venue/place where an Event is held (held In: Event -> Location; location Of: Location -> Event). In sigkdd, Conference is the event itself (with start/end dates, city, name, held by an ACM SIGKDD), not a place. The two denote different concepts: a place versus an event, so they are not equivalent.
A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a physical location (Conference hall, a kind of Place). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

In cmt, Program Committee Chair is a subclass of Chairman and Program Committee Member, a specific committee role that ends reviews. In edas, Conference Chair is a top-level Person role that initiates calls and reviews papers, a broader organising role. The cmt role is a specific chair role, not the general conference chair; the edas Conference Chair is more general and does not correspond to the PC chair role. Hence Program Committee Chair is subsumed by the broader Conference Chair concept rather than equivalent.

A's Review preference is a per-reviewer/topic preference record (degree, topic, submission contribution) used for reviewer assignment. B's Personal Review History is a historical record of reviews a reviewer has performed, linked only to Reviewer. They capture different concepts (preference vs. past reviews) and do not denote the same instances.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection, child of Decision) about whether a paper is accepted. B's Reception is a social event (child of Social Event, sibling of Excursion) at the conference. Different domains and kinds; the label similarity is coincidental.

Both are registration-fee classes for non-member attendees, but A is a generic non-member fee while B is specifically for SIGKDD members (a member category in the SIGKDD ontology), so they overlap in the registration-fee context but do not denote the same concept.

ekaw Location is a general place/venue for events (held In / location Of), while iasted Building is a specific kind of Place (a physical building) that can host conferences and be occupied. A Building is a Location, but a Location need not be a Building (e.g. a city or country), so Location is more general and subsumes Building.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation between an abstract and its presentation artefact). B's 'paperInVolume' relates a paper to a volume (a containment relation between a paper and a proceedings volume). The domains, ranges and intended meanings differ, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document type (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc. under Conference document), while B 'Conference airport' is a physical building/place (sibling of Conference hotel, Conference restaurant under Building). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A is a research topic class in a topic taxonomy (a subfield of Computer Networks), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical computer) under Audiovisual equipment alongside projectors and video players. They share only the word 'Computer' and denote entirely different concepts.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has Email' is a datatype property of Person/Contact Information giving an email address. They relate different kinds of data (surname vs. email address) and are not the same relation.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference) under Event > Scientific Event, while B's Conference building is a physical building under Place > Building that hosts delegates. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. venue/building), so they are not equivalent.

Author is a Person who writes papers; Individual Presentation is a Scientific Event (a talk) that presents a paper. They belong to different branches (Person vs Event) and have incompatible properties (Author writes papers, Individual Presentation presents papers), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Pending Paper' is a paper in a submission state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper under Paper). B 'Deadline Author notification' is a deadline event (sibling of abstract/paper submission deadlines under Deadline). Different kinds of entities: a document state vs. a temporal deadline; no overlap.

Both are subclasses of Place in their respective ontologies and both denote physical locations used for conference sessions, but 'Session room' is a generic room where sessions are held while 'Conference hall' is a specific large hall type; they overlap in use but are not the same concept, and each ontology has the other's counterpart as a sibling (iasted has Conference hall, sigkdd has Hotel/Main office), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a document type) with abstract-related properties, while B's Best Research Paper Award is a subtype of Award, an honour given to a paper. They denote different concepts: a document vs. an award, so they are unrelated.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an action performed by an Administrator that results in a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), i.e. the act of finalising the assignment of papers to a conference. B's 'issues' is a Publisher's act of issuing Conference proceedings (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings). Different agents (Administrator vs Publisher), different objects (Conference vs Conference proceedings), and different intended meanings (finalising paper assignment vs publishing proceedings). They are not the same relation.

cmt:User is a general person role in the conference (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while iasted:Speaker is a specific delegate subtype (parent of Author, Reviewer) under Delegate. They overlap in that both cover authors/reviewers, but User is broader (includes Administrator) and Speaker is a narrower participant role, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Social event is a broad category of social events (children Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B's Dinner banquet is a specific kind of social program activity. A Dinner banquet is a Social event, but not every Social event is a Dinner banquet, so B is subsumed by A.
A's Presenter is a conference participant (a person who presents), while B's Presenter city is a kind of City (a location associated with a presenter). Different kinds of entities, so unrelated.

A's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. a reviewer inviting a co-reviewer. B's 'has Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (domain Paper, range Possible Reviewer), i.e. a paper being assigned a reviewer. The kinds of things related and the direction differ, so the two properties are not equivalent.
A's writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author; B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Conference. Different domain and range, different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's writeReview goes Reviewer -> Review (a reviewer writes a review); B's reviewWrittenBy goes Review -> Possible Reviewer (a review is written by a possible reviewer). They are inverse relations, not equivalent, and the property-and-inverse distinction means they must not be aligned as equivalent.

Track is a conference part (a thematic stream of the conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, with conferences having tracks), whereas Sponzorship is a kind of Money (sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members (people serving on the committee), while B's organisedBy links an Event to the organisations/persons that organise it. Different domain (Program Committee vs Event), different range (Program Committee Member vs Organisation/Person), and different meaning (committee membership vs event organisation); they are not the same relation.

A's Talk Event is a conference event (a scheduled talk such as a welcome or closing talk) under Academic Event, while B's Simulating is a research activity performed before the conference under Research, alongside Modelling. They belong to different branches (event vs. research activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person role in the conference), while B's Registration SIGMOD Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category). They denote different concepts: a person type vs. a fee type. Note B has a sibling Registration Student, which is the fee counterpart of A's Student, confirming they are not the same entity.

confOf's hasSurname is a specific datatype property for a person's family name, while sigkdd's Name is a general name property for a Person. A surname is a kind of name, so hasSurname is more specific and is subsumed by Name; they are not equivalent because Name can hold full names or given names, not only surnames.

A 'Fee for extra trip' is a charge for an additional excursion/trip, while B 'Sponzor fee' is a sponsorship fee. Both are subclasses of Fee but denote different kinds of fees; no synonymy or subsumption holds.

Conference fees is a broad class covering all fees paid for a conference (registration, extras, etc.), while Hotel fee is a specific fee for hotel accommodation, a sibling of Registration fee under Fee. They overlap in that both are fees, but neither subsumes the other: Conference fees is not a kind of Hotel fee, and Hotel fee is only one possible component of conference fees. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference/committee), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presented the document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's has VAT is a datatype property giving a tax string for social/working events; B's held In is an object property linking an event to its location. Different kinds of things related (string vs Location) and different meaning, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference topic about computer-network sensors (a research subject under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a state of being a sponsor in the iasted ontology (sibling of Conference state and Presenter state). They belong to entirely different branches (Topic vs State) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

has Member relates a Conference to its Person members (committee/participants), while written By relates a Document to the Person who authored it. Different domains (Conference vs Document) and different intended relations (membership vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

Acceptance is a decision outcome class (sibling of Rejection under Decision), while Accepted contribution is a document/contribution class (a reviewed contribution that was accepted, parent of Camera ready contribution). They are conceptually linked (an accepted contribution results from an acceptance decision) but denote different kinds of entities: a decision vs. a document. Thus they are related, not equivalent.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact. B's 'Workshop' is an academic event (subclass of Academic Event, sibling of Talk Event, Paper Presentation), i.e. an occurrence. A document and an event denote different kinds of things, so the classes are not equivalent and do not even overlap.

A's Conference Event is an event (with attendees, programme, start/end times, location) while B's Place is a physical location (conference hall, hotel, office) where a person can stay. They denote different concepts; the only overlap is that a Conference Event has a location, but the entities themselves are not the same.

Committee member (Conference) denotes a person who is a member of a committee, with subclasses Chair and Co chair, and is linked to Committee via has members / was a member of. Possible Reviewer (ekaw) denotes a person who may review papers, with subclass PC Member, and is linked to Paper and Review via has Reviewer / review Written By / reviewer Of Paper. The two concepts overlap (PC members are typically committee members and reviewers) but are not coextensive: a committee member need not be a possible reviewer, and a possible reviewer need not be a committee member. Hence they are related, not equivalent.

A 'Conference Paper' is a type of academic paper (a Document > Paper subclass, sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Demo Paper, etc.), while B 'Mailing list' is a Document used for communication (sibling of Invitation letter, Form, Review, Submission). They denote different concepts despite both being Documents.

A's Topic is a subject area of papers/conferences (has Topic from Conference/Paper, children are research areas like Antennas, Cryptography). B's Time is a temporal entity (children Conference days, Deadline, Trip day; used as range of is held after/before, is present, is sent after/before). Different domains entirely, no overlap.

A's 'paper Due On' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime deadline (the submission deadline for papers). B's 'presentation Of Paper' is an object property linking an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper it presents. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Individual Presentation), range (dateTime vs Paper), and meaning (deadline vs presented paper), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members (people serving on the committee), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (a paper). Different domain (Committee vs Author), different range (Committee member vs Contribution), and different intended relation; they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

Both classes denote the same concept: a social event within a conference. In confOf, Social event is a subclass of Event with children Banquet, Reception, Trip. In edas, Social Event is a subclass of Non Academic Event with children Excursion, Reception. The shared child Reception and the synonymous labels/paths (Event > Social event vs Conference Event > Non Academic Event > Social Event) indicate the intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a human role: active/passive participant, reviewer, chair), while B's 'Conference activity' is a subclass of Activity (an event such as lecture, coffee break, registration). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and are not equivalent.

A's 'adjusted By' links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusts it, while B's 'written By' links a Contribution (paper) to its Author. Different domains (Bid vs Contribution) and different ranges (Reviewer vs Author), so the relations are not the same.

A 'CAD Topic' is a subject area (a kind of Topic) in the edas ontology, while B 'Program Committee' is a committee (a kind of Committee) in sigkdd. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment of a paper for review), while B's 'pay' links a Person to Money (a payment relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's hasCity is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string city name, while B's locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and direction of relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (printing hardcopy mailing manifests), while B's 'send' relates a Person to an Item. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Subject Area in cmt is a topic classification of papers (range of has Subject Area from Paper), while City in confOf is a geographic location of organizations/persons (range of has City from Organization and Person). Different intended instances and different roles in the domain, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Participant is a general role for anyone taking part in the conference (children include Member, Regular, Student, and siblings include Author, Chair PC, Volunteer), whereas ekaw's Presenter is a specific kind of Conference Participant who presents a paper (child Invited Speaker, sibling Session Chair etc.). Every Presenter is a conference participant, but not every Participant is a Presenter, so Participant is strictly more general: subsumed_by.

A's 'Personal Review History' is a per-reviewer record/collection of reviews (a history object linked to a Reviewer via has/is Review History Of), whereas B's 'Review' is a single review document (a subclass of Document, sibling of Submission, Form, etc.). One is a history/aggregate of reviews, the other is an individual review document, so they do not denote the same concept.

A's 'Hotel fee' is a subclass of Fee (a monetary charge for lodging), while B's 'Hotel' is a subclass of Place (a physical location). They denote different concepts (a cost vs. a venue), so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Conference Trip is a subclass of Social Event (an organised social activity during the conference, sibling of Conference Banquet). In iasted, Trip city is a subclass of City (a city that is the destination of a trip, sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city). One denotes an event/activity, the other a location/city; their intended instances cannot coincide.

A's addProgramCommitteeMember relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (adding a person to a committee), while B's initiates relates a chair/TPC member to a Call (starting a call for papers). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subtype covering anyone contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants), while IASTED non member is a Delegate subtype specifically denoting a delegate who is not an IASTED member. The two concepts differ in scope and in the membership criterion; neither subsumes the other in the intended domain.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (domain Reviewer, range Paper), while B's hasReview relates a Paper to a Review (domain Paper, range Review). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent; at best they are inverses of different relations, not the same property.

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property from Review expertise to a literal (expertise topic), while B's 'has Review' is an object property from Paper to Review. They differ in domain, range, and kind, so they are not the same relation.

A 'Call For Papers' is an announcement/request for submissions (a call document, sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews under Call), whereas B 'Rejected Paper' is a specific paper that has been evaluated and rejected (subclass of Evaluated Paper). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A ('Information for participants') is a conference document providing participant information, while B ('Deadline Paper Submission') is a submission deadline event. They belong to different branches (document vs. deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Full Version' is the complete version of a submitted paper (sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), whereas B 'Invited Talk Abstract' is an abstract of an invited talk (sibling of Tutorial Abstract under Abstract). They denote different document types in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it, while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domains (Event vs Document), different ranges (Organisation/Person vs Speaker), and different intended relations (organising vs presenting); they are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is the abstract-only submission form, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper. Regular Paper (ekaw) is a paper category (full/regular paper) sibling of Poster Paper, Demo Paper, etc. They denote different concepts: an abstract vs. a regular paper type, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document announcing the event and inviting submissions, while B 'Conference Proceedings' is a published multi-author volume collecting accepted papers. They are different document types with different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's `author Of` goes Person -> Document (a person authors a document), while B's `is writen by` goes Item -> Person (an item is written by a person). They describe the same authorship relation but in opposite directions, so they are inverses, not equivalent.

A's Conference Chair is a Person who initiates calls and reviews papers (a chair/organiser role), while B's Reviewer is a Speaker/Delegate who reviews papers. Although both can review papers, Conference Chair is a distinct organising role, not a reviewer; the paths (Person > Conference Chair vs Delegate > Speaker > Reviewer) and sibling sets (Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member vs Author) show different intended concepts.

A's 'Written contribution' is a conference contribution (a paper-like submission, with children Regular/Submitted contribution) under Conference document > Conference contribution. B's 'Publication' is a generic Item (siblings include Card, Document, Transport vehicle) with children Book proceeding and Cd proceeding, i.e. published proceedings/books rather than submitted contributions. They overlap in that both concern written/published material, but the intended instances do not coincide: a written contribution is a submitted paper, a publication is a published artefact. Hence related, not equivalent.

Rejection is a decision outcome on a paper (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), while Excursion is a social/non-academic conference event (sibling of Reception under Social Event). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's 'Passive conference participant' is a participant who does not actively contribute (sibling of 'Active conference participant'), a role distinction based on activity. B's 'Late Registered Participant' is a participant distinguished by registration timing (sibling of 'Early Registered Participant'), not by activity. The two classifications are orthogonal: a late registrant may be active or passive, and a passive participant may register early or late. They do not denote the same concept.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference, Tutorial and Workshop (things that happen at the conference), while B 'Delegate' is a subclass of Conference building/Person covering attendees such as Speaker, Session chair and Listener. One denotes an event, the other a person/role; their paths, parents and children do not overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a committee (a group of people) that organizes a conference, sibling of Program/Steering committee. B's 'Academic Institution' is an organisation (a university/research institute) that can scientifically organise events. Different kinds of entities: a committee vs. an institution; no subsumption or overlap.

A Talk Event is a specific kind of academic event (a talk with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), while B Scientific Event is a broad category covering conferences, sessions, tracks, workshops and presentations. Every talk event is a scientific event, but not vice versa, so Talk Event is strictly more specific: subsumed_by.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a chair/committee role (subclass of Chairman and Conference Member, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), while B's 'Regular' is a plain participant type (subclass of Participant, sibling of Student and Member). They denote different concepts: an organising/chairing role versus an ordinary attendee category.

A's email is a Person's email address; B's has Last Name is a Person's family name. Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote different attributes (email address vs. last name), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property of Conference www with range string, while B's 'has amount of' is a datatype property of Money with range int. They relate different kinds of things (a URL vs a monetary amount) in different domains, so they are unrelated.

A's co-writePaper relates a Co author to a Paper (author -> paper direction), while B's writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author (paper -> author direction). They are inverse relations, not equivalent, and the domain/range classes differ (Co author vs Contribution, Paper vs Author).

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a numeric (int) property of a Conference giving the number of reviews per paper, while B's 'City of conference' is a string property giving the location of a conference. They share only the domain (Conference) but have different ranges and clearly different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Time in iasted is a general temporal class with children Conference days, Deadline and Trip day, and is used as the range of many temporal relations (is held after/before, is present, is sent after/before). Deadline in sigkdd is a specific kind of time point (a submission/notification deadline) with its own subclasses and a Date property. Thus iasted Time is broader and subsumes sigkdd Deadline; they are not equivalent.

A's 'done till' is a datatype property from Deadline to a date literal (the deadline's end date), while B's 'submit until' is an object property from Document to Deadline (the deadline by which a document must be submitted). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Deadline vs Document), and range (date literal vs Deadline class), so they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant under Conference applicant (a person who registers late and pays), while B 'Registration Non Member' is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for non-members). They belong to different branches (person vs fee) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.
A is a research topic in computer networks security; B is the program committee of a conference. Different domains entirely.

A Presenter is a conference participant who gives a presentation (a role within the Person hierarchy, with child Invited Speaker). B Non speaker is a Delegate who does not speak, i.e. the complement/opposite role. They denote disjoint roles, so they are not equivalent.

A's Topic is a subject area of papers/reviews/conference parts (it is a topic of conference parts, has a name, is linked to reviews and submissions). B's Place is a physical location (building, room, city) with children Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office, Session room and properties about being situated in, equipped by, held in. The intended instances do not coincide: a research topic is not a place, and the contexts (review/submission vs. location/activity) share no meaning.

A is a person role (an active conference participant, a subclass of Conference contributor/participant, sibling of Invited speaker and Regular author) that gives presentations. B is an event type (Individual Presentation, a Scientific Event with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial) that has a paper presented as it. A person and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property of Contact Information with range string, capturing a postal address code; B's is_dated_on is a datatype property of Activity with range dateTime, capturing a temporal date. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'gives presentations' links an active conference participant to a Presentation (the act of presenting), while B's 'related To Paper' links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (the paper being presented). Both connect a presenter/presentation to the presented content, so they overlap in the conference domain, but the domains and ranges differ (participant vs. paper presentation; presentation vs. accepted paper), so they are not the same relation.

A's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a reviewer-centric record of past reviews), while B's hasReview links a Paper to a Review (a paper-centric link to a single review). They have different domains (Reviewer vs Paper), different ranges (Personal Review History vs Review), and different directions of association, so they are not the same relation.

confOf Author is a person who writes contributions (domain of writes, range of written By). ekaw Possible Reviewer is a person who may review papers (domain of reviewer Of Paper, range of has Reviewer/review Written By), with child PC Member. The intended instances differ: an author writes papers, a possible reviewer reviews them; the shared parent Person and the word overlap are not enough for equivalence.

A is a kind of Paper (a document submitted to a conference), while B is a physical Place (a hall where the conference takes place). They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Place) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (a call for papers announcement, sibling of Conference announcement, Review, etc.), while B's 'Medicine Topic' is a subject/topic area under Topic (sibling of Cryptography Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts.

Both classes denote the fee paid for registration at a conference. In iasted, 'Registration fee' is a subclass of Fee under Money, with siblings Hotel fee and Fee for extra trip, and children for attendee/member/nonmember/student registration fees. In sigkdd, 'Registration SIGKDD Member' is a registration fee class under Registration fee, with siblings Registration Non Member and Registration Student. The intended instances coincide: fees charged for conference registration, specialized by attendee category.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Paper' is a contribution (a submitted/accepted scientific work). They denote different concepts: one is a call/announcement, the other is the paper itself. No subsumption or overlap in the intended instances.

A's 'Submitted Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document submitted to a conference, with children like Assigned Paper), while B's 'Transport vehicle' is a subclass of Item covering cars, buses, taxis and vans. They share no meaning in the conference domain and belong to entirely different branches (Document vs. transport), so they are unrelated.

Bid in cmt is a reviewer's bid on a paper (domain/range Reviewer->Bid, Paper->Bid), while Person in iasted is a general human agent (parent of Delegate, Sponsor) involved in activities, items, places and money. A bid is not a person; the concepts are unrelated.

Author Not Reviewer is a subclass of Author in cmt, denoting a person who is an author but explicitly not a reviewer. Paper Author in ekaw is a subclass of Person denoting anyone who authors a paper, with no exclusion of reviewers. The two classes have different intents: one is a role with a negative constraint, the other is a general author role. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in a way that a reference alignment would record.

Both properties relate a written work (Paper/Item) to its author (Author/Person) in the same direction. 'is Written By' and 'is signed by' are synonymous authoring relations in the conference domain; the domain/range classes Paper~Item and Author~Person are themselves equivalent, so the properties coincide.

A's hasSurname relates a Person to their surname, while B's hasFirstName relates a Person to their first name. These are distinct datatype properties capturing different name components, not synonyms; a reference alignment would not equate them.

Conference in confOf is a working event (a kind of event such as tutorial or workshop), while Mobile Computing Topic in edas is a subject area/topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's `related To Event` links an Accepted Paper to its Paper Presentation (paper -> presentation), while B's `write` links a Person to an Item (person -> item). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference fees' is a class about the cost/fee aspect of a conference, while B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself (with children Single/Two Level Conference and properties like has Name, paper Due On, has Member). The fee concept is not the same as the conference event, so they are unrelated.

Both properties express where an event takes place, but A's `location` is a datatype property mapping an event to a string, while B's `has Location` is an object property mapping a Conference Event to a Place individual. They are semantically related (same intended information) but not equivalent because their ranges and property types differ.

A Workshop is a working event (a small interactive meeting held alongside a conference, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas an Industrial Session is a conference session within a scientific event's programme. They denote different concepts: one is an event type, the other a session type, with no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper), while B's `design` relates the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's hasLastName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's is_given_to is an object property mapping an Item to a Person (an item being given/assigned to a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Industry Organization is a for-profit/commercial organization, a sibling of Academia Organization, Government Organization and NGO under Organization. B's Research Institute is an academic institution, a sibling of University under Academic Institution. They denote different kinds of organizations (industry vs. academic), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has workshops' relates a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a whole-part/containment relation within a conference event structure). B's 'is equipped by' relates a Place to an Item (equipment located at a place). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A 'Regular Paper' is a kind of academic Paper (a document submitted/published at a conference), while B 'Mailing list' is a Document used for communication/administration in the conference organisation. They share no intended instances; the only overlap is the generic Document ancestor, which is not enough for equivalence.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee), while B's is_visited_by relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a place being visited by a person). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the directions differ, so they denote different relations.

A is an object property linking a conference part to a conference volume (part-whole relation between documents/volumes), while B is a datatype property giving the start date/time of a conference. They relate entirely different kinds of entities (Conference part -> Conference volume vs Conference -> dateTime) and have no overlap in meaning.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings with range int (the volume number of the proceedings), while B's 'City of conference' is a datatype property of Conference with range string (the city where the conference is held). They relate different kinds of things (proceedings volume number vs. conference location) and have different domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.

Programme in edas is a subclass of Document (a conference programme document, sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set), whereas Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (a person who presents documents, parent of Author and Invited Speaker). They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and have no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'has Conference Member' links a Conference to its members (a whole-part/roster relation), while B's 'parallel with' links two Administrative events that run concurrently. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a leadership role within a committee), while B's 'writtenBy' relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship of a paper). Different domains, ranges and meanings; they are not the same relation.
A's 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts, while B's 'has City' links an Organization or Person to a City. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

A's Person is a human agent (author, participant, reviewer) with properties like authorOf and writtenBy; B's Place is a physical location (conference hall, hotel, office) that a person can stay in. They denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an Administrator action whose range is a Conference (the administrator runs the paper-assignment process for a conference). B's 'give' is a generic Person-to-Activity/Item relation (e.g. giving a talk or an item). Different domains (Administrator vs Person), different ranges (Conference vs Activity/Item), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Paper Abstract in cmt is the abstract/summary document, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper. Conference Paper in ekaw is a broad class of paper submitted to a conference, with many specific paper types as siblings. They overlap in that a conference paper has an abstract, but they denote different concepts: one is the abstract artefact, the other is the full conference paper category. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's Published Paper is a paper that has been published (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Pending/Withdrawn Paper, i.e. a status of a paper in the review/publication workflow). B's Industrial Paper is a paper type/track (sibling of Regular Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Workshop Paper, Conference Paper), denoting papers from industry rather than a publication status. Different intended instances, so not equivalent.

A 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area / research topic in the EDAS taxonomy of conference topics, whereas B 'Video cassette player' is a concrete piece of audiovisual equipment (a device) in the iasted equipment inventory. They belong to entirely different branches (Topic vs Item/Audiovisual equipment) and denote different kinds of things (topic vs physical device), so they are not equivalent.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings). B's `lists Event` relates a Programme Brochure or Web Site to the Events it lists (domain Programme Brochure/Web Site, range Event). The domains and ranges are disjoint kinds of entities, so the properties do not denote the same relation.

hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (domain Paper, range Bid), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not the same relation.

A's Decision is the outcome of a review (children Acceptance/Rejection, range of has Decision from Paper), while B's Call is a call for papers/manuscripts/reviews issued by chairs with submission deadlines and instructions. They denote different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties are inverses, not equivalents: Conference's 'has a review' goes from Reviewed contribution to Review, while ekaw's 'review Of Paper' goes from Review to Paper. They relate the same kinds of things but in opposite directions, so a reference alignment would not record them as equivalent.

Both ontologies define an 'Invited Speaker' class under Person, with the same label and the same intended meaning: a person who gives an invited talk at the conference. In ekaw it is a subclass of Presenter (Conference Participant > Presenter > Invited Speaker); in sigkdd it is a subclass of Speaker (Person > Speaker > Invited Speaker). The slight difference in the intermediate parent (Presenter vs Speaker) does not change the intended instances, which coincide exactly. Thus the two classes are equivalent.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (declaring a conflict of interest in a paper/review), while B's is_paid_with relates Money to an Item (payment relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's email is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (contact address), while B's Price links a Registration fee to an int (monetary amount). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they share no concept.

A's NGO is a subclass of Organization (a non-governmental organisation type, sibling of Academia/Government/Industry Organization), while B's Sponsor is a subclass of Person (an individual who sponsors, sibling of Delegate). They denote different kinds of entities (organisation vs. person) and sit in different taxonomies, so they are not equivalent.

A's Accommodation Place is a kind of Place (lodging venue, sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), while B's Taxi is a kind of Transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Shuttle bus, Van). They denote different concepts: a lodging location versus a means of transport, with no overlap in instances or properties.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (sessions scheduled in parallel), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's hasHomePage links a Person to a URL/string of their homepage; B's hasBiography links a Person to a biographical text. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they capture different information (homepage URL vs. biography), so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference) under Event > Scientific Event, with siblings Session, Track, Workshop. B's One conference day is a time interval under Time > Conference days, with sibling Delegate. They denote different concepts (an event vs. a day of the event), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to an anyURI (a logo image address), while B's 'location Of' is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the inverse of an event's location). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Location), range (anyURI vs Event), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a collection of that reviewer's reviews), while B's reviewOfPaper links an individual Review to the Paper it reviews. Different domains (Reviewer vs Review), different ranges (Personal Review History vs Paper), and different intended relations; they are not equivalent.

A's Paper Abstract is a document type (a subclass of Paper, sibling of Paper Full Version) representing the abstract submission. B's Paper Presentation is an academic event (subclass of Academic Event, sibling of Talk Event/Workshop) representing the act of presenting a paper, with properties linking it to Accepted Paper. Different kinds (document vs event) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in cmt, while Track is a scientific event subdivision in ekaw; they belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote different concepts.

A's 'employed By' links a Person to an Organization (employment relation), while B's 'is paid for' links Money to an Activity or Item (payment relation). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while B's Platinum Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsoring organisation). They denote entirely different concepts: a person role vs. a sponsorship level, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Student lecturer' is a Lecturer who is also a student (a teaching role held by a student), while B's 'Author of paper' is a person who authors papers, sibling to 'Author of paper student'. Both sit under Author but denote different specialisations: one is a student who lectures, the other is a paper author. They overlap only in that both are Author subclasses, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Meta Reviewer in cmt is a strict specialization of Reviewer (its parent is Reviewer, and it is described as 'a special type of Reviewer' with additional duties). The edas Reviewer is the general reviewer role. Thus Meta Reviewer is subsumed by Reviewer, not equivalent.

A's University is an academic institution (a kind of organisation), while B's Presenter university is a building/place where a presenter stays, sibling to Conference hotel and Presenter house. They share only the word 'university' and denote different concepts (organisation vs. venue/building), so they are not equivalent.

confOf Event is a conference event (administrative/social/working) with start/end times, while iasted Item is a physical or informational object (equipment, card, document, publication, vehicle) that is given, paid for, or made from other items. Their children, properties and intended instances do not overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (domain Topic, range Review preference), while B's deals With links a Contribution to a Topic (domain Contribution, range Topic). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not inverses either, so they are unrelated.

A Program Committee Member in cmt is a specific role within the conference (a Conference Member who is on the PC, with properties like member Of Program Committee and max Papers), whereas confOf's Participant is a broad role covering all people participating in the conference (parents of Member, Regular, Student, Author, Chair PC, etc.). Every PC member is a participant, but not every participant is a PC member, so Program Committee Member is strictly more specific than Participant.

A's 'Committee member' is a Person (a role an individual plays on a committee), while B's 'Organization' is an institution with subclasses Company and University. They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A is a student registration fee (a fee category for students), while B is a registration fee for SIGMOD members. They are different fee categories: student status vs. SIGMOD membership. B's sibling 'Registration Student' is the counterpart of A, not B itself.

A's property links a Topic to a Conference part (a topical/part-of relation), while B's 'parallel with' links two Administrative events (a scheduling relation between concurrent events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a specific role class (a co-author of a contribution, sibling of 'Contribution 1th author') under 'Regular author', whereas B's 'Author' is the general author class (parent of 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student', with properties submit/obtain/notification). The co-author role is strictly narrower than the general Author concept, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole event type, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) that hosts the conference; B's Paper Presentation is a specific academic event within a conference (a talk/presentation of an accepted paper, sibling of Talk Event and Workshop). They denote different concepts: a conference is not a paper presentation, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an action of an agent on a whole conference), while B's 'has_parts' is a mereological property relating a Conference volume to its Conference parts. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'employed By' relates a Person (domain) to an Organization (range), i.e. employment. B's 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item (domain) to a Person (range), i.e. the person who gives/presents an activity. The domains, ranges and intended meanings differ, and they are not inverses of each other either, so they are unrelated.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper they author), whereas B's `paper In Volume` relates a paper to the volume/proceedings it appears in. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role in the conference organisation (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/Chair, linked to Conference via member Of Conference). B 'Fee' is a monetary amount (parent Money, children Registration fee/Hotel fee). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A Conference Dinner is a specific meal event, while B Social program is a broader conference activity that includes a Dinner banquet as a child. The Conference Dinner is thus a kind of social program activity, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A is 'Accepted Paper' (a paper that has been accepted, sibling of Rejected Paper, Pending Paper, etc. under Paper), while B is 'Rejected Paper' (a paper that has been rejected, under Evaluated Paper). They denote opposite review outcomes, so they are not equivalent; they are disjoint sibling concepts in the conference domain.

A's Person is the general superclass of all people in the conference domain (committee members, participants, reviewers, authors), while B's Student is a specific subclass of Person (path Person > Student, siblings include Paper Author, Possible Reviewer). Person is strictly more general than Student, so Person subsumes Student; they are not equivalent.

A's 'was a program committee of' links a Program committee to a Conference volume (the committee is a committee of a conference), while B's 'has Programme' links a Conference Event to a Programme (the event has a programme/schedule). The domains and ranges differ (Program committee vs Conference Event; Conference volume vs Programme), and the relations are not inverses of each other, so they denote different relations.

confOf's Social event is a subclass of Event covering Banquet, Reception and Trip, i.e. organised social gatherings. edas's Break Event is a subclass of Non Academic Event covering Coffee Break, Free Time Break and Meal Break, i.e. breaks in the programme. Both are non-academic conference events, so they overlap, but a coffee break is not a social event and a banquet is not a break; neither subsumes the other. edas's actual counterpart of Social event is its sibling Social Event, not Break Event.

A's Web Site is a Document (a published artefact such as a conference web page, with properties like event On List, lists Event, publisher Of), while B's Author information form is a Form (a document used to collect author data, sibling of Registration form and Hotel registration form). They share no intended instances and have different parents, siblings and properties, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) relation between a Conference volume and its Conference parts, whereas B's 'holded by' relates a Conference to the organising body ACM SIGKDD. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Both denote a full research paper submitted to a conference: A's Paper is a Regular contribution (sibling of Extended abstract) with an abstract, and B's Regular Paper is a kind of Paper (sibling of Poster Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). The intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

Company (confOf) is an Organization subtype representing a corporate entity, while Review (sigkdd) is a Document subtype representing a review of a paper. They belong to different branches (Organization vs Document) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop is a type of academic event (a gathering/session at a conference), while a Power Point presentation is a type of presentation activity (a talk delivered using slides). They belong to different branches (event vs. activity) and denote different concepts; a workshop is not a presentation format.

A's Tutorial is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation session), while B's Speaker is a person role who gives presentations. They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an activity) in ekaw, while B Conference hotel is a building/place in iasted. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. location) and are not synonyms in the conference domain.

Company in confOf is an organization (sibling of University, subclass of Organization), i.e. a commercial entity. Presenter university in iasted is a Building (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Presenter house, Sponsor company house), i.e. a physical venue. Different intended instances; unrelated.

A's `date` is a datatype property of Conference with range date (a date value), while B's `Name of conference` is a datatype property of Conference with range string (the conference's name). They share only the domain; the intended relations (date vs. name) are different, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'Submission event' is the administrative event of submitting contributions, while iasted's 'Accepting manuscript' is the activity of accepting a manuscript (sibling of Receiving/Refusing manuscript). They belong to the same submission/decision workflow but denote different stages: submission vs. acceptance. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

A's Break Event is a non-academic conference event (a pause: coffee break, meal break, free time), while B's Presentation is an academic conference activity (a talk, with PowerPoint/video subtypes). They belong to different branches (Non Academic Event vs Conference activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to a Contribution (the reviewing relation), while B's `submit until` relates a Document to a Deadline (a submission deadline). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Industrial Paper is a subclass of Paper (a full paper type in ekaw), while Abstract in sigkdd is a distinct document type sibling to Paper and Review, not a kind of paper. They denote different concepts.

A's 'Call For Reviews' is a call document (a subclass of Call, sibling of Call For Papers/Manuscripts), i.e. an announcement soliciting reviews. B's 'Review' is a document type (subclass of Document, sibling of Paper/Abstract), i.e. the review itself. One is a call for reviews, the other is a review; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (an assignment action), while B's isReviewHistoryOf relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (a record's back-reference). Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person who finalizes paper assignment), while B's 'scientifically Organises' relates an Academic Institution to an unspecified range (an institution scientifically organises an event). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Committee member' is a Person subtype (a role in the conference organisation, with children Chair/Co chair and properties linking to Committee), while B's 'Place' is a spatial location class (children Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, etc., with properties like is held in / is situated in). They denote entirely different concepts and share no instances.

Presenter (ekaw) is a Conference Participant who presents, with child Invited Speaker; Listener (iasted) is a Delegate who listens, sibling of Speaker. They denote opposite roles in the conference and are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which an accepted paper is presented), sitting under Conference Event > Academic Event with siblings Workshop, Talk Event, Organizational Meeting, and it is linked to Accepted Paper. B 'Programme Brochure' is a Document (a publication listing the programme), sibling of Paper, Review, Flyer, Web Site, and is linked to Event via eventOnList/listsEvent. One is an event, the other a document; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Building in iasted is a specific kind of physical location (a building) that is a subclass of Place; sigkdd's Place is the broader category of locations (its children include Conference hall, Hotel, Main office). A Building is a Place, but not every Place is a Building, so Building is subsumed by Place rather than equivalent.

A's hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its title string, while B's Nation links a Person to a nationality string. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Poster is a specific kind of conference contribution (a presentation format), while B's Paper is the general document submitted by an author. A Poster is a Paper in the broad sense, but the sigkdd Paper class is more general (it also covers regular papers, etc.), so Poster is subsumed by Paper rather than equivalent.

A's 'has a publisher' relates a Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the publishing body of the proceedings), while B's 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (a person preparing some item, e.g. a paper). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

City in confOf is a location entity (range of has City for Organization/Person), while Contact Information in edas is a contact-details class with properties for city, email, phone, postal code and street. The edas class merely contains a city field; it is not the city itself, so the two classes are not equivalent.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to a Contribution (a person reviews a paper), while B's `is paid for` relates Money to an Activity or Item (a payment covers something). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

attendeeAt relates a Person to the Conference Event they attend (Person -> Conference Event), while organisedBy relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it (Event -> Organisation/Person). The directions and the kinds of things related are different: one is attendance, the other is organisation, and they are not inverses either (inverse of attendeeAt would be attendedBy, not organisedBy).

A's 'Registeered applicant' is a subclass of Conference applicant (a person who has registered, with child Paid applicant), i.e. a registration-status role. B's 'Presenter' is a subclass of Conference Participant denoting someone who presents a paper, with child Invited Speaker and siblings like Session Chair, Early/Late Registered Participant. The two denote different roles in the conference domain (registration status vs. presentation role), so they are not equivalent.
A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee; B's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author. Different domain, range and intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

Author is a person who writes/submits papers (subclass of Conference Member/User, with properties write Paper, submit Paper, has Author). Organizer is a person who organizes the conference (chair/organizing role), a different role in the conference domain. They are distinct concepts, not synonyms, and neither subsumes the other.

Both denote the person who chairs the program committee: cmt's Program Committee Chair is a Chairman and Program Committee Member who reviews (end Review), and confOf's Chair PC is a Person role in the conference organization (confTool). Same intended instances, so equivalent.

cmt:Paper is the general paper class (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with authors, reviews, decisions), while ekaw:Industrial Paper is a specific paper type under ekaw:Paper, sibling to Conference Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, etc. The cmt class is strictly more general, so it subsumes the ekaw class rather than being equivalent to it.

A's 'Invitation letter' is a Document (an artefact sent to invitees), while B's 'Author' is a Person/Speaker who writes papers. They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.
A's name is a general datatype property for Conference and Person, while B's has an ISBN is specific to Conference proceedings; they relate different kinds of things and are not the same relation.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property giving the title (string) of a Social/Working event, while B's 'done till' is a datatype property giving the date by which a Deadline is done. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.
