A's 'Program committee' is a committee (a group/body) that a conference volume has, with siblings Organizing committee and Steering committee. B's 'Program Committee member' is a person role under Organizator, sibling of General Chair and Program Chair. A committee and an individual member of that committee are different concepts (group vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (a person/role on the committee), while B's belongsToEvent relates a Programme to a Conference Event. Different domains (Conference vs Programme) and different ranges (Conference Member vs Conference Event), so the relations do not coincide.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chair of the conference, under Person > Chairman), while Tutorial is a working event (under Event > Working event). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Author in cmt is a specific role (a person who writes/submits papers, with properties like write Paper, submit Paper, has Author), while ekaw's Conference Participant is a broader class covering all attendees (chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.). An Author is a kind of conference participant, but not every conference participant is an author, so Author is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Conference Participant.
A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while B's 'design' links an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline. Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip), while B's Research is an activity (child of Activity before conference, with children Modelling and Simulating). They denote different concepts in the conference domain.

A's hasStreet is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string street address, while B's heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

Conference document is a broad class covering calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc., with properties like contributes, has a date of issue, and has authors. Award is a specific recognition entity with children such as Best Research Paper Award and properties award, awarded by, and obtain. Their intended instances do not coincide; an award is not a kind of conference document, and a conference document is not an award.

A's Social Event is a subclass of Event (a social gathering such as a banquet or trip), while B's Speaker is a subclass of Person (someone who gives a presentation). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (event vs. person) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Abstract is a generic abstract that is part of a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a regular contribution's extended abstract), while B's Invited Talk Abstract is a specific subclass of Abstract for invited talks, sibling to Tutorial Abstract. They denote different concepts: one is a general abstract artefact, the other a talk-specific abstract type.

A's 'has important dates' is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity (a set of deadlines), while B's 'start Date' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a single dateTime value. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Conference volume vs Conference) and range (Important dates vs dateTime), so they do not denote the same relation.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the person hierarchy), while B is a conference document (Call for participation, a subclass of Conference document). They denote entirely different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference part is a broad container for Track, Tutorial and Workshop (parts of a conference volume), while B's Conference Session is a scheduled session within an academic event that can be linked to documents and persons. Both are sub-units of a conference, so they overlap, but a session is not a track/tutorial/workshop part and the property contexts (parts of conference volumes vs. related documents) differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference airport' is a physical building/place (a subtype of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference restaurant, etc.) used as a venue location. B's 'Conference' is the event itself, with properties for city, start/end dates, name, and being held by ACM SIGKDD. A place and an event are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative event (sibling of Submission/Reviewing/Camera Ready events) covering the participant registration process, while B's 'Organizational Meeting' is an academic event (sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop) denoting a meeting held at the conference. Different parents (Administrative vs Academic Event), different siblings, and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'was a committe co chair of' relates a Co chair to a Committee (a role/committee-membership relation, subproperty of 'was a member of'), whereas B's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (authorship). Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's Organization is a conference-domain class for an organizing body (institution/society), while B's Item is a very broad top-level class covering physical/abstract things (Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle) with properties like 'is made from', 'is paid with', 'is equipped by'. Organization is not a kind of Item and the two do not denote the same concept.

A's 'is made from' relates Items to Items (a part/derivation relation within the same class), while B's 'obtain' relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track (a structural part-of relation within a conference), while B's 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place/Time (attendance at an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property giving a string title to Social/Working events, while B's 'has End Date Time' gives a dateTime end to a Conference Event. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning (title vs. end time), so they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference Dinner' is a meal event (a social/academic event in the conference programme), while B 'Conference restaurant' is a building/place where meals may be served. They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Place) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's Trip is a social event involving an excursion/travel, while B's Reception is a standing social gathering (sibling of Excursion). They are distinct social-event types; Trip corresponds to edas Excursion, not Reception.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (who prints hardcopy mailing manifests), while B's property relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (the proceedings it issues). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property of Review preference expressing the degree/strength of a reviewer's preference, while B's 'Price' is a datatype property of Registration fee expressing a monetary amount. Although both have range int, their domains (Review preference vs Registration fee) and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

A 'Track workshop chair' is a person who chairs a track, workshop, or tutorial (a Conference part), while B 'Session Chair' is a person who chairs a session and initiates calls/reviews papers. Both are chair roles under Person, but they cover different organisational units (track/workshop/tutorial vs. session) and have different associated properties, so they are related chair roles rather than equivalent.

A's contributes relates a Person to a Conference document (authoring/submitting a paper), while B's pay relates a Person to a Registration fee (paying to attend). Different ranges and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' (a paper/poster/talk submitted to a venue), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself, with properties like start/end date, city, and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. A contribution is not a conference event; the entities denote different concepts.

A's `name` is a general name property applying to both Conference and Person, while B's `has the last name` is specifically the surname of a Person. The general name property subsumes the more specific last-name property, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the conference event itself: cmt's Conference has members, dates, submission handling and administrator details; sigkdd's Conference has name, city, start/end dates and is held by an ACM SIGKDD. Same intended instances (conferences), so they are equivalent despite differing property sets.

Associated Chair is a conference committee role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member who helps organise the conference), while Sponsor is a person or organisation providing financial support. Their paths, parents and siblings differ (Chairman/Conference Member vs Person/Delegate), and the roles are conceptually distinct, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (things that happen), while B's 'Deadline' is a submission/notification deadline with a date, not an event type. Different intended instances and no subsumption relation.

A's Event is the general conference event class (children: Administrative, Social, Working event), while B's Social Event is a specific kind of non-academic event (children: Excursion, Reception; siblings: Break Event, Meal Event). Social Event is a narrower concept than Event, so Event subsumes Social Event; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference, Tutorial, Workshop (organisational events with topics, titles, choices). B's 'Non speaker' is a subclass of Delegate covering Student/Worker non speakers (a kind of attendee). The two denote different concepts in different branches of the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic in the EDAS taxonomy of conference subject areas (a kind of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Communications Topic, etc.), while B is a physical item type in the IASTED ontology (a kind of Item with child Credit card, sibling of Document, Publication, Transport vehicle). They share no meaning in the conference domain; the word overlap is only incidental.

A's Science Worker is a general person role (sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant) under Person, while B's Student lecturer is a very specific academic role nested under Lecturer > Author > Speaker > Delegate, so the two denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's Document is a broad class of conference documents (Abstract, Paper, Review, Web Site, etc.) authored by Persons. B's Form is a specific kind of Document (a fillable/administrative form such as Registration form, Hotel registration form) under Item > Document. Although both are documents, the intended instances do not coincide: A's Document covers papers and reviews, not administrative forms, and B's Form is a narrow administrative artefact. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in the intended sense.

A's Student is a subclass of Person denoting a person enrolled in study, with siblings like Paper Author and Possible Reviewer; B's Author of paper is a subclass of Author (itself under Speaker) denoting a person who authored a paper. The two concepts are orthogonal: a Student need not author a paper, and an Author of paper need not be a student. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's 'Short paper' is a submission-type contribution (sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution), i.e. a short version of a paper submitted to a conference. B's 'Accepted Paper' is a stage in the review workflow (a paper that passed evaluation, sibling of Rejected Paper under Evaluated Paper). They denote different concepts: one is a kind of contribution, the other a review outcome. A short paper could be accepted or rejected, and an accepted paper could be full-length, so neither subsumes the other.

A's writtenBy relates a Review to its Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (domain Author, range Contribution). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent; at best they are inverses of different relations, not the same relation.

A's `lists Event` relates a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event (a document listing events), while B's `is given by` relates an Activity/Item to a Person (an activity being presented by a person). Different domains and ranges, different intended relations; not equivalent.

A's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (a person role), while B's 'initiates' links a Conference Chair/Session Chair/TPC Member to a Call (an event/call for papers). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class describing a reviewer's expertise/preference area (domain of 'belongs to reviewers', range of 'has a review reference or expertise' from Reviewer). B's 'Contribution' is a submitted work (Paper/Poster/Short paper) with title, abstract, keywords, written by an Author. The two denote different concepts: one is an expertise/interest descriptor, the other is a submission artefact. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's Invited speaker is a specific conference contributor role (sibling of Regular author and Active conference participant), while B's Author is a broad class under Speaker with many subclasses (Lecturer, Tutorial speaker, Plenary lecture speaker, etc.). An invited speaker is typically an author who gives an invited talk, so the concepts overlap but neither subsumes the other: not all authors are invited speakers, and B's Author is not restricted to invited speakers. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's startReviewerBidding is an Administrator action that opens reviewer bidding for a Conference; B's need relates a Person to an Item (a requirement). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B is a document type (Brief introduction for Session chair) under Document in iasted. One denotes a committee member, the other a piece of text, so they are unrelated.

cmt:User is a general person role in the conference system, with subclasses Administrator, Author, Reviewer and siblings such as Chairman and Program Committee Member. sigkdd:Speaker is a person who gives a presentation (domain of presentation to Document), with subclasses Author and Invited Speaker and sibling Listener. The intended instances do not coincide: a User need not be a Speaker, and a Speaker need not be a User in the cmt sense. They share only the parent Person, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic, while B's hasTopic links a Working event to a Topic. Different domains (Review preference vs Working event) and different ranges (Submitted contribution/Topic vs Topic), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's Review Question is a question/field on a review form (with numerical and textual subtypes), while B's Review is a document (a subclass of Document, sibling of Abstract and Paper) representing the review itself. A review question is not a review document; the entities denote different concepts.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/member of the conference committee) in cmt, while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (a building/venue location) in iasted. They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. location) and share no intended instances.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who started the bidding process), while B's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (inviting co-reviewers). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'adjusted By' links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it (domain Bid, range Reviewer). B's 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History record to the Reviewer it belongs to (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer). Although both have range Reviewer, the domains are entirely different concepts (a Bid vs. a review-history record), and the relations express different meanings (who adjusted a bid vs. whose review history a record is). They are not the same relation.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authoring/submitting a paper), while B's 'pay' relates a Person to Money (paying a fee). Different ranges and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event/activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas B's 'Cd proceening' is a publication item (a CD proceedings, sibling of Book proceeding). They belong to different branches (Event vs Publication) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's University is an academic organization where scholars study (domain of 'study At'), while B's Proceedings Publisher is an organization that publishes proceedings; they are different kinds of organizations with no overlap in intended instances.

A's email is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address), while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item (acquiring an item). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no shared meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'name' is a datatype property giving a string name for a Conference or Person, while B's 'has Start Date Time' gives a dateTime start time for a Conference Event. They relate different kinds of entities to different value types (string vs dateTime) and denote different relations, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an activity) in the conference domain, while B Presenter house is a building/place where a presenter stays. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. place) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area of conference papers (a subclass of Topic), while B 'LCD projector' is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a subclass of Audiovisual equipment). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's property links an Important dates entity to a Conference volume (a publication/volume concept), while B's 'need' links a Person to an Item. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's isInitiatedBy relates a Call to people (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) who initiate the call, while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document they present. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

An edas Conference Session is a slot/grouping of presentations within a conference, while an ekaw Individual Presentation is a single talk (with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial) that is presented at a session. They are closely related (a session contains presentations) but not the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Invited Speaker' is a Person (a Presenter subtype, i.e. a person who gives an invited talk), while B's 'Speaker lecture' is an Activity (a Session subtype, i.e. a lecture/session event). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. event), so they are not equivalent; at most they are loosely related by the speaking event, but the intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a conference contributor role (a person invited to speak), while B's 'Author book proceedings included' is a specific author subtype whose papers are included in the book of proceedings. They are different concepts: an invited speaker is not necessarily an author of proceedings papers, and an author of proceedings papers is not necessarily an invited speaker. They overlap only in that both can be persons involved in a conference, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

A's 'accepted By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's 'scientifically Organises' relates an Academic Institution to something it organises (e.g. an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address), while B's 'authorOf' is an object property linking a Person to a Document (authorship relation). They have different ranges (string vs Document) and denote entirely different relations, so they are unrelated.

A's Published Paper is a specific state of a Paper (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Pending Paper), i.e. a paper that has been published. B's Submission is a document submitted to the conference, with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript, i.e. the submitted material before/at review. A published paper is not a submission (it is the post-acceptance, published artefact), and a submission is not necessarily published. They overlap in that both concern papers in the conference process, but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so 'related' is the safest non-equivalent relation.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant under Conference applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity before the conference (the act of accepting a submitted paper). They belong to different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Call for participation' is a general conference document inviting participation (siblings include Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.), while B's 'Call For Manuscripts' is a specific call for paper submissions under the 'Call' parent, sibling to Call For Papers and Call For Reviews. They overlap in the call-for-submissions sense but are not the same concept: a call for participation is broader than a call for manuscripts.

A's 'enter Conference Details' is an object property from Administrator to Conference (an action of an administrator entering conference details), while B's 'Name of conference' is a datatype property from Conference to string (a data attribute giving the conference's name). They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Administrator vs Conference), and range (Conference vs string), so they do not denote the same relation.

Country is a geographical entity used as the range of an organization/person's country property, while Conference is an event with dates, city, name and an organizing ACM SIGKDD. They share no instances or meaning; the pair is a false positive.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a Person who applies to a conference and has a child 'Registeered applicant' (a registered applicant), while B's 'Early Registered Participant' is a Conference Participant who registered early. Both concern people registering for a conference, but A is the broader applicant/registration role (with a registered-applicant child) and B is a specific early-registration participant subtype; they overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to reviewers/committee members (domain Paper, range people roles), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item) — different direction and different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's Person is a human agent (committee members, reviewers, authors, participants) with name/email/gender and authorship relations. B's Organization is an institutional entity (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provides sponsorships. The two classes have disjoint instance sets and no shared properties, so they are unrelated.

A's Regular is a Participant subtype (a person who is a regular participant, sibling of Member and Student), while B's Sponsor is a Person subtype denoting a sponsoring person/organisation, sibling of Delegate. Different intended concepts; no subsumption or overlap.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class for people involved in a conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), whereas Paid applicant in Conference is a narrow subclass of registered conference applicant who has paid. The two concepts have different intents and different positions in their taxonomies; they are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's volumeContainsPaper relates a volume to the papers it contains (part-whole containment of documents in a proceedings volume). B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presents a document). Different domain/range kinds and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (domain Committee, range Chair), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (domain Author, range Contribution). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has Title' is a datatype property of Contribution giving the title of a paper/contribution. Different domains (Person vs Contribution) and different intended values (surname vs title), so they are not the same relation.

confOf Member is a Participant subtype (alongside Regular and Student), i.e. a conference attendee/registrant category. sigkdd Organizing Committee member is an Organizator subtype (alongside General Chair, Program Chair, etc.), i.e. a role in the organizing committee. Different parent branches (Participant vs Organizator) and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Program Committee Member is a Person who is a member of a program committee (a role/agent class with properties like max Papers, member Of Program Committee), whereas Conference:Program committee is the committee itself (a Committee, with properties has a program committee / was a program committee of). The member is not the committee; the member class is subsumed by the committee concept only in the loose sense that a member belongs to a committee, so the correct relation is subsumed_by (the member is a part/role of the committee, not equivalent to it).

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the person a paper is assigned to for review), while B's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract (its summary text). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

Author (cmt) is a conference-domain person role who writes/submits papers, while State (iasted) is a geographical/administrative region occupied by or visited by persons. Different domains and no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

A's `date` is a datatype property of a Conference giving its date; B's `has a location` is a datatype property of a Conference volume giving a string location. Different domains (Conference vs Conference volume) and different intended values (date vs location), so they are not the same relation.

A's max Papers is a datatype property of Program Committee Member giving the maximum number of papers a PC member may handle; B's has amount of is a datatype property of Money giving a monetary amount. Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome of a submission). B's is_held_in relates an Activity to a Place/Time (where and when an event takes place). Different domains (Paper vs Activity) and different ranges (Decision vs Place/Time), so the two properties denote different relations.

A's Invited Speaker is a subtype of Presenter (a person who gives a talk), while B's Non speaker is a subtype of Delegate denoting someone who does not give a talk. They are near-opposites in the conference domain, not equivalent.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (the administrator enters review criteria for a conference), while B's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to a person role (a paper is reviewed by a reviewer/chair). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Track is a conference part (a thematic session track, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, linked from Conference volume via has tracks). B's Fee is a monetary charge (subclass of Money, with children Registration fee, Hotel fee, Fee for extra trip). They share no meaning, no properties, and no context; a track is not a fee.

Both are social/after-conference activities involving a trip/tour, but ekaw's Conference Trip is a Social Event (a subclass of Event) while iasted's Full day tour is an Activity after conference; the categories (Event vs Activity) and the specific scope (conference social trip vs post-conference full-day tour) differ, so they overlap but are not the same concept.

A's Workshop Chair is a conference participant who chairs a workshop (sibling of Demo Chair, Tutorial Chair, etc.), while B's Session chair is a delegate who chairs a session. Different roles in the conference organisation; neither subsumes the other.

A's Excursion is a social event (sibling of Reception) within Non Academic Event, while B's Coctail reception is a conference activity (sibling of Coffee break, Lecture, etc.) and not classified as a social event. They denote different kinds of conference-domain entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a specific organizational role within the conference), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a generic giving relation, e.g. giving a talk or item). The domains (Chair vs Person) and ranges (Committee vs Activity/Item) differ, and the intended relations are different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (a subclass of Social Event, sibling of Conference Trip) held during a conference. B's 'Trip city' is a subclass of City describing a city associated with a trip, sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city. One is an event, the other a location/city; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (authorship relation), while B's 'is Provider Of' links an Organization to a Sponsorship (sponsorship relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (domain Program Committee, range Program Committee Member), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair). B's 'Presenter city' is a subclass of City, i.e. a location associated with presenters, not a person or role. The entities denote different kinds of things (person role vs. city), so they are unrelated.

A Conference Banquet is a social event (sibling of Conference Trip under Social Event), while B Technic activity is a technical conference activity (sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break, etc. under Conference activity). They denote different kinds of events/activities and are not equivalent.

Author is a subclass of Person (a person who writes contributions), while Document is a class of written artefacts (with subclasses Paper, Review, Abstract, etc.). They denote different kinds of things: one is an agent, the other an information object. Although Author is linked to Document via writes/written By, the classes themselves are not equivalent.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is an event type (Tutorial, a kind of Individual Presentation). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

A is a document type (the abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B is a subject-area topic in a topic taxonomy (a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

Sponsorship is a funding arrangement class in edas (with provider, cost amount and cost currency properties), while Currency in iasted is a monetary unit class. They denote different concepts; the only connection is that Sponsorship has a cost currency attribute, which is not equivalence.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a Conference contributor (a person who gives an invited talk), while B's 'Non speaker' is a Delegate who does not speak, with children Student/Worker non speaker. The two denote opposite roles (speaker vs. non-speaker) and sit in different hierarchies, so they are not equivalent.

A's Break Event is a non-academic event covering coffee/meal/free-time breaks, while B's Social Event covers banquet and trip; they are distinct subclasses of the event hierarchy with no overlap in intended instances.

A's 'author Of' is an object property linking a Person to a Document (authorship relation), while B's 'E mail' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and denote entirely different relations, so they are unrelated.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume, i.e. the committee that organizes a conference event/volume. B's 'technicallyOrganised By' is a sub-property of 'organised By' and denotes the technical (programme) organization of a conference, typically by a person or institution, not a committee-to-volume relation. The two overlap in the general notion of organizing a conference but differ in domain/range and specificity, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Invited talk is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a document-like contribution given by invitation), while B's Speaker lecture is a session within a lecture activity, i.e. a scheduled event/session rather than a contribution type. They both concern a talk given by a speaker, so they overlap in the conference domain, but their ontological roles (contribution vs. session) differ, so they are not equivalent.

edas hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper they are related to (e.g. authored/co-authored), while ekaw referencedIn relates a paper to the paper that cites it (inverse of cites). Both concern paper-to-paper/author-to-paper citation-like links but differ in direction and argument types, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a conference-organisation event class (parent of submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration events) in confOf, while B is a subject-area topic (Computer Networks Applications) in edas. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role (a subclass of Person, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc., and properties linking it to a Conference). B 'Activity after conference' is a subclass of Activity (an event/temporal activity, with children Departure and Full day tour). They denote fundamentally different kinds of things (person vs. event/activity), so they are unrelated.

A is a deadline date (abstract submission date, domain Important dates, range date), while B is textual submission instructions (domain Call, range string). Different kinds of things and different directions of meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'read By Meta Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (who reads it), while B's 'belongs to a review reference' relates a Topic to a Review preference. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both classes sit under Paper and denote the final, complete version of a paper: cmt's Paper Full Version is the full paper as opposed to the Paper Abstract, and ekaw's Camera Ready Paper is the final version submitted for publication. In the conference domain these coincide as the finished full paper, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's `send` is an object property from Person to Item (sending some item/paper), while B's `E mail` is a datatype property from Person to string (an email address). They share the Person domain and both concern communication, but the ranges differ (Item vs string) and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent; they are only loosely related.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), i.e. a symmetric co-occurrence relation between events. B's 'lists Event' relates a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event, i.e. a document-to-event listing relation. Different domains, different ranges, different direction and meaning; they are not the same relation.

A is a class representing a person's personal publication history (a history/record of publications by a person), while B is a Review document class in the iasted ontology. They denote different concepts: one is a history of publications, the other is a review document. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are named Document, but they denote different concepts. In edas, Document is a broad class whose children are Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, Meal Menu, and it is linked to academic events, conferences, sessions and persons via has Related Document / relates To. In iasted, Document is a subclass of Item and its children are administrative artefacts such as Form, Invitation letter, Mailing list, Payment document, Record of attendance, Submission, Viza, Brief introduction for Session chair, Review, Transparency. The two classes overlap only partially (e.g. Review appears under both) and neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Organization is a general class for institutions/organisations (e.g. the body an author is affiliated with), whereas B's Organizing Committee member is a role a Person plays in a conference (a subclass of Organizator, sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote different kinds of entities (organisation vs. person-role), so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document type (a written contribution with reviews, authors, presentation), while B's Audiovisual equipment is a physical item category (projectors, computers, video players) under Item. They share no intended instances and no domain role; the only overlap is the generic word 'equipment/paper' being artefacts, which is not enough.

A's External Reviewer is a person assigned to review papers for another reviewer (a role in the review process, with assign/assignedBy properties to Reviewer). B's Scholar is a person in a price category who studies at a university (a fee/registration category, with studyAt property). The intended instances and contexts differ: one is a reviewing role, the other a registration/fee category, so they are not equivalent.

A's Session Chair is a generic person role that chairs a session (siblings include Conference Chair, Reviewer, TPC Member; it initiates Calls and reviews Papers). B's Demo Chair is a specific conference-participant role for chairing demo sessions, sibling to Session Chair, Workshop Chair, Tutorial Chair, PC Chair. They are distinct roles, not synonyms; B even has a separate Session Chair class, confirming Demo Chair is a different concept.

A's title is the title of a Paper (a document's name), while B's has VAT is the value-added-tax amount of a Social/Working event. Different domains (Paper vs event), different intended meaning; only the datatype string range is shared.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (a person entering conference data), while B's 'has a track workshop tutorial topic' relates a Conference part to a Topic (a structural containment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad class covering all people taking part in a conference (its children include Active/Passive conference participant, and its siblings include Committee member, Reviewer, etc.). B's 'Speaker' is a narrower class under 'Delegate' whose children are Author and Reviewer, i.e. only people who present/speak. Every Speaker is a conference participant, but not every conference participant is a Speaker, so Conference participant is more general and is subsumed by Speaker's broader counterpart, not equivalent.

cmt:User is a Person subclass whose children are roles (Administrator, Author, Reviewer) — a generic system user/role holder. confOf:Member is a Participant subclass (siblings Regular, Student) denoting a registered conference participant category. Both are person-role classes but neither subsumes the other: User covers administrative/authoring roles, Member covers participation/registration status. They overlap in that a conference member is typically a user, but the intended instances do not coincide, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Conference Participant' is a subclass of Person (a human role: chairs, presenters, authors, attendees), while B's 'Activity before conference' is a subclass of Activity (a process/event such as receiving or accepting manuscripts). They belong to disjoint top-level categories (Person vs Activity) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Conference part is a structural component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) in the Conference ontology, whereas OC Member is a person role (Organising Committee member) in ekaw. Their instances are disjoint (events vs. people), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an abstract' relates a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract; B's 'designed by' relates a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Tutorial is a kind of conference part/event (sibling of Track and Workshop, with has tutorials from Conference volume), whereas B's Programme is a Document (sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set) that belongs to a Conference Event. A tutorial is an event/session, not a document, so the two classes denote different concepts.

A's 'Call for participation' is a conference document announcing participation, while B's 'Call' is a broader class covering calls for manuscripts, papers and reviews, with properties linking it to events, deadlines and chairs. A is a narrower kind of call, so it is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's Author is a person role (subclass of Person) who writes contributions; B's Author information form is a document/form artefact (subclass of Form) used for author details. Different kinds of entities, so not equivalent.

A's has Subject Area links a Paper to its Subject Area (topic), while B's has tracks links a Conference volume to a Track (a subdivision of the conference). Different domains (Paper vs Conference volume), different ranges (Subject Area vs Track), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (the author), while B's 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (a person signs an item). The domains and ranges are reversed and the intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent.

A is a placeholder/test topic in the EDAS topic taxonomy (a conference subject area), while B is a physical transport vehicle category in the iasted item taxonomy with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van. They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's Review is a document produced in the conference peer-review process (child of Document, sibling of Paper, written by a Reviewer, subject of Meta Review), while B's Value added tax is a subclass of Tax under Money, a financial concept with no connection to the conference domain. They share no meaning.

A's Conference is the conference event itself (has a name, has a Conference volume, part, proceedings, publisher, topic), while B's Place is a physical location (children Accommodation, Conference Venue, Dining, Meeting Room; has Location / is Location Of a Conference Event). A conference is not a place; the entities denote different concepts.

A's 'has a publisher' links a Conference proceedings to a Publisher (a publication relation), while B's 'follows' links one Administrative event to another Administrative event (a temporal/ordering relation between events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'deals With' relates a Contribution to a Topic (a paper is about a subject), while B's 'is paid with' relates Money to an Item (a payment is made using something). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a chairing role (child of Chairman, sibling of Program Committee Chair), i.e. a person who chairs the conference. B's 'Member PC' is explicitly commented as 'Reviewer' and has properties expertOn(Topic) and reviewes(Contribution), i.e. a program-committee member/reviewer. These are distinct conference roles, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'has a name' is a generic naming datatype property whose domain spans Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, with range string. B's 'registration Due On' is a specific deadline property with domain Conference and range dateTime, described as the conference registration date/time deadline. They relate different kinds of things (a name vs. a deadline) and have incompatible ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the person a paper is assigned to for reviewing), while B's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (the person who wrote it). These are different relations in the conference domain: reviewing assignment vs. authorship, with different domains (Paper vs. Contribution) and ranges (Reviewer vs. Author). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to the Event held there (domain Location, range Event). B's 'is used for' relates an Item to the Activity or Money it is used for (domain Item, range Activity/Money). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Academic Event is a scholarly event (conference, workshop, talk, paper presentation) with a Call and related documents; B's Conference activity is a broader Activity covering social and technical activities (coffee break, registration, social program) as well as lectures/presentations. Academic Event is a narrower, more specific notion than the general Conference activity, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's property links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (organisational role relation), while B's presentation links a Speaker to a Document (a talk/presentation relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A 'Performance Topic' is a subject area / topic category in the EDAS taxonomy (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), i.e. a classification of paper subject matter. B 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of scientific event / individual presentation (sibling of Invited Talk, Tutorial) in the EKAW event hierarchy. One is a topic, the other an event type; their intended instances do not coincide.

A is a member registration fee (fee category for members), while B is a student registration fee (fee category for students). They are distinct fee categories under Registration fee; a member fee is not a student fee, and neither subsumes the other.

Conference applicant is a Person who applies to register for a conference (parent Person, child Registered applicant), while ekaw Presenter is a Conference Participant who presents (parent Conference Participant, child Invited Speaker). Both are conference-domain person roles, but an applicant is not necessarily a presenter and a presenter need not be an applicant, so they overlap without being equivalent.

A's Chair is a committee member role (a person who chairs a committee, sibling of Co-chair, linked to Committee via chairing properties). B's Sponsor is a person who funds the conference, a sibling of Delegate under Person. Different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a kind of Chairman/Person) while B is a conference event (Coffee Break, a kind of Break Event). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (a call soliciting submissions), while B's 'Tutorial' is a working event held at a conference. They belong to different branches (document vs event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Medicine Topic is a specific topic (a subclass of Topic in edas), while Research Topic in ekaw is the general class of topics that events and papers cover. Medicine Topic is therefore a narrower concept subsumed by the broader Research Topic, not equivalent to it.

ekaw:Organisation is an agent (institution/agency/publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings, with properties like organises and publisher Of. sigkdd:Place is a physical location (conference hall, hotel, office) where a person can stay. Different intended instances and roles; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to an anyURI (a web address for the conference logo), while B's 'City of conference' links a Conference to a string naming the host city. They share only the domain (Conference) but have different ranges and completely different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an organized excursion for conference attendees), while a Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (a means of transportation). They belong to different branches (Event vs Item/Transport vehicle) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Paper' is a specific kind of paper (a document submitted to/published at a conference), while B 'Document' is a broad top-level class covering forms, invitations, mailing lists, reviews, submissions, etc. A Conference Paper is a Document, but not every Document is a Conference Paper, so A is strictly more specific than B (subsumed_by).

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the outcome of reviewing a paper). B's is_used_for relates an Item to an Activity or Money (a resource used for an activity or funding). The domains (Paper vs Item) and ranges (Decision vs Activity/Money) are disjoint, so the properties denote different relations.

Both are subclasses of Deadline representing the deadline for submitting papers: iasted's 'Submissions deadline' and sigkdd's 'Deadline Paper Submission' have the same parent (Deadline) and analogous siblings (camera-ready, notification, registration vs abstract submission, author notification). They denote the same conference-domain concept.

A's 'was a committe co chair of' relates a Co chair to a Committee (a role-membership relation, subproperty of 'was a member of'), while B's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (a spatiotemporal containment relation). Different domains, ranges and meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) property relating a Conference volume to its Conference parts, whereas B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that announces a conference. B 'Single Level Conference' is a kind of conference event (subclass of Conference, sibling of Two Level Conference), i.e. a conference without sub-events. The two denote different concepts: a document vs. an event type, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Short paper' is a kind of contribution (a submitted paper of short length). They denote different concepts: one is a call/announcement, the other a type of paper. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's Paper is a document type (subclass of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Deadline is a temporal milestone class (with a date and submission/notification deadlines). They denote different concepts and share no intended instances.

cmt:User is a general person role in the conference system (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while confOf:Regular is a specific participant category (sibling of Member and Student) under Participant. They denote different concepts: User is a broad system user, Regular is a non-student participant type. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's Excursion is a specific social event (sibling of Reception) under Social Event, while B's Social program is a broader conference activity that includes Dinner banquet, Coctail reception, etc. An excursion is a kind of social program activity, so Excursion is subsumed by Social program, not equivalent.

A Program Committee Chair is a specific role (a chair of the program committee, also a Program Committee Member), while B Committee member is the general class of anyone belonging to a committee, with Chair and Co chair as children. A PC Chair is a kind of committee member (specifically a chair), so A is strictly more specific than B: subsumed_by.

A's 'has an email' relates a Person to an email address string, while B's 'has Phone' relates a Person to a phone number string. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote different contact attributes (email vs. phone), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property mapping Contact Information to a string postal code; B's is_sent_before is an object property relating an Item to a Time. Different kinds (datatype vs object), different domains and ranges, and unrelated meanings in the conference domain.

A's Conference contributor is a broad Person subclass covering anyone contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants), while B's IASTED member is a specific Delegate subtype tied to IASTED membership. The paths, parents (Person vs Delegate), and sibling sets differ substantially, so the intended instances do not coincide.

A's hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (paper -> rating value), while B's reviewOfPaper relates a Review to a Paper (review -> paper). They differ in domain, range, and direction of the relation; they are not the same property nor inverses.

A Conference Banquet is a social event (a formal dinner) in the conference domain, while a Taxi is a transport vehicle used to travel to/from the conference. They belong to different branches (Event > Social Event vs Item > Transport vehicle) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a name' is a datatype property assigning a string name to entities like Conference, Publisher, Topic; B's 'speak in' is an object property relating a Person to a Place/Time. Different kinds (datatype vs object), different domains/ranges, and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call For Papers' is an announcement inviting submissions, a subclass of Call alongside Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews. B 'Review' is a Document (an artefact produced in the reviewing process), sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter, etc. The two denote different concepts: an invitation/announcement versus a review document. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Presenter in ekaw is a Conference Participant who presents, with child Invited Speaker; IASTED member in iasted is a Delegate subtype (a person affiliated with IASTED) with siblings like Speaker, Session chair, Hotel presenter. The two classes overlap in that presenters are typically IASTED members/delegates, but neither subsumes the other: not all presenters are IASTED members, and not all IASTED members present. Thus they are related, not equivalent.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a specific kind of regular contribution (a short/extended abstract submission), while B's 'Regular Paper' is the full regular paper category. They are distinct submission types in the conference domain, not synonyms; an extended abstract is not a regular paper.

A is a research topic class (a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic under Topic), while B is an organizational committee class (a subcategory of Committee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

cmt's assignedTo relates a Paper to the Reviewer assigned to review it, while iasted's is_given_by relates an Activity/Item to the Person who gives it (e.g. a presentation given by a speaker). Both link a work item to a person, but the direction of the roles differs: assignedTo is about review assignment, is_given_by about authorship/presentation. They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both are social events that are outings/trips: confOf Trip sits under Social event alongside Banquet and Reception, and edas Excursion sits under Social Event alongside Reception. Same domain concept of an organised excursion/trip during the conference, so they are equivalent.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'has tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts. Different domain (Conference vs Conference volume), different range (Administrator vs Tutorial), and different meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person role in the conference), while B's Student registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts: a person versus a fee.

A's Topic is the general subject area of a contribution, working event or PC member's expertise (dealsWith, expertOn, hasTopic). B's Communications Topic is a specific topic under the parent Topic in edas, one of many sibling topics (Antennas, CAD, etc.). Thus B is a narrower concept than A: A subsumes B, i.e. B is subsumed_by A.

A's property links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (organisational role for workshops/tutorials), while B's property links a Document to a Speaker (who presents a document). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Both are subclasses of Paper in the submission/review workflow: edas Active Paper is a paper that is active (not yet accepted/rejected/withdrawn) and has a rating, while ekaw Assigned Paper is a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer and leads to Evaluated Paper. They overlap in the review process but are not the same concept: Active Paper is defined by its lifecycle state (still under consideration), Assigned Paper by having been assigned for review. Neither subsumes the other cleanly, so 'related' is the safest verdict.

A 'Social program' is a conference activity (a social event such as a dinner banquet) under Conference activity, while B 'Speaker' is a person role under Person. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Decision is the outcome of a paper's review (children Acceptance/Rejection, range of hasDecision from Paper). edas:ReviewRating is a reviewer's rating value (children Accept/Reject/Weak Reject ratings, range of hasRating from Active Paper). Both concern accept/reject outcomes, but one is the final decision on a paper and the other is a rating assigned during review; they overlap in the accept/reject vocabulary but are not the same concept.

A's hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a paper). B's prepare relates a Person to an Item (a person preparing an item, e.g. a presentation or material). Different domains (Paper vs Person), different ranges (Author vs Item), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (a requirement/dependency relation), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker giving a presentation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference state' is a state/status of a conference (sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state under State), i.e. a situation or phase, whereas B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself with city, start/end dates, name and holding relations. The two denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Topic is the general subject area of a contribution, working event or PC member's expertise (confTool). B's Medicine Topic is a specific instance of the Topic class in edas (a child of Topic, alongside Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). Thus B is strictly narrower than A: every Medicine Topic is a Topic, but not vice versa. The relation is subsumed_by (A is more general than B), not equivalence.

Acceptance is a subclass of Decision (the outcome of a review, sibling of Rejection) in cmt, while Listener is a subclass of Person (a conference participant who listens, sibling of Organizator and Speaker) in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (decision outcome vs. person role) and share no intended instances.

A's hasTopic goes from Working event to Topic (event -> topic), while B's isTopicOf goes from Topic to Conference/Paper (topic -> event/paper). They are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.
Speaker is a subclass of Person in sigkdd (path Person > Speaker), so every Speaker is a Person but not vice versa; Person is strictly more general than Speaker.

A 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses like author, speaker, reviewer), while B 'Sponsor city' is a subclass of City (a city that sponsors a conference). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs City) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers), while B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (a member/participant). Different domain (volume vs conference) and different range (contribution vs person), so the relations do not coincide.

Conference participant is a general class for anyone participating in a conference, with subclasses Active/Passive conference participant. Workshop Chair in ekaw is a specific role (a kind of Conference Participant and PC Member). Thus the A class is strictly more general than the B class: A subsumes B, they are not equivalent.

A's property is a specific deadline (camera-ready paper submission date) within the Important dates class, while B's Date is the generic date property of a Deadline. The generic Deadline Date subsumes the specific camera-ready submission date, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A is a conference topic (a subject area for papers, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a conference activity type (a kind of lecture/session, sibling of Plenary lecture and Session). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic taxonomy vs. event/activity taxonomy) and share no intended instances.

A's property links a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the paper assignment tools), while B's property links a Conference or Paper to a Topic. Different domains and ranges, and different intended meanings (tool administration vs. subject classification), so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties linking a paper/contribution to its review: A's domain 'Reviewed contribution' is the conference ontology's term for a submitted paper, and B's domain 'Paper' is the same concept; both have range 'Review'. Same relation, same direction.

A's 'has Co author' links a Paper to a Co author (a co-author role/class), while B's 'is writen by' links an Item to a Person. They both express authorship of a written work, but the ranges differ (Co author vs Person) and the direction/domain granularity differ; they overlap in meaning but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's isReviewedBy relates a Paper to reviewers/committee members (domain Paper, range people roles), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (domain Speaker, range Document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning (reviewing vs. presenting), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the act/phase of submitting contributions), while B 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is a committee (a group of people) that selects best papers. They belong to different branches (Event vs Committee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (its author), while B's 'has Related Document' links an Academic Event/Conference/Session/Person to a Document (a related document). The domains and ranges differ (Person vs Document as range; Conference document vs Event/Conference/Session/Person as domain), so they relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not equivalent.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event/session, sibling of Conference and Tutorial) in confOf, whereas a Power Point presentation is a specific presentation format/activity (sibling of Video presentation) in iasted. They denote different concepts: an event/session versus a presentation medium, so they are not equivalent.

Academic Event in edas is a broad category of conference events (children include Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop), whereas Individual Presentation in ekaw is a specific scientific event (a presentation of a paper, with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial). Academic Event is more general and subsumes Individual Presentation, but they are not equivalent.

A 'Call For Manuscripts' is a call/announcement document (sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Reviews under Call), whereas B 'Review' is a document type representing a review of a submission (sibling of Submission, Form, etc. under Document). They denote different concepts: one is a solicitation announcement, the other a review artefact.

A's rejectedBy relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person who rejected it), while B's hasReview relates a Paper to a Review. Different ranges (Administrator vs Review) and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

OC Chair (Organizing Committee Chair) in ekaw is a member of the organizing committee, while Program Chair in sigkdd is an organizer responsible for the program committee. Both are senior conference roles but they are distinct positions: the OC Chair leads the local/organizing committee, the Program Chair leads the scientific program. They overlap in being conference organizers but do not denote the same concept, so 'related' rather than 'equivalent'.

In EDAS, Presenter is a subclass of Author (path Person > Author > Presenter), so every Presenter is an Author but not vice versa. CMT's Author is the broader concept (it has children like Author Not Reviewer and Co author and properties such as write Paper, submit Paper). Thus CMT Author is more general than EDAS Presenter, i.e. Author is subsumed_by Presenter's superclass relationship reversed: the EDAS entity is strictly narrower, so the CMT Author subsumes the EDAS Presenter. The correct relation is subsumed_by from A to B only if A is narrower; here A (Author) is broader, so relation should be 'subsumes'. However, since the question asks whether they are equivalent, they are not; the relation is that A subsumes B.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a place where meetings/sessions are held (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Accommodation Place, Dining Place), whereas B 'Hotel room' is a lodging room with children Single/Double hotel room, sibling of Conference hall and Session room. The intended instances differ: a meeting room is not a hotel room, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Camera ready contribution' is a subclass of Accepted contribution (a document/contribution in the submission workflow), while B's 'Camera Ready event' is an Administrative event in the event hierarchy. They denote different kinds of entities (a document vs. an event), so they are not equivalent.

A is a document/abstract class (a written abstract of a tutorial, sibling of Invited Talk Abstract under Abstract), while B is an activity/event class (a tutorial lecture, sibling of Plenary lecture and Session under Lecture). One denotes a text artefact, the other a scheduled event; they are not the same concept.

A Demo Session is a kind of Session (a slot in the programme where demos are presented), while a Plenary lecture is a kind of Lecture (a single talk given to the whole conference). They sit under different parents (Session vs Lecture) and denote different event types, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property of Conference with range int, counting the number of reviews per paper. B's 'paper Due On' is a datatype property of Conference with range dateTime, giving the paper submission deadline. They relate different kinds of values (integer count vs. date/time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property of Review expertise (the expertise a reviewer has for a review), while B's 'Nation' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's nationality. Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

isMenuOf relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (a menu is associated with a meal event), while partOfEvent is a mereological relation between events (an event is part of another event). Different domains/ranges and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is a full paper submission date' is a datatype property of the Important dates class with range date, recording the deadline for full paper submissions. B's 'early Registration' is a datatype property of Participant with range boolean, recording whether a participant registered early. They relate different kinds of things (deadline vs. participant flag) in different directions and have no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper (a document type: the full version of a paper, sibling of Paper Abstract). B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a subclass of Deadline (a due date for submitting papers, sibling of Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Author notification). One is a document/paper type, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A 'Single Level Conference' is a conference type (a subclass of Conference, sibling of Two Level Conference) in the edas ontology, whereas B 'Conference city' is a subclass of City describing the city in which a conference is held (sibling of Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city). They denote different concepts (a conference vs. a city), so they are unrelated.

confOf's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while edas's Active Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper in an active review state, with children Rated Papers and siblings Accepted/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper). Active Paper is strictly narrower than the general Paper concept, so confOf Paper is subsumed by edas Active Paper, not equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome of a submission), while B's can_stay_in relates a Person to a Place (where an attendee may lodge). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A is a class of documents (a paper that has been submitted, a subclass of Paper with children like Assigned Paper), while B is a time/deadline entity (a subclass of Deadline marking when submissions are due). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (document vs. time) and cannot denote the same concept.

A 'Single Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference in edas, denoting a conference type (single-track vs two-level/two-track). B 'Conference state' is a subclass of State in iasted, denoting a state/status of a conference participant or event (sibling of Presenter state, Sponsor state). Different parents (Conference vs State) and different intended instances; no equivalence.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has Postal Code' is a datatype property of Organization and Person giving a postal code. They relate different attributes (surname vs postal code) and are not the same relation, so they are unrelated.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of Conference participant (a person role, sibling of Active conference participant), while B 'Single Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference event, sibling of Two Level Conference). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (person vs. event) and share no intended instances.

Organization in confOf is an institution (Company, University) that employs people and has an address; Item in iasted is a physical/abstract thing (equipment, card, document, vehicle) used in activities. Their instances, children and properties do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

Administrator in confOf is a Person subtype (confTool administrator) with siblings Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc., while Reviewer in iasted is a Speaker subtype under Delegate, a conference participant role. The two denote different roles: an administrator manages the conference system, a reviewer evaluates submissions. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (membership of a conference), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (a person's requirement). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

Both properties relate a written work to its author: edas 'is Written By' has domain Paper and range Author, iasted 'is writen by' has domain Item and range Person. Paper/Item and Author/Person are the corresponding classes in the two ontologies, and the direction (work -> author) is the same, so the two properties denote the same relation.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper document), while B is a topic in the Computer Networks topic hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document types vs. subject topics) and share no intended instances.

Both denote the social/social-programme part of a conference: ekaw's Social Event is an Event subclass with children Conference Banquet and Conference Trip, while iasted's Social program is a Conference activity with child Dinner banquet and sibling Coctail reception. The intended instances (banquets, trips, receptions) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite the different parent (Event vs Conference activity).

Attendee in edas is a generic person who attends the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles), while Session Chair in ekaw is a specific organizational role responsible for a session, a subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member. The two denote different concepts: an attendee need not chair a session, and a session chair is a specific role rather than the general attendee class. They are not equivalent.

A's 'has a committee co chair' links a Committee to its Co chair (a person role), while B's 'hold' links an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference it organises. Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Conference participant is a broad class covering all people taking part in a conference (its children include Active/Passive conference participant, and its siblings include Committee member, Reviewer, etc.), whereas Program Committee member is a specific organizational role under Organizator. A PC member is a kind of conference participant, but not every conference participant is a PC member, so Conference participant is strictly more general and subsumes Program Committee member.

confOf's Administrative event is a subclass of Event covering organisational activities (submission, reviewing, registration, camera-ready), while iasted's Deadline is a subclass of Time representing a point in time by which something must be done. They are not the same concept: one is an event/activity, the other a temporal deadline. They are related in that administrative events are typically bounded by deadlines, but neither subsumes the other.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted academic work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by Author, reviewed by PC members, has title/abstract/keywords). Money in iasted is a monetary payment concept (parent of Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip; paid by Person, paid for Activity/Item, has amount). They share no instances and no properties; the only superficial link is that fees may be paid for conference contributions, which is not equivalence.

A is an administrative event (the activity/process of registering participants, sibling of Submission and Reviewing events), while B is a fee (a monetary charge with price, currency, and payer properties, parent of member/student registration fee subclasses). The event of registering and the fee paid for registration are different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chair of the conference, under Person > Chairman), while B 'Meeting Room Place' is a physical location (a place for meeting rooms, under Place). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a kind of submitted document), while B's Accepted Paper is a subclass of Paper restricted to papers that have been accepted. Every accepted paper is a paper, but not every paper is accepted, so A is more general than B; the two are not equivalent.

A's `name` is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's `E mail` is specifically an email address of a Person. They denote different attributes (a person's name vs. email address), so they are not equivalent.

A's `lists Event` relates a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event (a document listing events), while B's `give` relates a Person to an Activity/Item (a person giving a talk or item). Different domains (document vs person), different ranges (Event vs Activity/Item), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Paper Abstract is a document type (an abstract of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while Platinum Supporter is a sponsorship category in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Sponzor) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.
