Both properties link a paper to a review artefact, but the domains differ: A's domain is 'Reviewed contribution' (a paper that has been reviewed) and its range is a generic 'Review', while B's domain is 'Active Paper' and its range is specifically 'Review Rating'. The intended relations overlap (a paper having a review/rating) but are not the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'has an abstract' is a specific part-whole relation linking a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract. B's 'has Part' is the general mereological relation with unspecified domain/range. The specific relation is subsumed by the general one, not equivalent.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a chair role in the conference committee hierarchy (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), whereas B's 'Late paid applicant' is a registration-payment category of a conference applicant (sibling of Early paid applicant). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Industrial Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a scientific contribution submitted to a conference), while B's Document is a broad administrative artefact class whose children are forms, invitation letters, payment documents, reviews, submissions, etc. The two denote different concepts: a paper is not a document in B's sense, and B's Document is not a kind of paper. No subsumption or overlap holds.

A's 'adjusted By' relates a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it (domain Bid, range Reviewer), while B's 'updated Version Of' relates a Document to another Document that it is an updated version of (domain Document, range Document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is the event itself (has dates, accepts submissions, has members, has a logo). B's Conference_participant is a person role (a participant in a conference), with siblings like Committee member, Reviewer, Track workshop chair. The event and a person role are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has Been Assigned' relates a Reviewer to a Paper (a review assignment in the conference domain), while B's 'is occupied by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (occupancy of a location). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a numeric (int) count of reviews per paper attached to Conference, while B's 'remark' is a free-text string comment on a Contribution. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

Both classes denote the registration fee category for students: A's 'Student registration fee' sits under Registration fee alongside member/nonmember/author fees, and B's 'Registration Student' sits under Registration fee alongside member/nonmember fees. Same intended instances (student registration fees), same parent concept, same sibling structure.

Talk Event (edas) is a kind of academic event/talk, while Demo Session (ekaw) is a kind of session. They belong to different branches (Academic Event vs Session) and denote different concepts: a talk is a presentation, a demo session is a session containing demonstrations. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A 'Industrial Paper' is a kind of conference Paper (a scientific contribution submitted to a conference), while B 'Mailing list' is a Document used for communication/administration in the conference organisation. They share no intended instances: a paper is not a mailing list, and their paths (Paper vs Document) and sibling sets (Camera Ready Paper, Regular Paper, ... vs Form, Invitation letter, Review, ...) confirm different concepts.

A's 'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's 'scientifically Organised By' links an event/conference to an Academic Institution (the organising body), a subproperty of 'organised By'. Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's `location Of` relates a Location to an Event (the event is located at the location), while B's `hold` relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference (the organisation holds the conference). Different domains and ranges, and the directions/meanings differ; they are not the same relation.

A's Paper is a document/contribution class (a written submission with an abstract, sibling of Extended abstract), while B's Author of paper is a person role class (a kind of Author, sibling of Author of paper student). They denote different concepts: a paper is not an author, so the classes are unrelated.

A's Conference volume is an event/publication-like entity (has committees, tracks, contributions, important dates), while B's Building is a physical place (situated in, occupied by, paid in). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' relates a Conference document to a Person (the author of a paper), while B's 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (a person signs an item, e.g. a review or form). The domains and ranges are reversed and the intended meanings differ, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome for a submission). B's is_designed_for relates an Activity/Money/Time to an Activity/Person (a general-purpose 'intended for' relation in the iasted domain). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Paper/Decision vs Activity/Money/Time/Person), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person (a human role in the conference domain), while B's 'Author information form' is a subclass of Form (a document used to collect author details). One denotes a person, the other a document, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (a static informational artefact, sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.), whereas B's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the reviewing procedure. One is a document, the other an event; their intended instances do not coincide.

A 'Session chair' is a person role (a Delegate who chairs a session), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (a kind of Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote different concepts: a person versus a location, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has Surname' is a datatype property linking a Person to their family name string, while B's 'Nation' links a Person to a nationality/country string. Although both are Person->string datatype properties, they denote different attributes (surname vs. nation), so they are not equivalent.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B's Viza is a document (a visa document, sibling of Invitation letter, Payment document, etc.). They denote different kinds of things: an event vs. a document, so they are unrelated.

A's paper ID is an identifier of an individual Paper (domain Paper, range unsignedLong), while B's has an ISBN is an identifier of a Conference proceedings (domain Conference proceedings, range string). Different domains, ranges, and intended entities; they are not the same relation.

A 'Camera Ready event' is an administrative event in confOf (a deadline/phase for submitting the final version of an accepted paper), while B 'Workshop' is an academic event in edas (a type of conference event where papers are presented). They denote different concepts: one is a procedural deadline event, the other a kind of academic gathering. No subsumption or overlap in the intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'is present in' is an object property mapping a Person to a Place/Time (attendance at an event). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (Person -> Organization), while B's hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (Conference -> Person). They have different domains, different ranges, and opposite directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (organization provides sponsorship), while B's payed_by relates a Registration fee to a Person (fee is paid by a person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while B's 'is paid by' relates Money to a Person (payment). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation nor inverses.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome for a paper). B's go_through relates an Item to an Activity (an item undergoing some activity/process). The domains (Paper vs Item) and ranges (Decision vs Activity) differ, and the intended meanings are different: one expresses a paper's review outcome, the other an item's participation in an activity. They are not the same relation.

A is a research topic (Microelectronics Topic) under Topic, while B is an organizational body (Program Committee) under Committee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's `related To Event` links an Accepted Paper to its Paper Presentation (a presentation event), while B's `award` links something to an Award. Different domains and ranges, different intended relations; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's hasMenu relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (a specific catering/meal sub-event structure), while B's partOfEvent is a general mereological relation between an Event and its sub-events. Different domains/ranges (Meal Event->Meal Menu vs Event->Event) and different intended meanings; hasMenu is not the same relation as partOfEvent.

A's Conference Event is a broad event entity with attendees, programme, location and start/end times, whose children are Academic/Non Academic Event. B's Conference activity is a sub-activity of Activity (siblings: Activity before/after conference) whose children are concrete activities like Lecture, Coffee break, Registration. The two overlap in the conference domain but neither subsumes the other: A's events are not B's activities, and B's activities are not A's events. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'Review preference' is a reviewer's declared preference/degree of interest in topics or submissions (properties: has a degree, belongs to reviewers, has a topic or submission contribution), whereas B's 'Review' is a Document subclass representing an actual review of a paper. The two denote different concepts: a preference about reviewing vs. the review document itself, so they are not equivalent.

Demo Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a document type in ekaw), while Submission in iasted is a generic document representing a submitted item with children Initial/Final manuscript. They denote different concepts: a demo paper is not a submission, and a submission is not necessarily a demo paper. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's Review is the review document/process attached to a reviewed contribution (has a review / reviews). B's Review Rating is the rating value (accept, reject, weak reject, etc.) assigned to an active paper via has Rating. The review and the rating it contains are related but not the same concept: a Review is a broader artefact/process, while Review Rating is specifically the score/decision value. Hence related, not equivalent.

Volunteer in confOf is a generic Person subtype (sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.) with comment 'confTool', denoting a helper/volunteer role. PC Chair in ekaw is a specific conference participant who chairs the program committee, a subtype of PC Member. The two denote different roles with no overlap in intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a human person in the conference domain. cmt Person has children Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User and properties email, name, has Conflict Of Interest; ekaw Person has children Agency Staff Member, Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student and properties author Of, written By, organises, organised By. The differing children reflect different role taxonomies, but the intended instances (people involved in conferences) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to its authors (Person), while B's 'is prepared by' links an Item to the Person who prepared it. Both relate a document-like entity to a Person, but 'prepared by' is broader (preparer may be an author, editor, or organizer) and the direction/meaning differs from authorship. They overlap but are not the same relation, so 'related' rather than equivalent.

A 'Research Institute' is an academic organisation (a type of institution, sibling of University under Academic Institution), whereas B 'Research' is an activity performed before a conference (sibling of Accepting/Receiving manuscript). They denote different kinds of things (organisation vs. activity) and are not equivalent.

A's Conference Venue Place is a general venue location (siblings include Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), while B's Hotel is a specific lodging place (siblings Conference hall, Main office). A hotel is a kind of accommodation place, not a conference venue place; the two classes denote different concepts.

A's 'is connected with' is a general object property linking Activities/Persons to Items/Places, while B's 'Name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string literal. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain/range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Event is a broad umbrella (children: Administrative event, Social event, Working event) covering all conference-domain happenings, while sigkdd's Conference is a specific kind of event with city, name, start/end dates and held-by relations. A Conference is an Event, but not every Event is a Conference, so Event subsumes Conference.

A's hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime (a deadline date), while B's locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the event held at that location). They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and domains, so they are unrelated.

A's Session is a scientific event (a scheduled gathering such as a conference session, workshop session, poster session) within the event hierarchy. B's Main office is a physical place (an office location) alongside building, conference hall, hotel room and session room. The two denote different kinds of things (event vs. place) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

confOf's studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (the institution where the scholar studies/works), while ekaw's scientificallyOrganisedBy relates an event (e.g. a conference/session) to an Academic Institution that organises it scientifically. The ranges are compatible (University is a kind of Academic Institution), but the domains differ (Scholar vs. an event), and the direction/meaning of the relation is different: one is a person-to-institution affiliation, the other an event-to-institution organisation. They are therefore not equivalent, only loosely related.

A is a research topic area in computer networking (a subject category under Topic, with subtopics like security, switching, sensor networks). B is a physical piece of audiovisual equipment (a Computer under Audiovisual equipment, alongside projectors and video cassette players). Despite the shared word 'computer', they denote entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

In edas, Country is a specific geographic entity used as the location of a Conference (has Country: Conference -> Country). In ekaw, Location is a broader class that is the range of held In (Event -> Location) and the domain of location Of; it covers any place an event is held, including countries, cities, and venues. A Country is a kind of Location, but Location is not restricted to countries, so Country is strictly more specific: subsumed_by.

Bid in cmt is a reviewer's bid on a paper (domain/range Reviewer->Bid, Paper->Bid), while City in confOf is a geographical city linked to organizations and persons. Different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'has a review' relates a Reviewed contribution to a Review (the review artefact), while B's 'is Reviewing' relates a person role (Reviewer, TPC Member, etc.) to a Paper being reviewed. They concern the same reviewing activity but differ in domain and range and in direction of the relationship, so they are not equivalent; they are merely related.

A's Research is a conference activity (a subtype of 'Activity before conference', sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript), whereas B's Speaker is a person role (subtype of Person, with children Author and Invited Speaker, and properties presentation/presentationed by). The two denote different kinds of entities (activity vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's virtualMeetingEnabledBy links a Conference to the Administrator who enables virtual meetings; B's follows links one Administrative event to another in a temporal sequence. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'read By Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Reviewer (domain Paper, range Reviewer), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (domain Author, range Contribution). They differ in both domain and range and are not inverses of each other (the inverse of writes would relate a Contribution to an Author, not a Paper to a Reviewer). Thus they denote different relations.

A's Member is a subclass of Participant (a person role: a participant who is a member, sibling of Regular and Student participants). B's Registration Non Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for non-members, sibling of member/student registration fees). One denotes a person role, the other a fee type; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a document produced in the conference review process (child of Document, with review Of Paper and review Written By properties, subclasses Positive/Negative/Neutral Review). B's Tax is a monetary charge (child of Money, with Departure tax and Value added tax). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

Conference Chair is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in cmt, while Workshop is a scientific event in ekaw. They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a datatype property linking a Sponsorship to an integer cost amount; B is an object property linking an Event to a Location. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving an integer volume number, while B's 'max Choice' is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a positiveInteger choice limit (confTool). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Conference applicant is a Person who applies to/registers for a conference (parent Person, child Registeered applicant, siblings include Conference participant, Reviewer, Committee member). SC Member (Steering Committee Member) is a PC Member subtype in ekaw, a senior committee role. The two denote different roles: an applicant/attendee versus a steering-committee member. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances, so unrelated.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document/announcement (sibling of Call for participation, Conference announcement, Review), i.e. a call soliciting submissions. B's 'Workshop Paper' is a subtype of Paper (sibling of Conference Paper, Poster Paper, etc.), i.e. an actual submitted/published document. Different kinds of things despite the shared word 'paper'.

A's 'Conference fees' denotes a monetary charge/fee concept, while B's 'Conference' denotes an event (one edition of a conference) under Event > Scientific Event. They share only the word 'conference' and have different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Track workshop chair' is a person who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial (a specific organising role, related to Conference part via has a track workshop tutorial chair / was a track workshop chair of). B's 'Member PC' is a program-committee member whose comment is 'Reviewer' and who reviews Contributions and is expert on Topics. The roles differ: workshop/track chairing vs. PC reviewing, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's property relates a Topic to a Conference part (object property, domain Topic, range Conference part), while B's property gives the name of a Conference as a string (datatype property, domain Conference, range string). Different domains, ranges, and kinds; they denote different relations.

A's 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter of a paper), while B's 'notification until' links an Author to a notification deadline. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference, but cmt's `date` is a generic conference date (range date), while edas's `paper Due On` is specifically the paper submission deadline (range dateTime, comment 'Conference Paper Date and Time Deadline'). The paper deadline is one kind of conference date, so they overlap but are not the same relation; the intended instances do not coincide.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in cmt, while B is an administrative event (Reviewing results event) in confOf. They belong to different branches (Person vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'paper ID' is a datatype property mapping a Paper to an unsignedLong identifier, while B's 'is Written By' is an object property mapping a Paper to an Author. They have different ranges (unsignedLong vs Author) and different meanings (identifier vs authorship relation), so they are unrelated.

A's hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword; B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in domain, range, and kind, so they denote different relations.

A's min Choice is a datatype property giving a minimum number of choices (positiveInteger) for a social/working event, while B's organised By is an object property linking an Event to an Organisation or Person. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a kind of working event (a session/activity in the conference programme, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas B's Listener is a kind of Delegate (a person/role who attends, sibling of Speaker, Session chair, etc.). One is an event, the other a person role, so they cannot denote the same concept.

A's enableVirtualMeeting is an Administrator action that enables a Conference to be virtual (domain Administrator, range Conference). B's give is a Person action giving an Activity or Item (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a person who has registered for a conference (a subclass of Conference applicant, with child Paid applicant), whereas B 'Conference Participant' is a broader class covering all people participating in a conference (chairs, presenters, authors, students, etc.). A registered applicant is a kind of conference participant, but not every conference participant is a registered applicant, so A is strictly more specific than B.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Person) while B is an administrative event (Camera Ready event, a subclass of Administrative event). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

ekaw's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while sigkdd's obtain relates an Author to an Award (receiving an award). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'end Review' relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the chair ends a review), while B's 'is given to' relates an Item to a Person (e.g. an award or item given to a person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Country in confOf is a geographical entity used as the range of has Country (Organization/Person -> Country), whereas Organization in edas is an agent that provides sponsorships and has subclasses Academia/Government/Industry/NGO. They denote different concepts and are not related by subsumption or overlap.

A 'Government Organization' is a type of organization (sibling of Academia/Industry Organization/NGO under Organization), whereas B 'Sponzorship' is a kind of Money (sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain — an organizational actor versus a financial category — so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference fees' is a class of monetary charges (registration costs), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself, with properties for city, name, start/end dates and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. The two denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both denote a university as an organisation: confOf's University is a subclass of Organization, and ekaw's Organising Agency is a subclass of Organisation; a university is an organising agency/institution in the conference domain, and the sibling context (Academic Institution, Proceedings Publisher) matches the organisational role.

Organization in confOf is an institution (parent of Company and University, employs Persons, has address fields), while Document in sigkdd is a written artefact (parent of Abstract, Paper, Review, presented by Speakers, submitted until a Deadline). Their instances, children and properties do not overlap, so they denote different concepts.

Both entities denote the same concept: a paper/contribution in the conference domain. The labels 'Paper' and 'Contribution' are synonyms in this context, and their paths, parents, and properties (e.g., hasAuthor, hasReview) align, indicating they represent the same class of document submitted to a conference.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a social event (Conference Banquet, a kind of Social Event). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

A Conference Banquet is a social event (a dinner/meal event) in the conference schedule, while a Double hotel room is a type of hotel room (accommodation place). They belong to different branches (Event vs Place) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Sponsor state' is a state/status of a sponsor within the conference organisation (sibling of Conference state and Presenter state, subclass of State), whereas B 'Invited Speaker' is a kind of person (subclass of Speaker, sibling of Author). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Both denote the same conference-domain concept: an invited talk. In Conference it is a kind of Conference contribution/Presentation (a document/presentation given by an invited speaker), and in ekaw it is a kind of Individual Presentation (an event where an invited speaker presents). The labels match exactly and the surrounding concepts (Presentation vs Individual Presentation, sibling Contributed Talk/Regular contribution) confirm the same intended instances.

Conference contributor is a broad role class covering active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors, whereas Chair PC is a specific committee role (program chair). The two denote different concepts; Chair PC would be a sibling of Committee member rather than a subtype of Conference contributor.

A's 'Review Form' is the document/artifact used to record a review, whereas B's 'Possible Reviewer' is a person role (a Person who may review papers, parent of PC Member). The two denote different kinds of entities (form vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Short paper is a contribution type (sibling of Paper and Poster), while ekaw's Conference Paper is a document type under Paper, with siblings like Regular Paper, Poster Paper, Demo Paper. A short paper is a kind of conference paper, but the two classes are not coextensive: ekaw's Conference Paper covers regular papers too, and confOf's Short paper is a distinct submission category. They overlap in the domain but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so 'related' is the safest verdict.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (a chair of the conference), while Conference state in iasted is a state/status of a conference. They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track parts (a whole-part/containment relation within a conference), while B's 'is held in' relates an Activity to a Place and Time (a spatiotemporal location relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is the central domain class representing the conference event itself, with properties for submissions, dates, administrators, members and logo. B's Conference state is a state/status class (sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state under State), denoting a registration or participation status of a conference participant, not the conference event. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

Both are the top-level event class in the conference domain: edas Conference Event has children Academic Event / Non Academic Event, ekaw Event has children Scientific Event / Social Event, matching the same academic/social split. Both carry the same core properties (location, programme/part-of, organiser/attendee, dates), so their intended instances coincide.

Both entities denote the same concept in the conference domain: Paper (Ontology A) and Contribution (Ontology B) are synonyms for a submitted/peer-reviewed scholarly work; their contexts (authored by researchers, submitted to conferences, reviewed) agree.

A Workshop is a scientific event (sibling of Conference, Session, Track) held alongside a conference; B Tutorial is a kind of lecture/activity within a conference programme. They denote different concepts: a workshop is an event, a tutorial is a lecture-type activity, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'details Entered By' relates a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'has Event' relates an Event to a sub-Event (part/whole or sub-event relation). Different domains (Conference vs Event), different ranges (Administrator vs Event), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Attendee (edas) is a generic Person who attends a conference, sibling of Author/Reviewer/Chair roles. Program Chair (sigkdd) is a specific organizer role under Organizator, sibling of General Chair and PC member. They denote different concepts: an attendee is not a program chair, and the paths/parents differ (Person vs Organizator).

A's 'accepted By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted the paper), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (the payer). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes are named Review, both are direct subclasses of Document, and in the conference domain a review is the same concept in both ontologies (a document containing an evaluation of a submission). The differing siblings (administrative documents in iasted vs. Abstract/Paper in sigkdd) do not change the intended meaning of Review itself.

ekaw:Document is a broad class covering all written conference artefacts (Abstract, Paper, Review, Web Site, etc.), while iasted:Payment document is a specific kind of document (with children Bank transfer, Cheque) under iasted:Document. Payment document is therefore a narrower concept subsumed by the general Document class, not equivalent to it.

A's isReviewedBy relates a Paper to reviewers/committee members (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. the peer-review relation. B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker, i.e. who presents the work. Different kinds of things are related in different directions and senses, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Administrator is a Person role (confTool administrator) sibling to Author, Chair PC, Participant etc.; B's Author is a Speaker/Delegate role in a building hierarchy. Different concepts despite both being conference-domain person roles.

A's 'Speaker lecture' is a session/lecture type in the activity hierarchy (a kind of event/session), while B's 'Speaker' is a person role (subclass of Person, with Author and Invited Speaker as children). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote members of a program committee. In ekaw, PC Member is a subclass of Possible Reviewer under Person, with children such as PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc. In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a subclass of Organizator under Person, alongside Program Chair, General Chair, etc. The labels are synonymous in the conference domain, and the surrounding context (committee roles, chairs) agrees, so the intended instances coincide.

Both denote the abstract of a paper: cmt's Paper Abstract is a part of a Paper (sibling of Paper Full Version), and Conference's Abstract is a part of a Paper/Poster/Presentation (is the 1th part of) and is what a paper has an abstract of. The intended instances (abstracts of papers) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A's hasHomePage relates a Person to a homepage URL string, while B's hasFirstName relates a Person to a first name string. They denote different attributes of a person (web page vs. given name), so they are not equivalent relations.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to a Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. one reviewer was invited by another reviewer. B's 'is sent by' relates an Item to a Person (e.g. a paper/review sent by a person). Different domain and range, different direction of meaning, and no shared concept; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is the central academic event class (has papers, members, topics, deadlines), while B's Conference airport is a physical building/venue location under Place > Building, sibling to Conference hotel and Conference restaurant. They denote different concepts (event vs. venue building), so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Program committee to a Conference volume (committee-organisation relation), while B's 'occupy' links a Person to a Building/City/State (a location/occupancy relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs the conference, a leadership role under Chairman/Conference Member. Listener (iasted) is a Delegate subtype, i.e. an attendee who listens rather than presents. The two denote different roles in the conference domain and have no subsumption or overlap.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic's preference in reviewing), while B's property links an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

Abstract is a kind of Document (a written summary of a paper/talk), while Registration fee is a kind of Fee (a monetary charge for attending the conference). Their parents, children, siblings and properties (paper presentation vs. currency/price/payment) are entirely different, so the two classes denote unrelated concepts.

A's isMenuOf relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (catering/menu domain), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation domain). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document they have a conflict of interest with (a negative/declaration relation), while B's contributes relates a Person to a Conference document they authored/submitted. Same domain/range shape but different intended meaning, so not equivalent.

confOf's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while ekaw's Conference Paper is a specific subclass of ekaw's Paper (siblings Regular Paper, Poster Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). The confOf Paper is broader and corresponds to ekaw's Paper, not to the narrower Conference Paper, so confOf Paper is subsumed by ekaw Conference Paper.

markConflictOfInterest relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to record a conflict of interest, while reviewerOfPaper relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper to record reviewing eligibility. They have different domains (Author/Chairman/Reviewer vs Possible Reviewer) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.
A's Reviewer is a Person/Conference Member role (a person who reviews), while B's Review is a Document (the review text/artefact). Different kinds of entity, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings whose value is an ISBN string, while B's 'has Name' is a datatype property of Conference whose value is the conference's full name. They relate different subjects (proceedings vs. conference) to different kinds of literal values (ISBN vs. name), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author restricted to persons who are authors but not reviewers (a role exclusion), while B's 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Author denoting anyone who authored a paper, with no exclusion of reviewers. Their intended instance sets differ: a reviewer who also authored a paper is an instance of B but not of A, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's has Author relates a Paper to its Author; B's has Reviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a reviewer, not an author). Different relation kinds and different ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's NGO is a subclass of Organization (a type of organisation such as academia, government, industry), while B's Modelling is a subclass of Research under Activity before conference (a research activity alongside Simulating). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (organisation type vs. research activity) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document stage (the abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version), whereas Pending Paper in edas is a submission-status class (a paper awaiting a decision, sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper). They denote different concepts: one is a document type, the other a review status, so they are not equivalent.

A's location is a datatype property giving the venue/place where a Social event or Working event is held (domain: Social event, Working event; range: string). B's has Name is a datatype property giving the full name of a Conference (domain: Conference; range: string). They relate different kinds of things (event place vs. conference name) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference building' is a general building type whose children include Delegate (a person), and its siblings include Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc. B's 'Hotel' is a specific place type. A conference building is not the same as a hotel; they overlap only in that a hotel can be a conference building/venue, so they are related but not equivalent.

Publisher (an organisation that issues conference proceedings, with properties 'issues' and 'has a publisher') and Country (a geographic entity used as the location of a conference, with property 'has Country') denote clearly different concepts; they share no instances and no subsumption relation.

A's Review is a review of a submitted contribution (has a review / reviews a Reviewed contribution), while B's Flyer is a published document (publisher Of an Organisation), a sibling of Paper and Review in ekaw. Different intended instances and roles, so they are unrelated.

A's paperInVolume relates a paper to a volume (part-whole containment of a publication in a proceedings volume), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

Conference document is a document/publication class (children: Call for paper, Conference contribution, Review; properties: contributes, has authors, has a date of issue), whereas confOf Event is a scheduled happening (children: Administrative/Social/Working event; properties: starts on, ends on). Different intended instances and different properties, so they are not equivalent.

A Tutorial is a kind of scientific event/individual presentation in the conference programme, while B is a registration fee category (a monetary amount) in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Money/Fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is the event itself (has members, dates, submissions, administrators), while B's Conference Proceedings is a published document (a Proceedings volume) that results from a conference. They denote different concepts: an event vs. a publication artefact.

A is a research topic in computer networks (a subject area under Topic), while B is a committee role in the conference organisation (under Committee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's Conference is the event itself (has members, dates, submissions, administrators), while B's Conference Participant is a Person subclass (a person attending the conference, with chairs/presenters as children). Different kinds of entities: event vs. person role.

A is a Person subclass (a role: someone who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial), while B is an Event subclass (a working event such as a workshop). They belong to disjoint top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

Attendee (edas) is a generic person who attends a conference, sibling to Author, Reviewer, Chair roles. Student (ekaw) is a specific person type based on academic status, sibling to Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer. A student is not necessarily an attendee and an attendee is not necessarily a student; the concepts denote different classifications (role at event vs. academic status) and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'end Review' is an object property linking a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the act of finishing reviewing), while B's 'end Date' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (the conference's end date/time). They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property giving a person's surname (string), while B's 'has Home Page' gives a person's homepage URL (string). Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote entirely different attributes; sharing domain/range does not make them equivalent.

A's Deadline is a general time point class with children covering submission, notification, camera-ready, registration and hotel deadlines. B's Deadline Paper Submission is a specific deadline (paper submission) and is a child of B's own Deadline class. Thus A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

confOf's Social event is a subclass of Event covering only social gatherings (Banquet, Reception, Trip), while edas's Conference Event is the general superclass of all events at a conference (Academic Event, Non Academic Event). Social event is therefore strictly narrower than Conference Event, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'Early paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a Person who registered and paid early), while B's 'Accepting manuscript' is an Activity before the conference (the act of accepting a paper). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties linking a person to an email string; the edas domain is the more specific 'Contact Information, Person' but the intended relation (person's email address) is the same, so they are equivalent.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a scheduled gathering within a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session), whereas B 'Main office' is a physical place (a building/room location, sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Place) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A is an administrative event (the outcome/notification of reviewing, accessible to authors) under Event > Administrative event, while B is a deadline (a point in time) under Time > Deadline. They belong to different branches (event vs. time) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's User is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Introduction is a conference activity (parent Conference activity, sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Registration). They denote different kinds of things and cannot be equivalent.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person (domain) to an Organization (range), i.e. employment. iasted's is_given_to relates an Item (domain) to a Person (range), i.e. an award/prize being given to a person. Different domains, ranges and directions; not equivalent.

A 'Video presentation' is a kind of Presentation (a conference activity/event), while B 'Speaker' is a kind of Person who gives a presentation. They belong to different branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Member PC (comment 'Reviewer') is a person who reviews contributions and has topic expertise. ekaw's Possible Reviewer is the broader class of anyone who may review a paper, with PC Member as a child. A PC member is a kind of possible reviewer, but not every possible reviewer is a PC member, so Member PC is strictly narrower and thus subsumed by Possible Reviewer.

A's `email` is a datatype property of Person holding an email address string; B's `Nation` is a datatype property of Person holding a nationality/country string. Although both are Person->string datatype properties, they denote different attributes (email address vs. nationality), so a reference alignment would not equate them.
A is a physical place (accommodation venue) under Place, while B is a person role (student who is not a speaker) under Delegate/Non speaker. Different kinds of entities, no overlap.

Excursion is a social/non-academic conference event (sibling of Reception), while Speaker is a person role in the conference (parent of Author, Invited Speaker). They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Reviewer to a Review expertise/preference (the reviewer's declared expertise or preference for reviewing), while B's 'referenced In' is a generic bibliographic relation (e.g. a document referenced in another). Different domains/ranges and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Proceedings' is a published multi-author volume (a Document/Proceedings subclass) containing the conference's papers, whereas B 'Conference days' is a temporal entity (a Time subclass) covering the days of the conference, with children like Delegate and One conference day. They denote entirely different concepts (publication artefact vs. time period), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Non speaker' is a Delegate who does not give a talk (siblings include Speaker, Listener, Session chair), while B's 'Speaker' is a Person who gives a presentation (has presentation property, children Author and Invited Speaker). They are complementary/opposite roles, not the same concept.

A's 'organised By' relates an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it (domain Event, range Organisation/Person). B's 'go through' relates an Item to an Activity it undergoes (domain Item, range Activity). Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; not the same relation.

A's 'Tutorial speaker' is a subclass of Author (a person who gives a tutorial and is also an author), while B's 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Speaker (a person invited to speak, sibling of Author). Both denote conference speakers, but the tutorial-speaker role and the invited-speaker role are distinct specialisations; they overlap only in that a person could be both, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's writtenBy relates a Contribution (paper) to its Author; B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (the presented material). Different domain and range, different direction of meaning (authorship vs. presentation act), so they are not the same relation.

A 'Research Institute' is an academic organisation (a type of institution, sibling of University under Academic Institution), whereas B 'Modelling' is a research activity (a subtype of Research under Activity before conference). They denote fundamentally different kinds of entities (organisation vs. activity) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a physical place (a venue location, sibling of Accommodation Place and Dining Place under Place), while B is a social event (a banquet, sibling of Conference Trip under Social Event). A place and an event are different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A is a datatype property giving the submission deadline date of a full paper (domain Important dates, range date). B is an object property linking a paper to its individual presentation (domain Paper, range Individual Presentation). They relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions and cannot denote the same relation.

A's 'Member PC' is a program-committee member/reviewer (comment 'Reviewer', reviews Contributions, has expertise in Topics). B's 'Session Chair' is a person who chairs a session and initiates calls/reviews papers; it is a distinct role from a PC member/reviewer. Although both are subclasses of Person and both may review papers, the intended concepts differ (PC membership vs. session chairing), so they are not equivalent.

Attendee (a person who attends the conference) and Sponsor (an organisation or person providing financial support) are distinct roles in the conference domain; they share only the parent Person and are not synonyms.

cmt's hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome), while edas's hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a numeric score from a reviewer). The ranges are different concepts (Decision vs Review Rating) and the properties capture different relations, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subject/topic area in a topic taxonomy (a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic), while B is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation at a conference). Their intended instances are entirely different: topics vs. talks. No synonymy, no subsumption, no overlap.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a person is a member of the conference, e.g. committee member). B's is sent by relates an Item (e.g. a paper/submission) to a Person (the sender/author). Different domains (Conference vs Item) and different intended meanings (membership vs authorship/sending), so they are not equivalent.

In confOf, Tutorial is a specific kind of Working event, sibling to Conference and Workshop. In iasted, Lecture is a broad Conference activity whose children include Tutorial, Plenary lecture, Session and Presentation. Thus iasted's Lecture is a more general category that subsumes confOf's Tutorial (a Tutorial is a kind of Lecture/activity), but they are not equivalent since Lecture also covers plenary lectures, sessions and presentations.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of conference session/event) in confOf, sibling of Conference and Tutorial. B Coffee break is a conference activity (a break/refreshment activity) in iasted, sibling of Coctail reception, Lecture, Presentation, etc. They denote different concepts in the conference domain: a workshop is a scholarly meeting, a coffee break is a catering/social pause. No subsumption or overlap of intended instances, so unrelated.

A's hasCall relates an Academic Event to a Call (a call for papers), while B's hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (e.g. a sub-event or parent event). The ranges differ (Call vs Event) and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while B's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (sponsor). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; no overlap.

A's Workshop is a specific conference part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, a kind of session/event), while B's Working event is a broad category of Event whose children include Conference, Tutorial and Workshop. Thus Workshop in A is a narrower concept that falls under the general Working event category in B, not an equivalent class.

Author in cmt is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Activity in iasted is a general event/action category (with subclasses like Conference activity, Activity before/after conference) that persons participate in. Their paths, siblings, and property signatures do not overlap: Author is a subclass of Person, Activity is a temporal event class. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference part is a specific kind of conference component (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) that is part of a Conference volume, whereas Activity is a much broader notion covering anything that can be dated, located, paid for, or connected with persons/items, including activities before/after the conference. Every Conference part is an Activity-like event, but not every Activity is a Conference part, so Conference part is strictly more specific (subsumed by Activity).

A Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event) in confOf, while B Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment in iasted. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (event vs. item/equipment) and share no meaning.

A's memberOfConference is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference (a person-to-event membership relation), while B's City_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (its location city). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties of Conference with a date/time range, but cmt's `date` is a generic conference date (likely the main event date) while edas's `start Date` is specifically the conference start date/time. They overlap in the conference-date sense but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B 'Sponsor state' is a state/status of a sponsor (subclass of State, sibling of Conference state and Presenter state) in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different concepts: a person role versus a sponsorship status. No synonymy, no subsumption, no overlap.

confOf Event is a conference event (administrative/social/working) with start/end dates, while sigkdd Document is a submitted artefact (Abstract/Paper/Review) with presentation and submission deadline properties. Different intended instances and different property contexts, so not equivalent.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (a reviewer adjusting their bid for a paper), while pay relates a Person to Money (a payment). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not the same relation.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference www resource to a string URL, while B's 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference www vs Person), and range (string vs Item), so they denote different relations.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the person hierarchy), while B is a document type (Record of attendance, a subclass of Document in the item hierarchy). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Call For Manuscripts' is a subtype of Call (an announcement soliciting submissions), alongside Call For Papers and Call For Reviews. B's 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity in the conference workflow (a step before accepting/refusing manuscripts), not an announcement. Different kinds (call vs. activity) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's University is an academic organisation (an institution that employs researchers and hosts conferences), while B's Student lecturer is a person role (a delegate who is both a student and a lecturer) under Lecturer in the person hierarchy. They denote different kinds of entities (organisation vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference topic about enterprise computer networks (a research subject area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a computer device) under Audiovisual equipment alongside projectors and video players. They denote different kinds of things and are not the same concept.

A's Person is the broad top-level class covering all people (Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, PC Member, User), while B's Organizator is a subclass of Person restricted to people who organise the conference (General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, PC member, Webmaster). Organizator is therefore strictly narrower than Person, so Person is subsumed by Organizator's superclass rather than equivalent to Organizator.

A's 'starts on' is a datatype property of Event giving a start date/time (comment 'confTool'), while B's 'has Name' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's full name. Different domains (Event vs Conference) and different intended values (time vs name), so they are unrelated.

A's 'adjusted By' relates a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it (domain Bid, range Reviewer), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not the same relation.

A 'Free Time Break' is a non-academic break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break) in the conference schedule, whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (sibling of Hotel and Main office). A scheduled break and a venue location denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Cryptography Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in the edas ontology, whereas B 'Audiovisual equipment' is a physical item (with children Computer, LCD projector, etc.) under Item in iasted. They denote entirely different kinds of things (subject vs. equipment) and share no intended instances.

A's Paper is a generic regular contribution (sibling of Extended abstract, with abstract-related properties), while B's Rejected Paper is a specific evaluated paper that was rejected (sibling of Accepted Paper). They denote different concepts: a Paper need not be rejected, and a Rejected Paper is a specific outcome state, not a generic contribution type.

A Workshop is a working event (a small interactive session type, sibling of Conference and Tutorial) in confOf, whereas B Welcome Talk is a talk event (an opening address, sibling of Closing Talk) in edas. They denote different kinds of conference events and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Web Site' is a subclass of Document (a publication artefact, sibling of Paper, Abstract, Review, with properties like eventOnList, lists, publisherOf), whereas B's 'Webmaster' is a subclass of Organizator under Person (a role/person who maintains the site). One is a document, the other a person role; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person (signing/authoring), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). Different domains and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference topic (a subject area for paper submission) under Computer Networks Topic, while B is a physical piece of audiovisual equipment (a computer) under Audiovisual equipment alongside projectors and video players. They share only the word 'computer' and denote entirely different concepts.

The two properties are inverses: cmt's assignedTo goes from Paper to Reviewer, while ekaw's reviewerOfPaper goes from Possible Reviewer to Paper. They relate the same kinds of entities but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent (a property and its inverse are distinct).

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper-like entity), while B's `has Related Document` relates a broad set of entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person) to a Document. The domains and ranges differ substantially: `writes` is specifically about authorship of contributions, whereas `has Related Document` is a generic association to any document. They do not denote the same relation.

A 'Welcome Talk' is a type of conference event (a talk given at the start of a conference), while B 'Invited Speaker' is a type of person (a speaker who is invited). They belong to different branches of the domain (event vs. person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a member of the conference organising committee, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B 'Modelling' is a research activity (a kind of Research activity before the conference, sibling of Simulating). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Active Paper in edas is a paper in an active (under review) state, sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn/Pending/Published Paper and parent of Rated Papers; Industrial Paper in ekaw is a paper type/track (industrial vs regular, demo, poster, workshop), sibling to Regular Paper and Conference Paper. Different classification dimensions (status vs paper kind), so they are not equivalent.

Both properties express spatial location, but ekaw's heldIn relates an Event to a Location, while iasted's is_situated_in relates physical places (Building, City, Place) to places/states. The domains and ranges differ (Event vs Building/City/Place), so they are not equivalent; they overlap only in the general notion of being located somewhere.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that announces a conference, while B's 'Conference activity' is an event/activity (parent of Lecture, Presentation, Registration, etc.). They denote different kinds of things (document vs. event) and are not equivalent.

A is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date value (a submission deadline), while B is an object property linking an Abstract/Paper to an Individual Presentation (a presentation event). They relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Published Paper is a status-based subclass of Paper (siblings Accepted/Pending/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), i.e. a paper that has been published. In ekaw, Conference Paper is a type-based subclass of Paper (siblings Camera Ready, Demo, Industrial, Poster, Regular, Submitted, Workshop Paper), i.e. a paper submitted to a conference, not a publication-status class. The two overlap (a published paper is typically a conference paper) but their intended instances do not coincide, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a computer-networks switching research topic under Topic in the edas ontology, while B is a 'Trip day' time concept under Time in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (research subject vs. temporal entity) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.
A is a kind of conference paper (a document type), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment; they share no concept in the conference domain.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) in the conference-organisation domain. B's Communications Topic is a subject area / research topic (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.) under Topic in edas. They denote entirely different concepts: an event versus a research topic. No equivalence, subsumption or meaningful overlap.

cmt:Preference is a class of preferred/contributed paper types (a submission category), while confOf:Regular is a participant category (regular participant vs. member/student) under Person > Participant. They denote different concepts in different branches of the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who has paid early), while B is a subclass of Fee (a monetary charge for an extra trip). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event in confOf that reports the outcome of reviewing to authors, whereas B 'Call For Papers' is a call document soliciting submissions. They belong to different branches (Event vs Call) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'paper ID' is a datatype property mapping a Paper to an unsignedLong identifier, while B's 'submit' is an object property mapping an Author to a Paper (the submission relation). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Paper vs Author), and range (unsignedLong vs Paper), so they denote different relations and are unrelated.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event alongside Conference and Tutorial), while B Video presentation is a kind of Presentation (a conference activity alongside Power Point presentation). They belong to different branches (event vs. presentation medium) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a review' goes from Reviewed contribution to Review (a paper has a review), while B's 'reviewes' goes from Member PC to Contribution (a PC member reviews a contribution). They are inverse-like relations between different entity pairs, not the same relation.

Both properties link a presentation event to the document/paper being presented, so they overlap conceptually. However, the domains and ranges differ: ekaw's presentationOfPaper has domain Individual Presentation and range Abstract/Paper, while sigkdd's presentation has domain Speaker and range Document. The sigkdd property relates a speaker to a document (the act of a speaker presenting a document), whereas ekaw's relates a presentation event to the paper presented. They are related but not equivalent because the subject/object kinds do not coincide.

confOf Member is a Participant (attendee) subclass alongside Regular and Student, i.e. a conference attendee category. sigkdd Program Committee member is an Organizator subclass alongside General Chair, Program Chair, etc., i.e. an organizer role. Both are persons involved in the conference, but they denote different roles: a PC member is an organizer, not a generic participant/attendee. They overlap only in that a PC member may also attend, so the relation is related, not equivalent.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' relates an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the committee organizes a specific conference event/volume). B's 'scientifically Organises' relates an Academic Institution to an unspecified range (an institution scientifically organizes a conference/event). The domains differ (Organizing committee vs Academic Institution) and the ranges differ (Conference volume vs unspecified), so the relations do not denote the same relation in the same direction.

In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person who presents a paper). In ekaw, Invited Speaker is a subclass of Presenter, i.e. a specific kind of presenter (keynote/invited talk). The edas Presenter is broader (any author presenting), while the ekaw Invited Speaker is narrower, so edas Presenter is subsumed by the more general ekaw Presenter concept, not equivalent to Invited Speaker.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a leadership role over a committee), while B's 'reviewes' relates a Member PC to a Contribution (a reviewing activity). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas Conference Proceedings is a document (a multi-author volume of proceedings). They belong to different branches (Event vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that run in parallel, while ekaw's 'inverse of part Of 7' is the inverse of a part-of relation whose range is Event, i.e. it relates an Event to its whole/container. Both express a co-occurrence/containment-style relation between events, but they are not the same relation: one is symmetric parallelism between administrative events, the other is the inverse of a part-of (containment) relation over events. They overlap in the event-to-event domain but are not equivalent.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B Double hotel room is a type of hotel room (sibling of Single hotel room) under Place. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

ekaw's Submitted Paper is a specific stage of a paper (a Paper that has been submitted, with child Assigned Paper), while sigkdd's Paper is the general document class (parent Document, sibling Abstract/Review, domain of submit). Submitted Paper is strictly narrower than Paper, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

An External Reviewer is explicitly a person who reviews papers but is not themselves a Reviewer (per the cmt comment), so it is a narrower concept than the Conference ontology's Reviewer, which covers all people who review. External Reviewer is therefore subsumed by Reviewer, not equivalent.

A's 'Committee member' is a Person role in the conference organisation (parent Person, children Chair/Co chair, related to Committee via has members/was a member of). B's 'Money' is a financial amount concept (children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip; properties about amounts, payment, payers). They share no meaning, instances, or context; the only overlap is the word 'member'/'money' being absent entirely. Clearly unrelated.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (domain Location, range Event), i.e. the location where an event takes place. B's 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place/Time (domain Person, range Place, Time), i.e. a person's presence at a place/time. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference Participant' is a subclass of Person denoting human attendees/roles (chairs, presenters, authors), while B's 'Conference activity' is a subclass of Activity denoting events/activities (lectures, breaks, registration). They belong to different top-level categories (Person vs Activity) and have disjoint instances, so they are unrelated.

Both properties are named 'has Country' and link an entity to a Country, but their domains differ: in confOf the domain is Organization or Person (a person's/organization's country), while in edas the domain is Conference (the country where a conference is held). They share the same range and name but relate different kinds of subjects, so they are not equivalent; they are merely related by name and range.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a leadership/role relation within the organising body), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (a talk given at the conference). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is an abstract submission date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a literal date, i.e. the abstract-submission deadline itself. B's 'submit until' is an object property linking a Document to a Deadline resource, i.e. the document's submission deadline. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Important dates vs Document) and range (date literal vs Deadline class), so they do not denote the same relation.

Both properties link a conference/committee to its members, but the domains differ: A's domain is Conference (a conference has conference members), while B's domain is Committee (a committee has committee members). They are conceptually related (membership in the conference organisation) but not the same relation, since a conference and a committee are different entities and the ranges (Conference Member vs Committee member) also differ.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people), while B's was_a_steering_committee_of relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume; different domain/range and direction, so they are not equivalent.

A's Renting is an activity that occurs before the conference (a venue/equipment rental event), while B's Author of paper is a role of a person who wrote a paper. They belong to different branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a Person subclass who initiates calls and reviews papers), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote different kinds of entities and are unrelated.

Both are classes representing a conference venue/place. Ontology A's 'Conference Venue Place' and ontology B's 'Session room' both sit under a 'Place' parent and are siblings of other room/venue types (Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place vs Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office). The labels differ but the domain context (a physical location used for conference sessions) and identical path position under Place indicate they denote the same concept.

Bid in cmt is a reviewer's bid on a paper (Reviewer -> Bid, Paper -> Bid), while Conference in sigkdd is an event with city, start/end dates and a holding organization. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an activity, sibling of Conference Banquet under Social Event), while B Conference hall is a physical place (sibling of Hotel and Main office under Place). Different kinds of entities: an event vs. a location, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Session is a scientific event (a session within a conference, with subtypes like Regular/Poster/Workshop Session). B Lecture is a conference activity that has Session as a child, so a Session is a kind of Lecture in iasted, not the same concept. The two overlap in that both concern scheduled conference sessions, but they are not equivalent: ekaw's Conference Session is a subtype of Session, while iasted's Lecture is a broader activity that subsumes Session.

A's 'was a committe co chair of' links a Co chair to a Committee (a specific role relation, subproperty of was a member of), while B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (a general membership relation). Different domain, range, and direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Academia Organization' is a broad category of academic organisations (siblings: Government, Industry, NGO organisations), while B's 'Research Institute' is a specific kind of academic institution alongside University. A Research Institute is an Academia Organization, but Academia Organization also covers universities and other academic bodies, so A is more general than B; hence A is subsumed by B's narrower concept (B subsumes A).

Both classes denote a person in the conference domain: cmt Person is the superclass of Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User; sigkdd Person is the superclass of Listener, Organizator, Speaker. Both have email and name properties, and both are the general agent class of their ontology, so their intended instances coincide.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered conference details), while B's 'has a track workshop tutorial topic' links a Conference part to a Topic (the subject matter of a track/workshop/tutorial). Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A is an event type (a meeting of an organization, sibling of Workshop/Talk Event under Academic Event), while B is a person role (a member of the organizing committee, sibling of General Chair/Program Chair under Organizator). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and are not equivalent.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract; B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity/Item (a person gives a talk/item). Different domain, range and direction of meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's write relates a Person (author) to an Item (paper/contribution), i.e. authorship. B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document, i.e. presenting a document at a conference. Both connect a person to a document-like entity, but the intended relations differ (writing vs. presenting), so they are not equivalent; they merely overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'Personal Review History' is a record/history of reviews performed by a reviewer (a subclass of Personal History, with properties linking it to a Reviewer), whereas B's 'Reviewer' is a person role (a subclass of Speaker/Delegate). One is a data artefact, the other an agent; they are not the same concept.

A's Committee is a broad organisational body (with subclasses Organizing/Program/Steering committee, having chairs, co-chairs and members), whereas B's Organizing Committee member is a specific person role under Organizator, sibling of General Chair and Program Chair. A committee is not a person role, so the two denote different concepts.

A's 'was a steering committee of' relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume (committee -> event), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (event -> person). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they denote different relations.

Both properties link a Person to a Place, but 'is present in' also ranges over Time and denotes attendance/being at an event, whereas 'can stay in' denotes accommodation (staying in a place). They overlap in relating persons to places but are not the same relation.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has Postal Code' is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a postal code. Different domains (Person vs Contact Information) and different intended values (surname vs postal code), so they are unrelated.
