A's Presenter is a role of a person (a Conference Participant who presents), while B's Lecture is a conference activity/event (with children Plenary lecture, Session, Tutorial). A person role and an event are different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area (topic classification), while B's publisherOf links an Organisation to things it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no overlap.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (a committee role), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or a paper). Different domain, range and direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an administrative action performed by an Administrator on a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), whereas B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'assign External Reviewer' relates a Reviewer (domain) to an External Reviewer (range), i.e. the act of assigning an external reviewer to a reviewer. B's 'belongs to reviewers' relates a Review expertise/Review preference (domain) to a Reviewer (range), i.e. a reviewer's expertise or preference. The domains and ranges differ, and the intended relations are different (assignment vs. expertise/preference ownership), so they are not equivalent.
A's 'submit Paper' relates an Author to a Paper (submission act), while B's 'is sent before' relates an Item to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

A's Social event is a social/leisure gathering (banquet, reception, trip) under Event, while B's Talk Event is an academic talk (welcome/closing talk) under Academic Event. Different sub-domains of the conference; no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Published Paper' is a document state (a paper that has been published), while B 'Best Student Paper Award' is a type of award given to a student paper. They belong to different branches (Document/Paper vs Award) and denote different concepts; no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's Conference Member is a subclass of Person (a person involved in a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Tutorial is a Conference part (an event/activity alongside Track and Workshop). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to the contribution they review (domain Member PC, range Contribution). B's `is Review History Of` relates a personal review history record to a reviewer (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and directions of the underlying relation; they are not the same property.

A's hasTopic relates a Working event to a Topic (the subject matter of a conference event), while B's obtain relates a Person to an Item (a person acquiring something). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A 'Conference volume' is a publication/proceedings volume that belongs to a conference and aggregates contributions, tracks, committees and dates; B 'Conference' is the event itself with dates, country, members and topics. The two overlap (a volume is tied to a conference) but denote different concepts, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' relates a Person to their given/first name, while B's 'has Last Name' relates a Person to their family/last name. They denote different name components, so they are not equivalent (nor does one subsume the other).

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track (a structural part of the proceedings), while B's 'has Topic' relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (a subject area). Different domain (Conference volume vs Conference/Paper) and different range (Track vs Topic), so the relations are not the same.

Chairman in cmt is a specific role (a person chairing a committee/conference, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), whereas ekaw's Conference Participant is a broad class covering all people taking part in a conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants, OC members, etc.). Every Chairman is a Conference Participant, but not vice versa, so Chairman is strictly more specific: subsumed_by.

A's writtenBy relates a Review to a Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), while B's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (domain Paper, range Author). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions of the conference workflow, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to its website URI (range anyURI), while B's 'has Name' links a Conference to its full name string (range string, comment 'Conference Full Name'). They relate different kinds of values (URL vs name) and are not the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial or workshop), while B's Non speaker is a kind of Delegate (a person attending without presenting). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. person/role) and share no intended instances.

confOf's Administrative event covers organisational/paper-handling events (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration) under Event, while ekaw's Scientific Event covers academic programme events (Conference, Session, Track, Workshop, Individual Presentation). They are disjoint subcategories of Event, not synonyms.

A 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Call for participation, etc.) that announces a conference. B 'Invitation letter' is a document sent to invite someone (sibling of Payment document, Viza, Record of attendance). Although both are documents, they denote different artefacts with different purposes; no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B's Accepting manuscript is a pre-conference activity in the paper-handling workflow (sibling of Receiving/Refusing manuscript). They share no meaning, no properties, and no common parent beyond the trivial top-level Event/Activity split.
A is a person role (Conference Chair) under Person/Chairman, while B is a time point (Deadline hotel reservation) under Time/Deadline. They denote different kinds of entities and share no meaning.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a specific kind of regular contribution (a short/early version of a paper, with child 'Abstract'), whereas B's 'Published Paper' is a paper in a publication state, sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn papers. The two denote different concepts: one is a contribution type, the other a publication status of a paper. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

NGO is a type of non-governmental organization (a sibling of Academia, Government, Industry organizations), while Proceedings Publisher is an organisation that publishes conference proceedings (sibling of Academic Institution and Organising Agency). They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

Both properties express a spatial containment/location relation, but they are not the same relation: edas 'has Location' links a Conference Event to a Place (event venue), while iasted 'is situated in' links geographic entities (Building, City, Place) to larger geographic entities (Building, City, Place, State). The domains and ranges differ (event vs. geographic entity), so they overlap in meaning but are not equivalent; a reference alignment would not equate them.

A's Presenter is a Conference Participant who gives a presentation (parent Conference Participant, child Invited Speaker). B's Technical commitee is a subclass of Delegate in the iasted ontology, i.e. a person on a technical committee, not a presenter. The two denote different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A is a research topic class (a subject area for papers, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc. under Topic), while B is a document type (a kind of Abstract under Document). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain: a topic of interest versus a tutorial abstract document.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a document type) in the conference ontology, while B's Best Student Paper Award is a specific award category under Award. They denote different concepts: one is a kind of submission/document, the other a prize. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A 'Written contribution' is a document/contribution type (a paper-like artefact, sibling of Poster, Presentation, Invited talk, with children Regular/Submitted contribution), whereas B 'Poster Session' is a type of scientific event session (sibling of Regular Session, Workshop Session, Demo Session). One denotes a contribution artefact, the other an event/session; they are not the same concept.

A's write Review relates a Reviewer to a Review (a person writes a review). B's belongs_to_a_review_reference relates a Topic to a Review preference (a topic is linked to a reviewer's preference). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a kind of conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B 'Computer' is a piece of audiovisual equipment (sibling of LCD projector, Overhead projector). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Contribution in confOf is the general submission entity with children Paper, Poster, Short paper and properties like abstract, has Title, written By, reviewes; Document in sigkdd is likewise the general submission entity with children Abstract, Paper, Review and properties presentation, submit until. Both denote the same general concept of a submitted contribution/document in the conference domain, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A Reviewer in iasted is a kind of Delegate/Speaker (a conference participant who reviews papers), while a Webmaster in sigkdd is an Organizator role responsible for the website. They belong to different branches (participant vs. organizer) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference event/session), while B Plenary lecture speaker is a person role (a kind of Author/Speaker). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties capturing the deadline by which a full paper must be submitted: A's 'is a full paper submission date' (domain Important dates, range date) and B's 'paper Due On' (domain Conference, range dateTime, comment 'Conference Paper Date and Time Deadline'). The domain/range differences (Important dates vs Conference, date vs dateTime) reflect modelling choices, not different concepts; both denote the paper submission deadline.

A's Submission is a Document (a paper/manuscript artefact submitted to the conference, with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript), while B's Author is a Person (a Speaker who writes papers, with children Author of paper and Author of paper student). They denote different kinds of entities — a document versus a person — and share no subsumption relation, so they are unrelated.

A's Tutorial is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation at a conference), while B's Tip is a monetary category (a gratuity payment) under Money. The identical-looking labels are a false friend; the concepts share no instances and belong to entirely different branches of the domain.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC Member (reviewer) to a Contribution (paper) — reviewer -> paper. B's `is Reviewed By` relates a Paper to a reviewer/chair — paper -> reviewer. They describe the same reviewing relationship but in opposite directions, so they are inverses, not equivalent. Marked related rather than equivalent because the direction differs.

A's 'Conference volume' is a whole conference event/proceedings entity (it has committees, contributions, tracks, important dates), whereas B's 'Conference state' is a state of a conference (sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state), i.e. a status/phase, not a conference volume. Different intended instances and different contexts, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B is a conference activity (Introduction of speaker, a kind of Introduction) in the iasted ontology. They belong to different top-level categories (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Volunteer in confOf is a generic Person subtype (sibling of Participant, Author, Chair PC, etc.) with no conference-specific role beyond the confTool comment, whereas Workshop Chair in ekaw is a specific conference participant role (a PC Member who chairs a workshop). They denote different concepts: a volunteer is not a workshop chair, and the paths/siblings show no overlap in intended instances.

Both properties link a presentation/document to the person who delivers it: 'is given by' has domain Presentation and range Active conference participant, while 'presentationed by' has domain Document and range Speaker. In the conference domain a Presentation is a Document and an Active conference participant who gives a presentation is a Speaker, so the two relations denote the same connection in the same direction.

IASTED member is a subclass of Delegate (an attendee role in the iasted ontology), while Organizator is a Person subclass whose children are organizational roles (General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc.). An IASTED member is an attendee, not an organizer, so the two classes denote different concepts.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, and both denote the conference's end date/time (edas comment 'Conference End Date and Time'; sigkdd label 'End of conference'). Same intended relation, same direction.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the committee is a part/agent of the event's proceedings volume). B's 'hold' links ACM SIGKDD (the organising body/society) to a Conference (the event it holds). Different domains (committee vs. society), different ranges (volume vs. event), and different direction of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session/talk in which an accepted paper is presented), with siblings Talk Event, Workshop, Organizational Meeting and properties linking it to Accepted Paper. B's 'Paper' is a document (sibling of Abstract and Review) that an Author submits. The event and the document are different kinds of entities, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while B's Conference hotel is a building/place used by conference attendees. They belong to different branches (Event vs Place/Building) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote an organization in the conference domain. confOf's Organization has subclasses Company and University and is the employer of Persons; edas's Organization has subclasses Academia/Government/Industry Organization and NGO and is the provider of Sponsorships. The differing subclasses and properties reflect different modelling granularity, not different concepts; both are the general class of organisations involved in a conference.

A's Conference is an academic event with deadlines, topics, papers and members; B's Organisation is an organising body (institutions, agencies, publishers) that organises events. They denote different concepts and are not in a subsumption relation.
Paper Abstract (an abstract/short version of a paper) and Industrial Paper (a paper type by submission track) are different concepts; they share only the parent Paper and are not synonyms.

A's Meal Event is a broad non-academic conference event category (siblings Break Event, Social Event; child Conference Dinner), while B's Dinner banquet is a specific social-program activity (a dinner/banquet). A Meal Event subsumes a dinner banquet, but they are not equivalent: A also covers lunches, receptions, etc., and B is a single concrete social event.

Banquet is a specific kind of social event (a meal/banquet), while edas Social Event is the general category covering Excursion, Reception, Meal Event, etc. Banquet is therefore narrower than Social Event, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A 'Welcome Talk' is a specific talk event (a welcome address), while B 'Plenary lecture' is a specific lecture event (a plenary session). Both are kinds of conference talk/lecture events, but they denote different specific event types, so they overlap in the broader category of conference presentations without being equivalent.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, capturing the person's family name; 'Surname' and 'Last Name' are synonyms in the conference domain.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, relating a person to their email address; the labels 'has Email' and 'E mail' denote the same relation in the conference domain.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to a Conference proceedings (a publisher issues proceedings), while B's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (an author writes a paper). Different domain, range, and direction of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Abstract is a specific kind of conference contribution (an extended abstract, a document that is part of a Paper/Poster/Presentation), whereas B's Contribution is the general superclass of all submitted contributions (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with title, author, keywords, etc. Abstract is thus narrower than Contribution, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's Paper is a submitted document (has authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Call for paper is a conference document announcing the call for submissions. They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'paper'.

A's 'Author cd proceedings included' is a narrow subclass of Author (a delegate/speaker who is an author included in conference proceedings), while B's Author is the general author class with children Author of paper and Author of paper student. The A class is strictly more specific, so it is subsumed by B's Author rather than equivalent.

A's Reviewer is a Person subclass that reviews papers (has review history, is reviewing papers). B's Author is a Speaker/Delegate subclass that produces proceedings and lectures. Although B lists Reviewer as a sibling, the two entities denote different roles: reviewing vs authoring. They are not equivalent.

A's hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property linking a Call to a string of instructions, while B's submit is an object property linking an Author to a Paper. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Call vs Author), range (string vs Paper), and meaning (instructions text vs submission action), so they are unrelated.

A's 'review Criteria Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered the review criteria, while B's 'reviewes' links a PC member to the Contribution they review. Different domains (Conference vs Member PC), different ranges (Administrator vs Contribution), and different intended relations (criteria entry vs reviewing), so they are not equivalent.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (person belongs to a conference), while B's holded_by relates a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD organisation (conference is held by a sponsor/organiser). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person role in confOf), while B's Two Level Conference is a subclass of Conference (a conference type in edas). They denote entirely different concepts—a person role versus a conference category—so they are unrelated.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Organization or Person to a postal code string, while B's hasLastName links a Person to a last name string. They denote different attributes (postal code vs. surname) with different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). They have different domains and ranges and denote different relations, so they are unrelated.
A's Session is a scientific event (a time slot in which presentations occur), while B's Program Committee is a committee of people. Different kinds of entities with no overlap.

A's Conference is a working event (an organised meeting such as a tutorial or workshop), while B's 'Cd proceening' is a publication item (a CD proceedings volume, sibling of Book proceeding). They denote different kinds of things — an event versus a published artefact — so they are unrelated.

Accepted Paper in ekaw is a paper that has passed review and will appear in proceedings, a subclass of Evaluated Paper with sibling Rejected Paper. Abstract in sigkdd is a short summary document, a direct child of Document alongside Paper and Review. They denote different concepts: an accepted paper is a full paper in a specific acceptance state, while an abstract is a distinct document type (summary). Neither subsumes the other.

A's Social event is a subclass of Event covering banquets, receptions and trips, while B's Conference is a top-level class for the conference itself (with sessions, papers, members, deadlines). They denote different concepts: a social event is not a conference, and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Conference Session' is a temporal event/meeting within a conference (it relates to Documents and Academic Events), whereas B 'Building' is a physical place (a subclass of Place with children like Conference hotel, Session room, and properties about being occupied, paid in, situated in). They denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is an administrative event (the outcome/notification of reviewing, accessible to authors) in the event hierarchy of confOf, while B is a document/form (Author information form) in the item/document hierarchy of iasted. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. form) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the physical venue/building where a conference takes place. In edas, Conference Venue Place is a subclass of Place alongside Accommodation Place, Dining Place and Meeting Room Place, i.e. the location of the conference. In iasted, Conference building is a subclass of Building (itself a Place) and is the place where delegates are located (child Delegate), alongside Conference airport, Conference hotel, Conference restaurant, etc. The intended instances coincide: the building/venue hosting the conference. The differing siblings (accommodation/dining/meeting rooms vs. airport/hotel/restaurant) reflect different modelling granularity, not a different concept.

A's Author is a person class (a conference member who writes/submits papers), while B's Deadline Author notification is a deadline event class (a notification deadline for authors). Different kinds of entities: person vs. temporal deadline, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) in the conference-organisation domain, while B 'Computer Networks Enterprise Topic' is a research topic in the edas topic hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Paper is a conference document (subclass of Document, with children Accepted/Rejected Paper, properties is Written By, is Reviewed By, has Topic). B's Tip is a subclass of Money alongside Fee, Sponzorship, Tax — a monetary gratuity/payment, not a document. Same word 'Tip' vs 'Paper' is not even a synonym; the concepts are entirely different domains.

A's setMaxPapers is an object property linking an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a limit on committee members), while B's maxChoice is a datatype property linking a Social/Working event to a positiveInteger (a maximum number of choices for an event). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both classes are named Organization and represent the same concept in the conference domain: an institution such as a company or university. In Conference, Organization has children Company and University and is the range of employed By (Person -> Organization), matching confOf's Organization, which likewise denotes an organizational entity. The identical label, matching kind (class), and consistent contextual role (employer of persons, with address-related properties) indicate the two classes are equivalent.

confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution (paper) to its Author, whereas iasted's send relates a Person to an Item (e.g. sending a submission). The domains and ranges differ (Contribution->Author vs Person->Item), so they are not the same relation.

A is a document type (the abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B is a subject/topic category in a topic taxonomy (a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

Both denote the same social meal event of a conference: edas 'Conference Dinner' is a Meal Event under Non Academic Event, ekaw 'Conference Banquet' is a Social Event with sibling Conference Trip. 'Dinner' and 'Banquet' are synonyms for the same conference social gathering, and both are placed under the social/non-academic event branch.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies/registers for the conference (parent Person, child Registeered applicant, siblings include Conference participant/contributor), whereas B's 'Conference Chair' is an organising role that initiates calls and reviews papers (properties initiates/is Reviewed By/is Reviewing). The two denote different roles in the conference domain and do not coincide.

A 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while B 'Nonauthor registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount paid by non-authors). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference topic area (Computer Networks Applications) under the Topic taxonomy of the edas ontology, while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a computer) under Audiovisual equipment in the iasted ontology. They share only the word 'computer' and denote entirely different concepts.

A's Sponsorship is a funding arrangement class (with cost amounts, currencies, providers, and a Travel Grant child), whereas B's Sponsor state is a state/status of a sponsor within a State hierarchy alongside Conference state and Presenter state. They denote different concepts: a sponsorship entity versus a sponsor's state, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is Initiated By' relates a Call to conference roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. who initiated/issued a call for papers. B's 'is occupied by' relates a physical place (Building, City, State) to a Person, i.e. occupancy of a location. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's hasCostCurrency is a datatype property of Sponsorship giving the currency (a string, e.g. 'EUR') of a sponsorship cost. B's has_amount_of is a datatype property of Money giving a numeric amount (int). They relate different kinds of things (currency code vs. monetary amount) in different domains (Sponsorship vs. Money), so they are not equivalent.

A Talk Event is a scheduled academic talk (with children Welcome Talk, Closing Talk) within a conference event hierarchy, while B Session is a lecture-type conference activity with a Speaker lecture child. Both denote a scheduled speaking slot at a conference, so they overlap, but the taxonomies differ (Talk Event is a kind of Academic Event alongside Paper Presentation/Workshop; Session is a kind of Lecture alongside Plenary lecture/Tutorial), so they are not the same concept.

A's Organization is an institution (parent of Company and University, with address properties and 'employed By' from Person), while B's Person is an individual human (parent of Listener, Organizator, Speaker, with name, email, nation, and registration-fee properties). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while B's 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee (payment). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

Activity in iasted is a broad event/action class (conference activities, before/after conference activities, things given, held in places, dated) whereas Award in sigkdd is a specific recognition entity (best paper awards, awarded by, obtained by authors). Their instances do not coincide; Award is not a kind of Activity in the conference domain, so the classes are unrelated.

A's isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (sponsoring relation), while B's locationOf relates a Location to an Event (where an event takes place). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

cmt:Person is a broad class covering all people in the conference domain (Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User), while sigkdd:Speaker is a narrower subclass of Person restricted to those who give presentations (Author, Invited Speaker). Person is strictly more general than Speaker, so Person subsumes Speaker, not equivalent.

Conference contributor is a broad role class (parent of Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author) covering anyone contributing to a conference, while confOf's Student is a specific participant subtype (sibling of Member and Regular under Participant). The two denote different concepts: a Student is a kind of participant, not a kind of contributor, and contributor is not a subtype of participant. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's Call is a call-for-papers/reviews announcement issued by chairs, with children Call For Manuscripts/Papers/Reviews and properties like has Submission Deadline and initiates. B's Document is a submitted artefact (Abstract, Paper, Review) presented by a Speaker. The Call is not a Document; their instances and roles in the conference domain differ, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role in the conference organisation (a Chairman/Conference Member who chairs the conference), while B 'IASTED non member' is a delegate classification (a Delegate who is not an IASTED member). They belong to different branches (Person/Chairman vs Place/Building/Delegate) and denote different concepts; no equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's 'Organising Agency' is an Organisation subtype (a body that organises the conference, sibling of Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher), whereas B's 'Receiving manuscript' is an Activity before the conference (sibling of Accepting/Refusing manuscript). One is an organisational agent, the other a process; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in cmt, while B is an event type (Conference, a kind of Working event) in confOf. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Contact Information in edas is a class holding address/phone/email details (has City, has Email, has Phone, has Postal Code, has Street), whereas Document in ekaw is a written artefact with children Abstract, Paper, Review, etc., and properties author Of / written By. They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author (authorship relation), while B's pay relates a Person to a Registration fee (payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Session' is a temporal event/program slot in the conference (a class of academic events, related to documents and persons), whereas B 'Session chair' is a role of a delegate/person (a subclass of Delegate). One denotes an event, the other a person role, so they are not equivalent.

hasCountry relates an Organization/Person to a Country (the country an org/person is located in), while organisedBy relates an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it. Different domains (Organization/Person vs Event), different ranges (Country vs Organisation/Person), and different meanings; they are not inverses either, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (presentation relation). Different relation types and different ranges (Author vs Speaker), so they are not equivalent.

A's Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person who presents a paper), while B's Presenter university is a subclass of Building (a physical venue/building at the conference location). Despite the shared word 'Presenter', the intended instances are entirely different kinds of things (person vs. building), so the classes are unrelated.

A's Non Academic Event is a conference event (breaks, meals, socials) that happens during the conference, while B's Activity before conference covers pre-conference organisational steps (accepting/receiving/refusing manuscripts, renting, research). Different domains and different subclasses, so they are unrelated.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string email address, while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item; they relate different kinds of things and have different ranges, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation). B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference (organising/holding an event). Different domain and range, different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (Paper/Poster/Short paper) with title, abstract, keywords, authors and reviews. Conference Session in edas is a scheduled event slot that relates to documents and academic events/persons. Their intended instances do not coincide: a contribution is a document-like submission, a session is an organisational event. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (a paper is submitted to a proceedings/volume), while B's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (the inverse of an event's location). The domains and ranges are disjoint kinds of entities and the directions differ, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's Tax is a kind of Money (a charge/levy, with children Departure tax and Value added tax, siblings Fee, Sponsorship, Tip), whereas B's Sponzor fee is a kind of Fee (a payment, sibling Registration fee). Although both concern money, Tax and Sponzor fee denote different concepts: a tax is a compulsory levy, a sponsor fee is a payment made by a sponsor. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A 'Regular author' is a role of a person who contributes a regular (non-invited) paper to a conference, a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor. B 'Regular Session' is a type of scientific event session (a scheduled meeting slot) under Session. They belong to different branches of the domain (contribution/author vs. event/session) and share only the word 'Regular'; their instances cannot coincide.

Chairman (cmt) is a Person role who chairs committees/conferences, with children Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair. Registration Student (sigkdd) is a fee category under Registration fee, denoting a student registration fee, not a person role. Different domains and no overlap.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person/Contact Information to a string email address. B's is_used_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person (the inverse of a 'uses' relation). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

An Invited talk is a presentation-type contribution given by an invited speaker, while a Short paper is a written contribution category (sibling of Paper and Poster). They denote different concepts: one is a talk/presentation, the other a short written paper. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a conference paper/contribution: A's Paper is a kind of Conference contribution (a regular contribution with an abstract), and B's Paper is a Document that is written by authors, has topics, and is reviewed. The intended instances (submitted/accepted papers) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite differing parents and sibling structure.

A's hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime value (the deadline date of a call for papers). B's is_sent_before is an object property linking an Item to a Time, expressing a temporal ordering between two entities. They differ in domain (Call vs Item), range (dateTime literal vs Time object), and meaning (a deadline attribute vs a precedence relation), so they are not the same relation.

A Workshop is a small interactive working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial under Working event), whereas a Plenary lecture is a large formal lecture given to all attendees (subclass of Lecture, sibling of Session and Tutorial). They denote different kinds of conference activities and are not equivalent.

A's 'event On List' relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (where the event is listed), while B's 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item to a Person (who gives it). Different domains and ranges, different intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Paper is a document class (subclass of Document, with children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version and properties like has Author, assigned To, has Decision). B's Camera ready manuscript deadline is a subclass of Deadline under Time, a temporal milestone in the conference schedule. A paper is not a deadline; the entities denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

hasPart is a generic mereological property relating a whole to its parts, while award is a specific relation linking something (e.g. a paper or author) to an Award. Their intended meanings and ranges differ entirely; no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

In cmt, Program Committee Member is a Conference Member who reviews papers (has max Papers, member Of Program Committee, children Program Committee Chair). In iasted, Author is a Speaker under Delegate, a person who writes papers, with children about proceedings inclusion and lecture speakers. The two denote different roles (reviewer/PC member vs paper author) with different parents and properties, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Computer Architecture Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in the edas ontology, while B 'Organizing Committee member' is a person role under Organizator in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (topic vs. person/role) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) that hosts paper presentations, while B's Conference Banquet is a social event (sibling of Conference Trip) — a dinner/banquet. They share only the word 'conference' and belong to disjoint branches (Working event vs Social Event), so they are not equivalent.
A records whether a conference accepts hardcopy submissions (boolean), while B records the city where a conference is held (string). Different intended meaning, different value types, no overlap.

confOf Student is a role of a Participant (a person attending the conference as a student), while sigkdd 'Author of paper student' is a subclass of Author denoting a student who authored a paper. Both involve students but in different roles (participant vs. author), so they overlap but are not equivalent.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a committee role within a conference (sibling of Program committee and Steering committee, linked to a Conference volume), whereas B's 'NGO' is a type of organization (sibling of Academia/Government/Industry Organization). They denote different concepts in different branches of the domain, so no reference alignment would equate them.

A's 'enter Conference Details' is an Administrator action whose domain is Administrator and range is Conference, i.e. an admin enters conference details. B's 'relates To' is a Document property linking a Document to an Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session or Person. Different domains (Administrator vs Document), different ranges (Conference vs multiple entities), and different intended meanings (data-entry action vs document association), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Meta Review' is a document (a review of reviews) in the cmt ontology, while B 'Reviewer' is a person role (a delegate/speaker who reviews) in iasted. They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a scientific contribution (written by authors, reviewed, has topics, subclasses Accepted/Rejected/Pending Paper). B's Transparency is a document item (sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance) in the conference-organisation paperwork, not a scientific paper. Different intended instances despite both being Documents.

A's Conference Chair is a Person/Chairman role (a person who chairs the conference), while B's Technical commitee is placed under Delegate/Conference building and denotes a committee/group of delegates, not an individual chairing role. Different kinds (person role vs. committee/group) and different contexts, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a subject/topic area in computer networks. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document types vs. topics) and share no intended instances.

A's 'is Initiated By' relates a Call to committee roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. who initiated/issued a call. B's 'is paid by' relates Money to a Person, i.e. who pays a fee. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's `lists Event` is an object property linking a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event (it lists events), while B's `End of conference` is a datatype property giving a Conference's end date/time. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution (paper) to an Author; iasted's 'is prepared by' links an Item (paper) to a Person. Both express the authorship relation from a paper-like entity to a person-like entity, in the same direction, so they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

A's 'is Topic Of' relates a Topic to a Conference/Paper (topic is subject of a paper), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity/Item (person gives a talk/item). Different domain, range, and direction of meaning; no equivalence.

A's 'assigned By Administrator' relates a Reviewer to an Administrator (the person who assigned the review), while B's 'belongs to reviewers' relates a Review expertise/preference to a Reviewer. Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.
Conference www is a conference document (a web page about the conference, with a URL), while Hotel is a physical place (venue accommodation). Different kinds of entities with no overlap.

edas:ConferenceVenuePlace is a generic venue place (siblings: Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) under Place, while iasted:Conference_restaurant is a specific building type (a restaurant) under Building, sibling to Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc. A conference venue place is not the same concept as a conference restaurant; the restaurant is one specific kind of building, not a venue place in general.

A's Excursion is a social event (sibling of Reception) within the conference's non-academic events, while B's Departure is an activity after the conference (sibling of Full day tour), i.e. a post-conference departure/travel activity. Although both can involve travel, they denote different concepts: an excursion is an organized social outing during the event, whereas a departure is the act/arrangement of leaving after the conference. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's 'Plenary lecture' is a kind of conference activity/lecture (an event), while B's 'Invited Speaker' is a kind of person (a speaker). They belong to disjoint branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference document is a conference-level document (call for papers, announcements, etc.), while Abstract is a paper-level document with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract. They are different document types in the conference domain.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (a person), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (a paper). Different domain, range, and direction of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a publisher' links a Conference proceedings to a Publisher; B's 'has Menu' links a Meal Event to a Meal Menu. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are unrelated.

Organization in confOf is an institution (parent of Company and University) that employs people and has an address; Award in sigkdd is a prize given to papers/authors. Different concepts with no overlap.

A is an administrative event (the act/process of submitting contributions), while B is a deadline (a point in time) for registration. They belong to different branches (Event vs Time/Deadline) and denote different concepts; the only overlap is the word 'submission'/'registration' in the domain, not the concept.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (sibling of Single Level Conference, child of Conference), while B's 'IASTED member' is a kind of Delegate/person (child of Delegate, sibling of Speaker, Listener, Session chair). One denotes an event type, the other a person role; they are unrelated.
A's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (object property), while B's 'done till' relates a Deadline to a date (datatype property). Different domains, ranges, and kinds; no shared meaning.

A's Session is a scientific event (a time slot/meeting within a conference, with children like Conference Session, Workshop Session), while B's Author is a person role (a speaker who writes papers, with properties submit/obtain/notification). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. person) and share no intended instances.

Regular is a subclass of Participant in confOf, denoting a participant who is not a student or member (a specific registration category). Attendee in edas is a direct subclass of Person and is the general role of anyone attending the conference, with siblings Author, Reviewer, etc. Thus Regular is a narrower concept than Attendee: every Regular is an Attendee, but not every Attendee is a Regular. Hence Regular is subsumed by Attendee, not equivalent.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person who takes part in a conference (parent Person, children Active/Passive conference participant), whereas B 'Excursion' is a Social Event (a non-academic conference event, sibling of Reception). A person and a social event are entirely different kinds of entity, so the classes are unrelated.

A's Review is a document that is written by a reviewer and evaluated by the PC chair, with Meta Review as a child. B's Paper is a document written by an author, reviewed by reviewers, with children like Accepted/Rejected Paper. They are distinct document types in the conference domain (a review is not a paper), so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chair of the conference, sibling of Program Committee Chair, Author, Reviewer), while Meal Break is a non-academic conference event (a break event, sibling of Coffee Break and Free Time Break). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different kinds of things.

A 'Conference contribution' is a submitted scholarly work (paper, poster, talk) that is part of a conference volume and is submitted at a conference volume. B 'Payment document' is a financial document (bank transfer, cheque) under Document. Their paths, children, siblings and properties are entirely different; they share no intended instances.

A's 'ends on' is a datatype property of Event giving the end date/time of an event, while B's 'Name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's name. Different domains (Event vs Person) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Meal Break' is a non-academic break event in the conference schedule, while B 'Program Committee' is a committee of people. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. committee) and share no intended instances.

A's TPC Member is a Person who reviews papers and initiates calls (siblings: Reviewer, Author, Session Chair); B's Author is a Speaker/Delegate who produces proceedings and lectures (children: proceedings included, Lecturer, Plenary lecture speaker). The roles differ: program-committee membership vs. authorship, so the classes are not equivalent.

Break Event (edas) is a Non Academic Event covering coffee breaks, free time and meals, while Scientific Event (ekaw) is the parent of Conference, Session, Track, Workshop and Individual Presentation. They denote disjoint kinds of event (leisure/break vs. scientific activity), so they are not equivalent.

ekaw's `references` relates a paper/contribution to another paper it cites (bibliographic citation), while iasted's `sign` relates a Person to an Item (a person signing something). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of academic event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Presenter house is a building/place (sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts — an event versus a physical location — so they are unrelated.

A's Tutorial is a working event (a class of event, sibling of Conference and Workshop), while B's Tutorial Chair is a person role (a subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

A Workshop is a working event (a session type where participants work, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B Free Time Break is a non-academic break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break). They denote entirely different kinds of conference events and share no intended instances.

A's 'has the first name' is a specific datatype property for a person's given name, while B's 'Name' is a general name property for a Person. A first name is a kind of name, so the first-name property is strictly narrower than the general Name property; they are not equivalent.

A's Review is the general review document class (sibling of Paper, Programme, etc. under Document), while B's Positive Review is a specific subtype of Review (sibling of Negative/Neutral Review). A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

A's `location Of` relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location). B's `search` relates the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (sponsor), an entirely different relation in a different part of the domain. Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference, sibling of Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, etc.), whereas Exhibitor in sigkdd is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsoring organisation tier, sibling of Gold Supporter, Silver Supporter, etc.). One denotes a person, the other a sponsoring entity; they share no intended instances and are unrelated.

cmt's Conference Member is a broad class covering all people involved in a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, PC members, etc.), while ekaw's OC Member is specifically a member of the organising committee, a narrower role. They overlap in that OC members are conference members, but the intended instance sets do not coincide, so they are related rather than equivalent.

confOf Person is a person/agent class (children Administrator, Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.) with properties like has First Name, employed By, has Fax. edas Contact Information is an address/contact-details class (has City, has Email, has Phone, has Postal Code, has Street) whose instances are contact records, not people. Although both share contact properties, the intended instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A's `reviews` links a Review to the Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed), whereas B's `has Review History` links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a collection of that reviewer's past reviews). Different domains (Review vs Reviewer), different ranges (Reviewed contribution vs Personal Review History), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection) in cmt, while Rejected Paper is a document/paper state (sibling of Accepted Paper) in ekaw. They denote different kinds of entities (decision vs. paper), so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the non-academic social gatherings of a conference: edas 'Social Event' sits under Non Academic Event with children Excursion and Reception, while iasted 'Social program' sits under Conference activity with child Dinner banquet and sibling Coctail reception. The intended instances (receptions, banquets, excursions) coincide, so the two classes are equivalent despite the different labels and paths.

A's locationOf relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's is_made_from relates an Item to another Item (material composition). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'co write Paper' relates a Co author to a Paper they co-authored (domain Co author, range Paper). B's 'has Related Paper' relates an Author to a Paper that is merely related (e.g. a paper they reviewed or are otherwise associated with), not necessarily authored. The domains differ (Co author vs Author) and the intended semantics differ (co-authorship vs general relatedness), so the properties are not equivalent.

cmt:adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (the bid the reviewer adjusts), while ekaw:reviewerOfPaper relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the paper they review). Both connect a reviewer to a submission-related object, but the ranges differ (Bid vs Paper) and the intended semantics differ (adjusting a bid vs being assigned to review a paper), so they are not equivalent; they are related concepts in the reviewing workflow.

In ekaw, PC Chair is a subclass of both Conference Participant and PC Member, i.e. a person who chairs the program committee. In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a subclass of Organizator, i.e. a member of the program committee (not necessarily the chair). The two denote different roles: chair vs. member. Although related in the conference domain, they are not equivalent; the ekaw PC Chair is more specific than a generic PC member, but sigkdd's class is not the chair role, so neither subsumption direction holds cleanly. Hence unrelated.

A's 'reject Paper' relates an Administrator to a Paper (a decision action), while B's 'paper Presented As' relates a Paper to an Individual Presentation (a presentation-format relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A is a conference topic area (parallel/distributed computing) under Topic, while B is a research activity (simulating) under Activity before conference > Research. They denote different kinds of entities (topic vs. activity) and share no intended instances.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/member of the conference committee) in cmt, while B 'Activity after conference' is a social/event activity (with children Departure and Full day tour) in iasted. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (rejecting a submission), while B's issues relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing them). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so the properties are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a scientific meeting, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Conference Trip is a social event (an excursion, sibling of Conference Banquet). They share only the word 'conference' and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is an event/venue class (children Single Level Conference, Two Level Conference; properties like paper Due On, has Country, has Topic), whereas B's Conference Participant is a subclass of Person (a role a person plays at a conference). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person/role), so they are unrelated.

Reception is a social event (a gathering) in confOf, sibling of Banquet and Trip under Social event. Publication in iasted is a published item (parent of Book proceeding, Cd proceening) under Item. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Hotel fee is a specific kind of Fee (a fee charged for hotel accommodation), while sigkdd's Fee is the general superclass with children Registration fee and Sponzor fee. Thus Hotel fee is strictly narrower and is subsumed by Fee, not equivalent.

A's hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (e.g. a conference to its sub-events), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the person who presented it). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Non Academic Event covers breaks, meals and social events, i.e. non-scholarly activities, while B's Scientific Event covers conferences, sessions, tracks and workshops, i.e. scholarly activities. They are complementary opposites under Conference Event / Event, not the same concept.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to the Location where it is held (domain Event, range Location). B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD (the conference series/organisation) to a Conference (domain ACM SIGKDD, range Conference), i.e. the series holds/contains a conference edition. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A 'Talk Event' is an academic conference event (a talk given at a conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), while B 'Transport vehicle' is a physical item used for transportation (with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members; B's isProviderOf links an Organization to a Sponsorship. Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a talk given by an invited speaker), while B's 'Poster Session' is a session event in which posters are presented. They denote different concepts: one is a contribution type, the other an event/session type, with no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution holding the paper's abstract text (range string), while B's 'has amount of' is a datatype property of Money holding a monetary quantity (range int). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

confOf's Student is a Participant (a person attending the conference as a student), while iasted's Student lecturer is a role under Lecturer (a person who is both student and lecturer, i.e. a teaching assistant-like role). They overlap in that both denote students involved in the conference, but neither subsumes the other: a Student in confOf need not be a lecturer, and a Student lecturer in iasted is a lecturer role, not a participant category. Hence related, not equivalent.

Administrator in cmt is a person role managing the conference (accepts papers, assigns reviewers, enters conference details), while Scholar in confOf is a person with a price category (scholar) who studies at a university. Their paths, siblings, and properties do not coincide; no subsumption or overlap in meaning.

A is a research topic area (Operating Systems topics) under Topic in edas, while B is an organisation type (organising agency, e.g. a conference organising body) under Organisation in ekaw. They share no meaning, instances, or properties; the superficial word overlap ('Operating'/'Organising') is coincidental.

Both classes denote the physical place/location where a conference event is held. edas Place has children Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place and is linked to Conference Event via has Location / is Location Of; ekaw Location is linked to Event via held In / location Of. The domain/range patterns match exactly (Event -> Place/Location and Place/Location -> Event), so the intended instances coincide.

A 'Personal Publication History' is a record/history of an author's publications (a subclass of Personal History, sibling of Personal Review History), whereas B 'Publication' is a document/item class (subclass of Item, with children Book proceeding and Cd proceening). They denote different concepts: a history record vs. a published work, so they are not equivalent.

Both entities denote the role of a person who chairs a session at a conference. In edas, Session Chair is a subclass of Person with properties such as initiates Call and is Reviewed By Paper, which align with the responsibilities of a session chair. In ekaw, Session Chair is also a subclass of Person and is involved in similar relations (e.g., is Reviewing, is Reviewed By). The labels and contexts match, indicating they represent the same concept.

startDate is a datatype property (domain Conference, range dateTime) recording a conference's start date, while listsEvent is an object property (domain Programme Brochure/Web Site, range Event) linking a document to an event. Different kinds, domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman who leads the conference, sibling of Program Committee Chair and Author under Person > Chairman). B 'Student non speaker' is a delegate subtype (a student attending without presenting, under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Non speaker). They denote entirely different concepts: an organiser role versus an attendee category, with no overlap in instances.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a conference has members/participants), while B's presentationed by relates a Document to a Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Important dates' is a class of deadline/date information belonging to a conference volume (submission, acceptance, camera-ready dates). B's 'Individual Presentation' is a scientific event (a talk given at a conference, with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial) that presents a paper. The two denote entirely different concepts — a set of dates versus a presentation event — with no overlap in instances, properties, or position in the hierarchy.

A's reviewOfPaper links a Review to the Paper it reviews (domain Review, range Paper). B's presentationed_by links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A Meal Break is a break event (a pause for eating, sibling of Coffee Break and Free Time Break) within the conference schedule, whereas an EKAW Conference Trip is a social event (sibling of Conference Banquet) — an excursion/outing. They denote different kinds of conference events and are not equivalent.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role/author-position class (a first author of a contribution, sibling of 'Contribution co author', under 'Regular author'), while B's 'Proceedings' is a document/volume class (a multi-author volume containing conference proceedings). They denote different kinds of things (an author role vs. a published volume), so they are unrelated.

A is the registration fee for non-members, while B is the registration fee for students. They are distinct fee categories (siblings under Registration fee in both ontologies), so the classes do not denote the same concept.

A's `need` relates a Person to an Item (a person needs an item), while B's `searched by` relates a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (a sponsor is searched by a specific organisation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation nor inverses.

max Papers is a datatype property of Program Committee Member giving an integer maximum number of papers, while min Choice is a datatype property of Social/Working event giving a positiveInteger minimum choice; different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference/committee), while B's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship). They connect different kinds of entities in opposite directions and express different relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document/contribution class (parent Document, children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To Reviewer). B's Paper Presentation is an academic event (parent Academic Event, siblings Workshop/Talk Event/Organizational Meeting) that an Accepted Paper is related to. The two denote different concepts: a written contribution versus the event at which it is presented, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'default Choice' is a datatype property linking a Social/Working event to a positiveInteger (a default choice value, confTool-specific), while B's 'is given by' is an object property linking an Activity/Item to a Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, and range, so they cannot denote the same relation.

cmt:User is a general person role (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer) representing any system user, while ekaw:PC Member is a specific reviewer role (a Possible Reviewer who is on the program committee, parent of PC Chair, SC Member, etc.). The intended instances do not coincide: a User need not be a PC Member and a PC Member is a specific committee role. They are different concepts, so unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a surname literal), while B's 'authorOf' is an object property mapping a Person to a Document (authorship relation). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and cannot be equivalent.

A's 'Rejected contribution' is a specific outcome of review (sibling of Accepted contribution), while B's 'Evaluated Paper' is the general class of papers that have been evaluated, with children Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper. Thus Rejected contribution is strictly narrower than Evaluated Paper, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'has tracks' links a Conference volume to its Track(s) (a structural part-of relation, sub-property of has parts), while B's 'has Location' links a Conference Event to a Place (a spatial location relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (conference membership), while B's is occupied by relates a Building/City/State to a Person (occupancy of a location). Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Both are Person subclasses denoting the top-level conference organizer role. In edas, Conference Chair is a Person sibling of Author/Reviewer/TPC Member and initiates calls and reviews; in sigkdd, General Chair is an Organizator (organizing-committee role) alongside Program Chair and Webmaster. The intended instances coincide: the person who chairs the conference overall. The differing parent (Person vs Organizator) reflects only the local hierarchy, and the role is the same in the conference domain.

A's Talk Event is a kind of academic event (a scheduled talk such as a welcome or closing talk) within the conference event hierarchy, while B's Audiovisual equipment is a physical item (with children Computer, LCD projector, etc.) used for presentations. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A Talk Event is a single academic talk (with children Welcome Talk, Closing Talk) under Academic Event, while B Session is a broader scientific event containing multiple presentations (children Conference Session, Regular Session, etc.). A talk is a part of a session rather than the same concept, so they overlap but are not equivalent.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference, sibling of Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, etc.), while B's Registration SIGKDD Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category, sibling of Registration Student, Registration Non Member). One denotes a person type, the other a fee/payment category; they are not the same concept.

confOf's Participant is a broad role class under Person covering all conference attendees (children Member, Regular, Student; siblings Author, Chair PC, etc.), while iasted's Author is a narrow role under Speaker (a kind of Delegate) denoting someone who authored a paper. Every iasted Author is a conference participant, but not every Participant is an Author, so Participant is strictly more general than Author.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role (a Person subclass with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B 'Registration fee' is a monetary Fee subclass. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of regular conference contribution (sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract), i.e. a submitted paper type. B's 'Invited Talk Abstract' is an abstract document for an invited talk (sibling of Tutorial Abstract), a distinct document type tied to invited presentations. Different intended instances and different positions in the taxonomies, so they are not equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an activity) in the ekaw ontology, while B Sponsor company house is a building/place in the iasted ontology. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. location) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a Person (External Reviewer) in cmt, while B is a Document (Paper) in sigkdd. They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. documents) and share no properties or intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (a person/role in the committee), while B's is_submitted_at relates a Conference contribution (paper) to a Conference volume (proceedings/venue). Different domain and range, different direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

Conference www is a document/web-page class (a conference website) under Conference document, with property has a URL. Academic Event is an event class under Conference Event, with children such as Workshop and Talk Event and properties has Call / for Event. A website document and an academic event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

A 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (a conference activity such as a banquet, reception or trip), while B 'Document' is a subclass of Item and covers paper artefacts (forms, invitations, reviews, submissions). They share no instances and no properties; the only overlap is the word 'event'/'document' being unrelated concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference topic category (Operating Systems topics) under Topic, while B is a research activity (Simulating) under Activity before conference > Research. They belong to different branches (topic taxonomy vs. activity taxonomy) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Reception is a specific kind of social event (a reception), while ekaw's Social Event is the general category whose children are Conference Banquet and Conference Trip. Reception is therefore narrower than Social Event, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person denoting a person who participates in a conference (with subclasses Active/Passive participant). B's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and oddly also of Person/TPC Member) denoting a type of conference with two levels, not a person. The entities denote different kinds of things (person vs. conference), so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a conference event (Welcome Talk, a kind of Talk Event). Their paths, parents and siblings are entirely disjoint (Person vs Conference Event), so they denote different concepts.

A's Conference is a working event (a scientific meeting, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Conference Venue Place is a physical place (sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). One denotes an event, the other a location, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the person who delivers the talk), while B's 'is writen by' links an Item (a paper/contribution) to a Person (its author). Both relate a conference artefact to a person, but the artefact types (Presentation vs Item/paper) and the roles (speaker vs author) differ, so they are not equivalent; they overlap only in the general sense of attributing a person to a work.

A Workshop is a working event (a meeting/event type alongside Conference and Tutorial), whereas B Contributed Talk is a kind of individual presentation (a talk given at an event, sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a presentation, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the general notion of an event in the conference domain. confOf's Event is the superclass of Administrative/Social/Working events, and ekaw's Event is the superclass of Scientific/Social Event, with properties like starts/ends on and held In/organised By that describe the same kind of entity. The intended instances (conference events such as sessions, social events) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A 'Contributed Talk' is a kind of scientific event/individual presentation (a talk given at a conference), while B 'Sponsor state' is a state of a sponsor in the conference process. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs State) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Session chair is a role/person type under Delegate (a delegate who chairs a session). One is an event, the other a person role; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while B's 'Cryptography Topic' is a subject area/topic for classifying papers. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts.

A's 'Program committee' is a committee (a group/organisational body) that a conference volume has, with siblings Organizing committee and Steering committee. B's 'Conference Chair' is a Person role (sibling of Attendee, Author, Reviewer, TPC Member) who initiates calls and reviews papers. A committee and an individual person role denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent; the only shared word is 'committee/chair' context, which is insufficient.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman of the conference, subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while B 'Sponsor company house' is a building/place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. location), so they are unrelated.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person role in the conference), while B's Registration Non-Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category). They denote different concepts: a person type vs. a fee type. Note B has a sibling 'Registration Student' which is the fee counterpart, not the person class, so no equivalence.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Main office is a place (sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). An event and a location are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated despite the shared word 'conference'.

Both properties relate a Person to a written work: ekaw's authorOf has domain Person and range Document, while iasted's sign has domain Person and range Item, where Item is the iasted class for a written contribution (paper). The intended meaning — a person being the author of a document/item — coincides, so the two object properties are equivalent.

A's `obtain` is an object property linking a Person to an Item (a thing acquired), while B's `E mail` is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address). Different kinds of entities and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A is the deadline for notification of acceptance (author notification), while B is the deadline for paper submission. They are distinct deadlines in the conference timeline, with different siblings (A's siblings include Submissions deadline and Camera ready; B's siblings include Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Author notification).

confOf's 'Member PC' (comment: Reviewer) is a Person who reviews contributions and is expert on topics; ekaw's 'OC Member' is a Conference Participant who is a member of the organising committee (parent of OC Chair, sibling of PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.). Both denote a member of the programme/organising committee of a conference, i.e. a person serving on the committee that reviews and organises the conference. The labels differ but the intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

A's 'Invited Speaker' is a kind of person (a Presenter who is invited), while B's 'Presenter city' is a kind of City (a city where a presenter is located), as shown by its parent City and siblings Conference city, Sponsor city, Trip city. They denote different concepts (person role vs. location) and are unrelated.
