cmt:Conference Member is a broad role class (parent of Author, Reviewer, Chair, PC Member) covering anyone involved in a conference, while iasted:IASTED_member is a specific subclass of Delegate denoting a delegate who is a member of IASTED. The IASTED member is a kind of conference participant, so it is narrower than the general Conference Member; the two do not coincide.

A's 'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them; B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to the Speaker who presented it. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's Document is a conference submission artefact (children Paper, Review; range of hasConflictOfInterest), while B's Card is a physical item (sibling of Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle, with child Credit card). Different domains, no overlap.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class representing a reviewer's expertise/preference area, linked to Reviewer and Submitted contribution. B's 'Review' is a subclass of Document representing the review document itself, with siblings Abstract and Paper. They denote different concepts (expertise vs. review document), so they are unrelated.

A's `date` is a datatype property linking a Conference to a date value; B's `locationOf` is an object property linking a Location to an Event. Different domain, range, and kind, so they cannot denote the same relation.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad class of people involved in a conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers) with properties linking them to a Conference. In iasted, Non speaker is a subclass of Delegate denoting attendees who do not give a talk (students, workers), a much narrower and different concept. The two classes do not denote the same set of instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person who finalizes paper assignments), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (submission act). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

A Poster is a kind of conference contribution (a paper/presentation format with an abstract), while B Invitation letter is a document sent to invite someone (sibling of Form, Payment document, Viza). Different intended instances and different domain roles; no subsumption or overlap.

A's property links a Conference part to a Topic (the subject matter of a track/workshop/tutorial), while B's property links a Person to an Item (something a person needs). The domains (Conference part vs Person) and ranges (Topic vs Item) are disjoint, so the two properties relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's Chairman is a Person who chairs (has subclasses Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair) and is involved in conflict-of-interest marking. B's Member PC is a Person who reviews contributions and is expert on topics (comment: Reviewer). The chair role and the PC-member/reviewer role are distinct roles in the conference domain, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's Conference Venue Place is a kind of Place (a physical location where a conference is held), sibling to Accommodation/Dining/Meeting Room places. B's Sponsor city is a kind of City, sibling to Conference city, Presenter city and Trip city — i.e. a city role in the conference organisation (the city of a sponsor), not a venue place. Although both are location-like, the intended instances differ: one is a venue/place, the other a city classified by the role of its associated entity. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item to a Person (the giver/presenter), while B's 'award' relates something to an Award (a prize entity). Different domain and range, different intended meaning; not equivalent.

A Publisher is an organisation that issues conference proceedings (domain of 'issues', range of 'has a publisher'). ACM SIGKDD is a specific conference series/organisation that designs deadlines, holds conferences and searches sponsors; it is not a publisher of proceedings, and the two classes have no shared instances or properties in the conference domain.

A's property links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a committee entity), while B's property links a Conference to a Person (a member). Different domain (volume vs conference) and different range (committee vs person), so they are not the same relation.

Both properties link a document/activity to the person who presents/gives it, but the domains differ: iasted's 'is given by' applies to Activity or Item (broader, includes events and items), while sigkdd's 'presentationed by' applies only to Document and ranges over Speaker. The intended relation (presenter of a paper) overlaps but the iasted property is more general, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Topic is the general subject-area class (domain of dealsWith, expertOn, hasTopic), while B's Antennas Topic is a specific topic under the parent Topic in edas. The specific antennas topic is strictly narrower than the general Topic class, so A is subsumed by B's broader Topic concept; they are not equivalent.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it, while B's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it. Different domains (Sponsorship vs Event), different ranges (Organization vs Organisation/Person), and different intended relations (funding/sponsoring vs organising), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property holding a person's surname, while B's 'E mail' holds an email address; both are Person->string datatype properties but denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

A's User is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/Administrator), while B's University is an academic organisation (parent Academic Institution, sibling Research Institute). Different kinds of entities entirely.

A 'Personal Publication History' is a class representing a person's history/list of their own publications (a subclass of Personal History, sibling of Personal Review History). B 'Book proceeding' is a subclass of Publication denoting a published book of conference proceedings. They denote different concepts: one is a personal record/history, the other is a type of publication. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

Both classes denote the same role: the chair of the program committee. confOf's Chair PC is a Person role (comment 'confTool'), and ekaw's PC Chair is a Conference Participant that is also a PC Member, i.e. a program committee member who chairs it. The labels are synonyms and the intended instances coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper), while B's 'designed by' relates a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event (the act/phase of submitting contributions) in confOf, while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee (a group of people) in sigkdd. They belong to different branches (Event vs Committee) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Paper is the general document class for conference submissions (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, sibling of Review), while ekaw:Rejected Paper is a specific evaluated paper that was rejected, a sibling of Accepted Paper. The general Paper subsumes the more specific Rejected Paper, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role/class of authors (a person who is the first author of a conference contribution), sitting under Regular author with sibling Contribution co author. B's 'Conference' is a working event (a type of event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). They denote entirely different concepts — an author role versus an event — so they are unrelated.

A's setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while B's has_members relates a Committee to its members. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/member of the conference committee) in the cmt ontology, while B 'Conference restaurant' is a building/place in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. place) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a conference contributor who gives an invited talk, while B's 'Chair PC' is the person chairing the program committee (confTool role). They are distinct roles in the conference domain, with different parents (Conference contributor vs Person) and different siblings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a conference-role class (an Author who is not a Reviewer), while B's 'Student' is a general person type (a Person who is a student). Their paths, parents and siblings differ entirely: Author Not Reviewer sits under Author/Conference Member, Student sits directly under Person alongside Conference Participant and Paper Author. A student may or may not be an author, and an author who is not a reviewer need not be a student, so the classes do not coincide.

Both are datatype properties named 'has Street' mapping an entity to a string street address. Although the domains differ (Organization/Person in confOf vs Contact Information in edas), the intended relation is the same: the street part of an address. The domain difference reflects modelling style (edas groups address fields under a Contact Information class), not a different relation, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

Subject Area in cmt is a topic classification of papers (range of has Subject Area, Paper -> Subject Area), whereas Conference in sigkdd is an event with city, start/end dates, name, and held-by relations. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who did the inviting), while B's 'has Review History' relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History object. Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property of a Conference document (the date a paper/document was issued), while B's 'End of conference' is a datatype property of a Conference giving the conference's end date. Different domains (document vs conference) and different intended meaning (issue/publication date vs conference end), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (a kind of Conference, sibling of Single Level Conference), while B's 'Session Chair' is a person role (a Conference Participant). They denote different concepts entirely; the shared parent 'Person' in A is an artifact of edas's multiple inheritance and does not make them equivalent.

A's 'Sponsor company house' is a Building subtype used to house sponsor companies, while B's 'Hotel' is a Place subtype for lodging; they denote different concepts (sponsor accommodation vs. hotel), so a reference alignment would not equate them.

A's Presenter is a role a person plays at the conference (a subclass of Conference Participant, with child Invited Speaker), while B's Conference building is a physical venue (a subclass of Building, with child Delegate). They denote different kinds of entities (person role vs. place) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is the umbrella event entity (has dates, country, topics, papers due, sessions, members), while B's Committee is a group of people (with subclasses Organizing/Program/Best Paper Awards Committee). They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

Company in confOf is an organization type (sibling of University under Organization), denoting an industrial institution. Medicine Topic in edas is a research subject area under Topic, denoting a field of study. They belong to entirely different branches (organization vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

Conference part is a structural component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) in the Conference ontology, while Speaker is a Person subtype (with Author and Invited Speaker children) in sigkdd. Their paths, children, and properties (conference-part roles/topics vs. presentation relations) do not overlap; they denote different concepts.

A's Social Event is a broad category of non-academic social events (children include Excursion and Reception, siblings Break Event and Meal Event), while B's Conference Trip is a specific kind of social event (sibling Conference Banquet) under a Social Event parent. A is therefore more general than B, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a submitted document in the conference domain), while B is a subclass of Deadline (a time point for hotel reservation). They share no meaning, no properties, and belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Time).

A's has Cost Amount is a datatype property giving the monetary cost of a Sponsorship (range int), while B's Name of sponsor is a datatype property giving the name of a Sponzor (range string). They relate different kinds of values (cost vs. name) and are not the same relation.

Withdrawn Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document status), while Deadline Paper Submission is a subclass of Deadline (a time point). They belong to different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property giving a string title to Social/Working events, while B's 'has Start Date Time' gives a dateTime start to a Conference Event. Different domain concepts (title vs. start time) and different ranges (string vs. dateTime), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'relates To' links a Document to any of several entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person). Different domains (Conference vs Document), different ranges (Administrator vs a broad set), and different intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is a specific working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) under Event > Working event, whereas B's Academic Event is a broader category under Conference Event that has Workshop and other events as children. A Conference is a kind of academic event, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's hasEmail relates a Person to an email string, while B's hasPhone relates Contact Information to a phone string. They denote different contact attributes (email vs phone) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper they were assigned to review), while B's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a record of past reviews). The ranges differ (Paper vs Personal Review History) and the intended meanings differ: assignment of a paper to review vs. a history of reviews performed. They are not the same relation.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person who started the bidding process), while B's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Topic is a subject area / keyword used to classify reviews, contributions and conference parts (it has a name and is linked to Review preference and Conference part). B's Individual Presentation is a kind of Scientific Event (a presentation event with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial) that presents a Paper. A subject/topic is not an event, so the two classes denote different concepts and are unrelated.

Both are object properties linking a written work (Document in ekaw, Item in iasted) to a Person as its author, with the same direction (work -> person). The domain classes Document and Item denote the same kind of artefact in the conference domain, and the ranges are identical (Person), so the two properties relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (Paper/Poster/Short paper) written by an Author and reviewed by PC members, whereas Time in iasted is a temporal entity with children Conference days, Deadline and Trip day, used as the range of temporal relations such as is held before/after. The two concepts share no instances and no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial or workshop), while B's IASTED non member is a type of Delegate (a person attending). They denote different concepts (event vs. person/role), so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a document (a conference document, the review artefact, with properties linking it to a reviewed contribution), while B's Reviewing event is an administrative event in the reviewing procedure. They concern the same activity but denote different kinds of entities (document vs. event), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's `occupy` relates a Person to a physical location (Building, City, State), while B's `pay` relates a Person to a Registration fee. The ranges are disjoint kinds of entities (place vs. monetary fee), so the properties do not denote the same relation.

A's 'has gender' is a datatype property linking a Person to a gender value, while B's 'is present in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place/Time. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no shared meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a kind of conference contributor (a person invited to speak), while B's 'Administrator' is a confTool administrative role under Person, with no overlap in intended instances; the shared parent Person is too general to imply equivalence.

Both are social events of a conference, but an Excursion (a trip/outing) is not the same as a Conference Banquet (a formal dinner). They are distinct sibling-like social event types, so they are related but not equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (Paper/Poster/Short paper) with title, abstract, keywords, authors and reviews. Deadline in sigkdd is a submission/notification date with a dateTime value and submission deadlines. They denote different concepts (a work vs. a point in time), so they are unrelated.

Chairman is a person role (a subclass of Person, with children like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), while Deadline is a temporal concept (a subclass of Time, with children like submission and registration deadlines). They denote entirely different kinds of entities and share no intended instances.

A 'Conference proceedings' is a published volume (has publisher, volume, ISBN) that contains papers; B 'Document' is a general superclass of Abstract, Paper and Review. Proceedings are a kind of document/contribution, so Conference proceedings is strictly narrower than Document, not equivalent.

Company in confOf is an organizational entity (sibling of University under Organization), while Computer Networks Security Topic in edas is a research topic in a topic taxonomy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subclass covering all who contribute to a conference (authors, speakers, participants, committee members, reviewers), while Organizing Committee member is a narrower role under Organizator (alongside General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). The two overlap in that committee members are contributors, but neither subsumes the other cleanly: contributor is broader than the organizing-committee role, yet the sigkdd class is specifically an organizer role, not a general contributor. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a document/presentation given by an invited speaker), while B's 'Radio Communications Topic' is a subject-area topic used to classify submissions. They belong to entirely different branches (contribution vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact. B's 'Lecture' is a conference activity (subclass of Conference activity, with children Plenary lecture, Session, Tutorial), i.e. an event that takes place. A document and an activity denote different kinds of things, so the classes are not equivalent and do not even overlap.

A's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (author submits a paper), while B's expert On relates a PC member to a Topic (PC member's area of expertise). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent nor inverse.

confOf Scholar is a Person subclass representing a price category (scholar), with property study At (Scholar -> University). iasted Author is a Speaker subclass in the delegate hierarchy, with children for proceedings inclusion and lecture types. The intended instances differ: a Scholar is a fee/price category person, while an Author is a speaker who authored contributions. They are not the same concept.

University is a specific type of academic organization, while NGO (non-governmental organization) is a distinct organizational category. They are siblings under Organization in different ontologies but denote different concepts; a University is not an NGO.

A's 'Individual Presentation' is a Scientific Event (a talk/presentation event with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial), while B's 'Paper' is a Document (sibling of Abstract and Review). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a written document, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Camera Ready event' is an administrative event in the conference workflow (the deadline/step for submitting camera-ready versions), while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee (a group of people). They belong to different branches (Event vs Committee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both denote a tutorial event in the conference domain. In confOf, Tutorial is a Working event alongside Conference and Workshop; in iasted, Tutorial is a Lecture (a Conference activity) alongside Plenary lecture and Session. Despite different parent hierarchies, the intended instances coincide: a tutorial is a teaching/presentation activity at a conference, so the classes are equivalent.

A 'Rejected Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document that was rejected), while B 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity in the conference process (accepting a manuscript), not a document. Different kinds (class of documents vs. activity) and different meaning, so unrelated.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's 'is present' relates a Person to a Time (a person being present at a time). Different domains (Location vs Person), different ranges (Event vs Time), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a part-whole relation between a conference component and a published volume). B's 'hasEvent' relates an Event to an Event (a containment/aggregation relation between events, e.g. a conference has sub-events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic belongs to a review preference), while B's expertOn links a PC member to a Topic (a member is expert on a topic). Different domains (Topic vs Member PC), different ranges (Review preference vs Topic), and different directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference Member is a Person (a person who belongs to a conference, with subclasses Author, Reviewer, PC Member, Chair), whereas B's Committee is an organizational body (with subclasses Organizing/Program/Steering committee) that has members and chairs. The two denote different kinds of entities (person vs. group/body), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Member' is a Person subtype (a person involved in the conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's 'Conference Session' is an event/session entity related to documents and academic events. They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (the authors of a paper), while B's 'has Related Paper' links an Author to a Paper (papers related to that author). The domains and ranges differ (Conference document vs Author; Person vs Paper), and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

Research Topic in ekaw is a subject area that events and papers cover (covers Topic: Event, Paper -> Research Topic). ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd is the organising body/association that designs deadlines, holds conferences and searches sponsors. A topic of interest and an organisation are different concepts, so the classes are unrelated.
accept Paper relates an Administrator to a Paper (acceptance decision), while parallel with relates two Administrative events (scheduling overlap). Different domains, ranges and meanings.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution of a paper), while B's 'organised By' relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organiser of an event). Different domains (Person vs Event), different ranges (Conference document vs Organisation/Person), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is used by' is an object property linking an Item to a Person (the person who uses the item), while B's 'Nation' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their nationality). They differ in kind (object vs datatype), in domain (Item vs Person), in range (Person vs string), and in meaning, so they are unrelated.

A is a document type (an abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B is a subject area/topic (a kind of Topic, sibling of Cryptography Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

Both are classes named Review, both are direct subclasses of Document, and in the conference domain a review is the document containing reviewer evaluations. The sibling differences (Meal Menu, Programme, Slide Set vs Abstract) reflect broader ontology scope, not a different meaning of Review.

A's property links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (a reviewer's stated preference), while B's property links an activity/item to a person (the giver/author). Different domain and range concepts and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (a person is a member of a conference), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference (the organisation holds the conference). Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference submission document (children Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version; properties has Author, assigned To Reviewer, has Decision, has Subject Area). B's Meal Menu is a catering document for a meal event (properties has Menu / is Menu Of Meal Event). Despite both being subclasses of Document, they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

Company in confOf is a for-profit organisation sibling to University under Organization, whereas Research Institute in ekaw is an academic institution sibling to University under Academic Institution. They denote different kinds of organisation (industrial vs academic), so they are not equivalent.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Excursion, under Social Event), i.e. a social gathering. B's Welcome address is a conference activity (sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Registration), i.e. a formal opening talk. Although B's siblings include Coctail reception, the entities themselves denote different concepts: a social event vs. a speech/activity. They are not equivalent.
A's 'has a committee chair' relates a Committee to its Chair (a person role), while B's 'heldIn' relates an Event to a Location. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's hasCostCurrency is a datatype property mapping a Sponsorship to a string currency code, while B's is_paid_with is an object property mapping Money to an Item (the thing used to pay). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have different domains/ranges, so they are not the same relation.

Both denote the person who chairs a committee: cmt's Chairman is a Person with subclasses for conference/program-committee chairs and a conflict-of-interest role, while Conference's Chair is a Committee member who chairs a committee (has a committee chair / was a committee chair of). The intended instances coincide (a chairing person), so they are equivalent despite the different parent (Person vs Committee member).

Presenter house (iasted) is a Building subtype used as lodging for presenters, while Conference hall (sigkdd) is a Place subtype denoting a venue hall for conference sessions. Both are conference-related places, but they denote different kinds of location (accommodation vs. meeting venue), so they are not equivalent; they merely overlap as conference places.

SC Member (Steering Committee Member) is a role a person holds in the conference organisation hierarchy (a subclass of PC Member), whereas Registration Student is a fee category for a student registrant. They denote different concepts: one is a committee role, the other a registration fee type, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair in cmt is a conference-organisation role (a type of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, PC Chair, Reviewer). Hotel presenter in iasted is a type of Delegate/attendee who presents at a hotel venue, sibling of Speaker, Listener, Session chair. The two denote different concepts: an organising committee role versus an attendee presentation role, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'enable Virtual Meeting' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrator enables a virtual meeting for a conference), while B's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (scheduling overlap between events). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's `contributes` goes Person -> Conference document (a person contributes a document), while B's `is Written By` goes Paper -> Author (a paper is written by an author). These are inverse directions of the authorship relation, not the same property; a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B's 'Sponsor state' is a state/status of a sponsor (sibling of Conference state and Presenter state) in the iasted ontology. They denote different concepts (a committee role vs. a sponsorship status) with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property giving the title (a string) of a Social/Working event, while B's 'end Date' is a datatype property giving the end date/time of a Conference. They relate different kinds of things (title vs. end time) on different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an administrative action performed by an Administrator that results in a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), i.e. the act of finalising paper-to-session assignments. B's 'paper Presented As' relates a Paper to the Individual Presentation by which it is presented (domain Paper, range Individual Presentation), i.e. a presentation-mode relation. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering anyone contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants), while B's 'Program Chair' is a specific organizer role under Organizator. The two denote different concepts: one is a general contributor category, the other a specific committee role. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in the intended domain.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference activity, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Conference hotel is a building/place (sibling of Conference airport, Conference building, Presenter house). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a physical venue, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with children like Invited speaker, Regular author), whereas B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Scientific Event denoting one edition of a conference. They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property mapping Contact Information to a string postal code; B's is_sent_after is an object property relating an Item to a Time. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'for Event' links a Call to the Academic Event it is issued for. Different domains (Conference vs Call), different ranges (Administrator vs Academic Event), and different intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a Conference contributor who gives an invited talk, a sibling of 'Regular author' and 'Active conference participant'. B's 'Author of paper' is a subtype of Author/Speaker, i.e. anyone who writes a paper. An invited speaker is not necessarily an author of a paper and an author of a paper is not necessarily invited, so the intended instances do not coincide.

A's `name` is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's `has Email` specifically relates a Person/Contact Information to an email address string. Although both are datatype properties with string ranges and overlapping domains, they denote different relations (a name vs. an email address), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a short summary document of a conference paper (sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B 'Single hotel room' is a type of hotel room accommodation (sibling of Double hotel room under Hotel room). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. accommodation) and share no intended instances.

A is a class of persons (Paper Author, a subclass of Person), while B is a monetary fee category (Student registration fee, a subclass of Registration fee under Money). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

Both properties link a submitted paper/contribution to the review it receives: A's 'has been assigned a review reference' has domain Submitted contribution, Topic and range Review preference, while B's 'has Review' has domain Paper and range Review. In the conference domain a submitted contribution is a paper and a review preference/reference is the review record, so the two relations coincide in direction and intended meaning.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a submitted/regular paper with an abstract), while B's Accepted Paper is a paper that has passed evaluation and been accepted for proceedings. They overlap (an accepted paper is a paper) but neither subsumes the other cleanly: A's Paper includes non-accepted regular papers, and B's Accepted Paper is a specific lifecycle stage. The paths and comments show different intended extensions, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Conference is a whole scientific event (one edition of a conference), a top-level event type with siblings Session, Track, Workshop. B's Plenary lecture is a specific kind of lecture (a talk) within a conference activity, sibling of Session and Tutorial. A conference is not a lecture; the entities denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's min Choice is a minimum-participant-count datatype property on Social/Working events (range positiveInteger), while B's has End Date Time is a temporal datatype property on Conference Event (range dateTime). Different domain, range and meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A is a subclass of Paper representing a paper in the pending state (siblings: Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper), i.e. a document/contribution. B is a subclass of Deadline representing a time point (camera-ready manuscript deadline). A paper and a deadline are different kinds of things, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'written By' links a Document to a Person (its author), while B's 'submit until' links a Document to a Deadline (a submission deadline). Different ranges and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Attendee (edas) is a generic person who attends a conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles. Demo Chair (ekaw) is a specific organising role within Conference Participant, sibling of PC Chair, Workshop Chair, etc. A Demo Chair is a kind of participant/attendee, but the two classes do not denote the same concept: Attendee is the general category, Demo Chair is one specific chairing role. They are not equivalent.

Card in iasted is a physical item (a card, with child Credit card) used for payment/identification, while Author in sigkdd is a person role (Speaker > Author) who submits papers and receives notifications. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

A (Member PC) is a Person subclass representing a program-committee member/reviewer, while B (Review) is a Document subclass representing the review document itself. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' is a mereological/containment relation between a Conference part and a Conference volume (part-of hierarchy). B's 'parallel with' is a symmetric co-scheduling relation between two Administrative events (e.g. sessions running concurrently). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a written announcement soliciting submissions/attendance), sibling of Call for paper and Review. B's 'Organizational Meeting' is an academic event (a scheduled gathering), sibling of Paper Presentation and Workshop. A document and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

Both properties relate a Person to a written work: ekaw's 'author Of' has domain Person and range Document, while iasted's 'write' has domain Person and range Item. In the conference domain, Document and Item both denote the written contribution (paper), and authorship is the same relation in the same direction, so the two properties are equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a sponsorship level (Gold Supporter) under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'has title' is a datatype property linking events to a string title; B's 'go through' is an object property linking an Item to an Activity. Different kinds (datatype vs object), different domains/ranges, and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (domain Conference volume, range Organizing committee), while B's property links a Person to a Conference they belong to (domain Person, range Conference). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not inverses or subsumption-related, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote members of the program committee of a conference. In cmt, Program Committee Member is a subclass of Conference Member/Person with properties linking it to the Program Committee (member Of Program Committee, has Program Committee Member) and review-related attributes (max Papers). In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a subclass of Organizator/Person, alongside Program Chair and General Chair, i.e. the same role in the conference organisation. The labels match and the intended instances (people serving on the PC) coincide, so the two classes are equivalent.

A's 'reviewes' relates a PC member to a contribution (reviewing a paper), while B's 'is paid in' relates money to a building (payment location). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A Program Committee Member is a person role (a member of the program committee), whereas B Committee is the committee body itself, which has a Program Committee as a child. A person is not a committee, so they are not equivalent; the member concept is narrower/different in kind from the committee concept. The closest relation is that the Program Committee Member belongs to / is part of the committee structure, but as a class it is not subsumed by Committee in the strict subclass sense; however among the allowed relations, subsumed_by best captures that the member role is a narrower notion tied to the committee. Actually the member is not a kind of Committee, so the safest is unrelated/related; given the committee contains members, 'related' would be defensible, but the intended concepts differ in kind (person vs organization), so I choose subsumed_by with moderate confidence.

A is an administrative event (a process/activity in the conference workflow) in confOf, while B is a deadline (a point in time) in iasted. Although both concern the camera-ready stage, one is an event and the other a temporal deadline, so their instances cannot coincide.

A 'Welcome Talk' is a kind of Talk Event (an academic event/session in the conference programme), while B 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a kind of Document/Abstract (a written text). One is an event, the other a document, so their instances cannot coincide; they are unrelated despite both relating to talks.

A 'Conference Trip' is a social event (an activity, sibling of Conference Banquet) in ekaw, while B 'Conference Hiker' is a kind of delegate/person (a subclass of Delegate) in iasted. One denotes an event, the other a person role, so they cannot be equivalent.

In cmt, Paper is a specific document type (a submitted paper with authors, reviews, decisions) under Document. In Conference, Regular contribution is a broader category of conference contribution that includes Paper as a child, alongside Extended abstract. Thus Paper is a narrower concept than Regular contribution, so Paper is subsumed by Regular contribution rather than equivalent.

A is a document type (an abstract of an invited talk), a subclass of Abstract under Document; B is a person role (an invited speaker), a subclass of Speaker under Person. They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (documents vs. people) and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) property linking a Conference volume to its Conference parts, while B's 'need' links a Person to an Item (a requirement relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Paper is a subclass of Document (path Document > Paper), while B's Document is the broader class whose children include Paper, Abstract and Review. Paper is therefore strictly more specific than Document, so Paper is subsumed by Document rather than equivalent.

Accommodation Place is a physical location (a place where attendees stay), while Conference Banquet is a social event (a dinner/banquet activity). They belong to different top-level branches (Place vs Event) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a written submission, sibling of Paper), while B 'Overhead projector' is a piece of audiovisual equipment used at a conference. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. equipment) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Multimedia Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in the edas ontology, while B 'Computer' is a piece of audiovisual equipment under Audiovisual equipment in iasted. They denote different concepts (subject vs. physical device) and share no intended instances.

A's 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (a general dependency relation), while B's 'searched by' relates a Sponzor to the specific class ACM SIGKDD. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving an integer volume number, while B's 'default Choice' is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a positiveInteger (a confTool default choice). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Reject Rating' is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a rating value assigned to a review indicating rejection. B 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity in the conference process (accepting a submitted manuscript), sibling of Receiving/Refusing manuscript. One is a rating category, the other a process/activity; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document (child of Document, with children Accepted/Pending/Published Paper etc., written by an Author, reviewed by reviewers). B's Author is a person (child of Speaker under Person, with children Author of paper, and properties submit/obtain/notification). A paper and an author are distinct concepts in the conference domain, so the pair is unrelated.

Both classes represent the concept of a conference paper. In confOf, Paper is a subclass of Contribution, with siblings Poster and Short paper, indicating it is a type of contribution. In ekaw, Paper is a subclass of Document, with children such as Conference Paper, Poster Paper, etc., and properties like has Review, has Reviewer, and covers Topic, which are typical for papers. The intended instances coincide: both denote academic papers submitted to or presented at a conference. The different parent classes (Contribution vs Document) reflect different modeling choices but do not change the core meaning. Thus, they are equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' relates a Person to their given name, while B's 'E mail' relates a Person to an email address. Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote different attributes (first name vs. email address), so they are not equivalent.

Active Paper is a specific state of a Paper (a submitted paper that is under review, with a rating), while Submission in iasted is the general submitted document with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript. They overlap in that a submission is a paper, but Active Paper is narrower (a paper in the active/review state) and Submission is broader (any submitted document). Thus they are related but not equivalent.

A's assignExternalReviewer relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (domain Reviewer, range External Reviewer), while B's hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (domain Paper, range Possible Reviewer). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not the same relation.

confOf's Working event is a broad category of scheduled events (Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) with administrative/social siblings, while iasted's Lecture is a specific conference activity (with Plenary lecture, Session, Tutorial as children) under Conference activity. They overlap in that both cover conference sessions/tutorials, but neither subsumes the other cleanly: Working event includes whole conferences and workshops, Lecture is a single activity type. Hence related, not equivalent.

In confOf, Workshop is a Working event sibling of Conference and Tutorial, i.e. a type of event/meeting. In ekaw, Track is a Scientific Event sibling of Conference, Individual Presentation, Session and Workshop, i.e. a thematic track within a conference rather than a meeting event. Although both are subclasses of Event, their intended instances differ (a workshop is an event one attends; a track is a thematic subdivision of a conference), so they are not equivalent.

A is a type of organization (a government body) under Organization, while B is a role a person plays on a conference organizing committee under Person/Organizator. They denote different kinds of entities (organization vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Hotel' is a physical place (venue accommodation). Different domains (document vs. place), no shared instances; clearly unrelated.

Organizer in the Conference ontology denotes a role/agent that arranges a conference, whereas ekaw's Person is the general superclass of all human agents (including authors, participants, students). An Organizer is a kind of Person, so Organizer is strictly more specific than Person; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a document-like contribution given by an invited speaker), while B's 'Welcome Talk' is a talk event in the conference programme (sibling of Closing Talk, a scheduled event). They belong to different branches (contribution vs. event) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A is a kind of conference paper (a document submitted to or published at a conference), while B is a physical place (the main office) in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a conference has members/participants), while B's prepare relates a Person to an Item (a person prepares something). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their first name), while B's authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document (authorship). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have different ranges, so they are unrelated.

Subject Area in cmt is a topic classification of papers (domain of 'has Subject Area' with range Paper), while Money in iasted is a monetary amount with children Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers), while B's 'for Event' links a Call to the Academic Event it is issued for. Different domains (volume vs call) and ranges (contribution vs event), so the relations are not the same.

A's 'assigned By Administrator' links a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned them (range Administrator), while B's 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (range Personal Review History). Different ranges and meanings; not the same relation.

A's Workshop is a scientific event (a type of conference activity), while B's Conference hall is a physical place (venue location). They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties giving the date/time of a conference event: cmt's `date` has domain Conference and range date, edas's `has Start Date Time` has domain Conference Event and range dateTime. Conference and Conference Event denote the same event concept, and date/dateTime are compatible literal ranges, so the properties relate the same things in the same direction.

edas:isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference/committee), whereas ekaw:hasPart is a generic mereological part-whole property with unspecified domain and range. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's `location Of` relates a Location to the Event held there (domain Location, range Event), while B's `can stay in` relates a Person to a Place where they can stay (domain Person, range Place). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person, a general participant role sibling to Author, Reviewer, etc. In iasted, Author is a deep subclass of Speaker (Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Speaker > Author), a specific speaking/presenting role with children like Lecturer and Tutorial speaker. Attendee (general participant) and Author (presenter who writes papers) denote different concepts; neither subsumes the other.

A's Early Registered Participant is a Conference Participant distinguished by registration timing (sibling of Late Registered Participant), while B's Organizing Committee member is an Organizator role in the conference organization structure (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote different concepts: registration status vs. organizational role, with no subsumption or overlap.

The two properties are inverses of each other: A's 'has a track workshop tutorial topic' goes from a Conference part to a Topic, while B's 'topic Covered By' goes from a Research Topic to an Event or Paper. They relate the same kinds of things (conference events/parts and topics) but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent; they are related as inverse relations.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a specific kind of Paper (a document containing the full paper content), a subclass of Paper in cmt. B's 'Document' is a broad class under Item covering many conference artefacts (forms, invitations, payments, reviews, submissions, etc.), not a paper. The two denote different concepts: a full paper is not a general document in the iasted sense, and Document is far more general and not a paper. Hence unrelated.

Accepted Paper in edas is a paper that has been accepted (a status/outcome of the review process, sibling of Rejected/Pending/Withdrawn Paper), whereas Regular Paper in ekaw is a paper category/type (sibling of Demo, Poster, Industrial, Workshop Paper) describing the kind of submission, not its acceptance status. The two classifications are orthogonal, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an action of an admin entering conference data), while B's 'for Event' relates a Call to an Academic Event (a call being issued for an event). Different domains (Administrator vs Call) and different ranges (Conference vs Academic Event), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties expressing a deadline date/time, but they belong to different domains: 'paper Due On' is a property of Conference (the conference paper submission deadline), while 'done till' is a property of Deadline (the date until which a deadline is valid). They are conceptually related (both about deadlines) but not the same property, since their domains and intended subjects differ.

A's read Paper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer reads paper). B's presentationed by relates a Document to a Speaker (document is presented by speaker). Different domains/ranges and different directions of meaning; not the same relation.

A's start Date is a datatype property giving a Conference's start date/time (range dateTime), while B's event On List is an object property linking an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site where it is listed. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

Both classes are named Person and represent the general human participant in the conference domain. In confOf, Person is the superclass of all human roles (Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.) with personal attributes (name, email, phone). In iasted, Person is likewise the superclass of human roles (Delegate, Sponsor) and is the range of properties like is given by, is paid by, is present. The intended instances coincide: people involved in the conference. The differing children reflect different role taxonomies, not different concepts.

A's 'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation), while B's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (authorship relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role (a subclass of Person, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc., and properties linking it to a Conference). B 'Conference building' is a physical place (a subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel/airport/restaurant). The two denote different kinds of entities (person vs. building) and are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman who chairs the conference), while B 'Plenary lecture' is a type of conference activity/lecture event. They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Multi author Volume' is a subclass of Document (a publication/volume, parent of Proceedings, published by an Organisation), whereas B's 'Author' is a subclass of Speaker/Person (a person who submits papers and receives notifications). They denote different kinds of entities (a publication vs. a person) and are not equivalent.

confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution (paper) to its Author, i.e. authorship of a paper. iasted's sign relates a Person to an Item, which in the iasted ontology is a generic person-to-item association (e.g. a person signing up for/registering an item), not authorship of a contribution. The domains (Contribution vs Person) and ranges (Author vs Item) differ, and the direction/meaning do not coincide, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A is the camera-ready manuscript deadline (final version submission after acceptance), while B is the paper submission deadline (initial submission). They are distinct deadlines in the conference timeline, both siblings under Deadline, so they are not equivalent.

A's reject Paper relates an Administrator to a Paper (a decision action), while B's related To Paper relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a citation/association between papers). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity in the conference organisation, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). B's Modelling is a research activity that occurs before the conference, sibling of Simulating. They denote different concepts: one is an event, the other a research activity, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a conference committee: A's Committee has children Organizing/Program/Steering committee and is linked to chairs, co-chairs and members; B's Committee has children Organizing Committee, Program Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee. Same intended instances (committees of a conference), so they are equivalent.

confOf's studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (where they study); iasted's obtain relates a Person to an Item (something they acquire). Both are person-to-entity relations, but the ranges differ (University vs Item) and the intended meanings (studying at an institution vs obtaining an item) are not the same, so they are not equivalent; they only overlap in being person-directed relations.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a kind of event/conference structure), while B's 'Program Committee member' is a subclass of Organizator (a person role). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and are not equivalent.

A Programme Brochure is a document that lists events (a conference programme booklet), while an Author information form is a form used to collect author details. They share only the broad Document ancestor; their siblings, properties and intended instances differ, so they are not equivalent.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the person hierarchy), while B is a kind of conference contribution (Invited talk, a subclass of Conference contribution/Presentation). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (a decision action rejecting a submission), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent nor inverse.

A's Conference Member is a Person subtype (a person involved in a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Track is a Conference part (a thematic track of a conference volume, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. conference subdivision) and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while ekaw's Workshop Paper is a specific subtype of Paper (siblings Conference Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). The confOf Paper is broader and would include workshop papers, so it subsumes the ekaw Workshop Paper; they are not equivalent.

A Meta Review is a review of reviews (a document type in cmt), while a Positive Review in ekaw is a review with a positive recommendation/score. They share the parent Review but denote different concepts: one is a meta-level document, the other a polarity-based review subtype. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A is a person role (an active conference participant who gives presentations), while B is a physical place (a building that hosts conference-related locations). Their paths, parents, siblings and properties are entirely disjoint, so they denote different concepts.

read Paper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer reads paper), while written By relates a Contribution to an Author (paper written by author). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they are not the same relation.

A 'Published Paper' is a state of a paper document (a Paper that has been published), while B 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a type of Award given to a paper. They belong to different branches (Document/Paper vs Award) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'referenced In' relates a paper to another paper it cites (citation relation), while B's 'award' relates a conference/paper to an Award entity. Different kinds of things and different directions, so they are unrelated.

confOf Member is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference, sibling of Regular and Student, i.e. a registration category). ekaw OC Member is a subclass of Conference Participant denoting a member of the organising committee (parent of OC Chair, sibling of PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.). The shared word 'Member' does not make them the same concept: one is an attendee/registration type, the other an organisational role. They are different concepts, so unrelated.

A's Presentation is a kind of conference contribution (a talk given at the conference, with an abstract, given by a participant), while B's Conference is the conference event itself (with dates, country, members, topics). They denote different concepts and are not related by subsumption.

Both properties are named 'is given by' and relate a presentation/activity to the person who gives it. In Conference, the domain is Presentation and range is Active conference participant; in iasted, the domain is Activity/Item and range is Person. Presentation is a kind of Activity/Item and Active conference participant is a kind of Person, so the intended relation (the giver of a presentation/activity) is the same, just expressed at different levels of generality. The direction is identical, so they are equivalent.

Paper Abstract is a document type (a short version of a paper) under Document > Paper, while Operating Topicsystems is a research topic under Topic in edas. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while locationOf relates a Location to an Event (where an event is held). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for SIGKDD members). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. fees) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (things that happen), while B's 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person covering chairs, committee members and webmaster (people). Different roots, different instances, no overlap.

Both denote a conference as an event/edition in the conference domain. edas Conference is a top-level class with children Single Level Conference and Two Level Conference and properties like has Name, has Country, paper Due On, has Topic, has Member, matching the intended instances of ekaw Conference (an edition of a conference, a subclass of Scientific Event with siblings Session, Track, Workshop). The labels and domain roles coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI (its website), while B's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Event) and range (anyURI vs Location), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Technical commitee is a subclass of Delegate (a person/role in the conference building hierarchy). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a subclass of Conference applicant (a person who has registered, with Paid applicant as a child), i.e. a person/role in the registration process. B 'Working event' is a subclass of Event whose children are Conference, Tutorial, Workshop — a type of event/activity. The two denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property from Call to dateTime (the submission deadline of a call). B's notification_until is an object property from Author to a Deadline Author notification individual (when an author is notified). They differ in domain (Call vs Author), range (dateTime vs deadline individual), and meaning (submission deadline vs notification deadline), so they are not equivalent.

Subject Area in cmt is a topic classification of papers (range of has Subject Area from Paper), while Country in confOf is a geographic attribute of organizations and persons (range of has Country from Organization/Person). Different domains, different intended instances; no overlap.
A's 'has gender' is a datatype property of Person capturing gender, while B's 'has Surname' captures a person's surname; they relate different attributes of Person and are not the same relation.

A's Attendee is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference), while B's Memeber registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money (a monetary amount). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. fee), so they are unrelated.

Both are social events at a conference, but a Reception (a standing social gathering, often with drinks) and a Conference Banquet (a formal seated meal) are distinct event types; they overlap as social events without coinciding, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Short paper' is a kind of Contribution (a document/paper type, sibling of Paper and Poster), while B's 'Author of paper' is a role of a Person (a subclass of Author, sibling of 'Author of paper student'). They denote different concepts (a paper type vs. a person role), so they are unrelated.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person and is further specialized into Administrator, Author, Reviewer, so User denotes a person who uses the system. In sigkdd, Person is the general class of all people (with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker) and has no User subclass. Thus cmt:User is strictly more specific than sigkdd:Person; every cmt:User is a sigkdd:Person, but not vice versa.

A Coffee Break is a short refreshment pause within the conference schedule (a Break Event, sibling of Meal Break and Free Time Break), whereas an EKAW Conference Trip is an organised social excursion (a Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet). They are different kinds of conference events and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name, while B's 'has Name' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's full name (comment: 'Conference Full Name'). Different domains (Person vs Conference) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete version of a conference paper (a Document/Paper in the cmt ontology, sibling of Paper Abstract). B 'Registration form' is a Form document used for registration (sibling of Author information form and Hotel registration form). They denote different concepts: a paper artefact versus a registration form, with no overlap in intended instances.

A is an administrative event (a happening in the conference process, sibling of Submission/Reviewing events), while B is a deadline (a point in time, sibling of other deadlines). Although both concern camera-ready material, one is an event and the other a temporal deadline, so their instances cannot coincide.

A's Paper is a conference document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Tax is a monetary charge (child of Money, siblings Fee/Sponsorship/Tip). Different domains and no shared context, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Scholar is a price category (a person eligible for a reduced/student-like fee) with a studyAt property linking to a University; ekaw's Student is a plain subclass of Person with no such property and different siblings. The intended instances do not coincide: Scholar is a registration/fee category, Student is an academic status, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (domain: Program Committee Member, range: Administrator). B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (domain: Person, range: Activity, Item). The domains and ranges are disjoint in intent: one is about committee membership administration, the other about a person giving an activity/item. They are not the same relation.

A is a conference topic (a subject area under Computer Networks Topic in the edas topic taxonomy), while B is an event type (a kind of Individual Presentation at a scientific event in ekaw). They belong to entirely different branches (Topic vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a conference/working event to a Topic. In the Conference ontology, 'has a track workshop tutorial topic' has domain Conference part and range Topic; in confOf, 'has Topic' has domain Working event and range Topic. Conference part and Working event both denote the event/part-of-conference concept, and both properties relate such an event to a Topic, so they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered the conference details), while B's 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution (paper) to a Conference volume (proceedings/venue). Different domain, different range, different meaning; not equivalent nor inverse.

A's 'technically Organises' is a subproperty of 'organises' with domain Organisation, describing an organisation that organises an event. B's 'presentationed by' has domain Document and range Speaker, describing a document being presented by a speaker. Different domains, ranges and intended relations; not equivalent.

A's part Of is a generic mereological/part-whole property with no domain or range, while B's awarded by is a specific property linking an Award to the agent/organisation that granted it. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a subclass of Deadline (a submission deadline event). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Chair is a generic committee chair (parent Committee member, sibling Co chair, domain of 'has a committee chair' on Committee), while B's Session Chair is a specific conference-session role under Conference Participant and PC Member, sibling to PC Chair, Workshop Chair, Tutorial Chair, etc. They overlap in that both are chairing roles, but A is broader (any committee chair) and B is narrower (session chair), so they are related rather than equivalent.

Sponsorship (edas) is a funding arrangement class with cost amount/currency and provider relations to Organization; Person (iasted) is a human agent class with children Delegate and Sponsor and relations like give, is paid by, is present. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's Conference is the conference event itself (has members, deadlines, topics, related documents). B's Conference hall is a physical place (sibling of Building, Hotel room, Session room) under Place. A conference event is not a conference hall; they are different concepts.

A's Meal Break is a broader break event (siblings include Coffee Break and Free Time Break), while B's Coffee break is specifically the coffee break. A Meal Break is not the same as a Coffee break; A subsumes B.

A's location is a datatype property giving the venue/place string of a social or working event; B's paperDueOn is a datatype property giving the dateTime deadline for conference paper submission. Different domain (event vs conference), different range (string vs dateTime), and different meaning (place vs deadline), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's surname), while B's 'is given to' is an object property from Item to Person (an item is given to a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Session is a scientific event (a scheduled gathering such as a conference session, workshop session, poster session) under Event > Scientific Event. B's Session room is a physical location (a room where sessions take place) under Place, sibling to Building, Conference hall, Hotel room. The two denote different kinds of things (event vs. place), so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Worker lecturer is a person role (a lecturer who is also a worker, under Lecturer > Author > Speaker > Delegate). They denote entirely different concepts: an event versus a person, so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties from Review to the reviewed paper/contribution; 'Reviewed contribution' in the Conference ontology is the paper being reviewed, matching ekaw's 'Paper'. Same domain (Review), same direction, same intended relation.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Communication Theory Topic' is a subject-area topic in the EDAS taxonomy. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a class of rejected papers (a document in the evaluation outcome hierarchy), while B is a deadline (a time point for notification of acceptance). They belong to disjoint branches (Document vs Time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is present' relates a Person to a Time (attendance at a time), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (accommodation/location). Different ranges (Time vs Place) and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a short summary document of a conference paper (sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B 'Hotel registration form' is a form document used for hotel booking (sibling of Author information form and Registration form under Form). They share only the generic Document ancestor and denote entirely different concepts.

SC Member is a specific kind of PC Member (steering-committee member) in ekaw, whereas iasted's Reviewer is a person who reviews papers, placed under Speaker/Delegate. Both are persons involved in reviewing/conference organisation, but SC Member is a narrower committee role and Reviewer is a broader reviewing role; they overlap but do not denote the same concept.

Review in cmt is a document produced by a reviewer about a paper (written by a Reviewer, ended by the PC Chair, with Meta Review as a child). Meal Menu in edas is a catering document associated with a Meal Event (has Menu / is Menu Of). They share only the generic parent Document and have no overlapping properties or intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an activity) in ekaw, while Hotel is a physical place in sigkdd. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. location) and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A 'One conference day' is a temporal unit (a single day of the conference, under Conference days/Time), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (under Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). Different domains (time vs. location) and no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

A's memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation). B's isInitiatedBy links a Call to a chair/TPC member (initiation relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

Country (a nation, used as the location of a Conference) and City (a settlement that is situated in a State/Place and occupied by Persons) are different geographic concepts; neither subsumes the other in the conference domain.

Individual Presentation in ekaw is a kind of Scientific Event (a talk/presentation event, with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial, and properties linking it to a Paper), whereas Award in sigkdd is a prize given to authors/papers (children Best Research Paper Award etc., properties awarded by / obtain). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a person is a member of the conference), while B's is prepared by relates an Item to a Person (a person prepares an item). Different domains (Conference vs Item) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'reviews' relates a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's 'pay' relates a Person to Money. Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no overlap.

A's 'written By' links a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it (domain Review, range Reviewer).
