B's 'has a review reference or expertise' links a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference topics (domain Reviewer, range Review expertise/Review preference). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings differ: one is authorship of a review, the other is a reviewer's topical expertise/preference. They are not the same relation, nor inverses, nor in a subsumption relation.

A's 'follows' relates Administrative event to Administrative event (temporal ordering of events), while B's 'belongs To Event' relates a Programme to a Conference Event (containment/association). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (a person leading the committee), while B's 'reviewes' links a PC member to the Contribution they review. Different domains (Committee vs Member PC), different ranges (Chair vs Contribution), and different intended relations (chairing vs reviewing), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Review expertise' is a property (a reviewer's expertise/competence, domain Reviewer, range Submitted contribution), while B's 'Review' is a class (a document reviewing a paper, subclass of Document with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review). Different kinds and meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to a reviewer-type person (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), while B's 'is paid by' relates Money to a Person. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they share no concept.

A's Author is a broad role for anyone who writes/submits papers (siblings include Reviewer, PC Member, Chair), while B's Member PC is specifically a program-committee member/reviewer (comment 'Reviewer', property reviewes Contribution, expert On Topic). The two denote different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's 'follows' relates two Administrative events (temporal ordering of events), while ekaw's 'event On List' relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (publication of an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during a conference, while B's Card is a physical item (parent Item, child Credit card, sibling of Document and Audiovisual equipment). They share no meaning, instances, or context; the only superficial link is that a reception might involve a card, which is not an ontological relation.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper the reviewer was assigned to review), while B's has_a_review relates a Reviewed contribution to a Review (the review object produced for that contribution). Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning: assignment of a reviewer to a paper vs. a contribution having a review. They are not the same relation, nor inverses or subsumption-related.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (sessions running in parallel), while edas's 'is Menu Of' relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (catering). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence.

A's Author is a general person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers, has conflicts of interest, can be a reviewer or chair). B's Contribution co author is a specific subclass of 'Regular author' representing a co-author of a contribution, sibling to 'Contribution 1th author'. The intended instances do not coincide: B is a narrow sub-role of authorship on a contribution, not the general Author class, and the paths/parents/siblings differ substantially.

A's 'author Of' goes Person -> Document (a person authors a document). B's 'is sent by' goes Item -> Person (an item is sent by a person), i.e. the inverse direction and a different relation (sending vs authoring). They are not equivalent; at best they are inverses with different domains/ranges, so unrelated.

A 'Conference Proceedings' is a published multi-author volume of papers (a Document/Proceedings subclass), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Sponsor is a Person who funds the conference (sibling of Delegate under Person), while a Program Committee member is an Organizator who reviews papers (child of Organizator alongside General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote different roles in the conference domain, so the classes are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a subclass of Topic (a signal processing subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. topic) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented), while B 'Best Student Paper Supporter' is a sponsorship role/level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. sponsor) and share no intended instances.

A is a research topic area (Microelectronics Topic) under Topic in the edas ontology, while B is a physical item (Card) under Item in the iasted ontology, with a child Credit card. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

Both are subclasses of Place/City denoting a location associated with a conference, but 'Conference Venue Place' is the venue where the conference is held, while 'Presenter city' is the city a presenter comes from (sibling of Conference city, Sponsor city, Trip city). They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same concept.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review the paper). B's 'technically Organised By' is a subproperty of 'organised By' and relates an event/conference to the person or body that technically organises it. Different domain, range and meaning; not the same relation.

A's property relates an Administrator to a Conference (mailing hardcopy manifests), while B's property relates a Document to a Speaker (being presented by). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad class under Person whose children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, Conference Chair, Associated Chair — i.e. anyone involved in the conference. In sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is a narrower class under Organizator, sibling to General Chair, Program Chair, Program Committee member and Webmaster, denoting only members of the organizing committee. The cmt class is strictly more general than the sigkdd class, so Conference Member subsumes Organizing Committee member rather than being equivalent.

A's 'belongs to reviewers' links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (who is qualified to review), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not the same relation.

A's Administrator is a User/Person role that manages the conference (accepts papers, assigns reviewers, enters conference details), while B's Paper is a Document submitted by an Author. They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's isReviewedBy relates a Paper to reviewers/committee members (domain Paper, range persons in a reviewing role), while B's is_occupied_by relates a Building/City/State to a Person (physical occupancy). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no overlap.

A's hasCall relates an Academic Event to its Call (call for papers), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

In iasted, Transparency is a Document subtype alongside Submission, Review, Form, Invitation letter, etc. — it denotes a transparency/administrative document (e.g. a disclosure or open-access statement), not a scientific paper. In sigkdd, Paper is the core submission artefact (submitted by an Author, with Abstract and Review siblings). The two classes have different intended instances, so they are not equivalent; they are best treated as unrelated.

Conference applicant is a person who applies to/registers for a conference (parent of Registeered applicant), while Attendee is a person who attends the conference. They overlap in that applicants often become attendees, but the concepts are not identical: an applicant may not attend, and an attendee need not have applied. Thus related rather than equivalent.

A's defaultChoice is a confTool-specific datatype property on Social/Working events with range positiveInteger (a default choice count), while B's hasStartDateTime is a dateTime start time of a Conference Event. Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author (authorship), while B's references relates a paper to another work it cites (citation). Different kinds of things are related in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

University is a specific kind of academic organization; Academia Organization in edas is broader, covering universities and other academic institutions. University is thus subsumed by Academia Organization, not equivalent.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a committee (a group of people) within the conference organisation, with properties linking it to a Conference volume. B's 'Organising Agency' is an Organisation (an institutional body) that organises the conference, sibling to Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher. The two overlap in the conference-organisation role but denote different kinds of entities (committee/group vs. organisation/agency), so they are related rather than equivalent.

Decision is a class of outcomes (acceptance/rejection) of a paper review, with children Acceptance and Rejection and a has Decision property from Paper. Person is a class of human agents (with children Delegate and Sponsor) that participates in activities, gives items, is paid, etc. The two concepts are entirely different in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's co-writePaper relates a Co author (an authoring agent) to a Paper, while B's contributes relates a Person to a Conference document. Both express an agent-to-document contribution, but the domains differ (Co author vs Person) and the ranges differ (Paper vs Conference document), so they overlap in intent without being the same relation; a reference alignment would not equate them.

A's 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity in the conference process (sibling of Accepting/Refusing manuscript), while B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline date for paper submission. They are related (the submission deadline bounds the receiving-manuscript activity) but not the same concept.

A 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering all people contributing to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors, etc.), while B 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a narrow Author subclass for a specific speaker role. They overlap (a plenary speaker is a contributor) but neither subsumes the other in the intended sense: A is far more general and B is a specific role, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's logo URL is a datatype property linking a Conference to an anyURI image/logo location, while B's start Date links a Conference to a dateTime for the conference start. They share only the Conference domain; their ranges (anyURI vs dateTime) and intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publisher issues proceedings). B's 'searched by' relates a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (sponsor is searched by an organization). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence.

A's 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (a paper-to-proceedings submission relation), while B's 'part Of Event' is a mereological relation between an Event and a larger Event (e.g. a session within a conference). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both are object properties linking a paper/document to its author/person. cmt's hasAuthor has domain Paper and range Author; ekaw's writtenBy has domain Document and range Person. Paper and Document are equivalent classes in this domain, as are Author and Person, and both properties express the same authorship relation in the same direction (paper -> author). Thus they are equivalent.

Both are datatype properties with a date/time range that record the deadline for submitting a paper: A's 'is an abstract submission date' on Important dates and B's 'has Submission Deadline' on Call denote the same submission-deadline relation in the conference domain, differing only in the domain class naming (Important dates vs Call) and range datatype (date vs dateTime).
A's hasCall relates an Academic Event to its Call (call for papers), while B's award relates something to an Award (a prize). Different domain concepts and different ranges; no overlap.

A's Paper is a Regular contribution (full paper), while B's Short paper is a distinct sibling of Paper under Contribution in confOf. They are both contributions/papers but denote different kinds (full vs short), so they overlap without being equivalent.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Performance Topic' is a subject area/topic category in EDAS. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A's Steering committee is a committee (a group/organizational body) that oversees a conference series, with properties linking it to a Conference volume. B's Conference Chair is a Person role (an individual who chairs a conference), sibling of Attendee, Author, Reviewer, etc., and participates in reviewing/initiating calls. A committee and a person role are different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference www' is a document/webpage about a conference (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with a URL property), whereas B's 'Conference' is the event itself (a subclass of Scientific Event, sibling of Session, Track, Workshop). The two denote different kinds of things (a document vs. an event), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration about a paper), while B's speak_in relates a Person to a Place/Time (a speaking engagement). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A (Nonauthor registration fee) is a specific kind of registration fee for non-authors, while B (Registration fee) is the general registration fee class with children for member/non-member/student registrations. A is strictly narrower than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

In confOf, Tutorial is a Working event (a type of event/activity held at the conference), sibling of Conference and Workshop. In iasted, Session is a Lecture (a talk/presentation), sibling of Plenary lecture and Tutorial, with child Speaker lecture. The iasted ontology treats Tutorial as a sibling of Session under Lecture, so Tutorial and Session are distinct kinds of lecture/presentation, not the same concept. The confOf Tutorial (an event) does not coincide with the iasted Session (a lecture slot).

A's topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (the topic is covered by a paper/event), while B's designed_by relates a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (the deadline is designed by the conference). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

Both entities represent the same conference-domain concept: a paper/contribution submitted to a conference. Labels ('Paper' vs 'Contribution') and identical domain/range usage (authored by a Person/Author, submitted to a Conference, reviewed by a Reviewer) confirm equivalence.

A's 'was a track workshop chair of' relates a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (a chairing/role relation), while B's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (a scheduling relation). Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Person in cmt), while B 'Workshop' is an academic event type (subclass of Academic Event in edas). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'go through' relates an Item to an Activity (an item participates in/undergoes an activity), while B's 'obtain' relates an Author to an Award (an author receives an award). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people on the organising committee). B's inverse_of_partOf_7 relates something to an Event as the inverse of a part-of relation, i.e. it links a whole to its parts within the event decomposition. The domains/ranges and intended meanings differ (committee membership vs. event mereology), so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's end Date is the end date/time of a Conference (domain Conference), while B's Date is the date of a Deadline (domain Deadline). They relate different kinds of things in different contexts, so they are not the same property.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a conference structure/type (a conference with two levels, e.g. main conference plus workshops), while B 'Speaker' is a person role (a delegate who speaks). They denote different kinds of entities in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A is a Person (a conference contributor who gives an invited talk), while B is a Document (an abstract of an invited talk). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Document) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's set Max Papers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper quota), while B's is Member Of relates a Person to a Conference (membership). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings.

A's Presenter is a role of a person (a Conference Participant who presents), while B's Building is a physical place (parent Place, with children like Conference hotel, Presenter house, and properties about being occupied/visited by persons). They denote entirely different concepts and cannot be equivalent.

A is a conference-organisation event class (parent Event, children Submission/Reviewing/Registration events), while B is a research topic in a topic taxonomy (parent Computer Networks Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location (where the event takes place). B's 'Price' is a datatype property linking a Registration fee to an int (its cost). They relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions and belong to different subdomains (event venue vs. registration cost), so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is an academic event (with dates, country, members, topics, deadlines), while B's Document is a submitted artefact (parent of Abstract, Paper, Review, with presentation and submission deadline). They denote different concepts; Conference is not a Document.

confOf's Organization is a general organisation class with children Company and University, covering both commercial and academic bodies. ekaw's Academic Institution is a narrower class under Organisation, restricted to academic bodies (children Research Institute, University). Every Academic Institution is an Organization, but not vice versa, so Organization is more general and is subsumed by the broader ekaw Organisation concept; the two classes are not equivalent.

A 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity/process in the conference timeline (a sibling of Accepting/Refusing manuscript), whereas B 'Author' is a person role (a subclass of Speaker with properties like submit and obtain). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and cannot be equivalent.

Conference contributor is a Person who contributes to a conference (authors, speakers, participants), while confOf Participant is a Person taking part in a conference, with subclasses Member, Regular, Student. Every conference contributor is arguably a participant, but Participant is broader (includes administrators, assistants, volunteers, science workers who need not contribute), so Conference contributor is subsumed by Participant rather than equivalent.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while B's 'Paper Author' is a direct subclass of Person denoting anyone who authors a paper. Every co-author is a paper author, but a paper author need not be a co-author (single-author papers), so Co author is strictly narrower: subsumed_by.

A's 'Conference document' is a broad class covering calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc., while B's 'Document' is a narrower class whose children are Abstract, Paper, Review and which is presented by a Speaker. A's Conference document is more general (it includes non-presented items like calls and announcements), so it is subsumed by B's Document rather than equivalent.

Attendee in edas is a generic person who attends the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.), while PC Chair in ekaw is a specific committee role (a kind of PC Member/Conference Participant). A PC Chair is a specific role, not a generic attendee; the two concepts do not coincide.

Abstract in ekaw is a document type (a subclass of Document, with children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and it is presented as a paper/presentation). Award in sigkdd is a prize given to authors (children are Best Paper awards, and it is linked to Author via obtain and awarded by). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad role class covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors (siblings include committee member, reviewer, chair), whereas B's 'Sponsor' is a person who funds the conference, a distinct role with no overlap in intended instances.

A's 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor, denoting a person role in authoring a contribution. B's 'Author attendee book registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, denoting a monetary fee category. They belong to entirely different branches (contribution/author vs. money/fee) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Conference is the main organising entity (has members, topics, deadlines, country, name). In iasted, Conference activity is a subclass of Activity covering individual scheduled events (lectures, coffee breaks, registration, welcome address), not the conference as a whole. The two concepts denote different things despite the shared word 'Conference'.

A's Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster and Short paper under Contribution), while B's Best Student Paper Award is a specific award category under Award. They denote different concepts: a paper document versus an award, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Meeting Room Place' is a specific kind of place (a sibling of Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place under Place), whereas B's 'Place' is the general superclass whose children include Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office, Session room. A meeting room is a place, but not every place is a meeting room, so A is strictly more specific than B: subsumed_by.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property linking a Conference proceedings to an integer (the volume number), while B's 'paper In Volume' is an object property relating a paper to a volume entity. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (proceedings vs paper) and range (int vs volume), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a numeric/score value), while B's hasReview links a Paper to a Review (the review document/process). Different range concepts (rating value vs. review entity) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A Tutorial is a working event (a kind of conference session/activity) in confOf, while B Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment in iasted. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (event vs. item/equipment) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'name' is a datatype property of Conference/Person holding a string name, while B's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution holding the paper's abstract text. Different domains, different intended values; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial/workshop) in the conference-organisation domain, while B's Performance Topic is a subject area/topic category (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.) used to classify papers. They denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's Review is a document produced by a reviewer (a subclass of Document, sibling of Paper, with properties write Review and written By). B's Review Question is a question on a review form (parent of Numerical/Textual Review Question), not a document. They are related to the reviewing process but denote different concepts, so not equivalent.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event in confOf, covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, topics). B 'Test Only Topic' is a subclass of Topic in edas, a subject area (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). One is an event, the other a topic; their instances cannot coincide.

A Committee member is a person who belongs to a committee (has members / was a member of Committee), with subclasses Chair and Co chair. B Sponsor is a person who funds the conference, sibling of Delegate. Different intended instances and roles; no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's Paper is a conference submission/document with authors, reviews, decisions; B's Card is a payment/registration item (parent Item, child Credit card, siblings Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle). Different domains, no overlap.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (author writes paper), while B's `is Review History Of` relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (a history belongs to a reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Organizing committee is a committee (a group of people responsible for organizing the conference), while B's Sponsor is a Person (an individual or entity providing sponsorship). They differ in kind (group vs. person) and in role, so they are not equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an activity) in ekaw, while B Conference hall is a physical place in iasted. They belong to different top-level categories (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Signal Processing Topic' is a subject area/topic for classifying papers. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasTopic relates a Conference/Paper to a Topic (subject matter), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (the act/artifact of presenting). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

SC Member is a steering-committee person role in ekaw (a subclass of PC Member), while Sponzor fee is a type of conference fee in sigkdd (a subclass of Fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (people/roles vs. payments) and share no intended instances.

A's Meta Reviewer is a person role (a special type of Reviewer, a Conference Member) that reads papers and produces a meta-review. B's Review is a Document (an item/artefact) in the iasted ontology, sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter, etc. One is an agent/role, the other is a document artefact; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a document type (a review of a contribution, sibling of Conference contribution and Call for paper, with properties has a review/reviews linking it to a Reviewed contribution). B's Paper is the submitted document itself (sibling of Abstract and Review under Document, with submit(Author -> Paper)). A review and a paper are distinct artefacts in the conference domain, so the classes are not equivalent.

A is an administrative event (the act/process of registering participants) in confOf, while B is a deadline (a point in time) for registration in iasted. They are related in that the deadline concerns the registration event, but they are not the same concept: one is an event, the other a time point.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's One day presenter is a type of Delegate (a person attending for one day). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (a subclass of Decision, sibling of Acceptance), i.e. the act/result of rejecting a paper. B's Deadline for notification of acceptance is a temporal deadline (subclass of Deadline) for when authors are notified of acceptance. They belong to different branches (Decision vs Time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a specific subclass of Paper (sibling of Paper Full Version), while ekaw's Paper is the general class covering all paper types (Regular, Poster, Demo, etc.). Thus Paper Abstract is strictly more specific and is subsumed by ekaw Paper, not equivalent.

Both are the top-level conference-domain event/activity classes: confOf's Event has children Administrative/Social/Working event and start/end times, while iasted's Activity has children Activity before/after conference and Conference activity plus temporal and participation properties. They denote the same general concept of an organised happening in the conference domain, so a reference alignment would equate them.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a person's conflict of interest in a paper/review), while B's is_paid_for relates Money to an Activity or Item (what a payment is for). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both classes denote a human participant in the conference domain. iasted's Person has children Delegate and Sponsor and is involved in giving/preparing items and activities; sigkdd's Person has children Listener, Organizator and Speaker and has attributes Name, E mail, Nation and pays registration fees. The differing children are specialisations of the same general concept, and the properties are complementary aspects of the same class, so the two Person classes are equivalent.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference (a subclass of Conference, sibling of Single Level Conference), while B 'Invited Speaker' is a kind of person (subclass of Speaker, sibling of Author). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's `date` is a generic datatype property on Conference (the conference's date), while B's `has Submission Deadline` is a specific deadline property on Call (the call's submission deadline). They relate different subjects (Conference vs Call) to different kinds of dates, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'early Registration' is a datatype property from Participant to boolean (whether a participant registered early), while B's 'location Of' is an object property from Location to Event (the event a location belongs to). They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete version of a paper (sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), whereas B 'Slide Set' is a presentation slide collection directly under Document, sibling to Paper, Review, Programme, Meal Menu. They denote different artefacts in the conference domain and share no intended instances.

Administrator in cmt is a User subclass with broad conference-management powers (accepting papers, assigning reviewers, entering conference details, enabling virtual meetings), while Organizer in Conference is a distinct role concept for those who organize the conference. The two roles overlap in the conference-organisation domain but are not the same class: Administrator is a system/user role in cmt, Organizer is a domain role in Conference, and neither subsumes the other cleanly.
A's hasAuthor is an object property linking a Paper to an Author; B's hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string. Different domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Abstract is a document/contribution type (an extended abstract, part of a paper/poster/presentation), while B's Deadline Abstract Submission is a deadline event for submitting abstracts. They denote different concepts (a document vs. a temporal deadline), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Short paper' is a type of contribution distinguished by length/format (siblings Paper, Poster), while B's 'Accepted Paper' is a paper in a specific review state (siblings Active/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper). The two classifications are orthogonal: a short paper can be accepted or rejected, and an accepted paper can be short or full. They do not denote the same concept.

A 'Pending Paper' is a document/paper in a submission state (a subclass of Paper, sibling of Accepted/Rejected Paper). B 'Submissions deadline' is a time point (a subclass of Deadline, sibling of camera-ready and notification deadlines). One is a paper artefact, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's Accommodation Place is a subtype of Place (a physical location such as a hotel building), while B's Hotel presenter is a subtype of Delegate (a person role, a delegate staying at a hotel). The paths and parents show one is a location and the other a person/role, so they denote different concepts.

A 'Social Event' is a non-academic conference event (with children Excursion and Reception, siblings Break Event and Meal Event), whereas B 'Registration' is a conference activity (with child Delegate, siblings Coctail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Presentation, Social program, etc.). They denote different concepts: a social event is an event, registration is an activity/process. Although B's sibling 'Social program' is related to social events, the entities themselves are not equivalent.

A's Scholar is a subclass of Person (a person category, with a study At property to University), while B's Student registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money (a fee amount, not a person). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. monetary fee), so they are unrelated.
Proceedings is a document/volume class (a collection of papers), while Author is a person class (a speaker who writes papers). They denote different kinds of entities and cannot be equivalent.

cmt:email is a Person's email address (contact identifier), while edas:hasBiography is a Person's biographical text. Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote different attributes; a reference alignment would not equate an email with a biography.

A's virtualMeetingEnabledBy relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person who enables virtual meetings), while B's hasAttendee relates a Conference Event to a Person (attendees). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's 'Paper Abstract' is the abstract/short version of a paper (sibling of 'Paper Full Version' under Paper), whereas B's 'Workshop Paper' is a paper submitted to a workshop (sibling of Conference Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). They denote different concepts: one is a document-format/version distinction, the other a venue/type distinction. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

Company in confOf is a subclass of Organization, denoting an organizational entity (e.g., a corporate author/affiliation). Sponsor state in iasted is a subclass of State, denoting a status/role that a sponsor can have in the conference workflow. They belong to different upper categories (Organization vs State) and have different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's Decision is a review outcome (accept/reject) for a paper, with children Acceptance and Rejection and domain of has Decision (Paper -> Decision). B's Activity is a general event/activity in the conference domain (conference activities, before/after conference activities) with properties like give, go through, is held in, is dated on. The two concepts denote different things: a decision outcome vs. an event/activity. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper that is related to (but not authored by) that author, while B's authorOf relates a Person to a Document they authored. The intended relations differ: relatedness vs. authorship, and the ranges (Paper vs. Document) are not the same concept in these ontologies.

Both are datatype properties of a conference giving its web address: cmt's 'site URL' has domain Conference and range anyURI, Conference's 'has a URL' has domain Conference www and range string. Same intended relation (conference -> its URL), differing only in the literal datatype (anyURI vs string), which does not change the concept.

Both are the academic subcategory of Organization/Organisation; edas 'Academia Organization' and ekaw 'Academic Institution' denote the same class of academic organisations, with matching parent (Organization/Organisation) and analogous sibling structure (Government/Industry/NGO vs Organising Agency/Proceedings Publisher).

Conference contributor is a broad role for anyone contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants), while General Chair is a specific organizing role within the Organizator hierarchy. They overlap in that both are conference-related persons, but neither subsumes the other: a General Chair is an organizer, not necessarily a contributor in the author/speaker sense, and a contributor is not necessarily a chair.

Attendee (edas) is a generic person who attends a conference, a sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles under Person. Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is a specific organisational role responsible for tutorials, a subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member. A Tutorial Chair is a kind of participant, but the two classes do not denote the same concept: Attendee is far more general and covers all participants, while Tutorial Chair is a narrow role. They are not equivalent, and neither strictly subsumes the other in the given ontologies (Attendee is not a superclass of Tutorial Chair in ekaw's hierarchy), so they are best treated as unrelated.

Both classes are named Author, both sit under Speaker in the person/delegate hierarchy, and both denote a person who writes papers (A's children cover authored proceedings/lectures, B's children cover authored papers and B has properties submit/obtain/notification). The intended instances coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Conference contributor is a broad Person subtype covering anyone contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants), while B's Conference Hiker is a narrow Delegate subtype (a specific attendee role under Delegate, alongside Speaker, Listener, Session chair). The intended instances do not coincide: a contributor need not be a delegate/hiker, and a hiker is a specific delegate role, not the general contributor concept. Different paths (Person vs Place>Building>Conference building>Delegate) and different sibling sets confirm they denote different concepts.

Organizer (Conference) denotes a person who organises the conference, while Listener (iasted) is a Delegate subtype who attends without presenting. They are different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's markConflictOfInterest relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to record a conflict of interest, while B's has_been_assigned_a_review_reference relates a Submitted contribution/Topic to a Review preference, i.e. it records a review preference assignment. Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Organisation is an institution/agency class (parent of Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings. B's Speaker is a subclass of Person (sibling of Listener, Organizator) that gives presentations. They denote different concepts: an organisation is not a person/speaker, and neither subsumes the other.

A's Presenter is a role/person (a Conference Participant who presents), while B's Introduction of speaker is a conference activity (the act of introducing a speaker). A person role and an activity are different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean datatype property of Conference indicating whether a conference accepts paper submissions in hardcopy. B's 'write' is an object property from Person to Item indicating that a person writes an item. They differ in domain (Conference vs Person), range (boolean vs Item), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while sigkdd's obtain relates an Author to an Award (receiving an award). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

Conference Member in cmt is a person role (a member of a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, etc.), while Review in Conference is a conference document (a review of a contribution). They denote different kinds of things and have no overlap.

A's writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship of a paper), while B's search relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (sponsor lookup). Different domain, range and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's hasVAT is a datatype property attaching a tax string to social/working events, while B's listsEvent is an object property linking a programme brochure or web site to events. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

Topic in confOf is a subject area of contributions, PC members' expertise, and working events (deals With, expert On, has Topic). Activity in iasted is a broad event/action class (conference activities, before/after conference activities) with properties about persons, items, places, times and money. The two denote different concepts: a topic/subject area versus an event/activity, so they are not equivalent.

confOf Person is a human agent (author, participant, chair) with properties like has Email, has First Name, employed By; iasted Place is a spatial location (building, room, city) with properties like is equipped by, is situated in. They denote entirely different concepts despite both appearing in the conference domain.

A's Paper is a conference submission (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Transport vehicle is a physical vehicle class (children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) under Item. They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different domains.

A's 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (a dinner) within the conference, a subclass of Social Event with sibling Conference Trip. B's 'Conference' is the whole conference event, with properties for city, start/end dates, name, and being held by ACM SIGKDD. A banquet is a part/activity of a conference, not the conference itself, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract (range Abstract). B's 'paperPresentedAs' links an Abstract/Paper to an Individual Presentation (range Individual Presentation). The ranges are disjoint concepts (Abstract vs Individual Presentation) and the relations differ in meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type: the abstract version of a paper), while B is a subclass of Topic (a subject area in computer networks). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

cmt:User is a subclass of cmt:Person (path Person > User), so every User is a Person, but ekaw:Person is broader (it includes students, agency staff, participants, etc. who need not be users of the conference system). Thus User is strictly more specific than Person: subsumed_by.

A's Reviewer is a person role (a Conference Member/User who reviews papers, with children Meta Reviewer and siblings Author, Chair, PC Member). B's Submitted contribution is a document (a Written contribution that has been submitted, with child Reviewed contribution and sibling Regular contribution). The two entities denote different kinds of things (person vs. document), so they are unrelated despite both being involved in reviewing.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property of Conference www pointing to a string URL, while B's 'has Title' is a datatype property of Contribution pointing to a title string. They relate different kinds of things (a website's URL vs. a contribution's title) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Banquet is a social event (an activity held during a conference), while Conference hotel is a building/place where attendees stay. They belong to different top-level branches (Event vs Place) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent or in a subsumption relation.

A's 'Rejected contribution' is a subclass of Reviewed contribution (a submitted paper that was rejected), while B's 'Negative Review' is a subclass of Review (a review with negative content). One is a document/contribution, the other is an evaluation; their instances and paths differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is a full paper submission date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a literal date, i.e. it records the submission deadline date of a full paper. B's 'submit until' is an object property linking a Document to a Deadline individual, i.e. it records the deadline by which a document must be submitted. Both concern the paper submission deadline, so they overlap semantically, but they differ in kind (datatype vs object property), domain (Important dates vs Document) and range (date literal vs Deadline class), so they are not equivalent relations.
A is a person role (chair of a conference/committee) under Person > Chairman, while B is a physical venue (hotel) under Place. Different kinds of entities with no overlap in the conference domain.

Both properties link a reviewer/author of a reviewed contribution to the review they produce. In cmt, Reviewer write Review has domain Reviewer and range Review; in Conference, Reviewed contribution has a review has domain Reviewed contribution and range Review. The domain classes Reviewer and Reviewed contribution both denote the person/entity that writes the review (the reviewer is the author of the reviewed contribution), and both properties point to the same Review class, so they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

A's Paper is the general document class for papers (with children Accepted/Rejected/Published etc.), while B's Assigned Paper is a narrower class under Submitted Paper (a paper assigned to a reviewer). Every Assigned Paper is a Paper, but not vice versa, so Paper subsumes Assigned Paper.

A 'Extended abstract' is a kind of regular contribution (a submission type), while B 'Withdrawn Paper' is a paper status in edas. They denote different concepts: one is a document/contribution type, the other a lifecycle state of a paper. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

Meta Reviewer is a strict specialization of Reviewer (its parent in cmt is Reviewer, and the comment says it is 'a special type of Reviewer'). In the Conference ontology, Reviewer is the general class. Thus Meta Reviewer is subsumed by Reviewer, not equivalent.

A's 'Social Event' is a subclass of Event (a conference social gathering such as a banquet or trip), while B's 'Fee' is a subclass of Money (a monetary charge such as a registration or hotel fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (events vs. money) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

edas:Person is a broad top-level class whose children include Attendee, Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member, etc. ekaw:Conference_Participant is a subclass of ekaw:Person (path Person > Conference Participant) and covers only people participating in a conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants, PC members). Thus every Conference Participant is a Person, but not every edas:Person (e.g. an author not attending, or a generic person) is a Conference Participant. The edas class is strictly more general, so edas:Person subsumes ekaw:Conference_Participant; the pair is not equivalent.

A is a datatype property linking a Conference to its registration deadline (dateTime), while B is an object property linking a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event. They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship of a paper), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (who pays the fee). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Tutorial is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation at a conference), while Listener is a kind of person (an attendee who listens). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (event vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'is paid with' is an object property linking Money to an Item (the thing used to pay), while B's 'Currency' is a datatype property linking a Registration fee to a string literal naming the currency. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Money vs Registration fee), and range (Item vs string), so they do not denote the same relation.

Both entities denote the same concept in the conference domain: a document submitted to a conference, typically a paper or contribution. The labels 'Paper' and 'Contribution' are synonyms in this context, and their paths and properties align (e.g., both are authored by persons and reviewed).

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issues proceedings), while B's `write` relates a Person to an Item (an author writes a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a whole-part relation, subproperty of has parts), while B's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

Both classes denote a conference participant who is a member (as opposed to a non-member/regular/student participant). In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant alongside Regular and Student; in iasted, IASTED member is a subclass of Delegate alongside IASTED non member and other participant roles. The intended instances coincide: a registered participant who is a member of the organising body. The differing parent labels (Participant vs Delegate) are synonyms in this domain, and the sibling structure (member vs non-member/regular/student) matches.

A's Place is a generic location (parent of Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) that conference events are held at, whereas B's Conference is the event itself (with start/end dates, city, name, held by ACM SIGKDD). A location and an event are different concepts, so the classes are unrelated.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's writtenBy is an object property mapping a Document to a Person (the author of a document). They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a kind of conference event with two levels), while B 'Registration Student' is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for students). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event type vs. fee type) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines), while B's 'held In' links an Event to a Location (venue). Different domain, range and meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A's authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship of a paper), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (receiving a prize). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a degree' relates a Review preference to an int (degree of preference), while B's 'has amount of' relates Money to an int (monetary amount). Different domains and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

In cmt, Bid is a reviewer's expressed interest/score for a paper (domain/range Reviewer->Bid, Paper->Bid), whereas in iasted Money is a monetary amount with children Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Gold Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. sponsor) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a conference document (a peer review of a contribution, with properties reviews/has a review linking it to Reviewed contribution), while B's Value added tax is a kind of Tax under Money. The domains are entirely different (conference reviewing vs. taxation), so the classes are unrelated despite no shared context.

A's Member is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference, with siblings Regular and Student), i.e. a generic conference participant. B's IASTED non member is a subclass of Delegate in the iasted ontology and denotes a delegate who is not an IASTED member, contrasting with its sibling IASTED member. The two concepts differ in both scope and intent: one is a generic participant role, the other a membership-status distinction among delegates. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's 'Committee member' is a Person subtype (a person serving on a committee, with children Chair/Co chair and committee-membership properties), while B's 'Registration fee' is a Fee subtype (a monetary charge with Price/Currency and pay/payed by properties). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document type), while B 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is a subclass of Committee (an organisational body). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string biography, while authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document they authored. Different kinds of things are related (string vs Document) and the intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is Reviewing' relates a committee role (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper, i.e. the act of reviewing a paper. B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item, i.e. authorship. Reviewing and writing are different relations with different domains and ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name string, while B's Currency links a Registration fee to a currency string. They relate different kinds of things (person names vs. fee currencies) and have different domains/ranges, so they are unrelated.

A's `end Review` is a property of a Program Committee Chair that ends a Review (domain: Program Committee Chair, range: Review), i.e. a chair terminating a review process. B's `reviewes` is a property of a Member PC (a reviewer) that relates the reviewer to the Contribution they review (domain: Member PC, range: Contribution). The domains (chair vs. PC member/reviewer) and ranges (Review vs. Contribution) differ, and the intended relations differ (ending a review vs. reviewing a paper), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a specific reviewed submission outcome (sibling of Accepted contribution), while B 'Personal Publication History' is a container of a person's publications in edas. They denote different concepts: one is a document/review status, the other a personal history listing. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's hasLastName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's obtain is an object property mapping a Person to an Item (acquiring an item). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's contributes relates a Person to a Conference document; B's submit relates an Author to a Paper. Author is a kind of Person and Paper is a kind of Conference document, so the properties overlap in the conference domain, but they are not the same relation: contributes is broader (a person can contribute to a document without submitting it, e.g. as a co-author or reviewer), while submit is the specific act of submitting a paper. Thus they are related rather than equivalent.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (who prints hardcopy mailing manifests), while B's property relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (parallel sessions/events). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a scheduled part of a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Plenary lecture' is a kind of Lecture (a conference activity/session type) in iasted, while 'Best Research Paper Award' is a kind of Award in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (activity vs. award) and share no intended instances.

confOf Organization is an institution (Company, University) that employs people and has an address; iasted State is a geographical/administrative region (with Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state as subclasses) that contains buildings/cities and is occupied by or visited by persons. Different intended instances and different property contexts, so not equivalent.

In cmt, Paper Abstract is a document type (an abstract submission) sibling to Paper Full Version, i.e. a kind of paper content. In edas, Accepted Paper is a paper in a particular review state (accepted), sibling to Pending/Rejected/Withdrawn/Published Paper. The two denote different dimensions (document type vs. acceptance status) and their instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A 'Communications Topic' is a subject area of papers (a subclass of Topic in edas), while B 'Program Committee' is an organisational committee (a subclass of Committee in sigkdd). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Both are object properties named 'written By' linking a written work to its writer. In cmt the domain is Review and range Reviewer; in confOf the domain is Contribution (the paper/contribution) and range Author. Review and Contribution are the written artefacts of the respective ontologies, and Reviewer/Author are the persons who write them, so the relation 'written by' relates the same kinds of things in the same direction. The differing domain/range labels reflect the ontologies' class naming (Review vs Contribution, Reviewer vs Author), which are aligned concepts, so the properties are equivalent.

A's Extended abstract is a specific kind of regular contribution (a short/abstract-length paper), sitting under Regular contribution with sibling Paper and child Abstract. B's Abstract is a broader document category in ekaw, parent of Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, and is linked to presentations. A's Extended abstract is a narrower notion than B's Abstract, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A is a subclass of Presentation (a kind of conference activity/artifact, sibling of Video presentation), while B is a subclass of Person (a role of a person who presents, sibling of Listener and Organizator). They belong to disjoint branches (activity vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.

Submission event is a specific administrative event (the act of submitting contributions), while ekaw's Event is the general superclass of all events (scientific, social, administrative). The confOf class is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by the general Event class, not equivalent to it.

A's 'has Been Assigned' relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper the reviewer was assigned to review). B's 'technicallyOrganisedBy' is a sub-property of 'organisedBy' and relates a conference/event to the person or body that technically organises it. Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Document is a general class whose children are Paper and Review, i.e. it covers all conference documents. In ekaw, Web Site is a specific kind of Document (a sibling of Paper, Review, Abstract, etc.), so every Web Site is a Document but not vice versa. Thus cmt:Document is more general than ekaw:Web Site, making the pair subsumed_by rather than equivalent.

Cheque is a payment document (a financial instrument used to pay registration fees), while Abstract is a document type in the conference submission process (a short summary of a paper). They share only the generic Document ancestor and have no overlapping instances; the concepts are unrelated.

A's 'Tutorial speaker' is a specific kind of speaker (a speaker who gives a tutorial), sitting under Author in the iasted hierarchy. B's 'Speaker' is the general class of people who present documents, with children Author and Invited Speaker. Every tutorial speaker is a speaker, but not every speaker is a tutorial speaker, so A is strictly more specific than B.

Bid in cmt is a reviewer's expression of interest in reviewing a paper (domain/range Reviewer->Bid, Paper->Bid), while Country in confOf is a geographical country used as the range of has Country for Organizations and Persons. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Committee member (a Person who is part of a Committee, sibling of Chair/Reviewer) and IASTED member (a Delegate subtype in the iasted ontology, sibling of Speaker/Listener) both denote a person affiliated with the conference organisation, but they are not the same concept: committee membership is a specific role within a committee, whereas IASTED member is a general delegate affiliation. They overlap in that both are conference-affiliated persons, so 'related' rather than equivalent.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to their email address, while B's 'Nation' links a Person to their nationality/country. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote different attributes of a person and are not the same concept.

Workshop Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a paper submitted to a workshop), while sigkdd's Paper is the general class of papers. Workshop Paper is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

A's Topic is the general class of subject areas (it has a name, is a topic of conference parts, is referenced by reviews and submissions). B's Antennas Topic is a specific instance-level subject area under the general Topic class in edas (siblings are CAD Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.). Antennas Topic is a narrower concept than the general Topic, so it is subsumed by A's Topic rather than equivalent.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (sessions running in parallel), while B's 'related To Paper' relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative sub-event of a conference (the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions), while B's 'Conference' is the overarching scientific event (one edition of a conference). They are at different levels of the event hierarchy and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A is a document type (a full version of a paper, sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), while B is a type of session/event (a regular session, sibling of Poster Session, Workshop Session under Session). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (document vs. event) and cannot denote the same concept.

A's startReviewerBidding is an Administrator action that opens bidding for a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference). B's hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (domain Paper, range Possible Reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning: one is a bidding-process action, the other a paper-reviewer assignment relation. They are not equivalent.

A's Chair is a committee chair role (parent Committee member, sibling Co chair), while B's OC Chair is specifically an Organizing Committee chair under OC Member. The OC Chair is a narrower role within the organizing committee, so A's Chair is more general and B's OC Chair is subsumed by it. They are not equivalent because A's Chair can apply to other committees (e.g., program committee) beyond the OC.

Both properties relate a submission/document to a time/deadline by which it must be sent/submitted; 'is sent before' (Item -> Time) and 'submit until' (Document -> Deadline) express the same submission-deadline relation, with Item/Document and Time/Deadline being the corresponding classes in the two ontologies.

Both classes denote a workshop as a conference event/part. In Conference, Workshop is a kind of Conference part alongside Track and Tutorial, and is the range of 'has workshops' (Conference volume -> Workshop). In edas, Workshop is an Academic Event, a subtype of Conference Event, alongside other event types. The intended instances (workshops held at a conference) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite differing parent hierarchies.

A Talk Event is a single talk (a presentation event) with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk, while an EKAW Conference Session is a session that groups several talks/presentations (its siblings are Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session, Workshop Session). A talk is a component of a session, not the same concept, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted the paper), while B's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the presenter). Different domains (Paper vs Presentation) and different ranges (Administrator vs Active conference participant), and the intended relations differ: acceptance vs presentation delivery. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad class under Person whose children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, etc., i.e. it covers all people involved in the conference. In iasted, Author is a narrow class under Speaker (Delegate > Speaker > Author) denoting only authors of papers/proceedings. Thus Conference Member is strictly more general than Author; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (a publication/informational artefact, sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, Review) addressed to participants. B's 'Contact Information' is a data record holding city, email, phone, postal code and street for a person/organisation. They share no intended instances: one is a document, the other is contact data, so they are unrelated.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the outcome/acceptance of a paper), while B's is_sent_after relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering relation). Different domain, range and meaning; not the same relation.

A's Workshop is a working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial) in confOf, while B's Tutorial is an individual presentation (sibling of Contributed/Invited Talk) in ekaw. They denote different concepts: a workshop is a working event, not a tutorial presentation, and the two ontologies place them in different branches (Working event vs Individual Presentation).

Chairman is a person role in the conference organisation (a subclass of Person, with subclasses like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), whereas Fee is a monetary charge (a subclass of Money, with subclasses like Registration fee and Hotel fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and share no instances.

A's hasTitle is a datatype property of Contribution (a paper's title), while B's Name is a datatype property of Person (a person's name). They relate different kinds of things (paper vs. person) and are not the same relation.

A's readByReviewer relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the person who reads/reviews it), while B's reviews relates a Review to a Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed). They differ in domain, range, and direction: one links paper->person, the other review->paper. They are not the same relation, nor inverses (inverse of reviews would be reviewedBy linking contribution->review).

Positive Review is a subclass of Review in ekaw (a review with a positive verdict), while sigkdd's Review is the general review class. Positive Review is strictly more specific, so it is subsumed by Review, not equivalent.

A's Review is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a paper (sibling of Paper under Document, with write/writtenBy to Reviewer and end by PC Chair). B's Active Paper is a paper in an active state (subclass of Paper, with has Rating to Review Rating). One is an evaluation artefact, the other a paper lifecycle state; their instances cannot coincide.

ekaw's Student is a subclass of Person (a general person role), while iasted's Student non speaker is a subclass of Non speaker under Delegate, i.e. a conference attendee who is a student and not a speaker. The iasted class is a narrower concept (student delegate at a conference who does not present), so ekaw Student is more general and is subsumed by the iasted class rather than equivalent.

A's 'has gender' is a datatype property of Person capturing gender; B's 'Nation' is a datatype property of Person capturing nationality/country. Different attributes of a person, so they are not equivalent.

A is a person class (Student, a subclass of Person in ekaw), while B is a fee category (Nonmember registration fee, a subclass of Registration fee under Money in iasted). They denote different kinds of entities (a person vs. a monetary fee) and are not equivalent; at most they are loosely related through the conference domain, but no subsumption holds.

A's 'Invited talk' is a conference contribution/presentation (an event-type contribution), while B's 'Tutorial Abstract' is a document (an abstract text for a tutorial). Different kinds (contribution vs. document) and different subject matter (invited talk vs. tutorial abstract), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper in a specific publication state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper under Paper), i.e. a scholarly contribution. B 'Invitation letter' is a document sent to invite someone (sibling of Form, Payment document, Review, Submission under Document). Different concepts with no overlap.

Both classes denote a person taking part in a conference: ekaw's Conference Participant is a subclass of Person with subclasses for the various conference roles (chairs, presenters, registered participants), and iasted's Delegate is likewise a Person subclass with subclasses for the conference roles (speaker, session chair, listener, committee member). The intended instances coincide, so the two are synonyms in the conference domain.

confOf's City is a geographic location used as the range of has City (Organization/Person -> City). iasted's State is a broader geographic/administrative region that contains City (is situated in has range Building, City, Place, State; is occupied by/is visited by take Building, City, State). State is a super-region of City, not the same concept, and the two ontologies use different granularities; a reference alignment would not equate City with State.

A's has Rating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper's rating value), while B's is given to relates an Item to a Person (a recipient). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

Conference Participant is a broad role class covering all people attending the conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.), whereas Speaker in iasted is a narrower role under Delegate whose children are Author and Reviewer. A Speaker is a kind of conference participant, but not every conference participant is a speaker, so Conference Participant subsumes Speaker.

A's Paper is a specific kind of regular contribution (sibling of Extended abstract) within the Conference ontology, while B's Paper is a broad Document subclass with many children (Conference Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Regular Paper, etc.). A's Paper is narrower than B's Paper, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'Conference part' is a component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) that is part of a Conference volume, whereas B's 'Conference' is the whole event with dates, country, members and deadlines. A conference part is not a conference; the part is strictly more specific than the whole, so Conference part is subsumed by Conference.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subclass covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors; Worker lecturer is a narrow role under Lecturer (a kind of Author/Speaker/Delegate) in iasted. The lecturer role falls within the contributor concept, but contributor is far more general, so they are not equivalent; they overlap as related concepts.

A's Agency Staff Member is a Person who works for the organising agency (sibling of Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student), whereas B's Lecturer is a kind of Author/Speaker in the iasted hierarchy (parent Author, children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer). The intended instances do not coincide: an agency staff member need not be a lecturer/author, and a lecturer need not be agency staff. Different concepts despite both being persons.

Active Paper in edas is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that is active/under review, with a rating), while ekaw's Paper is the general class covering all paper types (submitted, camera-ready, demo, etc.). Active Paper is therefore strictly more specific than ekaw Paper, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a submission type, sibling of Paper, child of Regular contribution), while B's 'Best Student Paper Award' is a type of Award (an honor given to a paper/person). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. award) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chair of the conference, under Person > Chairman), while Tutorial is a type of scientific event/presentation (under Event > Scientific Event > Individual Presentation). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a specific committee of a conference). B's 'technicallyOrganises' links an Organisation to something it technically organises (e.g. a conference/event), a subproperty of 'organises'. The domain/range and intended meaning differ: one is a whole-part relation between a conference and its committee, the other an organising relation between an organisation and an event. They are not the same relation.

External Reviewer is a Person role (a person assigned to review a paper for another reviewer), while Review preference is a topic/degree preference record belonging to a reviewer. They denote different concepts: one is an agent, the other is a preference/topic association, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given to' is an object property linking an Item to a Person (e.g. an award/prize given to a person), while B's 'Name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string literal. They differ in domain, range, and kind (object vs datatype), so they cannot denote the same relation.

Student is a subclass of Person (a role of an individual in the conference domain), while Renting is an activity that occurs before the conference. They belong to different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic in mobile computing (a subclass of Topic in the edas ontology), while B is a physical item (a Card, with child Credit card) in the iasted ontology. They share no meaning in the conference domain and have different parents and contexts.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (domain Program Committee, range Program Committee Member). B's has_a_program_committee relates a Conference volume to its Program committee (domain Conference volume, range Program committee). The two properties have different domains and ranges and are not inverses; they denote different relations in the conference domain.

A's writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship of a document), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). They differ in domain, range, and direction of the relation, so they are not equivalent.

A is a person role (chair of a conference, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a kind of City (a city that sponsors the conference). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs City) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'obtain' is an object property mapping a Person to an Item (acquiring something). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's Attendee is a generic Person role (sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.), while B's Technical commitee is a specific sub-role of Delegate (a conference building occupant) alongside Speaker, Listener, Session chair. A technical committee is an organisational body, not a generic attendee, so the two classes do not denote the same concept.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). B's Conference state is a state of a conference participant (sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state), i.e. a status in a process, not an event. Different kinds and different domains, so they are unrelated despite the shared word 'Conference'.
