A 'Committee member' is a broad role covering chairs, co-chairs, reviewers, etc. (children Chair, Co chair; siblings Reviewer, Track workshop chair). B 'Organizing Committee member' is a narrower role under Organizator, sibling to General Chair, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster. The organizing committee is a specific committee, so its members are a subset of committee members in general; A is more general than B, hence B is subsumed by A.

A 'Week Reject Rating' is a review rating value (a subclass of Review Rating, sibling of Accept Rating/Reject Rating) used to score a paper after a week of reviewing. B 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity in the conference process (sibling of Receiving/Refusing manuscript). One is a rating class, the other a process/activity; their intended instances do not coincide.

edas:relatesTo is a very general Document-to-anything (event/session/person) association, while ekaw:organisedBy is the specific Event-to-Organisation/Person responsibility relation. They differ in domain (Document vs Event), range (includes sessions/conferences vs organisations), and meaning (generic relatedness vs organising responsibility), so they are not the same relation.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, whereas B's Activity before conference is a general activity category occurring before the conference, with children like Accepting manuscript and Renting. The two denote different concepts: a specific social gathering versus a temporal phase of activities, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Proceedings Publisher' is an organisation (a publisher of conference proceedings), while B 'Author cd proceedings included' is a role/type of author whose paper is included in proceedings. They denote different concepts (organisation vs. author role) and are not equivalent.

A's Member is a subclass of Participant (a person role: Regular/Student member attending the conference), while B's Registration SIGKDD Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for SIGKDD members). One denotes a person/participant type, the other a fee type; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated despite the shared word 'Member'.

A is a kind of academic event (a presentation of accepted papers, sibling of Talk Event/Workshop), while B is a specific award category (sibling of Best Research Paper Award). They denote different concepts in the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's Review is a conference document (a review of a contribution, with properties 'reviews' and 'has a review' linking it to a Reviewed contribution). B's Paper is a submitted document (with children Accepted/Rejected/Pending Paper, and properties like is Written By, is Reviewed By, has Topic). In edas, Review is a separate sibling class of Paper, so the two classes denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A is a class of documents (an accepted paper that becomes part of the proceedings), while B is a time point (the deadline for notification of acceptance). They belong to different branches (Document vs Time) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with two levels, sibling of Single Level Conference), while B 'Workshop Chair' is a person role (a Conference Participant who chairs a workshop). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Program committee' is a committee (a group of people) that organises the review process for a conference, sibling of Organizing/Steering committee. B's 'Programme' is a Document (sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set) that belongs to a Conference Event, i.e. the schedule/booklet artefact. Different kinds of things (group of people vs. document), so they are not equivalent.
A's remark is a free-text note on a Contribution (string), while B's has amount of is a numeric amount on Money (int). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; no overlap.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewing assignment), while B's occupy relates a Person to a Building/City/State (physical location). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Session Chair' is a Person role in the conference organisation (sibling of Author, Reviewer, TPC Member, with properties about initiating calls and reviewing papers), while B 'Sponzor fee' is a subclass of Fee (a monetary charge, sibling of Registration fee). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines), while B's 'has Programme' links a Conference Event to its Programme (schedule of sessions). Different domain/range concepts and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Active conference participant' is a subclass of Conference contributor/Conference participant, restricted to those who give presentations. B's 'Participant' is a broader class (parent of Member, Regular, Student, etc.) covering all conference participants, not only active presenters. Thus A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'Transport vehicle' is a physical means of transport (parent Item, children Car/Shuttle bus/Taxi/Van), while B's 'Organizator' is a person role in conference organisation (parent Person, children General Chair/Program Chair/Webmaster). Different domains and different kinds of instances; no equivalence, subsumption or meaningful overlap.

A 'Member PC' is a person role (a PC member/reviewer who performs reviews), while B 'Positive Review' is a subclass of Review, i.e. a document/artefact with a positive recommendation. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. review document) and are not equivalent.

A's 'max Papers' is a datatype property of a Program Committee Member giving the maximum number of papers that member may review; B's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving the number of volumes. Different domains (committee member vs. proceedings) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A is a full version of a paper (a document type under Paper), while B is a day of a trip (a time concept under Time). They belong to different branches (Document vs Time) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Scholar in confOf is a person role (a price category for a person, sibling of Author, Participant, etc., with property study At -> University), whereas Nonauthor registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee category (subclass of Registration fee under Money), not a person. They denote different kinds of entities and are unrelated.
A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while B's 'pay' links a Person to Money (payment relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'Published Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been published), while B's 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity in the conference process (accepting a submission), sibling of Receiving/Refusing manuscript. Different kinds (document vs. activity) and different meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'co write Paper' relates a Co author to a Paper (domain Co author, range Paper), i.e. an authorship relation between a co-author and a paper. B's 'is writen by' relates an Item to a Person (domain Item, range Person), i.e. the inverse direction of authorship (item written by person). They differ in direction and in the kinds of entities related (Co author vs Person, Paper vs Item), so they are not equivalent; at best they are inverses, which the instructions say do not count as equivalent.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (sibling of Extended abstract) with an abstract, while B's Conference Paper is a specific kind of Paper in ekaw, sibling to Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, Regular Paper, etc. A's Paper is narrower than B's Conference Paper, which covers all conference papers including submitted, camera-ready, demo, industrial, poster and workshop papers. Thus A is subsumed by B.

Both classes denote the same conference-domain concept: a coffee break. In edas it is a Break Event (a non-academic conference event) with siblings Free Time Break and Meal Break; in iasted it is a Conference activity alongside Coctail reception, Social program, etc. The labels are identical apart from capitalisation, and the surrounding contexts (conference event/activity, break/social activities) agree, so the intended instances coincide.

A Trip is a social event (an excursion/outing) in confOf, while a Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle in iasted. Although a trip may involve a shuttle bus, the classes denote different concepts: one is an event, the other a vehicle. Their parents (Social event vs Transport vehicle) and siblings (Banquet/Reception vs Car/Taxi/Van) confirm they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is an event (a working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Workshop Chair is a person role (a Conference Participant and PC Member). An event and a person role denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.
confOf:Event is a general conference event class, while edas:SocialEvent is a specific social gathering; neither subsumes the other and they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a Paper to the people who review it, but they are not equivalent: edas 'is Reviewed By' has range Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member (the actual reviewers of a paper), while ekaw 'has Reviewer' has range Possible Reviewer (candidate reviewers). The direction is the same (Paper -> reviewer), but the intended kinds of things differ, so they overlap without being equivalent.

Chairman is a person role in the conference organisation (a Person who chairs, with subclasses Conference Chair, PC Chair, Associated Chair), while Registration Non Member is a fee category (a kind of Registration fee) for attendees who are not members. They denote different concepts in different branches of the domain (person role vs. fee type), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering all people contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, participants, etc.). B's 'Technical commitee' is a specific Delegate subclass denoting a committee role, not a general contributor category. The two concepts do not coincide: a technical committee member is a narrow role, while a conference contributor is a general umbrella class. They are not equivalent, nor does one strictly subsume the other in the intended domain.

An Accommodation Place in edas is any place where one can stay (hotels, guest houses, etc.), while sigkdd's Hotel is specifically a hotel. A hotel is a kind of accommodation place, so Accommodation Place is broader and Hotel is subsumed by it. They are not equivalent because accommodation places include non-hotel lodgings.
A's 'relates To' is a Document->(Event/Person) property, while B's 'write' is a Person->Item property; they have different domains, ranges, and directions, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Steering committee' is a committee (a group of people governing a conference series), while B's 'Building' is a physical place with children such as Conference hotel, Session room, and properties like 'is occupied by' and 'is situated in'. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is a document/paper class representing the abstract of a paper, while Antennas Topic (edas) is a subject/topic class for conference topics. They belong to different branches (Document vs Topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (a decision to reject a submission), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a generic giving relation). The domains (Administrator vs Person) and ranges (Paper vs Activity/Item) differ, and the intended meanings are distinct, so the properties are not equivalent.

Both properties link a person to a country/nation, but A's hasCountry is an object property with domain Organization or Person and range Country (a class), while B's Nation is a datatype property with domain Person and range string. They overlap in intent (person's country) but differ in domain breadth and value type, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Conference Session is an event/session entity in edas (it is a domain of has Related Document and relates To, alongside Academic Event, Conference, Person), whereas B Abstract is a subclass of Document in ekaw (a written submission, sibling of Paper and Review). A session is not a document, so the two classes are unrelated.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a call inviting submissions/participation), while B 'Government Organization' is a type of organization (an organizational affiliation). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. organization) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Value added tax' is a specific kind of Tax (a government levy, sibling of Departure tax) under Money, while B's 'Registration fee' is a conference registration charge under Fee, with children for member/student registration and properties Currency, Price, pay/payed by. They denote different concepts (a tax vs. a conference fee), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper they author), while sigkdd's submit relates an Author to a Paper they submit. Both connect an author to a paper-like entity, but writing (authorship) and submitting are distinct relations in the conference domain; they overlap but are not the same relation.

A's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while B's Industrial Paper is a specific subtype of Paper (siblings Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). The general Paper is strictly more general than Industrial Paper, so A is subsumed by B's narrower concept; they are not equivalent.

A's Late Registered Participant is a Conference Participant classified by registration timing (sibling of Early Registered Participant), while B's Organizing Committee member is an Organizator role within the conference organization structure (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote different concepts: registration status vs. organizational role, with no subsumption or overlap.

Both classes denote the same concept: a social event in the conference domain. In edas, Social Event is a subclass of Non Academic Event with children Excursion and Reception; in ekaw, Social Event is a subclass of Event with children Conference Banquet and Conference Trip. The children (excursions/trips, receptions/banquets) are typical social events, and the labels and intended instances coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A's Review is a conference document that reviews a contribution (domain/range: Review -> Reviewed contribution, and Reviewed contribution -> Review). B's Web Site is a Document that lists events and is published by an organisation; its sibling Review in ekaw is a separate class. The two entities denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary fee for members). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a Document to a person, but they are not the same relation: ekaw's writtenBy relates a document to its author (Person), while sigkdd's presentationed_by relates a document to the person who presented it (Speaker). Authorship and presentation are distinct roles, so the properties overlap in domain but differ in intended meaning and range.

A's Organization is an institution (parent of Company and University, employer of Persons, with address properties), while B's City is a geographical place (parent of Conference/Presenter/Sponsor/Trip city, occupied by Persons, situated in States). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's `reviews` goes from Review to Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed), while B's `has Review` goes from Paper to Review. They are inverse relations, not equivalent: one links a review to its paper, the other links a paper to its review.

A's `send` relates a Person (sender) to an Item, i.e. a person sends an item. B's `presentationed by` relates a Document to a Speaker, i.e. a document is presented by a speaker. The domains (Person vs Document) and ranges (Item vs Speaker) differ, and the directions differ (person->item vs document->speaker). They are not the same relation, nor inverses of one another, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference document' is a broad class covering calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc. (its children include Call for paper, Review, Conference contribution), whereas B's 'Conference Paper' is a specific kind of Paper (sibling of Poster Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). A Conference Paper is a Conference document, but not every Conference document is a Conference Paper, so A is strictly more general than B.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while iasted's is_paid_in relates Money to a Building (payment location). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence.

Both properties link a document-like item to a person, but 'written By' expresses authorship of a Document while 'is sent by' expresses the sender of an Item (submission). Authorship and sending are different relations, so they are not equivalent; they overlap only in relating an item to a person.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper (a document type representing the abstract of a paper), while Programme Brochure in ekaw is a subclass of Document representing a conference programme brochure, with properties such as event On List, lists, and publisher Of. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and do not coincide.

A's 'assigned By Administrator' links a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned them (domain Reviewer, range Administrator). B's 'reviewer Of Paper' links a Possible Reviewer to the Paper they review (domain Possible Reviewer, range Paper). Different domains and ranges, different intended relations; not equivalent.

cmt:User is a general person role in the conference domain (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while iasted:Worker lecturer is a very specific academic staff role nested under Lecturer/Speaker/Author/Delegate. The iasted class is a narrow subtype of a person, not the same concept as the broad User role; they do not denote the same set of instances.

Both are datatype properties of Conference, but cmt's `date` is a generic conference date (range date), while sigkdd's `Start of conference` specifically denotes the conference start date/time (range dateTime). They overlap in that the start is a date of the conference, but they are not the same property; the start is a narrower concept than a general date.

A's 'go through' relates an Item to an Activity (a paper going through a conference event), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (an author submitting a paper). Different domain, range, and direction of relation; they are not the same property.
A's 'deals With' relates a Contribution (paper) to a Topic, while B's 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

Organization in confOf denotes an institution (Company, University) that employs people and has an address, while Money in iasted denotes a monetary amount with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment. They share no instances or meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference session/meeting), while B's Exhibitor is a sponsoring entity (a subtype of Sponzor/sponsor). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. sponsor) and share no intended instances.

Withdrawn Paper is a specific status of a Paper (a paper that was withdrawn), while Submission in iasted is a general document type that is the parent of Initial manuscript and Final manuscript. A withdrawn paper is not a submission in general, and a submission is not necessarily withdrawn; the two concepts do not coincide.

setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a limit on papers a PC member can review), while writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a person attending a conference without an active role (sibling of 'Active conference participant' under 'Conference participant'). B 'Trip city' is a city involved in a trip (sibling of 'Conference city', 'Presenter city', 'Sponsor city' under 'City'). One is a person role, the other a location; they denote entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (a person/role in the committee), while B's belong_to_a_conference_volume relates an Important dates entity to a Conference volume (a publication artefact). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's Web Site is a Document subtype that lists events and is published by an organisation (a conference website), while B's Paper is a Document subtype submitted by an author. They share only the Document parent; their properties and intended instances differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's isReviewedBy relates a Paper to the people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), while B's reviewWrittenBy relates a Review to the person who wrote it (Possible Reviewer). They both concern the review process but differ in domain (Paper vs Review) and in the kind of target (reviewer roles vs review author), so they are not the same relation; they are merely related.

A's 'has a committee chair' relates a Committee to its Chair (domain Committee, range Chair), while B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (domain Person, range Conference). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Program Committee Member' is a person role in the conference organisation (a subclass of Conference Member/Person, with properties like member Of Program Committee, max Papers), whereas B 'Social program' is a conference activity (subclass of Conference activity, with child Dinner banquet and siblings like Lecture, Registration). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. event/activity), so they are unrelated.

A is an object property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume (part-whole relation between entities), while B is a datatype property giving the name of a Conference as a string. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and cannot denote the same relation.

A's virtualMeetingEnabledBy links a Conference to an Administrator (the person who enables virtual meetings), while B's hasMember links a Conference to a Person (a generic member of the conference). Different ranges (Administrator vs Person) and different intended meanings; not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial/workshop), while B's Welcome address is a conference activity (a scheduled activity such as lecture, presentation, coffee break). They denote different concepts: an event type vs. a specific activity, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to their personal web page URL (comment 'confTool'), while B's Nation links a Person to their country/nationality. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote entirely different attributes; no subsumption or overlap exists.

A's Reception is a specific social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip), while B's Social Event is the general category that has Reception as a child. Reception is therefore strictly narrower than Social Event, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A is a conference event (a working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while B is a hotel registration form document (a Form alongside Author information form and Registration form). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Document in cmt is a broad class whose children are Paper and Review, i.e. any written artefact including reviews. Reviewed contribution in Conference is a specific stage of a submitted contribution that has been reviewed (children Accepted/Rejected contribution), and it is reviewed by a Review. Thus Reviewed contribution is a narrower concept than Document; Document subsumes Reviewed contribution, not equivalent.

confOf's Topic is the general subject area of a contribution, a working event, or a PC member's expertise. edas's Performance Topic is a specific topic under the parent Topic (siblings include Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), so it is a narrower concept. The general Topic subsumes Performance Topic, hence A is subsumed_by B.

Conference contributor is a broad class covering all people who contribute to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors), while ekaw's Invited Speaker is a specific kind of presenter/participant. The contributor class is strictly more general, so it subsumes Invited Speaker rather than being equivalent to it.

A's Short paper is a contribution type (a paper of short length, sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution), while B's Rejected Paper is a paper in the rejected outcome state of the review process (sibling of Accepted Paper under Evaluated Paper). Length/type of contribution and review outcome are orthogonal concepts, so the classes do not denote the same instances.

A's 'written By' links a Document to the Person who wrote it (authorship relation). B's 'notification until' links an Author to a Deadline Author notification, i.e. a deadline by which the author is notified. Different domain, range, and meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Conference volume' is the whole conference publication entity that has committees, tracks, parts, contributions and important dates; B 'Conference Proceedings' is the published proceedings volume of a conference, a Multi author Volume/Proceedings. Both denote the conference's proceedings volume as a whole, so their intended instances coincide.

A's Conference is the central academic event class (has papers, members, topics, deadlines), while B's Conference restaurant is a physical building/venue location under Place > Building, sibling to Conference hotel and Conference airport. They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

A's Workshop is a conference event (sibling of Track and Tutorial, part of a Conference, with has workshops linking a Conference volume to workshops). B's Taxi is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Shuttle bus, Van, under Transport vehicle). The shared word 'workshop' does not apply here; the entities denote entirely different concepts in different domains, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person (a human attending the conference, with subclasses Active/Passive participant), whereas B 'Conference Venue Place' is a Place (a physical location such as a venue, sibling of Accommodation/Dining/Meeting Room Place). They belong to disjoint top-level categories (Person vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a document type (with children like Conference Paper, Poster Paper) that is reviewed and covers topics; B's Review is a document type that is a sibling of Paper under Document. They denote different concepts (a paper vs. a review of a paper), so they are not equivalent.

A is a class of multi-author volumes (a kind of Document, parent of Proceedings, published by an Organisation), while B is an Author (a person, under Speaker/Delegate in the iasted ontology). A volume is a publication artefact, not a person, so the two classes cannot share instances and are unrelated.

Both denote the person who chairs a session: ekaw's Session Chair is a Conference Participant/PC Member role, iasted's Session chair is a Delegate role. Same intended instances (session chairs), differing only in the surrounding taxonomy.

A's 'Author attendee book registration fee' is a specific kind of registration fee (a sibling of student, member, nonmember, etc. registration fees), whereas B's 'Registration fee' is the general class of all registration fees. Thus A is strictly more specific and is subsumed by B.

A's 'paper ID' is a datatype property mapping a Paper to an unsignedLong identifier, while B's 'paper Presented As' is an object property mapping a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (a presentation event). They relate different kinds of things (identifier value vs. presentation entity) and are not the same relation.

A's 'Main office' is the administrative office of the conference organisation, while B's 'Conference hall' is the room where sessions take place. They are distinct sibling concepts under Place in both ontologies (A has Conference hall as a separate sibling, B has Main office as a separate sibling), so they denote different places and are not equivalent.

A's `related To Paper` links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (paper-to-paper relation), while B's `write` links a Person to an Item (authorship relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent nor inverse.

A's Author is a person role (a subclass of Person, with children like Presenter and properties linking to papers), while B's Student registration fee is a monetary fee category under Registration fee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection under Decision), i.e. the state/result of accepting a paper. B's Refusing manuscript is an activity (sibling of Accepting manuscript under Activity before conference), i.e. the act of rejecting a submission. One is a decision outcome, the other an activity, and they are even opposite in polarity (acceptance vs. refusal), so they are not equivalent.

Both are object properties named 'has Topic' linking a conference-domain entity to a Topic. Although confOf restricts the domain to Working event and edas allows Conference and Paper, the intended relation (an event/paper having a topic) is the same; the differing domain is a modelling restriction, not a different relation, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), expressing that two events run in parallel. edas's 'has Location' relates a Conference Event to a Place, expressing where an event is held. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person role in the conference), while B's Registration Student is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for students). They denote different concepts: a person type vs. a fee type, so they are not equivalent.

A's `abstract` is the abstract text of a Contribution (a paper), a datatype property with domain Contribution. B's `has Submission Instructions` is the instructions for submitting to a Call, with domain Call. Different domains (paper vs. call) and different intended content (paper abstract vs. submission instructions), so they are not the same relation.

A is a research topic area (Computer Architecture Topic) under the Topic hierarchy in edas, while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (LCD projector) under Audiovisual equipment in iasted. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'was a track workshop chair of' relates a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (a role-to-event/part relation within the conference structure). B's 'initiates' relates a Conference Chair / Session Chair / TPC Member to a Call (a person-role initiating a call for papers). The domains and ranges differ (Conference part vs Call; Track workshop chair vs Chair/TPC Member), and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Camera ready contribution' is a final, accepted paper version ready for publication, located under Accepted contribution in the Conference ontology. B 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a submission deadline event, a subclass of Deadline in sigkdd. They denote different concepts (a document vs. a temporal deadline) and are unrelated.

A's Rejected Paper is a paper that was not accepted (sibling of Accepted Paper, Pending Paper, etc.), while B's Submitted Paper is a paper that has been submitted and can be assigned for review (parent of Assigned Paper, sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, etc.). A rejected paper is a subset of submitted papers, but the two classes denote different stages/outcomes and are not equivalent; the intended instances do not coincide.

Both classes denote the subject area of a paper/conference: edas Topic is the topic of a Conference or Paper, and ekaw Research Topic is covered by an Event or Paper. Same intended instances (subject areas), same role in the domain, so they are equivalent.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Workshop' is an academic event type. They belong to different branches (document vs. event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while iasted's is_equipped_by relates a Place to an Item (equipment). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

confOf's Event is the general conference event class (children: Administrative, Social, Working events), while edas's Academic Event is a specific subtype of Conference Event (siblings: Non Academic Event). Event is broader and would subsume Academic Event, not be equivalent to it.

A 'Double hotel room' is a subtype of Hotel room (a lodging place for attendees), while B 'Conference hall' is a venue/room where the conference takes place. They are different kinds of places with no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people on the committee), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference it holds/organises. Different domain and range, different direction of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's property links a Review preference to the topics/submissions it prefers; B's hasReviewer links a Paper to a possible reviewer. Different domain (Review preference vs Paper), different range (Submitted contribution/Topic vs Possible Reviewer), and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a distinguished conference contributor (a Person) who gives an invited talk, sibling to Regular author and Active conference participant. B's 'One day presenter' is a Delegate (a role at a building/place) who presents for one day, sibling to Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc. The concepts differ in kind (invited/keynote speaker vs. one-day presenter) and in ontology placement (Person vs. Delegate/Place), so they are not equivalent.

Sponzorship is a general money/funding concept (sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip under Money), while Best Student Paper Supporter is a specific sponsorship level/role under Sponzor. They are related (both concern sponsorship) but not equivalent: one is the general sponsorship concept, the other a particular supporter category.

A's hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to a Subject Area (topic classification), while B's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship). Different domain/range semantics and direction; they are not the same relation.

A is a class of accepted papers/contributions in the conference document hierarchy; B is a deadline (a time point) for submissions. They belong to different branches (document vs. time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's reviewOfPaper relates a Review to the Paper it reviews (domain Review, range Paper). B's write relates a Person to an Item they authored (domain Person, range Item). Different subject and object kinds and different direction of the conference relation (reviewing vs authoring), so they are not equivalent.

Reviewer in the Conference ontology is a Person who reviews papers (has review expertise/preferences, invites co-reviewers, is invited by other reviewers). Scholar in confOf is a Person with a price category who studies at a University; its siblings (Administrator, Assistant, Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, Science Worker, Volunteer) show it is a generic attendee/role category, not a reviewing role. The two denote different concepts despite both being subclasses of Person.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (a committee member). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. a textual artefact. B's 'Technic activity' is a conference activity (sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Registration), i.e. an event. Different kinds and different domains, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (domain and range both Administrative event), expressing that events run in parallel. edas's 'has Call' relates an Academic Event to its Call for papers (domain Academic Event, range Call). Different kinds of things are related in different directions, so the properties are not equivalent.

Both denote the conference-domain concept of a Call for Papers: A's 'Call for paper' is a Conference document sibling of Call for participation/Conference announcement, and B's 'Call For Papers' is a Call sibling of Call For Manuscripts/Call For Reviews. Same intended instances, only spelling differs.

A's 'Submitted Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, etc.), i.e. a paper in its submitted state. B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a subclass of Deadline (sibling of Deadline Abstract Submission, Deadline Author notification), i.e. a submission deadline event. One is a document, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's Student is a subclass of Person denoting a person enrolled in study, with siblings like Paper Author and Possible Reviewer; B's Author is a subclass of Speaker denoting a person who submits papers and receives notifications/awards. The intended instances differ: a Student need not be an author, and an Author need not be a student. Although B has a child 'Author of paper student', that is a distinct narrower concept, not the same as A's Student. Hence the two classes are not equivalent.
A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while B's 'pay' links a Person to a Registration fee (payment). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; no overlap.

Both classes denote a physical location/venue in the conference domain. edas Place is the superclass of Accommodation, Conference Venue, Dining Place and Meeting Room; iasted Place is the superclass of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office and Session room. The children are the same kinds of physical places (rooms, buildings, venues), and both are used as the location of events/activities (edas: has Location / is Location Of with Conference Event; iasted: is held in with Activity, is situated in with Building/City/Place). The intended instances coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A Workshop (edas) is an Academic Event held alongside a conference, sibling of Paper Presentation and Talk Event. B Tutorial (iasted) is a Lecture, a kind of Conference activity, sibling of Plenary lecture and Session. Although both are conference activities, a workshop is not a tutorial: they are distinct event types with different structures and purposes, and the paths/parents differ (Academic Event vs Lecture). No subsumption holds either, so they are unrelated.

Both entities denote the same conference-domain concept: a paper/contribution submitted to a conference. The labels 'Paper' and 'Contribution' are synonyms in this domain, and the surrounding context (authors, reviews, conference track) agrees, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent classes.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but A's 'paper Due On' is a submission deadline for a Conference paper, while B's 'is dated on' is a generic date attached to an Activity. They overlap in that both assign a date to an event-like entity, but the intended meanings differ (deadline vs. occurrence date), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a kind of Author/Speaker who gives a plenary talk, while a 'Program Chair' is an Organizator role in the conference committee. They belong to different branches (Author/Speaker vs Organizator) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'deals With' relates a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter of a paper), while B's 'is sent after' relates an Item to a Time (temporal ordering of a submission). Different domain, range, and meaning; no overlap.

A's 'Session Chair' is a conference participant role (a person who chairs a session), sitting under Conference Participant and PC Member. B's 'IASTED non member' is a delegate classification (a delegate who is not an IASTED member), sitting under Delegate alongside IASTED member, Listener, Speaker, etc. Although B has a sibling named 'Session chair', the candidate entity is 'IASTED non member', which denotes membership status, not the chairing role. The two concepts are unrelated.

A's has Last Name is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's author Of is an object property mapping a Person to a Document (the papers they authored). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have different ranges, so they are not the same relation.
TPC Member is a Person role (program committee member) in edas, while Registration fee is a Fee/Money concept in iasted; they share no meaning, instances, or hierarchy, so they are unrelated.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (membership relation). B's reviewes relates a Member PC to a Contribution (reviewing relation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while B's 'has Country' is an object property linking a Conference to a Country. They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Regular contribution' is a kind of conference contribution (a document/paper submitted to a conference, with children Extended abstract and Paper), while B's 'Regular' is a kind of Participant (a person, sibling of Member and Student, comment 'confTool'). The shared word 'Regular' is coincidental: one denotes a submission type, the other a person category, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'Camera ready contribution' is a specific stage of an accepted contribution (the final version prepared for publication), while B's 'Conference Paper' is the general class of papers presented at a conference, with 'Camera Ready Paper' as one of its subclasses. The camera-ready contribution is thus a narrower concept than the general Conference Paper, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's property relates a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference (domain Reviewer, range Review expertise/Review preference), while B's property relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer). They connect different kinds of entities and run in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment relation), while B's 'is held after' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

A's 'technically Organises' is a subproperty of 'organises' with domain Organisation, relating an organisation to what it organises (e.g. an event). B's 'occupy' has domain Person and range Building/City/State, relating a person to a physical location. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's `contributes` goes Person -> Conference document, while B's `is sent by` goes Item -> Person, i.e. it is the inverse direction (Item sent by Person). They describe the same submission relationship from opposite ends, so they are related (inverse) rather than equivalent.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a scheduled gathering such as a regular, poster or workshop session) under Event > Scientific Event > Session. B 'Session room' is a physical place (a room where sessions are held) under Place, sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room. One is an event, the other a location, so they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A Workshop is a working event (a small interactive meeting held alongside a conference, sibling of Conference and Tutorial under Working event), whereas B Closing Talk is a talk event (a scheduled presentation session, sibling of Welcome Talk under Talk Event). They denote different kinds of conference events with no overlap in intended instances, so they are unrelated.

ekaw:Location is a venue/place where events are held (domain/range of heldIn and locationOf, linking Events to Locations). iasted:Time_zone denotes a time zone (a temporal/geographic offset concept), not a physical location of an event. Different intended instances and no shared properties; the pair is unrelated.

A's Paper is the general document class (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Abstract is a specific document type (parent of Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, presented as a presentation). They denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Administrative event' is a subclass of Event covering organisational events (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration) with properties like follows/parallel with; B's 'Paper' is a subclass of Document covering the written contribution with properties like is Written By, has Topic, is Reviewed By. Different domains (event vs document), different parents, siblings and properties, so they are unrelated.

Presenter (ekaw) is a Conference Participant who presents a paper, a subclass of Person with children like Invited Speaker. Sponsor (iasted) is a Person who funds the conference, sibling of Delegate. They denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'has short title' is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving an abbreviated title string, while B's 'City of conference' is a datatype property of Conference giving the host city. Different domains, different intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'has a name' is a datatype property attaching a string name to entities like Conference, Publisher, Topic; B's 'obtain' is an object property relating a Person to an Item. Different kinds (datatype vs object), different domains/ranges, and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is Initiated By' relates a Call to a committee role (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. who initiated/owns a call for papers. B's 'send' relates a Person to an Item, i.e. a person sending some item. Different domains (Call vs Person), different ranges (committee roles vs Item), and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Short paper' is a specific kind of contribution (a short paper), while B's 'Paper' is the general document class that authors submit. A short paper is a paper, so Short paper is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

A's read Paper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the reviewer reads the paper they review), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper). Different domains (Reviewer vs Author) and different directions of the authoring/reviewing relationship; they are not the same relation.

A's belongsToEvent links a Programme to the Conference Event it belongs to (domain Programme, range Conference Event), while B's partOfEvent is a mereological relation between Events (domain Event, range Event). They both express a containment/participation link involving events, but the domains differ (Programme vs Event) and B is a general event-to-event part relation, not a programme-to-event membership. They overlap in intent but are not the same relation, so 'related' is the safest verdict.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while B's 'awarded by' links an Award to the entity granting it. Different domains (Contribution vs Award) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Slide Set is a presentation artifact (sibling of Paper, Review, Programme under Document), while B's Paper is the written contribution with children like Conference Paper, Submitted Paper and properties such as has Review, covers Topic. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a kind of conference paper (a document type), while B is a sponsorship level in the SIGKDD ontology. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A relates an Administrator to a Conference (running paper assignment tools), while B relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher (having a publisher). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A Banquet is a social event (a meal/celebration) under Event > Social event, while Accommodation Place is a physical place (lodging) under Place. They denote different concepts: an event vs. a location, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type, the abstract version of a paper), while B is a subclass of Topic (a subject area such as cryptography). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'Conference Venue Place' is a kind of Place (a physical location such as a venue building/room) under Place alongside Accommodation, Dining and Meeting Room places. B's 'Conference city' is a kind of City (a geographic city) under City alongside Presenter, Sponsor and Trip cities. Both concern the location of a conference, but a venue place and a city are different concepts (a city is not a place in the venue sense, and a venue place is not a city), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Worker non speaker' is a person (a delegate who is not a speaker), sitting under Delegate > Non speaker, while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place under Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office. Different kinds of entities (person vs. venue), so they are unrelated.

Both denote a person who organizes a conference. In the Conference ontology, Organizer is the class of people who organize the event; in sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is a subclass of Organizator covering the same role. The intended instances coincide (people serving in the organizing role), so they are equivalent despite the different labels and the slightly more specific-sounding sigkdd label.

OC Chair (Organising Committee Chair) is a member of the organising committee, while Session chair is a delegate who chairs a session. Both are chairing roles in the conference domain, but they are distinct concepts: OC Chair is a committee leadership role, Session chair is a session-level role. They overlap in that both involve chairing, but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Working event' is a broad event category (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop; sibling of Administrative/Social event) covering the whole working part of a conference, while B's 'Registration' is a specific conference activity (a sub-activity of Conference activity, with Delegate as child) that is a registration process, not an event category. Their paths, parents, children and siblings do not coincide, so they denote different concepts.

A's Tutorial is a working event (a hands-on instructional session) alongside Conference and Workshop. B's Organizational Meeting is an academic event alongside Paper Presentation, Talk Event and Workshop, i.e. a meeting for organising the conference rather than a tutorial. Different intended instances, so not equivalent.

A 'Conference Trip' is a social event (an activity, sibling of Conference Banquet) in ekaw, while B 'Conference building' is a physical place/building in iasted (sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). Different kinds of entities (event vs. location), so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a conference paper: A's Paper is a Regular contribution (a full paper) with an abstract, sibling of Extended abstract; B's Paper is a Contribution sibling of Poster and Short paper. Same intended instances (full papers submitted to a conference), so they are equivalent.

A's Paper Abstract is a document type (the abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper). B's Assigned Paper is a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer (child of Submitted Paper, parent of Evaluated Paper). They denote different concepts: one is a document form, the other a workflow state of a submission.

A's 'technically Organised By' is a subproperty of 'organised By' in the conference-organisation domain, relating an event/conference to the person or body that organises it technically. B's 'presentationed by' has domain Document and range Speaker, relating a document (paper/presentation) to the speaker who presents it. The kinds of things related (event vs. document; organiser vs. speaker) and the direction of the relation differ, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members (a membership/participation relation), while B's parallel_with links an Administrative event to another Administrative event (a scheduling/concurrency relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment relation), while B's 'go through' relates an Item to an Activity (participation/process relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Committee member' is a general role for anyone serving on a committee (its children include Chair and Co chair), while B's 'Conference Chair' is the specific chair role. The chair is a kind of committee member, so Committee member subsumes Conference Chair; they are not equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a specific social event (sibling of Conference Banquet), while B Conference activity is a broad category covering all conference activities (lectures, breaks, registration, social program, etc.). The trip is one kind of conference activity, so A is strictly narrower than B.

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property on Review expertise (a reviewer's expertise value), while B's 'is connected with' is a broad object property linking Activity/Person to Item/Place. Different domain, range, and kind (datatype vs object), so they do not denote the same relation.

A is a conference-domain role (a co-author of a contribution, sibling of first author), while B is a hotel-room type (single room, sibling of double room). They share no meaning and belong to entirely different branches of the domain.

A's 'was a steering committee of' links a Steering committee to a Conference volume (a governance relation over a publication series), while B's 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event (an event-organising relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is a general submission class whose children include Paper, Poster and Short paper, and it carries submission metadata (title, abstract, keywords, authors, reviews). Paper in sigkdd is a specific document type under Document, with only a submit property. Contribution is strictly more general than Paper, so confOf's Contribution subsumes sigkdd's Paper rather than being equivalent to it.

Both are subclasses of Place in the conference domain, but 'Session room' denotes a room where sessions are held, while 'Hotel' denotes a lodging venue. They are related (both places used for conference activities) but not the same concept; a session room is not a hotel.

A's 'Organising Agency' is a subclass of Organisation (an institution/organisation that organises a conference), while B's 'Organizing Committee member' is a subclass of Person (an individual person serving on the committee). They denote different kinds of entities (organisation vs. person) and are not equivalent.

Sponzorship in iasted is a general money/financial category (sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip under Money), while Bronze Supporter in sigkdd is a specific sponsorship tier (sibling of Gold/Silver/Platinum Supporter under Sponzor). They denote different concepts: a broad financial category vs. a particular sponsor level, so they are not equivalent.

A's Session Chair is a Person who chairs a session (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair, TPC Member; involved in reviewing papers and initiating calls). B's OC Chair is an Organising Committee member who chairs the whole conference organisation (subclass of OC Member, alongside other OC roles). Both are chairing roles within the conference, but they denote different roles (session chair vs. organising-committee chair), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Regular author' is a kind of conference contribution/contributor role (a person who is a regular (non-invited) author of a contribution), while B's 'Lecturer' is a subclass of Author in the delegate/speaker hierarchy, denoting a person who gives lectures. Both denote author-like persons in the conference domain, but the intended instances do not coincide: 'Regular author' contrasts with invited speakers/contributions, whereas 'Lecturer' contrasts with student/worker lecturers and plenary/tutorial speakers. They overlap (an author who lectures) but are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a document type (a full paper submission) in the cmt ontology, while B 'Overhead projector' is a piece of audiovisual equipment in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Item/Audiovisual equipment) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a document type that is written by authors, has topics, and is reviewed; B's Review is a distinct document type (sibling of Paper and Abstract) representing a review of a paper. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Session Chair (ekaw) is a conference participant who chairs a session, a role under Conference Participant/PC Member. General Chair (sigkdd) is an organizer role under Organizator, the top-level conference organizer. Different roles with different parents and siblings; not the same concept.

cmt:User is a general person role (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer) representing any system user, while iasted:Student lecturer is a very specific academic role nested under Lecturer > Author > Speaker > Delegate. The two concepts do not coincide: a User need not be a student lecturer, and a student lecturer is a specific kind of author/speaker, not a generic user. Different intended instances and different positions in the hierarchies, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is Provider Of' relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (sponsoring relation), while B's 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (a dependency/requirement relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property on Person with range string, while B's 'has Phone' is a datatype property on Contact Information with range string. They relate different kinds of things (email vs phone) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the chair of the program committee: cmt's Program Committee Chair is a subclass of Chairman and Program Committee Member, and ekaw's PC Chair is a subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member. The labels are synonymous and the parent contexts (chair role plus PC membership) agree, so the intended instances coincide.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person/Contact Information to an email string, while B's Name links a Person to a name string. They denote different attributes (email address vs. name), so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Conference Member is a broad class of people involved in a conference (parents Person; children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, Conference Chair), whereas ekaw:SC Member is a specific steering-committee role nested under PC Member. Every SC Member is a conference member, but not vice versa, so Conference Member is more general and SC Member is subsumed by it.

A's has City is a datatype property of Contact Information whose value is a city string; B's Name is a datatype property of Person whose value is a person's name. Different domains (Contact Information vs Person) and different intended values (city vs name), so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a conference contributor (a person invited to speak at a conference), while B's 'Worker lecturer' is a subclass of Lecturer under Author/Speaker/Delegate in a building/place hierarchy, denoting a lecturer who is a worker (as opposed to a student lecturer). The two concepts differ in both role and context: one is an invited conference speaker, the other a category of lecturer by employment status. They do not denote the same class.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event (an activity in the conference process, sibling of Reviewing event, Camera Ready event), whereas B 'Conference Paper' is a document type (a subclass of Paper). One denotes a process/event, the other a document artefact, so their instances cannot coincide.

A is the registration deadline (deadline for registering for the conference), while B is the paper submission deadline (deadline for submitting papers). They are distinct deadlines in the conference domain, as confirmed by their siblings: A's siblings include Submissions deadline and Camera ready manuscript deadline, while B's siblings include Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Author notification. They share only the parent Deadline and the word 'deadline'.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a specific kind of submitted paper that has undergone review, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution and review-related properties. B 'Activity' is a broad event/action concept (conference activities, activities before/after the conference) with properties about persons, places, money and time. The two denote different concepts; a reviewed paper is not an generic activity, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties are inverses of each other: cmt's read By Reviewer goes from Paper to Reviewer (a paper is read by a reviewer), while edas's is Reviewing goes from Reviewer (and other roles) to Paper (a reviewer is reviewing a paper). They relate the same kinds of things but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent; a reference alignment would record them as inverse/related rather than equivalent.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to the Organization that employs them (employment relation), while ekaw's technicallyOrganises is a subproperty of organises relating an Organisation to the event/thing it technically organises. Different domain (Person vs Organisation), different range, and different meaning; they are not the same relation.

A is a conference event (a working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while B is a person role (a workshop chair, a kind of conference participant). An event and a person role cannot denote the same concept, so they are unrelated.

A Meta Review (cmt) is a review of reviews, a subclass of Review in the document/review hierarchy. B Personal Publication History (edas) is a record of a person's publications, a subclass of Personal History alongside Personal Review History. They denote different concepts with no overlap: one is a review artefact, the other a personal history record.

A's 'has the last name' relates a Person to their family name, while B's 'has First Name' relates a Person to their given name. They are different datatype properties with different intended values (surname vs. forename), so they are not equivalent.

Conference volume is a conference event/publication entity (has committees, tracks, contributions, important dates), while State in iasted is a geographic/administrative region occupied by or visited by persons. They share no intended instances and no meaningful overlap.

A's 'is an abstract submission date' is a specific deadline (the abstract submission deadline) within the Important dates class, while B's 'Date' is the generic date property of any Deadline. The abstract submission date is one kind of deadline date, so A is strictly more specific than B; they are not equivalent.

A's Conference Venue Place is a generic place where a conference is held (sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place under Place), while B's Conference hotel is a specific Building subtype (a hotel used for a conference). A conference venue place can be a hotel, but also a university, convention centre, etc., so the hotel is a narrower concept: Conference hotel is subsumed by Conference Venue Place, not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person who reviews papers in the conference domain. In cmt, Reviewer is a Conference Member/User who is assigned papers to review (has Been Assigned, assigned To, read By Reviewer, assign External Reviewer). In iasted, Reviewer is a Delegate/Speaker who reviews, sibling of Author. The intended instances coincide: a reviewer of conference submissions. The differing parent hierarchies (Conference Member vs Speaker) reflect different modelling choices, not different concepts.

Both classes denote the geographic city concept: confOf's City is the range of has City (Organization/Person -> City), and iasted's City is a location occupied by/visited by persons and situated in places, with subclasses for conference/presenter/sponsor/trip cities. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a call inviting submissions/participation), while B 'Industry Organization' is a type of organization (an organization belonging to industry, sibling of Academia/Government/NGO). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person (path Person > Student), while sigkdd's Person is the general superclass of all people (children Listener, Organizator, Speaker). A Student is a kind of Person, so Student is strictly more specific: subsumed_by, not equivalent.

In cmt, Document is a general class whose children are Paper and Review, so Document subsumes Paper. In ekaw, Paper is a subclass of Document (path Document > Paper), confirming that Document is the broader concept. The two entities are therefore not equivalent: cmt's Document is more general than ekaw's Paper.

A's 'assign External Reviewer' relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (a person assigned to review), while B's 'reviewer Of Paper' relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the paper being reviewed). The ranges differ (person vs. paper) and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's contributes relates a Person to a Conference document (authoring/submitting a paper), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (receiving a prize). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Sponsorship is a funding arrangement class (with cost amount/currency and provider relations, child Travel Grant), while B's Sponsor city is a subclass of City denoting a city where a sponsor is located. They share only the sponsor stem and have different parents, siblings and properties, so they denote different concepts.

A Presenter is a Conference Participant who presents; B Speaker is a Person who gives a presentation (has presentation property to Document). Every presenter is a speaker, but sigkdd's Speaker also covers authors and invited speakers more broadly, so Presenter is narrower and subsumed by Speaker.

A's 'Call for participation' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) announcing the event and inviting submissions. B's 'Simulating' is a research activity performed before the conference (sibling of Modelling). They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (a kind of Conference/event structure), while B 'Demo Chair' is a person role (a Conference Participant who chairs demos). They denote different concepts: one is an event, the other a person/role, so they are unrelated.

Paper in cmt is a document submitted to a conference (subclass of Document, with children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version, and properties like has Author, assigned To, has Decision). Social event in confOf is a subclass of Event (with children Banquet, Reception, Trip) representing social gatherings. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Break Event is a non-academic conference event (parent Non Academic Event, children Coffee Break, Free Time Break, Meal Break), i.e. a scheduled pause/refreshment period. B's Technic activity is a conference activity sibling to Lecture, Presentation, Registration, Welcome address, i.e. a technical/session-type activity. Although both ontologies contain a Coffee break concept, the classes themselves denote different categories (break event vs. technical activity), so they are not equivalent.

A's Topic is the general class of subject areas (it has a name, is a topic of conference parts, is linked to reviews and submissions). B's Cryptography Topic is a specific subject area, a child of edas:Topic. Thus Cryptography Topic is strictly narrower than the general Topic class, so A is subsumed by B's parent rather than equivalent to the specific Cryptography Topic.
Conference Member is a person role in the cmt ontology, while Fee for extra trip is a monetary charge in the iasted ontology; they belong to disjoint domains and have no semantic overlap.

A's Workshop is a kind of academic event (a session held at a conference), while B's Simulating is a research activity performed before the conference, sibling of Modelling. They share no meaning: one is an event, the other a research method/activity, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to the Reviewer it is assigned to (reviewing assignment). B's 'has a submitted contribution' links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (the paper a reviewer is qualified to review). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; not the same relation.

A's isProviderOf is an object property linking an Organization to a Sponsorship (a sponsorship entity), while B's Name_of_sponsor is a datatype property giving the name string of a Sponzor. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Organization vs Sponzor) and range (Sponsorship vs string), so they do not denote the same relation.

In confOf, Workshop is a Working event (a type of event/meeting, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). In edas, Paper Presentation is an Academic Event that is the presentation of an accepted paper (related to Accepted Paper), sibling of Workshop, Talk Event and Organizational Meeting. The edas Workshop is a separate sibling class, so the confOf Workshop does not correspond to edas Paper Presentation; they denote different concepts.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (a static informational artefact, sibling of Call for paper, Conference contribution, Review), whereas B's 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative event (sibling of Submission event, Reviewing event). One is a document, the other an event, so their instances cannot coincide.

A's `location Of` relates a Location to the Event held there (domain Location, range Event), i.e. the inverse of an event's location. B's `holded by` relates a Conference to the ACM SIGKDD organisation that holds it (domain Conference, range ACM SIGKDD), i.e. an organising-body relation. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A Meta Review is a review of reviews (a document that aggregates reviews), whereas a Reviewed contribution is a paper that has received reviews. They are different concepts: one is a review artefact, the other is a submitted paper in the review process. The properties of Reviewed contribution (has a review, reviews) confirm it is the paper being reviewed, not a meta-review.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the cmt person hierarchy), while B 'One conference day' is a temporal entity (a subclass of Conference days under Time). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Regular Session is a session within a scientific event (sibling of Conference Session, Demo Session, etc.). A conference is not a session; the entities denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A is 'Cd proceening' (CD proceedings), a Publication subtype alongside Book proceeding, i.e. a published collection of conference papers. B is 'Review', a Document subtype alongside Abstract and Paper, i.e. a review document/referee report. They denote different concepts (proceedings volume vs. review document) with no subsumption or overlap, so they are unrelated.

cmt:assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review the paper), while ekaw:referencedIn relates a paper to a document/event in which it is cited or referenced. Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type: the full version of a paper), while B is a deadline (a point in time for submitting papers). They belong to different branches (Document vs Time) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Country in confOf is a geographic entity used as the range of the has Country property (Organization, Person -> Country), whereas Person in sigkdd is a human agent class with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker and properties such as E mail, Name, Nation, can stay in, pay. A country is not a person; the two classes denote disjoint concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Organizing committee' is a committee (a group of people) that organizes a conference, sibling of Program/Steering committee. B's 'Organisation' is an organization/institution (parent of Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings. The committee is a body within the conference, while Organisation is an external institution; their instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (Reviewer -> Review); B's writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author (Contribution -> Author). They are inverse-like relations between different entity types (Reviewer/Author, Review/Contribution), not the same relation in the same direction, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'has First Name' is a specific datatype property for a person's first name, while B's 'Name' is the general name property. A first name is a kind of name, so hasFirstName is strictly narrower than Name; they are not equivalent.

confOf's Science Worker is a Person subtype (a person working in science, sibling of Author, Chair PC, etc.), while iasted's Worker non speaker is a Delegate/Non speaker subtype, i.e. a conference attendee who is not a speaker and works. Both denote working persons in the conference domain, but they sit in different taxonomies (Person vs Delegate/Non speaker) and neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they overlap rather than being equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person with range string, while B's 'has Cost Amount' is a datatype property of Sponsorship with range int. They relate entirely different kinds of entities (person names vs sponsorship costs), so they are unrelated.

A's finalizePaperAssignment is an Administrator action that assigns papers to the conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), while B's presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper being presented (domain Individual Presentation, range Abstract/Paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

cmt:Paper is a document (a submission with abstract/full version, authors, reviews, decisions), while ekaw:Event is a general happening (scientific or social event) with locations, organisers and programme listings. They denote different concepts; the only link is that an event 'covers' a paper's research topic, which is a relation, not equivalence.

A's Poster is a specific kind of contribution (a poster presentation), a sibling of Paper and Short paper under Contribution. B's Paper is the general document class for submitted papers (parent of Abstract and Review, range of submit). A poster is a paper-like contribution, so Poster is narrower than Paper; they are not equivalent.

A is an organizational type (academic institution) under Organization, while B is a research activity (modelling) under Activity before conference > Research. They denote different kinds of things (organization vs. activity) and share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to people who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domains (Call vs Document), different ranges (organisational roles vs Speaker), and different intended meanings (initiation vs presentation), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewing assignment), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (authorship). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not inverses either, so they are unrelated.

Meal Event is a general non-academic conference event covering any meal (lunch, dinner, banquet), with Conference Dinner as a child; Conference Banquet is a specific social event (the banquet dinner). The banquet is one kind of meal event, so Meal Event is broader and subsumes Conference Banquet, but they are not equivalent.
