A is a subclass of Place representing a physical conference venue location (siblings: Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). B is a subclass of Delegate representing a person role (a hotel presenter), with siblings like Speaker, Session chair, Listener. A denotes a place, B denotes a person/role; they are fundamentally different kinds of entities and cannot be equivalent.

A is a class of persons (authors who are not reviewers) under Author in cmt, while B is a class of contributions (co-authored papers) under Regular author in Conference. They belong to different branches (person vs document) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's has Street is a datatype property mapping Organization/Person to a string (a street address), while B's is connected with is an object property mapping Activity/Person to an Item/Place. They share only a broad domain (Person) but differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item/Place) and meaning (address vs connection), so they are not the same relation.

Company in confOf is an organization (sibling of University, subclass of Organization), while Meeting Room Place in edas is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place). They denote different concepts and are unrelated.

Scholar in confOf is a person role (a price category for a person, subclass of Person, with property study At), while Sponzor fee in sigkdd is a subclass of Fee (a payment category), so the two denote different kinds of entities and are unrelated.

A is a conference topic (a subject area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a kind of scientific event (an invited presentation). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (topic taxonomy vs. event taxonomy) and share no intended instances.

edas:Paper is the general paper class (parent of Accepted/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), while ekaw:Workshop_Paper is a specific kind of paper (sibling of Conference Paper, Poster Paper, Demo Paper, etc.) under ekaw:Paper. The edas class is strictly more general than the ekaw workshop-paper class, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

Both are datatype properties with string range that capture an email address, but their domains differ: cmt's email is a property of Person (an author/attendee), while confOf's contactEmail is a property of Contribution (a paper/submission) and is annotated as a confTool field. They relate different kinds of subjects to an email string, so they are not equivalent; they are only loosely related as email-address properties.

A 'Paid applicant' is a person who has paid a registration fee, while B 'Credit card' is a payment card item. They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Item) and have no shared superclass or semantic overlap.

Active conference participant is a person role in the conference domain (a contributor who gives presentations), while City is a geographic location class with children like Conference city and Presenter city. Their paths, siblings, and properties (gives presentations vs. is occupied by / is situated in) do not overlap; they denote different concepts.

A's Registration is a conference activity (an event in which delegates participate), while B's Registration fee is a monetary fee with price/currency and payment relations. They denote different concepts (activity vs. fee), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author (the author who wrote a paper), while iasted's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/presenting something). The domains and ranges differ (Contribution->Author vs Person->Activity/Item), and the directions of the intended relations do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (domain Committee, range Chair), while B's 'is Initiated By' links a Call to the people who initiated it (domain Call, range Conference Chair/Session Chair/TPC Member). Different domains, different ranges, and different intended relations (committee leadership vs. call initiation), so they are not equivalent.

A is a document type (an abstract version of a paper) under Document > Paper, while B is a subject/topic category (Communication Theory) under Topic. They denote entirely different concepts: a paper artefact versus a research topic, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while B's Conference Hiker is a kind of Delegate (a person attending a conference). They belong to different branches (Event vs. Person/Delegate) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the person who gives it (range: Active conference participant), while B's 'lists Event' links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to the Events it lists (range: Event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's writtenBy relates a Review to its Reviewer (authorship of a review), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (a talk given by a speaker). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Conference Hiker is a kind of Delegate (a person attending a conference building). One denotes an event, the other a person role, so they are unrelated.

A's remark is a datatype property of Contribution (a free-text note about a paper), while B's Name is a datatype property of Person (a person's name). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Session is a scientific event (a scheduled meeting slot within a conference, with children like Conference Session, Workshop Session), while B's Fee is a monetary charge (with children Registration fee, Sponzor fee). They share no meaning, instances, or properties; the only overlap is the word 'session'/'fee' being absent entirely, so they are unrelated.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property on Conference giving an integer count of reviews per paper, while B's 'has Rating' is an object property from Active Paper to a Review Rating individual. They differ in domain, range, and kind (datatype vs object), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome of a submission), while B's hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country (an affiliation/location attribute). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they share no concept.

A's Tutorial is a kind of scientific event/individual presentation (a session type at a conference), while B's Modelling is a research activity occurring before the conference, sibling of Simulating. They belong to different branches (event vs. activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is the event/meeting itself (it has a name, a volume, proceedings, publisher, topic). B's Conference Hiker is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. a person who attends a conference building — an attendee role, not the event. Different kinds of things (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A's `reviews` is a property of a Review linking it to the Reviewed contribution (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution). B's `reviewes` is a property of a Member PC linking them to a Contribution (domain Member PC, range Contribution). The subjects differ (Review vs Member PC), so the relations are not the same; they are not inverses either, since the subject/object roles do not align.

A's 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (a role/person leading the committee), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving something). Different domains (Committee vs Person), different ranges (Chair vs Activity/Item), and different intended meanings; they are not the same property.

A is a conference event (a working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while B is a person role (a conference participant who chairs demos). They denote entirely different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair in cmt is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), whereas Organising Agency in ekaw is an organisation (a kind of Organisation, sibling of Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher). A person role and an organisation are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the same concept: an organisation in the conference domain. The ekaw class Organisation has children Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher and properties organised By, organises, publisher Of, technically Organises, which match the Conference class Organization's role as an entity that organises events and publishes proceedings. The spelling difference (Organization vs Organisation) is a British/American variant, and the context (organising events, publishing) agrees.

A's min Choice is a datatype property giving a minimum number (positiveInteger) for a social/working event, while B's obtain is an object property relating a Person to an Item. Different kinds (datatype vs object), different domains (event vs person) and ranges (integer vs item), so they cannot denote the same relation.

Both are subclasses of Event representing social gatherings at a conference; confOf's Social event has children Banquet, Reception, Trip and ekaw's Social Event has children Conference Banquet, Conference Trip, matching the same intended instances (banquets, trips, receptions). Same label, same parent, same domain role.

A's Poster is a kind of Contribution (a submitted work presented as a poster, sibling of Paper and Short paper), whereas B's Abstract is a kind of Document (a text artefact, sibling of Paper and Review). Although both are conference-domain entities, a poster contribution and an abstract document denote different concepts; the shared context of 'contribution/document' does not make them equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.
Trip is a social event (an excursion) in confOf, while Value added tax is a financial tax concept in iasted; they share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Abstract), while B's 'Best Student Paper Supporter' is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsorship level, sibling of Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (chair ends a review), while B's reviews relates a Review to a Reviewed contribution (a review is of a contribution). Different domains, ranges, and directions; not equivalent.

A's 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (a record of reviews a reviewer performed), while B's 'write' links a Person to an Item (authorship of a paper). Different domain, range, and direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

In cmt, Conference is the central organising entity that accepts submissions, has members, dates, and administrators; in confOf, Event is a broader category (with children Administrative event, Social event, Working event) that merely has start/end times. A conference is a kind of event, so Conference is more specific than Event; they are not equivalent.

Participant is a class of persons (a role in the conference, with subclasses Member, Regular, Student and property early Registration), whereas Nonauthor registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, i.e. a monetary amount, not a person. They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference contributor is a broad role for anyone contributing to a conference (author, reviewer, committee member, attendee), while B's Conference Participant is a narrower role for someone attending/participating in a conference. The paths differ (A: Person > Conference contributor; B: Person > Conference Participant) and B's children (Demo Participant, Early/Late Registered Participant, OC Member, PC Chair, Presenter, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair) are all attendance/participation roles, whereas A's siblings (Agency Staff Member, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student) include non-participant roles. They overlap in meaning but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Submitted contribution' is a specific kind of written contribution that has been submitted and can be reviewed (it has review expertise, review preferences, and reviewed children). B's 'Document' is a broader class whose children include Abstract, Paper and Review, and which is presented by a Speaker and has a submission deadline. A submitted contribution is a document (paper) that has been submitted, so the intended instances of 'Submitted contribution' are a subset of those of 'Document'; 'Document' is more general. They are not equivalent because 'Document' also covers abstracts and reviews, which are not submitted contributions.

A's isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event (the place hosts the event), while B's is_situated_in relates a Building/City/Place to a Building/City/Place/State (spatial containment of places). Different domain/range kinds and different direction of meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference volume' is a publication/proceedings entity (it has contributions, tracks, committees, important dates), while B 'Conference hall' is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

Company in confOf is an organization type (sibling of University under Organization), denoting an industrial institution. Microelectronics Topic in edas is a research subject area under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches (organization vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property of Person (a person's email address), while B's 'contact Email' is a datatype property of Contribution (the contact email recorded for a paper/contribution, per the confTool comment). Different domains (Person vs Contribution) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes are subclasses of Place and denote the physical room where conference sessions take place. 'Meeting Room Place' in edas and 'Session room' in iasted have the same intended instances (rooms used for sessions/meetings), and their sibling sets (other venue-related places) are consistent with this reading.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a physical location (a subtype of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place) where conference activities occur. B 'Hotel registration form' is a Document/Form artefact used for hotel registration. They denote entirely different concepts (location vs. document) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has a name' is a datatype property assigning a string name to entities like Conference, Publisher, Topic; B's 'topic Covered By' is an object property linking a Research Topic to an Event or Paper. Different kinds (datatype vs object), different domains/ranges, and different intended relations, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'written By' relates a Contribution to its Author (domain Contribution, range Author), while ekaw's 'has Part' is a generic mereological/part-whole property with unspecified domain and range. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a subclass of Person (a person who applies to register, with child 'Registeered applicant'), while B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Working event (an event such as a conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and are unrelated.

A's Decision is the outcome of a paper review (children Acceptance/Rejection, domain of has Decision from Paper), while B's ACM SIGKDD is the conference organisation itself (holds conferences, has deadlines, sponsors). Different concepts.

A's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (submission act), while B's study At relates a Scholar to a University (affiliation/education). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; no overlap.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (author writes paper), while B's `reviewWrittenBy` relates a Review to a Possible Reviewer (review is written by a reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they are not the same relation.

A's 'read By Reviewer' relates a Paper to the Reviewer who read it (domain Paper, range Reviewer), while B's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer who invited them (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's reviewCriteriaEnteredBy links a Conference to the Administrator who entered review criteria; B's reviews links a Review to the Reviewed contribution it concerns. Different domains (Conference vs Review), different ranges (Administrator vs Reviewed contribution), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (membership of a conference), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity/Item (a person giving something). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Conference vs Person as domain; Person vs Activity/Item as range), so the properties denote different relations and are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a document type (a full paper submission, sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), while B 'Main office' is a physical place (a building/room under Place, sibling of Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname (range string), while B's 'Price' is a datatype property of Registration fee giving a monetary amount (range int). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they denote different relations.

A's Conference is a kind of working event (a meeting/event), while B's Delegate is a person/role (a conference participant, parent of Speaker, Session chair, etc.). They denote different concepts: an event versus a person, so they are unrelated.

Meal Event is a specific non-academic conference event (a meal, with a menu, whose only child is Conference Dinner), whereas Social program is a broader category of conference activity that includes Dinner banquet, Coctail reception, Coffee break, Welcome address, etc. Every Meal Event is a kind of social-program activity, but Social program also covers non-meal activities, so Meal Event is strictly more specific: subsumed_by.

Paper Abstract is a document type (a paper's abstract) in the conference domain, while Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment; they share no intended instances and belong to entirely different branches of the domain.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name, while B's 'has Title' is a datatype property of Contribution giving the title of a paper/contribution. Different domains (Person vs Contribution) and different intended meanings (first name vs title), so they are unrelated.

A's hasPart is a generic mereological/part-whole property with no specified domain or range, while B's awarded_by is a specific relation from an Award to the awarding body. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a human attending the conference, with subclasses Active/Passive participant), whereas B's 'Social Event' is a subclass of Non Academic Event (an event such as Excursion or Reception). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a paper's submission bid), while B's issues relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issuing proceedings). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Poster is a kind of contribution (a paper/presentation type) in confOf, while Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship level in sigkdd; they belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's property records the specific acceptance-announcement date of a conference (domain Important dates, range date), while B's property records the date/time on which any Activity occurs (domain Activity, range dateTime). Different domains and different intended meanings: a general activity timestamp is not the same relation as a conference acceptance-announcement date.

Both classes denote the conference event itself: A's Conference has a name and a conference volume/proceedings, and B's Conference is the central event class with dates, country, members, topics and deadlines. The intended instances (conferences) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

Conference document is a class of documents (calls, contributions, reviews) with authors and issue dates, while Time in iasted is a temporal class (conference days, deadlines, trip days) used as the range of temporal relations like is held before/after. They share no instances and play different roles in the domain, so they are unrelated.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (membership relation). B's was_a_committee_chair_of relates a Chair to a Committee (chairing relation), and is a subproperty of was_a_member_of. The two properties relate different kinds of things (member vs chair) in the same direction, so they are not equivalent; the chairing relation is a specialization of membership, not the same as generic PC membership.

A is a conference topic area (Parallel and Distributed Computing) under Topic, a subject classification. B is a research activity (Modelling) under Activity before conference > Research, a kind of activity performed. Different domains (topic vs. activity), no shared instances; unrelated.

A's hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to a URL/string home page, while B's Name links a Person to their name string. They share only the domain (Person) and range (string) but denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a role played by people contributing to a conference, with children like Invited speaker, Regular author), while Banquet is a subclass of Social event (a social gathering at a conference, sibling of Reception and Trip). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (person/role vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.
Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment, while Listener is a person role; they denote different concepts.

A's Review is a document/contribution class (a review artefact, sibling of Conference contribution, with properties 'has a review' and 'reviews' linking it to a Reviewed contribution). B's Reviewer is a person role (a Delegate/Speaker who reviews), sibling of Author. A review document and a reviewer person are different concepts, so the classes are unrelated.

Both properties link a paper/contribution to its authors: Conference's 'has authors' has domain Conference document and range Person, while confOf's 'written By' has domain Contribution and range Author. Conference document corresponds to Contribution (a paper) and Person to Author, so the two relations connect the same kinds of things in the same direction and are equivalent.

Author in confOf is a Person who writes Contributions (subclass of Person, with writes/written By properties). ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd is an organisation/society that designs deadlines, holds conferences and searches sponsors. They denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Agency Staff Member is a Person who works for the organising agency (sibling of Conference Participant, Paper Author, Student), whereas Author of paper is a Person who has written a paper (subclass of Author/Speaker). The two denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's isMenuOf relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (a menu-to-event link), while B's hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event (a part/containment relation between events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

ekaw's hasPart is a generic mereological property with unspecified domain/range, while iasted's sign is a specific relation from Person to Item (a person signing an item). They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Submission event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the act/phase of submitting contributions), while B's 'Initial manuscript' is a document item (the submitted paper itself, sibling of Final manuscript). They are related (the submission event produces/handles the initial manuscript) but denote different concepts: an event vs. a document, so not equivalent.

A's paper ID is a datatype property identifying a Paper (domain Paper, range unsignedLong), while B's Name is a datatype property naming a Person (domain Person, range string). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while B's 'pay' links a Person to a Registration fee (payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

Pending Paper is a review-status state of a paper (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), whereas Conference Paper is a paper type/genre (sibling of Demo/Poster/Workshop Paper). They classify papers along different dimensions and do not denote the same concept.

A 'Committee member' is a person who belongs to a committee (has members / was a member of a Committee), with subclasses Chair and Co chair. B 'Agency Staff Member' is a person affiliated with an agency (e.g. an organising agency), a sibling of Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer and Student. The intended instances do not coincide: committee membership is not agency staffing, and neither class subsumes the other.

Event in confOf is a conference event/activity with subclasses Administrative, Social and Working event and start/end times; Speaker in sigkdd is a Person subtype (with Author and Invited Speaker children) who presents documents. Different domains (event vs person), no shared instances.

Paper Abstract is a document type (a short paper/abstract submission) in the conference domain, while NGO is a type of organization (non-governmental organization). They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Organization) and share no intended instances.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' is a Conference-domain property linking a conference to the Administrator who finalized paper assignments. B's 'give' is a Person-domain property linking a person to an Activity or Item they give. The domains (Conference vs Person), ranges (Administrator vs Activity/Item), and intended meanings differ; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes papers), while B's 'Research Topic' is a subject area covered by events/papers. They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. topic), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has authors' goes from Conference document to Person; B's 'authorOf' goes from Person to Document. They relate the same kinds of entities (documents and persons) but in opposite directions, so they are inverses, not equivalent.

A's Paper is the general paper class (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, sibling of Review, with submission/review/decision properties), while B's Poster Paper is a specific paper type under Paper, alongside Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc. A's Paper is more general and corresponds to B's Paper, not to Poster Paper, so A subsumes B.

Company is an organizational entity (a type of Organization, sibling of University) in the conference domain, whereas Computer Networks Optical Topic is a research subject/topic area. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a subclass of Conference contributor (a person role), while B's 'Introduction of speaker' is a subclass of Introduction, a conference activity (the act of introducing a speaker). One denotes a person, the other an event/activity, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Personal Publication History' is a class under Personal History representing a person's record/history of publications (sibling of Personal Review History), i.e. a biographical/history entity. B's 'Paper' is a document class (subclass of Document) with children like Conference Paper, Submitted Paper, and properties such as has Review, covers Topic. The two denote different concepts: a history/record versus a publication document. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's Conference contributor is a broad role class under Person covering invited speakers, regular authors and active participants; B's Lecturer is a narrow subclass of Author (with children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer) in the iasted hierarchy. They overlap in that a lecturer is a kind of contributor, but neither subsumes the other cleanly: contributor is far more general than lecturer, and lecturer is a specific author role not present in A. Hence related rather than equivalent.

Break Event is a specific kind of non-academic conference event (coffee break, meal break, free time), while iasted's Conference activity is a broad umbrella covering all conference activities (lectures, presentations, registration, social program, etc.). Break Event is therefore strictly narrower than Conference activity, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

Both are classes named Review under Document in the conference domain; cmt's Review has children Meta Review and is written by a Reviewer, and edas's Review is a sibling of Paper under Document, matching the same intended instances (reviews of papers).

A's 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (the venue/proceedings where it is submitted), while B's 'relates To' is a broad property linking a Document to any Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session or Person. The ranges differ substantially (Conference volume vs. events/sessions/persons) and B is far more general, so they are not equivalent; they only overlap in that both connect a paper-like entity to a conference-related entity.

Both denote a session within a conference: edas Conference Session is a subclass of Conference/Academic Event with related documents and persons, while iasted Session is a Lecture subtype under Conference activity. In the conference domain a 'session' is the same organisational unit (a slot of talks) in both ontologies, so the intended instances coincide despite differing parent hierarchies.

In cmt, User is a general person role with children Administrator, Author, Reviewer; in iasted, Reviewer is a specific role under Speaker/Delegate. User is strictly more general than Reviewer, so User subsumes Reviewer, not equivalent.

Reviewer and TPC Member are distinct roles in the conference domain. A TPC Member is a program-committee member who may review papers, while a Reviewer is anyone who reviews (including non-PC reviewers). The edas ontology itself lists Reviewer and TPC Member as separate sibling classes under Person, confirming they are not equivalent. They overlap in that TPC members often review, hence 'related' rather than 'unrelated'.

confOf's Paper is a generic contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while ekaw's Evaluated Paper is a specific stage in the submission workflow (a paper that has been assigned and evaluated, with children Accepted/Rejected Paper). Every Evaluated Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is evaluated, so Paper is more general and is subsumed by Evaluated Paper.

In confOf, Author is a Person who writes Contributions (properties writes/written By). In edas, Reviewer is a Person who reviews Papers (has Review History, is Reviewing). An author and a reviewer are distinct roles in the conference domain; although a person could be both, the classes denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a conference has members/people), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Conference (an organization holds a conference). The domains and ranges are disjoint in kind (Person vs Conference, Conference vs ACM SIGKDD), so the properties are not equivalent; they are unrelated.

Conference contributor is a broad role class under Person covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors; Listener is a specific delegate role (a non-speaking attendee) under Delegate. A listener is a kind of conference contributor, but the two classes are not coextensive: contributors include speakers, authors and chairs who are not listeners, and the iasted Listener is a narrow sub-role. They overlap in the domain but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

A's 'has a name' is a generic naming datatype property with domain covering Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, and range string. B's 'manuscriptDueOn' is a deadline property with domain Conference and range dateTime, described as the manuscript submission deadline. They relate different kinds of things (names vs. dates) and have incompatible ranges, so they are unrelated.

cmt's Chairman is a general chair role with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, and Program Committee Chair, and it is involved in conflict-of-interest marking for papers. edas's Session Chair is a narrower role that initiates calls and reviews papers, sitting alongside Conference Chair and TPC Member as a sibling. The cmt Chairman is broader (it subsumes the conference chair role), while Session Chair is a specific session-level role, so they are not equivalent; Chairman is more general.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing/issuing a proceedings volume), while B's `has Call` relates an Academic Event to a Call (an event issuing a call for papers). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole event such as a conference with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's Session is a lecture-type activity within a conference (a session with speaker lectures, sibling to plenary lecture and tutorial). A conference is not a session; the entities denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Author is a person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers, sibling of Reviewer, Chair, PC Member), while B's Written contribution is a document/contribution type (sibling of Poster, Presentation, Invited talk, child of Conference contribution). The entities denote different kinds of things (person vs. document), so they are not equivalent.
Both denote the conference chair / administrator role in the conference organization; labels and context agree.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (sibling of Extended abstract) that has an abstract; B's Submitted Paper is a subclass of Paper in a hierarchy that also contains Regular Paper, Conference Paper, Camera Ready Paper, etc. A's Paper corresponds to a specific kind of paper (regular contribution), while B's Submitted Paper is the general class of papers submitted to a conference, which is broader and includes A's Paper as one of its subtypes. Thus A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing participant information, while B's 'Best Student Paper Supporter' is a sponsorship role under Sponzor (sibling of Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor). Different domains (document vs. sponsor role) and no shared meaning.

A's relatedToPaper links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (paper-to-paper relation), while B's presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (document-to-person relation). Different domains and ranges, and the directions/meanings do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a review' relates a Reviewed contribution to its Review (domain Reviewed contribution, range Review), while B's 'review Written By' relates a Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it (domain Review, range Possible Reviewer). They differ in both domain and range and are not inverses either; they are distinct relations.

A's hasRelatedDocument links events/sessions/persons to a Document (a related artefact), while B's write links a Person to an Item they authored. Different domain (broader vs Person only), different range (Document vs Item), and different meaning (association vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author restricted to people who author but do not review, a role combination specific to the cmt ontology. B's 'Scholar' is a person category in confOf (a price category for conference fees) with a 'study At' property, sibling to Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc. The two denote different concepts: one is an author-role exclusion, the other a fee/participant category. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

Rated Papers is a subclass of Active Paper (a paper that has received at least one review/rating), whereas sigkdd's Paper is the general paper class (parent of Abstract and Review, domain of submit). Every rated paper is a paper, but not every paper is rated, so Rated Papers is strictly narrower and is subsumed by Paper.

Both classes denote a reviewed submission that has been accepted: A's 'Accepted contribution' sits under 'Reviewed contribution' with sibling 'Rejected contribution' and child 'Camera ready contribution'; B's 'Accepted Paper' sits under 'Evaluated Paper' with sibling 'Rejected Paper'. The ekaw comment explicitly distinguishes accepted paper from camera-ready paper, matching A's structure where camera-ready is a child (a later stage) of accepted contribution. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a short summary document that is a kind of Paper (sibling of Paper Full Version) in cmt, whereas ekaw's 'Flyer' is a promotional document published by an organisation (publisher Of), sibling of Programme Brochure and Web Site. They denote different document types with different roles and properties, so they are not equivalent.

Both are direct subclasses of Person denoting people who take part in a conference. confOf Participant has children Member, Regular, Student and property early Registration; ekaw Conference Participant has children Early/Late Registered Participant, Presenter, Session Chair, etc. The intended instances coincide (attendees/participants of a conference), so they are equivalent despite differing child taxonomies.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (domain Program Committee, range Program Committee Member). B's was_a_committee_chair_of relates a Chair to a Committee (domain Chair, range Committee), i.e. it identifies the committee a chair leads, not membership. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Reviewer is a broad role (parent of Meta Reviewer, sibling of Author, PC Member, etc.) covering anyone who reviews papers. In ekaw, SC Member is a specific sub-role of PC Member (Steering Committee member), a much narrower concept. A Reviewer in cmt is not necessarily an SC Member, and an SC Member is a kind of PC Member/reviewer, so Reviewer is more general than SC Member; the two are not equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a working event (a hands-on instructional session) while B's Workshop is a scientific event; they are distinct kinds of conference events, not synonyms, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'was a committee of' links a Committee to a Conference volume (a committee is part of a conference event), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives/presents something). Different domain (Committee vs Person), different range (Conference volume vs Activity/Item), and different meaning; they are not the same relation.

Conference Chair in edas is a Person who initiates/organises the conference (initiates Call, reviews papers), while Speaker in sigkdd is a Person who gives a presentation of a Document. Different roles with different properties; neither subsumes the other.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the assignment tools), while B's property relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (where it is submitted). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Submitted Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a document submitted to a conference, with children like Assigned Paper), while B's Submission is a broader document category that includes both Initial manuscript and Final manuscript. The two overlap in the initial-submission sense but are not coextensive: B's Submission also covers the final manuscript, and A's Submitted Paper is a subtype of Paper rather than a top-level document category. Hence they are related, not equivalent.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person (path Person > Conference Member) restricted to people involved in a conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), whereas Person in Conference is the general superclass of all people (committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers). Conference Member is therefore strictly narrower than Person, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a submission of a bid/review offer), while B's is paid for relates Money to an Activity or Item (payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference document is a broad class covering calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc., with properties contributes, has a date of issue, and has authors. B's Payment document is a specific financial document (parent Document, children Bank transfer and Cheque) used for conference fees. The intended instances do not coincide: a conference contribution or call for papers is not a payment document, and a cheque or bank transfer is not a conference document. They are unrelated concepts despite both being documents.

A's 'Presenter university' is a Building subtype used as lodging for presenters, while B's 'Conference hall' is a Place where the conference takes place; both are conference venues but denote different roles, so they overlap only loosely.

A's `date` is a generic datatype property of a Conference (the conference's date), while B's `is a date of acceptance announcement` is a specific deadline property of the Important dates class, denoting the acceptance-notification date. Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is the general document class for conference submissions (parent of Accepted/Pending/Rejected/Published/Withdrawn Paper, with authors, topics, reviews), while B's Poster Paper is a specific kind of Paper (sibling of Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). A's Paper is strictly more general than B's Poster Paper, so A subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page/document about the conference, with a URL), while B's 'Conference building' is a physical building/place where delegates are located. They share only the word 'Conference' and denote different kinds of entities (document vs. place), so they are unrelated.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property on Conference giving an integer count of reviews per paper, while B's 'review Of Paper' is an object property linking a Review to the Paper it reviews. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Review), and range (int vs Paper), so they are not the same relation.

A's write Review relates a Reviewer to a Review (the actual review document produced), while B's has a review reference or expertise relates a Reviewer to Review expertise / Review preference (topics the reviewer is qualified for). Different kinds of things are related, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (Reviewer -> Paper), while B's reviews relates a Review to a Reviewed contribution (Review -> Reviewed contribution). The domains and ranges differ, and the direction of the relation is different (reviewer reading a paper vs. a review being about a contribution), so they are not the same relation.

A's `location Of` is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the event held at that location), while B's `Date` is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a dateTime literal. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Location vs Deadline), range (Event vs dateTime), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's `reviews` links a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's `award` links something to an Award. Different domain, different range, different intended relation; no overlap.

A's Workshop is a conference event/activity (sibling of Track and Tutorial, part of the conference programme, with property 'has workshops' from Conference volume), whereas B's Workshop Paper is a type of Paper (a document, sibling of Conference Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). One denotes an event, the other a document, so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Document is a general class whose only children are Paper and Review, i.e. it covers the written contributions of the conference. In iasted, Document is a subclass of Item and is a broad administrative category (forms, invitations, mailing lists, payment documents, records of attendance, etc.), with Review and Submission among its children. The iasted Document is thus a much wider notion of any conference document, while cmt's Document is restricted to papers/reviews. cmt Document is therefore subsumed by iasted Document, not equivalent.

A's Conference is the event itself (has dates, country, members, topics, deadlines), while B's Conference Paper is a document type (a Paper subclass alongside Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a publication artefact.

A's 'Chair PC' is a program committee chair (a Person role, comment 'confTool'), while B's 'Reviewer' is a person who reviews papers, placed under Speaker in iasted. A PC chair is not a reviewer; the roles overlap only in that both are conference persons involved in reviewing, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's property relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (committee membership of a conference), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship of a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent, not inverse, and no subsumption.

A's Conference is the central event/organisation class of the cmt ontology (it accepts submissions, has members, deadlines, administrators). B's Time is a temporal class with children Conference days, Deadline and Trip day, used as the range of temporal relations such as is held before/after and is present. A conference is not a time period; the only overlap is that a conference has dates, which is a different concept. Hence unrelated.

A's 'Conference Venue Place' is a place where a conference is held (siblings: Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), whereas B's 'Main office' is an administrative office location (siblings: Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room). They denote different kinds of places and do not coincide.

Both classes denote a review of a paper/contribution: cmt's Review is a Document written by a Reviewer and ended by the PC Chair, with Meta Review as a child; Conference's Review is a Conference document reviewed by a reviewer and linked to a Reviewed contribution. Same intended instances, so equivalent.

Travel Grant (edas) is a sponsorship/funding concept under Sponsorship, while Sponsor city (iasted) is a type of city under City, describing a location associated with a sponsor. They share only the word 'sponsor' and denote different concepts (funding vs. city), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) giving general participant information. B's 'Viza' is a specific document type (visa document) under Document, sibling of Invitation letter, Payment document, etc. Although both are documents, a visa document is a specific artefact, not the general participant-information document; the intended instances do not coincide.

Conference applicant is a general person role for someone applying to/registering for a conference, with a child Registered applicant; Demo Chair is a specific conference participant role (chair of the demo session) under Conference Participant. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

Both properties link a paper-like item to a person-like entity, but the domains/ranges differ in generality: cmt's assignedTo is specifically Paper -> Reviewer, while iasted's is_given_to is Item -> Person. They overlap in the conference domain (assigning a paper to a reviewer) but are not the same relation, since iasted's property is broader and may cover other item-to-person assignments.

A's 'has parts' relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts (whole -> part). B's 'part Of' is the inverse direction (part -> whole). They are inverses, not equivalent; a reference alignment would not equate them, though they are closely related.

A's Paper is a conference submission/document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Registration fee is a monetary fee for conference registration (child of Fee, with price/currency and payer). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A is an administrative event (a deadline/activity in the conference process, sibling of Submission event and Reviewing event), while B is a type of document (a Paper in the camera-ready state). Although both involve 'camera ready', one denotes an event and the other a document, so their instances cannot coincide.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property giving a person's first name (string), while B's Nation gives a person's nationality/country (string). Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote different attributes; a first name is not a nation, so the properties are unrelated.

Evaluated Paper in ekaw is a paper that has been assigned and evaluated (subclass of Assigned Paper, superclass of Accepted/Rejected Paper), whereas Abstract in sigkdd is a document component (a summary of a paper, sibling of Paper and Review). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the subject area / topic of a paper or conference. In Conference, Topic is linked to reviews, submissions and conference parts (a paper's subject area); in edas, Topic is linked to Conference and Paper via has Topic / is Topic Of, with children being concrete research areas (Antennas, Cryptography, etc.). Same intended instances: research topics of papers/conferences.

A 'Call For Manuscripts' is a call/announcement document (sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Reviews under Call), whereas B 'Conference Paper' is a type of paper document (subclass of Paper). One is a solicitation event/document, the other a submitted/ published paper artefact; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's hasConferenceMember goes from Conference to Conference Member (a conference has members), while B's was_a_member_of goes from Committee member to Committee (a person is a member of a committee). They are inverse-like and operate on different subject/object types (Conference vs Committee member), so they are not equivalent; they are only loosely related through the membership notion.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a Person subclass (a person who contributes to a conference, with children like Invited speaker, Regular author), while B's 'Registration' is a Conference activity (an event/process with child Delegate). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. activity), so they are not equivalent.

Topic in confOf is a subject area of contributions/events (dealt with by Contribution, expertise of PC members, topic of working events), whereas Place in sigkdd is a physical location where a person can stay (children: Conference hall, Hotel, Main office). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Members (people on the organising committee), while B's hasCall links an Academic Event to its Call (call for papers). The ranges (Conference Member vs Call) and the intended relations are entirely different, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Accepted Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been accepted), while B's 'Best Student Paper Supporter' is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsorship role/entity). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. sponsor) and share no intended instances.

Both classes denote a workshop event. In confOf, Workshop is a Working event alongside Conference and Tutorial; in edas, Workshop is an Academic Event alongside Paper Presentation, Talk Event and Organizational Meeting. The intended instances (workshop events at a conference) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite different parent hierarchies.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad class covering all people involved in the conference (with subclasses Active/Passive participant, and siblings like Committee member, Reviewer, etc.). B's 'PC Chair' is a specific role held by a conference participant (a subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member). Thus A is more general than B: A subsumes B, not equivalent.

Author (cmt) is a person role who writes papers and submits them; Conference volume (Conference) is the whole conference event/volume that has committees, tracks, parts and contributions. They are entirely different kinds of entity, so they are unrelated.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to its Decision (domain Paper, range Decision), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not the same relation.

ekaw's hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event (domain Event, range Event), while iasted's give relates a Person to an Activity/Item (domain Person, range Activity, Item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's Conference is a conference event (has a name, children like Conference volume, related to proceedings/publisher/topic). B's State is a geographical/administrative region (children Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state; occupied by/visited by persons, situated in places). The shared word 'conference' in B's child 'Conference state' refers to a state of a conference (a status), not a conference event. Different domains, no equivalence.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a specific document type (the abstract portion of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version), whereas Regular contribution in Conference is a broad submission category that subsumes Extended abstract and Paper. They denote different concepts: one is a document part, the other a contribution type, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Video cassette player' is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a device) in the iasted ontology, while B 'Organizator' is a person role (a subclass of Person) in sigkdd. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (device vs. person) and share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's email is a datatype property of Person holding an email address string; B's Currency is a datatype property of Registration fee holding a currency string. Different domains, different intended values, no conceptual overlap.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author restricted to people who are authors but not reviewers, while B's 'Author' is the general class of authors (with children Author of paper, Author of paper student). Every Author Not Reviewer is an Author, but not every Author is an Author Not Reviewer, so A is strictly more specific and is subsumed by B.
Trip is a social event (an excursion) in confOf, while Departure tax is a monetary tax in iasted; they share no meaning, instances, or context.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with children like Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author), whereas B's 'Non Academic Event' is a subclass of Conference Event (an event such as a Break, Meal or Social Event). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Conference Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an Administrator action that opens the bidding phase for a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference). B's 'reviewes' is a Member PC relation to a Contribution, i.e. a PC member reviewing a paper. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; not equivalent.
ekaw:Paper and iasted:Item both denote conference contributions, but Paper is a specific written artefact while Item is a broader submission entity; they overlap without being identical.

A's Conference is the top-level class for the whole conference (it has a name, parts, proceedings, publisher, topics, and a 'Conference volume' child). B's Conference Dinner is a specific social/meal event nested under Conference Event > Non Academic Event > Meal Event. A conference dinner is a small part of a conference, not the conference itself, and the two classes have no shared instances or properties; they are unrelated.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subclass covering anyone contributing to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors), while OC Chair is a specific Organising Committee leadership role under OC Member. The two concepts do not coincide: an OC Chair is not necessarily a conference contributor in the A sense, and a contributor need not be an OC Chair. No subsumption holds either, since OC Chair is not a subclass of Conference contributor in A's hierarchy.

A's isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event (the place hosts/is the location of the event), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference (the organization holds the conference). The domains differ (Place vs ACM SIGKDD) and the ranges differ (Conference Event vs Conference), so they are not the same relation; they are not inverses either, since neither is the inverse of the other.

Conference in confOf is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas Program Committee in sigkdd is a committee (an organizational group, sibling of Organizing Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee). They denote different concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A's hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper (a general related-paper relation between people and papers), while B's updatedVersionOf links a Document to another Document (a versioning relation between two documents). Different domain, range and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Chair is a person role (a chairperson who chairs the conference), while Main office is a physical place (an office location) under Place. They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A's hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper's rating), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Submitted contribution' is a paper/contribution that has been submitted and can be reviewed (it has review expertise, review preferences, and is a parent of 'Reviewed contribution'). B 'Form' is a document artefact (with children like Author information form, Hotel registration form, Registration form) used for data collection, not a scholarly contribution. The paths, siblings and properties show different intended instances, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document (submitted contribution with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Call For Papers is a call/announcement event under Call, sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews. They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'paper'.

Chairman is a role/person class (a Person who chairs, with subclasses Conference Chair, PC Chair, Associated Chair) in cmt, while Event in confOf is a happening with start/end times and subclasses Administrative/Social/Working event. They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Excursion) held during the conference, while a Full day tour is an activity after the conference (sibling of Departure). They differ in timing and nature, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Regular author' is a kind of conference contribution/author role (a person who is a regular author of a contribution), while B 'Two Level Conference' is a type of conference (a conference with two levels, sibling of Single Level Conference). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A relates a Program Committee to its members (committee membership), while B relates a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (chairing role over a conference part). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent.

A Free Time Break is a break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break) within the Non Academic Event branch, i.e. a scheduled pause during the conference. B Conference Trip is a Social Event (sibling of Conference Banquet), i.e. an organised excursion/outing. Although both are non-academic, a break/pause is not the same concept as a trip/excursion, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' links a Conference to the Administrator who finalizes paper assignments (a workflow/administrative action). B's 'technically Organises' is a sub-property of 'organises' linking an Organisation to whatever it technically organises (e.g. an event/conference). Different domains (Conference vs Organisation), different ranges (Administrator vs unspecified event-like entity), and different intended meanings (finalizing assignments vs organising an event). They do not denote the same relation.

Both classes denote a person who authors a conference paper/contribution. In Conference, 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor and is the parent of the first-author and co-author roles, i.e. the role of an ordinary (non-invited) paper author. In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Author (itself under Speaker/Person) and is the non-student author role, sibling of 'Author of paper student'. The intended instances coincide: persons who have authored a submitted paper. The differing parent structure (contribution-role vs person-role) reflects modelling style, not a difference in denotation, so the reference alignment would record equivalence.

Associated Chair is a person role in the conference committee hierarchy (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while Industry Organization is a type of organization (sibling of Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. organization) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Dinner' is a social meal event (a subclass of Meal Event under Non Academic Event), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical place (a subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. location) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a postal code string; B is an object property linking an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

A is a class of accepted papers (a document/contribution in the review workflow, sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B is a time point (a deadline for notification of acceptance) under Deadline. A document class and a deadline time point denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference document' is a broad class covering all conference-related documents (calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, www, participant info) with properties contributes, has a date of issue, has authors. B's 'Document' is a sibling of Publication, Card, Audiovisual equipment under Item, and its children (Form, Invitation letter, Mailing list, Payment document, Record of attendance, Viza, Submission, Review, etc.) are administrative/paperwork artefacts rather than the scholarly conference documents A intends. The two classes overlap (both include Review and submission-like items) but neither subsumes the other: A includes scholarly contributions and calls, B includes forms, payment and visa documents. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's forEvent relates a Call to the Academic Event it is a call for; B's listsEvent relates a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event it lists. Different domains (Call vs. Programme Brochure/Web Site) and different intended relations (calling for vs. listing), so they are not equivalent.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference, e.g. a student author/participant), while B's Registration SIGMOD Member is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a fee category for SIGMOD members. They denote different kinds of things (person vs. fee) and are not equivalent; the sibling 'Registration Student' in B is the fee counterpart, not A's Student.

Banquet and Reception are distinct social event types; in confOf Banquet is a sibling of Reception, and in edas Reception is a sibling of Excursion. They denote different kinds of social events, not the same concept.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a place for holding meetings (a room/venue for conference sessions), while B 'Single hotel room' is a specific type of hotel accommodation (a single-occupancy sleeping room). They denote different concepts: one is a meeting facility, the other a lodging unit. Their parents (Place vs Hotel room) and siblings (Accommodation/Conference Venue/Dining Place vs Double hotel room) confirm distinct subhierarchies, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Student is a subclass of Participant (a kind of person attending the conference), while in edas Attendee is a direct subclass of Person representing anyone attending. A Student is a specific type of attendee/participant, so Student is narrower than Attendee; they are not equivalent because Attendee also covers non-student participants (authors, chairs, etc.).

A's read By Meta Reviewer relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (a person/role who reads it), while B's has Rating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a numeric/qualitative score). Different domain/range kinds and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's City is a general city class used as the range of has City (Organization, Person -> City), i.e. any city. B's Sponsor city is a specific subclass of City (path City > Sponsor city, siblings Conference city, Presenter city, Trip city) denoting the city of a sponsor. Sponsor city is strictly narrower than City, so A subsumes B (B subsumed_by A), not equivalent.

A Dining Place is a specific kind of place (a restaurant/dining venue), while B Building is a broader class covering hotels, restaurants, airports, universities, etc. A Dining Place is thus more specific than Building, so it is subsumed by Building rather than equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an activity, sibling of Conference Banquet) in ekaw, while B Conference restaurant is a building/place in iasted (sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). Different kinds (event vs. place) and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasEndDateTime is a datatype property of Conference Event giving the event's end time, while B's Date is a datatype property of Deadline giving the deadline's date. Different domains (Conference Event vs Deadline) and different intended meanings (event end time vs deadline date), so they are not equivalent.

A's `obtain` is an object property linking a Person to an Item (a person obtains an item), while B's `City of conference` is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (the city where a conference is held). They have different domains (Person vs Conference), different ranges (Item vs string), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

In the conference domain, the Conference Chair (cmt) is the person who chairs the conference as a whole, which corresponds to the General Chair (sigkdd), the top organizer of the conference. Both are the highest-ranking person roles in their respective hierarchies (Chairman/Conference Member vs Organizator), and their siblings (Program Committee Chair, Author, Reviewer vs Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, Webmaster) are compatible with the same conference-organisation role. The labels differ but denote the same intended concept.

A 'Conference applicant' is a Person (a person who applies to a conference), while B 'Conference' is the conference event itself. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (committee -> event/volume), while B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (event -> person). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Workshop is an academic event type (a kind of conference event, sibling of Talk Event and Paper Presentation). B's Author book proceedings included is a subclass of Author describing an author role/status related to book proceedings, in a completely different branch (Place > Building > ... > Author). The two denote different concepts (event vs. author role), so they are unrelated.

A 'Rejected Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document that was rejected), while B 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity in the conference process (the act of receiving a submission), sibling of Accepting/Refusing manuscript. One is a document state, the other a process/activity; they do not denote the same concept.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a document type (a complete version of a paper, sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), while B 'Communications Topic' is a subject area/topic in the EDAS taxonomy (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Conference contributor (a person contributing to a conference, with subclasses Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author) and Science Worker (a person in the confOf ontology, sibling of Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant) both denote persons involved in the conference domain, but they are not the same concept: Conference contributor is a broad role class covering authors, speakers and participants, while Science Worker is a more general person category in confOf. They overlap in intended instances but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Chair is a committee role (a person who chairs a committee), while B's Registration fee is a monetary fee category with price/currency properties. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person/committee vs. fee/payment) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has members' relates a Committee to its Committee members (people), while B's 'reviewes' relates a PC member to the Contribution they review. Different domain (Committee vs Member PC) and different range (Committee member vs Contribution), so the relations are not equivalent.

A 'Sponsor city' is a city that sponsors a conference (a subclass of City, sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Trip city), whereas B 'Conference hall' is a physical venue/place (subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel, Main office). They denote different concepts: a city acting as sponsor vs. a building where a conference is held.

A's belongsToEvent links a Programme to the Conference Event it belongs to (domain Programme, range Conference Event). B's eventOnList links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site on which it is listed (domain Event, range Programme Brochure/Web Site). The domains, ranges and directions differ: one expresses membership of a programme in an event, the other expresses an event's appearance on a publication/website. They are not the same relation.

A's 'has a date of issue' relates a Conference document to a date (publication/issue date), while B's 'has Title' relates a Contribution to a string (its title). Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's `reviews` relates a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution). B's `is Reviewing` relates a person (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper they review (domain person, range Paper). The two properties have different domains and different directions of participation: one is review->paper, the other is person->paper. They are not equivalent, but they are related in that both concern the reviewing relation between a reviewer/review and a paper.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership of an individual in a conference), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference (an organisation holding a conference). Different domains (Person vs ACM SIGKDD) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title; B's has Last Name is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname. Different domains (Paper vs Person) and different intended values, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'initiates' relates a person role (Conference Chair/Session Chair/TPC Member) to a Call, while B's 'held In' relates an Event to a Location. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Submitted contribution' is a written conference contribution that is submitted and reviewed; B's 'Paper' is a document submitted by an author. Both denote the submitted paper/contribution artefact in the conference domain, with matching submission context (A: submitted contribution/review expertise; B: submit Author->Paper). The paths differ in granularity but the intended instances coincide.

A's Conference Member is a Person subtype (a person involved in the conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Place is a location subtype (with children Accommodation, Conference Venue, Dining, Meeting Room) that is the location of a Conference Event. They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. location) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A Presenter is an Author who presents a paper at the conference, while an Invited Speaker is a distinguished speaker invited to give a talk (a sibling of Author under Speaker). Both are people who speak at the conference, so they overlap, but neither subsumes the other: a presenter need not be invited, and an invited speaker need not be an author/presenter of a submitted paper.

Both classes denote a review of a conference contribution/paper: A's Review is a Conference document with properties linking it to a Reviewed contribution (has a review / reviews), and B's Review is a Document sibling of Abstract and Paper, i.e. the review document produced for a submitted paper. Same intended instances in the conference domain.

A's hasCountry links an Organization or Person to a Country (a location/affiliation relation). B's is_designed_for links an Activity, Money or Time to an Activity or Person (a purpose/beneficiary relation). The domains and ranges are disjoint in kind (Country vs Activity/Person) and the intended meanings differ, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B 'Presenter university' is a subclass of Building (a place/building where presenters stay), sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc. One denotes a person role, the other a physical building/venue; they cannot have the same instances and are unrelated.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer they are assigned to (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer), i.e. a reviewer-assignment relation. B's 'belongs to reviewers' links a Review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (domain Review expertise, Review preference, range Reviewer), i.e. a topic-expertise relation. Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Tutorial is a kind of working event (a session type) in confOf, while Program Committee is a committee (a group of people) in sigkdd. They belong to different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings whose value is an ISBN string, while B's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution whose value is the abstract text. They have different domains (Conference proceedings vs Contribution) and different intended values (ISBN vs abstract text), so they are not the same relation.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person role in the conference organisation hierarchy (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member who chairs the conference), while Late paid applicant (Conference) is a registration-payment status of a conference applicant. The two concepts belong to different subhierarchies (organisational role vs. registration/payment status) and have no overlap in intended instances.

A's 'accept Paper' relates an Administrator to a Paper (the act of accepting a submission), while B's 'related To Event' relates an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (linking an accepted paper to its presentation event). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

confOf's Scholar is a price category (a person with a scholarship, linked to a University via study At), while edas's Author is a person who writes papers (linked to Paper via has Related Paper / is Written By). The intended instances and the surrounding properties differ, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's writtenBy relates a Review to its Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), while B's hasReview relates a Paper to its Review (domain Paper, range Review). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent; at best they are inverses of different relations, not the same property.

A's Abstract is a subclass of Document in ekaw, specifically the abstract of a paper (it has children Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract and is linked to Paper via paper Presented As / presentation Of Paper). B's Document is a general Item in iasted whose children are administrative artefacts (Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Review, Submission, etc.).
