The two denote different concepts: a paper abstract versus a generic document/item, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'paper Assignment Finalized By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who finalizes paper assignments), while B's 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publisher issues proceedings). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.
A's write Paper goes Author -> Paper; B's written By goes Contribution -> Author. They are inverse relations (and even then, Paper vs Contribution differ), so they are not equivalent.
A Meta Review is a specific kind of review (a review of reviews), while B's Review is the general review class. Meta Review is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by Review, not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person who authors conference contributions. In cmt, Author is a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers (has Author, write Paper, submit Paper). In iasted, Author is a Speaker/Delegate who authors proceedings contributions (Author book proceedings included, Author cd proceedings included). The differing parents (Conference Member vs Speaker) reflect different modelling choices, but the intended instances coincide: people who author papers/proceedings. Sibling Reviewer in both further supports the same role distinction.

A's Conference is a general working event (siblings Tutorial, Workshop), while B's Two Level Conference is a specific kind of conference (sibling Single Level Conference) under a broader Conference class. Thus the general Conference concept subsumes the more specific Two Level Conference, so A is subsumed_by B's narrower class rather than equivalent.

A's 'has tutorials' relates a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a whole-part relation within a conference), while B's 'need' relates a Person to an Item (a person's requirement). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Regular is a subclass of Participant (a person category: regular participant, sibling of Member and Student), i.e. a type of attendee. B's Registration SIGKDD Member is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a fee category for SIGKDD members, sibling of Registration Non Member / Student. One denotes a person role, the other a fee/registration category; they do not denote the same concept.

Sponsor is a Person subtype in iasted representing an entity that funds the conference, while General Chair is an Organizator subtype in sigkdd representing a specific organizational role. They share no parent beyond Person, have different siblings (Delegate vs. Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, etc.), and denote different concepts in the conference domain.

Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while Microelectronics Topic is a subject area for classifying papers in EDAS. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic taxonomy) and share no intended instances.

A's City is a general city class (range of has City for Organization/Person). B's Conference city is a subclass of City (path City > Conference city) restricted to the city where a conference is held, alongside Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city. Thus Conference city is strictly more specific than City, so A is subsumed by B.

A's Associated Chair is a chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), while B's Reviewer is a reviewing role under Speaker/Delegate. Different roles in the conference domain; no subsumption or overlap.

A's Reception is a social event (a gathering held during the conference, sibling of Banquet and Trip), while B's Refusing manuscript is a pre-conference activity in the manuscript-handling workflow (sibling of Accepting/Receiving manuscript). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Paper is a kind of conference contribution (a submitted/accepted document, sibling of Extended abstract, with an abstract and parts). B's Call For Papers is a call/announcement event under Call, sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews. A paper is not a call; the entities denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference contribution is a subclass of Conference document and denotes the scholarly content (papers, posters, talks) submitted to and published in a conference volume. Administrative event is a subclass of Event and denotes organisational events such as submission, reviewing, camera-ready and registration events. The two concepts have different parents (Conference document vs Event), different children (Invited talk/Poster/Presentation vs Camera Ready event/Reviewing event/Submission event) and different properties (has contributions/is submitted at vs follows/parallel with). They denote different kinds of things in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A's Place is a spatial location (venue, room, accommodation, dining) that Conference Events are held at, while B's Time is a temporal entity (conference days, deadlines, trip days) that activities are held before/after/in. The two denote different dimensions of the conference domain (space vs. time) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call For Papers' is a solicitation/announcement entity (sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews under Call), whereas B 'Reviewer' is a person role (a subclass of Speaker/Delegate). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Submission event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the act/phase of submitting contributions), while B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a specific deadline date for paper submission. They are related (both concern paper submission) but denote different concepts: an event/activity vs. a temporal deadline. Hence not equivalent.

A's Talk Event is a specific kind of academic event (a talk, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk, siblings Paper Presentation and Workshop), whereas B's Conference is a whole conference edition (a scientific event with siblings Session, Track, Workshop). A talk is a component of a conference, not the conference itself, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about a conference, with a URL), while B's 'Tutorial' is a working event (a type of event held at a conference). They belong to different branches (document vs event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (a chair involved in a conference, under Person > Chairman), while B is a kind of event (an invited talk, under Event > Scientific Event > Individual Presentation). They belong to disjoint top-level branches (Person vs Event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chairing role within the conference committee hierarchy (subclass of Chairman and Conference Member), whereas Invited speaker (Conference) is a conference contributor who gives an invited talk, sibling of Regular author. The roles are distinct and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Non Academic Event' is a conference event type (break, meal, social) in the event hierarchy, while B 'Registration SIGKDD Member' is a registration fee category under Fee > Registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'was a committee of' relates a Committee to a Conference volume (organisational affiliation), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both are classes named Paper under Document in the conference domain, with matching intended instances (submitted/accepted papers). EDAS Paper has richer subclasses and properties, but SIGKDD Paper (submitted by Author) denotes the same concept.

A's `references` relates a paper to the works it cites (a bibliographic citation relation), while B's `award` relates something (e.g. a paper or author) to an Award entity. They denote entirely different relations with different ranges, so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type, the full version of a paper), while B is a subclass of Author (a person role, the author of a paper). They belong to disjoint branches (Document vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Presentation is a general conference contribution (a talk given at the conference, with an abstract, given by a participant, possibly invited). B's Video presentation is a specific kind of presentation activity (a video recording of a presentation), sibling of Power Point presentation. A Presentation is broader and would include B's Video presentation as one of its forms, so A is subsumed by B's parent Presentation, not equivalent to the narrower Video presentation.

A's 'belong to a conference volume' links an Important dates entity to a Conference volume, while B's 'has Programme' links a Conference Event to a Programme. The domains (Important dates vs Conference Event) and ranges (Conference volume vs Programme) are different concepts, so the properties relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome), while B's submit_until links a Document to a Deadline (a submission date). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

In iasted, Form is a subclass of Document (path Item > Document > Form) and its children are specific forms (author information form, hotel registration form, registration form). In sigkdd, Document is a broader class whose children are Abstract, Paper, Review, and which is the range of presentation/submit until. A Form is a kind of Document, so Form is strictly more specific than sigkdd's Document; they are not equivalent.

edas:Person is a broad superclass covering Attendee, Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc. iasted:Speaker is a specific subclass of Delegate (a kind of attendee who presents). A Speaker is a Person, but not every Person is a Speaker, so Person is more general and Speaker is subsumed by it.

A is an administrative event (a process/activity of registering participants) in confOf, while B is a deadline (a point in time) for submitting the camera-ready manuscript in iasted. They differ in kind (event vs. time point) and in topic (registration vs. camera-ready manuscript), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a subclass of 'Reviewed contribution' (a document/contribution that was rejected), while B 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the reviewing procedure. They belong to different branches (contribution vs event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

ekaw:Event is a conference-domain event (scientific/social events, held in a location, organised by people, part of other events), while iasted:State is a geographic/administrative region (occupied by or visited by persons, situated in other places). Their children, properties and domains/ranges do not overlap; the shared word 'state' is coincidental.

Track is a conference part (a thematic stream of the conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, with conferences having tracks), whereas Sponzor fee is a type of Fee (a sponsorship payment, sibling of Registration fee). They belong to different branches of the domain (event structure vs. financial fee) and share no intended instances.

edas Academic Event is a subclass of Conference Event and covers only academic gatherings (organizational meetings, paper presentations, talks, workshops), while ekaw Event is the broader top-level class with children Scientific Event and Social Event, covering all events including social ones. Academic Event is therefore strictly more specific than Event, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to an Administrator (the person who entered conference details), while B's 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organisation publishing the proceedings). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Important dates' is a class of deadline/date entities (submission, camera-ready, acceptance dates) belonging to a conference volume, while B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself with city, name, start/end times and held-by relation. The two denote different concepts; the shared word 'conference' in A's property names does not make them equivalent.

A's Person is a broad class covering chairs, committee members, reviewers and users, while B's TPC Member is a specific role (a subclass of Person in edas) that reviews papers. TPC Member is strictly narrower than Person, so it is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.

Conference Event in edas is a broad event class with children Academic Event and Non Academic Event, covering all conference events (sessions, talks, social events). Conference Banquet in ekaw is a specific social event (a subclass of Social Event, sibling of Conference Trip). The edas class is strictly more general than the ekaw banquet class, so Conference Event subsumes Conference Banquet; they are not equivalent.

Author is a person role in the conference organisation (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Nonmember registration fee is a monetary fee category under Registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Both are classes named Reviewer, both sit directly under Person, and both are defined by the same role: a person who performs reviews (A: belongs to reviewers / has review expertise; B: has Review History / is Reviewing / is Reviewed By). The intended instances coincide, so the two classes are equivalent.

A 'Conference contributor' is a Person (a role played by an individual, with subclasses like Invited speaker and Regular author), whereas B 'Introduction' is a Conference activity (an event such as a welcome/introductory session, with child 'Introduction of speaker'). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (a person/role in the committee), while B's issues relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publication artefact). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Member' is a Person (a person affiliated with a conference, with subclasses Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B 'Conference Banquet' is a Social Event (a meal event at a conference). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Committee member (Conference) is a Person who belongs to a Committee, with children Chair/Co chair and properties linking to Committee. Participant (confOf) is a Person attending the conference, with children Member/Regular/Student and a registration property. The intended instances do not coincide: a committee member need not be a participant and vice versa, and the contexts (committee roles vs. attendance/registration) differ.

cmt:Paper is the general document class for submitted papers (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, sibling of Review), while ekaw:Conference Paper is a specific subclass of ekaw:Paper (siblings include Poster Paper, Demo Paper, Workshop Paper, etc.). The cmt class is broader than the ekaw conference-paper subclass, so cmt:Paper is subsumed by ekaw:Conference Paper only in the sense of being more general; the two do not denote the same concept.

Conference in confOf is a working event (a type of academic event such as tutorial/workshop), while Meal Break in edas is a non-academic break event. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Attendee (edas) is a subclass of Person denoting a person who attends a conference, while Student registration fee (iasted) is a subclass of Registration fee denoting a monetary amount charged to students. They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and have different instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution holding the paper's abstract text; B's 'has Postal Code' is a datatype property of Contact Information holding a postal code. Different domains, different ranges of meaning, no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Program Committee is a group of people who review papers (it has members and a member-of relation), while B's Conference is an event with a city, start/end dates, a name, and a holding organisation. The two concepts denote different things in the conference domain and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

Money is a payment/fee concept with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip and properties about amounts and payers; Person is an agent class with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker and properties like Name, E mail, Nation. They denote different concepts and are not in a subsumption relation.

A's submitPaper is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper). B's is_an_abstract_submission_date is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date value (a deadline). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have different domains/ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person covering people who contribute to a conference (authors, speakers, participants), while B's 'Sponsor state' is a subclass of State describing a status/phase of a sponsor, not a person role. Different parents (Person vs State), different siblings, and no shared instances; they denote different concepts.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with two levels of reviewing), while B 'Presenter' is a role of a person (a conference participant who presents). They denote different concepts: one is an event type, the other a person role. No equivalence, subsumption or meaningful overlap.

A's 'co write Paper' links a Co author (an author entity) to a Paper, while B's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person. Both express authorship of a document, but the domain/range kinds differ (Co author vs Conference document, Paper vs Person), so they are not the same relation; they overlap in intent but are not equivalent.

A is a research topic (a subject area for papers) under Topic, while B is an organizational committee (a group of people) under Committee. They denote different kinds of entities in the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's hasTopic relates a Conference/Paper to a Topic (subject matter). B's volumeContainsPaper relates a volume to a paper (containment of documents). Different kinds of things and different directions of meaning; not equivalent.

edas:Call is a call-for-papers/reviews/manuscripts announcement issued by chairs, with submission deadlines and instructions; sigkdd:Deadline is a specific due date (abstract, paper, notification) that documents are submitted until. They overlap in that a call carries deadlines, but a Call is not a Deadline: the Call is the announcement/event, the Deadline is a point in time. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (the event has a programme), while B's listsEvent links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (a document lists events). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the directions of the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's has Phone relates a Person to a phone number string, while B's has Last Name relates a Person to a surname string. They are different datatype properties with different intended values, despite sharing the same domain and range.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to the Event held there (domain Location, range Event), while B's 'is equipped by' relates a Place to an Item that equips it (domain Place, range Item). The ranges differ fundamentally (Event vs Item) and the intended relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference submission document (parent Document, children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version, properties like has Author, assigned To, has Decision). B's Computer Networks Measurements Topic is a subject-area/topic category under Topic > Computer Networks Topic, with sibling topics. A paper is not a topic; the entities denote different concepts.

A is an organizational type (academic institution) under Organization, while B is a research activity (simulating) under Activity before conference > Research. They belong to entirely different branches (organization vs. activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.
Both terms denote the same conference-domain concept: a person who reviews papers. 'reviewer' and 'reviewer' are identical labels and intended meanings.

A's `part Of` is a generic mereological/structural property with no specified domain or range, while B's `presentationed by` is a specific relation from a Document to a Speaker (the presenter of a document). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and do not denote the same relation.

Both are registration-fee classes for students, but A is specifically the fee for an author who is also a student, while B is the fee for any student registrant (SIGKDD/SIGMOD member or non-member). The intended sets overlap but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'is present' is an object property linking a Person to a Time (attendance at an event). They share only the domain Person; their ranges and intended meanings differ completely, so they are unrelated.

Decision in cmt is the outcome of a paper review (children Acceptance/Rejection, range of has Decision from Paper), while Country in confOf is a geographical entity used by organizations and persons. They denote entirely different concepts.

A 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a human role: active participant, invited speaker, regular author), while B 'Activity before conference' is a subclass of Activity (an event/process such as accepting or receiving manuscripts). They belong to different top-level categories (Person vs Activity) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

ConferenceVenuePlace is a venue where a conference takes place (siblings: AccommodationPlace, DiningPlace, MeetingRoomPlace), whereas SponsorCompanyHouse is a building housing a sponsor company (siblings: ConferenceAirport, ConferenceBuilding, ConferenceHotel, PresenterHouse, PresenterUniversity). Different intended instances and roles in the conference domain.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper (a document/contribution in the conference domain), while B 'Audiovisual equipment' is a subclass of Item covering physical devices (Computer, LCD projector, etc.). They share no meaning, no properties, and no common instances; the only superficial link is that both are kinds of 'Item/Document' in their respective hierarchies, which is not enough for equivalence.

A's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event (a process/activity in the reviewing procedure), while B's 'Review' is a Document (an item, sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter). One is an event, the other a document artefact; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (a person giving a talk), while B's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (a sponsor). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A 'Track workshop chair' is a Person who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial (a specific role tied to a Conference part, with properties linking to Conference part), while B 'General Chair' is an Organizator role (sibling of Program Chair, Webmaster) denoting the overall conference chair. Different roles in the organisation hierarchy, so they are not equivalent.

A Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference event, sibling of Paper Presentation and Talk Event) in edas, whereas an Industrial Session in ekaw is a kind of Conference Session, i.e. a slot within a conference programme. A workshop is a whole event, not a session, and an industrial session is not a workshop; the two concepts do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

confOf's Participant is the general conference participant class (parent of Member, Regular, Student, with an early Registration property), while ekaw's Early Registered Participant is a specific subclass of Conference Participant distinguished by registration status. The confOf class is strictly more general, so it subsumes the ekaw class rather than being equivalent to it.

A's Attendee is a subclass of Person (a role/type of participant), while B's Nonmember registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money (a monetary amount). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `write Paper` relates an Author to a Paper (author -> paper). B's `has authors` relates a Conference document to a Person (document -> person), i.e. the inverse direction and a different subject (document vs author). They are not the same relation; at best they are inverses, which the instructions say do not count as equivalent.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to an anyURI (a web address for a logo image), while B's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location (where the event takes place). They differ in domain (Conference vs Event), range (anyURI vs Location), and meaning (image URL vs physical venue), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class describing a reviewer's expertise/preference for reviewing a submitted contribution (it is the range of 'has a review expertise'/'has an expertise' and the domain of 'has a submitted contribution'). B's 'Review' is a subclass of Document, i.e. the actual review document/artefact produced in the reviewing process. The two denote different concepts (expertise record vs. review document), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Silver Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. sponsor) and denote different concepts.

A 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses like author, speaker, participant), while B 'One conference day' is a subclass of Conference days under Time (a temporal unit, sibling of Delegate). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Time) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Administrative event' is a subclass of Event covering organisational events (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration) and is a sibling of Social event and Working event. B's 'Social Event' is a subclass of Non Academic Event covering Excursion and Reception, i.e. the social side of the conference. They are disjoint branches of the event hierarchy, not the same concept.

A's Abstract is a specific kind of conference contribution (a document/paper subtype, sibling of Paper/Poster/Presentation under Extended abstract), whereas B's Activity is a general event/action class (parent of Conference activity, activities before/after the conference) with properties like give, is held in, is dated on. The intended instances do not coincide: an abstract is a written contribution, not an activity. No subsumption or overlap in meaning.

A's property links a Reviewer to a Review expertise or Review preference (the reviewer's declared expertise/preference), while B's 'references' is a generic bibliographic reference relation between documents/contributions. They relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

Both are object properties relating a monetary amount to a person who pays it, with the same direction (Money/Registration fee -> Person). 'is paid by' and 'payed by' (misspelling) denote the same relation in the conference domain; the domain difference (Money vs Registration fee) is a minor granularity variation, not a conceptual difference.

hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country, while is_connected_with relates an Activity or Person to an Item or Place. The ranges are disjoint (Country vs Item/Place) and the intended meanings differ: one expresses nationality/affiliation, the other a generic connection to an item or place. They are not the same relation.

A's Paper is a conference submission/document with authors, topics, reviews; B's Card is an item with a Credit card child, clearly a payment/identity card, not a scholarly paper. Different concepts despite both being 'items'.

A 'Short paper' is a contribution type (a short-length submission), while B 'Rejected Paper' is a paper status (a paper that was not accepted). They classify papers along orthogonal dimensions (length/type vs. review outcome), so their instances do not coincide.

A's 'Transport vehicle' is a physical means of transport (children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) under Item, while B's 'Speaker' is a person role (children Author, Invited Speaker) under Person. Different domains and no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Talk Event' is a kind of academic event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), whereas B 'Committee' is an organizational body with children such as Program Committee and Organizing Committee. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole event with papers, reviews, etc.), while B's Tutorial is a specific kind of individual presentation/session within a scientific event. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'Rejected contribution' is a reviewed submission that was not accepted, a subclass of Reviewed contribution with sibling Accepted contribution. B's 'Abstract' is a document type alongside Paper and Review, not a decision outcome on a submission. The two denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'accept Paper' relates an Administrator to a Paper (accepting a paper), while B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authoring). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent.

A's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper), while B's hasReview relates a Paper to a Review (the paper has a review). Different domain, range, and direction of the underlying relation; they are not the same property.
Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event) in confOf, while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment in iasted; they share no meaning or context.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/Chair), while B 'Conference Dinner' is a social meal event (parent Meal Event under Conference Event). They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. event) and share no intended instances.

Both properties link a paper/item to its author/person in the same direction (Paper -> Author, Item -> Person). In the conference domain, 'is Written By' and 'is sent by' both express the authorship/submission relation between a contribution and a person; the domain/range classes Paper/Author and Item/Person are the corresponding concepts in the two ontologies.

Topic in confOf is a subject area of contributions/events (dealt with by Contribution, expertised by PC members, had by working events), whereas Person in iasted is a human agent (parent of Delegate and Sponsor, giving/preparing items, being paid, present at times). The two denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances or properties.

In cmt, Paper Abstract is a document type (the abstract-only submission), sibling of Paper Full Version, both subclasses of Paper. In edas, Published Paper is a status/state of a paper (sibling of Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.), not a document type. The intended instances do not coincide: an abstract submission is not a published paper, and a published paper need not be an abstract. Different classification dimensions, so unrelated.

Both are subclasses of Author denoting a person who has authored a paper: cmt's Co author is linked to Paper via co write Paper / has Co author, and sigkdd's Author of paper is the author-of-paper role under Author. Same intended instances (authors of papers), so they align as equivalent.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a subclass of 'Regular author' (a person role in authoring a contribution), while B's 'Presenter' is a Conference Participant who presents, with children like Invited Speaker. The two denote different roles (authoring vs presenting) and sit in different hierarchies, so they are not equivalent.
A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (authored work), while B's `pay` relates a Person to a Registration fee (payment). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; no overlap.

A's 'Presenter city' is a subclass of City, i.e. the city where a presenter is located (siblings: Conference city, Sponsor city, Trip city). B's 'Conference hall' is a subclass of Place, a physical venue/building (siblings: Hotel, Main office). A city and a conference hall are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a person attending a conference without an active role (sibling of 'Active conference participant' under 'Conference participant'), whereas B 'Conference city' is a geographic city hosting a conference (sibling of Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city under City). Different kinds of entities (person vs. location) with no overlap.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a kind of conference event with two levels), while B's 'OC Member' is a subclass of Conference Participant (a person role in the organising committee). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a broad document type with many subtypes (Accepted, Rejected, Published, etc.) and is written by authors, reviewed, and topic-tagged. B's Abstract is a sibling of Paper under Document, so in sigkdd an Abstract is a distinct document artefact from a Paper. They are related (both conference documents) but not equivalent; A's Paper is more general than B's Abstract, which is a specific document kind.

A's 'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of Conference participant (a person role, sibling of Active conference participant), while B's 'Conference state' is a subclass of State (a status/state of a conference, sibling of Presenter state and Sponsor state). They belong to different upper categories (person role vs. state) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is the central organising event class (has members, topics, deadlines, country, name), while B's Conference Trip is a social event (sibling of Conference Banquet) under Event > Social Event, i.e. an excursion, not the conference itself. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

cmt:assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review the paper), whereas ekaw:hasPart is a generic mereological/part-whole property with unspecified domain and range. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and do not denote the same relation.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a conference participant role), while B's Best Student Paper Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsorship level). They denote entirely different concepts: a person role versus a sponsor category, so they are unrelated.

A's has Member relates a Conference to a Person (a conference has members/participants), while B's is present in relates a Person to a Place or Time (a person is present at a location or time). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Conference vs Person as domain; Person vs Place/Time as range), and the intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

A's Presentation is a specific kind of conference contribution (a talk given at the conference, with an abstract, given by a participant, and having Invited talk as a child). B's Contribution is the general superclass of all submitted contributions (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like title, abstract, keywords, author, topic. Presentation is thus a narrower concept than Contribution, so Presentation is subsumed by Contribution rather than equivalent.

A's 'has contributions' is an object property linking a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (whole-to-part membership), while B's 'has Keyword' is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword. They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

Publisher in the Conference ontology is an organisation that issues conference proceedings (it has a name, issues Conference proceedings, and is the range of has a publisher). Money in iasted is a monetary amount with children Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip and properties about being paid by a person and paid for an activity/item. The two concepts share no instances and no meaning in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Presenter house is a specific building where presenters stay, while Hotel is a general lodging place; they overlap in that a presenter house is a kind of hotel/accommodation, but the concepts are not identical.
Both entities denote the role of chairing a conference or program committee; labels and context agree.

Conference Chair is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Person) in cmt, while Track is a scientific event component (subclass of Scientific Event) in ekaw. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee), while B's prepare relates a Person to an Item (preparing some item such as a paper). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties express spatial location, but they differ in kind and domain/range: A's 'has a location' is a datatype property mapping a Conference volume to a string, while B's 'is situated in' is an object property relating places (Building, City, Place) to places or states. They overlap in meaning (location) but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Trip is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception) organised during the conference, whereas B's Car is a transport vehicle (sibling of Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) used for transportation. Although a trip may involve a car, the classes denote different concepts in different branches of the domain, so they are not equivalent.

In Conference, 'Invited speaker' is a subclass of Conference contributor, a person invited to speak. In sigkdd, 'Author' is a subclass of Speaker and is the general class for people who submit papers (with children Author of paper, Author of paper student). 'Invited Speaker' is a sibling of Author in sigkdd, so the two are distinct: an invited speaker is not an author, and an author is not necessarily an invited speaker. They are different concepts, not equivalent.

A's 'Review preference' is a class representing a reviewer's preference/degree of interest for a topic or submission (it has a degree, links reviewers to topics/submissions). B's 'Review' is a document (a subclass of Document) representing an actual review artefact. The two denote different concepts: a preference/interest record versus a review document, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to a homepage URL string, while B's E-mail links a Person to an email address string. They relate different kinds of information (web page vs. email address), so they are not equivalent despite sharing the same domain and range.

A's hasCall relates an Academic Event to its Call (a conference call for papers), while B's searched_by relates a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (a sponsor being searched by a specific organization). The domains, ranges and intended meanings are entirely different, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's has VAT is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a tax string, while B's Name is a datatype property of Person giving a name string. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they share only the string range.

A's 'end Date' is the conference end date/time, while B's 'Start of conference' is the conference start date/time. They denote opposite temporal boundaries of a Conference, so they are not equivalent (nor inverse-equivalent in the required sense).

In iasted, Lecturer is a subclass of Author (path: ... > Author > Lecturer), i.e. every Lecturer is an Author, but not every Author is a Lecturer. In cmt, Author is the general class of people who write/submit papers. So cmt:Author is more general than iasted:Lecturer; the two are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person who authors papers/contributions. In cmt, Author is a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers; in confOf, Author is a Person who writes Contributions. Same intended instances and same role in the conference domain, so they are equivalent.

A's University is an Organization (a type of institution, sibling of Company) that scholars study at. B's Student non speaker is a person role (a Delegate who is a Non speaker, sibling of Worker non speaker) located under Conference building. One is an institution, the other a person role; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

Company in confOf is an organization type (sibling of University, subclass of Organization), while Sponzorship in iasted is a financial concept (subclass of Money, sibling of Fee/Tax/Tip). They denote different concepts: an organization vs. a funding arrangement, so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference topic (a subject area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a document type (an abstract for an invited talk under Abstract). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic taxonomy vs. document types) and share no intended instances.

A's Workshop is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, range of 'has workshops'), while B's Workshop Chair is a person role (a Conference Participant and PC Member). An event and a person role cannot denote the same concept, so they are unrelated.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to an Administrator (the person who entered conference details), while B's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to Important dates (deadlines). Different domain, range, and meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's User is a Person subtype (a conference participant role, with children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Research is an Activity-before-conference subtype (with children Modelling/Simulating). Different roots (Person vs Activity) and incompatible contexts, so they denote different concepts.

Active Paper in edas is a paper that is still active (has a rating, not yet accepted/rejected/published/withdrawn), while Rejected Paper in ekaw is a paper that has been evaluated and rejected. They denote different states of a paper's lifecycle and are not equivalent; Active Paper is a broader category that could include papers later rejected, but the intended concepts differ, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a conference-role person (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B's 'NGO' is a type of Organization (sibling of Academia/Government/Industry Organization). They denote entirely different concepts in different branches of the domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Registration fee' is the general fee category (parent of author/non-author/member/student registration fees), while B's 'Registration Student' is a specific student registration fee that is a child of B's 'Registration fee'. A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'is paid in' relates Money to a Building (payment location). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Conference is the event/meeting class (it has a name and a volume, and is the domain of 'has a name'), whereas B's Conference airport is a physical building/venue (a subtype of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference restaurant, etc.). The shared word 'conference' refers to the event in A and to a location in B, so the intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution (a document type, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract), while B's 'Audiovisual equipment' is a physical item (parent of Computer, LCD projector, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'done till' is a datatype property of Deadline giving the date by which something must be done; B's 'Price' is a datatype property of Registration fee giving an integer cost. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a document/item to a person involved in its presentation, but 'is prepared by' (Item -> Person) is broader than 'presentationed by' (Document -> Speaker), which specifically denotes the presenter/speaker of a document. They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering anyone contributing to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors, and by siblings also committee members, applicants, participants, reviewers, chairs). B's 'Organizator' is a Person subclass restricted to people organising the conference (general chair, organizing committee, program chair, PC member, webmaster), with siblings Listener and Speaker. The two overlap (organisers are contributors) but neither subsumes the other: contributors include authors/speakers who are not organisers, and organisers include roles not clearly covered by contributor. Hence related, not equivalent.

cmt's `date` is a datatype property of Conference with range date, while edas's `has End Date Time` is a datatype property of Conference Event with range dateTime. Both relate a conference/event to a date/time value, so they overlap in meaning, but the domains differ (Conference vs Conference Event) and the ranges differ (date vs dateTime), and `has End Date Time` specifically denotes an end date-time rather than a generic date. They are therefore related rather than equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Trip city is a subclass of City describing a city associated with a trip. They denote different concepts (event vs. location) and share no intended instances.

A's 'accepted By' links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it; B's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization providing it. Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A Track is a thematic subdivision of a scientific event (sibling of Conference, Session, Workshop under Scientific Event), whereas a Plenary lecture is a specific kind of Lecture (a talk given to the whole conference, sibling of Session and Tutorial under Lecture). They denote different concepts: a track is a grouping of papers/sessions, not a type of talk, so they are unrelated.
Trip is a social event (an excursion) in confOf, while Fee is a monetary charge in iasted; they belong to different branches (Event vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both denote the published collection of conference papers: ekaw's Proceedings is a Multi author Volume (a document collecting multiple authors' papers) with a child Conference Proceedings, and iasted's Book proceeding is a Publication (book-like) with a sibling Cd proceeding, i.e. the proceedings of a conference. The intended instances coincide, so they are equivalent.

hasFirstName is a datatype property of Person whose range is a person's first name (a name string), while Nation is a datatype property of Person whose range is a country/nationality string. They relate persons to different kinds of values (name vs. nation), so they are not equivalent.

A is a form document used to collect author information (a subclass of Form/Document), while B is a physical place (a Hotel, subclass of Place). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but their domains differ: A's 'is dated on' applies to any Activity, while B's 'Date' applies specifically to a Deadline. A Deadline is a kind of Activity/event, so the properties overlap in meaning but are not equivalent; B's Date is a specialization of A's is dated on.

ekaw:Organisation is an organised body (academic institution, organising agency, publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings. iasted:State is a geographical/administrative region (with children Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state) that is situated in places and occupied/visited by persons. The two concepts share no intended instances and no properties; they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document type (an abstract of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B 'Satellite And Space Communications Topic' is a conference subject/topic area. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Attendee is a subclass of Person (a person who attends the conference), while B's 'Author attendee cd registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a monetary fee category for author-attendees paying by CD. They belong to different branches (Person vs Money/Fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person who authors papers: edas Author is a subclass of Person with properties linking to Paper (has Related Paper, is Written By), and ekaw Paper Author is a subclass of Person whose name and context indicate the author of a paper. They are synonyms in the conference domain.

In the Conference ontology, 'Regular contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution'/'Written contribution' whose children include 'Paper' and 'Extended abstract'; it is a broader category of written contributions. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a direct subclass of 'Document' with siblings 'Abstract' and 'Review', and is the range of 'submit' (Author -> Paper). A Paper is a kind of regular contribution, but 'Regular contribution' also covers extended abstracts and other written contributions, so the Conference class is more general than sigkdd's Paper. Hence A subsumes B, not equivalence.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a subclass of Chairman (a person who chairs the conference as a whole), while in sigkdd Program Chair is a subclass of Organizator and is the chair of the program committee. The cmt ontology has a separate Program Committee Chair class, so Conference Chair corresponds to the general chair role, not the program chair. The two denote different roles in the conference organisation.
A's held In relates an Event to a Location (object property), while B's has amount of relates Money to an int (datatype property). Different domains, ranges, and kinds; no conceptual overlap.

A's Program Committee Chair is a specific chair role (a Chairman who is also a Program Committee Member, ending reviews), while B's Co chair is a generic committee co-chair role (sibling of Chair, linked to Committee). They are both conference committee leadership roles but neither subsumes the other: A is program-committee-specific, B is a general co-chair position.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (scientific programme activities), while B 'Main office' is a subclass of Place, a physical location. Different branches of the taxonomy (Event vs Place) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A TPC Member (Technical Program Committee member) reviews papers and initiates calls; an OC Member (Organizing Committee member) is a conference participant who organizes the conference, with OC Chair as a child. The two roles are distinct in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call for participation' is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while B's 'Modelling' is a research activity performed before a conference. They belong to different branches (document vs. activity) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a document type (a full paper submission) in the cmt ontology, sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper. B 'Full day tour' is a social/leisure activity after the conference in the iasted ontology, sibling of Departure under Activity after conference. They share only the word 'Full' and belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Activity); they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's Abstract is a kind of conference contribution (an extended abstract document, part of a Paper/Poster/Presentation), while B's Time is a temporal entity with children Conference days, Deadline, Trip day and is used as the range of temporal relations (is held before/after, is present in). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.
A's has Bid relates a Paper to a Bid (a review offer), while B's has Country relates an Organization or Person to a Country. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's Topic is a subject/keyword area used to classify reviews, contributions and conference parts (it has a name, belongs to review preferences, is a topic of conference parts). B's Paper is a document submitted by an author (subclass of Document, sibling of Abstract and Review). A topic is not a paper: topics are classification categories, papers are submitted artefacts. The contexts (properties, parents, siblings) do not coincide, so the two classes are unrelated.

A's hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (the rating value of a paper), while B's reviewWrittenBy links a Review to a Possible Reviewer (the author of a review). Different domain, range, and direction of relation; they do not denote the same relation.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person (domain) to an Organization (range), while iasted's is_used_by relates an Item (domain) to a Person (range). The kinds of things related and the direction differ entirely, so they are not the same relation.

cmt:title is the title of a Paper (a datatype property giving the paper's name), while confOf:remark is a free-text remark/comment on a Contribution (comment 'confTool'). Although both are string-valued datatype properties on a paper-like class, a title is a required identifying name whereas a remark is an optional annotation; they denote different relations, so they are not equivalent.

A relates a conference part to a conference volume (part-whole containment), while B relates a document to a speaker (who presents it). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (the act of a reviewer writing a review). B's hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper having a rating value). Different domain, range, and direction of meaning; not the same relation.

A is a conference topic (a subject area for papers) under Computer Networks Topic, while B is a time concept (a day of a trip) under Time. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

Rejection is a conference decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), while Taxi is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Shuttle bus, Van under Transport vehicle). Different domains and no shared meaning.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a role/type of author (a person who co-authored a contribution), sitting under Regular author alongside 'Contribution 1th author'. B's 'Proceedings' is a multi-author volume document (a collection of papers), under Multi author Volume. One denotes an author role, the other a published volume; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property of a Conference document (a paper/contribution) giving the date it was issued/published, with range date. B's 'paper Due On' is a datatype property of a Conference giving the submission deadline date/time for papers, with range dateTime and comment 'Conference Paper Date and Time Deadline'. Although both involve papers and dates, one denotes the publication/issue date of a document and the other the submission deadline of a conference; they relate different kinds of things (document vs conference) and have different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship relation), while B's 'has Country' links an Organization or Person to a Country (geographic affiliation). Different domain, different range, and different intended relation, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Review preference to a Topic or Submitted contribution, while B's hasReview links a Paper to a Review. Different domains (Review preference vs Paper), different ranges (Topic/Submitted contribution vs Review), and different intended relations; they are not the same relation.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings). B's `topic Covered By` relates a Research Topic to the Event or Paper that covers it (domain Research Topic, range Event/Paper). The domains, ranges and intended meanings are entirely different, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee), while B's is_occupied_by relates a Building/City/State to a Person (a person occupying a location). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the relations are inverse in direction and different in meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a name' is a generic naming property whose domain is Conference/Publisher/Topic etc., while B's 'has Last Name' is a person-specific surname property with domain Person. They relate different kinds of things and are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person (a person who is a member of a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, PC Member, etc.), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself (with children Single/Two Level Conference and properties like end Date, has Country, has Topic). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a broad working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Workshop is a specific academic event type. A Conference is not a Workshop; they are distinct event types, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track (a structural part of the conference), while B's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic of expertise. Different domains (Conference volume vs Member PC), different ranges (Track vs Topic), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's max Choice is a datatype property of Social/Working event giving a maximum number of choices (positiveInteger), while B's end Date is a datatype property of Conference giving its end date/time (dateTime). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Both properties link a paper/presentation-giving entity to a presentation, but the domains differ: A's domain is 'Active conference participant' (a person/role) while B's domain is 'Abstract, Paper' (the document). They describe the same activity from different perspectives (person gives presentation vs. paper presented as presentation), so they overlap but are not equivalent.

Both are classes named Paper under Document, with the same sibling Review and analogous roles (submitted/authored paper with reviews). The cmt Paper has richer properties but the intended instances coincide with sigkdd Paper.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a leadership role within a committee), while B's 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person (a signature/authorisation relation). The domains and ranges differ (Chair/Committee vs Item/Person) and the intended meanings are distinct, so the two properties are not equivalent.

Meta Reviewer is a specialized kind of Reviewer (a subclass of Reviewer in cmt), while confOf's Member PC is the general PC member/reviewer class. Every Meta Reviewer is a Member PC, but not every Member PC is a Meta Reviewer, so Meta Reviewer is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Member PC.

A 'Workshop Paper' is a kind of academic Paper (a Document) in the conference domain, while a 'Video cassette player' is a piece of Audiovisual equipment (an Item). They share no meaning, no parent, and no properties; the only superficial link is the word 'paper'/'player' being absent, so they are clearly unrelated.

Both are direct subclasses of Person and represent people involved in a conference. cmt's Conference Member has children Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, Conference Chair, Associated Chair, and is linked to Conference via has Conference Member / member Of Conference. Conference's Conference participant has children Active/Passive conference participant and siblings Committee member, Reviewer, Conference contributor, etc. Both denote the general role of a person participating in a conference, so they are equivalent.

A Reception is a social event held during the conference (sibling of Excursion under Social Event), whereas B Departure is an activity after the conference (sibling of Full day tour). They denote different concepts: a social gathering vs. a post-conference departure activity.

A's 'has short title' is a datatype property mapping a Social/Working event to a string (an abbreviation of the event's title), while B's 'lists Event' is an object property mapping a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event it enumerates. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), in domain (event vs document), in range (string vs Event), and in meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Assigned Paper' is a specific stage in the paper lifecycle (a submitted paper assigned to a reviewer), a subclass of Submitted Paper. B's 'Document' is a broad top-level artefact class whose children include Review, Submission, Payment document, etc. The two do not denote the same concept: Assigned Paper is a narrow paper-role class, Document is a general document category. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in the intended domain sense.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering anyone contributing to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors), while B's 'Webmaster' is a specific organizing role under Organizator. The Webmaster is an organizer, not a generic contributor, and the two classes have different intents and disjoint role contexts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Track is a conference part (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, containing sessions/papers), while B's Workshop is a scientific event (sibling of Conference, Track, Session). Although both ontologies have a Workshop class, the candidate pairs A:Track with B:Workshop, which denote different concepts: a track is a thematic subdivision of a conference, a workshop is a separate event. They are not equivalent.

A's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (author submits paper), while B's publisher Of relates an Organisation to publications such as Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site (organisation publishes those artefacts). The domains (Author vs Organisation) and ranges (Paper vs Flyer/Volume/Brochure/Web Site) are disjoint, and the intended relations differ; they are not equivalent.

In confOf, Workshop is a specific kind of Working event, sibling to Conference and Tutorial. In ekaw, Session is a broader Scientific Event whose children include Workshop Session, Regular Session, Conference Session, etc. A Workshop is not a Session in ekaw's sense (a Workshop Session is), and a Session is not a Workshop. They overlap in that workshops are held as sessions, but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's property records the acceptance-announcement date within the Important dates class, while B's property records the submission deadline within the Call class. These are distinct conference milestones (acceptance notification vs. paper submission deadline) with different domains and ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property linking a Conference volume to a string (a textual location), while B's 'is equipped by' is an object property linking a Place to an Item (equipment). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Both are datatype properties with range string that assign a name to entities. Although the domain sets differ (cmt: Conference, Person; Conference: Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic), both denote the same generic naming relation in the conference domain, and a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while B's has an abstract relates a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract (a part-whole/content relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Author is a person role in the conference (a subclass of Person, with children like Presenter and properties linking to papers). B's 'Author attendee book registration fee' is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a monetary fee category for an author who also attends and books. The two denote different kinds of things (person vs. fee) and are unrelated.

Both properties relate a reviewer to a paper they review: cmt's 'read Paper' has domain Reviewer and range Paper, ekaw's 'reviewer Of Paper' has domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper. 'Possible Reviewer' in ekaw is the class of people who may review (i.e. reviewers), so the two relations denote the same reviewer-of-paper relation in the same direction.

A's Organization is a conference-domain class for an organizing body (institution/committee), while B's Activity before conference is a subclass of Activity covering pre-conference tasks such as accepting/receiving/refusing manuscripts, renting and research. They share no intended instances and have different parents, children and domain roles, so they are unrelated.

Both are classes named Review, both sit directly under Document, both represent the review of a paper written by a reviewer (cmt: write Review Reviewer->Review, written By Review->Reviewer; ekaw: review Written By Review->Possible Reviewer, review Of Paper Review->Paper). The children differ (Meta Review vs. sentiment subclasses) but that is a modelling detail; the intended instances (reviews of papers) coincide.

In confOf, University is a direct subclass of Organization alongside Company, i.e. a specific kind of organization. In ekaw, Academic Institution is a subclass of Organisation that has University as a child, so University is strictly more specific than Academic Institution. The two are not equivalent; University is subsumed by Academic Institution.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing practical information to attendees. B's 'Simulating' is a research activity (sibling of Modelling) performed before a conference. They share no meaning, instances, or context; the only superficial link is the word 'participants' vs. an activity, which is not a synonymy.

A's 'reviews' relates a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution). B's 'is Review History Of' relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Workshop Session is a session within a scientific event (sibling of Conference Session, Regular Session, etc.). They denote different concepts: a conference vs. a workshop session, so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a conference part (sibling of Track, Tutorial, etc.), while B's Tutorial is a working event (sibling of Conference, Workshop). The labels differ and the paths show different roles: Workshop in A is a sub-event/part of a conference, whereas Tutorial in B is a standalone working event. They are not the same concept.

A's 'submit Paper' relates an Author to a Paper (submission of a paper), while B's 'speak in' relates a Person to a Place/Time (giving a talk at a venue/time). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

Assistant in confOf is a Person subtype (a helper/assistant role, sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.), while Reviewer in iasted is a Speaker subtype (a delegate who reviews papers). The intended instances differ: an assistant is not a reviewer, and the paths (Person > Assistant vs Delegate > Speaker > Reviewer) show different roles in the conference domain.

A Meta Review is a review of reviews (a document aggregating reviews), while a Neutral Review in ekaw is a review with neutral sentiment, sibling of Positive/Negative Review. Different concepts despite both being subclasses of Review.

A's Tutorial is a working event (a session/activity held at a conference, sibling of Conference and Workshop), whereas B's Invited Talk Abstract is a document (an abstract text, sibling of Tutorial Abstract under Abstract). One is an event, the other a document; they denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A is a kind of paper (a document submitted to a conference), while B is a city where a conference takes place. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (Document vs. City) and share no intended instances.

Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection under Decision) in cmt, while University is an organization type (sibling of Company under Organization) in confOf. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A is a research topic area (a subject category for papers, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a kind of conference presentation event (a Contributed Talk, sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic taxonomy vs. event taxonomy) and cannot denote the same concept.

A 'Government Organization' is a subtype of Organization (a kind of entity/organisation, sibling of Academia Organization, Industry Organization, NGO). B 'Sponsor state' is a subtype of State, alongside Conference state and Presenter state — it denotes a state/status of a sponsor (a role/status in the conference process), not a type of organisation. Different parent hierarchies (Organization vs State) and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A's Call is a conference call-for-papers/reviews entity that initiates submissions and has deadlines; B's Time is a temporal entity (parent of Deadline, Conference days, Trip day) used for temporal ordering of activities, persons and items. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people/roles), while B's has_parts relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts (e.g. proceedings parts). Different domains and ranges, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (object property), while B's Name_of_conference relates a Conference to a string (datatype property). Different range kinds and different intended meaning (location vs. name), so they are not equivalent.

A Meta Review is a review of reviews (a subclass of Review), while B Abstract is a summary of a paper (a subclass of Document). They denote different concepts with different parents and roles in the conference domain.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference, e.g. a student author/participant), while B's Registration Non Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a fee category for non-members). They belong to different branches (person vs. fee) and denote different concepts; note B's sibling Registration Student is the fee counterpart, not A's Student.

assignReviewer (cmt) is an action property from Administrator to Reviewer, expressing that an administrator assigns a reviewer. reviewerOfPaper (ekaw) is a static relation from Possible Reviewer to Paper, expressing which papers a potential reviewer reviews. They differ in domain, range, and direction of meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Main office is a physical place (sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room). An event and a location are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

ekaw:Person is a broad class covering all people in the conference domain (authors, participants, students, committee members, etc.), while sigkdd:Author is a narrower class for people who write/submit papers, located under Speaker. Every Author is a Person, but not every Person is an Author, so Person subsumes Author.

A's assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to a paper), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presenting a document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity), while B's Plenary lecture speaker is a person role (a speaker/author). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Rejected Paper' is a class of documents (a paper that was evaluated and rejected), while B's 'Refusing manuscript' is an activity in the conference process (the act of refusing a manuscript), not a document class. They are conceptually linked (the activity produces the rejected paper) but denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's Modelling is a research activity (sibling of Simulating, under Research/Activity before conference), while B's Organizing Committee member is a person role under Organizator. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'is given by' relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it (agent direction), while B's 'paper Presented As' relates a Paper/Abstract to the Individual Presentation in which it is presented (paper-to-event direction). The domains and ranges are disjoint kinds of entities and the relations point in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference Event is an event in the conference domain (has attendees, programme, start/end date, location), while B's State is a geographical/administrative region (occupied by persons, situated in other places, visited by persons). Their children, properties and domains/ranges do not overlap; the shared word 'state' is not a synonym for 'event'.

A Programme in edas is a conference programme document that belongs to a Conference Event and is the range of has Programme; B Web Site in ekaw is a document that lists events and is published by an organisation. Although both are Documents, their intended instances differ: a programme schedule vs. a website. They are not synonyms and neither subsumes the other.

A's `abstract` is a datatype property linking a Contribution (paper) to its abstract text, while B's `Nation` links a Person to their nationality. Different domains, different ranges, different intended meaning; they are unrelated.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a specific role (first author of a contribution), a subclass of 'Regular author', whereas B's 'Author' is the general class of persons who write contributions. Every first author is an author, but not every author is a first author, so the A class is strictly narrower and subsumed by B's Author.

A is a Conference, a kind of working event (an event/activity with siblings Tutorial and Workshop). B is a Registration form, a kind of Form/Document (an artefact with siblings Author information form and Hotel registration form). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a document/form, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial or workshop), while edas's Organizational Meeting is an academic event (alongside paper presentations, talks, workshops). Both denote conference-like gatherings, but they sit in different taxonomies: confOf's Conference is a specific working-event type, whereas edas's Organizational Meeting is a broader academic-event category that includes presentations and talks. They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same concept, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

Person in cmt is a human agent (parent of Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, PC Member, User) with email and name properties. Contact Information in edas is an address/contact data record (city, email, phone, postal code, street) — a value object, not a person. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

confOf's 'Member PC' has the comment 'Reviewer' and reviews contributions (reviewes), while edas's 'Reviewer' reviews papers; both are Person subclasses denoting the program-committee reviewer role, so their instances coincide.

A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee (organisational structure), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity/Item (a person giving something). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not the same relation.

Conference in confOf is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas Hotel in sigkdd is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference hall and Main office). They denote different concepts: an event versus a venue/location, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract. B's 'volume Contains Paper' links a proceedings volume to a paper it contains. Different domain (paper vs volume), different range (abstract vs paper), and different direction of containment; they are not the same relation.

A 'Regular contribution' is a kind of conference contribution (a written/regular paper submission), while B 'Submission' is a document submitted to the conference, with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript. Both concern submitted papers, but A is a contribution type in a contribution taxonomy (siblings: Invited talk, Poster, Presentation) whereas B is a document in a document taxonomy (siblings: Review, Payment document, Form). They overlap in the submission process but are not the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.
