A's hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome), while B's hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic (subject area). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the act/occasion of submitting contributions), while B 'Transparency' is a kind of Document (an item, sibling of Submission, Review, Form, etc.). Different kinds (event vs document) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

cmt's Paper is the general document class for submissions (it has children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version and is reviewed, assigned, accepted), while ekaw's Regular Paper is a specific paper type sibling to Poster Paper, Demo Paper, Workshop Paper, etc. The cmt Paper is broader and would include ekaw's Regular Paper, so cmt Paper subsumes ekaw Regular Paper rather than being equivalent.

A is a conference-document class (a document giving information to participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a subject/topic class under Topic (a microelectronics research area). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer assigned to review a paper), while B's search relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (conference searching for sponsors). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'Member PC' is a Person who reviews contributions (comment 'Reviewer', property reviewes), i.e. a program-committee member/reviewer. B's 'Program Chair' is an Organizator who chairs the program committee, a distinct role (sibling of General Chair and Program Committee member). Different roles, so not equivalent.

A's Meal Menu is a document describing a meal event (has Menu / is Menu Of link it to Meal Event), while B's Review is a document containing a reviewer's evaluation of a submission. They share only the generic Document parent; their intended instances and roles in the conference domain are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

A 'Regular contribution' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a paper-like submission, with children Extended abstract and Paper), whereas B 'Conference Session' is a kind of event/session (with child Industrial Session). They belong to different branches (document vs event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Organizing committee is a committee (a group of people) that organizes a conference, sibling to Program committee and Steering committee. B's Industry Organization is a type of organization (an institution's sector), sibling to Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO. Different kinds of entities: committee vs. organization type. No equivalence.

A's Review is the general class of reviews of contributions (domain/range: reviews a Reviewed contribution, and is the range of 'has a review'). B's Negative Review is a specific subclass of Review in ekaw, sitting alongside Neutral Review and Positive Review. Thus A's Review is strictly more general than B's Negative Review, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper a reviewer is assigned to review). B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the speaker who presents the document). The domains and ranges differ (Reviewer->Paper vs Document->Speaker), and the intended relations are different: assignment for reviewing versus presentation by a speaker. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A is a conference topic area (Computer Networks Topic) under Topic, a subject category for papers; B is a physical item (Card) under Item, a payment/identification artefact. Different domains and no shared instances.

A's Research Topic is a subject area covered by events/papers in the conference domain; B's Currency is a monetary unit in the iasted ontology. Different domains and no shared instances, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a submitted contribution to a review expertise (the topic/skill area a paper is about), while B's property links a personal review history to a reviewer (the person who owns that history). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subclass covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors, while edas Attendee is a Person subclass for people attending the conference. They overlap (attendees are contributors) but neither subsumes the other: contributors need not attend, and attendees need not contribute.

User in cmt is a person role (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while Registration SIGMOD Member in sigkdd is a registration-fee category (parent Registration fee, siblings Registration Non Member/Student). Different kinds of entities: person vs. fee type.

A 'Committee member' is a person role in the conference organisation (a Person who belongs to a Committee, with children Chair/Co chair and properties has members/was a member of). B 'Taxi' is a transport vehicle (Item > Transport vehicle > Taxi) with siblings Car, Shuttle bus, Van. The two denote entirely different concepts in different branches of the domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name; B's 'has Keyword' is a datatype property of Contribution giving a keyword string. Different domains (Person vs Contribution) and different intended meanings (first name vs keyword), so they are unrelated.

A's 'part Of Event' is a mereological relation between two Events (domain Event, range Event), expressing that one event is part of another. B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (domain Person, range Activity/Item), expressing that a person gives/presents something. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while B's 'submit until' links a Document to a Deadline (temporal submission constraint). Different domain, range, and meaning; not the same relation.

Both are object properties linking a topic to a paper (and event/conference), with the same direction (topic -> paper). The labels 'is Topic Of' and 'topic Covered By' express the same relation in the conference domain, so they are equivalent.

Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection under Decision) in the review process, while Sponzorship is a money/funding concept (sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip under Money). They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's User is a general person role in the cmt ontology, parent of Administrator, Author and Reviewer, i.e. any system user. B's SC Member is a specific steering-committee role under PC Member, a narrow sub-role of Possible Reviewer. The two classes denote different concepts: a User need not be a PC/SC member, and an SC Member is a specific committee role, not a generic user. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in the intended domain.

Workshop is a working event (a type of event/activity) in confOf, while Conference hall is a type of Place (a physical location) in sigkdd. They denote different concepts: an event versus a venue/location, so they are unrelated.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted; B's 'early Registration' is a boolean flag on Participant indicating early registration. Different domains (Conference vs Participant) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference announcement document soliciting submissions, while B 'Mailing list' is a document used to manage a list of recipients. They share only the broad Document parent and have no overlapping intended instances; the siblings and paths (Conference document vs Item > Document) confirm different concepts.

Both denote a document submitted to/part of a conference: A's 'Conference contribution' is a Conference document with children like Poster, Presentation, Regular contribution, and is submitted at a Conference volume; B's 'Conference Paper' is a Paper (Document) with siblings like Submitted Paper, Regular Paper, Poster Paper. The intended instances (papers/contributions to a conference) coincide, so they are equivalent despite differing labels.

A's Government Organization is a subtype of Organization (a type of institution/affiliation), while B's Organizing Committee is a subtype of Committee (a group of people organizing the conference). They denote different concepts with no overlap.
Currency (a monetary unit) and Person (a human participant with name, email, nation, roles like Listener/Organizator/Speaker) denote entirely different concepts; no overlap in the conference domain.

assignReviewer (Administrator -> Reviewer) is the act of assigning a reviewer to a paper, while reviewes (Member PC -> Contribution) is the act of a PC member reviewing a contribution. Both concern the reviewing relation between a person and a paper, but the domains differ (Administrator vs Member PC) and the directions/intents differ (assignment vs performing the review), so they are related but not equivalent.

In confOf, Trip is a subclass of Social event (an organized excursion/activity during the conference). In iasted, Trip city is a subclass of City (a city associated with a trip, alongside Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city). One denotes a social event, the other a type of city/location; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'Regular author' is a specific kind of conference contribution/contributor role (a regular (non-invited) authored contribution), while B's 'Author' is a person role (a delegate/speaker who authors things, with subclasses for proceedings inclusion and lecture speakers). The intended instances do not coincide: A denotes a contribution type, B denotes a person. However, a regular author is a kind of author, so A is more specific than B; hence subsumed_by rather than equivalent.

A 'Regular author' is a conference contribution role (a kind of contribution/author role), while B 'Tutorial speaker' is a specific speaker role under Author in a different hierarchy. They denote different concepts: one is a regular author of a contribution, the other is a speaker for a tutorial. No subsumption or overlap in the intended instances.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while B's Gold Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor (a sponsorship level). They denote entirely different concepts: a person role vs. a funding/sponsorship category. No overlap in intended instances.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author and PC Chair), while B's 'Conference Trip' is a social event (a kind of Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet). They belong to different branches (person vs event) and denote different concepts.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) announcing a conference, while B 'Video presentation' is a kind of Presentation activity (sibling of Power Point presentation). They denote different concepts in different branches (document vs. activity) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a Chairman/Conference Member role (general conference chair), while B's 'Chair PC' is the chair of the program committee (confTool role), sibling of Member PC. They are distinct chairing roles that overlap only in being chair positions, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'Conference www' is a document (a web page about a conference) under 'Conference document', with a URL property; B's 'Conference' is a working event (a type of event) under 'Working event'. They denote different kinds of things (document vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string title, while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in domain, range, and kind, so they denote different relations.

In edas, Attendee is a general Person role (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles) denoting anyone attending the conference. In iasted, Reviewer is a specific role under Speaker (Delegate > Speaker > Reviewer), i.e. a delegate who speaks and reviews. An attendee is not necessarily a reviewer, and a reviewer is a narrower, different role; the two classes do not denote the same concept.

A's write Review is an object property linking a Reviewer to a Review (domain Reviewer, range Review). B's has an expertise is a datatype property on the class Review expertise, relating a reviewer to a literal expertise value. They relate different kinds of things (Review object vs. literal expertise) and have different domains, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a submission type, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract), while B's 'Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic' is a subject-area topic in the EDAS taxonomy (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a scientific submission with an abstract, sibling of Extended abstract), while B's Flyer is a published document (sibling of Paper, Review, Programme Brochure) that an organisation publishes. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to the Administrator who started reviewer bidding; B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document they present. Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.
Paper Author (a Person who authors papers) and Platinum Supporter (a sponsorship level) are different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'authorOf' relates a Person to a Document (authorship of a paper), while B's 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item (acquiring something). Different domain/range semantics and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Sponsor state' is a state of a sponsor (a phase in the conference process, sibling of Conference state and Presenter state under State), while B's 'Program Committee' is a committee entity (sibling of Best Paper Awards Committee and Organizing Committee under Committee). They denote different concepts in different branches of the domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of contribution (a submission type, sibling of Paper and Poster), while B 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a kind of Award (an honour given for an application paper). They belong to different branches (Contribution vs Award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'was a track workshop chair of' links a Track workshop chair (a person role) to a Conference part, while B's 'organisedBy' links an Event to an Organisation or Person. Both express an organisational/chairing involvement, but the domains and ranges differ (Conference part vs Event; Track workshop chair vs Organisation/Person), so they are not equivalent; they overlap in the general sense of an organising relation.

Industrial Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a paper written for/with industry), while sigkdd's Paper is the general class of conference submissions. The ekaw class is strictly narrower than the sigkdd class, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A 'Meal Event' is a subclass of Non Academic Event (a social/meal gathering such as a conference dinner), while B 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person (a person who organises the conference). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (event vs. person) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's hasTopic relates a Conference/Paper to a Topic (subject matter of a paper), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity/Item (e.g. a person giving a talk or item). Different domains and ranges and different intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'was a committee of' relates a committee to a conference volume (a publication artefact), while B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference event. The domains and ranges differ (Committee vs ACM SIGKDD; Conference volume vs Conference), so the relations are not the same.

A's 'Rated Papers' is a subclass of Active Paper (a paper that has received ratings), while B's 'Review' is a sibling of Paper under Document, denoting the review document itself. A rated paper is the object being reviewed, not the review; the two denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role (a Person subclass, parent of Author/Reviewer/Chair) involved in a conference, while B 'Meal Event' is a non-academic conference event (parent of Conference Dinner) with menu properties. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Conference Event) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Student is a subclass of Participant (a kind of participant in a conference). In ekaw, Conference Participant is a broad class whose children include Student, so Student is strictly more specific than Conference Participant. Thus confOf Student is subsumed by ekaw Conference Participant, not equivalent.

A's Student is a subclass of Participant (a person role in the conference), while B's Best Student Paper Award is a subclass of Award (a prize). They denote different concepts: a person vs. an award, so they are unrelated.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper a reviewer has been assigned to review), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (the paper an author submits). Different domain (Reviewer vs Author) and different intended relation (review assignment vs submission), so they are not equivalent.
A's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'pay' relates a Person to Money (payment). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's State is a geographic/administrative region (a place that contains cities, is situated in other places, and is occupied/visited by persons), while B's Conference is an event with a name, start/end dates, a city, and held by an ACM SIGKDD group. They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A's `location` is a datatype property of Social event / Working event giving the place where an event is held (range string), while B's `City of conference` is a datatype property of Conference giving the city where the conference takes place. Both express a location of an event, but they have different domains (social/working events vs. the conference as a whole) and different granularity (generic location vs. city), so they are related rather than equivalent.
A's hasCountry relates Organization/Person to Country; B's hasReview relates Paper to Review. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Event is a general event class with children Academic Event and Non Academic Event, and it has attendees, a programme, a location and start/end times. B's Conference is a specific kind of event (held by an ACM SIGKDD, with a city, name and start/end dates) — it is a narrower concept than the general Conference Event. Thus Conference Event subsumes Conference, i.e. A is subsumed_by B's more specific class.
A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a paper), while B's is_paid_by relates Money to a Person (payment). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they share no concept.

A's Conference Chair is a chairing role (sibling of Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair) under Chairman/Conference Member, i.e. a person who chairs the conference. B's SC Member is a Steering Committee member, placed under PC Member (Possible Reviewer > PC Member > SC Member), a reviewing/committee membership role, not a chairing role. Different intended concepts, so not equivalent.

confOf's 'Chair PC' is the chair of the program committee (a PC role), while edas's 'Conference Chair' is the general chair of the conference who initiates calls and reviews. They are distinct conference roles that both sit under Person; they overlap in being senior organising roles but do not denote the same concept.

Meta Review is a subclass of Review (a document/review artefact in the conference reviewing process), while Company is a subclass of Organization (an organisational affiliation of a person). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Paper (a document submitted to a conference, with authors, reviews, decisions) and Organization (an institution such as a company or university that employs people) denote entirely different concepts; they share no instances and no meaningful overlap.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document they have a conflict of interest with, while authorOf relates a Person to a Document they authored. Although both have domain Person and range Document, they denote different relations in the conference domain; a conflict of interest is not authorship.

A's Paper is a document (a paper submitted to a conference, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Author is a person (a speaker who submits papers and receives notifications). They denote different concepts: one is the written contribution, the other the person writing it. No equivalence, subsumption or meaningful overlap.

A's hasCostCurrency is a datatype property of Sponsorship giving a currency string, while B's Price is a datatype property of Registration fee giving an integer amount. They belong to different domains (sponsorship cost vs registration fee) and have different ranges (string currency vs int price), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's title is a datatype property linking a Paper to a string (its name), while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item (acquiring something). Different domain, range, and meaning; no equivalence.

cmt's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person involved in the conference), while ekaw's organisedBy links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Both relate an event/conference to people involved in running it, so they overlap, but the ranges differ (Conference Member vs Organisation/Person) and the direction/intent is not identical; they are related rather than equivalent.

ekaw's organises relates an Organisation or Person to an Event (organising a conference/event), while iasted's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (giving a talk/presentation or item). Both involve a person and an event-like activity, so they overlap, but the domains differ (Organisation allowed in A, not B) and the ranges differ (Event vs Activity/Item), and the intended relations (organising vs giving) are not the same, so they are not equivalent.

cmt's memberOfConference links a Conference Member (a person on the organising committee) to a Conference, while edas's attendeeAt links a Person to a Conference Event. The domains differ (committee member vs. generic person) and the ranges differ (Conference vs. Conference Event), so they are not the same relation; they merely overlap in that both connect a person to a conference-related entity.

Country in edas is a geographical entity used as the range of Conference->Country, while Person in sigkdd is a human participant with children Listener/Organizator/Speaker and properties such as Name, E mail, Nation. They denote different concepts; the only link is that a person has a Nation string, not a Country class.

A 'Regular Paper' is a specific kind of paper (a document type), while B 'Document' is a broad class covering forms, invitations, reviews, submissions, etc. A Regular Paper is a Document, but not every Document is a Regular Paper, so A is strictly more specific than B (subsumed_by).

Both properties link a program committee/programme to the conference event/volume it serves: 'was a program committee of' has domain Program committee and range Conference volume, while 'belongs To Event' has domain Programme and range Conference Event. In the conference domain a program committee is the committee of a conference, and a programme belongs to a conference event; the two relations express the same committee-to-conference membership in the same direction, so they are equivalent.

A's hasCo-author relates a Paper to its Co-author (domain Paper, range Co author), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They connect different kinds of entities in opposite directions, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Hotel fee' is a specific fee for lodging, a sibling of 'Registration fee' under 'Fee'. B's 'Registration fee' is the general conference registration fee with member/student subclasses and payment properties. They are distinct fee types, not the same concept.

Both denote the person who chairs the programme committee of a conference: edas 'Conference Chair' is a Person who initiates calls and reviews papers, and ekaw 'PC Chair' is a Conference Participant and PC Member who chairs the PC. The roles coincide in the conference domain, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

Participant is a subclass of Person representing an attendee/role in confOf, while Registration fee is a subclass of Fee representing a monetary charge in sigkdd. Their paths, siblings, and properties (early Registration vs. Currency/Price/pay) show they denote different concepts: a person versus a fee.

cmt:Person is a broad class covering all people in the conference domain (chairs, committee members, reviewers, users), while iasted:Speaker is a specific subclass of Delegate restricted to people who present/speak. Speaker is therefore strictly more specific than Person, so Person subsumes Speaker (Speaker is subsumed by Person).

A's 'Short paper' is a specific kind of contribution (sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution), while B's 'Paper' is the general document class with subclasses Accepted/Pending/Rejected etc. A short paper is a paper, so Short paper is strictly narrower than Paper; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B's 'Departure' is an activity after the conference (sibling of Full day tour) in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different concepts (a person role vs. a post-conference activity), so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Member' is a Person (a person affiliated with a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair roles), while B 'Conference Session' is a Session (a Scientific Event, sibling of Workshop/Poster/Regular Session). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Author is a person who writes/submits papers (has Author, write Paper, submit Paper), while ekaw:Possible Reviewer is a person who may review papers (has Reviewer, reviewer Of Paper). They overlap in that both are persons involved in the conference paper process, but the intended instances differ: an author writes papers, a possible reviewer reviews them. Neither subsumes the other (an author need not be a reviewer and vice versa), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference/Tutorial/Workshop (things that happen at a conference), while B 'Conference building' is a subclass of Building/Place, a physical location. Their intended instances (events vs. buildings) do not coincide, and the paths, parents and children are entirely different.

A's max Papers is a datatype property from Program Committee Member to int, expressing a maximum number of papers a PC member can review/handle. B's submit is an object property from Author to Paper, expressing the act of submitting a paper. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (PC member vs Author), and range (int vs Paper), so they denote different relations.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract (domain Paper/Poster/Presentation, range Abstract). B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (domain Author, range Contribution). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not inverses either, so they are unrelated.

A's Presenter is a role a person plays at the conference (a subclass of Conference Participant, with Invited Speaker as a child), whereas B's 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a Document item (a subclass of Document, sibling of Review, Submission, Invitation letter). A person-role and a document are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

A 'Closing Talk' is a type of talk event (a session/event in the conference programme), while B 'Invited Speaker' is a type of person (a speaker role). They belong to disjoint branches (event vs. person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a narrow conference topic (a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic under Topic), while B is a scientific event type (a Workshop under Scientific Event). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject area vs. event kind) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Paper in cmt is a document (submitted contribution with authors, reviews, decisions), while Working event in confOf is an event category (Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) with topics, titles and locations. Different domains and no shared instances.

Both properties link a document-like entity to a person, but 'written By' expresses authorship of a Document, while 'is given to' expresses the recipient of an Item (e.g. an award or gift). They relate different kinds of things in different directions of meaning, so they are not equivalent; they only overlap in connecting an item to a person.

A's 'Personal Review History' is a class of historical records of reviews performed by a reviewer (a personal history entity, sibling of Personal Publication History, linked to Reviewer via is Review History Of). B's 'Review' is a document type (sibling of Abstract and Paper under Document) representing the review document itself. The two denote different concepts: a history/record of reviews versus the review document, so they are not equivalent.

Reviewer (edas) is a Person who reviews papers, with review-history and reviewing properties. Speaker (sigkdd) is a Person who gives presentations, with presentation properties and children Author/Invited Speaker. Different roles in the conference domain; no subsumption or overlap.

Organization in confOf is an institution (parent of Company and University, employer of Persons, with address properties), while Review Rating in edas is a category of review outcome (parent of Accept/Reject ratings, attached to Active Paper). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Organization is a general organization class with children Company and University, while B's NGO is a specific subtype of Organization (sibling of Academia/Government/Industry Organization). NGO is strictly narrower than Organization, so Organization subsumes NGO; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a kind of conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact. B's 'Conference' is a working event (sibling of Tutorial, Workshop), i.e. an event. Different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Organizational Meeting is a sibling of Workshop under Academic Event, so it denotes a distinct kind of academic event (e.g. a business/organisational meeting), not a workshop. In ekaw, Workshop is a Scientific Event alongside Conference, Session, etc. The two classes denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A 'Tutorial Chair' is a person role (a Conference Participant / PC Member who chairs tutorials), while B 'Author attendee cd registration fee' is a monetary registration-fee category for author attendees. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Money/Fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasTopic relates a Working event to a Topic (the subject matter of a conference event), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving a prize). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's `write` relates a Person (author) to an Item (paper) — the act of authoring. B's `presentationed by` relates a Document to a Speaker — the act of presenting. Different domains/ranges and different intended relations (authoring vs presenting), so they are not equivalent.

A's studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (where they study), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (what they submit). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'assigned To' relates a Paper to a Reviewer (conference domain), while B's 'is occupied by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (physical location domain). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Organizer (Conference) is a person/role who organizes an event, while Organisation (ekaw) is an organizational entity (academic institution, agency, publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings. They are related through the organising relation but denote different kinds of things (person/role vs. organization), so they are not equivalent.

Author Not Reviewer is a subclass of Author in cmt (an author who is not also a reviewer), while edas Author is the general author class. The cmt class is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by the edas Author class, not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties expressing a deadline date/time, but A is the registration deadline of a Conference (domain Conference, range dateTime), while B is the completion deadline of a Deadline entity (domain Deadline, range date). They concern different subjects (conference registration vs. a deadline's completion) and different ranges, so they are related deadline notions rather than the same relation.

A Workshop is an academic event (a gathering/activity) in edas, while Conference Proceedings is a published multi-author volume (a document) in ekaw. They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Document) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome). B's notification_until relates an Author to a Deadline Author notification (a deadline by which the author is notified). Different domains (Paper vs Author), different ranges (Decision vs Deadline), and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Closing Talk' is a talk event that closes a conference (sibling of Welcome Talk, a subtype of Talk Event). B 'Introduction of speaker' is a conference activity that introduces a speaker, a subtype of Introduction. They denote different concepts: one is a closing talk event, the other is a speaker-introduction activity. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (a person who speaks), with children covering various speaker roles; in sigkdd, Author of paper is a subclass of Author (a person who authors a paper). The iasted Author is a broader speaker/person concept, while sigkdd's Author of paper is specifically a paper author. The iasted Author is more general than the sigkdd Author of paper, so iasted Author is subsumed by sigkdd Author of paper only in the sense that a paper author is a kind of author; however, the iasted Author includes speakers who may not author papers, so it is not equivalent. The relation is subsumed_by (iasted Author is subsumed by sigkdd Author of paper) if we consider the paper-authoring aspect, but strictly the iasted Author is broader. Given the paths, iasted Author is a speaker role, sigkdd Author of paper is a paper author, so they are not equivalent; iasted Author is more general, so sigkdd Author of paper is subsumed by iasted Author. Thus relation should be subsumes (iasted Author subsumes sigkdd Author of paper). However, the question asks whether A and B are equivalent; they are not. The correct relation is subsumes (A subsumes B). I will set relation to subsumes.

A is a full version of a paper (a document type under Paper), while B is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. sponsors) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee (a group of people), while B's 'scientifically Organised By' links an event/conference to an Academic Institution. Different domain and range, and different intended meaning (committee vs. institution), so they are not equivalent; they are unrelated relations.

A's Conference is the central event class of the conference domain (it has a name, parts, proceedings, publisher, topic). B's Conference city is a subclass of City describing the city where a conference is held, sibling to Presenter city, Sponsor city and Trip city. The two denote different concepts (event vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Assistant is a helper role (comment 'confTool', sibling of Administrator/Volunteer), while edas's Attendee is a generic person attending the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles). The intended instances do not coincide: an assistant need not be an attendee and an attendee is not necessarily an assistant. They share only the Person parent, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer), i.e. an assignment relation. B's 'invited by' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer), i.e. an invitation relation between reviewers. Different domain, different intended meaning; not equivalent.

Tutorial Chair is a specific chair role (a Conference Participant/PC Member who chairs tutorials) in ekaw, while General Chair is the top organizer role in sigkdd under Organizator. They are different roles with different scopes and different parents; neither subsumes the other.

A's 'has a name' is a datatype property assigning a string name to entities such as Conference, Publisher, Topic, etc. B's 'end Date' is a datatype property assigning a dateTime end date specifically to a Conference. They relate different kinds of values (string vs dateTime) and have different intended meanings (naming vs temporal end), so they are not equivalent.
A is a conference document providing information to participants, while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a computer) under Audiovisual equipment. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

Both classes denote the conference chair role. In cmt, Conference Chair is a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member under Person, with siblings like Program Committee Chair and Associated Chair; in edas, Conference Chair is a direct subclass of Person with siblings like Session Chair and TPC Member. Both are the person who chairs the conference, and edas's properties (initiates, is Reviewed By, is Reviewing) are consistent with the chair role. Same label and same intended instances, so equivalent.

A's 'location Of' relates a Location to an Event (the event takes place at the location), while B's 'is held after' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domain/range kinds and different meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Accommodation Place is a kind of Place (lodging location for conference attendees), while B's Car is a kind of Transport vehicle (a vehicle item). They belong to different branches (Place vs Item/Transport vehicle) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `name` is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's `has an email` is specifically an email address property for Person. They denote different attributes (name vs. email address), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is paid with' relates Money to Item (a payment instrument), while B's 'pay' relates Person to Registration fee (an agent paying a fee). Different domains, ranges, and direction of meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author denoting a person who authors papers but is excluded from reviewing; B's 'Reviewer' is a person who reviews papers. The two concepts are complementary/opposite roles rather than the same concept, and neither subsumes the other (an author-not-reviewer is not a reviewer, and a reviewer need not be an author).

A's contactEmail is a datatype property from Contribution to string (an email address of a contribution), while B's send is an object property from Person to Item (a person sending an item). They differ in domain, range, and kind, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Accept Rating' is a review-rating value (a score category used in reviewing, sibling of Reject Rating and Accept If Room Rating), whereas B's 'Rejected Paper' is a document/paper class in the submission-evaluation hierarchy (sibling of Accepted Paper). One is a rating value, the other a paper outcome class; they denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class covering all people affiliated with a conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), while Track workshop chair in Conference is a specific chair role for a track/workshop/tutorial. The cmt class is strictly more general, so it subsumes the Conference class rather than being equivalent to it.

confOf's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper-like artefact), while iasted's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or presentation). Both involve a person producing/contributing something, but the ranges differ (Contribution vs Activity/Item) and the intended relations are not the same: writing a paper is not the same as giving a presentation. They overlap in the general sense of a person producing something, so related rather than equivalent.

A 'Workshop Session' is a specific kind of session (a session within a workshop), while B 'Session' is a general session concept in the iasted ontology. A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's max Papers is a datatype property of Program Committee Member limiting the number of papers a PC member can review/handle, while B's max Choice is a datatype property of Social event and Working event limiting the number of choices for those events. Different domains, different intended meaning, no subsumption.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, mapping a person to their first name. The confOf comment about middle name does not change the intended meaning; the labels and paths match, so they denote the same relation.

A's hasStreet is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a street address string; B's Name is a datatype property of Person giving a person's name. Different domains, different intended meanings, no subsumption or overlap.

A's Meeting Room Place is a place for holding meetings (a room/space), while B's Hotel is a lodging establishment. Although both are subclasses of Place, they denote different concepts: a meeting room is not a hotel. A's sibling Accommodation Place would be the closer counterpart to Hotel, so these two are unrelated.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a Person subclass (a person who applies, parent of 'Registeered applicant'), while B's 'Registration' is a Conference activity (an event with child 'Delegate'). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. activity), so they are not equivalent.

A's Slide Set is a presentation artefact (sibling of Paper, Review, Programme under Document), while B's Review is the evaluation document (sibling of Submission, Form, Payment document under Document). They denote different conference artefacts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'organised By' is an object property linking an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organiser), while B's 'City of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (the host city). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and denote different relations, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Trip is a social event (a subclass of Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet), i.e. an activity/outing. B's Trip day is a temporal concept (subclass of Time, sibling of Conference days and Deadline), i.e. a day on which a trip occurs. The two denote different kinds of things (event vs. time interval), so they are not equivalent.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) in confOf, while B Welcome address is a conference activity (sibling of Coctail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, etc.) in iasted. Although both are conference-related events, a reception is a social gathering, whereas a welcome address is a formal opening talk; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Departure is an activity that occurs after the conference (a temporal event, sibling of Full day tour), whereas Main office is a physical place (a location, sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They denote different kinds of entities in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A's 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a committee entity), while B's 'organisedBy' links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Both express the organisation of a conference/event, but the domain (Conference volume vs Event) and especially the range (Organizing committee vs Organisation/Person) differ, so they are not equivalent; they overlap in intent and are best recorded as related.

A's 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (a conference social gathering such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B's 'Form' is a subclass of Document (a paper form such as Registration form, Hotel registration form). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a document artefact. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

A is a research topic (a subject area for papers) under Topic, while B is an organizational committee (a group of people) under Committee. They denote entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chair of the whole conference, a sibling of Program Committee Chair and Associated Chair under Chairman. Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is a specific role chairing tutorials, a sibling of Workshop Chair and Demo Chair under Conference Participant. Different roles in the conference domain; not equivalent.

Both denote the act/event of presenting a paper at a conference: edas 'Paper Presentation' is an Academic Event linked to an Accepted Paper, and iasted 'Presentation' is a Conference activity with subtypes (Power Point presentation, Video presentation) that are ways of presenting. The intended instances (a presentation given at the conference) coincide, so they are equivalent despite differing parents.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while B's 'references' is a citation relation between documents/papers. Different kinds of things and different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Published Paper' is a document/paper in a publication state hierarchy (siblings Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), while B 'Renting' is an activity performed before a conference (sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript). Different kinds (class of documents vs. class of activities) and different meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while B's hasLocation links a Conference Event to a Place (spatial location). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both are conference-domain places for hosting events, but 'Conference restaurant' is a specific Building (a dining venue) while 'Conference hall' is a generic Place (a hall/venue). They overlap in being conference venues but neither subsumes the other cleanly; a reference alignment would likely not record them as equivalent.

A's property is a specific deadline relation: it links the Important dates container to the date of camera-ready paper submission. B's property is a general temporal relation linking any Activity to a dateTime. They differ in domain (Important dates vs Activity) and in specificity (camera-ready deadline vs any activity date), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author (a person who authors but does not review), while B's 'Author' is the general class of persons who write contributions. Every Author Not Reviewer is an Author, but not every Author is an Author Not Reviewer, so A is strictly more specific and is subsumed by B.

A's has Call links an Academic Event to its Call (a document/announcement), while B's part Of Event links an Event to a sub-event (mereological containment). Different domain/range semantics and direction of relation; not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document giving practical/organisational information to attendees, while B's 'Conference Proceedings' is a multi-author volume collecting the conference's papers. They are different document types with different roles and no subsumption relation.

A is a specific conference topic (Computer Networks Optical Topic) under the Topic hierarchy, while B is a sponsor-related state in the conference workflow (State > Sponsor state). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

Contact Information in edas is a class holding address/phone/email details of a person or organisation, with properties has City, has Email, has Phone, has Postal Code, has Street. Time in iasted is a temporal class with children Conference days, Deadline, Trip day and is used as the range of temporal relations such as is held before/after and is present. The two denote entirely different concepts (contact details vs. time points/intervals) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Review preference' is a class whose instances are preferences/degrees of a reviewer for a topic or submission (it has a degree, belongs to reviewers, and links topics/submissions to reviewers). B's 'Document' is a general document class whose children are Abstract, Paper and Review, and which is presented by a Speaker and has a submission deadline. A review preference is not a document, and Document is not a preference; the two concepts are disjoint in the conference domain.

A's `date` is a datatype property giving a Conference a literal date value. B's `belong to a conference volume` is an object property linking an Important dates entity to a Conference volume. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Important dates), and range (literal date vs Conference volume), so they denote different relations.

Conference document in the Conference ontology is a document artefact (call for papers, contribution, review, announcement) with authors and an issue date, whereas Activity in iasted is a general event/activity (before/after conference, conference activity) with participants, places, times and money. The intended instances do not coincide: documents are not activities, and the property sets (authors/date vs. place/time/money/participants) confirm different concepts.

A's hasStreet is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (a street address), while B's locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the event held at that location). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not the same relation.

Both properties link an Author to a Paper, but 'write Paper' denotes authorship (creating the paper) while 'submit' denotes the act of submitting a paper to a conference. They are closely related but not the same relation; a reference alignment would not equate them.

A's Registration is a conference activity (an event with Delegate participants, sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Coffee break), while B's Registration Student is a fee category (a subclass of Registration fee, sibling of Registration Non Member / SIGKDD Member). One denotes an activity, the other a fee type, so they are not the same concept.

A 'Camera ready contribution' is a document/contribution in the final accepted-and-prepared form (a subclass of Accepted contribution in the document hierarchy). B 'Submissions deadline' is a time point (a subclass of Deadline) by which submissions must be made. One is a document type, the other a temporal event; they share no instances and are not related by subsumption.

Reception is a specific kind of social event (a subclass of Social Event in edas), while ekaw's Social Event is the general category covering banquets, trips, etc. Thus Reception is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Social Event, not equivalent.

A's 'set Max Papers' is a property of a Program Committee Member (a person) setting a maximum number of papers, while B's 'submit_until' is a property of a Document giving a submission deadline. Different domain, range and intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has amount of' is a datatype property from Money to int, expressing a numeric quantity of money. B's 'Currency' is a datatype property from Registration fee to string, expressing the currency unit (e.g. USD/EUR) of a fee. They relate different kinds of things (amount vs. currency unit) in different domains, so they are not equivalent.

cmt's Associated Chair is a specific chair role (a Chairman who is also a Conference Member, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), while edas's Conference Chair is the general chair role that initiates calls and reviews. They overlap in the conference-organisation domain but denote different roles: Associated Chair is a narrower/auxiliary chair position, not the same concept as the top-level Conference Chair. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's Person is a human agent (children: Committee member, Reviewer, Conference participant; properties: has an email, has gender, has first/last name, contributes to a Conference document). B's Activity is an event/action (children: Activity before/after conference, Conference activity; properties: is dated on, is held in, is given by, is paid for). Person and Activity denote different kinds of things (agent vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

Program Committee in cmt is a group of people (members) that reviews papers, with properties linking it to Program Committee Members. Sponsorship in edas is a funding arrangement with cost amount/currency and a provider organization, with a child Travel Grant. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's `obtain` is an object property linking a Person to an Item (a thing obtained), while B's `Name` is a datatype property linking a Person to a string literal. They relate different kinds of entities (object vs literal) and have different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a conference entity to a topic: confOf's hasTopic relates a Working event to a Topic, while ekaw's coversTopic relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic. The ekaw property is broader in both domain (Event, Paper vs. Working event) and range (Research Topic vs. Topic), so hasTopic is strictly more specific and is subsumed by coversTopic rather than equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (an event/activity with siblings Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Conference Proceedings is a document (a multi-author volume under Proceedings). An event and a publication are different kinds of things, so the classes are not equivalent.

cmt's Administrator is a User (a Person subrole) with conference-organisation powers (accepting papers, assigning reviewers, entering conference details), while ekaw's Agency Staff Member is a generic Person subrole for staff of an agency, not specifically a conference organiser. They overlap in being non-author/non-reviewer persons involved in the conference, but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Conference Session' in edas is a scheduled academic event/session within a conference (it is related to Documents, Persons, Academic Events, Conferences). B 'Conference days' in iasted is a temporal unit under Time, with children Delegate and One conference day, and siblings Deadline and Trip day. One denotes an event/session, the other a time period (day) of the conference; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to a string URL (homepage), while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item (acquiring an item). Different range kinds (string vs Item) and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Simulating' is a research activity (sibling of Modelling under Research, an activity before the conference), while B's 'Organizing Committee member' is a person role (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, etc. under Organizator). They belong to entirely different branches (activity vs. person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' is an action property with domain Administrator and range Program Committee Member, used to add a member to a committee. B's 'has members' is a structural property with domain Committee and range Committee member, expressing committee membership. They differ in domain (Administrator vs Committee), range (Program Committee Member vs Committee member), and intended meaning (action vs membership relation), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Technic activity' is a kind of conference activity (an event such as a lecture or presentation) under Activity > Conference activity, while B 'Conference hall' is a physical place under Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office. An activity and a location are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's co-writePaper relates a Co author to a Paper (authorship/co-authorship relation). B's presentationed by relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'is Initiated By' relates a Call to the people who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), i.e. the initiators of a call. B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item, i.e. a person giving/producing something. The domains (Call vs Person) and ranges (people vs Activity/Item) are disjoint, and the directions differ, so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

Trip (confOf) is a social event (excursion) under Social event, while Departure (iasted) is an activity after the conference, sibling of Full day tour. Both are post-conference activities involving travel, so they overlap, but Trip is a social/excursion event and Departure is a departure/return activity; neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to its Committee (a structural part-of relation), while B's 'initiates' links a person role (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call (an action of starting/issuing a call). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Reviewer is a Person who reviews papers (has review expertise/preferences, invites co-reviewers). B's Author is a Speaker/Delegate who writes papers (parent Speaker, children include proceedings-inclusion and lecture speakers). Although B lists Reviewer as a sibling of Author, the two classes denote different roles: reviewing vs authoring. They are not equivalent.

A's 'Regular author' is a kind of conference contribution (a paper written by a regular author), sitting under Conference contribution alongside Poster, Presentation, Invited talk. B's 'Presenter' is a kind of person (Conference Participant) who presents at the conference, with child Invited Speaker. One denotes a document/contribution, the other a person role, so they are not equivalent.

A's property is a very specific relation from a Conference to the Administrator who prints hardcopy mailing manifests, while B's relatesTo is a general Document-to-entity relation (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person). Different domains (Conference vs Document), different ranges (Administrator vs multiple entities), and different intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Numerical Review Question' is a specific type of review question (a question with a numeric answer scale) within a review form, whereas B 'Review' is the document/artefact produced by a reviewer about a paper. They denote different concepts: one is a question item, the other is the review document itself. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote a person who writes/submits papers in the conference domain. cmt's Author is a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers; sigkdd's Author is a Speaker who submits papers and obtains awards. Despite differing parent paths (Conference Member vs Speaker), the intended instances coincide: authors of conference papers. Both have paper-related properties (write Paper / submit Paper vs submit Paper), confirming the same concept.

A's Published Paper is a paper that has been published (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/etc. under Paper), while B's Rejected Paper is a paper that was evaluated and rejected. They denote different statuses of a paper and neither subsumes the other; a published paper is not a rejected paper.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a person role in the conference committee hierarchy (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while B's 'Academia Organization' is a type of Organization (a university or academic institution). They denote different kinds of entities (person role vs. organization) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties linking a committee to one of its members, but A's range is any Program Committee Member while B's range is specifically a Co chair (a narrower role). They overlap in the committee-membership sense but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Reject Rating' is a specific rating value/score used in the review process (sibling of Accept Rating, Week Reject Rating), i.e. a category of review outcome. B 'Review' is a document type (a subclass of Document, sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter) representing the review document itself. A rating is not a document, and the intended instances do not coincide; they are unrelated concepts.

A 'Poster Session' is a type of scientific event/session (a scheduled gathering where posters are presented), while B 'Session room' is a physical place (a room where sessions are held). They belong to different top-level categories (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving its name (Paper > title > string), while B's done till is a datatype property of Deadline giving a date by which the deadline is completed. Different domains (Paper vs Deadline), different ranges (string vs date), and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's User is a Person subtype (a human role in the conference, with children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Session room is a Place subtype (a physical room). Different domains and no overlap.

Both properties link an event/activity to the place where it occurs: edas hasLocation has domain Conference Event and range Place, while iasted is_held_in has domain Activity and range Place, Time. The core meaning (event held at a location) is the same; the extra Time range in iasted is a broader range but the intended relation is the same, so they are equivalent in the conference domain.

Pending Paper (edas) is a paper in a not-yet-decided submission state, sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper. Poster Paper (ekaw) is a paper type/format, sibling to Regular, Demo, Industrial, Workshop Paper. They denote different concepts: submission status vs. paper category, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Accept Rating' is a specific review-rating value (a subclass of Review Rating, sibling of Reject Rating), i.e. a verdict/score category. B's 'Review' is a document type (subclass of Document, sibling of Paper/Abstract), i.e. the review document itself. Different kinds of things: a rating value vs. a review document, so they are not equivalent.

A's reviewWrittenBy relates a Review to its Possible Reviewer (domain Review, range Possible Reviewer), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'organised By' relates an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it (domain Event, range Organisation/Person). B's 'is designed for' relates an Activity/Money/Time to an Activity/Person it is intended for (domain Activity/Money/Time, range Activity/Person). The domains and ranges do not coincide, and the intended meanings differ: organising an event is not the same as being designed for something. No subsumption or overlap of the same relation, so unrelated.

A's 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person (a person affiliated with a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair roles), while B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Scientific Event (one edition of a conference). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a paper), while B's payed_by relates a Registration fee to a Person (who pays the fee). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a literal date (the camera-ready submission deadline), while B is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper). They differ in kind, domain, range and meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Dining Place' is a place for eating (siblings: Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Meeting Room Place), whereas B 'Hotel room' is a lodging room with children Double/Single hotel room and siblings Building, Conference hall, Session room. They denote different concepts in the conference domain; a dining place is not a hotel room.

A's 'has gender' is a datatype property of Person whose value is a gender; B's 'Name' is a datatype property of Person whose value is a string name. They relate different attributes of a person, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference, Tutorial and Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, choices, VAT), while B's 'CAD Topic' is a subject-area topic (Computer-Aided Design) under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc. They denote entirely different concepts (event vs. topic) and share no instances.

A 'Conference Venue Place' is a generic venue location (sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) under Place, while B 'Conference airport' is a specific building type (sibling of Conference hotel, Conference restaurant, etc.) under Building. The airport is a transport facility, not a conference venue place; the intended instances do not coincide.

Both denote a member of the programme committee: Conference's 'Committee member' is a Person who was a member of a Committee (has members / was a member of), with children Chair and Co chair; ekaw's 'PC Member' is a Possible Reviewer who is a Person, with children PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair. The intended instances (people serving on the programme committee) coincide, and the sub-role structure (chairs as subclasses) matches, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'Steering committee' is a committee (a group of people governing the conference series), while B's 'Possible Reviewer' is a person role (someone who may review papers, superclass of PC Member). Their paths, parents, siblings and properties (conference-volume governance vs. paper/review relations) do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'relates To' is a Document->(Event/Person) property, while B's 'give' is a Person->(Activity/Item) property. They have different domains and ranges and opposite directions of association, so they do not denote the same relation.

A's Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes or submits papers), while B's Programme is a Document (a conference schedule/programme artefact, sibling of Paper and Review). They denote different kinds of things and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Tutorial Abstract' is a kind of document (an abstract for a tutorial), a subclass of Abstract under Document. B's 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a kind of Deadline (a submission deadline for abstracts), a subclass of Deadline. They denote different concepts (a document type vs. a temporal deadline), so they are unrelated.

Scientific Event in ekaw is a broad class of scholarly gatherings (conferences, workshops, sessions, tracks) under Event, while Presentation in iasted is a specific conference activity (a talk, with PowerPoint/video subtypes) under Conference activity. A presentation is not a scientific event; the classes denote different kinds of things and neither subsumes the other.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific chair role (a type of Chairman/Conference Member), while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a broader organizing role under Organizator. They overlap in that both are conference organizers, but neither subsumes the other: Associated Chair is a chair-specific role, whereas Organizing Committee member includes non-chair roles (e.g., Webmaster). Thus they are related but not equivalent.

In cmt, Chairman is a general role with children Associated Chair, Conference Chair, and Program Committee Chair, so it subsumes the more specific Program Chair role in sigkdd. The sigkdd Program Chair is a specific chair position (sibling of General Chair), while cmt's Chairman is the broader chair role, so they are not equivalent but Chairman is more general.

A's 'inverse of part Of 7' is the inverse of a part-of relation with range Event, i.e. it relates an Event to its parts (whole-to-part), while B's 'give' has domain Person and range Activity/Item, relating a person to what they give. Different domain/range and direction; not equivalent.

A's Scholar is a person role (a price category for a person, sibling of Author, Participant, etc., with property study At -> University), while B's Memeber registration fee is a monetary fee category (subclass of Registration fee under Money, sibling of Student/Nonmember registration fees). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. fee) and are not equivalent.

Paper Full Version is a specific kind of Paper (a full-length paper, sibling of Paper Abstract), while edas Paper is the general paper class with children Accepted/Rejected/Published etc. The cmt class is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by the edas Paper class rather than equivalent.

A's Talk Event is a broad category of talks (children include Welcome Talk and Closing Talk, siblings include Paper Presentation and Workshop), while B's Contributed Talk is a specific kind of individual presentation (siblings Invited Talk, Tutorial). A Talk Event is more general than a Contributed Talk, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A's Paper is the submitted contribution (has Author, has Decision, assigned To Reviewer, accepted By Administrator), while B's Review is the evaluation document (review Of Paper, review Written By Possible Reviewer, subclasses Negative/Neutral/Positive Review). They are distinct concepts in the conference domain, not synonyms.

A's Meeting Room Place is a room where conference meetings/sessions take place, a sibling of Conference Venue Place and Accommodation Place. B's Main office is the organisation's administrative office, a sibling of Conference hall and Hotel. They denote different kinds of place (meeting room vs. office), so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paper (the full version of a submitted paper, sibling of Paper Abstract), i.e. a document type. B is a subclass of Deadline (the camera-ready manuscript submission deadline), i.e. a point in time. They belong to disjoint branches (Document vs Time) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

Company (a for-profit organization) and NGO (non-governmental, typically non-profit organization) are distinct organization types; they are siblings under Organization in their respective ontologies but denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Pending Paper in edas is a paper in a submission/review state (siblings Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, Published, Active), whereas Workshop Paper in ekaw is a paper type by venue/format (siblings Conference Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Regular Paper, Submitted Paper). The two classifications are orthogonal: a workshop paper can be pending, accepted, etc. Different intended instances, so not equivalent.

A Track is a conference part (a thematic stream of papers, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, with 'has tracks' from Conference volume). B Departure tax is a kind of Tax under Money in the iasted ontology. The two concepts come from entirely different domains and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a document class (a review of a paper, with children Positive/Negative/Neutral Review and properties review Of Paper, review Written By), while B's Departure tax is a subclass of Tax under Money, a financial charge. The two concepts belong to entirely different domains and share no instances.

A's Person is a broad class covering all people in the conference domain (committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers, chairs), while B's Author is a narrower subclass of Person (path Person > Author) restricted to those who write contributions. Thus Person is strictly more general than Author, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A's 'assigned By Administrator' relates a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned them (domain Reviewer, range Administrator). B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item they author (domain Person, range Item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not the same relation.

A's Review is a document produced by a reviewer about a paper (sibling of Paper, written by Reviewer, parent of Meta Review), whereas B's Publication is a generic published item (parent of Book proceeding and Cd proceeding, sibling of Document and Card). The intended instances do not coincide: a review is not a publication, and a publication is not a review.

A's memberOfConference goes from ConferenceMember to Conference (a member points to its conference), while B's hasMember goes from Conference to Person (a conference points to its members). They are inverse relations, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not the same relation.

A's 'Personal Review History' is a record/history of reviews performed by a reviewer (a data artefact about a person's reviewing activity, sibling of Personal Publication History). B's 'Possible Reviewer' is a role/type of person (a subclass of Person, superclass of PC Member) who can be assigned to review papers. One denotes a history record, the other a person role; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Presenter is a role of a conference participant (a person, parent of Invited Speaker). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and are not related in the conference domain.

A's hasCo-author relates a Paper to a Co author (a person who co-authored the paper), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper written). They are not the same relation: one goes Paper->Person, the other Person->Paper, and the entities differ (Co author vs Author, Paper vs Contribution). Even as inverses they would not be equivalent, and the domain/range mismatch makes them unrelated.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while B's 'Member PC' is a program-committee member/reviewer (comment 'Reviewer') who reviews Contributions and is expert on Topics. Different roles: co-authoring vs reviewing; no equivalence or subsumption holds.

edas:initiates relates a chair/TPC member to a Call (a person initiating a call for papers), while ekaw:organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organiser of an event). The domains and ranges are disjoint (person->call vs event->agent), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a session within a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session, child of Session under Event). B 'Conference days' is a temporal concept (a Time interval, parent of Delegate and One conference day, sibling of Deadline and Trip day). One denotes an event, the other a time period, so they are not equivalent.

A's Review is a document/artefact class (a review of a contribution, with properties has a review / reviews linking it to Reviewed contribution), while B's Reviewer is a person role (a subclass of Person, sibling of Author, Attendee, TPC Member, with properties about review history and reviewing papers). A review is not a reviewer; the entities denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a document type (a full paper submission) under Document > Paper, while B 'Exhibitor' is a sponsor category under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (submissions vs. sponsors) and share no intended instances.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment of a paper to a reviewer), while B's is_paid_by relates Money to a Person (payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A is a kind of document (an abstract for an invited talk), while B is a category of registration fee (nonmember fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. money/fees) and share no intended instances.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author (authorship relation), while B's pay relates a Person to Money (payment relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they share no concept in the conference domain.

An Invited speaker is a distinguished conference contributor who gives a talk by invitation, whereas a Reviewer is a delegate/speaker who evaluates submissions. They are different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

Both are datatype properties giving the end time/date of an event: confOf's 'ends on' has domain Event and range string, edas's 'has End Date Time' has domain Conference Event and range dateTime. Conference Event is the edas counterpart of confOf's Event, and both properties express the same relation (event -> its end date/time), so they are equivalent despite the differing range datatypes.
