A's 'review Criteria Entered By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who entered review criteria), while B's 'has Review' relates a Paper to a Review. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of academic/scientific event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial) in confOf, while B Coffee Break is a non-academic break event (sibling of Free Time Break and Meal Break) in edas. They denote different concepts: one is a scholarly event, the other a catering/social break. No subsumption or overlap.

A's 'Regular contribution' is a broad category of conference contributions (its children include Extended abstract and Paper, and it is a sibling of Poster, Presentation, Invited talk), whereas B's 'Short paper' is a specific contribution type alongside Paper and Poster. They overlap in that a short paper is a kind of regular contribution, but neither subsumes the other cleanly: A is broader than B, yet B is not a subclass of A in the given hierarchy (B's parent is Contribution). Thus they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Submitted contribution' is a document/contribution artefact (a paper that has been submitted), sitting under Conference document > Conference contribution > Written contribution, with children like Reviewed contribution and properties about review expertise, topics and review references. B 'Possible Reviewer' is a person role (a Person who may review), with children PC Member and properties like reviewer Of Paper. The two denote different kinds of things (artefact vs. person role), so they are not equivalent.

Program Committee Member (cmt) is a specific role within a conference, while Conference contributor (Conference) is a broader category that includes invited speakers, regular authors, and committee members. They are related but not equivalent; the cmt class is subsumed by the broader Conference contributor concept.

A's Conference is the central event class of the cmt ontology (with submissions, dates, administrators, members), while B's Conference hotel is a physical building/venue (a Place > Building) where a conference is held. They denote different concepts: an event vs. a lodging building, so they are not equivalent.

A's Program Committee is a specific committee composed of members who review papers; B's Organizing committee is a distinct committee (sibling of Program committee and Steering committee) responsible for organizing the conference. They are different committees within the same domain, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the outcome of reviewing a paper), while B's is_present relates a Person to a Time (attendance at an event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's website URI, while B's 'has Home Page' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's homepage string. Different domains (Conference vs Person) and different intended concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Presentation in the Conference ontology is a specific kind of conference contribution (a talk given by an active participant, with an abstract, sibling of Poster and Invited talk). Item in iasted is a very broad class covering physical/abstract things such as Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle, and is used as the object of properties like 'is made from', 'is paid with', 'is equipped by'. A presentation is not an item in this broad sense, and the two classes have no shared instances or intended meaning; they are unrelated.

A's 'registration Due On' is the deadline for conference registration (a submission/registration deadline), while B's 'End of conference' is the date the conference finishes. Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, but they denote different deadlines/events in the conference timeline, so they are not equivalent.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a registered conference applicant who has paid early), while B is a subclass of Committee (the program committee of the conference). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person/registration vs. committee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer assigned to review a paper). B's awarded_by relates an Award to something (the entity granting the award). Different domains (Reviewer vs Award), different ranges (Paper vs unspecified), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Co chair' is a Committee member (sibling of Chair) that co-chairs a committee, with properties linking it to Committee. B's 'Chair PC' is a direct child of Person (sibling of Member PC, Author, etc.) and denotes the chair of the program committee. Both are conference chair roles, but they are distinct roles (committee co-chair vs. PC chair) in different hierarchies, so they overlap rather than coincide.

A's 'has Attendee' relates a Conference Event to a Person (attendees of an event), while B's 'holded by' relates a Conference to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (the body that holds the conference). Different domain, different range, and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Trip day' is a day of the trip/conference (a time period within the event), while B 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a specific submission deadline. Although both are time-related, they denote different concepts: a trip day is a duration/period, a deadline is a point in time for a submission. They are not equivalent.

A Welcome Talk is a ceremonial opening talk at a conference, while an Invited Talk is a presentation by an invited speaker; both are talk events but they denote different roles, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's writtenBy relates a Review to its Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), while B's send relates a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes a paper/contribution). B's `is Reviewed By` relates a Paper to a reviewer-type agent (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) — the direction and the kinds of things related are different (author→contribution vs paper→reviewer). They are not the same relation, nor inverses of one another.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman of the conference, under Person > Chairman), while B 'Session' is a scientific event (a subdivision of a conference, under Event > Scientific Event). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a Program Committee Chair (a chairing role over the PC, sibling of Conference Chair and Associated Chair, parent Chairman/PC Member), while B is a Tutorial Chair (a chairing role for the tutorial track, sibling of Workshop Chair, Demo Chair, etc.). They are distinct chairing roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

submit Paper goes Author -> Paper, while written By goes Contribution -> Author. They are inverse-like in direction and connect different entity types (Paper vs Contribution), so they are not the same relation.

iasted Activity is a broad event/action class (children: Activity before/after conference, Conference activity; properties about being given, held in a place, dated, paid for), whereas sigkdd Document is a written artefact class (children: Abstract, Paper, Review; properties about presentation and submission deadline). Their intended instances do not coincide: a conference activity is not a document, and a paper/review is not an activity. The shared word 'presentation' does not make them equivalent.

A's Trip is a social event (a journey/excursion), while B's Conference Banquet is the banquet dinner event. They are distinct sibling social events in the conference domain (ekaw even has a separate Conference Trip class), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people), while B's was_a_committee_of relates a Committee to a Conference volume. Different domains, ranges, and directions; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Program Committee Chair' is a Person (a role/individual who chairs the program committee), while B's 'Program committee' is a Committee (the organisational body itself). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. committee), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address), while B's writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person (authorship). They differ in domain, range, and meaning; they are not the same relation nor inverses.

A's Decision is the outcome of a review process (acceptance/rejection of a paper, range of has Decision from Paper), while B's Social event is a conference social gathering (banquet, reception, trip) under Event. Different domains and no shared instances.

A's 'Fee for extra trip' is a specific fee for an optional trip, sibling to Hotel fee and Registration fee under Fee. B's 'Registration fee' is the main conference registration fee with member/student subclasses and payment properties. They are distinct fee types, not synonyms.

A 'Working event' is a conference-domain event class (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop; sibling of Social/Administrative event), while B is a specific research topic under Computer Networks Topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference to an anyURI image/logo location, while B's 'has Name' links a Conference to its full name string. They relate different kinds of values (URI vs string) and denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

In edas, Reviewer is a Person who actually performs reviews (has Review History, is Reviewing Paper). In ekaw, Possible Reviewer is a broader role: it is the range of 'has Reviewer' and 'review Written By', and its child PC Member is a kind of possible reviewer. A Possible Reviewer may or may not actually review, so the edas Reviewer (an actual reviewer) is strictly narrower than the ekaw Possible Reviewer. Hence Reviewer is subsumed by Possible Reviewer, not equivalent.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B's 'Presenter house' is a building/place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport) in the iasted ontology. A person role and a physical building are different concepts; the shared word 'presenter/chair' does not make them equivalent.

Both are object properties from Person to a thing the person acquires/commits to (Item vs Registration fee), but 'sign' (signing up for an item) and 'pay' (paying a registration fee) denote different relations; they overlap in the registration context but are not the same relation.

A's hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property from Call to a string (textual instructions for submitting), while B's submit_until is an object property from Document to a Deadline (a temporal deadline). They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Conference applicant is a Person subclass (someone who applies to register for a conference), while Session is a Scientific Event subclass (a time slot of presentations). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Program Committee Member is a member of the program committee (a reviewer-like role, with properties like max Papers, member Of Program Committee), while B's Program Chair is an organizer role (sibling of General Chair, Organizing Committee member) that chairs the committee. They denote different roles, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'author Of' goes Person -> Document (a person authors a document), while B's 'is prepared by' goes Item -> Person (an item is prepared by a person). They are inverse in direction and relate different kinds of entities (Document vs Item), so they are not equivalent.

Chairman (cmt) is a Person who chairs a committee, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair. Conference contributor (Conference) is a broader Person role covering Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author. A chairman is a conference contributor in the broad sense, but the two classes are not coextensive: contributors include authors and speakers who are not chairs, and the cmt Chairman is a specific chairing role. They overlap without being equivalent, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

Both classes denote an organisation/institution in the conference domain. confOf's Organization has children Company and University and is the employer of Persons; ekaw's Organisation has children Academic Institution, Organising Agency and Proceedings Publisher and organises events. The intended instances (companies, universities, publishers, organising bodies) coincide, differing only in spelling (Organization vs Organisation).

A 'Short paper' is a kind of contribution (a document type submitted to a conference), while B 'Cryptography Topic' is a subject area/topic of papers. They belong to different branches (Contribution vs Topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a physical place (a subclass of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), whereas B is a temporal deadline (a subclass of Deadline, sibling of submission/notification/registration deadlines). They denote different concepts: a location versus a point in time, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to its Program committee (a committee entity), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (a person who presents it). Different domain, different range, and different intended relation; they are not equivalent.

A's 'deals With' relates a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter of a paper), while B's 'is sent before' relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering relation). Different domain, range, and meaning; no equivalence.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. a written artefact. B 'Welcome address' is a conference activity (subclass of Conference activity, sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Registration), i.e. an event. Different kinds and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Medicine Topic' is a subject-area topic (a research field under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), while B's 'Simulating' is a research activity performed before a conference (under Activity > Activity before conference > Research, sibling of Modelling). One denotes a topic/field, the other an activity; their intended instances do not coincide.

Both are datatype properties named 'has Postal Code' with range string, capturing the postal code of an addressable entity. Although confOf attaches it to Organization/Person and edas to Contact Information, the intended relation (entity -> postal code string) is the same; the differing domains reflect modelling granularity rather than a different relation.

A Closing Talk is a talk that closes a conference (sibling of Welcome Talk, a ceremonial/plenary event), whereas an Invited Talk is a presentation given by an invited speaker (sibling of Contributed Talk and Tutorial). They denote different kinds of talk: closing vs. invited. Neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (chair of the conference/committee) under Person > Chairman, while B is a physical building (hotel hosting the conference) under Place > Building. Different kinds of entities with no overlap.

A's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event (domain Programme, range Conference Event), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (domain Person, range Activity/Item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

Conference Chair (edas) is the general chair of the whole conference, a top-level Person role that initiates calls and reviews. Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is a Conference Participant/PC Member role responsible only for tutorials. Different roles with different scopes and no shared properties; not equivalent.

A is a research topic (Antennas Topic) under the Topic hierarchy in edas, while B is an award category (Best Applications Paper Award) under Award in sigkdd. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's given name), while B's 'is given to' is an object property from Item to Person (an item is given to a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to the Location where it takes place; B's 'is equipped by' relates a Place to an Item that equips it. Different domains (Event vs Place), different ranges (Location vs Item), and different intended meanings (spatial occurrence vs equipment), so they are not the same relation.

A's Viza is a visa document (sibling of Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance, etc.), a bureaucratic artefact in the iasted ontology, whereas B's Paper is the scientific contribution submitted by an Author and reviewed. They share only the generic Document parent; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

ekaw:Event is a broad class of occurrences (scientific/social events) with children Scientific Event and Social Event, and properties like held In, organised By, has Event, part Of Event. sigkdd:Document is a written artefact with children Abstract, Paper, Review and properties presentation/presentationed by/submit until. The intended instances do not coincide: an event is not a document, and the contexts (children, properties) are entirely different. Hence unrelated.

A 'Call For Manuscripts' is a call/announcement for submissions (sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Reviews, under Call), whereas B 'Camera ready manuscript deadline' is a temporal deadline (under Deadline, sibling of submission and notification deadlines). One is a call document, the other a point in time; they denote different concepts.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to the Location where it is held; B's 'searched by' relates a Sponzor (sponsor) to ACM SIGKDD. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so the properties are unrelated.

A's 'has tracks' links a Conference volume to its Track (a thematic track of the conference), while B's 'has Administrative Event' links a Working event to an Administrative event (e.g. registration, reception). The domains and ranges are different concepts, so the properties do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent.

Conference:Committee is a conference-organisation body (organizing/program/steering committees, with chairs, co-chairs and members). edas:Organization is an external sponsoring entity (academia/government/industry/NGO) that provides sponsorships. Their children, properties and domain roles do not coincide, so they denote different concepts.

A's Decision is the outcome of a review (children Acceptance/Rejection, domain of has Decision from Paper), while B's Speaker is a role of a Person who gives a presentation (parent Person, children Author/Invited Speaker). They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A is a conference-document class ('Information for participants', sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic class under Computer Networks Topic in edas. They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's `name` is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's `has Postal Code` is a specific address component for Organization and Person. Although both are datatype properties with string ranges and overlapping domains, they denote different relations (a name vs. a postal code), so they are not equivalent.

edas:Paper is a document that is written, reviewed, and has topics; iasted:Submission is a document with children Final manuscript and Initial manuscript, i.e. the submitted manuscript rather than the paper as a whole. A submission is a stage/version of a paper, so the concepts overlap but are not equivalent; Paper is broader than Submission.

A's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (co-reviewer invitation), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (the presented material). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action of entering review criteria for a conference), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a paper being presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip under Social event), i.e. a social gathering. B's Registration is a conference activity (sibling of Coffee break, Lecture, Welcome address) with child Delegate, i.e. the administrative act of signing up attendees. Different concepts despite both being conference-related.

Both denote the event of presenting a paper at a conference: ekaw's Individual Presentation is a Scientific Event with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial and is linked to Paper/Abstract via 'paper Presented As' and 'presentation Of Paper'; iasted's Presentation is a Conference activity with children Power Point presentation and Video presentation, i.e. the same intended instances (a talk/presentation given at a conference). The differing children (Tutorial vs. Power Point/Video presentation) reflect different granularity of subtyping, not a different concept, and the sibling contexts (Conference, Session, Track, Workshop vs. Lecture, Introduction, etc.) are compatible with the same conference-domain notion.

A's Conference Member is a Person subtype (a person affiliated with a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Conference Event is an event/activity with attendees, location, programme and start/end times. They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and share no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Proceedings Publisher' is an Organisation (a publisher of conference proceedings), while B 'Refusing manuscript' is an Activity before the conference (rejecting a submitted paper). They belong to different top-level branches (Organisation vs Activity) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is made from' relates Item to Item (a composition/derivation relation between items), while B's 'can stay in' relates Person to Place (a person's ability to stay at a location). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'reviewes' relates a PC member to a Contribution (the paper they review), while B's 'is sent before' relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering). Different domains, ranges and meanings; not the same relation.

Both properties link a person/author to a contribution/item they produce. In confOf, 'writes' has domain Author and range Contribution (a paper/contribution). In iasted, 'prepare' has domain Person and range Item, where Item is the general artefact (paper) produced by a person. Author is a subclass of Person and Contribution is a kind of Item, so the two relations denote the same authoring relation in the conference domain, just at different levels of generality in the class hierarchy.

A's Program Committee Member is a Person who reviews papers (has max Papers, member Of Program Committee, added By Administrator), while B's Organizing Committee member is a Person under Organizator, a sibling of Program Committee member and General/Program Chair, i.e. an organiser role rather than a reviewer. The two roles overlap in that both are conference committee persons, but they are not the same concept; B's Program Committee member is the closer counterpart to A's class.

A's 'site URL' is a datatype property holding the conference's website URI (range anyURI), while B's 'City of conference' holds the city name as a string (range string). Although both are datatype properties of Conference, they denote different attributes (web address vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference topic (a subject area for papers) under Computer Networks Topic, while B is a document type (an abstract for an invited talk) under Abstract. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic taxonomy vs. document type) and share no intended instances.

A's Submitted Paper is a paper that has been submitted and can be assigned (child Assigned Paper), i.e. a submission-stage paper. B's Final manuscript is the final version of a submission (sibling of Initial manuscript), i.e. a camera-ready/final version. These denote different stages of the paper lifecycle, so they are not equivalent; in fact A's Submitted Paper corresponds more to B's Initial manuscript, and B's Final manuscript corresponds to A's Camera Ready Paper.

A's 'Organising Agency' is an Organisation (an institution that organises a conference), while B's 'Organizing Committee' is a Committee (a group of people within the conference organisation). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A's Author is a person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers), while B's Nonauthor registration fee is a monetary fee category for attendees who are not authors. They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Dining Place' is a physical location (a Place, sibling of Accommodation Place and Meeting Room Place) where meals are eaten, whereas B 'Conference Trip' is a social Event (sibling of Conference Banquet), an organised activity. Different kinds (Place vs Event) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

In Conference, 'Invited speaker' is a specific kind of conference contributor (a person invited to speak), sibling to 'Regular author' and 'Active conference participant'. In confOf, 'Member' is a participant subtype (sibling to 'Regular' and 'Student'), likely a registered member/attendee, not a speaker role. The intended instances do not coincide: an invited speaker is not necessarily a member and a member is not necessarily an invited speaker. Different roles in the conference domain, so unrelated.

A is a conference document type (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a subject/topic area in a topic taxonomy (Computer Networks Security Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

confOf's hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (a sub-event/activity), while ekaw's organisedBy links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name; B's 'has Email' is a datatype property of Person/Contact Information giving an email address. They relate different kinds of information (name vs. email address) and are not the same relation, so they are unrelated.

Presenter in ekaw is a Conference Participant who presents (a role within the conference participant hierarchy, with Invited Speaker as a child). Delegate in iasted is a broad attendee/participant class under Conference building, with children covering speakers, listeners, session chairs, committee members, etc. Both denote conference attendees, but Presenter is a narrower role (one who presents) while Delegate is the general attendee category; they overlap but are not equivalent.

Both properties express where an event takes place, but they differ in kind and range: confOf's `location` is a datatype property mapping Social/Working events to a string, while ekaw's `held In` is an object property mapping any Event to a Location class. They overlap in meaning (event venue) but are not the same relation, so a reference alignment would not record them as equivalent.

Company (a commercial organisation, sibling of University under Organization) and Organising Agency (the body that organises the conference, sibling of Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher under Organisation) are both organisations but denote different roles: a company is a type of organisation, while an organising agency is the entity responsible for organising the event. They overlap in that both are organisations, but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Audiovisual equipment' is a subclass of Item (a physical device category with children like Computer, LCD projector, Overhead projector, Video cassette player), whereas B's 'Speaker' is a subclass of Person (a role played by a person, with children Author and Invited Speaker and properties presentation/presentationed by). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (equipment vs. person role) and share no intended instances.

Both denote a thematic track of a conference. In Conference, Track is a part of a Conference (sibling of Tutorial/Workshop) and is the range of 'has tracks' from Conference volume. In ekaw, Track is a Scientific Event (sibling of Conference, Session, Workshop), i.e. a scientific event that is a sub-event of a conference. The intended instances coincide: a track is a thematic subdivision of a conference in both ontologies, so the classes are equivalent despite differing parent hierarchies.

A's 'event On List' relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (where the event is listed), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a document/event), while B's 'Invited Speaker' is a kind of person (Speaker). They denote different entity types (an event vs. a person), so they are not equivalent.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issues proceedings), while B's `has Topic` relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic. Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; no overlap.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B's 'Introduction' is a conference activity (subclass of Conference activity, sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Welcome address). A document and an activity are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated despite both being part of the conference domain.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer assigned to review a paper). B's designed_by relates a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (who set the deadline). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while B's 'award' links something to an Award (conference award). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'rejected By' links a Paper to the Administrator who rejected it (domain Paper, range Administrator), while B's 'parallel with' links two Administrative events that run in parallel (domain and range Administrative event). Different domain, range, direction and meaning; they are unrelated.

Both are subclasses of Paper, but they denote different concepts: cmt's Paper Full Version is the complete version of a paper (contrasted with Paper Abstract), while ekaw's Conference Paper is a paper submitted to/published at a conference (contrasted with Workshop Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). They overlap (a full paper can be a conference paper) but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Working event' is a conference-domain event class (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while B 'Antennas Topic' is a specific research subject under Topic. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper) in the cmt ontology, while B is a subclass of Topic (a cryptography research topic) in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

A's External Reviewer is a Person (a role/agent) who reviews papers for another reviewer, with properties assign/assigned By Reviewer linking to Reviewer. B's Review is a Conference document (an artefact produced by reviewing), with properties has a review/reviews linking to Reviewed contribution. One is an agent, the other a document; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

Accommodation Place in edas is a place for lodging (siblings include Dining Place, Conference Venue Place, Meeting Room Place), while Session room in iasted is a room where sessions are held (siblings include Conference hall, Hotel room, Building). They are both subclasses of Place and can overlap (a session room may be in an accommodation venue), but they denote different concepts: lodging vs. meeting/session space. Thus they are related, not equivalent.

A's Topic is the general class of subject areas for papers/reviews (it has names, is linked to conference parts, reviews and submissions). B's Communications Topic is a specific topic under the parent Topic, alongside many other specific topics (Antennas, CAD, etc.). Thus Communications Topic is a narrower concept than the general Topic, so A is subsumed by B's broader Topic class; they are not equivalent.

A's hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to a Subject Area (topic classification), while B's can_stay_in relates a Person to a Place (physical location). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'Member PC' is a Person subclass explicitly commented as 'Reviewer', with properties expert On (Topic) and reviewes (Contribution) — it denotes a program-committee member/reviewer. B's 'Author' is a Speaker subclass (path Delegate > Speaker > Author) with children about proceedings inclusion and lecture speakers, i.e. a person who authors/presents work. Although B has a sibling 'Reviewer', the candidate entity is 'Author', not 'Reviewer', so the two denote different roles (reviewer vs author) and are unrelated.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event (the outcome/notification stage of reviewing, accessible to authors) under Event, while B 'Program Committee' is a committee of people under Committee. They denote different concepts (an event vs. an organisational body) and share no subsumption relation.

A's 'Registration fee' is a specific kind of fee (a child of Fee, with its own subclasses for author/member/student registration), while B's 'Fee' is the general fee class whose children include Registration fee. Thus A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A is a research topic (Antennas Topic) under the Topic hierarchy in edas, while B is a document type (Tutorial Abstract) under Document > Abstract in ekaw. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (subject area vs. publication artefact) and share no intended instances.

A's topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to the Event/Paper that covers it (topic -> event/paper), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it (document -> speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'end Review' is an object property from Program Committee Chair to Review (the act of ending a review), while B's 'End of conference' is a datatype property from Conference to dateTime (the closing time of the conference). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'technically Organised By' is a sub-property of 'organised By' in the conference-organisation domain, relating an event/conference to the person or body that organises it technically. B's 'awarded by' has domain Award and relates an award to the agent that grants it. The kinds of things related (event vs. award) and the direction/meaning differ, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing practical info to attendees, while B's 'Security Topic' is a research topic in the EDAS topic taxonomy (sibling of Cryptography, Computer Networks, etc.). Different domains (document vs. topic) and no shared meaning.

A Conference Trip is a social event (excursion) within the conference programme, while B Departure is an activity after the conference (leaving the venue). They differ in kind (social event vs. post-conference activity) and in timing/purpose, so they are not the same concept.

Tutorial in ekaw is a kind of scientific event (an individual presentation given at a conference), while Exhibitor in sigkdd is a sponsoring entity (a subtype of Sponzor). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. sponsor) and share no intended instances.

Conference Chair is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in cmt, while Workshop is a working event (a kind of Event) in confOf. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person vs. event) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Written contribution' is a broad category of written conference contributions (parent of Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, sibling of Poster, Presentation, Invited talk), while B's 'Conference Paper' is a specific kind of Paper (sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Regular Paper, Submitted Paper, Workshop Paper). They overlap in that written contributions are typically papers, but A is broader (covers submitted/regular contributions as subclasses) and B is a specific paper type, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a physical place (a type of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place) where attendees stay, while B is a monetary fee (a type of Fee, sibling of Hotel fee and Registration fee) charged for an extra trip. They belong to different top-level branches (Place vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.
Car is a transport vehicle class in iasted, while Listener is a person role in sigkdd; they share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'Conference www' is a web page/document about a conference (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with a URL property), whereas B's 'Conference Proceedings' is a published multi-author volume of papers. They denote different artefacts and are not equivalent.

City in iasted is a specific kind of location (a city, with children like Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city) that people occupy/visit and buildings are situated in. Place in sigkdd is a broader location concept (children Conference hall, Hotel, Main office) that a person can stay in. A city is a kind of place, but Place is more general and includes non-city locations such as halls, hotels and offices, so the two are not equivalent; they overlap as related location concepts.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving a string name for a Conference or Person, while B's `Start of conference` is a datatype property giving a dateTime start time for a Conference. They relate different kinds of values (string vs dateTime) and denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

A's Presenter is a role of a person (a Conference Participant who presents), while B's Presenter house is a physical building/place where presenters stay. Different kinds (person role vs. building) and different paths (Person vs. Place), so they are unrelated.

A 'Social program' is a conference activity (a social event such as a dinner banquet) under Activity > Conference activity, while B 'Organizator' is a person role under Person, with children such as General Chair and Program Chair. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties from Author to the paper/contribution class (cmt Paper is the contribution written by an author; confOf Contribution is the paper). Same domain (Author), same range concept, same direction, so they denote the same relation.

A's Presenter is a Person (a conference participant who presents), while B's Presentation is a Conference activity (an event such as a talk or video presentation). One is an agent/role, the other is an activity/event; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Organizational Meeting is a kind of academic event (a meeting held during a conference), while B's Best Paper Awards Committee is a committee (a group of people). They belong to different branches of the domain (event vs. committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Chair PC' is a generic PC chair role directly under Person (siblings include Member PC, Author, Participant), while B's 'Workshop Chair' is a specific workshop-organising role under Conference Participant and PC Member, sibling to PC Chair, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair, Demo Chair. The two denote different roles (general PC chair vs. workshop chair), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a review expertise' links a submitted contribution to a review expertise (the topic/competence area a paper is about), while B's 'has Review History' links a reviewer to their personal review history (past reviews performed). Different domains (contribution vs reviewer) and different ranges (expertise vs history), so the relations do not coincide.

A's 'Personal Review History' is a record of reviews a reviewer has performed (domain Reviewer, range Personal Review History, sibling of Personal Publication History under Personal History). B's 'Paper' is a document submitted by an author (subclass of Document, sibling of Abstract and Review). They denote different concepts: a history/record of reviewing activity versus a submitted document. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

confOf's Event is a broad umbrella for all conference events (its children include Administrative, Social and Working events), whereas edas's Talk Event is a specific kind of academic event (siblings include Paper Presentation, Workshop, Organizational Meeting). Talk Event is therefore a narrower concept subsumed by the general Event class, not equivalent to it.

A's Positive Review is a subclass of Review (a review with a positive verdict), while B's Abstract is a subclass of Document (a summary of a paper). They share no intended instances: a positive review is an evaluation, an abstract is a document part. Different parents (Review vs Document) and different siblings (Negative/Neutral Review vs Paper/Review) confirm they denote different concepts.

In EDAS, 'Conference Session' is a broad session concept (a session within a conference, related to documents, events, and persons). In EKAW, 'Regular Session' is a specific kind of Session, sibling to Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, and Workshop Session. Thus EDAS's Conference Session is more general and would include EKAW's Regular Session as one type, so A is subsumed by B's broader Session concept, not equivalent to the narrower Regular Session.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a Conference contributor (a person role in the conference programme, sibling of Regular author and Active conference participant). B's 'Hotel presenter' is a Delegate under Conference building, i.e. a presenter located at a hotel venue, sibling of Speaker, One day presenter, Listener, etc. The intended concepts differ: an invited speaker is a distinguished invited contributor, whereas a hotel presenter is a presenter tied to a hotel building/venue. They share only the loose notion of presenting and are not the same concept in a reference alignment.

A's 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing/issuing a proceedings volume), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents a document). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'written By' links a Review to its Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), i.e. the author of a review. B's 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (domain Member PC, range Contribution), i.e. a PC member reviewing a paper. The subjects, objects and direction differ: one relates a review to a person, the other a person to a paper. They are not the same relation, nor inverses of one another.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' (a written artefact such as a paper, poster, presentation, invited talk) that is submitted to and contained in a conference volume. B's 'Event' is a general happening (scientific or social) with children Scientific Event and Social Event, held in a location, organised by persons/organisations, and part of other events. The intended instances do not coincide: contributions are documents, events are occurrences. The shared word 'conference' does not make them equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper), while B's `related To Paper` relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a presentation is related to the paper it presents). Different domains (Author vs Paper Presentation) and different ranges (Contribution vs Accepted Paper), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a call inviting participation, sibling of Call for paper and Conference announcement), whereas B 'Deadline hotel reservation' is a time/deadline entity (a specific deadline under Deadline). They denote different concepts: a document vs. a temporal deadline, so they are unrelated.

confOf Participant is a general conference attendee (parent Person, children Member/Regular/Student, property early Registration), while sigkdd Author is a specific role under Speaker who submits papers and receives notifications/awards. They overlap (an author is typically a participant) but neither subsumes the other: Participant includes non-authors, and Author is a narrower role. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'Important dates' is a class of deadline/date milestones belonging to a conference volume (submission, camera-ready, acceptance, start/end dates). B's 'Activity' is a general event/activity class (conference activities, before/after conference activities) with properties like give, go through, is held in, is dated on. The intended instances do not coincide: one is a set of dates, the other a set of events/activities. They are not synonyms and share no meaningful subsumption.

Scientific Event (ekaw) is a subclass of Event covering conferences, workshops, sessions, etc., while Speaker (sigkdd) is a subclass of Person covering authors and invited speakers. They belong to different branches (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its committee members (range Conference Member), while B's relatesTo links a Document to events, sessions or persons. Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference domain), while B's Registration Student is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a fee category for students. They share the student concept but denote different kinds of entities (person vs. fee), so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'Paid applicant' is a subclass of Person (a registered conference applicant who has paid, with children Early/Late paid applicant), whereas B's 'Payment document' is a subclass of Document (an artefact such as a bank transfer or cheque). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Item/Document) and denote a person versus a document, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference submission (has authors, reviewers, decisions, subject areas), while B's Viza is a document type under Item > Document alongside forms, invitation letters and mailing lists; the label 'Viza' does not denote a paper, so the two classes are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Technical commitee is a kind of Delegate (a person role in a conference building). One denotes an event, the other a person/committee role, so they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented), while B 'Bronze Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. sponsor) and share no intended instances.

A's Conference Chair is a person role (a chair of the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B's Best Paper Awards Committee is an organizational committee (sibling of Organizing and Program Committees). One is a person, the other a group/committee; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

Preference in cmt is a class representing a reviewer's preference/interest in a paper (a value attached to a reviewer-paper relation), whereas Organizer in Conference is a person/role responsible for organising the conference. They denote different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a scientific gathering, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) in the event hierarchy, while B's Meeting Room Place is a physical location (a room where meetings are held, sibling of Accommodation Place and Conference Venue Place) in the place hierarchy. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. venue/room) and are not equivalent.

A 'Multi author Volume' is a kind of Document (a published multi-author volume, parent of Proceedings) in the ekaw ontology, whereas B 'Author information form' is a Form (an administrative document used to collect author details) in iasted. They share no intended instances: one is a publication artefact, the other a data-collection form. Different parents (Document vs Form) and different siblings confirm they denote different concepts.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to a contribution (reviewing), while B's `submit` relates an author to a paper (submission). Different domain, range, and direction of the conference relation; they are not the same property.

A's Review is a document/contribution class (a review of a paper, with properties linking it to a Reviewed contribution), while B's Conference Chair is a Person role (a person who initiates calls and reviews papers). They denote different kinds of entities in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

Pending Paper in edas is a paper in a submission/review state (sibling of Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, Published, Active Paper), i.e. a status of a paper in the review process. Industrial Paper in ekaw is a paper type/track (sibling of Conference, Workshop, Demo, Poster, Regular, Submitted, Camera Ready Paper), i.e. a kind of paper by its origin/venue. The two classifications are orthogonal: a paper can be both industrial and pending, and neither subsumes the other. They share only the parent Paper, so they are unrelated.

A's 'contact Email' is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string (an email address), while B's 'is sent by' is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Contribution vs Item) and range (string vs Person), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Submitted Paper' is a kind of Paper (a scientific contribution submitted to a conference), while B's 'Transparency' is a Document used for presentation/overhead slides. They share no intended instances and belong to different subhierarchies (Paper vs. Document/Transparency), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.) that informs participants about the conference. B's 'Record of attendance' is a document recording who attended, a different artefact with a different purpose. They share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a specific role: the first author of a contribution, a subclass of Regular author. B's 'Author of paper' is the general class of persons who author a paper, a subclass of Author. Every first author of a contribution is an author of a paper, but not every author of a paper is a first author, so A is strictly narrower than B (subsumed_by). They are not equivalent because A encodes first-author position while B does not.

A's isMenuOf relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (a menu belongs to a meal event), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presents a document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Workshop Session' is a kind of scientific event session (a scheduled activity within a conference), while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee (a group of people/organisational body). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (Event vs Committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) announcing the conference, whereas B 'Coffee Break' is a scheduled non-academic break event in the conference programme. They belong to different branches (document vs. event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

TPC Member in edas is a Person who reviews papers and initiates calls, while Conference Participant in ekaw is a broader role covering all attendees (including chairs, presenters, registered participants). TPC Member is a specific reviewing role, not equivalent to the general participant role; they overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly.

A's property links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (committee -> event/volume), while B's isMemberOf links a Person to a Conference (person -> event). Different domains and ranges, so the relations are not equivalent.

Person in the Conference ontology is a broad class covering all people involved in the conference (committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers, chairs), whereas Author in edas is a specific subclass of Person (path Person > Author) denoting someone who writes papers. Thus Person is strictly more general than Author, so the correct relation is subsumes (A subsumes B), not equivalence.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving a string name to a Conference or Person; B's `obtain` is an object property relating a Person to an Item (e.g. a fee or award). Different domain, different range, different kind (datatype vs object), and different meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is used by' is an object property linking an Item to a Person (a usage/attribution relation), while B's 'E mail' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address). They have different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic in signal processing (a subject area under Topic), while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical device under Audiovisual equipment). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Demo Session' is a kind of scientific event session (a slot in the conference programme where demos are presented), while B 'Program Committee' is a committee of people (the PC that reviews papers). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference ontology (Event vs Committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role in the conference organisation (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/Chair, linked to Conference via member Of Conference). B 'Place' is a physical location (children Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room; linked to Activity/Person via is held in / is present in). The two denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a role of the first author of a conference contribution (a subclass of Regular author, sibling of Contribution co author), whereas B's 'Invited Speaker' is a person who gives an invited talk (subclass of Speaker, sibling of Author). The first-author role and the invited-speaker role denote different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a committee co chair' links a Committee to its Co chair (a committee-role relation), while B's 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (a reviewing relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Bid in cmt is a reviewer's bid on a paper (domain/range Reviewer->Bid, Bid->Reviewer, Paper->Bid), while Publisher in Conference is an organisation that issues conference proceedings (issues Publisher->Conference proceedings). Different concepts with no overlap.

University is an academic organization (subclass of Organization, sibling of Company, domain of 'study At' with Scholar as range), while Numerical Review Question is a kind of review question used in the reviewing process (subclass of Review Question, sibling of Textual Review Question). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A 'Conference Chair' (edas) is a Person who chairs the conference and initiates calls, reviews papers, etc. B 'Conference Hiker' (iasted) is a subclass of Delegate under Conference building, a participant role with no chairing duties. Different concepts despite both being person roles.

A is a document type (an abstract of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B is a type of session/event (a demo session, sibling of Conference/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session under Session). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (document vs. event) and share no intended instances.

A's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (the venue's country). B's speak_in relates a Person to a Place/Time (where/when a person speaks). Different domains (Conference vs Person), different ranges (Country vs Place/Time), and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.
A is a class of paper (a rejected submission) in the document hierarchy, while B is a deadline (registration deadline) in the time hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Both are classes named Review under Document, representing the review of a paper in the conference domain; the cmt Review has children (Meta Review) and properties linking reviewers, while sigkdd Review is a sibling of Paper/Abstract under Document, but both denote the same concept of a review document.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address), while B's authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document. They relate different kinds of things (string vs. Document) and represent different relations (contact email vs. authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a conference activity (Coffee break, a kind of Conference activity). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

A's Scientific Event is a broad academic event class (parent of Conference, Workshop, Session, Track, etc.) under Event, while B's Social program is a specific conference activity (parent of Dinner banquet, sibling of Coffee break, Welcome address) under Conference activity. They denote different concepts: one is a scientific/academic event, the other a social programme of a conference.

A's hasReview relates a Paper to its Review (domain Paper, range Review). B's give relates a Person to an Activity/Item (domain Person, range Activity, Item). The domains and ranges are disjoint kinds (Paper vs Person, Review vs Activity/Item), so the properties do not denote the same relation; they are unrelated.

Academia Organization is a subclass of Organization in edas (path Organization > Academia Organization), so it is strictly more specific than the Conference class Organization; the two do not denote the same concept.

A's 'accepted By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepts it), while B's 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (the publisher issues the proceedings). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Conference applicant is a person who applies to/registers for a conference (parent Person, child Registeered applicant, siblings include Conference participant and Reviewer), whereas ekaw Student is a generic person role (sibling of Paper Author, Possible Reviewer) with no conference-application meaning. They share only the Person parent; the intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person in the conference domain: same label 'Person', both have first name, last name, email properties, and both are the root of a hierarchy of conference roles (Committee member/Reviewer/Author/Chair PC/Participant etc.). The confOf comment 'confTool' is just a tool annotation, not a semantic distinction. The intended instances coincide.

edas:Paper is the general paper class (parent of Accepted/Rejected/Pending/Published/Withdrawn Paper), while ekaw:Regular Paper is a specific paper type under ekaw:Paper, sibling to Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Workshop Paper, etc. The edas class is broader and subsumes the ekaw subclass; they are not equivalent.

A's topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to the Event/Paper that covers it (domain Research Topic, range Event/Paper), while B's write relates a Person to an Item they author (domain Person, range Item). Different domains, ranges and directions; no equivalence or subsumption.

Country in confOf is a geopolitical entity used as the range of has Country for Organizations and Persons. Place in edas is a physical location (with subclasses Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) used as the range of has Location for Conference Events. A country is not a place in the edas sense (a venue/room/dining location), and the property contexts (Organization/Person -> Country vs Conference Event -> Place) do not coincide, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'has tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (domain Conference volume, range Tutorial, parent 'has parts'), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (domain Speaker, range Document). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while B's 'Paper' is the submitted document itself, with children Accepted/Pending/Rejected Paper and properties like is Written By Author. The two denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document submitted to a conference (with authors, reviews, topics), while B's Deadline is a point in time (a submission/notification/camera-ready date). They belong to different branches (Document vs Time) and share no instances; the only link is that a deadline may concern a paper, which is not equivalence.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Computer Architecture Topic' is a research topic area used to classify papers. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of contribution (a paper submission), while B 'Best Research Paper Award' is a kind of award. They belong to different branches (Contribution vs Award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair (cmt) is a chair role in the conference organisation, a sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair under Chairman. Early Registered Participant (ekaw) is a conference participant distinguished by registration timing, a sibling of Late Registered Participant under Conference Participant. The two denote different concepts (organisational role vs. registration status) with no overlap in instances, so they are unrelated.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (Publisher -> Conference proceedings), while B's `hold` relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference it holds (ACM SIGKDD -> Conference). Different domains and ranges: publishing proceedings vs. organising/holding a conference, so the relations are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties linking a deadline/important-date concept to a date value, but A's 'is a starting date' specifically denotes the start of a date range within Important dates, while B's 'Date' is the generic date of a Deadline. They overlap in the conference-deadline domain but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'is signed by' relates an Item (e.g. a paper/contribution) to a Person who signs it, while B's 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee. The domains, ranges and intended meanings differ entirely, so the two properties are unrelated.

A 'Regular' is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference, sibling of Member and Student), while B 'Regular Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Poster Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Administrative event is a subclass of Event covering organisational events (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration) that occur during a conference. edas's Call is a request-for-submissions entity (Call For Papers/Manuscripts/Reviews) that initiates submissions and has deadlines; it is not an event and does not denote the same concept. The two entities share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both entities denote the same concept: a company/organization in the conference domain. The paths and labels align (Company vs Organization), and the context of conference organization supports equivalence.

Conference proceedings in ontology A is a publication artefact (a class of documents with publisher, volume, ISBN, name, topic), whereas Time in ontology B is a temporal entity (parent of Conference days, Deadline, Trip day, with properties like is held before/after, is present in). They share no intended instances and no subsumption relation; the only superficial link is that proceedings may be published at a conference, which is not an ontological equivalence.

A's 'Written contribution' is a kind of conference contribution (a paper-like submission, with children Regular/Submitted contribution), while B's 'Payment document' is a kind of Document covering bank transfers and cheques. They share no intended instances and belong to different branches (contribution vs. payment/document), so they are unrelated.

A's enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference (enabling a virtual meeting), while B's prepare relates a Person to an Item (preparing an item). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's `sign` relates a Person (domain) to an Item (range), i.e. a person signs up for/registers for an item. B's `payed by` relates a Registration fee (domain) to a Person (range), i.e. a fee is paid by a person. The domains and ranges are disjoint (Person->Item vs Registration fee->Person), so they are not the same relation; at best they are loosely related through the registration/payment scenario, but they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission act), while isHeldAfter relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap.

ekaw Location is a venue/place where events are held (held In: Event -> Location; location Of: Location -> Event), while sigkdd Place is a location where a person can stay (can stay in: Person -> Place) with subclasses Conference hall, Hotel, Main office. Both denote physical places, but the intended usage differs: Location is tied to events, Place to accommodation of persons. They overlap but are not the same concept, so 'related' rather than 'equivalent'.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (domain Contribution, range Author), while B's 'has Related Paper' links an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). The domains, ranges and directions differ, so they are not the same relation; at best they are inverses of different concepts, not equivalent.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class describing a reviewer's expertise/preference area, linked to Reviewer, Review preference and Submitted contribution. B's 'Personal Review History' is a subclass of Personal History recording a reviewer's past reviews, linked to Reviewer via has Review History / is Review History Of. The two denote different concepts (expertise vs. review history), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role in the conference organisation (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/Chair, with properties member Of Conference and has Conference Member). B 'Hotel fee' is a monetary fee (parent Fee, siblings Registration fee, Fee for extra trip). They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. money), so they are unrelated.
A 'Reception' is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) in the conference domain, while B 'Credit card' is a payment card item; they denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Paper Abstract is a specific part of a paper (the abstract), while B's Paper is the whole regular contribution. The abstract is a component of a paper, so Paper Abstract is strictly narrower than Paper; they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a general conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, Review) addressed to all participants. B's 'Author information form' is a specific Form (sibling of Registration form, Hotel registration form) that authors fill in. Different kind (document vs. form), different audience (participants vs. authors), and different paths; they do not denote the same concept.

Chair is a committee role (a person who chairs a committee, sibling of Co chair, domain/range of committee-chair properties), while Country is a geographical entity used as the range of has Country for Organizations and Persons. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B's 'Organizational Meeting' is an academic event (subclass of Academic Event, sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop). A person role and an event are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated.

Publication in iasted is a subclass of Item (a document-like artefact, with children Book proceeding and Cd proceeding), whereas Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (a person who presents, with children Author and Invited Speaker). They denote different kinds of entities (artefact vs. person) and are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person in the conference domain. Conference's Person is the general superclass of participants, reviewers, committee members, etc., and iasted's Person is likewise the general superclass of Delegate and Sponsor, with properties relating persons to activities, items, money, and time. The intended instances coincide (people involved in the conference), so the two classes are equivalent.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track (a part-whole relation between a conference and its thematic tracks), while B's 'follows' relates one Administrative event to another (a temporal ordering between events). Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Company in confOf is a subclass of Organization (sibling of University), while edas Organization is the general superclass with children Academia, Government, Industry, NGO. Company is thus a narrower concept subsumed by the broader edas Organization, not equivalent.

Associated Chair is a conference-organisation role (a chair who is associated with the conference, sibling of Conference Chair, PC Chair, Author, Reviewer under Chairman/Conference Member). Listener is a type of Delegate/attendee who merely attends without presenting, sibling of Speaker, Session chair, etc. The two denote different concepts: an organiser role vs. a passive attendee role, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' is an action property with domain Administrator and range Program Committee Member (an administrator adds a PC member). B's 'was a program committee of' relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (a committee serves a conference). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Person) while B is a type of event session (Regular Session, a subclass of Session/Event). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is a specific registration-fee category (author attendee with CD registration fee), a subclass of Registration fee, while B is the general Registration fee class with children for member/non-member/student registrations. A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action of entering conference data), while B's 'lists Event' relates a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (a publication listing events). Different domains (Administrator vs Programme Brochure/Web Site) and different ranges (Conference vs Event) mean the relations do not coincide.

A 'Regular contribution' is a kind of conference document/contribution (a paper-like submission), while B 'Author' is a person role (a speaker who writes papers). They belong to different branches (document vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.
Hotel fee (a fee for hotel accommodation) and Sponzor fee (a sponsor's fee) are distinct fee subtypes under the common Fee parent; they denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Published Paper' is a conference paper that has been published (a Document/Paper in the edas ontology), while B 'Cheque' is a payment document (a financial instrument) under Item > Document > Payment document. They share no intended instances; the only overlap is the generic word 'document' in their paths, which does not make them the same concept.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to a Conference proceedings (a publisher issues proceedings), while B's `written By` relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.
A's 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to its Review, while B's 'award' links something to an Award (a prize). Different domain, range and meaning; no overlap.

A's Chair is a committee role (a Person who chairs a committee, sibling of Co-chair, with committee-chair properties). B's Scholar is a price/registration category of Person (comment 'price category - scholar', sibling of Administrator, Author, Participant, etc., with a studyAt property). The intended instances do not coincide: a chair need not be a scholar and a scholar need not chair anything, so the classes are unrelated.

Chairman is a person role (a subclass of Person, with subclasses Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, etc.), while Social program is a conference activity (a subclass of Conference activity, with child Dinner banquet). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person vs. event/activity) and share no intended instances.

Organization in edas denotes an institutional body (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provides sponsorships. Item in iasted denotes a physical or informational object (audiovisual equipment, card, document, publication, transport vehicle) used in activities. Their children, properties and domains/ranges do not overlap: Organization is tied to Sponsorship, Item to Activity/Person/Place/Money. They denote different concepts.

A 'Security Topic' is a subject area (a kind of Topic) in the edas ontology, while B 'Tutorial Abstract' is a document type (a kind of Abstract) in the ekaw ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Topic vs Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (a person-to-institution affiliation), while B's relatesTo relates a Document to events, sessions or persons (a document-to-topic/participant link). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Early paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a registered conference attendee who paid early), while B's 'Author' is a subclass of Speaker who submits papers and receives notifications/awards. They belong to different branches (registration/payment vs. authorship/speaking) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both ontologies define a class for administrative events. In confOf, 'Administrative_event' is a subclass of 'Event' and represents administrative activities. In edas, 'AdministrativeEvent' is also a subclass of 'Event' and represents the same concept. The names, paths, and parent classes are identical, indicating equivalence.

A 'Working event' is a conference-domain event class (parent Event, children Conference/Tutorial/Workshop, with properties like has title, location, has Topic), while B 'Computer Networks Switching Topic' is a specific research topic under Computer Networks Topic. They denote entirely different concepts (event vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad Person subclass covering all people who contribute to a conference (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors). B's 'One day presenter' is a specific Delegate subtype in the iasted ontology denoting a presenter attending for a single day. The two concepts differ in scope and kind: one is a general contributor role, the other a narrow attendance/presentation category, so they do not denote the same class.

A's writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (the act of writing a review), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (giving a presentation). Different domain (Reviewer vs Speaker), different range (Review vs Document), and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Power Point presentation' is a kind of Presentation (a conference activity/artefact), while B 'Organizator' is a kind of Person (an agent role such as General Chair or Program Chair). They belong to disjoint branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.
