A's 'has a name' is a generic naming property whose domain spans Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, while B's 'has First Name' is a person-specific datatype property (domain Person, comment about middle name). They relate different kinds of things and are not the same relation.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property mapping a Conference volume to a string (a textual location), while B's 'is Location Of' is an object property mapping a Place to a Conference Event. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and direction (B is the inverse of a 'has location' relation between events and places), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to a Review (a review of a paper), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (a talk given by a speaker). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship of a paper), while B's 'attendee At' links a Person to a Conference Event (attendance at an event). They relate different kinds of things in opposite directions and capture different relations (authorship vs. attendance), so they are not equivalent.

The two properties are inverses, not equivalents: cmt's readByReviewer goes from Paper to Reviewer (the reviewer who reads a paper), while ekaw's reviewOfPaper goes from Review to Paper (the paper a review is about). They relate different kinds of things in opposite directions, so a reference alignment would not record them as equivalent.

A 'Short paper' is a short contribution (sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution), while B 'Regular Paper' is a full-length paper (sibling of Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Workshop Paper under Paper). They denote different paper categories, not the same concept.

A's hasTopic relates a Working event to a Topic (subject matter), while B's hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (event composition/participation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A Conference Banquet is a social event held during the conference (sibling of Conference Trip under Social Event), whereas B Departure is an activity occurring after the conference (sibling of Full day tour under Activity after conference). They denote different kinds of events/activities with no overlap in intended instances.

A's Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference event/session), while B's Student lecturer is a person role (a kind of Lecturer/Speaker/Author/Delegate). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A Presenter in edas is an Author who presents a paper (path Person > Author > Presenter), i.e. a role of an author. In iasted, One day presenter is a subclass of Delegate (path Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > One day presenter), a delegate who attends/presents for one day, alongside Hotel presenter, Speaker, Listener, etc. Both denote a person who presents, but they are defined under different superclasses (Author vs Delegate) and with different intended instances (paper-presenting author vs one-day conference delegate), so they overlap but are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a conference event: edas Conference has name, country, dates, members, topics, and is a subclass context of Academic Event; sigkdd Conference has name, city, start/end dates, and is held by ACM SIGKDD. Same intended instances in the conference domain.

A's 'Student registration fee' is a specific kind of registration fee (a subclass of Registration fee, one of several attendee-type fees), while B's 'Registration fee' is the general fee class with children for student, member and non-member registrations. Thus A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's 'has a steering committee' relates a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a committee membership relation), while B's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (a topical expertise relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). B's Conference days is a temporal concept (a Time subclass, sibling of Deadline and Trip day, with children Delegate and One conference day). One denotes an event, the other a time period, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Chair in cmt is a specific committee role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while Science Worker in confOf is a broad top-level category of person (sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.). The two do not denote the same concept; Conference Chair would be a narrow role, not a general science worker.

Both are datatype properties expressing a deadline date/time, but A is a specific conference manuscript deadline attached to Conference, while B is a generic deadline completion date attached to Deadline; they overlap in meaning but are not the same relation.

A's 'assigned By Administrator' is a specific relation from a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned the review. B's 'give' is a general relation from any Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or a paper). The domains (Reviewer vs Person) and ranges (Administrator vs Activity/Item) differ, and the intended meanings do not coincide; at best 'give' is a much broader relation, but not a subsuming relation of this specific assignment relation.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation between a document and its parts), while B's 'is Topic Of' relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper (a subject-matter relation). The domains and ranges are disjoint kinds of entities (Abstract vs Topic) and the intended meanings differ, so the properties are not equivalent.

Publisher in the Conference ontology is an agent/organisation that issues conference proceedings (domain of 'issues', range of 'has a publisher', has a name). Time in iasted is a temporal entity with children Conference days, Deadline, Trip day, and is the range of temporal relations such as is held before/after and is present in. The two concepts share no instances and no meaning; they are unrelated.

A's readByReviewer links a Paper to the Reviewer who reads it (domain Paper, range Reviewer). B's belongs_to_reviewers links a Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer (domain Review expertise/Review preference, range Reviewer). The subject kinds differ (Paper vs. expertise/preference), so the relations are not the same; they are unrelated.

A's forEvent links a Call to the Academic Event it is a call for (domain Call, range Academic Event), while B's hasEvent links an Event to a sub-event (domain Event, range Event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.
A's Tip is a gratuity/payment under Money, while B's Sponzor fee is a sponsorship fee under Fee; different concepts despite both being monetary.

A's Accommodation Place is a kind of Place (lodging venue for conference attendees), while B's Van is a kind of Transport vehicle (a means of transport). They belong to different branches (Place vs Item/Transport vehicle) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasFirstName is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's first name), while B's obtain is an object property mapping a Person to an Item (acquiring an item). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (a person giving a talk), while B's 'is visited by' links a Building/City/State to a Person (a place being visited). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

In cmt, Associated Chair is a kind of Chairman/Conference Member (a general conference-organisation chair role), while in ekaw Workshop Chair is a Conference Participant who chairs a workshop and is also a PC Member. The two roles have different parents (Chairman vs Conference Participant) and different intended instances: an associated chair of the conference is not a workshop chair. They share no defining context, so they are unrelated.

A's Poster is a kind of Contribution (a paper/presentation type, sibling of Paper and Short paper), while B's Silver Supporter is a sponsorship level under Sponzor (sibling of Gold/Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (scientific contribution vs. sponsorship), so they are unrelated.

A's Talk Event is a kind of academic event (a scheduled talk such as a welcome or closing talk) within the conference event hierarchy, while B's Document is a generic item (forms, invitations, reviews, submissions) in the iasted ontology. They denote different concepts with no overlap in instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a document artefact (subclass of Document, with children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version, and properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To Reviewer). B's Activity before conference is a temporal activity phase (subclass of Activity, siblings Activity after conference/Conference activity, children Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript, Renting, Research). The intended instances do not coincide: one is a submitted document, the other a pre-conference activity such as manuscript handling. No equivalence, subsumption or meaningful overlap.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' relates an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the committee organized a particular conference/volume). B's 'scientifically Organised By' relates a conference/event to an Academic Institution (the scientific organizer of the event). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Organizing committee vs. event; Conference volume vs. Academic Institution), and the direction of the relation differs, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Trip' is a social event (an activity, sibling of Conference Banquet) in ekaw, while B 'Conference city' is a subclass of City (a location) in iasted, sibling of Presenter city, Sponsor city and Trip city. One denotes an event, the other a place, so they are unrelated.

A's Deadline is a general class for all conference deadlines (submission, registration, camera-ready, notification, hotel), while B's Deadline Author notification is a specific deadline (notification of acceptance) that is a subclass of Deadline in sigkdd. Thus A is more general and B is subsumed by A.

In the Conference ontology, 'Invited speaker' is a subclass of 'Conference contributor' (a person who gives an invited talk), while in edas 'Attendee' is a direct subclass of 'Person' denoting any person attending the conference. An invited speaker is a specific kind of contributor, not a general attendee, and the two classes have different parents, siblings, and intended instances; they are not equivalent.

A's Scholar is a subclass of Person (a person with a price category, with property study At), while B's Author attendee cd registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, i.e. a fee amount, not a person. Different kinds and domains, so they are unrelated.

A's 'manuscript Due On' is the deadline for submitting the manuscript (a submission deadline), while B's 'End of conference' is the date the conference finishes. Both are Conference datatype properties with range dateTime, but they denote different deadlines/events in the conference timeline, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has authors' relates a Conference document to a Person (document -> person), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (author -> paper). They are inverse in direction and connect different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Member' is a person role (a Person subclass, parent of Author/Reviewer/Chair) in cmt, while B 'Social Event' is a non-academic conference event (parent of Excursion/Reception) in edas. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Conference Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair is a person role in the conference organization (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while University is an academic institution (a subclass of Academic Institution). They belong to disjoint branches of the ontology (Person vs Organisation) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Member is a Person (a person involved in a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's Conference volume is a Conference (an event/volume with committees, tracks, contributions and dates). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. conference/event), so they are unrelated.

A 'Cd proceening' is a publication type (a proceedings CD, sibling of Book proceeding under Publication), while B 'Invited Speaker' is a person role (a Speaker under Person). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Document in edas is a general artefact class (parent of Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, Meal Menu) that can be related to events, sessions and persons. Sponzor in sigkdd is a sponsor organisation class with subclasses Gold/Bronze/Silver/Platinum Supporter, Exhibitor, etc., and properties like Name of sponsor and search/searched by linking it to ACM SIGKDD. The two classes denote entirely different concepts (document vs. sponsor) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's readByReviewer relates a Paper to a Reviewer (domain Paper, range Reviewer), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

Country in confOf is a nationality/geographic country used as range of has Country for Organizations and Persons, whereas Place in sigkdd is a physical location (with subclasses Conference hall, Hotel, Main office) that a Person can stay in. A country is not a place of stay and the intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are unrelated.

Both classes denote a conference paper/contribution. In cmt, Paper is a Document with authors, reviews, decisions; in Conference, Paper is a Regular contribution (a Conference document) with an abstract. The intended instances coincide: submitted/published papers. The differing parents (Document vs Regular contribution) reflect different upper-level structuring, not different concepts, and both have paper-specific subparts (Paper Abstract/Full Version vs Extended abstract sibling).

A is an administrative event in the conference organisation process (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration), while B is a subject-area topic (computer networks) used to classify papers. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's hasBid links a Paper to a Bid (an offer to review), while B's hasReview links a Paper to a Review (the completed evaluation). Although both are Paper-to-review-process object properties, Bid and Review are distinct entities in the conference domain (a bid is a reviewer's expression of interest, a review is the resulting evaluation), so the properties are not equivalent.

Country in confOf is a geographical entity used as the range of has Country (Organization, Person -> Country). Money in iasted is a monetary amount with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

cmt:Paper is the general document class for conference submissions (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with authors, reviews, decisions). ekaw:Assigned_Paper is a much narrower class: a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer, sitting below Submitted Paper and above Evaluated Paper. Every Assigned Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is assigned, so cmt:Paper is more general and is subsumed by the ekaw class in the sense of being its superclass.

A Reviewer is a Person who reviews papers; B's PC Member is a Possible Reviewer (a person who may review) and is the parent of PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc. Every PC Member is a possible reviewer, but a Reviewer in the Conference ontology is any person with review expertise/preferences, not necessarily a program-committee member. The B class is broader (it includes chairs and committee roles that are not simply reviewers), so Reviewer is subsumed by PC Member rather than equivalent.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a kind of conference document (an announcement/call-type document, sibling of Call for paper, Call for participation, Review), whereas B's 'Conference Paper' is a paper submitted to a conference (sibling of Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, Regular Paper). The announcement is a document about the conference, not a paper; the shared word 'Conference' does not make them the same concept.

A 'Session chair' is a Delegate who chairs a session, while B 'Organizator' is a Person who organizes the conference and is the parent of roles like General Chair, Program Chair, and Webmaster. The two roles overlap in that both are conference organizers, but they are not the same concept: a session chair is a specific session-level role, whereas an organizer is a broader conference-level role. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic's preference in a review), while B's submit links an Author to a Paper. Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they do not denote the same relation.

In cmt, Chairman is a general role class with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair, so it covers more than just the conference chair. In edas, Conference Chair is a specific role (sibling of Session Chair, TPC Member, etc.) with properties about initiating calls and reviewing papers. The cmt Chairman is therefore broader than the edas Conference Chair; the edas class corresponds to the cmt subclass Conference Chair, not to Chairman itself.

cmt:Paper is a document artefact (subclass of Document, with children Paper Abstract / Paper Full Version, and properties like has Author, assigned To, has Decision). iasted:Research is an activity performed before the conference (subclass of Activity before conference, with children Modelling / Simulating, siblings Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript). A paper is not a research activity, so the two classes do not denote the same concept.

A's 'Paid applicant' is a subclass of Person/Conference applicant (a registered applicant who has paid), while B's 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (banquet, reception, trip). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Departure tax is a specific tax on travel departure (sibling of Value added tax under Tax), while Registration fee is a conference registration charge (parent of member/student registration fees, with properties Currency, Price, pay, payed by). They denote different concepts in different subdomains (taxation vs. conference fees), so they are unrelated.

A's 'submit Paper' is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper). B's 'has Submission Deadline' is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime (the deadline date). They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Author vs Call), range (Paper vs dateTime), and meaning (submission act vs deadline date), so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a conference submission document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Currency has no context in the conference domain and clearly denotes a monetary unit; the entities share no intended instances.

Both classes denote the subject area of a paper/conference. confOf's Topic is used by Contribution (dealsWith), PC member expertise (expertOn) and working events (hasTopic); edas's Topic is used by Conference and Paper (hasTopic/isTopicOf) and has a taxonomy of subject topics. Same intended instances (subject areas), so equivalent.

A's Topic is a subject/keyword area used to classify reviews, contributions and conference parts (it has a name, belongs to review preferences, is a topic of conference parts). B's Document is a generic document artefact with children Abstract, Paper and Review, presented by a Speaker and having a submission deadline. Topic is a classification concept, not a document artefact, so the two classes do not denote the same concept.

A's 'Committee member' is a Person who belongs to a committee (has members / was a member of Committee), while B's 'Building' is a Place (a physical location occupied by persons, paid in money, situated in places). They share no instances and no meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'has important dates' is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity (a container of dates), while B's 'Date' is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a dateTime literal. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), domain (Conference volume vs Deadline), and range (Important dates vs dateTime), so they do not denote the same relation.

A's forEvent relates a Call to an Academic Event (the call is for an event), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity/Item (a person gives something). Different domains (Call vs Person), different ranges (Academic Event vs Activity/Item), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

confOf Participant is a broad role class (parent of Member, Regular, Student, Author, Chair PC, etc.) covering anyone taking part in the conference, while edas Author is a narrower role for people who write papers (parent of Presenter, with properties has Related Paper / is Written By). An Author is a kind of Participant, but Participant is not an Author, so the classes overlap without coinciding; the correct relation is related (or subsumed_by from Author's perspective), not equivalent.

cmt's Conference Member is a broad role class (parent of Author, Reviewer, Chair, PC Member) covering anyone affiliated with the conference, while confOf's Member is a narrower subclass of Participant (siblings Regular, Student) denoting a paying/registered participant category. Conference Member is more general than Member, so it subsumes Member (Member is subsumed by Conference Member).

A's 'Chair PC' is a Person who chairs the program committee (a role in the PC), while B's 'Webmaster' is an Organizator responsible for the conference website. They are different roles with different parents (Person vs Organizator) and different siblings (Author, Member PC vs General Chair, Program Chair), so they do not denote the same concept.

A is a document type (an abstract version of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B is a research subject area (a topic under Topic, sibling of Computer Networks Topic etc.). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Attendee is a Person subclass (a human participant), while Record of attendance is a Document subclass (a paper/electronic artefact recording attendance). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Full Version), while Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions). They denote different concepts: one is a type of paper, the other a call/announcement, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a reviewer/review to a paper, but the domains differ (Reviewer vs Review) and the direction is the same only in the sense of connecting a reviewing entity to a paper; they are not the same property.

A's Conference is the event itself (accepts submissions, has dates, administrators, members, logo). B's Conference volume is a publication/volume entity that belongs to a conference and contains contributions, tracks, committees, and parts. The two denote different concepts (event vs. proceedings volume), though they are related since a conference volume belongs to a conference.

A's Topic is a subject area of papers/reviews/conference parts (has a name, belongs to review preferences, is topic of conference parts). B's Place is a physical location where a person can stay (children: Conference hall, Hotel, Main office; property 'can stay in' Person -> Place). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a review expertise' links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (a topic/skill area), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution. Different domains (Submitted contribution vs Author), different ranges (Review expertise vs Contribution), and different intended relations; they are not the same property nor inverses.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to an integer (volume number), while B's 'has Administrative Event' is an object property linking a Working event to an Administrative event. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference (domain Reviewer, range Review expertise/Review preference), while B's property links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a document-like contribution given by an invited speaker), while B's 'Demo Session' is a kind of Session (an event/session in the conference programme). They belong to different branches (contribution vs. event/session) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's `for Event` links a Call to the Academic Event it is issued for (domain Call, range Academic Event). B's `inverse of part Of 7` is the inverse of a part-of relation whose range is Event, i.e. it relates something to an Event as a whole/part relationship, not a call-to-event relation. Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Chairman is a Person role (a chair of a conference/committee, sibling of Program Committee Member, domain of conflict-of-interest marking), while B's Break Event is a non-academic conference event (parent of Coffee Break, Meal Break). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Conference Event) and share no intended instances.

A's Van is a transport vehicle (a means of transport), while B's Organizator is a person role in the conference organization hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches (Item > Transport vehicle vs Person > Organizator) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference domain), while B's Worker non speaker is a subclass of Non speaker under Delegate, i.e. a conference attendee who is not a speaker and works. The two denote different concepts: a student person vs. a working non-speaking delegate; neither subsumes the other.

A 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page/document about the conference, with a URL), while B 'Sponsor company house' is a building/place (a house for sponsor companies). They belong to different branches (document vs. place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a physical place (accommodation venue) under Place, while B is a person role (a non-speaker worker) under Delegate/Non speaker. They denote different kinds of entities (place vs. person) and share no intended instances.

A's max Papers is a datatype property on Program Committee Member with range int, expressing a maximum number of papers a PC member can handle. B's has Name is a datatype property on Conference with range string, giving the conference's full name. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's isReviewHistoryOf links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (a person's history of reviews), while B's hasReview links a Paper to a Review (the review of a paper). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's Dining Place is a specific kind of place (a subclass of Place, sibling to Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Meeting Room Place), whereas B's Place is the general superclass covering buildings, halls, rooms, offices, etc. Dining Place is therefore strictly more specific than Place, i.e. subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a physical location (a subtype of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place), whereas B 'Hotel fee' is a monetary charge (a subtype of Fee, sibling of Registration fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (location vs. cost) and denote different concepts.

A's Paper is a contribution type (a document submitted to a conference, sibling of Poster and Short paper). B's Deadline Paper Submission is a deadline/date for submitting a paper, sibling of Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Author notification. One is a document class, the other a temporal event/deadline; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'Deadline hotel reservation' is a deadline for reserving a hotel room, while B's 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is the deadline for submitting an abstract. Both are subclasses of Deadline but concern different events, so they are not equivalent.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B is a conference activity type (Technic activity, a kind of Conference activity such as a session/lecture) in iasted. They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'enable Virtual Meeting' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an admin enabling a virtual meeting for a conference), while B's 'gives presentations' relates an Active conference participant to a Presentation (a participant giving a talk). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; they are not the same relation.

A Program Committee Member is a specific kind of conference member who reviews papers, while B's Possible Reviewer is the broader class of any person who may review a paper (its child is PC Member). Every PC member is a possible reviewer, but not every possible reviewer is a PC member, so A is strictly more specific than B.

A's Trip is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception) that takes place during the conference, whereas B's Receiving manuscript is an activity before the conference in the manuscript-handling workflow (sibling of Accepting/Refusing manuscript). They denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Session Chair (edas) is a Person role that initiates calls and reviews papers, sitting alongside Conference Chair, Reviewer, TPC Member. B General Chair (sigkdd) is an Organizator role in the organizing committee, sibling of Program Chair and Webmaster. A session chair runs a session, not the whole conference; the general chair heads the conference organization. Different roles, different contexts, so they are not equivalent.

Both are object properties linking a paper/document to its author/person. edas 'is Written By' has domain Paper and range Author; ekaw 'written By' has domain Document and range Person. In the conference domain, Paper and Document denote the same artefact (a submitted paper) and Author and Person denote the same individual, so the two properties relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are equivalent.

Conference Chair is a person role in the conference organisation (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while Dining Place is a physical location (a kind of Place) in the EDAS ontology. They share no meaning, instances, or context; the only overlap is the word 'Chair' in unrelated senses.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a class of conference documents (a submitted paper that was rejected), a subclass of Reviewed contribution. B 'Week Reject Rating' is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a rating value given by a reviewer in a particular week of the review period. One denotes a document, the other a rating value; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's hasRelatedDocument links events/sessions/persons to a Document (a general related-document relation), while B's paperPresentedAs links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the presentation event of a paper). Different domains and ranges, and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Company in confOf is an organizational entity (sibling of University under Organization), while Satellite And Space Communications Topic in edas is a research topic under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'was a committee chair of' relates a Chair to a Committee (a role/leadership relation within the conference organisation), while B's 'heldIn' relates an Event to a Location (a spatiotemporal containment relation). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Conference applicant is a person who applies/registers for a conference (parent Person, child Registeered applicant, siblings include Conference participant and Reviewer), whereas PC Member is a program-committee member, a kind of Possible Reviewer with children PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc. The two denote different roles: an applicant is not a committee member, and the paths/siblings/properties do not overlap.

A's hasStartDateTime is a datatype property linking a Conference Event to a dateTime value, while B's hasEvent is an object property linking an Event to another Event (sub-event structure). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain/range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Rated Papers' is a subclass of Active Paper in the paper-review workflow (papers that have received ratings), while B 'Card' is a subclass of Item with a child Credit card, denoting a physical payment/identity card. Different domains and no shared instances, so unrelated.

A is a document type (the published proceedings volume of a conference, a subclass of Proceedings/Multi author Volume), while B is a role/status of an author (an author who has a CD of the proceedings included), a subclass of Author. They denote different kinds of entities (a publication vs. a person role) and are not equivalent.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person/Contact Information to an email string, while B's Nation links a Person to a country string. They relate different kinds of information (email address vs. nationality), so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference paper in a review workflow (subclass of Paper, with a rating property), while B is a physical item (subclass of Item, with Credit card as a child) in a completely different taxonomy. They share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (co-reviewer invitation), while B's 'reviewer Of Paper' relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the paper being reviewed). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasBid is an object property linking a Paper to a Bid (a review offer), while B's has_amount_of is a datatype property linking Money to an int. Different domains, ranges, and kinds of relation; they do not denote the same relation.

A's hasName is a datatype property giving a Conference's full name (range string), while B's heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's acceptedBy links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it; B's relatedToPaper links a Paper Presentation to the Accepted Paper it presents. Different domain, range and direction of relation, so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person restricted to people involved in a conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), with properties linking it to a Conference. In edas, Person is the broader class covering all people (including attendees, session chairs, etc.) with properties like has Email, has First Name, is Member Of. Conference Member is strictly more specific than Person, so it is subsumed by Person rather than equivalent.

A 'Single hotel room' is a subtype of Hotel room (a lodging place for one person), while B 'Conference hall' is a large venue space for holding the conference itself. They are different kinds of places with no overlap in intended instances.

A's Reviewer is a person who reviews papers and has review expertise/preferences; B's Session Chair is a person who chairs a session and initiates calls. Although both are subclasses of Person and both appear in the 'is Reviewed By'/'is Reviewing' property ranges in edas, the Session Chair is a distinct role (session organiser) from a Reviewer (paper evaluator). They are different concepts, not synonyms.

In sigkdd, Program Committee is a sibling of Organizing Committee under Committee, so they are distinct committees. In cmt, Program Committee is the committee of reviewers. The two denote different committees (program/reviewer committee vs. organizing committee), though both are committees, so they are related but not equivalent.

A's 'has a steering committee' links a Conference volume to its Steering committee (a sub-property of 'has a committee'), while B's 'hold' links an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference it holds. Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Social Event is a broad category of non-academic conference events with children Excursion and Reception, while B's Dinner banquet is a specific social-program activity (a banquet dinner). A Dinner banquet is a kind of social event, so Social Event is more general and subsumes Dinner banquet.

Associated Chair is a conference committee role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while Dining Place is a physical location (a kind of Place). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A 'Regular Session' is a kind of scientific event session (a slot in the conference programme), while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee (a group of people). Different domains (event vs. committee), no shared instances; unrelated.

In cmt, Author is a broad role for anyone who writes/submits papers (with children Author Not Reviewer and Co author, and properties write Paper, submit Paper). In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a narrower class under Author (path Person > Speaker > Author > Author of paper), with sibling 'Author of paper student'. The sigkdd class denotes specifically an author of a paper, a subclass of the more general Author role in cmt. Thus cmt Author is more general and sigkdd Author of paper is subsumed by it.

A's 'has a publisher' relates a Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organisation/person publishing the proceedings), while B's 'writtenBy' relates a Document to a Person who authored it. Different domain, different range, and different intended relation (publishing vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

coversTopic relates an Event/Paper to a Research Topic (the subject matter a paper or event is about), while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (the act of a speaker presenting a document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

IASTED non member is a subclass of Delegate (a person/attendee category), while Conference hall is a subclass of Place (a physical location). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A's 'is paid with' relates Money to an Item (the thing money is used to pay for), while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (the payer). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they are not the same relation.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses like Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author), whereas Presenter house is a subclass of Building/Place (a physical building where presenters stay). They belong to disjoint top-level categories (Person vs Place) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

has Menu relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (the menu of a meal event), while need relates a Person to an Item (something a person requires). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name; B's 'remark' is a datatype property of Contribution holding a free-text note (comment 'confTool'). Different domains (Person vs Contribution) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A Poster Session is a type of Session (a scientific event where posters are presented), while a Plenary lecture is a type of Lecture (a talk given to all attendees). They belong to different branches (Session vs Lecture) and denote different kinds of conference activities, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to its Committee (a part-of/structural relation), while B's 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event (an agentive relation). Different domains and ranges, different directions of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration), while B's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (an academic conference with tutorials/workshops as siblings), while B's Conference restaurant is a building/place (a restaurant facility at a conference venue, sibling to Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc.). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. physical place), so they are unrelated.

Company (confOf) is an Organization subtype representing a corporate entity, while Author of paper (sigkdd) is a Person subtype representing someone who authored a paper. They belong to disjoint top-level branches (Organization vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type, with children like Assigned Paper and siblings like Camera Ready Paper), while B is a subclass of Deadline (a time point for notification of acceptance). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. time) and denote different concepts.

Both properties relate a document/paper to its authors: Conference's 'has authors' has domain Conference document and range Person, while ekaw's 'written By' has domain Document and range Person. In the conference domain, a document's authors are exactly those who wrote it, so the two relations denote the same concept in the same direction.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with a two-level programme committee structure), while B 'Student' is a kind of person. Their intended instances are disjoint (events vs. people), so they are unrelated despite both being classes in the conference domain.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a kind of conference contributor (a person invited to give a talk), while B's 'Tutorial speaker' is a kind of Author who gives a tutorial; the two denote different roles with different contexts and no subsumption relation.

A is a document/form artefact ('Author information form') in the iasted ontology, a subclass of Form alongside registration forms; B is a person role ('Author of paper') in the sigkdd ontology, a subclass of Author/Person. One denotes a form document, the other a person, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an email' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (an email address), while B's 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A Demo Chair is a conference participant role responsible for demo sessions, while a Program Committee member is an organizer role reviewing papers. They are different roles in the conference domain, with different parents (Conference Participant vs Organizator) and different siblings (Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair vs General Chair, Program Chair).

Company in confOf is a subtype of Organization (a business entity, sibling of University), whereas Hotel in sigkdd is a subtype of Place (a physical venue, sibling of Conference hall and Main office). They denote different concepts: an organisation vs. a location, so they are not equivalent.

Both entities denote the same concept in the conference domain: the class of conference papers/contributions. The labels 'Paper' and 'Contribution' are synonyms in this context, and their paths, siblings, and properties (e.g., authoredBy, hasAuthor) agree, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (paper). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A Published Paper is a Paper in a state of the publication workflow (siblings: Accepted, Pending, Rejected, Withdrawn), i.e. a paper that has been published. B Final manuscript is a Submission (sibling: Initial manuscript), i.e. the final version of a submitted document. Both concern the final/published version of a paper, so they overlap, but they are not the same concept: one is a paper in a publication state, the other a submission document version. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference www to a string URL, while B's 'has Name' links a Conference to its full name string. They relate different kinds of information (URL vs. name), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Committee member' is a general role for anyone serving on a committee (with subroles Chair, Co chair), while B 'Session Chair' is a specific role chairing a session. They overlap in that a session chair is a person involved in the conference organisation, but neither subsumes the other: a committee member need not chair a session, and a session chair need not be a committee member. Hence related, not equivalent.

A 'Test Only Topic' is a placeholder topic in the EDAS topic taxonomy (sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B 'Best Research Paper Award' is a type of Award (sibling of Best Applications Paper Award, Best Student Paper Award). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic classification vs. award) and share no intended instances.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string postal code, while B's is_used_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' is a meronymic property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume (domain Conference part, range Conference volume), while B's 'part Of Event' is a generic mereological property linking an Event to a sub-Event (domain Event, range Event). Both express a part-of relation, but they relate different kinds of entities (conference parts/volumes vs. events), so they are not equivalent; they are only broadly related as part-of relations.

A's 'paper In Volume' relates a paper to the volume/proceedings it appears in (a bibliographic containment relation), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/presenting something). Different domain (paper vs person) and different range (volume vs activity/item), so the relations are not the same.

A's Poster is a kind of conference contribution (a document/paper presented as a poster), while B's Speaker is a person role (a person who gives a presentation). They belong to different top-level branches (document vs person) and have incompatible properties (Poster has an abstract; Speaker presents a Document), so they do not denote the same concept.

A's has Topic relates a Conference/Paper to a Topic (subject matter), while B's presentationed by relates a Document to a Speaker (the person who presented it). Different domain, different range, and different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A is a person role (Session Chair, a Conference Participant/PC Member who chairs a session), while B is an event type (Session, a kind of Lecture/Conference activity). One denotes a person, the other an activity, so their instances cannot coincide; they are unrelated despite the shared word 'Session'.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a paper), while B's designed_by relates a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (who set the deadline). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

A's Conference is the event itself (has members, dates, accepts submissions, administered by an Administrator), while B's Conference proceedings is the published volume of collected papers (has a publisher, volume, ISBN). Different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

A's Topic is a subject area of contributions, PC members and working events (dealsWith, expertOn, hasTopic). B's Place is a physical location with subclasses Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office, Session room and properties about being situated, equipped, held in, etc. The two denote entirely different concepts (subject matter vs. location), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a Conference contributor (a person who gives an invited talk), while B's 'Worker non speaker' is a Delegate/Non speaker, i.e. an attendee who works but does not present. They denote different roles: one is a speaker, the other explicitly a non-speaker, and their paths (Person > Conference contributor vs Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Non speaker) share no common concept.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime. A's hasSubmissionDeadline is the deadline date of a Call; B's Date is the date of a Deadline. In the conference domain, the submission deadline of a call is exactly the date attached to the deadline entity, so the two properties denote the same relation (a call/deadline to its dateTime). The differing domain names (Call vs Deadline) reflect the ontologies' modelling of the same concept, not a semantic difference.

Author (confOf) is a subclass of Person representing someone who writes contributions, with properties writes/written By linking to Contribution. Conference Session (edas) is an event/session entity that relates to Documents and academic events, not a person. Different kinds of things with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Session is a broad Scientific Event with children such as Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session and Workshop Session, i.e. a generic grouping of presentations. In iasted, Plenary lecture is a specific kind of Lecture (a talk), sibling to Session and Tutorial, so it denotes a single plenary talk rather than a session grouping. The two concepts differ in specificity and intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A is Conference Chair (chair of the whole conference, under Chairman), while B is Workshop Chair (chair of a workshop, under Conference Participant). Different roles with different scopes; neither subsumes the other.

A's 'written By' links a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it (domain Review, range Reviewer). B's 'invited by' links a Reviewer to the Reviewer who invited them (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer). Different domain, different intended meaning (authorship vs. invitation), so they are not equivalent.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title; B's City of conference is a datatype property of Conference giving the city where the conference is held. Different domains (Paper vs Conference) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Call is a call-for-submissions entity (children Call For Papers/Reviews/Manuscripts, linked to Academic Event and deadlines), while B's Abstract is a document subtype (sibling of Paper, Review, Flyer) representing an abstract text. Different concepts despite both being conference-domain entities.

cmt's writtenBy relates a Review to its Reviewer (domain Review, range Reviewer), while iasted's write relates a Person to an Item (domain Person, range Item). They are inverses/overlapping notions of authorship (a person writes an item vs. a review is written by a reviewer), not the same relation in the same direction, so they are related rather than equivalent.

An Invited speaker is a specific kind of conference contributor who gives a talk, while Speaker in iasted is a broad class of delegates that includes authors, reviewers, session chairs, etc. Every invited speaker is a speaker, but not every speaker is an invited speaker, so Invited speaker is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Speaker.

In edas, Paper is a broad document class whose children include Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, Pending Paper, Withdrawn Paper, etc., and which is written by authors and has topics. In ekaw, Evaluated Paper is a narrower class under Assigned Paper, with only Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper as children, i.e. a paper that has received a review decision. Every Evaluated Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper (e.g. a submitted or withdrawn paper) is an Evaluated Paper, so edas Paper is more general and the ekaw class is subsumed by it.

A is a chair role in the conference committee hierarchy (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while B is a registered conference applicant who has paid early. They belong to entirely different branches (organizer/chair vs. attendee/applicant) and share no intended instances.

A's 'Hotel room' is a lodging room (with children Double/Single hotel room) under Place, while B's 'Conference hall' is a meeting venue under Place. They are different kinds of places and neither subsumes the other.

A's Topic is the general class of conference topics (it is the range of 'has a track workshop tutorial topic' and domain of 'has a name'/'is a topis of conference parts'), while B's Microelectronics Topic is a specific topic under the parent Topic in edas. Microelectronics Topic is therefore a narrower concept, strictly subsumed by the general Topic class.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is an administrative event (the submission event in the conference process). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's Reviewer is a role a delegate/speaker takes on to review papers, while B's Invited Speaker is a distinguished speaker invited to present; they are different roles in the conference domain despite both being subclasses of Speaker.
Both are datatype properties named hasCity relating an entity (conference/contact information) to a city string; same label, same kind, same intended relation in the conference domain.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving the ISBN string of a proceedings volume. B's 'has Submission Instructions' is a datatype property of Call giving submission instructions text. They belong to different subject classes (proceedings vs. call) and denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

A's Simulating is a research activity (sibling of Modelling, under Activity before conference > Research), while B's Webmaster is an organizational role/person (under Person > Organizator). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Person is a human agent class (children Delegate, Sponsor; domain/range of give, is given by, is paid by, etc.), while B's Deadline is a temporal milestone class (children are submission/notification deadlines; properties Date, submit until). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a specific kind of contribution (one that was reviewed and rejected), while B 'Contribution' is the general class covering all submissions (Paper, Poster, Short paper). A is strictly narrower than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

Both are Document subclasses representing the conference programme: edas Programme is linked to a Conference Event via belongs To Event / has Programme, and ekaw Programme Brochure is linked to Events via event On List / lists Event and is published by an Organisation. Same intended artefact (the printed/electronic programme of the conference), so they are equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Conference part (domain Topic, range Conference part), while B's partOf is a generic mereological property with unspecified domain/range. They overlap in the part-whole sense but A is a domain-specific topic-to-part relation, not the same concept as the general partOf.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to the Administrator who started reviewer bidding, while B's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to the people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'written By' is an object property linking a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'Nation' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (nationality). They have different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'starts on' is a datatype property of Event giving a start date/time (string), while B's 'Name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's name. Different domains, different ranges, different intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's property records the acceptance-announcement date of a conference (domain Important dates, range date), while B's property records whether a participant registered early (domain Participant, range boolean). Different domains, ranges and meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Both classes denote a conference contribution: A's 'Conference contribution' is a kind of conference document with children Invited talk, Poster, Presentation, Regular contribution, Written contribution, and is linked to a conference volume via has contributions / is submitted at; B's 'Contribution' has children Paper, Poster, Short paper and is written by an Author, reviewed by a PC member, and has title/abstract/keywords. The intended instances (papers, posters, talks submitted to a conference) coincide, so the classes are equivalent despite differing labels and surrounding structure.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Conference hall is a physical Place (sibling of Building, Hotel room, Session room). One denotes an event, the other a venue/location, so they are not equivalent.

A's Scientific Event is a subclass of Event covering conferences, workshops, sessions, etc.; B's Author is a subclass of Speaker/Person denoting a person who writes papers. They belong to different branches of the conference domain (event vs. person) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (where a scholar studies/works), while B's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an excursion/outing) under Social Event, while a Coffee break is a scheduled conference activity (a break for refreshments) under Conference activity. They denote different concepts: one is a social outing, the other a refreshment pause, so they are not equivalent.

A's Published Paper is a Paper in a publication state (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), i.e. a full paper that has been published. B's Abstract is a distinct document type (sibling of Paper and Review), the short abstract text, not a published paper. Different concepts despite both being Documents.

A's hasConflictOfInterest is a specific relation from a Person to a Document (the paper/contribution that person is conflicted about). B's is_connected_with is a very general relation from Activity or Person to Item or Place, covering any connection. The domains and ranges differ substantially, and the intended meanings do not coincide; the specific conflict-of-interest relation is not the same as a generic connection relation.

Both classes denote a person who reviews papers. In cmt, Reviewer is a Conference Member/User with review-related properties (bid, assignment, conflict of interest, reading papers). In Conference, Reviewer is a Person with review expertise/preference and co-reviewer relations. The intended instances coincide: individuals who perform reviews. The differing parent structure (Conference Member vs Person) reflects ontology design, not a difference in concept.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person (path Person > Student), so every Student is a Person. In iasted, Person is a broad class with children Delegate and Sponsor and many properties (give, is given by, is paid by, etc.) covering all human participants. Student is strictly more specific than Person, so Student is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.

A's reject Paper relates an Administrator to a Paper (a rejection action), while B's has a publisher relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher (a publication attribute). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Author is a person role (a conference member who writes/submits papers), while Track is a subdivision of a conference (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, part of a Conference volume). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people/committees), while B's is_a_topis_of_conference_parts relates a Topic to a Conference part (e.g. tracks/events). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Short paper' is a contribution type distinguished by length/format, while B 'Industrial Paper' is a paper distinguished by its industrial (non-academic) provenance. They are different classification dimensions and neither subsumes the other; a short paper can be academic or industrial, and an industrial paper can be short or regular. No reference alignment would equate them.

A's Possible Reviewer is a person role in the review process (a subclass of Person, superclass of PC Member, involved in reviewing papers). B's Sponzor is a funding/sponsorship entity with subtypes like Gold Supporter and Exhibitor, and properties linking it to ACM SIGKDD and a sponsor name. The two denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a monetary fee in the conference domain. In iasted, Fee is a subclass of Money with children for extra trip, hotel, and registration fees; in sigkdd, Fee has children for registration and sponsor fees. The shared label, shared parent concept of money/payment, and overlapping children (registration fee) indicate the same intended concept.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a subtype of Regular contribution (a full-length submission category), while B's 'Demo Paper' is a subtype of Paper denoting a demonstration submission. They are different submission categories in the conference domain, not synonyms; no subsumption holds either.

A's Paper is a submitted document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions, subject areas). B's Call is a call-for-papers/manuscripts/reviews announcement issued by chairs with submission deadlines and instructions. They denote different concepts: a paper is the artefact, a call is the solicitation event. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A 'Paper Abstract' is the abstract/short version of a paper (sibling of 'Paper Full Version' under Paper), whereas B 'Poster Paper' is a paper intended for poster presentation (sibling of Conference Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). They denote different kinds of paper: one is a document-version distinction, the other a presentation-format distinction. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

ConferenceVenuePlace is a specific kind of place (a venue where a conference is held), while sigkdd's Place is a general location class with children Conference hall, Hotel, Main office and a 'can stay in' property. The EDAS class is strictly narrower than the general Place, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

Ontology A's 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant under Conference applicant, denoting a person who registered and paid late. Ontology B's 'Renting' is an activity before the conference, sibling to manuscript handling and research activities. The two entities belong to different branches (person vs. activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Poster Paper' is a kind of academic Paper (a document submitted/presented at a conference), while B 'Silver Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor (sponsor). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. sponsorship) and share no intended instances.

A's Conference Trip is a social event (a trip organised during the conference, sibling of Conference Banquet), whereas B's Sponsor city is a type of City (a city category, sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Trip city). They denote different concepts: an event vs. a city classification, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Chair PC' is a generic PC chair role directly under Person (siblings include Member PC, Author, Participant), while B's 'Tutorial Chair' is a specific conference-participant role under Conference Participant and PC Member, sibling to Workshop Chair, Demo Chair, etc. They denote different roles (general PC chair vs. tutorial chair), so they are not equivalent.

A relates a Conference to an Administrator (who prints hardcopy mailing manifests), while B relates an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation event. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A Reviewer is a Person who reviews papers, while B's Conference Participant is a broad class covering all people involved in a conference (chairs, presenters, authors, etc.). A reviewer is a kind of conference participant, so Reviewer is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Conference Participant. Note B also has a separate 'Possible Reviewer' class, confirming Reviewer is not equivalent to the general Conference Participant.

A's State is a geographical/administrative region (a place that occupies/visits persons, situated in other places), while B's Speaker is a person role (a subclass of Person that presents documents). They share no intended instances and belong to different branches of the conference domain.

Break Event is a specific kind of non-academic conference event (a break, with children Coffee Break, Free Time Break, Meal Break), whereas ekaw's Event is the most general event class, with children Scientific Event and Social Event. Break Event is therefore strictly narrower than Event, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'enter Conference Details' is an Administrator action whose domain is Administrator and range is Conference, i.e. an admin entering data about a conference. B's 'organises' relates an Organisation or Person to an Event, i.e. organising an event. Different domains (Administrator vs Organisation/Person) and different intended meanings (data entry vs organising), so they are not equivalent.

Organizer in the Conference ontology is a person/role responsible for arranging a conference, whereas Organizational Meeting in edas is a type of academic event (a meeting held to organise the conference), so the two denote different concepts despite the shared word 'organiz'.

ekaw:Event is a broad class of occurrences (scientific/social events) that can be organised, held in a location, and cover topics. iasted:Place is a physical location (building, room, hall) that activities are held in and people are present in. Event and Place denote different kinds of entities (occurrences vs. locations), so they are not equivalent.

A's Associated Chair is a chair/committee-role class (a kind of Chairman and Conference Member, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), whereas B's Member PC is a program-committee member/reviewer (comment 'Reviewer', reviews Contributions, expert on Topics). A chair role and a PC member/reviewer role are distinct concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution (a document submitted to a conference, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract). B's 'Card' is an Item with child Credit card, sibling of Document, Publication, Transport vehicle — a physical payment/identity card, not a conference document. Different domains and no shared context, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific chair role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair), whereas Science Worker in confOf is a broad category of person (sibling of Author, Participant, Scholar, etc.) with no chair-specific meaning. The two denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session in which accepted papers are presented), while B 'Author of paper student' is a subclass of Author (a person role, a student author of a paper). They belong to different branches (event vs. person) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a role/class of authors who co-authored a contribution (a sub-role of Regular author within the document/contribution branch), whereas B's 'Participant' is a general person role at a conference (parent of Member, Regular, Student, etc., with an early-registration property). The intended instances do not coincide: a co-author is a specific authorship role, not a conference participant in general. Different paths, parents, siblings and properties confirm they are unrelated concepts.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an admin entering conference data), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presenting a document). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

Conference applicant is a Person subtype (someone applying to attend), while Committee in sigkdd is an organizational group with subcommittees (Best Paper Awards, Organizing, Program). Different kinds of entities: person vs. group; no overlap.

A's 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor (a role a person plays as author of a regular contribution), while B's 'Regular' is a subclass of Participant (a person who is a regular participant, not a student or member). Different paths, parents and siblings: one is an authorship role within contributions, the other a participant type. They do not denote the same concept.

Demo Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a paper submitted for a demo), while sigkdd's Paper is the general class of conference papers. Demo Paper is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by Paper, not equivalent.

Both classes denote the central conference event in the conference-organisation domain. A's Conference has properties for submissions, dates, administrators, members and logo; B's Conference is the top-level event class with a child Conference volume and a name property. The labels and domain roles match, so they are equivalent.

A's 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a part/committee relation), while B's 'hold' links an ACM SIGKDD to a Conference (an event-hosting relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (a reviewer inviting co-reviewers), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a document being presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document (path Document > Paper) and is a specific artefact with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, plus properties like accept Paper, assigned To, has Decision. In ekaw, Document is a broad class whose children include Abstract, Flyer, Multi author Volume, Paper, Programme Brochure, Review, Web Site, and whose properties (author Of, written By, has Updated Version) apply to any document. Thus cmt:Paper is strictly more specific than ekaw:Document; every cmt Paper is an ekaw Document but not vice versa, so Paper is subsumed by Document, not equivalent.

Ontology A's Conference is the central conference-organisation class (accepts submissions, has members, deadlines, review criteria). Ontology B's Conference_airport is a physical building/location (sibling of Conference building, Conference hotel, Conference restaurant) under Building. Different intended instances: an event vs. a venue building, so they are unrelated.

Attendee is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference), while Nonauthor registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (authorship of a paper), while B's 'designed by' links a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (who set the deadline). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Research Institute' is an academic organisation (a type of institution, sibling of University under Academic Institution), whereas B 'Simulating' is a research activity (a subtype of Research under Activity before conference). They denote different kinds of entities (organisation vs. activity) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's has VAT is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a tax string; B's done till is a datatype property of Deadline giving a date. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

hasAdministrativeEvent is a specialized sub-property of ekaw's hasEvent: its domain (Working event) and range (Administrative event) are both subclasses of ekaw's Event, and it only relates working events to administrative events, whereas hasEvent relates any Event to any Event. Thus confOf's property is strictly narrower (subsumed by) ekaw's hasEvent, not equivalent.

A's 'Accept Rating' is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a value/rating category used in the review process. B's 'Reviewer' is a subclass of Speaker under Delegate, i.e. a person role in the conference. A rating category and a person role denote completely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both properties express the location of an event-like entity, but they differ in kind and range: A's 'has a location' is a datatype property from Conference volume to a string, while B's 'is held in' is an object property from Activity to Place/Time. They overlap in intent (where something takes place) but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a preference/interest of a topic in being reviewed), while B's hasReview links a Paper to a Review (the actual review of a paper). Different domains (Topic vs Paper), different ranges (Review preference vs Review), and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Conference participant is a general Person role with subclasses Active/Passive conference participant, covering all persons involved in a conference. Conference Hiker is a specific subclass of Delegate in the iasted ontology, i.e. a particular kind of conference attendee/delegate. Thus Conference Hiker is narrower than Conference participant, so Conference participant subsumes Conference Hiker (equivalently, Conference Hiker is subsumed by Conference participant). They are not equivalent because the A class is broader and includes roles not covered by the B class.

A's Paper is a document/contribution class (a regular contribution with an abstract, sibling of Extended abstract), while B's Paper Author is a subclass of Person denoting an author of a paper. They are different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Presenter is a Conference Participant who gives a presentation (sibling of Session Chair, PC Chair, etc., child Invited Speaker). In sigkdd, Organizator is a Person who organises the conference (parent of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc.), a role disjoint from presenting. Different intended instances and different positions in the hierarchy, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'Rejected Paper' is a paper that has been evaluated and rejected (sibling of Accepted Paper under Evaluated Paper). B's 'Initial manuscript' is the first version of a submission (sibling of Final manuscript under Submission), with no evaluation/rejection semantics. Different concepts.

confOf's University is a sibling of Company under Organization, while ekaw's Research Institute is a sibling of University under Academic Institution. They are both academic organisations but neither subsumes the other: a university is not a research institute and vice versa, though they overlap as academic institutions.

A's 'Paid applicant' is a subclass of 'Registeered applicant' (a person who has registered and paid), with children 'Early paid applicant' and 'Late paid applicant'. B's 'Early Registered Participant' is a subclass of 'Conference Participant' and is a sibling of 'Late Registered Participant', 'Presenter', 'Session Chair', etc. The two classes sit in different taxonomies: A's class is about payment status of an applicant, B's class is about early registration among conference participants. Neither subsumes the other, and their intended instances do not coincide.

A's Workshop is a scientific event (a kind of conference event with papers/sessions), while B's Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. They belong to different branches (Event vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.
A's email is a Person's email address; B's has First Name is a Person's given name. Different datatype properties with different intended values, despite both being Person->string.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered early and paid), while B is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount for nonmembers). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote a person vs a fee, so they are not equivalent.

A's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author (authorship relation), while B's updatedVersionOf relates a Document to another Document (versioning relation). Different domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper they author), while B's 'volumeContainsPaper' relates a conference volume/proceedings to a paper it contains. Different domain and range and different direction of meaning, so they are not equivalent.
