A's 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B's 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (a kind of Conference, sibling of Single Level Conference). They denote different kinds of things (person role vs. event type) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Paid applicant' is a person (a registered conference applicant who has paid), while B 'Travel Grant' is a sponsorship/funding category, not a person. Their paths, parents and intended instances differ, so they are not equivalent.

Both are registration-fee classes for attendees who are not members: iasted's 'Nonauthor registration fee' sits under Registration fee alongside member/student/author fees, and sigkdd's 'Registration Non Member' sits under Registration fee alongside SIGKDD/SIGMOD member and student fees. The intended instances (non-member registration fees) coincide, so they are equivalent.

Associated Chair in cmt is a kind of Chairman/Conference Member (a person chairing/assisting in the conference organisation), while Webmaster in sigkdd is an Organizator responsible for the website. They are different organisational roles with no subsumption or overlap.

Company in confOf is an organizational entity (sibling of University under Organization), i.e. a type of institution. Computer Networks Enterprise Topic in edas is a research topic about enterprise computer networks, a subclass of Computer Networks Topic. They denote different concepts (organization vs. topic) and share no intended instances.
A is a specific deadline type (hotel reservation deadline) in iasted, while B is the general Deadline class in sigkdd. A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

Country in confOf is a geopolitical entity used as the range of has Country (Organization/Person -> Country). Place in iasted is a physical location with subclasses Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office, Session room and is used for physical containment (is situated in, is held in, is present in). A country is not a physical place in the iasted sense, and the contexts (geopolitical affiliation vs. physical location) do not coincide.

A 'Hotel presenter' is a kind of Delegate (a person who presents at a hotel venue), while B 'Conference hall' is a Place (a building/room). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'reviews Per Paper' is a datatype property from Conference to int, counting the number of reviews per paper. B's 'write' is an object property from Person to Item, relating a person to what they write. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Person), range (int vs Item), and meaning (a count vs an authorship relation), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper, with properties co write Paper / has Co author). B's 'Personal Review History' is a subclass of Personal History, an information record about a Reviewer's reviews (properties has Review History / is Review History Of). One is a person role, the other a data record; their instances and relations do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has authors' relates a Conference document to its authors (Person), a standard authorship relation. B's 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person in a requirement/dependency sense (an item needed by a person), not authorship. The domains differ (Conference document vs Item) and the intended meanings do not coincide, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while B's 'designed by' links a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (who set the deadline). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Trip' is a social event (an activity, sibling of Conference Banquet) in ekaw, while B 'Conference airport' is a physical building/place (sibling of Conference hotel, Conference building) in iasted. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A Tutorial is a working event (a session type in the conference programme) under Event > Working event, while B Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment under Item > Audiovisual equipment. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (event vs. equipment) and share no intended instances.

A's 'has a URL' is a datatype property of Conference www giving a web address (string), while B's 'City of conference' gives the city where a conference is held. They relate different kinds of information (URL vs. city) and are not the same relation, so they are unrelated.

A's reviewCriteriaEnteredBy relates a Conference to an Administrator (who entered review criteria), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (author writes a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), i.e. the final verdict that a paper is rejected. B's Week Reject Rating is a review rating category (sibling of Accept Rating, Reject Rating, etc. under Review Rating), i.e. a per-reviewer score used during reviewing. They belong to different branches (decision vs. review rating) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Contribution 1th author' is a role of a person (first author of a conference contribution), while B 'Single hotel room' is a type of hotel room accommodation. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (authorship vs. venue/accommodation) and share no intended instances.

A 'Plenary lecture' is a kind of conference activity/lecture (an event), while B 'Program Committee' is a committee (a group of people). They belong to different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property linking a Conference proceedings to a string ISBN. B's 'publisher Of' is an object property linking an Organisation (publisher) to published artefacts (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have different domains/ranges, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'designed by' relates a Deadline to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (who set the deadline). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Paper Full Version in cmt is a document type (the full version of a paper, sibling of Paper Abstract), whereas Pending Paper in edas is a submission status (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published/Withdrawn Paper). They denote different concepts: a full paper is not a pending paper, and the status dimension is orthogonal to the document-type dimension.

Scholar in confOf is a subclass of Person (a person category, with a study At property to University), while Nonmember registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Registration fee under Money (a fee amount). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. monetary fee), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a name' is a general naming property whose domain is Publisher/Topic/Conference proceedings (a broad naming attribute), while B's 'has short title' is a specific abbreviation property for Social/Working events. Different domains and different intended meanings (full name vs. short title), so they are not equivalent.

Banquet is a specific kind of social event (a meal/feast), while ekaw's Social Event is the general category covering banquets, trips and receptions. Banquet is therefore strictly narrower than Social Event, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a social event (an organized activity during a conference, sibling of Conference Banquet), while B Car is a type of transport vehicle (sibling of Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). Although a conference trip may involve a car, the classes denote different concepts: an event/activity versus a physical vehicle. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's User is a Person subtype (a human role: author/reviewer/administrator), while B's Conference Session is a Session subtype (an event). Different branches (Person vs Event) and incompatible instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer they are assigned to (domain External Reviewer, range Reviewer). B's 'has been assigned a review reference' links a Submitted contribution/Topic to a Review preference (domain Submitted contribution, Topic, range Review preference). The domains and ranges are entirely different concepts, so the two properties do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are not equivalent.

A's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location (a place), while B's 'is dated on' is a datatype property linking an Activity to a dateTime (a temporal value). They relate different kinds of entities (place vs. time) and have different ranges, so they are not the same relation.

Both are the direct subclass of Event covering the professional/scientific side of the conference (conferences, workshops, tutorials/sessions), as opposed to social/administrative events. confOf's Working event has children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop and siblings Administrative event, Social event; ekaw's Scientific Event has children Conference, Workshop, Session, Track, Individual Presentation and sibling Social Event. The intended instances coincide: the working/scientific events of a conference.

Paper Abstract is a subclass of Paper (a document type), while Web Site is a sibling of Paper under Document, representing a web resource with properties like event On List and publisher Of. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Review Rating (edas) is a class of rating values assigned to a paper's review (children Accept Rating, Reject Rating, etc., domain of has Rating from Active Paper), whereas Possible Reviewer (ekaw) is a subclass of Person representing a person who may review papers (parent Person, child PC Member, range of has Reviewer and review Written By). One denotes a rating value, the other a person role; they share no instances and are unrelated.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to its Decision (accept/reject outcome), while B's hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event (part-of hierarchy). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'enter Conference Details' is an Administrator action whose range is a Conference (the administrator enters details of a conference), while B's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domain (Administrator vs Event), different range (Conference vs Organisation/Person), and different meaning (data-entry action vs organisational responsibility), so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties of Conference with a date/time range, but cmt's `date` is a generic conference date (likely the conference start/occurrence date), whereas sigkdd's `End of conference` specifically denotes the conference's end date. They overlap in the conference-date domain but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Publisher (Conference) is an organisation that issues conference proceedings, with properties has a name and issues (Publisher -> Conference proceedings). Research Topic (ekaw) is a subject area covered by events and papers, with properties covers Topic and topic Covered By. The two denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Author is a general person role in the conference domain (parent Person, children Presenter, properties has Related Paper / is Written By). B's 'Author book proceedings included' is a very specific subclass of Author in iasted, denoting an author whose book/proceedings contribution is included, sibling to 'Author cd proceedings included', Lecturer, Plenary lecture speaker, Tutorial speaker. The two do not denote the same concept; B is a narrow specialisation, not the general Author class, so they are unrelated (or at most B subsumed_by A, but the intended concepts differ).

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property on Review expertise (a review's expertise value), while B's 'expert On' is an object property from Member PC to Topic (a PC member's topic expertise). Different domains, ranges, and kinds (datatype vs object), so they do not denote the same relation.

Author is a person/role class (a conference member who writes papers), while Individual Presentation is an event class (a scientific event such as a talk or tutorial). Their paths, parents, siblings and properties are entirely different: Author has properties like write Paper and submit Paper, whereas Individual Presentation has presentation Of Paper and paper Presented As. They denote different concepts and are unrelated.

PC Member in ekaw is a specific reviewer role (a subclass of Possible Reviewer, with children such as PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair). Organizator in sigkdd is a broader class covering all conference organizers, including General Chair, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster, etc. A PC Member is one kind of organizer role, so PC Member is strictly more specific than Organizator; they are not equivalent.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a conference attendee who does not actively contribute (sibling of 'Active conference participant' under 'Conference participant'), whereas B 'Organizing Committee member' is a person who organizes the conference (subclass of 'Organizator', sibling of chairs and PC members). The intended instances differ: passive participants attend, organizing committee members organize. Different concepts, so unrelated.

A's Programme is a conference programme document (sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set; linked to a Conference Event via belongs To Event / has Programme), whereas B's Review is a review document (sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter). Different intended instances; the shared parent Document is not enough.

A 'Camera ready contribution' is a contribution that has been accepted and is in its final camera-ready form, while B 'Accepted Paper' is any paper that has been accepted, including those not yet in camera-ready form. The camera-ready stage is a narrower, later stage of the accepted-paper lifecycle, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

In cmt, External Reviewer is a person who reviews for another Reviewer but is explicitly not a Reviewer, and is tied to Reviewer via assign/assignedBy. In ekaw, Possible Reviewer is a broad class of anyone who could review a paper (parent of PC Member, with has Reviewer, review Written By, reviewer Of Paper), i.e. a potential reviewer rather than a non-reviewer assistant. The intended instances do not coincide: cmt's class excludes Reviewers while ekaw's includes PC Members and other potential reviewers, so the classes are not equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference announcement document soliciting submissions, while B 'Abstract' is a short summary of a paper. They are different document types with different roles in the conference domain; the shared parent 'Document'/'Conference document' is too generic to imply equivalence.

Author in cmt is a subclass of Person (path Person > Conference Member > Author) and denotes someone who writes/submits papers, whereas Person in Conference is the general superclass covering all people (committee members, applicants, participants, reviewers). Author is strictly more specific than Person, so Author is subsumed by Person, not equivalent.

Attendee in edas is a generic participant in a conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles), while Organizator in sigkdd is a person who organizes the conference (parent of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc.). The intended instances do not coincide: an attendee is not necessarily an organizer, and an organizer is a specific staff role, not a generic attendee. Thus the classes are unrelated.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (a subclass of Conference in edas, alongside Single Level Conference), while B 'Program Chair' is a person role in the organizing committee (subclass of Organizator in sigkdd). They denote entirely different concepts—an event type versus a person role—so they are unrelated.

Chairman in cmt is a general person role that subsumes the more specific chair roles (Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair), whereas sigkdd's General Chair is a specific organizational role under Organizator, sibling to Program Chair and Webmaster. The cmt Chairman is broader than the sigkdd General Chair, so it subsumes it rather than being equivalent.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document type (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc. under Conference document), while B's 'Reception' is a social event (child of Social Event). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts (a whole-part relation, subproperty of has parts), while B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (membership). Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Conference part to a Topic (thematic classification of tracks/workshops/tutorials), while B's property links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper), while B's `reviewerOfPaper` relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the reviewer reviews the paper). Different domain (Author vs Possible Reviewer) and different intended relation (authorship vs reviewing), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a distinguished conference contributor (a Person subtype, sibling of Regular author), while B's 'Student lecturer' is a specific kind of Lecturer/Author/Speaker within a Delegate hierarchy, denoting a student who lectures. The concepts differ in both role and domain; they are not the same concept.

A's max Choice is a datatype property giving the maximum number of choices/participants for a social or working event (range positiveInteger, comment confTool), while B's organised By is an object property linking an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

Administrative event in confOf is a subclass of Event covering submission, reviewing, registration, camera-ready, etc. Committee in sigkdd is an organizational group (organizing, program, best paper awards committees), not an event. They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap.

A's Taxi is a transport vehicle class (sibling of Car, Shuttle bus, Van) in the iasted ontology, while B's Organizator is a person role (subclass of Person, parent of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.) in the sigkdd ontology. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'is sent before' is an object property linking an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering relation). They share neither domain/range nor meaning, so they are unrelated.

A is a specific kind of registration fee (for nonmembers), while B is the general Registration fee class with children for member, non-member, and student registrations. A is therefore strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, linking a person to their email address; the labels 'has an email' and 'E mail' denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Both properties relate a review/item to the person who wrote it, in the same direction. cmt's writtenBy has domain Review and range Reviewer; iasted's is_writen_by has domain Item and range Person. In the conference domain, a Review is a kind of Item and a Reviewer is a kind of Person, so the intended relation (author of a review) coincides. The label similarity and matching domain/range specialisation support equivalence.

Paper Abstract in cmt is the abstract/summary document of a paper (sibling of Paper Full Version), whereas Withdrawn Paper in edas is a paper withdrawn from the conference (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper). They denote different concepts despite both being subclasses of Paper.

Important dates is a class of conference deadlines (submission, acceptance, camera-ready, start/end dates) with properties linking it to a Conference volume and to dates. Time in iasted is a much broader temporal class whose children include Conference days, Deadline and Trip day, and which is used as the range of many temporal relations (is held before/after, is present, is sent before/after). A Deadline is a kind of Time, so the conference important-dates concept is a narrower notion subsumed by the general Time class, not equivalent to it.

A's hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to a string URL (homepage), while B's writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person (authorship). They differ in domain, range, direction and meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's property links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (the contribution a reviewer is qualified to review), while B's 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/presenting something). Different domains (Review expertise vs Person) and different ranges (Submitted contribution vs Activity/Item), so they denote different relations.

A's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event (a programme is part of an event), while B's 'technically Organises' is a sub-property of 'organises' linking an Organisation to what it organises. Different domains (Programme vs Organisation), different ranges (Conference Event vs unspecified), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Reviewed contribution' is a subclass of Submitted contribution (a paper that has been reviewed, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution), whereas B's 'Review' is a Document sibling of Paper/Abstract, i.e. the review artefact itself. The two denote different concepts (the reviewed paper vs. the review document), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Workshop Session' is a type of scientific event/session (a temporal gathering within a workshop), while B 'Session room' is a type of place (a physical room where sessions are held). They belong to different top-level categories (Event vs Place) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Presenter city is a subclass of City describing the city a presenter comes from. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.
A is a datatype property linking a Call to a string of submission instructions; B is an object property linking an Event to a Location. Different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Dinner banquet' is a social-program activity (a conference event), while B 'Organizator' is a person role (a subclass of Person with children such as General Chair and Program Chair). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A's Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while B's Conference is an event/venue entity with a name and conference volumes/proceedings. They denote different kinds of things and share no properties or context, so they are unrelated.

A is the conference event class (a working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while B is a city associated with a presenter (a subclass of City alongside Conference city and Sponsor city). They denote different concepts: an event versus a location role, so they are unrelated.

A's hasAttendee relates a Conference Event to a Person (attendee), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Conference. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not the same relation.

Both are object properties from Author to the paper/contribution entity (Paper in cmt, Contribution in confOf, which are the same concept). 'submit Paper' and 'writes' both relate an author to the paper they authored, so they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

A 'Dining Place' is a kind of Place (a location where one eats), while B 'Van' is a kind of Transport vehicle (a means of transport). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (venue/location vs. transport) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop is a scholarly conference part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, linked to a Conference volume via has workshops), whereas a Free Time Break is a non-academic break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's Conference is the conference event itself (has dates, deadlines, country, members, topics, related documents). B's Conference hall is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel and Main office), i.e. a venue room, not the event. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person and is a broad role covering anyone attending the conference (siblings include Author, Reviewer, etc.). In ekaw, Late Registered Participant is a subclass of Conference Participant, which is itself a subclass of Person; it denotes a narrower role (a participant who registered late), alongside Early Registered Participant. Thus every Late Registered Participant is an attendee/participant, but not every Attendee is a late-registered participant, so Attendee is more general: Attendee is subsumed by the narrower ekaw class, i.e. relation subsumed_by.

A 'Slide Set' is a presentation artefact (sibling of Paper, Review, Programme under Document in edas), while B 'Workshop Paper' is a specific kind of Paper (a written contribution submitted to a workshop). They denote different concepts: one is presentation material, the other a paper type, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'author Of' is an object property linking a Person to a Document (authorship relation). B's 'Nation' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (nationality). Different kinds of things are related (Document vs string) and the intended meaning differs entirely, so they are unrelated.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes; B's `search` relates ACM SIGKDD to a Sponzor (sponsor). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not the same relation.

Both properties link a Paper to the people who review it, but cmt's readByReviewer is restricted to Reviewer, while edas's isReviewedBy ranges over Reviewer plus Conference Chair, Session Chair and TPC Member. The edas property is therefore broader: readByReviewer is subsumed by isReviewedBy, not equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Conference part (domain Topic, range Conference part), while B's partOfEvent links an Event to a sub-Event (domain Event, range Event). Both express a part-whole relation, but over different entity types (Topic vs Event), so they are not equivalent; they overlap only in the general notion of parthood.

A's assignExternalReviewer relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (a person assigned to review), while B's has_a_review_reference_or_expertise relates a Reviewer to Review expertise/Review preference (topics or expertise areas). The ranges denote different kinds of things (person vs. topic/expertise), so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'Track workshop chair' is a Person who chairs a track/workshop/tutorial (linked to Conference part via has a track workshop tutorial chair / was a track workshop chair of). B's 'Chair PC' is a Person who chairs the Program Committee (comment 'confTool', sibling of Member PC). Both are chair roles within the conference, but they chair different things (track/workshop vs. program committee), so they are related rather than equivalent.

confOf's 'parallel with' is a symmetric relation between Administrative events (e.g., sessions running in parallel), while ekaw's 'technically Organises' is a subproperty of 'organises' relating an Organisation to the event it organises. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not equivalent.

A's max Choice is a datatype property giving the maximum number of choices for a social/working event (range positiveInteger), while B's obtain is an object property relating a Person to an Item. Different domain, range, and meaning; no equivalence.

In edas, Industry Organization is a subclass of Organization (a type of institution, sibling to Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO). In iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person (a role played by an individual, sibling to Delegate). An organizational/institutional entity is not the same concept as a person acting as a sponsor; the intended instances do not coincide, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'read By Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the person who reads/reviews it), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives/participates in something). The domains (Paper vs Person) and ranges (Reviewer vs Activity/Item) differ, and the directions of the relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Contribution co author' is a role/class of co-authors of a contribution (a sub-role of Regular author, sibling of 'Contribution 1th author'), i.e. an authorship role tied to a contribution. B's 'Lecturer' is a subclass of Author in the delegate hierarchy (a person who gives lectures), with children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer. The two denote different concepts: one is a co-authorship role on a contribution, the other a kind of author/lecturer person. They do not coincide, nor is one strictly more general than the other.

A's 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to its Program committee (a whole-part/structural relation), while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

A's isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event (venue hosting an event), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (a person's requirement). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B's Form is a document type (parent Document, children include Registration form and Hotel registration form). They denote different concepts in different branches of the domain, so they are unrelated.

write (Person -> Item) and submit (Author -> Paper) both link an author-like agent to a paper-like artefact, but writing and submitting are distinct activities in the conference domain; they overlap in that submitting a paper typically follows writing it, but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both are datatype properties named date/Date, but A's date attaches a date to a Conference (the event's date), while B's Date attaches a dateTime to a Deadline (a submission deadline). They relate different kinds of things in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent; they are only loosely related by the shared notion of a date.

A's Workshop is a type of academic event (a session/event at a conference), while B's Best Paper Awards Committee is a type of committee (an organisational body). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (event vs. committee) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A 'Reception' is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) in the conference domain, while B 'Reject Rating' is a review rating category (sibling of Accept Rating) used to score submissions. They belong to entirely different branches (social event vs. review rating) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a specific kind of conference contribution (a subtype of Regular contribution, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract), whereas B's 'Document' is a broad administrative item (parent of Review, Submission, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc.). The intended instances do not coincide: an extended abstract is a submission/contribution, not the general administrative document class. No subsumption holds either, since B's Document is not a superclass of A's Extended abstract in the conference domain.

Both properties express the end of a temporal interval: A's 'is an ending date' gives the end date of an 'Important dates' interval, while B's 'ends on' gives the end of an 'Event'. They play the same role (end boundary of a time span) but have different domains (Important dates vs Event) and ranges (date vs string), so they are not the same property; they are related by shared temporal-end semantics.

A is a conference-organisation event class (parent of submission, reviewing, registration events), while B is a research topic in computer networks. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's 'Program Committee' is a committee/group entity whose members are Program Committee Members; B's 'Author' is a subclass of Person who writes Contributions. A committee is not a person, and the confOf counterpart of a program committee would be a committee class (e.g. PC/Chair PC/Member PC context), not Author. Different kinds of things, so unrelated.

A's 'Conference Session' is a generic session type in edas (a session of a conference, related to documents and academic events), while B's 'Demo Session' is a specific kind of scientific session for demonstrations, sibling to Conference Session, Poster Session, Regular Session and Workshop Session in ekaw. They denote different session types, not the same concept.

A's 'is a starting date' is a datatype property of the 'Important dates' class (a deadline/event date, e.g. the start of a submission or conference deadline period), while B's 'start Date' is a datatype property of the 'Conference' class giving the conference's start date/time. They belong to different domains (Important dates vs Conference) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Social event' is a conference event (banquet, reception, trip) under Event, while B 'Hotel room' is a physical place (single/double room) under Place. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

A 'Research Institute' is an academic organisation (sibling of University under Academic Institution), while B 'Best Research Paper Award' is a type of Award given at a conference. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship of a paper), while B's 'has Attendee' links a Conference Event to a Person (attendance at an event). Different domains (document vs. event) and different intended relations (authorship vs. attendance), so they are not equivalent.

A's read By Meta Reviewer relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (domain Paper, range Meta Reviewer), while B's reviews relates a Review to a Reviewed contribution (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent; at best they are loosely related through the review process, but the intended relations differ.

A's 'adjust Bid' relates a Reviewer to a Bid (domain Reviewer, range Bid), i.e. a reviewer adjusting a bid. B's 'is Review History Of' relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer), i.e. the inverse direction and different subject. They do not denote the same relation.

A's 'written By' goes from Review to Reviewer (the person who wrote the review), while B's 'has a review' goes from Reviewed contribution to Review (a paper having a review). They relate different kinds of things in opposite directions and are not inverses either, so they are unrelated.

A 'Member PC' is a person (a PC member/reviewer) in confOf, with properties expert On and reviewes. B 'Review Question' is a class of questions (numerical/textual) used in reviews in edas. They denote different concepts: a person versus a review form question, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference contribution' is a document/paper submitted to a conference (a subclass of Conference document, with children like Poster, Presentation, Written contribution, and properties linking it to a Conference volume). B 'Activity' is a much broader event/activity concept (children include Activity before/after conference and Conference activity; properties like is held in, is dated on, is given by). A conference contribution is a kind of conference activity, so the contribution class is strictly more specific than Activity; they are not equivalent.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chair of the whole conference, a subtype of Chairman/Conference Member. Demo Chair (ekaw) is a Conference Participant responsible for the demo track, sibling of Workshop Chair, Tutorial Chair, etc. Different roles with different scopes and different parent hierarchies; not equivalent.

A's Talk Event is a kind of academic event (a session such as a welcome or closing talk) in the conference schedule, while B's Author is a person role (a speaker who authors papers, with properties submit/obtain/notification). They denote different concepts entirely: an event versus a person, so they are unrelated.

A's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it (domain Event, range Organisation/Person). B's 'is used for' links an Item to the Activity/Money it is used for (domain Item, range Activity/Money). Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Break Event is a non-academic conference event (coffee/meal/free-time breaks) under Non Academic Event, while B's Registration is a conference activity with Delegate as a child, i.e. the act/process of registering delegates. They denote different concepts and are not related by subsumption.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper authorship relation). B's `part Of` is a generic mereological/part-whole property with unspecified domain and range, used in ekaw for structural composition (e.g. an event being part of a conference). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

A's location is a datatype property from Social/Working event to a string (the place where the event is held). B's locationOf is an object property from Location to Event, the inverse direction of a location-to-event relation. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), direction, and domain/range, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the whole conference event (has members, country, name, deadlines, topics, related documents). B's Conference days is a time sub-concept under Time, with children Delegate and One conference day and siblings Deadline and Trip day — it denotes the days/duration of a conference, not the conference event itself. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

A's 'scientifically Organises' relates an Academic Institution to the events it organises (domain Academic Institution), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (domain Speaker, range Document). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Volunteer is a subclass of Person (a person role in the conference), while B's Two Level Conference is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference event). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Personal Publication History' is a class in edas representing a person's history of publications (a subclass of Personal History, sibling of Personal Review History). B 'Final manuscript' is a subclass of Submission in iasted, denoting the final version of a submitted document. They denote entirely different concepts: one is a biographical/history record, the other a document type in the submission process. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.
A's Paper is a conference document (submitted/ reviewed/ written by authors), while B's Value added tax is a kind of Tax under Money; the two concepts share no meaning in the conference domain.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them; B's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization providing it. Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasFax is a datatype property linking a Person to a fax number (comment 'confTool'), while B's hasLastName links a Person to their last name. They relate different kinds of information (fax number vs. surname) in the same direction, so they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

A's 'logo URL' is a datatype property of Conference pointing to an anyURI (a conference's logo image location), while B's 'has First Name' is a datatype property of Person pointing to a string (a person's first name). They have different domains (Conference vs Person), different ranges (anyURI vs string), and entirely different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties giving a start time, but confOf's 'starts on' has domain Event (any event, including conferences, sessions, etc.) while edas's 'start Date' has domain Conference only. The edas property is thus a more specific version of the confOf property, so confOf's starts_on subsumes edas's startDate (startDate is subsumed_by starts_on). They are not equivalent because the domains differ in generality.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a role of a person (a Conference contributor who gives an invited talk), while B's 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference event (a conference with a two-tier programme committee structure). They denote different concepts in the conference domain and share neither instances nor meaning.

A's 'has tracks' links a Conference volume to its Track (a subdivision of the conference proceedings), while B's 'has Topic' links a Working event to a Topic (a subject area). The domains (Conference volume vs Working event) and ranges (Track vs Topic) differ, and the intended relations are different: one is a structural part-of relation, the other a subject classification. They are not equivalent.

A's hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime (a deadline), while B's heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no overlap in meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference fees' is a monetary charge paid to attend a conference, while B's 'Conference Proceedings' is a published multi-author volume of papers (a Document/Proceedings). They share only the word 'Conference' and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic in the EDAS topic taxonomy (a subject area for classifying papers), while B is a document type in EKAW (an abstract of an invited talk). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (topic vs. document) and share no intended instances.

A is a class of accepted papers/contributions in the Conference ontology (a reviewed, accepted written contribution with camera-ready children), while B is a registration deadline in the iasted ontology (a time/deadline entity). They denote entirely different concepts: a document/contribution versus a temporal deadline, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a role/person (a subclass of Chairman/Person, a member of the conference organisation), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself, with properties for city, start/end dates, name, and being held by ACM SIGKDD. A person role and an event are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's ReviewRating is a class of rating values (children: Accept Rating, Reject Rating, etc.) used as the range of hasRating from Active Paper. B's Review is a document type (sibling of Abstract and Paper under Document), i.e. the review document itself, not a rating value. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a conference part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, linked via 'has workshops' from Conference volume), while B's Tutorial is a kind of Lecture (a conference activity, sibling of Plenary lecture and Session). Although both ontologies contain a Tutorial concept, the pair compares Workshop with Tutorial, which denote different things: a workshop is a parallel event/part of a conference, whereas a tutorial is a lecture-type activity. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

In ekaw, Assigned Paper is a Submitted Paper that has been assigned to a reviewer (a subclass of Submitted Paper, with child Evaluated Paper). In iasted, Submission is a Document that is submitted to the conference, with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript. A Submission is the general submitted document, which is broader than an Assigned Paper (a submission that has been assigned for review). Thus Assigned Paper is more specific and is subsumed by Submission, not equivalent.

Administrator in confOf is a generic Person role (confTool administrator, sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.), while General Chair in sigkdd is a specific organizing role (parent Organizator, sibling of Program Chair, Webmaster). They denote different concepts: an administrator is not a general chair, and neither subsumes the other.

A's has Call relates an Academic Event to a Call (event-to-call), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (person-to-thing). Different domains, ranges and directions; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Co chair' is a committee member role (sibling of Chair, domain/range of committee co-chair properties), while B's 'Sponsor' is a Person subtype (sibling of Delegate) denoting a funding entity. Different concepts despite both being persons.

A's 'Reviewed contribution' is a submission (a paper) that has undergone review, sitting under Submitted contribution with children Accepted/Rejected contribution. B's 'Review' is the review document itself, a sibling of Paper under Document. The two denote different concepts (the reviewed paper vs. the review record), so they are not equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a working event (a scheduled activity alongside Conference and Workshop), while B's Tutorial Abstract is a document (an abstract text, sibling of Invited Talk Abstract). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

Chairman is a person role (a subclass of Person, with children like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), whereas Lecture is a conference activity (a subclass of Conference activity, with children like Plenary lecture and Session). They denote different kinds of things and are not related by subsumption or overlap.

A's Trip is a social event (a type of excursion/outing) under Event > Social event, alongside Banquet and Reception. B's IASTED non member is a kind of Delegate (a person role) under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate, alongside Speaker, Session chair, etc. One denotes an event, the other a person role; they share no intended instances and are unrelated.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the paper assignment tools), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's Conference Trip is a social event (a trip/outing) under Event > Social Event, while B's Conference days is a time interval under Time with children like Delegate and One conference day. They denote different concepts (an activity vs. a temporal period), so they are not equivalent.

A is a datatype property linking a Call to a string of submission instructions; B is an object property linking a Location to an Event. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B's 'Company' is an organization (sibling of University). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Non Academic Event is a conference event category (breaks, meals, social events) under Conference Event, while B's Registration SIGMOD Member is a fee category under Registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. fee) and denote different concepts.

A's Workshop is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, part of a Conference volume), while B's Speaker is a person role (subclass of Person, with children Author and Invited Speaker). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

Meta Reviewer is a special kind of Reviewer (a person role) in cmt, while Paper is a document in sigkdd. They belong to different branches (Person vs Document) and denote different concepts; no equivalence or subsumption holds.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B is a Workshop, an academic event in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Conference Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic class (a subcategory of Computer Networks Topic, a subject area for papers), while B is a person role (Webmaster, a kind of Organizator). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic taxonomy vs. person/organisation roles) and cannot share instances.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a subclass of Conference contributor (a person role: an invited speaker who contributes to a conference), while B's 'Presenter state' is a subclass of State (a status/phase of a presenter, sibling of Conference state and Sponsor state). One denotes a kind of person, the other a state/status; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to a Contribution (the PC member reviews a paper), while B's `is used by` relates an Item to a Person (a person uses an item). The domains and ranges differ (Member PC vs Item, Contribution vs Person), and the intended meanings (reviewing vs using) do not coincide, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'is given by' relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the presenter), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper). Different domains, ranges, and directions: presenting a talk is not the same relation as authoring a paper.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing practical information to attendees, while B's 'CAD Topic' is a subject-area topic (sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.) used to classify papers. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. topic) and denote different concepts.

A 'Rejected Paper' is a paper that has been evaluated and rejected in the review process, while B 'Abstract' is a document that is an abstract of a paper (a summary document), not a rejected paper. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who registered late and paid), while B 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity before the conference (receiving a submitted manuscript). They belong to different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's eventOnList relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (a listing of events in a publication), while B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (a talk given by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Conference applicant is a Person subtype (someone applying to attend a conference, with child Registeered applicant), while Two Level Conference is a Conference subtype (a conference with two levels, also oddly parented by Person/TPC Member). They denote different concepts: a person role vs. a conference type.

A's Presentation is a kind of conference contribution (a talk given at the conference, with an abstract, given by a participant, sibling of Poster and Invited talk). B's Document is a generic administrative item (parent of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Review, Submission, etc.), not a conference talk. The two denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Member PC is a program-committee member (comment: Reviewer; reviews Contributions), while ekaw's Paper Author is a person who authors papers. They are distinct roles in the conference domain, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'starts on' is a datatype property of Event giving the start time (string), while B's 'done till' is a datatype property of Deadline giving the end date. Different domains (Event vs Deadline), different semantics (start vs end), and different ranges (string vs date); they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'rejected By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person/role that rejected it), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting). They differ in domain, range, and direction, so they are not the same relation.

confOf Member is a subclass of Participant (a person participating in the conference, with siblings Regular and Student), i.e. a generic conference attendee/participant category. ekaw PC Member is a subclass of Possible Reviewer and is a specific programme-committee role, with children PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair. The two denote different concepts: one is a general participant type, the other a reviewer/committee role. They overlap only in that a PC member is also a participant, so they are related, not equivalent.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' is an administrative action relating an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (adding a member), while B's 'reviewes' relates a PC member to a Contribution (reviewing a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; not equivalent.

A is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date literal (a submission deadline), while B is an object property linking a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (the topic's coverage). They share neither domain, range, nor intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Review Rating is a class of rating values (with children Accept Rating, Reject Rating, etc.) attached to a paper via has Rating, whereas B's Positive Review is a subclass of Review denoting a review whose outcome is positive. They both concern the positive/negative assessment of a paper but are different kinds of entities (rating value vs. review document), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Industry Organization is a for-profit/commercial organization, a sibling of Academia Organization, Government Organization and NGO under Organization. B's University is an academic institution, a sibling of Research Institute under Academic Institution. They denote different kinds of organizations (industry vs. academic), so they are not equivalent.

Conference Member (cmt) is a subclass of Person representing people involved in a conference (authors, chairs, reviewers, PC members), with properties linking it to a Conference. Place (sigkdd) is a location class (conference hall, hotel, main office) that a Person can stay in. They denote entirely different concepts: a person role versus a physical location, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a document/item to a person, but the intended relations differ: 'is writen by' expresses authorship (Item -> Person), while 'presentationed by' expresses presentation by a speaker (Document -> Speaker). Authorship and presentation are distinct roles in the conference domain, so the properties are not equivalent, though they overlap in relating documents to people.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document announcing/requesting participation (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, Review), whereas B 'Record of attendance' is a document recording who attended (sibling of Form, Payment document, Invitation letter). They denote different document types with no overlap in intended instances.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (event-to-event, symmetric co-occurrence), while B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity/Item (person-to-thing, e.g. giving a talk or item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

cmt:assignedTo relates a Paper to its Reviewer (a review assignment), while ekaw:partOf is a generic mereological/containment relation with unspecified domain and range. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not the same relation.

cmt:User is a general person role in the conference system, parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer, and sibling of Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member. ekaw:Conference Participant is a person who participates in a conference, parent of various chair roles, Presenter, and registered participants, sibling of Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student. Both are broad person-role classes under Person, but their intended extensions differ: User covers system users (including administrators and reviewers) while Conference Participant covers people attending/participating in the conference. They overlap (authors, reviewers, chairs can be both) but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Regular Session is a kind of Session (a scheduled slot in a conference, sibling of Workshop/Poster/Demo Session) in ekaw. B Plenary lecture is a kind of Lecture (a talk/activity, sibling of Session and Tutorial) in iasted. A session is a container of presentations, whereas a plenary lecture is a single talk; the concepts denote different things and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Session Chair' is a Person role (a person who chairs a session), while B's 'Poster Session' is an Event/Session type. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. event) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a person who takes part in a conference, with subclasses Active/Passive participant), whereas B's 'Conference' is the event itself (with subclasses Single Level/Twisted Level Conference, and properties like end Date, has Country, has Member, paper Due On). A person role and a conference event are different concepts, so the classes are unrelated.

A's 'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a part-whole relation between a document and its abstract-bearing contribution). B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a document being presented by a person). The domains (Abstract vs Document) and ranges (Paper/Poster/Presentation vs Speaker) differ, and the intended relations are different: one is a compositional relation, the other an agentive presentation relation. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B is a conference structure type (Single Level Conference, sibling of Two Level Conference) in edas. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Abstract), while B's 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a subclass of Award (a prize category, sibling of Best Research/Student Paper Award). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (document vs. award) and denote different concepts.
A's Reviewer is a Person (a person who reviews), while B's Review is a Document (the review artefact itself). They are different kinds of entities (person vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

Author (cmt) is a person who writes/submits papers, a Conference Member/User with children Author Not Reviewer and Co author, and is domain of write Paper, submit Paper, has Author. Presenter (ekaw) is a Conference Participant who presents at the conference, with child Invited Speaker and siblings like Session Chair, PC Chair. Writing a paper and presenting it are distinct roles; an author need not present and a presenter need not be an author, so the classes are not equivalent and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Review Form' is the document a reviewer fills in to submit a review of a paper; B 'Registration form' is a form used to register for the conference (sibling of 'Hotel registration form' and 'Author information form' under Form). They denote different artefacts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated despite both being forms.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs the conference (a Chairman/Conference Member role in cmt), while B 'IASTED member' is a Delegate subtype in iasted, i.e. an attendee who is a member of IASTED. The roles differ: chairing the conference vs. being a member/attendee. Different parents (Chairman vs Delegate) and different sibling sets confirm they denote different concepts.

A's 'Conference hall' is a physical place (a room/venue building) under Place, sibling of Building, Hotel room, Session room. B's 'Conference' is the event itself, with start/end dates, city, name, and held-by relations. A venue location and a conference event are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's title is the title of a Paper (domain Paper), while B's has First Name is the given name of a Person (domain Person). Different domains and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a person's reviewing role to a record of their reviewing activity: A's 'has a submitted contribution' goes from Review expertise to Submitted contribution, B's 'has Review History' goes from Reviewer to Personal Review History. They are conceptually related (a reviewer's history of submitted contributions/reviews), but the domains and ranges differ (Review expertise vs Reviewer, Submitted contribution vs Personal Review History), so they are not the same relation.

Student is a subclass of Person (a conference participant role), while Best Applications Paper Award is a subclass of Award (a prize category). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'name' is a datatype property giving the name (string) of a Conference or Person, while B's 'has a date of issue' gives the issue date (date) of a Conference document. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A is a research topic in the conference subject taxonomy (a child of Topic, alongside Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a physical item type (a child of Item, alongside Document, Publication, Transport vehicle) with child Credit card. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Conference participant' is a Person (a human attending the conference), while B 'Session' is a Lecture/Conference activity (an event). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'was a committe co chair of' relates a Co chair to a Committee (a role/committee-membership relation, subproperty of 'was a member of'), while B's 'reviewes' relates a Member PC to a Contribution (a reviewing relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Chairman is a general chair role with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, and is domain of a conflict-of-interest property. B's Chair PC is specifically the program-committee chair (comment 'confTool'), a sibling of Member PC. A program-committee chair is a kind of chairman, so Chairman is broader and Chair PC is subsumed by it; they are not equivalent.

A's has VAT is a datatype property of Social/Working event giving a tax string; B's has Email is a datatype property of Person/Contact Information giving an email address. Different domains, different intended relations, no overlap.

A's hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to its Subject Area (topic), while B's is_held_in relates an Activity to a Place/Time (location/schedule). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A is a physical place (a venue location, sibling of Accommodation/Dining/Meeting Room places under Place), while B is a temporal deadline (a date by which a hotel reservation must be made, sibling of submission/camera-ready/registration deadlines under Deadline). They denote different concepts in different branches of the ontology (place vs. time), so they are unrelated.

A's Committee is a conference organisation body (with chairs, members, subcommittees like Program committee), while B's State is a geographical/administrative region occupied by persons and containing buildings/cities. Their children, properties and domains/ranges do not overlap, so they denote different concepts.

Author is a person role in the conference domain (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Time in iasted is a temporal entity (parent of Deadline, Conference days, Trip day) used as range of temporal relations like is held before/after. They share no meaning, instances, or properties; the pair is unrelated.

A's 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an Administrator->Conference action property (an administrator runs the assignment process for a conference), while B's 'presentationed by' is a Document->Speaker relation linking a document to the speaker who presents it. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

confOf's Social event is a subclass of Event (a social gathering such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while edas's Place is a location entity (Accommodation, Conference Venue, Dining, Meeting Room) that serves as the range of has Location and domain of is Location Of. They denote different concepts: an event versus a location, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'follows' orders Administrative events (domain and range both Administrative event), while B's 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place/Time. Different domain, range and meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference/committee), while B's is_needed_for relates an Item to a Person (an item being required by a person). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Person->Conference vs Item->Person), so the two properties denote different relations and are not equivalent.

A's Conference Session is a specific kind of session within a scientific event (siblings: Demo, Poster, Regular, Workshop Session), while B's Session is a broader lecture-type activity (siblings: Plenary lecture, Tutorial) that is not restricted to conference sessions. B's Session is more general, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A 'Communication Theory Topic' is a subject area/topic of papers in the edas ontology (a subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Invited Talk' is a kind of scientific event/presentation (subclass of Individual Presentation, sibling of Contributed Talk and Tutorial). They denote entirely different concepts—a research topic versus an event type—so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Abstract), while B's 'Best Student Paper Award' is a subclass of Award (a prize category, sibling of other best-paper awards). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (document vs. award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'speak in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place/Time (an event-participation relation), while B's 'Name of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (a naming attribute). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are unrelated.

A's 'has a name' is a datatype property assigning a string name to entities like Conference, Publisher, Topic. B's 'publisherOf' is an object property relating an Organisation to published artefacts (Flyer, Volume, Brochure, Web Site). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the whole conference event/organisation (has members, administrators, submissions, logo, dates). B's Important dates is a bundle of deadline dates belonging to a conference volume; it is a part/attribute of a conference, not the conference itself. Different intended instances, so unrelated.

A's readByMeta-Reviewer relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (domain Paper, range Meta Reviewer), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like abstract, hasTitle, writtenBy, and is reviewed by PC members. Review Question in edas is a question used in reviewing (parent of Numerical/Textual Review Question), a completely different concept. They share no intended instances.

Both classes are named Organization and represent the same concept in the conference domain: an organizing body that provides sponsorship. Ontology A's Organization has children Academia/Government/Industry/NGO Organization and is linked to Sponsorship via is Provider Of / provided By, matching edas's Organization as the sponsor/organizer entity. Same label, same intended instances, no conflicting context.

A's Possible Reviewer is a Person who can review papers (parent Person, child PC Member, domain/range of reviewer Of Paper / review Written By). B's Author is a Speaker/Delegate in the conference-building hierarchy (parent Speaker, children include Lecturer, Tutorial speaker, proceedings-inclusion classes) and is a sibling of Reviewer, not a reviewer role. The two denote different roles in the conference domain (potential reviewer vs. author/speaker), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Assistant is a Person subtype (comment 'confTool') covering helpers/assistants in the conference organisation, while ekaw's Agency Staff Member is a Person subtype for staff of an agency involved in the conference. Both are non-author, non-participant support persons, so they overlap, but neither is strictly more general than the other and their intended instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling to Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B 'Closing Talk' is a talk event (subclass of Talk Event, sibling to Welcome Talk). They belong to different branches (document vs. event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A TPC Member is a program-committee person who reviews papers (is Reviewing Paper, is Reviewed By Paper), while B's Speaker is a Delegate who presents; B's reviewer role is a separate sibling class (Reviewer) under Speaker, and B's Technical commitee is the closer analogue of TPC Member. The two classes denote different roles in the conference domain.

A's 'has an abstract' links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract; B's 'write' links a person to an item they authored. Different domain (Paper/Poster/Presentation vs Person), different range (Abstract vs Item), and different direction of relation. They are not the same relation.

A's Chair is a generic committee chair (sibling Co chair, domain of 'has a committee chair' on Committee), while B's Program Chair is a specific organizer role alongside General Chair and Webmaster. A Chair is broader and would include a Program Chair, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

ekaw's `references` relates a Paper to the Paper(s) it cites (a bibliographic citation relation between documents), whereas iasted's `give` relates a Person to an Activity/Item (a person giving/presenting something). Different domain and range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (the score given to a paper), while B's hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (the person assigned to review). They link different kinds of entities (rating vs. person) and are not inverses or subsumption-related, so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Conference Participant (a person role: someone who registered early), while B is a Conference activity (the act/process of registering) whose child is Delegate. They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event/activity), so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Author is a person who writes/submits papers (subclass of Conference Member and User, with properties write Paper, submit Paper, has Author). Conference:Active conference participant is a conference contributor who gives presentations (sibling of Regular author, Invited speaker, Passive conference participant). The two overlap in that an author may be an active participant, but the intended concepts differ: Author is defined by authorship of papers, Active conference participant by giving presentations at the conference. Neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both are Person subclasses representing members of the programme committee: Conference's 'Committee member' (parent Person, children Chair/Co chair, linked to Committee via has members/was a member of) and edas's 'TPC Member' (parent Person, sibling Reviewer/Conference Chair, involved in reviewing papers via is Reviewing/is Reviewed By). The intended instances coincide — people serving on the programme committee — so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

Both properties link a Topic to the things it is a topic of, but the ranges differ: A's range is Conference part (a part of a conference such as a track/session), while B's range is Conference and Paper. They overlap in intent (topic-of relation) but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Week Reject Rating is a specific review-rating value (a rating category used when a paper is rejected in a given week) under Review Rating, while Negative Review is a type of review document (a review whose recommendation is negative) under Review. They both concern negative evaluation outcomes but denote different kinds of entities (rating value vs. review document), so they are related rather than equivalent.

hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author (authorship), while paperPresentedAs relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (presentation event). Different kinds of things are related, so the properties are not equivalent.

hasCountry relates a Conference to its Country, while heldIn relates an Event to a Location. Both express a spatial association, but the domains (Conference vs Event) and ranges (Country vs Location) differ; Country is a kind of Location and Conference is a kind of Event, so the properties overlap but are not the same relation.

Banquet is a specific social event (a meal/ceremony) in confOf, while Non Academic Event in edas is a broad category covering breaks, meals and social events. Banquet is therefore strictly narrower than Non Academic Event, not equivalent.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete version of a paper (a subclass of Paper, sibling of Paper Abstract), whereas B 'Flyer' is a promotional document (sibling of Paper, Review, Abstract, etc., and the range of publisherOf). They denote different concepts: a full paper is not a flyer, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'has a degree' is a datatype property of Review preference with range int, expressing a reviewer's preference strength; B's 'has Biography' is a datatype property of Person with range string, giving a person's biography. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held during the conference, while B's Receiving manuscript is an activity before the conference (sibling of Accepting/Refusing manuscript). They share only a superficial word stem and denote different concepts.

A's `related To Paper` links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a paper-to-paper relation within the conference submission structure). B's `give` links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person-to-artefact/event relation, e.g. giving a talk or presentation). The domains (Paper Presentation vs Person) and ranges (Accepted Paper vs Activity/Item) do not coincide, and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

A is a piece of audiovisual equipment (an overhead projector) under Item > Audiovisual equipment, while B is a person role (organizer) under Person. They belong to completely different branches of the conference domain and cannot denote the same concept.

A's Document is a broad class of written artefacts (Abstract, Paper, Review, Flyer, etc.) authored by Persons, while B's Deadline is a temporal milestone (submission/notification dates) with a Date property and children for specific deadlines. Their instances, properties and contexts do not coincide; the only link is B's 'submit until' property pointing from Document to Deadline, which is a relation between the two, not an equivalence.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'Currency' links a Registration fee to a string (the currency of the fee). Different domains, different intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type: the camera-ready version of a paper), while B is a subclass of Deadline (a time point: the registration deadline). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. time) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Track (a part-of structure under 'has parts'), while B's 'has City' relates an Organization or Person to a City (location). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they denote no common relation.

A's 'Conference fees' is a class about the fees charged for a conference (a monetary/payment concept), while B's 'Conference Event' is the general event class with children Academic/Non Academic Event and properties such as hasLocation, hasProgramme, hasStartDateTime, hasAttendee. They denote entirely different concepts; the shared word 'Conference' is not enough to make them equivalent.

A's 'has tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a sub-part relation under 'has parts'), while B's 'has Programme' links a Conference Event to its Programme. The domains (Conference volume vs Conference Event) and ranges (Tutorial vs Programme) differ, and a tutorial is a specific event type, not the overall programme, so the two properties do not relate the same kinds of things.

A 'Neutral Review' is a specific review verdict (sibling of Positive/Negative Review) in ekaw, while B 'Abstract' is a document type (sibling of Paper/Review) in sigkdd. They denote different concepts: a review verdict vs. a document summary, so they are unrelated.
