A's Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person who presents a paper), while B's Presenter city is a subclass of City (a city where a presenter comes from). They share only the word 'presenter' and denote different kinds of entities (person vs. city), so they are unrelated.

Member in confOf is a generic participant category (siblings Regular, Student), while Student non speaker in iasted is a specific non-speaking delegate subtype. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

Both entities denote the same concept in the conference domain: the class of conference papers/contributions. The paths, siblings, and properties (e.g., being authored by a Person, having a Document as range) agree, so they are equivalent.

In cmt, 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author denoting an author who is not also a reviewer (a role exclusion). In edas, 'Presenter' is a subclass of Author denoting the person who presents a paper. The two concepts capture different roles and do not coincide: an author-not-reviewer need not present, and a presenter may also be a reviewer. They share only the Author parent, so they are unrelated.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the paper assignment tools), while B's submit relates an Author to a Paper. Different domain, range, and direction of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's has Phone relates a Person to a phone number string; B's has City relates Contact Information to a city name string. Different domains (Person vs Contact Information) and different intended values (phone number vs city), so they are not the same relation.

A is a document type (full version of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while B is a subject/topic area (computer networks security) in the edas ontology. They belong to different branches (Document vs Topic) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Student non speaker' is a Delegate/Non speaker who is a student and does not give a talk; B's 'Author of paper student' is a Speaker/Author who is a student and has written a paper. Both denote students in the conference domain, but A explicitly excludes speakers while B requires being a speaker/author, so their intended instances do not coincide; they overlap only in the general notion of a student participant.

Topic in confOf is a subject area that contributions deal with, PC members are expert on, and working events have as topic. Conference Session in edas is a scheduled academic event (a subclass of Academic Event) that can have related documents and relate to documents/events/persons. A topic is not an event/session; the two concepts are unrelated.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact. B's 'Conference Event' is an event/activity with attendees, location, programme and start/end times, and has subclasses Academic Event and Non Academic Event. A document and an event are different kinds of things, so the classes are not equivalent and neither subsumes the other.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to a Conference Member (a person playing a committee role), while B's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference. They are not the same relation: the domain/range are swapped (A: Conference->Conference Member; B: Person->Conference), and B is the inverse-like relation of membership, not the committee-member relation. A's property is closer to an inverse of B's, but even then the range of A (Conference Member) is a role class, not a generic Person, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/member of the conference committee) in cmt, while B 'Conference Trip' is a social event (an excursion) in ekaw. They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A Workshop Chair is a conference participant who chairs a workshop (a PC Member subtype in ekaw), while B Webmaster is an organizing-committee role responsible for the conference website. Different roles with different responsibilities; no subsumption or overlap.

A's hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string title, while B's has_amount_of links a Money entity to an integer amount. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a conference submission document (parent Document, children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version, properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To Reviewer). B's Wireless Communications Topic is a subject-area/topic category (parent Topic, siblings are other research topics). A paper is not a topic; the entities denote different concepts.

A is a Paper Abstract (a document type under Paper), while B is a Gold Supporter (a sponsorship level under Sponzor). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's Participant is a subclass of Person (a conference attendee role with subclasses Member, Regular, Student and a property early Registration), while B's entity is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary fee category for author attendees who book). They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote a person role versus a fee, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Conference is a working event (a specific kind of event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while edas's Single Level Conference is a subclass of a broader Conference concept that also has Two Level Conference as a sibling. The edas Conference is the general conference concept, so confOf's Conference is narrower and falls under it; they are not equivalent because edas's Conference also covers two-level (multi-track) conferences.

Chairman is a role/person class (a Person who chairs, with subclasses Conference Chair, PC Chair, Associated Chair) in cmt, whereas Scientific Event is an event class (parent of Conference, Session, Track, Workshop) in ekaw. They denote different kinds of things (a person role vs. an event), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference building' is a physical building (a Place/Building subclass, sibling of Conference hotel/airport, parent of Delegate) whereas B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with properties for city, start/end dates, name and being held by ACM SIGKDD. The two denote different concepts (venue building vs. event), so they are unrelated.

Administrator in confOf is a generic Person role (sibling of Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.) with comment 'confTool', denoting a system administrator. Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a specific Organizator role (sibling of General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster), denoting a member of the conference organizing committee. The intended instances do not coincide: an administrator is not necessarily an organizing committee member, and vice versa. Different paths (Person > Administrator vs Person > Organizator > Organizing Committee member) and different sibling sets confirm they are distinct concepts.

Reviewer in cmt is a specific role (a Conference Member/User who reviews papers, with bid and assignment properties), while ekaw's Conference Participant is a broad class covering all attendees (chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.). A Reviewer is a kind of Conference Participant, but not every Conference Participant is a Reviewer, so Reviewer is strictly more specific.

In edas, Accepted Paper is a direct subclass of Paper and is a sibling of Rejected Paper, Pending Paper, etc. In ekaw, Evaluated Paper is a subclass of Assigned Paper and is the parent of both Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper. Thus ekaw's Evaluated Paper is a broader class covering all papers that have been reviewed (accepted or rejected), while edas's Accepted Paper is only the accepted subset. Accepted Paper is therefore strictly more specific than Evaluated Paper, so it is subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'name' is a general datatype property giving the name of a Conference or Person, while B's 'has Cost Currency' is a datatype property specific to Sponsorship giving the currency of a sponsorship cost. They have different domains (Conference/Person vs Sponsorship) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is the published volume of collected papers (has publisher, volume, ISBN, issued by a Publisher), whereas B's 'Conference' is the event itself (has city, start/end date, held by an ACM SIGKDD). The entities denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has tutorials' is a specific part-whole relation from a Conference volume to its Tutorials (a subclass of its parent 'has parts'). B's 'has Event' is a very general mereological/structural relation from any Event to its sub-Events. The two are not the same relation: 'has tutorials' is narrower (only conference volumes to tutorials), while 'has Event' applies to arbitrary events and event parts. Thus A's property is strictly more specific than B's, i.e. subsumed_by.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with two levels, sibling of Single Level Conference under Conference), while B 'Webmaster' is a person role in the organizing committee (Organizator). They denote entirely different concepts (event vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document type (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact. B's 'Proceedings Publisher' is an organisation (subclass of Organisation, sibling of Academic Institution and Organising Agency), i.e. an agent that publishes proceedings. The two denote different kinds of entities (document vs. organisation) and are not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B 'Presenter house' is a building/place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). They denote entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a document submitted to a conference (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while B's Communication Theory Topic is a subject-area/topic category under Topic. They denote different concepts: a paper artefact versus a research topic, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/committee member who chairs the conference), while B 'Conference Dinner' is a social meal event in the conference event hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. event) with no overlap.

A's 'Organizing committee' is the general committee that organizes the conference, while B's 'Program Committee' is the committee handling paper review/program. In B, 'Organizing Committee' exists as a separate sibling, confirming that 'Program Committee' is a distinct, narrower concept. They are not equivalent; at most they are related as different committees, but the intended instances do not coincide.

A's Track is a thematic stream of the conference that groups papers/sessions (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, range of 'has tracks' from Conference volume), whereas B's Tutorial is a specific kind of lecture/activity (subclass of Lecture, sibling of Plenary lecture and Session). Although A's ontology also has a Tutorial class, the candidate pairs A:Track with B:Tutorial, which denote different concepts: a track is not a tutorial.

A's Talk Event is an academic event (a scheduled happening such as a welcome or closing talk) in the event hierarchy, while B's Invited Talk Abstract is a document/abstract artefact in the document hierarchy. They belong to different branches (event vs. document) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (authorship relation), while B's 'is paid by' links Money to a Person (payment relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property mapping Contact Information to a string postal code, while B's locationOf is an object property mapping a Location to an Event. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's updatedVersionOf relates a Document to another Document (a versioning relation between documents), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/performing something). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas B's 'Tutorial' is a working event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Conference and Workshop). A document and an event are different kinds of things, so the classes are unrelated.

confOf's 'deals With' relates a Contribution to a Topic (Contribution -> Topic), while ekaw's 'topic Covered By' relates a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (Research Topic -> Event/Paper). They are inverses of each other in direction and have different domains/ranges, so they are not equivalent; they are related as inverse/overlapping relations about the topic of a paper.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Author is a person role (a Speaker who authors proceedings, sibling of Reviewer). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in the cmt ontology, while B's 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is a committee (a group/organisational body) in sigkdd. One denotes an individual person role, the other a collective committee; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a person role), while B's Student registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money (a monetary amount). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. fee) and are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), whereas B's 'Conference' is an event (a subclass of Scientific Event, sibling of Session, Track, Workshop). A person role and an event cannot denote the same concept, so the pair is unrelated.

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property of Review expertise (a reviewer's expertise, a literal value), while B's 'has Rating' is an object property from Active Paper to Review Rating (a paper's numeric rating). Different domains, ranges, and kinds (datatype vs object), so they denote different relations.

A's Chair is a generic committee chair (sibling Co-chair, domain/range Committee->Chair), while B's Workshop Chair is a specific conference-participant role (sibling Demo Chair, Tutorial Chair, etc.). A Workshop Chair is a kind of chair, so A is more general and subsumes B; they are not equivalent.

Associated Chair (cmt) is a chair role under Chairman, a member of the conference organisation; Demo Chair (ekaw) is a specific conference participant role responsible for demos, sibling of Workshop Chair and Tutorial Chair. They denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper) in the cmt ontology, while B is a subject-area topic (Antennas) under Topic in edas. They denote entirely different concepts: a document type versus a research topic, with no overlap in instances or meaning.

A's 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings giving the ISBN string, while B's 'ends on' is a datatype property of Event giving an end date/time string. They relate different kinds of things (proceedings vs. events) and have different meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Registration form' is a Document/Form artefact used to register (siblings: Author information form, Hotel registration form). B 'Registration Student' is a fee category (a kind of Registration fee, siblings: Registration Non Member, Registration SIGKDD Member, Registration SIGMOD Member). One is a form document, the other a fee type; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A's 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), while B's 'is visited by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person who visits it. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper) in the cmt ontology, while B is a subclass of Topic (a subject area in the edas ontology). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. topic) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Presentation is a kind of conference contribution (a document/contribution that is presented, with an abstract, given by a participant, and having an invited-talk subtype). B's Paper Presentation is a kind of Academic Event (a session/event at which accepted papers are presented, related to Accepted Paper). The two denote different categories (contribution vs. event) that are connected in the domain (a presentation contribution is given at a presentation event), so they overlap but are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person who writes papers: cmt Author is a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers (write Paper, submit Paper, has Author Paper->Author), edas Author is a Person who writes papers (is Written By Paper->Author, has Related Paper Author->Paper). Same intended instances, same domain role, despite differing parent hierarchies.

Both classes denote the subject area / topic of a paper: cmt's Subject Area is the range of has Subject Area (Paper -> Subject Area), and edas's Topic is the range of has Topic (Conference, Paper -> Topic) and domain of is Topic Of. The intended instances (e.g. Computer Networks, Cryptography) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's IASTED member is a kind of Delegate (a person/role, sibling of Speaker, Session chair, Listener). They denote different concepts: an event versus a person role, so they are unrelated.

Publisher in Conference is an organisation that issues conference proceedings (domain of 'issues', range of 'has a publisher'), whereas Topic in edas is a subject area of papers/conferences (domain of 'is Topic Of', range of 'has Topic'). They denote different concepts with no overlap.

Money in iasted is a general monetary amount class with children Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip and properties about paying/being paid; Sponzor in sigkdd is a sponsor organisation (with supporter/exhibitor subclasses and a name), not a monetary amount. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'contact Email' is a datatype property of Contribution giving an email address. Different domains (Person vs Contribution), different ranges (surname string vs email string), and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's `date` is a datatype property giving a Conference a literal date value, while B's `held In` is an object property relating an Event to a Location entity. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Event) and range (literal date vs Location), so they do not denote the same relation.

A Meal Break is a break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Free Time Break) under Non Academic Event > Break Event, i.e. a generic catering/rest break during the conference. B Conference Banquet is a Social Event (sibling of Conference Trip) under Event > Social Event, i.e. a formal evening social dinner. Both are non-academic conference events involving food, so they overlap, but a banquet is a specific social event, not a generic meal break; neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with children like Invited speaker, Regular author), while B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Working event (an event such as a conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event) and share only the word 'conference', so they are unrelated.

A 'Refusing manuscript' is an activity/process in the pre-conference phase (sibling of Accepting/Receiving manuscript), whereas B 'Author' is a person role (subclass of Speaker) who submits papers and receives notifications. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (process vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A's Topic is the general class of conference topics (it is the domain/range of properties linking topics to reviews, submissions, conference parts, and has a name). B's Performance Topic is a specific topic category under the parent Topic in edas, alongside many other specific topics (Antennas, CAD, etc.). Thus Performance Topic is a narrower concept than the general Topic; A's Topic subsumes B's Performance Topic, so they are not equivalent.
A's 'has a committee co chair' links a Committee to its Co chair (a person role), while B's 'held In' links an Event to a Location. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no overlap.

A 'Paid applicant' is a registered conference applicant who has paid, a subclass of Person via Conference applicant > Registeered applicant. B 'Participant' is a broader Person subclass covering all attendees (Member, Regular, Student, etc.). A paid applicant is a kind of participant, but participants need not be paid applicants, so Paid applicant is strictly narrower and subsumed by Participant.

Conference document is a broad publication/document class (children include Call for paper, Conference contribution, Review; it has authors and a date of issue), whereas edas Contact Information is a class holding address/phone/email details (has City, has Email, has Phone, has Postal Code, has Street). They denote different concepts and share no instances.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name; B's 'has Cost Currency' is a datatype property of Sponsorship giving the currency of a sponsorship cost. Different domains (Person vs Sponsorship), different intended meanings, only share the string range.

A's 'has members' relates a Committee to its Committee members (people belonging to a committee). B's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/presenting something). Different domain (Committee vs Person), different range (Committee member vs Activity/Item), and different meaning; they are not the same relation.

A 'Non Academic Event' is a conference event such as a break, meal or social event, while B 'Author' is a person role (a speaker who submits papers and receives notifications). They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. person) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Demo Paper is a specific kind of Paper (a document type in ekaw), while Abstract in sigkdd is a distinct document entity (a summary of a paper), sibling of Paper and Review. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Banquet is a social event (a meal/celebration) in confOf, while Audiovisual equipment is a physical item (equipment such as projectors) in iasted. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Item) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an Administrator action that opens bidding on a Conference; B's 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authoring a paper). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an Administrator action that assigns papers to reviewers for a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference). B's 'presentation Of Paper' links an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper being presented (domain Individual Presentation, range Abstract/Paper). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and serve different purposes, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome), while in ekaw hasReview links a Paper to a Review (the evaluation document). A Decision and a Review are distinct concepts: the review is the input, the decision is the outcome. The properties are therefore not equivalent, though they are related in that a decision is typically based on reviews.

A's Session is a scientific event (a scheduled meeting slot with children like Conference Session, Workshop Session), while B's Session chair is a person role (a Delegate who chairs a session). Different kinds of entities: event vs. person, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document (a written contribution with reviews, topics, presentations), while B's Author of paper is a role/person type (a subclass of Author, sibling of Author of paper student). They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person role), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword, while B's hasEvent is an object property linking an Event to another Event (e.g. sub-events). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have different domains/ranges, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Welcome Talk is a specific talk event within a conference (sibling of Closing Talk). A conference is not a talk; the entities denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Administrative event' is a broad organisational event category (submission, reviewing, camera-ready, registration) under Event, while B's 'Break Event' is a non-academic refreshment/rest category (coffee, meal, free time) under Non Academic Event. Their instances, parents, and children do not coincide; they are different branches of the conference event taxonomy.

A 'Working event' is a conference-domain event class (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop; has title, location, topics), while B 'Computer Networks Management Topic' is a specific research topic under Computer Networks Topic. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Topic) and denote different concepts.

A's Conference Session is an event/session entity (a gathering within a conference, related to documents and persons), while B's Document is a written artefact with subclasses Abstract, Paper, Review and properties like presentation and submit until. They denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties express the submission deadline of a call/document, but they are not equivalent: A is a datatype property from Call to dateTime, while B is an object property from Document to Deadline. They relate different kinds of entities (a call vs. a document, a literal date vs. a Deadline object), so they overlap in meaning but cannot be the same relation.

A Reception is a social event (sibling of Excursion) in the conference event hierarchy, while an Invitation letter is a Document item (sibling of Form, Review, Submission). They denote entirely different concepts: a social gathering versus a piece of correspondence, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has important dates' is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity (a container of deadlines), while B's 'Start of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a single dateTime value. They differ in kind (object vs datatype), in range (Important dates vs dateTime), and in meaning (all important dates vs the conference start date), so they are not equivalent.

An OC Chair (Organizing Committee Chair) is a specific role within the organizing committee, while sigkdd's Organizing Committee member is the broader class covering all committee roles (General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). The ekaw OC Chair is therefore a specialization of the sigkdd Organizing Committee member, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's given name), while B's 'is used by' is an object property from Item to Person (an item being used by a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), range (string vs Person), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'enter Conference Details' is an Administrator->Conference property (an admin enters details of a conference), while B's 'follows' is an Administrative event->Administrative event temporal/ordering relation between events. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's setMaxPapers is an administrative action assigning a maximum number of papers to a Program Committee Member (domain Administrator, range Program Committee Member), while B's obtain is a general acquisition relation from a Person to an Item. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not the same relation.

A's 'Early paid applicant' is a subclass of Person (a registered applicant who paid early), while B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Working event (an event type). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person/role vs. event) and cannot denote the same concept.

A 'Session Chair' is a person role (a Conference Participant who chairs a session), while B 'Viza' is a Document item (a visa document) under Item > Document. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Paper Abstract' is a subpart of a Paper (sibling of 'Paper Full Version'), i.e. the abstract text of a paper. B's 'Final manuscript' is a Submission (sibling of 'Initial manuscript'), i.e. the final version of a submitted document. They denote different concepts: an abstract is not a manuscript, and a final manuscript is not an abstract. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property giving a person's given name, while B's 'has Email' gives a person's email address. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote different attributes (first name vs. email), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Reject Rating' is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a rating value (a review outcome category), while B's 'Rejected Paper' is a subclass of Evaluated Paper, i.e. a document/paper that was rejected. One denotes a rating/review outcome, the other a paper, so their instances cannot coincide.

Sponsorship in edas denotes funding provided by an organization (has provider/provided by, cost amount/currency, child Travel Grant), while Fee in sigkdd denotes a monetary charge (children Registration fee, Sponzor fee). Both involve money in the conference domain but one is incoming funding and the other is an outgoing payment, so they are related but not equivalent.
Author in cmt is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes papers), while Author information form in iasted is a document/form artifact, not a person. Different kinds and no overlap.

Conference Proceedings (a multi-author volume collecting conference papers) and Abstract (a short summary document that is a sibling of Paper and Review) denote different concepts; they share no intended instances and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'adjust Bid' relates a Reviewer to a Bid (domain Reviewer, range Bid), while B's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference Banquet is a specific social event (a banquet), while B's Social program is a broader category of conference social activities that includes Dinner banquet as a child. The banquet is one instance/kind of social program, so Conference Banquet is subsumed by Social program, not equivalent.

A's 'gives presentations' relates an Active conference participant to a Presentation (person -> presentation). B's 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item to a Person (activity -> person), i.e. it is the inverse direction and a different subject kind. They are not the same relation; at best B's inverse ('is given by' from Activity to Person) corresponds to a presentation being given by a person, but the direction and domain/range differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Paid applicant' is a subclass of 'Registeered applicant' (a person who has paid a registration fee, with children Early/Late paid applicant), i.e. a paying conference registrant. B's 'TPC Member' is a program-committee member, a sibling of Author, Reviewer, Attendee, etc., and is the domain/range of reviewing and call-initiation properties. The two denote different roles in the conference domain: paying registrant vs. program-committee member. Neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

Both denote a poster contribution: confOf's Poster is a kind of Contribution (sibling of Paper, Short paper), and ekaw's Poster Paper is a kind of Paper (a Document). In the conference domain a poster is a paper/contribution presented as a poster, so the intended instances coincide.

write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (author writes paper); is prepared by relates an Item to a Person (item prepared by person). These are inverse-like relations between the same kinds of entities (person and paper/item), but the direction is reversed and the concepts (writing vs. preparing) differ, so they are not equivalent. They overlap in the sense of authorship/creation, hence related.

Both classes denote a tutorial event in the conference domain. In Conference, Tutorial is a Conference part alongside Track and Workshop, and is the range of 'has tutorials' (Conference volume -> Tutorial). In confOf, Tutorial is a Working event alongside Conference and Workshop. Same label, same intended instances (tutorial sessions), and compatible sibling context (workshop/track-like events) support equivalence.

A's 'is Reviewing' relates a person (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper they review. B's 'has Review' relates a Paper to a Review document. The domains and ranges differ (person->paper vs paper->review), and the direction of the reviewing relationship is opposite, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'issues' relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings), while B's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that run in parallel (domain and range Administrative event). Different domains, ranges and meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's property links a Conference part (track/workshop/tutorial) to a Topic, while B's coversTopic links an Event or Paper to a Research Topic. The B property is broader in domain (any Event or Paper, not just conference parts) and its range Research Topic is the same notion as Topic. A's property is thus a more specific case of B's coversTopic, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'is sent by' relates an Item (e.g. a paper/submission) to a Person, while B's 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person. Although both have range Person, the domains (Item vs Registration fee) and the intended relations (sending vs paying) differ, so they are not the same property.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (domain PC Member, range Administrator), while B's 'reviewes' links a Member PC to the Contribution they review (domain Member PC, range Contribution). Different ranges (Administrator vs Contribution) and different intended relations (membership administration vs reviewing), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a complete version of a conference paper (a document type under Paper), while B 'Single hotel room' is a type of hotel room (a place/accommodation type). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. accommodation) and share no intended instances.

A's Reviewer is a Conference Member/User who reviews papers (bids, assignments, conflicts), while B's Author is a Speaker/Delegate who writes papers; they are distinct roles in the conference domain, and B even lists Reviewer as a sibling of Author, confirming they are different concepts.

In iasted, Activity is a broad event/action concept with children including 'Conference activity', so a Conference is a specific kind of Activity. In cmt, Conference is a full-fledged class with its own administrative properties (accepts submissions, has conference members, dates, etc.). The two are not coextensive: Activity covers many non-conference activities (before/after conference, generic activities), so Conference is strictly narrower and thus subsumed by Activity.

EDAS 'Rated Papers' are papers that have received at least one review rating (a state of a paper after review activity), while EKAW 'Assigned Paper' is a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer/committee member for evaluation. Both concern papers in the review process, but they capture different stages/roles: being rated (review outcome recorded) vs. being assigned (reviewer allocated). They overlap in the review workflow but are not the same concept, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'abstract' is a datatype property of Contribution holding the paper's abstract text; B's 'Currency' is a datatype property of Registration fee holding a currency string. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Attendee is a generic person who attends a conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc. under Person), while General Chair is a specific organizer role (under Organizator, sibling of Program Chair, Webmaster). They denote different concepts: an attendee need not be a general chair and vice versa, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a distinguished conference contributor who gives an invited talk, while B's 'Student' is a participant category (a person's academic status). They denote different concepts with no subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment of a paper to a reviewer), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A 'Textual Review Question' is a type of review question (a prompt/field on a review form, sibling of Numerical Review Question), whereas B 'Negative Review' is a type of review document classified by its sentiment (sibling of Neutral/Positive Review). They belong to different branches (Review Question vs Review/Document) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

An Invited speaker is a distinguished person who gives a talk at a conference, whereas a Listener is an ordinary attendee who only listens. They are distinct roles in the conference domain, so the classes are not equivalent.

hasAuthor and isWrittenBy relate the same kinds of things (Paper -> Author) but in opposite directions: hasAuthor goes from Paper to Author, while isWrittenBy is the inverse (Author -> Paper in intent, though here declared Paper -> Author). A property and its inverse are not equivalent, so the pair is unrelated.

A's Paper is a general contribution type (siblings Poster, Short paper), while B's Rated Papers is a narrower subclass of Active Paper, i.e. papers that have received reviews/ratings. Every rated paper is a paper, but not every paper is rated, so Paper is more general and subsumes Rated Papers; the two are not equivalent.

A 'Co author' is a person (an Author who co-writes a Paper), while B 'Conference proceedings' is a published volume with a publisher, volume number and ISBN. They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. publication artefact), so they are unrelated.

A Meal Break is a specific break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Free Time Break) within the Non Academic Event branch, whereas iasted's Social program is a broader conference activity that has Dinner banquet as a child and includes social events like cocktail receptions. A meal break may be part of a social program, but the two classes are not coextensive: Social program covers more (dinner banquet, reception) and Meal Break is a narrower break category. Hence they overlap but are not equivalent.

A's 'Review expertise' is a class describing a reviewer's expertise/preference for reviewing a submitted contribution (it links Reviewer to Submitted contribution). B's 'Document' is a general class for submitted documents (parent of Abstract, Paper, Review) that is presented by a Speaker and has a submission deadline. The two denote different concepts: one is an expertise/preference record, the other a document artefact. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's Workshop is a working event (a type of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Hotel registration form is a document/form item (sibling of Author information form and Registration form). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Invited Speaker is a child of Presenter, so every invited speaker is a presenter, but not every presenter is an invited speaker. The Conference class Invited speaker is therefore more specific than ekaw's Presenter, making it subsumed_by.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference/committee), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (a requirement for some item). Different domains/ranges and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a submission of interest to review), while B's hasTopic relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (subject area). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

cmt:User is a broad person role class whose children include Author, Reviewer and Administrator, whereas confOf:Member_PC is specifically a PC member/reviewer (comment 'Reviewer', properties expertOn Topic and reviewes Contribution). A PC member is a kind of user, but not every user is a PC member, so Member_PC is strictly narrower than User.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document in a submission state), while B is a subclass of Deadline (a time point for registration). They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Social program' is a conference activity (a social event such as a dinner banquet) under Activity > Conference activity, while B 'Program Committee' is a committee of people under Committee. They denote different concepts with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

Both are subclasses of Person and both are broad umbrella categories for people involved in the conference, but their intended extensions differ: cmt:User covers all system users (Administrator, Author, Reviewer) including roles like Administrator that are not conference contributors, while Conference:Conference_contributor covers people contributing to a conference (Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author) and excludes pure system administrators. They overlap (authors, reviewers) without coinciding, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (setting review criteria for a conference), while B's 'is Reviewing' relates a person role (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper (a reviewer reviewing a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'was a committee of' relates a Committee to a Conference volume (the committee is part of a conference's organisation), while B's 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (a person belongs to a conference). Different domains (Committee vs Person) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

In edas, Organizational Meeting is an Academic Event (a meeting such as a program-committee or organisational gathering) alongside Paper Presentation, Talk Event and Workshop. In ekaw, Track is a Scientific Event that groups sessions/presentations (siblings Conference, Individual Presentation, Session, Workshop). An organisational meeting is not a track: the intended instances differ, so the classes are unrelated.

A's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer assigned to review a paper), while B's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (paper written by author). They have different domains/ranges and opposite directions, so they are not equivalent.

ekaw:Presenter is a conference participant who presents a paper, a role under Conference Participant. iasted:Hotel presenter is a Delegate staying at a hotel, a subclass of Delegate with no presenting semantics. Different intended instances despite the shared word 'presenter'.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details (domain Conference, range Administrator), while B's 'part Of Event' is a mereological relation between an Event and a larger Event (domain Event, range Event). Different domains, ranges and meanings; they are not the same relation.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Person in cmt), while B 'Conference' is an event type (a subclass of Working event in confOf). They denote fundamentally different kinds of entities (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

A's isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event (domain Place, range Conference Event), i.e. a venue hosting an event. B's is_present_in relates a Person to a Place/Time, i.e. a person attending/being present at a location. Different domains and ranges, different intended relations; they are not equivalent.

A's `name` is a general name property for Conference and Person, while B's `contact Email` is an email address property specific to Contribution (with comment 'confTool'). They denote different attributes (name vs. email) on different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Poster Paper' is a kind of conference paper (a document), while B 'Overhead projector' is a piece of audiovisual equipment; they belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's hasConferenceMember is an object property linking a Conference to a Conference Member (a person/role), while B's Name_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string. They relate different kinds of things (member vs. name string) and have different ranges, so they are not the same relation.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/document (a presentation given by an invited speaker, sibling of Poster and Regular contribution), whereas B's 'Closing Talk' is a scheduled conference event (a talk event, sibling of Welcome Talk). They belong to different branches (contribution vs. event) and denote different concepts; an invited talk is not the same as a closing talk.

Both are datatype properties with range string that give a person's email address. The domain of edas hasEmail is Contact Information or Person, which is broader, but the intended meaning (person's email) is the same, so they are equivalent.

A's hasEmail is a datatype property from Person to string (an email address literal), while B's is_used_by is an object property from Item to Person (an inverse-style relation linking an item to the person using it). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain (Person vs Item), and range (string vs Person), so they do not denote the same relation.

Both are datatype properties with int range expressing a monetary value, but A's domain is the general class Money while B's domain is the more specific Registration fee; they overlap in meaning (a registration fee's price is an amount of money) without being equivalent, since A can apply to any Money and B only to registration fees.

A's 'was a steering committee of' relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume (the committee is a committee of the conference series/volume). B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD organisation to a Conference (the SIGKDD group holds/organises a conference). The subject entities differ (steering committee vs. organising ACM SIGKDD body) and the object entities differ (conference volume vs. conference event), so the relations do not coincide.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'can stay in' is an object property mapping a Person to a Place (accommodation). They share only the domain Person; their ranges and intended meanings differ entirely, so they are not the same relation.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people on the conference committee), while B's gives_presentations relates an active conference participant to a presentation they deliver. Different domains (Conference vs. participant) and different ranges (Conference Member vs. Presentation), so the relations are unrelated.

A's Co chair is a specific committee leadership role (sibling of Chair, parent Committee member, tied to committees via has a committee co chair). B's Possible Reviewer is a general person role that can review papers (parent of PC Member, domain/range around Paper and Review). The intended instances do not coincide: a co-chair is not a possible reviewer, and the contexts (committee leadership vs. reviewing) differ.

A's 'Hotel presenter' is a subclass of Delegate (a person role: a delegate who presents at a hotel), while B's 'Hotel' is a subclass of Place (a physical building/venue). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A's has Title is a datatype property of Contribution (the title of a paper/contribution), while B's Name of conference is a datatype property of Conference (the name of the event). They relate different kinds of things (contribution vs. conference) and are not the same relation.

A's hasHomePage is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's homepage URL), while B's is_used_by is an object property from Item to Person (an item is used by a person). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), direction, domain and range, so they cannot denote the same relation.

A's `follows` relates Administrative events to Administrative events (temporal ordering of events), while B's `obtain` relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A is a full version of a paper (a document type under Paper), while B is a sponsor fee (a payment type under Fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a human attending the conference, with children Active/Passive participant and siblings Reviewer, Committee member, etc.). B's 'Non Academic Event' is a subclass of Conference Event (a non-academic happening such as Break, Meal, Social Event). One denotes a person role, the other an event type; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

Trip is a social event (an excursion/outing) in confOf, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a child) in iasted. They share no meaning, no properties, and no common parent; the only overlap is the generic word 'card'/'trip' being unrelated concepts.

Both are datatype properties with domain a deadline/important-dates class and range date, so they relate the same kinds of things (a deadline and a date). However, 'is a full paper submission date' denotes specifically the full-paper submission deadline, whereas 'done till' is a generic deadline date (the date by which something must be done), which is broader and not restricted to full paper submission. They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same relation, so 'related' rather than 'equivalent'.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Mobile Computing Topic' is a research subject area under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's Social event is a subclass of Event (a conference activity such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B's Place is a physical location (Conference hall, Hotel, Main office) that a Person can stay in. They denote different concepts: an activity vs. a location, with no shared instances or subsumption.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Communications Topic' is a subject area/topic category in EDAS. They denote different concepts with no overlap.

Author in cmt is a specific role (a person who writes/submits papers, with properties like write Paper, submit Paper, has Author), while Conference contributor in Conference is a broader category covering any person contributing to a conference (including invited speakers, active participants, regular authors). Author is thus a narrower concept subsumed by Conference contributor, not equivalent.

A's Review is a document type in the conference domain (a review of a contribution, with properties 'has a review' and 'reviews' linking it to a reviewed contribution). B's Abstract is a document type in sigkdd, a sibling of Paper and Review, denoting the abstract text of a paper. They denote different concepts: a review is an evaluation artefact, an abstract is a summary of a paper. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

iasted:Item is a very broad class whose children include Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication and Transport vehicle, so it covers physical and abstract things alike. sigkdd:Document is a narrower class with children Abstract, Paper and Review, i.e. written conference artefacts. Document is one kind of Item, so Item is strictly more general than Document (subsumes), not equivalent.

A's Paper is a conference submission/review artefact (has authors, topics, reviews, accepted/pending/rejected subclasses), while B's Mailing list is a document used for communication in the conference organisation (sibling of Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance). They share only the generic Document parent and denote different concepts.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a short abstract of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version. Extended abstract in Conference is a kind of Regular contribution (a submission type) with child Abstract. They both concern abstracts, but one is a document part and the other a submission category, so they overlap rather than coincide.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' is an administrative action property with domain Administrator and range Program Committee Member, i.e. it relates an administrator to a committee member they add. B's 'organises' relates an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. The domains (Administrator vs Organisation/Person) and ranges (Program Committee Member vs Event) are disjoint, and the intended relations differ (adding a member vs organising an event), so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname; B's 'has VAT' is a datatype property of Social/Working event giving a value-added-tax string. Different domains, different intended meanings, no overlap.

A's `date` is a generic datatype property on Conference, while B's `is a date of camera ready paper submission` is a specific date property on Important dates. The generic date subsumes the specific camera-ready submission date, so A is more general than B (A subsumed_by B in the sense that B is a narrower property).

A's `reviews` is a property of a Review linking it to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution). B's `give` is a property of a Person linking them to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or submitting an item). Different domains (Review vs Person), different ranges, and different intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's Conference Member is a Person (a person affiliated with a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair roles), while B's Conference activity is an Activity (an event such as a lecture, coffee break, or registration). They denote different kinds of entities (people vs. events) and are not equivalent.

A's has Street is a datatype property of Contact Information giving a street address string; B's E mail is a datatype property of Person giving an email address string. They relate different kinds of information (postal street vs. email) in different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to the Reviewer it is assigned to (a concrete assignment relation). B's 'has a review expertise' links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise topic, i.e. it expresses the subject area a contribution is about, not an assignment of a person. Different domain/range kinds (Reviewer vs Review expertise) and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members (domain Committee, range Committee member), while B's 'held In' links an Event to a Location (domain Event, range Location). They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions of meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A is a physical place (a type of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place) where one can stay, while B is a document (a Form under Document) used for hotel registration. They denote different kinds of entities (place vs. document) and are not equivalent.

Attendee in edas is a generic person who attends the conference (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Chair roles), while OC Chair in ekaw is a specific organising-committee leadership role (subclass of OC Member). An OC Chair is a kind of participant, but the two classes do not denote the same concept; Attendee is far more general and not equivalent to the specific OC Chair role.

Session Chair in edas is a Person who initiates calls and reviews papers (a committee/organisational role), while Author in sigkdd is a Speaker who submits papers and obtains awards. They denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Paper Author' is a general person role for anyone who authors a paper, a sibling of Conference Participant and Possible Reviewer under Person. B's 'Author of paper student' is a much narrower class: a Student who is an Author of a paper, sitting under Author alongside 'Author of paper'. Every instance of B (a student paper author) is an instance of A (a paper author), but not vice versa, so A is more general and B is subsumed by A.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper) in the cmt ontology, while B is a subject area/topic (Microelectronics) in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document type vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

A's hasPhone relates a Person to a telephone number (string), while B's E-mail relates a Person to an email address (string). These are distinct contact properties with different intended values, so they are not equivalent.

The two properties are inverses of each other: cmt's hasConferenceMember goes from Conference to Conference Member, while edas's attendeeAt goes from Person to Conference Event. They relate the same kinds of entities (a conference/event and a person attending it) but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call For Papers' is an announcement/invitation document (a subclass of Call, sibling of Call For Manuscripts and Call For Reviews), whereas B 'Conference Paper' is a type of Paper document (subclass of Paper, sibling of Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, etc.). One is a call/announcement, the other is the paper itself; their intended instances do not coincide.

Both properties link a person-like entity to a Document, but they are not the same relation: edas hasRelatedDocument is a broad association from Academic Event/Conference/Conference Session/Person to Document, while sigkdd presentation is specifically the act of a Speaker presenting a Document. The sigkdd property is narrower (domain Speaker, a subclass of Person) and denotes presentation rather than mere relatedness, so the two overlap but are not equivalent.

A's property links a Review preference to the Topic/Submitted contribution it prefers, while B's write links a Person to an Item they authored. Different domains (Review preference vs Person), different ranges (Topic/Submitted contribution vs Item), and different intended relations (preference over topics vs authorship), so they are not equivalent.

A's has Cost Amount is a datatype property mapping a Sponsorship to an integer cost amount. B's is paid with is an object property mapping Money to an Item (a thing used to pay). They differ in domain (Sponsorship vs Money), range (int vs Item), and kind (datatype vs object), so they do not denote the same relation.

Both properties are named 'obtain' and relate a person/author to something they receive, but the ranges differ: iasted's range is the general class Item, while sigkdd's range is the narrower Award. Since Award is a kind of item an author can obtain, the sigkdd property is more specific; the two overlap but are not equivalent.

Accommodation Place is a specific kind of place (a place to stay, sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place under Place), whereas iasted's Place is the general superclass of all locations (Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office, Session room). Accommodation Place is therefore strictly more specific than Place, i.e. subsumed by it, not equivalent.

A's 'Early paid applicant' is a subclass of 'Paid applicant' (a registered applicant who has paid early), while B's 'Late Registered Participant' is a conference participant who registered late. Both concern registration timing, but one is about early payment and the other about late registration; they are not the same concept, though they overlap in the registration-timing dimension.

A Demo Chair is a conference participant role responsible for demo sessions, a sibling of PC Chair, Workshop Chair, Tutorial Chair, etc. B Program Chair is an organizer role (sibling of General Chair, PC member, Webmaster) responsible for the program. Different roles with different responsibilities and different parent hierarchies (Conference Participant vs Organizator); they are not the same concept.
A's hasKeyword relates a Contribution to a keyword string, while B's hasLastName relates a Person to a surname string. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's property is the date of the acceptance announcement (a notification deadline within Important dates), while B's property is the start date of the conference itself. They denote different events/dates in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

confOf Contribution is a conference submission (Paper/Poster/Short paper) with properties like abstract, has Title, written By Author, reviewed by PC members. iasted Item is a generic physical/abstract object (Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle) with properties about being given, paid for, made from, needed for. The domains and intended instances do not coincide; Contribution is at most a very narrow special case of Item, but the contexts (conference submission vs. generic item) are unrelated.

A's belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event (domain Programme, range Conference Event), while B's hasEvent links an Event to an Event (domain Event, range Event). The domains and ranges differ, so they do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction; they are not equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Workshop, target of 'has tutorials' from Conference volume), while B's Sponzor fee is a type of Fee (sibling of Registration fee). They denote entirely different concepts: an instructional event versus a sponsorship payment.

A's 'Conference participant' is the general class of all people participating in a conference (its children are Active/Passive conference participant), while B's 'Demo Chair' is a specific role held by a conference participant (a subclass of ekaw's Conference Participant). The general participant class is strictly more general than the specific Demo Chair role, so A subsumes B; they are not equivalent.
A's 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee, while B's 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both classes denote the subject area of a paper/contribution: Conference's Topic is linked to Submitted contribution, Review preference and Conference part, while confOf's Topic is linked to Contribution, Member PC and Working event. Same intended instances (research topics), so they are equivalent.

A's Review is the general review document class (parent of Meta Review, sibling of Paper, written by a Reviewer), while B's Neutral Review is a specific review outcome/type under Review in ekaw, alongside Negative and Positive Review. A's Review is strictly more general than B's Neutral Review, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

A's 'Worker lecturer' is a Lecturer who is also a Worker (a staff member who lectures), sitting under Lecturer alongside Student lecturer. B's 'Author of paper student' is a Student who is an Author of a paper, sitting under Author alongside Author of paper. The two combine different roles (lecturer/worker vs student/author) and neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B 'Organizational Meeting' is a type of academic event (a meeting for organization). They belong to different branches (document vs. event) and have no overlap in meaning.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a kind of Paper (a scientific contribution submitted to a conference), sitting under Document > Paper with siblings like Camera Ready Paper and Regular Paper. B 'Record of attendance' is a Document used to record who attended, a sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Review, Submission, etc. The two denote different concepts: a paper vs. an attendance record. They share only the broad Document ancestor, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a role of a person (a Conference contributor, sibling of Regular author), while B's 'Conference state' is a state of a conference (sibling of Presenter state, Sponsor state). They denote different concepts: a person role vs. a conference status, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Accepted Paper' is a document (a paper that has been accepted, part of the proceedings), while B's 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity/process (the act of accepting a manuscript) under 'Activity before conference'. They are related (the activity produces the accepted paper) but denote different concepts, so not equivalent.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while B's 'Conference' is a working event (the event itself). They belong to different branches (document vs. event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Flyer is a specific kind of document (a leaf under Document in ekaw, with siblings Paper, Review, Abstract), whereas iasted's Document is a broad class covering many document types (Review, Submission, Form, etc.). A Flyer is a Document, but not every Document is a Flyer, so Flyer is subsumed by Document.

A 'Short paper' is a type of contribution (a paper of short length), while B 'Assigned Paper' is a submitted paper that has been assigned to a reviewer for evaluation. They denote different concepts: one is a document type, the other a workflow state of a submitted paper. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

A's Conference is the overall conference event/organisation (has members, deadlines, administrators, submissions), while B's Conference Banquet is a specific social event (a meal) within a conference, sibling of Conference Trip. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Proceedings Publisher' is an organisation (a publisher of conference proceedings, sibling of Academic Institution and Organising Agency under Organisation), whereas B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee (sibling of Program Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee under Committee). They denote different kinds of entities (organisation vs. committee) and are not equivalent.

A's Conference Banquet is a social event (an activity held during the conference, sibling of Conference Trip), while B's Conference restaurant is a building/place (sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport). One is an event, the other a physical location, so their instances cannot coincide.

A's Break Event is a general non-academic event class whose children include Coffee Break, Meal Break and Free Time Break; B's Coffee break is a specific conference activity. The general Break Event subsumes the specific Coffee break, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Assistant is a staff/helper role (sibling of Administrator, Volunteer, Chair PC) in the conference organisation, while ekaw's Student is an academic status of a person (sibling of Paper Author, Possible Reviewer). They denote different concepts; an assistant need not be a student and a student need not be an assistant.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad class of persons contributing to a conference (parents Person; children include Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author), whereas B's 'Session chair' is a specific delegate role (parent Delegate, sibling of Speaker, Listener, etc.). A session chair is a narrow role, not a general contributor, and the two classes do not have coinciding instances.

A 'Camera Ready Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document type), while B 'Deadline' is a subclass of Time (a temporal point with children such as camera ready manuscript deadline). They denote different concepts: one is a kind of document, the other a kind of time point. Although a camera-ready paper is associated with a camera-ready deadline, the classes themselves are not equivalent.

In the Conference ontology, Abstract is a specific kind of contribution (an extended abstract that is part of a paper/poster/presentation), whereas in sigkdd, Document is the general superclass of Abstract, Paper and Review. Abstract is therefore a narrower concept than Document, so Abstract is subsumed by Document rather than equivalent to it.

A's 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while B's 'search' links the ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (sponsor search). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'is held after' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events), while B's 'submit until' relates a Document to a Deadline (submission deadline for a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property of Conference volume giving the location/venue of a conference volume (a string location). B's 'Name of conference' is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's name. They relate different attributes (location vs. name) of different subjects (volume vs. conference), so they are not equivalent.

A's `follows` relates two Administrative events (temporal ordering of administrative events), while B's `has Programme` relates a Conference Event to its Programme (a part/whole structural relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Test Only Topic' is a placeholder topic in the EDAS topic taxonomy (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), while B 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a specific award type under Award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic vs. award) and share no intended instances.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/organiser of the conference, sibling of Program Committee Chair and Author under Chairman/Conference Member). B 'Author book proceedings included' is a subclass of Author describing an author whose book is included in the proceedings — a specific kind of author, not a chair. The two denote different concepts (organiser role vs. author-of-included-book), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's given name, while B's 'Name of sponsor' is a datatype property of Sponzor giving the name of a sponsoring organisation. Different domains (Person vs Sponzor) and different intended meanings (first name vs sponsor name), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Invitation letter' is a specific administrative document (an invitation sent to a participant), while B's 'Paper' is the scientific contribution submitted by an author (domain of submit: Author -> Paper). They are different document types with different roles in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A is a kind of Paper (a document submitted to a conference), while B is a kind of Building (a physical venue where a conference takes place). Their paths, parents and siblings are entirely different domains (Document vs Place), so they denote different concepts.

A's `reviews` links a Review to the contribution it reviews (range: Reviewed contribution), while B's `reviewWrittenBy` links a Review to the person who wrote it (range: Possible Reviewer). They relate different kinds of things (reviewed paper vs. reviewer), so they are not equivalent; in fact they are inverses of different relations and thus unrelated.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad class under Person whose children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, Conference Chair, etc., and it is linked to Conference via has Conference Member / member Of Conference. In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a narrower class under Organizator, sibling to General Chair, Program Chair, etc. The sigkdd class corresponds to one of the cmt subclasses (Program Committee Member), not to the general Conference Member, so cmt's Conference Member is strictly more general and subsumes the sigkdd Program Committee member.

cmt:User is a general person role (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer) representing any system user. iasted:Lecturer is a specific speaker role under Author (with children Student lecturer, Worker lecturer), a narrow subtype of author/speaker. The two do not denote the same concept; User is far more general and Lecturer is a specific academic role, so they are unrelated.

Conference applicant is a Person who applies to attend a conference (parent Person, child Registeered applicant, siblings include Conference participant, Reviewer, Committee member), whereas Program Committee member is an Organizator (parent Organizator, siblings General Chair, Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, Webmaster). They denote different roles in the conference domain: an applicant is a prospective attendee, while a PC member is an organizer. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

Both properties link a reviewer to the paper they review, in the same direction (reviewer -> paper). cmt's 'has Been Assigned' has domain Reviewer and range Paper; ekaw's 'reviewer Of Paper' has domain Possible Reviewer (a reviewer role) and range Paper. The domain difference (Reviewer vs Possible Reviewer) reflects the role/agent modelling difference between the ontologies, but the intended relation — a reviewer being assigned to / reviewing a paper — is the same, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'has Postal Code' is a datatype property of Contact Information with range string, capturing a postal/zip code; B's 'Name' is a datatype property of Person with range string, capturing a person's name. They relate different kinds of things (contact address vs. person identity) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

A's 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action of entering conference data), while B's 'event On List' relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (an event being listed in a publication). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Paper is a document class (subclass of Document, with children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version, siblings Review, and properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To). B's Deadline Author notification is a deadline/date class (subclass of Deadline, sibling of Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Paper Submission, with property notification until). They denote different concepts: a paper artefact versus a notification deadline, so they are unrelated.

A's `Regular` is a subclass of Participant (a person who is a regular participant, sibling of Member and Student), while B's `Regular Session` is a subclass of Session (a kind of scientific event, sibling of Conference Session, Demo Session, etc.). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has Surname' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'written By' is an object property mapping a Document to a Person (the author of a document). They differ in domain, range, and intended relation, so they are unrelated.

Accepted Paper is a subclass of Paper in edas (path Document > Paper > Accepted Paper), representing only papers that have been accepted. The sigkdd Paper class is the general paper concept (Document > Paper) with property submit (Author -> Paper), covering all submitted papers regardless of acceptance status. Thus Accepted Paper is strictly narrower than Paper, so Accepted Paper is subsumed by Paper.

A's Chair is a committee member who chairs a committee (domain/range: Committee -> Chair), while B's Session Chair is a person who chairs a session and reviews papers (initiates calls, reviews papers). Both are chair roles, but they denote different chairing functions (committee chair vs. session chair), so they overlap as chair roles without being equivalent.

A's 'Accepted Paper' is a specific state of a conference Paper (sibling of Rejected/Pending/Published Paper, related to a Paper Presentation), whereas B's 'Document' is a broad superclass of many conference artefacts (Review, Submission, Form, Invitation letter, etc.). The two do not denote the same concept: an accepted paper is a narrow subclass of paper, not a general document, and B's Document is not restricted to papers. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

Both denote a social conference event where attendees gather for drinks/reception. A's Reception is a Social Event (sibling Excursion), B's Coctail reception is a Conference activity alongside Social program and Coffee break. The intended instances coincide: a social gathering/reception at the conference.

A's hasAuthor relates Paper -> Author; B's hasRelatedPaper relates Author -> Paper. They are inverse-like in direction and denote different relations (authorship vs. related-paper linkage), so they are not equivalent.
