Both properties link a call/item to the people responsible for it, but the domains and ranges differ: edas restricts to Call -> committee roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), while iasted is broader Item -> Person. They overlap in intent (initiator/signer of a call or item) but are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor, i.e. a role a document plays (a paper written by a regular author), with children Contribution 1th author and Contribution co author. B's 'Participant' is a subclass of Person, i.e. a person attending the conference, with children Member, Regular, Student. The two denote different kinds of entities (document/contribution vs. person) and their contexts, parents, children and properties do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'is an abstract submission date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date value (a deadline for submitting abstracts). B's 'abstract' is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its abstract text (a string). They relate different kinds of things (date vs. string) in different contexts (deadline vs. paper content), so they are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is the abstract/summary document of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper. Demo Paper (ekaw) is a paper type for demonstrations, sibling of Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc. They denote different concepts: an abstract is a document part, a demo paper is a submission category. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's 'Review Form' is the document/form used to record a review, while B's 'Review' is the review itself (a Document in iasted). They are closely related (the form is the artefact that carries the review) but not the same concept: a form is a template/document, a review is the evaluation content. Hence related rather than equivalent.

A's 'assigned By Administrator' relates a Reviewer to an Administrator (a person who assigns reviews), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper in the published state (siblings: Accepted, Active, Pending, Rejected, Withdrawn — these are statuses of a paper). B 'Demo Paper' is a paper type/kind (siblings: Camera Ready, Conference, Industrial, Poster, Regular, Submitted, Workshop — these are paper categories). The two denote different dimensions (publication status vs. paper type) and do not coincide; a demo paper is not necessarily published and a published paper need not be a demo paper.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) relation between a Conference volume and its Conference parts, whereas B's 'is Location Of' is a spatial relation between a Place and a Conference Event. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no overlap in meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's submit Paper relates an Author to a Paper (submission act), while B's notification until relates an Author to a Deadline (notification deadline). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (path Person > Conference Member > Author > Co author), i.e. a co-author is a specific kind of author, while B's 'Author' is the general author class (Person > Author) that writes Contributions. The two do not coincide: every co-author is an author, but not every author is a co-author, so A is strictly more specific and is subsumed by B.

A's 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person (a person who belongs to a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself (with city, start/end dates, held by an ACM SIGKDD). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' and denotes the scholarly contribution (paper/poster/talk) submitted to and published in a conference volume, with children like Invited talk, Poster, Presentation, Regular contribution, Written contribution and properties linking it to a Conference volume. B's 'Document' is a general administrative artefact (siblings: Audiovisual equipment, Card, Publication, Transport vehicle; children: Form, Invitation letter, Mailing list, Payment document, Record of attendance, Viza, etc.) and is not the scholarly contribution concept. The two classes have different intensions and extensions, so they are not equivalent.

Workshop is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, part of a conference volume), whereas Program Committee is a committee of people (sibling of Organizing Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee). They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Paper (a document type, sibling of Paper Full Version), while B's 'Test Only Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. topic) and share no intended instances.

A's hasPhone is a datatype property linking a Person to a string phone number, while B's heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Conference Session is a general session type (its properties relate documents to Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person), while ekaw's Poster Session is a specific kind of Session, sibling to Conference Session, Demo Session, Regular Session and Workshop Session. A Poster Session is a kind of conference session, so the edas general class subsumes the ekaw specific class; they are not equivalent.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of contribution/submission distinguished by length, a sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution. B 'Withdrawn Paper' is a paper in the withdrawn status, a sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper under Paper. They denote different concepts: one is a submission type, the other a status of a paper; neither subsumes the other.

A 'Trip city' is a city associated with a trip (a subclass of City, sibling of Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city), whereas B 'Hotel' is a lodging place (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference hall and Main office). They denote different concepts in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a submission of interest to attend), while B's hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a person who may review it). Different range concepts and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'scientifically Organises' relates an Academic Institution to the events/conferences it organises (domain Academic Institution), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to the Speaker who presented it (domain Document, range Speaker). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Both Location (ekaw) and Place (iasted) denote the venue/place where events or activities are held. ekaw's Location is the range of 'held In' (Event -> Location) and domain of 'location Of' (Location -> Event); iasted's Place is the range of 'is held in' (Activity -> Place, Time) and is a superclass of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room, etc. The intended instances (rooms, buildings, cities where conference events occur) coincide, so the two classes are equivalent despite differing labels and surrounding property names.

Chairman (cmt) is a Person who chairs a conference/committee, with subclasses Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair. Speaker (iasted) is a Delegate who presents, with subclasses Author and Reviewer. The two denote different roles in the conference domain: a chairman organises/leads, a speaker presents. Their paths, parents, children and siblings do not overlap, so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference topic (a subject area under Computer Networks Topic), while B is a state of a sponsor in the conference process (sibling of Conference state and Presenter state). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'has members' relates a Committee to its Committee members (a domain-specific membership relation). B's 'has Part' is a generic mereological part-of relation with unspecified domain/range, not restricted to committees or members. They do not denote the same relation.

Company in confOf is an organization type (sibling of University under Organization), i.e. an institution that authors papers. 'Operating Topicsystems' in edas is a research topic under Topic, a subject area for papers. They denote different kinds of things (organization vs. topic) and are unrelated.

A's hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (author's related papers), while B's design relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline (a conference's design deadline). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.
A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while B's paper In Volume relates a Paper to a Volume (publication venue). Different domain/range and direction, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad class of persons contributing to a conference (parents Person; children Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author; siblings Committee member, Reviewer, etc.), i.e. anyone who contributes. B's 'Conference Chair' is a specific role (sibling of Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) that initiates calls and reviews papers. A chair is a specific role, not the general contributor class; the two do not denote the same concept, and neither subsumes the other in the intended sense (a chair is not a contributor in A's taxonomy, and contributor is not a chair).

Conference Chair is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the person hierarchy), while Social program is a conference activity (a subclass of Conference activity with child Dinner banquet). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology (Person vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Talk Event is an academic event (a scheduled happening such as a welcome or closing talk) under Conference Event, while B's Tutorial Abstract is a document (an abstract text) under Document > Abstract. They belong to different top-level branches (event vs. document) and denote different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a subclass of Conference applicant (a person who has registered, with child Paid applicant), i.e. a person/role. B 'Fee' is a monetary charge with children Registration fee and Sponzor fee, i.e. a payment concept. They denote different kinds of things (person vs. fee) and are not equivalent.

A 'Talk Event' is an academic event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), while B 'Silver Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (events vs. sponsors) and share no intended instances.

Company in confOf is an organizational entity (a type of Organization, sibling of University) representing a corporate affiliation of conference participants. Communication Theory Topic in edas is a research subject area (a type of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (organization vs. subject area) and share no intended instances.

A's 'reviewer Bidding Started By' relates a Conference to the Administrator who started the bidding process, while B's 'is Reviewing' relates a person (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper they review. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; they are not the same relation.

A relates a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (the chair's role over a conference component), while B relates a Call to a person role (who initiated the call). Different domains, ranges, and direction of meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

Both properties link a Conference to the people who are members of it. cmt's range Conference Member is a subclass of Person (a person involved in the conference), and edas's range Person covers the same individuals. The domain is identical (Conference) and the intended relation — a conference having a member — is the same, so the two properties are equivalent despite the different range class names.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial or workshop), while B's Worker lecturer is a person role (a lecturer who works), a subclass of Lecturer under Speaker/Author. The two denote entirely different kinds of entities (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the person who chairs the program committee of a conference. In ekaw, PC Chair is a Conference Participant and PC Member who leads the program committee; in sigkdd, Program Chair is an Organizator with the same role. The labels 'PC Chair' and 'Program Chair' are synonyms in the conference domain, and their contexts (leading the program committee) agree, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A 'Performance Topic' is a subject-area topic (a child of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.) used to classify conference papers. B 'Simulating' is a research activity (child of Research, sibling of Modelling) in the activity hierarchy of the conference organisation. They denote different concepts: a topic category versus a research activity, so they are not equivalent.

Negative Review is a subclass of Review in ekaw (a specific kind of review), while sigkdd's Review is the general review class. Negative Review is strictly more specific, so it is subsumed by Review, not equivalent.

A 'Committee member' is a broad role covering chairs, co-chairs, reviewers and other committee roles (its children include Chair and Co chair, and it is linked to Committee via has members / was a member of). B 'Program Committee member' is a narrower role under Organizator, sibling to Program Chair, General Chair, etc. Every program committee member is a committee member, but not vice versa, so A is more general than B (B subsumed by A).

A's `reviews` is a property from a Review to a Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed). B's `referencedIn` is a property relating a paper to a publication in which it is referenced (citation context). The domains and ranges differ: one is about the review process, the other about bibliographic citation. They are not the same relation.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution (a submission/document type, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract), whereas B's 'Review' is a document produced during the reviewing process (sibling of Abstract and Paper under Document). They denote different concepts: a submission type versus a review artefact, so they are not equivalent.
A Meta Review is a specific kind of review (a review of reviews), while B Review is the general review class. Meta Review is strictly narrower, so it is subsumed by Review rather than equivalent.

A's Paper is a general contribution (siblings Poster, Short paper), while B's Withdrawn Paper is a specific paper status under Paper in edas. A general Paper is not equivalent to a withdrawn paper; the edas Paper class (parent of Withdrawn Paper) would be the equivalent, so A is broader and B is subsumed by A.

confOf's employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment relation). iasted's is_connected_with is a very broad relation linking Activity or Person to Item or Place, with no employment semantics. The domains/ranges and intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent.

A is a research topic area (a subject category under Topic, sibling of Computer Networks, Cryptography, etc.), while B is a kind of document (an abstract for an invited talk, under Abstract). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property of Conference proceedings with range int, recording the volume number of a proceedings publication. B's 'Name of conference' is a datatype property of Conference with range string, recording the name/title of a conference event. They relate different kinds of things (proceedings volume number vs. conference name) in different domains, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (a scheduled gathering within a conference, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session), whereas B 'Hotel room' is a physical place (a lodging room, sibling of Conference hall, Session room). They denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while B's 'CAD Topic' is a subject-area topic (Computer-Aided Design) used to classify papers. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Personal History is a container of a person's publication and review history (children: Personal Publication History, Personal Review History), whereas B's Publication is a document item (sibling of Document, Card, etc., with children Book proceeding and Cd proceeding). They denote different concepts: a history record vs. a publication artefact.

A 'Security Topic' is a research topic (a subject area under Topic, sibling of Cryptography Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a kind of document (an abstract of an invited talk, under Abstract). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's reject Paper relates an Administrator to a Paper (a decision action), while B's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent nor inverse.

A 'Regular contribution' is a kind of conference contribution (a written submission such as a paper or extended abstract) in the Conference ontology, whereas B 'Document' is a broad administrative artefact class (forms, invitation letters, payment documents, records of attendance, etc.) under Item. Their intended instances do not coincide: a regular contribution is not a document in the iasted sense, and the Document class covers many things that are not contributions. The shared word 'document' in A's path is only an ancestor label, not an equivalence.

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper) in the document hierarchy, while B is a subclass of Topic (a medicine subject area) in the topic hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of Conference (a multi-track event) that is also a Person/TPC Member role in edas, while B's 'Technical commitee' is a Delegate subtype (a person role) in iasted. They denote different concepts: an event type versus a committee/person role, with no shared instances.

A's 'location Of' is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the event held at that location). B's 'done till' is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a date (the date by which something must be done). They relate different kinds of entities (Location->Event vs Deadline->date) and have different domains/ranges, so they are not the same relation.

A is an administrative event (the event at which reviewing results are made available to authors), a subclass of Administrative event under Event. B is a deadline (a point in time) for submissions, a subclass of Deadline under Time. They belong to different branches (Event vs Time) and denote different concepts: an event vs a temporal deadline. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

A's Review is a document produced by a reviewer about a paper (sibling of Paper, parent of Meta Review, written by a Reviewer). B's Review preference is a reviewer's declared preference/degree of expertise for a topic or submission, linked to Reviewer, Topic, Submitted contribution and an integer degree. The two denote different concepts (a review document vs. a preference/expertise record), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's Science Worker is a direct subclass of Person, a general role for someone working in science (siblings include Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.). iasted's Worker lecturer is a deep leaf under Lecturer > Author > Speaker > Delegate > Conference building > Building > Place, denoting a specific kind of employed lecturer in the conference hierarchy. The two concepts differ in generality and intended instances: a Science Worker need not be a lecturer, and a Worker lecturer is a narrow academic-role class, not a general person role. They share no meaningful domain concept, so they are unrelated.

A's 'was a program committee of' relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (a committee-to-event/volume relation), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a presentation authorship relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip under Social event), while B's Programme is a document (sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set under Document) that is linked to a Conference Event. A social gathering and a conference programme document denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'written By' relates a Contribution to its Author; B's 'has Review' relates a Paper to its Review. Different domain (Contribution vs Paper), different range (Author vs Review), and different meaning (authorship vs review assignment), so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the registration fee category for attendees who are not members of the sponsoring organisation. They sit at the same position in the fee hierarchy (Money > Fee > Registration fee vs Fee > Registration fee), share the parent Registration fee, and their siblings are parallel fee categories (member/nonmember, student, author/nonauthor). The labels 'Nonmember registration fee' and 'Registration Non Member' are synonymous in the conference domain.

Reviewer is a person role (a subclass of Person) in the Conference ontology, whereas Personal Review History is a record/history entity in edas, a subclass of Personal History. They denote different kinds of things (agent vs. information artefact), so they are not equivalent.
hasAuthor relates Paper -> Author, while submit relates Author -> Paper; they are inverse relations, not equivalent.

Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Conference proceedings is a published artefact with a publisher, volume and ISBN. Their contexts, parents and properties do not overlap; the shared word 'conference' is incidental.

In EKAW, Session is a general Scientific Event with children Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session, Workshop Session. The EDAS Conference Session is one specific kind of session, so it is strictly narrower than EKAW's Session. Hence EDAS Conference Session is subsumed by EKAW Session, not equivalent.

A's 'has a steering committee' relates a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a subproperty of has_committee), while B's 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; no overlap in the conference domain.

A 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about the conference, with a URL), while B 'Session room' is a physical place (a room where sessions are held). They belong to different branches (document vs. place) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a conference part (a type of event/activity alongside Track and Tutorial, with a 'has workshops' property from Conference volume), while B's Workshop Session is a specific session within a scientific event, sibling to Conference Session, Regular Session, etc. A workshop (the event) and a workshop session (a time slot within it) are related but not the same concept; the session is a part of the workshop event, so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference contribution that has passed review (a document/paper state, sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B is a review rating value ('Accept If Room') used by reviewers, sibling of Accept/Reject ratings. Different domains (paper lifecycle vs. review score), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Talk Event' is a subclass of Academic Event (a kind of conference event such as a welcome or closing talk), while B's 'Conference days' is a subclass of Time (a temporal span containing delegates and individual conference days). They belong to different branches (event vs. time) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) providing participant information, while B's 'Book proceeding' is a publication (sibling of Cd proceeding) that is a proceedings book. They denote different concepts: one is an informational document, the other a published proceedings volume.

A's submit Paper is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). B's is a date of camera ready paper submission is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value (domain Important dates, range date). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and represent different concepts (submission act vs. deadline date), so they are unrelated.

memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference, while hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person. Both express participation in a conference, but the subject/object kinds differ (member vs. event, conference vs. person), so they are not the same relation; they are only loosely related.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract; B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the talk they give). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a document/item to the people who authored it: Conference's 'has authors' has domain Conference document and range Person, while iasted's 'is signed by' has domain Item and range Person. In the conference domain, a document's authors are exactly the persons who signed/created it, so the two relations denote the same authorship relation in the same direction.

A's 'Conference airport' is a Building (a venue-adjacent building type, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference building, etc.), whereas B's 'Hotel' is a direct subclass of Place, not a Building. Although both are places in the conference domain, an airport and a hotel are distinct concepts; the shared 'conference' context does not make them equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property of Conference document giving the publication/issue date of a document, while B's 'Date' is a datatype property of Deadline giving the date/time of a deadline. Different domains (document vs. deadline) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's Abstract is a subclass of Extended abstract (a kind of conference contribution, the abstract text itself), while B's Paper is a top-level document class with siblings Abstract and Review; in sigkdd, Abstract is a separate sibling of Paper, so A's Abstract corresponds to B's Abstract, not B's Paper. The two denote different concepts.

A's property links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (an organisational role), while B's presentation links a Speaker to a Document (a talk given by a person). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B's 'Cd proceening' is a publication item (sibling of Book proceeding). They denote different concepts: informational document vs. published proceedings medium.

A 'Talk Event' is an academic event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk), while B 'Platinum Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (events vs. sponsors) and share no intended instances.

ekaw:Organisation is an organising body (academic institution, organising agency, proceedings publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings; sigkdd:Document is a written artefact (abstract, paper, review) presented by a speaker and submitted by a deadline. Different kinds of things with no overlap, despite both being classes.

A is a conference document type (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a narrow EDAS subject topic under Computer Networks Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A 'Camera ready contribution' is a class of accepted paper in its final form (a document/contribution in the submission workflow). B 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a subclass of Deadline, i.e. a temporal milestone for submitting papers. One is a document type, the other a deadline/event; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A 'Short paper' is a kind of Contribution (a submission category, sibling of Paper and Poster), whereas B 'Abstract' is a kind of Document (a written artefact, sibling of Paper, Review, Web Site). Although an abstract can be a short paper, the intended instances do not coincide: Short paper is a submission type, Abstract is a document type. They are not equivalent.

A 'Member PC' (confOf) is a person role — a PC member/reviewer who reviews contributions and has topic expertise. B 'Numerical Review Question' (edas) is a type of review question (a form field with a numeric answer) under Review Question. One is a person, the other a review-form item; they share no instances and are unrelated.

A's 'Academic Event' is a subclass of Conference Event (an event such as a workshop, talk, or paper presentation), while B's 'Speaker' is a subclass of Person (a role played by an author or invited speaker). They belong to different branches of the domain (event vs. person) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Presenter in ekaw is a conference participant who gives a presentation (a role, with child Invited Speaker), whereas Student non speaker in iasted is a delegate who is a student and does not speak/present. The two concepts are disjoint: a presenter is by definition a speaker, while a student non speaker is explicitly a non-speaker. Different paths (Person > Conference Participant vs Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Non speaker) and different siblings confirm they denote different concepts.

A's Paper is a kind of contribution (a document submitted to a conference), while B's Best Research Paper Award is a kind of Award (a prize given to a paper). They belong to different branches (Contribution vs Award) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Numerical Review Question' is a type of review question (a question with a numeric answer used in reviewing), while B 'Final manuscript' is a document/submission type (the final version of a submitted paper). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (review process vs. document lifecycle) and share no intended instances.

A's paper ID is an identifier attribute of a Paper (domain Paper, range unsignedLong), while B's has amount of is a monetary amount attribute of Money (domain Money, range int). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Conference part is a structural component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) with properties linking it to conference volumes, chairs and topics. Place in sigkdd is a physical location (Conference hall, Hotel, Main office) that a Person can stay in. Their children, properties and intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A is 'Rejected contribution' (a reviewed contribution that was rejected), while B is 'Accepted Paper' (a paper that was accepted). They are opposite outcomes of the review process, not the same concept. Although both are subclasses of a reviewed/submitted paper, their intended instances are disjoint (rejected vs accepted), so they are unrelated rather than equivalent.

A's 'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' relates an Administrator to a Conference (a mailing/manifest action), while B's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (scheduling overlap). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Coctail reception' is a social conference activity (a subclass of Conference activity, sibling of Coffee break, Welcome address, etc.), whereas B 'Organizator' is a person role (subclass of Person, superclass of General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and cannot be equivalent.

A's 'is paid for' relates Money to Activity/Item (money is paid for an activity or item), while B's 'payed by' relates Registration fee to Person (a fee is paid by a person). They differ in domain, range, and direction of the relation, so they are not equivalent.

In sigkdd, Speaker is a general role with children Author and Invited Speaker, so Invited Speaker is a proper subclass of Speaker. In Conference, Invited speaker is a specific contributor role. The two are not equivalent: A is strictly narrower than B.

A is a research topic area (Communication Theory Topic) under Topic, while B is an organizational body (Organizing Committee) under Committee. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

Both properties relate a document/item to the person(s) who authored it, in the same direction (document -> person). 'has authors' (Conference document -> Person) and 'is writen by' (Item -> Person) denote the same authorship relation; the domain classes Conference document and Item are the corresponding document concepts in the two ontologies.

A's Paper is a document submitted to a conference (parent Document, children Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version, properties like has Author, assigned To Reviewer, has Decision). B's Computer Networks Topic is a subject-area/topic category under Topic, with subtopics such as Computer Networks Security Topic. A paper is not a topic; the entities denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference (an admin enabling a virtual meeting for a conference), while B's organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (who organises the event). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both properties link a conference-domain entity to a Topic, but A's property is restricted to a Conference part (track/workshop/tutorial) as domain, while B's hasTopic applies to Conference and Paper. They overlap in relating conferences to topics but are not the same relation, since B also covers papers and A covers only conference parts.

A is a subclass of Paid applicant (a person who has paid early registration), while B is an activity in the pre-conference phase (receiving a manuscript). They belong to different branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Personal History in edas is a container for a person's publication and review history (children: Personal Publication History, Personal Review History), i.e. a record about an individual. Proceedings in ekaw is a document type (path Document > Multi author Volume > Proceedings, child Conference Proceedings), i.e. a published collection of conference papers. They denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

A's Reception is a social event (a gathering/party) in the conference event hierarchy, while B's Speaker is a person role in the person hierarchy. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's has Name is the full name of a conference, while B's City of conference is the city where the conference is held. Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range string, but they denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Program committee' is a collective committee (a group of people, sibling of Organizing/Steering committee, domain/range of committee-membership properties). B's 'Program Chair' is a single person role (a subclass of Organizator/Person, sibling of General Chair and Program Committee member). A committee is not a person role, so the two denote different concepts.

A's 'was a program committee of' relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (the committee serves a conference), while B's 'organised By' relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the event is organised by an agent). Different domain, range, and direction of relation; they do not denote the same relation.

Both entities denote the conference event itself: 'Conference' in the first ontology and 'Conference' in confOf have the same label, kind (class), and intended instances (a conference event with papers, committees, etc.). The paths and context agree, so they are equivalent.

A's Paper is a submitted document with authors, reviews, decisions and subject areas; B's Programme is a conference schedule document that belongs to a Conference Event and has a has Programme inverse. Different intended instances despite both being Documents.

A's 'Demo Chair' is a conference participant role responsible for demo sessions, sibling to PC Chair, Workshop Chair, Tutorial Chair, Session Chair. B's 'Session chair' is a delegate role in the iasted ontology, sibling to Speaker, Listener, etc. Although both are chair roles, they denote different specific roles (demo chair vs session chair), and the ontologies place them in different role hierarchies; a reference alignment would not equate them.

A's 'has a location' is a datatype property of Conference volume (the location of a conference/volume), while B's 'location' is a datatype property of Social event and Working event (where an event is held). Different domains (conference volume vs. events) mean the properties relate different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (event-to-event, symmetric co-occurrence), while B's 'is Location Of' relates a Place to a Conference Event (place-to-event, inverse of a located-at relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A is a document type (the full version of a paper, sibling of Paper Abstract under Paper), while B is a deadline (the abstract submission deadline, sibling of paper submission and author notification deadlines under Deadline). They denote different concepts in different branches of the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (e.g. a conference to its sub-events), while B's awarded_by relates an Award to the agent/organisation that granted it. Different domains and ranges, no shared meaning.

A's enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference (an admin enabling a virtual meeting for a conference), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (a document being presented by a speaker). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper with range string, denoting the title of a paper. B's Date is a datatype property of Deadline with range dateTime, denoting a deadline date. They relate different kinds of things (paper title vs. deadline date) and have different domains and ranges, so they are not equivalent.

A's Committee is a group/organisational body (with chairs, co-chairs, members, and subcommittees like Program committee), whereas B's Person is an individual human (with children Delegate and Sponsor, and properties like give, is paid by, is present). A committee is not a person, and neither subsumes the other; the entities denote different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Banquet is a social event (a festive meal) in the event hierarchy, while Trip day is a temporal unit (a day of a trip) under Time. They denote different kinds of things (event vs. time interval) and are not equivalent.

cmt's Conference Member is a broad class covering all people involved in the conference (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), while ekaw's PC Member is a narrower role restricted to program-committee members. The cmt class is strictly more general, so it subsumes PC Member rather than being equivalent.

A's 'Chair PC' is a Person subclass (sibling of Member PC, Author, etc.) representing the chair of the programme committee; B's 'SC Member' is a PC Member subclass denoting a member of the steering committee, with sibling 'PC Chair'. Both concern PC leadership/roles, but one is the chair role and the other a steering-committee member role, so they overlap in the PC context without denoting the same concept.

A is a person role (a chair of the conference, sibling of Author/Reviewer under Person > Chairman), while B is a physical building (a sponsor company house, sibling of Conference hotel/airport under Place > Building). Different kinds and domains, so they are unrelated.

A's Decision is the outcome of a review process (children Acceptance/Rejection, range of has Decision from Paper), while B's Organisation is an entity that organises events and publishes proceedings (children Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A's 'max Papers' is a datatype property on Program Committee Member with range int, expressing a numeric limit on papers a PC member can handle. B's 'has a name' is a datatype property with range string applying to Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, expressing a name. Different domains, different ranges, different intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Conference Paper is a specific kind of paper (a paper submitted to/presented at a conference), sitting under Paper alongside Camera Ready, Demo, Poster, Workshop, etc. B's Paper is the general document class (sibling of Abstract and Review, submitted by an Author). Conference Paper is thus strictly narrower than Paper, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

A's 'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them; B's 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Conference it holds. Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Committee member' is a role in the conference organisation (parent of Chair/Co chair, linked to Committee via has members/was a member of). B's 'Scholar' is a person price category (comment 'price category - scholar') with a study At property, sibling of Administrator, Author, Participant, etc. The intended instances do not coincide: a committee member is not necessarily a scholar and vice versa, and the contexts (committee roles vs. registration price categories) differ.

A's `issues` relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings). B's `relates To` relates a Document to events, sessions or persons (domain Document, range Academic Event/Conference/Conference Session/Person). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A is a research topic class (a subject area for papers, under Topic), while B is an organizational committee class (under Committee). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain and share no instances.

A's virtualMeetingEnabledBy relates a Conference to an Administrator (the person enabling virtual meeting support), while B's organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organiser of the event). Different domain (Conference vs Event), different range (Administrator vs Organisation/Person), and different intended meaning (enabling virtual meetings vs organising an event), so they are not equivalent.

Participant in confOf is a subclass of Person (path Person > Participant) restricted to conference attendees with children Member, Regular, Student and property early Registration. Person in ekaw is the general superclass of all people (children include Conference Participant, Paper Author, Student, etc.) with properties like author Of, written By. Participant is strictly more specific than Person, so confOf Participant is subsumed by ekaw Person, not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a conference part (a type of event/activity, sibling of Track and Tutorial), while B's Session is a scientific event that has Workshop Session as a child. In ekaw, Workshop is a sibling of Session, not equivalent to it; a Workshop Session is a session within a workshop, not the workshop itself. The two entities denote different concepts.

A's Conference Session is a session type in the EDAS ontology, while B's Workshop Session is a specific subtype of Session in EKAW. They are both session-related concepts but denote different session types; Conference Session is broader and not equivalent to Workshop Session.

A's 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while B's 'has Rating' links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (evaluation score). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A is a research topic area (Radio Communications Topic) under the Topic hierarchy in edas, while B is a kind of conference presentation event (Contributed Talk) under Individual Presentation in ekaw. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject area vs. event type) and share no intended instances.

A's belongsToEvent relates a Programme to a Conference Event (a programme belongs to an event), while B's holded_by relates a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD organisation (a conference is held by a society). The domains (Programme vs Conference) and ranges (Conference Event vs ACM SIGKDD) differ, and the directions/meanings are distinct, so they are not equivalent.

A's Workshop is a kind of working event (a session type, sibling of Conference and Tutorial) in the event hierarchy. B's Worker non speaker is a kind of delegate/attendee (a person role, sibling of Student non speaker) in the building/place hierarchy. One denotes an event, the other a person role, so they are unrelated.

A's Workshop is a working event (a kind of conference event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while B's Late Registered Participant is a person role (a conference participant who registered late, sibling of Early Registered Participant and various chairs). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (event vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.

A 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event in the conference process (the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions), while B 'Call For Papers' is a call document/announcement soliciting submissions. They belong to different branches (Event vs Call) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is the top-level class for the conference event/publication (it has a name and is linked to proceedings, parts, publishers, topics), whereas B's Conference Trip is a social event (a trip during the conference), a sibling of Conference Banquet under Social Event. They denote different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that run concurrently (domain and range both Administrative event), whereas ekaw's 'organises' relates an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. They share neither domain/range nor meaning, so they are unrelated.

Both denote the published collection of conference papers: ekaw's Conference Proceedings is a Proceedings (a Multi author Volume/Document) and iasted's Book proceeding is a Publication sibling of Cd proceeding, i.e. the printed proceedings volume. Same intended instances in the conference domain.

A's hasName is a datatype property giving a Conference's full name (domain Conference, range string), while B's obtain is an object property relating a Person to an Item. Different domain, range, and kind, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair is a person role in the conference committee hierarchy (subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while Hotel is a physical place (subclass of Place) in the sigkdd ontology. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's User is a Person (a human participant in the conference, with subclasses Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while B's Organising Agency is an Organisation (an institution such as an academic institution or proceedings publisher). They denote fundamentally different kinds of entities (person vs. organisation), so they are unrelated.

confOf Organization is an institution (Company, University) that employs people and has an address; iasted Building is a physical place (conference building, hotel, university building) that is occupied/visited by persons and paid in money. Different intended instances, so not equivalent.

A is a person role (a chair of the conference, subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while B is a conference activity (the welcome address event). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Activity) and denote entirely different concepts.

A's Conference is the event/organisation itself (has members, dates, administrators, accepts submissions), while B's Conference contribution is a document submitted to a conference (a subclass of Conference document with children like Poster, Presentation, Regular contribution). The entities denote different concepts: an event vs. a submitted document, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Workshop Paper' is a kind of academic Paper (a Document) in the conference domain, while B 'Shuttle bus' is a Transport vehicle used for transportation. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Item/Transport vehicle) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (the preference a reviewer expresses for reviewing a paper), while B's property links a personal review history to a reviewer (the reviewer that history belongs to). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same relation.

Author is a person role (a subclass of Person, with children Presenter and siblings Attendee, Reviewer, etc.), whereas Multi author Volume is a document type (a subclass of Document, with child Proceedings and siblings Paper, Review, etc.). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person (a person involved in the conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while B's 'Social Event' is a subclass of Event (a social gathering such as a banquet or trip). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while B's covers Topic relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (subject matter). Different domains, ranges and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is an event/meeting class (it has a name, proceedings, publisher, topics, and a 'Conference volume' child), whereas B's Place is a physical location (children Conference hall, Hotel, Main office; it is the range of 'can stay in' from Person). A conference is not a place, so the two classes are unrelated.

A's hasCo-author relates a Paper to a Co author (authorship relation), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation relation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation). B's is_given_by relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (authorship/presenter relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A is a paper abstract (a document type in the conference submission hierarchy), while B is a full-day tour, an activity after the conference. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (documents vs. social activities) and share no intended instances.

A is a research topic (Antennas Topic) under the Topic hierarchy in edas, while B is a document type (Invited Talk Abstract) under Document > Abstract in ekaw. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (subject area vs. publication artefact) and share no intended instances.

A's Workshop is an event type (a working event alongside Conference and Tutorial), while B's Session Chair is a person role (a conference participant who chairs a session). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person) and cannot be equivalent.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a subclass of Person (a registered applicant who paid late), while B 'Nonmember registration fee' is a subclass of Money (a fee category for nonmembers). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Money) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a human role: active/passive participant, sibling of Reviewer, Committee member), whereas B 'Activity before conference' is a subclass of Activity (a process such as accepting/receiving manuscripts, renting, research). They denote fundamentally different kinds of entities (person vs. process), so they are unrelated.

A's Presentation is a conference contribution (an event/talk given by a participant, with children like Invited talk and siblings Poster/Regular contribution), whereas B's Abstract is a document (a written summary, sibling of Paper and Review). Although A's Presentation has an 'has an abstract' property linking it to an Abstract, the two classes denote different concepts: a talk/event versus a written document. They are not equivalent.

A's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Members (people on the committee), while B's hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (the schedule of sessions). Different domain, range and meaning; the shared word 'Conference' does not make them equivalent.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a class of documents (a submitted contribution that has undergone review, with subclasses Accepted/Rejected contribution), whereas B 'Reviewer' is a class of persons (a Person who reviews papers). They denote different kinds of entities in the conference domain and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's 'reviewer Of Paper' links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (reviewing relation), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (presentation relation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a whole conference, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Tutorial is a lecture-type activity within a conference. They denote different concepts: one is the overarching event, the other a sub-event/session type. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A's Rejection is a Decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance), i.e. the act/result of rejecting a paper. B's Accepted contribution is a document type in the contribution hierarchy (a reviewed contribution that was accepted, parent of Camera ready contribution). One denotes a decision verdict, the other a class of documents/contributions; they are not the same concept, and neither subsumes the other.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class covering authors, chairs, PC members, and reviewers, with properties linking it to a Conference. Speaker in sigkdd is a distinct role class for people who present documents, with children Author and Invited Speaker and properties linking to Document. The intended instances and contexts differ: a conference member need not be a speaker, and a speaker need not be a conference member in the cmt sense. They are different concepts, not equivalent.

A's hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author (authorship of a paper), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Both are subclasses of Author, but Lecturer (iasted) is a teaching role with children Student lecturer and Worker lecturer, while Author of paper (sigkdd) is specifically someone who authors a paper, with sibling Author of paper student. They overlap (a lecturer can author papers) but neither subsumes the other, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'is held after' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (physical location). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Session is a scientific event (a scheduled meeting during a conference, with children like Conference Session, Workshop Session), while B's Research is an activity performed before the conference (with children Modelling, Simulating, siblings Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript). Different domains and kinds; no equivalence.

A's acceptedBy relates a Paper to an Administrator (the person who accepted it), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents it). Different domain/range concepts and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Author is a Person subclass (an agent who writes contributions), while B's 'Deadline Author notification' is a Deadline subclass (a time point by which authors are notified). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Deadline) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is held in' relates an Activity to a Place or Time (where an event takes place), while B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (accommodation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a specific chair role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Program Committee Chair and Associated Chair). In sigkdd, Organizator is a broad class whose children include General Chair, Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, etc. A Conference Chair is one kind of organizer, but Organizator also covers many other roles, so Conference Chair is strictly more specific: subsumed_by.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that announces a conference. B 'Free Time Break' is a scheduled non-academic event (a subclass of Break Event, sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break) representing free time during the conference. They belong to different branches (document vs. event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (a person on the organising committee), while B's is_signed_by relates an Item (e.g. a paper) to the Person who signed it. Different domains (Conference vs Item) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Paper Abstract' is a document/paper type (a subclass of Paper, sibling of Paper Full Version) representing the abstract text of a paper. B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a subclass of Deadline representing the due date for submitting a paper. One is a document artefact, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts despite the shared word 'Paper'.

Both classes denote a workshop event in the conference domain. In Conference, Workshop is a Conference part alongside Track and Tutorial, and is the range of 'has workshops' (Conference volume -> Workshop). In confOf, Workshop is a Working event alongside Conference and Tutorial, i.e. a type of event held at a conference. The intended instances (workshops held as part of a conference) coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

University is an Organization (a type of institution) in confOf, with scholars studying at it. Main office is a Place (a physical location) in sigkdd, sibling to Conference hall and Hotel. Different kinds (organization vs. place) and different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's hasReviewHistory relates a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (a record of reviews written by that reviewer), while B's presentationed_by relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domains (Reviewer vs Document), different ranges (Personal Review History vs Speaker), and different intended meanings (review record vs presentation relation), so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Late Registered Participant is a kind of person (a conference participant). They belong to disjoint top-level branches (Event vs Person) and denote entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to its Program committee (a specific committee), while B's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Both relate a conference/event to an organising body, but the ranges differ (Program committee vs Organisation/Person) and the domains differ (Conference volume vs Event), so they are not the same relation; they merely overlap in the conference-organisation domain.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a member of the conference committee who chairs the conference), while B 'Session' is a scheduled event/lecture slot within a conference activity. They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Activity) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a Person who applies to attend the conference (parent Person, child Registeered applicant), while B's 'Author' is a Speaker who authors papers (parent Speaker, children about proceedings/lectures). They overlap in that authors are typically conference participants, but an applicant is not necessarily an author and an author is not necessarily an applicant, so the classes are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Accepted contribution' is a class of documents/contributions that have passed review (sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B's 'Refusing manuscript' is an activity (a process of rejecting a manuscript), sibling of Accepting manuscript and Receiving manuscript under 'Activity before conference'. One is a document state, the other is an event/activity, and their senses are opposite (accepted vs refusing), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (authorship of a paper), while B's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who funds an event). Different domains, ranges and meanings; they merely share the generic 'by' phrasing.

A's Author is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes papers, submits papers, and can be a reviewer or chair), while B's Abstract is a document/contribution type (an extended abstract that is part of a Paper, Poster or Presentation). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (people vs. documents) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Reviewer is a person role (a Delegate/Speaker who reviews), while B's Review is a document (a Document subtype alongside Abstract and Paper). A person and a document are different kinds of entities, so the classes are unrelated despite the shared word stem.

A's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper authorship). B's 'searched by' relates a Sponzor (sponsor) to ACM SIGKDD, i.e. a sponsor being searched by a conference/group. Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Conference is the conference event/publication entity (has a name, has a Conference volume, appears in domain of 'has a name' with Conference part/proceedings/Publisher/Topic), whereas B's Conference activity is a subclass of Activity whose children are individual scheduled activities (Coctail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Presentation, Registration, etc.). The two denote different concepts: the conference as a whole vs. an activity occurring at a conference.

A 'Conference contribution' is a document submitted to a conference (a subclass of Conference document, with children like Poster, Presentation, Written contribution, and properties linking it to a Conference volume). B 'Registration fee' is a monetary Fee paid for registration (subclass of Fee under Money, with children like Student registration fee, Member registration fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (documents vs. money/fees) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A is an administrative event (the registration process/activity) in confOf, while B is a person role (a participant who registered early) in ekaw. They belong to different top-level categories (Event vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the abstract of a conference contribution. In Conference, Abstract is a part of a Paper/Poster/Presentation (is the 1th part of, has an abstract), and in ekaw, Abstract is a Document that is presented as a paper (paper Presented As, presentation Of Paper). The intended instances coincide: the abstract text associated with a paper/presentation. The differing parents (Extended abstract vs Document) reflect different modelling choices, not different concepts.

A's memberOfConference links a Conference Member (a person) to a Conference, i.e. membership of an individual in a conference. B's has_a_steering_committee links a Conference volume to a Steering committee, i.e. a conference's organisational body. Different domain/range kinds and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference volume' is a container/volume of conference contributions (it has committees, contributions, important dates, parts), whereas B's 'Conference' is a working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). They denote different concepts: a publication volume versus an event, so they are not equivalent.

A Committee member is a Person who belongs to a committee (domain/range: has members Committee -> Committee member; was a member of Committee member -> Committee), with children Chair and Co chair. B Conference Participant is a broader Person role covering presenters, authors, chairs, registered participants, etc. Every committee member is a conference participant, but not vice versa, so Committee member is strictly more specific: subsumed_by.

A is a subclass of Author (a person who authors but does not review) in cmt, while B is a subclass of Conference (a conference with two levels) in edas. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person role vs. event type) and share no intended instances.

A's 'is given by' relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it (a person/agent), whereas B's 'presentation Of Paper' relates an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper that is presented (a document). The ranges are disjoint (person vs. paper), so the properties are not equivalent; they are different relations.

confOf's Contribution is a submitted work (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with title, abstract, keywords, authors and reviews. edas's Document is a broader artefact category whose children include Paper but also Meal Menu, Programme, Review and Slide Set, and it is linked to events/persons via relates To. Contribution is thus a narrower notion than Document, so Contribution is subsumed by Document rather than equivalent.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (person-to-committee), while B's hasMember links a Conference to a Person (conference-to-person). Different domains, ranges, and direction of the relation; they do not denote the same relation.

A's Paper is the general document class for all papers (parents Document, children Accepted/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper), while B's Demo Paper is a specific kind of paper (parent Paper, siblings Regular Paper, Poster Paper, Workshop Paper, etc.). The general Paper subsumes the specific Demo Paper, so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (an organisational role assignment), while B's 'initiates' links a Conference Chair/Session Chair/TPC Member to a Call (an action of starting a call for papers). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Written contribution' is a broad class of written conference contributions (with subclasses Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, and siblings like Poster and Presentation). B 'Initial manuscipt' is a specific submission-stage document (sibling of Final manuscript) under Submission. Every initial manuscript is a written contribution, but written contributions also include final manuscripts and other written forms, so A is more general than B; they are not equivalent.

A's SC Member is a Steering Committee member, a role within the conference organisation (a subclass of PC Member, sibling of PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.). B's Registration SIGMOD Member is a registration-fee category for SIGMOD members attending the conference, a subclass of Registration fee. The two denote entirely different concepts (organisational role vs. fee category), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of Conference document (a written artefact such as a paper, poster, talk, or review submitted to a conference volume), while B's 'Participant' is a subclass of Person (an attendee such as a member, regular, or student). They belong to different top-level branches (document vs. person) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

A's hasConflictOfInterest is an object property linking a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest relation), while B's has_amount_of is a datatype property linking Money to an int (a numeric amount). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap.

A's 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (co-reviewer invitation), while B's 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper authorship). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property giving a person's given name (domain Person, range string). B's 'has Street' is a datatype property giving a street address (domain Organization, Person, range string). They relate different kinds of information (first name vs. street address), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Session Chair' is a conference participant who chairs a session (a role in the program committee/organisation), while B's 'One day presenter' is a delegate who presents for one day (a presenter subtype). They denote different roles: chairing a session vs. presenting for a single day. B's ontology even has a separate 'Session chair' class, confirming that 'One day presenter' is not the same concept.

A 'Neutral Review' is a subclass of Review (a document/evaluation artefact with polarity), while B 'Reviewer' is a person role (a Speaker who reviews). They denote different kinds of entities (review document vs. person), so they are unrelated.

A's 'reviewer Of Paper' is a specific relation from a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the paper being reviewed). B's 'give' is a broad relation from a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or item). The domains and ranges differ, and the intended meanings do not coincide; they are not equivalent.

In ekaw, PC Chair is a Person who is both a Conference Participant and a PC Member, i.e. the chair of the program committee. In sigkdd, General Chair is an Organizator, a distinct organizing role (conference general chair) with siblings Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, etc. The two denote different conference roles (program committee chair vs. general conference chair), so they are not equivalent; they are related only in that both are senior conference-organisation roles.

A's 'is an ending date' is a specific datatype property on the Important dates class denoting the end date of a conference event, while B's 'Date' is a generic datatype property on the Deadline class denoting a deadline's date/time. Both relate a temporal entity to a date value, but they are not the same relation: one is specifically an ending date, the other a general deadline date. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

A's Author is a person class (subclass of Person, with children like Presenter and properties linking authors to papers). B's Deadline Author notification is a deadline/event class (subclass of Deadline, sibling of submission deadlines) representing the author-notification deadline. They denote different concepts: a person role vs. a temporal deadline, so they are unrelated.

In iasted, Document is a broad administrative item (children include Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance, Review, Submission, etc.), whereas in sigkdd Document is a narrower scholarly artefact whose children are Abstract, Paper and Review and which is presented by a Speaker. The sigkdd Document is thus a specific kind of the more general iasted Document, so iasted Document subsumes sigkdd Document (sigkdd Document is subsumed by iasted Document).

A's Member is a subclass of Participant (a person participating in a conference, sibling of Regular and Student), i.e. a kind of attendee/participant. B's Two Level Conference is a subclass of Conference (a conference with two levels, sibling of Single Level Conference), i.e. a kind of event, not a person. The entities denote different concepts (person vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event such as tutorial or workshop), while B's Listener is a kind of Delegate (a person attending). They denote different concepts (event vs. person role), so they are unrelated.

A's 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (domain and range both Reviewer), i.e. who invited a reviewer. B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document, i.e. the presentation given by a speaker. Different kinds of things in different directions; no equivalence.

A's hasName is a datatype property of Conference giving the conference's full name, while B's Name is a datatype property of Person giving a person's name. They share the word 'Name' but have different domains (Conference vs Person) and thus denote different relations in the conference domain.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string postal code, while B's obtain is an object property linking Person to an Item. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (submission venue), while B's 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (the act of presenting a paper). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's Author is a person role in the conference (a subclass of Person, with children like Presenter and properties linking to papers). B's Author information form is a document/form artefact (subclass of Form, sibling of Registration form and Hotel registration form). They denote different kinds of things (person vs. form), so they are unrelated.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it; B's 'awarded by' links an Award to the agent that awarded it. Different domains (Sponsorship vs Award) and different intended relations (sponsoring vs awarding), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions/attendance), while B 'One conference day' is a temporal unit within the conference days hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches (document vs. time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Reviewer is a Person (a role/agent who performs reviews), while B's Positive Review is a subclass of Review, i.e. a Document/artefact with a positive outcome. They denote different kinds of things (agent vs. document) and are not equivalent; the shared word 'review' is misleading.

A's 'ends on' is a datatype property of Event giving the end date/time of an event, while B's 'has Last Name' is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname. They have different domains (Event vs Person) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's property links a Committee to its Co chair (domain Committee, range Co chair), while B's property links a Person to a Conference (domain Person, range Conference). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Member PC' is a Person subclass (a program-committee member/reviewer, with properties expert On Topic and reviewes Contribution), whereas B's 'Review' is a Document subclass (the review document artefact). One is an agent, the other an information artefact, so they denote different concepts.

A's isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership of a person in a conference/committee), while B's organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organiser of an event). The domains (Person vs Event) and ranges (Conference vs Organisation/Person) differ, and the directions of the relations are different, so they are not equivalent.

A's writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation). B's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a reviewer's record of reviews). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'is the 1th part of' is a specific, ordered part-of relation restricted to Abstract as domain and Paper/Poster/Presentation as range, whereas ekaw's 'part Of' is a general, unconstrained mereological relation. The specific relation is a specialization of the general one, so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

Tutorial is a working event (a type of conference activity) in confOf, while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment in iasted; they belong to entirely different branches of the domain and denote different concepts.

Conference applicant (a person who applies to register for a conference, with child Registeered applicant) and confOf Participant (a person participating in a conference, with children Member/Regular/Student and property early Registration) overlap in that applicants typically become participants, but they are not the same concept: an applicant is a pre-registration role, whereas a participant is an attendee role. The differing children and the registration-related property on Participant indicate distinct intended classes, so the reference alignment would not record them as equivalent.

Conference www is a specific conference document (a web page about a conference, with a URL), while ekaw's Web Site is a broader document type that can list events and be published by organisations. The Conference www class is narrower than Web Site, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.
