confOf's Author is a general person role (parent Person, sibling roles like Chair PC, Member PC, Participant) that writes Contributions. sigkdd's 'Author of paper' is a narrower class under Speaker > Author, specifically a person who authored a paper, with sibling 'Author of paper student'. Every 'Author of paper' is an confOf Author, but confOf Author also covers authors of other contributions (e.g. posters, demos), so A is more general: A is subsumed by B's concept? No—B is the narrower one, so A subsumes B, i.e. A is subsumed_by B is wrong. Correct: A (Author) is broader, B (Author of paper) is narrower, so A subsumes B, relation 'subsumes'.

A 'Conference contributor' is a Person (a human role: author, speaker, participant), while B 'Conference building' is a Place/Building (a physical venue whose child is Delegate). Different kinds of entities with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

cmt:User is a general person role in the conference system (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer, Chairman, PC Member, etc.), while Conference:Conference applicant is a person who applies/registers for a conference (parent of Registeered applicant, sibling of Committee member, Conference participant, Reviewer). Both are subclasses of Person and both cover people involved in a conference, but User is broader (includes organisers, chairs, PC members) and Conference applicant is narrower (applicants/registrants). They overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Invited speaker' is a role of a person (a Conference contributor who gives an invited talk), while B's 'Research Institute' is an academic organisation (sibling of University). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person role vs. institution), so they are unrelated.

A 'Dining Place' is a kind of Place (a location where one eats, sibling of Accommodation Place and Meeting Room Place), while B 'Shuttle bus' is a kind of Transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Taxi, Van). They denote different concepts in different branches of the conference domain (venue/location vs. transportation), so they are unrelated.

Paper in cmt is a specific document type (a submitted contribution with authors, reviews, decisions), while Conference document in the Conference ontology is a broader category covering calls, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc. Paper is one kind of conference document, so Paper is subsumed by Conference document, not equivalent.

A's 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it (domain Sponsorship, range Organization). B's 'is paid for' links Money to the Activity/Item it pays for (domain Money, range Activity/Item). Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning: sponsorship provision vs. monetary payment. Not equivalent.

A's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award. Different ranges (Contribution vs Award) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'topic Covered By' relates a Research Topic to the Event/Paper that covers it (domain Research Topic, range Event/Paper), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to the Paper they submit (domain Author, range Paper). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A is a conference document type (information for participants, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B is a research topic in the EDAS topic taxonomy (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A Demo Chair is a specific conference participant role responsible for demo sessions, while a General Chair is the top-level organizer of the conference. They are different roles with different responsibilities and different positions in their respective hierarchies (Conference Participant vs Organizator), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Shuttle bus' is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Taxi, Van) used to move attendees, while B 'Listener' is a person role (sibling of Organizator, Speaker) in the conference. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A Tutorial is a type of conference part/event (sibling of Track and Workshop) that is a session where teaching occurs. B Paper Presentation is an academic event where an accepted paper is presented (sibling of Talk Event and Workshop). Although both are event types, a tutorial is not a paper presentation; they denote different kinds of events with different properties and roles in the conference domain.

A's 'written By' is an object property linking a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'E mail' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address). Different domain, range, and intended relation, so they are unrelated.

Both entities denote the same conference-domain concept: a reviewer's history of reviews. The cmt entity 'Review History Of' and the edas entity 'is Review History Of' share the same label, kind (object property), domain (Personal Review History), and range (Reviewer), and their paths and contexts agree, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's Topic is the general conference subject area (domain of dealsWith, expertOn, hasTopic), while B's Microelectronics Topic is a specific topic under the parent Topic. B is strictly narrower than A, so A is subsumed by B's parent, not equivalent to this specific topic.

Both classes represent the outcome of a paper's review: cmt's Decision has children Acceptance and Rejection and is the range of 'has Decision' (Paper -> Decision); Conference's Reviewed contribution has children Accepted contribution and Rejected contribution and is the subject of 'has a review' (Reviewed contribution -> Review). The parallel acceptance/rejection subclasses and the paper-to-outcome property show the same intended instances, so they are equivalent.

A relates a conference part to a conference volume (object property, domain Conference part, range Conference volume), while B relates a conference to a city string (datatype property, domain Conference, range string). Different domain, range, and meaning; no overlap.

A 'Social event' is a subclass of Event (a conference social gathering such as Banquet, Reception, Trip), while B 'Payment document' is a subclass of Document (a financial artefact such as Bank transfer or Cheque). They share no meaning, no properties, and no common instances; the only superficial link is that both are subclasses of a generic top concept, which is not enough for equivalence.

In edas, Paper is a Document with children for accepted/rejected/published papers and properties for authorship, reviewing, and topics. In iasted, Publication is an Item whose only children are Book proceeding and Cd proceeding, i.e. a published proceedings artefact. A Paper is a broader scholarly contribution that may or may not be published, so Paper is more general than (subsumed by) the narrower Publication concept; they are not equivalent.

Both ontologies model the same conference-domain concept: a paper submitted to a conference. Ontology A's 'Submitted Paper' (path: Paper > Submitted Paper) and Ontology B's 'Paper' (path: Document > Paper > Submitted Paper) both have children like 'Assigned Paper' and siblings such as 'Camera Ready Paper', 'Conference Paper', 'Demo Paper', 'Poster Paper', 'Regular Paper', 'Workshop Paper', indicating they denote the same class of submitted contributions. The differing labels reflect naming conventions, not different concepts.

A's hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a conflict-of-interest declaration), while B's obtain relates an Author to an Award (receiving a prize). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

Both are direct subclasses of Organization denoting non-academic commercial organizations: confOf's Company (sibling University) and edas's Industry Organization (siblings Academia, Government, NGO) both represent the industrial/commercial organization category in the conference domain, so their intended instances coincide.

A's 'Contribution 1th author' is a subclass of 'Regular author' representing the first author of a conference contribution (a person/role in the authorship hierarchy). B's 'Author information form' is a subclass of 'Form' (a document/form artefact used to collect author details), sibling to registration and hotel forms. One is an author role, the other a document form; they denote different concepts and are unrelated.

A is a person role (a chair involved in a conference, under Person > Chairman), while B is a physical location (a hall where a conference takes place, under Place). They denote entirely different kinds of entities and share no meaning.

Reviewer (a person who reviews papers, with review expertise/preference and co-reviewer relations) and Author (a person who writes contributions) are distinct roles in the conference domain. Although both are subclasses of Person, their properties and intended instances differ: a Reviewer reviews, an Author writes. They are not synonyms and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author (a person who writes papers but is excluded from reviewing), while B's 'Member PC' is a Person who reviews contributions (comment 'Reviewer', property reviewes). The two denote disjoint roles: an author-not-reviewer is precisely not a PC member/reviewer, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Free Time Break' is a non-academic break event in the conference schedule (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break), while B 'Registration Non Member' is a registration fee category for non-members (sibling of member/student registration fees). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event scheduling vs. fee structure) and share no intended instances.

In iasted, Review is a Document subtype (a review document/artefact), sibling to Submission and Form. In sigkdd, Paper is a Document subtype that is submitted by an Author and is sibling to Review (a separate class). The two ontologies both distinguish Paper and Review as different concepts, so Review (iasted) and Paper (sigkdd) denote different things.

A's 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract (a text artefact), while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (a person who presents it). Different domain/range kinds and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a submission/notification deadline in the conference domain: iasted's Deadline (subclass of Time, with children for camera-ready, notification, registration, submission deadlines and a 'done till' date property) and sigkdd's Deadline (with children for abstract submission, author notification, paper submission and a Date property). Same intended instances and same role, so they are equivalent.

A 'Social program' is a conference activity (a social event such as a dinner banquet, with siblings like Coffee break and Welcome address), while B 'Program Committee member' is a person role (an Organizator, sibling of General Chair and Program Chair). They denote entirely different kinds of entities (event vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's Reception is a social event (a gathering) in the conference domain, sibling of Banquet and Trip. B's Accpet If Room Rating is a review rating category, sibling of Accept/Reject ratings. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's Reviewer is a Person (a role/agent who performs reviews), while B's Review is a Document (the artefact produced by reviewing). Different kinds and different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

A is a person role (a chair associated with a conference, subclass of Chairman/Conference Member), while B is a conference document (a call for participation, subclass of Conference document). They denote entirely different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A is a confOf administrative event class for the act/phase of submitting contributions (siblings: Camera Ready event, Reviewing event, etc.), while B is an iasted time/deadline class for the notification-of-acceptance deadline (siblings: submission deadline, camera-ready deadline, registration deadline). One denotes an event/activity, the other a point in time; they are not the same concept.

A's 'Extended abstract' is a kind of conference contribution (a document type, sibling of Paper, parent of Abstract) in the Conference ontology. B's 'Pending Paper' is a submission-status state of a Paper in edas (siblings: Accepted, Active, Published, Rejected, Withdrawn Paper). One denotes a document type, the other a review/submission status; their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'prepare' links a Person to an Item they prepare. Different domains (Conference vs Person), different ranges (Administrator vs Item), and different intended meanings, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's `reviewes` relates a PC member to a Contribution (a review action), while B's `is made from` relates an Item to an Item (a composition/material relation). Different domain/range and different intended meaning, so not equivalent.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it (domain Presentation, range Active conference participant). B's 'is Provider Of' links an Organization to a Sponsorship (domain Organization, range Sponsorship). Different domains, ranges and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's 'publisher Of' relates an Organisation (publisher) to published artefacts (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site), i.e. the organisation produces/publishes the item. B's 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item, i.e. a person acquires/receives an item. Different domain (Organisation vs Person), different range (publication artefacts vs generic Item), and different intended meaning (publishing vs obtaining). They are not the same relation.

A's Fee is a general money category (siblings: Sponsorship, Tax, Tip; children include Hotel fee, Registration fee, Fee for extra trip), while B's Registration fee is a specific kind of fee (parent: Fee; children are registration categories). Thus A is broader and subsumes B, not equivalent.

A's User is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Author/Reviewer/Administrator), while B's Session is a type of lecture/event (parent Lecture, child Speaker lecture). They denote different concepts: a person versus an event, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a submitted contribution' links a review-expertise entity to a submitted contribution (a paper under review), while B's 'presentationed by' links a document to its speaker/presenter. Different domains, ranges and intended relations; they do not denote the same property.

A's 'gives presentations' is a specific relation from an active conference participant to a presentation. B's 'give' is a much broader relation from any Person to an Activity or Item, covering giving talks, items, etc. The A relation is a specialization of the B relation, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's 'Regular contribution' is a kind of written conference contribution (a document/paper category, with children Extended abstract and Paper), whereas B's 'Talk Event' is a kind of academic event (a scheduled talk, with children Closing Talk and Welcome Talk). One denotes a written submission artefact, the other a spoken event; their paths, parents, children and siblings are entirely different, so they are not the same concept.

A's 'Paper Abstract' is a document part (a subclass of Paper, sibling of Paper Full Version), while B's 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a type of Award. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author (authorship of a paper), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (a person's requirement for some item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's contact Email is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string (an email address, per the confTool comment), while B's paper Due On links a Conference to a dateTime (a submission deadline). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in meaning.

A's Review is a document produced in the conference review process (sibling of Paper, parent of Meta Review, written by a Reviewer, ended by the PC Chair). B's Transport vehicle is a physical item (parent of Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) used for conference logistics. Different domains and no shared instances; unrelated.

A's 'has a name' is a general naming datatype property whose domain covers Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, whereas B's 'Name of conference' is restricted to Conference. The broader property subsumes the narrower one; they are not equivalent because A applies to many entity types beyond conferences.

Both classes denote conference participants/members: A's 'Conference participant' (path Person > Conference participant, children Active/Passive participant) and B's 'Member' (path Person > Participant > Member, siblings Regular/Student) have matching intended instances and compatible contexts.

A's Conference is the event itself (it has a name, parts, proceedings, publisher, topic), while B's Proceedings is a document (a Multi author Volume containing Conference Proceedings). The event and its published proceedings are different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Sponsor city is a city that sponsors a conference (a location/geographic entity under City), while Hotel is a lodging place under Place. They denote different concepts: a sponsor city is not a hotel, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, External Reviewer is a person who reviews for another Reviewer but is explicitly not a Reviewer, and is a sibling of Program Committee Member under Person. In ekaw, PC Member is a Possible Reviewer and the parent of PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair and Workshop Chair. The two denote different roles: an external reviewer is outside the program committee, whereas a PC Member is a member of the program committee. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in cmt, while B is a conference event (an edition of a conference) in ekaw. They belong to different branches of the domain (person vs. event) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, and their labels ('has the last name' vs 'has Last Name') denote the same attribute of a person's surname. The paths and domains/ranges match exactly, so they are the same relation.

A's Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection) under Decision, i.e. the final accept/reject verdict on a paper. B's Accpet If Room Rating is a review rating category (sibling of Accept Rating, Reject Rating, Week Reject Rating) under Review Rating, i.e. a reviewer's recommendation conditional on space. Different kinds of things (decision vs. review rating) and different contexts, so not equivalent.

Conference part is a part-of relation class (parts of a conference volume: tracks, tutorials, workshops), while confOf's Working event is a subclass of Event covering Conference, Tutorial and Workshop as events. The two overlap in extension (tutorials and workshops are both conference parts and working events), but Conference part is not a subclass of Working event: a conference part is a component of a conference volume, not itself an event, and Working event includes Conference, which is not a part of a conference volume. The intended concepts differ, so they are not equivalent; Conference part is narrower/more specific in the event hierarchy sense, hence subsumed_by rather than equivalent.

A's 'held In' relates an Event to the Location where it is held; B's 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place where they can stay. Different domains (Event vs Person) and ranges (Location vs Place), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Speaker is a subclass of Person in sigkdd (path Person > Speaker), so every Speaker is a Person, but Person in the Conference ontology is broader (includes applicants, participants, committee members, etc. who need not be speakers). Thus Person subsumes Speaker, i.e. Speaker is subsumed_by Person; they are not equivalent.

edas Contact Information is a class holding a person's/entity's address details (city, email, phone, postal code, street), whereas ekaw Location is a venue/place that an Event is held in (held In: Event -> Location). The intended instances do not coincide: one is contact/address data, the other is a physical or conceptual venue. Different properties and different domain roles confirm they are unrelated concepts.

A is an administrative event (the act/process of submitting contributions) in confOf, while B is a deadline (a point in time) for submissions in iasted. They are conceptually linked (the submission event has a submission deadline) but denote different things: an event vs. a time point. Hence not equivalent; they are related.

A is a conference event (a working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while B is a research topic in a topic taxonomy (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). They denote entirely different kinds of things: an event vs. a subject area. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a subclass of Submitted contribution (a document/paper that has undergone review), while B 'Possible Reviewer' is a subclass of Person (an agent who may review papers). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (document vs. person) and cannot denote the same concept.

Conference participant is a general role for anyone taking part in a conference (with subclasses Active/Passive participant), while Sponsor is a person or organisation providing financial support, a distinct role. They share only the parent Person and are not synonyms.

A's Conference Trip is a social event (sibling of Conference Banquet) held during the conference, while B's Activity after conference is a broader activity category occurring after the conference, with children Departure and Full day tour. They overlap (a trip can be a post-conference activity) but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'Tutorial speaker' is a specific kind of speaker (a tutorial presenter), sitting under Author in iasted. B's 'Author' is the general class of people who author papers, with children 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student'. A tutorial speaker is a narrower concept than a general author, so A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on Conference indicating whether hard-copy submissions are accepted; B's 'abstract' is a string text field on Contribution holding the paper's abstract. Different domain (Conference vs Contribution), different range (boolean vs string), and different meaning, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a written work (Paper/Item) to its author (Author/Person) in the same direction, expressing authorship; the domain/range classes are themselves equivalent in the conference domain, so the relations coincide.

Conference contribution is a document/paper submitted to a conference (a subclass of Conference document, with children like Poster, Presentation, Written contribution), whereas Author is a person role (subclass of Speaker/Person) who submits papers. They belong to different branches (document vs person) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties relate a location to an event, but they are defined in different ontologies (edas vs ekaw) with different local names and no explicit cross-ontology equivalence axiom; they are therefore treated as related but not equivalent.

Both classes sit at the same position in the submission lifecycle: a submitted contribution/paper that has been reviewed/evaluated, with children Accepted and Rejected in both ontologies. 'Reviewed contribution' has review properties (has a review / reviews) and 'Evaluated Paper' is the paper after assignment/evaluation, so their intended instances coincide.

A's 'Conference Proceedings' is a document (a multi-author volume of proceedings, subclass of Proceedings/Document), while B's 'Conference' is the event itself, with properties for city, start/end dates, name, and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. A publication volume and an event are different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a place for holding meetings (a room in a conference venue), while B 'Double hotel room' is a specific type of hotel room for accommodation. They are different kinds of places with no overlap in the conference domain; the shared word 'room' is not sufficient.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a scientific submission with an abstract, part of a conference contribution hierarchy), while B's Web Site is a Document subtype used for programme brochures and event listings (event On List, lists Event, publisher Of). They denote different concepts despite both being documents, so they are unrelated.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presented it. Different domains (Conference vs Document), different ranges (Administrator vs Speaker), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person (a person who takes part in a conference, with subclasses Active/Passive participant), whereas B's 'Conference' is the event itself, with properties such as city, start/end date, and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. A person and an event cannot denote the same concept, so the pair is unrelated.

A's write Paper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship). B's is the 1th part of relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (part-whole composition). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent nor inverse.

Both are datatype properties with a date/dateTime range denoting an end date, but A's 'is an ending date' is a generic end-date property of the Important dates class (used for any deadline/event end), while B's 'End of conference' is specifically the end of the Conference itself. They overlap in meaning but are not the same property, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (a paper being submitted to a venue/proceedings), while B's 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (an agent preparing some item). Different domain, range, and intended meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chair of the whole conference, a subtype of Chairman/Conference Member. Session Chair (ekaw) is a Conference Participant who chairs a session, a subtype of Conference Participant/PC Member. They denote different roles: one leads the conference, the other moderates a session. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (scheduling overlap between events), while ekaw's 'organised By' relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organiser). Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'Committee member' is a specific role a Person can take (a subclass of Person, with children Chair/Co chair and properties tying it to Committee), whereas B's 'Person' is the general superclass of all people (with children Delegate, Sponsor). Every committee member is a person, but not every person is a committee member, so Committee member is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Person.

ekaw:Organisation is an agent-like entity (academic institution, organising agency, publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings; iasted:Activity is a temporal happening (conference activity, before/after conference activity) that is given by persons, dated, held in places. The two denote different kinds of things (agent vs. event/activity), so they are not equivalent.

A's hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision (the accept/reject outcome for a paper). B's is_made_from relates an Item to another Item, a part-whole/composition relation within the iasted item hierarchy. Different domain/range kinds and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A Workshop is a working event (a type of event/activity in the conference programme, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). B Speaker lecture is a session within a Lecture, i.e. a specific talk/session type, not a workshop. The two denote different concepts: one is an event type, the other a session/talk type, so they are unrelated.

Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection under Decision) in cmt, while Company is a type of organization (sibling of University under Organization) in confOf. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (Program Committee Member), while B's has_a_committee_chair relates a Committee to a Chair. Different domain/range concepts (member vs chair) and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Both properties link a person/author to a paper/item they produce: cmt's writePaper has domain Author and range Paper, while iasted's sign has domain Person and range Item. In the conference domain, Author and Person denote the same kind of agent, and Paper and Item denote the same kind of written contribution, so the two properties relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are equivalent.

Both are direct subclasses of Person denoting someone who attends the conference. edas Attendee is a sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc., and ekaw Conference Participant is the general attendee class with subclasses like Presenter, Early/Late Registered Participant, PC Chair. The intended instances coincide: a person attending the conference. The ekaw class is somewhat broader (includes chairs, presenters, students), but in the conference domain 'Attendee' and 'Conference Participant' are used as synonyms for the same role.

A's 'adjusted By' relates a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it (domain Bid, range Reviewer), while B's 'pay' relates a Person to Money paid. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with a two-tier programme committee structure), while B 'Sponsor' is a kind of person (an organisation/person sponsoring the event). They denote different concepts in the conference domain and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with range date, but their domains differ: cmt's date applies to Conference (the event), while Conference's has_a_date_of_issue applies to Conference document (a paper/contribution). They relate different kinds of things, so they are not equivalent; they only share the date range.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them; B's 'has a committee co chair' links a Committee to its Co chair. Different domains (Program Committee Member vs Committee), different ranges (Administrator vs Co chair), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'can stay in' is an object property mapping a Person to a Place (accommodation). They share only the domain Person; their ranges and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic (a subject area under Topic, sibling of Computer Networks, Cryptography, etc.), while B is a document type (an abstract for an invited talk, under Abstract). They denote entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's markConflictOfInterest relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to record a conflict of interest (a negative association preventing assignment). B's hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer, i.e. it records who may review the paper (a positive assignment/eligibility relation). The direction is reversed (A: person->paper, B: paper->person) and the intended meaning differs (conflict vs. reviewer assignment), so they are not equivalent nor inverse-equivalent in the reference alignment.

Author in cmt is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes and submits papers), while Travel Grant in edas is a sponsorship/funding category, not a person. Their paths, parents and properties are entirely disjoint, so they denote different concepts.

SC Member (Steering Committee Member) is a specific kind of PC Member in ekaw, while Program Committee member in sigkdd is the general committee-member class. A Steering Committee member is typically a subset of the program committee, so SC Member is more specific and is subsumed by Program Committee member, not equivalent.

A's max Choice is a datatype property of Social/Working event giving a positiveInteger (max number of choices, confTool), while B's Start of conference is a datatype property of Conference giving a dateTime. Different domains, ranges and meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Trip day is a temporal unit under Time, sibling of Conference days and Deadline. They denote different concepts (event vs. time period), so they are unrelated.

A's markConflictOfInterest relates a Reviewer/Author/Chairman to a Paper to record a conflict of interest; B's parallel_with relates two Administrative events (scheduling overlap). Different domains, ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them; B's 'written By' relates a Document to the Person who authored it. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's property relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the paper assignment tools), while B's property relates a Paper to an Author. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Administrator in cmt is a system/organisational role (a User who manages the conference: accepts papers, assigns reviewers, enters conference details), whereas Paper Author in ekaw is a person who writes papers. Their intended instances and contexts differ; the only shared word is 'Author', which is a sibling of Administrator in cmt, not the same concept.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a role played by people who contribute to a conference, with children such as Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author), whereas Social event is a subclass of Event (a social gathering with children Banquet, Reception, Trip and properties like location, has title, has VAT). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (person roles vs. events) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

organises relates an Organisation or Person to an Event (organising a conference/event), while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (giving a presentation of a paper). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's 'add Program Committee Member' is a specific administrative action relating an Administrator to a Program Committee Member, while B's 'give' is a general relation from a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g. giving a talk or an award). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent.

A's memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (a person is a member of a conference), while B's holded_by relates a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD organisation (a conference is held by a society). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Conference Member vs Conference; Conference vs ACM SIGKDD), so the properties do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's 'is submitted at' links a conference contribution to the conference volume it was submitted to; B's 'awarded by' links an Award to the agent/organisation granting it. Different domains (Contribution vs Award), different ranges (Volume vs unspecified agent), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

read Paper is a property of a Reviewer linking to a Paper (the reviewer reads the paper), while review Of Paper is a property of a Review linking to a Paper (the review is about the paper). They have different domains (Reviewer vs Review) and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Both denote the person who chairs the program committee: confOf's 'Chair PC' (a Person role) and sigkdd's 'Program Chair' (an Organizator role) refer to the same conference role, with matching context (Person/Organizator hierarchies and PC-related siblings).

A is a subclass of Paper (a full version of a conference paper), while B is a research topic in parallel/distributed computing. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (document vs. subject area) and share no instances.

Conference contributor is a broad role class covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors (subclasses of Person who contribute to a conference), whereas confOf's Administrator is a specific organisational/administrative role (comment 'confTool', sibling of Assistant, Chair PC, Member PC, Volunteer). The intended instances do not coincide: an administrator is not a contributor in the paper/author sense, and contributors need not administer anything. Different roles under Person, so unrelated.

A's Topic is the general class of conference topics (it has a name, is a topic of conference parts, is referenced by reviews and submissions). B's Multimedia Topic is a specific topic nested under edas's Topic (siblings are Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), so it is strictly narrower than A's Topic. Hence A's Topic subsumes B's Multimedia Topic, i.e. B is subsumed_by A's Topic, not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties on Conference with a date/time range, but cmt's `date` is a generic conference date (e.g. conference date), while edas's `manuscriptDueOn` is specifically the manuscript submission deadline. They overlap in that both are conference dates, but they are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A is a subject/topic area within the conference taxonomy (a Computer Networks management research topic), while B is a kind of presentation event (a contributed talk, sibling of Invited Talk and Tutorial). They belong to entirely different branches (Topic vs Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A (confOf 'Member PC') is a person role — a program-committee member/reviewer, a subclass of Person with properties expert On and reviewes. B (ekaw 'Negative Review') is a subclass of Review (a Document) representing a review with negative content. One is a person, the other a document/review artefact; their intended instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title; B's has the last name is a datatype property of Person giving a person's surname. Different domains (Paper vs Person) and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's virtualMeetingEnabledBy relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables virtual meetings), while B's listsEvent relates a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (listing events). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

cmt:User is a subclass of cmt:Person and represents a person participating in the conference system (with subclasses Administrator, Author, Reviewer). edas:Person is the broader class of all persons (with subclasses Attendee, Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). Every cmt:User is a person, but edas:Person also covers persons not modelled as cmt:User (e.g. attendees, session chairs), so User is strictly more specific: subsumed_by.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a call inviting participation, sibling of Call for paper and Conference announcement). B 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline (a date by which papers must be submitted, sibling of Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Author notification). One is a document, the other a temporal deadline; they denote different concepts and are not equivalent.

An Industrial Session is a kind of Conference Session (a track/format within a conference where industry contributions are presented), whereas a Plenary lecture is a kind of Lecture (a single talk given to the whole audience). They sit in different branches (Session vs Lecture) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Both denote the person role responsible for workshop/track-workshop organization: A's 'Track workshop chair' is a Person role with properties linking it to a Conference part (has a track workshop tutorial chair / was a track workshop chair of), and B's 'Workshop Chair' is a Person role under Conference Participant/PC Member with the same intended instances. The labels and role semantics coincide in the conference domain.

A 'Communications Topic' is a subject area of papers (a subclass of Topic in the edas ontology), while B 'Organizing Committee' is a type of committee (subclass of Committee in sigkdd). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, sharing neither instances nor meaning.

A's 'Conference fees' denotes the monetary charges for attending a conference, while B's 'Conference Session' denotes a scheduled meeting/session within a conference (it is related to documents via hasRelatedDocument/relatesTo). The two concepts are semantically distinct: fees are not sessions, and sessions are not fees. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's has City is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string city name; B's has amount of links Money to an integer amount. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'early Registration' is a datatype property of Participant with boolean range (whether a participant registered early), while B's 'held In' is an object property linking an Event to a Location. Different domain, range, and meaning; no overlap.

A 'Communications Topic' is a subject area for conference papers (a subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Card' is a physical item (subclass of Item, with child Credit card and siblings Audiovisual equipment, Document, Transport vehicle). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In confOf, Country is a geographical/national entity used as the range of has Country for Organizations and Persons (e.g., an author's country). In ekaw, Location is the place where an Event is held (held In: Event -> Location; location Of: Location -> Event), i.e., a venue/site. A country is not a conference venue location, and the property contexts (nationality/affiliation vs. event venue) do not coincide, so the classes are not equivalent.

A's 'has an expertise' is a datatype property of Review expertise linking a review to an expertise value, while B's 'speak in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place/Time. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses like Invited speaker and Regular author), while B's 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with properties such as start/end date, city, and being held by ACM SIGKDD. The two denote different kinds of entities (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.
A's 'has gender' records a person's gender, while B's 'has First Name' records a person's given name; they relate different kinds of values and are not the same relation.

A's 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place/Time (attendance at a location/time), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (authorship submission). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference applicant' is a Person subclass (a person who applies to a conference, with child 'Registeered applicant'), while B's 'Registration Student' is a subclass of 'Registration fee' — a fee category for students, not a person. Different kinds (person vs. fee) and different paths, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the person who delivers it (Active conference participant), while B's 'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to the people who review it (Reviewer, TPC Member, chairs). Different domain (Presentation vs Paper), different range (presenter vs reviewer), and different intended relation (presenting vs reviewing), so they are not equivalent.

A's Taxi is a transport vehicle (a means of getting to the conference), while B's Listener is a person role (an attendee who listens to talks). Different kinds of entities with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's User is a person role in the conference (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while B's Non Academic Event is a conference event category (parent Conference Event, children Break/Meal/Social Event). They denote entirely different kinds of things (person vs event), so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (a meal/activity) under Event > Social Event, while B 'Conference hall' is a physical location under Place. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. place) and are not equivalent.

In cmt, 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a Paper), while in edas 'Reviewer' is a person who reviews papers, a distinct role. The two classes denote different roles in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies to attend a conference (parent of 'Registered applicant'), whereas B 'Session Chair' is a conference participant who chairs a session (a role within the conference programme). The two denote different roles with no overlap: an applicant is not yet a participant, and a session chair is a specific participant role. Their paths, parents and siblings differ entirely, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair is a person role in the conference committee hierarchy, while Book proceeding is a publication type. They belong to different top-level categories (Person vs Item/Publication) and share no meaningful overlap.

A's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (author), while B's 'send' relates a Person to an Item (submission action). The domains and ranges are reversed and the intended relations differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference is a working event (a type of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Conference hall is a physical Place (sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote different kinds of things — an event versus a venue/location — so they are not equivalent.

A's property links a Track workshop chair (a person role) to a Conference part (an event/venue component), i.e. chairing a workshop track. B's property links a Document to a Speaker, i.e. a paper being presented by a speaker. Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (submission target), while B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (presenter). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

A is a person role (Tutorial Chair, a subclass of Conference Participant/PC Member) while B is an activity type (Tutorial, a subclass of Lecture). A person who chairs a tutorial is not the tutorial event itself; the entities denote different kinds of things and are unrelated.

A's `name` is a general naming property applying to both Conference and Person, while B's `City of conference` is a specific property for the city where a conference is held. Although both are datatype properties with string ranges and Conference is a shared domain, `name` is far broader and does not denote the same relation as a city-of-conference property.

A 'Conference www' is a conference-domain document (a web page about a conference, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc., with a URL), while B 'Powerline Transmission Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in the EDAS ontology. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Author Not Reviewer is a subclass of Author in cmt, denoting a person who authors a paper but is excluded from reviewing it. Attendee in edas is a direct subclass of Person denoting any person attending the conference, with siblings Author, Reviewer, etc. The two concepts have different intents and neither subsumes the other: an author-not-reviewer need not attend, and an attendee need not be an author. They are unrelated.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (like call for papers, announcements) aimed at attendees, while B's 'Slide Set' is a presentation artefact document (sibling of Paper, Programme, Review). Different intended instances; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for papers, while B's 'Call For Reviews' is a call for reviewers, a distinct concept; B's sibling 'Call For Papers' would be the match for A, not 'Call For Reviews'.

A's memberOfConference is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference (a membership relation), while B's Name_of_conference is a datatype property giving a Conference a string name. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and cannot denote the same relation.

A's prepare relates a Person to an Item (a person prepares an item, e.g. a paper), while B's holded by relates a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD organisation (a conference is held by a sponsor/organiser). Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper (the title of a paper), while B's Name is a datatype property of Person (a person's name). They relate different kinds of entities and are not the same relation.

A is a conference topic about powerline transmission (a research subject under Topic), while B is a physical transport vehicle (Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) under Item. They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain.

A Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference event) in edas, while Speaker lecture in iasted is a session within a lecture activity, i.e. a talk/session, not a workshop event. Different kinds and contexts, so not equivalent.

A 'Conference city' is a subclass of City denoting the city where a conference takes place, while B 'Hotel' is a subclass of Place denoting a lodging venue. They share no intended instances and are not synonyms; the only overlap is that a hotel is located in a city, which is not equivalence.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a short summary document of a conference paper (sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B 'Bank transfer' is a payment document (sibling of Cheque under Payment document). They belong to entirely different subdomains (academic submission vs. payment/finance) and share no intended instances.

A's 'read By Meta Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (a person/role), while B's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'is Provider Of' relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (org provides sponsorship), while B's 'is paid by' relates Money to a Person (money is paid by a person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's Review is the general review document class (siblings are other conference documents, and it is the range of 'has a review' and domain of 'reviews' linking it to a reviewed contribution). B's Positive Review is a specific subclass of Review in ekaw, alongside Negative and Neutral Review. Thus A's Review is more general and subsumes B's Positive Review; they are not equivalent.

Both entities denote the same concept in the conference domain: a paper/document. The labels 'Paper' and 'Document' are used interchangeably in the OAEI Conference track, and their paths, parents, children, and comments align, indicating they represent the same class.

A's Program committee is a committee (a group of people) that reviews papers, a subclass of Committee alongside Organizing and Steering committees. B's Sponsor is a subclass of Person, a kind of individual who funds the conference, sibling of Delegate. Different kinds (group vs. person) and different roles; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'Administrative event' is a broad class of organisational events (submission, reviewing, registration, camera-ready) that are activities with temporal ordering (follows, parallel with). B's 'Deadline Author notification' is a specific deadline date for notifying authors, a sibling of paper/abstract submission deadlines. The two denote different concepts: one is an event category, the other a deadline milestone; no subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

Both are social/leisure activities within the conference domain, but they are not the same concept: ekaw's Social Event is a general category of social events (banquet, trip) that can occur at any time, while iasted's Activity after conference is specifically a post-conference activity (departure, tour). The scopes overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's assignedByAdministrator links a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned them (range Administrator), while B's has_a_review_reference_or_expertise links a Reviewer to their review expertise/preference topics (range Review expertise, Review preference). Different ranges and different intended meanings, so the properties are not equivalent.

Author (cmt) is a person role in the conference organisation, a subclass of Conference Member/User, with properties about submitting and writing papers. Place (iasted) is a spatial location with subclasses Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, etc., and properties about being situated in, held in, equipped by. The two concepts share no intended instances and no meaningful overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's Subject Area is a topic classification of papers (range of 'has Subject Area' from Paper), while B's Time zone is a geographic/administrative region concept in iasted; they share no intended instances and no contextual overlap.

A's 'was a committee of' relates a Committee to a Conference volume (committee -> conference), while B's 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (conference -> person). They have different domains, ranges, and directions, and are not inverses of each other either, so they denote different relations.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a kind of conference/event (a conference with two levels, sibling of Single Level Conference), while B 'Tutorial Chair' is a person role (a conference participant who chairs tutorials). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

Both are buildings/places used for conference activities, but 'Sponsor company house' is a building where a sponsoring company is housed, while 'Conference hall' is the venue where the conference takes place. They are different kinds of places in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent; they only share the general notion of a conference-related place.

A's hasReviewHistory relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a collection of reviews belonging to a reviewer), while B's reviewWrittenBy relates a Review to a Possible Reviewer (the author of a single review). They differ in domain (Reviewer vs Review), range (Personal Review History vs Possible Reviewer), and direction; B is closer to an inverse of a review-authorship relation, not equivalent to A.

Organization in the Conference ontology denotes an institution/affiliation (e.g. an author's organisation), while Time_zone in iasted denotes a geographical time zone. They share no instances and no domain role, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Personal Publication History' is a subclass of Personal History, representing a person's record/history of publications in EDAS. B's 'Abstract' is a subclass of Document in SIGKDD, representing the abstract text of a paper. They denote entirely different concepts (a personal history record vs. a document component), so they are unrelated.

A's Conference Member is a Person who belongs to a conference (author, chair, PC member, reviewer), while B's Academic Institution is an Organisation (a university or research institute). They are different kinds of entity entirely: one is a person role, the other an organisation, so they cannot denote the same concept.

A's 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events), while B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's 'accept Paper' relates an Administrator to a Paper (the act of an administrator accepting a paper), while B's 'related To Paper' relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a presentation being linked to the accepted paper it presents). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A's `writes` goes Author -> Contribution (an author writes a paper/contribution). B's `written By` goes Document -> Person (a document is written by a person). These are inverse relations, not equivalent: the direction and the domain/range roles are swapped. A property and its inverse are not equivalent, so the pair is unrelated.

A is a subclass of Author (an author whose CD proceedings are included), while B is an Invited Speaker, a subclass of Speaker distinct from Author. They denote different roles in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

A's 'Registation deadline' is a specific kind of deadline (a sibling of submission, camera-ready, notification and hotel deadlines under the parent Deadline), whereas B's 'Deadline' is the general class of all deadlines (its children include abstract submission, author notification and paper submission deadlines). The specific registration deadline is therefore subsumed by the general Deadline class, not equivalent to it.

A's 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chair of the conference, under Person > Chairman), while B's 'Trip city' is a kind of City (a location associated with travel), under City. They denote entirely different concepts (person role vs. location), so they are unrelated.

A's Conference is the central event entity of the cmt ontology (has members, dates, submission settings, administrators). B's Conference Hiker is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. a person/attendee role who hikes during the conference, sitting among Speaker, Listener, Session chair. A class of events and a class of persons cannot denote the same concept, so they are unrelated.

confOf Participant is a general conference attendee (parent Person, children Member/Regular/Student, property early Registration), while iasted Lecturer is a specific speaker role nested under Author > Speaker > Delegate. The iasted hierarchy places Lecturer as a kind of author/speaker, not a general participant, so the two classes do not denote the same concept.

Sponzorship in iasted is a subclass of Money (a financial category alongside Fee, Tax, Tip), i.e. the concept of sponsorship as a monetary/funding matter. Silver Supporter in sigkdd is a specific sponsorship level/role under Sponzor (alongside Gold, Bronze, Platinum, Exhibitor). They denote different concepts: a general money-related category versus a particular sponsor tier, so they are not equivalent.

Both are object properties with identical domain (Author) and range (Paper), and both express the same relation of an author submitting a paper; the only difference is the label wording (submit Paper vs submit).

A Pending Paper is a Paper in a particular review state (siblings: Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, Published, Active Paper), i.e. a submitted paper awaiting decision. B Submission is the general document submitted to the conference, with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript; it is not restricted to the pending state. A Pending Paper is thus a narrower concept than Submission (a pending paper is a submission, but a submission need not be pending), so A is subsumed by B rather than equivalent.

A's 'Call For Manuscripts' is a call/announcement (a subclass of Call, sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Reviews), i.e. a solicitation event. B's 'Final manuscript' is a document type (a subclass of Submission, sibling of Initial manuscript), i.e. the final version of a submitted paper. They denote different concepts: one is a call for submissions, the other is a submitted document, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a volume' is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to an integer (volume number). B's 'publisher Of' is an object property linking an Organisation to publications it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, etc.). Different domain, range, and meaning; not equivalent.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic's preference in reviewing), while B's property links an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of events). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

Pending Paper is a submission-status state of a paper (a paper awaiting a decision), while Regular Paper is a paper type/category (as opposed to demo, poster, workshop, industrial papers). Their sibling sets confirm this: Pending Paper's siblings are other statuses (Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn), whereas Regular Paper's siblings are other paper categories. They denote different concepts and do not subsume one another.

A's 'Conference www' is a conference document (a web page about the conference, with a URL property) under the Conference document branch, while B's 'Conference days' is a time entity (the days of the conference) under Time, with children Delegate and One conference day. They denote different concepts (a document vs. a temporal span), so they are unrelated.

A's Student is a subclass of Person (a person who studies), while B's Worker lecturer is a subclass of Lecturer under Speaker/Author/Delegate, i.e. a working lecturer who is also a worker. The two denote different concepts: a student vs. a lecturer who works. They share no parent, no properties, and the paths diverge (Person vs. Place/Building/.../Lecturer). Not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation.

A's 'Poster Paper' is a kind of academic paper (a document presented as a poster at a conference), while B's 'Cheque' is a payment document (a financial instrument). They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different subdomains (academic submission vs. payment), so they are unrelated.

Paper Presentation (edas) is an academic event in which an accepted paper is presented, whereas Abstract (ekaw) is a document that is a part of or presented as a paper. They belong to different branches (event vs document) and have different properties, so they are not equivalent.

Conference_www is a document/web-page class (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) whose only property is a URL, i.e. the conference website. The sigkdd Conference class denotes the conference event itself, with properties for city, name, start/end dates and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. They denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) property relating a Conference volume to its Conference parts. B's 'parallel with' is a symmetric co-scheduling relation between Administrative events (sessions running in parallel). Different domain/range kinds and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

Conference volume is a whole conference event/publication entity with committees, tracks, contributions and dates, whereas Participant is a person role (subclass of Person) with only an early-registration flag. They denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

A's 'is a starting date' is a datatype property linking an Important dates node to a date literal (start of a deadline/event period). B's 'location Of' is an object property linking a Location to an Event (the inverse of an event's location). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) while B is a social event (Conference Dinner, a kind of Meal Event). They belong to disjoint branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no intended instances.

A's 'reviews' relates a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution). B's 'searched by' relates a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (domain Sponzor, range ACM SIGKDD). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A Program Committee Member is a specific role within a conference (a member of the program committee, with properties like maxPapers and memberOfProgramCommittee), whereas B Conference Participant is a broader class covering all people participating in a conference (including demo chairs, session chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.). Every PC member is a conference participant, but not every conference participant is a PC member, so A is strictly more specific than B.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an Administrator action that assigns papers to the conference (domain Administrator, range Conference). B's 'related To Event' links an Accepted Paper to its Paper Presentation (domain Accepted Paper, range Paper Presentation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'Rejected contribution' is a reviewed submission that was rejected, sibling of Accepted contribution. B's 'Withdrawn Paper' is a paper withdrawn by the authors, sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Pending/Published Paper. Withdrawal and rejection are distinct outcomes in the conference domain (a withdrawn paper is not a rejected one), so the classes do not coincide.

A 'Multimedia Topic' is a research subject area under Topic in edas, while B 'Organizing Committee' is a committee type under Committee in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (topic vs. committee) and share no intended instances.

A's Program Committee is a group of people who review papers (members are Program Committee Members, with memberOf/hasMember relations). B's Organization is an entity that provides sponsorship (isProviderOf Sponsorship, with subclasses Academia/Government/Industry/NGO). The intended instances do not coincide: a program committee is not a sponsoring organization, and the properties (membership vs. sponsorship) confirm different concepts.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property giving a person's given name, while B's 'has Fax' gives a person's fax number. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote entirely different attributes (first name vs. fax number), so they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

A 'Conference Trip' is a social event (an activity) in the ekaw ontology, while B 'Hotel fee' is a monetary fee in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Event vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.
Paper in confOf is a contribution (sibling of Poster and Short paper), while Flyer in ekaw is a document type (sibling of Abstract, Paper, Programme Brochure, etc.). They denote different concepts.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a document type with an abstract, sibling of Extended abstract), while B's Best Paper Awards Committee is a committee (sibling of Organizing/Program Committee). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's 'adjusted By' links a Bid to a Reviewer (the person who adjusted the bid), while B's 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chairing role in the conference organisation, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, whereas Presenter (ekaw) is a conference participant who presents a paper, a subclass of Conference Participant. They denote different roles with no overlap in intended instances.

A's 'Published Paper' is a specific status of a Paper (a document that has been published), sibling to Accepted/Pending/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper. B's 'Publication' is a general Item (with children Book proceeding, Cd proceeding) covering published artefacts like proceedings, not a paper status. The intended instances do not coincide.

A's 'finalize Paper Assignment' is an administrative action performed by an Administrator that results in a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), i.e. the act of finalising the assignment of papers to the conference. B's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (domain Person, range Conference document), i.e. a person contributing a document to the conference. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; not equivalent, not inverse, no subsumption.

A's Accommodation Place is a general category of places for lodging (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), while B's Single hotel room is a specific room type (sibling of Double hotel room under Hotel room). A single hotel room is a kind of accommodation place, but the two classes are not equivalent: A is far more general and B is a specific room type. The relation is subsumed_by at best, not equivalence.

A's 'has a publisher' links a Conference proceedings to a Publisher, while B's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author. Different domains, ranges, and intended relations; they are not the same property.

A's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper), while B's initiates relates a chair/committee member to a Call (call for papers). Different domains, ranges, and intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

A's Associated Chair is a conference-organisation role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member who helps chair the conference), while B's Tutorial speaker is a kind of Author who gives a tutorial. They share no intended instances: one is an organising committee role, the other a presenting author role, so they are unrelated.

A 'Time zone' is a geographical/temporal region concept (a class of time zones), while B 'Deadline Author notification' is a specific deadline event in the conference timeline (a subclass of Deadline, sibling of submission deadlines, and range of the 'notification until' property). They denote entirely different concepts: one is a time-zone entity, the other a notification deadline. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap exists.

A's Review is a conference document (a submitted review artefact, linked to a Reviewed contribution via reviews/has a review). B's Review Question is a question type on a review form (with Numerical/Textual subclasses), not a document. Different concepts despite the shared word 'review'.
Student (a Person subtype in ekaw) and Platinum Supporter (a Sponzor subtype in sigkdd) denote entirely different concepts: a person role vs. a sponsorship level. No overlap in intended instances.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a kind of document/contribution), while B's Active Paper is a specific lifecycle state of a Paper (a subclass of Paper, with children Rated Papers and siblings Accepted/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn). A Paper in the Conference ontology is not restricted to the active state, so it is broader than Active Paper; Active Paper is a narrower concept subsumed by Paper. They are not equivalent.

A's Session Chair is a conference participant who chairs a session (a role held by a PC member/participant). B's Conference Hiker is a subclass of Delegate under a building/place hierarchy, and although B has a sibling named 'Session chair', the entity being compared (Conference Hiker) is a different concept (a delegate attending the conference as a hiker/participant), not the session-chair role. The two classes do not denote the same concept.

A's 'has authors' goes from Conference document to Person (document -> author), while B's 'writes' goes from Author to Contribution (author -> paper), the inverse direction. They describe the same authoring relationship but with reversed domain/range, so they are not equivalent; they are related as inverse-like relations.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a document presented at the conference), while B's 'Introduction of speaker' is a conference activity that introduces a speaker. They belong to different branches (document vs. activity) and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a submitted contribution (parent Document, sibling Review, with properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To Reviewer), while B's Review is a document artefact in the iasted ontology (sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter, Payment document). Although both sit under a Document parent, they denote different concepts: a paper/contribution versus a review document. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's hasFax is a datatype property linking a Person to a fax number string, while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and meaning (contact fax number vs acquiring an item), so they are not the same relation.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip) held for attendees, while B's Introduction is a conference activity (sibling of Lecture, Presentation, Welcome address) that has a child 'Introduction of speaker'. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and do not coincide.

cmt's Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), while ekaw's Rejected Paper is a document/paper in a rejected state (sibling of Accepted Paper under Evaluated Paper). They are related (a rejection decision concerns a rejected paper) but denote different concepts: an event/decision vs. a document, so not equivalent.

A's hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person (attendee of an event), while B's prepare links a Person to an Item (something a person prepares). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent nor inverse.

A's 'has authors' specifically relates a Conference document to a Person (its author), while B's 'relates To' is a broad relation from a Document to any of Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, or Person. Every has-authors link is a relates-To link, but not vice versa, so has authors is strictly narrower and thus subsumed by relates To.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while B 'Exhibitor' is a sponsoring entity (a subtype of Sponzor) that exhibits at the conference. Their paths, parents and siblings (documents vs. sponsor types) show entirely different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's hasCity relates Organization/Person to a City; B's hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country. Different domains, different ranges, and city vs country are distinct concepts, so the properties are not equivalent.

A's 'default Choice' is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a positive integer (a confTool default choice), while B's 'Start of conference' is a datatype property of Conference giving a dateTime. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

Conference contributor is a broad Person subclass covering active participants, invited speakers and regular authors, while confOf Member is a Participant subclass (sibling of Regular and Student) denoting a registered conference member. The two overlap in that members are typically contributors, but neither subsumes the other: contributors need not be registered members, and members need not contribute (e.g. student attendees). Hence related rather than equivalent.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document type in the conference domain (a short summary of a paper, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), while B 'Cheque' is a payment document (sibling of Bank transfer under Payment document). They share no meaning, instances, or context; the only overlap is the generic Document ancestor, which is not enough for equivalence.

cmt:Conference Member is a broad Person subclass covering all conference participants (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers) and is linked to a Conference via member Of Conference. iasted:Conference Hiker is a narrow Delegate subclass (a specific attendee type alongside Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc.) under Conference building. They overlap in that both denote conference participants, but neither subsumes the other: Conference Member is far more general, while Conference Hiker is a specific delegate role. Hence related, not equivalent.

A's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), while B's 'design' links an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline (a scheduling/deadline relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no overlap.

A 'Session Chair' is a Person role (a person who chairs a session), while B 'Session' is a Lecture/Activity (the event itself). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

In confOf, 'Chair PC' is a direct subclass of Person and denotes the chair of the program committee (a single role). In sigkdd, 'Organizing Committee member' is a subclass of Organizator and denotes a member of the organizing committee, a broader group that includes general chair, program chair, program committee member, and webmaster. The two concepts are not the same: one is a specific chair role, the other is a committee membership role. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in a clear taxonomic sense; they are best treated as unrelated.

A's 'Invited talk' is a kind of conference contribution/presentation (a talk given by an invited speaker), while B's 'Tutorial' is a distinct scientific event type, sibling of 'Invited Talk' in ekaw. They denote different concepts; in fact B's 'Invited Talk' would be the counterpart of A's 'Invited talk', not 'Tutorial'.

A 'Book proceeding' is a publication artefact (a type of proceedings volume, sibling of 'Cd proceening' under Publication), whereas B 'Author' is a person role (a Speaker who writes papers, with properties submit/obtain/notification). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.
