A's 'accepted By' relates a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it, while B's 'award' relates something to an Award (a prize). Different domain, range and meaning; not equivalent.

A's hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string postal code, while B's writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member in the person hierarchy), while B is a document type (a brief introduction document for a session chair, subclass of Document). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Document) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'done till' is a datatype property on Deadline giving a date (the deadline's completion date), while B's 'notification until' is an object property from Author to a notification deadline class. Different domain, range, and kind (datatype vs object), so they do not denote the same relation.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while B 'Submissions deadline' is a time/deadline entity. They belong to different branches (document vs. time) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Conference is a specific kind of organised gathering (a conference event with submissions, dates, committees), while ekaw:Event is the general superclass of all events (scientific and social events, with parts, locations, organisers). A conference is an event, but not every event is a conference, so Conference is strictly more specific than Event.

A 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (a subclass of Conference, alongside Single Level Conference), while B 'General Chair' is a person role in the organizing committee. They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person role) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A 'Review preference' is a reviewer's declared preference/degree of interest for a topic or submission (it has a degree, links reviewers to topics/submissions). B 'Review Form' is the form/artifact used to record a review. Different intended instances: preferences vs. forms, so they are not equivalent.

In edas, Academic Event is a broad category of conference-domain events (children include Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop; sibling Non Academic Event), i.e. it covers all academic events including conferences, workshops, etc. In ekaw, Conference is a specific Scientific Event (one edition of a conference), a sibling of Workshop, Session, Track. Thus Academic Event is more general than Conference: every Conference is an Academic Event, but not vice versa. Hence A subsumes B, not equivalent.

Company in confOf is a subclass of Organization (an organizational entity, sibling of University), whereas Main office in sigkdd is a subclass of Place (a physical location, sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They denote different kinds of things (organization vs. location), so they are not equivalent.

A 'Member PC' is a person role (a program-committee member/reviewer) in confOf, with properties expert On (Topic) and reviewes (Contribution). B 'Personal Publication History' is a subclass of Personal History in edas, i.e. a record/history of a person's publications, not a person or role. Different kinds of entities; no equivalence.

A's isReviewing relates a committee member (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper they review; B's presentation relates a Speaker to a Document they present. Different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings (reviewing vs. presenting), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document they authored (authorship relation). B's 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper they submitted (submission action). Authorship and submission are distinct relations in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's updatedVersionOf relates a Document to another Document (a versioning relation between documents), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (authorship). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

City in confOf is a geographic location used as the range of has City (Organization, Person -> City), whereas Research Topic in ekaw is a subject area covered by events and papers (covers Topic / topic Covered By). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), a subclass of Event. B's Conference days is a Time entity whose children are Delegate and One conference day, i.e. the temporal span of a conference, not the event itself. Different kinds (event vs. time interval), so they are not equivalent.

A's assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (the person who reviews it), while B's isWrittenBy links a Paper to an Author (the person who wrote it). These are different relations in the conference domain: reviewing vs. authorship, with different ranges (Reviewer vs. Author). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

Both denote the same social conference event: a dinner held as part of the conference. A's 'Conference Dinner' is a Meal Event within Non Academic Events, while B's 'Dinner banquet' is a Social program activity; the intended instances (the conference dinner/banquet) coincide, so they are equivalent despite differing parent hierarchies.

A's 'is given by' links a Presentation to the person giving it (range Active conference participant), while B's 'presentation' links a Speaker to the Document presented (range Document). They are inverses/related roles in the same presentation act but not the same relation: different domain, range, and direction.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Person) in the cmt ontology, while B 'Welcome Talk' is a conference event (a subclass of Talk Event) in the edas ontology. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person vs. event) and share no meaning in the conference domain.

In iasted, Activity is a broad concept with children 'Activity after conference', 'Activity before conference', and 'Conference activity'; a Conference is a specific kind of Activity (a Conference activity), so edas Conference is strictly more specific than iasted Activity. The properties of Activity (give, go through, is held in, is dated on, etc.) apply to all activities including conferences, confirming the subsumption direction.

A is a research topic area (a subject category under Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while B is a kind of conference event (an individual presentation such as a contributed talk or tutorial). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A is a research topic (Mobile Computing Topic) under Topic in edas, while B is a document type (Tutorial Abstract) under Abstract in ekaw. They denote different kinds of things (subject area vs. document), so they are unrelated.

A's `name` is a datatype property giving a string name to a Conference or Person; B's `organisedBy` is an object property linking an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. Different kinds (datatype vs object), different domains (Conference/Person vs Event), different ranges (string vs Organisation/Person), and different meaning (naming vs organising). They are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties named 'has First Name' with domain Person and range string, relating a person to their first name. The confOf comment ('involved middle name') is a minor annotation quirk and does not change the intended relation; the paths and signatures match exactly, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

An Accommodation Place (a place where one stays, e.g. a hotel) is a kind of Building in the iasted ontology: Building has children such as Conference hotel and Conference restaurant, and is occupied by / visited by persons, matching the intended instances of Accommodation Place. However, Building is broader (it also covers airports, offices, universities, company houses), so Accommodation Place is strictly more specific and is subsumed by Building rather than equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property giving a person's given name (domain Person, range string). B's 'has Postal Code' is a datatype property giving a postal/zip code for an Organization or Person (domain Organization, Person, range string). They relate different kinds of information (first name vs. postal code) and are not the same relation, so they are unrelated.

Rejection is a decision outcome (sibling of Acceptance under Decision) in cmt, while Trip is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Reception under Social event) in confOf. They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Author in cmt is a person role (a Conference Member/User who writes or submits papers), while Form in iasted is a document type (a Document with children such as Author information form, Registration form). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and share no intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a whole-part relation, sibling of 'has parts'), while B's 'deals With' links a Contribution to the Topic it is about (a subject-matter relation). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

Both are Author subclasses, but Presenter (edas) is a person who presents a paper, while Tutorial speaker (iasted) is a speaker at a tutorial event; they overlap in being speaking authors but are not the same concept.

A is a member registration fee (a specific registration fee paid by members), while B is a sponsor fee (a fee paid by sponsors). They are different fee types with different payers and different positions in the fee hierarchy; A's siblings are other registration fee subtypes, B's sibling is Registration fee itself.

In cmt, Document is a general class whose children are Paper and Review (scientific documents). In iasted, Payment document is a specific subclass of Document for financial paperwork (children Bank transfer, Cheque), alongside siblings like Review, Submission, Form. The two classes denote different concepts: a scientific document vs. a payment document. They are not equivalent.

A's 'assigned By Administrator' links a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned them (domain Reviewer, range Administrator). B's 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History to the Reviewer it belongs to (domain Personal Review History, range Reviewer). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they denote different relations.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person (a person who contributes to a conference, with children like Invited speaker, Regular author), while B's 'Conference days' is a subclass of Time (a temporal span, with children Delegate and One conference day). They belong to different top-level branches (Person vs Time) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A's 'issues' relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain Publisher, range Conference proceedings). B's 'holded by' relates a Conference to the ACM SIGKDD organisation that holds it (domain Conference, range ACM SIGKDD). Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; they are not the same relation.

A's 'write Paper' relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). B's 'inverse of part Of 7' relates something to an Event (range Event), and is the inverse of a part-of relation, i.e. a mereological/containment relation, not authorship. The kinds of things related and the direction differ, so the two properties are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document type (subclass of Document, with children like Conference Paper, Poster Paper, and properties such as has Review, covers Topic), while B's Review is a distinct document type (sibling of Submission, Form, Invitation letter) representing a review artefact. In ekaw, Review is a separate sibling class of Paper, not the same concept, so the two entities denote different things.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is the abstract/summary text of a paper, a sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper. Camera Ready Paper (ekaw) is a paper in its final, camera-ready form, a sibling of Submitted Paper, Regular Paper, etc. They denote different stages/parts of a paper and are not equivalent.

Organization in edas is an institution (with subclasses Academia/Government/Industry/NGO) that provides sponsorships, whereas Person in sigkdd is an individual (with subclasses Listener/Organizator/Speaker) with email, name, nation, place and fees. Different kinds of entities with no overlap.

A's 'invites co reviewers' is a Reviewer-to-Reviewer relation for inviting co-reviewers, while B's 'send' is a generic Person-to-Item relation for sending an item. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper that has been published (a subclass of Paper in the edas ontology, sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn papers). B 'Payment document' is a document used for paying conference fees (parent Document, children Bank transfer and Cheque). They share no intended instances: one is a scientific contribution, the other a financial artefact. Different paths, parents, siblings and properties confirm they denote different concepts.

confOf Member is a subclass of Participant (a person who is a member of the conference, with siblings Regular and Student), while ekaw Student is a subclass of Person denoting a person's student status. Member is a participant role in the conference, Student is an academic status; they are not the same concept, and neither subsumes the other.

Both are datatype properties linking a call/deadline entity to a date value representing the submission deadline. edas hasSubmissionDeadline has domain Call and range dateTime; iasted done_till has domain Deadline and range date. Call and Deadline denote the same conference-organisation concept (a call for papers with its deadline), and dateTime/date are compatible date-valued ranges, so the two properties relate the same kinds of things in the same direction and are equivalent.

Associated Chair (cmt) is a chair role under Chairman/Conference Member, i.e. a person helping organise the conference; Invited Speaker (sigkdd) is a speaker role under Speaker, i.e. a person giving a talk. Different roles with different parents and siblings, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (whole-to-part containment), while B's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.
A's 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while B's 'design' relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Deadline. Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no overlap.

A's `name` is a generic datatype property for Conference and Person (a label/name string), while B's `has Submission Instructions` is a Call-specific property holding submission instruction text. Different domains (Conference/Person vs Call) and different intended meaning, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Call for paper' is a specific conference document (sibling of Call for participation, Conference announcement, etc.), while B's 'Call' is a broader class with children Call For Manuscripts, Call For Papers, Call For Reviews. Thus A's Call for paper is a narrower concept subsumed by B's general Call.

A's memberOfProgramCommittee relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (a committee membership relation). B's sign relates a Person to an Item (a signing/authoring relation over items). The domains and ranges are disjoint concepts (committee member vs person, committee vs item), so the two properties do not denote the same relation.

Currency is a monetary unit class, while Registration fee is a fee/charge class (a subclass of Fee with children for member/non-member/student fees and properties Price, pay, payed by). They denote different concepts; Currency is only used as the range of the 'Currency' property of Registration fee, not equivalent to it.

A's Paper is the general conference submission class (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, with authors, reviews, decisions, bids). B's Withdrawn Paper is a specific status subclass of Paper in edas (sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper). The general Paper concept subsumes the withdrawn-paper status, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Camera ready contribution' is a document/contribution class (a written artefact that has been accepted and put into camera-ready form), whereas B's 'Submission event' is an administrative event (the act/occasion of submitting contributions). One is a document, the other an event; they do not denote the same concept. Note also that B's sibling 'Camera Ready event' is the event counterpart of A's class, not 'Submission event'.

A's Workshop is a conference part (sibling of Track and Tutorial) that a conference volume has workshops of; B's Demo Session is a kind of Session (sibling of Workshop Session, Regular Session, etc.). A workshop is an event/part, not a session type, and B's Demo Session is a session format, not a workshop. They denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Sponzorship is a subclass of Money (a monetary category alongside Fee, Tax, Tip), while B's Sponzor fee is a subclass of Fee (a specific fee type alongside Registration fee). Both concern sponsorship money, but one is a general money category and the other a specific fee, so they overlap rather than coincide.

A 'Submitted Paper' is a paper submitted to a conference (a subclass of Paper, with children like Assigned Paper), whereas B 'Invitation letter' is a document sent to invite someone (e.g. a reviewer or speaker). They denote different concepts despite both being documents, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) in cmt, while B 'Poster Session' is a type of scientific event session in ekaw. They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. event) with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while B 'Coffee break' is a conference activity (subclass of Conference activity, sibling of Lecture, Registration, etc.). They belong to different branches (document vs. activity) and denote different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

A's Track is a thematic stream of the conference (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop, linked from Conference volume via has tracks), whereas B's Workshop is a working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial under Working event). They denote different concepts: a track is not a workshop, and neither subsumes the other.

A's has Topic relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (subject matter). B's paper In Volume relates a paper to the volume/proceedings it appears in. Different kinds of things are related (topic vs. publication volume), so the properties are not equivalent.
Sponsor (a person or organization providing funding) and Listener (an attendee who listens) are distinct roles in the conference domain; neither subsumes the other.

A's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to the Conference Event it belongs to (domain Programme, range Conference Event), while B's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation/Person that organises it (domain Event, range Organisation/Person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; not equivalent nor inverse.

Travel Grant (a sponsorship category providing funding for travel) and Sponzor fee (a fee category, sibling of Registration fee) denote different concepts: one is a form of sponsorship/support, the other a type of fee. Their paths (Sponsorship vs Fee) and siblings confirm they belong to distinct branches of the conference domain.

A 'Personal Review History' is a record of the reviews a reviewer has performed (a subclass of Personal History, with properties linking it to a Reviewer). B 'Research Topic' is a subject area covered by events and papers. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances or properties.

A's 'expert On' relates a PC member to a Topic (expertise area), while B's 'publisher Of' relates an Organisation to published artefacts (Flyer, Volume, Brochure, Web Site). Different domains, ranges, and intended meaning; no overlap.

A's 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' (a written/submitted artefact such as a paper, poster, or talk submission, with properties 'has contributions' and 'is submitted at' linking it to a conference volume). B's 'Individual Presentation' is a subclass of 'Scientific Event' (an event that occurs at a conference, with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial, and properties linking it to a Paper/Abstract). One denotes a document/contribution, the other an event; their paths, parents, children and properties do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's writes relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes a paper/contribution), whereas edas's relatesTo relates a Document to events, sessions or persons (a document is about/associated with them). The domains (Author vs Document) and ranges (Contribution vs Event/Session/Person) differ, and the direction of the relation is different, so they are not the same property.

Associated Chair (cmt) is a chair role in the conference organisation, a sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair under Chairman; Invited Speaker (ekaw) is a presenter role under Presenter. They denote different roles with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

A's 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (a mereological/containment relation within the conference structure), while B's 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (a person signing/authoring an item). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's Conference hall is a room where conference sessions take place, while B's Main office is an administrative office space; they are distinct sibling place types (A even has its own Main office sibling), so the concepts do not coincide.

A's Organization is a general class for any organization, while B's Government Organization is a specific subtype of Organization (sibling of Academia Organization, Industry Organization, NGO). Thus Government Organization is strictly narrower than Organization, so A is subsumed by B's parent, not equivalent to the subtype.

A is a research topic in computer networks (a subject area under Topic), while B is the program committee (an organizational body under Committee). They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap.

A's run Paper Assignment Tools is an Administrator action that produces a Conference (domain Administrator, range Conference), i.e. the process of assigning papers to reviewers. B's has Topic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic (domain Conference/Paper, range Topic), i.e. a topical classification relation. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'start Reviewer Bidding' is an action performed by an Administrator that initiates the bidding phase and takes a Conference as its range. B's 'is Reviewing' relates a person (Reviewer, Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper they review. Different domain, range, and intended meaning; not the same relation.

A's contributes relates a Person to a Conference document (the paper they author/submit), while B's hasRelatedDocument relates a Person or event/session to a Document more broadly (e.g. proceedings, associated files). The ranges overlap (Document vs Conference document) and both link people to documents, but B is broader in domain and range and does not specifically mean authoring/submitting a paper, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Government Organization is a type of organization (sibling of Academia/Industry Organization, NGO) in edas, whereas Proceedings Publisher in ekaw is a role/type of organisation that publishes proceedings (sibling of Academic Institution, Organising Agency). They denote different concepts: a government body is not a proceedings publisher, and a proceedings publisher need not be a government organization.

A's 'has short title' is a datatype property of Social/Working events giving a string abbreviation, while B's 'done till' is a datatype property of Deadline giving a date. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A is a subclass of Paper (a document type: the abstract version of a paper), while B is a subclass of Topic (a subject area in signal processing). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's Conference is a working event (a kind of event/activity, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B's Sponsor state is a state of a sponsor (sibling of Conference state and Presenter state). They denote different concepts: an event type versus a status/state, so they are unrelated.

A's 'name' is a general name datatype property for Conference and Person, while B's 'has a URL' is a specific property for Conference www with a URL string value. They denote different attributes (a name vs. a URL), so they are not equivalent.

A's Author is a person role (Conference Member/User) who writes and submits papers; B's Award is a recognition given to papers/authors, with children like Best Research Paper Award. Different intended instances and no shared properties, so they are unrelated.

A 'Tutorial Abstract' is a document (an abstract text of a tutorial), while B 'Tutorial speaker' is a person (an author who gives a tutorial). They denote different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the same concept: a country. In confOf, Country is the range of hasCountry for Organization and Person; in edas, Country is the range of hasCountry for Conference. The differing domains reflect different modelling choices, not different concepts, and both ontologies use the identical label Country for the same domain notion.

A's Meta Reviewer is a specialized Reviewer role (a subtype of Reviewer, with a 'read By Meta Reviewer' property linking papers to meta-reviewers), while B's Author is a Person who writes papers (with 'is Written By' / 'has Related Paper' properties). The two denote different roles in the conference domain: a meta-reviewer reviews/oversees reviews, an author writes papers. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A's max Choice is a datatype property of Social/Working event with range positiveInteger (a capacity/limit on choices), while B's End of conference is a datatype property of Conference with range dateTime (a temporal endpoint). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a document type that evaluates a Paper (has Review, review Of Paper, review Written By), while B's Abstract is a short summary document, sibling of Paper and Review. They are distinct document types in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' relates an Administrator to a Conference (administrative mailing of hardcopy manifests), while B's 'paper Presented As' relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (a paper being presented in a session). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A is an event class (Paper Presentation, a kind of Academic Event with siblings Workshop/Talk Event, linked to Accepted Paper), while B is a person class (Speaker, a kind of Person with children Author/Invited Speaker). They denote different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

A 'Conference Trip' is a social event (an activity held during a conference, sibling of Conference Banquet), while B 'Fee' is a monetary charge (a kind of Money, with children like Registration fee and Hotel fee). One is an event, the other a payment; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has authors' goes from a Conference document to a Person (document -> author), while B's 'write' goes from a Person to an Item (author -> written item). They describe the same authorship relation but in opposite directions, so they are inverses rather than equivalent properties.

A 'Performance Topic' is a subject-area category (a subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.) used to classify papers. B 'Plenary lecture' is a kind of conference activity/event (subclass of Lecture, sibling of Session and Tutorial). One denotes a topic of interest, the other a scheduled event; their instances cannot coincide, so they are unrelated.

A's Review is a document/artefact produced by a reviewer (a subclass of Document, sibling of Paper, with properties write Review and written By linking Reviewer to Review). B's Call For Reviews is a call/announcement (subclass of Call, sibling of Call For Papers and Call For Manuscripts) soliciting reviews. One is the review artefact, the other is the solicitation for reviews; their intended instances do not coincide.

A's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its members (people belonging to the conference), while B's initiates links a chair/TPC member to a Call they initiate. Different domains (Conference vs. person roles) and different ranges (Conference Member vs. Call), so the relations are unrelated.

A's hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members (range Program Committee Member), while B's hasMember links a Conference to its members (range Person). The EDAS property is broader: a conference has members (including committee members), so the CMT property is a specialization of the EDAS one. They are not equivalent because the domains and ranges differ (Program Committee vs Conference, Program Committee Member vs Person).

confOf Topic is a subject area of contributions (dealt with by Contribution, expertise of PC members, topic of working events), whereas ekaw Event is a conference/scientific or social event that covers topics and is organised by people/organisations. Topic and Event denote different concepts; the only link is the property covers Topic whose range is Research Topic, not Event.

Viza is a visa document (a travel/administrative document for conference attendees) under Document in iasted, while Abstract is the summary of a paper under Document in sigkdd. They share only the generic parent Document; their intended instances (visa paperwork vs. paper abstract) do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties linking a paper-like entity to a topic/activity: confOf's 'deals With' has domain Contribution (a paper) and range Topic, while iasted's 'go through' has domain Item (a paper) and range Activity (a topic/theme). The paths Contribution > deals With > Topic and Item > go through > Activity express the same relation of a submission being about a subject, so they are equivalent despite the different labels.

Conference participant is a broad class covering all persons participating in a conference (its children are Active and Passive conference participant, and its siblings include Committee member, Reviewer, etc.). Session chair in iasted is a specific role under Delegate, alongside Speaker, Listener, etc. A session chair is a kind of conference participant, but not every conference participant is a session chair, so Conference participant is more general and is subsumed by the narrower Session chair relation (Session chair subsumed_by Conference participant).

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a subclass of Chairman/Conference Member, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair) in the cmt ontology. B 'Presenter house' is a building/place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport) in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different kinds of entities (person role vs. physical location), so they are unrelated.

A's 'Program Committee' is the group of people who review papers (domain of 'has Program Committee Member'), while B's 'Social program' is a conference activity (a subclass of Conference activity with children such as Dinner banquet). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman of the conference, sibling of Author, Reviewer, PC Chair), while B 'Free Time Break' is a non-academic conference event (a break period, sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break). They belong to entirely different branches (Person vs Conference Event) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's has Street is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string (a street address), while B's obtain is an object property linking Person to an Item (acquiring something). They share neither domain/range kinds nor meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's `reviews` links a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's `updated Version Of` links a Document to another Document it is a later version of (domain Document, range Document). Different domain, range and intended meaning; not equivalent.

A's has Topic relates a Conference/Paper to a Topic (the subject matter of a paper). B's scientifically Organises relates an Academic Institution to something it organises (e.g. a conference or event). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Administrator in confOf is a generic person role (confTool administrator) with siblings like Author, Chair PC, Participant; PC Chair in ekaw is a specific conference committee role (chair of the program committee), a subclass of PC Member. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

Administrator is a User subclass in cmt that manages the conference (accepts papers, assigns reviewers, enters conference details), while Reviewer in Conference is a Person subclass who performs reviews. They are different roles: an administrator is not a reviewer, and the properties (accept Paper, assign Reviewer vs. has a review reference/expertise) do not overlap.

An External Reviewer is a person who reviews papers on behalf of a reviewer, whereas a Paper Author is a person who writes papers. They are distinct roles in the conference domain, with different properties (assign/assigned By Reviewer vs. authoring relations) and no subsumption between them.

A 'Conference activity' is an event/activity in the conference programme (siblings: Activity before/after conference; children: Lecture, Presentation, Registration, Coffee break), whereas B 'Speaker' is a role of a person (parent Person; children Author, Invited Speaker; siblings Listener, Organizator). They denote different kinds of things (event vs. person role) and are not equivalent.

A's 'has a review expertise' links a submitted contribution to a review expertise (a reviewer's topic competence), while B's 'presentationed by' links a document to the speaker who presents it. Different domain/range and different intended relation, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/member of the conference committee) in cmt, while B 'Power Point presentation' is a kind of presentation activity in iasted. They denote entirely different concepts (person vs. presentation format) with no overlap.

A's hasSurname is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their surname), while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item (acquiring something). They differ in kind (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and meaning, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a chairing role within the conference committee hierarchy (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member), while Early Registered Participant (ekaw) is a conference attendee who registered early, a kind of Conference Participant. They denote different concepts: one is an organiser role, the other an attendee registration status. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

Both properties relate an author/person to the paper/document they wrote, in the same direction (Author -> Paper vs Person -> Document). In the conference domain, Author and Person coincide, and Paper and Document coincide, so write Paper and author Of denote the same relation.

A's Rejection is a subclass of Decision (the outcome of a review, sibling of Acceptance), while B's Speaker is a subclass of Person (a role in the conference programme, with children Author and Invited Speaker and properties linking to Document). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Conference in cmt is the event itself (has members, dates, submissions, review criteria), while Participant in confOf is a Person subtype (attendee with early registration). They denote different concepts and are not in a subsumption relation.

A's title is a datatype property of Paper giving the paper's title; B's has the first name is a datatype property of Person giving a person's first name. Different domains (Paper vs Person) and different intended relations, so they are unrelated.

A's hasPhone is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string phone number, while B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in domain, range, and kind (datatype vs object), so they do not denote the same relation.

City and Country are distinct geographic entities. In confOf, City is the range of has City (Organization, Person -> City), i.e. the location of organizations and persons. In edas, Country is the range of has Country (Conference -> Country), i.e. the country of a conference. They denote different concepts (a city vs. a country) and are not synonyms, so they are unrelated.

hasTopic relates a Working event to a Topic (event -> topic), while topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (topic -> event/paper). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent; a property and its inverse are not equivalent, so the relation is 'related'.

A's Paper Abstract is the abstract of a paper (a textual summary, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper). B's Slide Set is a presentation slide collection, a distinct document artefact under Document alongside Paper, Review, Programme. Different intended instances; no subsumption or overlap.

A's Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), a subclass of Scientific Event with siblings Session, Track, Workshop. B's Conference state is a subclass of State, alongside Presenter state and Sponsor state, i.e. a status/state of a conference rather than the event itself. Different kinds (event vs. state) and different paths, so they are not equivalent.

A's Presentation is a general conference contribution (parent of Invited talk, sibling of Poster, with abstract and presenter properties), while B's Power Point presentation is a specific subtype of Presentation in iasted, sibling to Video presentation. Thus A's Presentation is broader and B is a narrower kind of presentation, so A is subsumed by B's parent concept rather than equivalent to the PowerPoint-specific class.

A's Paper is a conference submission document (has authors, reviews, decisions, subject areas), while B's Contact Information is an address/phone/email record for a person. They share no instances and no properties; the pair is unrelated.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's given name), while B's 'is connected with' is an object property relating an Activity or Person to an Item or Place. They differ in kind (datatype vs object), in domain/range, and in intended meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's hasMenu relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (a catering/meal concept), while B's give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving something). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's coversTopic relates an Event/Paper to a Research Topic (the subject matter a paper or event addresses), while B's need relates a Person to an Item (something a person requires). Different domains (Event/Paper vs Person), different ranges (Research Topic vs Item), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.
Both entities represent the same concept of a conference presentation/paper presentation, with matching labels, paths, and properties.

A's 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers submitted to the volume), while B's 'has Review' links a Paper to its Review. The domains and ranges differ (volume vs paper, contribution vs review), so the relations are not the same.

A's Organizational Meeting is a kind of academic event (a meeting held during the conference), while B's Program Committee is a committee (a group of people). They denote different concepts: an event vs. an organizational body, with no subsumption or overlap.

A 'Working event' is a subclass of Event covering Conference, Tutorial and Workshop (organisational events with titles, locations, choices), while B 'Security Topic' is a subclass of Topic, a subject area for papers. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (event vs. topic) and share no instances.

A's 'is an ending date' is a datatype property of the class Important dates, giving the end date of a conference deadline/event; B's 'is dated on' is a datatype property of Activity, giving the date on which an activity occurs. They relate different kinds of things (a deadline's end vs. an activity's occurrence date) and are not inverses or synonyms, so a reference alignment would not equate them.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person (a person involved in a conference, with children Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while Activity in iasted is a general event/action class (with children Conference activity, Activity before/after conference) that is not a person. Their paths, siblings and properties (member Of Conference vs. is held in / is dated on) show different intended instances, so they are unrelated.

A's rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (a decision action), while B's write relates a Person to an Item (an authorship action). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

A's NGO is a subtype of Organization (a kind of organisation such as academia, government, industry), while B's Organising Agency is a subtype of Organisation denoting the body that organises a conference (siblings: Academic Institution, Proceedings Publisher). NGO is a type of organisation, not the conference-organising role, so the intended instances do not coincide.

ekaw's 'held In' is a specific spatial relation from an Event to a Location (where the event takes place). iasted's 'is connected with' is a much broader relation linking an Activity or Person to an Item or Place, covering many kinds of connections, not just event location. The two overlap in that an event's location is one kind of connection, but neither subsumes the other cleanly and they are not the same relation, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A's Presenter is a Conference Participant who presents at the conference (sibling of Invited Speaker, under Conference Participant). B's Author_book_proceedings_included is a very specific Author role (an author of a book of proceedings included in the conference), under Author > Speaker > Delegate. Both denote people involved in contributing/presenting at a conference, but they are not the same concept: Presenter is a generic presenting participant, while the B entity is a narrow authorship role tied to proceedings books. They overlap in the domain (a presenter is typically also an author) but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

A's property links a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the paper assignment tools), while B's property links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (how the paper is presented). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted, while B's 'Name of conference' is a string property giving the conference's name. They share only the domain (Conference) but have different ranges (boolean vs string) and completely different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's 'hasBeenAssigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper they review), while B's 'references' is a generic bibliographic citation relation between documents/papers. They relate different kinds of things in different directions, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Performance Topic' is a subject area of papers (a subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Organizing Committee' is a type of committee (subclass of Committee, sibling of Program Committee). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Both denote a chair-like committee role subordinate to the main chair: cmt's Associated Chair is a Chairman and Conference Member (a chairing person other than the Conference Chair/PC Chair), and Conference's Co chair is a Committee member distinct from Chair, with properties linking it to a Committee as its co-chair. The intended instances (persons serving as co/associated chairs of a conference or committee) coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution of a paper), while B's 'is Provider Of' relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (sponsoring). Different domains (Person vs Organization), different ranges (Conference document vs Sponsorship), and different intended relations, so they are not equivalent.

Review expertise is a class representing a reviewer's area of expertise (linked to Reviewer, Review preference, Submitted contribution), while Person is a general agent class (parent of Delegate and Sponsor) in the iasted ontology. They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

A's property links a Topic to a Conference part (topic is a topic of a conference part), while B's 'need' links a Person to an Item (a person needs an item). Different domains (Topic vs Person), different ranges (Conference part vs Item), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's has City is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string city name; B's obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. Different domains, ranges, and kinds (datatype vs object), so they cannot denote the same relation.

A 'Paper Full Version' is a document type (a complete paper, sibling of Paper Abstract) in the cmt ontology. B 'Simulating' is a research activity performed before a conference (sibling of Modelling) in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different branches (Document vs Activity) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a kind of Contribution (a conference submission such as a poster or short paper), while B's Test Only Topic is a subject/topic category under Topic in edas. They denote different concepts (a document vs. a topic), so they are unrelated.

A's co-writePaper goes from Co author to Paper (co-author -> paper), while B's isWrittenBy goes from Paper to Author (paper -> author). They are not the same relation: one links a co-author to a paper, the other links a paper to an author. Even ignoring direction, the domain/range kinds differ (Co author vs Author, and the inverse direction), so they are not equivalent; at best they are inverses/related, but as stated they are unrelated.

Decision in cmt is the outcome of a paper review (children Acceptance/Rejection, domain of has Decision from Paper), while Fee in sigkdd is a monetary charge (children Registration fee, Sponzor fee). Different concepts with no overlap.

A's Review is a conference document (a completed review artefact, with properties linking it to a reviewed contribution), whereas B's Textual Review Question is a type of review question (a form field/question used in the review form, sibling of Numerical Review Question). They denote different concepts: a review document vs. a question type, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Co author' is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a paper), while B's 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor, i.e. a kind of contribution role rather than a person class. They overlap in the conference domain (both concern non-invited authors of papers) but their intended instances differ: A denotes persons, B denotes contribution roles. Hence related, not equivalent.

A 'Paper Abstract' is a document/paper component in the cmt ontology (sibling of Paper Full Version), while B 'LCD projector' is a piece of audiovisual equipment in the iasted ontology. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

Reception in confOf is a specific social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip), while iasted's Conference activity is a broad category whose children include Coctail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Presentation, etc. A reception is one kind of conference activity, so Reception is strictly narrower and thus subsumed by Conference activity, not equivalent.

Both ontologies define 'Session Chair' as a role of a person who chairs a session; in edas it is a subclass of Person alongside Author/Reviewer/Conference Chair, and in ekaw it is a subclass of Conference Participant (and PC Member) alongside other chair roles. Same intended instances (persons chairing sessions), so the classes are equivalent.

A's Conference is the whole conference event (has dates, administrators, members, accepts submissions), while B's Conference part is a component of a conference (parent of Track, Tutorial, Workshop, part of a Conference volume). They denote different concepts: the whole event vs. its constituent parts.

A 'Single Level Conference' is a conference type (a conference without sub-events, sibling of 'Two Level Conference' under Conference), whereas B 'One conference day' is a temporal unit (a single day of a conference, under Time > Conference days). They denote different concepts: a conference structure vs. a time interval, so they are unrelated.

A (confOf Member PC) is a person role (a PC member/reviewer, subclass of Person, with properties expert On and reviewes), while B (ekaw Neutral Review) is a subclass of Review (a document/opinion artefact with polarity). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. review document) and are not equivalent.

A's Tutorial is a conference event/part (sibling of Track and Workshop, linked from Conference volume via has tutorials), whereas B's Tutorial Abstract is a document (subclass of Abstract, sibling of Invited Talk Abstract). The event and the document about it are different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

In edas, Paper is a subclass of Document (path Document > Paper), while in ekaw, Document is the broader class with Paper as one of its children (alongside Abstract, Flyer, Review, etc.). Thus edas Paper is strictly more specific than ekaw Document; the two are not equivalent.

Person (ekaw) is a human agent involved in conference organisation (author, reviewer, participant), while City (iasted) is a geographic location occupied by buildings and people. Their children, properties and paths are disjoint; no subsumption or overlap exists.

Tutorial is a type of lecture/activity in the conference programme, while Invited Speaker is a type of person (a speaker role). They belong to different branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (a record of reviews), while B's give links a Person to an Activity or Item they produce/submit (e.g. giving a talk or a paper). Both involve a person and something they contribute, but the ranges differ (review history vs. activity/item) and the direction/intent is not the same, so they are only loosely related, not equivalent.

A's Organisation is an organising body (academic institution, organising agency, publisher) that organises events and publishes proceedings; B's Conference is the event itself, with city, start/end dates and name, held by ACM SIGKDD. The two denote different concepts (organiser vs. event), so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Registration form' is a Document/Form artefact used to register (siblings: Author information form, Hotel registration form), whereas B's 'Registration Non Member' is a fee category (a kind of Registration fee, siblings: member/student fees). They denote different concepts—a form versus a fee—so they are unrelated.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person (a human role in the conference), while Administrative event is a subclass of Event (a process/activity such as submission, reviewing, registration). They belong to disjoint top-level branches (Person vs Event) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

ekaw:Event is a broad conference-domain class (parent of Scientific Event and Social Event, with properties like held In, organised By, has Event, part Of Event) denoting any organised happening. sigkdd:Award is a specific recognition class (parent of Best Research/Applications/Student Paper Award, with properties awarded by, obtain) denoting prizes given to authors. Their instances, parents, children and properties do not coincide; Award is not a kind of Event, so the classes are unrelated.

A's start Date is the start date/time of a Conference (domain Conference), while B's Date is the date of a Deadline (domain Deadline). They relate different kinds of things in different contexts, so they are not equivalent.

A 'Talk Event' in edas is an academic event (a talk given at the conference, with children Welcome Talk and Closing Talk, siblings Paper Presentation and Workshop). B 'Tutorial' in iasted is a kind of Lecture (a conference activity, sibling of Plenary lecture and Session). A tutorial is a lecture-style activity, not a talk event; the two denote different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a session, a role distinct from Possible Reviewer (ekaw), which is a person who may review papers and is the parent of PC Member. Their properties differ (Session Chair initiates calls and reviews papers; Possible Reviewer writes reviews and is reviewer of papers), and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'submit Paper' relates an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper), while B's 'is visited by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (domain Building, City, State, range Person). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; no equivalence or subsumption.

Participant (confOf) is a subclass of Person representing a person attending the conference, with subclasses Member, Regular, Student and a property early Registration. Sponzor (sigkdd) is a sponsor organisation with subclasses Gold/Silver/Bronze/Platinum Supporter, Exhibitor, Best Student Paper Supporter, and properties Name of sponsor and a search relation to ACM SIGKDD. A person attending a conference and a sponsoring organisation are different concepts, so the classes are unrelated.

A 'Reviewing event' in confOf is an administrative event covering the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions, sibling to Submission event and Camera Ready event. B 'Workshop' in edas is an academic event (a type of conference event), sibling to Paper Presentation and Talk Event. They denote different concepts: one is the review process, the other a type of academic gathering. No subsumption or overlap in the conference domain.

A's title is the title of a Paper (domain Paper, range string), while B's has Surname is the surname of a Person (domain Person, range string). They relate different kinds of entities and denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'Conference proceedings' is the published collection of papers (a document with name, volume, ISBN, publisher), while B's 'Proceedings Publisher' is an organisation (subclass of Organisation, sibling of Academic Institution and Organising Agency) that publishes proceedings. The two denote different kinds of entities (document vs. organisation), so they are not equivalent.

Both are object properties with domain Person and range a document/item produced by the person (Conference document vs Item). In the conference domain, a person contributing a conference document corresponds to a person signing an item (authorship/contribution relation), so the intended relation coincides.

A's Multi author Volume is a collection/volume of documents (parent of Proceedings, published by an organisation), while B's Abstract is a short summary document sibling to Paper and Review. They denote different concepts despite both being Documents.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a Conference participant who attends without an active role (sibling of 'Active conference participant'), whereas B 'Attendee' is a direct subclass of Person covering anyone attending the conference, including authors, reviewers, chairs, etc. The Attendee class is broader: every passive participant is an attendee, but attendees may also be active participants. Hence A is subsumed by B, not equivalent.

A's Web Site is a Document that lists events and is published by an organisation (a conference web page), while B's Registration form is a Form document used to register for a conference. They share only the broad Document ancestor; their intended instances and roles differ, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has a publisher' relates a Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the publishing body), while B's 'publisher Of' relates an Organisation (the publisher) to the things it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). The domains and ranges are disjoint and the direction of the publishing relation is reversed, so they are not the same relation.

Conference contributor is a broad role class covering active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors, whereas Agency Staff Member in ekaw denotes staff of the organising agency, a distinct kind of person. Their children/siblings and intended instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has parts' is a mereological (part-whole) relation between a Conference volume and its Conference parts, whereas B's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'for Event' links a Call to the Academic Event it is for (domain Call, range Academic Event). B's 'scientifically Organised By' links something to an Academic Institution that organises it scientifically, and is a subproperty of 'organised By'. The ranges differ (Academic Event vs Academic Institution) and the meanings differ (call-for-papers target vs scientific organiser), so they are not equivalent.

A's Conference Participant is a broad role class under Person covering all conference attendees (chairs, presenters, authors, registered participants). B's Conference Hiker is a specific subclass of Delegate (itself a subclass of Place/Building/Conference building) denoting a particular kind of delegate/attendee. The B concept is narrower and sits under Delegate, which corresponds to a participant role; thus Conference Hiker is subsumed by the more general Conference Participant, not equivalent.

Company (a type of Organization, sibling of University) is an organisational entity, while Taxi (a Transport vehicle, sibling of Car/Shuttle bus/Van) is a means of transport. They share no intended instances and belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain.

A's 'Paper Abstract' is a kind of document (a short paper/abstract submission, sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), whereas B's 'Communications Topic' is a subject area/topic of the conference (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc. under Topic). They denote different concepts: a document type versus a research topic, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Conference is a specific kind of Working event (siblings Tutorial, Workshop). In ekaw, Scientific Event is a broad category whose children include Conference, Workshop, Session, Track, etc. Thus every confOf Conference is an ekaw Scientific Event, but not vice versa; Conference is strictly more specific, so it is subsumed by Scientific Event, not equivalent.

A's `reviews` links a Review to the contribution it reviews (domain Review, range Reviewed contribution), while B's `presentation` links a Speaker to a Document they present (domain Speaker, range Document). Different domains, ranges and intended meaning; not the same relation.

Author is a person role in the conference (a Person who writes papers, with properties has Related Paper / is Written By), while Registration fee is a monetary Fee subclass with children for attendee/nonmember/student fees. They belong to different branches (Person vs Money) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper-writing relation), while B's `holded by` relates a Conference to the ACM SIGKDD organisation (a conference-sponsorship/ownership relation). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property giving a person's given name (domain Person, range string), while B's 'early Registration' is a boolean flag on a Participant indicating early registration. They relate different kinds of things (name vs. registration status) and have different ranges (string vs. boolean), so they are unrelated.

A's 'has parts' is a whole-part relation from Conference volume to Conference part, while B's 'inverse of part Of 7' is the inverse of a part-of relation whose range is Event. Both express a part-whole (meronymic) relation, but they differ in direction and in the kinds of entities they connect (volume/part vs. event/part), so they are not equivalent; they are merely related part-whole relations.

Both are the top-level umbrella class for anything that happens in the conference domain: ekaw Event has children Scientific Event and Social Event and is the range/domain of participation, location, organisation and part-of relations; iasted Activity has children for before/after/conference activities and is the thing persons give, attend, are connected with, and that is dated, held in a place/time. The intended instances (conference sessions, talks, social events, pre/post-conference activities) coincide, so a reference alignment would equate Event and Activity.

A 'Conference Chair' is a person role (a chairman/person who chairs the conference), while B 'Registration' is a conference activity (an event with Delegate as a child). They denote different kinds of entities (person vs. activity) and share no meaning, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has a name' is a general naming datatype property (range string) applicable to Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher and Topic, whereas B's 'Start of conference' is a temporal property (range dateTime) specific to Conference. They denote different relations (name vs. start time) and are not equivalent.

A's Session is a kind of Lecture (a conference activity/event), while B's Speaker is a Person who presents documents. They belong to different branches (Activity vs Person) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Tax (a general money category with children Departure tax, Value added tax) and Registration fee (a specific fee with member/student registration subclasses) are both money-related concepts but neither subsumes the other: a tax is not a registration fee and a registration fee is not a tax. They overlap only in being monetary charges, so they are related, not equivalent.

A's Conference is the whole conference event (has a name, has parts, proceedings, publisher, topic), while B's Conference Session is a specific session type within a scientific event (sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session). They denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a document (a contribution submitted to the conference, with authors, decisions, subject areas), while B's Review is the evaluation of a contribution (it reviews a Reviewed contribution). They are different concepts: Paper is the reviewed artefact, Review is the assessment of it. Different parents (Document vs Conference document) and different properties confirm this.

In edas, Workshop is a kind of Academic Event (an event type), while in ekaw Conference Session is a kind of Session (a slot within a conference), and Workshop Session is a sibling of Conference Session. The two denote different concepts: an event type vs. a session type, so they are not equivalent.

A's 'has the first name' is a datatype property giving a person's given name, while B's 'has Phone' gives a person's telephone number. Both are Person->string datatype properties, but they denote different attributes (name vs. phone number), so they are not equivalent.

A's property records the acceptance-announcement date (domain Important dates), while B's records the registration deadline (domain Conference). Different events and different domains, so they are not the same relation.

In edas, 'Active Paper' is a paper that is still in the review process (it has a rating and is the parent of 'Rated Papers'), whereas in ekaw 'Regular Paper' is a paper category distinguished by its submission type (as opposed to demo, poster, industrial, workshop papers). The two classifications are orthogonal: an active paper can be a regular paper or a demo paper, and a regular paper can be active, accepted, or rejected. They do not denote the same concept.

A's 'gives presentations' links an Active conference participant to a Presentation; B's 'related To Event' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation. Both connect a paper/presentation-related entity to a presentation event, but the domains differ (participant vs. accepted paper) and the ranges are not clearly the same concept, so they overlap in the conference domain without being the same relation.

A's Poster is a kind of Contribution (a paper/presentation type, sibling of Paper and Short paper), while B's Platinum Supporter is a kind of Sponzor (a sponsorship level). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.

A's contactEmail is a datatype property of Contribution holding an email address string (comment 'confTool'), while B's Name is a datatype property of Person holding a person's name. Different domains (Contribution vs Person) and different intended values (email address vs name), so they are not the same relation.

A 'One conference day' is a temporal unit within the conference schedule (child of Conference days), while B 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is an organizational committee. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

Conference Member (cmt) is a Person subtype representing people involved in a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs), while Building (iasted) is a Place subtype for physical locations (hotel, university, airport). Their paths, parents, children and properties (member Of Conference vs. is situated in / occupy) do not overlap; they denote entirely different concepts.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people on the organising committee), while B's isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event (the event held at that place). Different domain, range and meaning; no equivalence or subsumption.

A's 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event (domain Programme, range Conference Event), while B's 'is given by' links an Activity/Item to a Person (domain Activity, Item, range Person). Different domains and ranges, different direction of meaning; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) announcing a conference. B's 'Transparency' is a document type in iasted (sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc.), a transparency/overhead document, not a conference announcement. Different intended instances; no subsumption or overlap.

A's 'details Entered By' links a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details; B's 'is Menu Of' links a Meal Menu to the Meal Event it belongs to. Different domains, ranges and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

ekaw:Person is a broad class covering all people in the conference domain (authors, participants, students, staff), while iasted:Lecturer is a narrow role under Author > Speaker > Delegate, denoting someone who gives a lecture. Every Lecturer is a Person, but not every Person is a Lecturer, so Person is strictly more general.

Topic in Conference is a subject area used to classify reviews, conference parts, and submissions (it is the object of 'has a topic or a submission contribution' and 'has a track workshop tutorial topic'). Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) with title, abstract, author, and keywords, and it points to a Topic via 'deals With'. Thus Topic is a classification concept, while Contribution is the submitted artefact; they are not the same class.

Both classes denote the role of a person who chairs a session at a conference. In edas, Session Chair is a subclass of Person alongside Author, Reviewer, etc., and is involved in reviewing/initiating calls. In iasted, Session chair is a subclass of Delegate (a person role) alongside Speaker, Listener, etc. The labels are identical and the intended instances (persons chairing sessions) coincide, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

A's 'location Of' is a specific inverse-style relation from a Location to the Event held there (domain Location, range Event). B's 'is connected with' is a broad generic association from Activity/Person to Item/Place (domain Activity, Person; range Item, Place). The domains and ranges do not match (Location vs Activity/Person; Event vs Item/Place), and the intended meanings differ: one links a venue to its event, the other is a vague connectivity relation. They are not the same relation.
A's hasAuthor relates a Paper to an Author; B's presentationOfPaper relates an Individual Presentation to an Abstract/Paper. Different domains and ranges, and not inverses, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a paper (Accepted Paper / Paper) to its presentation (Paper Presentation / Individual Presentation). Although the directions appear reversed (edas: paper -> presentation; ekaw: presentation -> paper), the intended relation is the same paper-presentation association, and the domain/range classes correspond (Accepted Paper ~ Paper, Paper Presentation ~ Individual Presentation).

Both properties express committee membership, but the domains and ranges differ: A's 'was a member of' links a Committee member to a Committee, while B's 'is Member Of' links a Person to a Conference. They overlap in intent (membership) but are not the same relation with the same domain/range, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Both classes denote a conference edition: ekaw's Conference is 'One edition of a conference' under Scientific Event, and sigkdd's Conference has properties for city, name, start/end dates and is held by an ACM SIGKDD, matching the same intended instances.

cmt:Acceptance is a decision outcome (sibling of Rejection under Decision), while edas:RejectRating is a review rating (sibling of AcceptRating under ReviewRating). Different concepts: decision vs rating.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (who added them), while B's 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members. Different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning; not equivalent, not subsumption.

A's 'has the first name' relates a Person to their given/first name, while B's 'has Surname' relates a Person to their family/last name. They denote different name components, so they are not equivalent (nor does one subsume the other).

A 'Medicine Topic' is a subject area of conference papers (a subclass of Topic alongside Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), whereas B 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a kind of document (a subclass of Abstract alongside Tutorial Abstract). They denote entirely different concepts—a research topic versus a text artefact—so they are unrelated.

A's 'belong to a conference volume' links an Important dates entity to a Conference volume (a publication/volume), while B's 'organised By' links an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organiser). Different domains, ranges and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Rejected contribution' is a reviewed submission that was rejected, sibling of 'Accepted contribution'. B's 'Published Paper' is a paper that has been published, sibling of 'Rejected Paper' and 'Accepted Paper'. The two denote opposite outcomes (rejected vs published/accepted), so they are not equivalent; they are distinct classes in the review/publishing workflow.

Both classes denote a human person in the conference domain. confOf's Person is the general superclass of all human roles (Author, Chair, Participant, etc.) with personal attributes (name, email, phone, address); sigkdd's Person is likewise the general human class with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker and personal attributes (Name, E mail, Nation). The intended instance sets coincide, so the classes are equivalent.

A's 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to its Review; B's 'is paid for' links Money to an Activity/Item it pays for. Different domains, ranges and directions of meaning, so they are not the same relation.

A's Dining Place is a kind of Place (a location where one eats), while B's Taxi is a kind of Transport vehicle (a means of transport). They belong to different branches of the domain (place vs. vehicle) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Short paper' is a type of Contribution (a document/paper kind, sibling of Paper and Poster), while B's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a Deadline (a date/event, sibling of abstract submission and author notification deadlines). They denote different concepts: a paper artefact versus a submission deadline, so they are unrelated.

A's 'has the last name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (a person's surname), while B's 'is made from' is an object property relating an Item to another Item (a composition/material relation). They differ in domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Published Paper is a status-based subclass of Paper (siblings are Accepted/Rejected/Pending/Withdrawn Paper), i.e. a paper that has been published. In ekaw, Camera Ready Paper is a paper in its final, camera-ready form, a stage-based subclass of Paper (siblings are Submitted Paper and various paper types). Both denote a paper that has progressed past acceptance toward publication, so they overlap, but they are not the same concept: a camera-ready paper is the final manuscript version, while a published paper is one that has actually appeared. Neither strictly subsumes the other, so 'related' is the appropriate relation.

Student (a Person subtype in ekaw) and Gold Supporter (a Sponzor subtype in sigkdd) denote entirely different concepts: one is a person role, the other a sponsorship level. No overlap in intended instances.

Both properties relate a Review to the person who wrote it. cmt's writtenBy has domain Review and range Reviewer; ekaw's reviewWrittenBy has domain Review and range Possible Reviewer, and is a subproperty of writtenBy. The intended meaning (the reviewer who wrote a given review) is the same, so a reference alignment would record them as equivalent.

University is an academic organization (a subclass of Organization, sibling of Company, domain of studyAt), while Textual Review Question is a kind of review question used in the reviewing process. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no instances.

A's 'Conference part' is a generic component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) that is part of a Conference volume, whereas B's 'Conference' is the whole conference event with city, start/end dates, name, and held-by relation. A Conference part is strictly more specific than a Conference, so A is subsumed by B; they are not equivalent.

A is an administrative event (the registration process/activity for participants), while B is a committee (a group of people organizing the conference). They belong to different branches (Event vs Committee) and denote different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A is a conference topic (computer networks applications) under the Topic hierarchy, while B is a time entity (a day of a trip) under the Time hierarchy. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no intended instances.

A's property links a Topic to a Review preference (a topic's review preference), while B's property links a Speaker to a Document (a speaker's presentation). Different domains (Topic vs Speaker) and ranges (Review preference vs Document), so they denote different relations.

A's has Location relates a Conference Event to a Place (where an event is held), while B's hold relates an ACM SIGKDD (the organisation/series) to a Conference (the event it holds). The domains and ranges differ in kind: A's range is a location, B's range is a conference event, and A's domain is an event while B's domain is an organisation. They are not the same relation.

Contribution in confOf is the general submission class (children Paper, Poster, Short paper; written by Author, reviewed by PC member, has title/abstract/keywords). Active Paper in edas is a specific state of a Paper (a Paper that is under review, with a rating), a subclass of Paper. Contribution is broader than Active Paper, so Contribution subsumes Active Paper; they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a presentation given at a conference. In Conference, Presentation is a kind of conference contribution that is given by an active participant and has an abstract; in iasted, Presentation is a conference activity with subtypes such as Power Point presentation and Video presentation. Despite different parent categories (contribution vs. activity), the intended instances coincide: a presentation event/artefact delivered at a conference. The shared label and compatible domain roles support equivalence.

A's Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip under Social event), while B's Speaker is a person role under Delegate (with children Author and Reviewer). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

A's SC Member is a Steering Committee member, a role a person holds in the conference organisation (a subclass of PC Member under Person).
