B's Registration SIGKDD Member is a fee category (a subclass of Registration fee) describing a type of registration payment for SIGKDD members. They belong to different branches (person/role vs. fee) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Program Committee' is a collective body of reviewers (domain of 'has Program Committee Member', range of 'member Of Program Committee'), whereas B's 'Scholar' is a subclass of Person denoting an individual with a price category, sibling of Author, Chair PC, Member PC, etc. A committee is not a person, so the two classes are unrelated.

A is 'Accepted contribution' (a reviewed contribution that was accepted, sibling of Rejected contribution, parent of Camera ready contribution). B is 'Rejected Paper' (a paper that was rejected, sibling of Accepted Paper). They denote opposite outcomes of the review process, so they are not equivalent; in fact they are disjoint concepts.

A's 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor, i.e. a role a person plays as a contributor to a conference document (with children Contribution 1th author and Contribution co author). B's 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person, i.e. a person who authors a paper. The two overlap in the conference domain (a regular author is a paper author), but they are not the same concept: one is a contribution-role class under Conference contribution, the other is a person class under Person. They are related rather than equivalent.
A's 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to Publisher; B's 'writes' links Author to Contribution. Different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a regular contribution (a full paper document), while B's Abstract is a distinct document type (the abstract of a paper/talk), a sibling of Paper in ekaw. They denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Participant is a person role (a subclass of Person with children Member, Regular, Student), whereas Registration fee is a monetary fee (subclass of Fee). They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A Meta Review is a review of reviews (a document-level artefact, child of Review in cmt), whereas an edas Numerical Review Question is a type of review form question (a scoring question with a numeric answer, sibling of Textual Review Question). They denote different concepts: one is a review artefact, the other a question type used in the review form.

Both denote the abstract of a paper: cmt's Paper Abstract is a kind of Paper (the abstract version of a paper), and ekaw's Abstract is a Document that is presented as a paper / has a paper presented as it, i.e. the abstract of a paper. The intended instances (paper abstracts) coincide, so they are equivalent despite the different parent (Paper vs Document).

A 'Pending Paper' is a paper in the conference-submission workflow (a subclass of Paper, sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper). B 'Cheque' is a payment document (subclass of Payment document, sibling of Bank transfer). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (submission status vs. payment instrument) and share no intended instances.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a conference applicant who has registered (a subtype of Conference applicant, with child Paid applicant), i.e. an attendee/registrant role. B 'TPC Member' is a program-committee member role, a sibling of Author, Reviewer, Attendee, etc. The two denote different roles in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (the admin enters review criteria for a conference), while B's 'has Review' relates a Paper to a Review (a paper has a review). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (domain: Program Committee Member, range: Administrator). B's 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to its Program committee (domain: Conference volume, range: Program committee). Different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

Both denote a speaker who gives a distinguished/invited talk at a conference, but the contexts differ: A's 'Invited speaker' is a kind of Conference contributor (a person role alongside Regular author and Active conference participant), while B's 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a kind of Author (a person who has contributed a paper) and is a sibling of Tutorial speaker and Lecturer. A plenary lecture speaker is typically an invited speaker, so the concepts overlap, but they are not the same class in the two ontologies' hierarchies.

A's 'Submitted Paper' is a specific kind of paper (a Paper that has been submitted, with child 'Assigned Paper'), while B's 'Document' is a broad top-level artefact class whose children include Review, Submission, Form, Payment document, etc. Every Submitted Paper is a Document, but Documents include many non-paper items, so Submitted Paper is strictly narrower than Document.

A Free Time Break is a non-academic break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break) within the conference schedule, whereas B Trip day is a time unit (sibling of Conference days and Deadline) denoting a day of trips. They belong to different branches (event vs. time) and denote different concepts.

A 'Workshop Session' is a kind of Session (a scientific event/activity within a conference), while B 'Program Committee' is a Committee (a group of people). They belong to different branches of the conference domain (event vs. committee) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Person in cmt is a general class whose children include Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, and User, so it covers all people involved in the conference. PC Member in ekaw is a more specific class under Possible Reviewer, representing only program committee members. Thus Person is broader and subsumes PC Member, not equivalent.

A's Sponzorship is a subclass of Money (a financial category alongside Fee, Tax, Tip), i.e. the sponsorship payment/funding itself. B's Gold Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor, a specific sponsorship tier/role (alongside Platinum, Silver, Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor). One denotes a monetary amount, the other a sponsor role/level; they are not the same concept.

Paper Abstract in cmt is the abstract document of a paper (sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), whereas Poster in confOf is a distinct contribution type (sibling of Paper and Short paper under Contribution). They denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

In edas, 'Accepted Paper' is a specific status of a Paper (sibling of Rejected/Pending/Withdrawn/Published Paper), i.e. a paper that has been accepted. In ekaw, 'Submitted Paper' is a paper that has been submitted (parent of Assigned Paper), a different lifecycle stage. The two denote different statuses of a paper, not the same concept, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (informational material for attendees), while B's 'Platinum Supporter' is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. Different domains (document vs. sponsor role), no shared instances or properties.

A's hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people on the committee), while B's isTopicOf relates a Topic to the Conference or Paper it is a topic of. Different domains (Conference vs Topic), different ranges (Conference Member vs Conference/Paper), and different intended meanings; they are not the same relation.

A's 'Conference announcement' is a document (a subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. a written announcement about a conference. B's 'Conference Session' is a scientific event (subclass of Session, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session), i.e. a time slot of talks at a conference. A document and an event are different kinds of things, so the two classes are unrelated despite the shared word 'Conference'.

A 'Coffee Break' is a non-academic break event in the conference schedule, while a 'Program Committee' is a committee of people. They belong to entirely different branches (event vs. committee) and share no intended instances.

A's Conference Member is a broad role class covering chairs, authors, PC members and reviewers (children include Author, Conference Chair, Program Committee Member, Reviewer). B's Member PC is specifically a PC member/reviewer (comment 'Reviewer', property reviewes Contribution, expert On Topic). A PC member is a kind of conference member, so Member PC is strictly narrower: A subsumes B, i.e. B is subsumed_by A. They are not equivalent because A also covers authors and chairs.

A Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference event), while a Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship level under Sponzor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and denote different concepts.
